title: Every day is a little less than what you see.
text:
According to Mehr News Agency, as two of the specialists in facial plastic surgery say, the high rate of rhinoplasty in the country can not be considered a negative score alone, but what is important is the scientific and systematic implementation of rhinoplasty that causes the health of the person not to be damaged.
At the same time, entrusting your nose to people who do not have the expertise and knowledge of such surgeries will have unpleasant complications.
Amir Armin Sattar, a fellowship of facial plastic surgery and a professor at Tehran University of Medical Sciences, in an interview with Mehr News Agency, said: “Aesthetics is a problem in any society, which can be either inherent or caused by surgery. ”
Referring to the large amount of complaints from doctors following facial surgeries, he added: "Sometimes repeat surgery is inevitable and the patient should undergo surgery again because of the conditions he has."
But, we have many cases of needless surgeries that want to improve small defects that get worse, and that's a disaster.
Professor of Tehran University of Medical Sciences, in response to the high rates of rhinoplasty in the country, said: "It is not possible to make a law about the personal life of individuals."
The level of culture of our society is much higher than that of neighboring countries and the region, and at present, therapeutic tourism is considered a power in Iran.
This specialty of facial plastic surgery emphasized: To perform a rhinoplasty, three points should be considered.
First, it is the choice of the patient that should be made by a specialist doctor, and not everyone who wishes to have surgery should be operated on.
Second, there is a limit to surgery and it is for the betterment, not the idealization of the person.
The third point, he added, is that we should know that unnecessary surgeries do not help to be more beautiful and that such surgeries should be done again with research.
Meanwhile, Seyyed Ali Reza Mesbahi, a specialist in facial plastic surgery, in an interview with Mehr reporter, said: "The high rate of rhinoplasty cannot be considered as a negative score."
If there is a need for surgery, it is not a fault but the choice of the patient must be made correctly.
A healthy person means that the health of both body and soul exist together.
Beauty and aesthetics are very important and certainly the nose is no exception to this rule.
However, there are a number of scientific laws governing it that must be observed.
In the field of beauty, the patient does not comment on what form the nose has.
Rather, it is the physician who is qualified to tell the patient and determine how he or she should be treated.
This specialty of facial plastic surgery, referring to the demands and sometimes unreasonable demands of some patients for rhinoplasty, added: "One of our problems and the wrong thinking in the society is that girls and boys think that the smaller their nose, the more arches and the higher the tip, the more beautiful they are."
Which is not the case at all.
From the point of view of beauty, nose and face is beautiful that the proportions are observed in it.
That is, it does not harm your health.
He continued: The nose can be reduced to some extent, but the important thing is that in this operation, there is no complication for the patient.
That is, the cartilage and skin of the nose should not be destroyed, and also the respiratory condition of the patient should not be disturbed.
Moussahi, referring to the fact that the high rate of rhinoplasty is not considered a problem, said: It should be noted that how many of these surgeries are done correctly and how much the selection of patients is correct and scientific.
It is the duty of the doctor to perform a correct and scientific surgery according to his skill and competence.
The patient should know that if the shape of his nose changes, it can no longer be corrected and cannot be treated.
Day by day, surgeons who perform nose job based on scientific principles are increasing.
However, I have to say that we are still far from universal standards and this is a matter for the patient and the doctor.
This specialty of facial plastic surgery, said: loss of beauty and function of the nose are two important complications of cosmetic surgery in a non-scientific and incorrect way.

title: The beginning of the dolphin hunting season in Japan
text:
The AFP photo rights have begun in the Japanese city of Taiji, where a controversial annual dolphin hunt has begun.
The dolphins are driven into a small bay where some of the animals are slaughtered in shallow water.
Dolphins are also caught alive to be sold to aquariums and water parks.
Hunting in Taiji has been practiced in the area for decades, and global attention has grown after winning a documentary at the 2009 Oscars.
Japan has resumed whaling to sell its meat this year despite international protests.
This year ’ s hunt in Taiji began on Sunday, and according to Japanese media reports, the boats returned to shore without hunting any dolphins on the first day.
Today, the fishing boats are going back to the sea to try to steer the dolphins ashore.
Environmentalists say that this kind of hunting is very cruel because the dolphin has been suffocating for about 30 minutes.
But fishermen in Taiji say their livelihoods depend on dolphin hunting.
Playback of this file on your device is not supported.
The Japanese hunt whales again, and the dolphin-hunting period in the city is about six months long.
Japan has come under heavy criticism this year for resuming whale shapes.
The country has also withdrawn from the International Whaling Commission, whose main task is to monitor the status of whales and set a timetable for their hunting around the world.
Japanese whale-hunting ships left the coast on July 1, and to this day one whale has been killed and its meat sold.
According to the International Whaling Commission, hunting has been banned since 1986.
However, Japan never completely stopped whaling.

title: Tracing prostheses used in plastic surgery
text:
According to Mehr News Agency, Hamed Bateni, in connection with the issue of medical tourism, said: "The medical conditions of the country have scientifically caused patients from other countries to travel to Iran from the region and even from remote parts of the world and benefit from the medical field in Iran."
Pointing out that some people think that patients from other parts of the world come to Iran only because of the cheapness of medical services, he said: "This is a mistake because many countries offer cheaper services in the field of medicine, but patients do not trust and do not want to travel to their country for treatment because their medicine is not strong or the facilities of surgical centers are weak and sometimes unsterile."
The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons continued: In recent years, measures have been started to organize medical tourists through the Ministry of Health and gradually the programs are going to be written and comprehensive so that we hope that soon the field of medical tourism will be completely out of control and operated by translators or non-standard institutions and only under the supervision of the Ministry of Health.
In response to the question of what effect the sanctions of the enemies have had on the field of plastic and cosmetic surgery and whether you are facing a shortage of drugs in this field, he noted: The field of plastic and cosmetic surgery is not very dependent on the aspect of drugs with shortages, but equipment and devices such as implants, prosthetics and beauty products with changing currency fluctuations have increased prices and sometimes products are scarce and imports are not easy.
He said: "The equipment required by plastic surgeons is provided by different brands, depending on the company's production and distribution and their price varies, but all of these equipment and equipment are of good quality and there is no problem in this regard."
The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons noted that most of the equipment and equipment needed for plastic and cosmetic surgery such as implants and prostheses do not have passenger or luggage entry because the reference of these devices is known and all of them have serial numbers that can be traced on the website of the manufacturer and distributor, so there is no concern in this regard.
Bateni said that patients can use this serial number and specifications to track the prosthesis and device used in their body and make sure of its quality, because the prostheses used in plastic and cosmetic surgeries are different from some other surgeries and the patient has a direct role in its preparation.

Pepper gas was sprayed on our faces, our eyes, our clothes, even our sleeping bags and food.

The police sprayed pepper gas on everyone. ”
Humanité asks: “Does the law of the French Republic apply in Calais? ”

title: What is the great fear of contemporary man?
text:
According to the EurekAlert website, and based on studies by psychologists from Brigham Young University (USA), loneliness and social isolation are the greatest threat to humanity in the contemporary era.
The findings were published in the American Psychological Association ’ s 125 annual conventions.
According to experts, relationships with other people are a human need for people ’ s mental health and are key to humanity ’ s survival.
According to a study conducted by the AARP, 42.6 million American adults aged 45 suffer from chronic loneliness.
According to the 2014 census, more than a quarter of the population lives alone, and more than half of the citizens are unmarried.
The scientists conducted two experiments to get to the study.
The first experiment, which included 148 scientific papers, was conducted on 300,000 volunteers.
According to the study, strong social relationships lead to a 50 percent reduction in the risk of early death.
According to the second study, which involved 3.4 million people in North America, Europe, Asia and Australia, social isolation or loneliness increases the risk of early death.
This factor is even higher than obesity, with higher mortality rates.
Experts believe that social relationships have a huge impact on people ’ s health.
The construction of amusement centers and parks for retirees is a significant contribution to this global phenomenon.

title: When shopping, why should you be sensitive to the title of “transgenic ”?
text:
Genetically modified (genetically modified) crops and plants are among those challenging issues that always have a lot of support and opposition due to various issues such as environmental, economic and health.
They say that the problem of food supply, both in terms of quantity and quality, will be solved in the future with such technology.
While its opponents argue that without the need for such a new technology in the field of plant breeding, relying on indigenous methods and combining it with modern science and providing the necessary platform for the development of sustainable agriculture, the challenge of food production in the future can be solved.
These people say that, for example, if we want to study this technology from an economic point of view, because the genetically modified seeds are produced exclusively by a number of large multinationals, the most well-known of which is Monsanto, the method of producing such seeds (patent) is one of the secret secrets of these companies.
So farmers who use these seeds will no longer be able to reproduce like native seeds, and will have to buy their seeds from these companies every year.
With this kind of policy, these companies make farmers permanently dependent on them and eventually make large sums of money.
GMOs are plants that have received one or more of their limited genes in the laboratory through methods specific to molecular genetics or genetic engineering.
For example, in maize plants, they found species other than those that are related to maize because of their genetic structure.
In the field of genetic engineering, rather than trying to modify plants in conventional or classical ways, specialists try to separate genes for their desired traits, even from microbes or bacteria, and enter the plant cell.
The aim of these works is to improve the resistance of the plant to some pests and plant diseases and increase the tolerance of stresses such as salinity and dehydration, improve the quality and marketability of the product, increase the production and yield of the plant, increase productivity in agriculture and ultimately increase the level of community health through reducing the use of various pesticides and chemical fertilizers.
The major GM crops that have been placed on the world trade market are soybeans, rapeseed, corn and cotton.
Of course, the variety of products produced is greater than these four.
The United States, Brazil, Argentina, Canada and India have the highest levels of GM crops, respectively.
Of these, the United States is at the top with 75 million hectares.
It has been 22 years since the commercial cultivation of GMOs in the world, and during these 22 years the production of these products has been increasing.
Among them are the countries that have officially banned biotech cultivation in their own country.
Africa: Algeria (since 2000), Madagascar (since 2002), Asia (4 countries): Turkey, Kyrgyzstan, Bhutan, Saudi Arabia.
Americas (4 countries): Belize, Peru, Ecuador, Venezuela.
Europe (28 countries): Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Malta, Cyprus, Greece, Bulgaria, Russia, Serbia, Croatia, Italy, Denmark, Hungary, Moldova, Latvia, Lithuania, Austria, Poland, Slovenia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Luxembourg, Ukraine, Norway, Switzerland. It hasn't.
Rather, in some cases, GMOs due to the incompleteness of the health review process have had devastating effects on the health of the community and the environment.
Genetically modified plants, as defined by the World Health Organization, are either plants, animals or microscopic organisms whose genetic makeup (or DNA) has changed in a way that does not occur in nature through natural mating or natural recombination (conventional methods of plant modification).
In the classical method of plant breeding (non-transgenic), in the method of plant breeding, a set of genes (relatives of the plant in question) that carry different traits and characteristics in the plant are transferred to the plant.
Characteristics such as: resistance to cold, heat, pests, diseases, dehydration, salinity, increasing the efficiency of water consumption (producing more product for less water consumption).
While in transgenic plants, a few selected genes are transferred to the plant.
For this reason, the stability of plants in non-genetically modified methods against different environmental factors is higher due to the presence of different genes.
Or in other words, in this way, we are only speeding up processes that could have occurred naturally in the plant.
Critics of GMOs believe that the cultivation and production of these products have increased the use of toxins such as glyphosate poison (Roundup) at the farm level.
The introduction of these toxins into the human food cycle can cause disease.
Also, these plants can destroy beneficial soil bacteria by fixing large amounts of these toxins in the soil where they are cultivated and lead to loss of soil fertility.
Studies by some scientists show that GMOs can indirectly cause cancer and cause a variety of diseases.
Problems that consuming such products can cause include: (1) In many genetic manipulations, for reasons such as the interaction of the new (alien) gene with the genes of the plant in question can lead to unforeseen changes.
The altered genes can be combined in different ways with genes from other plants, microbes, and animals.
Most research on GMOs is done on the cells of laboratory animals, and the effects of their use in humans are very limited or difficult to investigate.
But some transgenic crops, such as corn, soybeans, and wheat, release a toxin called glyphosate due to its resistance, which can hold high amounts of this toxin in their edible tissues.
Toxic substances that eventually lead to serious illnesses.
A 2011 review published in the European Journal of Environmental Sciences evaluated 19 studies of mammals fed with genetically modified soybeans and corn.
In 90-day long trials, liver and kidney problems were identified as a result of the use of GMOs.
Kidney and liver function was impaired in 43.5% and 30.8% of cases, respectively.
In a two-year trial of rats consuming transgenic corn — rats that consumed 11 percent of GM corn in their diets — all female mice died two to three times faster than control mice.
The difference was most apparent in three groups of male mice that were fed GM crops.
Also, biochemical data (the study of chemical processes in the structure of living organisms) confirmed chronic kidney defects for all male and female control groups.
According to other reports, people who use transgenic products experience the following side effects: increased allergies, resistance to antibiotic drugs, internal organ problems, reproductive system disorders, and the growth of cancerous tumors.
Another study conducted over 10 years in Norway found that GMOs lead to obesity, digestive problems, and damage to important organs such as the liver, kidneys, pancreas, and reproductive organs.
Is it finally good or bad?
The main task of a researcher is to discover the truth, adhere to scientific ethics, accept reality by providing documentation, and avoid politicizing knowledge.
Contamination of scientific materials and documents with political issues and the lack of honesty in stating the facts due to financial, political, factional interests, gaining power, maintaining the job position, organizational interests and scientific trends is a deviation from the path of scientific ethics.
Despite all of the studies mentioned above, the technology of genetic manipulation, or GMOs, remains the subject of study and a point of contention for researchers.
In other words, the technology of genetic manipulation of living organisms is like a double-edged knife, which can be useful both according to the scientific opinion of some researchers, and according to the study and some other scientific studies, it has been found to have irreparable effects.
For this reason, the full recognition of the usefulness or harmful of GMOs due to the lack of ethical issues in the field of research and lack of scientific bias by a number of researchers has contradictory arguments, and it is still not possible to issue a single and decisive verdict on the health of GMOs.
However, at present in our country, according to the approval of a bill in the Islamic Consultative Assembly in the form of the national law "Biosafety" passed in 1388, all matters related to the production, release, export, supply, sale and use of genetically modified organisms are allowed, but the government is obliged to provide the necessary measures and tests to determine and inform what products are transgenic.
The government should also require manufacturers and importers to put labels on GM products.
A requirement that led some companies to remove the term "genetically modified" from their existing product combinations due to fear of declining sales.
The philosophy of requiring the label "GMO" on these products in many countries of the world and domestic law is that the consumer has the right to be aware of the GMO when purchasing the GMO product and to buy and consume the GMO product with his conscious discretion.
In the end, it should be added that it seems that the right decision and procedure in this regard, given the current uncertain situation, is that along with many countries in the world, as long as there are many doubts about the use of such technologies, to protect people ’ s health and prevent environmental destruction, the government and private agricultural sector investors will invest more in the field of environmentally friendly technologies.

title: Global warming is real.

In this particular study, we looked at the impact of temperature increases on major agricultural crops, such as wheat, rice, maize and soybeans, and found that any change in temperature would cause a sharp drop in yields.
On the other hand, in some countries, increasing the temperature will increase the yield; in northern China, for every degree of temperature increase, 2% added to the yield, and the same with rice and corn France, 4% increase. However, the professor continued: If the global temperature rises 4 degrees, we will see a 25% drop in the yield of these four important products.

title: US Opposes Iran ’ s Joining of International Thermonuclear Project
text:
The International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) is an international nuclear energy research project centered in France.
Since the JCPOA came into force, Iranian officials have promised to join the project, but now, the Journal of Science quotes Iranian and European officials as saying that Iran ’ s membership in the project has been opposed by one of its members, the United States.
The publication quoted Ali Akbar Salehi, the head of Iran ’ s Atomic Energy Organization, as saying that Iran ’ s membership process was going well until Donald Trump was elected president of the United States.
On Iran ’ s international cooperation in the nuclear field, Mr. Salehi added that Iran ’ s first priority is “preserving the integrity of the JCPOA. ”
According to Science, Iran has some minor cooperation with Europe in the field of nuclear, but by joining the ITER, Iran wants its students and scientists to gain more knowledge in this field.
One of them, Mahmoud Koranevis, head of the Plasma Physics Center in Iran, told Science that if the initial membership turns into a full membership within a few years, it could bring a lot of money to the research.
“There is no mystery in nuclear fusion, but in our case (Iran) science and politics are mixed. ”
We discussed Iran ’ s nuclear cooperation and the importance of membership in the ITER with Mark Fitzpatrick, executive director of the International Institute for Strategic Studies, in Washington.
Why is it important to join a project like ITER, and why is Iran pursuing a membership that is now, according to some unconfirmed reports, opposed by the United States?
One of the main goals of the 2015 nuclear deal, from Iran ’ s point of view, was to normalize the nuclear program, legitimize it in the eyes of the world, and be able to operate normally in the realm of nuclear trade and cooperation.
Iran ’ s long history of deception and violation of IAEA safeguards had diverted Iran from the main line.
In recent years, Iran has been trying to improve its position.
As a result, Iran ’ s attempt to join the Aiter Consortium has a symbolic aspect.
The JCPOA clearly indicates that other countries are cooperating with Iran on nuclear technology.
To refuse to accept membership in the ITR is the opposite of this clause.
How do you think Iran has so far not protested, or even made it a violation of the other side ’ s commitment?
Iran has made allegations of violations in other areas of the agreement.
For example, Iran ’ s actions to not encourage trade and commerce with Iran.
U.S. officials, including some senior officials, have unfortunately taken steps to deprive Iran of some of the benefits of the JCPOA.
As a result, there is no shortage in Iran to claim that the United States is violating the commitment.
Even their claims have been exaggerated.
This particular issue of nuclear cooperation, I think, has not yet been addressed by the Iranian authorities to turn it into a political issue, and this may be a good thing for the technical people in Iran.
They probably want to resolve the issue without drawing political attention, and perhaps they think they can become members of the Aitre before they become political.
It is true that the IAEA is monitoring Iran ’ s program, but in terms of transparency, does opening the way for this cooperation, and the entry of various organizations and groups, especially in the field of technology as well as nuclear security, and its normalization, not contribute to greater transparency of Iran ’ s program?
I think you made an important point.
Clarification is the goal of the international community in the context of Iran ’ s nuclear program, and cooperation in the field of nuclear security and other cooperation that is not related to the militarization technologies of the nuclear program helps to encourage transparency.
Of course, the other side of the coin is that for years, under sanctions imposed on Iran for violating safeguards, advanced countries have tried to block Iranian students from obtaining nuclear expertise.
The reason for this was that any science in this field can have a use in the production of weapons and can be an indirect use in some way.
Because learning nuclear energy doesn ’ t necessarily help weapons, increasing knowledge of plasma physics and advanced technologies, including through Aiter, may help with the science and expertise that could then lead to weapons development in a possible scenario.

title: The artwork was found 23 years after the theft.
text:
The painting, Portrait of a Lady, is a work of art stolen from the Piacenza Modern Art Gallery in northern Italy in 1977 and valued at around £50 million.
Following the disappointment of most experts, after removing the wall adhesive, a worker came across a black bag containing the missing painting.
The gallery refuses to officially declare the painting as belonging to Austrian painting until it is confirmed that it is the original painting.
However, initial research by an expert suggests that the painting is the work of the painter.
Also, a group of experts with scientific and artistic analysis examines the originality of the work.
Police are investigating whether the painting was hidden with the aim of being removed from the gallery wall after the media noise subsided.
Klimt painted a portrait of a lady at the end of her life.
Ten months before the robbery, art student Claudia Maga discovered that the painting had been painted on top of another painting.
To prove his hypothesis, the student convinced the former director of the Piacenza Gallery to have the work tested with X-rays.
Beneath the portrait of a lady was a portrait of a young girl from Vienna who died young, and Klimt created another work to forget the pain of her death.
In addition to his artistic activities, Klimt was a member of the Viennese separatist movement.
The movement was formed in 1897 by a group of Austrian artists who had resigned from the Association of Artists.
Klimt was the first leader of the movement.
Communicating and exchanging ideas with artists outside Austria, sparking artistic nationalism, reviving decorative arts and opposing the dominance of the Vienna Academy of Arts were among the goals of the movement.
He was also a great designer.
He has more than three thousand designs left to show his keen eye and powerful hand.
His bold and agile pen for human figures and postures inspired younger artists.

title: Global Warming Effects on Life: Why Winter Isn't Cold This Year
text:
Over the past few years, weather patterns have changed around the world.
The shifting of seasons, the changing migration patterns of plants and animals all point to the impact of global warming on human life.
He said: “This winter, there was not a lot of snow.
Of course, this is not a new course.
It has been a few years that the phenomenon of dry winters with warmer weather than usual occurs in Iran.
Climate change is not unique to Iran or the Middle East.
The weather around the world has changed dramatically.
For example, European winters have become longer.
Research suggests that the main reason for all of this is a phenomenon known as global warming.
A phenomenon that has accelerated since the mid-20th century, and now its effects are clearly visible.
Global warming is predicted to have strange, long-lasting, and in many cases destructive consequences for the Earth.
Humans are the main cause of global warming, and various research shows that the gradual warming of the Earth ’ s surface, oceans and atmosphere is caused by human activities.
One of the most important reasons is the use of fossil fuels, which release carbon dioxide, methane and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
Despite the numerous political controversies surrounding climate change, a report by a government research group on climate change in the United States found that scientists are more convinced than ever that there is a link between human activity and global warming.
More than 197 international scientific organizations agree that global warming is a real event and that global warming has already had devastating effects.
The ice melts and the lakes evaporate, says Joseph Verne, professor of geology and environmental science at the University of Pittsburgh, “It ’ s possible to really see what ’ s happening.
The ice at the Earth ’ s two poles is melting.
Lakes around the world are slowly evaporating, and in some cases evaporating much faster than their surroundings.
The migratory patterns of animals have changed, and plants have also changed the timing of their activity.
The trees will bloom earlier in the spring, and the leaves will fall earlier in the fall.
Before 2016, 2015 was the hottest year in the world, according to NASA data, since the record of global temperature has been recorded since 1895, 2016 has been the warmest year in all of this history.
In other words, this year the Earth's surface temperature is 1.78 degrees Fahrenheit (0.
99 ° C) was warmer than the average temperature for the entire 20th century.
According to NASA, prior to 2016, 2015 was the world ’ s warmest year.
This trend has been repeated in previous years.
In fact, 16 of the world ’ s 17 warmest years have been on record since 2001.
Extreme weather events are another consequence of global warming.
Global warming has caused summers to be warmer and in some regions winters colder than usual.
Changes in weather cause polar jet streams to move south.
These currents, which are in fact the boundary between the cold air of the Arctic and the warm tropical air, carry with them the cold air and the polar ice.
For this reason, in some areas, sudden cold or colder winters are observed than usual.
This trend, if repeated in the long term, is a consequence of global warming.
A cold or hot season or even a year with these characteristics will have little effect on the formation of the climate.
Changes in climate occur when the hot or cold years repeat and we realize that these changes are no longer a sudden phenomenon.
Global warming may also lead to extreme changes other than cold or unexpected heat.
The shape of the tornadoes, for example, is also changing.
This is still under investigation, but current atmospheric computer models suggest that hurricanes are slowing down on a global scale, but may increase in intensity.
Adam Sobel, author of a book on climate change, says that even though hurricanes happen less on a global scale, they are still more frequent in some regions.
In addition, scientists are confident that these hurricanes will become more intense due to climate change.
Because they draw their energy from the difference in temperature between warm, tropical oceans and cold air in the upper atmosphere, global warming makes that difference even more.
And when it comes down to it, the worst part is that it gets worse.
In addition to that, lightning is another consequence of global warming.
According to a 2014 study, the number of thunderstorms in North America is expected to increase by 50% if global temperatures rise.
The researchers found that for every 1 degree Celsius warmer in the atmosphere, the probability of a thunderstorm increases by 12 percent.
On the other hand, scientists predict more extreme weather events such as heat waves, droughts, storms and blizzards.
Climate models predict that global warming will cause air patterns around the world to change significantly.
This change is likely to include a change in wind patterns, annual precipitation, and seasonal temperature changes.
Also, because of high levels of greenhouse gas emissions, the climate may not change for years.
Change will continue for decades or more.
For example, in the northern states of the United States, precipitation increases annually, while in the Pacific Northwest, summer precipitation decreases.
The gradual reduction of snow fall is one of the early indicators of climate change as ice melts.
According to the Journal of Climate Change, residents of North America, Europe and Asia saw a decline in snowfall between 1960 and 2015.
According to the National Snow and Ice Center, the volume of permanently frozen land in the Northern Hemisphere has decreased by 10 percent since the early 1900s.
Microbes wake up, melting ice leads to drift and other sudden landslides.
It may also lead to a resurgence of long-dormant microbes, such as a 2016 case in which a reservoir of buried deer carcasses was discovered.
This led to an outbreak of anthrax.
One of the most dramatic effects of global warming is the decline of polar ice.
In the autumn and winter of 2015 and 2016, the volume of floating ice fell to the lowest level.
In this season, the amount of ice and snow should be highest.
The process of melting and reducing the thickness of the ice continues over the years.
According to a study conducted by NASA ’ s IceBridge operation, the shiny surface of the ice reflects less heat back into the atmosphere as a result.
Oceans that are darker in color absorb more heat.
All of these events cyclically lead to the melting of most of the ice.
Sea level rise and ocean acidification as a whole increase as the ice melts.
The World Meteorological Organization reported in 2014 that sea levels around the world had risen by 3 millimeters.
That ’ s nearly twice the average annual sea level rise in the 20th century (1.6 mm).
The melting of polar ice, along with reduced glacier volumes in Greenland, North America, South America, Europe and Asia, is contributing to sea level rise.
But there are also people to blame.
According to a 2013 report, scientists are 95 percent sure that warming oceans, melting ice, and rising levels since the 1950s were caused by humans.
This rate of growth is accelerating in the coming years.
If current trends continue, many coastal areas (where more than half of the world ’ s population lives) will be submerged.
According to the American Academy of Sciences, the impact of global warming on global ecosystems will be profound and widespread.
Many plants and animals are now migrating northwards or elevations as temperatures have risen.
This process doesn ’ t just mean immigration.
Animals are migrating from the tropics to the poles.
Simply put, they follow the trend of good weather.
But when the pace of climate change exceeds the rate at which species migrate, it will be challenging.
For this reason, many animals cannot survive in the new climate and are likely to become extinct.
Warmer weather also leads to the spread of many pathogenic pathogens that once existed only in areas around the equator, leading to the death of many plant and animal species.
Half of Earth ’ s plants and one-third of its animals could disappear by 2080.
Social impacts are also crippling as a result of these changes in agricultural systems.
The growing season changes in some areas, and along with drought, harsh weather and lack of accumulated snow, increased diversity of pets, depletion of groundwater resources and forest areas, leads to a decline in agricultural and livestock production worldwide.
There have been climate fluctuations in the history of the planet, and some scientists believe that these changes occur in cycles.
Dr. Jahangir Parhamat, a member of the Water Technology Development Headquarters, Drought, Erosion and Environment Vice-Presidency for Science and Technology, said: Human manipulation and climate fluctuations are the main causes of air pollution and warming that have changed the atmosphere of the Earth. Human manipulation and climatic fluctuations are the main causes of air pollution and warming that have changed the conditions of the Earth 's atmosphere.
The introduction of too much carbon dioxide into the Earth's layers and the heat from fossil fuels within 10 kilometers of the Earth's main atmosphere are the reasons for the warm weather this season.
Stating that the role of humans on the planet and the increase in carbon dioxide and the increase in energy from fossil fuels are effective, he said: "The heat of the earth is naturally from sunlight, but now industries and machines in the environment are spreading their energy and causing heat."
Stating that climate fluctuations have existed over the past 60 years, he noted: "During these years, hot and cold years, we had cold and hot periods; periods last several years."
He said that there have been climatic fluctuations in the history of the planet, so that the drought cycle in the 40-50 decade lasted nearly 16 years.
"Our data is based on data from the last 60 years, so we can't estimate how long the drought cycle will last, but the cycles are five to 13 years based on our data.
However, according to what has been said, the trend of climate change affecting the Earth seems to continue and we have to wait for a new era in which humans struggle to survive due to new weather patterns, agriculture, animal migration, ocean warming, etc.

title: The movie is in the dark, in the dark.
text:
Online Young Art and Culture Service: In August this year, the media announced the selection of a documentary as a representative of Iran's Oscar and wrote: The documentary film "In Search of Farideh", directed by Azadeh Mousavi and Cyrus Attaei, was selected to be the representative of Iranian cinema for the 2020 Oscar ceremony after the continuous meetings of the board of introducing the Iranian cinema to the Oscars.
"In Search of Farida" is about a woman named Farida, who was abandoned in the shrine of Imam Reza forty years ago and was adopted by a Dutch couple and taken to the Netherlands after being transferred to a nursery.
Farideh, who has not returned to Iran over the years due to fear of traveling to Iran, has started a remote search to find her real family for a few years.
After the strange and full selection of the representative of Iranian cinema, many experts and critics reacted coldly to the selection of this selection, and harsh criticism was directed at the decision of the authorities, but the only reason for the selection of the delegation was the presence of documentary cinema and the importance of Iranian documentaries.
Now, on December 16, the Academy announced that “Iran has been eliminated from the Oscar competition. ”
In the list of 10 films that were released by the Academy as the selected films of the competition for the Best International Film Oscar 2020, the name “In Search of Freida ” is not seen, and as it was predicted, Iranian cinema was removed from the competition at the same time. The question that comes to mind is why at the same time the representative of Iranian cinema did not listen to the sympathy and perhaps because of a stubbornness, ultimately made a strange selection. The Iranian cinema for the Oscars, which unlike previous periods had begun its activities in secret and without informing, in three sessions, in a hasty and unprofessional manner, selected a film that was not even a trusted option for various cinematic streams.
While the films of Rusty Little Brains, Bomb, A Romance, Cedar Under Water, Lovely Rubbish, Shirin Palace, In Search of Frideh, Cold Sweat, Six and a Half Meter, Indian and the Night of the Full Moon had formed the initial list of the Selection Board for the nomination of the Iranian cinema representative to the Oscar, at midnight on August 16, 2019, behind closed doors began to make decisions and eventually, and finally the documentary “In Search of Frideh ” as the Iranian Oscar nominee for Iran. After about 5 months of being selected by the authorities!
When the Oscars were removed from the competition, it should be asked whether the choice of a club and the head of stubbornness was worth removing Iran from the Oscar wheel?
Was it really not a good movie for last year ’ s Oscar nominations?
Have you seen movies like “Six and a Half Mile ” and“ The Night of the Full Moon ”?
If we consider all the criteria of the international screening of a film, all of them are gathered on the night of the full moon, numerous awards from different foreign festivals and the welcome of foreign audiences confirm the position that Narges Abyar could have been a good representative of Iranian cinema at the Oscars.
"Six and a half yards" also had this ability, but it is sad that the custodians of the affair decided to remove the Iranian cinema with unforgivable negligence. It is interesting that the panel still considers the effort to see documentary cinema as the criterion of their choice, but who does not know that this choice has nothing to do with the importance and priority of documentary cinema, because documentary films, whether short or long, do not need to be introduced to the Academy. Documentaries, other than fiction, can appear at the Oscars, and there was no need to send a documentary, albeit one, to the Oscars instead of a fiction film.
Although this imprudence, like many of the events of these days of Iranian cinema, will be forgotten, but it seems that the cinematic organization is not going to respond to public opinion because of the lack of work and wrong decisions of some of its colleagues and managers. Iran has been nominated for Oscar three times with the films “Children of the Sky ” directed by Majid Majidi,“ Nadir from Simin Asghar Farhadi ” and “The Salesman ” directed by Asghar Farhadi. This year, with a film like“ The Night of the Full Moon ”, it could have achieved this success that this golden opportunity was lost by the country ’ s cinematic authorities.

title: Food, to eat or not to eat?
text:
Photo copyright Getty Images The discussion of transgenic products is a heated and, of course, sensitive discussion.
Both opponents and proponents point to research that proves their point, and that neither side is free, in some ways resembling recent global warming.
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is trying to neither side the opposition nor the supporters.
While it acknowledges that “these products increase the production, variety and quality of food products and reduce the cost of production and environmental degradation, ” it also points to options such as ecological farming and climate-driven smart farming as options to consider.
FAO Secretary General José Graziano da Silva has said he does not oppose GM crops, but opposes the monopoly of GM seed production in the hands of several companies, and also points to "appropriate measures" to prevent environmental pollution, saying it should not be a priority to end world hunger.
The official source of statistics on the extent to which these crops are planted is not the United Nations, the World Health Organization, or the World Bank, but the International Service for the Use of Agricultural Biotechnology (ISAAA), which is headquartered in the United States and sponsored by companies producing these products, as well as several academic and research institutions in the United States, Asia, and Africa.
And what is the matter with us?
Is transgender good or bad?
To eat or not to eat?
Do we plant or not?
There is no definitive answer to this question at the moment; every informed citizen must decide for himself.
We try to answer these difficult questions as much as possible.
Let ’ s compare the arguments of opposites and opposites.
First, the World Health Organization defines GMOs as "plants, animals or microscopic organisms whose genetic composition (DNA) has been altered in a way that does not occur in nature through natural mating or recombination."
Getty Images: Do GM crops need a vegetable toxin?
Contrary to popular belief, GMOs are resistant to one or more pests, but not to other pests.
In addition, resistance to the transgenic product has been seen, in which cases poison must be used.
In some cases, GMOs have reduced the need for toxins, but the use of agricultural pesticides is increasing all over the world, which is a big concern for environmental activists.
In order to understand the subject of GMOs, we must always consider agricultural pesticides along with seeds.
Is eating junk food harmful to humans?
There is no evidence that eating these products harms human health.
That ’ s the biggest argument for consent.
Opponents, however, do not know enough about this argument.
Given that these products have been planted on a commercial level for almost 20 years, the research has not been so long that it is not clear what the long-term health effects of these products are: DDT, PCB, and thalidomide.
Some experts have raised concerns that these products may cause allergies and immune system diseases.
Is the consumption of agricultural pesticides reduced by the use of transgenic products and the product is increased?
Getty Images photo copyright is the second biggest argument for fans.
They say GM crops have been genetically modified to become resistant to pests, so both the need for toxins is reduced and the crop is increased because the pests do not kill it.
Opponents, however, do not accept this argument.
They say it uses toxins for transgenic crops, such as the world ’ s best-selling toxin – Roundup or Glyphosate – which is ineffective on Monsento ’ s GMO seeds but kills other pests and weeds.
There is disagreement between opponents and proponents as to whether glyphosate is carcinogenic or harmful to humans, and there is research that supports both sides of the story.
The World Health Organization calls it a "possibly carcinogenic", although the International Agency for Research on Cancer has recently been challenged.
A lawsuit has also been filed in U.S. courts, from farmers who say they have been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphatic cancer because of glyphosate use.
Playback of this file on your device is not supported.
Opponents and supporters of GM crops in Iran, do we need GM crops to solve the world ’ s hunger problem?
By 2050, when the world ’ s population reaches more than 9 billion people, agricultural production should increase by 60 percent.
This crowd needs food.
There ’ s also a lot of difference here.
Some experts say this should be considered according to the circumstances of each country and, for example, sub-Saharan Africa should not be compared to, say, Iran or Germany.
With the technology of the day, crop production increases and soil resources are exhausted to produce less crop and also less water is consumed.
They also accuse the opposition of opposing the advancement of science and technology.
Opponents have found evidence that poison consumption has increased after a short period, implicating the issue of water and water resources and global warming in crop yields.
They also say they have no objection to the advancement of science and technology, but history has shown that there can be serious consequences if the necessary precautions are not taken.
Getty Images: Is GMOs Harmful to the Environment?
Proponents of GMOs say the toxins used for GMOs are gradually broken down in the soil and converted into materials such as carbon dioxide and phosphorus.
Opponents say the toxins contaminate the soil and water and do not break down as described.
Proponents say that gene transfer from one organism to another has historically occurred in nature, causing species to diversify and survive.
Opponents say what the delicate balance of nature has done cannot be compared to what a few large corporations do for profit.
Is the production and supply of GMOs exclusive to specific companies?
The largest agricultural biotech companies in the world, known as the "Five Giants", are Monsanto (USA), Syngenta (Switzerland), Bayer (Germany), Basff (Germany), Dupont (USA).
One of the criticisms of monopolies and monopolies of these crops is that once the genetically modified seed begins to be planted, it creates a permanent dependence on the producer for seed and poison.
What is Getty Images' intellectual and scientific property rights?
Genetically modified products are subject to intellectual and scientific property law, and buyers, whether farmers or governments, must obtain permission to use or plant them from the manufacturer.
As for the GM crops that Iran says it produced itself, there is doubt that Iran did not produce the gene itself, but obtained the right to use it from the manufacturers.
For example, some say that the gene that went into Molaei ’ s Tarom rice was made by the Siba-Gaigi company, which has now been converted into Syngenta.
Syngenta told BBC Persian: "Syngenta has no detailed information or interests about the genetically modified rice program in Iran.
Since the exact information about the technology used in the program is unknown, we have no way to assess whether Syngenta ’ s intellectual property rights have been violated.
However, Syngenta is ready to license its biotechnology for innovation to a third party. ”
Playback of this file on your device is not supported.
What is Genetically Modified or Genetically Modified Food?
Organic and native?
Proponents say there is no evidence that a gene that has been manipulated into the plant has been gradually dispersed by wind, insects and other means (in plants that are not self-replicating) and has been gradually infecting non-GMO, native and organic culture.
Opponents argue the opposite and believe that there is not enough solid evidence to support this.
Regardless of which side is right, this is theoretically possible.
Could these altered genes be inserted into our own genes?
There is no evidence that these genes may somehow enter our genetic formula after being absorbed from the gut, but in theory such a possibility cannot be completely ruled out.
Genetically Modified: A New Crisis for Iran ’ s Environment?
Transgenic Products: A New Solution or a Crisis?
What is the Lord ’ s Supper?
In 2004, Iran announced that it would be planting Tarem Molaei rice, a genetically modified rice resistant to two stem worms, on a commercial level.
The news was widely reflected, and countries such as India and China — one of the largest GMO producers, where rice is a staple food — had not done so themselves.
It is said that fifty to one hundred thousand hectares were planted under genetically modified rice.
The product was ready to enter the market when the presidency of Mohammad Khatami ended and Mahmoud Ahmadinejad took his place and did not allow the product to leave the warehouses because there were no laws regarding the safety and health of these products.
In Hassan Rouhani ’ s first term, despite the government ’ s desire, the environmental organization opposed these products.
In the second period, with the coming of Jesus the sheriff instead of the innocent initiative, this obstacle was overcome.
Is there a transporter in Iran?
In Iran, it is not known where, how much, what types of products are imported and what foods are consumed.
The label is not required to clarify whether or not there are GMOs in a product and consumers are not aware of it.
In two studies of processed corn foods, such as popcorn and the like, GM corn was found in about a quarter of these crops.
Some officials have even said that almost all of the oil consumed in Iran is genetically modified.

title: Jeff Bezos donates $100 million to a nuclear fusion startup
text:
Jeff Bezos, the president of Amazon and the richest person in the world, has pledged $100 million to support an energy startup that plans to use nuclear fusion as a clean energy source.
General Fusion, a startup aiming to use nuclear fusion as a clean energy source, has so far raised only $65 million in funding and now $100 million from Jeff Bezos.
Bezos is an early investor in General Fusion.
It also announced that $50 million has been raised from the Strategic Innovation Fund of Canada, and to date more than $200 million has been raised to develop nuclear fusion energy.
The funding is intended for the construction and operation of the “Demonstration Fusion ” plant and the verification of the performance of the“ General Fusion ” technology.
Christopher Murray, chief executive of General Fusion, said in a press release that the world views nuclear fusion as a necessary complement to other technologies that collectively provide a carbon-free energy future.
The amount of investments is further evidence that global stakeholders are united in their efforts to achieve this goal.
We are proud that investors with this budget have shown their confidence in General Fusion.
General Fusion is among start-ups or startups that are developing alternative ways to produce clean energy, turning to nuclear fusion to achieve this goal, and raising capital.
Nuclear fusion is an attractive technology because, unlike nuclear energy, it leaves no waste.
But turning it into a commercial reality has not been realized in years due to the exorbitant cost of commercialization.
The ITER reactor, a French experimental fusion reactor, will be built in collaboration with seven countries and is estimated to cost $65 billion.
Nuclear fusion, or nuclear fusion, is the opposite of nuclear fusion.
In the process of nuclear fusion, light nuclei such as hydrogen, deuterium and tritium are fused together, producing heavier nuclei and some energy.
For fusion to be possible, the nuclei involved in the reaction must have sufficient kinetic energy to overcome the surrounding electrostatic field, so the temperatures associated with fusion reactions are extremely high.
In 1952, the first thermonuclear test explosion released a large amount of uncontrolled energy.
The experiment showed that if the temperature of a gas composed of charged particles — plasma — rises to a high density of 50 million Kelvin, it causes a nuclear fusion reaction in the ionized gas.
After the successful detonation of the hydrogen bomb, the search for controlled release of fusion energy began.
Fusion heat is the heat generated by nuclear fusion.
Nuclear fusion is a reaction quite the opposite of nuclear fission.
Instead of splitting large atoms into small atoms, small atoms are fused together to form large atoms.
This reaction releases a lot of energy because, according to Einstein's special theory of relativity, some of the matter in this reaction is converted into energy.
The fact is that outside of fusion power plants and in nature, we feel the effects of this reaction every day.
Nuclear fusion is what happens in the center of the sun.
The sun is a massive nuclear fusion reactor.
It converts hydrogen into heavy elements and sends light and heat from the reaction to us on Earth.
End of message.

title: Cannes has selected Panahi in the competition section and asked Iran to allow the director to leave.
text:
The directors of the 71st Cannes Film Festival on Thursday, April 12, asked the authorities of Iran and Russia to allow the departure of Iranian and Russian directors Jafar Panahi and Kirill Serebrennikov to participate in the festival.
The most recent films of these two directors have been selected for the competition section of the Cannes Film Festival.
Pierre Lesco, president of the Cannes Film Festival, said: “The Iranian authorities will receive a letter from us and the French authorities in the coming days asking for permission to leave the country so that Panahi can present his film at the festival and then be allowed to return to the country. ”
Jafar Panahi, following his support for the 2009 protests in Iran, has been sentenced to 20 years of a travel ban, as well as a ban on filmmaking inside Iran.
This year ’ s “Three Rocks ” film festival will feature his latest creation in the competition section.
At the 71st Cannes Film Festival, “Circle ”,“ Red Gold ” and “This Is Not a Film ” will be screened by the director in other categories.
Previously, Jafar Panahi ’ s “Taxi Tehran ” won the“ Golden Bear ” award at the 2015 Berlin Film Festival, although he was not allowed to participate in the festival.
Also, while Kirill Serbernikov ’ s “Summer ” will be in competition at the festival, he has been under house arrest since last year.
Kirill Serebrennikov is an acclaimed and creative Russian director who has previously made works criticizing Putin ’ s social conservatism and the growth of this thinking in Russian society.
He was arrested last year on charges of “misuse of public property, ” though he called the charge“ absurd. ”
He has since been under house arrest in Moscow.
So far, many cultural and artistic figures, as well as Russian intellectuals, have supported him.
The competition will feature 18 films, including “Everybody Knows ” by Asghar Farhadi, a joint production of Spain, France and Italy, as well as“ The Book of Pictures ” by French director Jean-Luc Godard and “The Sad Angel ” by young French director Christophe Honore.

text:

title: Jafar Panahi ’ s New Film Screening at Cannes Film Festival
text:
On the fifth day of the Cannes Film Festival, Iran once again became the center of attention.
With the screening of the film “Three Roads ” by Jafar Panahi in the absence of his director, as well as the release of two other films that Iranian cinematographers were among the most important factors in their production: the film“ Girls of the Sun ” by Golshifteh Farahani and the film “Fahrenheit 451 ” by Ramin Bahrani and his own writing and Amir Naderi.
In this regard, the festival on Saturday was dominated by Iranians.
Jafar Panahi, who, despite all requests, was not allowed to leave Iran, for the first time saw a film show of his career in the competition section.
He, who previously participated in other sections of the Cannes Film Festival, including A Look with “White Balloon ”,“ Red Gold ” and “This Is Not a Film ”, will try his luck for the Palme d ’ Or award this year with“ Three Roks ”.
This year, despite numerous requests from Iranian filmmakers and festival officials, he was not allowed to accompany his film at Cannes, and in his absence, Behnaz Jafari and Marzieh Rezaei from the actors of this film and the drunken immigrant film editor along with his children participated in the red carpet of his film.
Before and after the screening, the standing audience applauded the Iranian director for several minutes while Mr. Panahi ’ s empty chair was shown.
“Three Rokh ” is a road movie and narration of the journey of Jafar Panahi and Behnaz Jafari to one of the villages around Miyaneh to find a girl who has asked for their help by sending a video.
In the video, a young girl played by Marzieh Rezaei tells of her family ’ s opposition to her education at the university and apparently hanged herself.
The film narrates Chennahi and Jafari ’ s attempt to find this girl and talk to her family and surroundings.
For the followers of Jafar Panahi ’ s films, “Three Roks ” is the continuation of the“ Taxi ” route, with the difference that the camera has gone from the city to the village and depicts the problems of the poorer classes of Iran.
This time, unlike Taxi, we are faced with a more "directed" film, which shows the relative availability of the conditions for making the film in its specific definition for Mr. Panahi.
Along with the theme of prejudice and opposition to girls ’ education in the film, there are also references to the problems of active filmmakers before the Iranian revolution, and even Shahrzad, the marginal actor of several important films such as “Kaiser ”, enters the story.
The film also features an interesting scene in which Behrouz and Vosoughi are named in the middle of a strange conversation.
At times, the film is reminiscent of Abbas Kiarostami ’ s important films such as “Life and Nothing More ” and“ The Wind Will Take Us Away ”.
A journey through unspoiled nature in the wake of a character everyone at first tries to deny.
Although “Three Roks ” is a more“ directed ” and a more telling story than Mr. Panahi ’ s recent films, it is still far from the important films of his repertoire, such as “The Circle ” and“ Red Gold ”.
Nevertheless, it is considered a serious representative of the critical films of recent years of Iran.
Another women ’ s film about the Syrian war that was screened at the Cannes Film Festival on Saturday was “Girls of the Sun ”, starring Golshifteh Farahani as a Yazidi warrior girl in the midst of the Syrian civil war.
The film, directed by well-known French filmmaker Yves Hussen, tells the story of the strong presence of women in Syria.
In the film, Golshifteh Farahani plays an educated young man who is kidnapped by ISIS forces when he returns to his village in Kurdistan, along with his son and hundreds of other women.
He eventually escapes and joins one of the armed Kurdish women battalions to retrieve his son.
While recalling what happened to spring, the film tells the story of her accompanying an operation with French journalist Emmanuel Berco.
A companion who ends up in the same way.
Iranian cinema viewers had previously seen Golshifteh Farahani as a Kurdish girl in the film "Tears of the Cold".
At a time when women are the center of attention at the Cannes Film Festival, a film with women ’ s pivotal presence about one of the most inflamed events in the world right now is considered as one of the opportunities for attention at the closing ceremony.
In the late hours of Saturday, the final work of Ramin Bahraini, an Iranian filmmaker based in the United States, was also screened in the special section of the Cannes Film Festival.
The film, Fahrenheit 451, is a new adaptation of Ray Bradbury ’ s landmark story, which was made on a sizeable budget with well-known actors such as Michael B. Jordan and Michael Shannon.
Amir Naderi, a veteran filmmaker of Iranian cinema who has been living abroad for many years, has been the co-writer of this film.

title: Mithra Mehrad, a refugee who wanted to help his compatriots but drowned
text:
Image caption Mitra Mehrad was studying the mental health problems of her compatriots, whose main goal was to help her Iranian compatriots, an immigrant who died crossing the English Channel.
The 31-year-old was thrown off a boat in August off the coast of the British province of Kent and found dead in Dutch waters.
Police have now been able to identify him with the help of the BBC.
Her friends say that Ms. Mehrad was a doctoral student in counseling psychology and wanted to help her countrymen by researching Iranian mental health problems.
He and three others were thrown from the Qai on August 9 carrying 20 migrants – including four children – in a storm from northern France to the English coast, which led to a major rescue operation.
The lifeboats of a charity rescued two of them from the water and 19 people – 14 Iranians and 5 Iraqis – arrived in Ramsgate, but there was no sign of Mehrad.
Rescue operations resumed at sunrise, with British and Belgian coast guard helicopters joining the operation.
His body was finally found on 18 August by guards at a wind farm 50 kilometers off the coast of the Netherlands.
Image caption Mithra Mehrad, a graduate student in psychology, was unable to identify her for months until the BBC managed to locate her father and contact the Dutch embassy in Tehran.
After a DNA sample was taken and examined in a laboratory in the Netherlands, the news of her death was officially communicated to her father on Tuesday.
Ms. Mehrad had left her father ’ s home in Khuzestan province to continue her education, and in 2017 she earned a master ’ s degree in psychology from a university in Thailand.
Parvati Varma, one of the professors who judged Ms. Mehrad ’ s thesis, said: “She was a very motivated person.
He wanted to work hard and get a doctorate and make a living. ”
The subject of his dissertation was mental health issues among Iranians, and he traveled to Iran for field research and worked in a hospital to collect information on personality disorders.
An increasing number of Iranian asylum seekers in the UK, Ms Varma said: “She wanted to help the people of her country.
He said the reason for his interest in this field of research was the high prevalence of such disorders among the Iranian people. ”
He recalled his student saying, “I ’ m not interested in research that doesn ’ t help my people. ”
Ms. Mehrad started her PhD but could not find a job in Bangkok that would help her financially.
He left Bangkok in early 2019 and finally arrived in France.
Photo copyright SNSM Image caption French police rescued migrants who were hanging on a small boat the day she died, it is not clear when they decided to pay smugglers to take her across the English Channel, but it is clear from the shock of her death that she did not tell anyone.
In February, he told his colleagues that he planned to move to Canada to continue his research.
We made a little joke on the show: “I was wondering where Canada came from.
Did you find a Canadian boyfriend?
But he said no, no, no, we ’ ll talk later.
He then asked me to pray for him.
It was there that I thought it might be a different story. ”
In early August, Ms Mehrad arrived at a refugee camp in the port of Dunkirk, where hundreds of Iranian and non-Iranian migrants live, police said.
The UK ’ s National Crime Agency warned at the beginning of 2019 that the camp was being held by organised criminals who “use violence to force migrants to sail to the UK ”.
Two men who planned Ms. Mehrad ’ s transit have been arrested in France on charges of manslaughter.
Mitra had only stayed in the camp for a few days and had spoken to the Refugee Women ’ s Center before her fateful journey began.
Ms Varma said she could not understand Ms Mehrad's decision.
“This part of the story was unbelievable.
Why did he have to go so far? ”
British and Dutch newspapers had named Ms Mehrad a few days after her death, but Dutch police spokesman Ed Kraszewski said the force could not definitively confirm her father ’ s death until DNA was checked.
He said, “We can ’ t say he ’ s dead.
We have to be sure.
And his father, too.
He must be sure, too, or he may wait till the end for his daughter.
In such cases, survivors always hope that their lost one day will return. ”
According to Krasowski, a positive DNA test ended the family's painful wait.
They are now ready to bury their daughter four months after her death.

title: Japanese fishermen hunt 122 pregnant whales
text:
Copyright AFP Image caption Commercial fishing of minke whales is banned. Japanese fishermen have killed more than 300 minke whales, including 122 pregnant whales, in the Antarctic Ocean.
These whales are hunted annually in the Southern Ocean.
A report by the International Whaling Commission says 114 whales have not yet matured.
Japan has signed an international treaty to regulate whaling, but says it is hunting for scientific reasons.
Critics say the killing of whales is for commercial use, with Japan selling the meat and using it for food.
In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.

title: Jafar Panahi ’ s last film “Three Roads ” has been shown in French cinemas.
text:
Jafar Panahi, an Iranian filmmaker who has been banned from making films, writing screenplays, conducting interviews and leaving the country for 20 years since the re-election of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and campaigning against the Islamic Republic, continues to make films, write screenplays, conduct interviews and leave the country. The winner of the Best Screenplay Award is now on screen in French cinemas.
Jafar Panahi, in the eight years since the ban, has made four films, each of which has somehow made its way to the world festivals.
Films such as “It ’ s Not a Film ”,“ The Curtain ” and “Taxi ” won the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival in 2015.
She started filmmaking with the help of Abbas Kiarostami, in the film “Three Roks ” starring Behnaz Jafari and Marzieh Rezaei, she points her criticism at the living conditions of women in Iran and condemns the legal inequalities of women in her country.
Filmed in the father village of Jafar Panahi in northwestern Iran, the film tells the story of three women from three generations, each victims of the oppression and violence of a patriarchal society.
In this film, the famous actress Behnaz Jafari receives a video of a rural girl who has faced the opposition of her family to study cinema at the Art University of Tehran, who is suicidal and desperately asks her for help.
Behnaz Jafari, who is acting in a film at the time, is so upset that she leaves the set and, with filmmaker Jafar Panahi, they travel to a village in northwestern Iran in Azerbaijan province to solve the problem.
At first, they are attracted by the hospitality of the villagers, but soon discover that there are misconceptions, superstitions and patriarchal traditions in the village.
The film narrates the problems of the lives of three women actors in Iran: Shahrzad, a pre-revolutionary actor who has been prevented from continuing his work and living with his memories, Behnaz Jafari, a well-known actor who has his own view of this field, and Marzieh, a young girl who wants to start her studies in this field and dreams of becoming an actor.
“Jafar Panahi ” in“ Three Roks ”, like his previous film “Taxi ”, is seen more on his car, rarely gets out of the car and does not even enter the interior of the houses.
In most of the shots, the camera shows a winding path through the windshield.
"Three Faces", in the words of French critics, is a quiet tragedy in which the filmmaker, without violence and with a kind of artificial coolness, questions religious misconceptions, superstition, patriarchal thinking and gender discrimination in Iran, and like the films he made about women in the past, such as "White Balloon", "Mirror", "Circle" and "Offside", sympathize with the women of his country, which still has a path to freedom. uneven and long in front of them.

title: The most amazing science events of the second half of 2019
text:
Every year, Business Insider reviews the most amazing scientific discoveries and events of the year.
The report continues to highlight some of these issues.
The landing of the Japanese spacecraft on the space object Hayabusa-2, which was launched in 2014 by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, landed in July 2019 on the surface of a space object called Ryugu, located 8.851.390 km from Earth, to sample it.
By studying these samples, the researchers hope to gain a better understanding of how life on Earth formed when these space objects collided.
A black hole swallowed a neutron star in August, researchers detected the effects of a black hole colliding with a neutron star.
The catastrophic collision, which occurred nearly a billion years ago, distorted space and time, creating a phenomenon known as gravitational waves that passed through Earth in 2019.
This was the third event the researchers observed using gravitational wave detectors.
Einstein predicted the existence of gravitational waves in 1915, but thought they were too weak to be detected on Earth.
But now, advanced technology has shown the opposite.
Launching the first commercial spacecraft into orbit in March 2019, SpaceX launched the commercial Crew Dragon spacecraft, becoming the first commercial spacecraft designed to transport humans into space.
The successful flight of the spacecraft is a turning point for the United States.
Since NASA phased out its fleet of space shuttles in 2011, the United States has been using Russian rockets to transport astronauts to the space station.
Using solar energy to power a spacecraft in the summer of 2019, the US-based Planetary Society NGO sent LightSail2 into orbit.
Once in orbit, the satellite opened its 32-square-meter sail.
By colliding and reflecting particles of light into the sail, the momentum of the particles is transferred to the spacecraft, providing it with an unlimited source of energy.
With the advancement of this propulsion technology, it may one day be possible for spacecraft to reach nearby systems.
Now, due to the limited amount of fuel that can be carried by spacecraft, this is not possible.
The unprecedented melting of polar ice in April 2019 revealed that Greenland ’ s ice is melting at an average rate of 286 billion tons per year.
Just two decades ago, the average rate of ice melting was only 50 billion tons per year.
In 2012, Greenland lost 400 billion tons of ice.
Antarctica has lost an average of 252 billion tons of ice per year over the past decade.
In the 1980s, the annual melting rate of Antarctic ice was about 40 billion tons.
In addition, the Thwaites Glacier in West Antarctica is shrinking by 800 metres per year, and its melting water accounts for 4% of global sea level rise.
According to research published in July, the glacier is a ticking time bomb for Earth, which is approaching the point of no return, after which the entire glacier falls into the ocean.
In such a situation, the world ’ s sea level will increase by 45 centimeters.
In September, the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change said sea levels would rise by 90 centimeters by the end of the millennium.
It is challenging the lives of hundreds of millions of people living on small islands and coastal areas.
According to other research, if greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise in the same way, rising sea levels will result in 630 million people migrating by 2100.
According to a report published in April, about 40 percent of amphibians, more than 33 percent of all marine mammals and corals, and at least 10 percent of insect species are threatened by human activity.
The researchers also found that 500,000 inland species lack sufficient habitats to ensure long-term survival.
The research is yet another confirmation that Earth is in the midst of the sixth major extinction event in the history of life.

title: Wind speed and wind speed require research.
text:
Gholamreza Hassani Gharba added: Drought is the most important and destructive effect of climate change, which is followed by effects such as creating a fine dust center and increasing wind speed.
He said that in the past years, more than 90 percent of the country's dust was from the origin of centers outside the country, such as Iraq, adding that the reduction of rainfall has reduced vegetation cover and created these centers among the countries of the region.
Referring to the creation of dust canons in the country with the continuation of recent droughts, he said: The most important step to prevent the creation of these canons in order to prevent the rise of dust, is the reality of the desert, which should be included in the planning of the water field.
The Director General of Meteorology of Semnan Province stated: The lack of observance of the desert Haqabeh in the past years has led to the weakness of vegetation cover, which has turned the soil into dust with the loss of moisture.
Stating that the external origin of dust has remained constant and new centers have been established inside the country in provinces such as Ilam, Kurdistan and Khuzestan in recent years, he noted that the internal centers of dust and dust in the country are increasing.
Hasani Gharba pointed to the registration of the microdusting center on the border between Semnan province and Qom, Semnan and Isfahan based on satellite images and stated: Based on the observations of satellite images, the production of microdusts in these centers has increased in the past 2 years.
He pointed to the increase in wind speed as another phenomenon caused by drought and climate change, adding: With increasing temperature and decreasing humidity, unbalanced temperature conditions form between different points, which causes sudden movement of air flow and the formation of high-speed winds.
According to the Director General of Meteorology of Semnan Province, along with drought, increase in temperature and wind speed, three factors speed up the creation of dust and dust centers in arid and semi-arid areas.
Referring to some differences in dust with the center outside the country and inside the country, he said: Foreign dust is less than 2 microns in diameter, which means it is very light and capable of moving over large areas and long distances, as well as elevation, which is why the transfer from one country to another occurs.
Hassani Gharba said: For this reason, the dust produced in Iraq and Syria is drawn to the interior provinces after the crossing of the Iranian borders.
He continued: The dust from the internal centers, but the diameter is greater than 2 microns, and due to the heavy displacement, the dust that is created from the southern center of Semnan will eventually reach the province of Qom because the dust is heavy and will soon subside.
He emphasized the necessity of monitoring climate change data to investigate environmental changes for better management in the development of Semnan province and noted: Without careful review of data and monitoring of changes in nature, we will not be able to manage the conditions.
The Director General of Meteorology of Semnan province stated that climate change in the long term has other effects such as impact on the life of pests and insects, which will be effective in improving agricultural products.
Climate change is caused by greenhouse gases beyond the Earth and has effects such as rising temperatures, destructive floods, desertification, storm occurrence, increased evaporation, changes in bio-plants, changes in wind patterns, changes in rainfall types and land subsidence.

title: Clean up the gardens!
text:
