title: Astronomical hands to play the role of the victim in the series; on Turkish television, break the values and make money!
text:
According to the Young Journalists Club, violence against women, rape, beating and killing of women are among the most important social problems in Turkey, and hundreds of women are victims of male violence every year.
With more than 300 TV channels currently operating in Turkey, the spread of news about the violence has become a major competition, which not only does not reduce the stigma of this social problem, but also normalizes it.
In other words, television networks and cyberspace, with false activity and controversy, actually increase violence.
Of course, this is not only reflected in news programs and sensational reports, but television series are another part of the problem of spreading violence against women.
For $500 million, the TV industry in Turkey has become a huge, bread-and-water market with large investors and powerful stakeholders, and TV networks affiliated with large economic groups compete to create compelling TV shows.
Turkish television series inside the country rely on the advertising and advertising market, and the private sector practically pays for the advertising of goods and generates millions of profits for creators and agents.
But this huge income is not just limited to the inside, and now the Turkish series has found its way to the outside world and has become a very useful and lucrative export commodity.
The export revenue of Turkish TV series in 2013 was $150 million.
But in 2017, it reached $350 million, and in 2018, it was able to set a record revenue of $500 million.
In most Turkish television series, both in modern fiction and historical fiction, women and girls play a pivotal and exaggerated role, and producers and directors often prefer to use blond, light-eyed, European women and girls.
While even in the old Ottoman paintings and photographs, women are seen dressed and wearing large headscarves, in the historical series, they are all half-naked and, like the princes of European history, appear in semi-nude clothes and jewellery and makeup before the camera.
Although this is a blatant distortion of history, it seems that when it comes to money and the hunt for foreign audiences, the producers want to use everything and add occasional violence to the story to make it more interesting, in addition to the watery romance and the flirting scenes and the promotion of secret relationships.
As a result of the instrumental use of women in Turkish TV series, many social experts have raised their voices and believe that these TV profiteering will contribute to violence against women and their humiliation.
The endless happiness of the actors in the Turkish TV series makes a lot of money.
Famous actor such as Canaan Mirzalioglu receives 450,000 liras (1 billion tomans) for each episode of the television series.
Kovanch Tuttle also gets 250,000 lire for each episode, and the actresses get huge amounts of 80,000 to 150,000 lire for each episode.
Moreover, due to their fame in TV series, they also have a side income of several hundred thousand lira a year, and dozens of nosy photographers and journalists follow them wherever they go.
Paradoxically, an actor who has paid the equivalent of buying an apartment in Istanbul to play in an episode of the series, commits violence against women in front of the camera, as a man, and if she is a woman, she becomes a victim of violence and aggression, but in the real world and in cyberspace, condemns the rape of women and girls and the murder and beating of them!
This is one of the points that has been criticized by experts and critics who believe that in this regard, the actors of the Turkish television superstar, have been subjected to hypocrisy and immoral profiteering and a small number of these actors with billions of income, spend money in the public sphere of Al-Manfeh, Ehsan and charity.
Fatih Altayli, an analyst and author of the news media series, wrote: “Stop this hypocrisy.
You create a doomsday on social media and Twitter, and you put yourself in the line of the defenders of women and girls, but when you go in front of the camera, your whole story is about attacks on women, assaults, virginity and such inhumane topics that show that you are willing to make money from violence against women. ”
Although Turkey has taken steps forward in some areas of economic development, in many 81 provinces of Turkey, the society lives in a traditional way and retains its traditions, culture and values, and it is safe to say that the images of women and girls and their lifestyle in more than 90% of television series do not match the reality of society.
In most of these series, very young women and girls, prey to the rich and the mafia gangs and are themselves satisfied with this, or women and girls, are beaten and killed for a secret relationship, but at the heart of Turkish society, violence and aggression have different backgrounds and reasons that are not related to the fictional stories of the series and often women and girls who are victims in villages, small towns and traditional metropolitan areas. They become violent, aggressive and sensual, oppressed people who bear no resemblance to blond actors and sly women and girls in serials.
In these series, the woman and the relationship with the woman, the seducing and abduction of the girls, are considered as the main focus of the story, and if the hidden issues and relationships are taken away from the story, there is often nothing left.
In a general conclusion, it can be said that the world of media, and especially television, in Turkey is plagued by the same conventional disease as the instrumental use of women in Western societies, and the continuation of this trend leads to more cultural and social harms and problems.
Source: End of message.

title: Monsanto Sentenced to $289 Million
text:
Jurors in a San Francisco court ruled against the company by filing a lawsuit against Monsanto.
The person who complained about the company was formerly a janitor and now has lymph node cancer, which was blamed for the herbicide produced by Montenegro.
Doctors have found this person incurable.
The jury justified the verdict by saying that Montenegro had not warned its customers that herbicides could cause cancer and was “deceptive. ”
The 46-year-old has been working as a school janitor for years, using Monsanto in large quantities.
Dwayne Johnson, the plaintiff, is 46 years old and diagnosed with lymph node cancer. The company produces two herbicides known as Roundup and RangerPro, which use the chemical compound glyphosate, which may cause cancer.
Montenegro has denied the allegations, claiming that scientific research has shown that the chemical poses no danger to humans.
The company was recently acquired by the German company Bayer for $63 billion.
There are many differences of opinion about the possible carcinogenicity of glyphosate among experts.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, as well as regulatory agencies in the European Union and Germany, have concluded that the chemical does not cause cancer.
In contrast, the World Health Organization ’ s International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) declared three years ago that glyphosate “probably causes cancer in humans. ”
Thousands of cancer patients in the United States have accused Monsanto of cheating, citing the use of its herbicides.
Last month, a San Francisco state judge filed more than 400 other complaints about the company ’ s herbicide carcinogens.
Observers see the $289 million fine as a blow to Monsanto, which could have more severe consequences.
The company is currently facing more than 5,000 similar complaints in the United States.
Monsanto has said it will appeal against the ruling.
Glyphosate ’ s EU-wide broadcasting license was renewed for another five years in November 2017.
The chemical toxin is also used in Iran and is imported from China.

title: After the lawsuit, Bayer stressed that glyphosate is not a carcinogen.
text:
The Getty Images Image caption Horticulture is heavily used in horticulture after a California court ruled on Friday that Monsento should pay nearly $300 million to a farmer suffering from cancer.
Meanwhile, UK chain Homebase, which sells horticultural and agricultural products, said it would review the pesticides and herbicides it sells.
On Friday, August 10, a California court ruled that Monsanto, one of the world ’ s largest producers of GMOs and pesticides, had to pay $289 million to a man suffering from advanced cancer.
A spokesperson for Bayer said in a statement on Saturday: "Bayer is confident, based on the strength of scientific evidence and the conclusions of authorities around the world and decades of experience, that the use of glyphosate is harmless and does not cause cancer if used in accordance with the guidelines."
A California jury indicted Monsanto, saying the company had to warn its customers about the dangers of using two herbicides, Roundup and Ranger Pro.
Bayer bought Monsento last month for $66 billion, but a spokesman for Bayer told the BBC that the two companies operate independently.
What is food, to eat or not to eat?
AFP Image caption Dion Johnson hugged his lawyer after hearing the verdict, marking the first time a court has been set up to investigate the link between glyphosate and cancer.
The plaintiff is Devin Johnson, a man who was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphatic cancer in 2014.
He says he used Ranger Pro poison regularly when he kept a school playground.
Ranger Pro or Glyphosate, the world ’ s best-selling poison, is ineffective on Monsanto ’ s genetically modified seed, but kills other pests and weeds.
It is estimated that there will be an additional 5,000 complaints across the United States about the use of the toxin.
What is glyphosate and is it dangerous?
Monsanto produced glyphosate in 1974 and had a monopoly on its formula until 2000, but then various chemical companies started using it.
Currently, about 750 products in the United States contain glyphosate.
In 2015, the World Cancer Research Institute, the World Health Organization's cancer agency, concluded that glyphosate "may be carcinogenic" in humans.
However, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has insisted that the toxin is safe if used with caution.
The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) says glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer in humans.
Last November, EU countries voted to extend production permits despite protests and campaigns.
The BBC's North America correspondent James Cook says a judge here in California recently ruled that coffee should even be warned about carcinogens, but the agricultural industry has complained that it has been labeled as "glyphosate," even though it is on the state's list of carcinogens.

title: More than 60 refugees rescued in the English Channel
text:
Photo copyright PreMar Manche Image caption 14 asylum-seekers were taken by the French Coast Guard on a boat and taken to the French coastal town of Boulogne Sur Mer, where more than 60 migrants were taken in several boats trying to cross the English Channel to reach the UK on the day after Christmas.
It was reported that 49 people were taken from the water in four separate boats by British border guards and taken to England, as well as two other boats with 14 asylum-seekers on board by the French Coast Guard.
The Home Office says it will try to bring back anyone who wants to enter the UK illegally.
Refugee rights activists described the UK government ’ s “crackdown ” as“ very irresponsible. ”
The search and rescue operations began in the early hours of Thursday, December 26, a Christmas holiday in Britain, by helicopter, aircraft and two British Coast Guard boats.
Last night, a rescue boat sailed from the port of Dover to rescue the refugees.
Getty Images Image caption The Home Office's coastal border patrols said: "Illegal immigration is a criminal act, and those who try to come to the UK illegally, as well as the gangs that provide these illegal trips, are breaking the law and putting lives at risk."
The Home Office also said that coastal patrols on the French coast had doubled and that special vehicles and exploration equipment had been deployed.
Brigitte Chapman of the Kent Immigrant Action Network, which has worked directly with refugees arriving in the UK by boat, called the Home Office ’ s response “shameful. ”
Referring to the 1951 United Nations Refugee Convention, he said the British government ’ s “very harsh language ” on the issue had no place“ in international law. ”
Ms Chapman said in the convention that "refugees should not be punished for entering illegally."
“I remind the Home Office that Jesus was a refugee, didn ’ t they accept him? ”

title: 50 asylum seekers, including several Iranians, arrested in UK
text:
British authorities have detained nearly 50 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.
British border guards have seized four boats with 49 migrants trying to reach England's shores on the English Channel.
According to the newspaper, the British Border Service received reports of an illegal attempt to cross the strait at around 01.30 local time and rushed to the scene of the incident.
All of the detainees, including several citizens of Iran, Iraq and Afghanistan, were transferred to the British Immigration Service.
In addition, the newspaper reported that French authorities rescued 14 others who had been sent to Britain along with the 49-strong group, who had difficulty crossing the strait.
Illegal migrants often seek every opportunity to cross the English Channel, where they are granted asylum and financial benefits by the UK ’ s special social programme.
According to the Daily Mail, about 1.7 thousand asylum seekers arrived in the UK in January, a significant number of whom risked their lives to reach the UK.
On the other hand, the Home Office is spending millions of pounds to tackle illegal immigration.

title: 'Offside 'in the Apparatuses
text:

This week ’ s episode will be featured in the film ‘ Offside ’ by Jafar Panahi.
When a filmmaker is interested in raising social issues and red lines in his films, then football and the ban on women entering stadiums in Iran can be a good means to make a film for him.
Jafar Panahi did the same in Offside, but Offside isn ’ t just about football.
In this film, she once again paints a picture of Iranian society and the situation of women in the country.
Jafar Panahi made this film based on a shared script with Shadmehr Rasti in 1384.
"Offside" also found the fate of his previous films and could not be shown in Iran.
However, with this film, which was his fifth feature, Jafar Panahi continued his brilliant success at international film festivals and won the Silver Bear of the Berlin Film Festival in 2006, earning critical acclaim and film lovers.
The feature of the film 'offside' in football means to be outside the box, or offside is a vacuum-like space formed between the goalkeeper and the defenders.
The referee takes the error of the player on the opposing team who is in this situation.
Using such a term in football, Jafar Panahi tells a story of the restrictions and exclusion of Iranian women, while also showing a generation of girls today who are willing to do anything for their rights, even wearing men ’ s clothing.
Jafar Panahi in the film 'Offside' is trying to narrate the problems of women today, away from the slogans and clichés, and does not leave the circle of justice, and covers the bitterness of the film with satires of girls' conversations with soldiers of Tehran 's Freedom House.
Overall, the movie continues to have the same worries and concerns.
A filmmaker who wants to show the problems and social failures of the society from a football game in Azadi Stadium and make the audience think.
Photo copyright JP Image caption An overview of the film 'Offside' is a summary of the story of girls who beat themselves up to watch the match between Iran and Bahrain at the Azadi Stadium in Tehran.
They try to enter the stadium in disguise but are not allowed to enter and are arrested by the police.
The soldiers want to transfer them to the committee, but something else happens along the way.
About Director Jafar Panahi was born in 1960 and graduated in film production from Tehran Broadcasting School.
He began his career by making several short films in Iranian television centers in the 1960s, and then, after assisting in one of Abbas Kiarostami ’ s films, he released his first feature film “White Balloon ” with a screenplay by Abbas Kiarostami, for which he won the Golden Camera Award at the Cannes Film Festival in 1995.
Two years later, he made the film Mirror, which won the Golden Cheetah at the Locarno Film Festival.
These two films, the main heroes of which are young children, are the only feature films that have received a license to play in Iran.
Then, in 2000, based on a script from Cambodia, he directed the film 'Circle', which has a social theme and is a revolution in his long work.
With this film, he won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and three years later, with the help of a group of amateur actors and a screenplay by Abbas Kiarostami, he was able to win the Special Jury Award in the Best Film category at the 56th Cannes Film Festival and the Best Film Award at the 39th Chicago International Film Festival.
Panahi then finished the film Offside, which deals with the issue of banning girls from football stadiums in Iran.
The film was not released to the public in Iran like other films of the filmmaker, but Panahi was able to repeat the successes of his previous films at festivals outside Iran and win the Silver Bear at the 2006 Berlin Film Festival.
During the protests of the Iranian people against the results of the tenth presidential election, Jafar Panahi was arrested twice.
He was sentenced by the Iranian judiciary to six years in prison on charges of “assembly, collusion and propaganda against the Islamic Republic ” and 20 years of deprivation from filmmaking along with deprivation of social rights.
'This is not a film ';' The Curtain ',' Taxi 'and' Three Roks' are films that Jafar Panahi has made in the years following his conviction, and most of them have won major awards at international festivals.
His film “Three Faces ” has also been screened as one of the films of the 2018 competition section of the Cannes Film Festival and has won the Best Screenplay Award from the festival.

title: The number of hungry people increased for the third year in a row.
text:
Image caption The UN report says severe weather conditions are one of the reasons the number of hungry is growing, with the UN reporting that the number of hungry people in the world has increased for the third year in a row.
According to the report, 821 million people – one in nine – were malnourished last year.
The new report says more than 150 million children, more than 20 percent of all children under the age of five, have grown up in poverty.
Hunger and malnutrition have risen for the third year in a row, while they have declined in previous years.
The UN report says severe weather conditions are one of the reasons for the growing number of hungry people and calls for global action to tackle them.
The report, “State of Nutrition and Food Security in the World, ” also found that lack of access to nutritious foods has led to an overabundance of the global obesity problem, affecting one in eight people.
The UN report ’ s authors noted an increase in climate events such as floods, overheating, hurricanes and droughts, saying the number has more than doubled since the 1990s.
Climate change is directly affecting crops and access to food.
The World Food Report says hunger is dramatically worse in countries that are vulnerable to changes in rainfall and temperature.
The report ’ s authors call for concerted global and regional action to make countries more resilient to natural disasters related to climate change.

title: Iranian Refugees Steal Fishing Boat to British Coast
text:
Reports say 17 Iranian migrants made their way to British shores early Tuesday after hijacking a French fishing boat and crossing the English Channel, but were stopped by coast guard forces.
British officials have confirmed that the 17 migrants, including three children, were able to reach British shores by hijacking a 12-meter fishing boat near the French port of Calais early Tuesday.
French naval officials described the migrants ’ actions as “unprecedented ” and said they had previously tried to reach Britain in small boats, but in most cases failed.
The Home Office said in a statement that the group of migrants stopped arriving in Dover.
"They are 14 men and three children and all have declared themselves Iranian."
A Home Office spokeswoman said their asylum applications were being investigated and that three children had been handed over to the social services.
The report also said that three other small boats were stopped at Kent by the British Coast Guard on Wednesday, possibly from Iran.
According to the BBC, the passengers of one of the small boats were "seven men, a woman and a small child" and 10 other men were found in another boat.
According to the report, the British Coast Guard first noticed at 4: 30 that the passengers of a boat in the southwest of the shipping lane were in trouble and had gone to the aid of the refugees.
The second boat was found at 9: 00.
The report said five people on another boat were rescued a few miles off the coast of Ramsgate.
AFP says thousands of migrants from the Middle East and Africa are trying to reach Britain's shores.
The coastal city of Calais has the shortest water route between France and Britain, and since the destruction of the so-called "Jungle" camp, many Calais refugees have stepped up their efforts to reach Britain.

title: Half a million jobs lost in Kerman – trees that burn coal
text:
According to the development outlook plan, agriculture is considered the center of Kerman's economic development, but in this province, the average rainfall is only 120 mm per year in water, which has not been achieved for years, and farmers have focused the most pressure on harvesting water from underground sources, and a significant part of Kerman's groundwater reserves has been lost.
Changing local ecosystems in Kerman now, along with the drought, widespread climate fluctuations have caused local ecosystems in the province to change and local communities to suffer significant damage.
If you visit the palm farmers of the east, the pistachios of the north and the jalizars of the south and the gardeners of the west of the province, you can easily see hectares of agricultural land that have dried up and a lot of damage has been done to the farmers, a typical example of which is 2,400 billion tomans, which has been left as a loss of frost this year, and now the only way to make a living.
The head of the agricultural Jihad of northern Kerman province, confirming this figure, tells Mehr reporter: The climatic conditions of the seasons in Kerman have changed and affected agriculture.

title: Why do Iranians go to Britain by boat?
text:
PREMAR MANCHE Image caption Over the past three weeks, a boat group of asylum seekers, more than 100 migrants and asylum seekers who say they are Iranian, have tried to cross the dangerous route to Britain in small boats.
Why do they take such a perilous journey and where do they come from?
On November 23, shortly before sunrise, eight asylum seekers were found in a small boat in stormy waters off the coast of Kent in southeastern England.
They told rescuers they had been on the water for 12 hours.
A similar thing happened the day before.
Seven others were found in a boat off the coast of Dover.
A few hours earlier, the same number had been found in the same area in a windy boat.
Since November 3, 101 asylum-seekers, including children, have attempted a 34-kilometre route across the English Channel to reach Britain from France.
The Home Office has not released official figures on the number, but the BBC has found that at least some of them have been able to enter British waters since the beginning of the month.
All of them, without exception, have told the authorities that they are Iranian.
Image caption The BBC's Simon Jones posted a picture of one of the rescued boats around Dover, from the Balkans to Britain, why did so many boats sail to the coast of Kent in such a short time?
How are the authorities going to stop them?
Why are they all Muslims, as they say?
The answer to the last question lies about 2,000 kilometers away in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.
Miudrag Chakic, the managing director of Serbia ’ s refugee relief agency, which monitors the movement of migrants in the Balkans, said refugees arriving in the UK were among the thousands who flocked to Serbia after Serbia decided to revoke visas for Iranian citizens last summer.
The Serbian government ’ s decision to cancel the visa was originally intended to boost the country ’ s tourism industry and trade with Iran.
The plan, which was said to have “exploited ” migrants and asylum seekers to reach Western Europe, was scrapped on 17 October 2018.
By then, it is estimated that about 40,000 Iranians had traveled to Serbia.
It is not known how many of the passengers had returned to Iran, but according to Serbian media, many of the flights were filled and returned empty.
According to Info Park, a refugee support group in Belgrade, Serbian police estimate that about 12,000 Iranians have not returned home.
Photo copyright MIODRAG?? REFUGEE AID Image caption Most asylum-seekers in Serbia sleep in abandoned buildings, but some Iranians who went there to seek asylum or emigrate to Western Europe are said to stay in hotels, asylum seekers or tourists?
Mr Chakic said he heard in a circle of people and groups dealing with refugees that Iranians were using "fake passports and very sophisticated methods" to reach Western Europe.
Unlike many asylum-seekers, they start their journey with more preparation and stay in a hotel or hostel.
Refugees from countries such as Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq and Pakistan sometimes walk thousands of kilometers and then sleep through the streets and abandoned buildings of Belgrade at night.
Gordon Panovic, of Infopark Group, says Iranians “look more like tourists than the rest of the migrants. ”
There were kids, all in jeans and jackets and backpacks. ”
“Many [Iranians] travel with fake passports that cost between 3,000 and 6,000 euros in Istanbul, ” Panović said.
Their situation is not the same as other refugees and migrants who have very difficult conditions in the Balkans.
They don ’ t have to sleep like everyone else or go to refugee camps. ”
“They were here for a month, staying in a hotel and making arrangements with the smugglers for their journey. ”
Iranians may be different from other immigrants in terms of economic conditions, but for many of them, life is not so easy with an “oppressive ” government.
Photo copyright MIODRAG, AKIAGE / REFUGEE AID Image caption The situation of Iranians is generally said to be different from other asylum seekers in the Balkat region, where Kaveh Kalantari, of the Iranian Association that supports asylum seekers in the United Kingdom, says the lack of freedom and human rights violations are driving these citizens to emigrate from Iran.
“People are arrested at the risk of having liberal or left-wing views, or because they are from religious minorities, ” he says.
Many people see violence on a daily basis. ”
It is estimated that since the Islamic Revolution about four decades ago, between 15,000 and 200,000 Iranians have left their country each year to emigrate.
According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.
In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.
Image copyright NICOLAS ECONOMOU / NURPHOTO / GETTY IMAGES Image caption Tens of thousands of Iranians are believed to have emigrated to Belgrade, Mr Kalantari said: "It is not unusual for Iranians to come to Britain, but the way they are coming is unusual."
One theory about why Iranians risk their lives on boats, despite a better economic situation than other migrants, is that they have enough money to pay smugglers.
Maya Conforti, of the Migrant Hotel group that supports Calais refugees in France, describes this type of canal crossing as unique to Iranians.
"Crossing the Channel by boat (from France to the UK) is only possible for those with money," she said.
Africans have no money when they arrive in Calais. ”
"A new flood of Iranians has reached the port of Calais.
They seem to be the only ones who have the courage to do so and find a way. ”
Mr Chakic says Iranians moving to Kent in Britain have entered the European Union through Serbia.
“I don ’ t see any other explanation.
Serbia is the only country on the Balkan route that has a large number of Iranians. ”
Ingrid Parrot, who works for border forces in Cherbourg, France, has blamed "organized criminal and mafia networks" for the increased efforts to cross the canal.
Ms Parrot said there were 30 attempts to cross the canal in 2018, and the number was 12 and 23 in 2017 and 2016, respectively.
Photo copyright JEREMIAS GONZALEZ / IP3 Image caption The Calais Forest was dismantled in 2016, but refugees from different parts of Africa and the Middle East continue to live in refugee camps.
British border agents say it has become easier and cheaper to access smaller vessels, providing more opportunities for smugglers.
Charlie Alfik, MP for Dover and Dale in Britain's parliament, who described the increase in the number of attempts to cross the Channel as "unprecedented", said border forces needed more resources, including funding, to increase patrol boats as a deterrent force.
The number of refugees identified in Dover trucks has fallen by a third since the destruction of the Calais forest, the representative said.
But Bridget Chapman, of the Kent Immigrant Action Network, says the increase in channel crossings is "a natural consequence of becoming more violent and tightening conditions at borders."
“People are being forced to find ways that are becoming more dangerous day by day. ”
Damien Green, Ashford MP and former immigration minister, said there must be an emphasis on "where the refugees are coming from and the international criminal gangs behind it".
The Home Office says authorities are working "to identify criminal groups that facilitate illegal immigration".
According to Parrot, France has stepped up its measures to prevent attempts to cross the Channel, not just rescue operations.
"Our greatest concern is an incident that may result in loss of life or an incident at sea that requires our assistance.
"The fear that we will see wounded people on the water or the bodies that the water will bring to the shore."

title: FAO: Climate change is putting food security at risk
text:
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) said in a report released Wednesday that climate change is putting food security at risk.
According to the report, published on the FAO ’ s official website, climate change, along with land degradation and other factors, is hampering the world ’ s food supply.
The report says that increasing land populations have increased the need for affordable food, but climate change, water scarcity, destruction of fertile land and other factors have combined to challenge the agricultural sector, with 821 million people now facing malnutrition.
In other words, one in nine people is starving.
According to the report, the number of children under the age of five who have been killed in Yemen at risk of malnutrition and disease is likely to reach 85,000; famine in Afghanistan has forced 250,000 people to leave their homes and emigrate; and finally, the FAO secretary-general has announced that malnutrition and hunger in the world have increased to the level of the past decade.
"After years of fighting hunger, this setback is regrettable."
The current situation is while the FAO has predicted that the need for food will increase by 50% by 2050.
The report adds that greater use of fertile land also causes soil degradation and disrupts the ecosystems of countries.
FAO also says that China throws away 12 million tons of rotten grains each year, worth $2.6 billion.
In its 202-page report, FAO also gave a glimpse into the situation in Iran, saying that Iran ’ s loss of environmental diversity has reduced its chances of tackling some challenges, including climate problems.
The report adds that environmental diversity is an important driver for improving the resilience of smallholder farmers to tackle problems such as drought, water scarcity, climate change and pest outbreaks.
For example, FAO has suggested that Iranian farmers use seeds that can resist climate change.
However, statistics published by FAO on its official website on Iran indicate that 4 million people in Iran are malnourished.
At the beginning of 2000, the figure was 3.3 million, rising to 4.7 million 10 years later, but has fallen again.
Global grain production in 2018 is expected to fall 1.6% from the previous year to 2,607 million tonnes.
FAO forecasts in the field of human and livestock consumption of cereals also indicate a new record of 2,626 million tons.
Global grain stocks are expected to drop by 2.7% at the end of the agricultural season ending 2019.

title: And how many of them are in the kingdom?
text:

How many asylum seekers are there?
In 2017, 26,350 asylum applications were filed in the UK.
In comparison to other European countries in the same period, 198,255 asylum applications were filed in Germany, 126,550 in Italy and 91,70 in France.
Of these, 21,290 cases have been decided, with 31.8% receiving some form of support.
The UK offers asylum to people who fear being prosecuted in their home country because of their race, religion, nationality, political opinions and factors such as sexual orientation and are unable to live in their home country.
If the asylum application is accepted, people will be allowed to live and work in the UK for five years, after which they will be able to apply for permanent residence.
Not much is known about how the asylum seekers made their way to the UK, but a report from the Home Office ’ s Migration Advisory Committee released in May 2018 estimated that they were “sneaking in ”.
This includes people arriving either by boat to the British coast or being smuggled onto ships or trucks.

Which countries are asylum seekers from?

These statistics show that the success of Iranian asylum applications is higher than the average number of asylum seekers, or that Iranian asylum seekers have a higher chance of being accepted than other nationalities.
These statistics relate to cases in which a final decision has been made.
Others are in a “wait or wait ” situation.
At the end of last year, 24,557 people were waiting for the outcome of their asylum application, 42 percent of whom had been waiting more than six months.
Rejected asylum applications are usually admissible in court, and people who are rejected often appeal.

text:

title: Construction and operation of 12 pocket parks in Gorgan

Stating that these parks can be a refuge against the city crowds as well as a place for rest and relaxation, Sotoudeh Nia said: In the Fajr decade two pocket parks were exploited in the neighborhoods of Resalat Three and the city of Imam (ra) eight.

title: "Crossing the Channel by boat is dangerous, we came by truck."
text:
Image caption Maryam, Shea and Aziz Hanna, an Iraqi, were supposed to pay smugglers in France to take her family by airboat across the English Channel to Britain
But when he learned of his friend ’ s journey, which he had almost lost his life on the way, he changed his mind.
Aziz Hanna, his wife Maryam and five-year-old daughter Shea arrived in the French border town of Dunkirk in October 2018 and made more than 20 attempts to cross the English Channel.
They finally made it to Britain by truck last weekend.
For a while, they wanted to travel by inflatable rubber boat.
The smugglers had made it “safe ” to cross the canal and had told one of them to travel about 20 kilometers with the migrants.
"When you enter British waters, they call the police and the police come to your aid and take you to England," Aziz said.
All smugglers say the same thing. ”
At this point, the smuggler is said to be returning to France on another boat.
But the experiences of two dear friends at Camp Dunkirk frightened him.
Iranian and Christian Camp Dunkirk Bahadur and Shokouh with their two children, Maryam and Benjamin, were driven to a beach south of the port one winter morning and boarded a boat with six others.
About 15 minutes after the launch, the boat capsized and no one had a life jacket.
Seven-year-old Maryam says she was the only one who could swim.
He said: “It was very cold, very cold.
My feet were cold.
I wanted to die … I saw my brother, but I couldn ’ t reach him. ”
Fortunately, Bahadur was able to put them on a capsized boat.
Mary says, “The sea was going up and down … it was too fast and too dark.
My mother was crying and praying and others were screaming and asking for help. ”
They were eventually rescued, but both children were taken to the hospital to be treated for hypothermia.
Image caption Bahadur and his children Maryam and Benjamin Another story that kept Aziz from crossing by boat was the experience of his friend Solomon and his partner Solomon, Sayeri.
Both are Muslim Christians.
They were at sea for hours when the engine of the boat suddenly stopped working.
They and their companions tried to restart the engine, but a mixture of salt water and fuel engulfed the inside of the boat, causing burns to the people on board.
Solomon said, “Our skin was burning, it was very painful.
We were really scared.
Someone was crying, someone was praying.
The boat was going this way and that way. ”
“We ask God, ‘ Why?
What is happening to us? Why?
I also asked God, “Why did you bring me from Iran to die in this sea? ”
"No one knows where I am, even three hours after our engine failed, we were still at sea."
It was dark, and the boat that Suleiman thinks was British took them aboard a French ship, and all the passengers were taken to a hospital in France.
After hearing these stories, Aziz told smugglers in Dunkirk that he wanted to make the journey by truck.
His mother borrowed £10,000 from his home and gave it to people affiliated with smugglers in Iraq, after which the story of their unsuccessful attempts to cross the English Channel began.
Sometimes they were found by police dogs in a French port from a hidden truck.
Sometimes they had been moved in the wrong truck, which was heading towards Romania and Spain.
Once they went into a refrigerated truck, but Xia could not stand the cold and became ill.
Aziz says the French police were not strict when they found them and often wished good luck next time.
His successful crossing happened on a Saturday.
The smugglers beat them and took them by bus from Dunkirk to one of the truck parking lots in Belgium.
There they were transported in a truck belonging to a Romanian driver with another family, and Aziz and his family entered Britain through the Channel Tunnel (Eurotunnel).
Everyone was silent until the truck arrived in North Hampton, England, but as soon as the truck arrived they made noise until the driver stopped the truck and was surprised to see them.
Neil Crips, chief investigator of the South East Region Organized Crime Police Unit (SEROU), says investigators sometimes leave boats on their way to gather evidence against smugglers.
"In order to get good evidence and to eliminate this crime permanently and for the long term, we have to ignore an element of danger to the public."
An Iraqi Kurdish smuggler operating in northern France, Jano, says he spent four years in prison for human trafficking and returned to the illegal business after his release.
Aziz and his family hid in the trees until relatives living in the UK reached them and moved them to a safer place, and a few hours later Aziz went to the police station and asked for asylum.
Aziz says life in Iraq became dangerous because of her attempt to reach Britain as a teenager 15 years ago.
At that time, his companion died after jumping from a slow-moving truck.
Years later, he said, his uncle contacted Aziz and suddenly accused him of being responsible for the death of his travel companion, asked him for £50,000 in compensation and threatened to kill Aziz ’ s daughter if he did not pay.
Aziz says he didn ’ t want to stay in France because he speaks English and has relatives in Britain.
He also said the UK government is helping refugees and migrants.
“They give home and everything … In France, it ’ s not the same.
It helps, but not like this. ”
He added: “I am very happy and thank God.
England is like heaven to me.
No one can hurt us here, and after months have passed, we can sleep well.
My daughter can go to school and learn.
He ’ ll be very smart and maybe become a doctor. ”
Image caption Shea, the dear daughter of Rob Lowery, an immigration activist at Dunkirk Neil Crips, chief investigator of the South East Region Organised Crime Police Unit (SEROU), says the increased level of surveillance at ship ports and the tightening of truck inspections have recently made migrants more likely to choose to cross the English Channel by boat.
“I predict that in the spring when the weather is calmer, the number of boats will increase. ”
Bahadur, dear friend, despite his disastrous experience with his family, plans to cross the Channel again by boat.
He said, “We want to get out of here. ”
“We can ’ t go back to Iran because I ’ m a Christian and I ’ m definitely going to lose my life.
"The sea is dangerous, but Iran is more dangerous."

title: How can climate change change soil uptake?
text:
The researchers found that climate change could have a negative impact on soil, posing a threat to water resources and crop production.
Coasts, oceans, ecosystems, climate and human health are all affected by climate change, and now researchers say soil is no exception and may be affected.
The results of the new study suggest that climate change may reduce the ability to absorb soil in many parts of the world, which could have serious consequences for groundwater supply, production and food security, runoff, biodiversity and ecosystems.
The results of studies indicate that sea level rise, habitat destruction, coral bleaching, biodiversity loss, disease outbreaks and so on.
All are of the predicted effects of climate change.
Researchers at Rutgers University in the United States have shown that climate change can change how soil is absorbed.
The penetration of moisture, air and carbon dioxide into the soil is very important for plant growth.
Water in the soil helps store carbon, but if the soil breaks down and less water penetrates into the ground, it can lead to higher levels of carbon dioxide (CO2).
Carbon dioxide is one of the greenhouse gases associated with climate change.
Daniel Gimenez, co-author of the study, said: “Rainfall patterns and other environmental conditions are changing globally as a result of climate change, and the results suggest that the interaction of water with soil has changed dramatically in many regions of the world and is changing rapidly.
The researchers suggested that the direction, size, and rate of change should be measured and specified in predicting the ecosystem ’ s response to climate change.
The results showed that increasing rainfall leads to a decrease in the ability of the soil to absorb water, which is a factor for erosion and an increased risk of flooding.
Also, with increasing rainfall, the rate of water penetration changes and with less water in the soil, less water is provided to plants and crops.
Experts found that a 35 percent increase in rainfall over 25 years in Kansas City led to a 21 to 33 percent decrease in water penetration into the soil.
More rain will thicken the roots of the plants and leave less space to store rainwater.
The team will examine how increased precipitation due to climate change affects water and soil penetration in other regions of the world.
The findings were published in the journal Science Advances.
End of message.

title: Oxygen production on Mars + Photo
text:

title: Survivors of the flight to Tehran. Where and how can they ask for compensation?
text:
The very tragic incident of the downing of the Ukrainian plane on the morning of Wednesday, January 8, in which 176 people who had Iranian, Ukrainian, British and Canadian citizenship were deeply regrettable.
Until recently, due to the fact that the cause of the crash was not known, there was no legal analysis, but yesterday it was revealed that the plane was unfortunately targeted by military forces.
The Iranian government has admitted that the plane was unintentionally attacked and the government has accepted responsibility and apologized.
In any case, the loss of passengers to the survivors and the damage of the aircraft to the Ukrainian government must be paid.
Dr. Mansour Jabari Gharabagh, a lawyer and professor at Allameh Tabataba ’ i University and an expert in international aviation law, told Tabnak: “It is possible to raise different legal issues in this field.
One of the issues is the payment of compensation.
How and by whom it should be paid.
This is verifiable in a number of ways. ”
Asked whether the airline should pay compensation, which court is competent and which law is enforceable, he said: “The compensation is paid by air carriers in accordance with international conventions, which both countries have accepted and ratified in their country of origin and destination.
The two Warsaw Conventions of 1929 (its Protocols included the 1955 Hague Protocol and the 1975 Montreal Protocol) and the 1999 Montreal Convention on the Integration of Certain International Air Transport Regulations on Damages to Airline Passengers, in respect of Damages to Passengers, are applicable.
It remains to be seen which of these documents the country of origin and destination is a member of.
Of course, the ultimate goal is consideration.
Most of the passengers were from outside Ukraine.
Most of the passengers were flying to Europe or Canada. ”
“If the Warsaw Convention and its protocols are applicable on this flight (Iran has joined the convention and Ukraine, European countries and Canada are also members), the lawsuit can be filed by survivors at the carrier ’ s residence or the carrier ’ s main job center or the carrier ’ s trade center where the transport contract was concluded or at the destination provided that the country is a party to the Warsaw Convention of 1929.
Article 20 (1) of the Warsaw Convention “shall not be held liable if the carrier proves that he and his agents have taken all necessary measures to prevent damage or that such measures were not possible for him and his agents. ”
It is not expected that the Ukrainian airline was aware of the risks involved on that day, in particular of the Islamic Republic of Iran ’ s retaliatory actions for the martyrdom of the late General Soleimani; therefore, according to this convention, the Ukrainian airline is not responsible for compensation. ”
The author of Air International Law stated: “The second verifiable document is the Montreal Convention of 1999.
The basis of liability in this Convention has been changed and a dual system has been established regarding the responsibility of transport operators to passengers.
According to it, the carriers are fully liable for damages to the passenger, so that their liability is absolute up to 100,000 Special Drawing Rights (about US $140,000), and if the operator cannot prove that the damage was not caused by the fault, act or omission of his or her crew or representatives, in addition to $140,000, the carrier must compensate for all damages.
In other words, the 1999 Montreal Convention accepts the absolute responsibility of the carrier.
Most countries, including Ukraine, Canada and all EU member states, have ratified the Convention, but since Iran is not a party to the Convention, it is not applicable to Ukrainian airlines.
Given that the Warsaw and Montreal Conventions are not applicable, survivors can file lawsuits in Iran against the government (Iranian Civil Aviation Organization, Army or IRGC) in Iranian courts.
In case of non-payment of damages to foreign travelers, they should be able to follow up with the support of their government through international authorities. ”
Regarding the criminal responsibility of the perpetrators of the incident, he added: “Certainly, in these circumstances, the Civil Aviation Organization, the IRGC and the military should have ordered the cancellation of all passenger flights.
In addition, attacks on passenger aircraft are prohibited under all circumstances.
Those who have been guilty of negligence should be punished according to Iran ’ s Islamic Penal Code.
The first action expected from the judiciary seems to be to order a swift review and punish those who have failed to cancel flights and those who have caused the missiles to be fired at the aircraft.
The government has a duty to ensure the safety of the aircraft.
It is hoped that with the investigation and punishment of the perpetrators of this painful body, this will be the last incident on the plane. ”
The lawyer said that the government has announced that the Ukrainian passenger plane has been targeted by anti-aircraft defenses “due to human error and inadvertently ” and has been shot down.
This happened on the day when Iran was completely unsafe for passenger flights.
Following the assassination and the innocent martyrdom of General Qasem Soleimani, the IRGC and the army were planning operations against American forces and positions.
Airlines, their governments and even other Iranian entities were unaware of the operation.
It was very necessary that the cancellation of the flights was announced by the Iranian Civil Aviation Organization, the IRGC and the army.
There are two reasons for this: first, that the flights were in place at this critical time, and second, that the shooting of the passenger plane was carried out, an act which is strictly prohibited under international aviation law.
The positive point in this issue is that Iran has accepted the human error and unintentional nature of the incident, and this is effective in reducing the amount of damage, and if the damage is paid, there will be no other bad consequences except a bad memory for the people of the world, especially the survivors of this painful incident and an unfortunate and unforgivable experience for the aviation industry and military forces.
The amount of compensation must be agreed between governments.
Several times in the history of aviation, something similar has happened.
Jabbari Qarabagh reiterated about the occurrence of similar incidents of aviation and the ban on targeting of passenger aircraft: “The first downing by a missile is related to Korean Air 007.
On September 1, 1983, Soviet planes shot down a Boeing 747 Flight 007 with 269 passengers flying near Sakhalin Island in Soviet airspace.
The tragic incident raised serious questions about the international law governing such incidents and encouraged the International Civil Aviation Organization to develop rules.
Governments have committed to refrain from using weapons against civil aircraft and not to endanger the lives of people on board the aircraft and its security during interception.
Following the Korean Air 007 incident, the ICAO General Assembly amended the Civil Aviation Convention (known as the Chicago Convention) in 1984 by adding a new provision called Article 3bis.
Under this article, governments have committed to refrain from using weapons against civil aircraft and not to endanger the lives of people on board the aircraft and its security during interception.
According to this article, each State has the right, in exercising its sovereignty, to ask the aircraft of the State flying in its airspace without its permission to land at a certain airport, but it has no right to endanger it in any way.
In this regard, the former Soviet Union made a mistake in identifying the aircraft and considered it unintentional.
Since the incident occurred in peacetime and was unintentional, it is somewhat similar to the downing of a Ukrainian plane in Tehran.
Perhaps this is the only incident that can be said to have similarities with the current situation.
The second is the Iranian Air plane shot down by a US ship in the Persian Gulf, Iranian territorial waters, with two surface-to-air missiles launched by the USS Vincent.
The case was raised both at the International Court of Justice and at ICAO.
The International Court of Justice had appointed September 12, 1994, to hear the case, which was substituted a month before, with the approval of the Iranian government and the United States government.
After negotiations, the two governments reached agreements that on 22 February 1996, a final compromise was signed and the case was removed from the agenda of the Court.
In the settlement, the U.S. government agreed to pay the survivors of the incident.
The situation in which the Airbus aircraft took place is quite different from the current situation of the Ukrainian plane.
Another incident was the targeting of a Malaysian plane over Ukraine.
The plane flew from Amsterdam in the Netherlands to Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia when it was shot down over Ukraine.
The plane was shot down by a Russian-made missile in eastern Ukraine.
At that time, there were serious military conflicts in eastern Ukraine.
Most of the victims were Dutch.
Three Russians and one Ukrainian were accused of shooting down the plane and killing all 298 passengers and crew.
Survivors of the incident have filed lawsuits in different countries.
In one court, the four defendants were given arrest warrants and their trial is scheduled to take place on March 9, 2020 (in less than two months).
However, given the war situation at the time of the incident, this cannot be compared with the present case.
It is hoped that the authorities will take the matter seriously so that it can be a lesson for the future and prevent similar incidents. ”

title: Land, national wealth and a natural resource are vulnerable.
text:
A faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad said: “Soil, national wealth and a natural resource are vulnerable.
Also, it is a reservoir of nutrients needed for growth and the main growth bed of the plant.
Dr. Amir Fotout, today at the specialized meeting of agricultural insurance and natural disaster management held at the Central Organization of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, said on the importance of soil, water storage for plant growth, providing the air needed to grow roots, very strong refining, an important reservoir of greenhouse gases in the ground and...
Among other important features of soil.
Regarding the most important reasons for soil erosion and sediment in the country, he added: improper exploitation of soil resources and change of uses, conversion of pasture and forest lands to agriculture, construction operations, road building, mining, excessive grazing of rangelands and ploughing in the direction of slope are among the most important reasons.
The introduction of soil as a national wealth, a sensitive and vulnerable natural resource or an important biological system of the ecological system, legal explanation of the economic value of soil and documentation in order to prevent inappropriate use of soil resources are the sub-goals of the soil law.
The member of the faculty of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad stated: Developing legal foundations for the use, management and sustainable exploitation of soil resources, conservation, restoration, modification and promotion of optimal exploitation of soil resources and the development of legal bases to prevent inappropriate changes of soil resources are among the main goals of the compilation of soil law.
Dr. Hossein Sanainejad, a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, also continued the meeting on harmful atmospheric phenomena, stating: More than 80 percent of small farmers are exposed to atmospheric hazards.
Risks that put their food security, income and normal life at risk.
On the other hand, unfortunately, due to climate change, the frequency and intensity of harmful atmospheric phenomena such as floods and drought have increased.
He said: "The damage caused by these risks is compounded by the weakness of management and doubles their problems.
Also, lack of natural resources, quality of inputs and technology, transportation and warehousing, market connectivity and financial services leave these smallholder farmers vulnerable to loss of crops.
The WRMF is a joint organization between the World Food Program and Global Capital for Agricultural Development, established in 2008 to reduce the vulnerability of small farmers to harmful atmospheric phenomena and other hazards in order to provide global food security.
Regarding the activities of the WRMF, he noted: quality operational research, finding or enhancing risk management solutions for adverse climate phenomena for food and agricultural security, and applying initiatives and innovations to find appropriate solutions in risk management, such as the Agricultural Insurance Index, are among the activities.
Insurance is a vital element in agricultural development and risk management in developing countries and is difficult to access, especially for the most vulnerable farmers.
WRMF has been a leader in the use of insurance to reduce risk for smallholder farmers and innovative tools based on insurance indicators.

title: Are the Iranian victims of Ukrainian Airlines Flight 752 considered “martyred ” or“ martyred ”?
text:
It is no secret that the recent days have been one of the saddest and most distressing days and moments spent by Iranians all over the world, both at home and abroad.
The martyrdom of General Soleimani and the shooting of a Ukrainian plane over Tehran on Wednesday morning, January 8, were events that caused severe suffering and many questions and ambiguities for many Iranians.
Ukrainian Airlines Boeing 737 flight number 752 on Wednesday morning while flying from Imam Khomeini Airport and according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, was hit by a "human error" by the defense forces stationed at the site and crashed at 6: 18 near Saba city in Tehran province and all 176 passengers were killed.
After this incident, many officials initially stated that the main cause of the accident was a technical failure, tried to reject all the documents presented on social networks and stated that the main cause of the incident was a technical failure and then the crash of the plane; but after a while, the General Staff of the Armed Forces and the military officials in charge of issuing a statement and giving a speech to a large part of the doubts and ambiguities raised in recent days responded to the responsibility of the aircraft. And they accepted.
According to the official information available, the Boeing 737-800 aircraft belonging to Ukraine International Airlines, which had flown from Imam Khomeini Airport to Kiev with registration UR-PSR with flight number 752 at 6: 12 on Wednesday, 10 / 18, was carrying 167 passengers and 9 crew members.
This incident has raised a lot of questions in the public mind.
He questioned the look and feel of the people.
Some sought to identify and punish the culprit.
Some have been looking for the reason for this error, and others have raised the question, given the presence of travelers from different countries, most of whom are Iranian or have Iranian Canadian citizenship, how will the legal and judicial pursuit and compensation be?
Some of these questions were investigated in the past and some of the ambiguities of the issue were answered from the viewpoint of the lawyers of the country.
But the other question that was raised was, given the other cases that have happened before and even recently, are these travelers considered martyrs?
For example, during the unrest of November last month, when some of the compatriots lost their lives due to the indirect and unintentional presence in the scenes of the riots, according to the appeals made by Shamkhani, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, from the presence of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution, these people were considered martyrs and according to the orders of the Supreme Leader, they were to be completely appeased.
Now, according to the previous cases, the question is whether the passengers killed in this very sad loss can be considered a martyr or not.
In searching and scrutinizing the existing laws and regulations of the country, we will find that in order to answer this question, we should refer to "Regulations for determining the practical examples of the martyr, the martyr and other examples of sacrifice".
This bylaw, which is the last bylaw issued on these cases in 1393, has fully commented on the practical cases of the martyr and the martyr ’ s verdict. It should be noted that the Cabinet, on the proposal of the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Support, and the cooperation of the Martyr Foundation and Veterans Affairs Foundation and the General Staff of the Armed Forces, and based on Note (1) Article (4) 1) The Comprehensive Law on Service to Veterans (2012), the Regulations for Determining and Defining the Practical Examples of the Martyr, as a Martyr and Other Examples of Sacrifice (Missing, Veteran, Azadeh and Captive).
The date of the 10th of May 1393 has been approved.

title: The Dragon capsule is being tested again.
text:
SpaceX said in a tweet that it plans to conduct another test for the Dragon capsule this month.
SpaceX is getting one step closer to the Dragon capsule ’ s plan to send humans into space.
The company plans to test the Dragon capsule ’ s launch escape system on January 18.
The system will ensure the safety of the capsule and check whether the spacecraft can keep its astronauts safe in case of trouble during the ascent phase.
Previously, SpaceX had also tested the Dragon ’ s launch pad and parachute.
It should be acknowledged that the exact timing of such tests cannot be precisely determined.
This is because the weather conditions are very effective in such experiments.
If all goes according to plan, the mission will be the last major test of the crewed Dragon capsule to confirm the spacecraft's ability to send astronauts into space.
SpaceX is still hoping to conduct a crewed test of the Dragon capsule in 2020.
Earlier, NASA said the Dragon capsule could be ready for its first manned test flight to the International Space Station (ISS) in the first quarter of 2020.
The mission is called Demo-2.
According to NASA ’ s contract with SpaceX, the company has committed to sending astronauts to space and the International Space Station and back to the United States with one of the safest and most advanced systems ever built.
End of message.

title: The challenges of a healthy city from the perspective of a global organization
text:
Today, half of the world ’ s population lives in cities, and it is predicted that two-thirds of the population will live in cities by 2050.
It is also predicted that about 90% of these changes will occur in African and Asian countries.
This trend means that focusing on urban development in a way that is beneficial to health is becoming more important than ever before.
The report examines some of the existing links between urban life and health, and examines the ways in which cities contribute to healthier living.
The World Health Organization (WHO) has been working to improve the health of cities for decades and has introduced several key measures, including the World Health Organization ’ s Healthy Cities Network and various other networks and measures that support cities to work on specific issues.
Facing the issue of mental health in cities, poverty, unemployment, high population density, noise pollution, poor infrastructure and lack of adequate green spaces are some of the problems that city residents face.
All of these challenges can contribute to or exacerbate mental illness, making people feel lonely and isolated.
However, in most cities, people are helped to respond to these challenges through programs that align urban spaces with optimal mental health.
Living in urban areas limits the availability of adequate physical activity; skyscrapers are not the only challenge that pervades the lives of city dwellers, yet many people move to cities due to unemployment, divorce, loss of family members, violence, or physical and mental problems.
The reasons that force people to move to cities are also a risk factor in exacerbating mental health problems.
Since more than half of the world ’ s population now lives in cities, high population densities can be a big problem in cities.
This condition, along with noise pollution, is associated with double stress and social isolation.
In addition, poverty and inequality are often more pronounced in cities, making it more challenging for people to find jobs.
More than a third of the city ’ s population lives on streets and on the periphery of cities, where social and financial difficulties can exacerbate mental health conditions and increase the risk of depression or other mental health conditions.
In most cities, there is a lack of access to green spaces and natural environments.
Access to these environments is important for mental health, promotes social connections and physical activity, and reduces levels of stress, anxiety and depression.
Efforts to reduce road accidents are a number of reasons, including road failure and lack of enforcement of driving rules, which are the cause of road accidents and road accidents.
Improving road design, enforcing laws and being aware of interference methods that help improve the safety of urban roads and streets.
Road accidents are now the leading cause of death among people aged 5 to 29.
Each year, more than 1.35 million people die from road accidents and another 50 million are injured.
In many cities around the world, violence, including shootings and stabbings, is a leading cause of death among 15- to 44-year-olds.
Eating healthy meals in most cities around the world, filled with fast-food chains and restaurants, seems to be a “challenge ” — tens of millions of people are harmed each year by nonlethal violence, including assault, that can lead to behaviors that are dangerous to health.
Poverty, lack of access to social protection, educational problems, mental health problems, and easy access to alcohol, drugs and guns lead to increased levels of violence.
Around the world, one person is killed every minute of every day, and more people are injured, and a significant number experience violence with no significant physical consequences, but it deeply affects the feelings and cognitive strength of those who have been subjected to it.
There are many causes and factors that contribute to violence, and there are many ways to deal with it at different individual, family and social levels.
Establishing book parks, providing educational and recreational centers as well as counseling centers for family problems are among these solutions.
Air pollution in cities is making it hard to breathe, and 9 out of 10 people living in urban areas breathe polluted air every day.
Several factors, including traffic, factory operations, and household fuels, play a role in air pollution.
Heart, respiratory, asthma and lung cancer are among the complications of exposure to polluted air.
Smoking in public places affects people ’ s lack of access to clean air.
Each year, seven million people die from breathing polluted air.
One-third of all deaths from stroke, lung cancer and heart disease come from air pollution.
Microscopic pollutants in the air pass through the body ’ s defense systems and penetrate the respiratory and circulatory systems, damaging the lungs, heart and brain.
Since more than half of the world ’ s population now lives in cities, high population density can be a major problem in cities.
In addition to the health of smokers, tobacco smoke also harms the lung health of non-smokers exposed to smoke, causing 870,000 premature deaths per year.
Allocation of smoke-free urban spaces, in addition to maintaining health, encourages people to quit smoking, as there are limited areas for smoking.
In addition to the allocation of smoke-free urban spaces, the prohibition of all direct and indirect forms of tobacco advertising is also effective in reducing smoking.
In Jakarta, Indonesia, for example, there is an emphasis on strengthening the implementation of a ban on outdoor tobacco advertising, while in Kampala, Uganda, national smoke-free laws are applied throughout the city.
Encouraging physical activity to maintain a healthy physical activity helps prevent heart disease, stroke, diabetes and some types of cancer, as well as preventing weight gain and improving mental health, but living in urban areas limits the enjoyment of adequate physical activity.
The importance of physical activity for the benefit of physical and mental health has been acknowledged, but around the world a quarter of adults and three quarters of adolescents do not get enough physical activity.
In 2018, the World Health Organization created the world ’ s first global action plan on physical activity.
The goal of the program is to reduce inactivity by about 15 percent by 2030.
The challenge of ensuring everyone benefits from a healthy diet, eating healthy meals in most cities around the world, which are full of fast-food chains and restaurants, seems to be a “challenge. ”
Long hours in the workplace prevent people from having enough time to buy fresh and healthy food as well as cook it.
Every day, millions of people around the world struggle to prepare healthy and nutritious meals.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than 820 million people are deprived of their food every day.
For many people extreme poverty, lack of food or living in areas affected by climate change or conflict means that their access to food is limited or nonexistent.
Making healthier choices easier is a smart strategy that ensures people have access to healthy and desirable diets.
For example, citizens should be guaranteed easy access to healthy, local food at affordable prices, as is the case with processed, ready-made, high-fat, salt, and sugary foods.
End of message.

title: Iranian imam jailed for helping migrants cross La Mancha
text:
AFP Image caption The number of migrants attempting to cross the Channel by boat has jumped recently, and a French court has sentenced an imam of a mosque to two years in prison for helping migrants cross the Manash Canal in inflatable boats.
The 39-year-old Iranian man was accused of arranging migrant crossings from northern France to Britain on several occasions.
A 29-year-old Senegalese man who worshiped in the same mosque was also sentenced to nine months in prison and denied the right to visit Nur and Pa-de-Calais in northern France.
The imam of the mosque, named by French media, collapsed after hearing the sentence.
French newspaper La Figaro reported that the two men had admitted to providing six or seven small boats after being arrested in April.
The investigation began in late March when life jackets and a inflatable boat were found on a beach in northern France.
According to the prosecutor ’ s office, the imam of the mosque was in contact with organized smuggling groups and was getting a “brokerage fee ” to sell each boat.
Police found two boats, three boat engines and several life jackets at the Imam ’ s home.
The two men confessed to buying seven boats between December 2018 and April 2019.
The main accused claimed to have bought the boats from a store in Dolmont on the Belgian border for someone who introduced Kemal.
Both defendants claimed that they later determined that the boats were being used to illegally cross the Channel.
A Senegalese man told the court: “When I found out the children were on the boat, I thought to myself, ‘ People ’ s lives are in danger. ’
The priest said he was “ashamed. ”
Prosecutors said the defendants' explanations "do not reflect reality" and that the Iranian suspect was often at the spot where the boats were found.
Recently, the number of migrants attempting to cross the Channel by boat has jumped, despite the risk of dangerous currents, the cold water and the risk of colliding with other boats.

title: The sale price of the world ’ s largest aircraft
text:
Vulcan, owned by Paul Allen, the co-founder of Micrasoft, plans to sell the project to build Stratolaunch, the world's largest aircraft, for $400 million.
According to CNBC, Stratolaunch is intended to launch missiles into orbit from an altitude of 9,100 meters.
The Pegasus XL cruise missile will be launched to deliver commercial satellites into low Earth orbit, but the new aircraft will be able to carry up to three missiles in the future.
Stratolaunch, the world ’ s largest rocket aircraft, made its first flight in mid-April.
The plane took off from the field in the Mojave Desert, California, and flew for 2.5 hours at an altitude of more than 5 kilometers at a speed of 304 kilometers per hour.
The pilots assessed the flight ’ s technical and flight characteristics.
According to CNBC, the proposed price covers both the right to own the aircraft and the intellectual property and model of the infrastructure in connection with the Stratolaunch aircraft project.
The new aircraft is ready for use.

title: Global warming engages the African continent with drought and flooding
text:
Environmental experts warn that global warming is associated with more droughts and floods on the African continent.
British experts say global warming is leading to more cases of drought and flooding in Africa than previously predicted.
According to the new study, over the next 80 years, the continent will face more severe cases of rainfall.
In these circumstances, the likelihood of catastrophic floods, hurricanes and serious challenges in the agricultural sector increases.
In addition, these climatic conditions are associated with catastrophic droughts during the growing and crop season, which can damage crops and food production.
According to experts, this climate is caused by the combustion of fossil fuels, which increase the level of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and cause heat in the air.
Last month, carbon dioxide levels reached 415 parts per million.
Experts warn that the trend will increase over several decades, leading to a dangerous rise in global temperatures.
Africa is one of the regions of the world most vulnerable to climate change.
Studies on rainfall patterns also show serious problems with food security and drought facing the continent.
End of message.
