title: A neighborhood park is taking place in the area.
text:
ISNA / Hamedan Mayor of Malayer said: With the aim of developing urban green space and recreational centers and creating vitality for citizens, especially in areas with high population density, we have put on the agenda the construction of a neighborhood Shaghayegh park in Valiasr city.
In an interview with ISNA, Hossein Babaei added: Today, the design and construction of neighborhood gardens as part of urban green space is one of the important issues in urban planning, which, in addition to providing a suitable context for recreation and entertainment of residents and families, increases social and spatial interactions between citizens.
He said: In this regard, the neighborhood park of Shaghayegh in an area of 18 thousand square meters and in four levels that have a height difference and between three blocks (E, D, N) Valiasr city, which has a high population density, is running.
Babaei pointed out that Malayer is a city that has one of the highest per capita green space in the west of the country, but its distribution is unbalanced in the city, continued: Given that the creation of green space has a direct impact on the spiritual, psychological and daily life interactions and all of these effects on the quality of life of people, which are key components of development, vitality and social dynamism.
Mayor of Malayer added: Due to the lack of financial resources, the physical progress of the project has been slow and at times stopped, but now with the restart of work by the contractor, the construction of the project has been accelerated.
Babaei said: The first level of this park is dedicated to the installation and equipping of urban furniture for the use of the public, and the living pavilions are installed at the second level of the park.
He said: At the third level, fitness equipment is installed in a park so that we can take a step for the health of our fellow citizens, and the fourth level is dedicated to the sports area and children ’ s playground, at this level, football, volleyball, badminton and basketball fields are constructed and along with it, polyethylene play equipment for children, and we hope that the park will be used as soon as possible for the residents of the neighborhood.
Mayor of Malayer, in another part of the implementation of the 137 complaints system in the municipality, said: 137 is a three-digit telephone number belonging to the municipality and all Malayer citizens can ask for services, comments, criticisms and suggestions in the areas of the municipality, and in general, the communication bridge between citizens and the municipality.
Babaei pointed out that so far, the bridge to Malayer Municipality has only been through the telephone operator 137, which has traditionally been registered and tracked by the operator, but now, with the implementation of the 137 system, citizens can contact the municipality in a number of ways and to register their complaints and requests and receive their responses and feedback.
He added: In the first method, citizens can call 137 operator and express their complaints and problems and receive a tracking code, and in the second method, they can call 137 IVR phone 24 hours a day and register their request and receive a tracking code and feedback and the result of the work will be sent to them via SMS.
Mayor of Malayer mentioned the third method of installing the mobile app on the citizens ’ mobile phone and said: In this method, by using the 137 mobile app and submitting the request, citizens can take a video or photo of the location and send it.
Babaei explained: Given that the system is based on a GIS map, municipal experts can easily identify the location of the neighborhood or area in question automatically and quickly fix the problem.
He noted that in these methods, the system automatically registers the citizens ’ request and sends it to the relevant authority and sends feedback to the applicant, and people can do or fail to fulfill their request and their consent and dissatisfaction through the notification code to the municipality.
End of message.

title: Majid Majidi is the representative of the regime in cinematic diplomacy with America
text:
According to the predictions, Farabi Cinema Foundation has introduced Majid Majidi ’ s “The Sun ” as Iran ’ s representative to the Academy this year for participation in the Best International Film category.
With this choice, it became clear that in the competition between the domestic currents of power in cinema, Majid Majidi is still a more important figure than Mohammad Hossein Mahdavian.
According to the news released by the Farabi Foundation, it has been determined that three films "The Devil Does Not Exist" by Mohammad Rasoulof, Shahram Mokri 's "Crime of carelessness" and Ahmad Bahrami' s "Silent Plain", which were present at the most important international festivals of the past year, have not even been examined by the board formed by the Farabi Foundation.
All three films have critical themes and could have been serious claimants to the Academy Awards.
In the meantime, the lack of selection of the film “There is no Devil ”, which has won the most important award of the last year of Iranian cinema, the Golden Bear of the Best Film of the Berlin Film Festival, is worth considering.
The excuse for not paying attention to these films is their lack of release, which has prevented the presence of critical Iranian films at the Oscars in all past years.
In fact, the issuance of the state license has become a tool for the government management of cinema in Iran to take the opportunity to participate in the Oscars by not issuing this license for films with critical themes.
Meanwhile, the selection of Majid Majidi ’ s last film, “The Sun ” in the final competition with two films“ Walnut Tree ” by Mohammad Hossein Mahdavian and Masoud Bakhshi ’ s “Yalda ” shows that Majid Majidi ’ s status as one of the closest filmmakers to the main institution of power in the Islamic Republic of Iran has remained intact.
Even a man like him is not a threat to him.
Majid Majidi ’ s closeness to the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran began with Mr. Majidi ’ s presence in the artistic field and was consolidated by the issuance of the license for the film “Bedok ” under the supervision of the Supreme Leader ’ s office and continued with his subsequent films.
The announcement of the sun as the representative of Iranian cinema for the Oscars was probably made the day after Joe Biden was announced as president of the United States, taking a look at the nomination of “Children of the Sky ” during Bill Clinton ’ s presidency.
The cinematic diplomacy of Iran and the United States is approaching another test, and the Islamic Republic has sent its message by introducing a representative connected to the whole system.
The Academy has also shown interest in this diplomacy over the past year by condoning its violations (by accepting the introduction of the film from the Farabi Foundation as a government institution).

Interior Minister Priti Patel said she was deeply saddened by the incident and was ready to help French authorities continue the search and rescue operation.
Human rights and refugee advocates say the crash should be a wake-up call for the UK government, which is pushing anti-immigration policies to kill asylum seekers.
Amnesty International has called on the governments of London and Paris to facilitate migration so that asylum seekers do not have to travel dangerously.
However, differences between the two countries' authorities on how to deal with migrants are rising ahead of the end of London's transition from the European Union.
Britain wants France to seize an illegal refugee ship and return it to its shores instead of trying it.
But the Paris government is not under such a commitment.
Last year, the UK government introduced a new immigration scheme that would drastically reduce the chances of applicants lacking the skills and expertise to immigrate to the UK in the post-Brexit period.
The UK officially left the European Union on 31 January.
Representatives from both sides are negotiating for the continuation of cooperation between the two sides in the post-election period.
The repatriation of migrants to France is one of the issues that Britain seeks to gain concessions from the European side in negotiations with the European Union.

48 hours before the bodies arrive in Iran, they tell their families to get ready and they have to call the ambulance themselves.

The door opens and ambulances burst into the area.

Ali thanks those who waited until the twilight for his family to come and says they are waiting for Artin.

title: Palestinian PM: Normalization of relations is an attempt to escape peace
text:
The Palestinian Authority prime minister on Monday criticized the normalization of relations between Arab countries and the Zionist regime as an alternative to peace with Palestine, calling the move an attempt to escape.
Palestinian Authority Prime Minister Mohammed Ashtiyah said at the beginning of the weekly Palestinian Authority meeting that trying to portray the normalization of Arab relations with the Zionist regime as an alternative to peace with the Palestinians was an escape from the truth.
The Arab countries ’ move to discuss the opening of their embassies in the occupied territories is distressing, he added, especially since they do not have embassies and diplomatic missions in Palestine that they recognize.
We call for a serious peace process with Israel, a process that ends the occupation and blockade of the Gaza Strip and Jerusalem and stops settlement building.
We will never allow Israel to use our money to extort us.
He said the Zionist regime is obliged to adhere to all agreements and pursue a political process based on international principles and UN resolutions with full international supervision.
Palestinian officials said on Tuesday they had received an official letter from the Israeli government regarding their commitment to the agreements signed with the PLO.
Since April 2014, peace talks between Palestinians and Israelis have stalled due to Israel ’ s refusal to release former detainees, the settlement freeze, and the acceptance of pre-1967 borders as the basis for a two-state solution.
In mid-September, the UAE and Bahrain signed a US-brokered normalization agreement with Israel.
The move was widely condemned by Palestinian groups and leaders as a betrayal and a stab in the back against the Palestinian people.
The Palestinian leadership rejects any normalization of relations between the Zionist regime and Arab countries before the end of its occupation of Palestinian lands on the 1967 borders.
End of message.

title: Migrations: The narrative of death of Iranian Kurdish family on the way to Britain
text:
The story of the death of the Iranian Kurdish family on the way to Britain Ghyar Gol BBC image source, Family handout picture description, Anita Irannejad recently released a video of an Iranian Kurdish girl who drowned in the English Channel last month along with her family on the way to Britain.
The video shows the determination of a family that embarks on a risky journey for a better future for their children.
Nine year old Anita can laugh and cry at the same time: “My name is Anita Irannejad.
This was an audition for a local film called "The Walnut Tree" that was to be made in his hometown.
Behind the scenes, the voice of his father, Rasoul Irannejad, is heard quietly encouraging him: “I want to be an actor … Say … ”
This video shows a father who wants his daughter to pursue her dreams.
But this wish is not easy for a girl from a region that faces both economic poverty and political pressures.
The Anita family comes from Sardasht, a small Kurdish town on Iran ’ s western border with Iraq.
About a year after Anita ’ s audition, her father Rasoul, her mother Shiva Rasoul-Panahi and her brothers Armin, six years old and Artin, 15 months, embark on a dangerous journey to Europe.
But the Anita family ’ s hopes for a better future and a safer place fail on the English Channel on 27 October.
A small boat that sailed to Britain under adverse weather conditions capsized a few kilometres after the start of the voyage.
Shiva and her children are stranded in the cabin without a life jacket.
Rasul Irannejad, 35, and his family leave Iran in early August.
Their relatives did not comment directly on why they left Iran, but there are many reasons why they wanted to start life again somewhere else.
Sardasht in West Azerbaijan province, like many Kurdish regions of Iran, faces additional problems than other parts of Iran.
In the absence of major industries, the border regions have one of the highest unemployment rates in Iran.
Explaining the picture, the path of the family of Iranian refugees, many of Sardasht residents are forced to Kolbari and smuggling goods from the border of Iraqi Kurdistan to Iran.
It doesn ’ t make much profit, they get less than $10 per trip, but it ’ s risky.
Hundreds of kulbars have been killed or injured in shootings by Iranian border guards in recent years.
Many have fallen in hard-to-reach mountains or been buried in avalanches in the winter.
The area is also very safe and military.
Since the 1979 revolution, these mountainous and border areas have been frequented by Kurdish armed parties and clashes between them and Iranian security forces.
Refugee camps in France have been harsher in the Kurdish areas of Iran, and court orders against the harsher, about 10 percent of Iran ’ s 82 million population are Kurdish, but according to the United Nations, Kurds make up at least half of the country ’ s political prisoners.
The number of political and security prisoners in the region is high.
A friend of Shiva told the BBC that Rasul Irannejad had fled persecution by the government.
He says Shiva sold all their possessions and borrowed money from friends and family to pay for a smuggled trip to Europe, with the goal of reaching Britain.
Anita family ’ s first station was Turkey.
A clip shows Rasul singing a Kurdish song while his family waits for smugglers to take them to Europe.
"My heart is full of pain, a great sadness...
But what do I have to do to get out of here and leave? ”
The Prophet Noah nodded.
His son Armin laughs merrily.
His little son, Artin, goes to Tati Tati Tati and sits on his knee.
They are sitting in a big room with other refugees.
Turkey was once the final destination for thousands of Iranian refugees, but over the past seven years, Turkey ’ s political climate has changed that.
The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is dealing with hundreds of thousands of Syrian refugees.
Some migrants have reported that Turkish security forces have harassed Iranian refugees, especially Kurds, at police stations or deported them back to Iran upon arrival.
A number of Iranian dissidents in Istanbul have been assassinated or kidnapped and returned to Iran.
That is why Rasul and Shiva did not want to apply for UN asylum in Turkey.
In September, for €24,000, smugglers took them by boat from Turkey to Europe, then trucked them to a refugee camp off the coast of northern France.
Charlotte Dickenter, a volunteer at the Adra charity in the French coastal town of Dunkirk, says she saw Shiva in Gran Sint, the main camp of Iranian migrants and asylum seekers, while distributing food, saying: “Shiva was alive and hopeful.
"She was a small woman, very kind and loving.
I said a few words to you.
He laughed at me, and he was mad. ”
In a refugee camp in France, they steal Shiva and Rasul ’ s belongings.
The boat was sealed three days before the boat sank.
In a message to his friend in Calais, France, he said the boat trip was dangerous, but that he had no money to travel by truck because it would cost more.
He said, “I know it ’ s dangerous, but we have no choice. ”
Shiva makes it clear that he is struggling to find shelter for his family, “I have a thousand pains in my chest and now that I have left Iran, I want to forget my past. ”
One of Rasul ’ s friends, who describes himself as a “refugee, ” traveled from Iran to France with his family.
On the night of 26 October, the smuggler in Dunkirk, France, said it was time to cross the canal the next day.
Early in the morning they set off from a beach called Lon Plaza, a remote spot next to an oil depot.
The family set off from the Loon Pelage beach, the weather was very bad that day, with wind speeds reaching 30 kilometers per hour with waves one and a half meters high.
The wanderer gives up the trip and says it wasn ’ t worth the risk: “I was scared. I didn ’ t go.
I begged the messenger not to go.
He said he had no other choice. ”
Rasul ’ s brother in Iran said he paid smugglers 200 million tomans to cross the English Channel.
Ibrahim Mohammadpour, a 47-year-old actor and documentarian from Sardasht, was on the same boat with his brother Mohammad, 27, and his 17-year-old son.
He says the boat was small and was built to carry eight people, but smugglers had "crammed" 23 people into it.
He said: “Our eyes were blinded because we had suffered so much on this journey.
“At first I thought I didn ’ t want to get on this boat, but then I said I was going to get on, at least, to get out of this disaster and get to our destination. ”
Yasin, a 16-year-old boy from Sardasht, was also on the boat.
He and the other two men had life jackets.
He said none of Anita's family members had life jackets.
There were twenty-two passengers on the boat from Sardasht, and the ship was headed by a refugee from northern Iran.
Iranian migrants who have already arrived in the UK say smugglers often ask the least expensive passenger to steer the boat or force a refugee to sail the boat.
Ebrahim Mohammadpour, an actor and documentary filmmaker from Sardasht, said the incident was unforgettable for Anita, her mother and her brothers to go to the glass cabin of the boat that seemed warmer and safer.
But the cabin becomes a death trap for them.
According to Abraham, after about eight or nine kilometers, the boat was full of water.
He said: “We tried to get water out of the water, but it didn ’ t work.
We wanted to go back to Calais, but we couldn ’ t. ”
His brother Mohammed says the passengers panicked and went from one side to the other until the boat capsized.
Shiva and her children are trapped in the cabin.
Ibrahim (a.s.) said that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went under water and tried to save them, then he came out and cried out for help.
He is a 27-year-old economics student from Sardasht.
He was in that boat.
He said his attempts to break the glass of the cabin with a carpeted blade went nowhere.
“I saw the little Artin in the cabin floating on the water, ” he says.
The messenger of Shiva ’ s brother, who is a refugee in Germany, went to Dunkirk after the boat sank.
He told us in a phone call that he heard that Rasul, his son-in-law, had been able to get Artin out, and then he had come back to get the others out.
But the wave takes Artin with it.
Abraham saw the water flowing from the river.
Crying, she recounts those painful moments: “I grabbed the baby from the water, I thought it might be alive.
I held the boat with one hand and the other with the other.
I shook him to see if he was alive, but he didn't react. "
She continued, “I can ’ t forgive myself. ”
According to Muhammad, Ibrahim ’ s brother, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) came out of the boat whimpering and shouting the names of his family members.
Armin...
Artin...
Shiva...
Then he released his hand from the capsized boat and deliberately surrendered himself to the waves and died. ”
Image source Hengaw, Rasul Irannejad, 35, and his 15-month-old son Artin, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, Anita, 9, and Armin, 6, according to French authorities, at 9: 30 a.m. local time, a sailboat passing through the site sends a warning signal and goes to help the passengers on the sinking boat.
The first rescue ship arrived 17 minutes later.
Fifteen people are rescued and four bodies are pulled from the water.
Shiva's brother and sister identify the body, they were Anita's family.
No sign of Artin for 15 months.
Local authorities say he has disappeared into the sea.
According to the BBC and the Home Office, 297 people arrived in Britain in small boats in 2018.
In 2019, that number rose to 1,840, and in the nine months of this year, 8,000 people arrived in Britain, mostly from Iran.
Financial corruption, high prices and unemployment have led to widespread protests in Iran over the past few years, these protests have been severely suppressed and thousands of people have emigrated from Iran, and as economic pressures and repression of political activists and dissidents increase, the number of Iranians who seek refuge in Western countries increases.
Statistics from the British Interior Ministry show that in 2019, more than 5,500 Iranians applied for asylum in the UK.
In interviews with immigration officials, they must prove that if they return to Iran, they will be prosecuted for political, religious, racial, national and gender reasons.
A large number of Iranian refugees say converting to Christianity is the reason for fleeing Iran.
At least 10 people have died trying to reach Britain on the English Channel since 2019.
Refugee charities have advised French politicians to allow asylum seekers to apply before arriving in the UK.
Three days after the boat sank, Ibrahim Mohammadpour, his son and brother were able to reach the UK for £2,500 per person.
The Home Office plans to return those arriving by boat to countries of origin such as France and Belgium.

title: Improving Cultural Performance by Exploring Coronavirus Effects and Global Experiences
text:
On Sunday, December 22, the specialized meeting of “Cultural and Artistic Experiences of Different Countries Facing Coronavirus ” was held with the aim of recognizing international experiences in dealing with COVID-19 virus by the Research Institute for Culture, Art and Communications and the Organization of Islamic Culture and Communications.
In this meeting, which was held under the editorship of Mostafa Asadzadeh (PhD in Cultural Policy), cultural experts, along with Iranian cultural experts in Germany and Japan, expressed outstanding points about the way and type of exposure to Covid 19.
At the beginning of the meeting, Mohammad Solgi (Head of Research of Culture, Art and Communication) said: From the beginning and the outbreak of the coronavirus, the leisure time of the quarantines was discussed, especially since our encounter with this issue in Iran was accompanied by our holiday, and at that time the government, religious scholars and other experts talked about how to spend these times; after this period, the closure of cultural and artistic centers and entertainment even It was made from cinema to mosques and...
It was closed.
Other areas, such as education, went to cyberspace, and this even affected the field of books and publishing, and led to the closure of important cultural events such as the book fair.
In addition, a field such as tourism and even the type of cultural encounter with the coronavirus is one of the issues that is a detailed and important discussion, and the lifestyle that is influenced by culture and art originates from this issue.
During this period, much has been said about the performance of the government and its quality, but the measure and measure of our performance in this period should be a global standard, which was the necessity of such a meeting.
And we need to have a source for better performance by convening such meetings.
The other speaker of the meeting, Abolhassan Khalaj Monfared (Head of the Center for Strategic Studies of Cultural Relations of the Organization of Culture and Communication), said: “Corona has affected all aspects of our lives from personal and personal aspects to macro, global and social aspects; therefore, we must address this issue and consider the aspects and experiences of others. Iran has been involved and we have tried to formulate reports on this basis.
In addition, we asked our colleagues at the Institute to prepare effective and helpful articles in this area to provide a specialized perspective for our way in this direction.
We need to be aware of what other countries have done in this crisis and use their experiences to improve our intellectual and cultural performance.
How Germany faced the Coronavirus, then Hamid Mohammadi (the cultural attaché of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Germany) expressed the type of German encounter with the Coronavirus and said: "The Coronavirus issue in the 21st century has been a turning point for the division of history before and after the Coronavirus; in Germany, 120,000 people have been infected and 14,200 have died."
He continued: “At the beginning of the crisis, Germany was surprised, but because of its infrastructure, it acted differently; Germany had a budget surplus of $293 billion in terms of economic strength, which can be an important point in dealing with the crisis. ”
Germany is the first populous country in Europe; Germany ’ s approach to dealing with Coronavirus initially did not have a regular mechanism, that is, from late March to early May, its people were observant; but from the beginning of May, there was a nationwide shutdown that lasted until mid-August, and in the first shutdown everything from culture, art, school, factories, industry and so on.
The shutdown began with the ebb of the first wave, but with the difference that the places that needed social presence only worked with 30 percent of the capacity.
It includes movie theatres, galleries and...
Everyone started with 30 percent, but with the second wave starting in early August, the situation became more complicated, with 20,000 sufferers a day, and they resumed a national holiday on November 1.
In Germany, the decision was left to 16 state governments because education was so important to them and schools were open, but up to now 40 percent have been closed because, if there is one case, the school will be closed and reopened for two weeks.
Universities are completely closed and are held online.
Referring to the protests against the violation of civil rights in Germany, the cultural adviser said that although people were not harmed due to the government's support, and the country is in good condition culturally, but a significant population has protested against the government's policies of restricting social, economic and cultural activities, as 40,000 people protested in the center of Berlin and the police could not prevent them, and opposition parties believe that these restrictions are in violation of freedom. Freddie is at odds, and the government can ’ t say that family parties will be canceled and that walking down the street shouldn ’ t be more than two people.
Most people believe this is for their own health.
The individual rights of human beings are more important than their health, and the parliament gave the government the authority to make the necessary decisions.
According to German law, whatever decision the government takes is subject to the permission of the parliament, but in this case the government was given full authority and this caused a protest.
He continued: “In Germany, information is very accurate and people are obliged to observe; for example, stores have been obliged to maintain a social distance from the beginning, and for example, more than 20 people cannot enter a store at the same time.
People are also fully observant, they must wear masks and observe social distance, and they use disinfectants that are present at the entrance of all social centers and are constantly informed on social networks.
Previously, cases of corona have been quarantined by the municipality, which is responsible for this, and warned the centers that the person was in contact with or quarantined such centers, but in the second wave, this issue has been reduced due to the severity of the cases.
Except for those who protest, the majority of the people are strictly observant due to their trust (80% trust in the government).
And this has played an important role in getting the government to control the situation.
Municipalities are constantly in contact with the affected and quarantine the family and no one is left behind; that is, neither the sufferer nor his family and all are under the advice of the government.
In the meantime, everything has moved to digitization: universities, exhibitions, etc.
And the cases that used to be in person are now virtual and cover a lot of scope and have expanded the audience; for example, the book fair that was previously available to the people of Berlin is no longer limited to the location and has a large audience.
The suicides fuelled by Coronavirus were the next speaker, Hossein Diosalar, who described how Japanese culture has been able to help contain Coronavirus and improve the health of society.
He emphasized the role of NGOs in this issue and said: “More than the government should pay attention to the non-government sectors.
He added that in Japan, statistics of the first wave and the government ’ s action to hold emergency conditions were held.
It was followed as closely as possible.
After the peak, it was controlled quickly, but since last week and the last two or three days, the numbers have increased, and according to the latest statistics (yesterday), Tokyo has 534 people a day and the entire country has 126,000.
The total number of deaths is 1967 from the start of the conflict, which is not comparable to other countries but is worrisome.
Referring to the economic damage that existed during the quarantine period, Diosalar said that Japan's statistics were low from the beginning and still are.
The cancellation of cultural and artistic programs was the first consequence, and it was even said that the closure of some items, such as theatres, was unprecedented throughout Japanese history.
Virtual Tokyo International Film Festival was held and cinema, theater, sports and...
It was closed.
Iran's cultural attaché in Japan continued: "The first cultural, sporting and artistic blow that Corona gave to Japan was the Olympic debate, and the event was moved from 2020 to 2021, and this was a great loss for them."
And the cultural impact of these things was also important that we had an increase in youth suicides, which was always increasing at the start of the school year, and this year's coronavirus was added.
To stop this was in the hands of the government.
Suicide in Japan can be interpreted in other ways, as it has a separate philosophy, but it has increased in that time, with women ’ s suicides rising by 40 percent and men rising by 6 percent, according to Coronavirus social workers.
He continued: Tourism (to add the cancellation of the Olympics) has been one of the sources of income for Japan, and the country has always been a country with a high tourism capacity, which has been severely affected by the coronavirus, as in some months up to 99 percent of the non-entry of passengers, and this tourism has severely destroyed the country.
The closure of schools has led to an increase in household costs, which may not be a problem in Iran, but here it creates serious problems for families; increased pregnancy for young people due to the closure of schools and the change in lifestyle that attending the bar and so on.
It was, and continues to be, one of Japan ’ s most important cultural changes.
At the end, Dev Salar emphasized the cases that have affected the control of the COVID-19 method in Japan and said: Culturalization rooted in history and the past can be used in cases of such a crisis, as this culture shows its effects; virtual culture here is more prominent and presence at home is less and this corona has made less.
In addition, observing social distance and avoiding strangers and not shaking hands with friends (which is considered privacy) has caused control of the coronavirus.
Lack of family gatherings and gatherings outside the home; while they are an obedient society, this has been a component of their success throughout history and in a crisis like Coronavirus.
Legislation in this country is very high, and this has been very effective in controlling the coronavirus.
Avoiding excitement and turmoil is another important issue that can ’ t overcome their right behaviors.
Maintaining safety, cleanliness and cleanliness at all levels of society (individual and social), regular citizenship behavior, healthy eating habits, the multiplicity of bitter experiences (tsunamis, wars, earthquakes and volcanoes) that have increased social resilience, the health system has been a significant part of the corona outbreak.
These days, it ’ s about shopping, getting married, and...
What has happened in Japan has become more and more serious.
The authority area in Japan is for governorates and municipalities, for example, in Tokyo, municipalities make decisions in specialized groups; and the government is generally aware and announces cases.
In Japan, there was no serious opposition to the major decisions, and people were very supportive of the decisions for the community, and perhaps this helped the country in controlling the coronavirus.
The dual view that caused controversy was the final speech of the meeting by Esmail Gholamipour (Research Institute for Culture, Art and Communication), who said: General cultural discussion and specialized area of cultural and artistic activities were topics that we heard in the talks between German and Japanese society.
He added: "In the social and cultural sphere in Iran, from the beginning, we had challenges between different social forces in the face of the Coronavirus restriction, which ultimately led to the formation of the National Headquarters for the Coronavirus Crisis to make a decision for all sectors of society."
There was a twofold view that in some places health debate precedes religious debate and this conflict has created votes.
He emphasized that cyberspace and the Internet platform in this era became the dominant space for artistic presentation at this time; a subject that can help us to generalize culture by looking at and using the experiences of successful countries such as Germany and Japan.

title: Japan ’ s October suicides are “more than all Coronavirus deaths this year ”
text:
Official Japanese figures show there were 2,153 suicides last month, more than the total number of deaths from coronavirus this year.
CNN reported on Sunday that the number of suicides in October was the highest since May 2015, citing statistics from the Japanese Ministry of Health.
Experts say fears of poverty, the coronavirus outbreak, widespread unemployment and social isolation can lead to a psychotic crisis.
A total of 2,087 people have died from coronavirus in Japan since the start of the year, but the total number of suicides in Japan last year was 20,000, with the first half of 2020 dropping slightly, but rebounding over the past few months.
Japan has one of the highest suicide rates in the world, with 18.5 suicides per 100,000 people.
The October figures show that the suicide rate among Japanese women rose by 83 percent compared to last October and 22 percent among men.
Women in Japan are more active in sectors such as hotel services, food services and stores.
Japan is one of the most successful countries in containing the coronavirus outbreak, with a population of more than 126 million people, only about 2,000 victims have been recorded, but the country ’ s high suicide rate continues.

title: Japan warns: Suicide kills more people than coronavirus
text:
Doctors and experts have warned about the effects of coronavirus on the human psyche.
Japan has released statistics on the number of people who committed suicide in October.
A warning to the rest of the world.
On Sunday, November 29, CNN reported a significant increase in the number of suicides in Japan.
Japan has recorded 2,153 suicides in just one month (October).
The total number of people who died of COVID-19 in Japan this year is 2,083.
The suicide rate in one month was unprecedented in Japan since 2015.
In addition, figures released by Japanese government officials show that suicide rates have risen since March and peaked in October.
The publication of suicide statistics by countries around the world, especially industrialized countries, usually do not publish the number of suicides on a regular basis.
For example, the latest statistics on suicide in the United States are from 2018.
Japan has published suicide statistics this year to show the impact of the coronavirus outbreak on the psyche of its people.
It should be noted that Japan is among the countries that have imposed far fewer restrictions in terms of the coronavirus outbreak.
Thus, when the number of suicides in Japan has increased, it is not ruled out that the number of suicides in other industrialized countries is higher.
Among those contributing to the rise in suicide cases in Japan are unemployment, social isolation and concern for the future.
Michiko Ueda, a professor at Waseda University in Tokyo and an expert on suicide cases, said: “We have not had extensive restrictions on COVID-19 compared to other countries.
But despite that, we are seeing a significant increase in the number of suicides. ”
He also warned of higher suicide rates in other countries, as well as a further increase in suicides in Japan and globally as a result of the ongoing coronavirus crisis.

title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
text:
France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.
In recent months, with an increasing number of migrants trying to reach the British coast illegally, the English Channel has become one of the most dangerous crossings for asylum seekers.
Since the beginning of the year, seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel.
Britain ’ s interior minister, Priti Patel, announced on Saturday that the French and British governments had reached an agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.
Britain ’ s interior minister and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement, stressing that they intend to make it impossible for asylum seekers to cross the English Channel, which has reached more than 8,000 this year.
Priti Patel said that as part of the agreement, the French government has committed to doubling the number of its coast guard patrols in the area by December 1 to stop migrant boats in the Channel, and to use new equipment such as drones and radar to identify people trying to cross the Channel to reach the British coast.
Britain ’ s interior minister expressed his satisfaction with the signing of the agreement, saying: “This agreement will make it possible for both France and Britain to make it impossible for migrants to cross the Channel. ”
Signing a new 😍 😍 😍 😍 covenant to tackle small boat crossings.
There will be an increase in surveillance with cuttingedge tech introduce greater security at ports Ensure accommodation for migrants in France https: / / t.co / vjG1KiTkep pic.twitter.com / COJ1jncjcjitC — i Patel (@ pritipatel) November 28, 2020 According to AFP, the two countries have agreed to spend 31.4 million euros on the joint project.
In recent months, the number of migrants attempting to cross the English Channel illegally has increased dramatically.
News of the sinking of boats carrying refugees, which killed four people last year and killed seven this year, including a family of five, has made the Channel a dangerous crossroads for migrants and has severely affected public opinion.
Following the incident, the British government accused France of not doing enough to stop refugees from crossing the Channel.
In September, French authorities said they had blocked 1,300 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.
Between January 1 and August 31, some 6,200 asylum seekers, wearing life jackets and using a variety of inflatable boats, paddles and kayaks provided by smugglers, tried to reach the British coast by illegally crossing the English Channel.
On October 27, following the capsizing of the boat carrying refugees, the majority of whom were Iranian nationals, the 35-year-old Rasoul Irannejad, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, two children aged 6 and 9, and their 15-month-old baby, who were from Sardasht and were trying to cross the Channel from France to Britain, drowned and died.
One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.
Every year, thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries try to reach Britain through the English Channel.
The Channel, which lies between France and Britain, has seen a dramatic increase in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have died.

title: In Japan, suicide kills more people than coronavirus
text:

title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
text:
New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.
There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.
Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.
The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.
The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.
Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.
According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.
Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.
Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.
Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.
The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.
Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.
NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.
The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.
End of message.

title: The stolen painting returned home.
text:
A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.
In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.
The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.
The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.
Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.
Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.
Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.
After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.
The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.
It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.
Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.
Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity.
This painting is one of the works that Klimt created in the last years of his life.
End of message.

title: The New Wave of Iranian Cinema, Under the Spotlight of English Magazine
text:
According to a report by Farout magazine on Wednesday, although the peak of the new wave of Iranian cinema is generally considered to be in the post-1979 revolution and the overthrow of the Shah, it was actually launched two decades before the revolution.
Iranian cinema productions in this period gradually moved away from industrial works and became social documentaries that explored the cultural problems faced by Iranian society on a daily basis.
The new wave of Iranian cinema is often compared to the Italian Neorealist cinema, but many experts believe that these films had their own style and aesthetic characteristics.
The special cinematic language found in Iranian New Wave cinema examines the nature of the means of cinema and removes the boundary between the fictional space of the film and the reality of documentary filmmaking.
The current is divided into three waves, with the second wave having a greater global reputation.
Abbas Kiarostami, one of the prominent figures of the second wave of Iranian cinema, once said that each film has its own identity.
But it ’ s a film about humans and about humanity.
The different countries of the world, despite their differences in appearance, religion, language and lifestyle, all have one thing in common and that is what is inside of us.
If we take X-rays of different human bodies, we can ’ t tell just by looking at these pictures of people ’ s language, background, or race.
According to Kiarostami, blood flows in the same way, our nervous system and eyes work the same way, we cry and laugh the same way, we feel pain the same way, our teeth hurt the same way regardless of our nationality or background.
In the case of cinema and cinema subjects, the right way is to talk about pain and happiness because they are common among all countries.
Farout magazine, in its weekly article on world cinema, has introduced a list of the characteristic works of the new wave of Iranian cinema to help understand the unique artistic nuances of this important movement in the history of cinema.
You are still looking at this list.
This publication places Forough Farrokhzad ’ s Black House (1962) and Ebrahim Golestan ’ s Adobe and Mirror (1964) among the pioneers of the new wave of Iranian cinema.
The first wave: The cow film by Dariush Mehrjui (1969) The cow film, based on the novel by the Iranian writer Gholamhossein Saedi, is known among critics as the first new wave film of Iranian cinema.
The iconic film depicts the poverty of rural society during the reign of the Shah through an allegorical story about the death of a peasant man who loves his cow more than anything else in the world.
After the man's cow mysteriously dies, he begins to identify with the dead animal and believes that the cow is alive in him.
Over the years, The Cow has been widely praised for its portrayal of Marxist theories of social alienation.
The film criticizes the economic exploitation of nature and the superstition of the rural population in humorous language, and does it all by presenting a seemingly simple story about a man and a cow.
Farout refers to the film Kaiser by Massoud Kimiai as the second film of this group and after introducing the third film of the group.
Still Life (1974) is a minimalist look at the essentially isolated nature of man from the perspective of an elderly cocksucker who has been working in an abandoned train station for more than three decades.
It questions the monotony of our lives and breaks the boundaries between cinema and truth.
Still Life also made its way to the 24th Berlin International Film Festival and won the Silver Bear Award.
According to Sohrab Shaheed Saleh, director of this film, in the lifeless nature of women are female objects that are abused if they are present and their absence does not matter.
Second Wave: A Close Up by Abbas Kiarostami (1990) As Iran ’ s greatest New Wave filmmaker, Kiarostami ’ s post-modern documentary-drama Close-up skillfully blurs the line between fiction / non-fiction and fantasy / reality.
In this film, based on a true story, he narrates the tragic story of an ambitious and unemployed filmmaker named Hossein Sabzian.
In this metaphorical work, Kiarostami explores the roles we play in life with the precision of a surgeon and the subtlety of a poet.
Close-up can be a beautiful, yet disturbing, cinematic psychoanalysis of an ordinary man.
According to the director, in this type of cinema, whether you are dealing with professional or non-actors, the end result will be more desirable if you give them as much as you direct them as the director.
In this way, the real and individual strengths of the actors will be allowed to be expressed and this will have a profound impact on the audience.
Children of the Sky by Majid Majidi (1997) The children of the sky drama by Majid Majidi is often compared to the cinematic masterpiece Bicycle Thief by Vittorio De Sica, which is, of course, a justified analogy.
The Children of the Sky tells the story of a brother and sister named Ali and Zahra, who embark on an interesting adventure after Ali accidentally loses his sister ’ s shoes.
The film was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, but ended up losing the competition to The Beautiful Life by Italian filmmaker Roberto Benigni.
When asked why he prefers to see the world from the perspective of children, Majidi explains: “The world of children is a pure and unselfish world.
They will believe whatever you tell them.
The innocence of children affects adults as well, and that ’ s what I ’ m always trying to show.
The third wave: The English publication in this section refers to two films, A Time to Drunken Horses, followed by a rare separation from Simin.
The most recent example of the nuances of the new wave of Iranian cinema on this list is Asghar Farhadi ’ s complex psychological drama, A Nadir Separation from Simin, which examines the social consequences of the institution of marriage through the conflicts faced by the middle class.
Mahmoud Kalari ’ s cinematography and the moral intricacies of the story make this film one of the most prominent examples of the new wave of Iranian cinema.
Nader ’ s Separation from Simin was the first Iranian film to win the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival.
The film also won a Golden Globe for Best Foreign Film and was nominated for Best Original Screenplay, the first non-English language film to achieve this feat in five years.
Asghar Farhadi says about this film that this type of film allows the audience to explore, I consider this to be modern art in which the artist does not look at the audience from above and does not impose his view on the viewer.
If you answer the question, the movie will end up in the same room.
But when you ask questions, your movie starts fresh after you watch it.
In fact, the film will continue in the viewer ’ s mind.
The important thing is to give the audience a chance to think.
At the moment, the most important thing we need in Iran is to think about it.

title: Israel and Morocco agree on normalization of relations
text:
On Thursday, US President Donald Trump tweeted: “Today, another historic breakthrough has been achieved. ”
“Our two great friends, Israel and the Kingdom of Morocco, have agreed on full diplomatic relations — a tremendous advance for peace in the Middle East. ”
He also said in a separate message that he had signed a declaration recognizing Morocco ’ s sovereignty over the Western Sahara, a disputed area over which Morocco had claimed territory for years.
Since the occupation of Palestine by the occupying forces of the Zionist regime in 1948 and the war between Israel and the Arabs, it was the rule in the Arab world that normalization of relations with Israel was possible only if an independent Palestinian state was formed.
But in August this year, representatives from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain agreed to sign agreements called Abraham and mediated by the US government to establish full diplomatic relations with Israel.
Two months later, the African country of Sudan also announced the normalization of bilateral relations with the Zionist regime.
Morocco is now the fourth Arab country to establish diplomatic relations with Tel Aviv under Trump.
Only two Arab states, Egypt and Jordan, signed peace agreements with Israel in 1979 and 1994, respectively.
In addition to the shared borders with occupied Palestine, both countries participated in wars against Tel Aviv.
