title: The mysterious death of 29 asylum seekers in UK immigration centres
text:
According to IRNA, the Guardian ’ s identity and cause of death have not been revealed.
Most of them were between the ages of 20 and 40 and were physically healthy when they moved to the UK.
One of the victims was 27-year-old Mohammed Kamra from Côte d ’ Ivoire who was found dead in his room on November 9.
He arrived in England from Libya, suffering from back pain before his death.
Mohammed Camera arrived on the south-east coast of England by boat from the perilous English Channel.
A friend who accompanied him said that Mohammad was a social person and when we arrived in England he laughed because he believed he would have a new life.
A British Home Office spokesman confirmed the incident but did not specify the cause of his death.
Abdullah Ahmed Abdullah al-Habib, 41, who had emigrated from Yemen to the UK, was found dead on August 6 at an immigration centre of the Interior Ministry in Manchester.
Last summer, he travelled across the English Channel with other refugees from Yemen and Syria.
British border agents detained them for three days at a migration centre in Bedfordshire and then transferred them to Manchester.
On November 30, a jury in the United Kingdom ruled that the death of Oscar Okurim, a Nigerian refugee who died of a brain hemorrhage, was unnatural.
The Scottish Council has called for a full and independent investigation into the deaths.
A group of lawmakers from Glasgow also called for an investigation into the deaths of three people in the area.
Morsi Baguma, from Uganda, was found dead next to his son ’ s bed.
Adnan Olba and Badreddin Abdullah Adam from Syria were also shot dead by police.
Claire Moseley, founder of the charity Ker4Calais, said: “It is a shame that more asylum seekers are dying in the Home Office ’ s migration centres than in the port of Calais or those trying to cross the English Channel.
Refugees are resilient and tough people.
They are going through a difficult journey from hell to Libya, and they are going through incredible hardships to get here.
But the way we treat them in this country is outrageous.
Our government does not provide the basic necessities of life, such as food and clothing.
It locks them in military barracks and hotels, and threatens to deport them all the time, instead of dealing with them faster.
Earlier, one of the good compatriots living in the UK also described the deplorable situation of Iranian immigrants who are living in British immigration centers until their residence is clear.
Speaking to IRNA, he said migrants he has identified at an immigration centre in south London have been wearing the same clothes they were wearing at the time of their arrest for weeks.
Among them are children and women who receive only one meal a day from the government.
The developments come as the British High Court ruled yesterday that the Home Office has failed to meet its responsibility to protect human rights.

title: Canada casts doubt on Iran ’ s narrative of how Ukrainian plane was shot down
text:
Canada ’ s foreign minister called the explanations of the Islamic Republic ’ s officials who blame the shooting of two IRGC missiles at a Ukrainian International passenger plane as a human error.
François Philippe Champagne told CBC Canada on Wednesday that the missile fired on the passenger plane raised many questions and should be allowed to continue the investigation.
On January 8, a Ukrainian passenger plane, shortly after taking off from Tehran airport, was hit by two missiles from the Revolutionary Guards ’ aerospace defense system and shot down.
All 176 people on board lost their lives.
The authorities of the Islamic Republic, despite the evidence and reports that the missile hit the plane as the cause of its crash and despite the accurate knowledge of the cause of the incident, strongly denied these reports and provided false information.
Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram Amirali Hajizadeh, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said in a television interview three days later that the cause of the disaster was human error and that the IRGC air defense officer had “mistakenly identified the Ukrainian passenger plane as a cruise missile ” and fired at it.
Shortly before Francois Philippe Champagne ’ s comments, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau ’ s special adviser, Ralph Goodale, presented a 79-page report on the outcome of an independent group investigation, accusing the Islamic Republic of not answering many key questions.
Airplanes as human shields?
The downing of the Ukrainian plane came hours after the IRGC retaliatory operations and the firing of several missiles at a base used by U.S. and allied forces in Iraq.
The move was in retaliation for the killing of Qassem Soleimani, the commander of the then Quds Force, in a US drone strike near Baghdad airport.
On the night of the incident, the Revolutionary Guards were on high alert over fears of a U.S. military response, and missile defense systems were boosted in some locations, including around Tehran, but civilian flights continued as normal.
Some critics have accused the Islamic Republic of using civilian aircraft as human shields to prevent possible U.S. attacks.
In a report by Ralph Goodale, the Islamic Republic was asked why Iran ’ s airspace remained open in wartime conditions and how the country ’ s radar system threatened the airliner.
The report ’ s authors expressed disappointment at Iran ’ s seriousness in pursuing the investigation and clarifying the uncertainties.
The Canadian prime minister ’ s adviser, who is responsible for helping the survivors of the plane crash, said Iran should not be responsible for investigating the incident because of the role of Iranian military forces in the incident.
In a tweet, Trudeau called the victims of the Ukrainian plane “innocent people ” whose loved ones needed“ the transparency, justice and accountability of the perpetrators. ”
He promised that the Canadian government would continue to work together to fulfill the wishes of the survivors.
One of the unanswered questions is the introduction of a person or persons in the IRGC who ordered the missile to be fired.
Iranian authorities have previously reported the detention of six people in connection with the downing of the Ukrainian plane, but have not mentioned their identity or direction.
The case has been handed over to the Tehran military court.
Gholamabbas Turki, the military prosecutor of Tehran province, said three of the men were still detained.
According to reports, a number of survivors of the victims of the Ukrainian plane were present at the Tehran military court on Monday, December 14, and strongly protested against the lack of treatment by the authorities.
The criminal of calling Zarif and Hajizadeh, the father of Maryam Malek, one of the victims of the Ukrainian plane crash in the military court, explicitly called Amir Ali Hajizadeh, the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Corps, and Mohammad Javad Zarif, the foreign minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, a “criminal ” and called for the prosecution of those involved in the shooting down of the passenger plane.
Zarif has been repeatedly criticized for his repeated and fruitless talks with his Ukrainian counterpart.
Hamed Ismailion, a spokesman for the family of the victims of the 752 flight on May 7, criticized Zarif in a Twitter message in response to one of the talks.
One of the protests of survivors of the victims of the downing of the plane is their refusal to participate in the investigation of the case and the continuing secrecy of the authorities about many issues.
Watch the 04: 43 video of the speech of the father of Maryam Malek, one of the victims of the Tehran-Kiev flight from the remarks of Mr. Malek, two short films have been released in cyberspace.
In part of his speech, he criticized the authorities for “not considering that we, as parents, as livers, as those who are practically walking dead, should participate in the investigation and clarification of the facts. ”
Criticism of entrusting the investigation to “criminals ” by calling those like Hajizadeh involved in the investigation“ criminals ” said: “How can a bunch of criminals be involved in the investigation, how can a knife cut its own handle?
Is that possible?
"The aerospace commander, who has the blood of our children on his hands, will he allow the investigation to be conducted properly?"
Canada and Ukraine have repeatedly criticized the Islamic Republic for delaying its investigation and failing to answer important questions about the case.
A Washington-based law firm said in a statement that it had filed a complaint on behalf of a number of relatives of the victims of Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, who were American citizens, against the government of the Islamic Republic led by Ali Khamenei and the Revolutionary Guards under the command of Hossein Salami.
Last February, a legal team in Canada filed a lawsuit on behalf of survivors of the victims, demanding $1.5 billion ($1.1 billion) in compensation.
Many survivors of the victims have repeatedly said that it is more important for them to be clear about the details of how the plane was targeted and to identify and punish those responsible for the disaster than to receive compensation.

title: Corona Pandemic Delays Berlinale Film Festival
text:
Organizers of the Berlinale festival hoped that the coronavirus pandemic would be contained by the end of the year so much that it would be possible to hold its 71st edition in February next year.
It was officially announced on Friday 18 December that the Berlin Film Festival has been postponed and will not be held as usual in the upcoming period.
According to the German news agency, before the official confirmation of this issue, news had been published in the media.
Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram. In March 2021, the screening of films entering the competition phase of the festival will be shown online for fans and their public screening will take place three months later.
Marita Risen Beck, executive director of the festival, said there is a strong desire to be physically present at such events, but the current situation of the coronavirus outbreak does not allow this to happen in February.
He said that by changing the program of the 2021 festival, it will be possible to protect the health of the guests and support the re-launch of the activities of the cinema field.
If there is no unexpected change, the public release of the films will take place in both theaters and outdoor next summer.
The Berlin Film Festival, along with Cannes and Venice, is the most important artistic event in Europe and one of the most prestigious film festivals in the world.
The Berlinale has a special place in terms of public reception and attracting spectators, drawing several hundred thousand people to the cinema halls each year.
In February of this year, more than 330,000 tickets were sold.
Berlinale and Iranian artists in the 70th Berlinale edition of the film "Evil Does Not Exist", directed by Mohammad Rasoulof, was selected as the winner of the Golden Bear Award.
Rasoulof could not leave Iran to receive his prize and attend Berlin, and his daughter Baran did it in his place.
The Golden Bear of Berlinale was awarded to Jafar Panahi five years ago for the film Taxi, who was also unable to participate in the award ceremony due to the travel ban.
Panahi had previously won the Berlinale Silver Bear twice, once in 2006 for Offside and once in 2013 for the screenplay.
Nasrin Sotoudeh, a lawyer and human rights activist currently in prison, is in a short scene from Jafar Panahi ’ s Taxi.
The Berlin International Film Festival and the European Film Academy praised the efforts and activities of Nasrin Sotoudeh in a joint call for her immediate release.

title: Hemingway: A typewriter in the trenches
text:
Hemingway was the spokesperson for “Lost Generation, ” Ernest Hemingway liked to be a war reporter, professional athlete, hunter or adventurer.
He considered writing to be little, but eventually became one of the greatest writers of the 20th century.
He won the Nobel Prize for Literature and influenced many writers after World War II.
Today, Hemingway is one of the emblems of the modern world.
He ended his life 50 years ago.
Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois, North America in 1899.
Her father was a doctor and gave a good life to the family.
Ernest was playful in school and hated homework, but he was smart enough to get good grades.
Hemingway was drawn into journalism at the age of 18.
With a rebellious nature that never calmed down, his heart yearned for distant lands and found this “opportunity ” in war.
As an ambulance driver for the International Red Cross, he traveled to Europe in the last year of the Great War with American troops.
During the war, he felt the horror of death with flesh and skin.
Under Austrian bombardment, he suffered severe injuries and was hospitalized for several months.
At the hospital in Milan, more than 200 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body, and he used to pull metal from his leg with the tip of a knife.
Hemingway was also a lover and was impatient with beautiful women.
He was married four times in his life, amidst dozens of love stories.
At the hospital, she fell madly in love with her nurse.
But a few months later, after the war ended, he returned to the United States and married another woman.
He was 22 years old and his first wife was 29.
A decent and kind woman, who "accidentally" had a good financial situation.
A spokesman for Hemingway ’ s Lost Generation went to Europe in 1921 with his young wife, and in Paris joined the ranks of modernist writers who had gathered in the “capital of modern art ”: Scott Fitzgerald, John dos Passos, Ezra Pound, and others.
Gertrude Stein called it the “Lost Generation. ”
The children of this generation lost all hope and faith in the muddy fields of war and they no longer believed and trusted in anything.
The moral lessons and moral values and the bragging of “bourgeois civilization ” were seen as a bunch of deceptive lies.
Hemingway, who had begun to write real reports and his first short stories, brought this anger and frustration to paper in a new tone.
His stories, full of vitality, infused the deep anger and frustration of this generation with vivid and effective expression.
“The Sun Still Rises ” was a vivid account of the story of this generation, seeking consolation that could not be found in foreign cities.
The novel A Farewell to Arms, published in 1928, clearly expressed this disillusionment.
This wasn ’ t an ordinary princeling.
Someone was talking about the war, who had been wounded by it and still had its shrapnel in his body.
“I had seen nothing sacred, and the things that were glorious had no honor, and the victims were like cattle and sheep in the Chicago slaughterhouse — if they had nothing to do with the carcasses but to bury them. ”
(Farewell to Arms, translation of Najaf Daryabandari) This was the look of the masses of those who lost the war anyway, and this was of course different from the look and expression of the elites and commanders, for whom the war was a "field of honor" and full of "blessings".
Ernest Hemingway was married four times — his second wife, Pauline Pfeiffer, can be seen in this photo, some critics point out that Hemingway ’ s participation in the war was not just an individual experience that influenced his literary work, but, more than that, the war took over his whole being and his mentality, gave him a “war-torn ” temperament and shaped his worldview.
Hemingway was constantly ready to fight and saw in everything a challenge to fight: on the battlefield, in the boxing ring, or in the bullfight.
The novel The Sun Still Rises, published in 1927, illustrates this view in a variety of colorful depictions and images.
In Death in the Afternoon, published in the form of a true memoir or travelogue in 1932, the bullfight is a metaphor for confronting death: standing face to face with death, gazing into its eyes, shivering with this horror / pleasure, mingling with it, and finally sinking into its black palate.
It has been said that Hemingway ’ s hobbies, fishing, from hunting wild animals to hunting women, were manifestations of this constant temptation of war and bullying.
Even writing was a big challenge for him, with special preparation and discipline to “fight ” it.
Some critics have said that he saw killing and being killed as the only natural form of human history, so much so that he believed that a "healthy and natural" man should die on the field, not in bed.
There has always been a man of struggle and action in Hemingway ’ s “Square. ”
not from the works of others, as he has said with pride, but from blood and sweat.
Will Durant has said that in few writers life experiences are so closely intertwined with literary endeavors.
Hemingway hated intellectual habits and debate.
He despised the intellectuals who, steeped in abstract discussions, had forgotten the principle of life; he called them cowards and cowards.
He was not a theorist and did not even consider himself a literary and literary writer, in the classical sense.
He once said, “I ’ m not going to compete with Tolstoy. ”
In his Nobel Prize speech (1954), Hemingway's style and language explained his style with the metaphor of an "iceberg": "I try to be like an iceberg, seven eighths of which are hidden under water and only one eighth of which is visible.
The more we remove from the body of the story, the stronger the iceberg becomes.
The power of the story lies in what the author knows but doesn ’ t reveal.
If he omits something because he doesn ’ t know, there ’ s a hole in the story. ”
The author knows all about his space and characters but only gives the reader the least necessary information.
In this precise, measured and compact style, most of the notes and explanations are eliminated, but they do not go away; the reader senses them and is affected with far greater intensity.
With the technique of "elimination" in both story structure and language, a pure and clear text is provided that has a direct and lightning effect.
The plot or plot is missing.
The tongue is compact, concise, dry, and without sentimental frills.
Short sentences convey only a thin surface and leave the rest to the reader ’ s intelligence.
This is how the joy of reading the story is multiplied by the joy of discovery.
Hemingway wrote from real, live experiences.
(He even boasted that he had killed dozens of people in the war!)
It was the only objective language, unadorned and transparent, that could convey vivid experiences directly and directly, away from the repetitive pronouncements and fluttering sentimental adjectives.
Hemingway ’ s best work comes from personal tensions and struggles.
From a man ’ s quarrel with a giant fish, he presented one of the most fascinating stories of the 20th century.
It ’ s a true story with ancient myths.
All kinds of interpretations and interpretations have been published about "The Old Man and the Sea".
Hemingway ’ s own explanation is probably the best: “I have shown a true old man against a true fish in a true sea! ”
That too, true or false, had its origin in life.
Hemingway boasted that he once caught a 355-kilogram fish.
In the world of politics, Hemingway cannot be considered a “committed ” writer, even though he was“ engaged ” with political adventures all his life.
(His file on the FBI is thousands of pages!)
He was more or less present in all the important events of his time, a correspondent in the two world wars, and a little more active in the Spanish Civil War.
After all, he was a terrible writer.
The painful experience of war and the constant presence of death had engulfed his soul, infecting it with bitterness and deadly pessimism.
For the rest of his life, he looked at every struggle with ridicule and “cynicism ”.
Politics required a minimum of optimism and idealism, whereas Hemingway only “believed ” in himself and held the highest value in being“ loyal ” to himself.
Perhaps, following Nietzsche, without engaging himself with philosophical deliberations, he believed in individual power and “the will to power. ”
He had an iron fist, and he held his hand.
He had no weakness, no weakness, no weakness.
(He said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”)
He knew the people and the people of both worlds.
In extreme individualism, Hemingway's goodness is equal to joy.
He liked prosperity and pleasure, but with a more or less Bohemian tendency he avoided “bourgeois ” life and culture.
Most of his years were spent in "uncivilized" climates, in the wild jungles of Africa and on the shores of Latin America.
In the 1950s, Africa was home to his adventures, with a priceless achievement: a beautiful and moving story called “The Snows of Kilimanjaro. ”
The bottom line: Feminists don ’ t like Hemingway, and they ’ re right.
In his life and art, women have a secondary role, they are there to give men joy and peace, that is all.
The control of life is in the hands of “gentlemen ”:“ men without women. ”
Hemingway's legacy was a Image caption Hemingway was an adventurous and courageous hunter Ernest Hemingway wrote early and became famous and influential.
Those who have gone through the terrible crises and tragic tragedies of the twentieth century find the most effective narrative in Hemingway ’ s objective and concise style.
The grandiose “literary ” language and previous iterative descriptions were used to represent the anxieties of the twentieth century.
The authors of the novel sought, rather than poetic language, a concise, objective statement that burned and scratched the mind like a naked razor.
After the Second War, writers who spoke of the instability of life or the ills of existentialism, such as Jean-Paul Sartre and Albert Camus in France, or those who wrote about political perplexities, such as Cesare Pausé and Carlo Levy in Italy, or those who wrote about the horrors of the war, such as Wolfgang Borschert, Alfred André and Heinrich Belle in Germany, were all influenced more by Hemingway. It continues to this day, and in Iran.
And death...
Ernest Hemingway, on the battlefield, on dangerous adventures, on countless night walks and drunks, on several car and airplane accidents, had worn out his body and soul, but he still did not calm down.
At the age of 61, his thick beard and hair had turned white.
His mighty and heroic figure gradually melted away, but he still hooked and netted in the sea with feeble hands, ran after the prey with trembling feet, and shot with pale eyes.
During his life, he slept in a hospital bed dozens of times and underwent various surgeries.
In the last months he was constantly dealing with medicine and therapy, which infuriated him and plunged him into severe depression.
He could not bear old age, even in his own body.
It has been said that there was a brave hunter who could no longer hunt except himself.
And he did not hesitate.
One morning he went down the steps of the house and silently took out the double-barreled gun from the cupboard.
He put two bullets in the vault.
He put the tube in his mouth and pulled the trigger: early in the morning of July 2, 1961, in Ketcham, Idaho, the northwestern United States.
And to this day it is still in the grave.

title: Iran says Canada 'doing business' with grief over families of Ukrainian plane victims
text:
Iran says Canada "trades" with the grief of the victims of the Ukrainian airliner, MEHR Image source, Saeed Khatibzadeh, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Saeed Khatibzadeh, has warned Canada, accusing it of "doing business" with the "grief of the families" of the victims of the Ukrainian airliner "and" intervened the most unwarranted since day and tried to avoid the natural path of clarification. "
A spokesman for Iran ’ s foreign ministry accused Canada of trying to make a hat for themselves during the investigation of the Ukrainian plane ’ s downing, “out of the great sadness of these families, some are trying to make a hat for themselves and do business with it. ”
Canada has recently threatened to take Iran to the International Court of Justice if it is not satisfied with the investigation and punishment of those responsible for the downing of the Ukrainian plane.
A spokesman for Iran's foreign ministry accused Canada of "demeaning" and said its behavior was "totally political and non-legal".
"I am warning the Foreign Minister and the Government of Canada to be held accountable for their actions.
Khatibzadeh also promised that "the technical report of the Ukrainian plane crash has been prepared and will be published soon".
The Ukrainian passenger plane was shot down by two IRGC missiles on January 8 after takeoff from Imam Khomeini International Airport in southern Tehran.
138 of the 176 people killed in the shooting were Canadian citizens or residents, and the families of a number of survivors in Canada have filed lawsuits seeking legal action against Iran.
Despite Iran ’ s denial, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau was the first senior foreign official to speak of the plane ’ s crash as a result of a surface-to-air missile strike, and called for transparency in the information.
However, the possibility of the plane being shot down by military actions was first hinted at by the president of the United States.
After three days of denial, Iran finally acknowledged that the IRGC had shot down the plane “for human error. ”
Since then, the Canadian government has repeatedly stressed that it is pursuing a comprehensive investigation into the case and bringing justice to the victims.
During this period, the Iranian Foreign Ministry also criticized Canada for pursuing the rights of the dual nationals of the Ukrainian plane.

Foreign Minister of Canada to BBC Persian: If we are not satisfied with the investigation process, we will take Iran to the International Court of Justice, but the recent tensions between Iran and Canada have increased since Canada announced the possibility of pursuing the case at the International Court of Justice.
Recently, Canadian Foreign Minister François Philippe Champagne threatened the Iranian government that if the families were not satisfied with the process of prosecuting the perpetrators and reparations, Canada would certainly refer the case to the International Civil Aviation Organization, adding that if there were no results, Canada would be ready to sue Iran to the International Court of Justice.
In response to the remarks, the deputy chairman of parliament ’ s national security commission, Shahriar Heidari, said Canada was seeking to declare the downing of the Ukrainian plane in Iran “intentional ” but“ failed ” in this regard.
The deputy head of the National Security Commission of the Iranian parliament told the parliament news agency that after the review of the black box of the Ukrainian plane by experts, "it was determined that the crash of the Ukrainian plane was a human error and was determined to be unintentional."
Canadian officials have a very different view, accusing Iran of not being transparent.
About three months ago, Canadian transport and foreign ministers, after presenting an Iran report on the black box, said the report was "only about moments after the first missile hit and before the second missile hit, but it does not provide information on what happened after the second missile hit."
After reviewing the black box, Iranian aviation officials claimed that only 19 seconds of conversation between the three pilots was recorded after the first missile hit, and after the second missile, no sound was recorded from the cockpit due to "significant damage".
After a long period of refusal, Iran sent the plane ’ s black box to France and an international team was responsible for analyzing its data.
The group included representatives from Iran, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Sweden and France.
The families of the victims criticized the process of processing the file image source, PS752JUSTICE, explaining the image, the gathering of the mothers and relatives of a number of Ukrainian plane victims at the Tehran Military Prosecutor ’ s Office in the past year, the families of some of the Ukrainian plane victims have repeatedly complained about the process of downing the Ukrainian plane and even demanded the resignation of some officials.
Iran has told Ukraine it will provide compensation to the families of the victims, but this has not been confirmed.
The families of the victims have gathered and protested in recent weeks to demand the investigation and trial of the perpetrators of the incident and believe that the negotiations of the countries should be carried out in the next stage.
Iran and Ukraine have held several rounds of talks over the downing of the plane, but the case has yet to be resolved.
Although no report has yet been released on the punishment of the perpetrators of the air disaster, several protesters and mourners of the plane crash in Iran have been sentenced to prison or put under security pressure.
Earlier, the Civil Aviation Organization of Iran released a report on the progress of the investigation into the Ukrainian plane crash.
But the Association of Families of the Victims of Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 had previously criticized the investigation and lack of transparency in the investigation.
The group criticized the Islamic Republic, which shot down the Ukrainian plane, as leading the investigation, adding that Canada, Afghanistan, Sweden and the United Kingdom, which lost many of their citizens, do not have the right to participate actively in the investigation.

title: Top 10 Films of 2020
text:
Another year passed, but a year that was different from all other years, especially for the cinematographers.
Due to the Corona outbreak, cinema halls were closed in most countries, and many of the world ’ s major film festivals from Cannes to Locarno and Karlovy Vary were not held, and ultimately it was one of the saddest years in the history of cinema, so that choosing the top ten films of the year seems more difficult than previous years.
However, the tradition of selecting ten films must be kept in place to remind the flow of cinema and life, and to hope for a better year ahead.
Here are the author ’ s choices – unarranged – from the film festivals held, as well as the limited public screenings of European cinemas.
Another Round (also known as “Drunk ”) is a return to“ The Hunt, ” a stunning 2012 Winterberg film that challenged people ’ s moral judgment and challenged the notion of friendship and family.
Another round follows the same theme and calls into question all morality and moral judgments.
The film draws its strength from a place that goes against the entire current of society ’ s moral judgment, and in a bold work makes a mockery of all predetermined rules.
The film is very entertaining, and the perhaps stupid and dangerous decision of the main characters at first sight – in drinking alcohol – creates an absurd situation that the filmmaker links to the present situation of all humanity and in fact, in metaphorical language, depicts the fragility and emptiness of contemporary humanity.
This remarkable Greek film speaks of an epidemic and may now boast some sort of prophecy, but it takes a different form when people forget their own identity.
With long shots and often fixed cameras, the film tells the humorous story of a surreal world that easily accompanies its audience with the main character in an apocalyptic world in which all entrenched concepts are questioned and we are faced with an empty world that is astonishingly similar to the world of 2020.
The Evil Does Not Exist (Mohammad Rasoulof), winner of the Golden Bear of the Berlin Film Festival, is a continuation of the world of Iranian protesting filmmaker who, despite living in Iran, points his sharp and winning blade towards the dreaded layers of government in which the crime seems natural from repetition, whether it is a serial murder that “does not burn in the manuscripts ” or the execution that runs the story in this film.
But with a different style and style, the filmmaker tells four stories around execution about people who treat each other differently when blindly executed, with a quiet camera that is in no hurry to tell and often watches its characters in silence and stillness.
Where are you going, Ida?
(Quo Vadis, Aida? / Jasmina Zubanich) A spectacular film by a Bosnian filmmaker who brilliantly captures her feminine view of war, a male-dominated phenomenon, and takes us into the dark world of genocide in Bosnia, where in the midst of a crisis we face a middle-aged translator who wants to save her two sons at all costs.
The film goes straight to the point and narrates the whole story in a short time, the short time that the filmmaker tells us in the end how it extends to the present day.
The Human Voice (/ Pedro Almodovar) is a fascinating half-hour film by the acclaimed Spanish filmmaker Pedro Almodovar, which is a release adaptation of Jean Cocteau ’ s play.
We have a woman (Tilda Swinton) who, in the closed space of a film studio, experiences her last conversation with a lover who has left her.
Loneliness becomes the main theme of the film, which, along with the concept and function of the cinema, takes on an attractive dimension, and Almodóvar succeeds in making a film that after the outbreak of the coronavirus and after the beginning of its limitations, which means the double loneliness of human beings, depicts the situation of himself and us in the shortest possible time and, of course, ends with hope.
Dear comrades!
Dear Comrades! / Andrei Konchalovsky is a successful film by Andrei Konchalovsky (after several failed experiments by the Russian filmmaker) that narrates the shooting of protesting workers in a Soviet city in 1962, which allows the filmmaker, in a stifling communist atmosphere, to express the maternal feelings of a woman, who happens to be working for the Communist Party, for her daughter lost in this turbulent atmosphere. Draw a picture.
Konchalovsky, with an attractive atmosphere that could not be imagined other than black and white photography, shared the viewer in a complex and complex atmosphere.
Michel Franco ’ s most successful film, The New Order, depicts class divisions and government corruption boldly and recklessly, where an influential family on their wedding night is attacked by violent, impoverished rebels who turn their heaven into hell.
The second half of the film is even scarier when the family ’ s daughter is kidnapped by the military, who is supposed to be the keeper of order, for ransom.
The film is not afraid to show violence and, on the contrary, wants to engage its audience in a real hell and is largely successful.
Berlin Alexanderplatz / Burhan Ghorbani The spectacular film of Burhan Ghorbani, a German-born Afghan filmmaker who brings the novel of the 1920s to the present day and narrates the concept of immigration in today ’ s Germany, but more and more than that, it is a film about the concept of good and evil and the inner world of a man that portrays the filmmaker ’ s struggle in showing the world of his main African character, which goes beyond geography. The film attempts to show the contrast between good and evil within every human being anywhere in the world.
Armugan-Sol is a strange film from a Spanish filmmaker about death, in which he tells the life of a crippled man in a mountain whose job is to rid the old and disabled people who are suffering.
With as little dialogue as possible, the film portrays this man ’ s relationship with the man who helps him, and through it comes to the relationship with nature and the meaning of life and death, and its subtle anti-fiction narrative, with the help of attractive black and white images, reaches a child who is suffering and raises his basic question about the meaning of life.
The mosquito by Joao Nuno Pinto, the Portuguese filmmaker who opened the Rotterdam Film Festival, tells the story of a 17-year-old soldier sent to Mozambique during World War I and begins a long and strange journey for a character who faces the realities of war.
In a counter-narrative way, the film engages the viewer in a mental and melancholic atmosphere, and with mostly strong visuals, it can engage the mental world of a teenager with the violence around him.
The movie goes so far in this combination of mental and real space that it is impossible to distinguish reality from the mental delirium of this teenager.
Instead, this unfamiliar, heterogeneous atmosphere gives the filmmaker an opportunity to narrate the futility of war.
The film, without falling into the slogan, can beautifully depict the violence and senseless damage of the war and its uselessness.

title: The World in 2020: Living in Coronavirus Constipation
text:
World in 2020: Living in Corona Shock Image Source, Getty Images 2020 is undoubtedly the year of Corona.
The virus that swept the world killed more than 1.6 million people, gripped millions, and challenged everything from the world ’ s largest economy to the smallest, from the most remote cities to the most crowded.
COVID-19 became world news in the first month of the year and continues to be a major problem in the last few days.
For the first time in human history, the disease spread to all continents.
Its economic, social and political consequences will undoubtedly be universal.
This is also unprecedented in human history.
The year 2020 was also the scene of other important events: Donald Trump, in his final year in office, tried to consolidate his position in the Middle East, weaken Iran and strengthen Arab-Israeli ties.
In Europe, COVID-19 intertwined with economic problems and the migrant crisis and the aggressive policies of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, fueling tensions between EU member states and Turkey.
In this report, we review events that have had global impacts and are not limited to a single country.
Image source, Reuters, one of the vehicles attacked at Baghdad airport on the morning of January 3, at the beginning of the new year, a statement from the US Department of Defense reached the news agencies: “At the behest of President Donald Trump and in order to keep the forces stationed abroad safe, the US armed forces made a decisive decision and killed Qassem Soleimani. ”
The United States, which had withdrawn from the JCPOA with the advent of Donald Trump and had imposed unprecedented sanctions on Iran, had now removed a key player of the Islamic Republic, which had a special place to enforce the policies of the Iranian government in the region, and had rallied politicians and experts around the world.
Tehran ’ s response could have irreparable consequences, driving the Middle East, which has been in a state of instability for years, into yet another war.
In particular, Ayatollah Khamenei promised that "severe revenge" awaits the perpetrators and perpetrators of this "international face of the resistance" and emphasized that "all the relatives of his bloodthirsty resistance".
But “harsh revenge ” did not wreak havoc on the region, but claimed the lives of 176 people on board an airliner; mourned hundreds of families and brought a major scandal to Iran ’ s military.
Image source Getty Images January 8, a day after Soleimani ’ s funeral was held in Kerman, during which dozens of people were trampled and killed, Iranian ballistic missiles targeted two military barracks in Iraq that housed international forces, including the United States.
On the night of the attack, Iran ’ s defense system shot down a passenger plane belonging to Ukraine International Airlines, which was leaving Tehran for Kiev.
All crew and passengers were killed.
After three days of denial and concealment, Iranian officials finally claimed that the crash was the result of a “human error ” in the Revolutionary Guard ’ s defenses, but did not release any further information.
For months, he refused to hand over the plane ’ s black boxes and detained or pressured protesters and mourners.
Nearly a year after this humanitarian disaster, Iran has yet to clarify.
On January 11, tensions between Iran and the United States, its possible consequences, and the Ukrainian plane crash were at the top of the world news, with the release of a statement by the Chinese government drawing attention to the industrial city of Wuhan: “The first patient with the new coronavirus has died. ”
The COVID-19 outbreak, the AFP image source, had been circulating on social media for several days, suggesting that a disease was spreading in China, but authorities did not want it to go public.
The first person to reveal this was a doctor named Li Wen Liang, who reported on December 30 a new virus with acute respiratory syndrome in Wuhan.
The police arrested him on charges of “disturbing the public mind ” and forced him to sign a penal code guaranteeing that he would no longer publish“ false information. ”
Reality, however, was unstoppable.
The new coronavirus was spreading rapidly, not only from Wuhan, but also beyond the borders of China.
On January 13, the first patient with COVID-19 was identified outside of China in Thailand.
A week later, the coronavirus emerged in the United States, in Snohomich, Washington, in the northwestern United States.
On January 23, China finally announced it would quarantine the entire city of 11 million people in Wuhan.
That same week, the first case of COVID-19 was made public in Germany, and the World Health Organization declared a state of emergency to warn of the consequences of the global epidemic.
The coronavirus quickly spread to all countries of the world, reaching the South Pole at the end of the year.
Most of the world ’ s economies have been shut down for months.
Thousands of people lost their jobs, and the world witnessed a stillness and horror that had previously only been portrayed in fiction.
Research centers and institutes and pharmaceutical companies around the world, in an unprecedented move, have been exchanging information and teamwork for the birth of an anti-coronavirus vaccine.
Their research was successful in less than a year.
It is a rare event in the history of medicine, if not unprecedented.
Until the announcement, there are three vaccines in the United States and the United Kingdom, one in Russia and a Chinese-made vaccine that some countries around the world are vaccinating their citizens.
Image source Getty Images On December 9, 2019, 90-year-old Margaret Keenan, a British citizen, was the first person in the world to receive a coronavirus vaccine outside of testing conditions.
The UK has also approved a vaccine produced in the country, known as the Oxford Vaccine, for citizens, just one day before the end of the year.
Trump, Arab and Israeli image source, Reuters image description, flags of the US, Israel, the UAE and Bahrain on the wall of the old part of Jerusalem on January 28, Israeli Prime Minister Donald Trump was invited to unveil the “Peace in the Middle East ” plan.
The plan, which the US president says has “very good solutions for the security of Palestinians and Israelis, ” is a“ last chance for peace. ”
The “Deal of the Century ”, the result of“ three years of diplomatic work by the US administration, ” was opposed by Palestinian leaders and Jordanian officials.
Turkey called it a “theft of Palestinian soil ” and Iran described it as a“ nightmare for the region and the world. ”
Other countries in the region have been more cautious.
The United Arab Emirates called it “an important starting point for the resumption of negotiations. ”
Saudi Arabia praised the “efforts of the Trump administration, ” encouraged negotiations between the Palestinians and Israel, and, like Qatar, insisted on“ upholding the Palestinian right to an independent state. ”
Russia and the European Union saw the US president ’ s peace plan as inadequate and contrary to previous treaties, and eventually, the Arab League also opposed it.
Nevertheless, the year 2020 was a turning point in Arab-Israeli relations.
The consultations of Donald Trump ’ s administration accelerated the normalization of political relations between these countries.
On August 13, the US president announced an agreement between Israel and the United Arab Emirates.
The Pact of Abraham is the third peace agreement between Israel and the Arabs since the creation of Israel in 1948.
Previously, only Egypt and Jordan had made peace with Israel.
Image source, Reuters explaining the image, Donald Trump, Benjamin Netanyahu and the foreign ministers of Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates at the signing ceremony of the September 15 normalization agreement, Bahrain also joined the "Pact of Abraham".
A month later, the first Emirati delegation visited Israel, where the two sides agreed to revoke tourist visas and reopen the embassy.
At the same time, Sudan also announced its readiness to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed that the two sides will soon meet to discuss trade and agricultural cooperation.
On December 10, Morocco became the fourth Arab country to take steps to normalize relations with Israel this year.
Although Morocco and Israel have a long history of political relations compared to other Arab countries, and the revival of relations was not unexpected, the US president called it a historic event and a “significant development for peace in the Middle East. ”
According to experts, the Trump administration ’ s efforts to normalize Arab-Israeli relations were ultimately aimed at weakening Iran ’ s position in the region, complemented by the intensification of sanctions and the implementation of some destructive operations, including a series of explosions in Iran ’ s military and nuclear areas.
Image source, MAXAR image, satellite image of the explosion in eastern Tehran, which MAXAR provided to the BBC on June 26, after reports on social media were heard of an explosion in eastern Tehran, Iranian authorities initially announced the source of the sound as an explosion in a gas tank in Parchin, and an Iranian TV reporter went to an undisclosed location and showed burned gas tanks.
But then news agencies, citing satellite photos and confirmation from analysts, reported that the explosion probably happened at a base linked to Iran ’ s missile industry.
Satellite images of the explosion in eastern Tehran on Friday, July 27, 2020, after the explosion (Monday, July 29, 2020) before the July 2 explosion, first emerged news of a fire at the Natanz enrichment facility, Iran ’ s main uranium enrichment and nuclear research center.
Iranian officials again spoke of the fires.
But then, with the release of satellite images of the widespread destruction of a facility in Natanz, it became clear that once again, the Iranian authorities were concealing.
Until Behrouz Kamalvandi, a spokesman for Iran ’ s Atomic Energy Organization, spoke of sabotage at the Natanz site and acknowledged that “we have repelled cyber attacks many times and had a large number of industrial sabotage. ”
The National Security Council said it refused to comment on "the cause and manner of the incident because of security concerns".
The Israeli newspaper Jerusalem Post called the Natanz explosion a "physical sabotage" and its purpose was to "warn Iran" about its nuclear activities.
Reuters and the New York Times quoted “informed sources ” as saying it was likely that Israel, with US support, had engineered the attack.
The Natanz uranium enrichment plant was clicked before and after the incident on July 2, 2020 Date: July 7, 2020 Date: July 7, 2020 In July, several other explosions and fires occurred in Iran, including in Ahvaz, Mahshahr, Mashhad and in Baghershahr, which killed 2 and wounded 3.
The cause of these incidents is not clear.
But some media outlets have raised the possibility of these incidents being linked to sabotage at Natanz and the explosion in eastern Tehran.
However, there is still no evidence in this area.
On November 27, Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, head of the Defense Research Organization, was killed in the town of Absard, near Tehran.
The source of the image, fars to date, inaccurate explanations and sometimes contradictory statements by the Iranian authorities have not helped to better understand these events.
Iran has accused Israel and the MEK.
The operation also used a remote control weapon placed in a pickup truck.
Iranian authorities confirmed that no one was present, but it was later announced that some had been arrested.
According to Getty Images, some Iranian officials spoke of revenge.
But the Iranian government seems to be waiting for a new government in the United States.
Donald Trump lost the US election.
US Presidential Election: Trump did not accept defeat Image Source, Getty Images Description Image, US election of November 3, the 59th US presidential election was held in unprecedented circumstances.
On the one hand, more than 92,000 Americans were infected with COVID-19 every day and more than a thousand people were dying from the disease, and on the other hand, Donald Trump, seeing his position on the campaign trail weakened, talked about the possibility of electoral fraud and added to the fear and uncertainty of those days.
On November 7, after hours of waiting, counting and recounting the vote, the media declared Joe Biden the winner.
Donald Trump, in an unpopular move, did not accept the result of the vote and continued to emphasize the violation of the election.
On December 14, the Electoral College confirmed Joe Biden ’ s victory with 306 votes to 232 votes by Donald Trump to officially end the most controversial presidential election in the United States, although to date Donald Trump has refused to accept defeat and congratulate the president-elect.
Many around the world were waiting for the final outcome of the U.S. election, hoping that a change in power would change U.S. foreign policy.
The victory of the Democratic Party candidate was a return to diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation; a return to America ’ s international commitments, including the Paris Climate Accord, the World Health Organization and UNESCO, and of course the JCPOA.
Critics of the Trump administration believe that his foreign policies have strengthened the power vacuum in regional crises and added to existing tensions and instability.
One of the criticisms against the Donald Trump administration was the attempt to achieve peace with the Taliban.
US-Taliban peace: An unexpected meeting in Doha Image source, Getty Images Image description, Mullah Baradar, deputy Taliban leader and head of the Taliban political office in Doha and US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo at the end of February, the US government signed a peace agreement with the Taliban group in Doha, Qatar.
The two sides have spent 18 months negotiating a deal.
Under the agreement, all U.S. troops will leave Afghanistan within the next 14 months.
There will also be another phase of peace efforts aimed at reconciliation between the Taliban and the Afghan government.
The agreement was only about relations between the Taliban and the United States, and relations between the Taliban and the Afghan government were entrusted to negotiations between the two sides.
The most controversial part of the deal was the release of 5,000 Taliban prisoners.
In return, the Taliban would release 1,000 Afghan government prisoners under the deal.
The process of prisoner exchange, which was supposed to begin and be completed 10 days after the signing of the document, lasted for months.
The Afghan government opposed this part of the agreement because it saw the release of these forces, many of whom had committed serious crimes, sparking a new wave of violence in the country.
Image source, GMIC Image description, Mohammad Ashraf Ghani at the Loya Jirga began the process of releasing prisoners under US pressure, but the decision to release 400 “dangerous ” prisoners was left to the Loya Jirga who agreed to release them.
The release of Taliban prisoners has raised concerns among human rights organizations and Amnesty International.
France and Australia also formally shared their opposition to the release of a number of Taliban prisoners who were involved in the killing of their nationals with the Afghan Foreign Ministry.
In September, after the end of the first peace meeting between the Afghan government and the Taliban, the US Secretary of State held two separate sidelines meetings with the government delegation led by Abdullah Abdullah, and with the Taliban delegation.
One of the photos released from the sideline meeting, which showed Mullah Baradar, the deputy leader of the Taliban and the head of the Taliban political office in Doha, alongside US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, made news.
In November, a major meeting of the countries supporting Afghanistan was held in Geneva, the Geneva meeting with about $13 billion in conditional aid for the next four years of Afghanistan was a source of encouragement for the Afghan people and government, but peace remained a concern.
Despite efforts for peace, the violence in Afghanistan not only did not decrease, but intensified.
In recent months, attacks on a maternity hospital in Kabul, Kabul University and a wave of targeted killings targeting journalists, civil and social activists have dampened hopes for peace in Afghanistan.
Tensions and insecurity, of course, were not limited to Afghanistan in 2020.
Syria and the Mediterranean Sea became the scene of confrontation between Europe and Turkey.
Europe and Turkey: Ankara vs. Paris Image Source, Getty Images Image Description, Macron (right) and Erdogan discussed Libya in January 2020 in Berlin, February 28, more than 20,000 refugees gathered on the Turkish-Greek border and clashed with Greek police after trying to cross the border.
Europeans blame Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for these tensions.
They believe he used the migrant crisis as an excuse to change the 2016 agreement.
A treaty under which Turkey was obliged to provide Syrian, Afghan and sometimes Iranian refugees in the country for six billion euros in financial assistance.
Ankara, which in those days launched Operation Spring Shield in Syria ’ s Idlib province and engaged in a confrontation with the Syrian army on its southern border, was pursuing two goals: weakening the Kurdish forces and creating a refugee resettlement zone.
Recep Tayyip Erdogan, however, needed the support of NATO and, consequently, Europeans to achieve his goal.
While Europeans worried that Erdogan ’ s behavior would add to the tension in Syria, they saw Turkey ’ s military operation in Syria as “unacceptable. ”
On June 10, tensions between Europe and Turkey entered a new phase.
This time in the Mediterranean, when a French warship intervened to inspect a ship suspected of carrying weapons to Libya, Turkish frigates intercepted it and threatened to launch a missile attack on French troops who were present under the NATO flag.
Europe has accused Turkey of helping rebels in Libya despite a ban on arms shipments.
Image source Getty Images Image description, demonstrations in Istanbul against Macron on August 10, the presence of a cruise ship in the Turkish and Cypriot border waters created controversy.
Ankara said the aim of the operation was to find natural gas in the eastern Mediterranean, but Europe also condemned the move as provocative.
A week later, Greece began a three-day military exercise with France, Italy and Cyprus in the region.
In response, Turkey, which had won the support of Donald Trump, announced that it was conducting military exercises with a US destroyer in the region.
Ankara ’ s expansionist policies, which some European experts believe are interventionist and sometimes destructive, also created tension during the Nagorno-Karabakh war.
The war in Nagorno-Karabakh on September 27, the historical conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia over the Nagorno-Karabakh region suddenly erupted like a fire under the ashes and became the top of the world news.
A bloody war broke out between the two sides, leaving hundreds dead and wounded.
In the early days of the conflict, French President Emmanuel Macron accused Erdogan of fueling hostilities in the region by backing Azerbaijan and sending military aid.
The EPA of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan neither denied nor confirmed the allegations, emphasizing only that he would always support his “friend and brother ” country.
The Turkish president postponed his response to a few weeks later and at a more appropriate time.
On October 24, in response to the re-publication of cartoons of the Prophet Muhammad, which coincided with the start of the trial of the accused in the 2015 Charlie Hebdo attack, radical Islamism beheaded a schoolteacher in a suburb of Paris.
The French president ’ s defense of free speech provided an opportunity for President Tayyip Erdoğan to play on the wounded Muslim sentiment and launch attacks on his French counterpart.
This led to further deterioration of relations between Turkey and Europe.
On December 11, the Council of Europe announced that it would sanction Turkey for "illegal and violent actions" in the Mediterranean Sea.
Commenting on the failure of talks with Ankara, European Council President Charles Michel said: “When we see that there is no positive change [in Turkey ’ s behavior], we have to take advantage of the opportunities that we have. ”
The explosion in Beirut image source, Getty Images August 4, about six in the evening, Beirut shook.
A massive explosion leveled the Port of Beirut, killing 204 people and injuring more than 6,500.
The explosion occurred in a warehouse containing 2,750 tons of ammonium nitrate, causing many buildings around the port to be completely destroyed.
The explosion in the port of Beirut has once again brought Lebanon ’ s political-economic crisis to the top of the world news.
As aid troops arrived from France, the Netherlands and Tunisia, French President Emmanuel Macron went to Beirut and, after meeting with Lebanese officials, offered financial aid to Lebanon on condition that "serious political reforms" take place in Lebanon.
Many Lebanese considered the incompetence, incompetence and corruption of the government as among the reasons for the disaster.
Many demanded the resignation of the authorities and the prosecution of those responsible.
Street protests, which had been suspended for some time because of the COVID-19 outbreak, resumed.
The destruction of warehouses at the Port of Beirut due to the explosion on August 5, 2020 November 10, 2018, Prime Minister Hassan Diab resigned.
That same night, Donald Trump announced his readiness to help Lebanon.
Finally, with the support of the United Nations, in the first days after the explosion, around 250 million euros of aid was provided to the injured.
On December 10, a court in Lebanon charged Hassan Diab and three former ministers with “negligence and neglect of duty. ”
The good news, although the outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic and the increase in regional tensions and the continuation of devastating wars paint a not so promising picture from 2020, some hopeful news was also published in this unprecedented year.
The COVID-19 crisis also had unexpected consequences.
For example, when restrictions on movement and mass isolation of people were implemented in industrialized countries, nature took a new life.
Images of wild animals roaming across major cities in Asia, Europe, and the Americas have been circulating in the media and social media, surprising many and simultaneously promising that wildlife conservation is possible, if we give nature a chance.

title: Commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force Threatens Arab Countries: We Do Not Have to Limit the Range of Missiles
text:
Amir Ali Hajizadeh, commander of the IRGC ’ s aerospace force, threatened Arab countries, saying “no one has forced us to limit the range of 2,000 kilometers. ”
In an interview published Saturday in Tasnim news agency, he emphasized that “missile power in Gaza and Lebanon ” has been achieved with Iran ’ s support, and if there is a war between Iran and the United States,“ for us, the US base is no different from its host country, and naturally, the Arab countries in the region suffer the most.
In recent days, with some developments such as the attack on US diplomatic sites in Baghdad, the flight of US bombers in the Persian Gulf, as well as the increased readiness of Iranian naval forces in the Persian Gulf, there has been increasing speculation about the possibility of a military confrontation in the region.
The commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force has emphasized that missile range restrictions are not mandatory, while over the past years, senior officials of the Revolutionary Guards, including former IRGC commander Mohammad Ali Jafari, have emphasized that the range of Iranian-made missiles has been selected at 2,000 kilometers by order of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic.
Jafari said, “There are enough Americans in a 2,000 km radius around our country that they will be responded to in case of an invasion. ”
Iran ’ s missile program is one of the cases in which the United States accuses Tehran of creating instability in the region.
Over the past few weeks, as speculation has surged about the Biden administration ’ s return to the JCPOA, there have been comments about the possibility of negotiations over Iran ’ s missile program.
President-elect Joe Biden has said his administration is interested in discussing the future of Iran ’ s nuclear program and its missile program.
But the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, citing some analysis of the possibility of the Iranian government negotiating the missile program, said the missile program is a “red line ” and“ it would be wrong for anyone to want to negotiate on this ground. ”
He added that “no one is allowed to negotiate missile capability. ”
Hajizadeh also referred to the missile attack on the Ain al-Assad base in Iraq on January 8, saying that if the Americans “had responded, we would have hit all their bases from Jordan to Iraq and the Persian Gulf and all their ships even in the Indian Ocean. ”
He made no mention of the downing of the Ukrainian plane that occurred that night when two IRGC missiles were fired.
176 passengers were killed, and despite repeated requests from the families of the victims, no charges have been made against Amir Ali Hajizadeh, who is the commander of the IRGC Air Force.
The families of the survivors have repeatedly protested and criticized the performance of the commander of the IRGC Space Force over the past year.
In this regard, the writer Hamed Ismailion, who lost his wife and daughter during the downing of the plane, tweeted on May 8, referring to the remarks of Amir Ali Hajizadeh, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, wrote: “Murderers in the name of the national hero appear on television in defense of the Supreme Leader ’ s office and protestors of crime are in prison. ”
On December 16, the father of Maryam Malek, one of the victims of the incident, during a meeting with judicial officials, stressing that the IRGC ’ s aerospace commander has “blood on his hands ”, called him and Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif“ criminal ”.
Mr. Malik also asked the judicial officials present at the meeting why during the past year, Amir Ali Hajizadeh, who is “commander of aerospace and has direct military responsibility, has not been fired. ”
The Ukrainian plane, with the flight number PS752, was shot down on the morning of January 8 by at least two IRGC missiles near Tehran and all 176 people on board died.
The judicial authorities of the Iranian government have not yet reported on the manner in which this case was handled and the trial of the perpetrators, but in several separate cases, they have issued prison sentences for those who objected to the incident and the role and function of the Revolutionary Guards.
