title: Iran Declares 127 Passengers of downed Ukrainian Plane as ‘ Martyrs ’
text:
The head of the martyr foundation says that with the “agreement ” of the families and survivors of 127 Ukrainian passengers, these people were covered by the martyr foundation.
On Sunday, January 4, at his second news conference after taking office, Saeed Ohadi said: “Martyrs of this accident are no different from other martyrs and the services of the martyr foundation are proudly presented to everyone. ”
Stating that some of the 148 passengers on PS752 were citizens of other countries, he said that the families of the victims of the downed plane were contacted and a total of 127 cases were announced as "martyr status".
The remarks of the government official were made while earlier, the Association of Families of the Dead had issued a statement announcing the increasing pressure of the Islamic Republic on the survivors on the eve of the anniversary of the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane.
The statement, published on January 22, said Iranian government officials are trying to bring their desired narrative to the international community and “shed dust on their crimes. ”
The families of the victims stated that the Iranian government has tried over the past year to “usurp ” the Ukrainian plane from the burial site to the funerals and memorials of 176 victims.
The martyr foundation had previously announced its readiness to "fulfill its legal obligations" towards the Iranian victims of the flight, including "burial in the martyrs' section" and "granting the martyr's title" to them.
In recent days, Iran ’ s Vice-Presidency for Legal Affairs announced the payment of $150,000, or the euro equivalent, to the families and survivors of each of the victims.
Such statements by the Islamic Republic authorities have always followed the reaction of the families of the victims of the accident.
Survivors have repeatedly stated that they only want “justice ” and a clarification of the“ truth. ”
The Ukrainian plane, with the flight number PS752, was shot down by at least two IRGC missiles on the morning of January 18, and all 176 people on board died.
The Islamic Republic of Iran has declared the cause of the accident as “human error. ”
However, the governments of Canada and Ukraine have repeatedly said that Iran has not fulfilled its promises of full accountability and is not cooperating to clarify the “truth. ”
Ukraine has also stressed that the Iranian government cannot “unilaterally ” determine the amount of compensation.
According to a spokesman for Ukraine ’ s foreign ministry, the country will continue to work with other countries that lost their citizens in the disaster to bring justice to the case and bring the perpetrators to justice.
Using the report of Fars News Agency and Radio Farda / A.T. / K.R.

title: The council is strongly opposed to building in the capital ’ s parks.
text:
According to the Mehr News Agency, at the 262nd session of the Tehran City Council, the bill to exploit the cultural, social, artistic and sporting capacities of large-scale gardens was reviewed.
In reviewing the bill, two reports were read by the Commission on Health, Environment and Urban, Cultural and Social Services.
Zahra Nouri, head of the Health and Environment Commission of Tehran City Council, explained the views of the commission and said that gardens and green space are one of the needs of the life of cities, especially metropolises, and can distance citizens from the concerns of urban life and establish their relationship with nature.
He continued: Planning urban green spaces and gardens in the process of planning urban spaces is one of the most important factors in how to use limited resources, and on the other hand, how citizens use these spaces as public arenas, and the evaluation of parks in particular can be effective in determining the type of insight and decision making of managers and designers.
Nouri emphasized that gardens are one of the most important needs of urban life: because these recreational centers are a good place to forget the concerns of urban life and connect with nature.
In addition to being the lungs of busy cities, gardens have become places to refresh the soul and distance one from the buzz of everyday life.
Head of the Health, Environment and Urban Services Commission of Tehran City Council, referring to the comprehensive and detailed plan, said: The comprehensive and detailed plan approach is to assign each space to the type of function that is defined for it.
The procedure that has taken place in the municipality for many years has been that different uses are implemented in the spaces, which is contrary to the detailed and comprehensive plan.
The fact that the religious place becomes a commercial place, cultural place into sports, etc., has created a disorder and disorder in Tehran, which causes confusion and anxiety.
He continued: The performance of the gardens in the form of neighborhood, regional and trans-regional performance is also separated in the detailed plan, and the best thing is to allow the gardens to do their work and the park space to be assigned to the same use.
Therefore, the Health and Environment Commission rejected the mentioned bill and emphasized the need to pay attention to the space of gardens and their bodies.
Noori said: "Our emphasis at the Health and Environment Commission is to avoid any new building in the gardens in order to carry out various activities."
It is recommended that, regardless of any new building in the gardens, the orientation of cultural programs in the parks should be designed in such a way that, while eliminating social anomalies in some trans-regional gardens, appropriate conditions for the presence of families and participation of citizens in a relaxed atmosphere should be provided and cultural issues should be implemented with trust in citizen groups.
Finally, the members of the Tehran City Council voted in favor of the commissions on health, environment and urban services, cultural and social, and rejected the bill.

title: Rouhani ’ s 752 flight anniversary: The incident was caused by lack of management of a group; Zarif: I am still ashamed
text:
On the first anniversary of the downing of Flight 752 by the Revolutionary Guards, the Iranian president called the incident “the fault of one person and the imprudence of a community, ” and his foreign minister once again expressed shame and apology.
Thursday, January 8, coincides with the anniversary of the IRGC shooting down a passenger plane over Tehran, a shooting that killed 176 people and left thousands bereaved.
After three days of denial, the Islamic Republic finally admitted that the IRGC was responsible for the downing of the plane, but blamed it on “human error, ” a justification not accepted by the families of the victims, nor by the Ukrainian and Canadian authorities.
Now, Iranian President Hassan Rouhani says that “the incident was an incredible accident caused by the fault of one individual and the lack of prudence of a community, ” but he does not explain exactly what“ the lack of prudence of a community ” means.
He continued, “Of course, it ’ s all a mistake. ”
In the past year, there has been no news of the trial of six detainees in the case of shooting down a passenger plane, and it is not clear what the Islamic Republic ’ s judiciary has done in this regard.
The actual gunmen for the plane have not yet been identified.
Ukraine's foreign minister confirmed on Tuesday that Iran had submitted a technical report to Ukraine on Dec. 10 before the 12-month deadline for submitting a technical report expired.
However, the official responsible for the crash of Flight 752 in Ukraine on Wednesday, in an interview with Radio Farda, emphasized that his country is now waiting for the introduction and punishment of the real “officials ” responsible for the shooting of the plane and the announcement of“ real reasons ” by the Islamic Republic of Iran.
Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif, like Mr. Rouhani, has not mentioned the reasons for the incident and its actual officials.
In a message posted on his Instagram page, he described the shooting as a "terrible mistake of one or more people" and said, "I was one of the officials who, like other people, only heard media speculation until the last hours before the public announcement."
"As an official, I humbly and with a heart full of sadness have apologized to everyone, and I am still ashamed and sorry."
On Wednesday, on the eve of the anniversary of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps firing a missile at a passenger plane, Hassan Rouhani once again promised that those responsible for the downing of the Ukrainian passenger plane would “certainly ” be tried in court.
Hours later, Yevgeny Yinin, who was in charge of the flight 752 case in Ukraine, told Radio Farda: “Compensation is not Ukraine ’ s only goal.
“Justice is our most important value and priority, and until Iran takes full responsibility, doesn ’ t disclose the details of the incident, and doesn ’ t punish those responsible, neither Ukraine nor its allies will stop. ”
The Association of Families of the Victims of Flight PS752 released a statement on the eve of the anniversary of the downing of the Ukrainian plane, saying that the Iranian government is trying to pressure the families to accept compensation and confiscate the memorial ceremonies of the victims.

title: Hidden and visible damage to Turkish satellite networks
text:
Mehr News Agency, Provincial Group - Taher Kheiri * Media experts believe satellite networks are leading part of the audience 's lives.
Not only do these networks play a role in changing the lifestyle of individuals in society, but their impact has reached such a level that they turn anti-values into values and show anti-values.
Issues such as infidelity, extramarital relations between men and women, changes in clothing, how goods are consumed, and even the type of socialization, each of which can have a devastating effect on the foundation of the family and the relationships between individuals.
Private television networks began to be established in 1989, and several channels were launched nationwide or regionally by the owners of capital or with the support of major banks and institutions.
There are now more than 300 radio and television channels in Turkey with regional coverage, which is increasing in quantity and quality every year.
In recent years, various channels have been created in Turkey in the form of children ’ s channels, sports, news, movies and TV shows, music and entertainment, and these often private channels broadcast 24 hours a day according to the taste of the audience.
The managers and program makers of these networks now know the taste of their audience and know what programs the audience is looking for and plan according to the wishes of the audience, but it should not be overlooked that the goal of the owners of these networks is to earn money and media business activities through the absorption and distribution of advertising.
Turkey ’ s new media empire has been expanding its media umbrella for years.
The existence of satellite antennas on the rooftops further reveals the sad fact that the cultural authorities of the country are sleeping neglected or passing by this cultural ambush easily.
Sociologists and media experts should warn and inform the public about the hidden and visible damage of satellite networks.
In other words, it is necessary for people to increase their media literacy in the face of various satellite programs in order to avoid its damage.
The movies and series that are broadcast through Turkish satellite networks have more themes and content of betrayal, lies, revenge and so on.
The series, which employs attractive faces from actors, luxurious life and luxurious homes, trap the audience, especially teenage and young Iranian girls and boys, so that he can identify and imagine himself like the main characters of the series.
The reality is that watching Turkish series and films does not produce anything other than bad education, deidentification of individuals, breaking the sanctity and weakening family relations among Iranians, but rather by showing scenes of infidelity of couples and free relations between men and women, they light the fire of family disputes and exacerbate social damages.
For years, the Turkish media have entered our homes through satellite receivers.
Through this media and through widespread advertising about the country, billions of dollars are made by attracting Iranian tourists and travelers to their country.
The constant propaganda of the Turkish media empire has caused Iranians to spend their money in Antalya or Istanbul and buy property, unaware that our pristine views of Arasbaran are worth a thousand times more than the beaches of Antalya.
We proudly fill our shop windows with Turkish goods and show that we consume high-quality Turkish clothing, jewelry and furniture.
It seems that Turkey ’ s economic influence in the Middle East and Caucasus region has been supported by the country ’ s media and the expansion of its diverse network activities.
In fact, it can be said that the mission of these media in recent years is to make the country attractive to tourists and investors.
The unprecedented growth of investment in the country and the income of tens of billions of dollars from foreign tourists confirm this.
* Journalist

title: Trump from the Persian Gulf
text:
At a time when the world is shocked by the non-peaceful transfer of political power in the United States and the Trump supporters ’ occupation of Congress, the debate over impeachment and how he ended his term in the White House only two weeks before he ended his term in the White House, there seems to be more serious concerns for Iran.
Two major developments that took place in the last months of the Trump administration with his direct guidance and with the aim of tightening the pressure ring around Iran in the Persian Gulf region were the preparation of reconciliation and the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Zionist regime and some Arab countries, as well as the restoration of consensus and unity among Arab countries through the lifting of the blockade and sanctions on Qatar.
One of the most important developments in the Middle East under Trump was the joint statement of Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United States on August 13, 2020, known as the “Ibrahim Agreement ”.
The UAE and Bahrain, as the first Arab countries in the last quarter century, normalized their relations with the Zionist regime and opened diplomatic relations with the usurper regime on the basis of agreements.
The agreement was signed by Donald Trump during a ceremony at the White House.
Since then, in recent weeks, Trump has pressured the countries surrounding Qatar to sign a reconciliation agreement, and Saudi Arabia, which has lost its great supporter by expelling Trump from the White House and is now worried about the policies of the new US president Joe Biden against him, has moved faster than other allies to re-establish relations with Doha.
Last Tuesday, January 5, the 41st meeting of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was hosted by Saudi Arabia with the presence of officials from six member states in the city of Al-Ola in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia, which does not care much about the issue of its international credibility and national pride, imposed its opinion and humiliated other countries that had cooperated in the sanctions, forced them to forget the thirteen conditions they had set for Qatar in 2017 and to lift all sanctions and restrictions against Qatar without seeing any change in its approach.
Although none of Saudi Arabia ’ s partners dared to oppose the country ’ s irrational approach for fear of being isolated, the immediate abandonment of the peace summit by Egypt ’ s foreign minister, whose country once claimed to be the leader of the Islamic world, shows that the backstage of this political retreat has not been peaceful and uncomplainant.
Regardless of the details of these developments, it is important to note the consequences of the two developments in the Persian Gulf region in the near future for Iran.
There is no doubt in this regard that both agreements made in recent months have been designed in opposition to Iran and to strengthen the Arab Gulf approach to our country.
In particular, Ibrahim ’ s agreement, completely ignoring the common cause of the Islamic world and, of course, Iran ’ s approach to the Persian Gulf security system, has opened Iran ’ s number one enemy to a critical choke point in the region.
Despite the seriousness of these threats, it seems that the Islamic Republic of Iran has several ways to confront them; first of all, it is not only Iran that has problems with the peace agreement between the Arab countries and Israel; public pressure in the Islamic world, frequent anti-Israel protests in countries that have made peace with this regime, and the fear of countries aligned with the United States such as Kuwait and Saudi Arabia of normalization of relations with Israel show that despite the cold silence of many Islamic leaders in this field. Normalizing relations with Israel is taboo, and this will prevent more countries from joining the process, especially as the main planners and supporters of the program, Donald Trump and his son-in-law Gerald Kushner, have also been removed from the American political scene.
US President-elect Biden, if he wants to act like his democratic predecessor, will focus more on Palestinian and Israeli peace and will not pay much attention to the Zionist regime ’ s excesses.
Therefore, the Islamic Republic of Iran, by adopting media and cultural diplomacy, can attract the support of the public opinion of the Islamic world and the people of the region to cut off their relations with the Zionist regime, and through soft power tools, prevent the continuation of the normalization of relations between the sheikhdoms of the Persian Gulf and other Islamic countries with Israel.
But as for the Al-Ala deal and Qatar ’ s return to the Arab countries, it should be said that this peace, despite its hidden goals, is not something that is in opposition to Iran ’ s regional policies.
In recent years, the Islamic Republic of Iran has always emphasized on regional de-escalation and the formation of a regional peace forum to secure an indigenous and comprehensive peace in the Persian Gulf, and it can now take advantage of the assistance it has provided to Qatar during the three-year sanctions period to achieve this.
In the current situation, Qatar, Kuwait and Oman are the three countries that have more flexibility vis-à-vis the Islamic Republic of Iran and have the potential to bargain for the removal of regional hostilities.
Iran ’ s policy in the coming months should be to consult with these countries to stop normalizing relations with Israel in the Persian Gulf and instead to design an indigenous security system at this strategic crossroads.

title: Zionists dream of normalizing relations with Qatar
text:
In an interview with Israeli news outlet Ynet on Thursday, Cohen said that in the next few months, four other countries would sign a normalization agreement with Israel.
A reconciliation between Qatar and Saudi Arabia increases the likelihood of a normalization of Qatari relations with Israel, and we expect to sign a reconciliation agreement with Saudi Arabia, Oman, Mauritania and Niger.
The crisis of relations between the four Arab countries of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt and Bahrain with Qatar began on June 5, 2017, due to the text of the speech of the emir of Qatar in a military parade in which he called the Islamic Republic of Iran "hegemony" (the superior power) of the region and the two movements "Hezbollah" and "Hamas" Islamic and anti-Zionist forces.
The four Arab states have since severed diplomatic relations with Qatar by placing numerous accusations on Doha, and have besieged the country by land, sea and air.
Doha rejected the accusations made by its Arab neighbors and Egypt, accusing them of trying to encroach on Qatar ’ s sovereignty and control its resources.
The leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and the anti-Doha Front (Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain) agreed to normalize their political relations with Qatar at their twenty-first meeting held in the Saudi city of Al-Ala two weeks ago.
Earlier, the Israeli intelligence minister said that after normalizing relations with Morocco, Sudan, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, similar agreements are expected to be signed with six or seven Arab and Islamic countries in the future.
Despite pressure from Washington and the Arab Complacent Front to join the ranks of the compromisers with the Zionist regime, the Qatari government has always announced that it is committed to the Palestinian cause.
The newspaper Rai al-Youm on December 15 quoted an Arab diplomatic source, referring to the trip of Jared Kushner, the son-in-law and senior adviser of the US president to Doha, saying that during the trip, he explicitly called for Qatar to join the ranks of the compromisers during the remainder of the presidency of Donald Trump.
The diplomatic source, who was not named by Rai al-Youm, said Qatar ’ s response to the request was negative and that the country ’ s officials had also communicated this negative response to Kushner.
The Qatari foreign minister also condemned the move by some Arab compromise governments to normalize relations with the Zionist regime in late November, calling for the formation of a united front to end the Zionist occupation in the Palestinian territories.
Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani added that he believed it would be better to form a united Arab front to prioritize Palestinian interests and end the Israeli occupation.
Speaking at the global security conference via video conference, he said: “The countries that have established relations with the Israeli regime are ultimately the ones who decide what is best for their countries, but it is not expedient for them to separate for a concerted Arab effort to negotiate with the Palestinians and resolve the differences of the past decades between the two sides. ”
He stressed that Arab countries that establish relations with the Zionist regime undermine efforts to establish a Palestinian state.
The reconciliation agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain with the Zionist regime was officially signed on Tuesday evening in the presence of US President Donald Trump, and the two small Arab states of the Persian Gulf have revealed and formalized their secret relationship with the Zionists for several years.
The United Arab Emirates and Bahrain in the past months, through the mediation of the United States and compliance with Washington's request, have established their relations with the Zionist regime by turning their backs on the Palestinian cause.
Following these two countries, Sudan, under the pretext of being removed from the list of US state sponsors of terrorism, joined the ranks of conciliatory countries and established normal relations with Tel Aviv.
The last country that has agreed to normalize its relations with the Zionist regime with Washington ’ s promises is Maghreb, which has faced a wave of opposition inside the country.

title: Suicide rate rises in Japan during second coronavirus epidemic
text:
Suicide rates in Japan fell during the first wave of the coronavirus, but then rose by 16 percent during the second wave of the epidemic.
Scientists at the Tokyo Institute of Health and Longevity found that from February to June last year, when the first wave of the coronavirus epidemic hit Japan, the number of suicides dropped 14 percent from the same period last year, but in the second wave of the epidemic, from July to October, the suicide rate rose 16 percent.
The scientists believe that the decline in suicides during the first wave was due to the government ’ s financial assistance, the decline in daily work and online education, which in part led to a reduction in people ’ s mental strain.
The number of suicides dropped dramatically in Japan, especially in March-April: 27% in women and 21% in men.
However, during the second wave of the epidemic, the suicide rate in women increased by 37% (five times more than in men) and the suicide rate in children and adolescents under the age of 20 increased by 49%.

text:

title: Pandemic increases suicide rate in Japan after more than a decade
text:
Suicide rates in Japan have risen after a decade of declining declines with the COVID-19 epidemic.
The number of people who committed suicide in Japan rose again last year for the first time in more than a decade.
Japan ’ s Ministry of Health and Welfare said on Friday that according to preliminary data, around 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7 percent from the previous year.
During this period, more than 4,800 people in the country have died from COVID-19.
Last year was the first year in more than a decade that suicide rates in Japan increased, with women and children taking the largest share.
Japan has the highest suicide rate among the seven developed countries, although South Korea has the highest rate regionally.
In recent years, however, the Japanese government has been trying to provide support to people in need of mental health care.
The incidence of coronavirus in Japan is lower than in some other countries, so there are no strict restrictions.
The drop in suicide cases in the first half of 2020 raised hopes of limiting the impact of the epidemic, but the figures rose in July after the first state of emergency was lifted in May, with suicides often falling in the first phase of crises, such as wars and natural disasters, before rising too quickly, experts predict.
End of message.

title: “Smart Agriculture to Climate ” is a Holistic Approach

Also, due to the COVID-19 outbreak crisis, some measures and policies such as “financing agricultural and food businesses ”,“ supporting vulnerable groups ”, “supporting strengthening the value chain ” and“ market management ” have been prioritized.
However, the crisis management of the COVID-19 outbreak requires international and regional scientific, technical, consulting and financial cooperation.
Considering the consequences of climate change and related risks such as “soil erosion ”,“ desertification ”, “dust and sand runoff ”,“ forest fires and rangelands ”, “floods ”,“ early cold ”, “drought ” and“ increasing infestation of pests especially desert locusts ” that the world has faced in recent years more than in the past, is the priority of policy in food security.
It has been predicted that as the weather warms and changes in the pattern of precipitation, there is a possibility of a decline in global food production.
Given the increase in the world ’ s population, the food supply should increase by 60%.
Increases in climate change, followed by decreases in agricultural land productivity, decreases in income and puts greater pressure on resources to maintain or increase food production, leading to greater greenhouse gas emissions and, ultimately, threatening access to “food. ”
In order to “improve food security, ”“ reduce the risks of climate change and adapt to this phenomenon, ” and “conserve natural and biological resources, ” a transition to an efficient, productive, stable, resilient and sustainable agricultural production system is inevitable.
In this regard, “climate smart agriculture ” is promoted as a holistic approach through the integration of plans and strategies related to climate change and sustainable agriculture, in order to conserve natural resources and improve sustainable human benefits.
The three main pillars of climate-smart agriculture to achieve these goals are: 1.
Increase productivity and income in the agricultural sector 2.
Adaptation and strengthening resilience to climate change 3.
Reducing the share of agriculture in greenhouse gas emissions Iranian farmers have long been aware of the climate changes around them, and smart agriculture to the climate has a historical roots in Iran.
As the weather changed in their area, drymen changed their planting dates to make them less susceptible to adverse environmental impacts.
The creation of aqueducts and the use of pottery or terra irrigation in desert areas are among the concrete examples in this field.
The mentioned items are part of Iran ’ s agricultural heritage and indigenous knowledge and are full of innovations and creativity that can be used alongside the knowledge of the day to manage climate change.
In this regard, the Islamic Republic of Iran has adopted strategies to adapt to climate change, such as changing the growing season, improving crop yields, using new technologies, transferring cultivation from open to closed space, increasing the volume of water stored annually through the implementation of watershed operations, controlling soil erosion, sediment control and also increasing the production of fodder.
However, the management of these problems requires the utilization of international and regional scientific, technical, advisory and administrative capacities and cooperation, and it is hoped that the meeting will take great steps in this regard.
This major annual gathering provides an opportunity for major agricultural policy makers and food producers to interact closely with each other and contribute towards convergence.
I also hope that in the next year, we will meet face-to-face with the collapse of the pandemic dam and create better conditions for a boom in agricultural production.
Finally, with a renewed appreciation for the competent management of the meeting, while wishing good health to all present, I extend my gratitude on behalf of the Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

title: What are the most important space agencies in the world?
text:
Space studies and research and understanding what is happening on the other side of galaxies have always been a topic of interest to humans.
Humanity ’ s insatiable thirst for space exploration is commendable.
For this reason, each country has created its own space agencies and research centers to meet this human need.
There are a lot of these space agencies and research centers, but only a few of them are of high quality, do a lot of research, have advanced technology, and are generally recognized worldwide.
There are many space agencies in the world working in the field of space, but here we will introduce the top space agencies that have surpassed other space agencies in the world due to their advanced technology.
The United Nations Office for Space Affairs (UNOOSA) is a United Nations sub-agency established in 1958.
As a hub of United Nations space affairs, the organization works with the global space community every day to spread the benefits of knowing about space and human actions in this space.
Space agencies are a major part of this community.
According to the UNOSA website, the names of space agencies established around the world are as follows.
1. Algerian Space Agency (ASAL) 2.
Office of the National Space Programme of Angola (GGPEN) 3.
Australian Space Agency 4.
Bahrain National Space Science Agency.
Agencia Bolivariana para Actividades Espaciales (Agencia Bolivariana para Actividades Espaciales).
The Brazilian Space Agency (AEB).
Canadian Space Agency (CSA) 8.
China National Space Agency (CMSA).
China National Space Administration (CNSA).
Danish Agency for Science and Higher Education (DASHE) 11.
French National Centre for Space Studies (CNES) 12.
German Aerospace Center (DLR) 13.
Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO).
National Institute of Aeronautics and Space (LAPAN) 15.
Iranian Space Agency 16.
Italian Space Agency (ASI) 17.
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) 18.
Kenya's Space Agency (KENSA).
The Luxembourg Space Agency (LSA) 20.
Mexican Space Agency (AEM) 21.
Dutch Space Agency 22.
New Zealand Space Agency (NZSA) 23.
Norwegian Space Agency 24.
Pakistan's High Atmospheric and Space Research Commission (SUPARCO).
The Peruvian Space Agency (CONIDA) 26.
Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) 27.
Korea Institute of Astronomy and Space Science (KASI) 28.
Romanian Space Agency (ROSA) 29.
Russian Federal Space Agency (ROSCOSMOS).
Saudi Space Commission (SSC) 31.
South African Space Agency (SANSA) 32.
S. Pania Industrial Technology Development Center (CDTI) 33.
State Space Agency of Ukraine (SSAU) 34.
United Arab Emirates Space Agency 35.
United Kingdom Space Agency (UKSA) 36 National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) 37.
Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization (APSCO) 38.
The European Global Satellite Navigation Systems Agency (GSA) 39.
While most space-related research is carried out by astronomers with ground-based telescopes, physical exploration is carried out by both human spaceflight and unmanned robotic space probes.
The main goal of space exploration is to advance scientific research, unify different countries and ensure the survival of humanity for a long time.
The first spark for space exploration began as a "space race" between the United States and the Soviet Union.
Today, many countries have their own space agencies that operate under certain laws and policies.
More than 70 government space agencies and thousands of private companies are involved in space research activities.
NASA Established Year: 1958 Annual Budget: In 2021, NASA is worth $23.3 billion.
It was founded in October 1958 and has been involved in major space programs ever since.
The Apollo program was the first lunar exploration mission undertaken by NASA.
For six decades, NASA has made peaceful space exploration and learned a lot about Earth, other planets, our solar system, galaxies, and our universe.
NASA is an independent agency that is not part of any executive branch but reports directly to the President of the United States.
Since its founding, most space exploration efforts (in the United States) have been carried out by NASA.
NASA is made up of four mission departments: Aeronautical Research for the Development of Advanced Aviation Technologies.
The Science Department for the Study of the Genesis and Evolution of the Earth, the Solar System, and the Universe.
Space technology for the development of space exploration and space science technologies.
Human exploration and operations to manage manned space programs, including ISS programs, launch missions, space communications, and transportation.
NASA also has several research centers, including the Johnson Space Center, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the Goddard Space Flight Center, and the Langley Research Center.
The agency has successfully launched more than 200 manned flights, and they are currently working on more than 70 missions.
Some of its largest missions include the Apollo, Hubble Space Telescope, the Viking probe, which touched Mars in 1976, the Chandra X-ray Observatory, Cassini – Huygens, which reached Saturn in 2004, and Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, which made many important discoveries about Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, and interstellar space....
On May 30, 2020, after nine years, the United States launched a crewed spacecraft, SpaceX ’ s Dragon capsule, to the International Space Station, and NASA finally sent two of its astronauts to the International Space Station after 2011.
The mission was named Demo-2, Douglas J.
Douglas G. Hurley and Robert L. Hurley.
Robert L. Behnken was sent into space.
The last time American astronauts went into space by American spacecraft was on the last shuttle mission in 2011, and has been flying by the Russian Soyuz spacecraft ever since.
NASA plans to send the first man and woman to the moon in 2024.
The Artemis Program is a space program aimed at sending humans (the first woman) to the south pole of the Moon in 2024.
The project is being run by NASA and American commercial aerospace companies in collaboration with the European Space Agency, Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, the Canadian Space Agency and the Australian Space Agency.
The Parker Solar Probe, humanity ’ s first and largest advance to detect a nearby star, launched to the Sun on August 12, 2018, on August 12, 2018, and has so far achieved tremendous success, along with breaking the record for the fastest man-made object and being close to a star.
Parker Solar Probe is the first probe to approach a star.
The US Space Agency (NASA) has launched its first solar probe into orbit on a US Launch Alliance (ULA) Delta IV rocket to reveal some of the star ’ s best-kept secrets.
China National Space Administration Established Year: 1993 Annual budget: $11 billion (2018) The Chinese National Space Administration is responsible for planning and implementing all national space missions and signing government agreements related to space research.
Unlike other space agencies around the world, the Chinese National Space Administration is not a member of the International Space Station.
China has its own small space station.
It also runs regular launches using a family of consumer launch systems called the Long March.
Since 2003, they have launched many manned space missions, and so far 11 Chinese astronauts have flown into space.
In 2012, the first manned mission, Shenzhou 9, was launched, during which three astronauts went into space and the spacecraft was attached to the prototype Tiangong-1 space station.
In 2014, the agency successfully made the first soft landing on the moon using its first robotic lunar lander and rover, Chang'e 3.
In 2007, China successfully conducted an anti-satellite test on its space vehicles.
China launched its unmanned Chang'e 5 spacecraft to the Moon on November 23, 2020 at 15: 35 Eastern Time (00: 05 AM Tehran time).
China launched the unmanned spacecraft with the goal of returning samples of lunar soil and rocks back to Earth.
It was the first attempt by a country to bring a sample of Earth's natural satellite since the 1970s.
The mission was successful, and the probe returned to Earth after probing the Moon by collecting about two kilograms of samples from December 16, 2020.
European Space Agency Established Year: 1975 Annual budget: €6.68 billion (2020) The European Space Agency is one of the best organizations in launching vehicles into space orbits.
The organization was founded in 1975 by 10 member states.
It currently has 22 member states.
All member states together manage the space program of the organization.
The European Space Agency is one of the largest organizations working with the International Space Station.
Since its inception, it has been actively involved in unmanned exploration missions to the Moon and other planets, telecommunications, the development of launch vehicles, and Earth observation.
The agency has its own launch system called Ariane, which has undergone several generations of transformations over the past four decades.
Satellites and equipment developed by the European Space Agency have visited various planets in the solar system.
Its missions include Mars Express and Cassini (built in collaboration with NASA), which have been orbiting Saturn and its moons since 2004.
The European Space Agency's Rosetta spacecraft took close-up photos of comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko and sent a lander to its surface.
Its Gaia space telescope is also mapping billions of astronomical objects with high precision.
Other important recent projects include the Venus Express, which continuously sends data from its polar orbit around Venus.
Its LISA probe also studies gravitational waves and is developing the James Webb Space Telescope, led by NASA.
The agency already has projects to observe Jupiter, known as Jupiter's icy moons probe (JUICE), and Mercury, known as BepiColombo / Bepi Colombo.
They are also developing the next generation of their Galileo navigation satellite system.
The European Space Agency (ESA), with the help of NASA, built a solar probe called Solar Orbiter and launched it earlier this year.
The spacecraft, developed jointly with NASA, is expected to provide scientists with unprecedented insights into the sun ’ s atmosphere, solar winds and magnetic fields.
Russian Space Agency Established Year: 1992 Annual budget: 176 billion rubles (2020) Russian Federal Space Agency / Roscosmos is a coordinating center for a variety of space activities in Russia.
It carries out various civilian activities, including space and ground monitoring projects, and coordinates military launches with the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation.
Between 1955 and 1965, the Soviet space program achieved many global successes: the first artificial Earth satellite, Sputnik-1, the first man (Yuri Gagarin) and woman (Valentina Tereshkova), the first spaceflight to carry more than one crew into orbit (Voskhod 1), and the first spacecraft to be launched into orbit. The moon is near the moon (Luna 1).
Roscosmos was formed at a different time after the end of the Soviet program.
The agency now provides launch services to other countries and launches various space missions, including its own "GLONASS" navigation satellites, telecommunications and military satellites.
The agency is also putting a small portion of its resources on the International Space Station.
They are also developing a fully robotic lunar base (Luna-Glob), which is slated to launch early this decade (2020).
Indian Space Research Organization Established: 1969 Annual budget: $1.9 billion (2020) Indian Space Research Organization uses space technology for national development while pursuing planetary exploration and space science research.
They have carried out several major operations at the national and international level.
The agency maintains a series of fixed earth multipurpose satellites (INSAT) and remote sensing satellites (IRS) that meet the country ’ s growing demand for telecommunications and Earth observation, respectively.
It also develops special satellite tools to help with weather forecasts, navigation, geographic information systems, telemedicine, and search and rescue operations.
The Indian Space Research Organisation is known for its affordable and reliable launch systems.
India's first lunar probe was launched using a polar satellite launch vehicle in 2008.
The estimated cost for the project was only $54 million.
In 2014, they successfully sent a spacecraft into orbit on the first attempt.
The total cost of the mission was $75 million, making it the most cost-effective Mars mission to date.
This year, the organization set a world record for 104 satellites in one mission using the PSLV-C37 launcher, and the government was impressed by the progress of the organization, increasing the annual budget by 23%.
The agency is making progress with the development of reusable launch vehicles, one-stage and two-stage vehicles, semi-refrigerated engines, and human spaceflight projects.
Japan Aerospace Research Agency / JAXA Established Year: 2003 Annual budget: $1.7 billion (2017) The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency was established in 2003.
Its main job is to investigate technology development, research work and launch satellites into orbit, research on the moon, asteroid data, and much of space research.
They have been actively involved in building satellites for other agencies.
In 2005, they launched the 1R multipurpose transport satellite to monitor the weather.
A year later, they launched a second version of the satellite to help guide air traffic.
Communication technology testing continues to be the centerpiece of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.
The Kibo Space Laboratory is part of the International Space Station, designed and built by Japan Aerospace Research Agency.
The Kibo Space Laboratory is the largest piece of equipment designed for the International Space Station and went into full operation in 2008.
In 2020, the Hayabusa2 spacecraft returned to Earth after six years.
Hayabusa 2 is a sample return mission for asteroid Ryugu 162173 by the Japanese space agency JAXA.
The mission was launched on December 3, 2014, and the spacecraft reached Ryugu 162173 on June 27, 2018.
162173 Ryugu is one of the Apollo asteroids.
The mission was planned to collect more than 100 milligrams of samples.
German Aerospace Center Year of establishment: 1969 Annual budget: €3.816 billion (2017) The German Aerospace Center focuses on space, aviation, transport, energy, security and digitization.
In addition to carrying out its missions, the agency also plans and implements a space program on behalf of the German federal government.
The agency is working on highly efficient technologies, low carbon dioxide emissions and solar thermal power generation and renewable energy sources.
In the field of transport they are maintaining mobility, saving resources, protecting the environment and enhancing transport safety.
Some of their major projects include the Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System, Mars Express and the Radar Shuttle Positioning Mission.
In the coming years, they will work in areas such as propulsion technology, satellite development and space mission concepts.
The Italian Space Agency, although founded in 1988, used the work of many experienced Italian scientists and previous national organizations.
In 1996, they launched their first large satellite mission, BeppoSAX, which was developed to study the world by X-ray.
Since then, the agency has collaborated on several major international space exploration projects, such as Cassini – Huygens, Mars Express, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Venus Express, Juno and XM-Newton.
The Italian space industry is also involved in human spaceflight activities.
Its Shuttle Multi-purpose Logistics Module cargo containers play an important role in the storage and transport of instruments to the International Space Station.
It is currently a partner in the European Space Agency ’ s Ariane 5 heavy launch programme.
The rocket can carry a payload of more than 11,000 kilograms into geostationary orbit.
France National Centre for Space Studies Established: 1961 Annual budget: €2.780 billion (2020) The French Space Agency focuses mainly on five areas: civil applications of space, access to space, science and technology research, sustainable development and security and defence.
The agency is currently working with Germany and other governments to develop a reusable launch vehicle powered by methane.
Their goal is to reduce the development cost and recovery time of reusable missiles.
They are also developing a technique called flight arrangement that involves keeping several satellites and their heavy components in a tightly controlled configuration, close to hundreds of feet in orbit.
Canadian Space Agency Established: 1989 Annual Budget: $421.1 million (2019) The Canadian Space Agency has contributed research, technology and expertise to the world ’ s space efforts, especially when working with NASA and the European Space Agency.
The company has sent a $1.3 billion mobile service system to the International Space Station (ISS), including Dexter, Kendarm2, and several robotic workstations.
The space agency does not have the capability to launch rockets beyond the upper atmosphere.
It mostly relies on other countries such as India, the United States and Russia to launch its satellite into orbit.
However, the launch process will soon change as they plan to build a Canadian-made launcher.
End of message.

title: Climate change is a wake-up call for global agriculture.
text:
According to the website of the Food and Agriculture Security Organization (EOS), “In most parts of the world, climate change has changed the conditions of crop growth and made its future unpredictable. ”
The situation has become more difficult for farmers to plant and grow crops to provide enough food in the face of rising demand.
According to experts, maintaining the world ’ s food supply in the future requires examining the positive and negative aspects of the current global agricultural structure, including the infrastructure and technology for food distribution.
Small farmland, which accounts for about 90 percent of the world ’ s 570 million farmland, is particularly vulnerable to seasonal climate change.
The land that families have used for generations may suddenly become uncultivated.
Phenomena such as the El Niño Southern Oscillation, for example, can cause rainfall or droughts that destroy crops.
For example, in May 2020, the flooding of the Nzoia River in Kenya caused flooding in western Kenya.
Floods along with landslides destroyed homes, schools, roads, bridges and farmland of more than 32 square kilometers.
The report states that such problems are not confined to Africa.
Farmers in Iran, for example, face similar problems in the face of periods of drought and flooding.
According to a university professor and water resources engineer from Kurdistan University, recent severe droughts and heavy floods in the Middle East have destroyed much of the food supply.
Sporadic rainfall cycles not only reduce yields but can also lead to secondary impacts that worsen the food security situation, such as the wildfires that have ravaged the western United States, Australia, Brazil and other regions.
Financial and social inequality make climate-related food security issues more difficult.
Many small farmland farmers are poor and food insecure.
According to a professor at the University of Iran, climate change plays a key role as catalysts in problems that already exist in the field of resources, affecting the quality and quantity of food produced and how it is distributed equally.
Climate change also affects what happens underground.
To maintain agricultural mechanisms while maintaining high quality and stability, soil that can protect plants in the first place is needed.
According to a soil biochemist at the University of California, plants need the physical support of soil and also need nutrients and water to access it in the right forms and at the right time.
According to a 2015 report by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United States, about a third of the world ’ s soil is partly or very degraded, and the situation is getting worse overall.
Unsustainable farming practices harm soil health, and some are caused by climate change.
“For example, warm temperatures are associated with the rapid loss of soil organic matter.
This is a fundamental issue, as organic matter is the major store of food and energy for soil microbes, which play a role in regulating the availability of key nutrients.
According to a professor at the University of Iran, climate change is reshaping the relationships between crops, pests, pathogens and weeds, exacerbating a variety of trends, including a decline in insect pollination, an increase in water scarcity, an increase in ozone concentrations at ground level and a decrease in fisheries.
Climate change, with changing rainfall patterns, seasonal snow melt and saltwater intrusion into coastal aquifers, has created problems with the availability of water resources for agriculture.
Short-term reforms pose long-term problems about the role of humans in reducing soil health and the unpredictability of crops, including issues outside farmers ’ control: speed of modernization, inadequate infrastructure, unstable political relations, and war.
Problems such as poverty, hunger, government corruption and lack of education, and various food insecurity issues around the world.
However, some of the methods used by farmers to reduce doubts about the future of agriculture, which may have short-term gains, will worsen long-term crop growth conditions.
Soak land and land exposed to seasonal floods store more carbon than productive land, which means expanding agricultural activity can release more greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
Many manufacturers believe that increasing the amount of fertilizer is synonymous with good performance.
The use of fertilizer can also cause damage to the environment in the long run.
The addition of nitrogen fertilizers to agricultural areas is one of the most important reasons for the release of nitrous oxide into the atmosphere of nitrous oxide, the third most common greenhouse gas.
Food security in the future is unlikely to lessen the impact of climate change on farmers, given that more countries are lagging behind climate targets.
In some areas of the world where food security is not guaranteed, it is difficult to determine what measures are needed because the research does not cover food security.
Most experts agree that water availability continues to be a problem in expanding existing farmland and creating new farmland.
Climate impact is a major factor in reducing food security, experts say, but other factors, such as maintaining equality and economic stability in order to create sustainable agriculture, could play a role in the future of global food supply.
For example, factors such as what led to a convoy of thousands of people from Central America, and especially Guatemala, arriving in the United States.
Human migration is related to multi-year droughts in these countries between 2015 and 2017.
Political instability and falling incomes also forced them to migrate to find ways to support their families.
Socio-political factors and an understanding of the vulnerability of populations in these countries are more important than climate change.
Socio-economic factors and understanding the local vulnerability of populations in these countries are far more important than thinking of a stressor such as climate change that is driving farmers to migrate to new areas.
Not all countries or regions face the same socioeconomic problems as Guatemala, but this example emphasizes smart agricultural policies with respect to climate issues, taking into account vulnerabilities beyond climate change and socio-economic content.

title: Mohammad Rasoulof appointed as judge of Berlin 2021 festival
text:
The list of judges for the 2021 Berlin Film Festival has been published, and the name of Mohammad Rasoulof, an Iranian filmmaker who won the Golden Bear Prize, is also among the judges.
Following the coronavirus outbreak, the Berlin Festival will be held on two occasions this year.
The first part, which includes the European film market, will be held online from 11 to 15 March (1 to 5 March), and the second part, which includes screenings in cinemas, will be held from 9 to 20 June.
The Berlin 2021 Summer Film Festival will be smaller than the Winter Film Festival, and in May, only a few of the selected films will be shown at the Berlin Film Festival 2021.
Berlin Film Festival 2021 will be held virtually, and the organizers of the Berlin Film Festival have selected all of this year ’ s judges from among the directors who have won the Golden Bear Award in recent years.
Mohammad Rasoulof is the director of “The Devil Does Not Exist ”, Nedav Lapid is the director of“ Synonyms ”, Adina Pintielli is the director of “Don ’ t Touch Me ”, Ildiko Anidi is the director of“ In Body and Soul ”, Janfranco Rosi is the director of “Fire at Sea ” and Yasmila Zhabanich, the director of“ Gerbavita ” are the judges of the 2021 Berlin Film Festival.
The judging team has no boss, and the films in the main competition section will soon be shown to the judges in one of Berlin ’ s cinema halls.
Carlo Chatrian, director of the Berlinale International Film Festival, said in a recent interview with the jury at the 71st edition of the Berlinale: “I am delighted and honored that six acclaimed filmmakers have accepted our invitation to participate in this unique way of holding the festival.
Not only have they taken different paths to make films that are uncompromising and tell bold stories, but they are also known as part of Berlinale ’ s history. ”
Earlier this year, it was announced that the directors of the Berlin Film Festival will only be awarded the Best Actor award, and there will be no Silver Bear for Best Actress or Best Actor.
Carlo Chettrian and Mariette Risenbick described the move as a move towards gender equality and said in a statement: “We believe that the lack of separation of awards in the Best Actor category is a sign of rising gender awareness in the film industry. ”
Source: Variety The post Mohammad Rasoulof was selected as the judge of the 2021 Berlin Festival appeared first on Digikala Mag.

title: The brilliant report of Kish Free Zone in the health tourism boom
text:
According to the Public Relations and International Affairs of Kish Free Zone Organization, the development of health tourism, the targeted approach of Kish Specialized and Sub-specialized Hospital, according to the policies of the officials of this free zone, has been seriously pursued in recent years.
Before the outbreak of the coronavirus, the opening of the Health Tourism Office (I.P.D), the expansion of the health sectors and at the same time, the promotion of medical equipment for the admission of international patients began in Kish Hospital, and this specialized and subspecialty hospital welcomed health tourists from Canada, Ireland, Germany and the United Kingdom every month to perform facial beauty procedures, giving birth and receiving health services.
Signing contracts with facilitating companies in the referral of international patients based on the standards of the Ministry of Health, after the launch of the Health Tourism Office, has also been one of the measures taken to further boost health tourism in the island.
Kish Specialized Hospital has been working hard in recent years to introduce its medical capacities, equipment and services at international events and exhibitions, including Oman Health 2018, with the aim of attracting health tourists and other countries ’ awareness of the existing conditions, recognition of new business opportunities and expansion of business networks with the Persian Gulf countries.
The export of medical and tourism services of Kish Island, the development of tourism, especially health tourism as the third economic industry of the country, the inclusion of Kish Island in the list of destination countries with the aim of dispatching patients from Oman, achieving a proper share of the Oman health market due to its geographical and cultural proximity, as well as participation and investment in medical, pharmaceutical and equipment projects of this country are among the goals of Kish Free Zone Organization to participate in such an important scientific and economic event.
Kish Specialized and subspecialty hospital also won the statue of the top brand in the field of health tourism by attending the 4th International Health Congress of Islamic countries. In line with the implementation of the policies of Kish Free Zone Organization in the field of health tourism and quality promotion of this sector, the hospital officials negotiated and negotiated with about 20 Iranian, Iraqi, Azerbaijani and Omani tourism companies and prepared contracts with a number of these companies.
In addition to the specific geographical and climatic location of the region, there are very good opportunities for investment in various areas of Kish, which are promising the growth and development of the region, because parts of the island, including civilization, history and wealth, have been neglected over the years and can be exploited to build wealth and boost the economy.
It is worth mentioning that the capacity of accepting and hosting tourists in Kish Island annually is about 2 million tourists, which according to the policies of Kish Free Zone Organization in order to achieve the goals of tourism and economic prosperity, large projects such as the construction of a new terminal of Kish International Airport are being implemented to increase the capacity of tourists to 6 million annually.
This is possible with the promotion and development of the transport system of foreign tourists and the lifting of flight restrictions with the cooperation of the country ’ s aviation organization, and the arrival of health tourists along with the arrival of domestic travelers and tourists, will make a sustainable activity in this industry and economic field that its positive effects on Kish Island will be tangible in the near future.
Kish Hospital has standard conditions in terms of facilities and equipment and qualified physicians and providing competent services, and in recent years, it has been equipped with the latest model of CT scan (multi-slice 64), the best type of echo machine, as well as the latest model of endoscopy and colonoscopy devices and devices, and upgrading the mammography machine of this complex has been a priority on the agenda.
The favorable status of the presence of permanent specialists in the fields of cardiology, endocrinology, surgery, as well as the continuous presence of the best and most experienced physicians in Kish Island is one of the advantages of Kish Specialized and Sub-specialized Hospital for the admission of domestic and foreign patients.
Launching the traditional medicine center is another part of the Kish hospital ’ s actions, which has been considered by residents and tourists with the approach of taking advantage of the island ’ s climatic and maritime advantages under the supervision of the Department of Traditional Medicine of the Ministry of Health.
Also, a memorandum of understanding for the construction of the first health and wellness town with the aim of further development of the health tourism industry has been signed between Kish Free Zone Organization and Oriental Mis Malaysia Company, so that domestic tourists, ECO member states and the Middle East, due to the special conditions of Kish Island, including no need for visas, cheap medical costs, quality services, experienced medical staff, good urban and accommodation facilities, peace and security of the island.
The island has always been of interest to officials due to its strategic location, so last year senior officials of the Ministry of Health and the Social Security Organization met with Gholamhossein Mozaffari, the managing director of Kish Free Zone Organization, to implement health policies and strengthen cooperation for further development of therapeutic spaces.
It is worth mentioning that performing the first rectal surgery on a 63-year-old patient with cancer, transplantation of an arteriovenous fistula on a 42-year-old man as one of the most difficult surgeries, as well as vascular transplantation of a 23-year-old girl who was seriously injured due to the accident, is among the surgeries that were performed in recent months for the first time at the specialized and subspecialty hospital in Kish Island.
Increasing the number of beds of hospitalized patients from 32 to 64 beds, setting up a respiratory isolation ward, setting up a blood bank independent of the laboratory, manufacturing, equipping and standardizing a helicopter pad, purchasing a 4D ultrasound machine, setting up a virology laboratory and equipping it with a PCR machine, reconstruction, development and physiotherapy clinic, setting up a specialized dental clinic of the hospital with the efforts of the private sector, implementing the administrative building of the project, maintaining the accreditation of the hospital in the past 8 years, The two-layer triage of Kish Hospital for the first time in the country at the time of the onset of COVID-19, the establishment of an infectious clinic and technical orthopedic unit is also one of the important measures of this treatment complex, which has been achieved with the support of Kish Free Zone Organization and officials at different times.
Kish Island, with an area of 92 square kilometers in the heart of the Persian Gulf, hosts more than 1.8 million domestic and foreign tourists annually.

title: The Iranian film “Final Zone ” has entered the competition section of the Berlin Film Festival
text:
The 71st Berlin Film Festival on Wednesday announced the names of the films in the two sections “Panorama ” and“ Encounters ”, and the Iranian film “The End Zone ” is among the works in the Encounters section.
It is a place of worship, of worship, of worship, of worship, of worship, of worship, of worship, of worship.
The film was previously cast in Mohammed Rasoulof ’ s film The Devil Does Not Exist, which won the Golden Bear Award for Best Film at the Berlin Film Festival last year.
Farzad Pak and Amin Mirhosseini are the producers of the film "Final Zone".
The film has an apocalyptic theme and is about a poet who dies a slow death in the midst of trying to emigrate to the United States.
The “end zone ” of joint production between Iran and Germany has been introduced.
The "Encounter" competition section has been added since last year to introduce experimental and different works to the sections of this prestigious festival.

title: The Ukrainian prosecutor of Flight 752 case narrates the problems of dealing with Iran and cooperation with Canada
text:
Ukraine is not willing to blindly accept that Iran ’ s human error caused the downing of the Ukrainian plane in Tehran.
According to the prosecutor in charge of the case in Kiev, the explanations that Iran has given so far have added to the doubts, and Tehran ’ s secrecy proves that the situation is much more complicated than the error of the operator.
In a written interview with Radio Farda, Deputy Attorney General of Ukraine and head of the criminal investigation into the Ukrainian plane, Gyunduz Mamedov emphasized that Kiev is doing everything in its power to come to the truth about this crime, but the problems are numerous: “Unfortunately, Ukraine is left alone in its investigation.
Responding to inquiries we send will take months.
We understand that the coronavirus pandemic makes it difficult to communicate and transfer the necessary documents, but the work must not be stopped.
Sending documents from Canada is also problematic.
The Ukrainian prosecutors are in touch with their Canadian counterparts, but that does not speed up the execution of our requests to Canada.
For this reason, we even requested a Ukrainian delegation to visit Canada.
I hope they respond sooner. ”
What help does Ukraine expect from other countries?
What kind of collaboration can be effective?
We want to form a joint research group, like the one working on the downing of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17.
If not, at least respond early to our inquiries.
Did you propose to set up a joint research group in Canada?
Yes, we did, but they don ’ t have an independent criminal investigation.
Canadian law does not allow investigations into crimes committed outside the country ’ s territory.
That ’ s why our cooperation is done by asking for legal aid, and so far we have sent three requests.
The fourth request, which is also ready to be sent, relates to an audio tape reported by Canadian broadcaster CBC, which may contain information about the deliberate downing of the Ukrainian plane.
We hope that this tape will reach us sooner and we are ready to explore it in parallel with our Canadian counterparts.
In this way, we can speed up the research process in the hope that we will get to the truth sooner.
Iran says it has an "exclusive right" to a criminal investigation into the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane.
What do you think of that?
We have repeatedly shown Iran with evidence that this crime is in our jurisdiction and that we can investigate it.
The Code of Criminal Law of Ukraine gives us this right, and this right is guaranteed in international treaties, including the Montreal Convention of 1971.
We want to be completely transparent about this, which is why we have created a page in English on the official website of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine and the information will be up to date.
We also ask all those who have important information regarding this file to send it to the electronic address (PS752 @ gp.gov.ua).
Our job is to find the truth and we need everyone ’ s help.
Is Iran not cooperating at all?
We have not made much progress in our dealings with Iran.
The cooperation between Ukraine and Iran is now limited to technical research.
Iran has sent the technical report bill and the responsible body in Ukraine is studying it and sending their observations to Iran.
But in the field of criminal investigations, since the last round of negotiations in October, we have not had any answers to our questions.
Their explanations are not clear and they have not answered most of the questions.
They say it ’ s government secrets or military secrets.
We certainly don ’ t accept that.
Within the framework of the Intergovernmental Treaty of Legal Cooperation, we provided guarantees of confidentiality and requested that Iran provide us with a recording of the communications of the missile system operator team that fired at the aircraft.
Iran is not responding.
What secrets should not be revealed?
That they hit the plane deliberately and keep it a secret?
Iran insists on “human error. ”
Do you expect them to prove it?
I want to say that everything we have ever heard of Iran proves that this cannot be a convincing reason, and Iran ’ s refusal to provide objective evidence reinforces suspicions that the downing of the plane was intentional.
Iran does not explain what coordination between military and civilian institutions looked like, and in this concealment, we see again attempts to cover up the truth.
Explanation is extremely important because the Ukrainian plane had a flight license from the Iranian military, but they shot down the plane minutes later.
During his last interview on the first anniversary of the downing of the Ukrainian plane, the Tehran military prosecutor, who was in charge of the criminal investigation, presented the results of the simulation of the crash in Iran and said that the operator saw the aircraft system as a flying object moving toward it outside the flight path.
Ukraine did the same.
Was such a possibility investigated?
The Ukrainian plane did not fly off course.
And this explanation by Iran does not answer other questions.
At least due to the speed and altitude of the aircraft, the system operator had to distinguish between the aircraft and the missile.
Iran said the criminal investigation had ended and the case had been referred to the court.
Do you think that Iran ’ s cooperation with Ukraine in criminal investigations, even though it has been talked about so far, will be completely stopped?
I can imagine that Iran will soon report a court order against people whose names or roles we will not know and who will respond to our inquiries that they have been sentenced to “the heaviest penalty ” – three years in prison.
IRGC commanders have repeatedly said that after firing missiles at the U.S. base in Iraq, they were ready for full-scale conflict.
Is the downing of a Ukrainian plane a war crime?
We have defined the initial title for this crime as manslaughter, intentional destruction of property and violation of aviation regulations, and it is too early to talk about changing the type of classification.
At this stage, we focus on research and evidence gathering to understand the details of what happened that night.
Is it not a crime not to close the skies of Iran when there was a readiness for full-scale conflict?
According to the head of Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization, “coordination was at a high level, ” but there was no request to close the skies.
Are you investigating this?
Yes, it ’ s a research topic, but I can ’ t explain it.
What are the next steps?
Until we get to the truth, we will continue our investigation to ensure justice is served.
