title: The impact of green space on pollution.
text:
Chaharmahal va Bakhtiari, Associate Professor of Environmental Engineering at Shahrekord University, considered green space effective in reducing various pollutants and said: “Green infrastructure absorbs physical and chemical pollutants such as dust and suspended particles of air and chemical pollutants, in addition to reducing solar radiation and reducing vibrations and waves. ”
Ali Jafari, in an interview with ISNA, said that green space is referred to as human lungs or the ecological infrastructure of the urban environment, adding that green space plays a role in the process of CO2 absorption and oxygen release.
He pointed out that green space has an effect on climate modification, adding that it reduces high temperature averages and, on the other hand, increases humidity, prevents excessive dryness of the air and thus makes the environment livable and brings peace and comfort to humans.
The lecturer of the university considered the green space effective in reducing various pollutants and noted: The green infrastructure absorbs physical and chemical pollutants such as dust and suspended particles of air and chemical pollutants and sediment itself, in addition to reducing solar radiation and reducing vibrations and waves.
Jafari continued: Green space plays a role in providing habitat for many animal species, and living creatures in cities live in green spaces including soil, trunk and foliage of trees.
Associate Professor of Environmental Engineering at Shahrekord University said that green spaces are a place to spend the leisure time of the community, noting that these spaces play a role in reducing the psychological stress and work pressure of the community.
Emphasizing that not every green space can have the aforementioned functions, the university lecturer said: "For planning and implementation, a series of quantitative and qualitative indicators should be considered and the amount of green space should be appropriate in a city."
Jafari said that in terms of the quantity of green space per capita, it means how much green space there is per person, the creation of this per capita is subject to a series of climatic conditions, and it may not be possible to create a desired green space in a city due to climatic restrictions, or water and soil conditions are not suitable, and in terms of vegetation, it is not so rich that a series of species can be cultivated.
Associate Professor of Environmental Engineering at Shahrekord University added: Of course, the demand for green space is also important, and the demand of people depends on social, economic and cultural conditions, in addition to creating green space is costly.
According to the conditions of the country, in different cities, a series of standards for the amount of green space is proposed, the reference of this standard is the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development, for different cities of the country, seven to 12 meters of green space should exist.
In desert cities, this standard may not be able to be provided, but in northern cities, there may be more than normal green space.
He described the first criterion of the quality of green space as the distribution of that space in the city and stated: The distribution of green space is subject to various conditions such as the principles of ecology, the direction of air flow and the location of industries that this space greatly absorbs physical and chemical pollution.
Jafari considered the composition and diversity of plant species another criterion in the quality of green space and stated: Usually, the tree and shrub have a good climatic function, because a tree equivalent to one hectare has an ecological function, but the initial costs are more expensive to plant, it is better to build a green space from the tree and shrub, and if the cost is worth it, of course planting trees and shrubs should be appropriate for that city. The ornament went to the flower, the waterfront, and...
Associate Professor of Environmental Engineering at Shahrekord University said that the diversity of plant species should be considered in order to cultivate green space, noting that the diversity of plant species in Shahrekord is not high, and some species such as elm, pine, cedar, ash are seen in the city.
He pointed out that some other types of species, such as acorns, can be planted in the city and due to climate limitations in the city, pine trees and cypress are resilient in the harsh weather conditions of the city.
End of message.

title: Climate change has taken over the hands of farmers.
text:
ISNA / Golestan The trend of climate change this year, with the reduction of rainfall and early heat in the winter season, showed in Golestan, which caused a significant part of the province ’ s farmers to face problems.
A 63% decrease in rainfall and a 3.2 ° C increase in February temperatures in Golestan province clearly indicates that changes in the weather are taking place in this province.
Maybe these days step next to the trees to blossom plums and peaches feel refreshing and life again, and a sweet memory by photographing next to it, but at the beginning of March and blossoms?
Have you ever wondered why the blossoms that promise spring have come out of the branches of trees at this time?
These beautiful blossoms, which were kind of our uninvited guest, will not be our guest for a few days more; the weather forecast predicts that from tomorrow, a cold system will enter Golestan and the temperature will be below zero, and this will cause the blossoms to disappear, and in fact, the income of a year of gardeners will reach nothing.
The crops of Golestani are also not without climate change this year, and according to the agricultural authorities of the province, a significant part of the wheat, barley and rapeseed fields have not been green due to lack of proper rainfall.
Today ’ s climate change has become the main challenge of the agricultural sector in Golestan, whose neglect will ultimately affect the country ’ s food security.
Experts believe that this year, the trend of climate change in Golestan is different from previous years and its intensity has increased, and serious measures must be taken to adapt and reduce its effects.
Maryam Ghajar, expert in horticulture of Golestan agricultural Jihad, said in an interview with ISNA: This year, due to the untimely heat of the past month in the Golestan province, the seed and nuclear species in the region have been planted a month earlier than expected.
He pointed out that we expected this process to begin as in the years before April, noting that since about two weeks ago, we have been gradually swelling the buds in the seed and core trees in different parts of the province with different severity.
The gardening expert noted that in the past few years, we did not have this heat in the winter season in Golestan province, but now, physiologically, the tree is believed to be approaching the spring season and has resumed its developmental activities.
He said that early flowering will affect the physiological and fertility process of trees to some extent, but the extent of this effect depends on whether or not the late spring cold occurs.
According to the weather forecast, in February, we will have a late spring cold in Golestan, and for this reason, crystallized buds that are ready to form fruit will be affected and lead to a decrease in the economic fertility of the final product.
With emphasis on the regular management of fruit orchards, Qajar said: Potassium and phosphorus fertilizers can prevent the dangers of tree stress.
We recommend this food to the gardeners in the last month of winter.
Of course, the measures should be taken at a certain time period, and for example, if the late spring cold occurs in the first week of April, the process cannot be prevented in a few days before that, and if frostbite occurs, no garden management operations can prevent the damage.
Pointing out that the process of reaching the hazelnut phase is approximately 45 to 50 days, he said: "When the tree has passed various crises, including frostbite and wind, and reached the hazelnut stage, the fruit set spraying (nitrogen, zinc and on) is used to stabilize the fruit on the tree.
The horticulturist pointed out that nuclear trees are usually more affected by stresses than seeds, stating: In Golestan, the cultivation surface of nuclear species such as peaches, nectarines and plums is more granular species.
A total of 11,200 hectares of Golestan province lands are under cultivation of nuclear and granular species, most of which are located in the cities of Bandar Gaz, Kordkoy and Gorgan.
Last year, 140,000 tons of crops were produced in these gardens, which this year, due to weather forecasts predicting snow and frost, is expected to reduce production.
The effects of climate change have not only damaged the gardens of Golestan and the agricultural sector of the province has also suffered a lot from the reduction of rainfall, so that the deputy of plant production improvement of Golestan agricultural Jihad has said that the reduction of rainfall has caused the province's crops to grow for a month to 45 days.
Mohammad Reza Abbasi in an interview with ISNA said: "The greatest impact of drought has occurred in the northern region of the province, whose lands are more salty, and unfortunately 32,000 hectares of barley farms have not been green in these areas."
In the wheat crop, 30 to 40 thousand hectares of land have been damaged 100 percent.
He pointed out that there was a decrease in rainfall in all parts of the province, saying that rainfall in some cities has reached 68 percent.
In the western cities of the province, including Bandar Gaz, which had good rainfall every year, we also faced a significant reduction in rainfall.
Abbasi pointed out that this year in the southern regions of the province, which have better soil quality, we also had significant damage in wheat, barley and rapeseed crops.
With the cooperation of various experts, we are looking for arrangements to minimize the damage.
Deputy of improving plant production of Golestan Agriculture Jihad further stated: Based on the weather forecast from tomorrow to Saturday next week, we will have sub-zero temperatures in Golestan, which will seriously damage the gardens of the province, which entered the bloom one month to 45 days earlier this year.
Abbasi pointed out that in this remaining opportunity, to reduce the damage of frostbite, it can be used to irrigate in the form of rain or sinks and create smoke by burning the plant remains.
Other technical guidelines are being developed and will be announced to farmers soon.
He said: Due to climate change in the province, those who intend to create new gardens are advised to use cold-resistant and late flower cultivars for tree cultivation.
Some of these species are identified and are being reproduced for distribution among gardeners.
Deputy of improving plant production of Golestan Agriculture Jihad pointed to the impact of cold on crops and added: rapeseed plant is in the flowering stage and below zero degrees, the flowers will be destroyed, but this plant has a property that can be re-flowered and practically restored itself.
He added that about 15% of the barley and wheat fields of the province are in the germination phase and two leaves, which at this stage there is the possibility of cold damage to the plant.
Of course, in fields where wheat and barley are in the pawing phase, there will be no problem, and the plant can be revived using some fertilizers.
Abbasi pointed out that farmers can reduce frost damage to rapeseed, wheat and barley if irrigation systems are available, at the peak of the cold to irrigate the farm.
Deputy of Plant Production Improvement of Golestan Agriculture Jihad further emphasized that we are seeing the effects of climate change clearly this year, adding that measures should be taken including completion of irrigation systems and use of well water in autumn cultivation to reduce the impact of climate change.
Abbasi pointed out that the measures intended to reduce the effects of climate change need the participation of people, saying: Research on the anti-cold system in gardens is carried out and its equipment is made by domestic knowledge-based companies and gardeners need to invest in this sector.
In one of the gardens of Gorgan, this system has also been used and has been very effective.
Nature ’ s temperament has been out of order in recent years due to human activities, and it is imperative that we adapt to these newly created conditions.
End of message.

title: Japan sets up ‘ Ministry of Struggle against Loneliness ’
text:
Japan added a "loneliness ministry" to the cabinet due to the devastating consequences of the coronavirus epidemic and its impact on the country's rising suicide rate.
Research has previously shown that the country has a high level of social isolation, possibly due to the country ’ s culture of spending long hours at work.
The problem has been exacerbated by the coronavirus epidemic, especially among people living alone.
The Japan Times reported that Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga, in response to calls for action by the government to tackle social isolation and prevent rising suicide rates, had appointed Tetsuhi Sakamoto as the head of a specialized ministry for the issue.
Statistics show an increase in suicides in Japan in 2020.
According to the National Police Department of Japan, a total of 20,919 people died by suicide in Japan in 2020.
That ’ s an increase of 750 cases compared to 2019.
This is the first time in 11 years that suicide rates have increased.
This increase is largely linked to an increase in suicide among women and young people.
However, Suga stressed that isolation has different types that should all be considered.
It has also been noted that elderly people living in nursing homes have become more isolated due to the coronavirus.
The Japanese government has also set up a special task force to coordinate the work of various ministries to combat loneliness.
Japan almost always ranks poorly in studies of social isolation.
In 2015, a global study conducted by the country ’ s Cabinet Office found that 16.1 percent of Japanese over the age of 60 had no one to turn to for help, the highest figure in the world.
After Japan, the United States (13%) and Sweden (10.8%) are in second and third place.
According to the Independent newspaper, it seems that these days other countries are also struggling with this problem due to the Coronavirus crisis, and the restriction of work to remote work and quarantines has greatly increased the pressure of loneliness.
End of message.

title: The Cabinet of Japan is a lonely minister.
text:
Japan has appointed its first loneliness minister to tackle the country ’ s record increase in suicide rates in the past 11 years.
Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga added another minister to his cabinet earlier this month, whose job is to address the issue of loneliness.
He was inspired by Britain, which in 2018 was the first country to do the same.
Japanese Prime Minister Tetsuchi Sakamoto is the country ’ s first minister to tackle loneliness.
Sakamoto is also the minister of managing the birth rate cuts and strengthening Japan ’ s regional economies.
Speaking at his first press conference, Sakamoto said the Japanese prime minister had put him in charge of national affairs, including increasing the suicide rate of women in the coronavirus pandemic.
“Suga instructed me, in coordination with the relevant ministry, to investigate the matter and provide a comprehensive strategy. ”
He added: “I hope to carry out activities to prevent loneliness and social isolation and to protect the connection between people. ”

title: Previous PostPrevious Coronavirus suicide in Japan
text:
The coronavirus outbreak in Japan last year caused suicide rates in Japan to rise for the first time in 10 years.
According to the Japanese Ministry of Health, 20,919 Japanese committed suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7 percent from the previous year, while 7,700 people died during that time.
Japan ’ s suicide rate fell below 20,000 for the first time in 40 years.
The rise in the number of self-inflicted deaths last year, especially among Japanese women and children, has been a source of concern for Japanese authorities.
Japan has for years had the highest suicide rate among the G7 industrialized countries, including France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, the United States and Canada.
Of course, it is located at the regional level of the country, after South Korea, which has higher statistics.
Japan's suicide rate in 2017, 14.
Nine cases per 100,000 population, while the German rate was 9.5 and the US was 14.5.
It reached 16.6 in Japan in 2020.
The country ’ s high statistics are usually attributed to excessive work commitment and long hours.
On the other hand, it is not acceptable to talk about mental health problems and counseling in Japanese culture.
Suicide rates for women and children are generally higher among men in Japan, but the number of self-inflicted deaths among women has risen significantly in 2020.
This year, 6976 women committed suicide, 885 more than in 2019.
Suicides among women in their 20s have increased by 17 percent, and among women 19 and under, by 14 percent.
Katsuyoshi Shingyucci, director of the Tokyo Center for Mental Illness Counseling, said 70 to 80 percent of those who call the center are women between the ages of 20 and 30.
The suicide rate among men in 2020 is slightly lower than it was the year before, but the suicide rate among women has increased by 14%.
In Japan, women tend to have more family responsibilities, and the coronavirus has hurt industries where women are more likely to work, such as hospitals and hotels.
Japan ’ s NHK news network released a study two months ago that found that 26 percent of female employees have faced job problems such as layoffs since spring, compared with 19 percent of men.
The rise in suicide among children is another warning bell ringing in Japan.
More than 300 primary and secondary school children died within eight months from March to November 2020, a 30 percent increase from the same time in the previous year.
The reason for this is frustration about the future and reduced social interaction with peers following the coronavirus epidemic.
Coronavirus, the number one suspect, has infected more than 417,000 people in Japan and more than 7,000 people have lost their lives.
The incidence of coronavirus in Japan in the past year was lower than in many countries, and as a result, fewer restrictions were imposed.
Suicide rates continued to drop in the first half of 2020, but increased in the second half of the year, starting in the summer, shortly after the first restrictions and business closures in Japan.
Experts believe that this is the pattern seen in all crises; in the first stage of each crisis, the suicide rate decreases, but continues to rise.
Since Coronavirus has been cited as the main culprit in the country ’ s rising suicide rate, this trend is expected to continue this year.
Psychologists around the world have warned that as a result of the epidemic and economic and family problems, there is a possibility of a rise in the number of self-inflicted deaths; another reason for the rise in suicides in Japan is the feeling of guilt associated with the transmission of coronavirus.
About a month ago, a 30-year-old woman in Tokyo committed suicide after she and her daughter tested positive.
He had told his wife before that he felt guilty that he might have transmitted the virus to his son, as well as possibly to his classmates at school.
The effects of economic hardship are also cited as another reason for the rise in suicides among Japanese.
The last time Japan saw an increase in suicide was in 2009, following a global recession.
That year, when Japan was experiencing its worst recession since World War II, that number rose to 33,000.
Japan's suicide rate peaked in 2003 with 34,000 cases.
But government actions, including easing the pressure and the possibility of online consultations, helped control the numbers in the years that followed.
The seminar included helping people who had survived suicide and supporting those with mental health problems.

title: Increase in female suicides in Japan
text:
Japan reports suicide faster and more accurately than any other country in the world, and the country ’ s suicide figures are compiled at the end of each month, unlike most other parts of the world, but during the coronavirus epidemic, suicide in Japan has been a very worrying statistic.
Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years in 2020, but even more remarkable is that despite a slight decrease in male suicides, the rate of female suicides has increased by about 15%.
The suicide rate of women in the country in October 2020 experienced an increase of more than 70% compared to the same month of the previous year.
The report, published on the BBC's website, interviewed a Japanese woman who has repeatedly attempted suicide, detailing the following from the interviewer: "It is not a pleasant experience to meet a young woman face to face with a young woman who has committed suicide many times.
This has given me a lot of respect for those who work in suicide prevention.
I'm sitting in a clinic in the Red Light neighborhood of Yokohama.
The clinic is run by Bond Project, a charity active in suicide prevention.
On the other side of the table, a 19-year-old woman with short, bangs is sitting motionless.
Slowly and without emotion, he begins to tell the story of his life.
He says it started when he was 15.
Having been regularly harassed by his older brother since then, he eventually ran away from home.
But it was not the end of his suffering and loneliness.
He had no choice but to commit suicide.
He said: “I ’ ve been in the hospital so many times since last year.
I tried to commit suicide several times but failed.
So I think I ’ ve stopped trying to end my life.
But Bond Projekt ’ s contributions played an important role in preventing his suicide.
They found a safe place for her to live and gave her intensive counseling sessions.
Joan Tachibana, founder of the charity Bond Project, said: “When girls are in serious trouble and suffering, they don ’ t know what to do.
We are here to listen to them and tell them that we are on their side.
Tachibana says COVID-19 disease appears to have brought vulnerable people closer to the edge of the cliff.
He talks about the heartbreaking phone calls his firm has received in recent months.
Like, “I want to die and I have nowhere to go ” is a phrase we hear a lot.
They say, “It ’ s so painful, I feel so lonely that I want to disappear. ”
But the coronavirus epidemic has made things much harder for those who are physically and sexually abused.
A ‘ very unusual ’ pattern in Japan ’ s previous crises, including the 2008 banking crisis and the stock market crash and housing bubble of the early 1990s, was largely traumatized by middle-aged men.
During this period, suicide rates among men increased dramatically.
But COVID-19 is different and mostly affects young people, especially young women.
There are also complex reasons for this.
Japan had the highest suicide rate of any developed country in the past, but over the past few decades it has managed to reduce the number by about a third.
Michiko Ueda, a university professor and one of the leading experts on suicide, said: “The reversal in suicide rates over the past few months has been so shocking.
She said: “The current pattern of suicide among women is very unusual.
As a researcher in this field, throughout my career, I have never seen such an increase.
The point is that the coronavirus epidemic has hit industries where most of the employees are women, including tourism, the food industry and shops.
Japan has seen a rise in the number of single women who prefer to live alone rather than marriages where traditional stereotypes still exist.
Professor Ueda says that women are also more likely to work in jobs that are less secure.
She said: “A lot of women are single now.
They have to live their own lives where they don ’ t have a stable job.
It ’ s obvious that when something happens, these people get hurt.
Over the past eight months, the unemployment rate among temporary workers has been very high.
One month of the year gets more attention than the rest.
Over the past year, 879 women have committed suicide.
This means that women ’ s suicide rates increased by more than 70% this month compared to the same period in 2019.
On September 27, the body of a famous Japanese actress was found at her home, and she was later reported to have committed suicide.
Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist, is now the director of a non-profit organization called NPO, which works on suicide in Japan.
He said: “From the day the news of a celebrity ’ s suicide is published, the suicide rate goes up, and the trend continues for 10 days.
Within 10 days of the actress ’ s suicide on September 27, 207 other women had ended their lives.
But according to the data, the suicide rate among women around the same age is even more alarming.
Shimizu says women in their 40s are more affected than other age groups.
The suicide rate in this age group is more than twice that of other groups.
Other experts agree that there is a direct link between celebrity suicides and the rapid rise in suicide rates in the days that follow.
The phenomenon isn ’ t unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it ’ s so hard to report suicide.
Immediately after a famous person ’ s suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.
Mai Soganuma, a researcher at NPO, lost her father to suicide when she was a teenager.
He is now helping the families of people who have committed suicide.
The COVID-19 epidemic has made the lives of the families of suicide victims even more difficult because they, like the relatives of the deceased, do not have the opportunity to mourn their loved ones.
“When I talk to family members of suicide victims, the feeling of not being able to save a loved one ’ s life is so powerful that it often makes them feel guilty.
I blamed myself for not being able to save my father ’ s life.
He added: “Now they are told to stay at home.
I ’ m worried that the guilt will get stronger.
Japanese people don ’ t talk about death.
Talking about suicide is not common in our culture.
Following the outbreak of the third coronavirus in Japan in early January and the second declaration of a state of emergency, more and more restaurants, hotels and cafes are closing and more people are losing their jobs.
But there is one more question that haunts the mind of Dr. Oda.
When such things are happening in Japan, which has not imposed severe quarantine and has relatively low corona fatalities, what about the rest of the world, where the epidemic is worse?
End of message.

title: Berlin Festival: The beginning of the strangest period in 71 years
text:
Last year, in February, the Berlin Festival was held under the shadow of Corona.
China, Iran and Italy were the epicenter of the virus, but it had not yet disrupted the global mechanism, and the Berlin Festival could be held as usual.
This year, the Berlin Film Festival, like Venice, seemed to be able to be held on a regular basis, but the efforts of the organizers were met with opposition from the government, and they finally agreed to an unusual festival: a five-day online screening of films for the cinema and press in March, which began on Monday, and later screenings in Berlin ’ s cinema halls for the public in June. With the Coronavirus, it ’ s not that easy.
As a result, Berlin is now experiencing its most bizarre and diverse festival in 71 years, with cinema critics watching films on their television screens rather than on the long screen of the exciting Berlinale Hall.
But on the one hand, it seems that the Croatian mood has also affected the quality of the works and the presence of prominent filmmakers, so much so that Berlin is empty of big names this year.
The festival had at least three or four big names in the competition section each year, but this year there are no big names, and the most admired names this year are relatively younger filmmakers, such as Celine Siyama, who starred in the 2019 Cannes film Portrait of a Woman on Fire, and one of the filmmakers of the size of Bella Tar or Aki Kurismäki, who frequently participated in the competition section of the Berlin Film Festival. 'Nothing's going on.
Perhaps the fact that producers and distributors still keep their films for better days, as well as the current unstable conditions and closure of cinemas in most countries, has led many big names to wait for better conditions for their films to be shown at festivals, while some producers are fundamentally opposed to any kind of online screening and are not willing to submit their films to an online festival.
The films of the first two days of the competition section were often disappointing and did not promise a fruitful festival.
The most spectacular film so far was Maria Schrader ’ s “I Am Your Man, ” a German film that tells a simple yet engaging story: a middle-aged woman starts a short marriage with her to test a robot based on her interests and expectations of her ideal man.
The film creates a fascinating atmosphere and, without wasting time, looks at the world of tools from the very beginning sequence, in which love has become an incredibly complex category, and it seems that artificial intelligence will someday take action to solve this human problem.
The attractive humor of the film (including the reference of a woman to a robot man who is not so perfect and makes mistakes like a human being) is one of the strengths of a film that seeks to explore the complex demands of a woman in today ’ s world and with her feminine mood, in the absence of more spectacular films, have a chance to win an award.
This year six judges will judge the films in the competition category, four of whom have made it to Berlin and will apparently see the films on screen in private screenings, but Mohammed Rasoulof, the filmmaker who last year won the Golden Bear for the film Devil Does Not Exist and is in attendance this year as one of the judges in the main section, has a virtual presence.
He is one of two judges who has not been able to go to Berlin, and the reason for this absence, more than Coronavirus related, seems to be the issue of his travel ban from Iran, which prevented him from receiving his award in Berlin last year.
“The White Bull ” by Behtash Sanaei and Maryam Moghaddam is the only representative of Iran in the competition section of the festival that will compete with fourteen other films for the Golden Bear, while 20 (or more) films were screened in the competition section each year.
The film, screened at the Iranian Fajr Festival in 2019, is screened in Berlin with major changes.
In the "Encounter" section of the first work by Bardia Yadegari and Ehsan Mirhosseini entitled "The End Zone" will be displayed, which is a different experience in Iranian cinema, and the creators try to create an unusual atmosphere by combining the flow of the mind with the reality of the daily life of a poet-screenwriter (which can be clearly the filmmakers themselves).
Hami Ramezan ’ s “Soon ” in Finland starring Iranian actors in Persian (including Shahab Hosseini as the father of a refugee family) will experience its world premiere at the Berlin Film Festival in the“ Generation ” category.

title: The agricultural sector of the country is thriving with the return of forgotten plants
text:
Dr. Babak Kapoor added Wednesday in a gathering of reporters: By replacing the cultivation of smart plants adapted to climate change and the return of forgotten plants after the Green Revolution to the food basket of the people, prosperity can be restored to many villages that have lost the possibility of agriculture due to drought and drought.
Referring to the importance of food security as one of the important components of national security, he said: "In a situation where climate change and its devastating challenges such as drought, heat and salinity, as well as a sharp increase in population, providing healthy and nutritious food for citizens is becoming more difficult day by day," Green Biotechnology "can help provide technological solutions to secure the country's food.
He noted that the increasing decline in water and soil resources has led to the possibility of cultivation of conventional crops in large areas of the country less and less, which in these circumstances can be helped by replacing the cultivation of drought-tolerant and dehydrated plants to boost agriculture in unfavorable agricultural lands.
He said: Forgotten plants such as millet and sorghum, which are also known as smart plants due to their high nutritional properties and adaptation to climate and environmental changes, are suitable for alternative cultivation.
Head of Molecular Physiology Research Department of Agricultural Biotechnology Institute noted: In this regard, Biotechnology Research Institute has started working on various types of sorghum, grain millet and hybrid and free pollinator fodder by forming a strong research team.
He continued: For this purpose, numerous samples of fine and ordinary grain millet and fox tail have been collected from the southeast of the country and other regions, and we are trying to introduce appropriate varieties to the field of cultivation of these plants in the country.
The captain added: "Very good and unprecedented efforts have also been made in the production of various types of grain pearl millet and hybrid and free pollinator fodder, as well as finger millet - which has not been done so far in the country - and we hope that the first new hybrid and free pollinator varieties of pearl millet will be released and entered the market soon."
He stated: Pearl millet has the highest tolerance to drought and heat among grains, and when wheat, corn and rice are not able to grow and produce properly in harsh environmental conditions, this plant can easily grow in hot and dry conditions and replace corn grain in order to produce fodder or produce grain for animal feed.
Referring to the destruction of the country ’ s pasture reserves due to excessive livestock grazing, the captain said: In this regard, the plan of molecular and racial modification of cold fodder and mass production of modified seeds since the early 1980s is on the agenda of the research institute.
He noted: Our goal is to create hand-planted pastures and improve the production of the country ’ s pastures and provide forage for livestock, which is one of the key factors in ensuring the food security of citizens.
He emphasized that the important point about these plants is that the provision of forage is only 25 percent of the benefits of their cultivation, and 75 percent of its environmental benefits, including the creation of vegetation, the prevention of runoff, flood, soil erosion, and the nutrition of underground water aquifers and the preservation and improvement of biodiversity.
He added that in the areas of Azerbaijan where the cultivation of these weeds has been cultivated, farms have sheltered a variety of birds and insects and have improved the biodiversity of the region.
At the end, he expressed satisfaction that the important issue of food security has been considered as the central slogan of the fourth international conference and the 12th national conference on biotechnology in Iran, expressing hope that due to the increasing attention to this aspect of green biotechnology, more effective practical steps can be taken to solve the problems of the agricultural sector and reduce imports in this field.
The 4th International and 12th National Biotechnology Conference of Iran hosted by the Biotechnology Society of the Islamic Republic of Iran and in cooperation with Yazd University and scientific associations and research institutes in this field will be held from 31 August to 2 September 1400 with the slogan “1400 century: Biotechnology for food security and health ”.
Iran Agricultural Biotechnology Research Institute is based in Karaj.

title: There are 60 parks in the area.
text:
ISNA / East Azarbaijan Mayor of Tabriz announced the construction of 60 neighborhood parks by the end of the fifth term of the city council and said: "In the current urban management period, 40 neighborhood parks have been constructed and 16 other parks are under construction, which we are trying to bring this number to 60 neighborhood parks by the end of the current urban management period."
Iraj Shahin, in a speech before this week ’ s Friday sermon in Tabriz, said: “Since the first working day of the fifth term of the city council, we have had special planning in the area of sustainable urban green space development, especially in the less affluent areas of the city so that citizens can have easy access to green space.
He said: In addition to the construction of neighborhood parks, we have also put cultural, sports and recreational discussions in the form of the construction of playgrounds, recreational facilities, sports equipment, and libraries and reading houses on the agenda.
He stated: In addition to the construction of neighborhood parks, the construction and development of large parks and resorts with recreational, cultural and sports uses, including Baghshomal Park, Abbas Mirza Park, the development of Aoun Ben Ali Complex, 200 hectares of promenade and Arpadareh Sea Park and a large part of the Tabriz Great Park, which we are trying to be part of the big park and the opening of the lake next year. be.

Plant a seedling in the city, and in this regard, we ask the CEO of the Sima, Landscape and Green Space Organization of Tabriz Municipality to prepare spaces in different parts of the city for planting seedlings along with culture.

title: Marketing strategies in health tourism
text:
Marketing is the main factor of success in the health tourism industry, and the leading hospitals in countries with many medical tourists are those with strong marketing strategies and meet the needs of these patients well.
The core of medical tourism is to attract international patients, and as more competition is created, successful countries will be distinguished from other countries with the ability to attract medical tourists.
Today, major medical tourism destinations include countries such as Thailand, India, Mexico, South Korea and Malaysia that offer a combination of affordable and quality health care strategies, along with access to attractive and relaxing landscapes for recovery, and according to the 2016 Medical Tourism Index report, Europe, France, Germany, Switzerland, Italy and Poland are also gradually becoming the preferred destinations for medical tourism.
The strategies for creating a successful brand in the center of the medical tourism market are to meet the needs of the typical international medical tourist, and most of these solutions require effective cooperation between the public and private sectors.
The quality of health care is a driver of medical travel.
Industry activists have adopted several strategies to increase the value and quality of their services to make them stand out from competitors by creating competition in the health tourism market.
Countries and hospitals that provide high-quality healthcare services at affordable and highly competitive prices are taking a larger share of the health tourism market, the researchers said.
For example, as of 2016, the cost of hip replacement surgery in the United States, which is a common orthopedic procedure, is listed at $40,364, while patients in Thailand and India can get the same service and the same quality, at a cost of $17,000 and $7,000, respectively.
Government support could also play a role in motivating health tourism; Turkish Airlines, for example, offers discounts to medical tourists as a way to increase international patients.
Patients want to be confident of the competence of a facility ’ s healthcare professionals.
The availability of advanced technology infrastructure at the destination is of great importance for international medical tourism.
Therefore, a major marketing strategy in the health tourism market is to improve the quality of health care personnel and infrastructure, and Malaysia is a good example of this, which has experienced tremendous growth in the health tourism market over the past decade.
Another strategy used by leading hospitals in the field of health tourism is to display the number and competence of health professionals on web pages, and this factor alone has had a significant impact on the growth of medical travelers, especially travelers from Western countries.
International cooperation can be effective in stimulating and enhancing the health care professionals of world-class partner hospitals.
Medical tourists travel to countries that not only provide quality and affordable healthcare, but also experience comfort.
Hospitals should offer strategies that provide a stress-free experience for patients to receive more international protection.
Hospital International Patient Unit is the easiest way to reach target customers.
Services include providing valuable information to potential medical tourists about the services offered and avoiding communication barriers by using trained personnel who speak multiple languages to ensure easy communication with patients.
Other marketing strategies used by international tourism sectors are direct communication with patients through medical tourism agencies to provide medical transport services and amenities for the destination country.
Success in medical tourism, like any other industry, depends on the knowledge and correct implementation of the main strategies that must be based on the needs of potential consumers, thus creating a suitable medical tourism market requires cooperation between the public and private health sectors.
End of message.

title: Top countries in the field of health tourism / 1 /
text:

In countries around the world, the level of quality and cost of health care varies, and this has increased the popularity of medical tourism (a branch of health tourism) by increasing the number of patients who prefer to treat their disease abroad.

The main reasons why people choose a country other than their motherland as a health tourism destination include the following: 56% of patients want a high quality of treatment.
22% are looking for cheaper costs.

10% seek treatment as soon as possible and without waiting.
Top countries in the field of medical tourism include Thailand, Turkey, India, South Korea, Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Italy and Ukraine.

Turkey, due to its world-class medical equipment and equipment equipped with the latest technologies (leading hospitals in the US), the experience of physicians to gain new knowledge and experience in leading American and European clinics, and the two-to-four-fold reduction in treatment costs, has attracted the attention of patients in the Middle East, North Africa, North America, Europe and Russia.

title: Japan sets up the Ministry of Struggle against Loneliness
text:
The number of people who committed suicide in Japan in 2020 has risen to 20,919, the first increase since the financial crisis in 2009.
The Japanese government has blamed the rise in suicide on economic pressures, such as social disillusionment over the coronavirus outbreak and unemployment.
Remote work and lack of social connections during Japan ’ s fight against the coronavirus have made people more stressed and lonely, and the epidemic ’ s isolation is the main cause of Japan ’ s increase in suicides over the past 11 years.
Recognizing the serious problem, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga set up a cabinet ministry on Friday to address social isolation.
Tetsuhi Sakamoto, who was appointed to the post, will work as coordinator of efforts in several ministries and organizations.
Suga told Sakamoto at a meeting, “Women in particular feel more isolated and facing rising suicide rates, I want you to explore the issue and come up with a comprehensive strategy. ”
Sakamoto told reporters: “I hope to promote activities that prevent loneliness and social isolation and protect relationships between people. ”
Other responsibilities of his ministry include addressing the decline of births in Japan.
The total number of coronavirus cases in Japan has reached about 431 thousand people, about 7,800 people have died from coronavirus in the country.

title: Guterres: Climate change is a serious threat to international peace and security
text:
Antonio Guterres, speaking at a high-level UN Security Council meeting on climate change on Tuesday, said the climate emergency is the defining issue of our time.
The last decade was the hottest decade in human history.
Carbon dioxide levels are at the highest level, and wildfires, hurricanes, floods and droughts are new natural conditions.
These shocks not only damage the environment we depend on but also weaken our political, economic and social systems.
“We need to limit global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees by the end of the century, ” he said, adding:“ Our task is even clearer: we need to protect the people and communities affected by climate disruption. ”
We must step up the preparations to intensify the consequences of the climate crisis for international peace and security.
Guterres said: “Climate disruption is a amplifier and exacerbator of the crisis.
Where climate change is drying up rivers, reducing harvests, destroying critical infrastructure and displacing communities, it also exacerbates the risks of instability and conflict.
Referring to the effects of climate in different societies, he pointed to some countries and said that in Afghanistan, where 40 percent of the workforce is engaged in agriculture, reducing the harvest, leads people to poverty and food insecurity and makes them susceptible to attracting criminal gangs and armed groups.
Across West Africa and the Sahel, more than 50 million people depend on livestock to survive.
The shift in grazing patterns has led to increased violence and conflict between ranchers and farmers.
In Darfur, low rainfall and frequent droughts increase food insecurity and competition for resources.
The consequences are particularly devastating for women and girls who are forced to go farther to get water, putting them at greater risk of sexual and gender-based violence.
He added that vulnerability to climate risks is also linked to income inequality.
High levels of inequality can undermine social cohesion and lead to discrimination, increase tensions and unrest, and increase the risk of conflict.
The UN Secretary General also called climate disruption a cause of displacement around the world, noting that in some small island states in the Pacific, entire communities have been forced to relocate, with dire consequences for their livelihoods, culture and heritage.
Guterres said the forced displacement of more people around the world clearly increases the likelihood of conflict and insecurity.
More needs to be done to address the specific risks that the climate crisis poses to peace and security.
He defined four priority areas and said, “First, we need to focus more on prevention through robust, high-intensity climate action.
We must put the world on track to meet the goals of the Paris Agreement and prevent climate catastrophe.
We need to build a real global coalition to commit to zero carbon emissions by the middle of the century.
"We need to mobilize a decade of transformation through successful COP26 in Glasgow," he said, adding, "It will require all Member States to deliver nationally determined ambitious contributions before November, with targets that will allow us to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 45 percent from 2010 levels by 2030."
Second, we need urgent action to protect countries, communities and people from increasingly frequent and severe climate impacts.
We need a breakthrough in adaptability and flexibility, which means a dramatic increase in the level of investments.
He added that all donors and national and multilateral development banks should be involved.
Developed countries must maintain a commitment to transfer $100 billion annually to the Global South.
They have already lost the 2020 deadline.
He also called for investment in renewable energy and green infrastructure, saying, “In short, we need to close the financial gap by increasing support for countries and communities that are suffering the worst impacts of the climate crisis. ”
Guterres called his third priority to address a concept of security that puts people at the center, explaining that the COVID-19 pandemic represents the devastation that so-called non-traditional security threats can cause on a global scale.
He said prevention and alleviation of poverty, food insecurity and displacement caused by climate disruption will help maintain peace and reduce the risk of conflict.
The Secretary-General highlighted his fourth priority in the program as deepening cooperation across and beyond the UN system, noting that we must leverage the power of various stakeholders, including the Council, the Peace Commission, international financial institutions, regional organizations, civil society, the private sector, academia and other institutions.
Guterres said the Climate Security Mechanism, which brings together the Department of Political Affairs and Peacebuilding, the UN Development Programme and the UN Environment Programme, is the main blueprint for this cooperation within the UN system.
Emphasizing that the climate crisis is the multifaceted challenge of our era, he said, “It is already affecting every area of human activity.
Solving it requires coordination and cooperation on a scale that we have never seen before.
The engagement of all multilateral institutions, including this council, can play an important role in addressing this challenge.
The Secretary-General called on the Security Council to use its influence this important year to ensure the success of COP26 and to mobilize others, including international financial institutions and the private sector, to do their part.

title: New TV Shows Scenes Between Turkey and Saudi Arabia
text:
Turkish TV series, which has been broadcast as the country ’ s soft power in recent years, especially on the television of Arab countries, in addition to laying the groundwork for attracting tourists from these countries, is one of the important tools in advancing the cultural goals of the Ankara government.
Relations between Turkey and Saudi Arabia have deteriorated to the point that even Saudi Arabia ’ s MBC TV group, which broadcasts Turkish series in Saudi Arabia, stopped broadcasting them last year.
In its next step, MBC will be showcasing a series called Kingdoms of Fire from November 17.
The series depicts the end of the Mamlukan country, which was created by the Ottoman Empire from the early 16th century, and in this series, the Ottoman Empire is referred to as a bloodthirsty state.
Although the series has not yet been broadcast, the news of its broadcast in the Turkish media has been evaluated as Saudi Arabia ’ s hostility to Turkey.
The website of the Turkish state broadcaster "TTV".
RT News "In a news with the headline" Saudi Arabia, which has released Turkish TV series, broadcasts a series in which the Ottoman government has been badly introduced ", wrote: The MBC network, which is based in the United Arab Emirates and is founded by a Saudi capitalist, in a series on the overthrow of the Mamluk government, introduces the Ottoman government as an occupying force.
The website of the Turkish state broadcaster "TTV".
RT News "In a news with the headline" Saudi Arabia that has released Turkish TV series, a series in which the Ottoman government is badly presented, "wrote: The MBC network, which is based in the United Arab Emirates and founded by a Saudi capitalist, in a series on the overthrow of the Mamluki government, introduces the Ottoman government as an occupying force.
The series describes the Ottoman Empire as an empire that rules on the basis of human blood.
The base emphasized that MBC ’ s hostility to the Ottoman Empire is not unique to this issue, adding that the series ’ producer Yasser Harb called the occupation of the series in broadcasting scenes from the Ottoman Empire.
MBC was founded in 1991 by Saudi financier Wald bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim in the United Kingdom; the center of the company was later transferred to the United Arab Emirates and the company began broadcasting television programs in Arabic.
The channel is broadcast in many countries in the Middle East and North Africa, and is said to be broadcast in 24 countries with 18 different channels.
Earlier this year, Saudi Arabia changed its textbooks taught in elementary and high schools, and new books refer to the Ottoman state as an occupying power.
In Saudi textbooks, it is said that the Ottoman government oppressed the Arab people.

title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
text:
Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.
In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.
The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?
Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.
Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.
The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.
It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.
The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.
If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.
The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.
Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.
Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.
Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.
They say they show love with respect in this series.
The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.
The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."
Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.
He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.
Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.
Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.
The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.
The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.
Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.
Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.
Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”
The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.
In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.
But the hole has a different atmosphere.
The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.
In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.
Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.
On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.
The series was recently sold to Chile.
The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.
Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”
His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.
We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.
But now it seems to be getting better. ”
Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.
Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.
Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.
Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.
Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”
According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.
At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
text:
ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.
The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.
The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.
The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.
The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.
The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.
Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.
The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.
Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.
However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.
Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.
In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.
For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.
With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.

Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.
When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.
Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.
The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.
Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.
Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.
It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.
The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban.
