title: Is it going to be harder for Britain to get asylum?
text:
Will it be harder to get asylum in Britain?
Journalist Kianoosh Bustani An hour ago image source, Getty Images, a refugee boat in the south of the United Kingdom On Thursday, April 25, British Interior Minister Priti Patel unveiled in the House of Commons a plan that will soon be implemented and the future of asylum in the United Kingdom will undergo a serious and irreversible transformation.
Ms Patel said: “For the first time, asylum claims in the UK will be processed based on the route migrants took to reach the country.
Boris Johnson ’ s interior minister refers to migrants who reach northern France via the Central European or Spanish route and then arrive on small boats off the southern coast of England.
Last year, 8,000 refugees arrived in the UK via smugglers' boats, crossing the dangerous waters of the English Channel or English Channel.
Iranians are at the forefront of these travelers in terms of the number of refugees.
A journey that is not safe and in some cases ends up costing the lives of refugees.
Ms Patel, referring to international gangs of human trafficking, said: "Sufficient tolerance".
The Home Secretary pointed to the determination of the British government to destroy these gangs.
"The British government believes that human trafficking gangs are the same gangs that are involved in the trafficking of arms and drugs."
Ms Patel called them "organised and dangerous gangs" that take advantage of refugees trying to reach the UK.
The UK government considers its new asylum application process “fairer and quicker ”.
The Labour Party, the official government opposition in the British parliament, has called the plan lacking human sentiment and unable to resolve the issue.
Under the new scheme, people who enter the UK via routes deemed illegal by the UK government will not be given the same rights as those who enter the UK via ‘ authorised ’ routes.
The British government says the new plan will create “safe and legal pathways ” to seek asylum in the country.
The Home Office accuses many migrants arriving in the UK of using EU territory to reach the UK ’ s shores.
Interior Minister Preeti Patel made it clear in Parliament on Thursday that “if you ’ re going to enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you can apply for asylum, it ’ s clear that you ’ re not trying to escape danger.
“Contrary to the international community ’ s stated goals for asylum, you have only chosen the UK as your preferred destination. ”
Last year, news that refugees arriving by sea on the UK coast could be transferred to Ascension Island, a remote location in the South Atlantic, drew criticism from British charities and human rights organisations.
The plan, which his critics said was reminiscent of the relocation of refugees to remote Australian islands and "difficult living conditions" for asylum seekers in those areas.
The possibility of such a return to the Home Office has drawn criticism from the Conservative government.
Mike Anderson, executive director of the British Red Cross, said sending refugees to remote locations was “ineffective in solving the refugee problem. ”
Anderson says, “Such a plan ignores the root cause of the refugee influx. ”
He added: “The government ’ s plan will undoubtedly lead to unfortunate human consequences. ”
The source, Getty Images, has also faced criticism from political parties.
Nick Thomas Simond, Labour ’ s shadow cabinet interior minister, called Priti Patel ’ s remarks “absurd ” and a sign of“ the government ’ s lack of control over the refugee situation and lack any compassion. ”
In addition to the official opposition, the Liberal Democratic parliamentary party has joined the ranks of opponents of the new asylum plan.
Elder Carmichael, the party's spokesman for state affairs, called the plan ineffective and inhumane.
Mr Carmichael said: "The government should instead think of a plan for refugees who have been waiting more than six months to process their application."
In the face of all this criticism, the government considers changing the asylum procedure as the only way to avoid risking the lives of people who consider the sea route to be the best way to reach Britain.
With the end of the Brexit transition period in December 2020, the British government lost the right to access the EU ’ s integrated asylum rules, known as the Dublin Regulation.
According to these rules, the state that is obliged to process the asylum application is determined.
These rules allow union governments to ask another member to take responsibility for handling an asylum application or, in some cases, repatriation of an asylum seeker.
The general purpose of these regulations is to ease the burden of some countries and prevent rework at the EU level.
With the end of Britain ’ s membership in the European Union, the Conservative government sought to replace it with a similar deal, which was strongly opposed by the European Union.
The plan was to return all refugees arriving in the UK from a third country to EU countries.
The plan, which Brussels has called “unbalanced and unprofitable ” for the EU, has been rejected.
Is Britain a good destination for refugees?
According to the United Nations Refugee Agency, 79 million people are currently displaced from their homes.
Of these, 26 million are refugees.
Asylum seekers are people who leave their country in the hope of finding a safe environment for themselves and their families.
According to data from the Office of National Statistics, nearly 29,000 people applied for asylum in the UK last year, including more than 5,000 children.
More than 2,000 children arrived in the UK alone and without their parents.
Among them, Iran, with 4,000 refugees, is at the top of the countries seeking asylum.
This makes up 12% of all asylum seekers in the UK.
On average, more than half of Iranian asylum seekers received asylum in the first stage.
In addition to those seeking asylum on UK soil for the first time, nearly 6,000 asylum seekers who arrived in the UK years before Iran are still waiting to be resettled.
According to available information, 21% of the applicants received a negative response from the Home Office.
Iraq, Albania, Eritrea, Sudan and Syria are next in the rankings.
According to previous Home Office regulations, those entering the UK via water can apply for asylum on British soil.
In order to receive the right to asylum, people had to prove that they would be persecuted if they returned to their home country.
Racial, religious, sexual and gender discrimination or suppression of freedom of expression and opinion are the main reasons why asylum seekers seek asylum in the UK.

title: Climate change and 21% reduction in agricultural productivity
text:
In a new study led by Cornell University in the US, experts have found that farms have averaged 21 percent less yields over the past six decades as a result of climate change.
According to the researchers, this equates to a total loss of seven years of agricultural productivity growth.
Global agriculture is increasingly exposed to the effects of climate change, with warmer places such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most, and agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34%.
To quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on what economists call “total factor productivity or a measure of overall agricultural sector productivity, ” experts developed a comprehensive econometric model.
Professor Robert Chambers, from the University of Maryland, said the results show that climate-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity.
In this paper, we used a model to estimate how the total factor productivity patterns would be if climate change were not present.
Professor Ariel Ortiz Boba, principal investigator of the study and assistant professor at Cornell University ’ s School of Applied Economics and Management, said: “We found that climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years, equating to pressing the stop button for productivity growth in 2013, after which no progress has been made, and now human climate change is slowing down.
According to Professor Ortiz Boba, the group considered more than 200 systematic changes from the econometric model, and the results were largely consistent.
When we focus on different regions of the world, we find that the historical impacts of climate change have been greatest in areas that have become warmer, including areas of Africa, Latin America and Asia.
Most people see climate change as a distant problem, but it ’ s one that ’ s already having an impact.
We need to address climate change now so that we can prevent future generations from being harmed.
The study was published in the journal Nature Climate Change.
End of message.

title: How does NASA build a base with breathable air on Mars?
text:
The purpose of writing this article is to understand how we can now prepare for human life on an alien planet, and to do so, Digital Trends spoke to two experts.
Michael Hackett, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and Assad Abu Bakr, a NASA engineer, talk about how to keep astronauts alive on a planet that wants to take their lives.
The window of opportunity to send humans to the Red Planet has to pass some kind of necessary timeframe.
Because of the structure of the orbits of Earth and Mars, the easiest way to get from one planet to another is to use the Hohmann Transport Orbit, in which the spacecraft moves in an elliptical orbit and slowly and steadily pushes out.
Hackett explains, “It ’ s because of the way the planets move.
Earth is in orbit around Mars and is moving faster than Mars, so every once in a while they collide.
A year on Mars equals about two years on Earth. ”
So you have to go with the exact timing to launch astronauts to Mars.
Every Martian year, or every 26 months on Earth, is given a window of opportunity at which Mars is closest to Earth.
"So you have an optimal opportunity every 26 months to send a spacecraft to Mars through this orbit.
“So the plans for Mars are to send the infrastructure first, and then after 26 months, we ’ ll send the crew. ”
Sending infrastructure doesn ’ t just mean ensuring astronauts have access to air to breathe and food to eat.
It also means sending and building power plants, a habitat, rovers, and vehicles that will allow astronauts to leave Mars once the mission is complete.
Why is oxygen so important?
The first major problem to deal with when building a Martian base is the production of oxygen.
When you hear about producing oxygen on Mars, you ’ re probably thinking about the simplest human need: having air to breathe, and certainly not finding a way to produce a breathable atmosphere inside a confined habitat on Mars.
But the habitat will require, at least compared to other components of the project, very small amounts of oxygen.
By other components, we mean things like rocket propellants that lift astronauts off the surface of the planet.
Hackett explains, “We are trying to manufacture the drive prerequisites.
"We're not trying to make fuel, we're trying to get some of the necessary chemical reactions that we never think about on Earth."
On the ground, when you burn gasoline in your car ’ s engine, you use oxygen that weighs several times more than your fuel to cause that reaction.
The same is true of pieces of wood burning in the fireplace.
“But if you go somewhere where there is no free oxygen, you have to take oxygen with you. ”
Modern missiles have several liquid oxygen tanks that provide the final fuel and add a lot of weight to the entire payload.
“We ’ ll need about 30 tons of oxygen to get those astronauts off the surface and into orbit, and if we have to take those 30 tons of oxygen with us to Mars, the whole mission will be delayed for about a decade.
A much easier solution would be to send an empty tank there and fill it with oxygen. ”
Using what is available to produce oxygen on Mars, Hackett and his colleagues are working on a concept called In-situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).
Basically, it means using whatever is already found on Mars to build what we need.
They will have to experiment with a device called MOXIE, which, along with NASA's Endurance rover, successfully landed on Mars in February 2021.
MOXIE is essentially a miniature version of a much larger device that picks up carbon dioxide, which is found abundantly in the Martian atmosphere, and produces oxygen.
This device may seem complicated at first glance, but it ’ s actually similar to a very well-known technology on the planet.
According to Hackett, “MOXIE is very much like a fuel cell.
There is basically no difference between the two.
If you take a fuel cell and you reverse the two wires that have been wired into it, you have an electrification system.
This means that if the device is a fuel cell, you have a fuel and an oxidizer that deliver a stable molecule.
If you have carbon monoxide as fuel and oxygen, carbon dioxide is produced.
You also get electricity. ”
“Now, if you reverse that, you have to let in carbon dioxide and electricity, and what you get is carbon monoxide and oxygen.
That ’ s how we ’ ll solve the problem. ”
This seemingly simple idea is radical in that it addresses a problem that no one outside the aerospace community sees as a challenge: producing oxygen.
Hackett said, “Nobody wants to produce oxygen on Earth.
No one has a reason to do that.
Oxygen is everywhere. ”
How to build an oxygen machine?
Understanding the chemical rules of making an oxygen machine is one thing, and designing and implementing a version of it that fits inside a rover is another.
Abu Bakr, the MOXIE thermal engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and who has been involved in the development of the MOXIE project from the beginning, explains how the experimental device was built and what obstacles the NASA lab team had to overcome.
He said: “The biggest challenge we ’ ve ever had is a little bit of energy.
The rover has a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, which is a nuclear source of electricity, so people think the rover relies on nuclear power, but that's not the case.
The rover is powered by batteries and has an atomic charger next to it. ”
This means that researchers need to be very careful about how much energy is being used to keep the battery from draining.
The entire Mars Endurance operates at only 110 watts, which is just a little more energy than it takes to light a light-bulb bulb.
As a result, a device like MOXIE has to operate with very small amounts of energy.
Simple knowledge but equipment design is only one aspect of trial and error – the other is to see if the idea works at all on Mars.
Even with concepts that work well on Earth, an alien environment can have unforeseen consequences, from the impact of the planet ’ s thin atmosphere on how heat is transferred to the depreciation of equipment in unexpected ways due to weaker gravity and unknown dust.
That ’ s why NASA engineers will soon be collecting MOXIE data to test its performance in Mars ’ true environment.
“In many ways, ” says Abu Bakr,“ MOXIE doesn ’ t really collect scientific data. ”
Compared to scientific equipment such as telescopes and spectrometers used to analyze rock samples, the data collected by MOXIE is relatively simple.
“What we get is almost like telemetry data in engineering.
We measure voltages and currents and temperatures, things like that.
This is our data, and the data is very small.
You can almost fit all of them in a floppy disk. ”
This means the team can get very quick feedback on whether the system is working properly – in just a few days.
Unlike other instruments on the endurance rover, which require weeks, months, or even years to analyze the data, MOXIE is a demonstration of practical performance rather than trial and error.
Abu Bakr said, “What we ’ re doing is not science, it ’ s technology.
We want to know whether the system works, and if we want to increase the scale in the future, what we need to do to make our goal work. ”
If MOXIE is successful, it will show how practical the ISRU principle is on Mars.
Then expanding the scale of the project and building a version of the machine on a real scale that produces oxygen at a much higher rate will be relatively easy; and the good news is that a larger version will appear more efficient and produce significant amounts of oxygen without requiring much energy.
With the oxygen challenge solved, we could move on to other resources humans need to survive on Mars.
Another essential resource that we need to establish in order to produce it on the Red Planet is water.
Water isn ’ t just necessary for humans to drink, but it ’ s also important because of the hydrogen and carbon dioxide compounds that can bring a plethora of efficient chemical compounds.
Hackett said: “The idea in the short term is to automate certain amounts of ISRU to make our mission possible.
“Once we build our base on Mars — a base like the McMurdo Station in Antarctica or the International Space Station — we can move on to more sophisticated ISRU methods like ice extraction. ”
“A lot of people feel like we need to extract ice automatically.
But I say no, it ’ s not worth the effort.
Ice is a mineral, which means you have to look for it underground, dig it out of the ground, and purify it.
It would be easier to take ice with us to Mars.
It's like a moxie, but it's a mechanical tree.
It breathes carbon dioxide and exhales oxygen. ”
Hackett argues that MOXIE is much easier to find resources through mining.
“It doesn ’ t have to go anywhere, it doesn ’ t have to look for anything.
These are methods in IRSU that appear to be really practical in the short term.
“You ’ re doing things as simple as possible, and one day you ’ ll have access to enough people on the surface to do more complex things. ”
Mars has an unexpected bounty of water ice, but it ’ s found at the planet ’ s poles, and most Mars space missions focus on landing at the equator, which is more like a desert.
One of the current concepts for solving the problem is the idea of mapping the location of water ice on Mars, which also locates smaller amounts of ice to be exploited in the future.
Another way is to extract water from the minerals in the Martian soil.
“There are materials like gypsum and Epsom salts that are sulfated and absorb a lot of water, so you can pull them out of the ground and extract the water from them.
You can look for water in the soil, which is a lot of water. ”
But Mars simply doesn't have the same material as what we find on Earth.
Perchlorate is also found in very large quantities on Mars, which is dangerous to human health, and in small amounts on our own planet.
Despite being toxic, it is highly efficient due to its chemical properties and is used in things like rocket accelerators, fireworks and airbags.
"On Mars, most of the chlorine in the soil is actually perchlorate."
According to Hackett, “It makes up 1% of all soil and has incredible amounts of energy.
When you remove oxygen atoms from perchlorates to obtain chlorine, a mass of energy is extracted.
I ’ ve always thought it was a great resource to exploit. ”
Source: The End of the Message

title: ‘ indictment of 10 people ’ over downing of Ukrainian plane
text:
According to the former military prosecutor of Tehran province, 10 officials related to the downing of the Ukrainian plane in January 2019 have been indicted.
Gholamabbas Turki, at the introduction meeting of the new military prosecutor of Tehran, stated: “Ten officials involved in the incident of the Ukrainian plane crash have been indicted, which will be concluded in the court. ”
Ukrainian Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down by two IRGC air defense missiles shortly after taking off from Imam Khomeini International Airport on January 8, 2019, and all 176 passengers died.
The victims were from Canada, Ukraine, Sweden, Afghanistan and the United Kingdom.
Many of the passengers were Iranian citizens living in Canada.
The Islamic Republic officials initially denied the real cause, but after three days of mounting international pressure, they admitted that the plane had been shot down by the IRGC ’ s air defense.
Iran insists "human error" was the cause of the crash, but the families of the victims, the Canadian government and many experts have rejected the claim and called for further investigation.
Iran's Civil Aviation Organization released a final report blaming "air defense system malpractice", but Ukraine and Canada denied the report.
Ukraine's foreign minister, Dmitro Kolba, sharply criticized the report in a Facebook message on March 17, saying it was "a hypocritical attempt to hide the real reasons for the downing of the plane".
"We will not allow Iran to hide the truth, we will not allow it to evade responsibility for this crime."
Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Telegram channel and the Government of Canada called the report “incomplete and devoid of sufficient facts and evidence. ”
Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said: “We will continue, first and foremost, to work to deliver on the promise we have made to our families to find out exactly what has been done and that Iran must accept its responsibility for the loss of so many lives. ”
Trudeau said he would work with other countries to secure the rights of disaster victims and survivors.
The Iranian Civil Aviation Organization has submitted its final report on the cause of the downing of the plane on March 27.
The report identified the incident as the IRGC air defense system operator, who identified the Ukrainian airliner as a “hostile target ” due to a“ geo-orientation error ” and fired two missiles at it.

title: 20% reduction in food production due to climate change – Brilliant
text:
Studies show that climate change has reduced global food production by more than 20 percent in the past 60 years.
Farmers have one-fifth less food than they had in 1961; in warmer regions such as Latin America and Africa, the decline is up to 34 percent.
According to available data, the United States only sees growth of 5 to 15 percent, while the world's population is projected to reach 10 billion by 2050.
Experts believe that temperature in plant growth and development is one of the important factors.
Temperature, along with the surface of light; carbon dioxide, temperature humidity, water and nutrients, affect the growth and ultimately the production of crops.
All of these factors need to be balanced.
While the global population continues to rise, a new study suggests that agricultural productivity has fallen sharply due to the effects of climate change.
Worldwide, farmers have harvested 20 percent fewer crops than they did in the 1960s.
The researchers say the primary factor is changing weather patterns, including increasing floods and droughts in different regions.

title: Iran ’ s response to Ukraine ’ s chance to go to court: ‘ We accept no threats ’
text:
After Ukraine said it might take the Islamic Republic of Iran to international courts in connection with the downing of its passenger plane, an Iranian foreign ministry official said that “we do not accept any pressure or threat. ”
In this regard, Mohsen Baharvand, Deputy Minister for Legal and International Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, told Ukrainian officials on Wednesday that Iran “has not accepted any pressure or threat within the framework of its national sovereignty and will act proportionately against any unreasonable and unreasonable action in relation to itself and will respond to the smallest unilateral action by legitimate, legal and diplomatic means. ”
A day earlier, Gholamabbas Turki, a former military prosecutor in Tehran province, announced the issuance of indictments for “10 officials ” who were“ involved ” in the downing of the Ukrainian passenger plane, but did not name the defendants.
Ukraine ’ s foreign ministry has criticized the names and identities of the individuals, saying on Tuesday that “Iran ’ s decision to indict 10 Iranian officials for their role in the downing of Flight PS752 without naming them brings us ever closer to deciding on international legal action. ”
He added that Iran "still has a lot of work to do" to prove transparency in the investigation.
In response to the Ukrainian authorities, Mohsen Baharvand said in another part of his reaction on Wednesday that “the Islamic Republic of Iran has fulfilled all its duties in accordance with international law and will continue to do so until the end.
For this reason, he is not afraid of any rhetoric or other possible action outside of conventional wisdom. ”
The Ukrainian passenger plane was shot down by the Revolutionary Guards on the morning of January 8, 2019, shortly after flying from Tehran International Airport, due to two missiles, and all 176 people on board died.
After the downing of the passenger plane, the Iranian government, after several days of secrecy and false statements, finally acknowledged that Tehran ’ s anti-aircraft defense had shot down the Boeing plane bound for Kiev.
The Islamic Republic claims the shooting was caused by “human error, ” but Ukraine, Canada and many observers have expressed doubts about the authenticity of the claim.
Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization released a final report blaming the air defense system operator, but Ukraine and Canada have denied the report.
Ukraine ’ s Deputy Foreign Minister Yevgeny Yinin told Radio Farda: “The international community will not allow Iran to escape responsibility for the crime of shooting down the Ukrainian plane. ”

title: Climate and agricultural risks that threaten the world
text:
Cornell University scientists have discovered that since the 1960s, humanity has lost 21% of agricultural production growth due to climate change.
This equates to the loss of productivity growth over the past seven years.
According to experts, despite the development of the global agricultural sector, resistance to climate change has not increased.
The United Nations has warned of an impending “catastrophe ” of famine that will affect 34 million people worldwide.
Georgi Safunov, director of the Center for Environmental and Natural Resources Economics at the Russian Higher School of Economics, said: “Massive efforts and investments, including in new technologies, genetic engineering and other losses caused by frequent droughts and other climatic and climatic phenomena to increase the productivity of agricultural products, will no longer be compensated. ”
The problem of climate change also includes Russia.
On the one hand, crop production has been growing since 1990, but due to droughts in 2010 and 2012, wheat production has fallen by 33% and 25%, respectively.
This means that natural disasters still affect the agricultural sector, and it is unlikely that climate change will cause a 20% reduction in total agricultural production by 2040.
Alexei Kokorin, director of the program “Energy and Climate ” of the World Wildlife Fund in Russia, points out that global warming has caused an increase in the number of droughts in the southern Volga basin, and that agricultural production is expected to decline in the southern part of Europe and Russia.
He says climate change will also include Russia, although its impact will be greater in Asia and Africa.
It is now necessary to work on a strategy and mechanisms to adapt the agricultural sector to climate change.
To this end, Russia must import new technologies into the agricultural sector and grow new crops.
If all countries meet their commitments on carbon dioxide emissions, everything will be normal.

title: Fears, ears of farmers.
text:
According to many experts, drought is one of the harmful natural phenomena that is caused by climate change and, in a more detailed sense, the increase in the average temperature of the earth, and has many destructive economic and social effects.
A phenomenon that these experts believe that if no thought is made about it and no plan is formulated to control it, it will be a serious threat to the ecosystem, agriculture and human societies.
According to ISNA, Iran has not been far from this drought phenomenon, and according to the Ministry of Agriculture, rainfall in 1399 has decreased by 38 percent over the long term and 40 percent compared to the previous year, which shows that drought in the current agricultural year is certain and it is necessary for the relevant authorities and agricultural sector to be more vigilant than ever in this regard and take measures to control drought in the country before the natural phenomenon. It is a serious threat to the agricultural sector and the food security of the people.
The concept of drought and its cause, the provinces involved and ways to control this harmful natural phenomenon were issues that were discussed with Mehran Zand, head of the Department of Drought and Climate Change of the Soil Conservation and Watershed Management Research Institute.
He believes that the studies carried out by scientific and research centers indicate that the main culprit in the occurrence of natural disasters, including drought, is climate change, but failure to properly deal with the results of drought and lack of scientific and principled policies and programs in the face of this dangerous problem, in the long run, can lead to the complete destruction of natural resources of different regions and turn drought into permanent drought.
In short: What exactly is the concept of drought and when does this climatic phenomenon occur?
Drought is an unnatural and prolonged reduction of moisture sources (mainly precipitation) that have adverse effects on plants, animals and humans.
Meteorological droughts, referred to in many sources as climate droughts, are caused by a lack or reduction of rainfall over a period of time.
Meteorological drought occurs when annual rainfall is less than the long-term average.
Whereas agricultural drought is defined through an emphasis on such things as a deficit in precipitation, a lack of soil moisture, a difference between actual evapotranspiration and potential, a reduction in the level of reserves or groundwater, and so on that is linked to climate drought (or hydrology).
Which areas of agriculture and natural resources are most threatened by drought?
In order to investigate and analyze the situation of drought in agricultural lands and natural resources of the country, it is better to review the latest statistics and meteorological information.
In other words, given the importance that the origin and the main cause of the occurrence of drought in the agricultural and natural resources of the country changes in meteorological variables such as precipitation, temperature, humidity and so on.
Analysis of meteorological variables, especially precipitation, plays a key role in the occurrence and spread of agricultural and natural resources drought.
A quick look at the form below, which has been obtained from the latest data of the Meteorological Organization of the country, shows the drought conditions of the current agricultural year.
In this form, the blue section represents the long-term average of the cumulative rainfall of the country.
The brown and green curves show the cumulative rainfall changes of the previous and current blue years, respectively.
Comparing the green curve with the brown curve and the blue section shows the occurrence of a significant decrease in rainfall of the current agricultural year (-2.41% in the whole country) compared to the long-term and the previous agricultural year.
These conditions become more acute when we notice carefully in this form that the main and major part of the blue year has passed, and the forecasts of the competent centers (the Meteorological Organization of the country and affiliated centers) indicate that in the remaining months of the blue year, we will not have significant rainfall.
Therefore, and relying on the latest meteorological data, we are undoubtedly facing severe weather drought in most areas of the country in the current year.
In this regard, the provinces of Sistan and Baluchestan (-93 / -), Hormozgan (-91 / -), Khorasan (-57%), Semnan and Fars (-49) and Kermanshah (-43 / -) until April 23, 1400, have experienced the greatest decrease in rainfall and consequently the most severe weather drought over the long term.
In the case of drought in agriculture and natural resources, considering that after the occurrence of meteorological drought, the agricultural sector and natural resources, due to the great variety of phenological characteristics of plants are affected in different ways and with different severity and weaknesses, the subject has far more complexity than meteorological drought.
As mentioned in the definition of agricultural drought, in addition to precipitation, other important factors such as soil moisture and evapotranspiration conditions also determine the occurrence of this type of drought.
For this reason, in recent years, satellite images have been used to monitor the occurrence of drought in agricultural lands, forests and pastures.
One of the most common and widely used indicators of vegetation status, which is used to monitor the temporal and spatial changes of vegetation and agricultural products, as well as changes in these fields during the occurrence of drought in many parts of the world, is the Plant Normal Difference Index (NDVI).
The range of changes in this index is between minus one and positive one, but the usual range of changes in green plants is between 0.2 and 0.8.
In order to know the current conditions of drought occurrence in agricultural lands, forests and pastures of the country, accuracy in the map of the normal difference index of the plant can be helpful.
In this map, the yellow color spectrum toward light brown and dark indicates increased drought stress and, conversely, the light green color spectrum toward dark green indicates the occurrence of high normal and optimal conditions in terms of vegetation.
As seen in this map, significant parts of the country, including the provinces of Khorasan Razavi and North, East and West Azerbaijan, Zanjan, Central, Hamedan, Kurdistan, Fars, and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, are facing a significant reduction in vegetation in agricultural lands and natural resources.
This situation seems more critical when, on the other hand, we consider the reduction of about 85 percent of spring precipitation (which plays a vital role for wet crops) over the long term, and note that with the move to the warm season and increase in temperature and evaporation, followed by the reduction of soil moisture, this drought will increase and gradually most of the agricultural fields, forests and pastures of the country will face drought this year.
Does agricultural disruption have its roots in climate change or is it going back to mismanagement and mismanagement?
The geographical location of Iran in the dry and semi-arid belt of the world has caused drought and drought to be associated with the nature of this land.
Referring to the occurrence of severe and widespread droughts in historical texts alone can confirm this.
With the publication of numerous authoritative books, reports and scientific articles on the occurrence of climate change in different regions of the planet, which is the result of the efforts of the most experienced researchers in the world, there is no significant disagreement in this regard.
But the extent of these changes is very diverse in different parts of the planet and in vital parts of the world.
In Iran, with studies carried out by scientific and research centers, valid and acceptable documents have been presented in relation to the occurrence of climate change in the country.
Many of these investigations have also identified climate change as the main culprit in climate disasters.
Considering that one of the most important results of climate change is the increase of climatic extremes (maximum values) such as extreme rainfall, dust storms and severe and consecutive droughts.
It is therefore not surprising that the increasing frequency of agricultural drought events in recent years has been attributed to climate change.
Considering that the role of farmers and the relevant authorities is mainly in mitigating or intensifying the effects and consequences of agricultural drought, they cannot be blamed for increasing the occurrence of drought.
But at the same time, it should be noted that failure to properly deal with the results of drought and lack of policies and scientific and principled plans in the face of this dangerous disaster, in the long run, can lead to the complete destruction of natural resources of different regions and the conversion of drought to permanent drought.
What should farmers and farmers do to cope with the drought?
One of the most important characteristics of drought is that, in the current situation, humans do not yet have the ability to prevent the occurrence of this phenomenon.
Therefore, the most effective way to reduce the damage is to increase the readiness of farmers to deal with it more efficiently.
In recent years, two main short- and long-term approaches have been taken to deal with agricultural droughts.
Among the short-term methods of dealing with drought can be to manage water consumption, prevent water loss, reduce agricultural water consumption, appropriate fertilization, reduce moisture evaporation from the soil and deep ploughing.
Long-term methods include planting management, selection of dehydrated and adapted species to dry climates, habituation of plants to dry conditions, creation of windbreaks, strengthening of groundwater resources.
The methods of dealing with drought vary in different parts of the country and depend on the facilities and capital as well as the ability of the individual to solve problems.
The coping styles of individuals also depend on their individual, economic, social, environmental, attitudinal, cultural, and managerial factors.
In general, one of the most important strategies for reducing the occurrence of floods and turning them into opportunities and storing their water resources during droughts is watershed management activities.
Watershed management activities are very extensive and are usually carried out in a wide range of areas.
Implementing some structural and biological watershed management measures in small areas that have rapid hydrologic reactions will prevent the occurrence of floods (before the floods in the branches join together and create severe floods) and their water resources will be stored in aquifers by low-cost methods for dry years.
For example, consider that a heavy rainfall occurs in the tributaries of a large river, if watershed flood control activities such as gourds or flood spreading have not occurred, the floodwaters of the tributaries will join very quickly and may even cause financial and life damage downstream.
Even if the watersheds are extravagant, these valuable water resources are transferred to the sea by causing severe damage.
However, with watershed flood control measures, while controlling the floods in the headwaters, it is possible to store these valuable water resources and extract and use them in different ways in dry years.
Of course, these valuable water resources, which are sometimes stored by watershed management activities, should be used optimally.
In other words, a lot of efforts are being made to control and infiltrate the floodwaters in upstream areas and store them for dry years, so the drop of water resources should be used best.
Especially in the case of agriculture, the efficiency of water resources should be increased and provide maximum benefits.
Otherwise, many actions will remain ineffective or ineffective.
- Last word...
However, in order to deal with the effects of agricultural drought and reduce the damage caused by it, the relevant authorities can play a more important and important role.
Moving from risk management to crisis management and the creation and expansion of agricultural and natural resources drought monitoring and forecasting systems can be among the most important and necessary of these measures.

title: The Endurance rover produced oxygen on Mars.
text:
NASA's endurance probe produced oxygen on the surface of Mars for the first time.
Such an operation would provide a path for the exploration of the planet by astronauts.
The probe produced oxygen from the thin, carbon-dioxide atmosphere of Mars using the MOXIE instrument.
The technology could help astronauts breathe on the planet, as well as the process of returning rockets from the planet to Earth.
Oxygen production from Mars ’ atmosphere took place on Tuesday, just one day after genius ’ s helicopter flight.
Jim Reuther, a senior NASA administrator, said in a statement: “This is an important step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars.
Moxie has more work to do, but the results are promising tools.
The MOXIE tool is the size of a tester and exits carbon monoxide after producing oxygen from carbon dioxide.
This conversion process takes place at 800 ° C.
For this reason, the instrument is made of heat-resistant materials and has a thin gold coating that doesn ’ t allow too much heat to damage the endurance probe ’ s body.

title: Converting air from Mars into breathable oxygen
text:
In its latest experiment, the Endurance rover was able to convert some of Mars ’ air into breathable oxygen.
Although the ultimate goal of the Mars Perseverance rover is to study the signs of life on Mars, this goal does not prevent the Perseverance from carrying out scientific activities.
In its most recent activity, Endurance successfully removed some carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere and converted it into oxygen.
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) equipped the rover with a tool called MOXIE.
Similar to the toaster, the tool allows endurance to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules, providing carbon monoxide as a byproduct.
In its first experiment, MOXIE produced five grams of oxygen to allow astronauts to breathe for about 10 minutes.
According to NASA, the success of the experiment could pave the way for future missions, especially those involving astronauts.
NASA believes a rocket carrying four astronauts would need to store about 55,000 pounds of oxygen to take off from Earth.
Since transporting oxygen to Mars is not practical, future versions of the technology could work here.
End of message.

title: The Mars rover produced oxygen from the atmosphere for the first time.
text:
While the ingenious Mars rover passes the challenges of flying in the thin atmosphere of Mars, the Persistent Mars rover, in addition to imaging it, pursues its scientific experiments, including producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere.
The Perseverance Rover on Tuesday converted some of the carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere into oxygen during the first test of the scientific instrument MOXIE.
The name Maxi stands for the term oxygen experiment in situ from Martian sources.
After heating the scientific instrument for about 2 hours, Maxi produced about 5.4 grams of oxygen.
That ’ s enough to keep an astronaut alive for about 10 minutes.
It ’ s about the size of a toaster oven, and like a genius helicopter, it ’ s built to show off the technology on the rover.
Thus, scientists will have a better understanding of the methods and limitations of the work.
If the experiment continues to be successful, it could help future human exploration of Mars.
The thin atmosphere on Mars has 96% carbon dioxide and is not suitable for human respiration.
So if something can convert this carbon dioxide into oxygen, it could be beneficial in many ways.
Larger and more advanced versions of the Maxi in the future could extract and store oxygen for rocket fuel, as well as provide air for life-support systems.
It works by splitting carbon dioxide (CO2) molecules, which consist of one carbon atom (C) and two oxygen atoms (O2).
It separates and stores oxygen molecules and emits carbon monoxide (CO) as waste.
To accomplish this reaction, Maxi uses heat-resistant materials, such as gold plating and aerogel.
This is because the process of converting carbon dioxide to oxygen requires a temperature of 800 ° C.
These materials prevent heat radiation and damage to various parts of the rover.
Jim Reuter, director of NASA ’ s Space Technology Mission Directorate, said: “This is the first critical step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars.
Maxi is doing more, and the results from this demonstration of technology will ensure that one day we have humans on Mars.
"Oxygen is not only used for breathing, but rocket propellants are also dependent on it, and explorers will need it to produce propellants on Mars and back home."
To launch four astronauts from the surface of Mars, it would take about 6,800 kilograms of rocket fuel and 24,950 kilograms of oxygen.
But for life on the surface of Mars, rovers will consume much less.
Michael Hecht, principal investigator at MIT ’ s Haystack Observatory, said: “Astronauts who spend a year on the surface of Mars could use a ton of oxygen. ”
Getting that much oxygen from Earth to Mars would be difficult and expensive, and would require less space for other necessary space travel equipment.
But an oxygen exchanger weighing about 1 ton, the next generation and more powerful than Maxi, could produce enough oxygen in the long run.
For future experiments, maxi will likely produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour from the Martian atmosphere.
Over the next two years, the scientific instrument will conduct about nine more experiments, and the team will use the data to design the next generation of the Maxi.
In the first step, the mission team evaluates the tool ’ s performance.
In the second step, the maxi is tested under different conditions, such as different times of the day or different seasons.
In the third and final step, Maxi will consider new working modes or challenges, such as comparing activity at three or more different temperatures.
Maxi ’ s technology could help future astronauts live on the surface of the planet and use the resources around them.
Trudy Kortes, director of the technology show at NASA's Space Technology Mission Directorate, said: "The Maxi is not just the first tool to generate oxygen from the resources of another world."
He added: “This scientific instrument takes Mars ’ s rock folder and processes it into large structures or takes carbon dioxide from it to convert it into oxygen.
"This process allows us to convert these abundant materials on Mars into usable materials such as propellants, breathable air, or combined with hydrogen into water."
Positive results from these experiments will bring Mars missions like Elon Musk ’ s Mars project one step closer to landing humans on the Red Planet.

title: Oxygen production on Mars is a prerequisite for manned missions.
text:
Although the success of the April 20 MOXIE device installed on the project in producing five grams of oxygen is a small step for the US space agency NASA and its Mars rover, it is potentially a huge leap forward for humanity and its ambitions to access and colonize Mars.
While this small amount of oxygen from Mars ’ carbon-dioxide atmosphere is enough to keep an astronaut alive for about five minutes, the principle of testing the technology is important because it demonstrates the feasibility of producing oxygen on the surface of Mars, which is essential for permanently operating on the Red Planet and using it as a base to travel to other parts of space.
While Ingyanti is the first man-made device to fly an engine in an unknown location in the extraterrestrial world, the Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) is the first human-made experiment to produce oxygen in the universe and on a planet other than Earth.
These two experiments are of great importance due to the reduction of the distance between humans and Mars.
In fact, the success of the experiment is important because direct production of breathable oxygen on Mars is actually possible and astronauts will be able to return to Earth with rocket propulsion.
While humans could transport large oxygen tanks to Mars before sending humans to Mars, the cost and time of achieving this goal were prohibitive.
A group of four astronauts would need about a ton of oxygen to reach Mars within a full year, which would be extremely high if the amount of oxygen needed to launch a space rocket.
According to Michael Hackett, director of research at the Moxy Project, the mission would require about 25 tons (25,000 kilos) of oxygen, which would be the amount needed for astronauts to breathe and the maximum amount needed to transport and return astronauts.
The terms Mars and oxygen don ’ t go together because 96% of the planet ’ s atmosphere is covered in carbon dioxide.
The moxie separates the oxygen from the carbonic gas and the excess product is carbon monoxide.
Using electricity energy, the carbon dioxide molecule is converted into two other types of molecules, carbon monoxide and oxygen, which have a very similar function as fuel cells, although the function of this battery is reversed and produces electricity using fuel and oxygen and their combination.
Muxie's first test was to make sure the device was safe on a trip to Mars, but at least nine other tests have been planned over the course of a Martian year, which is roughly two Earth months.
The early achievements of the rover, which landed on Mars on February 18, about two months ago, have been encouraging, given the success of the Ingeonite helicopter in taking off the surface of Mars and the Muxie device on its mission.

title: The need to protect communities against the psychological consequences of all
text:
Undoubtedly, these days, the “mental health crisis ” is another epidemic that has plagued the world with the COVID-19 epidemic, raising concerns about the increased risk of suicide, especially among young people, due to the problems and limitations of the spread of the disease in different parts of the world.
Although studies in different countries paint a complex picture of different trends in suicide attempts, the rise in depression, anxiety and suicide rates has been almost constant across countries.
Data from past epidemics suggest a direct and significant link between the occurrence of epidemics and the rise in suicide.
For example, the Toronto Transit Commission in Canada reported that suicide attempts or deaths rose by almost a third in the first eight months of the epidemic.
There are many risk factors for suicide that are associated with the epidemic, including: anxiety and fear of family members, financial pressures, reduced social interactions with friends and social activities, interruptions in life goals and daily activities, feelings of hopelessness and helplessness, increased family stress due to remote work and home schooling, increased family fighting and conflict on the other hand, while some of the more affluent countries provided different statistics of suicide rates in the first months of the epidemic. There has been a decline in suicide attempts, but mental health experts still believe that the decline in suicide rates during the epidemic does not reflect the overall state of mental health in a society.
Although preliminary data suggest a decline in national suicide rates in 2020 in some countries, including the United States, these countries do not provide information based on demographic data.
Experts say the data should be analyzed and interpreted with "caution" because the mental and psychological damage caused by the epidemic may not have been directly presented.
Restrictions and quarantines, social isolation and economic insecurity have caused psychological harm to individuals, and many have hypothesized an increase in suicide rates in the past year.
However, preliminary data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show that the total suicide rate in the United States fell by 5.6% in 2020.
However, experts emphasize that these statistics may not have understood the interplay and complexity between the epidemic and how it affects the economy, job security, personal security and mental health.
While mental health experts stress the negative effects of the epidemic on mental health, a group of experts based on the new study claimed that suicide rates in rich countries remained stable in the first months of the COVID-19 outbreak.
A study published in the Lancet Psychiatry Journal found that suicide cases in middle and high-income countries remained largely unchanged or were lower than expected during the first months of the COVID-19 epidemic.
The study authors noted that many of these countries have established greater mental health support and established safe financial networks that may have helped to improve the initial negative effects of the epidemic.
However, they stressed that governments need to be vigilant and ready to respond in a timely manner due to the "uncertain long-term effects of the epidemic on mental health and its economic effects."
The study included national data from 10 countries and data from 25 specific regions in 11 countries.
The report found no evidence of an increase in suicide cases in any of the countries surveyed.
There is also evidence in 12 countries or regions that suicide cases are lower than expected.
The authors of the report cite several reasons why suicide rates did not rise during the first months of the epidemic.
Societies may have struggled to support at-risk individuals, individuals may have connected with others in new ways, and some relationships may have been strengthened by the presence of more family members in the home.
Jane Pirkis, director of the Centre for Mental Health at the University of Melbourne and senior author of the study, said: “We need to continue monitoring the data and be more vigilant about any increase in suicide rates, especially with the emergence of the full economic consequences of the epidemic.
Increasing mental health services and suicide prevention programs and providing safe financial networks may help prevent the possible and long-term damaging effects of the epidemic on suicidal tendencies.
We know that many people ’ s lives have changed dramatically during the epidemic and continue to do so.
We need to understand that suicide is not the only indicator of the negative impact of the epidemic on mental health – the level of community anxiety is high and we need to make sure people are supported.
The researchers also warned of some signals that the epidemic could affect suicide rates in low- and middle-income countries, although the data was only available to a small minority of these countries.
According to BMJ Medical Weekly, the high-income countries studied in the study included Australia, Austria, Canada, Chile, Croatia, UK, Estonia, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, South Korea, Spain and the United States.
The upper-middle countries included Brazil, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru and Russia.
In Japan, suicide rates have risen after a decade-long decline, coinciding with the COVID-19 epidemic.
Japan ’ s Ministry of Health and Welfare said on January 22 that according to preliminary data, about 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7 percent from the previous year.
Last year was the first year in more than a decade that suicide rates in Japan increased, with women and children taking the largest share.
End of message.

title: Deportation of thousands of illegal asylum seekers in the UK with the easing of Croatian restrictions
text:
The Guardian has gained access to the contents of a document in which a Home Office official wrote to city council chiefs in a letter that the process began with a view to cutting off government support for people whose asylum claims have been rejected.
Detainees will only have 21 days to evacuate the accommodation provided to them by the government and then leave the country.
Deputy Home Secretary Chris Phillip wrote in the letter that he would provide details of the cases of people under investigation by the Home Office to city councils for evacuation plans.
Meanwhile, a Home Office spokesman said the government has spent the past year using taxpayer money to resettle migrants whose asylum claims were rejected in the coronavirus outbreak, but with the reduction of Croatian restrictions and when rejected refugees can return to their homes, “it makes sense that this support should be stopped. ”
Charities and human rights activists have condemned the government ’ s decision as inhumane.
They have warned that the move will increase the number of homeless people in the city and lead to an increase in the number of people infected with coronavirus, and the UK's public health agency has also expressed concern about the government's decision.
According to the Guardian, around 60,000 migrants whose asylum cases have been rejected have been resettled by the Home Office.
Andy Hewitt, a senior fellow at the UK Refugee Council, said: “This is deeply troubling news for people in vulnerable situations, putting them at risk of homelessness.
We should not forget that the coronavirus epidemic has not yet ended and people are still denied access to humanitarian agencies and services.
The move comes as the UK government has recently made changes to the country ’ s immigration system, making it harder to grant asylum to people who enter the country illegally.
Home Secretary Priti Patel last month detailed the government ’ s plan, explaining that under the new rules, people who enter the UK illegally will not have the same rights as people who enter the UK legally.
He said many refugees, including women and children, had died en route to the UK, saying the new asylum system would work faster, more fairly and better to protect vulnerable people.
Stating that the way to prevent the death of refugees is to prevent human trafficking, he said the new measures by the London government have created a safe and legal route for immigration to the country.
“So if you enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you could apply for asylum, you ’ re not actually seeking asylum to escape an immediate danger, you ’ re choosing the UK as your destination. ”
He is referring to the refugees who took the perilous route of the English Channel by boat from France to reach England.
Activists and human rights activists described the immigration crackdown of the British interior minister as similar to the policies of the former US president and warned against repeating the fate of Donald Trump.
During his four years in office, Trump has implemented the most stringent immigration policies against Muslim-majority countries.

title: The second largest flight in the world.
text:
Two years after the first flight, the world ’ s largest plane has taken to the skies for another flight.
The Stratolaunch aircraft conducted a second test flight and a series of manoeuvres over Mojave Air and Space Station yesterday, and everything went as planned.
The plane made its second test flight on Thursday morning (April 29).
Stratolaunch was founded in 2011 by Paul Allen.
The first flight of the aircraft took place in April 2013.
The first flight lasted two and a half hours, during which it flew at 17,000 feet in the Mojave Desert, with a top speed of 189 miles per hour (304 km / h).
The aircraft, known as the "Roc", was originally designed as an airborne orbital launch system to carry missiles and satellites at altitude and then launch them into near-Earth orbit, but when the company was sold to its current owners in October 2019, there were changes to its purpose and the aircraft will now serve as a mobile launch pad for supersonic vehicles.
During Thursday ’ s test flight, Roc reached a maximum altitude of 14,000 feet (4,267 m) and a top speed of 199 mph (320 km / h).
Stratolaunch made the flight using its six 747s and then conducted a series of test maneuvers for its second successful flight.
The plane remained at altitude for 3 hours and 14 minutes.
End of message.

title: World ’ s largest plane successfully flew over a football field
text:
According to Space.com, the largest carrier aircraft, the Stratolaunch, which is ready to transport supersonic vehicles, carried out its second test flight on Thursday morning (April 29).
The wings of this giant aircraft are 117 meters, which is wider than a football field.
During its test flight on Thursday, Stratolaunch reached an altitude of 14,000 feet (4,267 m) and a top speed of 199 mph (320 km / h), which experts said was a success.
Speaking at a post-flight news conference, Stratolaunch's chief operating officer said: "We are very pleased with the performance of the Stratolaunch aircraft today and excited about how close the aircraft is to launching its first supersonic vehicle."
Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen introduced Stratolaunch in 2011 with the idea of being used to launch satellites in the air.
But Alan ’ s life was too short to see his dream come true: he died in October 2018.
The company was sold to its current owners in October 2019.
The aircraft will now act as a mobile launch pad for supersonic vehicles, moveable crafts that travel at least five times faster than the speed of sound.

title: 39 'Iranian' refugees detained on Britain's southeast coast
text:
Sean Gallup / Getty Images Image caption One of the boats normally used by asylum seekers to cross the Channel to the UK, four boats carrying 39 Iranian refugees were taken off Sunday, November 17, at separate events off Britain's southeast coast.
The British Interior Ministry confirmed that all of the asylum seekers identified themselves as “Iranian ”.
The first boat, which had nine people on board, took off at 4: 40 a.m. yesterday, while the second, with five people on board, reached the British coast at around 6 a.m.
According to the Coast Guard and Kent County Police, a boat with 11 people on board was seized at around 7 a.m. and a half hour later another boat with 14 people was taken off the coast of the UK.
As soon as they received a message of help from the boats, rescue helicopters, as well as rescue boats from the ports of Dover, Dunness and Hastings, as well as two coast guard vessels, took action to rescue the passengers.
A Home Office spokesman said: "Crossing the canal by these small boats is extremely dangerous.
For those who have gone through such a journey, their lives and their loved ones are at risk. ”
According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.
In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.
In November last year there was a significant increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to cross the English Channel to Britain, with the Home Secretary calling the issue a "serious incident" and calling for the French government to work together to resolve the issue.
Due to the increasing number of migrants and asylum seekers arriving on the east coast of the UK via the sea and the English Channel, the British Coast Guard has announced an increase in staff.

title: Drought threatens food security
text:
At the 6th International Regional Conference on Climate Change, Head of the National Meteorological Organization Sahar Tajbakhsh said: “Today ’ s climate change is considered as one of the security issues of our country.
What has happened in the climate has increased the incidence of extreme events.
One of the most fundamental influences on climate change is transportation, and aviation is one of the projects that play a very influential role in emissions of greenhouse gases and carbon dioxide.
Taj Bakhsh added: Today, issues related to climate change and the occurrence of extreme phenomena are among the most dangerous economic issues in the world.
4.5 billion people in the world are affected by natural hazards, 96% of which are affected by weather-related phenomena.
He noted that the number of fatalities and losses in the world has been increasing from 1980 to 2018.
Basically, what led to extreme phenomena is global warming, which in December, January and February, particularly the increase in global temperatures in the northern latitudes, has changed the course of precipitation around the world.
Parts of the Middle East and large parts of North Africa are affected by the drought, which has a significant impact on GDP reduction.
The head of the Meteorological Organization said that if the warming continues, it will lead to food insecurity in countries where the Middle East and North Africa are among the most affected areas of drought.
He said warnings of a three-degree rise in global temperatures mean that the vast majority of these countries will face food insecurity.
If we go to two degrees Celsius, the trend of tropical storms around the world will increase.
Another effect is sea level rise, which is a big problem for countries with overcrowding and beaches.
Tajbakhsh said that from 1970 to 2018, carbon dioxide emissions have increased significantly and climate risks will increase as the trend continues.
Heat waves also saw a significant increase from 2000 to 2018, with transport playing a 14% role.
Deputy Minister of Roads and Urban Development added: There are several fuel sources involved in transportation, which is a part related to land transportation and about 10 exajoules related to air transportation.
He continued: “In recent years, 30,000 kilometers of new air routes have been created in Iran, and the length of our air routes has increased from 60,000 kilometers to 94,000 kilometers, leading to shorter routes. ”
For example, the flight of Bandar Abbas to Tabriz on the old route took 121 minutes and 970 miles, which is now 104 minutes and 836 miles short on the new route, which leads to reduced fuel consumption and reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and only on this route we save more than two billion and 500 million tomans per day.
Taj Bakhsh said: “The other route from the northwest of our country in Alram to the Persian Gulf has been shortened by 281 miles and 28 minutes.
70% of flights from Europe to the Persian Gulf countries pass through this route.
Considering the average fuel consumption for each flight, we will see a reduction in the consumption of 3,700 kilograms of fuel per flight and more than 2,613 thousand kilograms of fuel consumption for 700 flights, which will reduce the cost of seven billion tomans per day and more than seven thousand tons per day to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
The head of the Meteorological Organization pointed out at the end: By turning the country ’ s atmosphere into an air highway within the framework of sustainable development, economic prosperity and the environment, we can expand our movement towards green transportation.

title: Stories of the iceberg.
text:
Some experts in world fiction literature believe that the turning point in the influence of Ernest Hemingway, the world famous writer in modern literature, was a theory that he himself invented in world fiction.
The “iceberg ” theory was a new mode of narrative that made the writing less intense and the reader ’ s imagination flaring.
The hallmark of iceberg stories is not telling a large part of the story and leaving it to the audience to think more and become curious.
Hemingway likened such short stories to an iceberg whose bulk is hidden underwater, and said that the glory of the movement of the iceberg is only seen in the one-eighth of the water.
The collection of stories of Parviz Shishegaran or flash fiction in the book "Ticket for sale at the end of the metro line" is very similar to the style of iceberg and is a prominent example of such stories.
The book is full of stories, stories, and stories, and so forth, and so forth, and so forth.
“Dream, ”“ Left Neighbor, ” “Fifth Man, ”“ Stranger, ” “Grandma, ”“ Station, ” and so on.
There are a number of stories in this collection, all written with the theme of war.
Each of the stories depicts a slice of the lives of combatants and minutes of people ’ s lives during and after the war, which not only makes us not tired, but also makes us curious.
In the story of the "ticket sale of the last station of the subway line", the subject of which dates back to the post-war years, we are faced with a veteran who needs oxygen in the congestion and crowds of passengers inside one of the Tehran subway due to respiratory problems caused by war injuries and before the oxygen arrives.
This story has a very different beginning: "One, five, one.
Excuse me. Emergency?
“Someone needs oxygen right away. ”
Here, instead of describing the moments of the veteran ’ s call to the emergency room, the author depicts it in dialogue to convey his message faster, or at the beginning of “The Stranger, ” we read:“ One, two, three, smile. ”
Suddenly there was smoke everywhere.
I eat heavily on the ground...
I drop the gun and I don ’ t see Akbar.
He said something in Arabic.
I don't understand.
It hit me in the face. ”
This is the beginning itself for the curious, searching and influential audience, or the story of the station begins: “It was the sunrise.
The woman opened her eyelids.
The man stood up.
The woman sat down.
The soldiers came in one by one.
A man and a woman looked at the train tracks.
The train whistled.
The old man shrugged his shoulders. ”
One of the defining features of iceberg stories is that they are visual, so Hemingway has had the chance to make multiple films out of most of his stories.
So a successful writer is one who creates the most pictorial scenes with the least number of sentences and satisfies the reader.
Parviz Shishegaran has done this in this collection and has delivered good stories to the audience, and the turning point of the stories of this book is their brilliant beginning and effective ending.
The only point that should not be overlooked is that in the stories of icebergs, we should not ignore the space building around us and just tell the story.
The structure of the stories in this book is based on the same theory of the iceberg, but in this book the author did not pay attention to space building and in some narratives narrated the story and quickly rejected.
This small book was published in 43 pages by Amirkabir Publications.

title: Iran strikes again on Canadian court ruling on Ukrainian plane
text:
Gholamhossein Esmaeili, a spokesman for the judiciary of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in response to the decision of the Supreme Court of Ontario in Canada, which on May 20 called the firing of two missiles by the Revolutionary Guards on Ukraine flight PS752 as intentional and terrorist, said that because “the incident occurred in Iran, the only competent authority to deal with it is the courts of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the courts of other countries, including Canada, do not have jurisdiction. ”
He described the court ’ s decision as “emotional, unscientific, speculative ” and lacking“ legal value and adequate documentation. ”
The spokesman for the Judiciary referred to the investigation carried out by the Judiciary Organization of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran and spoke of “carrying out various experts in various fields, especially technical reports of the accident and its compliance with international standards. ”
He claimed that "the situation of the reconstruction of the scene and the documents presented and explained" in the process of the court case in Iran is "accurate, comprehensive and extensive".
Gholamhossein Esmaeili spoke of the “accuracy ” of the investigations of the experts of the Judiciary Organization of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran, saying that the Islamic Republic lied in the media for three days based on“ expert investigations ” about the cause of the downing of the plane.
He called the Ontario court ’ s ruling “political ” and“ not judicial ” because “Canada has become the home of corrupters who are persecuted by the Islamic Republic of Iran. ”
The Canadian government has sent a message from Akhavan, a former Hague prosecutor, to the country ’ s top foreign ministry adviser in the case of firing missiles at a Ukrainian passenger plane.
A day before the appointment, Ontario ’ s Supreme Court ruled in an unprecedented ruling in Canada ’ s judicial history that the firing of missiles at the Ukrainian plane was “deliberate ” and“ terrorist. ”
The plaintiffs in the case of the downing of the Ukrainian passenger plane are four families of the victims, Ali Khamenei, Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic and Commander in Chief of Staff, Abdul Rahim Mousavi, Commander of the Army, Hossein Salami, Commander of the IRGC, Amir Ali Hajizadeh, Commander of the IRGC, Mohammad Hassan Bagheri, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and Ali Shamkhani, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
Iran ’ s foreign ministry spokesman earlier, like the judiciary ’ s spokesman, called the sentence, which was issued following their private complaint, “baseless ” and accused Canada of“ politically-motivated actions. ”
TEHRAN – Kyiv Flight PS752 was shot down on January 8, 2019, minutes after the aircraft took off with two IRGC missiles.
All 176 passengers and crew died, including 57 Canadians.
