title: The attack on Gaza calls into question the normalization of Arab countries with the Zionist regime
text:
According to an IRNA report on Tuesday, the apparent crimes of the Zionist regime in Gaza, aside from the sleep of the children of Gaza, but the lighting of the Israeli nights by the missiles of the resistance forces and the fear of the Zionist settlements, has shown a wider dimension of these attacks, including the fishing of Benjamin Netanyahu from the muddy water of violence and bloodshed in Palestine, to the question of the normalization of relations with a number of Arab countries.
Spain ’ s AFE news agency said Israel ’ s repeated attacks on the Gaza Strip call into question the so-called “normalization ” process with the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco, which was signed in the second half of 2020 as a peace agreement between the Arab states and Israel.
The issue of the duality of Arab states and nations in accepting and rejecting normalization with Israel has become the headline of this European media, while the signing of these agreements has put the signatory governments in a difficult situation.
If they support Israel, they will be severely blamed by their own citizens and by the international community, and if they support Palestine, they will turn their backs on the agreement with Israel.
In Morocco, last December ’ s agreement was initially seen as a win-win deal, in which in addition to commercial benefits for the country, recognition of Morocco ’ s sovereignty over the Western Sahara after years of tension with the Polisario Front seemed a valuable asset.
Now, with the escalation of Israeli military operations against Gaza entering its second week, the Maghreb government was forced to endure more than 50 gatherings of solidarity with the Palestinian people throughout the country by the end of last week.
Demonstrations whose message was not only to express support for Palestine but to “end normalization ” were the main demands of the demonstrators.
The Moroccan king has not yet spoken of condemning Israel ’ s recent violence, but the delivery of 40 tons of humanitarian aid, including food, medicine and clothing, to Palestine is a clear sign of support for the suffering nation.
In Bahrain, Shiite groups, which have been staunchly opposed to normalization with Israel from the beginning, have organized dozens of protest rallies condemning Israel ’ s actions since the start of the new round of tensions in Palestine.
Sunnis, who are traditionally loyal to the Bahraini monarch, and left-wing and liberal groups, as well as civil society, have called for a rethink of relations with Israel.
The United Arab Emirates, which has established the most ties with Israel by accepting the Treaty of Abraham in August 2020, has so far avoided direct criticism of Tel Aviv.
Rim al-Hashimi, the UAE ’ s Minister of International Cooperation, called for an immediate halt to violence and a ceasefire, but only addressed the unrest in East Jerusalem, not to mention the military operation in Gaza, which has cost 200 lives so far.
These days, the cries of the legitimate demands of the Palestinians from the youth of the conciliatory countries with the terrorist regime of Israel are more than ever to be understood by Rafael Masri, the head of the Confederation of Palestine in Latin America and the Caribbean (COPLAC), who said that the United States and Israel wanted to show the world that they were capable of breaking the Arab alliance on the Palestinian issue through signing agreements. The bottom line is that the result was a complete failure.
Also, the United States and Israel thought that some compromises would lead to modeling and signing chains of other countries, but this did not happen.
On the other hand, the governments that followed the US initiative were a number of US dependent countries in the Middle East geopolitics that play no other important role than providing land for Washington ’ s military bases.
So you can double down on this failure.
It should also not be forgotten that despite the behavior of the governments in these countries in normalizing relations, the active solidarity of the people in these countries with the Palestinian people and aspirations has been taken apart from the decisions made.

title: Israeli Arab partners ashamed of Gaza attacks
text:
The intensification of deadly violence between Israel and Palestine has caused some Persian Gulf states, which are new partners of Israel, to be embarrassed by diplomatic apologies, which have normalized relations with the Zionist regime and are signatories of the Treaty of Abraham.
The Treaty of Abraham, which was signed in September last year between the Zionist regime and first the United Arab Emirates, then Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco, has led to many criticisms of these countries.
But a new round of violence in the Gaza Strip has led Arab countries to finally decide to condemn Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip as they celebrate the end of Ramadan.
A year after signing an agreement to normalize relations with Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco are now forced to change course and turn to critical rhetoric.
Ilham Fakhro, an analyst at the Crisis Group think tank, told AFP: “These statements are mainly intended for domestic and regional Arab audiences and have no external uses. ”
“But the Abraham agreement actually destroyed decades of consensus and was denounced by Palestinian leaders as a ‘ betrayal. ’ ”
Bahrain, another signatory to the Pact, is witnessing daily anti-Israel protests, and protesters and civil society have called for a break in relations with Israel.
In the United Arab Emirates, where social media is severely restricted, many users have shared videos and photos to denounce the Israeli occupation and brutality.
For Hugh Lovett, an analyst at the European Council on Foreign Relations, the crisis is “the first real test ” for the UAE, which has quietly developed ties with Israel for years.
“Abraham ’ s agreement confirms Netanyahu ’ s long-standing belief that the Palestinians are effectively marginalized while Israel develops relations with neighboring countries. ”
"The current violence in Gaza is a test of whether the UAE is ready to put its relations with Israel on the line for the sake of the Palestinians," he said.
He said the answer was "no" given the achievements the agreement has made for the UAE, including technology partnerships and access to U.S. military hardware.
But while criticism in the UAE has been ignored, because of the presence of pro-Palestinian activist groups, the situation is more complicated for other Arab countries that have moved closer to Israel.
Faced with the pressure of street protests, Morocco eventually condemned the actions of Israeli forces in East Jerusalem.
However, normalization of the North African country ’ s relations with Israel is a strategic issue, as it relates to the US recognition of its sovereignty over the disputed territory of the Western Sahara.
Sudan, which acquiesced to Israel in exchange for its removal from the list of state sponsors of terrorism, condemned the Israeli attacks and warned that their actions would perpetuate a “cycle of violence. ”
Vali-Nasr, from Johns Hopkins University ’ s School of International Studies, tweeted: “Israel ’ s entire strategy through the Abraham Pact was based on the argument that the Palestinian issue was no longer the issue.
"But now, thanks to a series of Israeli mistakes, the Palestinian issue continues to be strong."

title: Climate crisis threatens a third of global food production
text:
On Saturday, The Guardian reported that if global warming continues at its current pace, food production areas will see significant changes in rainfall and temperature.
The report added that if the temperature rises to about 3.7 ° C and if the increase in greenhouse gas emissions is forecast, the food growing areas will see an increase in temperature and change in rainfall patterns.
A study by Aalto University in Finland found that about 95 percent of current crop production takes place in areas defined as having a healthy climate, or in conditions where temperatures, precipitation and drought fall within certain boundaries.
According to a paper published in the journal OneEarth, if temperatures rise to 3.7 ° C or so by the end of the century, safe zones will decline dramatically, most notably in South and Southeast Asia and sub-Saharan Africa.
But if greenhouse gas emissions are reduced or the Paris climate agreement is met, about half to eight percent of food production could be at risk.
The Paris Agreement aims to raise temperatures between 1.5 and 2 percent Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
Further increases in temperature will pose a risk to crops, and many areas are likely to face water shortages, according to the report.
Researchers examined the effects of climate change on 27 critically important food crops and seven livestock species.
The study also shows that by the end of the last century, global warming will increase if greenhouse gases continue to rise.
Recent research has highlighted previous findings that global warming has already had an impact on agricultural production.

title: Ukraine and Iran resume talks on 752 flight next week
text:
Radio Farda has been informed that the third round of talks with Iran on the downing of flight 752 will be held in Kiev next week, June 2 and 3.
The last round of talks took place in Tehran last month.
In an exclusive interview with Radio Farda reporter Anna Raiskaya, Ukraine ’ s deputy foreign minister and the head of the negotiating team with Iran, Yevgeny Yinin explained why the negotiations were taking a long break and what issues were on the agenda for the new round of talks.
Yinin: It was a long pause as we waited for the Iranian side to deliver on the promises it made in the previous round of negotiations.
We seem to have seen some developments, but if we look at the details and the depth of the story, we find that our many questions remain unanswered.
And about the final technical report that Iran has submitted during this period, which we have explicitly objected to.
Both the criminal investigation in Iran and the fact that to this day we do not even know the names of the suspects, and the joint investigation that was investigated during the previous round, but we still have not received Iran ’ s response to our offer.
For justice to be done, all questions must be answered, and we will ask these questions again.
We have always insisted that we will not be satisfied with the loss without the truth.
If Iran ’ s promises have not been fulfilled since the second round of talks, why do you see the need for a new round of talks?
The Iranian side has informed us several times that it is interested in continuing the negotiations.
I sincerely hope they come with clear answers.
Our negotiations are not separate from other developments on Iran.
We will ask how the change of government after the presidential election in Iran will affect the course of our negotiations.
Our allies, among other countries affected, have supported the continuation of the negotiations.
We believe that our joint efforts will succeed sooner or later.
We have a clear path ahead of us and we will take all necessary steps to ensure justice is served.
What exactly is the topic of the third round of negotiations?
As in the previous round, several working groups – the military, the prosecutor ’ s office and aviation – will negotiate.
We have a list of questions that will be reviewed and we hope to hear answers to at least some of these questions.
I know there are herds of Kennedy this way.
We wanted this case to be resolved as quickly as possible.
But there is no choice but to follow this path.
We will reaffirm for the Iranian side that justice is an inseparable element for a comprehensive resolution of this issue.
Is the issue of compensation being investigated?
To qualify for compensation, we need to know exactly what happened.
To avoid repetition, we need to know the truth.
Once we understand what caused the downing of the Ukrainian plane and what measures have been taken in Iran to prevent the recurrence of similar incidents, we will have a positive atmosphere about the compensation debate.
The amount of compensation will be determined by taking into account the reasons and conditions for the downing of Flight 752, as well as Iran ’ s level of cooperation in this case.
Compensation is not on the agenda of the third round of negotiations, but as soon as we have satisfactorily answered our questions, we will be ready to consider the issue of compensation.
Will the decision of the Canadian court, which called the downing of the Ukrainian plane a deliberate and terrorist act, have an impact on the negotiation process?
We know that Canadian citizens, based on Canadian laws that do not grant immunity to a country accused of terrorism, have chosen a path that allows them to seek reparations from Iran.
We know that Iran has dismissed the verdict of this court as baseless.
The Canadian judge's ruling is not the official position of the Canadian government.
Canada is a member of the group of countries affected by the downing of flight 752, and through negotiations with Iran, we intend to act in the direction of justice and compensation for the relatives of the victims of the flight.

title: Human Rights Watch: Families of Ukrainian plane victims under pressure from Iranian government
text:
Human Rights Watch says that since the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane by the Revolutionary Guards in January 2019, the families of the dead have been systematically harassed by Iranian authorities.
The international body, which released a report on Thursday, said governments involved in the Flight 752 investigation should support family members on the path to justice and accountability.
The Ukrainian plane, Flight PS752, was shot down by at least two IRGC missiles on January 8, 2019, and all 176 people on board, mostly Iranian and dual Iranian-Canadian citizens, died.
Citizens (including dual nationals) from Afghanistan, Britain, Germany, Sweden and Ukraine were also killed in the incident.
Michael Page, deputy Middle East director at Human Rights Watch, said: “The IRGC has killed 176 people without any accountability, and now Iran ’ s brutal security agencies are harassing family members to destroy any hope of justice. ”
“Instead of trying to rebuild people ’ s trust through a transparent investigation and compensation for families, the authorities are once again silencing efforts to hold them accountable. ”
Human Rights Watch reported that from October 2020 to January 2021, it spoke to 31 family members of the victims and individuals with knowledge of how the authorities treated the families.
Research shows that the security agencies of the Islamic Republic have been “arbitrarily ” arresting, summoning, interrogating, harassing, torturing and mistreating survivors ’ families during this period.
These institutions have also refused to return the property of the victims to their survivors and have clearly tried to confiscate the funerals and memorials of the victims.
On June 1, a report was published saying that the Canadian government has appointed the message of the Brotherhood, a lawyer and former investigator of the Hague Court of Justice, to be its chief advisor in the case of Flight 752.
The Association of Families of the Victims of the Ukrainian Airliner said in a statement on May 2 that Iran ’ s military court has issued a ban on prosecution for those at the highest levels of the government in the case.
According to the association, the military court has only issued “contracts for ten unnamed persons ” and“ the lawyers of the families to study the case, to learn about the expert ’ s methods and interrogations and statements of the defendants and to find their names has not been successful. ”
So far, there have been numerous reports of the Islamic Republic ’ s security forces attempting to intimidate the families of those killed in Flight 752.
Intelligence and Security Canada said in its annual report a few weeks ago that there were "credible reports" of harassment and intimidation of families and relatives of victims in Canada.
The Ontario Supreme Court in Canada ruled Thursday that the downing of the Ukrainian plane by the Revolutionary Guards was a “deliberate ” and“ terrorist ” act.

title: China's "artificial sun" record
text:
China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.
While similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea, the artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.
According to state media, China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.
State news agency Xinhua reported that the Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.
The report said the artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.
Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.
The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.
Another Chinese artificial sun project in Chengdu, the Tokamak HL-2m device, maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.
The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China ’ s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.
But there are many challenges that need to be overcome in the decades-long effort of the world ’ s scientists.
Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.
China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.
It is difficult to directly compare these types of experiments in different countries, because the devices are designed differently.
These facilities are called “artificial suns ” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.
When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.
To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.
Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.
Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.
The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.
China joined the ITER project in 2003 and at that time it was reported as an opportunity for its scientists to expand their expertise and gain an opportunity to emerge in the international scientific community.
The project in southern France has been repeatedly delayed, with the country ’ s latest plasma production target set for 2025.
The European Union has pledged $6.8 billion in new funding to the project in February.
Also, China National Nuclear Corporation will install the main equipment "ITER".
End of message.

title: China breaks record for building nuclear fusion reactor
text:
Chinese scientists set a record by reaching plasma temperatures of 120 million degrees Celsius in 101 seconds and 160 million degrees Celsius in 20 seconds.
According to the Global Times, the researchers say this is a major step toward reproducing the nuclear synthesis that occurs naturally in the Sun and other stars.
The record was broken at the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) at the Physical Science Institute in Hefei, China.
Previously, scientists working on the EAST project had achieved a temperature of 100 million degrees Celsius in 100 seconds.
At the same time, reaching a plasma temperature of more than 100 million degrees is one of the basic goals when using nuclear synthesis.
The temperature in the core of the Sun is believed to be 15 million degrees, making the plasma in the tokamak several times hotter than the Sun.
Scientists say it will take another 30 years to develop nuclear fusion systems.
The EAST test is part of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project, which China, India, the European Union, Russia, the United States and other countries are involved in.

title: "Hero" Asghar Farhadi goes to the 74th Cannes Film Festival to unveil
text:
The list of selected films at the 74th Cannes International Film Festival has been officially announced on Thursday, June 3, 2017.
The film "Hero", directed by Asghar Farhadi, a renowned Iranian filmmaker and starring Amir Jadidi and Mohsen Tanabandeh, will be screened in the competition section of the 2021 Cannes Film Festival for the first time.
According to the official announcement of the 74th Cannes International Film Festival, the film "Hero" by Asghar Farhadi, the famous Iranian cinematographer will be screened in the competition section of the festival for the first time.
After the unveiling at the Cannes Film Festival, Asghar Farhadi ’ s “Hero ” will also be released in French cinemas.
Asghar Farhadi, who has been in the official section of the Cannes Film Festival in recent years, will compete this year with the latest works of famous figures such as French cinematographer François Ozon, Italian director Nanni Moretti, French filmmaker Julia Ducorno and American film director, actor, screenwriter and producer Wes Anderson.
"Hero" is the ninth feature film by Asghar Farhadi, and actors such as Amir Jadidi, Mohsen Tanabandeh, Angel Sadr Arafai, Ehsan Goodarzi, Sarina Farhadi and a number of other actors, who are often new faces, have played roles in it.
Asghar Farhadi, who received the Best Screenplay Award at the Cannes Film Festival in 2016 for writing the screenplay for the film "The Salesman", has received several other international and prestigious awards in his artistic career.
In 2012, this famous Iranian director and producer won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay for “A Separation from Simin ”.
In the same year, he won the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Film for directing and writing "A Separation from Simin".
The Golden Bear of the Berlin Film Festival (2011) is another international achievement of Asghar Farhadi because of the separation of “Nader from Simin ” and the Silver Bear of the festival for“ About Ellie ” (2009).
The Cannes Film Festival, which was cancelled last year due to the coronavirus epidemic, has a detailed plan to hold its 74th edition in person this year.
This year ’ s Cannes Film Festival (2021) will welcome filmmakers and lovers of the seventh art from July 6 to 17 with films from all four corners of the world, featuring famous American director Spike Lee as the chairman of the jury of the competition section.

title: Allegations of four countries against Iran in relation to Ukrainian plane
text:
Canada, Sweden, Ukraine and the United Kingdom have made claims over the catastrophic downing of the Ukrainian plane.
According to a joint statement by the four countries of Canada, Sweden, Ukraine and the United Kingdom, published by the press office of the Foreign Ministry of Ukraine, these countries made claims for the catastrophic downing of the Ukrainian plane near Tehran on January 8, 2020.
Manouchehr Moradi, the Iranian ambassador to Kiev, had informed that the deputy foreign minister of Iran went to Kiev with a 12-member delegation for technical and legal negotiations on the case of the downing of the Ukrainian plane.
Ukraine claims that Iran sees the process of negotiating and answering technical questions as slow.
The perpetrators of the disaster have not yet been identified.
Mohsen Baharvand, Deputy Minister for Legal and International Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, accompanied by representatives from the Ministry of Roads, the Tehran Military Procuratorate, the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the Civil Aviation Organization, and the Presidential Office to discuss the Boeing 737 case.
The previous two rounds of talks between the two sides were held in August and November in Kyiv and Tehran.
Ukrainian officials have repeatedly criticized the slow pace of negotiations and Iran ’ s procrastination in answering technical questions, including the reasons why Tehran ’ s skies remain open in war conditions.
Mohsen Baharvand said that in a meeting with ICAO (International Aviation Organization) officials, he informed them of the legal and technical aspects of the case.
"We, the ministers and representatives of Canada, Sweden, Ukraine and the United Kingdom, today (June 3), have made our claims to the Islamic Republic of Iran regarding the downing of the Boeing 737 flight 752 of Ukraine International Airlines."
Iran ’ s actions and inaction are a violation of international standards.
"Our countries and their citizens and passengers of Flight PS752 suffered irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its full compensation obligations to the affected group."
The Ukrainian government, which talks with Iran on behalf of other countries concerned, has made the dispute over compensation contingent on Tehran ’ s level of cooperation and clarifying the possibility of firing missiles at the passenger plane.
The Deputy Attorney General of Ukraine also wrote on Twitter that he will ask the Iranian delegation to explain the criminal investigation of the case and how to handle the responsibility of the perpetrators.
Ukraine ’ s Boeing 737 International Airlines crashed on January 8, a few minutes after leaving Tehran airport.
176 people died: Afghan, German, Iranian, Canadian and Ukrainian citizens, as well as British and Swedish citizens, were on board the flight.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said the cause of the crash was a human error caused by mistaking the passenger plane as a missile.

title: A look at the history of beauty operations from ancient Egypt to the present day.
text:
According to the website of the Young Journalists Club, ancient Egyptians used artificial organs in addition to nose surgery.
In the year 2000, a mummy was discovered with an artificial toe — plastic surgery, no matter what the outcome, is synonymous with the search for beauty and youth, though for centuries it was done only by medical necessity, and evidence suggests that reconstructive surgery dates back to antiquity.
The earliest known cases appear in an ancient Egyptian medical text, the Edwin Smith Papyrus, named after the American Egyptologist who bought it in 1862.
The text contains examination of injuries and medical diagnoses, and shows how the Egyptians treated wounds and fractures.
In this papyrus, it is explained that for nose injuries, first put the nose in the desired position and then fixed it in place using a broken board, bandage cloth, cotton and wick.
Ancient Egyptians also used artificial organs.
In 2000, a mummy was discovered with an artificial toe that may have been used to help the woman walk.
Justin Yusuf, a surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital in Sydney, looks at the history of these types of surgeries and points to India.
In the 6th century BC, Indian doctors performed operations that were not unlike today ’ s rhinoplasty.
Sushruta, an Indian physician who is sometimes called the father of plastic surgery, describes in his book Sushruta Samhita an advanced method for skin transplantation.
In India, rhinoplasty was also performed, but according to Yusuf, the patient ’ s motivation was, in other words, for beauty.
Justin Yusuf, in an interview with CNN, refers to punishment in ancient India where criminals cut their noses to punish fornication or any other illegal act.
This punishment brought shame in society, and people knew immediately from the absence of the nose that the person had committed a crime.
Sushruta used skin from other parts of the body, possibly the cheek or forehead, to create a new nose for the patient.
But these practices were not limited to ancient Egypt and India.
The first known case of cleft lip and palate was performed by Chinese doctors in the 4th century BC.
In ancient Rome, encyclopaedist Elves Cornelius Celsus described a procedure in which excess skin was removed around the patient ’ s eyes, a procedure now called blepharoplasty or eyelid rejuvenation.
Progress in this field was slow in the following centuries, until the development of microbial disease theory and the development of anesthetic medicine in the 19th century transformed this field as well as other fields of medicine.
But another factor that speeded up progress in plastic surgery was the war.
In World War I, the sheer number of facial injuries allowed doctors to experiment with new methods.
But despite dramatic advances in skin and bone grafts, facial reconstruction and suture procedures, the use of surgery to improve appearance was still not common.
In the period between the First and Second World Wars, standards improved and the first attempts at gender reassignment were made.
According to Dr. Richard L.
In an article in the American Journal of Cosmetic Surgery in 1999, a number of nose and breast surgeries were performed in the 1930s, but most plastic surgeons wanted to be “taken seriously ” and avoided what was considered“ frivolous ” procedures.
The post-World War II era saw the evolution of the field, and advances in technology, risk reduction, and increased revenue played a key role in the growth of the popularity of plastic surgery.
By the 1960s, many common cosmetic procedures became common today, from breast augmentation to nose surgery and facial reshaping.
For example, Botox injections were first used to treat double vision and squint in the late 1960s and 1970s, and then approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in 2002 for the treatment of wrinkles and lines.
In the 1990s, plastic surgery flourished, and the number of procedures increased tenfold in the United States.
According to the Society for Plastic Surgery (ASPS), last year, 15.6 million cosmetic procedures were performed in the United States alone.
However, in the wake of the COVID-19 epidemic, this figure has fallen by 15 percent compared to 2019.

title: Strategies for the development of urban green space
text:
Urbanization and limited access to nature can increase exposure to some environmental hazards such as air and noise pollution.
Many urban areas are facing increasing populations, limited resources, and the growing impacts of climate change.
These challenges need to be addressed so that cities can provide a healthy and sustainable living environment.
Green spaces, urban neighborhood parks and other nature-based solutions offer innovative approaches to enhancing the quality of urban environments.
To maintain public health and reduce pollution of the urban environment, urban green space is an important investment that should be taken into consideration by city authorities and citizens.
Green space will reduce and control flood hazards; control soil erosion, control of wind; control of light and sunlight and reduce the intensity of summer heat; increase biodiversity, increase neighborhood flexibility, promote sustainable lifestyle, increase citizens ’ presence outside the home, increase social cohesion, increase citizens ’ physical and sports activities, and ultimately improve the physical and mental health and well-being of urban residents.
Ghaemshahr city has about 630 thousand square meters of green space, which according to the average population of 200 thousand people, the per capita green space of Ghaemshahr is about 3 square meters per person.
According to the UN recommendation, urban green space per capita is 20-25 square meters and at least 9 square meters per person is recommended by the World Health Organization.
The per capita green space in many cities of different countries is several times the global benchmark.
The per capita standard of green space in our country is recommended 12 square meters per person.
According to global and national benchmarks, the per capita green space of the city is very low, which is roughly equivalent to a quarter of the per capita of the country.
Therefore, one of the important priorities of the city council and municipality is to create and increase urban green spaces in any way possible to reach the per capita of the country.
To this end, a wide range of interventions can be implemented to increase per capita green space such as increasing linear green space (green belt, green passages, etc.), vertical green space (roofs and green walls) and expansive green space (types of parks, public and private gardens).
Hope to find at least green space for the welfare and welfare of the citizens of Qaemshahr.

title: Britain calls on social media to remove videos of crossing the Channel
text:
Britain has asked social media to remove videos of people crossing the English Channel (16 June 1400 – 6 June 2021) Image source, UK Home Secretary PA Media has called for social media to remove videos showing refugees crossing the Channel as "attractive" and encouraging them to cross.
Britain ’ s Interior Minister Priti Patel said in a letter to social media executives on Saturday that “videos ” of refugees crossing the English Channel from Europe to Britain were“ unacceptable ”.
Over the past week, hundreds of asylum seekers have crossed the Channel; five days ago, the Home Office confirmed that more than 568 people had crossed the Channel in four days.
Last Saturday alone, 336 people were taken off 19 boats and on Friday 144 on 7 boats.
The Home Office also said it was investigating reports that a British border patrol vessel had requested entry into French waters and that asylum seekers had been taken from a boat en route to Britain.
The British Home Secretary ’ s letter came after a widely circulated video on social media, including TikTok, showing a group of men crossing the English Channel.
The Interior Ministry says smugglers are using the video, which has been shared on Twitter, Instagram and Facebook, to advise desperate refugees to cross the Channel.
Ms Patel says the messages posted on social media that “promote this deadly crossing, and even make it look attractive, are unacceptable. ”
"These images encourage those in a safe European country to leave, putting their lives and their families at risk."
The UK Home Secretary says human traffickers are using the videos to promote their deadly trade.
The letter said: "What is not mentioned in the videos are those who lost their lives and that refugees must be stranded for at least 13 hours in an unfit boat in cold water."
The source, PA Media, said the British border boat had taken the refugees from the water, saying social media had made "great progress" in removing the videos, but that it needed to be done faster and more effectively so that more men, women and children did not die as they crossed the channel.
Less than a year ago, a family of five Iranians died crossing the Channel when the boat capsized: Rasoul Irannejad, 35, his wife, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, Anita Irannejad, 9, and Armin Irannejad, 6, died in the accident, and the body of their 15-month-old son was never found.
Britain ’ s Border Patrol says 83 people came to Britain on four boats last Friday alone.
The Home Office says it is fighting human trafficking gangs and has managed to stop some 4,000 asylum seekers from travelling to the UK last year.
The head of the refugee council says the government's measures are "not effective" and should instead "increase safe routes so people don't risk their lives".

title: What is the origin of the food crisis in Latin America?
text:
According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) website, the Latin American and Caribbean region produces enough food to meet the needs of all its inhabitants.
So the main problem with hunger in the region is not the lack of food, but the obstacles and difficulties faced by the poor to obtain it.
FAO Deputy General and Representative of the Organization for Latin America Julio Bardege told DW on the occasion of World Food Day that hunger in Latin America is due to insufficient income and significant economic inequality, which afflicts millions of people in the region.
According to a new report by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), food prices remained high for a seventh consecutive month in the last month of 2020, with dairy products and vegetable oils driving the biggest price increases.
According to the FAO, the rise in food prices was due to higher demand and weaker dollar values.
According to experts, although there is no pressure on food shortages, the impact of the epidemic on the supply chain and the restriction of traffic has caused damage to farms.
Latin America and the Caribbean, which produce more than 14 percent of the world ’ s food, are also looking to reshape their farming arrangements to feed 10 billion people by 2050.
However, the COVID-19 epidemic has caused an unprecedented setback in the region ’ s struggle against hunger, adding more than 20 million people to the ranks of poverty.
The unprecedented health crisis that has plagued the world for nearly two years has also hit Latin America.
Latin America, which was among the most vulnerable regions in the world due to the epidemic, has seen the spread of poverty and food shortages in recent decades, not only due to the spread of the coronavirus and the increase in deaths caused by it, but also due to numerous other factors such as climate change, mismanagement and the increasing deterioration of the labor market and sanctions.
The epidemic puts 45 million people in Latin America in a state of absolute poverty.
A situation that has sounded warnings and alarms about the lack of social security networks to reduce the consequences of the epidemic in Latin America.
The NGO Action Against Hunger reported a three-fold increase in the number of people suffering from food insecurity in Latin America in 2020 due to the outbreak of COVID-19.
In Peru, 80 percent of people lost their jobs or their incomes dropped by an average of 33 percent, according to the Humanitarian Institute ’ s survey.
The 20% drop in global food production due to climate change is another crisis that experts have warned of.
Studies show that climate change has reduced global food production by more than 20 percent in the past 60 years.
Farmers have one-fifth less food than they had in 1961; in warmer regions such as Latin America and Africa, the decline is up to 34 percent.
According to available data, the United States only sees growth of 5 to 15 percent, while the world's population is projected to reach 10 billion by 2050.
Climate change has changed the favorable conditions for growing crops and is hurting the food chain in the future.
Experts believe that temperature in plant growth and development is one of the important factors.
Temperature, along with the surface of light; carbon dioxide, temperature humidity, water and nutrients, affect the growth and ultimately the production of crops.
All of these factors need to be balanced.
While the global population continues to rise, a new study suggests that agricultural productivity has fallen sharply due to the effects of climate change.
On the other hand, some coercive measures by the hegemonic powers against the countries of the Latin American resistance, such as Venezuela, have exacerbated the food crisis in the region.
Along with mismanagement of the country ’ s food security, the impact of sanctions has affected 96 percent of Venezuelans, according to a new study.
The region ’ s response to the epidemic of the Director General of the Latin American Regional Agricultural Organization has increased despite the region ’ s worsening agricultural export unemployment during the epidemic.
In response to COVID-19 pandemic, the director of the Food and Agriculture Organization has sought to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of food production with a strategic approach, and has made a huge change in the agricultural sector with new regional initiatives.
The senior official of the agricultural organization of the region also emphasized the need for large-scale investments, especially in supply chain infrastructure and agricultural innovations, expressed hope about the region ’ s significant capacities, such as the enormous natural resources of the region, abundance of fresh water and fertile lands, as well as diverse ecosystems.
Despite this, the devastating effects of the epidemic will continue to plague the Latin American region.
Predictably, in most of these countries, rising debt due to the injection of emergency funds into the health sector and the provision of direct assistance to affected families and industrial sectors affected by the recession reduced economic activity by 7.7% in 2020.
The unemployment rate, which is the main cause of poverty, increased by 2.6 percent and with a significant portion of the workforce leaving, it reached 10.7 percent from its previous year in 2019.
In the same vein, because it was not possible for many jobs to work remotely, only 21.3 percent of those employed in the Latin American region were able to continue working this way.
According to the study, the highest unemployment rate was found in Peru (39.5%), Argentina (20.9%), Colombia (21.8%), Costa Rica (20.1%), and in the poorest households, informal work dominated.
According to the website Wordo Mitters, more than 33,581 million people in Latin America and the Caribbean have been infected with the coronavirus, and more than 1.2 million people have died from the disease.

title: COVID-19 Stress Increases Suicidal Tendency
text:
According to a study, COVID-19 pandemic has not only hit physical and economic health, but also affected mental health by increasing suicide rates.
A team of researchers from Cardiff University and the University of Swansea in Wales investigated which stressors associated with COVID-19 are likely to trigger suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
The survey involved more than 12,000 people who were asked to volunteer to share their experiences during the UK ’ s first quarantine period.
The results show that several stressors, such as social isolation, domestic abuse, relationship problems, adjustment of force, and financial problems, are strongly associated with suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
However, not everyone who experienced the condition reported suicidal thinking.
Those with high resistance and hope for the future were less affected by these pressures.
The researchers also discovered the important role that hope for the future can play — along with people ’ s levels of resistance — when coping with these stressors.
Read more at the end of the message.

title: It's a hell of a lot of weather for Madison!
text:
Mazandaran / ISNA, despite being a rainy region, has not been deprived of temperature changes, and this spring we saw more heat than we expected in this area, although some experts believe that dams can have favorable effects on climate adjustment.
For more than three decades, the issue of climate change has been raised globally and its effects and consequences are more or less evident. For this reason, the impact of climate change and the gradual process of global warming on development strategy in different areas has been more and more the focus of the authorities and scientific authorities, as water resources and energy fields to agriculture, food resources, health, forest and pasture and natural events such as floods and storms can be avoided. The climate is affected, although Mazandaran is a region with high rainfall, it is not without temperature changes, although some experts believe dams can play a very important role in climate adjustment.
Mohammad Reza Razavi said in an interview with ISNA that global warming is happening all over the world, but some countries, such as Iran, due to the use of fossil fuels and the lack of standard cars, are among the main polluting sources in the world.
He stated: The establishment of about a third of the country ’ s population on both sides of the Alborz, such as Mazandaran, Qazvin, Karaj, Tehran, Roudehen and Boomehen, has a significant impact on the heat.
Mazandaran Meteorological Director General, pointing out that last year was a warm year, noted that the average temperature in the past year was about 4.5 degrees increase, with the consequences of hot weather melting snow or preventing the occurrence of snow phenomenon can be mentioned.
Razavi said that Mazandaran has a strong dependence on mountain water resources such as Haraz River, Chalus, Sajjad Roud, Kelaroud River, and unfortunately, the warming of the air causes these rivers to become seasonal.
The official pointed out that in some provinces, although the rainfall is good, the snow melts suddenly, and sometimes in June the rivers dry, so turning the main rivers into seasonal rivers is not unexpected.
He pointed out that dam construction should be done before the seasonality of rivers, stressing that although environmental partners have considerations that do not allow the construction of dams anywhere, the construction of the dam causes adjustment of mountain climate and can prevent the seasonality of rivers.
Mazandaran Meteorological Director General, stating that the difference of one degree of temperature changes the regime of precipitation, added: "The world is seeking to allow only 1.5 degrees increase to the planet by the end of 2040, because with this one degree, the minimum increases and the maximum increases."
For example, in Mazandaran, a degree of reduced weather turns precipitation into snow, but if the same degree is lost, snow no longer occurs in the Mianband region.
Razavi continued: Climate change changes the time, location, intensity and duration of rainfall.
He pointed out that in addition to global warming, pollution is increasing sharply, noting: Last year, Mazandaran was one of the six polluted provinces of the country, one of the reasons for this was the Mazand Neka power plant, which produces about 4 percent of the country's electricity.
The Director General of Meteorology of Mazandaran added: "Travelling in Mazandaran increases waste, and unfortunately, garbage collectors start burning waste at dusk and night, and this cycle of pollution is constantly present in Mazandaran."
Razavi continued: Farmers burn straw and stubble about a month after harvesting the rice to create a second rice cultivation, which sometimes reaches 50 meters in view of the cities.
He said a more fundamental event in Mazandaran ’ s pollution is the plow and the groove again after the rice harvest for the second cultivation, and said: “The plow and groove again releases methane gas, which is 20 times more than carbon gas, which is able to maintain heat, that is, the land after the plough and groove gas that was hidden in the ground for 6 months, which it increases heating and pollution. ”
Mazandaran Meteorological Director General continued: "Continuation of this trend will lead to shorter winters, when cold and frost do not occur in the forests, some pests that die due to the cold will survive in the winter and cause problems such as the loss of swords."

title: World's most powerful magnet ready to join ITER fusion reactor
text:
The magnetic force of the world ’ s most powerful magnet is powerful enough to lift an aircraft carrier 2 meters into the air and is now on the verge of joining the world ’ s largest experimental fusion center.
The world ’ s strongest magnet is on the verge of joining the world ’ s largest experimental fusion center.
General Atomics, an American energy and defense company, is preparing to send the world ’ s first module of the world ’ s most powerful magnet, the Central Solenoid, to the world ’ s largest fusion center.
The magnet will become a vital component of the fusion reactor “ITER, ” a device that mimics the fusion power of the sun and is one of the most ambitious energy projects ever undertaken in the world.
The “ITER ” project is being built in 35 countries, including China, the European Union, India, Japan, Korea, Russia and the United States, in the south of France, and its mission is to demonstrate that the energy generated by hydrogen fusion can be created and managed, and that the materials needed to power global communities are readily available by hydrogen fusion in a carbon-free, safe and cost-effective manner.
Like almost any other project, the construction of ITER was hampered by the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, but it has made nearly 75 percent progress so far.
Its massive and unique components have been brought to France from three continents over the past 15 months, and when they come together, they will form the ITER Tokamak reactor, or the Sun on Earth, which will exhibit industrial-scale fusion.
Large magnets are needed to capture plasma in the tokamak, a fusion device in vacuum space.
ITER ’ s largest magnet, Central Solenoid, is made up of six modules and is one of the most important U.S. contributions to the ITER project.
The magnet is 18 meters long, 4.25 meters wide and weighs 1,000 tons.
This magnet is used to generate a powerful current in the plasma “ITER, ” which helps shape and control the fusion reaction during long pulses.
The magnetic force of the large magnet is strong enough to lift an aircraft carrier two meters into the air, and at its core it will have a magnetic field strength of 13 Tesla, which is approximately 280,000 times greater than the Earth ’ s magnetic field.
In addition, the support structures of this magnet must withstand forces comparable to twice the thrust of a space shuttle.
General Atomics completed the final test of its first module earlier this year, and this week it will be placed in a heavy-duty truck and then loaded onto a ship heading to the south of France, marking the beginning of an exciting story.
Dr Michael Mauel, from Columbia University, said: “The delivery of the first module of this magnet to ITER is an exciting milestone for the demonstration of fusion energy as well as a demonstration of the extraordinary success of the United States in building very large, high-field, high-energy superconducting magnets.
He added that the company ’ s success in manufacturing, testing and delivering superconducting magnets for fusion energy is a major breakthrough for the United States and will ensure fusion power is realized in the future.
End of message.

title: Ontario court ruling on Ukrainian plane
text:
According to the report of Human Rights Headquarters IRNA on Wednesday, the webinar on “Judicial Procedure Investigation in Aviation Accidents with Emphasis on the Ukrainian Aircraft Accident ” was held in continuation of the series of meetings of the International Claims Working Group of Human Rights Headquarters and the International Deputy of the Judiciary.
In this meeting, Hadi Mahmoudi, assistant professor of Shahid Beheshti University, after describing the history of aviation accidents that occurred with the involvement of military forces, examined the applicable rights in these cases and the international procedures of this issue.
According to Mohammadi, the rights applicable in these incidents can be divided into two categories of interstate relations and private relations.
Referring to the rights applicable in international relations, he stated: Among the general international rules, the Charter of the United Nations, especially paragraph 4 of Article 2 and Article 51, can be cited, and in particular the special rules of international law of the Chicago Convention, the Montreal Convention of 1971 and finally the European Convention on Human Rights, and the various obstacles that can be followed.
Emphasizing the sensitivity of the issue of compliance of the rules of each of these conventions with the incident, Mahmoudi said: "Given the secondary rules of international law, the intentional or unintentional commission of this incident cannot have an impact on the type of international responsibility of the Iranian government, but it may only have consequences for the payment of compensation."
Investigating the disqualification of the Canadian courts in the case of the Ukrainian aircraft, the assistant professor of the University of Judicial Sciences evaluated the competency basis of the Canadian courts ’ investigation of the case from the perspective of international law and domestic law, and said that the Canadian government has followed a wrong approach based on the US government, which has not been approved by international bodies and other governments.
Hossein Khalaf Rezaei, emphasizing that this was explicitly mentioned in the International Court of Justice ’ s decision in the case of Germany against Italy, said: “In fact, the court in this decision states that the US government ’ s practice in violation of the immunity of governments has not been accepted by other governments, so the court implicitly states that the US government ’ s practice is contrary to international rules. ”
He added that on this basis, the International Court of Justice has determined that the Italian courts ’ action to investigate alleged crimes by the Nazi army in this country is contrary to the principle of judicial immunity of governments.
Assistant Professor of Judicial Sciences University, emphasizing on the violation of the Canadian government ’ s immunity in the judicial process, referred to similar votes that have been made before the Canadian courts and rejected due to lack of jurisdiction, saying: “Among these cases, one of them is the case of Buzari and Kazemi, which in both cases, the jurisdiction of the Canadian courts is not approved. ”
But the turning point of the basis of the jurisdiction of the Canadian courts should be considered in the 2012 law, according to which the jurisdiction of the Canadian courts has been widely seen, hence, unlike previous cases, the Ontario Canadian court considers itself competent in dealing with the Ukrainian aircraft case.
Vahid Bazar, an international law researcher, referred to the Ontario court ’ s decision and said: “In this case, four Iranian individuals are wanted to fight, and the defendant is the Iranian government and the Iranian authorities, although what is read in the petition is different from the cases mentioned in the vote. ”
Despite the competency flaws in the case, he said the main objection to the verdict was the foundations and citations of the court, adding: instead of citing the official documents in this regard, the Ontario court has relied on reports and issued a verdict on the same basis, which is undoubtedly highly critiqued in legal terms.
The international law researcher went on to address the issue of compensation and, with a glimpse of the government ’ s practice of compensation, pointed out that although some international documents have mentioned amounts, there is no significant practice in this regard.
Bezar also examined the US government ’ s compensation in the case of Iranian Airbus, saying that in that case, the US government paid compensation to the victims without accepting responsibility for the incident.
The amount of compensation paid by the US government to the victims of the Airbus case cannot be cited in the case of the Ukrainian plane because the specificity of the agreement is explicitly stated.

text:
The 20-billion-euro power plant, called ITER, simulates the same reactions that occur in the sun, and aims to prove that power generation by nuclear fusion is possible on a commercial scale.
Now General Atomics, a U.S. energy and defense company, is preparing to send the world ’ s most powerful magnet, the Central Solenoid, to the plant in France.
The magnet becomes a major component of the ITER fusion reactor.
The ITER fusion reactor is a device that simulates the fusion power of the sun and is one of the most ambitious energy projects ever undertaken in the world.
The Central Solenoid magnet consists of six modules and is one of the most important contributions of the United States to the design of the ITER reactor.

The magnetic force of this large magnet can lift an aircraft carrier up to 2 meters into the air.
At its core, the magnet will have a magnetic field strength of 13 Tesla, which is approximately 280,000 times greater than the Earth ’ s magnetic field.
In addition, the support structures of the magnet must withstand forces comparable to the thrust of a space shuttle twice.
ITER is being built in the south of France in 35 countries, including China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the United States, and its mission is to demonstrate that hydrogen fusion energy can be created and managed to provide the electricity needed by global communities in a carbon-free, safe and cost-effective manner.
Construction of the ITER fusion reactor has been hampered by the COVID-19 pandemic, but so far it has made nearly 75 percent progress.
Its large and unique components have been brought to France from three continents over the past 15 months and, when brought together, will form the ITER reactor, which will demonstrate industrial-scale fusion.
General Atomics completed final testing of the first module earlier this year, and the magnet will be placed in a heavy-duty truck this week and then shipped on a ship to southern France.
The nuclear fusion plant, the first to use ultra-hot plasma, is expected to be completed by the end of 2025 and begin generating electricity.
The promise of using nuclear fusion is that it can produce unlimited, clean energy, but despite 60 years of research, it must overcome the technical challenges of harnessing very high amounts of energy.
In nuclear fusion, heavy hydrogen atoms combine to release an enormous amount of energy, but doing so would require a temperature of 150 million degrees Celsius, 10 times hotter than the core of the Sun.
Hydrogen fuel comes from seawater and only a few grams is enough, but nuclear fusion requires massive magnets to harness ultra-high-temperature plasma in a doughnut-shaped vacuum chamber called a tokamak.
This process, like conventional nuclear fission reactors, does not produce the carbon dioxide gas that contributes to global warming.
The advantage of fusion reactors is that they have no risk of melting and produce a much smaller amount of radioactive waste.

title: When the Yellow Series Affects Literature
text:
Einle Gharib, who believes that literature has been influenced by media art, says that the low-quality yellow series has caused us to know or not know the literature of a country.
In an interview with ISNA, the translator said about the situation of translating Persian literary works into other languages: In the field of translating Persian literary works into Turkish, I should say that fortunately Persian classics have been translated from the past into Turkish, and fortunately, these works are well known in Turkey and are mostly reprinted.
But contemporary Persian literary works, especially fiction and novels, have been translated very little.
He added that translation is very popular in Turkey and is not comparable to Iran, to the extent that some Turkish publishers have contracts with international publishing companies that are translated into Turkish at the same time as the work is published in the original language.
If we compare this situation with Iran, we can say that nothing from Persian is translated into Turkish or translated by a great distance, except when it is individual and special.
For example, there are many Armenians in Turkey, and for this reason, most of Ms. Pirzad ’ s work has been translated in Turkey.
There are a lot of leftists, and that ’ s why the major works of Samad are translated into color.
Or the book "I Love Manchester United" has been translated and published because of the translator's acquaintance with Mr. Yazdani Khorram.
But in general, systematic and methodical work is not done in the field of translating Persian literary works into Turkish.
Gharib said that unfortunately literature or all the arts have been influenced by media art, adding: "The driving force behind the intensification of the familiarity of Iranians with Turkey and their culture has been most of the Turkish series, and if we look from the perspective of someone like me who specializes in the philosophy of art, it is annoying that the yellow series not so high quality causes us to know the literature of a country or not."
But believe it or not, this is the case, and a significant group of general audiences have become familiar with Turkish culture in the past 10 years.
The translator also pointed to other artistic reasons that have made the Iranian people familiar with Turkish literature and culture: for example, Orhan Pamuk ’ s Nobel Prize was another factor that was very influential in Iranians ’ familiarity with Turkish literature.
But perhaps it is not arrogant to say that the works that have been translated by me and a few other Turkish translators in recent years have also contributed to this acquaintance.
For example, my first work was published 10 or 12 years ago, at that time even Pamuk had not received a Nobel Prize, and people did not know Turkish literature very well, and then it was translated by a number of translators into capable books of Turkish literature.
But even though it bothers me, I have to admit that the general audience is the first one, not the specific one.
The university professor said that if the classification is done, the main reason for the reception of the general audience of Turkish literature is the series and the award by the authors of the country, said: "The fact that Elif Shafak sells more in Iran than in Turkey should be measured from the perspective of the audience sociology, because these are really weak books, but the problem is that our audience mainly likes these types of yellow psychology books.
Just as Elif Shafak is selling, Jojo Moyes is selling, and these types of writers seem to be getting more attention.
Gharib continued: Some of the books that I have translated from Turkish have been writers who have accepted most of the European indicators, but have not been welcomed by the audience in Iran.
I think part of this is also related to us translators, if we are literary translators and we don ’ t pay attention to selling books, we have to wait and do things like that.
He went on to say that most translators translate Turkish works from English, saying: "Some people look more commercial in the name of literary translators, and this makes the general audience think that Turkish literature is of this type."
Both publishers and translators have to work hard and choose serious work because it will affect the public in the long run.
In response to a question about re-translation, Einle Gharib also stated: “I do not go for re-translation, but there is a commercial system in translation. ”
The author or the book is a great deal of value and literary sales, and some of the people who unfortunately call them translators or publishers tend to these works; it may be natural, but this is not art.
The main reason for this is that such books are guaranteed to sell.
But since they cannot admit it, they criticize the translator and the previous publisher in the simplest and most obscene way possible.
This has happened to me too.
Some of my books have been translated, and I, the publication of my source and editor, have rejected the Yazdani Khorram.
We went to Turkey last year and got the copyright from Pamuk himself, but it ’ s still not over because much of it has nothing to do with literature.
It may not be the first book to be translated, or it may be the first book to be translated.
We know that the book of Revelation is a good one, and it is a good one.
Unfortunately, most of our translations are like this, and someone like Nikki Karimi dares to re-translate a book that Shamlu has translated, which is really no longer related to literature.
Emphasizing that we do not have an opinion on translation, Gharib said: "We still think there is no more translation, and that is the same English system, that is, word-for-word translation with the help of dictionaries; that is, we think that whoever learns a language can translate, and language learning is required."
If we accept that there are different translations and translation methods and we have a theoretical discussion on this issue, then each translator can tell which method they are working in, and if the translator does not accept this method, they can translate it in another way.
Because we don ’ t have such a thing in Iran, translations happen according to non-objective indicators.

Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, referring to the report, said the official Islamic Republic ’ s version of the incident was “inconsistent, misleading and superficial, deliberately ignoring key factors ” and that if the outcome of the negotiations with Iran is not acceptable, Canada will go to the International Court of Justice.
The Ukrainian plane with flight number PS-752, January 8, 2019 was shot down by at least two IRGC defense missiles and all 176 people on board died.
The Islamic Republic denied shooting down the flight for three days, but after the US, Australia, Canada and the UK published evidence, it finally admitted under international pressure that the plane had been shot down by the IRGC ’ s missile defense system, but claimed that the incident was caused by “human error. ”
According to the Canadian government, there is no evidence that the strike was deliberate and “planned, ” but“ it does not in any way exclude Iran from responsibility for the deaths of 176 innocent people ” and “Iran bears the burden of providing the ultimate response to all aspects of the disaster. ”
The Canadian prime minister has insisted that "it is not easy to blame the downing of the plane on a few minor personnel" and that Iranian government officials whose decisions "led to this disaster" should not be allowed to hide behind them.
He referred to the final report of the Civil Aviation Organization on the incident, which did not directly come from the Revolutionary Guards and was blamed for the incident, only "the air defense system user", but the name or details of this "user" were not included in the report.
The Association of Families of the Victims of Flight PS752 also released a statement on Thursday, July 23, welcoming the report of the Canadian government ’ s investigation team, calling it “the crimes, secrecy and lies of the Islamic Republic. ”
The association, which works to “demand justice for this crime, ” has repeatedly emphasized that no one will accept compensation from the Islamic Republic as long as the leaders and perpetrators are not punished.
The Iranian government has previously said that in this case, indictments have been issued for “10 officials ” who were“ involved ” in the downing of the Ukrainian passenger plane, but the association of the families of those killed in the flight of Ukraine are nameless and “the main perpetrators of this crime, who are top officials of the government, have been issued a ban on prosecution. ”
In its new statement, the association said that the referral of the case to the International Court of Justice can be encouraging, calling the Canadian government ’ s decision to investigate an important but insufficient step that “cannot reach a final conclusion in the investigation of the events that took place on January 8. ”
The PS752 Dead Families Association has also called on the Canadian government to “recognize the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization ” and“ enforce targeted Magnitsky sanctions [Magnitsky Act] on the perpetrators of this crime ” and, in addition to discussing the referral of the case to the international court, “pursue the case in the domestic criminal court. ”
The phrase “Magnitsky Targeted Sanctions ” refers to a law passed by the US government in 1992 named after Russian anti-corruption lawyer Sergei Magnitsky and targeted human rights violators.

title: Go to the virtual Mars tour and see the stamina
text:
According to NASA, the NASA space agency posted a photo on its account an hour ago: "Know the location of the Mars Endurance rover on Mars.
Astronomy enthusiasts can visit NASA ’ s official site to see the map posted on the site and find out the location of the rover.
NASA said in a statement: "With this map, you can see the last place and route the Mars Endurance rover traveled at the crater of the island.
The Mars Endurance mission on the Red Planet is NASA ’ s most advanced and newest rover, designed by NASA ’ s scientists and engineers to carry out scientific missions.
For these missions, the rover has brought many scientific instruments to Mars, all of which are NASA ’ s most advanced instruments for research and exploration on other planets.
The equipment that has gone into space by Endurance includes ground-penetrating radar, spectrometers for soil composition analysis, panoramic and close-up cameras to capture images of the Red Planet ’ s surface, and instruments to produce oxygen from carbon dioxide.
All of these tools are designed to make future exploration by robots and humans easier and more efficient.
The mission to Mars serves two purposes.
One of these goals is scientific research to understand the Martian environment as well as to investigate the habitability of the planet.
The second goal is to collect samples of Martian soil and bring it back to Earth.
Another NASA mission to Mars in 2026 plans to bring test tubes collected by the endurance to Earth for further research.
The Endurance currently resides in the crater of the island on Mars, which is 28 miles long and holds old dry river deposits.
Researchers believe that 3.5 billion years ago the crater of the island was a large lake with a delta.
They say that although the lake dried up a long time ago, somewhere in the crater or 2,000-foot wall, there may have been signs of life in the past.
End of message.

The sixth episode shows a clash between "terrorists" and Turkish forces in northern Iraq, and the seventh episode shows a militant who vows to avenge his friend who was killed by Turkish forces.
The final episode of the series is an allusion to Eren Belbel, a boy who was said to have been killed in northern Turkey in 2017 by the "illegal" Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK).

Turkish TV series are popular around the world, and this episode shows agents sitting next to a young boy named Eren on a plane.
He said: “The Yankees have always been very brave.

The PKK has been fighting the government for decades for greater autonomy for the Kurdish minority in Turkey.
The party is on the list of terrorist organizations in Turkey, the United States and the European Union.
Turkey has carried out several operations against the group in northern Iraq.
In January, the Turkish Interior Ministry announced the start of "Operation Ern" against the PKK "in memory of Ern Nightingale, who was martyred by the separatists of the terrorist organization."
The foreign policy of Mitt ’ s characters repeatedly underscore the importance of patriotism as they fight the opposition.
In the opening scene of the first episode, neo-Nazis in Germany lead the attack on a house owned by Turkish immigrants, leaving Mitt's future agent Sardar orphaned.
The source of the image, TRT explaining the picture, the attack on Turkish immigrants in a scene from the series apparently refers to the Salingen attack.

A diplomat promised to bring Sardar to Turkey after the raid.
When Sardar says he has no one, the diplomat replies, “You have your country. ”
The camera then focuses on the diplomatic ring, which has an image of the Turkish flag engraved on it.
The series ’ tenth episode, after a character asks about Turkey ’ s presence in Syria, focuses on Turkey ’ s military policies in the region.
“What are Italy, France, the United States and Russia doing there?
What is China doing there? ”
Another officer, referring to the Ottoman period, added: “The place we call Syria has been a part of the motherland for the last 100 years. ”
The comments echoed what Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in March 2020: “They ask what Turkey is doing in Syria.
But they don ’ t ask other countries that question. ”
The ninth episode shows a conversation between two agents and a local man in the Greek city of Kozani, reflecting the Turkish government ’ s criticism of the Greek government.
The man says, “They [the Greeks] don ’ t want us to have the rights of minorities.
Everyone is working to take children away from their own language, religion and culture. ”
Western Thrace Muslims in Greece are the cause of tensions between Turkey and Greece, and Ankara often accuses Athens of violating minority rights.
The impact of the series has attracted attention on social media and social media.

Each episode had more than three million viewers on YouTube, and people made passionate comments about it.
One of the comments at the bottom of the last part reads: "[This message] was sent throughout the whole series: Don't go head-to-head with the Turkish government."
High-ranking security expert Mathew Yarar praised the series for showcasing the “advances ” of the Turkish intelligence agency, the technology used in warfare and covert operations.
But some critics discredited the series as a "propaganda" series.
One user wrote, “This series is entirely a propaganda series for the ruling Justice and Development Party. ”
TV critic Sina Kluoğlu in the Milliat newspaper added: “Advertising in this type of series is natural.
The point is that it should be done cautiously. ”
Internationally Benefit?
Formation is one of several T.R.T. series that deal with national and religious issues in parallel with the government ’ s vision.
The series, centering on its story, the founder of the Ottoman Empire, gained international fame with its religious flavour and heroic stories.
The recently released “Bir Zamanlar Kibris ” depicts attacks on the island ’ s Gravey-Turkish family in 1963 before Turkey ’ s controversial intervention.

Many of our products have attracted the attention of international viewers in recent years.

title: Luhansk region and the values of European parks
text:
I remember the ambivalent feelings when I saw how in Prague or Warsaw locals play football in parks, organize exhibitions or sports competitions.
Ukraine still lives on the Soviet imperative: "do not walk on the lawns", with all the ensuing consequences.
The essence of the European "park" paradigm is that such territories are not considered only as places for green spaces.
These are full-fledged public spaces open to people coming with different goals and interests.
Including for physical education and sports.
In the Luhansk region launched an innovative portal that will promote the region Based on this, the requirements for the park as a place of socialization are applicable.
It should be interesting for a teenager on a skateboard, and for a mother with a stroller.
It seems to me that our people are already ready to perceive a new park culture, with a synthesis of environmental and utilitarian functions.
Finding for yourself an opportunity to retire, and a space for communication, and – involvement in the cultural landscape.
In this context, we are trying to fit the program of creating a network of sports grounds in the Luhansk region within the framework of the national project of the President "Healthy Country".
Its essence is in the creation of new public spaces on the territory of local communities.
Not just sports, but universal, for interesting pastime of different social groups.
We have already received funds for 52 sites, and in two years we expect to build 215.
80% of the cost will be provided by the state, subject to 20% co-financing by the community and the region.
The most effective and initiative communities will receive the right to participate in the project.
See also See Paris and the Maldives without going abroad: 5 places in Ukraine, where you have not been yet Provide for the creation of a navigation map for the active involvement of different age groups.
We will install information stands and QR codes on the simulators to watch video instructions of the exercises through a smartphone.
We will provide a unified concept and design of sites.
We will make the highest environmental and safety requirements to minimize the risk of accidents.
Attracting public investment in the construction of health infrastructure is not just a mechanism for updating existing simulators.
This is an attempt to instill in the Luhansk region the European trends of public park spaces.
A significant part of the sports grounds will be placed in areas with green spaces or in places where they will be equipped in the future.
It can be small squares or front gardens, which will appear thanks to new sports locations.
This format, by the way, corresponds to the modern trend of leaving one central park.
European urbanists believe that for the balanced development of territories in the context of decentralization, in addition to the main, the so-called pocket parks in different parts of the community are important.
This provides aesthetic pleasure and stimulates the physical activity of local residents.
At the same time, natural ecosystems are comprehensively protected and local communities are economically strengthened.
The weak point of park zones in Ukraine is their actual availability at certain hours.
The downside of this phenomenon is their attraction to anti-social elements.
The presence of sports infrastructure will increase their public value and eliminate security risks.
And over time, it will instill life there and help attract investments.

title: Mini-gardens with wildflowers will improve the life of butterflies and bees in Moscow — World news today NTD
