Wildflowers and a gravel path.
Such a mini-garden called “Memories of the Meadow ” grew up in one Moscow courtyard.
It was broken in the framework of a natural project, which was launched by biologist Nadezhda Kiyatkina.
[Nadezhda Kiyatkina, biologist]: “Common mullein, dye-dyed bathing, acute-flowered broom – all these are our local plants of the Moscow region.
We specially selected them so that, on the one hand, it was beautiful flowering plants, quite decorative, on the other hand, were exclusively local species.
Because only native species can support our butterflies, bees, and beyond. ”
Bringing the idea to life helped the residents of the yard.
They allocated more than 90 thousand rubles for the creation of two gardens - solar and shadow.
The project participants hope that people will love local plants, and landscape designers will use them more often in their work.
In addition, the mini-gardens will allow the city not to turn into a concrete island, not suitable for the life of insects and birds.
[Elena Shelyagina, biologist]: “In order for the city not to become such an obstacle, it is important for us that nature also existed in this city and that it was not just in the form of large pieces, but in the form of beads that string these natural territories like a necklace and thereby allow organisms to move, multiply, enrich and so on. ”
Some plants for the gardens were provided free of charge by nurseries, including the Botanical Garden of Moscow State University.
[Alexander Rappoport, Deputy Director of the Botanical Garden of Moscow State University]: “In the era of globalization, very little remains of something of its own.
And just these local species can give some special place.
Still, we have cultural roots, some kind of architecture in the middle zone of Russia. ”
Now the gardens are taken care of by the locals.
[Vladimir Krasyuk, a resident of Moscow]: “For me personally, this is more of a social mission, because I want to communicate more, interact with residents of the house, yard, district.

It ’ s very cool and interesting. ”
Participants in the experiment want to inspire people to create mini-gardens with wildflowers in their yards.

title: In the Southern Urals, business came up with how to develop medical tourism
text:
According to South Ural entrepreneurs, public-private partnership can contribute to the expansion of the presence of business in the field of social services.
For example, such their type as medical tourism is not yet developing too actively, while the country has set a goal to quadruple the export of health services by 2024 - up to a million dollars a year.
What business and the authorities of the Chelyabinsk region should do for this, the correspondent of "RG" found out.
There are also a lot of non-resident patients in Yekaterinburg.
After the procedures, they could not be bored in the hospital, but to see the sights.
Photo: Tatyana Andreeva / RG Better you to us In the Southern Urals, dentists began to attract patients "from the outside", then ophthalmologists, traumatologists, and other narrow specialists began to occupy market niches.
There are also multi-purpose centers that receive visitors.
This even caused talk that, they say, strangers will create a queue, and there are not enough medical facilities for their own...
Such fears are devoid of grounds, said the vice-president of the Chelyabinsk branch of the “Support of Russia ” candidate of medical Sciences Alexei Larin.
Yes, he notes, there are problems with the primary link in the region, they must be solved.
But in the field of specialized assistance, there is a reserve - it is possible to increase its volumes several times rather quickly.
Dmitry Dovbnya, Chairman of the Committee on Tourism of the Chelyabinsk branch of OPORA, notes: it is necessary to distinguish between medical exports and tourism.
The first is tied exclusively to the consumption of medical services: residents of other regions or countries came, received assistance, left back.
The range of services of the second is wider.
For example, there are procedures, such as IVF, that require the patient to live near the clinic for some time.
Waiting he "compensates" acquaintance with the city, its sights.
Sanatorium patients are even more active in this regard.
The districts of Sochi and Kavminvod have long demonstrated how beneficial the arrival of people whose goal is to improve their health can be for the territory.
This experience should be used in the Southern Urals, which was once the health resort of the entire industrial Urals: local lakes went from Yekaterinburg, Tyumen, Perm, northern regions, those who are contraindicated in a sharp change in climate.
The task of the business is to expand the range of purely tourist services for such guests.
When the South Urals go to be treated in other regions, this is also medical tourism, but at the same time the Chelyabinsk region loses an amount close to a billion rubles.
Irina Gekht, the first vice-governor in charge of social issues, draws attention to the fact that along with the export of medical services there are also imports.
When the South Urals go to be treated in other regions, this is also medical tourism, but at the same time the Chelyabinsk region loses an amount close to a billion rubles.
Therefore, it is interested in attracting consumers of services from other regions, for the provision of which it has the necessary competencies.
Speech, in particular, about transplantation, pediatric neurosurgery, a number of other areas where Chelyabinsk doctors work at the level of European standards.
Alexey Larin lists: private clinics of the region are able to provide high-tech assistance in the field of oncology, ophthalmology, traumatology and orthopedics, obstetrics and gynecology...
What attracts foreign patients?
In some countries, Dmitry Dovbnya notes, due to traditional specifics or policies aimed at limiting the birth rate, a number of medical services have been banned.
In China, it is in vitro fertilization, in Arab countries - laser treatment.
Residents of China are also interested in dental services - here they are cheaper than in their homeland.
Among the clients of private medicine, there are many former compatriots who left for Germany, Israel, scattered around the world.
They often visit relatives, and the price and quality of medical services encourage them to seek help in Chelyabinsk clinics: in developed countries, similar treatment for the family budget is much more burdensome.
Frequent guests in medical institutions of the region and residents of Kazakhstan.
Moreover, it is they who form the main flow from the near abroad.
Director and chief physician of the private medical center Elena Kolyada said that 95 percent of all international appeals to her institution are accounted for by residents of the neighboring republic.
Among the most popular services are IVF, surgical treatment, polyclinic examination, pediatrician consultations.
Many, as, indeed, all over the world, are concerned about prevention - comprehensive examination programs have been developed for such tourists.
Unfortunately, there are no statistics in the field of medical tourism in the region yet.
Each institution counts its own figures, for example, for the clinic Elena Kolyada this market annually grows by 10-15 percent.
Coordinator of international internships of the Ural Society of Aesthetic Medicine Specialists Irina Kuznetsova says that everything depends on the profile of the medical institution - for some, the growth reaches 25-32 percent.
To spur the development of exports can create a unique product that does not exist in other territories.
For the firm headed by Irina, this was an international project involving Italian surgeons invited to Russia: they provide high-tech care to patients, including those with severe post-traumatic consequences.
It is clear that the goal of the development of medical tourism, as well as any other services, is additional financial revenues to the budgets of clinics, the city, the region.
After all, Russians from other regions "bring" with them funding through compulsory health insurance, foreigners - "live" money.
At the same time, even in state medical institutions, the receipt of extra-budgetary funds can increase many times.
However, representatives of Opora Rossii believe that private clinics should be the basis for the development of the export direction, since the main function of public health is social.
But public-private partnership will clearly benefit the industry, especially when it comes to creating infrastructure, acquiring expensive equipment. - The modern world is generally moving towards car sharing: when you use, but do not own.
This principle can open a second wind to medical entrepreneurship, which remains the marketing of the product, its promotion, - says Dmitry Dovbnya. - We would like business to complement the system that already exists, - develops the idea of Irina Gekht, - maybe offering assistance that the state does not provide so professionally, as a socially oriented non-profit organization does, engaged, for example, in the rehabilitation of children with autism.
Officials are ready to include entrepreneurs providing such services in state support programs: to reduce taxes for them, to provide subsidies, to open access to the compulsory medical insurance system.
And similar examples in the region already exist, one of them is a Magnitogorsk company that carries out early diagnosis of oncological diseases.
But before spreading the experience, the authorities want to understand how many social entrepreneurs there are in the region, in what areas they work, and how effective they are.
The next stage is the creation of a self-regulatory organization uniting social business, or a state structure under the auspices of the regional government.
The Russian capitals have already reached this level of development: in St. Petersburg, the medical tourism agency was created under the regional Ministry of Health, in Moscow it exists as a private initiative, but also works effectively.
Expanding the export of health services will require other interactions.
On the one hand, you will need new hotels, hostels where patients can stay, new tourist products, and this is an uncultivated field for business.
On the other hand, logistics and infrastructure development will have to be addressed.
So it is impossible to do without cooperation with the authorities.
According to the Medical Tourism Index (MTI), by 2025, the turnover of this market in the world will exceed three trillion dollars.
The annual increase is estimated at a minimum of 25 percent.
Among the most popular countries among tourists going for medical care are Canada, Great Britain, Israel, Italy, Germany, France, South Korea, Singapore, India.
Russia is not yet among the leaders of such ratings, but experts believe that it has great potential.

title: Lake Vyrlitsa: reserve, or recreation area for Kyiv residents
text:
All parties agree that the lake should benefit the residents of the city In Kiev, discussions continue around the largest in the capital of the lake Vyrlitsa, reports Apostrophe.
The local authorities have been trying to make the right decision about his fate for several weeks in a row.
On the positive side, the fate of the lake in the most densely populated area of the city is in the focus of attention of all participants in the discussion, and the mayor and deputies give the opportunity to all parties to conduct a dialogue within the walls of the KSCA.
Now the main task of the deputies of the Kyiv Council is to decide what status the lake and its shore should receive, as well as to answer an equally important question - who will finance the necessary measures for the preservation of the lake and the improvement of the embankment.
After all, all participants in the discussion agree that the state of the lake is deteriorating from year to year and it accumulates unsafe chemicals and debris.
Be always up to date with the telegram channel Quick Focus.
Today, there are two main positions, polar in implementation, but solidary in one: the lake must be preserved and made accessible and comfortable for the people of Kiev.
Yevgenia Kuleba, a deputy of the Kyiv City Council, and eco-activists insist on creating a landscape reserve in Vyrlitsa to preserve the existing ecosystem of the lake.
Representatives of the community and business are sure that the reserve will not allow people to use the recreational potential of the lake - it is necessary to preserve the islands of nature, but add a well-equipped embankment with recreational infrastructure for citizens next to them.
On July 13, two events took place in the building of the Kyiv Council, within the framework of which the issue of Lake Vyrlitsa was discussed: a meeting of the environmental commission of the Kyiv Council and the working group of the permanent land use commission, where the issue of Vyrlitsa was discussed.
The discussion was hot but constructive.
The result of the working group, which was supported by the head of the environmental commission Denis Moskal, and the chairman of the commission on architecture, urban planning and land relations Mikhail Terentyev, was a protocol decision.
The essence of which is to collect from all relevant commissions of the Kivsovet and departments of the City Hall, representatives of the Metropolitan, KP "Pleso", tenants of coastal areas additional information, discuss it, and only then make a comprehensive and balanced decision in the interests of the residents of the capital.
The first is the legal procedure for granting the status of a landscape reserve, which was noted by the representative of the Department of Land Resources and the Deputy of the Kyiv Council, Chairman of the Standing Commission on Architecture, Urban Planning and Land Relations Mikhail Terentyev.
“The question is that the draft decision, any draft that is adopted by Kievrad at its meeting, could not in any case be challenged.
That's what I'm worried about.
So that the whole procedure was fully followed and all the necessary approvals were carried out, ” Mikhail Terentyev commented.
According to the law on the Nature Reserve Fund of Ukraine, the project of the reserve, and not only graphic materials, as in the case of Vyrlytsia, must be approved by the Kyiv State Administration.
What has not been done.
The second is the need to protect the nearest metro branch from flooding.
Creating a landscape reserve will make it impossible any work on shore protection in the future.
And such a need is already ripe - according to the deputy general director of "Kyivmetrobud" Oleg Borisov, if you do not strengthen the coastline of Vyrlitsa, it can threaten serious consequences for this metro line.
“The station itself (Vyrlitsa metro station – auth.) – when it was opened in March 2006, it had to be closed in July, as the station was constantly flooded.
It continues to flood, flood protection is activated.
Tunnels were built in the 90s of the last century, and then insulation materials were calculated for a service life of 15 years.
Therefore, we all need to be prepared that soon we will have to allocate large enough funds to prevent future flooding, ” he said.
It turned out that initially the artificial lake Vyrlitsa, which previously occupied only 10 hectares, and now increased to 90 hectares, were going to fall asleep for the construction of a depot.
But due to the extension of the metro line and flooding, this idea was abandoned.
The third is the issue of land lease.
The fact is that the company "Mriya-Invest", which leased several land plots near the lake Vyrlitsa, in 2010 ended the lease term of one of the land plots.
Eco-activists believe that the company no longer has the right to lease land near Lake Vyrlitsa.
Representative of the enterprise Alexander Krupnik believes, on the contrary.
According to him, the company over the past three years has paid to the local budget more than 30 million hryvnias only rent for land and the company has submitted documents for the extension of the lease of the land, but the Kiev authorities have not yet made their decision.
Lawyers in the hall - participants of the discussion clarified that if the tenant continues to use the land, fulfills its financial obligations and no other decisions were made on the leased plots, the lease is considered to be extended.
The fourth is whether there is any funding at all and who has to implement measures to preserve the lake and improve its shore.
“Any discussion is always good and the community of Kiev is grateful to the deputies of the Kiev Council and Yevgenia Kulebe that the lake Vyrlitsa finally worried and this issue is discussed at such a high level.
The only thing is that it is important to understand who will fund any changes adopted as a result of the discussion.
There is no financial justification in the draft decision on recognition of Vyrlitsa as a landscape reserve.
Pleso, under whose authority they want to transfer the lake, will be able to allocate money for it?
Or do we get the same thing we have around other lakes?
And this is nothing.
Due to the lack of funding, ” said a member of the Public Council at the Darnitskaya RSA Alexander Kulabukhov.
There are no answers to the main questions yet.
Therefore, after considering the issues of Lake Vyrlitsy, the working group decided not to hurry and take time to understand the situation in more detail.
What about abroad?
Around the world, the issues of supporting the volumes of the "green" fund at the proper level in the context of the development of modern megacities are always the most controversial.
How to keep in a big city a sufficient number of corners of wildlife, while ensuring that the needs of its residents in modern infrastructure are met at the same time?
What should be the priority - the needs of citizens, or, flora and fauna living in the discussed "green" territories?
Usually, when such topics are raised in public discourse, as in our country, two polar points of view prevail – from “everything for people as the city develops ” to“ everything for nature ”.
But in most cases, the truth is somewhere in the middle.
So, in German Hamburg there are lakes with minimal construction of such areas, for example, Lake Stadpark in the park of the same name, and then completely surrounded by lake buildings, like Binnenalster and Alster, in the immediate vicinity of which there are department stores, residential buildings and various social and cultural objects, such as the Hamburg Picture Gallery.
Therefore, in light of the accumulated issues to both one and the other initiatives on Lake Vyrlitsa, the decision of the Kiev authorities to postpone and publicly find a compromise in this matter can be considered, at the moment, the most balanced.
Given that such a decision the fate of the lake will be determined at least for several decades ahead.
We will continue to monitor how events unfold.

title: In the United States, in the midst of the pandemic, the death rate from overdose reached a record 93 thousand
text:
In the United States, in the midst of the pandemic, overdose deaths reached a record 93 thousand.
In the United States, at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, 93,000 people died from overdoses.
The previous record in the country was set a year earlier, when 72,000 Americans were victims of drugs.
About it with reference to data of the American government, published on Wednesday, July 14, reports The Associated Press.
In Japan, as a result of suicides in a month died more people than from coronavirus for the whole of 2020 "This is a staggering loss of human lives, - said researcher from Brown University Brandon Marshall, who monitors overdose cases. - COVID significantly increased the crisis."
According to experts, coronavirus restrictions have isolated people suffering from drug addiction and made it difficult for them to access treatment.
For comparison, in 1970, when the heroin epidemic raged in the United States, fewer than 7.2 thousand deaths were associated with an overdose, and at the height of the crack epidemic in 1988, about 9 thousand.
At the same time, all of these drugs have been supplanted in recent years by fentanyl, a dangerously potent opioid developed to treat severe pain caused by diseases such as cancer.
As the newspaper writes, “increasingly it is sold illegally and mixed with other drugs. ”
Fentanyl was responsible for more than 60% of overdose deaths last year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
In general, 2020 was the deadliest year in the history of the United States - more than 3.3 million deaths were registered in the country, 378 thousand of which, by the way, are associated with COVID-19.
In Japan, more people died from suicide in a month than from COVID-19 complications in all of 2020.

title: Recipe from loneliness for the world ’ s loneliest Japanese men in the pandemic era
text:
Okamoto Junko considers Japanese middle-aged men “the loneliest in the world, ” and the COVID-19 pandemic could lead to an intensification of this trend, she warns in an interview with Nippon.com.
Specialist in Communication Strategies.
She is a graduate of the Faculty of Political Economics at Waseda University and a graduate in international relations at Cambridge, a visiting researcher at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
She worked in the economic department of the newspaper "Yomiuri Shimbun", as well as a public relations consultant in the company "Dentsu", subsequently established JSC "Glocomm" and became its president.
He is the author of the book “Japanese middle-aged men are the loneliest in the world ” (Sekaichi kodokuna nihon no odzisan, 2018).
The COVID-19 pandemic preceded an epidemic of no less serious modern disease – loneliness.
In Western countries, it has already been noticed that social isolation has a more serious impact on the psyche and health than smoking and obesity, and also increases the risk of death, so combating this phenomenon is an urgent task.
"Medical studies confirming the negative effects of loneliness, like stars in the sky.
They show that loneliness increases the risk of cardiovascular disease by 29%, equates to smoking 15 cigarettes a day and increases the risk of Alzheimer's by 2.1 times.
Vivek Murphy, chief medical officer in the Obama administration, published an article based on a nationwide study arguing that loneliness is a common factor in a host of social problems, including abuse, bullying, poverty, alcoholism, and drug addiction.
In the UK, the position of Minister for Loneliness was established in 2018, and this problem is being solved at the state level. ”
Declining birth rates, aging societies and urbanization create a favorable environment for the spread of loneliness - a disease that affects people regardless of gender and age.
The characteristics of middle-aged Japanese, such as pride and poor communication skills, contribute to social isolation, emphasizes Okamoto in the book “Japanese men are the loneliest in the world ” (Sekaichi kodoku na nihon no ozisan).
It is expected that in the conditions of the “new normal ” against the background of the pandemic, this population group has become even more lonely.
Why do middle-aged Japanese become the target of loneliness?
According to Okamoto, this is largely due to the specific Japanese culture and value system.
“Two years ago, when the book came out, I received a lot of negative reviews from male readers.
We are used to idealizing loneliness.
“A man lives alone, what ’ s wrong with being alone? ” the readers wrote.
People believe that loneliness is the absence of collective pressure, dependence on people and independence.
The Japanese word kodoku has two meanings – “loneliness ” (a lonely state that causes anguish and anxiety) and“ solitude ” (time spent with pleasure alone), so people confuse these two concepts.
I mean long and hopeless loneliness, when a person wants but cannot communicate, when he needs support, but there is nowhere to wait for help and he continues to live alone. ”
The idealization of loneliness is due, among other things, to the appearance of several bestsellers, but Okamoto considers their popularity to be evidence of the presence of a huge number of lonely people.
“People want their sad loneliness not to be condemned, but to be perceived positively. ”
“Many men do not want to admit that they suffer from loneliness, ” said Okamoto Junko (@ Nippon.com) Another factor is the highly contextual culture of communication, formed in the context of a single cultural background.
People are required to “read the air ” and understand without words, so many Japanese do not have high communication skills.
Middle-aged men, who spend most of their lives in a corporate culture with hours of overtime, vertical relationships, and collective pressure, become dependent on work and lack the skills to communicate with people outside their circle, so they are exposed to loneliness.
A study by the American company Gallup shows that the quality of communication at work affects the productivity of the company.
“However, Japanese companies, especially large enterprises, still did not fully realize the importance of communication between employees.
In international studies, Japanese employees demonstrate a minimum level of involvement (an index calculated on the basis of desire to contribute to the company, motivation and responsibility), as well as a minimum level of productivity among the top 7 countries.
The Japanese have a strong sense of belonging to the company, but they do not invest in the work.
“People think they ’ re being assigned to departments against their will and forced to do hateful work, they don ’ t connect with colleagues and the company.
At the same time, they depend on the company like birds in a cage.
Sitting in a cage, they cannot fly freely, but they do not know how to act if the cage disappears.
There are a lot of such people in Japan, ” Okamoto said.
After retirement, men begin to spend time at home, but the wives treat them as a hindrance and are awarded unflattering nicknames - "large-sized garbage" or "wet fallen leaf".
“They did not like work, but work was the meaning of life, giving them recognition and a sense of self-importance.
This is especially true for the 60-70-year-old generation.
The company satisfied their need for respect, so, having lost belonging to the organization, they feel empty.
After retirement, they planned to have a good time, but they have no hobbies and nothing to do.
Life expectancy is about 90 years, and to live a few decades after retirement in hopeless solitude is sad. ”
“In the regions, men participate in traditional festivals, so they are involved in the life of the local community, but in large cities, many old people turn into reclusive hikikomori.
Women are more active in society, they account for up to 95% of residents' associations.
When asked “Where is your husband? ” they usually answer“ At home, ” “In the library, ” or“ In heaven. ”
Okamoto also notes that it is not only middle-aged men who are at risk of social exclusion.
Among hikikomori there are people of all ages, and this phenomenon has become one of the serious problems of modern society.
“More and more women are having trouble establishing human relationships. ”
As a communications coach, Okamoto trained about 1,000 people – company presidents and executives.
She believes that in Japan there is too little know-how to improve communication skills and few places to learn communication skills.
“The shift from vertical communication to more cohesive communication increases employee motivation and impacts productivity.
However, Japanese leaders are used to reading the text on a piece of paper without changing their facial expressions.
Communication that doesn ’ t affect emotions can ’ t strengthen cohesion, but people don ’ t have the skills to communicate successfully. ”
The spread of remote work against the backdrop of the pandemic and the holding of webinars creates additional barriers to communication.
“During communication, we perceive not only verbal information, but also read information from the whole body.
To ensure the transfer of information at remote work, you should not just read the text on a piece of paper, but actively use gestures and facial expressions.
Remote work can increase the tendency of one-way communication, but many middle-aged people do not like to communicate over the Internet and come to the office despite the recommendations to work from home.
“If men listen to each other, they will get rid of loneliness, but in the current conditions they can ’ t even go out for a drink together.
Some men listen to women, but are not ready to be frank with each other. ”
Low social capital In recent years, social capital has become one of the main indices indicating the level of well-being of society.
This new concept refers to the existence of trusting relationships and connections with people outside the family – for example, participation in volunteer activities and the work of the local community.
However, in the ranking of social capital, calculated by the British analytical center Legatum Institute in 2019, Japan ranks 132nd out of 167 countries and is in last place among the G7 countries.
“In Japan, there is a concept of self-help and state assistance, but the intermediate link existing between these concepts is not developed.
In Western countries, the “third social group ”, that is, the layer between the individual and the authorities, plays a huge role.
As a rule, these are non-profit associations that provide opportunities for volunteer activities and form a safety network in society.
In addition, it is a popular place of work, where promising employees seek employment.
In the United States, there are about one and a half million NGOs, which employ about 10% of the employed population, but in Japan there are only about 50,000.
They are little known in society, and we do not have a culture of participation in such organizations. ” Given the weak foundation of mutual aid, Okamoto ’ s tendency to care exclusively for his own well-being is very disturbing.
“It seems to me that lately more and more people believe that a person should live alone, so if you take care of yourself, you can not think about others.
They say that social exclusion and poverty are a problem within the framework of personal responsibility.
Society is a structure based on mutual aid, carried out through activities such as donations and volunteering, but we have lost the ability to understand the position of the weak.
After the earthquake and tsunami in East Japan in March 2011, people realized the importance of interpersonal connections and sought to help each other, but I have a feeling that the coronavirus pandemic increases the ability to survive independently and increases resistance to loneliness.
The most realistic method is the creation of a thin, like a web, security network within the framework of urban infrastructure.
To do this, it is enough to have several places where every resident can go.
Attention should be paid to weak connections and microcommunities.
This will save us from the need to belong to such formalized structures as the company and the family.
Buddhist temples, cafes, public santo baths, gyms and hairdressers provide an opportunity for easy communication that can save us from loneliness.
My ideal is a society that forms weak connections to prevent a situation where a person has no one to talk to for many months and years. ”
“Before the pandemic, I recommended snack bars as the best choice.
Alcohol facilitates communication, the hostess of the institution plays the role of an intermediary and stimulates communication between visitors so that they communicate not so much with the hostess as with each other.
Communication does not always go smoothly, but people need to learn to overcome mutual frictions and gain the ability to work out a compromise.
“We don ’ t need a society in which everyone sits in a shell and damages the shells of others during collisions.
In a pandemic, face-to-face meetings are considered a crime, and we seem to challenge the basic human need of connecting with people.
We need to think about measures to combat this phenomenon » Interview and article text – Itakura Kimie, Nippon.com Header photo: company employees communicate in a pub in Tokyo ’ s Yurakucho district after the lifting of the state of emergency, May 29, 2020 (© Jiji)

title: Japan will fight loneliness among Japanese citizens abroad
text:
Tokyo News, July 19 (Jiji Press).
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has launched a project to address loneliness and isolation among Japanese citizens living abroad in collaboration with five non-profit organizations.
The ministry connects expats who feel lonely and isolated with NGOs to help them consult with the organizations ’ staff using chat apps and social media.
It is also setting up a hotline with NGOs to report urgent cases, such as domestic violence and child abuse, so that employees of Japanese diplomatic missions abroad can quickly respond to them.
In February, the Japanese government created an office and ministerial post to address the problems of social loneliness and isolation, which are becoming more serious in the face of the ongoing pandemic of the new coronavirus.
The Ministry considers it necessary to take measures for Japanese expatriates, as isolation and other stringent measures against COVID-19 taken abroad can increase their sense of isolation.
According to a survey by the ministry, suicide was the second leading cause of death among Japanese citizens living abroad in 2019 after injuries and illnesses.
People living abroad are particularly vulnerable to loneliness and isolation, Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu said at a press conference on July 9, when the ministry's project was launched.
"We would like to make an effort to listen carefully to the voices of such people."
The five NGOs that have joined the project include Anata-no ibasyo, which offers a 24-hour online chat service, and the Support Center for Children Under the Age of 18.

title: Gornyak22: Multi-level courtyards are being designed in new buildings in Barnaul due to land shortage • 20.07.2021 • GORNYAK22
text:
Project 5-level yard in Barnaul Photo: Elena Bulavina Land deficit and strict urban planning requirements encourage Barnaul architects to design multi-level yards in new buildings In recent years, the projects of Barnaul new buildings have increasingly encountered multi-level courtyards.
As a rule, they consist of two tiers, but there are examples of three – and even five-step house territory.
“Tolk ” found out why such planning decisions became widespread and how they are implemented in practice.
The first high-rise building with a bunk yard in Barnaul appeared in the new building of the company "Self" on pr.
Komsomolsky, 45a, back in 2016.
Here, on the lower platform (at ground level), a parking lot for cars was designed.
Without walls, but under the roof, on which the second floor of the yard is located - leisure (playgrounds for children, sports and recreation for adults).
In the process of implementation, the project of the Parallel workshop, which received a diploma at the competition in Moscow, was simplified, but the essence remained the same.
The project of a house with a two-level yard on pr.
Komsomolsky, 45a Photo: Elena BulavinaThe project of a house with a two-level yard on pr.
Komsomolsky, 45a Photo: Elena BulavinaThe project of a house with a two-level yard on pr.
Komsomolsky, 45a Photo: Elena Bulavina Such an idea should be implemented in a 10-storey new building, which is now being completed at 138 Molodezhnaya Street, Algorithm Group.
Here, the height difference allowed on one side of the house to arrange a parking lot, close it on top of the roof, which stretched to the other side of the skyscraper and leveled with the ground level.
In this space, the designers from "ArchGroup" placed a full-fledged large courtyard - playgrounds with appropriate equipment and benches.
Project of a house with a two-level yard on Molodezhnaya Street, 138 Photo: "ArchGroup" Project of a house with a two-level yard on Molodezhnaya Street, 138 Photo: "ArchGroup" Project of a house with a two-level yard on Molodezhnaya Street, 138 Photo: "ArchGroup" Also at the stage of coordination another LCD with an interesting leisure space on Proletarskaya Street, 182.
It consists of two residential buildings of 13-16 floors, which are united by a street platform designed to store cars.
Part of it is blocked by the second level, on which there is a children's playground, a playground with simulators, a huge sports box and even a fountain in a special recreation area for adults.
Project of a house with a two-level yard on the street. Partizanskaya, 182 Photo: Elena BulavinaProject of a house with a two-level yard on the street. Partizanskaya, 182 Photo: Elena Bulavina It is interesting that the second levels always have reliable fences and the same coatings as in ordinary yards: rubber-polymer in children 's, sports areas, tiled or asphalted pedestrian paths, artificial green lawns or natural flower beds and trees.
To do this, you even have to import soil and lay a layer for planting.
To withstand such loads, the structure must be particularly strong.
As a rule, designers provide for several dozen pillars that hold reinforced concrete floors.
For convenience, access to all levels of the yard is made from the entrance, and from the street they communicate with each other by stairs.
Five reasons for stepped courtyards The appearance of such urban planning solutions, of course, has its own reasons.
According to experts, the most important is the shortage of land in Barnaul.
This problem is especially acute in the city center, where developers of point LCD manage to rent, settle and buy a small plot.
In the house it is profitable to lay as many apartments as possible.
“This, in turn, makes it necessary to make the yard more spacious.
According to the norms, it is necessary to place parking, sports, and playgrounds.
There is a lack of territory.
That is why designers and developers go to such tricks ”, – told “Tolku ” the head of the Barnaul workshop“ Classics ” Alexander Dering.
February 24, 8: 51 In the center of Barnaul decided to build an American skyscraper with auto elevators The developer of the site in the Pervomaisky area changed the architecture of the high-rise.
And although the city council criticized it, but still approved the constantly tightening regulations can be considered another reason for the expansion of courtyards.
Architects "finish" the missing leisure areas on the roof of parking lots, extensions or residential buildings themselves.
According to Alexander Dering, this is more often done only in the sketch for passing examinations.
Projects are sometimes very embellished and look too futuristic.
That is why many of them are not implemented in the original idea, and customers are not responsible.
The third reason is the need for a clear separation of flows.
“With this spatial solution, all cars can be taken to the lower levels, and on the upper ones leave only a zone for walking.
This is primarily safe, including for children, as in the pedestrian zone are excluded driveways.
At the same time, there is more space for a full-fledged arrangement of public space, the courtyard is not cluttered, ” says the chief architect of Tectonica Elena Bulavina.
Another reason is aesthetics.
In houses with multi-level courtyards, flowers, greenery, colorful children ’ s towns and fountains are visible from the windows, rather than cars standing “on top of each other ”.
The functional adjacent territory makes the performance of the LCD more modern and cozy, says Bulavina.
The exception here are only the lower tiers, but they can be given for economic and commercial needs.
The fifth reason can be considered the features of the sites in Barnaul.
Many of them are uneven and have terrain differences of tens of meters in height.
“Here God himself ordered to beat them usefully, to make several levels in the yard to fit everything you need, ” says Elena Bulavina.
Barnaul architects have already begun to plan in new buildings courtyards with three and even five tiers.
Recently, Tectonics developed a project of a 23-storey candle on pr.
Red Army, 50.
It has a lawn at ground level and an entrance to the underground parking lot.
Above it there was a second tier with open parking, entrances to the house and a separate area with street simulators.
And part of this street parking is covered with the third level, where there is a children's play area with a sandbox and gazebos for adults.
The project of a house with a 3-level yard on pr.
Krasnoarmeysky, 50 Photo: Elena BulavinaThe project of a house with a 3-level yard on pr.
Krasnoarmeysky, 50 Photo: Elena BulavinaThe project of a house with a 3-level yard on pr.
Krasnoarmeysky, 50 Photo: Elena BulavinaThe project of a house with a 3-level yard on pr.

Krasnoarmeysky, 50 Photo: Elena Bulavina In 2014, Elena Bulavina designed a five-step courtyard in a 12-storey building on Montazhnikov Street.
Here, due to the sharp drop in heights, it was possible to create four levels for storing cars (the lowest was completely underground, the rest were partially open).
And on the last tier, it was proposed to place only a courtyard with walking areas.
Project of a house with a 5-level yard on Montazhnikov Street Photo: Elena BulavinaProject of a house with a 5-level yard on Montazhnikov Street Photo: Elena BulavinaProject of a house with a 5-level yard on Montazhnikov Street Photo: Elena BulavinaProject of a house with a 5-level yard on Montazhnikov Street Photo: Elena Bulavina However, these ambitious projects remained unrealized.
Another house with a classical courtyard has already been built on Montazhnikov Street.
Krasnoarmeisky, 50, after long discussions, also approved another concept - a 23-storey American-style building with a two-level underground parking and an elevator, above which a leisure space will be located.
Experts believe that with the development of technology and a total shortage of territories, multi-level yards in Barnaul should take root.
Developers will master them more and more, since such a layout can really be the only way out when point multi-apartment skyscrapers appear in small areas.
Now everything rests on parking, but this problem may soon exhaust itself by car sharing.
As told “Tolku ” Dering, more and more people refuse to maintain personal cars and use cars for rent.
In the summer of 2021, carsharing has already appeared in Barnaul.
If it takes root, then huge spaces for parking near the house will become unclaimed, and small cozy yards with children's and sports grounds will again be able to fit in a small house plot.

title: Due to climate change: 2 / 3 of the territory of Ukraine can become a zone of risky farming
text:
In the future, climate change may lead to the fact that two-thirds of the territory of Ukraine will become a zone of risky farming.
This assumption was made by the Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food Roman Leshchenko.
According to him, agriculture is quite susceptible to climate change.
Therefore, already today in Ukraine, climatic zones of agriculture are shifting to the north by hundreds of kilometers. — We see that the temperature regime has increased by more than 1 ° C for 10 years.
This has a very serious impact on the farming area.
Objectively speaking, with such dynamics as today, we can come to a situation where 2 / 3 of the territory of Ukraine will become a zone of risky farming, ” the minister said.
Roman Leshchenko added that global climate change poses very big threats to agriculture.
First of all, they are a decrease in production productivity, a loss of ecosystem stability and a deterioration in the quality of life of people.
Therefore, according to the minister, it is necessary to move to more economical means of land cultivation in terms of technology, as well as to increase the share of organic products.

title: Le Figaro – quarantine or pandemic – scientists have found out what is worse
text:
Le Figaro – quarantine or pandemic – scientists have found out what is worse During quarantine and other harsh measures that have been taken in different countries, people wondered if they are not doing more harm than COVID-19 itself.
Therefore, scientists decided to conduct an analysis and compare data from 94 countries of the world to assess the relationship between strict quarantine measures and mortality in the pandemic era, writes Le Figaro.
During the quarantine, many wondered whether restrictive measures do more harm than the disease itself.
So scientists decided to investigate this issue, writes Le Figaro.
The researchers analyzed the impact of government restrictions on mortality rates, habitual health services, suicide rates, and mental health status.
Data came from 94 countries.
As a result, analysts concluded that nowhere was there both high mortality and severe quarantine measures, and at the same time a low number of cases of COVID-19.
This is necessary to conclude that the high mortality was caused by the quarantine.
For example, Australia or New Zealand had significant restrictions, but there was no high mortality.
In Brazil, Sweden and Russia, on the contrary, the restrictions were small, but the mortality rate is high.
According to the authors of the study, quarantine can even reduce mortality compared with previous years, since common diseases such as the flu are less common and the number of accidents is reduced.
But they also found a link between government restrictions and a reduction in routine visits to doctors.
This can be caused by a lack of doctors, and people ’ s fears that in clinics you can get infected with coronavirus.
The authors of the article admit that in general the pandemic affected the mental health of people, but the number of suicides has not increased.
And where suicides have increased, as, for example, in Japan, this is not due to quarantine, but to unemployment, and this happened after the return to normal life.
The pandemic has also affected international health programmes.
Funds earmarked for the fight against HIV and tuberculosis have been partially redirected to the coronavirus.
But to assess this aspect is quite difficult.
The authors of the study agree that the quarantine has had a negative impact on people, but they concluded that government intervention has contributed to a reduction in deaths from COVID-19 and that the quarantine cannot be worse than the damage from the pandemic, at least in the short term.

title: What hinders the development of medical tourism in the Crimea
text:
In Crimea, representatives of medical and tourism clusters discussed the prospects for the development of medical tourism.
This direction would help to expand the framework of the holiday season and would contribute to an increase in tourist flow in the off-season.
It is necessary to make clarifications in the legislative framework and offer your own unique product.
Just note that in this case we are not talking about sanatorium-resort treatment, but about the cooperation of private medical clinics with hotels and tour operators.
According to experts, young people, unlike older people, have little interest in improving health in sanatoriums, but do not refuse medical services and diagnostics during rest.
Associate Professor of the Department of Tourism, Service and Hotel Business of the Institute of City Development of Sevastopol State University, Director of the travel agency Elena Odariuk notes that the legislation does not have a clear definition of the concept of "medical tourism".
There is no program for its development in the Crimea, and the players of the tourist market and medical communities do not understand what a unique medical product Crimea can offer vacationers. - The definition of the term "medical tourism" in the legislation is not made, the meaning of this term and the World Tourism Organization are not defined.
To begin with, it is necessary to adopt some bylaw on medical tourism at the level of the Crimea, and to separate the concepts of "sanatorium treatment" and "medical tourism", as well as to determine what includes each of these concepts, - says Olena Odariuk.
Medical tourism is developed in Germany and Israel, there clinics offer treatment of various diseases, including rare ones, according to the latest methods.
Crimea cannot compete with these countries.
But it may well form some of its own product, taking into account the request of consumers and the capabilities of domestic medicine.
Experts of the tourism industry recall how in the 2000s, residents of Israel flew to the Crimea to treat teeth, here in several private clinics they put implants on advanced technologies.
Qualitatively and much cheaper than in Europe and the same Israel.
There were dental "tourists" from Germany and Poland, they rested in hotels by the sea and visited medical clinics.
Today, Crimea should focus not on foreigners, but on residents of the mainland of the Russian Federation.
According to experts, there is a demand in society for diagnostics on vacation and for rehabilitation after the covid.
Tourists want to combine the pleasant with the useful: relax on the seashore and go through some examinations or treatment programs.
In the Crimea, many large hotels open medical centers with modern equipment on their base.
They offer not only traditional climatotherapy, but also a set of medical services, develop health programs, for example, for the spine, blood vessels, respiratory organs, nervous system.
There could be more such hotels if they began to cooperate with medical clinics, representatives of the medical community are sure.
After all, the medical business knows how to get a license, and there are already equipment and professional staff.
Director of the medical center "Angelina" Sergey Veretnov notes that although private medical clinics have enough customers, but they are interested in tourists. - If hoteliers have a territory and a desire to expand, not only increasing the number of rooms, but also offering an additional product, then we as specialists in the field of medicine are ready to help them, - says Sergey Veretnov.
He recommends opening branches of medical centers already operating in the Crimea on the territory of the hotel.
According to Veretnov, everyone will benefit from such cooperation, including residents of small resort villages.
In the summer to receive medical services in the hotel will be vacationers, and in the off-season - local residents.
As for the Crimean medical product, doctors doubt that they will be able to offer guests something unique.
These can be programs for early diagnosis of diseases, prevention of occupational diseases, etc. In turn, the head of the Crimean Hotel Association Sergey Makovey believes that in order to develop medical tourism, it is necessary to promote the Crimea in the regions of the Russian Federation as an all-Russian health resort.
- Young people do not know that the Crimea was once an all-Union health resort, for them the peninsula today is associated mainly with a beach holiday.
The tourist community knows how to organize holidays, sell vouchers.
Visits of representatives of the tourism industry to the regions of the Russian Federation with a presentation of the tourist potential of the Crimea are not accompanied by professionals from the medical community who could tell what medical and health services can be obtained in the region. - says Sergey Makovey.
By the way, in 2016, about 33 thousand foreigners received medical care in Russia, in 2017 - 110 thousand, in 2018 - 300 thousand people, in 2019 - more than half a million.
About 40 percent are residents of Europe, the rest are residents of former Soviet countries.
According to the Association of Health Tourism, 80-90 thousand Russians annually go to foreign clinics for treatment.

title: Europe is floating, the States are burning, and humanity is suffering from new diseases: why natural disasters have become more frequent and what to expect next
text:
The climate crisis is one of the most serious challenges facing humanity.
The weather in Ukraine and the world every year more and more surprises people - the air temperature continues to rise, the phenomenon of "rain" has turned literally into "flooding", and the usual seasons in specific periods of the year are no longer in question, they have radically shifted.
The reason is the gradual climate change, the consequences of which are becoming more and more tangible.
Over the past 50 years, according to the UN, dangerous natural phenomena that lead to human casualties have increased significantly.
He died most of all because of the extreme heat.
According to the new UN report “Climate Change 2021: Data from the Physical Sciences ”, authored by 234 specialists, if not taken action, by the end of the century the air temperature could rise by 3 ° C, which will lead to changes in the world ’ s ecosystems.
Why frequent natural disasters and what it threatens in the future, understood TSN.ua.
The weather this summer was marked by unusual trends for the whole world.
Heavy rains and devastating floods flooded Western Europe in July, now the US states were suffering from unbearable heat, and now suffer from large-scale forest fires.
In the end, cataclysms came to China, where in the central province of Henan floods led to human casualties, evacuations, water flooded infrastructure and eroded roads.
And this is not a complete list of natural phenomena that test humanity for sustainability.
And given the current situation, this is only the beginning and we need to prepare for more dangerous cataclysms in the coming decades.
For example, Joyce Msuya, deputy executive director of the United Nations Environment Programme, said the COVID-19 pandemic “was a warning that the situation could worsen even further if we do not change our behavior. ”
Indeed, the coronavirus was like a stop signal to humanity, which turned out to be helpless in front of an invisible enemy who daily chooses more and more victims.
Natural disasters are no less dangerous.
So, according to the UN, over the past 50 years, the most victims among people were recorded precisely because of the extremely high temperature.
The heat has claimed at least 55,000 lives.
Other hazards that have resulted in the largest loss of life over a 50-year period include droughts – 650,000 deaths, storms – 577,232 deaths, floods – 58,700 deaths, extreme temperatures – 55,736 deaths.
As explained by WMO Secretary General Petteri Taalas, as the atmosphere heats up, it begins to retain more moisture, which means that during storms will fall more rain and accordingly increase the risk of floods.
“Strong warming ” in the Arctic affects the dynamics of the atmosphere in the northern hemisphere, as evidenced by stagnant weather systems and changes in the behavior of the jet stream, ” said Petteri Taalas, Secretary General of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
Most scientific evidence suggests that natural disasters are a consequence of human activities.
In particular, according to experts, climate change caused by greenhouse gas emissions, which increased the likelihood of heat waves by at least 150 times.
In 2025, gas boilers may be banned: why and what alternative to increasing the concentration of greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, in our atmosphere, leads to the combustion of fossil fuels, coal, gas and oil.
Construction of structures, clearing of land for agriculture, use of energy, exhaust of cars and air transport increase the warming effect.
Another equally important factor in climate change is deforestation and wetlands that could store carbon dioxide.
Speaking of climate change, society is accustomed to believe that it means its impact on nature, but above all, humanity suffers from unusual phenomena.
“You say that you love your children more than anything, but at the same time you steal their future just in front of their eyes, ” environmental activist Greta Thunberg said aptly a few years earlier.
Thus, according to a special report of the IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change), even a rise in temperature to 1.5 ° C, which threatens humanity between 2030 and 2052, will lead to catastrophic consequences and inequality in society, not to mention the 3 ° C that experts predict in the latest UN report.
First of all, as stated in the scientific journal The Lancet, climate change increases the likelihood of outbreaks of infectious diseases, because, as you know, bacteria, pathogens are especially well developed in humid and warm climates.
Scientists warn of more dangerous diseases, such as malaria and dengue fever, as mosquitoes carrying the pathogen will be able to live in large areas.
Allergies will also become more common, because due to climate change, the flowering periods of plants are lengthened, which increases the amount of pollen.
In addition, the impact of climate change can violate a number of human rights – from the rights to water and food, to the rights to adequate housing.
For example, the people of the Marshall Islands, even now, regularly suffer from floods that destroy their homes and deprive them of their livelihood.
Climate change could also exacerbate inequality, particularly in North America, where people often live near power plants and refineries.
Thus, this increases not only the risks of infection with respiratory diseases, but also cancer.
The increase in temperature also affects the yield.
Even now, even on the example of Ukraine, we can observe how frosts and rains in the spring and ruthless heat in the summer destroyed the harvest of fruits and berries.
And the ones that are left are sold at exorbitant prices.
And this trend, experts warn, will only intensify, leading to malnutrition, and these are significant health problems.
According to the forecast, limiting global warming to 1.5 ° C compared to 2 ° C, will lead to lower yields of corn, rice, wheat and potentially other crops, especially in sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, Central and South America, as well as the nutritional value of rice and wheat, which depends on CO2.
Reduction in food availability is expected to be more global warming of 2 ° C, compared to 1.5 ° C, in the Sahel region, southern Africa, the Mediterranean, Central and Amazon.
“Agricultural animals will be adversely affected by rising temperatures, depending on the prevalence of changes in feed quality, livestock morbidity and water availability, ” the IPCC document states.
Experts add that depending on future socio-economic conditions, warming could reduce by about 50% the proportion of the world ’ s population experiencing water shortages.
Among other dangerous effects of climate change are: Increased intensity and frequency of hurricanes, floods, droughts and storms.
Desertification of territories and reduction of water reserves.
Reduced fishing and destruction of coral reefs.
Loss of valuable habitat, biodiversity, important ecosystems and species.
According to the calculations of climatologists, it is expected that the number of hot days will increase in most land regions with the greatest increase in the tropics.
“On extremely hot days in mid-latitudes it will become warmer by almost 3 ° C in case of global warming by 1.5 ° C and almost 4 ° C in case of warming by 2 ° C, and on extremely cold nights in high latitudes it will become warmer by almost 4.5 ° C in case of warming by 1.5 ° C and almost 6 ° C in case of warming by 2 ° C, ” the IPCC report says.
It is also assumed that the risks from heavy precipitation will be higher in several high-latitude and / or high-altitude regions of the Northern Hemisphere, eastern Asia and eastern North America.
If humanity plans to reduce temperature rise, human-produced greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced by 50% by 2030, according to the IPCC.
And the first step in this struggle should be the transition to green energy to reduce the production of heat and electricity and the activities of other sectors closely related to energy production.
It is equally important to change a car to a bicycle or to cover distances on foot, because it is transport that accounts for 14% of all CO2 emissions.
According to experts from the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe, electrification is a key element in improving the environmental friendliness of transport.
In particular, a significant reduction in emissions of harmful greenhouse gases in cities will lead to the abandonment of buses with diesel engines.
The UN proposes to use not only electric cars, but also electric bicycles and electric scooters.
As an example, the decision of the Italian government to introduce the so-called “mobility bonus ”, providing citizens from large urban areas with a one-time voucher of up to 500 euros for the purchase of a bicycle, electric bike or scooter.
Thanks to this, in September 2020, less than 2.5% of the population of large cities purchased an electric scooter, many people switched to bicycles.
Also, to preserve the planet, you should avoid disposable materials and choose those that can be reused.
Among other easy and affordable ways to reduce your carbon footprint: Take a shower for less than 5 minutes.
Use eco-bags for shopping.
Avoid air travel by choosing to stay closer to home.
Reduce waste.
Turn off the lights and other electrical devices.
Buy locally produced products.
Eat less meat and more plant foods.
Give the waste to recycling.
For her part, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Patricia Espinosa believes that decisions to be taken this year will determine whether it will be possible to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius by the end of the century compared to the pre-industrial era.
According to her, now the world is moving on the opposite path, which can lead to an increase in temperature by three degrees Celsius.
Even small steps and efforts can change the world for the better.

title: Unbearable heat and incredible floods: why Ukraine and the world shaking from cataclysms
text:
Why Ukraine and the world shakes from cataclysms / ua.depositphotos.com Weather in Ukraine and the world every year more and more surprises people - the air temperature continues to rise, showers regularly lead to floods, and about the usual calendar times categorically moved.
According to the portal TSN with reference to experts, the reason is that the planet is shaking in the paroxysms of the climate crisis.
Given the current situation, experts say, both Ukrainians and other inhabitants of the Earth only need to prepare for more dangerous cataclysms in the coming decades.
For example, the Deputy Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Programme, Joyce Msuya, believes that the COVID-19 pandemic was a warning that the situation could worsen even more if earthlings do not change their behavior.
Scientists warn of more dangerous diseases, such as malaria and dengue fever, as mosquitoes that carry the pathogen will be able to live in large areas.
Allergies will also become more common, because due to climate change, the flowering periods of plants are lengthened, which increases the amount of pollen.
In addition, the impact of climate change can violate a number of human rights – from the rights to water and food, to the rights to adequate housing.
For example, residents of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific are already regularly suffering from floods that destroy their homes and deprive them of their livelihood.
The increase in temperature also affects the yield.
Already now in Ukraine frosts and rains in the spring, and then - the relentless heat in the summer destroyed the harvest of fruits and berries.
The ones that are left are sold at exorbitant prices.
And this trend, experts warn, will only intensify.
This will lead to malnutrition, and then to serious health problems.
Destructive flooding in Germany: big water provoked an environmental disaster Recall, earlier astropsychologist Valentina Wittrok said - that many countries of the Earth in the summer of 2021 collapsed natural disasters - floods, heavy rains, storms and hurricanes - to blame the "axis of catastrophes" - the collision of the lunar nodes, North and South.
And it denotes an imaginary confrontation between two evil and immobile stars - Aldebaran and Antares, which are in the constellations of Taurus and Scorpius.
