title: Legendary Writers Who Suffered From Mental Disorders (Photo)
text:
And the ascent to glory, however smooth it may seem, is almost always accompanied by a dangerous flirtation with the unknown, forbidden or insane.
I present to you a list of authors not quite healthy in soul, who gave the world not only magnificent literary works, but also brilliant creative inspiration for years to come.
Edgar Allan Poe American writer, poet (1809-1849) Diagnosis: Mental disorder, an exact diagnosis is not established.
Symptoms: Fear of the dark, memory lapses, persecution mania, inappropriate behavior, hallucinations.
Since the late 1830s, Edgar Poe suffered from frequent depressions.
In addition, he abused alcohol, which affected his psyche not the best way: under the influence of drunk writer sometimes fell into a state of violent insanity.
Opium was soon added to the alcohol.
Significantly worsened the mental state of Poe severe illness of his young wife (his cousin Virginia he married thirteen years; after seven years of marriage, in 1842, she fell ill with tuberculosis, five years later died).
After the death of Virginia - in the remaining two years of his life - Edgar Poe fell in love several times and made two attempts to marry.
The first failed because of the refusal of the chosen one, frightened by his next failure, the second because of the absence of the groom: shortly before the wedding, Po got heavily drunk and fell into an insane state.
He was found in a cheap Baltimore tavern five days later.
The writer was placed in a clinic, where he died five days later, suffering from terrible hallucinations.
One of Poe's main nightmares - death alone - came true: many of whom he took the promise to be with him at the last hour, but at three o'clock in the morning on October 7, 1849, none of the loved ones were near.
Before his death, Poe desperately summoned Jeremy Reynolds, a North Pole explorer.
Ideas given to the world: Two of the most popular modern literary genres.
The first is a novel (or story) of horrors.
A great influence on Edgar Poe had Hoffmann, but the gloomy romanticism of Poe for the first time thickened to the consistency of a real nightmare - viscous, hopeless and very sophisticated ("Heart-denunciator", "The Fall of the House of Eschers").
The second genre is the detective.
It was Monsieur Auguste Dupin, the hero of the stories of Edgar Poe (“Murder on the Rue Morgue ”,“ The Mystery of Marie Roger ”), who became the founder of the deductive method and its apologist, Mr. Sherlock Holmes.
Friedrich Nietzsche German philosopher (1844-1900) Diagnosis: Nuclear mosaic schizophrenia (more literary variant, indicated in most biographies - obsession).
Symptoms: delusions of grandeur (sent notes with the text: "In two months I will be the first person on earth", demanded to remove from the walls of the picture, because his apartment is "temple"); obscuration of mind (hugging a horse in the central city square, interfering with street traffic); severe headaches; inadequate behavior.
The medical record of Nietzsche, in particular, stated that the patient drank his urine from the boot, gave inarticulate screams, took the hospital guard for Bismarck, tried to barricade the door with fragments of a broken glass, slept on the floor by the bed, jumped goat, grimaced and bulged his left shoulder.
Case history: Nietzsche suffered several apoplexic blows; suffered from a mental disorder for the last 20 years of his life (it was during this period that his most significant works appeared - for example, "So Spoke Zarathustra"), 11 of them he spent in psychiatric clinics, his mother took care of him at home.
His condition was constantly deteriorating - at the end of his life, the philosopher could make up only the simplest phrases.
Ideas presented to the world: The idea of ​ ​ a superman (paradoxically, it is this comrade who jumped in a goat and protruded his left shoulder that we associate with a free, supramoral, perfect, existing on the other side of good and evil personality).
The idea of a new morality (the morality of masters instead of the morality of slaves): a healthy morality should glorify and strengthen the natural desire of man for power.
All other morals are morbid and decadent.
The ideology of fascism: the sick and the weak must die, the strongest must win ("Push the Falling One!").
The assumption is “God is dead. ”
Ernest Hemingway American writer (1899-1961) Diagnosis: Acute depression, mental disorder.
Symptoms: Suicidal tendencies, persecution mania, nervous breakdowns.
In 1960, Hemingway returned from Cuba to the United States.
He was plagued by frequent depression, a sense of fear and uncertainty, he could hardly write - and therefore voluntarily agreed to undergo treatment in a psychiatric clinic.
Hemingway suffered 20 sessions of electroshock, about these procedures he responded as follows: "Doctors who gave me electroshock, writers do not understand: What was the point in destroying my brain and erasing my memory, which is my capital, and throwing me to the side of life?
It was a brilliant treatment, but they lost the patient. "
After leaving the clinic, Hemingway became convinced that he still could not write, and made his first suicide attempt, but his family managed to prevent him.
At the request of his wife, he underwent a second course of treatment, but did not change his intentions.
A few days after discharge, he shot himself in the head from his favorite double-barrel, preloading both barrels.
Ideas given to the world: The idea of a "lost generation".
Hemingway, like his comrade Remarque, was referring to a particular generation, grinded by the millstones of a particular war, but the term turned out to be painfully seductive and convenient - since then, each generation has found reasons to consider itself lost.
A new literary technique, the "iceberg method", when a stingy, concise text implies a generous, heartbreaking subtext.
"Machism" of a new pattern, embodied both in creativity and in life.
The hero of Hemingway is a harsh and short-spoken fighter who understands that the fight is useless, but fights to the end.
The most uncompromising Hemingway macho was, perhaps, the fisherman Santiago (“The Old Man and the Sea ”), in whose mouth the Great Ham put the phrase:“ Man is not created to suffer defeat.
A man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”
Hemingway himself - a hunter, a soldier, an athlete, a sailor, a fisherman, a traveler, a Nobel laureate, whose body was completely covered with scars - to the great disappointment of many, did not fight to the end.
However, the writer did not change his ideals.
“A man has no right to die in bed, ” he said,“ either in battle or a bullet in the forehead. ”
Franz Kafka Czech writer (1883 – 1924) Diagnosis: Severe neurosis, psychasthenia of a functional nature, non-periodic depressive states.
Symptoms: Excitability, interspersed with attacks of apathy, sleep disturbance, exaggerated fears, psychosomatic difficulties in the intimate sphere.
The roots of Kafka ’ s deep psychological failures stem from conflict with his father, difficult relationships with his family, and complex, confusing love stories.
The fascination with writing in the family was not encouraged, and it had to be done secretly.
“For me, this is a terrible double life, ” he wrote in his diary,“ from which perhaps there is only one way out: madness. ”
When his father began to insist that after the service the son also worked in his shop, and not engaged in nonsense, Franz decided to commit suicide and wrote a farewell letter to his friend Max Brod "At the last moment I managed, intervening completely unceremoniously, to protect him from" loving parents, "writes Max Brod in his book about Kafka.
In his mental state, there were periods of deep and even calm, followed by equally long periods of painful state.
Here are lines from his Diaries that clearly reflect this inner struggle: “I can ’ t sleep.
Only visions, no sleep.
The strange instability of my whole inner being.
The monstrous world I carry in my head.
How can I get rid of it and free it without destroying it? ”
The writer died at the age of 41 from tuberculosis.
For three months he was in agony: not only the body but also the mind was destroyed.
Ideas presented to the world: Kafka was not known during his life, little printed, but after his death, the writer ’ s work conquered readers with a new direction in literature.
The Kafkaesque world of despair, horror and hopelessness grew out of the personal drama of its creator and became the basis of a new aesthetic direction of “literature with a diagnosis ”, very characteristic of the 20th century, which lost God and received in return the absurdity of existence.
Jonathan Swift Irish writer (1667-1745) Diagnosis: Peak disease or Alzheimer's disease - experts argue.
Symptoms: Dizziness, disorientation in space, memory loss, inability to recognize people and surrounding objects, catch the meaning of human speech.
Case history: A gradual increase in symptoms up to complete dementia at the end of life.
Ideas given to the world: A new form of political satire.
Gulliver ’ s Journey is certainly not the first sarcastic look of an enlightened intellectual at the surrounding reality, but the innovation here is not in the look, but in the optics.
While other scoffers looked at life through a magnifying glass or through a telescope, the dean of St. Peter ’ s Cathedral.
Patrick made for this lens with a fancifully curved glass.
Subsequently, this lens was enjoyed by Nikolai Gogol and Saltykov-Shchedrin.
Jean-Jacques Rousseau French writer and philosopher (1712-1778) Diagnosis: Paranoia.
Symptoms: Persecution mania.
Rousseau saw conspiracies everywhere, he led the life of a wanderer and did not stay anywhere for long, believing that all his friends and acquaintances were conspiring against him or suspected him of something.
As a result of the writer ’ s conflict with the church and the government (in the early 1760s, after the publication of the book “Emile, or On Education ”), Rousseau ’ s original suspicion acquired extremely painful forms.
He saw conspiracies everywhere, he led the life of a wanderer and did not stay anywhere for a long time, believing that all his friends and acquaintances were conspiring against him or suspected him of something.
So, one day Rousseau decided that the inhabitants of the castle in which he was staying, consider him the poisoner of the deceased servant, and demanded an autopsy of the deceased.
Ideas given to the world: Pedagogical reform.
Modern manuals for the upbringing of children on many points repeat "Emile": instead of the repressive method of education, Rousseau offered a method of encouragement and affection; he believed that the child should be freed from the mechanical hardening of dry facts, and explain everything on living examples, and only when the child is mentally ready to accept new information; the task of pedagogy Rousseau considered the development of inherent talents, not adjustment personality.
A new type of literary hero and new literary directions.
Created by Rousseau ’ s fantasy, the good-natured creature — the tearful “savage ”, guided not by reason, but by feeling (but by a highly moral feeling) — further developed, grew and aged within the framework of sentimentalism and romanticism.
The idea of a democratic state based on the rule of law, directly deriving from the essay "On the Social Contract".
The idea of revolution (it was Rousseau ’ s works that inspired the fighters for the ideals of the French Revolution; Rousseau himself, paradoxically, had never been a supporter of such radical measures).
Nikolai Gogol Russian writer (1809-1852) Diagnosis: Schizophrenia, periodic psychosis.
Symptoms: Visual and auditory hallucinations; periods of apathy and inhibition (up to complete immobility and inability to respond to external stimuli), followed by bouts of excitement; depressive states; hypochondria in an acute form (the great writer was convinced that all organs in his body are somewhat displaced, and the stomach is located "upside down"); claustrophobia.
Some manifestations of schizophrenia accompanied Gogol throughout his life, but in the last year the disease has progressed markedly.
On January 26, 1852, the sister of his close friend Ekaterina Mikhailovna Khomyakova died of typhoid fever and this death caused the writer to have a severe attack of hypochondria.
Gogol plunged into incessant prayers, practically refused food, complained of weakness and malaise, and claimed to be mortally ill, although doctors did not diagnose him with any disease other than a small gastrointestinal disorder.
On the night of February 11-12, the writer burned his manuscripts (the next morning he explained this act by the machinations of the evil one), then his condition was constantly deteriorating.
Treatment (not too professional, however: leeches in the nostrils, wrapping with cold sheets and dipping the head in icy water) did not give positive results.
On February 21, 1852, the writer died.
The true cause of his death remains unclear.
However, most likely, Gogol simply brought himself to complete nervous and physical exhaustion - it is possible that the timely help of a psychiatrist could save his life.
Ideas given to the world: A specific love for a small person (a philistine), consisting of half disgust, half pity.
A whole bunch of surprisingly accurately found Russian types.
Gogol developed several role-playing models (the most striking are the characters of Dead Souls), which are quite relevant to this day.
Guy de Maupassant French writer (1850-1893) Diagnosis: Progressive paralysis of the brain.
Symptoms: Hypochondria, suicidal tendencies, bouts of violence, delusions, hallucinations.
All his life Guy de Maupassant suffered from hypochondria: he was very afraid of going mad.
From 1884, Maupassant began frequent nervous seizures and hallucinations.
In a state of extreme nervous excitement, he twice tried to commit suicide (once with a revolver, the second with a paper knife, both times unsuccessfully).
In 1891, the writer was placed in the clinic of Dr. Blanche in Passy, where he lived in a semi-conscious state until his death.
Ideas given to the world: Physiology and naturalism (including erotic) in literature.
The need to tirelessly fight against the spiritless society of consumption (peculiar clones of the "Dear Friend" are diligently recreated by the now living French writers Michel Houellebecq and Frederic Begbeder, our Sergei Minaev also tries to keep up).
Virginia Woolf English writer (1882-1941) Diagnosis: Depression, hallucinations, nightmares.
Symptoms: Being in deep depression, Virginia complained that all the time she "hears the voices of birds singing on the olives of ancient Greece."
Often and for a long time I could not work because of insomnia and nightmares.
Since childhood, she suffered from suicidal tendencies.
When Virginia was 13 years old, she survived an attempted rape by her cousins visiting the house.
This marked the beginning of a persistent dislike for men and the physical side of relationships with them throughout Virginia ’ s life.
Shortly thereafter, her mother died of pneumonia.
A nervous, impressionable girl from despair tried to commit suicide.
She was saved, but deep, lingering depressions have since become a part of her life.
A severe attack of mental disorder overtook young Virginia after the death of her father in 1904.
Emotionally candid letters and works of Virginia Woolf give grounds for the conclusion about the non-traditional sexual orientation of the writer.
However, this is not exactly the case.
Because of the tragedy she experienced in childhood, the fear she felt about men and their society, she fell in love with women - but at the same time she was disgusted with all forms of intimacy, including with them, did not tolerate hugs, did not allow even handshakes.
Having been married to Leonard Wolf for 29 years (and this marriage is considered exemplary in terms of devotion and emotional support of each other ’ s spouses), the writer, according to some reports, was not able to enter into a marital relationship with her husband.
In early 1941, the night bombing of London destroyed the writer ’ s house, burned down the library, almost killed her beloved husband – all this completely upset her nervous system, doctors insisted on treatment in a psychiatric clinic.
Not wanting her husband to spend the rest of her life in the cares associated with her insanity, on March 28, 1941, she performed what she described more than once in her works and what she tried to do in practice - she committed suicide by drowning herself in the Ous River.
Ideas presented to the world: Innovation in the ways of presenting the transient worldly bustle, displaying the inner world of the characters, describing the many ways of refraction of consciousness - the works of Virginia Woolf entered the golden fund of literary modernism and were enthusiastically accepted by many contemporaries.
A faithful student of Tolstoy, she developed and perfected the "inner monologue" in English prose.

title: Foreigners go to Russia for high-quality dentistry
text:

title: A million people will live on Mars!
text:
Currently, there are almost 50 projects of manned flights to Mars.
The most grandiose of them belongs to the American engineer and entrepreneur Elon Musk, who plans to transport a million people to the Red Planet in the coming decades to create an independent civilization.
This idea seems absolutely fantastic – and meanwhile, the company Srace X, led by Mask, announced that very soon will begin the first flights of its space shuttles.
Go to the Red Planet!
At the International Astronomical Congress held in September 2016 in Mexico, the report of the engineer and entrepreneur made a real sensation.
According to Elon Musk, only the resettlement of a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.
Life on our planet can be interrupted by many factors: the explosion of a nearby supernova, superflares on the Sun, falling into a black hole, a global epidemic, a collision with a huge asteroid, a man-made disaster.
A large colony of people on another planet will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.
Why choose Mars?
Compared to other celestial bodies of the solar system, it is better suited for the possible life of earthlings.
The day here lasts 24 hours 37 minutes - that is, suitable for our residents and plants.
Gravity is much smaller than the earth, but is quite suitable for the normal functioning of the human body.
Finally, there is water – albeit in the form of polar ice caps, but it can be easily reached, and pieces of ice melt and use.
The rest of the planets of the solar system are practically unsuitable for such a mission: Mercury has extremely high surface temperatures during the day and very low at night, Venus has a too aggressive atmosphere, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are mostly composed of liquefied gas.
The closest suitable celestial body to us is the Moon, but it depends entirely on the Earth and in the event of a space disaster may die with it.
Why is the number of one million people chosen?
According to experts, this is the minimum number of people so that their colony can become completely independent and develop.
It will have specialists of all the necessary professions, it will cope with possible diseases and epidemics, as well as ensure a stable natural population growth.
At first, the colonists will face the most difficult task - to turn the Red Planet into their home.
The set of actions to achieve this goal, Maek called the term “terraforming ” – that is, changing the conditions of life on another planet in such a way that they resemble earthly ones.
First of all, you need to melt a sufficient amount of ice at the south pole of the planet, since it will turn to the Sun in the summer, which means that it will be easier to do this than at the north pole.
The water accumulated here is enough to create an ocean several meters deep on the planet.
As the ice cap decreases, a chain reaction will begin - water vapor will begin to compact the atmosphere, which, in turn, will retain more solar heat, due to which the melting process will be more intense.
Technically, it can be launched using nuclear charges or placing laser devices over the south pole of Mars.
After liquid water appears on the planet, you need to start planting plants: initially it will be mosses, but later - vast forests that will saturate the atmosphere of Mars with oxygen (now it is 95% carbon dioxide).
According to Musk, the cultivation of “green lungs ” and the creation of a livable air without spacesuits will take from 300 to 1000 years.
But after that, the Red Planet can be considered terraformed, and people will choose where they live - on Mars or on Earth.
100 thousand flights Elon Maek listed the things and equipment that the first colonists needed.
First of all, these are devices for the production and conversion of energy - nuclear or space.
The most promising direction, the researchers of the company Srace X consider the delivery to Mars of a large number of light folding solar panels.
It will also require a huge amount of plants, both to create oxygen and to supply the settlers with food.
Until the atmosphere of the planet is formed properly, earthlings will need means of protection from solar radiation - after all, until this time, Martian cities will have to be under special domes.
First, the settlers will build small houses, then they will equip complexes, where there will be not only housing, but also schools, hospitals, shops, etc.
Experts Srace X calculated: one flight with the colonists should account for nine flights with payload.
It is based on a ship capable of carrying 100 passengers.
Thus, the total number of flights required to create a million colony on the Red Planet will be about 100 thousand (10 thousand - passenger flights, 90 thousand - cargo).
Elon Maek has already announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods should begin at the end of 2022.
By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching the Red Planet in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.
The main obstacle to the implementation of such a large-scale project, according to Musk and his team, is the high cost of a flight to the Red Planet.
In fact, it is steadily declining.
In 1989, the US national aerospace agency YABA estimated sending astronauts to Mars at $450 billion.
It was assumed that there will be from four to six earthlings — that is, each place was estimated at about $100 billion.
But already in 2004, the same agency reduced the cost of the project nine times — to $50 billion.
Thus, the flight of one person would cost a little more than 10 billion dollars.
This figure is still too high, but the trend towards its decline is clearly visible, and therefore such a task can be solved.
Elon Maek believes that the optimal amount for a flight of one person should be 500 thousand dollars – this is the approximate cost of a middle-class house in a good place.
Moreover, people should understand that they will become real space pioneers, the first permanent residents of another planet – and therefore must pay for their flight themselves.
Opinions of economists and psychologists are unambiguous: only in the United States there are at least a million people who will agree to pay such money for an unprecedented space travel.
But how to reduce the cost of flying each person from 10 billion to 500 thousand dollars, that is, 20 thousand times?
Elon Mayek knows the answer to that question.
Rocket from a private company Team plan Srace X works in two directions.
The first of these is the creation of spacecraft, each of which will be able to carry at least 100 people.
The company Ilona Mask has a successful experience in the construction of devices of a new type.
The engineer and entrepreneur himself says that the huge cost of missiles is primarily a consequence of the lack of competition and the presence of a huge number of subcontractors.
NASA constantly entrusts the execution of its orders only to a few companies.
For example, ULA (United Launch Alliance), a joint venture owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, regularly performs missions of the space agency and the US Department of Defense, but at the same time receives more for each launch than anyone else in the world.
Under the pretext of national security, the system of government orders in this area is completely opaque, and the task of many companies is not to reduce the cost of the spacecraft, but to make it more expensive for their own benefit.
In turn, having received the order, large companies transfer it in parts to small subcontractors, who also inflate prices.
But the main thing is that in the absence of competition, there is no need to invent something new!
As a result, the technology of modern spacecraft at best dates back to the 1990s, and the costs of their production and launch are declining extremely slowly.
SpaceX was the first company to start working on a fundamentally different scheme.
Not fulfilling an order, but creating your own device, cheaper and more reliable, which can then be offered to space agencies and organizations.
The company was founded in 2002 with the personal funds of Elon Musk, received from the development and operation of the largest electronic payment system in the United States.
The company created its first rocket, called the Falcon 1 (translated from English “falcon ”).
The two-stage vehicle and its engine were made by Space X workers without the help of intermediaries.
The first three launches ended in accidents.
But the fourth flight, which took place in 2008, was successful.
A cargo detachment simulation was conducted (it remained in the rocket so as not to increase the amount of space debris), and the first stage made a safe landing.
At the same time, Elon Maek, who was in the Mission Control Center at Cape Canaveral, heard the clap, ran out into the street in despair - he thought that this test ended in an explosion.
But it turned out that the sound was caused by the passage of the disconnected first stage of the rocket sound barrier.
The successful launch of the Falcon 1 cost $7.9 million – three times cheaper than the best alternative indicators.
At the end of 2008, Musk signed a contract for 12 flights to transport cargo to the ISS.
In 2010, the company Space X created a new rocket – Falcon 9, much more powerful.
But both she and the company ’ s manned Dragon spacecraft are too small to fly to Mars.
Therefore, in the near future, the company plans to create a huge Mars Colonial Transporter rocket capable of lifting a spacecraft with a hundred passengers into orbit.
The second direction of the Space X team ’ s work to reduce the cost of each flight is the reusable use of spacecraft.
Unfortunately, the American shuttles performed this task only in words - the landed ships required many months of inspection and repair, so that their cost advantage was actually reduced to zero.
Space X has developed its own interplanetary transport system, called the Interplanetary Transport System (ITS).
The rocket will launch a large spacecraft into Earth orbit, then detach and return to Earth.
Maek sets the task so that she is ready for a new flight within an hour after landing.
Currently, the company is working on prototypes of such missiles, one of them has already made a successful landing from a height of 1000 meters.
In orbit, each ship with passengers will be refueled - a rocket from Earth will deliver fuel for it for several flights, after which it will proceed to the launch of the next vehicle, and the module with passengers will open solar panels and begin independent movement to Mars.
In his report and on his Twitter page, Elon Maek revealed some technical details of future devices for traveling to the Red Planet.
The height of the rocket together with the manned module will be 122 meters, the power of solar panels will be 200 kilowatts.
Each rocket, capable of putting 550 tons of cargo into orbit, is powered by 40 Raptor engines, the development and testing of which the company has been engaged since 2009, they work on liquid methane and liquid oxygen.
The ability to reuse spacecraft will reduce costs hundreds or even thousands of times.
So the launch of 100 thousand ships does not look unreal.
Of course, one of the most important tasks of space resettlement will be to ensure the safety of future colonists.
The most terrible for flights is radiation.
In near-Earth orbits, astronauts are protected by the magnetic field of our planet, but during the journey to Mars it will no longer be.
Radiation can cause irreversible damage to the human body, and protection against it will lead to an increase in the mass of the ship - that is, to a rise in the price of each flight.
This task will be solved by the specialists of the company Srace X in the next few years.
Danger for future colonists are also cosmic rays - fast elementary particles and nuclei of atoms that move with great speed in interplanetary space.
These particles can destroy brain cells.
Scientists compared the brains of ordinary mice and rodents that have been in space and exposed to cosmic rays.
It turned out that the latter significantly decreased the number of neural processes in these animals, memory deteriorates and interest in life disappears.
How to help immigrants to the Red Planet to avoid such an ailment?
Another difficulty is the weakening of the body in conditions of weightlessness.
Scientists estimate that it takes two years for an astronaut to fully recover from an eight-month space flight.
But these are trained people who have undergone a long special training!
What can be said about space tourists who will pay a large sum to become colonists of Mars?
In what condition will they be there?
There are suggestions that the ship in the way must somehow unwind — then the force of gravity will be replaced by centrifugal force.
Technically, this problem has not yet been solved.
Scientists also note the possible psychological aspects of a long flight.
A large number of people in a confined space inevitably create discomfort for each other.
In order to avoid aggression and conflict, stress-resistant people should be selected, ideally taking into account their religion, philosophy, lifestyle.
How to combine all this with the ability to pay for the flight?
Problems can be possible breakdowns of equipment (to combat which you need to have at least initial skills with space devices), providing passengers with water and food (despite the fact that part of the drinking water on modern orbital stations is obtained from the urine of astronauts), combating Martian dust after arriving on the Red Planet, etc.
But there is still time and opportunity to solve these problems.
In 2008, Esquire magazine named Elon Musk among the 75 most influential people of the 21st century, recognizing that he knows how to achieve this goal.
And his fantastic project has already acquired the concrete outlines of the most grandiose event in the history of mankind.

title: Biologist has estimated the possibility of the disappearance of habitual products due to climate change
text:
Climate change can undoubtedly affect the crops and products of various crops.
However, this trend is likely to mean short-term problems.
Alexander Markov, Doctor of Biological Sciences, Head of the Department of Biological Evolution of the Biological Faculty of Lomonosov Moscow State University, told Zvezda.
According to him, despite the information that appeared in the media that climate change threatens the disappearance of most of the familiar products, this situation is not entirely true.
The reason is that in the case of a change in the usual climate, manufacturers will simply have to rebuild, which will take a certain time.
However, everyone ’ s favorite products will not disappear because of this.
“Climate change can affect the crops and products of various crops, plants, animals and so on.
If it gets warmer or colder, it will affect the productivity of the system.
In some regions it can be a positive impact, in others it can be negative.
In general, any climate change will cause short-term problems: something is changing, agricultural producers have adapted to certain conditions, but those have changed.
You will have to grow crops in other places.
These will be short-term problems for sure, ” Markov said.
The expert added that climate change could cause local problems with agricultural productivity in all regions.
But we can adapt to the changes.
“These are not fatal processes, ” he concluded.
Earlier in the media there was information that, according to scientists, climate change can supposedly lead to the disappearance of most of the usual human products - from potatoes to olive oil.
At the same time, British researchers are convinced that coffee can disappear, and by 2050 the territory suitable for its cultivation will be halved.
And after another 30 years, the plant will completely disappear.

title: Medical tourism for beginners: how to save money and not fall into the trap of scammers
text:
The more popular foreign medicine is, the more people who want to make money on this trend.
Both intermediary companies and clinic employees can do in bad faith with the patient.
But if in case of obvious deception we can only contact the police with a full stack of correspondence and signed contracts, then with the rest of the "400 relatively honest ways" to rob the patient is more and more difficult.
In such cases, it is best to arm yourself with the experience of experienced people, keep your ear open and try to stop attempts to cheat on money.
And for this you need to first find out what are the pitfalls in medical tourism.
FROM HOME: BECOME A CHANCE AND CONDUCT A TENDER Having learned that treatment abroad will definitely be needed, it is first of all necessary to understand a few facts about foreign medical tourism and act on these proven truths, explains Irina Litovchenko, co-founder of the Tabletochki Foundation.
First of all, you need to get a certificate from the chief freelance specialist of the Ministry of Health (only he approves) and become in line for payment for treatment - it is formed by the Ministry.
According to Litovchenko, the state annually allocates considerable funds for this, and all the wards of the fund, which he helped to go abroad in 2016, received the bulk of the sums from the state.
Careful!
Only hidden intermediaries call back quickly.
CLINIC SEARCH.
Elena Chernenok from Kiev, who recently underwent a bone marrow transplant in Israel, first of all advises to entrust the organization of departure to a relative or friend who is able not to whip fever and think soberly: it is difficult for a patient in a state of stress to master a huge layer of information and make informed decisions.
“When I found out that the transplant would cost $250 thousand, I was shocked, ” she recalls. – Miraculously managed to ward off panic and treat the search as a job. ”
To start, according to her, it is necessary to study general information on forums and thematic sites about where they specialize in the right direction, to choose several countries and clinics.
You will have to read a lot of information until you decide on the country, and then - an intermediary assistant (especially relevant in Israel).
Elena, after all, also faced with sluggish international departments and confirms: do not hope that as soon as the clinic receives your request, they will immediately rush to call.
“As a rule, managers of such departments do not respond quickly or ignore letters: they have a flood of requests and little desire to delve into the situation of hundreds of patients, from whom, perhaps, will not be useful, ” Chernenok shares.
And if you answered immediately, it is a sure sign that instead of the clinic ’ s website, you have found yourself on disguised intermediaries.
Only they process requests so quickly and even call back.
DIFFICULTIES OF COMMUNICATION.
Clinics are very reluctant to communicate directly with patients, although many have international departments to which you can send your applications by email.
It is usually easier and faster to do this through proven volunteers, representatives of the diaspora or charitable organizations operating in almost every clinic.
“Without the help of such friends who will“ get ” the institution calls, letters and visits, it is almost impossible to agree, – explains Litovchenko. – There is also a paid option – the same assistants, but for money: they will increase the estimate by 30-40%, but speed up the process, and this can be very important. ”
Moreover, many international departments are sharpened precisely to cheat bills, Sergey Sirosh, the father of a sick child with two years of experience in communicating with European clinics, is sure.
“Most likely, they will initially calculate everything according to the maximum complexity factor, enter several optional additional services in addition to the unprofitable package, ” he shares his experience.
TENDER.
In many cases, attempts to directly agree on a survey plan with the clinic lead to the fact that all procedures and consultations will last for several weeks according to the queues, and living abroad, we recall, costs a penny.
Therefore, it makes sense to find a sensible assistant on the spot, who will tamp everything into a compact schedule and generally will represent your interests.
The initial search for an intermediary usually occurs chaotically, the main advice is not to rush to the first proposal, but to study them for at least a week or two, to contact at least 3-5 companies.
You just need to write that you need advice on such an issue, waiting for an offer.
The more clarifying questions you ask, the sooner you will understand whether they are trying to cheat you for money or not.
If they write something like "$10,000 from you, come!" - most likely, they are trying to weld interest on you 50-80 of the declared amount, Elena notes.
The correct answer is the price for each analysis, the name of the attending physician and other details, ideally, the proposal is made on a letterhead, the size of the commission is a separate item.
“From such a list it often turns out that the company wants to put in the amount of a transfer from the airport worth $500 or accommodation for 150 per day, although you can really find a carrier and apartments much cheaper without much difficulty.
In general, the less empty promises and pink prospects, the more solid your interlocutor is.
Self-respecting doctors never give 100% guarantees, and even remotely.
But scammers like to play on the fact that the patient of despair is happy to believe in a miraculous healing, and rip it off like a sticky, only to sign a contract.
ABOUT FRIENDS.
The features of our mentality are such that we believe the recommendations of friends categorically.
If we are told that they have a "friend" (a medical intermediary) abroad, we automatically give this "friend" a bonus of trust and decide not to contact anyone else.
"Don't be fooled.
They do nothing for free and from the heart.
As a result, such “friends ” often make godless markups, ” emphasizes Chernenok.
One of the most expensive items of stay abroad is accommodation, especially if it is directly in the clinic.
“Try to plan your trip so that the period of stay in the medical institution was minimal, and at the first opportunity, move to an outpatient apartment or home, ” advises Irina Litovchenko.
After all, a lot of tests and examinations in our time it is possible to do outside the hospital, and spend your free time is more pleasant not for felting in the ward, but for sightseeing or meeting new friends.
If you need to save money, refuse to pay for single accommodation.
Do not think that the common ward in Europe is 7-8 seriously ill on 10 square meters, as in our country.
Most likely, the usual room will be double, well, or triple, but quite comfortable for a stay.
And the presence of neighbors in some cases is an antidepressant, and even the most urgent medical care.
By the way, about the assistant nearby: such an additional service in the price list is also available.
A relative or friend, who is with you around the clock, will pull up to another 100 euros per day (the hospital provides him with food and a bed).
Of course, it is often pleasant to see relatives nearby in a difficult moment, but, except for psychological, no help to the patient from the accompanying person is required.
“A nurse in a German clinic is like a mother.
Her duties include full care of the patient: whether it is personal hygiene or assistance in finding a contact lens.
This is not a Ukrainian department with two nurses at the post, which is always impossible to get, - says Zhytomyrets Sergey Sirosh. - Even after a severe operation, an adult patient does not need the round-the-clock presence of relatives, so they can safely stay in rented housing - so cheaper. "
DEAR PROFESSOR.
Another expensive Ukrainian habit is to go through doctors.
We are used to not trust the first doctor we come across and rely on regalia: they say, if the professor or the department, then there are more chances that it will not go wrong.
European doctors for what they do not understand yet, do not take.
So be sure: you will be provided with a doctor who can cope with a particular problem, or they will invite a more experienced one.
You can "order" a professor on your own initiative.
But this whim again costs extra money.
Having caught the love of our medical tourists to communicate with titled doctors, hospitals are happy to offer to include a professor, or even not one.
If you feel more comfortable, pay.
But be sure: if there are difficulties, the clinic itself will hurry to invite the best specialists, because it has already been paid for solving your problem, and with the help of what resources it will do it, it is not your concern.
LANGUAGE KNOWLEDGE.
Medical tourism operators often recommend hiring an interpreter to communicate with the hospital staff, they say, in the interests of their own health and comfort.
“In practice, average knowledge of English or basic German guarantee mutual understanding at a sufficient level: doctors themselves are interested in conveying their information to you and getting an answer, ” says Sergey. – European clinics in all possible ways try to solve the language problem and often have standard forms of documents in different languages, including Russian.
The treating doctors always tried to explain themselves to us without narrow medical terms, in simple words, so that everything was clear.
The interpreter was useful only for the first meeting with the doctor and signing documents. ”
overseas chambers.
It is designed for a maximum of 2-3 patients.
STRONG BY PRICE: ACCOUNTING TOGETHER Usually, clinics offer patients services in whole packages, which include all the necessary standard manipulations.
“But if there are complications, be ready to pay extra, and often a lot, ” — emphasizes Litovchenko.
Therefore, before starting treatment, ask for a detailed estimate, which will describe what exactly is included in your package, and for what they will ask in addition to it and how much.
Check to see if you really need all the services.
Any hospital consciously or accidentally can bill exorbitantly - do not be lazy to understand why.
The task of a decent intermediary is to save your money and time.
Important: examination and treatment is more profitable to take place in the same institution, so immediately ask to calculate the cost of both.
It may be that one clinic will offer an examination for $5,000, but the treatment in it will cost 150 thousand, and the other will immediately scare the bill for 8000 for the examination, but will treat for 60 thousand, that is, in the amount of the second option is more profitable.
In such cases, the intermediary, conscientiously saving your money (and this is his job), is indispensable: he knows the hospital "kitchen" like no one else, and is able to use the already paid package to the maximum, put everything necessary for the patient in the "package" period and reduce to zero additional expenses.
“Mine saved me a lot of money.
We wanted, for example, to issue additional bills for preliminary consultations, but he did not allow: they say, our 3-month all inclusive package begins to operate in 10 days, we will wait, we do not need anything additional.
They tried to enter paid medicines for $1000 a month, he argued and knocked out the free ones already included in the package, ” Elena quotes personal examples.
Well, while there is no confidence in the absolute integrity of your assistant, check every step.
After receiving the initial bill, specify the name of the doctor and contact him.
“Let him confirm that he has actually seen your medical records and recommends this treatment regimen or examination.
Sometimes, an international department or an intermediary simply writes into the account unnecessary, assuring doctors that the patient himself asked them, ” adds Sirosh.
Sites that lure for treatment in Israel, divorced so much that unfair earnings on patients worried even in the Israeli Medical Tourism Association (IMTA).
Its leading experts gave several tips on how not to get on scammers and not to waste money in vain.
They are also suitable for other countries. 1.
CLONE WEBSITES.
There are not so many clinics in Israel, as there are various offices offering the same services, but for a completely different price.
Knowing the patient ’ s desire to communicate with doctors directly, intermediaries clone the official websites of hospitals, and many do not immediately realize that they communicate and almost agree with a third party.
Pay attention first of all to the language of the site: if it is ideally Russian-speaking and at the same time there are no options for switching to Hebrew and English - 100% the site is intermediary and is designed for naive residents of the CIS.
Pay attention to the address and contact numbers: often "assistants" do not even bother to rent an office and leave mobile phones for communication, which respectable clinics never do.
Or leave the physical address of your company, which is easy to compare with the real coordinates of the clinic you are interested in.
REVIEWS.
Decent sites and forums should contain feedback from their satisfied patients.
Texts can only be trusted if they have some healthy criticism.
But it is better to watch the videos: the game of actors from natural behavior and impressions of people is not difficult to distinguish.
PREPAYMENT.
It is indeed required only in exceptional cases, in others there is no point in making it, and a serious institution will never require it.
The scheme of work of clinics is standard: services are paid in cash, card or transfer immediately before their provision, when the patient has already arrived in the country.
Not sure if you are that rare case - do not make a prepayment, no matter how you are asked. 4.
WITH LICENSE.
The most reliable intermediary companies are those that employ doctors with an Israeli medical license.
No doctor will want to risk his reputation and license, so the likelihood that you will be deceived is extremely low.
Most players of medical tourism do not have such specialists - that is, there will be no one to guide you from the beginning of treatment to the end, which will affect the optimization of the process and cost.
At the end of treatment, it is very important to get an epicrisis signed by a doctor: this means taking responsibility for all the manipulations that have been carried out with you.
No need for money in advance.

title: Weather conditions and condition of crops in January 2017 - NAAS of Ukraine
text:
The impact of weather conditions 15: 43 Source: APK-Inform Views: 55 Weather conditions and the state of crops in January 2017 - NAAS of Ukraine It is impossible not to agree with the fact that in recent years the agricultural sector of the world economy increasingly feels the manifestations of global warming.
A convincing example of this is the recognition of 2016 as the warmest year in the history of regular meteorological observations.
This also applies to most of the territory of Ukraine, in particular the steppe region, where traditionally significant areas are allocated by agricultural producers for winter crops.
Consequently, the increase in annual air temperature in most cases is still positive, although it requires farmers to more flexible tactics of applying basic technological techniques that allow to grow in recent years high yields of both winter wheat and winter barley - the most common winter crops in the farms of this agroecological zone.
A relative increase in temperature indicators and an increase in precipitation in the winter period allow plants of winter cereals and rapeseed to winter successfully even in cases when they begin wintering not in an optimal morphophysiological state.
This, as a rule, is a consequence of dry pre-sowing and early autumn periods and forces farmers to sow and receive seedlings of winter crops in a relatively late time.
This winter is most likely an exception to the weather rules that have been formed and observed in recent years.
It is characterized not only by a long cold period (almost without thaws), but also by a sufficient amount of precipitation, which made it possible to create a snow cover with an average height of 20-30 cm, which is held in the fields for almost two months of the calendar winter.
This allows plants to feel quite comfortable even with frosts, reaching on some days -20... -23 ° C.
At the same time, the problem of overwintering winter wheat plants and other winter crops from year to year remains relevant and is of great importance in the aspect of food and economic security of our state.
Measures to eliminate its consequences associated with additional material costs for seed and restructuring the schedule and plans for spring field work depend on the size of the possible death of winter crops.
As a rule, significant damage and death of winter crops inevitably leads to late sowing of spring crops, and consequently to a decrease in their yield and a decrease in the grain balance of the share of high-quality food grains.
Constant monitoring of indicators of hydrothermal conditions and monitoring of the state of plants in winter crops indicate that during the first two months of the calendar winter, there were no significant reasons for damage, and even more so for the death of crops.
This is due to the fact that December and January were characterized by small amplitude fluctuations in air temperatures, which approached the average long-term values, moderate soil temperature at the depth of the tillering node of plants and a sufficient height of the snow cover formed in areas occupied by winter crops.
So, in the third decade of December, the average air temperature was -3.3 ° C, which was only 0.3 ° C below the average long-term norm.
On some days, the maximum air temperature rose to + 1.5 ° C and decreased to -15.0 ° C. The average rainfall was insignificant and amounted to about 5 mm with an average long-term value of 16 mm.
At the end of the decade, the height of snow cover in winter fields averaged 8-10 cm, soil freezing reached 22 cm. The soil temperature at the depth of the tillering node of winter wheat was at the level of -1.7... -1.9 ° C, which was significantly higher than the critical freezing temperature of plants.
In general, in December, the average air temperature was -3.8 ° C with an average multi-year rate of -2.3 ° C. Precipitation for the month fell 29.8 mm, or about 65% of the average multi-year rate.
Most of January was characterized by a slight elevated temperature regime and a sufficient amount of precipitation, which fell mainly in the form of snow.
In the first decade of January, relatively unstable weather with precipitation prevailed.
The average air temperature was -3.3 ° C, which was 1.0 ° C above the average long-term norm.
On some days, the maximum air temperatures increased to 1.1 ° C of heat, and the minimum decreased to 11.6 ° C of frost.
The surface of snow in the daytime warmed up to + 1.4 ° C, and at night - cooled to -13.0 ° C.
The soil temperature at the depth of the winter wheat tillering node did not exceed -3.6 ° C at the calculated critical freezing temperature of plants -17.3 ° C. The depth of soil freezing during the decade was 22-23 cm. In the last days of the decade, the height of the snow cover increased to 25-30 cm, and the water reserves in the snow mass increased to 400 t / ha.
The average rainfall for the first decade of January was 24.5 mm, and exceeded the average long-term indicators by 7.5 mm.
In the second decade of January, the elevated temperature regime continued to be maintained, although on some days there were short-term sharp cooling.
So, the average temperature over the decade was -4.8 ° C, which was 2.0 ° C above the climatic norm.
In the daytime, the air temperature increased to 2.9 ° C, and at night - decreased to -17.6 ° C.
At the same time, the surface of the snow was cooled to -21.0 ° C.
A sufficiently powerful snow cover prevented the penetration of cold and a decrease in temperature indicators in the upper layers of the soil, and therefore at the depth of the tillering node of winter wheat, even in the coldest days, the soil temperature was not lower than -4.7 ° C, which was 12.6 ° C higher than the calculated critical freezing temperature of plants.
At the end of the decade, the average depth of freezing of the soil was about 21-23 cm, and the height of the snow cover - 25-28 cm. The average rainfall over the decade was 10.5 mm with an average long-term rate of 12 mm.
At the same time, precipitation during the reporting period fell mainly in the form of snow, although at the beginning of the decade there was even light rain and ice groats.
This led to the formation of a small hanging ice crust, which had a loose structure and reached 1.5-2.0 cm in thickness.
It should be added that a similar phenomenon was observed in the middle of the first decade of January.
As a result, an ice crust was formed in the fields of winter crops (with a thickness of not more than 0.5-0.6 cm), which was localized at a height of 8-10 cm from the soil surface and did not constitute an obvious threat to plants, since the thickness, structure and nature of its occurrence did not prevent gas exchange between winter crops and the environment.
At the same time, it can be argued with a high degree of probability that even the total effect of two low-power hanging crusts, which are observed in the fields in certain regions, is not able to lead to damage and death of plants during the last winter month.
For most of the third decade of January, a moderate hydrothermal regime was maintained.
The temperature indicators of the air during the day ranged from 1.5 ° C of heat to 18.3 ° C of frost.
However, in the last two days of the decade, there was a significant cooling in most of the territories of our country.
The air temperature decreased to -22... -24 ° C.
The soil temperature at the depth of the tillering node of winter wheat dropped to -5.0 ° C. The average amount of precipitation was close to the climatic norm.
Complex and threatening weather events for winter crops for a decade were not observed.
It is important to recall that in winter the plants of winter grain crops are in a state of forced rest.
Their damage and death in the field during this time are possible from the harmful effects of a complex of factors: low temperatures, ice crust, fouling, soaking, bulging, as well as diseases caused by adverse winter conditions and violations of agricultural technology.
The resistance of individual crops and varieties to such a complex relationship between biological features and a dynamic combination of environmental conditions and meteorological factors was called winter hardiness.
At the same time, frost resistance of plants is their ability to withstand temperatures below 0 ° C and at the same time maintain further viability.
It is known that winter damage by low temperatures (freezing) is considered the most common and most dangerous phenomenon.
The freezing of winter crops can occur in different periods of overwintering: in the beginning of winter, when severe frosts are observed in the absence of snow, in the middle and end of the winter period, as well as in early spring, when the winter hardiness of plants is significantly weakened.
Its value depends on the degree of hardening and frost resistance of plants.
Determination of the state of plants in winter crops can be carried out by a number of methods, namely, growing plants in monoliths, in aqueous and sugar solutions.
The most objective and reliable way to determine the viability of winter wheat plants in winter is the method of monoliths, the selection of which, according to existing recommendations, should be carried out on January 25, February 23 and March 10.
In addition, they are additionally taken after a sharp and prolonged decrease in the temperature regime.
Sampling should be carried out on plants of different degrees of development (good, medium and poorly developed) separately.
To do this, in the fall, even before the soil freezes, the places of selection of monoliths are marked.
Samples of plants of winter grain crops, selected by the method of monoliths in scientific institutions at the end of January, indicate that their viability, according to preliminary data, is quite high.
However, the final results will be known after growing the plants under controlled conditions for 10-14 days.
Thus, in the near future, the threat of mass damage and death in the fields of winter crops and rapeseed from freezing and ice crust is not expected.
In the current conditions of moderate hydrothermal regime in the future there are all prerequisites for the completion of wintering with winter crops with the least losses.
According to the materials of the National Academy of Agrarian Sciences (NAAS) of Ukraine Comments You must be authorized to leave a comment

title: The flow of migrants to the European Union through Libya will not decrease
text:
[Fabrice Legeri, CEO of Frontex]: “We have to be ready to meet the same number of migrants.
Last year, they increased by 17%.
We have recorded about 180,000 cases of illegal border crossings. ”
The number of migrants fleeing to the European Union through Libya and the Mediterranean Sea this year will be the same as last year.
This was announced by the head of the European Agency for the security of external borders Frontex.
Between 2014 and 2016, one million 600 thousand migrants arrived in the European Union via the Mediterranean Sea.
In March last year, the EU and Turkey signed a migration agreement.
According to it, Turkey must stop boats with refugees sailing from its shores to Greece.
After that, the main route of migrants was the way through Libya and the Mediterranean Sea to Italy.
According to the director of Frontex, EU countries should provide support to the Italian authorities, since a large number of refugees will arrive in the country.
The European Union is looking for ways to reduce the scale of the migration crisis, as well as to ensure that people do not die at sea.
The refugees arrive in Europe in the boats of illegal carriers.
As a rule, they are overcrowded and therefore often drown.
More than 5,000 refugees died and went missing in the Mediterranean last year.
[Fabrice Legeri, Executive Director of Frontex]: “I hope that in 2017 we will see a positive shift thanks to cooperation with countries of transit and origin of refugees.
Campaigns are underway to inform migrants about the risk, but it takes time for these measures to work. ”
According to the EU, about 70% of migrants arriving from Africa through Libya are fleeing poverty.
Since there are no military conflicts or repression by the authorities in their countries, the European Union intends to deny them asylum and deport them.
Frontex said the EU expelled 176,000 migrants last year.

title: Medical tourists from Russia are not afraid of high prices
text:
Experts of the Russian Association of Medical Tourism (AOMMT) together with foreign partners conducted an analysis of the outbound flow of medical tourists from Russia for 2016.
The analysis showed that Russian patients abroad are mainly looking for high-tech care and an impeccable level of service, and in the last place in their motivation is the price, unlike medical tourists from other countries of the world who go to be treated abroad in order to save money.
Over the past year, the behavior of medical tourists from Russia has changed in the direction of minimizing intermediary services in this area.
More and more Russians who have decided to undergo treatment abroad are independently contacting clinics and doctors, as well as forming a cultural and entertainment program for themselves.
The most popular health and medical directions in 2016 among Russians were: 1.
Israel; and 2.
Germany; and 3.
China; 4. USA; 5.
Ukraine; 6.
India; and 7.
Belarus.
Despite the 20-30% reduction in the volume of outbound medical tourism in 2016 (about 80 thousand Russians were treated in foreign clinics), such luxury health destinations as Switzerland practically did not lose their customers from Russia.
In general, wealthy patients from Russia and Asia are ready to pay about $8,000 per night.
In addition, there are several centers specializing in detox therapy and cosmetology.

title: In the Japanese city of Taiji began hunting for dolphins
text:
Tokyo, 09: 11 — REGNUM September 1 began the hunting season in the Japanese city of Taiji, which is known for its whaling.
The hunt did not cause a wave of outrage from animal advocates.
According to the Japanese news agency Kyodo Tsushin, dolphin hunting is carried out by pen, which in many countries of the world is considered inhumane: fishermen drive dolphins and small cetaceans into the bay, blocking their way back into the ocean with boats and nets.
Despite the criticism, this method is quite popular among Japanese fishermen.
In Japan, dolphin hunting and whaling are a traditional occupation, for many it is the main source of income and food.
Japan was forced to join the International Whaling Commission in 1988 and justified fishing for “research purposes ” until it finally withdrew from the membership on June 30, 2019.
Now fishermen from animal rights activists and other activists are protected by the police and the coast guard.
On September 1, according to Kyodo Tsushin, there were only 10 activists, but the fishermen returned with nothing.

title: LTV7: How Latvia will adapt to climate change
text:
Exotic fruits and floods, a rich harvest and the transfer of cities away from the sea.
All this awaits Latvia by the end of the XXI century.
The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development is already preparing a plan: what to do and how to live the national economy in the new climatic conditions, reports Russian Broadcasting LTV7.
Melons and peaches are already grown in Latvia.
Maybe there will be local pineapples?
Climate change is inevitable.
Every year there will be less frosty days, and more hot days and tropical nights.
This is evidenced by studies of Latvian climatologists.
“If earlier there was an average of 15 such days, then by the end of the century it is predicted to increase by a month and a half and, accordingly, it will be warmer and more days when the temperature rises above 25 degrees, ” says climate scientist Svetlana Aniskevich.
By the end of the century, summer in Latvia will become hotter by 5-6 degrees, and in winter it will be warmer by as much as 13 degrees.
This means that the average maximum temperature will rise from + 29 degrees to + 35, and the average minimum will rise from -24 degrees to -11.
“It is also predicted that there will be more precipitation, especially in winter, and given that the temperature will rise in winter, it will mostly be rains, ” says Aniskevich.
The climate is changing, and therefore the national economy of Latvia must also change.
The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development has already started working on Latvia ’ s national strategy “Adapting to Climate Change ” and is advising entrepreneurs to prepare for change as well.
“In a few months, we plan to start a public discussion of the draft Strategy and consultations with all the parties involved.
And then in the middle of the year it can be approved.
The strategy will determine what will help reduce the negative impact of climate change and how to exploit the positive aspects of climate change.
We will include the most significant measures in the policy planning documents to approve them in the Cabinet of Ministers, and then they will become mandatory, ” says Ilze Prouse, director of the Department of Climate Change of the ISDA.
Agriculture must benefit from warming.
The growing season will increase, which means that it will be possible to grow not only new, thermophilic crops, but also to harvest twice per season.
For other industries, change threatens losses.
City streets during the rains, which will become more, will flood more and more.
Due to climate change, coastal erosion will also increase.
“In principle, we are likely to have to move along the coast of individual objects, but there are also cities.
We understand that, and it ’ s terrible.
Obviously, if it is impossible to move, then it will be necessary to build infrastructure to protect these territories.
But among the flooded places is not only the coastal strip, it is also the territory along rivers and lakes.
This means that we will need to think about flood protection more than we do now, and not only during the spring flood.
And this is the cost of money, ” said Pruse.
Perhaps by the end of the century, there will be no trace of the usual Latvian landscapes.
The plant and animal world will change.
Already, scientists are observing the migration of many species of plants and animals.
Malaria mosquitoes have appeared in Latvia.
Pests from more southern regions used to die here in winter, and now they survive.
This is changing the environment more and more.
