title: Pioneer of improvement
text:
Strelka Institute in the framework of the partnership project "Urban Designer" prepared for Sib.fm an interview with the adviser to the mayor of Novosibirsk Alexander Lozhkin and the leading architect of KB "Strelka" Olga Deribas about what is happening in the capital of Siberia.
Novosibirsk is one of the cities participating in the large federal program of the Foundation for the Unified Institute of Development in the Housing Sector (created by AHML) and Strelka Design Bureau for the development of the urban environment.
Already in 2017, the first works on the development of key urban public spaces will be completed here, as well as in many other cities of Russia.
The next stage of improvement will be completed in 2018-2022.
What background?
Did the city not think about the development of public spaces, given that in Moscow, St. Petersburg and other cities the first changes date back to 2011?
Lozhkin: We started preliminary work on the development of public spaces back in 2014, when we held a project seminar together with a group of enthusiasts.
It resulted in the understanding that a systematic approach is needed to the development of public spaces.
We initiated the development of a comprehensive concept for the development of green areas and received the support of the new leadership of the City Hall, primarily the Department of Culture, which manages the parks.
Support at the first stages was still moral and administrative, since the financing of the concept was not included in the budget.
The budget of Novosibirsk for the improvement of the city: in 2017 - 274.8 million, in 2018 - 275.6 million, in 2019 - 276 million rubles And we made the first step that could be done without money: we invited 50 experts - architects and landscape designers, environmentalists, dendrologists, real estate market analysts, representatives of the development community, business, city activists...
We told them about the planned work and, based on the results of their survey, compiled a list of landscaped areas of public use of citywide significance, there were 32 such green zones.
Then we conducted an assessment of the state and potential of all 32 territories.
Every week for five months, from February to June, we went to some park or a group of squares.
Each trip was attended by 5 to 15 people from our pool of experts.
Our program of “checks ” was as follows: we inspected the territory, then for an hour and a half with passion interrogated the park director or the person responsible for the green area.
Interrogated?
Lozhkin: This is called an in-depth interview.
We have compiled a questionnaire of 25 positions, 125 assessment points, which allow us to assess the existing state of the territory and the potential for its development.
Each expert completed the questionnaire based on the results of the interview and examination and gave their recommendations.
Then we supplemented this initial assessment with historical, dendrological, sociological, urban planning, transport studies, big data analysis, and as a result we developed a general concept for the development of green areas of the city and prepared development passports for all 32 territories.
These trips also helped us to form a team that continued to do this work.
The increased attention of the media to our work, the reaction of experts and citizens to it helped to prove the need for the city administration to continue working in this direction.
Today, the Green City is one of the three official priorities of the city administration.
What led to the creation of these development passports?
Why are they needed?
Lozhkin: There is a general comprehensive concept for the development of green areas of the city, which contains functional, spatial, economic-marketing and organizational blocks.
And there is a vision of scenarios for the development of each of the 32 green zones, which allows, on the one hand, to easily enter the development of design projects of these territories and, on the other hand, to direct the current financing of repair and local landscaping works in such a way as to get the maximum effect.
The presence of passports also helps in the preparation of agreements of municipal-private partnership, when proposals for the development of squares and parks from business are received.
We presented the concept to the deputies of the city council, presented it at the public expert council on urban planning.
Support was unanimous.
During this period, we began an exchange of ideas and practices with Strelka Design Bureau, we initially had a very good relationship with them.
And then the program started, and we began to officially work together.
A question in between.
Is your cooperation with Strelka in Novosibirsk perceived positively or as a kind of intervention?
Lozhkin: I will not deceive, there is a tense attitude to the “Moscow expansion ”.
The Department of Construction and Architecture of the Novosibirsk City Hall was approved on October 9, 2007, Novosibirsk is a city with many architects and a strong local expert community.
So, of course, the question arose, why Muscovites, why Strelka?
Are we so stupid here, can't we do it ourselves?
We explain that Strelka Design Bureau works in cooperation with local architects, and many in the city managed to bring the benefits of such cooperation.
The work of local designers together with Strelka is the complementarity of professional competencies.
Local designers know the context and features of the territories, Strelka has an invaluable experience in implementing public space projects in Moscow in cooperation with the best world architects.
And combining different approaches is very useful for the development of the city.
Was there no work on the streets?
Only parks?
Lozhkin: Even before the Program appeared, we had a public group that began to develop a program for the improvement of Lenin Street and conducted pre-project studies.
Such studies are necessary because there is a conflict between pedestrians and motorists and it is necessary to choose the optimal development scenario.
Today, together with Strelka, with activists and with Novosibirsk architectural bureaus that are engaged in the development of the design project, we just want to come to a consensus.
What are Novosibirsk architectural bureaus?
Lozhkin: The Adaptik-A team is engaged in two park territories.
They helped us to develop the concept of green public spaces, made the concept of the development of the central park, in the portfolio of their implementations there is a favorite of the residents of Akademgorodok "Pond with ducks".
Lenin Street and Krasny Prospekt are designed by the Siberian Center for the Promotion of Architecture, they have experience in forming interdisciplinary teams to solve complex complex problems.
And activists who began to work on Lenin Street are included in the work.
Now a little more about the projects.
What is planned to be done in Novosibirsk in the framework of work with Strelka?
Deribas: At the end of 2016, our specialists conducted anthropological and other studies in the city, within the framework of which the key public spaces of the city were identified, which are most popular among residents or have cultural or historical value.
The results of the study were then discussed with the city administration.
As a result, the program included the territories, the improvement of which had to be carried out in the first place: Mikhailovskaya embankment and exit from the metro station "Rechnoy vokzal", a park in the Zatulinsky residential area, Lenin Street and Krasny Avenue.
Moreover, we plan to transform the embankment already in 2017, the remaining projects will be implemented in the near future, in 2018-2022.
Tell us about the roles and responsibilities of all participants in the process.
Deribas: The Novosibirsk architectural workshop Adaptik-A is engaged in the development of the Mikhailovskaya embankment of Novosibirsk, Strelka Design Bureau does not create a concept for this territory.
The role of the design bureau is exclusively in the preparation of a preliminary technical specification for the design and subsequent author ’ s supervision.
0 events in Novosibirsk is organized by the Union of Architects of Russia in 2017, as follows from the schedule of the design bureau together with the local administration, taking into account the preliminary anthropological studies and analysis of the territory, prepares a vision of the technical task of the future development of the embankment.
After the design bureau agreed on the vision with all interested parties, the workshop "Adaptik-A" began to develop the design and working documentation of the project.
By the end of April-early May 2017, the workshop will present a preliminary concept of the city administration.
It is important to understand that the local architectural workshop is engaged in the development of the territory - therefore, in the work it takes into account its experience as residents of Novosibirsk, its own developments and the results of research of Strelka Design Bureau.
Construction and implementation of the concept is on the side of the city administration.
All of this is funded by federal subsidies.
What are the main trends and features of the design and construction of modern embankments in Russia?
Deribas: At the moment, in Russia, when designing embankments, special attention is paid to their coastline, whether it is necessary to strengthen it artificially, or whether the river already has naturally formed banks.
Eco-embankments, where the banks of the river are fortified in a natural way, can develop further or change over time (for example, due to the organization of the beach, approaches to the water, the expansion of the embankment).
Where the river has formed natural banks, it is not necessary to strengthen them artificially.
Lies in landscaping: an interview in 2012 by architect Alexander Lozhkin about the impracticability of the master plan of Novosibirsk What difficulties do specialists face in the reconstruction of existing embankments?
Deribas: The main difficulties: outdated communications, technical miscalculations of previous works, self-construction, strengthening of the coastline, preparation of organized approaches to the water.
Also, when working, it is necessary to take into account such an important factor as shipping.
This factor can make important adjustments to the development of the waterfront concept (for example, the presence of a berth).
The perfect waterfront – what do you think it is?
Deribas: It is better to talk about the typology of the ideal embankment than about the “ideal embankment ”.
Any embankment should be a continuous walking route so that people are comfortable and comfortable walking along the embankment in their city.
In addition, more convenience for people gives the distinction of walking and cycling routes and the identification of areas of quiet and active recreation.
It should be present recreation areas where a person tired of walking could relax.
Ideally, there should be the possibility of cultural events or sports training.
The waterfront should attract new groups of people.
The embankment should be a barrier-free environment suitable for use by everyone, from children to disabled categories of citizens.
In addition, a diverse landscape should be presented on the embankment.
30 kilometers is the length of the longest embankment in Europe.
It is important to take into account the “environmental factor ” of the object, when starting work, you need to understand the meaning of the embankment (for example, the beach will not look normal in the center of the city, and the cultural site will be out of place on the outskirts).
Has this been sorted out, and the participation of residents in the discussion of projects is being carried out or only planned?
Deribas: First of all, preliminary studies were carried out before the development of the technical specification: anthropological, GIS-analytics, analysis of social networks, and so on.
In addition, the city administration shared its knowledge with us.
In addition, about every two weeks, Strelka specialists come to the city to discuss current work, meetings with the administration and Novosibirsk experts.
That ’ s not to mention the endless conference calls we hold almost daily.
LAUGHTER: Let me add, my friends.
On March 10, we held the first workshop on the waterfront.
It was very successful, in total, more than a hundred people attended the event, 64 people worked in the project teams, and this is all Novosibirsk, active citizens and experts.
And there were useful results, some provisions of the terms of reference were revised according to the results of the workshop.
We have adjusted the location of the zone of the Football Summer festival, some of the people from the project teams were involved in further work.
In April, within the framework of the famous architectural festival "Golden Capital", a two-day workshop was held dedicated to Lenin Street, with the invitation of tutors from other cities. * * * How to create a cultural center The online school of urban entrepreneurs Vector of the Strelka Institute launched a new educational program.
The course "How to open a cultural center" tells how art platforms are organized and live in Russian cities and what you need to do to open your creative space.
The course is equally useful for an employee of the creative space, an organizer of mass events, a representative of an NGO or a creative entrepreneur.
Each of the seven lessons is devoted to a specific topic - from research in the city and determining the format of the project to the choice of premises and filling the program grid.
The course helps to understand how to effectively work with finances, attract partners and sponsors and set up channels for promoting your cultural center.
Clear language, practical tasks, experiments and more than twenty relevant examples of creating successful creative spaces are what helps to look at entrepreneurship in the field of culture from the inside, analyze developments and neutralize the weaknesses of your project in time.
The main characters and co-authors of the course were Julia Krivtsova and Sergey Kremnev, curators of the TEXTIL cultural center and the regional agency of creative initiatives LIFT-project from Yaroslavl, as well as Julia Terekhova and Maxim Muzalevsky, creators of the Museum "House with a Lion" and the cultural center "New House" from the Saratov region.
A trial lesson is already available on the project website.
You can get access to all lessons by paying a subscription for 2 999 rubles.
The final task of the course is the presentation of your art project.
When completing all the course tasks, participants will receive an official certificate of the online school.
Vector is an online school of urban entrepreneurs of Strelka Institute for those who want to study their city, find ideas for new projects and create them.
The school teaches the entrepreneurial way of thinking.
Vector courses help to find new niches in the city, understand people ’ s needs, turn problems into solutions and create successful urban projects – commercial and social, long-term and short-term, large-scale and small.
Currently, there are eight courses available on Vector: "How to create a successful public space", "How to create a sports project", "Excursions as a business", "Financial literacy for entrepreneurs", "How to create a mobile application", "How to open a hostel", "How to create a new urban startup", "How to explore the city in creative ways".

title: Spray on ribonucleic acid can replace pesticides
text:
Scientists from the University of Queensland (Australia) have developed a nano-biodegradable compound on a double-stranded macromolecule of ribonucleic acid, used to control weeds, pests and plant diseases.
Scientists have named a compound that can replace pesticides, “BioClay ” (BioClay).
The development report is published in the journal Nature Plants.
When the composition is sprayed on plants, a virus-specific double-stranded RNA is released, which triggers a natural protective mechanism in the plant.
In the process, RNA breaks down into small fragments that attack the virus without affecting the genome of the plant.
The first experiments showed that after a single spraying, the composition can protect tobacco plantations from viruses for 20 days.
Testing could begin by the end of 2017.
"The first tests will be on viruses that affect chilli peppers and tomatoes," lead researcher Neena Mitter told SciDev.Net.
“Even using pesticides, we lose about 40% of the crop due to pests and pathogens.
We hope that the use of our development will reduce the level of losses, "Mitter said.
According to her, the advantage of "Bioglina" is that it, unlike pesticides, does not kill beneficial microorganisms along with pests.
Technological solutions based on RNA are used by many agricultural corporations.
Recall that now in the United States, Monsanto, one of the world's largest manufacturers of agrochemicals, is suing the authorities of California, which require to place labels on products warning about the danger of herbicides - means to combat weeds.
Monsanto claims that the remedy does not carry risks to human health.
Against the company at the trial will testify the relatives of farmers claiming that they got cancer because of the use of the herbicide Roundup.
The material was provided by the project "+ 1".

title: Top 5 books from the sister of the national writer of Kyrgyzstan Roza Aitmatova
text:

Today, Roza Aitmatova is a guest of our traditional top-5 category and presents her favorite books.
The story "White steamer" Chingiz Aitmatov.
In the story Chingiz Torekulovich raised the eternal theme of good and evil.
It is a message to humanity: do good in this world.
In addition, I think the work forms in a person a sense of humane and careful attitude to nature.
Another important aspect that Chingiz Torekulovich reveals to us is the preservation of the value of the family.
Children should not be left orphans with living parents.
Rose Aitmatova is wise, isn't it?
“Grandfather says that if people don ’ t remember their fathers, they will go bad.
Grandfather says that then no one will be ashamed of bad deeds, because children and children of children will not remember them.
And no one will do good things, because the children will not know about it anyway, ” the book says.
I think that this story and now, in the age of globalization, more than ever should be in demand for the younger generation.
We must not forget our roots and national traditions.
This, as you know, leads to the decline of culture.
Turning to metaphors through the legend of the horned Mother of the Deer, Chingiz Torekulovich reminds us of how important the spiritual connection of generations is for our people.
Rose Aitmatova The problem of good and evil is the basis of fairy tales and legends.
But if in fairy tales good almost always triumphs, and evil is punished, then in reality this is not always the case.
I think the story "White steamer" is also interesting because it simultaneously coexists modern life and ancient legend, and the problem of good and evil is solved differently from the usual outcome.

2 The novel “Syngan kylych ” (“ Broken sword ”) by Tologon Kasymbekov.
It was difficult for the Kyrgyz historical path to independence.
“Broken Sword ”, telling us about the turbulent and complex historical events during the period of Kyrgyzstan ’ s accession to Russia, reminds us that we must take care of our history more than ever.
This level of historical works in Kyrgyz literature is not enough.
Knowing your history is the key to the future.
You can read the novel here.
Ernest Hemingway ’ s “The Old Man and the Sea ”.“ Oh, I wish there was a boy with me! ” But there is no boy with you, ” he thought. “You can only count on yourself, and even though it is dark now, it would be better if you tried to get that last forest, cut it off and tie two spare skeins...
What simple words.
"Fish," he called quietly, "I will not part with you until I die."
For many people, including me, this is a very powerful work.
One that needs to be read between the lines.
The artistic power of the story is to show the inner strength of a person and his ability to realize not only the beauty and grandeur of the surrounding world, but also his place in it.
A person should always be able to win, no matter what difficulties in life.
In 1954, Ernest Hemingway was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature “for the storytelling skills demonstrated in The Old Man and the Sea, as well as for the influence on modern prose. ”

4 thoughts on “1916.
Diaries.
A letter to Stalin by Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.
“By the will of fate, I have witnessed the events of the greatest historical epoch.
Therefore, historically interesting fixation of what you saw, experienced, felt for each day.
This can be done with the help of a diary, and I will try to do it.
True, I do it with a great delay, but better late than never, ” wrote Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.
"My diary...
From now on, you are my only, faithful and silent friend.
Faithful for time and time.
You are loyal to me as long as you are in my hands, or you can become a traitor when you pass into the wrong hands.
The last possibility is not excluded, but still I will not hide anything from you.
I will tell you the thoughts and experiences not only of a political figure, but also of a mortal person, ” Reading Abdrakhmanov ’ s diaries, you imagine what life was like in our society in the thirties of the last century.
Immerse yourself in that difficult time for our people, the history of which for many years was distorted and in every possible way concealed from society.
Between these very personal lines you can feel the scale of Abdrakhmanov as a statesman who faithfully served the country for its prosperity.
Reflections of Zhusup Abdrakhmanov, his feelings for the future of the country, active work on the creation and strengthening of our statehood should serve as a vivid example for the current generation.

The life of the famous poetess Tenti Adysheva in our history occupies a special place.
Describing her life, she captured the period of the rise of Kyrgyz literature from the times of Zhoomart Bokonbaev, Mukay Elebaev, Aala Tokombaev, Zhusup Turusbekov, Temirkul Umotaliev, Kubanychbek Malikov, Alykul Osmonov, Tugelbai Sydykbekov.
As a poet, she managed to describe her memories in a poetic way, which causes great reader interest.
Kyrgyz women have always played a special role.
Tenti Adysheva is one of such bright personalities that left an indelible mark on our memory.
Given that the formation of her personality took place in the difficult circumstances of the totalitarian regime of Soviet power, her life positions and fate can serve as a vivid example for the younger generation.
Rose Aitmatova The story “My Komuz with torn strings ” was reprinted twice, instantly diverged and became a bibliographic rarity.
In it, in the magnificent literary Kyrgyz language, live portraits of the "Mighty Bunch" of great personalities - the founders of Kyrgyz literature, culture, art and science are given.

title: Climate change threatens coffee quality
text:
Coffee crops are becoming more scarce due to global warming, lack of rainfall and the spread of disease.
This is reported by Bloomberg with reference to market participants and researchers.
According to estimates of the international bank Rabobank International, the coffee production market is declining for the fourth year in a row due to the lack of quality raw materials.
At the same time, demand for coffee in the United States is expected to be the highest this year.
Geneticists at the World Coffee Research (WCR) are looking for plants that can adapt to environmental changes.
“Global warming means that the places that will remain suitable for growing coffee are colder or higher, ” said lead geneticist Christophe Montanon.
His team collected 30 varieties of coffee trees from 20 countries and planted them in a controlled environment in Laos, where they grew at temperatures up to two degrees.
The seven species that survived the cold snap will now be sent for testing in vivo to other regions, from Brazil to Guatemala.
According to conservation organization Conservation International, to meet global demand for coffee, production needs to increase by at least 50% by 2050.
At the same time, as the researchers from WCR calculated, the soils on which coffee is grown, used in famous coffee houses around the world, will be halved by then.
In Brazil ’ s famed coffee state of Espirito Santo, production has plummeted due to the region receiving only 50% of its normal rainfall over the past three years and the average temperature rising by three degrees.
Some farmers, due to weather conditions, moved to other regions or invested in other crops, such as pepper.
Also, the harvest of coffee beans is threatened by disease.
For example, in 2013, Otto Pérez Molina, then President of Guatemala, declared a national emergency situation due to the spread of the fungus Roya fungus.
The disease affected about 70% of the country ’ s coffee crop, resulting in a loss of nearly $1 billion for coffee producers in Guatemala, a coffee-exporting country.
According to WCR, the fungus destroyed about 18.2 million bags of coffee worth about $2.5 billion from 2011 to 2016.
The losses left 1.7 million people unemployed.
In the world there are plants, which global warming, on the contrary, has benefited.
According to a study published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, rising temperatures will lead to a significant increase in olive yields in the Mediterranean.

title: Pandora ’ s Box – In the United States for the first time rolled out of the hangar the largest aircraft in the world (PHOTOS, VIDEO)
text:
May 31, 2017 in Mojave (California) took place the roll-out of the almost completed construction of the Stratolaunch Model 351 carrier aircraft (also sometimes referred to as "Roc", in fact, the official name has not yet been assigned) of the aerospace system "air launch" Stratolaunch, created by the American company Stratolaunch Systems (as part of Vulcan Aerospace Corporation). The BMPD blog.
Rolling out of the carrier aircraft Stratolaunch Model 351 aerospace system "air start" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems.
Mojave (California), 31.05.2017 (c) Stratolaunch Systems The built twin-body Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is the largest aircraft in history, having a wingspan of 117 m and a length of 73 m. The maximum take-off weight should be 590 tons, with a suspended payload weight of 230 tons.
Thus, the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft in wingspan exceeds the former largest aircraft in the world, the Soviet An-225 "Mriya" (which has a wingspan of 88.4 m), although the An-225 retains an advantage in length (84 m) and maximum take-off weight (640 tons).
The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is equipped with six twin-circuit Pratt & Whitney PW4056 turbojet engines with a thrust of 25 tons, removed from two decommissioned Boeing 747-400 aircraft.
The landing gear of the aircraft is 28-wheel, take-off distance with full load should be calculated to be 3800 m. The maximum range of the aircraft with full load will not exceed 3700 km.
The aircraft is designed to be used as a carrier for the aerospace system Stratolaunch, created by the American company Stratolaunch Systems, founded by co-founder Microsot Paul Allen and the famous aircraft designer Bert Rutan (who acted as the actual chief designer of the aircraft) (since 2015 Stratolaunch Systems is a subsidiary of the corporation created by the same Paul Allen Vulcan Aerospace).
The aircraft is designed to launch space launch vehicles using the "air launch" method, which will be carried out from an altitude of approximately 10,500 m. The launch vehicle should be suspended under the central part of the wing between the fuselages.
In the course of design and construction, the SpaceX Falcon 9 Air and Orbital ATK Pegasus II launch vehicles were successively replaced as payload options, and now only the long-known Orbital ATK Pegasus XL light launch vehicle used for “air launches ” from“ conventional ” aircraft in the United States since 1990 is considered as such (starting mass of 23.2 tons, payload mass load of 443 kg), and for which there was no need to create such a giant carrier - although the possibility of carrying and launching from it in one flight up to three Pegasus XL launch vehicles is claimed.
In light of this, the outlook for Stratolaunch is still uncertain.
In 2014, the notorious Sierra Nevada Corporation announced the development of a smaller version of the project of its lightweight manned shuttle Dream Chaser (previously rejected by NASA), which was to be launched using an unnamed launch vehicle developed by the Orbital ATK.
However, there is no information about the development of this project in relation to Stratolaunch.
During the launch vehicle roll-out ceremony on May 31, Stratolauch Systems CEO Joan Floyd said that the company would "actively explore a wide range of launch vehicles, allowing us to provide more flexibility for customers."
Rolling out of the carrier aircraft Stratolaunch Model 351 aerospace system "air start" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems.
The Stratolaunch Model 351 was designed and built under the contract of Stratolaunch Systems by Scaled Composites, founded by Bert Rutan and now owned by Northrop Grumman Corporation.
The project was announced in December 2011.
The construction of the aircraft was carried out in a specially built for this purpose in 2012 in Mojave giant hangar.
The scheme of the intended use of the aircraft carrier Stratolaunch Model 351 of the aerospace system "air launch" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems (c) Stratolaunch Systems The program is lagging behind in terms of about two years.
Currently, the beginning of flight tests of the carrier aircraft is scheduled for the end of 2017, and the first demonstration space launch from it - in 2019.
The start of commercial launches will be possible in this case from 2020.

title: The wine of the climate change era
text:
Mireya Torres is a representative of the fifth generation of the famous family of Spanish hereditary winemakers.
These vineyards are over 150 years old.
But today they face a new threat: climate change.
The scorching summer sun, heat waves and droughts could complicate the lives of more than 4,000 wineries across Spain in the future.
The volume of this industry is 7 billion euros per year.
Mireya Torres, owner of the Torres wineries: “It all started in 2008 when my father watched Al Gore ’ s documentary The Inconvenient Truth, he was just shocked.
And from our own observations and evidence that in the summer we had more and more days with temperatures above 30 degrees, he realized that we had problems, and we had to start working. "
Recent studies have shown that due to a temperature increase of 2.7 to 4.7 degrees and a decrease in precipitation by 40%, grape cultivation will become impossible in Southern Europe and the Mediterranean by 2070.
Due to global warming, the familiar taste of the beloved Cabernet will change very much and irrevocably.
Mireia Torres: "Some varieties that are currently commercial are very well established, and they produce wines of really high quality in most Spanish wineries, but by the end of the century they will change and will not be the same."
In search of a milder temperature, the Torres family climbed the mountains.
Colder nights in the foothills of the Catalan Pyrenees allow the grapes to ripen to a perfect level of sweetness and peel color.
Jaime Velázquez, Euronews: “When the Torres family bought this plot of land 1,000 meters above sea level, they had no idea they would eventually plant a vine on it.
Winters here, in the foothills of the Catalan Pyrenees, are very long and severe, but the vine took root and began to grow quite quickly.
How soon will high-altitude vineyards become the norm if we don ’ t stop global warming? ”
Javi Ermella, manager of the Torres vineyard in San Miguel, says that with every hundred meters above sea level, the temperature drops by almost a degree, so that in the conditions of warming, the vineyards will rise.
Javi Ermella, manager: "In the plains, in the lowlands, vineyards now have problems during periods of intense heat.
As a result, the wine loses its freshness, aroma.
They lose balance.
And the only way to solve this problem is to move to higher areas. ”
But back to the valley.
Here, Spanish growers are restoring a traditional vineyard that has been abandoned for decades in favor of more commercial varieties.
This vine is well adapted to adverse weather conditions.
Perhaps behind some forgotten indigenous varieties is the future of Spanish vineyards.
Why doesn ’ t this Forcada fault become the Chardonnay of the climate change era?

title: Russian scientists will test the equipment for the ITER reactor at the Globus-M2
text:
NOVOSIBIRSK, July 18 – RIA Novosti.
The completion in 2018 of the modernization of the unit of the unique research complex "Globus-M" in St. Petersburg will partially reproduce the conditions of the experimental international thermonuclear reactor ITER, the launch of which is scheduled for 2025, according to a joint press release of the Physical-Technical Institute (PTI) of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Institute of Nuclear Physics (INP) of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
It is explained that the opportunity to test the equipment developed in the PTI for ITER will appear after an increase of 2-2.5 times in the research complex "Globus-M" of the magnetic field, as well as current flowing through the plasma.
As a result of the modernization of the Globus-M tokamak, the temperature and density of the plasma will significantly increase, and, consequently, the radiation load on the inner surface of the discharge chamber will also increase.
Thus, it becomes possible to reproduce conditions close to those that will be in the near-wall area of the ITER reactor, the launch of the first plasma in which is planned in 2025, "Vasily Gusev, chief researcher of the Ioffe Institute, said in a statement.
He noted that the PTI was responsible for the development of three diagnostic systems for ITER.
The equipment can be tested on the Globus-M2 tokamak now.
For example, there will be tests of a plasma diagnostic system for the scattering of laser radiation.
The ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) reactor is being built near the Cadarache Research Center in southern France jointly by the European Union, Russia, China, India, Japan, South Korea and the United States.
This will be the first large-scale attempt to demonstrate the feasibility of using a fusion reaction to generate energy on an industrial scale.
The reactor is based on the use of the tokamak thermonuclear system - an installation for magnetic confinement of plasma, having the form of a ring.
If the ITER project is successful, humanity will be able to count on the possession of an almost inexhaustible source of energy.

title: Due to the pollution of the atmosphere, crops will grow
text:
Anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide have led to plants opening their stomata less and growing much faster than usual, consuming the same amount of water.
Australian researchers analyzed how plants' consumption of carbon dioxide and water changed between 1982 and 2011.
It turned out that plants began to absorb 17 percent more CO2 each year than 35 years ago.
However, their water consumption has not changed.
Due to human carbon dioxide emissions, they began to use available water more efficiently.
This reduces the likelihood of droughts and increases yields around the world.
This article is published in Nature.
The authors used data from satellite images and a number of ground-based observations on different continents of the Earth to determine how the primary bioproductivity of land plants changed in 1982-2011.
They define bioproductivity as the absorption of the main building material of plants – carbon dioxide.
It has grown by 17%.
This was partly due to the growth of the area occupied by vegetation (reducing the area of ​ ​ deserts), partly due to the more intensive growth of plants where they already were.
In both cases, the cause was an increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide.
In 1982, it was only 340 parts per million in the atmosphere, today due to emissions from power plants - more than 400 parts per million.
CO2 not only acts as the main building material of plants (from it and water they receive nutrients during photosynthesis), but also increases the efficiency of their use of water.
Ground-based plants get carbon dioxide by opening the stomata.
When its content in the atmosphere increased, the plants began to open the stomata weaker or even reduced their number per unit surface area.
Therefore, they began to lose less water in the process of breathing.
As shown by the study, the loss of water for evaporation by flora for 1982-2011 years practically did not change.
Despite this, the increase in total productivity was 17 percent.
The researchers note that the increase in the efficiency of water use was especially active in tropical forests and temperate forests (in the illustration).
The latter, as seen on the map, particularly affected Russia, Sweden, Finland and part of Canada.
In the north, this process, scientists believe, is mainly due to the active growth of leaf area in forests.

title: Weather swing
text:
Over the last hundred years, the average annual temperature in Russia has increased by 1.29 degrees Celsius, on a global scale - by 0.74.
In Bashkortostan over the past 30 years, the growth amounted to 0.7 degrees.
These seemingly relatively small averages lead to an increase in the number of particularly hot days of summer and winter thaws with frequent transitions through zero, as well as droughts, floods, tornadoes and windstorms.
Therefore, the question of what consequences global warming will have for Bashkortostan and its capital, and how the current weather surprises are associated with it, is becoming more and more relevant.
If in the period from 1998 to 2005 their number in the region ranged from 5 to 11, then in 2010 there were 37, and in 2016 – 34.
This is causing serious damage.
In 2010, most of Russia, including our republic, was dominated by an anomalous blocking anticyclone lasting about 50 days, although usually the duration of such weather events does not exceed 5-7 days.
The result was a severe drought, because of which an emergency was declared in the region, and the economic damage amounted to more than 13 billion rubles.
The situation, albeit on a smaller scale, was repeated in 2012.
In the republic, due to high air temperature and a shortage of precipitation, an emergency mode was also introduced, and the economic damage amounted to 2.5 billion rubles.If severe droughts happened before, then a new negative natural phenomenon was the severe tornadoes that had passed through the territory of Bashkortostan in 2007 and 2014, which had not previously been observed.
In 2007, squally wind swept through the territories of Birsky and Dyurtyulinsky districts, mainly forests affected by it.
The 2014 crash had more serious consequences.
In Krasnokamsk, Yanaul and Kaltasinsky districts, 478 residential buildings were damaged, gas and electricity supply was disrupted.
Damage from the elements amounted to about 200 million rubles.
According to meteorologists, such powerful tornadoes are characteristic of the equator and subtropics, and in our latitudes are anomalous and associated with changes in global processes in the layers of the atmosphere.
This phenomenon occurred in 2013, when due to heavy rains in the Abzelilovsky and Beloretsky districts, 1094 residential buildings, 13.5 km of roads and 14 bridges fell into the flooding zone, and the total amount of damage exceeded 250 million rubles.
According to the doctor of agricultural sciences, Professor Khalil Safin, under the influence of erosion processes, Bashkortostan annually loses about 3 million tons of humus, which ensures soil fertility.
If 50 years ago, the content of humus in the arable layer of the republic was 11-12%, now it has decreased to 7-8%, and a decrease to 2-3% is considered critical for chernozems.
According to experts, the soil crisis may occur in the steppe zone of the Trans-Urals in 20 years, in the Pre-Ural steppe - in 40, the Southern forest-steppe - in 50.
The most alarming situation is in the Northern forest-steppe zone, where it can begin in 10 years.A serious threat to the agricultural sector are insect pests, which in recent years do not die due to warm winters and quickly multiply in the hot spring-summer period.
This applies, first of all, to locusts: its spread now reaches the Karmaskalinsky and Ufa districts, and in 2016, due to the invasion of insects in 6 districts, an emergency was declared.
Dry years have a negative impact on the state of the forest fund, causing an increase in fire risk.
In 2010, 635 forest fires were registered on the territory of the republic, destroying more than a thousand hectares of forests, in 2012 there were 243 fires, in which about 900 hectares of forest were lost.
Several arid years in a row weaken trees, lead to diseases, parasite damage and death.
In 2013-2014, 1.6 and 1.58 thousand hectares of forest, respectively, died, which is one and a half times higher than the losses from fires in the period of drought.Heat in the metropolis Climate change affects not only the processes in the forest and agricultural sector, but also the infrastructure of cities.
During the abnormally hot summer of 2010, asphalt on the roads was heated to a temperature above + 60, and road bitumen according to Russian state standards should retain its working properties only up to + 45-50.
As a result, shear gauges were formed on many roads, especially in Ufa, which was loaded with transport.
Great damage to roads was caused by the abnormally warm winter of 2015 / 2016, when more than 60 transitions of outdoor air temperature through the zero mark were recorded - from minus to plus and back, while the average for our climate indicator of such transitions is no more than 10 per season.Dry weather and a decrease in the level of rivers leads to problems of drinking water supply.
In August-September 2010 in the area of ​ ​ the capital was the lowest level of White in the entire history of observations - minus 152 centimeters above zero post.
As a result, serious problems with drinking water have arisen in many settlements located near Ufa and do not have a centralized water supply.
Low water also seriously affects the work of large water intakes.
In shallow rivers, the concentration of harmful substances increases, the water becomes more rigid.
So, at the level of the Ufa River 2.5 meters, there are no problems with the hardness of drinking water, and with a decrease to 1.5 meters and below, it increases sharply.
According to the department of agrometeorology and agrometeorological forecasts of the Bashgidrometcentr, thanks to climate warming, the yield of grain in 30-40 years can increase by 6.1%, in 60-70 years it will increase by 12.9%.
Improving yields in the medium term will be influenced by factors such as an increase in positive temperatures during the growing season, an increase in average annual rainfall, a greater number of warm winters and an extension of frost-free periods.
However, a further increase in temperature can lead to droughts and a drop in yields. Due to mild winters and a shorter heating season, there is a steady trend in the republic and Ufa to reduce heat consumption.
If the 2014 / 2015 season lasted 218 days, then 2015 / 2016 – only 203.
As a result, the supply of heat only at BashRTS fell by 0.8 million gigacalories, which significantly reduced payments to the population.
Another advantage of milder winters was a decrease in the number of accidents in the utility system.
In the penultimate heating season, the engineering equipment of the resource supplying organizations of Ufa recorded a decrease in the accident rate by 6%, which is largely due to the warm winter, reducing the load on the grid.According to experts, agriculture and urban economy should as soon as possible begin to adapt to the conditions of global warming, minimizing the negative and using the positive moments of climate change.

title: Humanity will face a protein deficiency by 2050
text:
Increasing carbon dioxide levels due to global warming reduces the amount of protein in staple crops such as rice and wheat.
The lack of an important component in food will endanger the health and lives of vulnerable groups of the world's population.
According to a report published in the journal Environmental Research Letters, more than 150 million people around the globe will be at risk of protein deficiency by 2050.
About the results of the new study, scientists reported the publication AFP.
Many studies confirm the reduction in the amount of protein in plants under the influence of the increasing concentration of CO 2 in the atmosphere of the planet.
In plants, other vital trace elements - zinc and iron - also break down.
Scientists cannot find a reason for how or why carbon dioxide emissions reduce the nutrient content of plants.
For the first time, a group of scientists from Harvard University conducted a field experiment in which plants were exposed to high concentrations of carbon dioxide.
The hypothesis was that carbon dioxide increases the percentage of starch in foods, thereby reducing the amount of protein and other nutrients.
The lead author of the study, a senior researcher at the School of Health.
Shanna at Harvard University Samuel Myers said that the theory was not confirmed.
“Our short answer is that we don ’ t know why (the amount of protein decreases – ‘ + 1 ’), ” Myers said.
Scientists estimate that by 2050 the protein content in barley will decrease by 14.6%, in rice by 7.6%, in wheat by 7.8%, in potatoes by 6.4%.
76% of the world ’ s population depends on these cultures.
Acute deficiency of protein and trace elements will be experienced by residents of sub-Saharan Africa, India, and South Asia.
The diet of the inhabitants of these countries will lose 5% or more protein.
According to the UN, if the menu is not enough protein, children remain stunted, more sick, and more likely to die at an early age.
William Cline, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for World Economics, presented a report in March 2008, which was published in the journal Finance and Development.
Klein studied the risks of developing countries and stressed that poor regions are more affected by climate change than economically developed countries.
They are more attached to agriculture and slower to adapt to change.
Harvest losses due to high temperatures can be up to 50% during the growing season (the time when growth and development of plants are possible).
“According to forecasts of climatologists, climate change in general will have a negative impact on crops.
In case of delay in reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the world can expect an even greater spread of hunger, forced migration and wars for food and water, "Polina Karkina, an expert at Greenpeace Russia, told" + 1 ".
If the situation with emissions does not change, the agriculture of states with good productive potential will also be threatened.
"Greenpeace Russia" cited estimates of Roshydromet, according to which by the end of the century the productivity of individual regions of Russia may decrease by 50%, which indicates the global nature of the problem.
Since the authors of the study from Harvard University did not find the causes of protein decay, they offer some measures to combat the effects of global warming.
According to scientists, to prevent protein deficiency in the diet can be a gradual transition to less dependent on carbon dioxide crops.
Existing crops can be enriched with additional nutrients or add alternative sources of protein to the diet.
Meanwhile, William Cline is confident that increasing agricultural productivity will not solve the problems with climate.
“Russia should focus on energy efficiency.
Today, almost every second ton of coal, oil and cubic meter of gas are burned in vain.
It is necessary to engage in the development of renewable energy sources, proper management of forests and the introduction of separate waste collection throughout the country, ” said Karkina, an expert at Greenpeace Russia.
The material was provided by the project "+ 1".

title: In the wall of the Italian Museum found a painting by Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ” stolen 22 years ago – and he was one of the most wanted art objects – Meduza
text:
Polizia di Stato / Reuters / Scanpix / LETA In the Italian city of Piacenza found a painting by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is estimated at 60 million euros.
The painting was stolen in 1997 and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.
The painting was found in the wall of the Ricci Oddy gallery, from where it was taken 22 years ago.
Examination has not yet confirmed the authenticity of the painting, but the gallery staff believe that it is the original.
Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.
In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.
The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery, which received his name.
“Portrait of a Woman ” was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.
In 1996, 18-year-old art student Claudia Maga noticed that Portrait of a Woman was similar to another female portrait of Klimt that no one had seen since 1912.
The magician made photocopies of both works of the artist from the album on art and with the help of tracing paper superimposed on each other.
Contours and sizes matched.
She told about her find to the then director of the gallery Ricci Oddi Ferdinando Arisi.
He took the Portrait of a Woman to the hospital to check the canvas on an X-ray machine.
It turned out that under the top layer of paint is really hidden another.
“Portrait of a Woman ” was the only“ double picture ” of Klimt.
Who is depicted on it is not known exactly.
It is assumed that it is the muse of Klimt Alma Mahler or another lover of the artist Ria Munch, who posed for him for several portraits.
According to a 2016 BBC story, Klimt fell in love with a young girl from Vienna and painted her portrait in a wide-brimmed hat and fur boa.
When the girl died suddenly, Klimt rewrote the painting so that it did not remind him of the loss.
In honor of the opening of the "double picture" of Klimt, the Ricci Oddi Gallery decided to organize an exhibition in the palace of the XIII century in Piacenza.
At the same time, the gallery building was closed for reconstruction.
There were workers, paintings were taken to storage, and the alarm was turned off.
In February 1997, the “Portrait of a Woman ” disappeared, and the disappearance was not immediately noticed: the curators did not see the canvas since Tuesday, but reported to the police only on Saturday.
Later, a frame was found on the roof of the museum.
This gave rise to the version that the picture was pulled out with a fishing rod through a window in the ceiling (it was quickly abandoned because the frame was larger than the window opening).
In April 1997, Italian customs reported that the "Portrait of a Woman" had been found on the Italian-French border.
The canvas was planned to be sent to the former Prime Minister of Italy Bettino Craxi, who at home was accused of corruption and fled to Tunisia.
Employees of the gallery rushed to the border - they were in such a hurry that they received a fine for speeding by 240 thousand liras (about $140 at the exchange rate of 1997).
However, on the spot, it quickly became clear that the picture was a fake: it smelled fresh paint.
Portrait of a Woman, which was one of two paintings by Klimt in Italy, became the second most valuable painting sought in the country (the first was Caravaggio ’ s “Christmas with St. Lawrence and St. Francis ”, stolen from Palermo in 1969).
It was suggested that it might have been a contract theft because the fame of the painting would have prevented it from being sold; but the police were unable to find the alleged customers and perpetrators.
In 2014, the case was reopened, as the police found a match fingerprint on the frame with some other prints.
However, this lead did not lead to the disclosure of the crime.
In November 2015, a man claiming to be an art thief offered to reveal the location of the Portrait of a Woman in exchange for 150,000 euros.
The police refused to pay.
A year later, the BBC published an interview with an unnamed resident of Piacenza, who in the past allegedly stole art, and later began to help the police in exchange for immunity from criminal prosecution.
The man claimed that he stole the “Portrait of a Woman ”.
He claimed that at first, with the help of one of the employees of the gallery, he replaced the original with a fake, and a few months later he took it out to cover his tracks.
A BBC interviewee said he sold the painting for cash and cocaine.
He added that the canvas will return to the gallery for the 20th anniversary of the theft, that is, by February 2017.
The forecast came true almost three years late.
On December 10, 2019, “Portrait of a Woman ” was discovered by an employee of one of the municipal enterprises of Piacenza, who was cleaning the walls of Ricci Oddi ’ s gallery from ivy.
He saw a cavity in the wall closed by an iron door; inside lay a painting wrapped in a black plastic garbage bag.
Employees of the gallery identified it as “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt.
They examined the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and suggested that the find was the original (about six or seven fakes of the Portrait of a Woman had previously surfaced).
However, its authenticity will be determined by the examination.
Klimt il giorno dopo Telelibertà Piacenza It is assumed that the thieves planned to return for the canvas of Klimt, but failed to do so due to increased security measures in the gallery of Ricci Oddi.
The head of the Department of Culture of the City of Piacenza, Jonathan Papamareng, questioned this version.
First, according to him, after the theft, the territory of the gallery was thoroughly inspected.
Secondly, the canvas is too well preserved.
“It is in excellent condition.
It is hard to believe that it has been hidden in a wall for 22 years, close to the ground and plants, ” Papamareng told Reuters.
Olga Korelina

title: Vladislav Kurash | A touching story of one great love
text:
Dedicated to my wife, Alyona Gordienko-Kurash Postmodernism is a painful marginal state of modern culture, a rush between the obsolete past and the unmarked future, dragged on for many decades.
For the most part, the futile chaotic search for new revolutionary forms of self-expression and reflection of reality.
An attempt to escape from traditional conventional systems and categories of perception and thinking.
Trying to create a new order of things.
Attempt of a coup and reorganization of public consciousness.
An attempt to rethink the moral foundations and reassess universal human and cultural values.
Attempt to reorient the spiritual aspirations of man.
The father of “minimalism ” and, accordingly, spun off from it at the beginning of the second millennium and formed as an independent artistic direction of“ artistic documentalism ”, many contemporaries consider Ernest Hemingway.
He once argued with Francis Scott Fitzgerald that he could write a very short story.
Hemingway won the argument, and wrote a story in which there were only six words, a tiny touching story of the life of one little boy: “For sale are children ’ s shoes.
"For sale: baby shoes, never worn".
After Hemingway, many famous masters tried themselves in this direction.
And Raymond Carver, and Charles Bukowski, and Aram Saroyan, and Mary Robinson.
The list of famous names can go on indefinitely.
Speaking of minimalist writers, it is impossible not to recall Vasilisk Gnedov and his "Poem of the End".
This “poem ” is a blank sheet of paper and nothing more.
However, to assert that the poem is wordless and meaningless I would not, there is a title in which the deep idea of the author is enclosed.
I would like to say a few words about the novel by Vladimir Blinov, which consists of one phrase: “Do not!
“Me ” is just four words.
Nevertheless, Vladimir Blinov defines his creation as a novel, considering it multifaceted and multivariate, opening up a rich space for the imagination of the reader.
As a minimalist writer, one day I too wanted to write my own tiny touching story, as multifaceted, deep and multivariate as Hemingway and Blinov ’ s.
And this is what I got.
I wrote a six-word story that contained a life-long story: “I don ’ t want to live without you. ”
I called the story “A touching story of one great love. ”
After that, I realized that I simply had to formulate, at least for myself, some theoretical aspects of my work.
Of course, nothing super original came of it, but there was a clear awareness of what I was doing, what I was killing all my free time for.
Minimalism is an artistic direction in literature, based on the minimization of the use of materials, tools and means of artistic expression in the creative process, on the minimization of the number of words used in the transmission of maximum information, on the desire for simplicity and uniformity of forms.
Heroes in minimalist works are usually faceless and do not have characteristic features.
Minimalist works depict only the most necessary, basic features and details.
The author, instead of describing every detail or detail, gives only the basic context, offering the reader ’ s imagination to “finish ” the story.
Artistic documentalism is an artistic direction in literature, which is based on the creation of a document that reflects a particular feature of reality.
Artistic documentalism is based on eleven principles: Credibility of the artistic image. Laconism.
To create a full-fledged authentic artistic image, a minimum set of means of artistic expression is sufficient.
The unity of typification and individualization of the artistic image.
Character is the central, dominant image of the artistic work.
Detail of the artistic image.
Every detail is important for creating a full authentic artistic image.
The object of the artistic image is the person and the world around him.
Ideological content is an integral component of an artistic work.
A work of art is a system of value orientations.
Cognitive, educational and aesthetic functions of a work of art.
The pathos of the artwork.
Emotionality is the core element of any artistic image, any character and the entire work of art as a whole, the most effective means of influencing the reader.
At the heart of any work of art is fiction, which is the author ’ s way of reflecting reality.
Documentalism.
Every work of art is a kind of document, in an artistic form fixing certain features of reality.
Vladislav Kurash Warsaw August 5, 2017

title: Russia is a rising superpower in the global food market
text:
It is often heard about Russia that, with the exception of energy resources, it produces almost nothing of what is most in demand in the world.
The dependence of the Russian economy on energy exports looks like a huge time bomb, laid for the future of the country, given the current popularity in the West and in China of the idea of ​ ​ reducing the use of hydrocarbon fuels.
Ironically, however, Russia appears to be reaping notable benefits from climate change, which scientists believe is fueled by the use of hydrocarbons: its brilliant prospects as the world ’ s largest exporter of wheat and grain superpower are not least driven by global warming.
During the previous accounting year, which lasted from July 2016 to June 2017, Russia exported 27.8 million tons of wheat, more than all the countries of the European Union combined.
For the first time since the EU began to be counted as a single bloc, Russia turned out to be the world ’ s largest exporter of wheat.
In the current accounting year, according to the forecast of the US Department of Agriculture, Russia's exports will be 31.5 million tons, significantly strengthening its position as a global leader.
There are reports that Russia is already facing some infrastructural constraints due to the gigantic harvest.
It is also a leading exporter of corn, barley and oats.
Along with Ukraine and Kazakhstan, Russia has become part of a new force that has an increasingly significant impact on global grain markets.
Experts of the food market, this force is known by the acronym RUC.
The Minister of agriculture of Russia Alexander Tkachev has repeatedly stated that in the foreseeable future there will come a time when grain will displace oil as the largest source of export income of the country.
This view is not particularly pleasing in the Kremlin – there would prefer to hope for a technological boom, but Tkachev ’ s prophecy for a number of reasons may be more realistic.
The first two of these reasons are beyond Russia ’ s competence: the growing population of the planet and climate change.
Global grain consumption increased by an average of 2.8 percent per year during 2011-2016, and the International Grains Council predicts an annual increase of 1.4 percent through 2021.
At the same time, climate studies show that, compared with the late eighties, the time of the collapse of the Soviet Union, which had a strong negative impact on Eurasian agriculture, the average temperature in the grain-producing areas of Eurasia will increase by 1.8 degrees by 2020 and by 3.9 degrees by 2050, mainly in winter.
This will lead to a longer growing season and an increase in average yields.
Increasing the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is also beneficial for crops.
The climate factor may have already helped Russia capture vast new markets in Asia this year as Canadian and Australian competitors suffer from droughts.
Climate change also means that over time, Russian agricultural enterprises will be able to expand their land northward, cultivating land that has never been used to grow grain before.
More importantly, however, global warming will help Russia, and to a lesser extent Ukraine and Kazakhstan, reclaim arable land that was uncultivated from 1991 to 2000, totaling about 57 million hectares.
These lands were abandoned in the early years of post-Soviet capitalism because they required too much investment and at the same time yielded little or no profit.
However, in recent years, the situation is rapidly changing, thanks to both climate change and technological advances.
In recent years, these changes have been taking place in Russia and neighboring grain-producing countries continuously.
The capitalist transformation of the Russian economy and the almost free, albeit excessively bureaucratic, trade in land have led to the creation of several dozen large agricultural conglomerates that have adopted Western technologies to increase yields and which, since 2005, when the Kremlin declared agriculture a national priority, have received increased state support.
These vertically integrated giants are both a boon for Russian grain exports, as they have become the main driver of its growth, and a curse.
A recently published collection of scientific articles on the Eurasian Wheat Belt pointed out that small private farms manage the land more efficiently and achieve higher yields than large corporations.
The scientists recommended that Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan reform their land laws to encourage the development of small agricultural farms.
Russia has already taken an important step in this direction, since in the early 2000s it liberalized land ownership.
Unlike Russia, there is no legal land market in Ukraine today, which, according to analysts, can explain the low growth rates of grain production in recent years.
However, given that much of the country ’ s industrial complex is in the war zone, Kiev has to rely increasingly on agriculture.
In addition, Ukraine is under pressure from the International Monetary Fund, recommending to allow the free sale of land.
Although a warmer Ukraine benefits less from climate change than Russia, it still has huge untapped resources in this area.
Taken together, factors such as global warming, global population growth, the continued technological lag of post-Soviet agriculture from Western agriculture, as well as the opportunity to improve ineffective legal regulation, create enormous growth potential for Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Although the political paths of these countries diverge, nevertheless, the three can to some extent share a common economic future in the new post-oil world.
Of course, the emphasis on agricultural exports is still linked to dependence on commodity markets and means vulnerability to global trends in a market far less concentrated than that of oil.
So, in 2012, Russian wheat was sold at $350 per ton, but now the price has dropped to $180.
In addition, in agriculture, growth is heavily dependent on government support, unlike hydrocarbon production, where the government can simply passively charge rent.
Export infrastructure, given that the Russian state retains the transportation system, is also a bottleneck that requires taxpayer money.
However, this support could eventually translate into considerable dividends if Russia manages to form a more profitable agricultural production.
First of all, we are talking about the production of meat, milk and vegetable crops, which Russia still imports.
The Russian government is trying to stimulate this process by imposing an embargo on the import of Western products, and this has already contributed to the growth of domestic production to a certain extent, but so far Russian manufacturers lack the knowledge, experience and resources to make a real breakthrough.
Even though it is ruled by a corrupt, backward and authoritarian regime, Russia is a country of tremendous resilience and should not be dismissed as an economy that is about to collapse.
This is eloquently evidenced by the current growing influence of Russia in the world grain market.

title: Global warming threatens coffee plantations in Latin America
text:
Climate change could cause 88% of coffee plantations in Latin America to become unsuitable for growing coffee beans, according to a study published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
About the results of the work told the portal Phys.org.
"Coffee is one of the most valuable products in the world, in order to produce it efficiently, you need a suitable climate and pollinator bees," said Taylor Ricketts, director of the University of Vermont's Gunda Environment Institute and co-author of the study.
Using spatial analysis and field data, the scientists assessed the possible impact of global warming on coffee plantations in Latin America, and also modeled the change in the habitat of bees, the presence of which is necessary for the cultivation of coffee.
The analysis showed a larger reduction in the area of ​ ​ coffee plantations than previous researchers had anticipated.
According to the forecasts of scientists, Nicaragua, Honduras and Venezuela will suffer the most from the loss of areas suitable for growing coffee.
“Coffee is the main source of income for millions of poor rural residents, so the decline in crop yields will affect the living conditions of vulnerable groups, ” warns Ricketts.
However, scientists predict a slight expansion of areas suitable for coffee plantations in Mexico, Guatemala, Colombia and Costa Rica, mainly in mountainous areas where temperatures are expected to be suitable for coffee growth.
The study also highlights the importance of rainforests, which are key habitats for wild bees and other pollinators.
Thus, the conservation of these forests will be crucial to sustaining the existence of coffee plantations.
The study also provides recommendations for Latin American farmers to help them achieve improved coffee growth and create favorable conditions for pollinators.
Strategies developed by the authors of the study include measures to protect forests, expand habitats for bees near coffee plantations, as well as the creation of windbreaks and hedges.
According to the International Coffee Organization, the largest producers of this crop in the world are Brazil, Vietnam and Colombia, in 2016 these countries produced 3.3 million tons, 1.5 million tons and 870 thousand tons of coffee, respectively (55 thousand, 25.5 thousand and 14.5 thousand tons of coffee, respectively).

In total, 9.2 million tons of coffee beans (153,869,000 bags) were produced worldwide in 2016.
Total revenue from coffee sales in the world in 2012 was $24 billion, in 2002 - just over $5 billion.
