title: Tusk called on the EU to hold a summit on migration with the participation of Arab states
text:
The European Union should hold an emergency summit on migration with the League of Arab States.
This was stated on Wednesday, September 19, the President of the European Council Donald Tusk before the start of the EU summit in Salzburg, Austria.
According to him, such a summit could be held in February 2019 in Egypt.
Tusk intends to make a proposal in Salzburg.
“Despite the aggressive rhetoric, the situation is moving in the right direction, ” the head of the European Council said.
In particular, the level of illegal migration to the EU has decreased from 2 million people in 2015 to less than 100 thousand this year.
This is due to the policy aimed at protecting the external borders of the European Union and cooperation with states outside it, Tusk said.
He called on EU countries to return to constructive partnership on migration issues and stop mutual accusations.
It is unacceptable to divide into "those who want to solve the problem and those who intend to use it for political purposes," the president of the European Council said.
The European Union summit in Salzburg takes place on September 19 and 20.
Its participants will discuss migration issues, EU security policy and the upcoming exit of the UK from the European Union (Brexit).
The first goal is to survive Fleeing from war and grief in 2015-2016, hundreds of thousands of people, primarily from Syria, rushed to Europe through Turkey and Greece.
On the Greek islands of Samos, Lesbos, Chios, there are still about 10,000 refugees.
From January to May 2017, more than 6,000 people arrived there.
Millions of migrants tried in 2015-2016 to get to Western Europe from Greece and Turkey on the so-called "Balkan route": on foot through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary.
The flow of refugees stopped only when many countries closed their borders and the route ceased to operate.
Today, refugees are fleeing to Europe via the Mediterranean Sea.
Their sea route begins off the coast of Libya.
This photo in September 2015 shocked the whole world: on one of the Turkish beaches waves carried the body of drowned three-year-old Syrian boy Aylan Kurdi.
The photo appeared on all social networks and became a symbol of the migration crisis and the tragedy of Syrian refugees.
Knowing that the path to Europe will soon be closed, thousands of refugees desperately tried to reach Croatia in crowded trains and buses.
A few days later, in October 2015, Hungary officially closed its borders.
At the same time, a camp appeared on the territory of the country, in which refugees were forced to live, waiting for official permission to grant them asylum in the EU.
This picture in September 2015 caused widespread outrage: Hungarian journalist Petra Laszlo set a foot in the running Syrian man who was carrying his son.
He tried to break through a police cordon near the Hungarian border with Serbia.
At the peak of the migration crisis, voices of discontent with the influx of refugees into Europe began to sound louder.
The official closure of the Balkan route in March 2016 led to riots and clashes with police at border sections where thousands of refugees were stuck.
Many have tried to cross borders, bypassing controls, such as this group of refugees on the Greek-Macedonian border.
A child in dust and blood is a photo of 5-year-old Omran from Aleppo shocked the public and in 2016 became a symbol of the horrors of the civil war in Syria and the suffering of civilians.
A year later, photos and videos of the same boy with his father, but already smiling and healthy, appeared on social networks.
And supporters of Bashar al-Assad criticized the West for the fact that the first picture was used for propaganda purposes.
Photos that remind of the fate of refugees Unknown in a foreign country In the pouring rain, a Syrian refugee carries his daughter in the Greek Idomeni on the border with Macedonia.
He hopes that his family will soon be safe.
According to the Dublin agreements, migrants can only apply for asylum in the EU country they cross first.
Many refugees are being sent back.
In the hope of help, Germany remains the number one target for most refugees, although due to the large flow of asylum seekers in Germany, the country ’ s migration policy has been tightened.
No EU member state has taken in as many refugees as Germany – about 1.2 million people.
Many newcomers are immensely grateful to Chancellor Angela Merkel for her immigration policy.
In the north of France, in Calais, in October 2016, the authorities eliminated a spontaneous refugee camp.
In this case, a fire broke out in it.
Some 6,500 refugees living here had to go elsewhere.
Six months after the camp was dismantled, humanitarian organizations reported a large number of minors who were in the vicinity of Calais without a roof over their heads.
Maritime patrols rescuing refugees Despite the huge risk, many refugees, fleeing war and poverty, decide to get to Europe by sea.
Rubber boats with migrants are regularly in distress in the Mediterranean.
In 2017 alone, 1,800 people venturing on such a dangerous journey drowned at sea.
In 2016, the death toll was 5,000.
Thousands of people from North Africa and the Middle East are in refugee camps in Libya, seeking to reach Europe by sea.
The business of smugglers and human traffickers is flourishing here.
According to humanitarian organizations, the living conditions in the refugee camps are appalling.
Prostitution and modern slavery are not uncommon.
But people still hope for a better future in Europe.
Author: Charlotte Hauswedel, Natalia Pozdnyakova

title: We'll have no sweets. Chocolate and bananas may disappear in the world
text:
We'll have no sweets.
Global climate change in the coming years may lead to the fact that chocolate will become an expensive and rare delicacy, like black caviar and truffles.
And that's not all bad news.
The climate is changing, and this is obvious to everyone.
The fact that the seasons have shifted by a month, and winter now begins in January, and spring - in April, today complain not only Russians, but also Americans.
As for scientists, they have any talk about climate today is accompanied by permanent hysteria.
Entomologists complain that over the past ten years in Europe, three-quarters of insect species have disappeared, zoologists - that the habitats of many animals are rapidly narrowing.
Botanists lament that the boundaries of the growth of many familiar trees, such as spruce and fir, are rapidly moving to the north.
But most affected by climate change are farmers, who last year faced an unprecedented drought across the entire subtropical belt — from China to Australia and from the Middle East to South America.
India, which had to endure the worst drought in 140 years, farmers took to the streets to demand material assistance.
The case came to clashes with the police, in which five people were killed.
Tamma A. Carlton, a professor at the University of California at Berkeley, even conducted a special study, during which she established a clear link between warming and the number of suicides among Indian farmers.
According to her calculations, an increase in temperature by one degree relative to the average for a given day leads to seventy new suicides of Indian peasants.
Most residents of megacities know nothing about these trends.
But soon they will be able to feel the effects of climate change on their diet.
International organization Bioversity International is engaged in an analysis of the situation in world crop production, and every year its reports are becoming more alarming.
The greatest concern of experts are cocoa and bananas.
Just the shock of Cocoa, or chocolate tree (scientific name - Theobroma cacao, theobroma), is considered one of the most capricious crops.
Theobrome needs a very warm, humid climate and very poorly tolerates even short-term droughts.
It does not tolerate direct sunlight and does not like strong winds.
The first flowers appear on the tree at the age of 5-6 years, but the high yields of the theobroma begin to give only from the age of twelve.
A high harvest is considered to be several dozen fruits.
And although the tree may have several thousand flowers on the tree, cocoa reacts to the slightest changes in the weather by a sharp decrease in the number of fruits.
The problem is that although the chocolate tree is native to South America, today the main volumes of cocoa are grown in Africa: more than half of its production is provided by three countries - Côte d ’ Ivoire, Ghana, Cameroon, whose weather is becoming drier and hotter.
According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), in the next decade, more than half of the African territories where theobrome grows today will become unsuitable for growing cocoa due to reduced rainfall.
The situation is aggravated by the fact that during the entire period of cultivation of cocoa people practically did not engage in the selection of this culture in order to adapt it to a more arid climate.
Moreover, the genetic monotony of theobroma makes it very vulnerable to infections that flare up more often (which scientists also attribute to climate change).
One of the largest such outbreaks occurred in the nineties of the last century in Brazil and led to a decrease in cocoa production in the country by almost half - from 320 to 190 thousand tons per year.
The combination of increased droughts and increased pests, Bioversity International estimates, will lead to the complete destruction of the chocolate industry in the next forty years.
But long before that, chocolate will become a rare expensive delicacy, like truffles or black caviar, available only to the wealthiest inhabitants of the planet.
Banana fungus and berry are also under threat.
However, here the main danger is on the climate, and the pest is the soil fungus Fusarium oxysporum f. sp.
Cubense which lives in the soil and through the roots penetrates into the leaves of banana trees, after which they die.
The fungus itself and the Fusarium disease caused by it, or “Panamanian disease ”, were discovered in the twenties of the last century, but over the past hundred years, scientists have not found a means to combat the pest.
The fungus was very resistant - it almost does not react to chemicals.
In the middle of the last century, the spread of the “Panamanian disease ” led to the complete destruction of the main variety at that time, Gro-Michel.
Fortunately, scientists were able to find another variety resistant to the disease - "Cavendish", which today we all see in stores and which has become a new basis for the entire banana industry.
It seemed that the problem was solved, but at the end of the last century in Southeast Asia, a new more aggressive species of fungus Fusarium appeared, which has since systematically destroyed banana plantations.
In two decades, the fungus has destroyed most of the Cavendish plantations in Asia and Australia, and now it has reached Africa – recently the “Panamanian disease ” was discovered in Mozambique This means that in five years, all African banana plantations will be destroyed, and then the harmful fungus will only have to get to South America, to finally deprive humanity of the most popular berry (from the point of botany banana - the same The fruit is like a watermelon, because it is a juicy multi-seed fruit).
“With the current trend of travel, there is almost no doubt that the fungus will reach the main Cavendish plantations in South America, ” said phytopathologist Randy Ploetz of the University of Florida, who is considered the world ’ s leading specialist in the“ Panama disease ” of bananas..
Now botanists and representatives of the banana industry are equipping expeditions to the jungles of New Guinea in the hope of finding a variety of bananas that survived the invasion of a new strain of the fungus Fusarium.
However, the main hope for the salvation of bananas, like cocoa, associated with genetic engineering.
Geneticists from the University of California, USA have already developed a method of “editing ” the DNA of the theobrome, which, according to them, will help adapt the chocolate tree to global warming.
The project is funded by companies - the world's largest chocolate producers.
Genetic engineering is also being used to make Cavendish bananas resistant to Panamanian disease.
No progress has been reported, but it is only a matter of time.
So it remains only to sympathize with the opponents of GMOs, who will soon face a difficult choice: to give up the principles or remain without sweets.

title: Hundreds of court cases against Monsanto are awaiting a verdict on the carcinogenicity of the Roundup herbicide
text:
Hundreds of lawsuits against Monsanto for injuries and premature death are moving forward after a scientific analysis (1) was heard in court detailing the carcinogenicity of the Roundup herbicide.
An expert opinion on the toxicity of glyphosate included in the Roundup may be allowed in the trial against Monsanto pending the final decision of the judge.
The first trial in the Roundup case is scheduled for June 18, 2018 in the Superior Court of the District of San Francisco.
The stakes are high for hundreds of farm families who have lost loved ones to a particular type of cancer called non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Cancer is more common among farmers.
More than 365 lawsuits are pending in the U.S. District Court in San Francisco.
People who filed lawsuits against Monsanto claim that the herbicide Roundup caused cancer in their loved one and that Monsanto concealed these risks.
The court promised to consider the cases as one, only if there is enough evidence of the carcinogenicity of glyphosate.
The second week of March was important in this regard.
The court devoted the entire week to hearing the scientific evaluation of glyphosate, the main component of Roundup.
Epidemiologists, toxicologists and biomedical statistical analysts testified in court, presented and presented evidence of the harm of glyphosate to humans.
Judge Vince Chabria presided over the case and now has to decide whether the trials against Monsanto can move forward.
The implications of these lawsuits are enormous, as more than 3,500 cases are pending in state courts, which say Monsanto concealed the risk of cancer due to Roundup.
A video of the trial has been made public and is available on USCourts.gov (2).
So far, the whole world has trusted Monsanto ’ s words that Roundup is 100 percent safe for humans.
Now, this massively used herbicide is finally being questioned by experts, grieving families, and most importantly, the courts.
The greatest amount of evidence came from Dr. Chadi Nabhan, an oncologist with 17 years of clinical practice and academic research on lymphomas.
He discussed the results of a study by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (2015) and the reasonable procedures they adopted, starting in 1965.
After careful examination, an independent research body classified glyphosate as a “probable carcinogen ” in 2015.
Dr. Nabhan said the IARC findings are compelling, and that ’ s what “patients need to know. ”
This is a very important issue for Monsanto, as the company does not recognize the carcinogenicity of glyphosate.
Almost a third of Monsanto ’ s revenue comes from glyphosate products.
If the megacorporation is found guilty, agriculture will be changed around the world, especially in the US, where Monsanto ’ s genetically modified seeds (GMO seeds) are systematically modernized to resist its glyphosate.
Finally, the world can witness a court decision that will acquit the victims of the Monsanto herbicide.
Finally, people will be able to learn the truth about Roundup, that it is the poison of daring cancer in humans.
If Monsanto is found guilty in the face of growing evidence, it will only be the beginning for the collapse of Monsanto ’ s empire.
Roundup is already found in organic products and human breast milk, it is already poisoning the last corners of our world, destroying not only plant life, but also destroying the protective microorganisms that live in our gastrointestinal tract. Summary.

title: NASA began to assemble a new rover
text:
Engineers of the aerospace agency NASA have started assembling a new rover, which will go to the Red planet in July 2020 with the help of the carrier rocket “Atlas 5 ”.
The new rover will be assembled at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena.
Approximately, the process of assembling a new autonomous Martian scientific laboratory will take a year and a half.
“Parts and equipment for the rover come not only from different cities in the United States, but from all over the world, ” commented the head of the assembly and testing of the rover in JPL David Gruel portal Space.com.
Spain.
One of the main tasks that will be set before the new Mars 2020 rover (the name, most likely, working, and a more appropriate designation the rover will receive, most likely, after its assembly is completed), will be to search for signs of life on our planetary neighbor.
As noted by experts from NASA, “the device will explore the geological structure of Mars, the composition of the atmosphere, make an assessment of natural resources and the threats that people may face during future expeditions to this planet. ”
One of the scientific instruments of the new rover will be designed to obtain oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide.
In addition, the autonomous Martian laboratory will collect soil and rocks, which in the future, during the development of the planet will be sent to Earth for further analysis.
The new rover will get the size of a small car.
Its length will be about 3 meters (excluding the mechanical manipulator arm), width - 2.7 meters, and height - 2.2 meters.
At the same time, its weight will be about 1050 kilograms, which is about 150 kilograms more than the weight of Curiosity, which has spent more than 2,000 Earth days on Mars.
By the way, during the development of Mars 2020, it was decided to borrow a lot of nodes and parts from the latter.
The final choice of the landing site of the new rover NASA has not yet made, but among the most likely are the Jezero crater, the Gusev crater and the northeastern part of the low shield volcano Big Sirte.

title: Became known the date of the first flight of the world's largest aircraft (Video)
text:
Venture aerospace company Stratolaunch Systems said that the flight of the Scaled Composites Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft will take place this summer.
This was announced at the scientific conference of the 34th Space Symposium in Colorado Springs.
However, according to experts, it is possible that the expected date may be moved to a later date.
This is due to the complexity of the design and the use of fundamentally new design solutions.
Now behind the plane — a number of successfully passed ground tests.
In February of this year, it became known that the Scaled Composites Stratolaunch Model 351 as part of the steering tests reached a speed of 46 mph (74 km / h).
The test took place in Mojave, California.
The first taxiing tests of the aircraft performed even earlier, and rolled it out on May 31 last year.
At the same time, the first high-quality photos of the almost completed winged car appeared.
It is worth noting that, although small aircraft are able to rise into the air at relatively low speeds, for the take-off of such a large machine will require a much greater speed.
At the same time, engineers did everything possible to facilitate the aircraft.
The company Scaled Composites used the most advanced composite materials in the construction.
The aircraft is made according to a very original two-fuselage scheme.
It has six Pratt & Whitney PW4056 twin-circuit turbojet engines.
The car has the largest wingspan in history.
It can also be considered the largest aircraft.
Immediately behind the Scaled Composites Stratolaunch Model 351 is the Soviet transport aircraft An-225 ("Mriya"), significantly inferior to the "American" in wing span.
The third place is occupied by Airbus A340-600.
The largest production aircraft in the world and the largest passenger capacity recognized the famous Airbus A380.
Recall that the aerospace system "air launch" Stratolaunch presented back in 2011.
It is designed to put 6.12 tons of payload into low Earth orbit.
The complex includes three main components: a giant aircraft, a multi-stage rocket and a system that allows you to combine these two segments.

title: Stratolaunch Systems will fly the largest aircraft in the world
text:
Stratolaunch Systems plans to test the flight of the largest aircraft in the world - the two-fuselage Stratolaunch Model 351.
This is reported by the online edition of Space News.
Testing is planned for the summer of 2018.
At the same time, it is possible that the terms of flight testing will be postponed due to the complex structures of the aircraft.
It is noted that in early March, the aircraft has already passed high-speed ground tests, during which it accelerated to a record 74 km / h.
This aircraft is considered the largest in the world.
Its wingspan is 117 meters and its height is 15 meters.
The aircraft consists of two fuselages, its mass with fuel is 340 tons, with a full load - 590 tons.
Aircraft is made according to two-fuselage scheme.
It has six Pratt & Whitney PW40 engines.
Also, the aircraft is equipped with a 28-wheel chassis that can withstand such loads, so it can simultaneously carry up to three Orbital ATK Pegasus XL missiles and put into orbit from an altitude of about nine thousand meters.
After commissioning, it will become a platform for launching small launch vehicles: it will raise them to a height of 9,100 meters above the ground - from there, the missiles will launch to low-Earth orbit on their own.
It is planned that the commissioning of the aircraft will take place no earlier than 2019.

title: Terra Preta in the Middle Urals
text:

195 participants of the forum agreed to prevent an increase in the average temperature on the planet by 2100 by more than 2 degrees Celsius compared with the pre-industrial era.
The ecosystem is very different from the ecosystem.

Nature itself is trying to compensate for the losses incurred.
There is no such perfect balance in the agro-ecosystem.
When we intervene in it more and more actively, we must compensate for the losses - to apply fertilizers, ameliorants, etc., and mainly nitrogen orientation.

In the 80s of the last century, our country developed a program for the use of various inhibitors (chemicals) that suppress the chain of microbiological processes leading to the formation of greenhouse gases.
About 320 million tons of organic waste are produced annually in Russia, 250 million of which are agricultural and forest waste. One of the modern technologies is the introduction of biocoal into the soil.
The use of this product, obtained as a result of carbonization of plant biomass, allows solving a number of environmental problems.
First, plant waste is involved in the production cycle, which can strengthen the nitrogen and carbon cycles if it is not involved in economic activities.
In Russia today, agricultural waste is an almost unclaimed resource.
Secondly, the growing concentration of nitrogen dioxide in the atmosphere decreases, since carbon absorbed by plants during photosynthesis does not return to the atmosphere, but is preserved in the form of carbonized biomass, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The introduction of biochar as an ameliorant in the soil plays a key role in changing the physicochemical properties of soils that affect the microbiological processes responsible for the formation of greenhouse gases, while simultaneously improving the dynamics of nutrients necessary for plant growth and development. – How long has biochar been used in agricultural work? – In the late 90s, German scientists drew attention to artificially created soils, actively used in agriculture in the Brazilian part of Latin America. America.
The soils, called "Terra Preta", were formed by local residents as a result of regular burning of grassy and shrub vegetation and embedding the resulting material into the arable layer.
Soils with large amounts of charcoal have also been found in Europe.
The results of research by scientists from St. Petersburg demonstrate that the introduction of biochar into the moderately cultivated soil reduced the emission of nitrous oxide by an average of 33%.
Among the scientists there was an idea of ​ ​ the prospects of using carbonized materials in agriculture to improve soil characteristics and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
And this, as already mentioned, is consistent with the problems of our time - global climate change and food security in the world.
More details about this are stated in Irina Mukhina ’ s thesis “The influence of carbonized biomass on the fertility parameters of sod-podzolic soils and the emission of greenhouse gases ” (excerpts are given in the boxes – approx. ed). – Despite the usefulness of biocoal widespread in Russia, he has not yet found.
Why? — In our country, economic judgments play an important role so far.
Apparently, it is unprofitable to provide each farm with furnaces for the production of carbonized mass.
In addition, the plant waste from which biocharcoal is made, and the product itself are individual.
The region of application is also of great importance - the climate is everywhere special.
A lot of research needs to be done before biocharcoal is put into mass use.
The use of environmentally friendly pyrolysis of plant residues (biochar) can reduce anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases by 12% annually. – Nevertheless, in the future it is visible? – If we take the north-west of Russia, we have been studying the influence of biochar on agricultural soils for 8 years.
And there hasn ’ t been a single year in which biochar options haven ’ t shown a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in soils.
We can also argue that soil properties that are useful for plant growth and development are improving. – When people talk about the “greenhouse effect ”, it seems to many that this is a problem from a distant perspective.
How does it affect nature, people and cities in which we live? – If initially scientists talked about global warming, now they have changed their intonation a little and have already begun to talk about global climate change.
Everyone notices that there is a shift in monthly weather changes, seasons.
If earlier the winter months were December, January and February, today winter, at least in the Northwest, begins in mid-January, and spring in March and does not think to start.
The agrarian aspect is also changing: those cultures that grew in the south are now growing well, for example, in central Russia.
Climate risks could lead to more desertification – where there were fertile lands.
Some global change is happening, and the main reason, of course, is the increase in the concentration of anthropogenic greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
Interviewed by Kristina Shabunina

title: After plastic surgery, the patient recovered from the insurance company more than 800 000 rubles. – Rambler
text:
After plastic surgery, the patient recovered from the insurance company more than 800 000 rubles.
The court of the Amur region recovered from the insurance company 865 000 rubles in favor of a tourist who was hospitalized in Thailand shortly after breast augmentation surgery.
A resident of the city of Tyndy at the end of September 2016 with her family went to Thailand for a couple of weeks.
On the eve of the trip, she entered into an insurance contract with ERV Travel Insurance JSC in case of unforeseen medical expenses, as well as expenses related to forced cancellation of the trip or change of its terms.
In Thailand, a woman underwent breast augmentation and liposuction.
She was discharged, but the next day she again went to the doctors because of acute abdominal pain, severe nausea and vomiting.
The woman was hospitalized.
She had to pay for medical services and purchase air tickets for another flight for herself and the child.
Returning home, the tourist sent to the insurance company an application for reimbursement of expenses in the amount of more than half a million rubles, but she was refused.
The insurance company considered hospitalization as a consequence of plastic surgery, and according to the contract, the costs of the client associated with cosmetic or plastic surgery, carried out for aesthetic or cosmetic purposes, were not subject to reimbursement.
Then the client filed a lawsuit against the insurers in the Tyndinsky District Court of the Amur Region, demanding to recover in her favor the amount of expenses and compensation.
The court was presented with the conclusion of the Bureau of forensic examination that the symptoms of the disease during the re-hospitalization are not a consequence of the plastic surgery.
This is evidenced, in particular, by the results of computed tomography performed in the hospital, indicating the localization of the pathological process in the gastrointestinal tract and abdominal cavity, which cannot be a consequence of the operation, as well as the later development of pain syndrome - not on the first, but on the second day after surgery.
As the court found, the diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis indicated in the medical certificate, in general, does not contradict the treatment carried out in the hospital.
As a result, the court came to the conclusion that the disease of the plaintiff during the re-hospitalization is not a consequence of the plastic surgery, which means that it is considered an insured event.
As a result, the court recovered from the insurance company compensation for expenses in the amount of 523,679.42 rubles, a penalty of 50,000 rubles, compensation for moral damage in 3,000 rubles and a fine for non-satisfaction of consumer claims in the amount of 288,339.71 rubles.
In total, the defendant must pay the tourist 865,019.13 rubles.

title: Farmers need to adapt to climate change – experts
text:
Farmers need to take into account climate change and adapt to it.
This opinion was expressed today during a press conference in Kiev by specialists of the Ukrainian Hydrometeorological Center.
According to the head of the department of agrometeorology of the Ukrainian Hydrometeorological Center Tatyana ADAMENKO, today the increase in the heat supply of the growing season of plants due to warming leads to an increase in the productivity of crops, "but how long this period will last is a question, perhaps it will be ten years."
“And then, if this trend and the intensity of warming continues in the summer months, then we will gradually move into a period of unfavorable agrometeorological conditions due to the fact that this will lead to a decrease in precipitation, ” the expert said.
According to the head of the Hydrometeorological Center Nikolai KULBIDA, certain positive factors that took place at the beginning of warming and in the middle of this process, with the maximum values of temperature growth, which are possible already in the next 10-20 years, will have reverse processes when the negative impact will exceed the positive factor.
According to T. ADAMENKO, farmers need to monitor trends in climate change and make appropriate decisions.
“There are a lot of questions – both the selection of varieties, and their adaptation to new agroclimatic conditions.
Neither our technology nor our varieties are adapted to the European winter.
Given the fact that we are warming in the winter period, we need to take the experience of Western countries, their seeds, their technologies, etc., ” she said.

title: Migrant camp in Europe: The world through barbed wire - PHOTO REPORT
text:
Baku.
9 March.
REPORT.AZ / Since the beginning of the military confrontation in Syria, which seems to have no end, the flow of refugees from this country to Europe has been increasing.
As a result of the migrant crisis that has befallen the European Union, a number of spontaneous camps have already emerged for refugees who have come here in search of a better life.
Report presents a photo report from two such camps - "Dunkirk" and "Jungle", located near the French city of Calais.
They are home to about 7,000 refugees from Syria, Iraq, Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Sudan, Eritrea, Kosovo, Iran and Pakistan.
And living conditions here are often far from European standards, people are forced to live here in complete unsanitary conditions, in the mud, in the open air.
According to Azerbaijani activist and human rights activist Fuad Alekperov, who visited Dunkirk and Jungle camps as a volunteer, living in Scotland, people here live in inhuman conditions.
In addition, people are experiencing post-traumatic stress due to the long journey to Europe and the deaths they were forced to see at every turn in their country.
There are also a lot of orphans who lost their parents during a dangerous voyage on inflatable boats across the Mediterranean Sea.
The refugees living in these camps are eager to get to the UK and get asylum there, because the legislation of this country is softer than the emigration policy of France.
But this path is very difficult, as the camp is surrounded by barbed wire, through which current is passed, and the attempt to get to the UK through the "Eurotunnel", often ends with the death of "daredevils".
The French authorities have now begun the gradual demolition of the Jungle camp.
The authorities are trying to get rid of the camp, but what about the people?
Many do not want to return to their countries where there is a war.
Neither France nor the UK want to see these migrants.
Note that the photo is provided by F. Alekperov.

title: The 71st Cannes Festival opens in France – Rambler / entertainment
text:
The 71st Cannes Film Festival Javier Bardem opens in France.
For the first time since 2004, the festival will open a film not in French or in English - "Everybody Knows It" by Iranian director Asgar Farhadi, which starred Penelope Cruz The picture tells the story of Laura, who lives with her husband and children in Buenos Aires.
When they return to their home village in Spain for a family holiday, unexpected events change the course of their lives.
In the center of the plot, as always in Farhadi ’ s films, are family ties, as well as the moral choice that circumstances put before them.
Farhadi quickly established himself as one of the most influential and internationally renowned Iranian filmmakers.
In 2011, his “Nader and Simin ’ s Divorce ” won the Golden Bear of the Berlinale and the Golden Globe, the Cesar Award and the Academy Award for Best Foreign Film.
Farhadi ’ s last film, The Salesman, entered the official Cannes program and won the prize for best screenplay.
He also won an Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film, but the director did not come to pick him up in protest against the new US immigration policy.
In total, more than 20 films will compete for the Palme d ’ Or.
When announcing the program, the director of the show, Thierry Frémaud, noted that in the formation of the competition this year, the selectors deliberately included not the most famous directors.
Among them, for example, the director A. B. Shoki, who will present his debut “Yomeddine ” in Cannes, as well as the Frenchwoman Eva Hasson with the work“ Girls of the Sun ”.
In addition to Hasson, the program includes the films of only two women directors: Capernaum by Lebanese Nadine Labaki, Happy as Lazzaro by Italian Alice Rohrvacher, who received the Grand Prix of the Cannes jury for the picture “Miracles ” in 2014.
Of course, it will not do without famous directors who will show their films in Cannes not for the first time.
So, a live classic of world cinema Jean-Luc Godard with a video essay “Le livre d ’ image ”, a Turk and the owner of the Palm branch Nuri Bilge Ceylan with the film“ Wild pear tree ” and “Dog Man ” by Italian Matteo Garrone will come to the screening.
Also, Polish director and Oscar winner Pavel Pawlikowski will tell a love story in post-war Poland in the film “Cold War ”, and American Spike Lee will bring to the review a black comedy“ BlacKkKlansman ” about an African-American policeman from Colorado, infiltrating the Ku Klux Klan.
Another American director whose premiere is eagerly awaited is David Cameron Mitchell and his Under the Silver Lake.
Strong in program and Asian presence.
So, it includes “Thieves in the store ” and“ Asako I and II ” Japanese Hirokazu Koreeda and Ryusuke Hamaguchi, “Burning ” Korean Lee Chan-dong,“ Ashes are the purest white ” Chinese Jia Zhanke.
At the same time, while in Russia they are discussing the inclusion in the program of the main competition of the film by Kirill Serebrennikov “Summer ”, there is another disgraced director – the Iranian Jafar Panahi.
He is also under house arrest and, unlike his Russian counterpart, his fate has already been decided: he was banned from making films for twenty years, which, however, did not prevent him from sending a flash drive with a documentary film hidden in a cake to Cannes in 2011.
Fremo asked the Iranian government to release the director to the premiere of the film and allow him to return to his homeland.
This year, the organizers of the festival decided to return the tradition of the closing film and gave this honor to the film “The Man Who Killed Don Quixote ”, a long-suffering project of American director Terry Gilliam.
He tried to implement it for twenty years, but faced more and more problems before or during filming, so some managed to call him “the damned ”.
Finally, Gilliam managed to shoot a picture with Adam Driver Jonathan Price, Stellan Skarsgard and Olga Kurylenko in the lead roles.
However, his misfortunes did not end there - the former producer of the project is trying to ban the show at the Cannes Film Festival.
Another festival miracle was the return of “persona non grata ”, Danish director and famous provocateur Lars von Trier.
In 2011, during a press conference of his film “Melancholia ”, which participated in the main program of the review, Trier inadvertently expressed his sympathy for Adolf Hitler.
This did not prevent the jury from awarding the award for the best female role to the American actress Kirsten Dunst, but pretty spoiled the relationship of the organizers with the director.
Seven years later, Cannes is ready to take the scandalous director back.
His film “The House That Jack Built ” about the serial killer Jack performed by Matt Dillon will be shown out of competition.
Despite the well-known high-headedness of Cannes selectors, in recent years, the review is not complete without loud premieres of American blockbusters.
This time on the Cote d ’ Azur out of competition will host the world premiere of “Han Solo: Star Wars.
Stories "by Ron Howard, which tells the story of aspiring smuggler and pilot Han Solo performed by Alden Ehrenreich.
Curious and, according to some critics, even more interesting films parallel programs.
The Cannes Classics program will mark the 50th anniversary of Stanley Kubrick ’ s 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Viewers will be shown a 70-millimeter unrestored film, and the film will be presented by the British director Christopher Nolan.
For the first time since its premiere fifty years ago, the public will see the famous science fiction without digital tricks, edited effects or revisionist edits.
Russia in Cannes The main and parallel programs of the festival included several Russian films.
So, in the main program, Russia will be represented by the film “Summer ” by Kirill Serebrennikov, who is currently under house arrest in the case of the“ Seventh Studio ”.
The entire film community cherishes the hope that the director will still be released to Cannes so that he can present the film in person.
Meanwhile, the court extended his house arrest until July 19.
The plot of the film is based on the little-known history of relations between the leader of the group “Kino ” Viktor Tsoi, musician Mike Naumenko and his wife Natalia.
The events unfold in the summer of 1981 in Leningrad, where under the influence of Led Zeppelin, David Bowie and other Western rock stars, Russian rock is born.
This summer, Victor is recording his first album, and Mike is putting together a band called Zoo.
The main roles in the film were performed by Theo Yu, Irina Starshenbaum, musician Roma Beast.
The script of the film was written by Mikhail and Lily Idova, as well as Serebrennikov himself, based on the memoirs of Natalia Naumenko.
Also included in the main program was a film by Russian director Sergei Dvortsevoy “Hayk ” co-production of Russia, Germany, Poland and Kazakhstan about a young immigrant from Kyrgyzstan, who works illegally in Moscow.
Dvortseva already came to Cannes in 2008 and received the main prize of the second most important program of the festival “Un Certain Regard ” for the film“ Tulip ”.
At the same time, short films by young Russian directors will be presented in parallel programs: Igor Poplaukhin ’ s Calendar in Cinéfondation and Mikhail Borodin ’ s I Am Normal in Film Criticism Week.
As chairman of the jury of the main competition of the Spanish director Pedro Almodovar was replaced by Australian actress Kate Blanchett.
She came to Cannes both as an actress and as a producer, but to judge the paintings of her colleagues will be the first time.
In total, the jury included five women and four men of seven nationalities and from five continents.
One of them was the Russian director Andrei Zvyagintsev, who has repeatedly brought his films to the screening, and last year won the Grand Prix of the jury with the tape “Dislike ”.
“Participation in the jury of the Cannes Film Festival is a great honor, it can not be overestimated.
The last time a Russian member of the jury, screenwriter Maria Zvereva was invited in 1995, ” said the constant producer of the films of the Russian director Alexander Rodnyansky He noted that according to Fremo, Zvyagintsev is now undergoing an intensive course of learning English to be able to fully participate in discussions with other members of the jury.
Zvyagintsev ’ s colleagues this year will be Chinese actor Chang Chen, American writer, director and producer Ava DuVernet, singer Hajja Nin from Burundi, French actress Lea Seydou and her American colleague Kristen Stewart, French director Robert Gedigian, Canadian director Denis Villeneuve.

title: UN: Wars in Syria and Iraq lead to increased asylum requests in industrialized countries
text:
Baku.
26 March.
REPORT.AZ / In 2014, 866,000 asylum requests were filed in industrialized countries, which is 45% more than the year before.
According to a report published in Geneva by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), this is the highest figure since the conflict in the Balkans 22 years ago.
Among the reasons for such a sharp increase, experts call the wars in Syria and Iraq, armed conflicts and instability in a number of other countries, human rights violations.
The largest number of asylum requests last year came from Syrians – about 150,000.
In second place are the Iraqis – about 69,000.
This is followed by Afghans (60,000), residents of Serbia, including Kosovo, and Eritreans.
As for the host countries, the largest flow of refugees rushed to Germany - 173 thousand applications during the year.
121,000 people sought asylum in the United States, 87,000 in Turkey and 75,000 in Sweden.
At the end of 2013, there were 51.2 million people in the world who had to flee their homes due to persecution, conflict, violence or human rights violations.
Of these, 16.7 million are refugees, 33.3 million are internally displaced persons and 1.2 million are asylum seekers.

title: Adamenko: Ukraine in 20 years will become a steppe
text:
Sergei Levitsky, RIA Novosti Ukraine It is expected that this year will be hot not only the second half of spring, but also summer.
According to meteorologists, in Ukraine in the coming years, an increase in the number of droughts and dry winds is expected, which can reduce the yield of crops.
Due to frequent droughts, the country could lose about a third of its arable land.
Farmers now need to invest in the irrigation system, because without irrigation the land will be unsuitable for agriculture.
At the moment, the soils are intensively losing moisture, while the steppes are actively spreading to the North at a speed of 100-150 km per 10 years.
Thus, the climatic zone of the northern steppe has already reached the Cherkasy and Poltava regions, while desertification is observed in the southern steppe (Kherson region).
By the level of moisture in the soil, the south of Kherson region is already approaching the Kalahari desert in Africa.
On the impact of abnormally hot spring on the harvest and the consequences of global warming in Ukraine RIA Novosti Ukraine told the head of the Department of agrometeorology Hydrometeorological Center of Ukraine Tatyana Adamenko.
What is the situation with winter crops? - With winter crops is not so bad.
Despite the fact that there were abnormal temperature conditions, April was one of the warmest in the history of meteorological observations, exceeding the average monthly temperature reached about three degrees.
The highest temperatures were in the West.
It was even hotter than in the south.
But due to the fact that we had a fairly snowy winter and spring, the soil has accumulated quite a lot of moisture.
The cold period begins on November 1 and ends on March 10.
We had a lot of rain during this period.
And all this went to the ground.
Since the soil was thawed, not deeply frozen, most of the moisture was absorbed by crops.
We have formed a wonderful resource of moisture.
And this resource is what saved crops from heat stress in April.
Winter crops are now in good condition, the expansion of heat has pushed them to develop very quickly.
Development is within the normal range, maybe a little faster than normal, there is moisture in the soil.
The development of plants allows the use of moisture deep layers.
So with the winter, we are currently seeing an optimistic picture.
The situation is somewhat worse in Kherson and Mykolaiv regions, where there was no rain for about 30 days, in some areas we can talk about soil drought.
The yield potential of winter crops is above average, and a quantitative forecast can be made only after May 25, when the critical period of winter crops will pass and a spike will be formed.
What are the forecasts for spring crops? — With spring did not work very well, because we had snow in early April, when it was necessary to sow.
And when the snow came down, the soil dried up very quickly.
This happened in a very short time, that is, not very favorable conditions were created for spring crops.
However, there are no mass shoots yet, so it is too early to assess.
In the second half of May, temperatures will drop across the country.
There will be some rain at first, but it will be uneven.
Somewhere after 15-17, if nothing changes, a cyclone with already normal rains will come.
What is the prognosis for stone fruits?
Last year, frosts severely damaged the fruit and we had a bad harvest.
The most dangerous period according to climate data is until May 25.
The probability of frost before May 25, it exists annually.
No frost is expected this year until May 20.
A decrease in temperature is expected in the West - by 4-6 degrees, but there will be no frost there, so we do not expect damage to the fruits.
However, a high yield of fruit is also not worth counting on.
Due to the dry air, the trees bloomed ahead of time, respectively, there will be less pollination of flowers.
You have previously predicted an increase in the number of droughts.
What caused such a forecast?
This is not only my forecast, but also the forecast of world experts that the number of droughts in Ukraine will grow and they will be observed more often.
The most unpleasant thing is that they will cover more and more territories.
If earlier we observed dry winds in the south of the country, now they have reached Kiev and are actively spreading to the West.
This year, the probability of a cold summer is very low.
In the past 10 years, it has been above normal, so there is no reason to expect a temperature below normal in August.
It is very likely that the summer will be very dry, the fire hazard is now reaching grade 5, there is no rain for a month, which increases the risks of forest fires.
What are the forecasts for climate change in Ukraine in the medium term? — There is a great risk that within two decades the forest-steppe will turn into a steppe under the influence of climate change.
What is climate change?
This is an increase in the average annual temperature, and not only for us.
All over the world, this trend is observed.
If we have warming before 2000 was due to winter, then after 2000 the temperature rises in the summer.
If spring is cold, then warm, then the temperature in July-August is definitely higher than normal - in 90% of cases.
The consequences of climate change are its variability - colossal deviations of the weather from its average values, the presence of non-characteristic phenomena.
For example, the western regions of Ukraine have always been favorable for agriculture due to the temperate climate and high humidity, but this year in the region there is a huge number of dry winds, the temperature in Ternopil region was higher than in the Kherson region, this indicates climate variability.
As for the southern territories, in 10-20 years it will be impossible to conduct agriculture here without artificial watering of crops.
Accordingly, the field irrigation system needs to be developed now.

title: Ryazan became the center of domestic medical tourism
text:
According to the results of 2017, Ryazan became the most visited city in Russia due to the development of medical tourism, and there is reason to believe that this trend will continue this year.
Many residents of the capital and the Moscow region, planning to organize a beach or excursion tour with onlinetours.ru, prefer to strengthen their health in domestic clinics and beauty centers.
Exemplary level of service in medical institutions of Ryazan along with affordable pricing and transport accessibility of the region guarantees the city a never-ending flow of tourists who are ready to enjoy the local beauties after examinations and treatment.
The development of tourist attractiveness of Ryazan continues for many years, but the medical direction has become in high demand recently.
Despite the serious competition of clinics in Moscow, the pricing policy of many medical institutions remains inflated, which not only residents, but also guests of the capital are not ready to put up with.
Ryazan, a three-hour drive away, offers an excellent alternative in the form of first-class service and an attractive price list.
Of course, to solve alarming medical problems, Russians prefer to contact Moscow doctors, so only some medical areas are in demand in the region - dentistry, cosmetology, gynecology, urology, plastic surgery.
According to the data voiced by the expert and analytical center of the RANEPA, not only Russians from the capital come to the doctors of Ryazan, but also citizens of Vietnam, China, Japan and South Korea.
It is significant that the services of Russian medicine were also interested in some Europeans, in particular from Germany and Finland.
And if excursion tours to the region, available for order on the page ryazan.onlinetours.ru, while in stable demand, the demand for medical tours in Ryazan is growing rapidly, which is explained by the action of "word of mouth" and the price difference that plays into the hands of thrifty tourists (in dollar equivalent, medical care abroad costs 80% more expensive than in Russia with similar indicators quality of services).
The high success of Ryazan in the field of medical tourism can quickly be leveled against the background of the growing activity of other cities - St. Petersburg, Voronezh, Vladimir, Novosibirsk and, of course, Moscow.
Experts believe that local clinics should improve the quality of service, order advertising campaigns on foreign thematic sites, and the leadership of Ryazan should initiate the introduction of a tax free system, providing for the possibility of returning part of the cost of services in a medical institution or when crossing the border.
Last year, on the initiative of the head of the Ryazan region Nikolai Lyubimov, an atlas of medical services for Russians was created, and the adaptation of this guide for tourists is also a priority task of the local authorities.

title: Climate spoils rice
text:
Scientists have found that a high concentration of carbon dioxide leads to changes in vitamins and trace elements in rice.
“If we don ’ t do anything, there will be big negative impacts on human health, ” said Kristie Ebi, one of the authors of the study conducted in Japan, China.
It was there that 18 varieties of rice were studied in the open air.
During the experiment, they were exposed to carbon dioxide, much higher than natural indicators.
The study showed that at high concentrations of CO2, the content of vitamin B1, B2, B5 and B9 in the plant decreased by 25% -30%.
The study also confirmed a decrease in protein, iron and zinc.
“The strongest impact of carbon dioxide has on folic acid (vitamin B9).
And as you know, deficiencies in this vitamin in pregnant women can lead to the appearance of children with various anomalies, ” says Ebi.
Her findings seem to confirm scientific research related to wheat.
As it turned out, the yield of this cereal decreases as the planet warms.
Scientists suggest that if you compare the rice of today's crop and rice grown 10 years or more ago, you will already notice a difference in its composition - you just need to pick up samples.

title: Air pollution could lead to global rice crisis
text:
In connection with the upcoming problems of food, scientists have high hopes for cereals, in particular, rice.
Geneticists are looking for ways to create new varieties that are resistant to disease, but these measures may not be enough.
According to the new work, rice plantations are threatened by another problem - environmental pollution.
And the quality of the grains poisoned with carbon dioxide is noticeably affected.
Rice is one of the most important crops in the world, which, by the way, has been “domesticated ” several times.
Especially popular, as you know, rice has in Southeast Asia, where it accounts for up to 76% of the calories of the entire diet of local residents.
Geneticists have long begun to increase the resistance of rice to various negative factors, including they presented "superrice", which is not afraid of disease.
An international team of researchers from China, Japan, Australia and the United States made a disappointing statement: a real “rice crisis ” may occur in the world due to carbon dioxide pollution of the atmosphere.
Experts explain that elevated levels of greenhouse gas negatively affect the protein composition, as well as reduce the amount of vitamins and trace elements in rice grains.
The consumption of such “poisoned ” cereals can adversely affect human health, as the nutritional value of rice will continue to decline.
Researchers built open greenhouses to allow rice to grow naturally, but artificially raised CO2 levels in the air above the greenhouses by releasing gas from special pipes.
The concentration of carbon dioxide as a result reached 568-590 parts per million.
Today, recall, this figure is kept at the level of 410 units, but the growth rate of atmospheric pollution suggests that by the end of the century it will increase just to the designated numbers.Laboratory tests have shown that at high concentrations of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, the content of vitamins B1, B2, B5 and B9 in the plant decreased by 12-30%.
It is noted that the most decreased levels of vitamin B9, also known as folate (so called the natural form of the vitamin, and its synthetic counterpart is known worldwide as folic acid).
It is known that vitamin B9 deficiency harms any body, but most of all it affects pregnant women, their children and even grandchilds.In addition, the amount of protein in the "poisoned" greenhouse gas rice fell by 10%.
Also in cereals decreased levels of iron and zinc and other valuable trace elements.Researchers immediately explain one contradiction that can arise in anyone who is familiar with the term photosynthesis.
Recall, this chemical process involves the conversion of light energy into the energy of chemical bonds of organic substances.
This includes carbon dioxide.
However, this is the case when quantity does not mean quality, says co-author Lewis Ziska (Lewis Ziska) from the US Department of Agriculture.
If we were talking about the productivity of plants alone, then for them the increase in carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere would be an absolute plus.
But if we talk about the usefulness and nutritional value of these same plants, here the facts speak for themselves. The team also emphasizes that most previous work in this area has focused on how environmental and climatic conditions affect the growth of crops.
For example, it has been proven that due to global warming, wheat yields are reduced. However, very little attention was paid to another problem: the nutritional value of natural products of the "generation of anthropogenic changes".
Experts believe that in this area it is necessary to carry out more work in order to analyze the situation in detail and look for ways to solve such problems.By the way, the food of the future can help to escape from the food crisis - a snack from jellyfish, meat products from insects, chicken meat "from a test tube", as well as "food from electricity" and from natural gas.

title: US Justice Department approves merger of Bayer and Monsanto
text:
Moscow. May 29.
INTERFAX.RU - The US Department of Justice approved the deal on the merger of Bayer with the American Monsanto, but demanded from the German company to sell assets worth about $9 billion.
The companies agreed with the Ministry of Justice terms of the transaction, which negate its fears that the merger of Bayer and Monsanto will harm competition in the American market, the Ministry of Justice said in a statement.
The agreement requires the most significant concessions in terms of the sale of assets in the history of such cases, the statement said.
In particular, Bayer agreed to separate assets in the production of cotton, canola, soybeans and vegetable seeds, as well as the herbicide division Liberty, whose products compete with Monsanto's Roundup.
In addition, Bayer will sell part of its intellectual property and R & D assets, reports Dow Jones.
Without the sale of these assets, the merger of Bayer and Monsanto would have suppressed competition in a number of segments, which would have contributed to higher prices and reduced choice for consumers.
The terms of the agreement negate this threat, the report said.
German Bayer announced a merger with Monsanto, the world leader in plant biotechnology, as part of a $66 billion deal in September 2016.
The approval of the US Justice Department was the last of the serious obstacles on the way to the deal.
Shares of Monsanto rose 0.7% during trading in New York on Tuesday.

title: MEPhI told about the prospects of the artificial sun of China
text:
In 2020, Chinese scientists will launch a new experimental fusion reactor HL-2M as part of the EAST project.
Such installations are sometimes called "artificial Sun" - they undergo the same processes as in the core of our star.
About the prospects of the Chinese project and in general about the technology of thermonuclear fusion "360" talked with Professor George Tikhomirov - Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of NRNU MEPhI.
The head of the Southwest Institute of Physics, Duan Xuzhu, previously said that the HL-2M reactor will be able to heat the plasma to a temperature above 200 million degrees Celsius.
The previous record was also set in China: a year ago in another experimental tokamak EAST - HT-7U - the peak temperature was 100 million degrees.
Tokamak HT-7U project EAST Tokamak is an abbreviation of "toroidal chamber with magnetic coils".
The name was invented by Soviet physicists in the 1950s, at the same time the first experiments were carried out to retain heated plasma with the help of powerful magnets.
Thermonuclear reactions are constantly on the Sun.
In the core, whose temperature reaches 15 million degrees Celsius, hydrogen is converted into helium.
A huge amount of energy is released.
To recreate the process on Earth, it is necessary to heat the hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium to a temperature above 100 million degrees Celsius.
At this point, the gas becomes plasma.
Such temperatures are needed to achieve a higher density of energy release than on the Sun, Tikhomirov explained.
The sun is very large, and therefore the energy it gives is enough for everyone.
And on Earth, we create conditions to a lesser extent.
If the conditions are close to solar, it does not allow us to use them for practical needs.
Georgy Tikhomirov Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI In addition, for a functional thermonuclear reactor (which would give more energy than spent) it is necessary to hold the plasma inside the tokamak for a long time and obtain high-density plasma.
According to Tikhomirov, the Chinese installation HL-2M “in some respects will surpass the existing ones, ” but“ there is no breakthrough in this. ”
The deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology recalled that the largest thermonuclear reactor in the world, ITER, is being built at the Cadarache Research Center in France.
This international project involves the EU, Japan, Russia, the United States, China, India and South Korea.
The reactor, which is planned to be completed by 2025, the Chinese “can not surpass ”, the professor is sure.
Most likely, they will create some compact small installation, where they will achieve good plasma parameters.
But there will be no breakthrough in energy.
Georgy Tikhomirov, deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI, added that in Russia thermonuclear research "is developing in various directions."
“We will soon launch the T-15, our tokamak, there are other installations.
We are also part of the ITER program.
This topic is known, and we are not inferior to the Chinese here, ” Tikhomirov said.
The professor noted that the launch of a thermonuclear power plant has great prospects, because the fuel that can be used is deuterium "very much in the oceans."
