title: Nushiravan Maharramli: The activities of organizations that calculate the rating of TV programs are opaque - INTERVIEW
text:
© Report.az "Unfortunately, the AGB organization does not understand its responsibility in Azerbaijan and does not want to invest the necessary investments" Baku.
August 23.
Report Interview of the Chairman of the National Council of Television and Radio of Azerbaijan Nushiravan Maharramli. - How do you assess the quality of programs broadcast on Azerbaijani TV channels? - The situation in the television space of Azerbaijan is generally satisfactory.
However, there is still much to be done in this area.
We are concerned about the low level of broadcasts on local television, especially on private television channels.
There are objective and subjective reasons for this.
The objective reasons are mainly related to the situation in the advertising market of Azerbaijan.
Sometimes programs on private TV channels are compared with programs on Turkish, Russian television.
But they do not take into account the situation in the advertising market of those countries.
The difference between spending on shooting TV series, show business programs in these countries compared to ours is heaven and earth.
For this reason, the situation on local TV channels is bleak.
The situation in the advertising sphere of Azerbaijan is also connected with the economic situation.
The economic difficulties observed in recent years in the world, in one way or another, affect our country.
In addition, the personnel problem of private TV channels is a concern.
The situation on state-funded TV channels is different.
In this area a little limp only the dynamism, efficiency.
In comparison with previous years, there has been a significant reduction in the number of offences on private TV channels.
There is a culture of ether, and the current situation with the language is comparatively better than in previous years.
However, there is still a lot to be done in this area...
In addition, there have been no changes in people ’ s thinking about TV channels, they think that the situation is deplorable.
In general, triviality in the programs of TV channels, movies, TV series is inherent not only in our country, but all over the world. - Now the solution of problems with advertising does not depend on TV channels.
Therefore, the issue of not attracting advertising by educational programs is often raised, and as a result, the number of entertainment programs is growing.
How can this be prevented? - The solution of the advertising problem by TV channels is connected with the issue of economic development in the country.
But there are projects that we are working on.
We are concerned about the lack of transparency, unhealthy attitude in the activities of organizations that count the rating.
These rating organizations prefer show business programs, constantly show them rating.
The question is who is doing this calculation and in what stratum of society.
No one knows how they do this job.
Sitting in an ordinary room, they can easily give such information themselves.
No one checks them, does not control the activity, it is unknown among which people the survey is conducted.
We carry out certain works, in this regard, and we have plans and goals aimed at the future.
In Azerbaijan, the rating was measured by an organization called AGB (Nielsen Media Research).
After the transition to digital broadcasting, this work faded into the background.
They are trying to make a big profit with a small investment.
That's not true.
After switching to digital broadcasting, they should increase the number of piplemeters.
In previous years, in Baku, the rating was 200 piplmeters, and in other areas, too, 200 piplmeters.
This is shared advertising.
But after the transition to digital broadcasting, this process was greatly reduced, because they carried out measurement work on analog broadcasting.
Now digital broadcasting is carried out only on cable networks.
The cable network does not cover the whole country, there are only in Baku, Sumgayit and Ganja.
Therefore, there are problems with their rating.
We see these problems and we have appeals in this regard.
Unfortunately, the AGB organization does not understand its responsibility in Azerbaijan and does not want to invest the necessary investments.
They want to do this work at the expense of Azerbaijan ’ s own capital.
In general, such organizations not only here, but also in other countries have created great problems.
Therefore, these organizations often change.
We are trying to make positive changes in this area. - You say that there is a problem with personnel on TV channels.
How can this problem be solved? - This question should be considered together with other problems.
The current situation on private TV channels is a cause for concern: poor quality of broadcasts, preference for vulgar and banal broadcasts.
I don ’ t think TV channels are doing this intentionally.
It's just what they can do today.
The personnel problem is a serious issue.
Especially TV presenters should be hired after careful consideration.
The host of both programs about cuisine, show business and intellectual should have a broad worldview, know the topic and norms of the literary Azerbaijani language well.
Otherwise, the integrity is violated, the program becomes monotonous, tedious.
Viewers, seeing such a speech of the presenter, remain dissatisfied.
As a result, TV channels of other countries are chosen.
Naturally, the creation of good personnel is not a one-sided work.
This process begins with a secondary school, a higher educational institution and flows into public life.
The issue of personnel training is an issue that requires an integrated approach and will be resolved over time. - Nushiravan Muellim, the process of transition to digital broadcasting has been completed.
Are there any problems in this area? - In general, the transition to digital broadcasting is a technical process.
In this regard, there are no longer any problems.
Some channels have updated the equipment for better broadcasting of programs.
These innovations are now being applied in the countries of the world, because if you fall behind the system, you will not be able to function.
ATV and Xəzər channels have done a lot of work in this direction.
Other channels will also do this work with the improvement of the material situation.
TV channels that use frequencies spend a lot of money.
- Today, one of the factors causing concern on Azerbaijani TV channels is the violation of the norms of the literary language.
You also conduct regular monitoring.
How do you feel about the fact that everyday spoken language finds its way to TV channels? - In Soviet times, TV channels mainly spoke in the academic style, and it was not allowed to speak the everyday language.
It was an extreme measure.
But after independence, we went to the other extreme.
Today we do not speak a literary language, we speak everyday, everyday language.
Of course, it is necessary not to separate one from the other, but to maintain balance.
Everyday spoken language is more evident in the speech of the audience invited to the broadcast.
It is also possible in performances, films, documentaries.
But it is impractical for the presenter to use in speech a spoken language, words borrowed from a foreign language.
In a globalizing world, the languages of great powers influence the languages of peoples like ours.
Therefore, we must choose a method of self-defense and resist.
This resistance should be mainly provided by the intelligentsia.
Unfortunately, our intelligentsia is indifferent to this issue, and sometimes they cannot express their views in their native language.
The role and responsibility of television in protecting these issues is great.
Because people look at them and take them as examples, and everything they see is perceived as correct.
Therefore, it is important for TV presenters, directors and broadcasters to know the norms of the Azerbaijani literary language.
In general, regardless of race, religion, anyone who lives in this country, a citizen of Azerbaijan, should know the state language.
Unfortunately, there are serious problems in this area.
Some of our officials, composers, speak Russian.
Even our performers, despite the fact that they sing in their native language, sometimes express their views in Russian.
These are the most worrying factors.
A few years ago, state funds were allocated for the creation of local television series.
Today, TV channels managed to make a breakthrough with the series.
What are the shortcomings in this area? - In allocating funds for the series, the Azerbaijani government sought to revive this sector.
Our desire was for the youth to be formed not on the basis of foreign series, but on the basis of national ones.
One - time financial assistance has been provided to support this area.
So I think we have managed to create a revival in this sector.
At the previous stage, there were too many series, and their quality was a concern.
Because they were of very low quality.
But high quality series also require funds.
I noted that in neighboring countries - in Turkey and in Russia, advertising is expensive.
In these countries, one minute of advertising costs from 40 to 50 thousand dollars, but we do not have 1,000 dollars.
The quality of broadcasts corresponds to advertising.
But recently, the TV channels Xəzər, ATV are releasing new series at their own expense.
It's progress.
The state is studying this issue, and we will come back to it if necessary.
But, as you know, these issues should be regulated by market relations.
Sponsors have to find entrepreneurs, rich people have to do it.
I believe that after a while our country will be the way we want it to be.
There was a time, we only watched Brazilian TV series, then Turkish, and then we switched to our TV series.
As Azerbaijan develops economically, progress will be made in this area.
Unfortunately, there are problems with the series itself.
After all, the series should also have an educational role.
For example, one of the best moments for me in Turkish TV series is that the person sitting behind the wheel of a car, first of all fastens a seat belt.
This is a signal that everyone should do this while driving a car.
Also, don ’ t talk on the phone while driving.
But, unfortunately, in Azerbaijan, TV shows often send negative messages.
Most of all, the place is given to criminal issues.
Problems with the language in the series are also not happy.
But this problem exists not only among our actors, but also among our officials and intellectuals.
Unfortunately, we cannot keep the middle ground.
The work of improving the language in gardens and schools will also spread to society.
Problems will be solved if society becomes healthier in this matter. - What should be done to meet the demand for children 's programs, cartoons? - We are concerned about the small number of children' s programs and cartoons in Azerbaijan.
Our children are raised on foreign cartoons.
Therefore, we would like to increase the production of local cartoons.
Previously, we recommended that each TV channel once a year produce one cartoon, even if it does not have direct responsibilities.
If each TV channel shoots one cartoon a year for ten years, then there will be a hundred cartoons.
In this case, our children will not be brought up under the influence of cartoons of foreign countries.
The State Committee for Family, Women and Children Affairs was making active efforts to establish children's television.
As you know, the creation of television for each region (religious, educational, youth, etc.) is not typical for countries such as Azerbaijan.
The opening of television channels is a real desire.
But the channel must have an audience, a market.
We have already opened two sports channels.
A sports channel for a country like Azerbaijan is a burden.
But the state has shouldered this burden because it pays special attention to sports and culture.
The Gütb TV channel, previously operating in Guba, has changed its direction of activity.
Now it is called "Günəş" and broadcasts programs for children.
We even placed this channel on the cable network, although he did not have such a right.
Thus, the channel is also broadcast in Baku.
We want improvements in this area.
If Güneş TV can form itself, it could be seen in the future as a children ’ s television broadcast across the country.

title: SpaceX sent to the ISS robot-assistant CIMON with the AI system IBM Watson
text:
Today, SpaceX launched another Dragon cargo ship to the ISS as part of the Commercial Resupply Services supply contract.
In addition to scientific equipment and food, the CRS-15 spacecraft will deliver a new crewmember to the orbital station - CIMON assistant robot with artificial intelligence.
During the launch, the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket and the Dragon spacecraft (for the third time) were used: the first stage flew as part of the TESS mission, and the cargo ship as part of the CRS-9 mission.
The launch was broadcast on the SpaceX YouTube channel.
The Falcon 9 rocket with the CRS-15 Dragon mission cargo spacecraft launched from the launch pad of the SLC-40 complex at Cape Canaveral at 12: 44 Kyiv time.
The return of the first stage was not made, as this launch was the last for the missiles in the Block 4 modification.
Ten minutes after launch, the ship was launched into the target orbit and undocked from the second stage.
It is expected to arrive at the ISS on Monday, July 2, after which it will be captured by a robotic arm and docked to the station.
The CIMON robot was developed by Airbus.
It weighs about five kilograms and is equipped with 14 fans to move around the station.
On one side of this flattened "bell" is a screen on which all sorts of useful information and tips can be displayed.
The “brain ” of the robot is the artificial intelligence system IBM Watson.
In total, Dragon will deliver about 2.7 tons of payload to the ISS.
In addition to CIMON, there are other important equipment, tools and samples for experiments: Rodent Research-7 to study the effects of microgravity on the intestinal microflora of mice and the effects of changes on other physiological systems (immunity, metabolism and circadian rhythms), Made In Space Fiber Optics to create high-quality optical fibers, Angiex Cancer Therapy to study the effects of anticancer drugs and spare Capture for the Canadarm2 robot arm, which is used to dock incoming ships, including for the Dragon itself.
The Dragon cargo ship will spend about a month in orbit around the ISS, and then with the cargo will be sent back to Earth.
It will bring about 1.8 tons of cargo and waste to Earth.
Cargo missions to the station as part of the Commercial Resupply Services program since 2012 have been carried out by the Dragon and Cygnus spacecraft, created by SpaceX and Orbital ATK.
From next year, cargo will be delivered under the CRS2 program, and Dragon and Cygnus in the future should join the space shuttle Dream Chaser, which is currently undergoing testing.
In August, the first demonstration (unmanned) flight of the spacecraft SpaceX Crew Dragon, which is being developed as part of the program for the development of private manned spacecraft for the delivery of astronauts to the ISS NASA Commercial Crew Development.
It is currently in the final phase of testing at NASA.
In addition to SpaceX, Boeing (CST-100 Starliner), Blue Origin (New Shepard) and Sierra Nevada (Dream Chaser) are also developing ships for NASA under the Commercial Crew Development program.
Source: SpaceX

title: A holiday of Turkic peoples was held in Baku in honor of the 25th anniversary of TURKSOY - PHOTO
text:
A festive evening dedicated to the 25th anniversary of the International Organization of Turkic Culture (TURKSOY) was held at the Rashid Beybutov State Song Theater, Trend reports.
The concert program was attended by groups and performers from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Russia.
Director General of TÜRKSOY Dusen Kaseinov noted that for 25 years the organization has passed a glorious path, conducts great work to promote Turkic culture, literature, art, implements important projects aimed at promoting and popularizing the rich pan-Turkic culture in the world, promotes fruitful cooperation between the Turkic peoples for the preservation, development and transfer to future generations of common material and cultural monuments of Turkic peoples.
The organization dates back to 1992, when meetings were held in Baku and Istanbul, at which the ministers of culture of Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Turkey and Turkmenistan declared their readiness to cooperate within the framework of a joint cultural project.
As a result of the agreement signed on July 12, 1993 in Almaty, the Organization for the Joint Development of Turkic Culture and Art was established.
In 1996, official cooperation with UNESCO was launched.
In 2009, the organization received its current name.
The main goal of TURKSOY organization: - development of cultural ties between peoples, countries and ethnic groups speaking Turkic languages; - research, study, protection and bringing to the world samples of Turkic culture; - elimination of differences in the culture of Turkic peoples that arose for historical, political and geographical reasons and under the influence of foreign countries; - proof of the commonality of Turkic culture; - protection of Turkic culture from the harmful effects of other - preservation of the alphabet and language between Turkic states and communities living in a vast geographical area; - dissemination of Turkic culture, which occupies an important place in world culture, and in other places; - creation of a center for storing documents related to Turkic culture, art and archival documents; - popularization of outstanding historical figures, thinkers, poets all over the world and writers, as well as statesmen of the Turkic world, etc.
To achieve these goals TURKSOY takes the following measures: - develops and strengthens ties between the Turkic-speaking peoples in the field of culture and art, ensures the joint implementation of various programs and projects for this purpose; - implements measures aimed at identifying, preserving, studying, developing and promoting common spiritual values, historical heritage, samples of literature and art, traditional sports and folk games; - carries out orders for the creation of radio and television programs, documentary - organizes festivals and competitions in the field of theater, music, opera and ballet art, participates in similar events held by structures of another profile; - organizes exhibitions, art exhibitions and other events aimed at the development of fine and plastic arts; - publishes periodic and one-time printed products; - organizes anniversaries, memorial evenings and other mass events. events dedicated to the anniversaries of important events of the all-Turkic history, outstanding personalities who made a significant contribution to the development of the language, literature, culture and art of the Turkic-speaking countries; - within the framework of the goals and objectives of TURKSOY holds international scientific conferences, symposia, discussions, etc.; - establishes mutual relations in the field of culture, art, education, etc., cooperates with them in the implementation of joint programs.

title: How climate change is assessed in Uzbekistan
text:
Since 2014, each subsequent year has been declared by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) the warmest on record.
Most likely, 2019 will be no exception to this alarming trend.
This July rewrote the history of climate, setting dozens of new temperature records at local, national and global levels, WMO Secretary-General Petteri Taalas said.
Uzbekistan is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change.
Since 1880, the average annual temperature in the country has risen by 1.6 degrees Celsius (from 13.2 to 14.8 degrees), which exceeds the average growth rate on the planet.
It is predicted that in 2030 – 2050 the air temperature in the Central Asian region may increase by another 1.5 – 3 degrees.
Here, the greatest increase in air temperature is expected in the Aral Sea region, since due to the drying up of the Aral Sea there are also specific local climatic changes.
As assessed by climate change, Uzbekistan has been a party to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) since 1993 and ratified the Paris Climate Agreement in 2018.
The country has made voluntary quantitative commitments to reduce the carbon intensity of GDP (specific greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP) and adaptation to climate change.
Uzhydromet under the Ministry of Emergency Situations is the responsible organization for fulfilling the obligations under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement.
Earlier, Uzhydromet prepared the first (1999), second (2008) and third national communications on climate change (2016).
The Paris Agreement requires the country to maintain: reports on the inventory of sources of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and the assessment of the impact of mitigation measures every two years; national communications on climate change every four years.
Inventory of sources of anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases.
Since 2019, the preparation of the fourth national communication has begun, which will take about two years, Uzhydromet expert Raisa Taryannikova, who participated in the preparation of the third national communication, told Gazeta.uz.
As a result, in 2021, the first biennial report on the inventory and assessment of the impact of mitigation measures and the inventory of sources of greenhouse gas emissions for 1990 - 2018 should also be prepared.
Where and how should this data be used?
The most vulnerable agriculture provides food for people.
And it is the most sensitive to climate change, said the expert of the enterprise UZGIP (Uzgipromeliovodkhoz) Tatyana Khamzina at a training for journalists on September 10, organized by the Regional Environmental Center of Central Asia.
Irrigation of agricultural land with an area of ​ ​ 4.3 million hectares is spent 90-92% of all water used in the country, the agricultural sector accounts for 27% of employment in the country, and the livelihoods of rural residents mainly depend on agricultural production, the expert said.
Increasing heat supply with a warming climate can bring benefits to agriculture - for example, the overwintering of animals will be easier, less need to cover heat-loving crops for the winter, may increase the sugar content of grapes.
Opportunities for obtaining several harvests per year, growing late-ripening and heat-loving crops are increasing – however, these benefits will be real only with sufficient water supply, Tatyana Khamzina emphasized.
At the same time, there are more and more problems with water supply: according to the World Bank, the need for water for irrigation in agriculture is not fully met today.
Due to the lack of water by 2030, we can expect a decrease in the yield of winter wheat, cotton and orchards, respectively, by 7 − 9%, 4 − 5%, 6 − 8%.
The damage to the economies of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Kyrgyzstan caused by climate change is from 0.4% to 1.3% of their annual GDP, according to the World Bank.
In Uzbekistan, it is also necessary to analyze the possible damage to the main sectors of the economy - water supply, energy, agriculture, forestry, transport - from climate change, World Bank expert Benoit Boske told Gazeta.uz.
A number of state programs are devoted to the Aral Sea region to mitigate the consequences of the Aral disaster and the development of the region; documents on the development of agriculture, irrigation, improvement of land reclamation and the use of water resources have been adopted.
At the same time, the World Bank expert notes the fragmented nature of this work, since there is no “single national coordination mechanism that would take effective measures in response to the challenges of climate change. ”
Indeed, the country does not yet have such a comprehensive strategy for responding to climate change that would oblige to take these changes into account in the adoption and implementation of all national and sectoral development programmes and plans.
Recently, the development of an agricultural development strategy for the next ten years has been initiated, which will largely reflect the responses to climate challenges.
One of the main directions of the strategy is to increase efficiency and keep records of water use, as well as the introduction of water-saving technologies on 200 thousand hectares of areas every year.
“200 thousand hectares each year on water-saving technologies is a very ambitious task.
But if we do not set such ambitious goals, there will be no progress, ” Aleksey Volkov, National Coordinator of the Small Grants Program of the Global Environment Facility (SGP), commented to Gazeta.uz. “We hope that the experience of the SGP of the GEF on soil protection agriculture will be reflected in the draft of this strategy. ”

title: SpaceX for the 10th time in a row tested the parachutes of the Crew Dragon spacecraft, becoming one step closer to the first manned mission to the ISS
text:
SpaceX has completed this year with an important achievement that brings it one step closer to the long-awaited first operational Crew Dragon flight with a crew as part of the Demo-2 mission.
Yesterday, the space company Ilona Mask for the tenth time in a row successfully tested the redesigned parachute system of the third version, once again demonstrating its safety.
Recall that in May 2019, the tests of the previous version ended in an accident and then Elon Musk said that SpaceX will conduct “a minimum of 10 successful tests before launching astronauts. ”
Yesterday the team completed the 10th successful multi-chute test in a row of Crew Dragon ’ s upgraded Mark 3 parachute design – one step closer to safely launching and landing @ NASA astronauts pic.twitter.com / nfFjnKygB4 – SpaceX (@ SpaceX) December 23, 2019 By the way, last month as part of a series of tests, SpaceX successfully tested new parachutes for Crew Dragon 13 times in a row, and also conducted static tests of the Crew Dragon emergency rescue system in a new configuration with ruptured diaphragm valves in the boost tubes instead of titanium valves.
The improvement should prevent the very possibility of a repeat of the scenario that led to the crash in April.
So far, SpaceX has not publicly evaluated those tests.
The only thing that separates SpaceX from the first manned flight of Crew Dragon, tentatively scheduled for the first half of 2020, is additional optional tests of the SAS with shooting the capsule in flight.
The ship certification program does not require this, but SpaceX on its own initiative intends to conduct these tests to demonstrate the reliability of the SAS.
The first Pad Abort Test with a simulation of a rocket crash before launch and shooting the capsule from the launch pad SpaceX held back in 2015.
Recall, just recently Boeing CST-100 Starliner — the second manned spacecraft, which is being developed as part of NASA ’ s program to stimulate the development of private ships in order to gain independence from Russia — returned to Earth after the failed first flight to the ISS.

title: Europe's stock markets are declining
text:
The main European stock exchanges are trading with negative dynamics, as traders are concerned about the potential impact of the financial crisis in Turkey on the banking sector in Europe, according to trading data.
As of 12.26 Moscow time, the British FTSE 100 index fell by 0.52%, to 7627.25 points, the French CAC 40 by 0.26%, to 5401.31 points, the German DAX - by 0.57%, to 12353.98 points.
The dynamics in the stock markets is due to the concern of traders with the situation in Turkey.
In recent months, the Turkish lira has repeatedly updated historical lows against the dollar and the euro, since the beginning of the year it has depreciated against these currencies by more than 30%.
The crisis escalated on Friday when US President Donald Trump said he had authorized a doubling of tariffs on aluminum and steel from Turkey to 20% and 50%, respectively.
The exchange rate of the Turkish lira on Monday night updated another historical low of 7.1326 lira per dollar.
Against this background, shares of European banks with a significant presence in Turkey are becoming cheaper.
Thus, the securities of the Spanish BBVA are reduced in price by 2.71%, the Italian Unicredit - by 2.06%, the Dutch ING - by 1.6%.
Shares of French BNP Paribas fell by 0.78%, British HSBC - by 0.19%.
“Despite the fact that the country itself has limited ties with the rest of the world, the spread of the crisis to Europe through the impact on banks is a serious problem, ” said Konstantinos Anthis, head of research at ADS Securities.
The pessimism of investors is also associated with the scandal around the Bayer concern.
His papers collapsed 11% after a California jury ordered herbicide manufacturer Monsanto to pay compensation of about $290 million to a former gardener who accused the company of developing a malignant tumor because of its herbicides.
In June, Bayer announced the completion of its Monsanto acquisition.

title: Drought and a catastrophically low harvest: what did the summer heat bring to Europe?
text:
Heated as in the desert air this summer turned the usually green pastures and gardens of Europe into a scorched, arid landscape in brown tones.
Drought, especially in the northern and central regions of the continent, has had a devastating impact on farm crops.
We studied in detail the causes of the summer drought to understand how global climate change could be the cause for such weather changes.
ESA satellite imagery of the Copernicus project Drought in Europe in 2018
According to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), in the first half of the summer, the drought was caused by prolonged periods of hot weather, record high temperatures and catastrophically low rainfall.
Already the spring months, April and May, have become the warmest, judging by the average temperatures in Europe according to long-term observations.
This trend continued in the summer, with June and July temperatures well above average, especially in the Nordic countries.
Temperatures exceeded 30 ° C in the Arctic Circle: in Norway, the thermometer on July 17 rose to a record level of 33.5 ° C, and Finland experienced the hottest July on record.
Precipitation levels were also extremely low: a precipitation map compiled by the European Climate Observatory shows extensive areas of “extreme aridity ” that stretch from Belgium and the Netherlands to Finland and Estonia.
What caused the drought in Europe?
Scientists point to a combination of several factors, such as global climate change on the planet and a zone of increased atmospheric pressure that remained motionless over European territory for a long period.
The question of what causes these anticyclones to remain “locked ” for such a long time remains open.
Scientists are trying to understand whether climate change on the planet is affecting the increase in surface temperature of the world's oceans.
This, in turn, can affect atmospheric flows, leading to stagnant phenomena of weather conditions.
Is global climate change causing drought?
“Undoubtedly, the effect of dry weather is amplified by climate change.
And this trend, unfortunately, will only intensify, - told euronews one of the world's leading experts in the field of climate Jean-Pascal van Ipersel. - The EU plan to combat climate change was prepared in 2015, on the eve of the Paris conference.
And since then, the plan has not been updated, although it has been three years since the conclusion of the Paris climate agreement! "
“The level of ambition does not correspond to the stated goal of the Paris Agreement: to keep the growth of average annual temperatures at a level not higher than 1.5 ° C in the next 30 years, ” continues Mr. van Ypersel,“ It is not too late to try to get away from the worst scenario.
But it is obvious that completely avoiding the [negative] impact on the climate, which we are witnessing today, will not be possible. "
"The effect of global climate change is already quite obvious.
And it is a clear reminder that collective efforts must be much more serious than what we see today.
We must completely rid the world economy of hydrocarbon dependence, - says Jean-Pascal van Ypersel. - And this applies to human activities in all sectors: it is necessary to get rid of fossil energy sources as soon as possible.
This requires a strong political will, which we have not seen so far. ”
What is already being done to combat drought in Europe?
Brussels has responded to requests from EU member states by easing regulation and speeding up payments to drought-stricken farmers.
Farmers will be able to receive up to 70% of direct subsidies and 85% of aid for rural development in mid-October, rather than in December 2018, as previously planned.
Livestock breeders will also be able to use paired land, which is not normally intended for exploitation, to feed livestock.
What are the effects of drought in Europe?
Farmers across Europe are preparing for one of the worst harvests in the history of our generation, and the yields of some vegetable crops will drop by 50%.
“In the hot and dry weather that lasted throughout July, vegetable crops continue to suffer across much of the continent, yields have plummeted, ” the European Association of Fruit and Vegetable Producers said in a statement.
German potato chip manufacturers are concerned that a drought could lead to a shortage of potatoes needed for industrial production of chips, according to a major company.
Analysts at Strategyie Grains, meanwhile, said wheat and barley yields in Germany and Scandinavia this year could be assessed as "catastrophic."
At the same time, grain yields declined in France, Italy, the United Kingdom, and countries in Central and Southeast Europe.
At this stage, it is not clear what impact the drought will have on consumer prices, but farmers are already under economic pressure because of … hay prices.
Many of them had to buy more hay for feed because the grass on which their herds usually graze has not grown this year.
Meanwhile, electricity prices in Norway are expected to continue to rise due to the country ’ s high dependence on hydropower.
Country breakdown: Which parts of Europe suffered the most?
Sweden ’ s wheat harvest could fall by more than 40% this year due to dry and hot weather, said the head of the grain department of the largest Swedish farm Lantmannen.
The wheat harvest could fall by more than a million tonnes, forcing the country to switch from grain exports to imports, Lantmannen ’ s Mikael Jeppson said.
The drought has also led to numerous wildfires, the geography of which this year extends all the way to the Arctic Circle.
Finnish farmers suffered losses due to wet and cold weather last year, and this summer are seriously affected by drought, the Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners emphasizes.
The organization calls for a review of the policy on imported products, arguing that the drought has led to market distortions and loss of competitiveness of farms.
“I ’ ve never seen such hot and dry weather in my life, and I ’ ve been farming for more than 30 years, ” Max Shulman told NBC News, the owner of a farm 50 km from Helsinki that grows beans, oats, wheat and oilseeds.
Shulman claims that the precipitation over the territory of his farm since the end of April does not exceed 75 mm, compared with the usual for these places 250-350 mm.
Temperatures in early August approached 30 ° C in Finland, although the average in August is 19 ° C.
Given that few people in the country use air conditioners, one supermarket in Helsinki offered to spend the night in a cooled room to 100 customers of the store.
Many parts of England and Wales have not seen rain since the end of May this year, which has created conditions of "increased flammability", as noted by the National Farmers Union (NSF).
Due to dry weather, grass growth has greatly decreased and the yield of some crops has decreased, the NSF said in a statement.
“These unprecedented weather conditions must be a signal for all of us, ” said the head of the NSF, Minette Butters,“ This is a kind of reminder that we should not take food production for granted. ”
According to the state agency PAP, about 65% of arable land in Poland has been affected by drought.
May in Poland was the warmest in the last 55 years, said Suzanna Savinska of the Poznań University of Natural Sciences.
Germany May temperatures are the highest since 1881.
According to forecasts, the grain harvest in the country this year will fall due to drought by 20%.
"In many areas, farmers are suffering from severe shortages of animal feed," German Agriculture Minister Julia Klockner said in early August.
According to her, some farmers are forced to cut costs by sending animals for slaughter ahead of schedule.
According to the Estonian Meteorological Service, rainfall in May was 60% lower than the average, and the number of sunny days increased by 48%.
From 30% to 70% of the harvest this summer may be lost, said the Minister of agriculture of Estonia Tarmo Tamm.
Farmers are considering the possibility of selling cattle, since the farms do not have enough feed, said Urmas Kruuse, deputy chairman of the Agricultural Committee of the Estonian Parliament.
The government has already allocated 20 million euros to farmers affected by the drought.
The drought in Latvia was a "national disaster", which was announced in June.
Farmers sell cattle due to lack of feed.
“Last year we had heavy rains and floods: my fields were under water and I could not harvest, ” Dainis Rutenbergs, whose farm is located near the city of Dobele, told AFP.
I am very concerned about the payment of interest on bank loans. "
The Latvian Horticultural Association has warned that 90% of the cranberry crop, 60% of the strawberry crop and 40% to 50% of the apple and pear crop could be lost this year.
Lithuania ’ s government declared a national emergency in July.
According to the Ministry of Agriculture of the country, the yield of agricultural crops decreased by 15-50% compared to the level of 2006.
The country has asked the EU to allow grazing of livestock on lands reserved for the preservation of the environment.
Total grain production in Lithuania is expected to drop to 5.5 million tonnes due to drought, down 13% from last year.
The Swiss army in August carried out an operation to deliver water by air for cows in high-altitude pastures that were affected by hot weather.
The federal government is cutting import tariffs on livestock feed to help farmers fight drought.
Philippe Loiba, head of the economy and sports in the government, said Switzerland had not seen such a drought since 1921.
From flowing through Switzerland, the Rhine caught tons of dead fish, affected by the increase in water temperature, which, in turn, affects the content of oxygen in it.
According to Troel Toft, a spokesman for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food of Denmark, the drought has seriously hit Denmark, and the spring harvest of cereals and vegetables has decreased by 40-50%.
The losses will cost the country's agricultural industry 8.5 billion Swedish kroner [about 828 million euros], Toft added.
“We haven ’ t seen anything like this in the last 150 years or so, ” he said,“ when you ’ re driving around Denmark, it ’ s not the country we ’ re used to seeing.
Some farmers will go bankrupt, that ’ s for sure.
If any of them had problems before the drought, it is now the situation will push them even further to collapse. "

title: Scientists have estimated the loss of agriculture from insects due to warming
text:
Moscow.
31 August.
INTERFAX.RU - American scientists have estimated the loss of world agriculture from insect pests, the activity of which will increase due to global warming.
Even under a safe scenario, annual wheat crop losses will reach 59 million tonnes against the current production of 749.4 million tonnes.
Together with rice and corn, the loss will be about 213 million tons, writes N + 1 with reference to the journal Science.
Global climate change, in particular, will lead to more frequent and intense droughts, dangerous for crops.
In addition, warming can “reshape ” the map of world agriculture, shifting the boundaries of regions where the climate allows you to grow certain varieties of plants.
Curtis Deutsch, from the University of Washington, has estimated how much increased insect activity, which previous studies have linked to warming, will affect crops of rice, corn and wheat - three key crops for about 4 billion people, according to statistics from the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
According to FAO, in 2016, 749.4 million tons of wheat, 740 million tons of rice and 1.06 billion tons of corn were grown worldwide.
"We expect crop losses due to insect activity to increase for two reasons.
First, warming exponentially increases the rate of metabolism in insects.
Secondly, everywhere except the tropics, warming will increase the rate of their reproduction.
As a result, there will be more insects that will eat more, ” said Deutsch, who is quoted by the press service of the university.
Scientists used data from previous laboratory experiments and observations on the influence of temperature on the metabolism and reproduction of 38 species of insect pests: in particular, these studies showed that if the metabolic rate increases steadily with the ambient temperature, then there is an optimal temperature for reproduction, after which its speed reaches a plateau or decreases.
As a result, scientists built a model of the dynamics of their population depending on different scenarios of climate change and combined this data with data on yields and the projected increase in global average temperature until 2050.
The geographical resolution of the model allowed them to make forecasts for individual regions: for example, the most pronounced effect of warming will be in regions where the climate is now temperate, for example, in the "corn belt" in the Midwest of the United States and in Europe, where annual losses of wheat crops while maintaining the current trajectory of temperature growth can exceed 16 million tons.
The authors of the study showed that each additional degree of future warming will lead to an increase in annual crop losses by 10-25 percent.
The relatively safe two-degree warming scenario envisaged by the 2015 Paris Agreement would thus result in losses of approximately 213 million tonnes per year, reducing corn yields by 31%, rice by 19% and wheat by 46%.
Today ’ s major producers of these crops, such as the United States, China and France, will suffer the most.
The most pronounced effect will be on wheat, while rice and corn growing in warmer climates will suffer less.
According to co-author of the study Rosamond Naylor (Rosamond Naylor), to combat the increased activity of insects will need all the technologies of modern agriculture, including pesticides, the use of GMOs and practices like crop rotation, not available to all countries.
But even so, in most warming scenarios, "insects still win," Naylor says.
In a commentary on the study published in the journal Science, Markus Riegler of the University of Western Sydney notes that the authors' model may underestimate crop losses, for example, due to the fact that many insects simultaneously carry pathogens dangerous to crops.
On the other hand, warming will affect the natural enemies of insects, and in addition to rising temperatures, they will be affected by other factors of climate change, such as changes in rainfall patterns or more frequent periods of extreme temperatures.
Earlier, another group of scientists said that if humanity does not start taking measures to combat climate change before 2035, it will not be able to limit the increase in global average temperature to a safe two degrees Celsius.
However, even if humanity complies with the Paris Agreement, the average temperature on Earth can still rise by another 3-4 degrees due to irreversible climatic processes that will trigger warming.

title: Nabil Shaath: Trump wants to use Arabs against Russia and Iran
text:
A quarter of a century ago, on September 13, 1993, on the White House lawn, Palestinian and Israeli leaders exchanged a historic handshake, turning from sworn enemies into partners in a Middle East settlement.
The Oslo process, which got its name from earlier secret talks in the Norwegian capital, allowed the Palestinians to gain self-government, but has not yet led to liberation from occupation, full statehood and peace.
One of the key participants in the Washington ceremony and the implementation of the agreements signed there, the foreign policy adviser to the President of Palestine Nabil Shaath recalls in an interview with RIA Novosti how he “in the name of peace ” persuaded Yasser Arafat to do without kissing, but did not even try to convince him to change his military jacket for a civilian jacket.
He explained how the current US President Donald Trump is trying to kill the peace process, and told whom to blame for the failure of the Palestinian-Israeli summit, which Moscow tried to organize on the sidelines of the World Cup 2018. – Today it is 25 years since the leaders of Palestine and Israel signed the Declaration of Principles in Washington and exchanged a historic handshake on the lawn at the White House.
Is this date a cause for celebration or mourning for the Middle East peace process, the Oslo process counting down from that ceremony?
© AFP 2018 / Nicholas Kamm The State Department called the condition for the resumption of the work of the Palestinian diplomatic mission in the United States - Mr. (US President Donald) Trump wants to stop this process, invent a new one and destroy everything that remains.
He is doing everything possible to destroy it.
But Oslo is with us, we are here — 6.4 million Palestinians in their homeland, and we believe in peace with the Israelis.
We offered the Israelis a mono-state solution — a single democratic, multi-confessional, multi-ethnic state with the separation of religion and state, but they do not want to.
Therefore, a two-state solution, two states living in peace with each other, is the only option.
There is no other alternative to Oslo, the process it has launched.
There are two peoples living on the land that has been ours for the last 1,500 years.
In our view, we have already recognized Israel, we are ready to live side by side with two States.
We have created state institutions, an independent economy.
Yes, surrounded by Israelis, dependent on them, controlled by them.
But this is the economy, state mechanisms, international relations, 138 countries that have already recognized our statehood.
Oslo can be corrected, it is too early to mourn.
Oslo ’ s path is not perfect, but it is not Oslo ’ s own mistakes.
They are made by the Israelis with the support of the Americans.
The United States is not putting enough pressure on Israel to comply with Oslo.
Mr. Trump should take Oslo from the intermediate stage to the final stage in order to get two states.
“President (Yasser) Arafat appointed me to lead these negotiations in Washington, but I was not actually in Oslo and was, like many, surprised by the agreements that were reached there.
I remember meeting with Abu Mazen (the pseudonym of the current president of Palestine, Mahmoud Abbas) and Abu Ammar, Mr. Arafat.
I have listed to them what, in my opinion, are the strengths and weaknesses of Oslo.
These shortcomings have actually become a real problem.
The issue of Jewish settlements had not been properly resolved, the status of Jerusalem had been postponed until final status negotiations and the final status itself had not been clearly spelled out.
These are the problems of Oslo, and they remain relevant to the peace process.
It was assumed that we would gain an independent state within a maximum of five years from the real launch of Oslo.
Time has passed and we are still in the middle.
That's what I warned you about.
Then I was appointed to oversee the first negotiations on the implementation of the Oslo Accords — the development of the so-called Gaza-Jericho agreement.
Oslo is principles, and I led the Palestinian delegations in Taba and Cairo, where the principles were transformed into applied arrangements that allowed the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Palestine Liberation Army to return to Gaza and Jericho, and from there to the rest of the West Bank, to complete the interim phase within two years and begin negotiations on a final settlement, which were supposed to be completed in five years.
That was the plan.
So I was very closely involved in the implementation of Oslo in Gaza and Jericho, then in the transfer of authority in the West Bank, followed by new negotiations in Washington, the negotiation of the Wye River and Camp David agreements.
Could you share an episode like this? – There was a story going on in Washington.
We were recognized by the United States, at least they recognized the PLO, the Palestine Liberation Organization, and Yasser Arafat, our leader, was equal to Yitzhak Rabin in presenting and signing the first bilateral agreement.
It allowed the return of the Palestinian leadership and the 9,000 members of the Palestine Liberation Army to become police forces in Gaza and Jericho, and then throughout the West Bank.
It paved the way for a settlement of the conflict.
It was a historic event.
I was there and in many ways served as an emissary between Arafat and (US President Bill) Clinton, between Arafat and Mr. Yitzhak Rabin, with whom I had established very good relations during the talks in Washington and Madrid.
© Photo: Public domain Yitzhak Rabin, Bill Clinton and Yasser Arafat, September 13, 1993.
Washington © Photo: Public domain Yitzhak Rabin, Bill Clinton and Yasser Arafat, September 13, 1993.
Washington There were many difficulties, different moments.
I'll tell you one case.
I get a call from President Clinton and he says, "I want to ask for the important concession that is necessary to ensure the success of this meeting." Okay, what are we talking about? "" Could you convince Mr. Arafat to wear a civilian jacket instead of a military jacket? "
We believe it is important to demonstrate a real transition from armed struggle to peace. "
I said I'm sorry, but I can't do it.
I had already tried when he came to the UN in 1974.
I arrived there in advance and prepared all the preparations for his performance.
Arafat replied, “No, because what matters is what you believe, not how you dress. ”
After that, he made his famous speech: “I came here with a revolutionary pistol in one hand and an olive branch of peace in the other.
Don't let the olive branch fall out of my hand. "
So I told Clinton that Arafat would not do it — that is the image of our people.
The president said, "Okay.
I'm going to ask you one more favor.
Could you ask him to do without kisses, hugs and just shake hands? "
I said, "It's very difficult, but for the sake of peace I will do it."
As a result, you can see Arafat shaking hands with Rabin and Clinton.
After this signing, Rabin came to me and asked if we could arrange a small meeting of the three of us, Arafat, he and I.
I asked Clinton to provide us with a room in the White House, and there the only thing Rabin Arafat asked for was to call King Hassan of Morocco, asking him to let the Israeli prime minister stay in Casablanca on the way from Washington to Tel Aviv and accept him officially.
Arafat said, "I think I can do it, but why do you need it?"
Rabin explained: “I want to show my people that the signing of peace with the Palestinians opens the gate to the Arab world for Israel, and this is my main incentive to strive for peace.
This is not just peace with you, but the road to peace with the Arab countries. ”
Arafat immediately called King Hassan and arranged for Rabin to be received in Casablanca.
These small episodes show how this meeting at the White House melted the ice and gave an opportunity to start the peace process.
I can say that Arafat and Rabin became committed to the peace process, and the assassination of Rabin dealt him the first real blow.
He was killed by extremist Jewish-Israelis who did not want to implement the Oslo Accords, did not want to stop settlement construction, did not want to develop relations that would lead to an independent Palestinian state living side by side with Israel.
I remember being informed of the murder, and I went to Arafat.
He was standing in his office next to a chair.
I said to him, "Abu Ammar, Rabin has just been attacked.
He is killed. "
And Arafat collapsed, collapsed on a chair.
He said to me, "Nabil, today the Oslo agreement is dead."
This can give you an idea of how important these two leaders were.
A few years later, the Israelis also killed Yasser Arafat.
Arafat ’ s death was another powerful blow to Oslo. — The ice that was melted in Washington 25 years ago now seems to have frozen again.
Do you think the Trump administration ’ s initiatives — recognizing Jerusalem as Israel ’ s capital, cutting aid to the Palestinians, shutting down your diplomatic mission in Washington — represent a long-term course of American policy, or will the situation return to normal with the change of president, by the time of Clinton or Barack Obama? — Mr. Trump is bad news for everyone in America and the rest of the world.
The balance of power has changed in the world, and he does not want to admit it.
He says he wants to make America great again, and no one doubts that America is a great country.
But the fact is that America is no longer the only great country in the world.
Putin ’ s Russia is not Yeltsin ’ s Russia of 1991.
Russia today is a great power in the world.
China is an economic giant.
Europe has become very important politically and technologically.
What is important is South Africa, which fought for independence for a long time, Brazil.
The world is changing, we are moving towards a multipolar world order, and Mr. Trump continues to make terrible mistakes because he believes that America can still rule the world alone.
It won't work that way.
That's why we rejected his plans, we rejected him.
We do not want the United States to be the sole curator of the peace process in the Middle East.
Our relations with other countries, with Russia, China and Europe, are based on international law, friendship, cooperation and a sincere desire to achieve peace.
© AP Photo / Andrew Harnik US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House © AP Photo / Andrew Harnik US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House © RIA Novosti / Vladimir Trefilov Go to the photo bank Palestine called the condition of US mediation in negotiations with Israel Mr. Trump has no plan.
Mr. Trump is simply giving Mr. (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu everything that deserves to be discussed in the format of the Oslo process.
He doesn't consult us when he talks about the deal of the century.
The deal involves two partners, otherwise it is not a deal.
He moved his embassy to Jerusalem and declared the city the capital of the Jewish people.
It halted allocations to UNRWA (the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East), saying that refugees had no right to return to Palestine.
He ordered the U.S. State Department not to use the word "occupied" in reference to the West Bank and Gaza.
He instructed this Haley, a woman who represents the United States at the United Nations, not to criticize the colonial settlement that the Israelis are engaged in.
He changed everything in favor of Israel, in favor of Netanyahu.
It has nothing to do with Palestine.
He seeks to bribe Mr. Netanyahu and pressure the Arabs so that Israelis and Arabs, especially the Arab Gulf states and Egypt, fight for him with Iran and contain Russia ’ s growing influence in Syria and other parts of the region.
It is a political game that will destroy the rights of the Palestinian people, a political game that cannot succeed.
That is why our president is very specific: "I want peace, I want peace on the basis of a two-state solution.
I remain committed to Oslo, and if we do something now, it will be with Russia, China, Europe, the United States, maybe other partners, not just the United States.
We do not exclude the United States, but we do not want the United States to exclude Russia, China, Europe.
I want the process to proceed on the basis of the Oslo Accords, the UN Charter, international law.
Then I will join the peace process, without it, I will not.
I will not participate in the process with this – I do not want to insult anyone – crazy policy, which Mr. Trump implements, regardless of us. ” – President Abbas is going to give a speech at the UN General Assembly, and, according to some publications, it may be accompanied by resonant statements.
They say, for example, that he will declare Palestine a state under occupation or say that the Oslo process is dead.
He will make it clear that we reject Mr. Trump ’ s plan and Mr. Trump ’ s policies.
Totally and unequivocally.
That we are ready to return only to the negotiating arena with many participants, guided by the Charter and UN resolutions, the agreements that we signed 25 years ago.
He'll make that very clear.
He is seeking recognition of Palestine as a member state of the United Nations.
We already have observer status, the next step requires the consent of the Security Council, which will be blocked by the United States.
But he'll ask for it.
He will ask again for international protection.
He will again raise the issue of punishing Israel for what it is doing against our people.
All this has already been said, but there will be another comprehensive statement in which our policy will be very clearly set out to the international community.
We want peace, but not such peace. — There were reports in the media that Russia proposed to organize a meeting between President Abbas and Prime Minister Netanyahu in Moscow on the sidelines of the World Cup.
The Palestinians are said to have been in favor, but the Israelis rejected the initiative.
Can you confirm that?
Russia is ready to participate in a possible meeting with Netanyahu and Abbas.
Russia has offered this twice, not only this time, but even earlier.
Mr Netanyahu said he was ready for the meeting while he thought Mr Abbas would not agree to it.
At the moment when Mr. Abbas accepted the offer, he (Netanyahu) began to justify himself by saying that “the time is not right now, ”“ I have domestic political problems, ” “maybe another time. ”
When Russia repeated the offer during the championship, he said no.
- Does President Abbas plan to visit Moscow again? - There are always such plans.
It's a matter of timing.
Our relationship with Russia has always been one of allies and friends.
We coordinate on all matters.
Together with Mr. (Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail) Bogdanov, I head the Russian-Palestinian Working Committee on the Middle East.
Sometimes it goes to the level of presidents Abbas and Putin, but on a permanent basis in this structure we co-chair with Mr. Bogdanov. — Is it fair to say that Ramallah prevented the achievement of agreements on a long-term truce in the Gaza Strip between Hamas and Israel? — Before that, there were three attempts to negotiate a ceasefire — in 2009, 2012 and 2014.
For a long time these agreements were not enough.
It is now a long - term process that can only be pursued by a single and independent Palestinian Government.
No one recognizes Hamas as a government of Palestine or Gaza.
There is separatism here.
Then you can not make an agreement, giving up a lot of things, including the airport, which will not be clear where, the sea harbor, which will be either in Sinai or in Cyprus.
What kind of agreement is this?
We insisted only on the need to initially agree on national unity.
When that happens, let ’ s negotiate with Israel.
In a situation of secession, separatism, this cannot be done, because the conditions in both cases will be worse. — The Egyptians, as the main mediators in the processes of resolving the situation in the Gaza Strip and inter-Palestinian reconciliation, agreed with your position? — Yes, the Egyptians have made it very clear that there will be no long-term agreements until national unity is achieved. — Now that the negotiations for a long-term truce are stopped, do you see the probability of a new war in the Gaza? - I don't know.
The Israelis are talking about war.
They have fought there three times.
Each time it led to destruction, the murder of innocent civilians and everything returned to normal.
If there is a war, it will be for domestic Israeli reasons.
I don't know if the Israelis want to fight again or not.
The war will not change anything, only increase the suffering of Gaza, increase instability in the Middle East, where Mr. Trump will do even worse things with the peace process.
We are against war, we are committed to peaceful resistance and international legitimacy.

title: Leyla Aliyeva: Through work, hope, faith, patience and love, we will be able to solve all problems and create a brighter future
text:
Baku.
28 October.
REPORT.AZ / An event dedicated to World Food Day was held at the Heydar Aliyev Center on October 27.
The event was organized jointly by the IDEA Public Association, the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations – FAO.
Vice-president of the Heydar Aliyev Foundation, founder and head of IDEA Public Association, FAO Goodwill Ambassador Leyla Aliyeva attended the event.
In her speech, Leyla Aliyeva noted that the current event is a great opportunity to draw the world ’ s attention to such challenges as hunger and food security.
Touching upon the theme of this year ’ s Food Day, Leyla Aliyeva stressed that as FAO Goodwill Ambassador and tireless environmental activist, and most importantly, a resident of the planet, she is very sensitive to this issue.
“In connection with the new realities of a changing climate, we must radically change the ways of food production and consumption, ” Leyla Aliyeva said and stressed the importance of the Paris Climate Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
“If we want to ensure the food security of a gradually increasing world population, we must achieve sustainable, fruitful and lasting development in agriculture, ” said the head of the IDEA Public Association.
She noted that climate change had the greatest impact on the ecosystem and rural populations.
Leyla Aliyeva noted the importance in this sense of promoting the FAO concept of climate-smart agriculture around the world in order to change agricultural systems and give them a new orientation.
Leyla Aliyeva spoke about the activities of the IDEA Public Association headed by her, the measures taken over the past five years, and informed about a new project of special importance for food security and environmental protection.
“Thanks to our efforts to contribute to the revitalization of the marine environment and to assist dependent rural communities, IDEA recently launched a project to comprehensively clean up the Kura Delta.
What is the importance of this project?
First of all, I would like to emphasize that starting from our western borders, Kura overcomes about a thousand kilometers to the Caspian Sea, and is very important for the lives of people living on the coast of this river.
In addition, Kura is the main breeding area of sturgeon, the most ancient and unique species of fish in the Caspian Sea, ” said Vice-president of the Heydar Aliyev Foundation.
Saying that the new project is aimed at increasing fish resources, water quality and improving the ecology in general, which will be very beneficial for the environment and the local population, the Vice-president of the Heydar Aliyev Foundation stressed that the number of people suffering from lack of food is higher than those who die from diseases such as AIDS, malaria and tuberculosis.
“Through work, hope, faith, patience and love, we will be able to solve all problems and create a brighter future, ” Leyla Aliyeva concluded.
Touching upon the significance of the event, Minister of Ecology and Natural Resources Huseyngulu Bagirov stressed that today everyone is concerned about the issues of climate change and food security.
The minister said that climate change is causing the greatest damage to the agricultural sector, noted that thanks to investments made in recent years, water resources have increased in our country, spoke about the work to prevent environmental pollution, stressed that as a result of the use of alternative energy and the campaign to plant trees in Azerbaijan, the territories of forest plots have been much expanded.
The Minister said that the amount of harmful gases emitted into the atmosphere has decreased significantly.
Four wind and four solar power plants were installed.
Our goal is to produce 25 percent of our energy from alternative sources in the future.
G. Bagirov brought to attention that over the past 15 years, more than 100 million trees have been planted in our country on an area of ​ ​ 144 thousand hectares.
Melek Chakmak, Head of the FAO Partnership and Coordination Office in Azerbaijan, spoke about the history and mission of the structure she represents.
She stressed that without solving the problems arising from climate change, it is impossible to defeat poverty and hunger.
It is important to join forces on this issue.
She said the world ’ s population is expected to reach 9.6 billion by 2050.
In this regard, FAO believes that until 2050, agricultural production should increase by 60 percent.
Climate change may be one of the biggest challenges.
The theme for this year ’ s World Food Day is “Climate is changing: food and agriculture must change ”.
177 countries have signed the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.
At the same time, to completely eliminate hunger in the world, the target year is set for 2030.
This was followed by a video message from FAO Director José Graziano da Silva on World Food Day.
The event continued with panel discussions on the theme “Climate change, food security and small family farms ”.
The panel session, chaired by Deputy Minister of Agriculture Seyfaddin Talybov, was attended by representatives of the ministries of ecology and natural resources, agriculture, ADA University and FAO.
The discussions covered the impact of climate change on food security, small family households, the identification of difficulties in combating the negative effects of climate change by the state, civil society and other stakeholders, the identification of opportunities and topics for expanding cooperation with FAO and other key stakeholders, etc.

title: Meteorologists have determined how the climate of Belarus will change in the coming decades
text:
September 20, Minsk / Corr.
BELTA /.
Meteorologists have determined how the climate of Belarus will change in the coming decades.
This is stated in the analytical note "Agroclimatic zoning of the territory of Belarus taking into account climate change", which is posted on the website of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection, BelTA has learned.
Experts systematized information on climatic and agro-climatic conditions in Belarus for the period from 1989 to 2015.
According to meteorologists, since 1989 Belarus has begun the longest period of warming for the entire time of instrumental observations over the past almost 130 years.
For the period from 1989 to 2015, the average annual air temperature in Belarus exceeded the climatic norm by 1.3 degrees.
In 2015, the average annual air temperature was plus 8.5 degrees, which is 2.7 degrees above the climatic norm, and was the highest for the entire observation period.
As a result of warming in Belarus, the borders of agro-climatic zones have changed.
The northern agroclimatic region has disintegrated, and a new, warmer zone has been formed in the south of Polesie.
Now the territory of Belarus is divided into four agro-climatic regions: northern, central, southern and new.
Studies show that the trend of climate change towards warming in the coming decades will continue.
Researchers have studied several climate models to predict climate change.
The authors consider two scenarios: average anthropogenic radiation exposure and severe.
The second scenario is considered unlikely.
According to the first scenario, the duration of the warm period with the sum of air temperatures above zero by 2041-2060 will increase by an average of 35 days and will range from 280 to 310 days.
“And in the extreme south-west in the Brest region, the average duration of such a period will be 365 days, that is, there will be no winter, ” the document says.
Average temperatures at different times of the year will increase by 1.6-2.4 degrees.
A slight increase in rainfall is expected in autumn and winter.
In spring and summer, their number will practically not change, but the moisture supply of crops in the summer will decrease due to an increase in air temperature.
The hard scenario assumes an increase in the warm period with the sum of air temperatures above zero by 2041-2060 by 54 days.
Average temperatures at different times of the year will increase by 2.3-3.1 degrees.
In this case, in the summer, due to high temperatures and lack of moisture, the aridity of the territory will increase, which will require changes in the technology of cultivation of a number of crops.
In the coming decades, new changes in the boundaries of agro-climatic zones are expected in Belarus. "The central agro-climatic region will actually disintegrate by 2030, and its place will be taken by the former southern region.
At the same time, almost throughout the territory of Belarus, it will be possible to cultivate corn for grain and sunflower.
The new agro-climatic region will move far north and take the place of the southern, and even warmer agro-climatic regions will appear in the south of the country, ” the analytical note says.
A significant change in the conditions of growing crops will require adjustments in agricultural practices and taking into account when developing a strategy for the development of agricultural production.
In some areas on the territory of Belarus there may be more favorable conditions for agriculture (in particular, crop production) in terms of heat supply.
Increased productivity can be achieved through the introduction and expansion of more thermophilic and more productive crops.
At the same time, the indicators of soil moisture supply are expected to deteriorate and the risk of droughts will increase.
Meteorologists note that farmers will need to adapt to both the positive and negative effects of climate change.

title: Five ways to contribute to the fight against global warming
text:
Scientists say that climate warming primarily affects high latitudes, mainly the Arctic Data presented this week by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) indicate that the increase in average air temperature on our planet may by 2040 exceed a threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius compared to pre-industrial era levels.
According to experts, this could lead to an increase in extreme weather events - droughts, forest fires and floods, as well as food shortages that will affect the fate of hundreds of millions of people around the world.
The IPCC report states that if the world is to avoid exceeding this threshold, rapid, far-reaching and unprecedented changes are needed in all aspects of human society.
What can I do for that?
Rightholder illustration Getty Images Image caption Save water as you can, environmentalists call “There are many measures based on common sense, ” says lead author and coordinator of the IPCC report Aromar Revy, a specialist in urbanization and sustainable development.
"Citizens and consumers will be critical actors in the upcoming effort to contain the pace of global warming," he said.
Here are five things that everyone can change in their lives today to contribute to international efforts to curb the forces of nature.
The right holder of the illustration Getty Images Image caption How developed is public transport in your city?
The choice of means of transportation in the city has a noticeable impact on the level of greenhouse gas emissions.
You can give up your personal car in favor of walking, cycling or public transport.
Dr Debra Roberts, one of the co-chairs of the IPCC, said: “If you don ’ t have public transport, you as a voter can step in and give your vote to the politicians who advocate for its development. ”
Riding a bicycle is a healthy and eco-friendly way to travel in an increasingly warm climate If you have no choice but to use a car, opt for electric cars and go on long journeys by train rather than by plane.
Give up the next business trip and replace it with a video conference.
The right holder of the illustration Getty Images Image caption It is not only about switching to alternative energy sources, but about reducing energy use in general Dry laundry on a rope, and not in an electric dryer.
Set a lower switching temperature on the thermostat of the heating system.
Install thermal insulation in the attic and under the roof to reduce heat loss in winter.
When buying electrical appliances, pay attention to the energy consumption figures Disconnect electrical appliances that you do not use.
Consider installing energy-saving systems, such as a solar water heater.
These measures may seem trivial, but they can actually save a lot of energy.
Eat more vegetables and locally produced products Meat production entails significantly larger greenhouse gas emissions than chicken production, growing vegetables, fruits and grains.
At the Paris Summit, 119 countries pledged to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the agricultural sector.
However, it was not specified exactly how they intend to achieve this goal.
But you can do a lot personally.
Reduce meat consumption in favor of fruits and vegetables.
If this is difficult to achieve, try not to eat meat once a week.
It is also necessary to reduce the consumption of dairy products, the production and transportation of which is accompanied by significant emissions of coal gas.
Try to buy local and seasonal food and reduce the amount of food thrown away.
Dispose of waste, use of recyclables, even water Rightholder illustrations Getty Images Image caption Water also needs to be saved We are constantly talking about the importance of collecting household waste.
But the transportation and processing of such waste is accompanied by the release of large amounts of CO2 into the atmosphere.
Recycling reduces energy consumption, but it would be even better to reuse products or reduce consumption.
The same applies to water consumption.
"We have to conserve and regenerate water, while at the same time attracting more people to collect rainwater," says Aromar Revi.
To inform and train the Rightholder of the illustration Getty Images Image caption Training in resource saving measures should begin at an early age It is necessary to disseminate as widely as possible knowledge about climate change and what they carry with them.
Create community groups to implement sustainable management practices at the local level.
Create interest groups for the purpose of joint operation of garden equipment.
“All these measures, if used by billions of people every day, will ensure sustainable development and almost no impact on the standard of living of the population, ” said Aromar Revi.
