title: The world ’ s largest aircraft is preparing for its first flight
text:
Stratolaunch was created as an aerial platform for launching Pegasus XL launch vehicles designed to launch satellites into orbit.
It is a structure of two 72-meter fuselages connected by a common wing with a length of 117 meters.
The aircraft is powered by six Pratt & Whitney engines.
The weight of the aircraft is 250 tons, with a full load - about 590 tons.
Movement on the runway is provided by a 28-wheel landing gear.
It is assumed that at the first stage the aircraft will carry one missile, in the future - up to three missiles fixed in the lower part of the fuselage.
After reaching a predetermined altitude - about 9 thousand meters - the rocket will be dropped, then its engine will turn on, after which the carrier will put the satellite into orbit.
The test run took place on the runway of the airfield in the Mojave Desert (California).
During the run, the plane accelerated to about 128 km / h, while in previous taxiing tests held a few months ago, Stratolaunch developed a speed of up to 74 km / h.
The company Stratolaunch Systems, which owns the aircraft, expect that its first flight will take place in the near future.
Before that, it is planned to conduct several more similar steering tests, increasing the speed of the run.
Initially, the first flight of the Stratolaunch was planned for the summer of this year, but it had to be postponed.

title: Medicine of South Korea: high technology and qualified doctors
text:
Photos provided by the National Tourism Organization of Korea The American Agency for Financial and Economic Information Bloomberg has determined the rating of the effectiveness of the health care system of the countries of the world, in which South Korea was in fourth place.
What allowed her to soar so high, competing with recognized “medical ” powers, and what can expect Russian tourists going to Korea for treatment – in the material Sib.fm.
Since 2009, the government has been developing medical tourism in Korea, with foreign patients being treated in the same clinics as the local population.
Priority areas are diagnostics and treatment of oncology, radiology, gynecology and oncogynecology, plastic surgery, therapeutic treatment of spine diseases using both modern and traditional medicine, urology, arthroplasty, ophthalmology.
The equipment of the Clinic in Korea is a non-profit organization.
The profit of medical institutions is not taxed, but it is allowed to spend only on the development of the hospital - reconstruction, repair, purchase of new equipment, expansion of staff, bonuses to qualified specialists.
Is it any wonder that in Korean hospitals you will not see the walls with peeled paint?
According to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (US government agency), 10 years ago, the number of MRI equipment per million inhabitants in South Korea was more than in Belgium, Canada, France.
In terms of the number of CT installations per million inhabitants, South Korea overtook France, Italy, Austria and Canada.
Korean news portal www.newsis.com published the report of the Health Committee of the National Assembly of Korea.
In the calculation for every million inhabitants of the country there are thirty-seven installations for CT, 24 for MRI, four for PET (PET - positron emission tomography, a diagnostic method necessary to detect metastasis in some types of oncology, as well as used for patients with epilepsy, strokes, Alzheimer's disease).
For comparison, in Russia with almost 150 million population there are 53 installations for PET.
In Korea, most general clinics are equipped with this equipment.
In 2016, 30 clinics in South Korea were accredited according to the world "gold standard" of quality of medical services by JCI.
In our country, three organizations that receive and maintain JCI accreditation provide patients with the best possible level of care today.
It is not easy to become a practicing doctor in Korea.
Medical students study for 9-12 years.
then they practice in clinics in Korea, Europe and the USA.
But patients can be sure that there are no random people in Korean medicine.
The income of an ordinary doctor is $5,000 per month, a high-class surgeon receives 20,000, the salaries of highly qualified narrow specialists in the top of the income rating in Korea.
There is competition between doctors in the country and in order to withstand it, specialists must constantly improve their skills at home and abroad.
The main directions of medical tourism in Korea are oncology, neurosurgery, endoprosthetics, plastic surgery.
Korea ranks first in the world for five-year survival after treatment for many types of cancer (five-year survival is a generally accepted indicator of the effectiveness of treatment), as well as for thirty-day survival after stroke.
The total number of tomographs involved in private and public clinics in Russia is estimated at about 3-4 thousand devices, and the cost of Russians for such studies is 15 billion rubles a year or about 3% of the entire private market of medical services Operations in Korean clinics are usually performed in a minimally invasive way, that is, providing less interference in the body, without significant damage to soft tissues.
This reduces the rehabilitation time to a few days.
Robotic surgeons "Da Vinci" is equipped with most of the multidisciplinary clinics.
For the treatment of oncology here are widely used "Cyber Knife", "Gamma Knife" and the system for accurate radiation therapy RapidArc.
Examination to be examined if "nothing hurts"?
Many diseases, including oncology, are often asymptomatic.
In Korea, a complete check-up examination of the body has become commonplace over the past ten years.
You can pass such a survey here in half a day, and the results of the survey will be ready in a week.
If the examination revealed pathologies that require treatment, then patients will be offered to start it in the coming days.
Check-up programs are formed depending on the wishes and needs of the patient.
This can be, for example, a male or female detailed examination, examination of the heart, digestive system, brain, a couple about to become parents, and so on.
The cost of check-up ranges from several tens of thousands of dollars to several hundred depending on the program.
A woman ’ s examination is usually more expensive because it requires more tests.
Before treating foreigners, Korean clinics must pass state accreditation, acquire an international department and translators.
Foreign patients can be treated by doctors with at least 15 years of experience.
Clinics that have received the right to receive foreign patients, as a rule, open their representative offices in foreign countries.
The patient only needs to contact the consultant in his country, send him the results of the examinations and discuss his wishes, including the volume of procedures and cost.
Within a period of one to seven days, the patient receives a preliminary medical opinion from the clinics, a planned treatment program, where the need for surgery and the cost of treatment are stipulated.
When the program is agreed, the patient is issued a call from the hospital.
At the airport of Korea, he is met by an employee of the clinic and an interpreter, taken to the clinic, helped with the settlement.
Russian patients can stay in Korea without a visa for two months, and if the treatment is longer, the clinic ’ s curator helps to draw up the necessary documents.
The cost of treatment depends on the level of the medical institution.
The third, the highest, level is clinics where the most experienced doctors work, conduct scientific research and introduce advanced methods.
The second level is clinics, multidisciplinary hospitals.
The first level is polyclinics and separate medical offices.
Treatment in Korea, even in clinics in Seoul, will cost the patient cheaper than in Europe, Israel or the United States.
The difference in prices is from 10 to 50%.
In addition, you do not have to pay for the services of an interpreter - if in Europe it costs 50 euros per hour of work, then in Korea the interpreter works for free with patients.
“Treatment center abroad ” is a highly specialized company.
Today it is the only company in Novosibirsk and the region, engaged exclusively in the organization of all types of examinations, treatment, plastic surgery and cosmetic procedures abroad.
By contacting the company until December 31, 2018, you can get a discount of up to 30% on complex and additional examinations.
Attention residents of Novosibirsk!
On November 16, the event “Medical Tourism in South Korea ” will be held, where every resident of Novosibirsk can come and get acquainted with medicine in South Korea, ask questions and get advice from Korean doctors, as well as take memorable photos and participate in traditional Korean master classes.
The event will be held at the address: Aura shopping center, Voennaya street, 5, Novosibirsk, from 15: 00 to 20: 00.
The material was prepared with the support of the Korean National Tourism Organization.
Elena Klimova Journalist Author

title: "No corset." Korean women have decided to break the standards of beauty
text:
As Seoul turns into a world center of beauty and plastic surgery, protests of women from South Korea are gaining momentum on the Internet.
Activists oppose makeup and plastic surgery, and the “No Corset ” movement is growing in local social networks.
In June, South Korean blogger Lina Bae posted a video on YouTube titled “I ’ m ugly. ”
The first half of the video resembles a regular beauty blog, where a girl applies makeup.
But instead of the standard beauty blog subtitles, which explain which cosmetics are better to use, the girl included comments from Internet users, which she often receives: "You can look attractive if you try", "You need a foundation!", "You need a plastic surgery!", etc.
In the second half of the video, Lina, tired of being judged, takes off her makeup and says, “I ’ m ugly.
But that's normal.
Don ’ t be what others are trying to make you.
Look for your own colors. ”
The video received five million views.
Other South Koreans followed.
The girls began to post photos of how they remove makeup and throw out cosmetics.
Flashmob has turned into a movement called "Without corset" and stands for natural beauty.
Immediately remembered the artist and photographer Ji Yo.
For several years, she has been posting photos of Korean girls immediately after plastic surgery and arranging performances.
The artist goes outside with a sign “I want to be perfect ” and invites passers-by to mark the place on her body with a marker that needs to be changed with plastic surgery.
South Korea ranks first in the world in the number of plastic surgeries per capita (Russia is in 23rd place).
According to one source, one in three women in South Korea between the ages of 19 and 29 had plastic surgery, and one in two.
The place of power of plastic surgeons is located in the Seoul district of Gangnam, where there are more than four hundred clinics (it was about this area that the South Korean rapper PSY sang in the song Gangnam Style).
Image copyright JUNG YEON-JE / AFP / Getty Images Image caption Gangnam Medical centers attract not only local residents, but also beauty tourists from around the world.
Plastic surgery in South Korea is most interested in residents of China, the United States, Australia and Japan.
Among those who come to Seoul for plastic surgery, there are also Russians.
According to the company "Kogan tour", which carries out trips to plastic clinics in Korea, customers from Russia are mainly women from 20 to 70 years old, with an income significantly above the average, as a rule, residents of large megacities, as well as some cities of Primorsky Krai (Yakutsk and Khabarovsk).
Many clinics have a Russian menu and translators.
According to doctors, clients from Russia, as a rule, do not dare to drastic changes in appearance, and are limited to anti-aging operations and rhinoplasty (correction of congenital or acquired deformities of the nose).
Unlike Russian women, South Koreans often resort to plastic surgery with the intention of seriously changing their appearance.
In addition to the traditional for many Asian countries fair skin, small nose and wide eyes, South Korea has its own unique and extremely strict requirements for female beauty.
First of all, it's the oval face.
It should be perfect and B-shaped in the lower part, so it is often possible to see advertisements for operations on the lower jaw.
Secondly, the Korean beauty trend is straight eyebrows.
Doctors surgically remove the curvature of the eyebrows and transplant new hair to new eyebrows.
It's called an eyebrow transplant.
Surgeons also correct the forehead - it should not be flat.
With the help of injections, doctors pump liquid there, giving the forehead volume.
The advertisement says that the updated forehead will help women become sexier.
Doctors also add bags under the eyes to patients.
The procedure forms a layer of skin under the eyelids, due to which the eyes appear larger than they actually are.
As in many other Asian countries, in South Korea, the harmony of the figure is highly appreciated.
And we are talking not only about reducing the hips or creating a thin waist, but also about changing the shape of the calves, for example.
Calf reduction operations are one of the most popular in South Korea.
“It ’ s very hard to imagine for a Western person.
But here no one discusses the appropriateness of plastic surgery.
If you have made plastic and began to look better, everyone congratulates you without hesitation.
Colleagues or classmates will rejoice as much as in the Western world they compliment their clothes or their hair, and say, "Great operation, it suits you very well."
And relatives will celebrate this event as if the girl entered a prestigious university, ” said Chen Tian De, a student from China who studied in South Korea.
Plastic surgery in South Korea is not only a desire to look better, but also an opportunity to find a job.
Employers often look closely not only at education and work experience, but also at the appearance of the candidate.
Many parents give their children surgery as a birthday gift or graduation from school and university.
Plastic clinics often organize actions for schoolchildren and students.
For example, if several students of the same class come to a plastic surgeon, they have a high chance of getting a discount.
Speaking of beauty standards in South Korea, it is necessary to mention not only plastic surgery, but also makeup.
The beauty market of South Korea is estimated at more than $13 billion and is among the top ten global beauty markets.
Judging by the growth rate, Seoul will soon be able to compete with Paris and Tokyo for the title of the world's main cosmetic center.
The copyright holder of the illustration Chung Sung-Jun / Getty Images Lipstick and foundation with the effect of protection from the sun begin to use even preschoolers, and to come without makeup to the university or to work - it means to show disrespect to colleagues.
“It ’ s a kind of social contract.
That's how you show respect for people.
In schools and universities, makeup for a girl is like a mandatory additional homework.
I hardly use makeup.
And when I was in Korea, I had to paint.
When I did it for the first time, not only the students, but also the teachers noted that I did well, and I did the right thing to finally put on my makeup, ” another student from China, Yichin, told the BBC.
In addition to the primacy in plastic surgery and cosmetics, South Korea is a leader in the speed and spread of the Internet in the world.
Almost every home in South Korea has internet access.
“People who spend a lot of time on the Internet and do not fit into the generally accepted norms of their country, see that in other places there is an alternative way of life.
As a result, they change the idea of ​ ​ social norms, and they begin to do things that are not accepted in their culture, ” says Olga Gulevich, Doctor of Psychological Sciences, Professor at the Higher School of Economics.
Image copyright holder JUNG YEON-JE / AFP / Getty Images For six months of active protests, the # MeToo movement in South Korea began to undergo small changes.
“I have lived here for 2.5 years.
When I first came here, it was almost impossible to see a girl without makeup on the street.
Now I began to notice that some girls and women really stopped using bright makeup and without hesitation go outside, ” says a resident of Seoul Anastasia.
However, it is unlikely that activists will be able to resist the billion-dollar industry in the near future.
Under the influence of numerous complaints, the administration of the Seoul subway promises to ban advertising plastic surgery at stations and on subway trains.
However, it will be possible to do this only after 2022 - contracts for advertising plastic clinics for the next three to four years have already been concluded.

title: Say yes to treatment in South Korea
text:
TODAY 04: 10 2018-10-31T04: 53: 42 + 03: 00 Three answers to the question of why you need a medical tour to the Land of Morning Freshness Resize the text: A A Medical tourism is a concept that has rapidly burst into our lives and has quickly become popular.
And among the directions that our compatriots choose, it was South Korea that took a leading position in Asia.
Why should this country receive priority when choosing travel for health and beauty?
We are ready to give answers to those who want to know everything and even a little more about Korean medicine.
The answer is No1.
High quality medicine and state control.
This criterion thousands of Russians called the priority and main when choosing a foreign medical tour.
"The quality of medical diagnostics, treatment, rehabilitation and aesthetic medicine in Korean clinics is not inferior to the world!" - reviews of those who were treated not only in Korea, but also in other countries.
But the choice was made in favor of the Country of morning freshness.

South Korea ranks second after Switzerland in terms of medical equipment.
We add to this the presence of mandatory international accreditation of JCI as a prerequisite for the implementation of activities for clinics in the country.
And in order to receive it, the hospital must meet the standards of quality of medical services, staff qualifications and patient safety.
The country has very strict state control over the quality of medical services.
Not everyone knows that today South Korea came out on the first place in the world in terms of the amount of state budget financing for health care.
It was Korea that initiated the International Award “MedicalAsia ”, which for more than 10 years has the status of the main medical event of the Asia-Pacific countries.

The exchange of experience, the search for modern directions in medical tourism, new approaches and practices - all this will be the topic of meetings of leading players in the world market of medical and pharmaceutical services, authoritative scientists and specialists from Europe, the United States and Asia.
The opening will take place on November 1 this year in Seoul, the capital of Korea.
On this day, the whole country will learn the names of the best medical centers and clinics, pharmaceutical companies and government agencies that are engaged in medical tourism, the Doctor of the Year 2018 will be named.
We began to get acquainted with the medicine of Korea, promising to give three answers as the three main advantages of medical tourism.
Continuing the review.
The answer is No2.
A doctor in Korea is more than a doctor.

The competition for medical universities is the highest in the world.
Medical students have been studying for more than 10 years, they are required to regularly attend international seminars and conferences in order to keep abreast of modern medical achievements.
About 30% become therapists, the rest - narrow specialists.
At the stage of training, the selection of the best specialists is very strict, so less than 10% of all students of medical universities become doctors.
No less high requirements for the average medical staff.
Answer No 3.
Treatment in Korea is beneficial.
Don't be surprised, it's true.

title: How the Altai Territory intends to become the capital of medical tourism
text:
Foreigners began to come more often to be treated in the Altai Territory.
Tourists are attracted by low prices for services and affordable medicine.
Moscow experts believe that the region can become a leader in medical tourism.
However, it is necessary to solve a number of problems for which serious financial investments are required.
Why Altai Medical Tourism?
According to the regional department of tourism, only in the first 6 months of 2018, 5 thousand medical tourists came to the Altai Territory.
Of these, 50% are residents of the regions of Russia, the second half are foreigners.
This is less than 1% (0.65%) of the total number of tourists in the region - for the first six months in the region, according to official data, 800 thousand people visited.
But the authorities are convinced that medical tourism will increase tourist flow and solve the problem of seasonality.
Elena Evsyukova, acting deputy head of the regional department for tourism: The sharply continental climate imposes its restrictions on the development of tourism.
Three summer months form 50% of the tourist flow in the region.
But in the sanatorium-resort direction, seasonality is not so pronounced.
Therefore, medical tourism will allow to level seasonal fluctuations and increase the length of stay of tourists in the region.
In addition, the more tourists will come to Altai, the more money they will leave here, according to the department.
Nature of Altai. Mountains.
Anna Zaykova Why Altai?
In the region, three medical areas are in high demand among tourists - cosmetology, dentistry and diagnostics.
In cosmetology, tourists are popular with injection procedures on the face, blepharoplasty (surgery to change the shape of the eyelids, eye incision), surgical correction of age-related changes in the face, breast augmentation and others.
Medical tourists also turn to the diagnostic center.
They show great interest in checkups (from the English check up - to check - approx. ed.) - these are short-term survey programs.
For example, if a person is worried about headaches, and he wants to find the cause, then he chooses the appropriate complex for this, for one to three days, doctors determine what is with him and prescribe the appropriate treatment.
Tatyana Smyshlyaeva, Deputy Chief Physician for the outpatient section of the Diagnostic Center of the Altai Territory: For example, a person has pain in the chest.
He does not know where to turn - to a neurologist, cardiologist, pulmonologist or some other specialist.
We help him understand the problem, accompany the patient.
As a result, he is undergoing an examination that is right for him.
Some tourists come with specific problems - to clarify the diagnosis or to carry out an operation.
Residents of Russian regions and other countries also travel to the Altai Territory to treat their teeth.
In recent years, tourists have become more interested in blich-restoration (white teeth), said the chief doctor of the dental clinic "Albus" Alexander Elashkin.
They are also treated with problems in the temporomandibular joint.
This direction is in demand, but not so few such clinics, many are ready to go from afar to Barnaul.
Dentist.
Dental treatment.
According to the authorities, there is everything necessary for the development of medical tourism in the region - a medical cluster has been created, modern technologies and equipment are used in treatment, qualified personnel work in hospitals.
However, tourists and representatives of medical centers and clinics say that in the region to be treated is simply cheaper.
In Altai, in cosmetology, the optimal ratio of price and quality, noted in the clinic "Anthurium".
According to her, the cost of plastic surgery in Barnaul is three times less than in Moscow, and two times less than in Novosibirsk.
For example, the average price in Barnaul for blepharoplasty is 50 thousand rubles, in Moscow - about 100 thousand rubles.
Plastic belly here can be done for 50-65 thousand rubles, and in the capital, the price tag starts from 150 thousand rubles.
It is cheaper to treat or “make ” teeth in Barnaul, because clinics do not overestimate the price tag, they explain in local medical institutions.
Therefore, dental services in the region are sometimes 3-5 times cheaper than in some other regions.
In addition to the low price for a comprehensive diagnosis of the body, tourists are also attracted by the availability of the service - you can get it literally in a day.
Therefore, this type of survey is popular among those who briefly stop in Barnaul, before going to Gorny Altai or Belokurikha. Tourism.
Travels.
The main part of foreign tourists are former compatriots who at one time left the Altai Territory, but continue to be treated in the “small homeland ”.
Some of them bring foreigners with them, said Tatyana Tatyanina, managing the clinic of aesthetic medicine "Anthurium".
However, word of mouth cannot give a large flow of tourists to the region.
An important condition for attracting foreign medical tourists is the presence of international certificates at medical institutions.
They are needed to work through medical agencies in Europe, which could promote Altai clinics.
However, the passage of such certifications require “serious ” financial costs, said Konstantin Nedoseko, deputy chief physician of the regional clinical hospital.
To obtain the international JCI certificate (standard of quality and safety of medical activities), it is required to improve the level of service and management in the institution, to make sure that the premises meet the specified level, notes Tatyana Smyshlyaeva.
The lack of international certificates also prevents travel agencies from working with service companies that can promote clinics to foreign markets, notes Lyudmila Ivanova, head of the travel agency "Friday".
Their agency is interested in working with medical tourists, even there were attempts, but unsuccessful.
Lyudmila Ivanova, head of the travel agency "Friday": A year ago, we were approached from abroad to conduct an oncological operation.
It was difficult to work with clinics, because they told us that they accept patients on a first-come, first-served basis and they do not have any privileges for foreign clients.
At that time, we were forced to refuse the client because we could not offer a suitable service.
So far, the situation has not changed, but the problems have already begun to be solved.
To do this, a working group was created in the region, which includes a lawyer, travel agents, representatives of medical institutions.
They will study foreign experience, decide which contracts should be made by agents working in the field of medical tourism, which responsibility should be borne by the clinic, and which travel agency.
Therefore, medical permits to Altai will appear no earlier than 2019.
What can be done now Altai medical tourism is actively interested in Moscow companies.
Tatyana Sokolov, head of MedicaTour agency, believes that the potential of the region is high, it can be promoted, but for this it is still necessary to determine the priority areas.
Tatyana Sokolov, head of MedicaTour (Moscow): Recently, we signed a contract with a Swiss company, they provide us with tourists for therapeutic fasting on Lake Baikal.
I know that in Altai there is also a program of such starvation.
This is as one of the options for which medical tourists can come to Altai. Doctor. Patient.
According to Vadim Prasov, Vice-President of the Federation of Restaurateurs and Hoteliers of Russia, it is worth focusing on Russians: it is a good time for this – compatriots are interested in treatment at home.
Sergey Khitrov, Head of RosBusinessConsulting Group.
Market Research ” (Moscow): Until 2014, about 1% of Russians went abroad for medical care every year.
That ’ s about 1 million people.
Now this figure has halved and amounted to 0.5% (500-600 thousand people).
It turns out that the economic crisis has led to the fact that Russians are now more actively considering proposals for treatment within the country.
If the medicine in our clinics is all right, then the service leaves much to be desired.
Therefore, first of all, medical institutions should “turn ” to the client, believes Nadezhda Fedulova, head of D-ZERTS Medical Consulting, an expert in the opening, management and automation of business processes in medical centers (Moscow).
This will help to compete with neighboring Siberian regions, which “step on the heels ” of Altai medical tourism.
In the Novosibirsk region, according to six medical institutions, in 2017 visited more than 17 thousand medical tourists.
According to Tatiana Smyshlyaeva, they are already creating competition to the region, so it ’ s time to take action to catch up or overtake the “neighbors ”.
However, in the department of tourism, competitors from the Siberian regions are not seen.
On the contrary, the end can begin to cooperate with them.
Elena Evsyukova, Acting Deputy Head of the Regional Department for Tourism: We discussed with our colleagues from Novosibirsk that the medical tourism market is only being formed and its potential is huge.
Therefore, in principle, the regions of the SFO have enough customers, there is no sense in competition
Here, on the contrary, it is necessary to unite and jointly move to the foreign market, complementing each other.

title: Reduction of water resources of Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030
text:
Astana.
7 November.
KazTAG – The reduction of water resources in Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030, the press service of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports.
“Among the threats posed by climate change to Kazakhstan ’ s agricultural sector is water scarcity, which is projected to be reduced by 25% by 2030, putting additional strain on the sector and leading to even greater aridity, especially in the southern and central regions of Kazakhstan, ” FAO said on Wednesday.
Another expected impact of climate change in the organization called the drying of pastures and reduced access of livestock to water sources.
“Changes in weather cycles can also cause spring floods, torrential autumn rains and early frosts, leading to crop losses.
That is, strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector to such phenomena through targeted investments that contribute to reducing vulnerability both within the country and in individual regions is an urgent task, ” the UN agricultural organization stressed.
FAO stressed that now the task of adapting to a changing climate is one of the key priorities in the world.
Climate change, including disruption of rain cycles, droughts, floods, and the spread of pests and diseases, according to the organization, both directly and indirectly affect agricultural productivity.
“Accelerating the adoption of climate technologies is a significant step towards addressing these challenges.
The use of modern climate technologies is a key element in the transition to more sustainable food production systems, ” said Nuno Santos, economist at the FAO Investment Centre.
In close cooperation with local governments, FAO and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) organized the workshop to serve as a platform for dialogue among all stakeholders – the private sector, government agencies, research institutions, international organizations and civil society.
“All of them can play a role in supporting the implementation of climate technologies in Kazakhstan, ” the report said.
The participants of the seminar, according to FAO, noted the key trends in the implementation of climate technologies in the agri-food sector of Kazakhstan and focused on identifying problems and opportunities for private sector investment in modern agri-food technologies.
“The participants also shared their experience and made proposals to overcome difficulties and create a favorable climate for private investment.
The workshop also discussed possible areas for public support and collaboration with donors and international financial institutions to accelerate technology adoption, as strategic alliances and close collaboration among stakeholders are key to achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030.

title: Half of the world ’ s annual rainfall now falls in an average of 12 days
text:
Meteorologists have described a new climate trend that has persisted for almost 20 years.
Its essence lies in the fact that half of the entire annual norm of precipitation falls on average in just 12 days, and such a law works anywhere in the world.
In the future, the pattern of rainfall distribution is likely to become even more one-sided.
Experts from the American National Center for Atmospheric Research in the course of a new study found that half of all annual precipitation falls on average in just 12 days.
And such a "law" works anywhere in the world.Recently, researchers are conducting more and more work that allows you to simulate possible scenarios of the future climate associated with global warming.
According to forecasts, in the future, the frequency of extreme weather events will increase, but the average amount of precipitation around the world will decrease.
In this case, experts wanted to consider how these two trends will affect precipitation.
The lead author of the new work, Angelina Pendergrass (Angeline Pendergrass) said that the maximum amount of precipitation will continue to fall in the wettest periods.
In other words, the rainy days will become even rainier.
Accordingly, the dry periods will become even drier, which for some regions of the planet is also a big problem.Climatologists specify that in the course of work they considered the data on precipitation collected for each day in the period from 1999 to 2014.
It is noted that the selected 16-year period covers the most noticeable fluctuations in the average annual rainfall, including those caused by the El Niño effect and other short-term climatic events.
Of course, in different years and in different regions, this event does not fall on one specific date, but the trend is very clear.
Meanwhile, half of the annual precipitation rate, as already noted, falls during a 12-day period. "I would assume that the figures will be larger, perhaps a month.
But when we looked at the data from all the available observation stations, it turned out only 12 days, ” says Pendergrass.In addition, experts used 36 different climate models to assess how the “law of precipitation ” may change in the future.In particular, according to one of the scenarios, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere could increase by 2100 to 936 parts per million (recall, today this figure is about 410 parts per million).
Under such conditions, the distribution of precipitation will become even more "one-sided", and by the end of the century, half of the entire annual norm will fall no longer in 12, but in 11 days, according to a brief note in the journal Science, dedicated to the publication of the results of the study.
Therefore, new data can be useful to urban planners and rescue services.In addition, the results of the work raise concerns for agricultural yields, because most cereals and other plants are accustomed to a more even distribution of precipitation.
In particular, the authors note that in this case, a large amount of precipitation for such a short period can hardly be regarded as an "extreme" climatic event.
On the contrary, this has turned into a trend, and the very definition of "extreme" rainfall in the light of new data can already be equated with the term "average rainfall" .And, apparently, this is not the only distinction that will be "washed away" by the elements of global warming. nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about other changes caused by rising temperatures around the world.
Thus, the warmed Arctic is gradually captured by plants, fish move to the cool "twilight zone", and birds die out in the tropics.Meanwhile, the next few years will be, according to forecasts of climatologists, abnormally hot even against the background of global warming, and due to prolonged droughts, the world, as it turned out, may be left without beer.

title: Money grows on trees
text:
Botir Kobilov is an economist, a scientific researcher at the Harvard Business School.
He holds a master ’ s degree in economics from Duke University (USA).
Previously, he worked as a leading economist at the Central Bank of Uzbekistan.
Member of the Expert Council "Buyuk Kelazhak".
One of the most famous public spaces in the world, Central Park is located in the center of New York City in the United States, and it is literally a park with trees, a lake, sports grounds and even a zoo.
More recently, it became known that Tashkent Central Park will be built in the very center of the capital of Uzbekistan.
In our case, despite the use of the word “park ” in the name, this is a shopping and entertainment complex, a hotel, a bank building.
Within a radius of several hundred meters from the site where it is planned to create a “park ”, there are already three hotels and four banks.
Let us consider the pressing issue of preserving trees and increasing the area of plantations and parks from the point of view of economic benefits.
Money actually grows on trees, and you need to act on the basis of scientific research and, in the end, common sense.
The beneficial functions of trees in an urbanized environment cannot be overstated.
Despite the public outcry of the capital and other cities of the country against the cutting of trees and in their defense, it is obvious that there is a lack of understanding of the crucial biological role of green spaces in urban conditions.
Recognizing and appreciating these benefits can help make the right decisions about how best to manage (not cut down!) our urban trees.
City authorities may perceive trees as "expensive ornaments", or as an obstacle to buildings, roads, or the construction of new structures.
But in reality, they are much more than just trees.
They are an essential part of infrastructure and public health.
And that ’ s why we should finally start taking care of trees and parks.
In Tashkent, the share of urban forest in the total area is less than 10%, which is much lower than in other capitals and cities.
It is important to stop the relentless decline of trees and green areas in general.
Source: Planting Healthy Air Report, 2016.
Trees can cool cities by 2-8 degrees Celsius.
Trees planted near buildings can reduce air conditioning use by 30% and, according to the UN Office for Urban Forestry, reduce thermal energy consumption by another 20 to 50%.
According to a study by the U.S. Forest Service, every dollar spent planting trees creates direct and indirect benefits totaling at least $2.7.
A similar study in the UK found that £1 spent on tree planting saves £7, or a potential £2.1 billion per year in healthcare costs.
In the developed cities of the world, you can see a trend towards greening.
According to the UN definition, London can be classified as a forest: 8.4 million trees – almost one for each person – decorate and clean this metropolis.
The total annual cash benefit from these trees is about 130 million pounds.
If you call the predominant color in the “fashion capital ” – Milan – it ’ s gray, not only because of the blocks of neoclassical stone buildings for which this city is famous, but also because of its often gray sky caused by air pollution.
However, today Milan wants to shift its color palette towards green.
The city has ambitious plans: by 2030, it is planned to plant 3 million new trees.
A view of a vertical forest on residential towers in Milan, Italy.
Source: Commercial Real Estate Journal.
In Atlanta (USA), everyone will be fined up to $1,000 for cutting down a single tree up to 15 cm in diameter, and the law regulates cutting down trees even on private property.
As in Atlanta, and in many cities of the world, every tree is numbered and protected.
The experience of preserving trees is diverse, it involves residents, authorities, it relies on technology.
Researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have created a project that tracks the degree of greening of the streets of major cities in the world.
In this city, public trees are also protected by state laws.
Such ads can be seen near potential trees that fell under felling in the city of Cambridge, Massachusetts.
Cutting down healthy trees requires a public hearing and the consent of local residents.
It can be stated with absolute certainty that if such public hearings were held before the destruction of the historical oasis in the center of Tashkent and perennial chinar, now Amir Temur Square and the centers of other cities of the republic would have a completely different appearance...
Amir Temur Square in Tashkent before cutting down trees.
Source: Diary of an unknown traveler.
In practice, there are cases of taking care of green spaces.
In particular, the reconstruction of the former Telman Park, which is also now called Central Park, took into account the proposals of the residents of the city and preserved trees, many of which are more than 100 years old.
This means that the effect of feedback from the population and taking into account the opinions of citizens exists.
It is important to systematize this process in all other social and economic issues that residents face.
Researchers at the University of Chicago, using data from Toronto in Canada, found that “having an average of 10 additional trees in urban neighborhoods improves residents ’ perception of health in ways comparable to increasing annual personal income by $10,000 or becoming 7 years younger. ”
A study examining the health effects of trees found that mothers living in homes with more trees within a 50-meter radius were less likely to have underweight babies.
The view of the trees from the house gives residents a greater sense of well-being and satisfaction from their surroundings.
It is also proven that a hospital bed overlooking a tree accelerates the recovery of patients and reduces the number of complications than comparable patients who do not have access to such species.
The question of life and death of a city is decided whenever it comes to preserving trees and creating urban parks and green areas.
Well-planned parks (alleys) work as economic catalysts that stimulate and support private investment, both residential and commercial.
All things being equal, most people are willing to pay more for a house next to a beautiful park and a garden with trees.
Economists call this phenomenon “hedonic value or valuation. ”
Numerous studies have shown that the estimated value of the property of homes adjacent to parks and open spaces with trees is typically 8 to 20% higher than comparable homes in other places with fewer trees.
This means that people will pay 8 – 20% more for the same house on the same area if the house and land are in close proximity to a quality park.
There is no better historical example of how a city park affects the market value of real estate than New York ’ s Central Park.
In fact, Frederick Lowe Olmsted, the legendary landscape architect who designed it, studied the effect of his famous project back in the 1850s and was able to prove to the city council that New York would profit from Central Park.
Imagine that in 2014 alone, the proximity to Central Park added more than $26 billion to the market value of properties in the coming quarters, which in turn is reflected in property taxes.
Hedonic assessment can also be applied to commercial and retail facilities.
Kathleen Wolf (2003) investigated the role of trees in consumer behavior in retail areas and found that consumers are willing to pay 9 – 12% more at outlets located along tree-lined streets compared to a comparable tree-free area.
In addition, in this case, buyers are even willing to pay more for parking.
Another study found that rental rates for commercial office properties were about 7% higher on plots with quality landscape, including trees.
Unfortunately, it would be naive to believe that in the near future, trees and parks in Uzbekistan will be protected in the same way as in developed countries.
This is hampered by the lack of development of mechanisms for the implementation of laws, the specifics of the perception of civil position and rights given by laws, as well as decision-making without relying on scientific research.
The head of state, in a speech dedicated to the Constitution Day, criticized the parliament for “lack of initiative and inertia ”.
In August, the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis did not support the appeal, which was voted by more than 12 thousand citizens concerned about the ongoing felling of trees throughout the country.
Settlements (settlements, villages, districts, cities) are created, first of all, for residents, for their healthy life.
The green spaces necessary for this should be protected and increased in proportion to the growth of road and other urban infrastructure and the overall burden on the urban ecosystem.
As noted by a German specialist in the preservation of architectural heritage, only a genuine building carries information and traditions, the way of life of Tashkent, all of Uzbekistan.
Especially in the construction of new shopping centers and high-rise buildings, the city with its functions, traditions and architectural solutions represents a particularly valuable potential for the future of the country, which should not become a victim of short-term profit interests.
Without trees, green areas, parks and the benefits they create, the city will lose attractiveness for tourists and foreign investment.
Even if the examples used in this article do not always establish a direct causal relationship, it is important to study the results of the research, listen to the scientists and take into account the scientific facts and the position of the population.
And they say, “Seven times, cut off one. ”
The opinion of the author may not coincide with the opinion of the editorial board.

title: Japan announces withdrawal from International Whaling Commission
text:

It is reported by RBC-Ukraine with reference to the agency Kyodo.
As stated in the government of the country, Japan is preparing to resume commercial whaling in July 2019.
At the same time, Tokyo plans to remain in the IWC as an observer and participate in the discussions.
Earlier, a government source told Kyodo that Japan will announce its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission.
According to the source, in this way, Japan will be able to catch whales in its internal waters, where they are now hunted for these animals "for scientific purposes."
Over the past few years, the level of consumption of whale meat in Japan has decreased to 5 thousand tons per year.
And in 1960, this figure was about 200 thousand tons.
Japan has been a member of the IWC since 1951, and in 1982 the commission passed a ban on commercial whaling.
Five years later, Japan began to catch whales in the Antarctic Ocean, explaining this “scientific purposes ”.
But in 2014, the UN International Court of Justice ruled that Japan should stop whaling in Antarctica.
Tokyo did not comply with this decision, but reduced the number of prey.

title: Japan legalizes commercial whaling
text:
Tokyo plans to notify the Commission of its decision by January 1 to resume commercial whaling from July 2019.
It is assumed that it will be conducted in the exclusive economic zone of Japan, and not in Antarctica, where the “scientific ” fishing was conducted.
The latter was seen as a cover for commercial mining and was criticized by international organizations.
In case of withdrawal from the IWC, Japanese whalers will not be able to hunt in the Antarctic Ocean.
Japan stopped commercial whaling in 1982 and began hunting for research purposes in 1987.
If in the 1960s the annual consumption of whale meat in the country was about 200,000 tons, in recent years, according to the government, about 5,000 tons.
Tokyo has lobbied for the resumption of commercial whaling for the past 30 years, but these initiatives have been blocked by Australia and New Zealand.
In 2007, Japan threatened to withdraw from the organization in protest against the ban on commercial whaling, but under pressure from the United States retained its membership in the organization.

title: Japan to resume whaling

text:
The Japanese government officially announced on Wednesday it will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission to resume commercial whaling in July next year.
This was announced at a press conference in Tokyo by the Secretary General of the Cabinet of Ministers Yoshihide Suga, Armenpress reports referring to Tass.
“Our country in the framework of the Commission sincerely participated in the dialogue on whaling for more than 30 years, – he said. – There are well-confirmed scientific data on a sufficient number of whales.
However, some countries ignore them and show no willingness to converge.
Therefore, we have decided to withdraw from the commission, but we will contribute to international efforts to control marine resources. ”

title: Japan to resume whale hunting
text:
The move will allow Tokyo to resume whale hunting.
Japan has complied with the commission ’ s requirements for more than 30 years, however, according to Yoshihide Suga, the secretary-general of the cabinet, scientists have confirmed a sufficient number of these mammals.
Suga said that the production will be carried out exclusively in the territorial waters and exclusive economic zone of Japan.
Withdrawal from the commission will allow whalers to go to sea on June 30, 2019.
Whale hunting has been banned since 1982.
Japan, however, continued this practice under the guise of scientific activity, which provoked protests from environmentalists.
Every year, Japanese whalers captured about 1,000 individuals.
The local government has repeatedly explained that eating whale meat is a national tradition.
In addition to Japan, whaling continues in Norway and Iceland.

title: Whaling in Japan to resume in 2019
text:
Whaling in Japan will resume in 2019.
Photo: nashzeleniymir.ru https: / / racurs.ua / n116112-kitoboynyy-promysel-v-yaponii-vozobnovyat-v-2019-godu.html Racurs.ua The Japanese government decided to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and restore commercial whaling.
A member of the Japanese government Yoshihide Suga said that from July 2019, Japan will resume commercial whaling, reports AFP.
According to the official, Japan will resume whaling only in its territorial waters and will not engage in whaling in Antarctic or southern hemisphere waters.
Withdrawal from the commission will give Japan the right to hunt the minke whale and other whales, which are currently protected by the IWC.
However, not all Japanese approve of this decision.
Animal rights groups and Greenpeace Japan have criticised the country's withdrawal from the commission.
According to Sam Annesley, executive director of Greenpeace Japan, the move threatens the preservation of the future of the oceans.
Japan has often been criticized for catching large quantities of whales in Antarctic waters, ostensibly for scientific purposes, which was allowed as part of the whaling commission.
Meanwhile, in the summer, an Icelandic whaling company for the first time in 40 years killed a giant blue whale that is on the verge of extinction.

title: Japan allowed to kill whales for meat, because it is “part of the culture of the country ”
text:
Japan has allowed the killing of whales for meat, because it is "part of the culture of the country" In Japan, they believe that whales are quite enough and their advocates ignore scientific evidence.
Photo: pixabay In Japan, they believe that whales are quite enough and their defenders ignore scientific data.
Japan is withdrawing from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in 2019 to resume commercial whaling.
This was announced by the Secretary General of the Japanese Cabinet of Ministers Yoshihide Suga, reports the "Russian Air Force Service".
According to him, some countries included in the Commission, ignore the scientific data indicating a sufficient number of whales, and do not demonstrate readiness to bring positions closer.
In this regard, Japan is forced to leave the organization.
According to Suga, Japan plans to resume commercial whaling from next July.
Hunting will be conducted within the exclusive economic zone of the country, fishing in Antarctic waters will not be conducted.
Commercial whaling was banned by the IWC in 1986 after some whale species were almost completely wiped out.
Japan stopped commercial whaling, but then partially resumed fishing, but hunting was allowed only for scientific purposes.
Whale meat appeared in Japanese restaurants and shops, which gave opponents of whaling doubt about the scientific nature of this activity.
Japan calls the consumption of whale meat part of the country ’ s culture.
As noted by the Kyodo Agency, whale meat was the main source of food for the inhabitants of the country in the post-war period and was included in school lunches.
According to Suga, in the 60s of the last century, the Japanese annually ate up to 200 thousand tons of whale meat, but in recent years its consumption has decreased to 5 thousand tons.
According to the Japanese authorities, 48 IWC members are currently opposed to commercial whaling, while 41 countries are inclined to resume it.
According to Whale and Dolphin Conservation, whaling still exists in many countries.
Whales are still hunted for their meat in Norway and Iceland.
Norway refused to support a moratorium on fishing, and Iceland partially agreed to it.
The Japanese government has already been criticized by the authorities of Australia, one of the main opponents of whaling.
Foreign Minister Marisa Payne and Environment Minister Melissa Price said in a joint statement that they were extremely disappointed with Japan ’ s decision.
"Australia remains strongly opposed to all forms of commercial and so-called 'scientific' whaling," the statement said.
The local Greenpeace office appealed to the Government of Japan to reconsider the decision.
Sam Annesley, CEO of Greenpeace Japan, warned that this could negatively affect the holding of the G-20 summit in Osaka in June 2019.
As reported by Ukrainian News, a dead whale with a full stomach of plastic was found in Indonesia.
Earlier, whalers in Iceland killed a rare blue whale, which is one of the largest creatures on the planet.

title: Japan to resume whaling for first time in 30 years
text:
Japan will cease membership in the International Whaling Commission from 2019.
This was reported by the representative of the government of the country, reports AFP.
The government of Japan made this decision because the country ’ s attempts to convince the commission to restore commercial whaling failed, due to resistance from countries struggling with whaling.
Government spokesman Yoshihihido Suga said Japan is withdrawing from the commission to restore commercial whale hunting on its own in July 2019.
“Commercial whaling will be restored in July next year and will be limited to Japan ’ s territorial waters and the country ’ s exclusive economic zones.
We will not hunt in Antarctic waters or in the southern hemisphere, ” Suga said.
Australia and New Zealand have always opposed attempts to restore commercial whaling.
Both countries are calling for a complete end to whaling.
Iceland and Norway have traditionally opposed the moratorium on whaling in addition to Japan.
Both Scandinavian countries have limited whaling.
Japan has officially stopped commercial whaling under a moratorium imposed in 1986.
But in two years, Japan resumed whaling in Antarctic waters “for scientific purposes. ”

title: The UK is concerned about the number of “storming ” the English Channel migrants
text:
Home Secretary Sajid Javid also expressed his intention to hold an urgent telephone conversation with his French counterpart on this matter.
The UK is concerned about the sharp increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to get into the country through the English Channel.
This was stated in the Ministry of internal Affairs of the country, reports Reuters.
“The Minister insisted that the Interior Ministry treat the situation as a serious incident and request daily updates, ” the ministry said in a statement.
British Interior Minister Sajid Javid also expressed his intention to hold an urgent telephone conversation with his French counterpart on this matter.
The minister added that he wants to do everything possible to deter migrants from a dangerous journey “in the wake of concern that the death of people is only a matter of time. ”
About 70 people have been intercepted in the English Channel during an attempt to cross one of the busiest sea straits in boats over the past three days.

title: Crisis in the English Channel: Britain and France agreed to increase patrols
text:
Britain and France have agreed to strengthen joint patrols and expand the tracking system in the English Channel to cope with the flow of migrants trying to illegally cross the strait by boat.
Home Secretary Sajid David agreed on a joint plan of action in a telephone conversation with his French counterpart on Sunday evening.
The plan calls for the suppression of organized criminal groups involved in the transport of illegal migrants, as well as sensitizing migrants themselves to the risks of trying to cross the English Channel.
On Sunday morning, six more Iranians crossing the English Channel by boat were found ashore near the town of Deal in the English county of Kent.
After the initial medical examination, the detainees were handed over to border guards.
On Saturday evening, French authorities said they had managed to thwart another attempt to cross the strait illegally.
Home Secretary Sajid David cut short his Christmas holiday with his family in Africa on Sunday and returned home to tackle a difficult situation with an unexpected wave of illegal migrants arriving in Britain by boat from France.
About 60 migrants have been reported to have come to Britain in small boats over the past week, but NGOs and refugees in Calais, France, say the figure could be higher.
Since the beginning of November, more than 220 migrants have attempted to illegally enter the UK in this way.
On Saturday, Deputy Minister for Immigration Caroline Knox went to Dover urgently, and the interior Minister said that the Home Office has taken control of the situation, and now he is personally responsible for the response strategy, receiving daily updates on the situation.
Image caption Six men were detained near the town of Deal Dangerous Enterprise, many migrants trying to cross into Britain in small inflatable boats hailing from Syria, Afghanistan and Iran.
As one Afghan refugee told the BBC, Brexit has created panic among migrants, and all they say is that control at the border will increase after Britain leaves the EU and therefore it is necessary to act quickly.
The owner of the illustration Getty Images Image caption The interior minister who interrupted his vacation said that he would review the resources allocated for patrolling coastal waters In addition, among migrants gathering in groups in French Calais in the hope of finding a way to move to Britain, there is a misconception that in the midst of the Christmas and New Year holidays control over the border will be weakened.
One refugee charity claims that mainly Iranian Kurds are trying to reach Britain by boat.
As Bridget Chapman of the NGO Kent Refugee Action Network, which helps migrants, noted, these people could have legitimate reasons to apply for refugee status and they should not have risked their lives.
"The government should find a way to consider their applications back in France, and then transport them," she said.
“I saw from the photos that they were not wearing life jackets – it ’ s scary.
I hope that the authorities can find the political will to prevent anyone from drowning off the coast of Britain, "Chapman said.
Under current rules, asylum seekers are required to file an application in the first safe country in which they find themselves, where the application should be considered.
However, many migrants expect that in Britain they will be treated more hospitable.
One of the illegal migrants who tried to cross the English Channel in a boat smugglers, but was detained in neutral waters and returned back by the French border service, said in an interview with the Telegraph: "It is better to drown at sea than to return to France."
Migrant rights advocates say increased security around Calais has made it much harder for refugees trying to enter the UK illegally to get on ferries, trucks and trains crossing the English Channel, prompting more people to use motorboats for this purpose.
How do smugglers work?
British newspapers on Sunday described a scheme that smugglers offer to migrants in France who want to get to Britain.
The Sunday Telegraph correspondent who went to Calais, using the example of 38-year-old Mahmoud from Iran, tells how in the evening of December 26 he received SMS messages with an address at which he was to be picked up by a person in a car and taken to the shore, where a boat will wait.
British authorities fear that in the coming weeks the number of attempts to swim across the English Channel will increase. His brother, who is in Iran, in advance put 3 thousand pounds on hold in the account of smugglers, which they will receive only if Mahmoud gets to the British shores.
That same evening, Mahmoud and 10 other migrants were put in a seven-piece rubber boat operated by a smuggler who called himself “Bruce Lee. ”
He drove them halfway, then transferred them to a motor boat following them, where his partner was, and, threatening with a gun, ordered the migrants to move further themselves towards Britain.
At one point, the boat was spotted by fishing boats and ferries and alerted French border guards, who sent a patrol ship and returned the migrants to a tent camp in Calais.
Mahmoud told the newspaper that the migrants had sailed 15 nautical miles northwest of Calais, while the shortest distance to Britain through the strait was 18 nautical miles.
“I couldn ’ t believe my eyes!
How could a French patrol be so close to Britain?
We were told that as soon as we were in British waters, everything would be fine, which means we are in place, "Mahmoud said.
According to the newspaper, the French asked the British for additional help, complaining that to catch migrants they have to go into British territorial waters.
According to the Daily Telegraph, just in the Christmas week, that is, since December 24, 94 migrants in 12 boats tried to cross the English Channel.
Lewis Morris Image caption A group of six people was discovered on Sunday morning.
The Mail on Sunday, in its own report on the situation with migrants, writes that many of those who now sail in this way are educated middle-class people fleeing religious oppression in Iran.
Unlike Africans and Afghans living in coastal French refugee camps, they have the means to pay smugglers.
They first arrived in Calais six months ago, and now there are about two hundred of them there.
Many of them told the newspaper that they would try to repeat this dangerous voyage until they got to Britain.
To get to Britain, illegal migrants pay significant sums to smugglers The newspaper, citing an Iranian living in a French refugee camp, writes that the entire operation is led by Kurds living in Britain, who have their own agents in the refugee camps.
As he tells the migrants before being sent to swim in the boats, they take away mobile phones and give one phone with a British SIM card, which migrants can use only when they approach Dover.
The Mail on Sunday also reports that a smuggler from the French coast brings migrants only half the way, and then returns to France on an accompanying boat.
Newspapers also note two other factors that may have contributed to the increase in the influx of migrants - this is the relatively warm weather now standing off the British coast, and Christmas holidays, because, according to the plan of smugglers, during this period there is usually a lull, in particular, in terms of patrolling the water space.
British authorities have been sharply criticized in recent days for their inability to cope with this situation.
A number of MPs have called for more patrol ships to be placed in the strait, but Britain ’ s Home Secretary has said it is necessary to find a balance between protecting migrants and protecting the border.
Only one specialized patrol boat of the British service, capable of simultaneously rescuing passengers of several boats, is now located in the English Channel.
The other four boats are now engaged in search and rescue operations in the Mediterranean, and the Home Office has not yet announced whether they are planned to return for patrol around the south-east coast of Britain.
Sajid David had previously stated that he did not want to encourage people to risk their lives trying to cross the strait, and that the issue of the number of boats is now under consideration.
Chris Hogben, a spokesman for the National Crime Agency, said that such a high level of migration from Iran is something new and that these groups are transferring quite serious money to organized gangs that are engaged in the illegal transfer of people.
According to him, the agency ’ s employees also note an increase in the number of migrants who are trying to organize transit on their own, buying folding or stealing boats.
Hogben expects that in the coming weeks the number of attempts to cross the English Channel in this way will increase.
Defence Secretary Gavin Williamson said the armed forces were ready to offer assistance if needed.

title: The British Navy will help catch migrants
text:
Britain will send a Navy patrol ship to the English Channel to prevent the transfer of illegal migrants from the continent to the island.
The Ministry of the Interior requested the help of naval sailors, after another ship with illegal immigrants was intercepted in the area of Dover.
Interior Minister Sajid Javid said the sailors would protect the kingdom ’ s borders and prevent loss of life in the English Channel.
According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, in 2018, 539 people illegally crossed the strait.
80% of cases occur in the last three months.
On 25 December alone, at least five such incidents were recorded off the coast of the United Kingdom.
On January 2, police detained two people in Manchester on suspicion of organizing the illegal movement of migrants through the English Channel.
Migrants wishing to reach the British Isles have been gathering near the French city of Calais for many years.
Many of them try to get to the other shore, hiding on ferries and in trucks crossing the tunnel under the English Channel.

title: SpaceX made its first launch in 2019. The final batch of ten Iridium NEXT communications satellites went into orbit
text:
Click to share on Telegram (Opens in new window) Click to share posts on Pocket (Opens in new window) Click to share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) Click here to share content on Facebook.
(Opens in new window) Click to share on Twitter (Opens in new window) American private aerospace company SpaceX successfully launched its first launch in 2019.
Just recently, the Falcon 9 rocket launched into orbit the next ten communication satellites for the satellite provider Iridium Communications.
This is the last batch in the framework of the signed contract for the launch of 75 satellites.
Live broadcast of the launch is conducted on the SpaceX channel on YouTube.
The missile was launched at 17: 31 Kyiv time from the SLC-4E site at Vandenberg Air Force Base in Santa Barbara County, California.
It was the second launch of the first stage of F9 B5 B1049.2, which was used for the September launch of the Telstar satellite last year.
Approximately three minutes later, the stages were separated, and seven minutes after the start, the first stage successfully landed on the Just Read the Instructions barge in the Pacific Ocean.
Unfortunately, at the time of landing of the stage, the broadcast was interrupted, but the stage successfully sat down.
Falcon 9 first stage has landed on the Just Read the Instructions droneship. pic.twitter.com / 8l5fdMyJgH — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) January 11, 2019 At 17: 41 there was a planned shutdown of the second stage engines, the second stage together with the satellite entered the phase of passive flight.
After about 40 minutes, the engines of the second stage will restart and the satellite will be delivered to the planned orbit.
Over the past year, SpaceX has successfully completed 21 launches, which is a new record.
Of particular interest is the next launch, which will take place in February.
This will be the launch of the Falcon 9 with the long-awaited demonstration mission Demonstration Mission 1 (DM-1), as part of the Crew Dragon spacecraft will make its first unmanned flight to the ISS.
If all goes well, then in June 2019, SpaceX will start using Crew Dragon to deliver crews to the International Space Station (ISS).
Updated: Confirmation of successful deployment of all satellites in orbit has been received.

title: The first flight of the Stratolaunch aircraft will take place soon.
text:
The final ground test of a giant aircraft developed by the American company Stratolaunch Systems, in order to check its take-off system indicates that very soon the first flight of this aircraft may take place.
On January 9, the company reported that the aircraft, which has the largest wingspan in aviation history, performed the fastest ground test to date, which took place at the Mojave aerospace port in California (USA).
The aircraft reached a speed of 219 kilometers per hour.
As part of the test, a “lifting maneuver ” was also carried out, in which the pilot briefly lifted the bow of the ship from the ground.
This was the last ground test in a series of tests in which the aircraft moved independently on the runway, but did not take off from it.
The testing program began at the end of 2017, during which specialists gradually increased the speed of movement of air vehicles.
During a briefing with journalists in April 2018, representatives of the company said that they plan to conduct three more steering tests before making the first flight.
According to them, the final test will be the one in which they can reach a speed of 220 kilometers per hour.
At that time, the company believed that the aircraft would be ready for its first flight in the summer of 2018, but then it was reported that the timing was postponed without explanation.
Industry experts have speculated that Stratolaunch could make the first lift to the air before the end of last year, but their forecasts turned out to be erroneous.
Once the aircraft makes its first flight, it will move on to the next phase of the vehicle testing program.
Last year, the organization said it would take 18 to 24 months to complete all the tests.
It will then have to obtain a certificate of suitability for flight from the Federal Aviation Administration, and only then the aircraft will be able to be used as a platform for launching spacecraft.
Stratolaunch Systems is going to use the aircraft to launch Pegasus XL rockets into space, which will be provided to it by Norhrop Grumman Innovation Systems.
It will be able to carry up to three missiles in one flight, which will be installed on the pylons of the wings between its two fuselages.
However, the company is creating its own launch vehicles, which can also be transported by plane.
Its representatives said in August last year that the medium-lift carrier rocket, capable of placing 3,400 kilograms of cargo in low Earth orbit, is scheduled to launch in 2022.
The manufacturer has plans to create a heavier version of the rocket, capable of putting 6,000 kilograms into orbit, as well as concepts for a crewed space plane.
These devices will be equipped with engines of its own design called PGA.
This propulsion system uses liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen propellants to produce a thrust force of 90,000 kilograms.
In November, Stratolaunch said it had successfully tested the engine at NASA ’ s Mississippi Space Center.
The engine was named after Paul Gardner Allen, an American billionaire who founded the company and died in October 2018.
Allen ’ s head of Vulcan, a holding company, said they would continue to support the institutions founded by the entrepreneur, but gave no details about the future of Stratolaunch.

title: In the United States conducted a test flight competitor of the Ukrainian “Mriya ”: published video
text:
On January 9, the American company Stratolaunch Systems tested a two-fuselage transport vehicle Stratolaunch Model 351, which surpasses the wingspan of the Ukrainian An-225 Mriya.
