Given the huge wingspan (more than 117 meters), the aircraft can be called the largest in history.
Until that time, the record for wingspan was held by the American Hughes H-4 Hercules, and the An-225 was in second place.
The length of the Stratolaunch transporter is 73 meters, and the maximum take-off weight is almost 600 tons.
The weight of the suspended payload is 230 tons.
During the tests, the aircraft was accelerated to a speed of 218 kilometers per hour.
The tests were considered successful, because the device can make its first flight in the near future.
Stratolaunch Model 351 will serve as a platform for the air launch of launch vehicles.
According to unconfirmed reports, in the future the aircraft may become part of some military programs.
"Note that the An-225 will have to surpass the new American aircraft in terms of maximum take-off weight (640 tons) and payload (250 tons)," the statement said.
As reported by “Apostrophe ”, in Kiev in a crowded place beat the aircraft designer of the plant“ Antonov ”, co-author of the aircraft “Mriya ” Viktor Kovalsky.

title: Alive Ken wants to “pump out ” his face back
text:
Alive Ken wants to "pump" his face back Plastic surgery works wonders.
One such miracle is 35-year-old Rodrigo Alves, like two drops of water similar to Barbie ’ s friend Ken.
Many plastic surgeries have so changed the appearance of a man that not only his mother, but also robots at passport control will not recognize him.
Now the human doll wants to turn everything back and again lies under the surgeon ’ s knife to become himself, the real one.
What threatens the reverse transformation of Ken in human form — read on.
Now Rodrigo once again goes to Iran, to the clinic of plastic surgery, but now in order to return his real face.
This decision of the secular party guy was inspired by... passport control.
The fact is that the robots that identify with the photo in the passport, no longer recognize Rodrigo.
This will be the 63rd operation he will perform.
But in addition to this surgical intervention, 7 more procedures will be required.
As a result, the face of the victim of plastic surgery will be reshaped 69 times.
“This is going to be the most important surgery of my life, ” Rodrigo says.
Surgeons will take cartilage from the ribs of a man to restore his nose.
The complex for the reconstruction of the face will consist of several stages.
The novice star had to postpone for a while lessons on vocals and recording songs.
Rodrigo was born in Brazil, but spent most of his life in London.
This week, he flew to Tehran, where he will undergo a complex operation to change the shape of his eyes.
Surgeons will have to make an incision in the head and return the displaced muscles to their place.
In addition, Roddy will do a cheek lift, neck liposuction and remove a silicone implant from the chin.
This will be followed by a change in lip shape and restoration of the middle part of the face.
Operations will take place within a week.
“The goal of all these operations is to reduce the parameters of my face so that it becomes more recognizable.
My nose is now broken and I have difficulty breathing, so I need to do something quickly.
Iran is the place to help me! ” Roddy says with hope.
Rodrigo is sure that the Iranian specialists are the best in the field of plastic surgery.
These are not his first operations here, so he safely lies under the knife of the Iranian esculapes.
BigPicture.ru Doll Man hopes that this will be his last surgery on the nose.
He is a little nervous before the procedure, but wants to fix the situation with the face.
Roddy does not know if this plastic will be the last in his life and plans to soon resume active participation in social gatherings.
Ken in human form continues to sacrifice his health for the sake of popularity.
Fame requires new experiences and extravagant actions, often putting human life at stake.

title: Will the American aircraft giant Ukrainian “Mriya ”: the opinion of experts
text:
Photo: "Mriya" and Stratolaunch Model 351 (collage RBC-Ukraine) Ukrainian experts compared two aircraft - Ukrainian An-225 Mriya and American Stratolaunch Model 351 Recently, the network published a video of the latest tests of the Stratolaunch Systems aircraft - a two-body transport vehicle Stratolaunch Model 351.
During the tests, the car was accelerated to a speed of 218 kilometers per hour.
Tests experts recognized as successful, and the aircraft in the near future will be able to make the first flight.
With a wingspan of more than 117 meters, it surpasses the Ukrainian An-225 Mriya.
It can be called the largest aircraft in history.
Up to this point, the record for the largest wingspan was held by the Hughes H-4 Hercules manufactured in the United States, and the An-225 took second place.
The length of the Stratolaunch is 73 meters, and the maximum take-off weight is almost 600 tons.
The weight of the suspended payload is 230 tons.
This year, the plane will send a rocket into space for the first time.
Video: During the tests, the car was accelerated to a speed of 218 kilometers per hour (Youtube / Stratolaunch) The network has already talked about the fact that the new aircraft will push the An-225.
But will the new aircraft actually compete with the Ukrainian “Mriya ”?
Is it correct to compare them at all, because two planes have different tasks?
With these questions we turned to Artem Kulikov, the commander-instructor, in the past - the test pilot.
For 25 years he has been flying Ruslan, teaching and testing young pilots.
He also flew a lot on Mriya.
The son of the instructor, Nikolai Artemovich, is also a pilot.
He also gave an expert assessment of the aircraft.
It is unlikely that a new American aircraft will compete with Mriya in commercial transportation, because it is intended for completely different tasks, Artem Kulikov is sure.
“Large-sized cargo, which can take on board our Ruslan or Mriya, this aircraft will not be able to“ master ”.
It was created for other, narrower purposes.
In particular, to produce the air launch of rockets into orbit, spacecraft.
After all, starting from the ground is expensive: there will be a very large fuel consumption.
Launching missiles from such an aircraft will be much cheaper.
Apparently, it was created by the Americans for work related to space, with the testing of rockets or other equipment, ” explains Artem Nikolayevich.
Photo: An-225 “Mriya ” (antonov.com) For these reasons, it is not quite correct to compare both aircraft, he believes.
“Even visually looking at the design of this aircraft, it is clear that it is not able to carry large loads.
In addition, not every airfield in the world can accept such an aircraft.
It's an experimental model.
As a commercial aircraft for Mriya, and even more so for Ruslan, there will be no competition, "adds Nikolai, son of Artem Nikolaevich.
Two unique aircraft "Mriya" - a unique aircraft of its kind, more versatile in use.
Stratolaunch Model 351 is also a unique aircraft, experts say.
"The Stratolaunch Model 351, like the An-225, has six engines.
The wing is also somewhat similar, but the goals and objectives are different.
Designers before the process of creating an aircraft always have certain very specific tasks.
They know in advance what this or that model will be used for: it will be either a fighter that will catch up with enemy aircraft in the air, or a transport, or an amphibious aircraft, or a sports one.
One way or another, the design bureau performs the task that was set in advance, ” says Artem Kulikov.
Photo: Stratolaunch Model 351 (wikipedia.org) The wingspan of the Stratolaunch Model 351 is larger than that of the Mriya, says the specialist.
"The American plane has two fuselages.
Between the fuselages is the so-called wing of the centroplane (centroplane - the central part of the aircraft, connecting the right and left half-planes of the wing - ed.).
Because of this, yes, in size it is more "Mriya".
But as for the take-off weight, I doubt it will be heavier than ours, even though it has six engines, "Kulikov added.
In the meantime, the Mriya remains, as it was, one of the largest aircraft in the world, he emphasizes.
"In the status of" number one "for commercial transportation" Mriya "will be for many years" American aircraft will definitely not take the place of "Mriya" in the air cargo market, Artem Nikolaevich is sure.
“In the status of the number one commercial transport carrier, I am sure that the An-225 will remain for many more years, ” he said.
He expressed hope that in the future the aviation sector in Ukraine will be more financed by the state.
Photo: Stratolaunch Model 351 (wikipedia.org) "This is a very expensive industry in any country.
It requires huge investments.
Not every country can afford such an expensive and large-scale production.
Unfortunately, our state has left this issue to its own devices.
Although there are patriots of the sphere, the company "Antonov" - designers, test pilots who want to revive this sphere.
So far, there is a catastrophic lack of funds for this, but let ’ s hope that the situation in the future will change for the better, ” he adds.
An-225 - more versatile aircraft Closer to the time of publication its comment on the characteristics of both aircraft edition received from experts of SE "Antonov".
"The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft was designed as part of the aerospace system as a carrier aircraft and a platform for the air launch of the spacecraft.
This is its main and only function ”, – commented in the company.
Photo: An-225 “Mriya ” (antonov.com) In contrast, the An-225 is more versatile.
"Created within the framework of the space program" Energia-Buran "for the transportation of large-sized elements of the space system, as well as for launching a reusable spacecraft into orbit," Mriya "can also be used as a regular transport aircraft for the transportation of large-sized cargo for various purposes both inside the cargo cabin and on the outer suspension (" on the back "of the aircraft)," the press service of the enterprise reported.
At the same time, the An-225 is certified as a transport aircraft for commercial cargo transportation around the world.
In addition, the An-225 exceeds the Stratolaunch Model 351 in carrying capacity, experts say SE Antonov.

title: Venezuela: what to rejoice or compete with Muslims?
text:
In Venezuela, driven by its authorities to bankruptcy, mass poverty, hunger, flight of the population, millions of people took to the streets to once again say to all this: “Enough! ”.
Opposition leader and Speaker of Parliament Juan Guaido announced the deposition of current President Nicolas Maduro, as well as the fact that he assumes the temporary exercise of his powers.
The latter's reaction was predictable - he announced a coup attempt and once again used the police and army forces still loyal to him against his people.
No less predictable was the reaction of one of his best friends, Vladimir, who just recently gave a generous gift to a fellow dictator: he restructured $3.4 billion in debt, including not reclaiming it in the next six years.
As they say, “Russia is a generous soul. ”
Not for its citizens lately.
In today ’ s statement, the Russian Foreign Ministry in connection with the events taking place in Venezuela states, in particular, the following: “Extremist opponents of the legitimate government of Venezuela, having failed in their attempts to remove N. Maduro, including through his physical elimination, chose the most confrontational scenario of confrontation. ”
"The swearing in of the opposition 'interim president of Venezuela' and the immediate recognition of him in this capacity by the United States and a number of regional states is aimed at aggravating the split in Venezuelan society, the growth of frontal street fighting, cardinal destabilization of the internal political situation and further escalation of the conflict."
Yes, of course, who would doubt.
In short, as the Muslims of Russia, oppressed by a related regime, we have every reason to rejoice at the imminent collapse of one of its satellites.
However, this joy is overshadowed by the fact that Maduro managed to bet a leader for whom we have different feelings than for Putin - Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
In recent years, he has decided to take on the political and financial tug of the Venezuelan leader, who, like a drowning man, is now grasping at any straw.
And who has recently become a big fan of Turkey, Erdogan personally and even their favorite series Ertuğrul.
But the question arises: what will be the attitude of millions of Venezuelans eager for the fall of the dictator to Erdogan, Erdogan, Turkey and everything connected with them?
Erdogan on Twitter urged his friend to "stand until the end", adding that Turkey will be with him ("we are with you").
But is it justified, as the Russians say, to put all the eggs in one basket?
And is betting on an odious bankrupt leader who has divided his society and is a red rag, if not for a large part, then for a large part of it, the best way to promote Islam, and indeed the "soft power" of Turkey itself?
It is necessary to understand that the times in which the main criterion for assessing a leader, a regime or a country was their anti-Americanism are already in the past.
America is increasingly being pushed by China, and not always what is associated with the first is bad, and with the second is good, which is clearly demonstrated by the history of both the Rohingya and the Uighurs.
Which, of course, does not mean the opposite - that Muslims need to focus on America and associate some hopes with it.
The new world brings with it new threats and new sets of forces, and those who want to take their rightful place in them need to understand them well and make decisions based on this understanding and their capabilities and interests, and not in spite of someone.
This is what I would like to advise on the example of the events in Venezuela to the Muslims of both Turkey and Russia.

title: The largest aircraft in the world was tested on the runway in the United States
text:
The world ’ s largest Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft has been tested on the runway of the airfield in the Mojave Desert (USA).
He scored a speed of 219 kilometers per hour and tore off the front chassis from the runway, Business Insider reported.
According to him, the huge two-fuselage aircraft should be the first commercial vehicle that will bring cargo to low Earth orbit.
Stratolaunch is called the largest aircraft in the world.
By the length of the hull and take-off weight, it is less than the An-225 Mriya, but holds a record for wingspan - as much as 117 meters.
Stratolaunch has never been in the air, but is close to it.
During the tests, which are held at the airfield in the Mojave desert, the giant machine was dispersed to the “speed of separation ” – 219 kilometers per hour.
With this acceleration, the front landing gear Stratolaunch broke away from the runway.
The creators of the unique device say that it is ready for flight.
But the date of the start of flight tests is not yet.
Perhaps Stratolaunch will conduct a series of ground tests before sending it to the sky.

title: Why Russian Women Like Turkish TV Shows
text:
Why do Russian women like Turkish TV series Series, telling about the life of the Ottoman sultans and their concubines, are doomed to success.
At least in Russia.
Yeah, yeah, yeah!
Therefore, "The Magnificent Century" and "The Sultan of My Heart" have high ratings from the first episodes.
But why?
This question was answered by the family psychologist Ksenia Ulyanova.
If men, especially at the age of 50, perceive the series as soap operas, then with the beautiful half of humanity another story.
Women generally like to watch telenovelas.
“As a rule, ladies choose romantic series, ” our expert explains. – In such tapes, the characters overcome different obstacles and then remain together.
Like in a fairy tale: they lived happily ever after.
That is why the series do not lose their popularity.
When it comes to serial tapes about sultans and harem, where love is associated with great competition, it causes a hotter interest.
There are intrigues, machinations, and female envy, and competition in a different form from the usual Russian women.
For example, in reality, a girl is waiting for a handsome man to pay attention to her, and in the Sultan ’ s harem, she must prove herself and influence the choice of the person she likes.
Therefore, the series associated with oriental fairy tales, cause a lot of emotions, ” commented Ksenia Ulyanova.
No matter how strong and self-sufficient a woman may be, deep down she dreams of trying on the role of a weak girl.
The series about sultans help the beauties feel defenseless.
“In the image of the Sultan, there is often a strong, strong-willed man who is able to protect.
He has power.
He is not constrained in finances.
In a sense, this is a prototype of a real man, therefore it causes great sympathy in the female part.
Can the love of such series speak about the subconscious desire to be in the harem?
Perhaps some women really feel the desire to be in a situation where she will be forced to express herself in order to be chosen.
But for the most part, girls do not want to be in harem, but they want to be the one at the sight of which the heart of a strong man melts.
After all, stories about sultans and concubines tell about a obstinate and rebellious girl who is able to fall in love with the main character.
Therefore, Russian women dream of being in her place, ” the family psychologist continues.
Life in the harem is not for Russians But no matter how beautiful the series is, life dictates its own rules.
In reality, the harem story is not for the Russian mentality.
At least, according to the expert portal Teleprogramma.pro.
“In our mentality, there is a reference point for a relationship with one man, and this man should have one woman, not a harem.
The interest is stiff competition.
We are interested in how events will develop in such a situation, how would a Russian woman behave in the environment of competitors, how she will seduce the Sultan.
But to fully immerse yourself in the harem life is not our story, ” the expert concluded.
Psychologist Ksenia Ulyanova

title: SpaceX for the first time launched a manned spacecraft Crew Dragon to the ISS
text:
What has been waiting for many years and that was postponed during repeated transfers: the launch of Crew Dragon from SpaceX took place.
Just recently from the LC-39A launch pad of the Space Center.
Kennedy in Florida (from there took off the “Apollo ” and space shuttles) took off the rocket Falcon 9 with the mission SpX-DM1.
Together with her, the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon (Dragon 2) with a mannequin Ripley (the main character of the Alien film series) went into space and headed for the International Space Station.At 2: 49 am (ET) – 10: 49 MSK – Crew Dragon took off into the sky and turned around in orbit just 11 minutes later.
SpaceX then landed its Falcon 9 rocket on one of the barges in the Atlantic — for the company it was the 35th successful launch.
The capsule, which is now in Earth orbit, will attempt to dock with the International Space Station tomorrow morning.
Crew Dragon is an important part of NASA's program to develop private manned spacecraft, which revolves around the development of a private spacecraft to send people to the International Space Station and back.
As part of this program, two companies — SpaceX and Boeing — are developing their own capsules that will be able to take NASA astronauts into space and then return them to Earth.
But before these capsules can carry humans, NASA wants to see the transport in action.
And SpaceX's Crew Dragon takes to the skies for the first time! pic.twitter.com / 2ze0wSmLbb — Loren Grush (@ lorengrush) March 2, 2019 Main engine cutoff and stage separation confirmed.
Second stage engine burn underground pic.twitter.com / TY5CT14g7g — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) March 2, 2019
Ripley pic.twitter.com / Z9Ztram8Ai — Elon Musk (@ elonmusk) March 1, 2019.
But a smart mannequin named Ripley — equipped with sensors and dressed in a SpaceX suit — kept an eye on the situation.
Sitting in one of the four passenger seats, Ripley collects data on how the flight may affect the human body.
SpaceX ’ s live broadcast also gave insight into Ripley ’ s condition during launch.
In addition, inside the vehicle was placed a small toy in the shape of the Earth, which floated into the air when Crew Dragon was in microgravity conditions.When on Sunday morning Crew Dragon with Ripley on board meet with the ISS, the capsule will maneuver in the direction of the station and try to join the free port.
This dock was installed specifically for SpaceX and Boeing.
Using a series of lasers and software, Crew Dragon identifies the docking adapter and joins it on its own, without the help of astronauts aboard the station.
Supplying materials to the ISS, the cargo version docks, rather than docks.
A crew member aboard the ISS uses the station's robotic arm to grab the cargo capsule and deliver it to the port.
Crew Dragon will be completely independent.

title: Dragon-2 with Ripley mannequin successfully docked with the ISS
text:
The first private reusable spacecraft Dragon-2 (Crew Dragon) for manned flights on Sunday, March 3, successfully docked with the International Space Station (ISS).
Before docking at 05.51 North American Eastern Time (13.51 MSK), the ship performed a series of maneuvers.
Developed by a private American company SpaceX, the Crew Dragon spacecraft was launched into a test flight from Cape Canaveral in Florida on the night of March 2.
Director of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Jim Bridenstine described the launch as “a revolutionary step towards humanity ’ s flights to the Moon, Mars and beyond. ”
“A quiet night on the ISS before the advent of a new era of space flight, ” wrote American astronaut, participant of the 57th and 58th long-term expeditions of the station Anne McClain in his microblog Twitter.
In a special seven-seat capsule for astronauts aboard Crew Dragon is a mannequin clad in a spacesuit, which SpaceX founder Elon Musk named Ripley (after the character of the film “Alien ” by British director Ridley Scott).
Sensors on the dummy will allow you to measure the overload waiting for future astronauts.
Manned launches are expected in the summer Crew Dragon is an improved version of the reusable Dragon spacecraft manufactured by SpaceX, with which cargo was repeatedly delivered to the ISS.
Already in 2019, NASA plans to launch the Crew Dragon with a crew.
The first is expected in July.
SpaceX, along with the American corporation Boeing, participates in the NASA Commercial Crew Program, the purpose of which is to deliver astronauts into space.
In 2011, the United States completed the Space Transportation System program, and the reusable Shuttle space shuttles used in the program were decommissioned.
After that, the delivery of American astronauts and cargo to the ISS took place only with the help of Russian Soyuz missiles.
The contract with Russia expires in November 2019, after which the task will be carried out by SpaceX and Boeing.

text:

The @ SpaceX Crew Dragon is attached to the @ Space _ Station!
It's a first for a commercially built & operated spacecraft designed for crew!
# LaunchAmerica pic.twitter.com / ddck58TVnP — NASA Commercial Crew (@ Commercial _ Crew) March 3, 2019 An important difference between the Crew Dragon and the cargo version of the Dragon and the ships of other companies docking to the American segment of the ISS, such as Cygnus and HTV, is that all stages of its docking with the station fully automated.
This flight, as you know, was conducted without people, on board only a mannequin named Ripley, named after the heroine of the film “Alien ”, as well as 180 kg of cargo for the crew of the station.
The main purpose of the unmanned mission Demo-1 was to test all systems within the framework of the NASA approved certification program Crew Dragon.
Recall, the latter consists of four flight tests: two tests of the crew rescue system (from the launch table and in flight), as well as two flights to the ISS - without a crew and manned.
Thus, Crew Dragon has already successfully passed the tests of the crew rescue system with simulated accident at the start, and also successfully made the first flight without a crew.
Crew Dragon ’ s manned flight is scheduled for July 2019.
Note that Crew Dragon is able to spend more than 200 days docked to the ISS.
As for this particular test mission, Crew Dragon will stay in orbit for almost a week, and then return to Earth, delivering some kind of cargo from the station (research results and something else).
The DM-1 mission will culminate in the splashdown of Crew Dragon in the Atlantic Ocean 390 kilometers east of Cape Canaveral on March 8.
Interestingly, the current contract with NASA requires SpaceX to use a new Crew Dragon every time.
At the same time, NASA ’ s contract with Boeing allows the same Starliner to be used repeatedly.
Perhaps in the future, NASA will allow SpaceX to use Crew Dragon again, as it was with the cargo version of the Dragon.
Recall, Crew Dragon was officially introduced in 2014, and in 2017, SpaceX demonstrated the interior decoration of the shuttle.
It has four windows through which the crew can observe the Earth, the Moon and other objects of the solar system without getting up from their seats.
The seats are made of high-quality carbon fiber and lined with alcantara.
The ship is equipped with an advanced system of ejection of the capsule with the crew in case of an accident.
When ejection astronauts experience overload similar to those that occur at attractions in Disneyland.

title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
text:
This content was published on March 20, 2019.
9: 26 in San Francisco.
March 20.
German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.
According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.
During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.
In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.
Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.
According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.
Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.
Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.
In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.
A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.
During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.
According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.
There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.
The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously.

title: Scientists: Global warming will give rise to hordes of hungry insect pests
text:
Scientists have long warned that global warming poses a significant threat to agriculture.
And it ’ s not just the loss of crops due to drought.
A new study shows that by 2050, a significant part of the crop will be eaten by hordes of hungry insects, for which rising temperatures mean rapid metabolism and a constant need for food, reports Day.Az with reference to Vesti.
The team, led by Curtis Deutsch of the University of Washington and Joshua Tewksbury of the University of Colorado, analyzed how insect pests eating three major crops — rice, corn and wheat — would respond to different climate scenarios.
Their calculations showed that with an increase in the average annual temperature of one degree, crop losses would increase by at least ten percent, and in the worst cases by all twenty-five.
At the same time, an increase in temperature of two degrees will lead to the loss of 213 million tons of grain.
"When the temperature rises, the metabolism of insects increases, so they should eat more, which is not good for crops," said co-author Scott Merrill of the University of Vermont.
As for the intensity of pest reproduction, there is no direct relationship.
The fact is that for each species there is a comfortable breeding temperature, with a deviation from which the increase in the number of insects decreases.
Therefore, the biggest crop problems can begin in temperate areas, while in the tropics the impact of warming will not be as noticeable.
According to forecasts, wheat, which is usually grown in cool climates, will suffer most from pest activity.
And the losses of the rice crop, the main production of which is carried out in warm countries, will stabilize (with an increase in temperature by three degrees since these conditions will no longer be comfortable for insects).
Corn is grown in different climatic zones, so its losses will vary depending on the region.
The greatest economic damage from the heating of the planet can get the United States, France and China, which are the largest producers of corn, and also grow a lot of wheat.
The attention of scientists to three crops is not accidental: corn, rice and wheat account for 42% of the calories consumed by the population of the Earth.
Thus, crop losses can cause food shortages (and armed conflicts), especially in countries where they are already present.
Fortunately, farmers still have time to prepare for the hard times and, together with science, find new ways to protect plants from pests.
Detailed results of the study are presented in the journal Science.

title: Monsanto's second defeat
text:
The second defeat in the US court suffered in the last 8 months Monsanto Company.
On Wednesday, the Federal District of San Francisco ordered the world leader of plant biotechnology to pay more than $80 million to Edwin Hardman.
The 70-year-old farmer, who for 25 years sprayed the most famous herbicide Monsanto Roundup on his site, was diagnosed with cancer of the lymphatic system.
During the trial, which lasted a month, the jury ruled that the plaintiff developed cancer as a result of the use of Roundup (the main active ingredient of which is glyphosate) and that Monsanto did not properly inform consumers about the dangers of its products.
German chemical company Bayer, which owns Monsanto Company today, said it was "disappointed by the jury's decision" and would appeal the verdict.
In the United States, another 11,000 Roundup lawsuits are on the way; six hearings are scheduled this year alone.
Since its purchase of Monsanto last June, Bayer has lost more than 45% of its market value.
The news of the second verdict further plunged into the "red" actions of the chemical giant.
The first person to win the case against Monsanto was school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who used the herbicide extensively.
In August last year, a California court ordered to pay him more than $289 million, later the amount of compensation was reduced to $78 million.

title: Da Vinci, Vermeer, Klimt: stolen and not found canvases
text:
Elena Korovushkina Author of Finparty All articles by Da Vinci, Vermeer, Klimt: stolen and not found canvases It is only in Hollywood action movies that famous works of art are stolen with the help of modern technology and super-skills of robbers.
In ordinary life, thieves are helped by the negligence of museum workers and the effect of surprise.
The New York Times writes about the disappearance of Leonardo da Vinci ’ s painting “Savior of the World ” worth $450 million
The information is still semi-official, perhaps a stir arose from scratch and the canvas is in the possession of its rightful owner - the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia.
However, there are no official refutations, the examination of the picture was canceled, and in September 2018, an exhibition was not held, where the Savior of the World was to become the highlight of the program.
Let da Vinci be found, but in the meantime we will remember other famous works of art, whose whereabouts remain unknown.
Jan Vermeer.
Date of disappearance: March 18, 1990 Location of disappearance: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum (Boston, USA) Estimated value: $200 million The Gardner Museum robbery is considered one of the largest art thefts in history.
13 works of art worth $500 million were stolen.
In the middle of the night, two men in police uniforms called the art gallery.
Allegedly, they heard a suspicious noise in the courtyard of the building and had to check if everything was in order.
Once inside, the robbers handcuffed two guards and froze in the halls for more than an hour.
They carved the paintings out of the frames, took with them a Chinese wine bowl and a bronze tip from the Napoleonic flag.
The most valuable of the stolen paintings was Vermeer ’ s “Concert ”.
Judging by the rudeness of the work and the illogical choice of works of art, there were amateurs at the Gardner Museum.
However, over the past 29 years, the stolen items have never been found, and empty frames hang on the site of the missing paintings.
In 2013, the FBI announced that it had found out the names of the criminals, but it turned out that they had already died.
The hype around the robbery was even parodied in The Simpsons: in one episode, the drunken father of the Homer family accidentally finds the “Concert ” in the house of his boss.
Gustav Klimt.
“Portrait of a Woman ” Period of Disappearance: 1996 – 1997 Place of Disappearance: Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art (Piacenza, Italy) Estimated Value: Unknown This work by Klimt hung quietly in the provincial Italian Museum, until a glazatnaya art student saw the similarity of the canvas with the“ Portrait of a Young Woman ”, which was considered lost in the 1910s.
The gallery director took an X-ray and discovered that one painting was written on top of another.
Immediately came to light a romantic story about how Klimt fell in love with a beautiful girl, but she died early, and the artist painted her portrait so as not to poison his soul.
On such a sensational occasion, the management of the museum decided to organize an exhibition and started repairs.
The director of the gallery later admitted that he wanted to stir up interest in the upcoming exhibition by faking the theft of the canvas.
But it turned out that “everything has already been stolen before us. ”
After a while, the museum noticed that in the turmoil of repairs Klimt ’ s painting really went somewhere, and it is not known exactly when.
Carabinieri found a frame from it on the roof of the gallery.
The investigation yielded unexpected results: there is no absolute certainty, but it seems that the stolen work was a skillful forgery, and the original disappeared a few months before the official disappearance.
Paul Cézanne.
"View of Auvers-sur-Oise" Date of disappearance: 1 January 2000 Place of disappearance: Ashmolean Museum (Oxford, UK) Estimated value: £3 million Good physical shape, scalpel, scotch, rope ladder, smoke bomb, small fan - this is all that it took an unknown robber to become the happy owner of an unfinished (but by no means unfinished) cheap) landscape of Cezanne.
On New Year ’ s Eve, when it was difficult to hear something because of the explosions of fireworks, the robber climbed onto the roof of the museum, cut a hole in the glass window on the ceiling, went down, smoked the surveillance cameras, stole the picture and disappeared in an unknown direction.
The whole theft took ten minutes.
Neither the painting nor the criminal was found, so the museum lost its only Cezanne.
Surely the management imagined the “year 2000 problem ” in a different way.
Vincent Van Gogh.
Maki Date of disappearance: August 21, 2010 Location of disappearance: Museum of Mohammed Mahmoud Khalil (Giza, Egypt) Estimated value: $50-55 million And it is also said that the projectile does not hit the same funnel twice.
With the Macs of Van Gogh, this is exactly what happened.
The painting was first stolen from an Egyptian museum in 1977, but found in Kuwait ten years later.
The management of the institution did not draw proper conclusions, and the canvas was stolen again in 2010.
As it turned out on hot tracks, in the gallery out of hand poorly protected exhibits from intruders: out of 43 surveillance cameras, only seven worked.
The guards were busy with their own affairs, so the criminal calmly moved the sofa, climbed onto it, cut the Maki out of the frame and took it with him unhindered.
Eleven employees of the Egyptian Ministry of Culture have been brought to trial on charges of negligence.
And the minister complained in an interview how he was tired of thinking alone about the safety of national museum treasures, how he woke up in the middle of the night from terrible dreams and how much he was tired of incompetent workers.
Auguste Renoir.
"Madeleine with flowers in her hair, leaning on the elbow" Date of disappearance: September 8, 2011 Place of disappearance: private house in Houston (USA) Estimated value: $1 million If your living room hangs the original Renoir, it is worth taking care of the safety of the room.
But even this does not always save collectors from unpleasant surprises.
The owner of a private house in Houston was watching TV in the evening when he heard a noise on the ground floor.
She fearlessly went to find out what was happening, and ran into an armed robber wearing a mask.
When he demanded money and jewelry, the hostess pointed to the picture on the wall, explaining that it is worth much more than anything else.
The woman, fortunately, was not injured, and the stolen Renoir is listed in the FBI ’ s “Top 10 Wanted Works of Art ” list.
Auguste Renoir.
“Bay, sea, green rocks ” Date of disappearance: November 28, 2018 Place of disappearance: Dorotheum auction house (Vienna, Austria) Estimated value: $130,000 – 180,000 Theft in the spirit of the“ Tretyakov Style ”.
Three criminals (one with a touching paper bag from the Ecco shoe store), without hiding, entered the auction house, climbed to the second floor, calmly removed the canvas, took it out of the frame and took it with them.
According to the report of the Association for the Investigation of Crimes against Art ARCA, the Dutch police arrested one of the suspects - a citizen of Ukraine Vadim Guzhva.
The same paper bag was found in his hotel room in Amsterdam.
At home, Guzhva was accused of stealing Aivazovsky ’ s painting in the Odessa Art Museum and Polenov ’ s work in Sevastopol.

title: The world's largest aircraft Stratolaunch made the first test flight - VIDEO
text:
The company Stratolaunch Systems conducted on Saturday in the West of the United States the first flight tests of the world's largest aircraft Stratolaunch, designed for the air launch of launch vehicles, reports Report with reference to TASS.
Photojournalists Matt Hartman and Jack Beyer confirmed this video.
"Stratolaunch managed to make its first flight," Hartman wrote on Twitter.
According to him, the flight took place over the Mojave Desert in California.
The company Stratolaunch Systems, which owns the aircraft, has not announced the test.
On the website and Twitter of the company there is no information about this flight, its speed and altitude.
The Stratolaunch consists of two 72-meter fuselages connected by a common wing with a length of 117 m. The aircraft is equipped with six Pratt & Whitney engines.
The weight is 250 tons, with a full load of about 590 tons. Movement on the runway provides a 28-wheel chassis.
Stratolaunch Systems was created in 2011 by American billionaire Paul Allen, one of the founders of Microsoft Corporation.
Allen died last year at the age of 65 after battling cancer.

Thus, the investigation will continue under the articles of the Criminal Code, which provide for liability for the intentional murder of two or more people and the destruction of the aircraft.

title: The French opened an investigation into the “daughter ” Bayer
text:
The French prosecutor ’ s office on Friday, May 10, opened a preliminary investigation against the company Monsanto.
She is accused of making a list of people who criticize the company ’ s products in order to later influence them.
The list includes about 200 people, including journalists and parliamentarians, according to French media.
The company, owned by the German concern Bayer since June 2018, has been the object of increased interest of law enforcement agencies for several months.
Monsanto ’ s weed killer contains the herbicide glyphosate.
In March, a San Francisco court found the chemical a "significant factor" in the development of cancer in a 70-year-old man who had been using it extensively for nearly three decades.
This is the first time the case has been brought before a U.S. federal court.
In total, there are almost 13 and a half thousand lawsuits against Monsanto in US courts.
In October 2018, a court in California ordered Monsanto to pay another victim with cancer 78 million dollars.
The jury found that glyphosate "significantly" contributed to the development of the disease in the 46-year-old man, who also used the company's products for several years.
According to the jury, Monsanto did not warn buyers that herbicides can lead to cancer.
WHO admits that glyphosate may be a carcinogen Experts do not agree on the effect of glyphosate on human health.
Earlier, the US Environmental Protection Agency and a number of regulatory bodies in the European Union reported that there were no risks of developing cancer as a result of the use of this herbicide.
In 2015, the World Health Organization (WHO) stated that the substance may be a carcinogen.
Monsanto is one of the leaders in the global market of genetically modified seeds and herbicides.
Glyphosate is widely used, including in Russia, where this chemical as a means of weed control is sold under the brands "Roundup", "Glyfor", "Tornado", "Hurricane". _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ Subscribe to DW news in | Twitter | Youtube | or install the DW application for | iOS | Android See also: Gallery: The largest mergers and acquisitions of German business abroad Bayer and Monsanto Based in Leverkusen, the pharmaceutical concern Bayer on September 14 agreed to acquire the American seed producer Monsanto for a record $66 billion.

title: Death in the garden: an American corporation found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide
text:
When the elderly Pilliod of California heard the fatal diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, they did not know that a few years later they would win a lawsuit against Monsanto, the world ’ s largest producer of chemicals for the agro-industrial complex.
However, this trial was only the tip of the iceberg, because thousands of Americans with cancer caused by Monsanto products are ready to file similar lawsuits.
Izvestia found out what transnational corporations are ready to do for billions of dollars in profits.
The manufacturer does not warn Alberta and Alva Pilliod began using Monsanto's Roundup herbicide to kill weeds in 1975.
Roundup was a novelty: Monsanto employee John Franz synthesized the active ingredient of the herbicide, glyphosate, only in 1970.
The couple bought Roundup for four decades, until in 2011 Alva heard a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system with lesions of the bones, including the spine.
Four years later, non-Hodgkin lymphoma was found in his wife Alberta, but with brain damage.
In 2017, the couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto, based on the fact that two years earlier, the International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate.
In addition, their claim was not the first: at that time, the courts had already considered several similar complaints.
The case was accelerated due to the poor health of the plaintiffs, who at that time were already in their 70s, and on May 14, 2019, the jury decided after five weeks of consideration that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks, in connection with which it must pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages in favor of the plaintiffs.
This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.
Monsanto Roundup sprayers in a garden shop Photo: REUTERS / Yves Herman Representatives of the owner of Monsanto - the German concern Bayer - said that they do not agree with the decision and will appeal because "all the world's leading health organizations agree on the safety of glyphosate and its non-carcinogenicity" It seems that justice has been served, greedy industries the nics got what they deserved, and the ordinary people who suffered from their actions left as winners.
If not for a few “but ”: first, victory in court will not save the lives of cancer patients.
And, secondly, the compensation awarded to them to the Pilliod spouses will not receive soon and in the wrong volumes.
The fact is that, according to a 2016 ruling of the US Supreme Court, the amount of the fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.
Thus, even if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments to the maximum possible, the Pilliod spouses will receive, in addition to their compensatory $55 million, only $495 million.
This is the most favorable outcome for the plaintiffs.
Throughout the process, Monsanto ’ s lawyers argued that their products were harmless, as confirmed by research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), a federal agency that develops and monitors compliance with environmental and human health standards.
Moreover, in April, the EPA confirmed its initial findings, saying that while glyphosate use does entail some environmental risks, the agency ’ s findings on its impact on human health are consistent with those of other federal agencies.
“If we are going to feed 10 billion people by 2050, we will need all the tools at our disposal, including glyphosate, ” U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said in a statement.
Monsanto ’ s defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, and Bayer said after the verdict that the decision would not have been so harsh if the scientists ’ findings had been taken into account.
According to the defendant, Alva and Alberta Pilliod suffered from various diseases for a long time, which became the main factor in the development of cancer.
The concern also noted that if it were not for glyphosate, which is poured into fields to destroy weeds, the soil would have to be plowed regularly, which is expensive and harmful to the environment, since a large amount of carbon dioxide is emitted due to the overturning of the earth.
During the judicial investigation, it turned out that those conclusions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which the company refers to more than once as a justification for the safety of Roundup, can be questioned.
Demonstrators protest against Bayer Monsanto on the Place de la République in Paris Photo: REUTERS / Philippe Wojazer At the disposal of CNN was the correspondence of a Monsanto employee with one of the Agency officials Jess Rowland.
In it, a federal employee notes that if he can “kill ” glyphosate research at the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances and Diseases, he will“ deserve a medal. ”
Monsanto employees in internal correspondence note a low probability that Rowland and the EPA will be able to stop the study of another agency, but note that there is hope.
Judging by the fact that the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, Rowland, already happily retired, coped with the task.
The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.
In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.
The first lawsuit against Monsanto was considered by the court last year.
In August, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer.
However, a few months later, the judge reduced this amount to $78 million.
The case did not end there, as Bayer filed an appeal.
As a result, after almost a year, the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded to him.
In March this year, a California resident was awarded $80 million after he sued Monsanto for developing non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
The result is predictable: Bayer appealed, far from the outcome.
Thus, the concern is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products.
In addition, there are about 130,000 such claims under consideration in the United States.
And even for a giant like Bayer, it ’ s a pretty sensitive punch.
Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.
Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.
According to The Fortune, Bayer shareholders told the company ’ s CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence.
He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place.
Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves.
Despite this, in 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years.
Photo: Global Look Press / Christian Charisius / dpa In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015.
Also in the country you can freely buy the herbicide Roundup, both wholesale and retail.
In addition, Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000).
The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year.
Monsanto is no stranger to scandals with seven-mile-long steps: since the 1980s, the company has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War.
In addition, several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002.
So why are the US, EU and other countries stubbornly renewing the license to use glyphosate-containing herbicides?
Thanks to the more than $4 million that, according to OpenSecrets, Monsanto spends annually on lobbying?
Or because otherwise you will have to use more expensive ways to control weeds, which will reduce the effectiveness of soil use? bed Red-brown grass after treatment with a herbicide Photo: Depositphotos Probably, each of the reasons can be called correct.
World agriculture is dependent on chemical fertilizers, the former methods of tillage already seem ineffective.
Governments and world leaders are thinking about how to feed millions of people, forgetting that they may be losing their health.
In addition, the harm of glyphosate has not been proven, and this makes it possible to sleep peacefully.

title: NASA's $2.5 billion mission aims to find signs of life on Mars
text:
NASA ’ s mission to search for signs of life on Mars will involve a new generation of rover that explores the delta of the river age of 3.5 billion years.
Susan Carlin of the Fast Company visited the "clean room" (hall for assembling precision instruments, in which air quality is strictly controlled - approx. ed.)
NASA ’ s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and found out how the development of a new spacecraft is progressing.
JPL ’ s “Clean Room ” is similar to the television room in Willie Wonka and the Chocolate Factory: it ’ s a flawlessly clean room where people in white jumpsuits and masks engage in technological magic.
But instead of a camera that turns children into miniature figures, the centerpiece here is the new Mars 2020 rover that NASA plans to send to Mars this summer.
Although Mars 2020 does not pose the same challenge to the laws of physics as the Wonka camera, it is no less magical for one good reason: this device may finally answer the question of whether there was life on Mars.
Journalists are interviewing engineers working on the Mars 2020 mission.
The photo was taken in JPL ’ s “clean room ” on December 27, 2019.
Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech In the last days of 2019, JPL, located in Pasadena, California, provided journalists with a rare opportunity to see High Bay 1, a spacious “clean room ” with a constant online broadcast, where NASA engineers are designing the Mars 2020 rover, as well as systems for descent to the planet and a seven-month journey on it.
Strict control of temperature, humidity and working processes in this room minimizes biological pollution, as well as the amount of dust and particulate matter that can interfere with electronics.
It requires strict rules for guests.
Before entering the “clean room ” we put on“ bunny suits ” – white polyester overalls, boots and hoods, as well as surgical masks and latex gloves glued to the sleeves.
We are also led through the cabin, where strong air currents remove microscopic debris from workwear.
It is not allowed to have cosmetics, perfumes, clothes made of wool and with torn edges, as well as fabric straps on cameras.
At the very door of technology wipe cameras and smartphones with alcohol.
JPL employees can only use unscented shampoos and one type of deodorant, and taking a shower before entering the “clean room ” is prohibited.
Even the High Bay Bob clean room mascot, a mannequin wearing bright green Christmas style sunglasses, wears a white protective suit.
“We don ’ t want to send a spacecraft to Mars and then say, ‘ Hey, there ’ s my hair. ’
All the rules about what you can ’ t do or bring with you are designed to protect the scientific component of this mission, ” said David Gruel, Mars 2020 Assembly, Testing and Launch Manager.
In search of life, Mars 2020, which JPL began building in 2011, will be the first rover to search for evidence that microorganisms lived on Mars in the past.
It will be engaged in drilling, analysis and collection of geological samples from areas that previously could have been inhabited.
It is assumed that future missions will return them to Earth in 2026 for more detailed study.
The launch of Mars 2020 is the first step towards a goal that JPL began discussing back in the 1980s and which eventually became a campaign to obtain geological samples from Mars.
After studying them, some important questions will be answered in the laboratory.
“Could life have formed on Mars, did it happen, and if not, why? ” — quotes the Director of JPL Michael Watkins.
The $2.5 billion project will also test the technologies humans will need for a long-term stay on Mars.
These include tools that improve landing, produce oxygen from Martian air rich in carbon dioxide, determine the composition of soil and groundwater, and record weather conditions.
Among the projects, there is even a small solar-powered helicopter, which is designed for flights taking into account the Martian atmosphere and reduced gravity.
This spring, NASA will announce the official name of Mars 2020, selected from more than 9 million options.
The rover will be launched from Cape Canaveral in Florida during the July-August window, landing on Mars is scheduled for February 8, 2021.
The device will begin its journey around the planet from the crater Jezero, the basin of an ancient lake, where in the past there was a high probability of life.
The mission will last at least one Martian year (approximately 687 Earth days) and cover up to 12 miles (more than 19 km).
One of the most serious problems in the operation of the “clean room ” is the danger of particulate pollution, and the other is the protection of highly sensitive electronics.
Special tape barriers keep reporters a short distance from mechanics to prevent accidental electrostatic discharges.
"The human body is made up of so much water that it is able to conduct electricity.
Electric shock from walking on the carpet and touching the door handle is about 20 thousand volts.
You can damage some of these high-speed electronic devices using just five volts.
We reduce this risk by controlling electrostatic discharge, ” said James Sean Howard, Head of Equipment Inspection at Mars 2020.
To do this, the equipment is surrounded by air ionizers, which neutralize static electricity, filling the air with positively and negatively charged ions.
The “clean room ” also maintains a humidity level above 30%, which makes the air more conductive and allows it to absorb and distribute excess charges.
When engineers work on mechanics, they connect special bracelets to a wire that returns electricity to the ground to prevent sparks.
Protective suits also contain carbon elements to relieve static stress from the fabric.
Faraday cells and electrostatic discharge needles — metal spikes on the outer surface of the rover — will protect electronics on Mars.
Another significant obstacle is the complexity of the instruments and moving parts, many of which the rover displays only after landing.
It uses more than 30 systems that control moving elements.
“Each of these mechanisms, gearboxes and engines is made up of hundreds of small parts, and they all have to be designed, analyzed, assembled and tested.
It ’ s hard to make them super reliable.
And, of course, there is no way to fix them on Mars, ” said Matt Wallace, deputy project manager for Mars 2020.
An engineering model of the Mars 2020 rover is being tested on Mars Yard, an area that mimics Martian conditions.
Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech Protecting a system from Earth pollution that will place samples of Martian soil in test tubes is especially important.
"The front third of the rover is equipped with a mechanism similar to a Swiss watch, which takes a sample from a robotic arm, evaluates it and seals it tightly in a test tube.
To work on this equipment, a second set of sterile gloves was required, ” says engineer Zach Ousnamer.
The Mars 2020 rover borrowed a lot from Curiosity, while developing new technologies.
It is slightly larger than Curiosity: its length is 10 feet (about 3 m, not including a folding 9-foot robotic arm), width is 9 feet (about 2.7 m), height is 7 feet (about 2.1 m) and weight is 2,314 pounds (more than a ton).
Like Curiosity, Mars 2020 is powered by a combination of nuclear, battery and solar energy.
Its six aluminum wheels have a stronger construction and coating to avoid dents, holes and broken treads that interfered with Curiosity.
The Mars 2020 descent and landing system will repeat the stunning decline of Curiosity, known from the video “Seven Minutes of Horror ”.
Mars 2020 will travel to Mars in a protective airshell consisting of an upper skin and a lower heat-shielding shield.
A circular descent stage with eight brake rockets will be attached to the rover like a jet backpack that will drop it to the surface of the planet.
A few minutes before that, the parachute on the top of the airshell will slow the descent of the device until the need for a heat-shielding screen disappears and it comes off.
At this point, the descent stage will detach from the upper skin, release brake missiles towards the surface of Mars to slow down the descent, and ensure a careful landing of the rover.
Then it will detach, fly away and fall at some distance.
This time, several new onboard technologies will provide more controlled descent maneuvering, accurate landing, and data collection for future missions.
The device will also include a set of cameras and microphones to view what is happening in the first person and listen to the sounds of the landing.
The sensors will measure the temperature of the upper skin and the lower heat shield.
One navigation system will control the descent, focusing on the time of deployment of the parachute and the position of the spacecraft relative to the descent point.
The second will help land, highlighting the dangerous terrain during the descent by comparing fresh images of the approaching surface with a pre-loaded map of Mars.
Once on the surface of Mars, seven instruments — selected from 58 proposals around the world and including the development of the French, Spanish and Norwegian — will conduct a geological assessment of the area in which the rover descended to try to detect signs of ancient Martian life.
Curiosity confirmed that Mars had suitable conditions for microscopic life forms.
Mars 2020 will look for evidence of this in the form of biological features — chemical and molecular fossils.
Jezero crater 3.5 billion years ago contained a lake and a river delta, and the rocks formed in the water can preserve evidence of life there.
Mars 2020 has the tools to take geological samples, analyze them and store them in 43 test-tube containers, which it will leave on the surface of Mars for later retrieval.
This will require the launch of a separate mission, because the landing system cannot deliver both the rover and the probe to transport samples.
The system for searching for life includes modern cameras that can produce panoramic and stereoscopic survey and analysis of minerals, radar for underground research and spectrometers for the study of minerals and organic compounds.
Unlike Curiosity, Mars 2020 cameras will shoot colors for image spectroscopy, which can determine the chemical composition of samples.
Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech Scientists are looking for not so much fragments of microorganisms as residual chemical traces.
The spectrometer, called SHERLOC — short for “Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics and Chemicals ” — will emit ultraviolet rays to get a spectral analysis of the extracted samples.
This will help determine their composition and see, for example, the presence of nitrates or chlorates.
"All of this will signal that there is a chance of finding biological signatures in a particular sample, and so we should send it to Earth," explains SHERLOC principal investigator Luther Beagle.
Mars 2020 will also help future robotic and human missions on Mars by testing how certain technologies work in the Martian environment.
The on-board ground-based weather station will measure the temperature, pressure, size and shape of the dust to better understand the composition of Mars' atmosphere and winds.
The rover will also test the production of oxygen from carbon dioxide and perform 90-second test flights and aerial photography with a small helicopter attached to its bottom.
If successful, it will be the first flight to another planet.
"We hope to answer the fundamental question of whether life could have evolved elsewhere than Earth.
We have reached the threshold of this question, now it is time to go through the door, ” Wallace concluded.

title: Rouhani said that the authorities should create a special court in the case of the downed missile “Boeing ”
text:
Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said that all those responsible for the unintentional hit of missiles on a Ukrainian passenger plane near Tehran should be brought to justice by a special tribunal.
According to the Iranian president, the tragedy that occurred with the Ukrainian airliner is not an ordinary case that requires the authorities to create a special court chaired by the supreme judge, with the participation of the most professional experts in this field.
It is known that the flight PS752 of the international airline Ukraine followed to Kiev.
On board were mainly Iranian and Canadian passengers.
The plane crashed a few minutes after take-off near the capital of Iran.
In their initial assessments, Iranian officials attributed the crash to a technical failure and rejected the possibility that the plane was shot down by missiles.
However, after a thorough investigation, the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces issued a statement in which it admitted that the Ukrainian plane was shot down by a missile fired “unintentionally ” because of“ human error. ”

title: British and French authorities detain more than 70 illegal immigrants
text:
The authorities of the UK and France detained on Saturday 74 migrants who made an illegal attempt to cross the English Channel at night in a northerly direction and settle in the United Kingdom.
This is reported by TASS with reference to the British Ministry of the Interior.
According to him, the migrants went on the journey in eight small boats, but only one of them managed to reach the British coast and land people on the beach near the camp in the town of Winchelsea in East Sussex.
Two more boats were detained on the high seas by the French border services, and the remaining five by the British.
"The number of migrants crossing the strait at night is a matter of deep concern," Home Secretary Sajid Javid said.
According to him, “those who chose this dangerous journey on one of the busiest shipping routes in the world are putting their lives in mortal danger. ”
The Minister also promised that he would do everything in his power to stop the flow of violators of the regime of crossing the British sea border.

title: Border guards detained 74 refugees trying to cross the English Channel
text:
British border guards detained 74 refugees who tried to intercept the English Channel on boats and illegally enter the territory of the Kingdom.
One of the eight boats managed to disembark passengers near a camping site in the British town of Winchelsea.
Among the detainees were several children.
Two more boats were detained on the high seas by the French border services, and the remaining five by the British, reports the Independent.
Last month alone, more than 140 people attempted to cross the English Channel.
All of them were detained.
In November last year, London and Paris agreed to work together to combat criminal gangs that smuggle illegal immigrants from the mainland.
A clearing house has been established.
The UK has also increased the number of patrol vessels in the strait.
Refugees are looking for every opportunity to cross the English Channel and find themselves in the UK, where they are attracted to the social program and the possibility of receiving benefits.

title: It is time to change the packaging of household chemicals
text:
Check of household liquid "KROT" has begun.
A conclusion will be presented on its results.
About this "Russian newspaper" reported in Rospotrebnadzor.
The resonant case of poisoning with a means for cleaning pipes of the famous producer and musician Bari Alibasov revealed a serious problem: the packaging of hazardous household chemicals can pose a threat to human life and health.
And the rules of its design must be changed.
As explained in Rospotrebnadzor, today the requirements for the labeling of household chemicals are contained in the Unified sanitary and epidemiological and hygienic requirements for products (goods) subject to sanitary and epidemiological supervision (control).
For example, consumer labeling of synthetic detergents and household chemicals should be applied with clear, legible, easily visible and indelible letters, resistant to chemicals, climatic factors, and persist throughout the entire period of use of the product.
Bottles containing household chemicals, in particular, should contain information on the composition of products and "other data that clearly distinguish a particular product from other products on the market."
There should also be a description of the danger that carries such products, measures to prevent the danger.
For example, such inscriptions: "Keep away from children!", "Keep out of the reach of children", "The product has an irritating effect on the skin", "The use of hand skin protection products is mandatory."
"I am sure that all household chemicals that are sold in stores are of high quality and meet the requirements for labeling.
After all, no one will deliberately harm the health of consumers, creating this anti-advertising.
But life, as always, makes its own adjustments, - said in an interview with "RG" the Chairman of the Union of consumers of Russia Peter Shelishch. - The case of Alibasov proved: the packaging of some household chemicals needs to be changed.
I saw a photo posted by someone from Alibasov's entourage, with bottles of pipe cleaning liquid and yogurt.
I think it ’ s easy to confuse them. ”
Shelishch recalls that on packs of cigarettes now there are very catchy "scary pictures" and large inscriptions about the dangers of tobacco.
And on the packaging of household chemicals warning labels still need to be found and read.
"Yes, they comply with all the rules, but then these rules and regulations are not enough to protect the consumer, - the expert notes. - Unfortunately, there are no statistics on how many people are poisoned with household chemicals.
But according to scattered reports, it can be understood that the case of Alibasov is not the only one.
Perhaps you need to write in very large letters on the packages that their contents should not be drunk.
And it is even better to make difficult opening plugs.
Drug manufacturers are making them to protect children. "
Relatives of the producer intend to file a lawsuit against the manufacturer of the means for cleaning the pipes.
How realistic is it to win a case in court?
"The case of Alibasov is regrettable, I wish him a speedy recovery, - says the head of the commercial practice of the law firm Denis Frolov. - But filing a lawsuit against the manufacturer - it will be more a PR action than a real attempt to obtain compensation.
On the goods of household chemicals are always indicated instructions for use and warnings in case of their violation.
If the consumer, despite this, confuses these goods with edible products, it is not the fault of the manufacturer.
However, the court will accept the claim if it formally meets the requirements of the law.
Another thing is that there are practically no prospects for such a case, since there are no grounds for satisfying the plaintiff ’ s claims under the existing legislation. ”
But in any case, it will draw attention to the problem.
And the labeling rules will still be tightened, as Peter Shelisch suggests.
The courts of the state of California in the United States in recent months have several times obliged the company Monsanto, part of the structure of Bayer, to pay huge compensation to consumers for the lack of warnings on the package about the carcinogenicity of one of its products.
This is glyphosate, a worldwide weed killer known under the brand name Roundup.
For example, in May, a jury awarded astronomical compensation of $2 billion to a couple from California ’ s Oakland.
A San Francisco court ordered Monsanto to pay $80 million to farmer Edwin Hardman.
The lion ’ s share of this payment is a fine for the fact that Monsanto, according to the jury, deliberately did not impose appropriate warnings on the packaging and, moreover, sponsored studies that proved the safety of this herbicide.
The victims claimed that due to the lack of warnings on the package, glyphosate was sprayed for years and safely allowed the substance to fall on unprotected skin.
Later, they were diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and, as the jury considered, the herbicide is to blame.
Monsanto insists that studies clearly do not confirm the carcinogenicity of glyphosate and fiercely challenges these resonant verdicts.
After all, several thousand similar lawsuits are now waiting for their turn in the courts.
Prepared by Igor Dunaevsky

title: World's Largest Aircraft to Sell for $400 Million
text:
The price includes ownership of the aircraft, intellectual property and infrastructure related to the project.
The holding company Vulcan late co-founder of Microsoft Paul Allen plans to sell the project associated with the world ’ s largest carrier aircraft Stratolaunch for $400 million.
About it reports CNBC with reference to informed sources, reports RIA Novosti.
The carrier aircraft of the Stratolaunch project is designed to launch rockets into orbit from an altitude of 9.1 thousand meters.
Initially, venture aerospace company Stratolaunch Systems plans to launch a Pegasus XL cruise missile, which is designed to launch commercial satellites into low Earth orbit.
In the future, the aircraft will be able to carry up to three missiles.
In mid-April, the world's largest carrier aircraft Stratolaunch made its first flight.
The plane took off from a test site in the Mojave Desert (California), the flight lasted 2.5 hours at an altitude of more than 5 kilometers with a maximum speed of 304 kilometers per hour.
During the first flight, the pilots evaluated flight characteristics.
According to the channel, the price includes the right to own the aircraft, intellectual property and infrastructure associated with the project.
Sources told the TV channel that the company appealed to British businessman Richard Branson to sell the project to the conglomerate Virgin Group, but the billionaire allegedly in response offered a symbolic $1 for the rights to the project.
The channel adds that neither Stratolaunch nor Vulcan commented on the information about the sale, but a representative of the company told him that the plane is ready for operation.

title: The plane with the largest wingspan in the world will be put up for sale. PHOTOS
text:
This is reported by the CTC with reference to CNBC, reports BusinessCensor.
The holding company Vulcan, owned by the late billionaire and initiator of the Stratolaunch project Paul Allen, is now seeking to sell Stratolaunch, sources familiar with the matter said.
The price of $400 million includes not only the ownership of the aircraft itself, but also intellectual property rights to it and the related infrastructure.
The aircraft was planned to be used as an aerial platform for launching launch vehicles to deliver cargo to low Earth orbit.
Several options were studied for what kind of rockets Stratolaunch was supposed to put into orbit - the first partner was Elon Musk's SpaceX, then the choice fell on Northrop Grumman Orbital and the Pegasus XL launch vehicle.
The Stratolaunch project to create its own fleet of missiles was curtailed in January this year.
As Reuters informs, this year the Stratolaunch project is steadily declining - most of the workers have already been laid off.
And, despite plans to launch the Northrop rocket in 2020, the company is in the process of winding down operations.
According to one of the sources, one of the factors holding back the sale of Stratolaunch at the moment is an internal disagreement between the company ’ s CEO Gene Floyd and Allen ’ s sister Jody, who is the head of Vulcan, as well as the manager of its assets.
Floyd states that Vulcan supports the Stratolaunch program, especially by preserving the company's intellectual property, and Jody Allen would like to sell the company directly.
One of the main potential buyers of the media called Richard Branson, but, according to available information, he is not ready to pay the asking price for the plane.
Two months ago, Stratolaunch made its first and so far only flight, starting from the aerodrome of the aerospace test center in the Mojave desert.
The aircraft was in the air for more than two hours, the flight was carried out successfully.
The unusual aircraft is equipped with six engines from the Boeing 747 aircraft.
The wingspan of the Stratolaunch is 117 meters (this is the largest wingspan of an aircraft in the history of world aviation), length - 73 m, weight - 230 tons.
According to calculations, it will be able to lift up to 250 tons of cargo into the air.
Ukrainian An-225 "Mriya" with a wingspan of 88 m, a length of 84 m and a weight of 250 tons has a maximum take-off weight of 640 tons.
