title: The West is ready to invest in Russian medicine
text:
According to international estimates, in terms of the attractiveness of medical and health tourism, Russia ranks fifth in the world.
It is understandable: the prices for medical services bite us not as much as in the West, and their quality is still at a height.
According to the data, which is officially advertised by the Ministry of Health, in 2017 (there are no more recent ones yet) about 100 thousand foreign patients received medical care from us as part of this medical tourism.
The revenue amounted to $250 million – exactly a quarter of the amount that the government planned for this type of export for 2024.
A couple of months ago, a coordination center was created at the Ministry of Health, which will help the regions to equip medical tourism (MT), local passports of the project were approved (it is called “Development of Export of Medical Services ” and has a federal status), that is, the municipal authorities received an official document on the basis of which they can further form a budget for the benefit of all visiting patients. There was a minimal understanding of how to do it, - says Yevgeny Chernyshev, president of the National Council of Medical Tourism. - Today we see obvious signs that this is not another newfangled export idea, but a very systemic market that will develop rapidly.
Uniform pricing standards are introduced for foreign tourists.
Insurance companies began to actively sell them health insurance.
An indirect signal is the annual growth of the incoming tourist flow, and legislative initiatives (for example, the recently adopted law on telemedicine), and the opening abroad of representative offices of Russian medicine, so that the patient after returning home has the opportunity to receive post-treatment observation.
There is an active international certification of our clinics, which have already appreciated the benefits of MT.
For example, now one of the largest private medical centers in Moscow allocates a whole wing of its hospital exclusively for foreign patients and in the future plans to open a center of specialized care for IVF only counting on tourists from Southeast Asia and Europe.
In general, the process is underway, and on an increasing basis.
But in this process it would be nice to be guided by the interests of the customer, said Andy Freca, Director of the Consulting company "American": - Half a year ago, your official structures handed me a list of federal medical centers from Moscow and St. Petersburg and asked me to make an appointment there in English.
For the experiment.
And I was a little surprised.
For example, one site was written in English, but not a word was understood.
In another hospital with the translation was all OK, but when I got to the application form, it somehow turned out to be in Russian (and this is about the same as Arabic or Georgian for you).
On the third site, everything was fine until I read the last paragraph: “The patient will arrange a visa and an interpreter for himself. ”
In general, this is not the service that a foreign client will run to.
In Russia, there is such a repair - called "under the euro".
It makes me very sad when you say that.
You should not provide European-level medicine, you should do it better, but do not forget about identity.
It is not necessary in the intervals between procedures to place a foreign patient in the Holiday Inn hotel, it is at his home.
Send him to the sanatorium, let him go for a massage, in the sauna, under Charcot's shower, eat local dishes.
It will be a pleasant bonus for him.
And then on his return, he will definitely tell all his relatives not only about the sanatorium, but also about the benefits of treatment in Russia in general.
DIRECT SPEECH Marina Melgunova, Advisor to MEDIGO in Russia: — In the course of assessing the export potential of Russian medical services among 71 regions of the country (14 for a number of reasons preferred to withdraw), at least five leaders have already been identified.
These are Tyumen, Kaliningrad, St. Petersburg, Moscow and Primorye.
The most popular among foreign tourists are now our reproductive technologies, dentistry, plastic surgery, traumatology, orthopedics and ophthalmology.
There is also a great potential for health and rehabilitation tourism - our sanatoriums and health resorts.

title: Kiev asks Iran to transfer the “black boxes ” of the UIA aircraft
text:
The Ukrainian side is taking all measures to ensure proper decoding of the black boxes and preservation of evidence in the investigation of the circumstances of the crash of the Ukrainian International Airlines flight shot down by the Iranian military, the Office of the Prosecutor General informed.
The Office of the Prosecutor General and the Security Service of Ukraine appealed to the competent authorities of the Islamic Republic of Iran with a request for legal assistance related to the transfer to Ukrainian law enforcement officers of flight recorders (black boxes) from the Boeing 737 aircraft of Ukraine International Airlines, which operated flight PS752 Tehran Kiev and was shot down by the Iranian military, the press service of the Office reported on January 15.
"The Ukrainian side is taking all measures to ensure proper decoding of flight recorders and preservation of evidence in the investigation of the circumstances of the crash," the statement said.
The Office of the Prosecutor General noted that “based on the results of processing data obtained as a result of cooperation with international partners, as well as from Ukrainian law enforcement officers and experts from the scene of the tragedy, and given Iran ’ s recognition of the downing of the UIA aircraft by the military of this country, the Office of the Prosecutor General decided to change the qualification of the criminal offense for which the proceedings were opened. ”
The GPU asks the Cabinet of Ministers to increase fines for violation of fire safety requirements "The investigation will continue under the articles of the Criminal Code of Ukraine, providing for responsibility for the intentional murder of two or more people and the destruction of the aircraft.
The pre-trial investigation was entrusted to the Main Investigation Department of the SBU, "the press service added.
A passenger plane Boeing 737-800 flight PS752 of Ukraine International Airlines crashed on January 8 near Tehran shortly after takeoff.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
No one survived.
Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau on January 9, citing intelligence data, said that the Boeing 737-800 was shot down by an Iranian surface-to-air missile.
The same was stated by British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison.
They assumed it was unintentional.
According to the American media, there were two missiles.
In Iran, at first, this version was called a lie.
On January 11, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Iran said that the UIA plane was shot down by the Iranian military by mistake.
The ministry said that the disaster occurred shortly after Iran shelled US military bases in Iraq.
The aircraft, as stated in the message, approached one of the important objects of the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and “the shape and height of the flight resembled an enemy object. ”
The black boxes of the downed plane will be transferred to France for decoding, Iran said.
On January 11, the French Bureau of Investigation and Analysis of Civil Aviation Safety announced that it would take part in the technical work.
The report indicates that the Iranian authorities are responsible for the investigation schedule.
On January 14, the president of Ukraine International Airlines, Yevgeny Dykhne, said that the black boxes of the downed plane were likely to be deciphered in Ukraine.
One of the leaders of the group that leads the investigation Updated at 10: 06 January 15 in Kiev waiting for the head of the aviation authorities of Iran Updated at 11: 51 The case is being investigated under the articles of the Criminal Code of Ukraine, providing for responsibility for the intentional murder of two or more people and the destruction of the aircraft.

title: Turkish series "Windy": the content of all the series
text:
A new 12-episode story about love and revenge in modern Turkey has already won the hearts of Russian viewers.
The first chance to taste Turkish TV series residents of our country received about 30 years ago - after the release of the film adaptation of the novel Reshad Nuri Guntekin "King - songbird".
Love, jealousy, family secrets - everything that viewers love so much was present in this series.
Now, when times have changed, Turkish cinema gives us much more interesting series with a variety of plot – from historical, as “The Magnificent Age ”, to the most modern.
And in each of them, as before, laid the foundation that so attracts film lovers - a fascinating story, beautiful actors, and national musical motifs background.
This year, the “First channel ” pleased the Russians with the series“ Sultan of my heart ”, which starred, including our actors.
If you are already tired of reviewing it, the portal Teleprogramma.pro is ready to advise you and other quality series come from Turkey.
For example, excellent reviews were awarded to the recently released series “Windy ”.
We have already watched it and compiled for you the content of all 12 episodes.
Young Beauty Rayyan Shatoglu in his home does not feel his own.
She has a loving mother, father and younger sister, Gul, but the head of the family, grandfather Nasukh Shatoglu, for some reason never showed affection for Rayyan.
From him she received only cuffs and reproaches.
One morning, a girl takes a horse and, while everyone is asleep, goes to her favorite place on the edge of the mountain.
On the way back, the horse is almost hit by the car of a 27-year-old guy named Miran Aslanbey - he came to their town of Midyat under the guise of a businessman from Istanbul, made a major deal with the Shatoglu family, and now he was witness to their Reyan fall from the horse to the ground.
He took the girl home and took the opportunity to ask the family for her hand.
However, Nasukh Shatoglu instead of one granddaughter offered another - the daughter of his youngest son, Yaren, who had seen Miran before and managed to fall in love with him.
But for some reason, the guy needs Rayyan.
It turns out that he considers the Shatoglu family his blood enemies and intends to destroy them, using an innocent girl for this.
2 series Rayyan, as it turned out, is needed not only Miran.
Her uncle ’ s son Azat has been in love with her since childhood and now, when she can get to another, he can no longer hide his feelings.
In fact, Reyan is not his cousin, because Khazar Shatoglu is not her own father, he married her mother when she was 17 years old and remained a widow.
Gradually, Rayyan falls in love with Miran and it goes to the wedding.
Azat tries to prevent this, but he does not succeed.
Yaren, burning with envy, tears up the wedding dress of her cousin, and her mother has to give her bride her, which she kept for many years.
The wedding was played and now Miran ’ s revenge moves into the final stage.
He likes Reyan, his cruel heart, previously knowing nothing but a thirst for revenge, slowly thaws.
But his grandmother, Azizeh Aslanbey, instigates the young man, not allowing him to forget about the parents, allegedly killed by the girl ’ s father, Khazar.
Miran and Reyan leave the wedding, near the house after their departure, drunk and heartbroken Azat begins to shoot with a gun.
One of the bullets hits baby Gul.
Newlyweds spend their first wedding night in an abandoned hut.
Reyan doesn ’ t know that this night should be the last – her husband dresses and leaves, leaving her alone.
The guy just used it, and the marriage wasn't real.
A fire starts in the hut, the girl no longer wants to live and stays inside.
At the last moment, she is taken out of the fire by the guard Azizé.
They bring a poor girl dressed in a wedding dress to the main square of the city and throw her out of the car.
For the Shatoglu family, this is a great shame, because Reyan does not immediately decide to go home - for some time she sleeps in the house of an old man who took pity on her and let her into his house.
In the hospital, meanwhile, the struggle for Gul ’ s life continues.
Doctors carry out a successful operation, but the bullet that hit the girl ’ s head, they are forced to leave inside in order to avoid the risk of brain damage.
Miran suffers, remembering how cruelly he acted with his beloved.
He tries to find her and take her away from the family, because after such shame, Shadoglu can kill her.
Her grandfather trusts Azat, although he, of course, is not going to harm her.
Azat takes her out of town, but on the bridge they are blocked by the car of Miran and his friend Firat.
While the men argue and threaten each other with weapons, Rayyan jumps from the bridge into the river.
Miran rushes after, finds her under the water and takes her to the shore.
The girl is very offended, she does not want to talk to her savior.
Soon they are found by Firat and taken to his mother ’ s house, where no one lives.
They spend the night there.
Miran repents, he gives Rayan a gun and she shoots him in the chest.
Later, she herself, under his strict guidance, pulls out the bullet.
In the hospital, Gul wakes up after the operation, she wants to see her sister, but no one knows where she disappeared.
Miran brings Reyan to his home, which does not please Gönul - his cousin, whom he is actually married, but never touched her with a finger.
Gönul then tries to strangle Reyan with a pillow in his sleep, but wants to take his own life.
Meanwhile, Yaren continues to plot and meets with Firat to find out useful information.
Gul refuses to eat, wanting to see his sister.
Her mother Zehra came to the house of the Aslanbeys and asks to give her daughter.
Miran says he only wants to save the girl from the wrath of her grandfather Nasukh.
The insidious Yaren helped to organize a meeting of Reyan with her sister Gul - the girl and Miran came to the Shadoglu mansion at night and Reyan was able to communicate with her sister.
When they were about to leave, Nasukh caught them and wanted to kill them, but Gul appeared in time and the old man was forced to release the uninvited guests.
Gönul intends to tell Reyan that she is Miran ’ s real wife, but she fails to pull it off.
Reyan is hysterically smashing the room.
Shadoglu and Aslanbei meet to discuss business issues.
Aziza Aslanbey offers to repay the debt to Shadoglu, if they give her their mansion.
While everyone is busy with their own business, Aziz ’ s granddaughter, Elif, runs away from home, and her grandmother thinks she was stolen by Shadoglu.
Miran brings Rayyan to her favorite place, where on the edge of the abyss he set up a swing before the wedding.
Then they go to the house where she shot him.
While Miran is not in the house, Azat and Gönul come there.
The latter tells Rayyan that she and Miran are married.
Shocked by this news, the girl leaves with Azat.
On the way, they get into an accident and Rayyan is taken to the hospital.
There Miran brought Genoel, who wounded herself with a knife and lied that Rayyan had done it.
Fyrat finally opens his eyes: he realizes that Yaren has been using him all this time.
Reyan agreed to become Azat ’ s wife and came to Shadoglu ’ s house.
But even Khazar does not want this marriage, because he knows that his daughter does not love Azat.
Reyan tells his father about the reasons for Miran's revenge.
He swears that he did not kill the boy ’ s parents, everything was the opposite – he loved his mother, she also loved him, but they were separated.
Ryza, an assistant in the Shadoglu family, brings Reyan to her swing, where she meets Miran.
She refuses to go with him and leaves with Azat.
Reyan returns to the family, but he still does not want to marry Azat.
The wedding date, meanwhile, has already been set.
Miran sees Khazar at his parents' grave.
He tells the boy that he loved his mother, and would never hurt her.
Miran goes to his grandmother and demands to tell him the truth.
But she again tells him that the hatred for Shadoglu flares up with renewed vigor.
Azizé wants to send Elif to London.
She refuses to leave and leaves the house.
And Reyan, leaving Azat a farewell letter, along with the cook Melike.
Gul, along with Ryza, goes to Miran and asks to bring his sister home.
Thanks to the girl's clues, he finds Rayyan.
Episode 9: Azizé Reveals the Terrible Truth.
Khazar and Miran's mother loved each other, but the Aslanbeys separated them.
From Khazar, she gave birth to Miran and an unrelated grandmother began to raise him as an instrument of revenge.
Rayan drives Miran away, but she is stung by a scorpion and the guy stays with her.
Azat arrives there, and a fight breaks out between them.
Azat and Miran spend the night under the walls of the Shadoglu mansion, because grandfather Nasukh does not let them inside.
Miran returns home to deal with Gönul for lying about the stab wound.
At this point, the Sultan talks about the secrets of Aziz.
Grandfather is furious about the fact that for debts he will take the mansion.
He hits Reyan and she runs away from home with a gun.
In Miran's office, she meets her father, who wants to kill the young man, but Rayan does not allow him to do the terrible thing and takes him out of the office.
Miran offers Shadoglu to close their debts and end the war if they let Rayyan go.
Nasukh rejects this offer – he still wants to pass Rayan off as Azat.
Azat learns about the secret of Rayyan ’ s parents and tells her this secret.
Brothers Jihan and Khazar quarrel, Nasukh refuses to marry Azat "this girl."
The old man wants to make sure that the girl goes missing and no one else finds her.
Miran informs Genol and the whole family that they are divorcing.
On the night of henna – the night before Rayyan ’ s wedding – Miran kidnaps Azat ’ s fiancée.
Episode 11: Azat kidnaps Gönul and asks her to be exchanged for Reyan.
The Sultan searches for his daughter in the house of Shadoglu, but does not find her.
Reyan escapes Miran at a gas station and hides in a truck.
Bad people found her there and began to molest her, but Miran arrived in time.
They're staying at a hotel.
Khazar, meanwhile, is looking for a daughter.
He told his wife how much he loved Miran's mother.
Gönul persuades Azat to give her a phone so she can call home.
Miran asks Rayyan for 24 hours in the hope that during this time she will love him again.
If he doesn ’ t, he ’ ll be out of his life forever.
Reyan agreed to spend one day with Miran and listen to him.
He explains why he married Gönul.
Firat received information about Miran's whereabouts, but his mother asked him not to extradite a friend to his grandmother Aziza.
She kidnaps Yaren and wants her to find out where Aziz is hiding Gönul.
He wanted to release the prisoner, but she shot him in the back.
Azizé goes for Miran, and Khazar goes for Reyan.
He brings his daughter home.
Miran threatens Nasukh, forbidding him to harm Rayyan.
Aziza meets her sister Hanife, who lived in the house of Shadoglu for many years.
Miran takes Rayan out of the house again, and his grandmother gives Shadoglu a week to free the mansion.
Miran rebuilt the hut where he and Reyan spent their first night, and again invites her to marry him - now for real.

title: The government will pay the families of Ukrainians killed in the crash of the UIA flight 200 thousand UAH – Honcharuk

title: UN: The number of refugees in the world has reached a new record
text:
According to the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, the number of people who left their homes due to crises, for the first time since the end of World War II approached 71 million people.
The number of refugees in the world in 2018 for the first time since the end of World War II reached 70.8 million people.
This follows from the report on refugees in the world, presented by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) on Wednesday, June 19, in Berlin and Geneva.
According to the UN, the number of people who are forced to leave their homeland due to war, the threat of hunger, natural disasters or violence is growing every year.
According to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi, the true number of people forced to leave their homeland due to various kinds of crises is probably even higher than the official figures.
In particular, these statistics do not take into account part of the four million Venezuelans who have left the country in recent months.
For comparison: in 2017, the official number of refugees in the world, according to the UN, was 68.5 million people, in 2009 - 43.3 million people.
Germany for the UN - a model in terms of migration policy Germany belongs to the countries that have received the largest number of refugees.
According to data for 2018, this is 1.1 million people.
Referring to this fact, Grandi praised the migration policy of Germany, pointing out that the country is making voluminous investments in the integration of new arrivals and successfully processing applications for political asylum that have accumulated since 2015.
According to Grandi, the example of Germany dispelled the myth that the migration crisis is impossible to cope with.
"Germany is a model that other countries should follow," he said.
At the same time, he also praised the personal contribution of German Chancellor Angela Merkel in the fight against the migration crisis.
“She showed courage and I ’ m sure history will appreciate it, ” Grandi said.
According to UN statistics, more than half of the 70.8 million people forced to leave their homes remained in their homeland (41.3 million people).
20.4 million people have fled to other countries due to wars and persecution.
In addition, the statistics take into account 5.5 million Palestinians who are subject to special protection by UNHCR.
An additional 3.5 million people are currently waiting to be granted refugee status.
Tens of millions of people have been forced to flee their homes.
This is where they come from. pic.twitter.com / 2WNUbYGvd3 — UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency (@ Refugees) June 19, 2019 The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) provides the latest figures on the number of refugees in the world every year on the eve of World Refugee Day, which is celebrated on June 20.

title: Japan officially leaves IWC and starts commercial whaling
text:
TOKYO, June 30 / PRIME /.
Japan officially leaves the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday and stops whaling in Antarctica and the North Pacific for scientific purposes.
Instead, it will now be able to start commercial fishing in its exclusive economic zone for unthreatened whale species.
So far, quotas and species of whales whose fishing will be allowed have not been made public.
Since 1988, Japan, as a member of the International Whaling Commission, has voluntarily renounced commercial whaling, reserving the right to fish for scientific purposes.
All this time, the Japanese government explained the appearance of a small amount of whale meat in stores by the fact that it is a kind of "by-product" research whales, which require an indispensable study of the state of their stomachs, which requires their killing.
In the past 10 years, Japan has been heavily criticized by environmental organizations, primarily Australian and New Zealand, for catching and killing whales.
The explanations of the Japanese side that the fishing takes place within the quota allowed by the commission were not taken into account.
In the early 2010s, a serious war broke out between Japanese whalers and the Sea Shepard organization using water cannons and incendiary bottles.
In the last year of its membership, Japan tried to convince colleagues on the commission that of the 86 species of whales, many are not on the verge of extinction and their fishing within reasonable limits will not affect their numbers.
But the organization was relentless.
Then Japan took the last step - announced its withdrawal from the commission, which automatically blocks its access to whale fishing in the Antarctic and the North Pacific, albeit for scientific purposes, but instead opens up the possibility of "home" fishing in its economic zone, but already in the amount in which it deems necessary.
Whales as part of culture.
The history of whale meat consumption in Japan dates back about 400 years.
It is often argued that due to the limited territory of Japan lacks plant and especially animal types of protein.
Since ancient times, the natural source of protein in the diet of the Japanese was fish and whale meat as part of marine resources.
The ban on whaling and whaling, and even by countries that do not eat whale meat, is perceived by the vast majority of Japanese at all levels as an attack on national culture and diktat.
The only last concession Japan made before starting fishing was a one-day delay.
She could formally announce permission to fish certain species of whales in her waters as early as Sunday.
But Japan decided to postpone it until Monday, waiting for the end of the G20 summit, which took place in Osaka on June 28-29, so as not to expose itself, the country chairing the forum, to criticism from partner countries.

title: Japan withdraws from International Whaling Commission
text:
TODAY 07: 38 2019-06-30T07: 38: 20 + 03: 00 Resize: A A Japan ’ s membership in the International Whaling Commission (IWC) expired on Sunday, June 30, and the country may resume catches.
In this case, Japanese fishermen will be allowed to fish in the territorial waters of the country and its exclusive economic zone.
Japan ’ s withdrawal from the IWC was announced in December last year.
Then the authorities of the country criticized some members of the organization, including Australia.
In Tokyo, in turn, stressed that the scientifically established population of a number of species of whales allows them to resume commercial fishing; the Japanese authorities also noted that eating whales has been part of the culture of the country since ancient times.
At the same time, Tokyo said that the country intends to remain in the ranks of the commission as an observer.
Japan stopped commercial whaling in accordance with an international moratorium in 1982.
Subsequently, the fishery was partially resumed; in Tokyo, the decision was motivated by the need to study migration routes, diet and other factors related to marine mammals.
At the same time, the meat of the killed animals is sold to Japanese restaurants and supermarkets, which gives grounds for opponents of the fishery to doubt the nature of this activity.
According to Kyodo, 48 members of the international commission, including Australia and Brazil, are strongly opposed to whaling.
At the same time, Tokyo notes that 41 IWC member countries, including Norway and Iceland, are inclined to resume it.
SOURCE KP.RU

title: Japan resumes commercial whaling for first time in 37 years
text:
Japan is resuming commercial whaling for the first time in 37 years.
Today, the country has officially left the International Whaling Commission and is no longer bound by its restrictions.
The decision to withdraw from the organization was made in Tokyo at the end of last year and drew criticism from Australia, New Zealand, as well as Greenpeace.

title: Whaling in the world
text:
Whaling - the extraction and processing of whales, as well as the production of products from whale raw materials.
The whaling reached its highest intensity in the 20th century, when its products were used in the food, leather, soap, textile, chemical, as well as in the perfume and cosmetic industries.
The population of the shores of the Kola and Iberian peninsulas, the Bay of Biscay, as well as the territory of modern Japan, caught whales in the IX-X centuries.
In the 16th century, whaling was carried out in the English Channel, off the coast of Ireland and the eastern coast of North America.
In the XVII – XIX centuries, intensive fishing of bowhead whales was carried out in the area of ​ ​ the islands of Spitsbergen and Jan Mayen, in the XVIII century began fishing for these whales in the Baffin Sea and in the Davis Strait.
In the XVIII – XIX centuries, active hunting of southern smooth whales was carried out in the warm and Antarctic zones of the Southern Hemisphere.
The fishery of sperm whales was opened in the south of the North Atlantic at the beginning of the XVIII century, later - in the warm and temperate zones of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans.
In the XIX – XX centuries, the leading places in the world whaling were occupied by Norway, Great Britain, the United States, Russia and Japan.
Since the beginning of the 20th century, the main area of whaling has been Antarctica.
In order to ensure the proper conservation of whale populations and the orderly development of whaling, the International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling was signed in 1946.
In accordance with the Convention was approved (ICC, International Whaling Commission).
The main task of the IWC is to monitor and, if necessary, adjust the measures regulating whaling in the world.
The Commission also coordinates and in some cases finances the conservation of many species of cetaceans.
As of June 2019, 89 countries were members of the ICC.
The International Whaling Commission identifies three types of whaling.
The second type of whaling is commercial.
It is also regulated by the ICC, but a moratorium was imposed in 1982, beginning with the 1985-1986 season.
The third category is special permissive (or scientific) whale hunting.
It is not regulated by the ICC.
Currently, aboriginal whaling is allowed for the indigenous populations of Chukotka (Russia), Greenland (Denmark), Alaska (USA) and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
For Russia and the United States for 2013-2018, joint block-quotas were established in the amount of 744 gray and 336 bowhead whales.
The quota for 2019-2025 is set at 392 Greenland whales and 980 gray whales.
According to the International Whaling Commission, the indigenous population of Chukotka caught 127 gray and one bowhead whale in 2013, 124 gray whales in 2014, 125 gray whales in 2015, 120 gray and 2 bowhead whales in 2016, and 119 gray and one bowhead whale in 2017.
Alaska ’ s indigenous population caught 57 bowhead whales in 2013, 53 in 2014, 49 bowhead whales in 2015, one humpback whale, two minke whales (all three unauthorised) and 59 bowhead whales in 2016, one grey whale (unauthorised selection) and 57 bowhead whales in 2017.
For Greenland, the International Whaling Commission allocates separate quotas for the west and east coasts.
For the eastern coast of Greenland, a quota of 12 minke whales per year was set for the period from 2005 to 2018.
For the west coast of Greenland for the period 2015-2018, the following annual quota was established - two Greenland whales, 19 fin whales, 164 minke whales and 10 humpback whales.
The annual quota for 2019-2025 for the east coast of Greenland is 20 minke whales, for the west coast - 19 fin whales, 164 minke whales, two Greenland whales and 10 humpback whales.
According to the International Whaling Commission, six minke whales were caught near the east coast of Greenland in 2013, 11 in 2014, six in 2015, 15 in 2016, and 10 minke whales in 2017.
In 2013, nine fin whales, eight humpback whales and 175 minke whales were caught off the west coast of Greenland; in 2014, 12 fin whales, seven humpback whales and 146 minke whales; in 2015, 12 fin whales, six humpback whales, 133 minke whales and one Greenland whale; in 2016, nine fin whales, five humpback whales were caught off the west coast of Greenland. In 2017, eight fin whales, two humpback whales and 133 minke whales were caught.
For Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, the ICC has set a quota of 24 humpback whales for the period 2013-2018.
For the period 2019-2025, the quota size is 28 humpback whales.
According to the International Whaling Commission, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines produced four humpback whales in 2013, two humpback whales in 2014, and one humpback whale in 2017 and 2015.
Commercial whaling is currently carried out by countries that are not members of IWC, as well as by a number of countries that have raised objections or reservations to the moratorium.
Despite the fact that these countries provide catch data to the Commission, the IWC does not regulate this whaling.
Among the IWC member countries, Norway and Iceland conduct commercial whaling.
The Russian Federation has also registered an objection to the moratorium, but does not currently engage in commercial whaling (the USSR conducted commercial fishing in 1985-1986).
Norway produces minke whales in its exclusive economic zone, and Iceland within its exclusive economic zone produces minke whales and fin whales.
According to the IWC, Norway produced 594 minke whales in 2013, 736 minke whales in 2014, 660 minke whales in 2015, 591 minke whales in 2016, 432 minke whales in 2017; Iceland produced 134 minke whales and 35 minke whales in 2013, 137 minke whales and 24 minke whales in 2014, 155 minke whales and 29 minke whales in 2016. – 46, in 2017 – 17 minke whales.
The International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling (1946) permits the slaughter of whales for research purposes (Article VIII).
The responsibility for establishing and regulating these catches rests with individual Governments, not with the ICC.
Each country must report to the Commission all special authorizations issued.
Governments may revoke their authorizations at any time.
Scientific information obtained from special whaling should be submitted to the Commission annually.
In different years, whaling for scientific purposes was conducted by Iceland, South Korea and Norway.
Currently, scientific whaling is carried out by Japan, which from the very beginning did not agree to a moratorium on commercial whaling and protested.
However, in 1987, she withdrew it, saying that she would stop commercial fishing and limit herself to whaling under the JARPA (Japanese Research Program in Antarctica) program, which was later replaced by the JARPA II program.
The Japanese have repeatedly been caught in the fact that under the guise of hunting for scientific purposes, they are in fact engaged in commercial fishing.
In particular, in 1994, genetic studies showed this: IWC specialists analyzed whale meat and fat from Japanese markets.
Activists of the environmental organization Greenpeace regularly spoke out exposing Japanese whalers.
The Australian government won the case in the International Court of Justice, which in 2014 banned Japan from whaling in Antarctic waters, recognizing that the JARPA program does not correspond to scientific status.
In 2015, the Japanese government launched a new special whaling program in Antarctica called NEWREP-A.
In June 2015, the scientific committee of the International Whaling Commission said the program had "insufficient information" and demanded that the Japanese government provide more evidence of the need for "scientific fishing."
However, in October, the Japanese government told the UN that it would not accept the jurisdiction of the international court and would resume fishing.
In November 2016, the Japanese government circulated a proposal for a new North Pacific whaling program called NEWREP-NP.
In December 2018, Japan announced its intention to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in 2019 in order to resume whaling from July.
The hunt will be conducted in the territorial waters of the country.
According to the results of the Antarctic season 2013 / 14, Japan has produced for scientific purposes 476 whales, 2014 / 15 – 196 whales, 2015 / 16 – 520 whales, 2016 / 17 – 488 whales, 2017 / 18 – 596 whales.
Since the moratorium was introduced, 17,839 whales have been produced for scientific purposes, including 310 fin whales, 56 sperm whales, 1,563 seyvals, 734 Bryde whales and 15,176 minke whales.

title: Japan resumes whaling after 30 years
text:
Japan has left the International Whaling Commission (IWC), of which it has been a member for more than 60 years.
Now the Japanese authorities, writes Kyodo, plan to resume commercial whale hunting.
It has been banned in Japan for more than 30 years.
The decision, the agency explains, came after Tokyo ’ s latest proposal to resume whaling was rejected at the IWC ’ s annual meeting last September.
After that, Japan threatened to leave the international organization, which still does not agree on commercial whaling: some of its members are in favor of whaling, some against, others from time to time support either side.
Commenting on the situation, Japanese Cabinet Secretary General Yoshihide Suga said that the refusal of the IWS member countries to support Tokyo ’ s proposal in September last year “revealed the fact that in the organization, countries with different views, it is impossible even to try to coexist together. ”
Japan announced plans to leave the organization in December last year, which drew criticism from Greenpeace and a number of IWC members, such as Australia and New Zealand.
The International Whaling Commission was established in 1948.
Initially, it consisted of countries that supported whaling.
The purpose of this organization was to ensure “the proper conservation of whale stocks and thus enable the orderly development of whaling. ”
However, since then, more and more countries have joined the IWC, which opposed commercial whaling.
Japan has been a member of this organization since 1951.
It stopped whaling in accordance with the moratorium adopted by the Commission in 1982.
However, there are cases when whales were hunted in Japan for “research purposes ” (this happened in 1987 and in 1994), recalls Kyodo.
The international community then criticized these actions, noting that they are a cover for commercial whaling.
It is known that the meat of the caught whales, the agency said, was sold in the domestic market.
At the same time, the resumption of commercial whaling relative to individual species (such as minke whales) Tokyo, Kyodo continues, has lobbied for the past 30 years as a member of the IWC.
However, its attempts to resume whaling have each time been blocked by the so-called anti-whaling countries.
Now commercial whaling Japan, according to the Agency, plans to resume from Monday, July 1.
Hunting will be conducted within the exclusive economic zone of Japan.

title: Japan has allowed 227 whales of three species to be caught by the end of the year.
text:
TOKYO July 1 / PRIME /.
Japan resumes whaling on Monday, setting a quota for the extraction of 227 whales of three species before the end of this year, the country's fisheries management said.
According to him, whalers for commercial purposes in the Japanese economic zone are allowed to catch 52 minke whales (Balaenoptera acutorostrata), 150 Bryde whales (Balaenoptera brydei) and 25 savals (Balaenoptera borealis).
For comparison, the ministry cites data on whale catches by other countries in 2018, including: 120 whales in Russia, 1,278 whales in Norway, 378 in Iceland, 176 in Denmark and 51 whales in the United States.
The resumption of whaling in Japan was made possible after the country ’ s withdrawal the day before from the International Whaling Commission (IWC), which it joined in 1951, and has maintained a moratorium on commercial whaling since 1982.
Whaling was carried out only for scientific purposes outside the Japanese economic zone, but the meat of the whales caught for research appeared on store shelves and in restaurants.
Japanese authorities insist that eating whale meat is a national tradition.
This product was the main source of food for the inhabitants of the country in the post-war period, when whale meat was included in school lunches.
However, there are many books on this topic, from which it follows that whale meat was never considered a national food of the Japanese, and after World War II it was included in the diet solely due to economic difficulties.
As John Newton, an Australian professor from Melbourne, wrote in a book about the history of whaling in the Pacific, in 1911 a local fisherman in Aomori prefecture even burned the Toyo Hogei meat processing plant, as waste blood and whale fat contaminated local waters and threatened conventional fishing.
Moreover, the Japanese in some parts of the country worshiped whales as deities, legends are made about them, and their murder requires respect at least honors, and at most simply unacceptable.
In different areas you can find sanctuaries in honor of killed whales, memorial plaques, mounds with buried bones.
As the newspaper Asahi wrote, in 1962 the production of 233 thousand tons of whale meat was registered, that is, the average Japanese then ate 2.4 kilograms of whale meat per year.
Recently, when the diet of the Japanese included pork and beef, the annual consumption of this type of meat has decreased to 3-5 thousand tons.
And the inhabitants of areas with whaling tradition in Japan have already become weaned from whale meat against the background of an abundance of beef, pork and chicken.
