title: Expert: commercial whaling in Japan will not reduce their numbers
text:
Workers prepare to unload the caught minke after the opening of commercial whaling in the port in Kushiro, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan Workers prepare to unload the caught minke after the opening of commercial whaling in the port in Kushiro, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan MOSCOW, July 2 - RIA Novosti.
Japan will catch fewer whales for commercial purposes than before in scientific, so fishing will rather help save whales, Maria Vorontsova, senior adviser to the program for the conservation of the seas of the International Fund for the Conservation of Animals (IFAW), a repeated participant of the International Whale Commission (IWC), told RIA Novosti.
Yesterday, Japan withdrew from IWC and announced the start of commercial whaling.
“It sounds terrible, but in fact, objectively, fewer whales will be killed.
According to the Japanese scientific quota, they could catch 900 whales in international waters, now there will be commercial fishing in coastal waters and a quota of 227 whales, "Vorontsova said.
She said that the Japanese have long insisted on allowing them to aboriginal fishing, but the Commission did not meet.
However, despite the start of commercial production, there is no market for whale meat.
“This year, Iceland, which traditionally hunted whales and supplied the Japanese market, refused to fish.
No demand.
In Japan, whale meat is eaten only by grandparents, ” explained Vorontsova.
She also noted that the withdrawal of Japan from the IWC will not put an end to the work of the Commission.

title: Tropical nights, floods and short winters: How Latvia ’ s climate will change in the coming years
text:
The climate in recent decades is changing so fast that our children will raise their children, perhaps in a completely different country in terms of weather conditions.
But even if you do not look into such a distant future, now in everyday life and when solving purely domestic issues, experts recommend taking into account climate risks in the construction process, buying an insurance policy, taking care of health, choosing clothes and places for recreation.
The main climatic risks in Latvia are an increase in the average annual air temperature by more than one degree, a reduction in the number of frosty days and days with snow cover, an increase in the intensity and volume of precipitation, the number of tropical nights.
And this is not our distant future, this is our present.
The above changes have taken place over the past 50 years and are a fait accompli.
Although climate change is a natural process, never before in the history of mankind has it been so rapid and comprehensive as in recent decades, according to the Department of Climate Change of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development.
The specialists of this department prepare reports and studies on how the weather conditions will affect the sectors of the national economy of Latvia.
According to their projections, six sectors are most affected - agriculture and forestry, construction and infrastructure, tourism and landscape planning, health, civil defence and emergency assistance, biodiversity and ecosystems.
The main threats to real estate are a strong wind, which can lead to the collapse of building structures and roofs, floods, wet snow, which will increase the load on the roofs in the winter.
When operating buildings, it is important to consider the need to cool the
Experts already recommend that during the insulation and reconstruction of houses to think not only (and not so much) about reducing heat loss and improving energy efficiency, but also about appropriate ventilation to prevent the accumulation of moisture and mold, as well as assess the risks of flooding, overheating of buildings and damage that can cause strong wind.
Landscape planning should take into account the availability of drinking water and create shaded areas in the public space, as heat waves will become longer.
Before buying a real estate object (land, houses and even apartments), not to mention the construction, you should carefully collect information about the place - whether there is a threat of soil erosion, destruction of banks, floods.
In other words, people who have already settled near ponds or are just going to do it, should be very careful.
It is also necessary to take seriously the choice of materials for construction, assessing their safety and strength, the ability to withstand strong winds and extreme amounts of precipitation, significant temperature changes.
Since one of the main risks in Latvia is heavy rainfall (showers and heavy snowfalls), experts recommend designing a system for draining melt and rainwater so that it can cope with large volumes falling out in a short time, as well as accumulate water to use it during periods of drought.
It will not be superfluous to find out in what condition the existing state, municipal or private land reclamation system is, whether it is being built or repaired in accordance with the expected loads.
According to the Latvian Association of Insurers, payments for property insurance policies against fires, damage caused by natural disasters, are growing.
If in the first quarter of 2017, insurance companies paid almost 8.23 million euros in the form of reimbursements for this type of policy, then in the first quarter of 2018 the total amount of reimbursements amounted to 9.43 million euros, and in the first quarter of 2019 already reached 14.54 million euros.
Most often, the cause of an insured event is a storm (about 50%), lightning (about 20%), continuous snowfall (about 10%), flooding (about 10%), hail (3%).
According to Swedbank apdrosinasana, from 11 to 13 June, when thunderstorms with strong gusts of wind raged in Latvia, more than 50 applications for compensation were received.
The damage was mainly caused to real estate by wind and water - the roof was blown off, fallen trees knocked out the window or damaged the roof, the cellar was flooded, the bath was burned as a result of a lightning strike, etc.
The average amount of compensation was about 600 euros.
Bad weather can harm and destroy not only real estate (about 90% of all insurance cases), but also transport (9%), as well as damage to people ’ s health.
Extreme weather conditions are increasingly leading to accidents, in connection with which insurance companies are also increasing the size of payments.
Thus, in the first quarter of 2017, insurance companies reimbursed 141.92 thousand euros for accident insurance policies, in the first quarter of 2018 - 196.74 thousand euros, and in the first quarter of 2019 - 242.19 thousand euros.
An insurance policy will not be a matter of free choice, but a necessity, and this will have an additional burden on the family budget, especially if there are a lot of property that will have to be insured, and a large family, all members of which will also need a policy.
In addition, as the demand for such services of insurance companies increases, prices are likely to rise.
Wind gusts will lead to power outages, periods of heat and icing will also affect the condition of power lines.
Water levels in rivers during periods of drought can fall, which will affect the operation of hydropower plants; increased demand for energy in the summer (for air conditioning), and in winter consumption will decrease as winters become warm.
Roads The state of roads has also become a hostage to climate change.
Meteorologist Toms Bricis pointed out this last year at the annual conference "The future of the state road network: opportunities and challenges", which is organized by SJSC Latvijas valsts celi.
Gallery: Chaka Street as if after the war He paid special attention to the fact that warming is mainly due to winters.
They become shorter and warmer, the number of frosty days without thaw is reduced, and the number of days when the air temperature fluctuates around zero, on the contrary, increases, and all this has a bad effect on the condition of asphalt and dirt roads, which we witness in the spring.
But there is good news.
First, the construction season, which, like the growing season, begins at a temperature above + 5 degrees, will be longer.
According to the scenarios of climate change developed by the Latvian Centre for Environment, Geology and Meteorology, the growing season is now about 200 days, but by 2100 it can increase by 27 days (if the scenario of moderate climate changes is implemented) or by 49 days (if the scenario of significant climate changes is implemented).
Secondly, in the coming decades, Kurzeme may have winters without snow and frost, which will save on snow removal and road surface treatment with deicers.
According to the same forecasts of the meteorological center, if in 2010 there were about 125 frosty days, then by 2100 their number will be reduced by 25 days (the scenario of moderate climate changes) or by 81 days (the scenario of significant climate changes).
This is just a small list of climate threats to the construction and infrastructure sector.
In total, 53 risks were identified, including deformation of rail tracks and road surface due to an increase in the number of frost-thaw cycles, heat and temperature periods "near zero"; instability of railway embankments; the threat of flooding of roads near water bodies, etc.
Agriculture and forestry Fields Agriculture and forestry are also at risk.
As noted in the Department of climate change, these sectors of the national economy can suffer from the spread of diseases and pests.
The yield and quality of the crop can be reduced due to uneven rainfall (then little, then much).
The productivity of farm animals can also deteriorate and immunity can weaken under the influence of extreme weather conditions.
Maira Dzelzkalea-Burmistre, deputy chairman of the Peasant Sejm, in a conversation with the LETA agency notes that in the past five years, weather conditions have become more contrasting - drought and heat, then torrential rains.
However, farmers are not inclined to consider them only in the context of global warming, since weather conditions are cyclical and previously there were years without winter in Latvia, for example, in the 70s and 90s.
“The industry is influenced not only by the climate, but also by politics, the situation in the markets, demand, and we have to adapt to everything, ” says a representative of the Peasant Sejm.
For example, in the last five years, in order to receive per hectare payments, it is necessary to grow beans and peas.
This also changes the environment, the composition of the soil, leads to the reproduction of new pests.
"There are things that affect the climate, and there are things that affect the climate, - continues Maira Dzelzkaleja Burmistre. - Take rapeseed, which until 2000 in Latvia believe that there was no, but the policy has changed and rapeseed began to grow for the production of biofuels.
Rapeseed has a very deep root system and a large root mass, and therefore this culture has enriched the soil, making it more fertile.
In turn, the cultivation of flax led to the appearance of many pests, the same can be said about beans with peas.
Each culture brings something of its own, and affects both animals and climate, because in nature everything is interconnected, ” concludes M. Dzelkaley-Burmistre.
On behalf of the farmers, she expressed the wish to receive more accurate weather forecasts from the weather center, since this is very important for farmers.
Now, in her opinion, weather forecasts are at a very weak level and this complicates the work of peasant farms.
She also noted the importance of cooperation between private land owners, the state and local governments in the field of land reclamation.
“It is expected that the downpours can be even stronger, and to avoid the situation a few years ago, when farmers could not harvest because of the water standing in the fields, it is necessary to invest in a system of land reclamation so that the weather conditions do not cause much damage, ” she says.
Gallery: Flood in Plavinas At the same time, climate change can also contribute to agriculture.
It will be possible to grow new crops for Latvia due to higher air temperatures and to harvest a richer harvest.
In addition, the growing season will increase, which will extend the season of grazing.
The main threat to forestry experts consider storms.
In the last ten years, the direct losses of forest owners amounted to 164 million euros.
In the future, the speed and strength of the wind will only increase, which means that more fallen trees and trees with a weakened root system will appear in the forests, which in turn will become an excellent target for rapidly multiplying pests under the influence of higher temperatures.
Another major threat to the forest is fires.
Head of the Forest and Environment Protection Department of the State Forest Service (SLS) Andris Purs notes that in recent years the risk of forest fires has increased due to natural disasters resulting from climate change.
The fire and spread of fire are influenced by a number of factors, including the volume and type of combustible materials present in the forest, humidity, air temperature, wind speed and topographic features of the area.
The danger of fires increases with the preservation of hot, dry and windy weather.
According to GSL, in 2018 there were 972 fires, during which 2,864 hectares of forest were damaged.
This is the largest number of forest fires in the last 10 years.
But it is worth noting that there were years and more terrible than the past.
Thus, in 2006, there were 1,926 fires, affecting 3,790 hectares, and in 1992 there were 1,510 fires on an area of 8,412 hectares.
The weather will also affect tourism.
The duration of the winter tourist season will change, as well as its signs.
The risk of flooding will increase due to rising water levels in rivers and lakes.
The coast of the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Riga will be subject to flooding and erosion.
The only good news is that the duration of the summer tourist season will change.
“What we think of in the winter may change.
Opportunities for winter recreation will be less, and for winter entertainment will have to go further north.
Accordingly, for the industry, this may mean a reduction in income from winter tourism services, but at the same time, the opportunities for summer holidays will expand, as the summer season will become longer, ” said Edgars Malinovskis, a climatologist at the Latvian Centre for Environment, Geology and Meteorology.
To adapt the tourism sector to the changing climate, it is proposed to carry out a number of measures, including respectively plan and protect areas at risk, strengthen the coast, build dams and protective structures, buy snow cannons and install air conditioning systems to cool in the summer, build indoor sports and entertainment facilities (skating rinks, swimming pools) and stadiums).
The climatic factor must be taken into account when planning a holiday not only in Latvia, but also abroad, because the climate is changing all over the world.
Also, weather conditions will affect the activities of manufacturers of clothing and footwear - warm winter clothes and shoes will be needed less, and summer from natural, "breathing" materials - more.
Living in unusual weather conditions, according to experts of the Department of Climate Change, will lead to the emergence of new health problems.
Outbreaks of intestinal diseases, exacerbation of chronic diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, an increase in the number of deaths from them, the risk of endemic infectious diseases will increase, morbidity and mortality from respiratory diseases will increase, people will more often suffer from heat strokes.
At the disposal of the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) there is no data that would confirm the impact of climate change on the morbidity of residents or the increase in the activity of pathogens and their vectors, the head of the communication department of the CDC Ilze Araya told LETA.
For example, the activity of ticks in comparison with the 90s even decreased, despite the warm winters and hot summers.
However, in recent years, a rare genus of ticks - Dermacentor reticulatus (meadow mite), which are carriers of the same diseases as well known taiga and dog mites, has become more active in Latvia.
"This may be due to many factors, including warm winters, but it should be noted that in Lithuania, where the climate is little different from ours, this kind of ticks has always been and its spread can be explained by abandoned logging, neglected fields that have not been cleared of shrubs for years, and migration of animals," explains I. Araya.
However, she adds that the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development emphasizes that the hypothesis of the relationship between climate change and infectious diseases still requires careful assessment and analysis.
To date, there has been no conclusive evidence that a changing climate is affecting the spread of non-communicable diseases.
President of the Latvian Society of Physicians Ilze Aizsilniece also attributes climate change to the fact that in the last 100 years, humanity has invented more than 800 chemicals that are dangerous for all living organisms and for humans, but only a few of them are well studied.
“These substances have a serious impact on human health, including affecting hormonal receptors, synthesis and conversion of hormones.
The wide prevalence of endocrine system disorders among people, the growth of diseases associated with endocrine system disorders and laboratory studies that prove the destructive effect of chemicals on the endocrine system of not only humans but also wild animals, allow us to talk about chemicals that destroy the endocrine system, ” emphasizes the President of the Latvian Society of Doctors.
In some countries, a large proportion of young men (40%) have poor semen quality, which reduces their chances of procreation. In newborn boys, genital pathologies are increasingly detected.
In many countries, the number of premature births and babies born with low birth weight is increasing, Ilze Aizsilniece lists shocking facts.
In some countries, most children have neurological behavioral disorders associated with thyroid disease, and the number of such cases has been increasing in recent decades.
Over the past 40-50 years, the incidence of cancer, caused by disorders of the endocrine system (cancer of the breast, uterus, ovaries, prostate, testicles and thyroid gland), has increased worldwide.
In all countries where relevant studies were conducted, it was found that the breasts in girls begin to develop at an earlier age, which is a risk factor for the development of breast cancer later on.
For 40 years, the number of people suffering from obesity and type 2 diabetes has dramatically increased worldwide.
According to the World Health Organization, 1.5 billion people worldwide are obese, and between 1980 and 2008, the number of people diagnosed with type 2 diabetes rose from 153 million to 347 million.
The use of pesticides in agriculture also affects the ecosystem and human health, causing all sorts of allergies.
The President of the Latvian Society of Physicians gives several recommendations on how to protect yourself: proper nutrition that does not contribute to the appearance of free radicals in the body, reducing the consumption of sugar (especially fructose) and grain products, quitting smoking, physical activity, reducing the use of pesticides in agriculture.
Specialists of the Department of Climate Change believe that it is possible to reduce risks to human health by means of an early warning system about periods of heat, availability of drinking water in public places, special cooling pauses for workers in the open air, etc.
In this area, the main risks are fires, floods (floods), storm winds, which can provoke an increase in the level of water in the sea.
Specialists offer the following adaptation measures - an early warning system, a unified system for collecting data on destruction, monitoring and forecasting, education of the population.
Climate as a threat The climatologist of the Latvian Center for Environment, Geology and Meteorology Edgars Malinovskis notes that the most significant changes in the past half century occurred precisely in the minimum temperature values.
That is, the average minimum temperature rises and warming occurs not due to a hotter summer, but due to milder and shorter winters, which are characterized by unstable snow cover and heavy snowfalls.
Regarding the summer season, E. Malinovskis says that in the future the summer will be similar to the cool and rainy summer of 2017, and not to the hot and dry summer of 2018.
In general, we need to prepare not for total unbearable heat or drought (although there will be such periods), but for sharp changes in weather conditions - they will become more extreme (contrast).
Increasingly in Latvia will be observed such a phenomenon as tropical nights, when the minimum temperature during the day does not fall below + 20 degrees.
The number of summer days will increase when the air temperature exceeds + 25 degrees.
Extreme weather conditions are dangerous because they harm people, the environment or industries.
Suffice it to recall the downpours in 2017, the drought in 2018, the intense snowfalls this year.
Since 2007, the World Economic Forum has assessed the 50 most significant risks to the global economy, and since 2015, the top five dominant threats include climate change and extreme weather.
A distinctive feature of the ongoing climate changes is that they are based not on natural processes, but on human activity.
In the last century, the most rapid changes in climatic parameters in the history of instrumental meteorological observations were recorded.
And much says that in the 21st century, weather conditions will change even faster, and will affect both society as a whole and individual sectors of the national economy.
According to the latest data from the European Environment Agency, economic losses from extreme weather conditions in Latvia in the period from 1980 to 2017 amounted to 412 million euros.
For comparison: in Estonia, this figure is 108 million euros, in Lithuania - 976 million euros.
The record for the amount of damage caused by bad weather are Germany (almost 96.5 billion euros), Italy (64.7 billion euros), France (62 billion euros), the United Kingdom (50.5 billion euros) .The total amount of economic losses in the 33 countries of the European Economic Area from 1980 to 2017 amounted to 453 trillion euros (in 2017 prices, expressed in euros).

title: The project in the format of “star wars ”: why the Pentagon plans to create a military orbital station
text:
The US Department of Defense has announced a tender for the development of a project for an autonomous orbital space station.
The Pentagon ’ s list of “desirable future capabilities ” for this facility includes“ conditions for transporting people ” and “the possibility of changing orbit. ”
However, at the initial stage, the station should be uninhabited and suitable for various kinds of experiments.
Experts talk about the “purely military purpose ” of the new project, which, taking into account the latest initiatives of Washington in space, can serve as a command post.
According to analysts, the entire policy of the White House in this area is aimed at militarizing interstellar space, which poses a threat to international security.
The US Department of Defense is looking for a contractor to develop its own orbital station.
Applications will be accepted until July 9.
This is stated in the tender posted on the website of the Defense Innovation Division of the Pentagon.
“The US Department of Defense is looking for projects for an autonomous orbital station.
The project should support assembly in space, microgravity experiments, logistics and storage, production, training, evaluation tests, payload placement and other functions.
The projects should be put into low Earth orbit within 24 months from the date of the contract and have guidance, navigation and control systems for long-term autonomous operation, ” the document reads.
According to analysts of the American portal Breaking Defense, based on the main requirements of the customer, we can conclude that we are talking about an uninhabited station with an internal volume of not more than 1 cubic meter.
m and a payload of 80 kg.
However, this object may well become the basis for a larger orbital station with a crew on board.
The American experimental aircraft Stratolaunch Model 351 made its first flight.
The machine is considered to be the world's largest flying machine.
Thus, in the application of the US Department of Defense in the list of “desired future capabilities (available as options at the initial or future stage of implementation) ” refers to the implementation of“ temporary or permanent docking with other modular stations of the same type (manned or unmanned) ”, as well as “conditions for transporting people ”,“ the possibility of changing the orbit ” and “ensuring radiation resistance for use outside low Earth orbit ”. at a distance of more than 2,000 km from Earth.
According to Breaking Defense, the Pentagon ’ s plans demonstrate that the prospects for the appearance of American troops in space, both at special stations in Earth orbit and in the space between the Earth and the Moon, are “no longer just science fiction. ”
As noted in an interview with RT, military expert, head of the Department of Political Science and Sociology of the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics Andrei Koshkin, the project of the space station of the US Department of Defense resembles the program of “star wars ” of the times of Ronald Reagan.
Then, within the framework of the Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI) project, the United States considered the possibility of deploying military installations designed to destroy Soviet intercontinental ballistic missiles in space.
"This is a project in the format of" Star Wars ".
That is, we are talking about a space platform on which installations for attacks from space will be placed.
For example, nuclear pumped lasers or missiles, ” suggested Koshkin.
In turn, the expert of the magazine “Arsenal of the Fatherland ” Alexei Leonkov believes that the United States does not have a rich experience in creating its own orbital stations.
The most ambitious project – the Freedom station – appeared just during the time of the SDI Reagan as a response to the Soviet “World ”.
But this project, which involved the participation of European and American allies, was never implemented until the end.
Remains of the development of that time - the American segment of the International Space Station (ISS).
ISS © NASA / Roscosmos "If the Pentagon intervenes in the affairs of the orbital stations, it suggests that the station will have a purely military purpose.
All experiments on board will be carried out in the interests of the Pentagon.
And it is clear that this project will not be international, ” says Leonkov.
According to military expert Yuri Knutov, the station can also be used to control other space objects.
For example, the orbital aircraft of the US Air Force Boeing X-37, the tasks of which in space the Pentagon does not apply.
"If you dock these two projects, everything falls into place, - says Knutov. - This station will control the actions of ships such as the Boeing X-37, which will wage war in space.
The station can become a command post and a center for the placement of space weapons. ”
Space military programs of the United States officially since the Cold War do not involve the creation of manned orbital combat stations.
However, the current President Donald trump is in favor of the fact that within the armed forces of the United States functioned space troops as a separate type of armed forces.
Also on the topic “Ready to fight and conquer ”: how the US is going to militarize space, the US Air Force command expects to increase by 20% the cost of activities in outer space.
This was stated by the Chief of Staff...
In December last year, he signed a decree establishing the Pentagon ’ s Space Command.
In addition, the administration has repeatedly stated the need to overcome the alleged lag behind Russia and China in the use of outer space for military purposes.
The US Air Force, in preparation for more intensive use of outer space, even developed a special training mobile application for combat pilots.
Earlier, the Russian Foreign Ministry said that it was ready for dialogue on the prevention of an arms race in outer space.
At the same time, the Russian Foreign Ministry noted that the United States is preventing the development of an international agreement that would stop the militarization of space.
“Such a scenario was generally expected taking into account the US line to ensure its unilateral dominance in space by any means, which, in particular, is evidenced by Washington ’ s decision to deploy missile defense components in near-Earth space by 2030, ” the Russian Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Formally, the United States, like other parties to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, can create military stations in low-Earth orbit.
International law prohibits the deployment of weapons of mass destruction in space, as well as the use of the moon and other celestial bodies for military purposes.
However, the militarization of space does not contribute to reducing international tensions, experts say.
In addition, the Pentagon is openly studying plans for military expansion beyond the Earth ’ s orbit.
For example, a joint report published in May by the US Air Force Research Laboratory and the Experimental Directorate of Defense Innovation states that in the medium and long term (5 years or more), the development and deployment of systems and facilities in space will have two incentives: “The first is the need for the armed forces to expand the basing and operation of critical objects in circumlunar space in order to reduce the ability of our opponents to detect these objects and strike them., as well as to strengthen our capabilities and reduce the ability of our adversaries to use force through space, from space and in space.
The second incentive is the need to create the proper infrastructure and facilities for the return, and then for a permanent U.S. presence on the moon and beyond. ”
However, the deployment of a US military base on the moon would be a direct violation of the 1967 treaty, experts say.
“The United States threatens international security because it does not consider the international legal documents limiting the withdrawal of weapons into outer space, ” said Koshkin.
As the first deputy chief of the Main Operations Directorate of the General Staff, Viktor Poznikhir, noted earlier, the deployment of American weapons in space can be aimed at launching a preventive strike against Russia, China or any other state and destroying ballistic missiles in the early stages of flight.
Viktor Poznihir RIA Novosti © Press service of the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation As an adequate response, Moscow was called the adoption of the Sarmat and Avangard complexes capable of overcoming the American global missile defense system.
In turn, the head of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Russia Valery Gerasimov noted that Moscow will respond with “mirror and asymmetric measures ” to the placement of American weapons in space.
“Military space plans of the United States are a danger to all countries, — said Koshkin. — Russia will have to respond with its space program, which will neutralize such a threat. ”
According to Alexei Leonkov, there are two directions of countering the plans of the Americans.
The first way is diplomatic — increasing international pressure on the United States.
The second is military-technical – strengthening its own defense potential.

title: In the near future, Europe and Russia are unlikely to ban glyphosate
text:
Austria was the first EU country to ban the use of plant protection products based on glyphosate, one of the most common herbicides in the world, Deutsche Welle reported.
The safety of glyphosate is being debated after last year ’ s San Francisco District Court ordered Monsanto, acquired by Bayer, to pay $289 million to gardener Diwan Johnson, who claimed that working with the herbicide Roundup, the active substance of which is glyphosate, he contracted cancer.
The gardener used this drug for many years and several times inadvertently spilled it on himself.
Although Monsanto insisted that numerous studies do not confirm the threat of glyphosate to human health, more than 13,000 lawsuits have been filed against the company.
In May, a California jury found that Roundup likely caused cancer in Alva and Alberta Pilliod and awarded them over $2 billion.
The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers glyphosate “probably carcinogenic, ” although the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency claims it is safe when used cautiously.
In the EU, glyphosate is allowed to be used until 2022, and member states can only ban approved chemicals in exceptional cases.
The European Commission has three months to challenge Austria ’ s decision.
However, it is possible that other states may follow the example of the country.
According to Vladimir Alginin, Executive Director of the Russian Union of Manufacturers of Chemical Plant Protection Products, each EU country has the right to abandon the use of glyphosate before 2022, but most countries in the world are in no hurry to do so.
“For example, in the US, glyphosate is used as the main herbicide in full.
In Russia, there are some restrictions on the use of the drug, first of all, in the households of the population, - he commented to Agroinvestor. - In this matter, I did not want to mindlessly go about other countries.
In Russia, the consumption of glyphosate in terms of hectare and so is several times less than in the United States, but in a number of technological operations to replace it with nothing. ”
The general director of Shchelkovo Agrokhim, Salis Karakotov, believes that in the coming year there will be no ban on glyphosate in Russia, as well as in Europe.
Now in our country, manufacturers of glyphosate in conjunction with the Institute of Hygiene and Toxicology.
Erismana is conducting two-year studies to monitor the effects of the chemical on human health and the environment in order to independently draw conclusions about its danger or safety, he says.
“Russia annually uses 40 thousand tons of plant protection products based on glyphosate for 10-12 million hectares.
And if suddenly we ban such drugs, then first of all farmers who work on zero farming technologies will suffer, - says Karakotov. - And today, with the increase in prices for fuels and lubricants, the number of enterprises that use arable technologies is growing, and they desperately need Glyphosate-based crop protection products for treatment against weeds, so sales of such drugs are growing. "
The general director of the company "Rodnoe" (Tula region) Dmitry Inyutin says that glyphosate herbicides are mainly needed by enterprises that use vapors.
“We are moving away from them, so they stopped using glyphosate in their fields, although preparations based on it are quite effective, ” he notes. – We know that Europe is gradually abandoning glyphosate, but our departure from it is associated not with this factor, but with a change in the technological process in the economy. ”
The question is also why Austria banned the use of glyphosate, adds Karakotov.
“Have we really found evidence of harm to human health with this drug, or are well-known multinational companies developing an alternative herbicide that needs to make room in the market? ” he asks.
Meanwhile, shares of Bayer, which since March fell by more than 20% due to lawsuits against Monsanto, at the end of June rose by almost 9% to 60.86 euros, Reuters reported.
The rapid growth, the most significant daily average in a decade, was due to Bayer ’ s announcement of plans to settle glyphosate lawsuits.
She hired an outside lawyer to advise the supervisory board and set up a committee to help resolve the litigation issue.
The company ’ s shareholders expect litigation to be settled sooner than expected.

title: The catastrophe of the UIA aircraft: in London, developed a provision on cooperation with Iran
text:
The foreign ministers of the five countries whose citizens were killed in the UIA plane crash near Tehran on January 8 have developed a regulation on further cooperation with Iran.
This is reported by RBC-Ukraine with reference to CBC.
According to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, François-Philippe Champagne, the provisions are based on five key elements.
“Today, the members of the coordination group have developed a position of cooperation with Iran, which will be published later.
These provisions are based on five key elements that will become a roadmap for our cooperation with the Iranian authorities, ” he said.
The five key elements of the provision are: Iran must ensure full and unimpeded access for foreign diplomats to provide consular services; Iran must ensure that the process of identifying those killed is conducted transparently and in accordance with international standards.
At the same time, the wishes of the relatives of the deceased regarding repatriation should be respected; Iran should ensure a full, independent and transparent international investigation in accordance with the provisions of the International Civil Aviation Convention; Iran should assume full responsibility for the downing of flight PS 752 and recognize its responsibilities to the relatives of the deceased, including compensation issues; Iran should ensure that the people who will be held responsible for the downing of the aircraft as part of the criminal investigation, through a transparent and independent trial. with international standards of judicial processes and human rights.
According to Champagne, Tehran has already demonstrated a high level of cooperation, however, the countries will continue to observe on a daily basis and will call on the Iranian side to continue to cooperate.
The amount of compensation to the families of victims of the plane crash of the passenger plane of Ukraine International Airlines will depend on the agreements reached between Iran and Ukraine.
It was also reported that Iran canceled the visit of its expert to Ukraine as part of the investigation of the UIA plane crash.
Also, the Ukrainian side has prepared a second request for legal assistance to Iran with a request to provide access to the black boxes, but there is still no response.

title: Foreign Ministers of five countries called on Iran to ensure the responsibility of those responsible for the downing of the UIA aircraft (video)
text:
The leaders of these agencies intend to get Iran to conduct a thorough, independent and transparent international investigation of the crash.
Foreign Ministers of Ukraine Vadym Prystaiko, Canada François-Philippe Champagne, Great Britain Dominique Raab, Sweden Ann Linde and Acting Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Idrees Zaman call on Iran to ensure the responsibility of those who shot down the plane of Ukraine International Airlines near Tehran.
Champagne said this at a press conference after a meeting with the foreign ministers of Ukraine, Britain, Sweden and Afghanistan in London, which was broadcast on the Canadian television channel CBC.
Read alsoUIA plane crash: the affected countries will demand from Iran to provide access to all investigation materials In particular, on behalf of the foreign ministers of the five countries, Champagne said that today joint efforts have developed common principles for the purpose of interaction with the Iranian authorities.
According to him, these principles are based on five main key elements that will determine the interaction of Canada, Ukraine, the UK, Sweden and Afghanistan with Iran to ensure, first, full and unhindered access for officials to visit Iran and travel within that country for the purpose of carrying out consular services.
Secondly, said Champagne, it is about the need to ensure that "the process of identification of victims is conducted with dignity, transparency and in accordance with international standards and that the wishes of families for repatriation are respected in all cases".
“Third, to ensure a thorough, independent and transparent international investigation open to (affected) states that are in mourning, ” Champagne said, adding that this investigation should be guided by the provisions of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.
"Fourth, ensure that Iran takes full responsibility for the shooting down of flight PS 752 and recognizes its obligations to the families of the victims, including compensation," Champagne added.
Ukraine asks Iran to hand over to it the "black boxes" of the plane of the deadly flight PS752 "Fifth, to ensure responsibility for those who are guilty (in the shooting down - UNIAN) through an independent criminal investigation, after which there will be a transparent and impartial prosecution that will comply with international standards of due process and human rights", - said Champagne.
As UNIAN reported, on January 8, an UIA plane crashed in Iran, killing 167 passengers and nine crew members.
The plane, which was carrying out flight PS752 on the route Tehran-Kiev, took off from the airport at 6: 10 local time and disappeared from the radar a few minutes after departure.
On board the Boeing 737 were 11 citizens of Ukraine, including 9 crew members, as well as 82 citizens of Iran, 63 citizens of Canada, 10 citizens of Sweden, four citizens of Afghanistan, three citizens of Germany and three citizens of the United Kingdom.
On January 11, Iranian President Hassan Rouhani officially admitted that the plane was shot down “as a result of an unintentional human error ” and promised to bring those responsible to justice.

title: The expert predicts difficulties with the cultivation of cocoa in the world because of the climate
text:
GENEVA / MEXICO, July 11 – RIA Novosti, Elizaveta Isakova, Dmitry Znamensky.
Climate change in the world will lead to the fact that many lands will become unsuitable for growing cocoa beans, but it is too early to talk about the disappearance of chocolate, Ethan Budyansky, director of the environment department of the World Cocoa Fund, told RIA Novosti.
Beginning in 2013, a series of media articles led cocoa farmers and chocolate lovers to worry that chocolate would die out in the next few decades.
But these stories only partially interpreted the study, which was conducted by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture.
The good news is that it ’ s too early to say goodbye to chocolate.
However, due to climate change, it is becoming increasingly clear that some lands will be less suitable for the production of cocoa beans, ” he said.
According to him, now it is necessary to qualitatively change the approach to growing cocoa beans.
The World Cocoa Fund is working on this problem and, together with farmers and governments, is trying to develop a new strategy for growing products in the face of climate change and active deforestation, as well as illegal cocoa cultivation in national parks.
The Fund believes that improving the quality of planting materials and training farmers in more professional farming methods will not only help increase farm productivity, but also reduce the negative impact of climate change on the production of cocoa beans.
"Today, because of outdated farming practices, the productivity of most cocoa farms is much lower than it could be," Budyansky said.
In particular, small farmers often face economic difficulties and are affected by fluctuating weather conditions and prolonged drought, especially in Latin America.
However, many experts are optimistic about the future of cocoa and cocoa products.
For example, Mexico is counting on a stable situation with the production of these products in the world.
“We are optimistic that Mexican agriculture (in terms of cocoa) is being devoted to programs, the government is helping with planting trees in the south-eastern regions.
We are confident that other countries are making similar efforts to ensure that chocolate continues to be present on our tables and delight those who eat it with their taste, ” said Alicia Paramo, Director General of the National Association of Chocolate Producers of the country.
According to her, the confidence of chocolatiers is given by the rapidly growing gastronomic market of Mexico, where chefs are increasingly using chocolate when cooking dishes.
It is in Mexico, by the way, they eat mole - a meat dish cooked in a special chocolate sauce with spices.
Now the Association is working on the establishment in Mexico of its national holiday of chocolate.
“For four years now, we have been working to declare September 2 a national day of cocoa and chocolate, in order to support the socio-cultural preservation of these products in the daily consumption and habits of Mexican families, ” said Paramo.
According to the calculations of the Association, Mexico expects annual growth in the chocolate industry by about 5% for the year.
In 2018, cocoa production, according to preliminary forecast, amounted to about 30 thousand tons, and by 2030 it should grow to 47.6 thousand tons.
In 2017, the value of cocoa produced approached 1.1 billion pesos ($56.4 million).
At the same time, the industry provides 90 thousand direct and about 135 thousand related jobs.

text:

title: FIGURE OF THE DAY. "Porcelain" histories.July 21, 2019
text:
July 21, 2019 "Those who fight in the war are the most remarkable people.
AND THE NEarer TO THE PREVIOUS, THOSE MORE NOTIFIED PEOPLE WILL MEET THERE.
These are the pigs who think only about economic competition and what it can bring about... ''
These words were written long ago by Ernest Miller Hemingway, born exactly 120 years ago, on July 21, 1899, in the small American town of Oak Park, Illinois, in the family of a doctor.
Since childhood, he has been fond of hunting and fishing.
And I read a lot.
His only dream was to become a writer.
And one day it came true.
He became a writer.
Not just a writer, but a world-famous writer.
He wrote books that are familiar to every educated person.
Such as "Farewell, weapon", "And the sun rises (Fiesta)", "For whom the bell tolls", "Death in the afternoon", and many others.
His novel The Old Man and the Sea, written in 1952, won the Pulitzer Prize in 1953 and the Nobel Prize a year later.
He fought in Italy.
He lived in Cuba.
He traveled to Africa.
He's been looking for himself all his life.
But I guess I never found it.
When Ernest was 12 years old, his grandfather gave him a 20-caliber single-shot rifle.
He immediately rushed to the street to boast of a gift to friends from the poor outskirts of Chicago, where at that time he lived with his parents.
Seeing him, an old wise Indian woman said, '' Be careful, lad.
These toys tend to go anywhere, including on their owners... "
She must have known what she was saying.
Exactly 50 years later, the world-famous writer Ernest Hemingway shot himself with the same gun.
Subsequently, this model was called Hemingway.
But before that, fate repeatedly tested him for strength.
Dozens of times he was within a hair's breadth of death.
Once in battle he was struck by 273 mine fragments, and his legs pierced by machine gun fire!
But he survived.
He survived five accidents and seven catastrophes.
He was injured twice while hunting and almost burned down during a forest fire.
The old Indian must have known something.
Hemingway once argued with fellow writers that he would write a six-word story in English that would be the most touching of all he had ever written.
They doubted.
And he took and won the argument: '' For sale — baby shoes, never used... ''
(For sale are baby shoes.
Unwanted... ").
After that, all over the world began to hold competitions for the shortest story, in which the tie, climax and denouement would be mandatory.
Here are just a few examples that have become widely known.
"The driver lit a cigarette and leaned over the gas tank to see if there was much gas left.
The deceased was 23 years old. ” — O. Henry
"The last man on earth was sitting in a room.
There was a knock on the door... "
(Frederick Brown).
In his life, he was very unpretentious.
He was guided by what he once threw out on a blank sheet of paper: “Now is not the time to think about what you don ’ t have.
Think about how to handle what you have... "
For many years, looking at the beautiful porcelain composition presented to your attention today, brought by me from Spain, I see in its main character Ernest Hemingway.
For some reason, it seems to me that he was just like that...
To all of today ’ s birthday guests, let me wish you good and happiness.
And you, my friends, have a good day.
As always, sincerely yours.

title: Ernest Hemingway: “I didn ’ t go to Russia because there are bad, dirty hotels ”
text:
1.
It is known that Hemingway ’ s parents had problems with the psyche.
The father suffered from severe depression and eventually committed suicide (so will the son).
The mother, a failed opera singer, was a little hopeless: at some point she decided to dress Ernest and his sister Marceline, born a year earlier, the same way.
Dress and hats.
I called them “daughters. ”
And sometimes, on the contrary, she dressed Marceline and Ernest as boys and called them “sons ”.
Maxim Chertanov, the author of the biography of Hemingway, a few years ago published in the publishing house “Young Guard ”, believes that she wanted to see them as same-sex twins.
There are researchers who believe that this broke the masculinity of Hemingway - which is why he so passionately then all his life tried to establish it with the help of purely male activities: trips to war as a soldier or journalist, safari, fishing...
In fact, there is no evidence for this: despite the hats, Hemingway was from the very beginning a typical boy who loved games of Indians, football, boxing, travel.
There are researchers who believe that Hemingway passionately all his life tried to establish himself with the help of purely male pursuits.
In 1918, Hemingway rushed to the First World War: "If I do not go, after the war I will not be able to look people in the eye."
Like many young men at the time, he saw war as something of a football match.
He described the shelling as follows: “The guest team started a dirty game.
What will our answer be? ”
However, soon his opinion began to change: too often had to contact with the corpses.
“After a direct hit, you ’ re all splattered by what ’ s left of your buddies.
“It ’ s literal, ” he wrote to his parents.
Then he himself was wounded - dozens of fragments were pulled out of his body (one of them he carried with him all his life as an amulet).
It was very painful, but he became a star: he was considered the first American wounded in Italy, he was in the spotlight of photographers and journalists, the king of Italy wrote him military awards.
And Hemingway in the hospital for the first time seriously fell in love with nurse Agnes von Kurowski, who was older by 8 years; it is believed that from this episode then grew the plot of the novel “Farewell to arms! ” 3.
Hemingway was an idol in Russia in the 1960s.
And he was a huge fan of Russian literature, read Turgenev, Tolstoy and Gogol.
And at the same time, he was never in Russia - although he could: in the early 20s they wanted to send him to Moscow as a journalist.
He refused to travel.
Then he said that this is due to the fact that in Russia, as he was told, “bad and dirty hotels. ”
Ernest Hemingway was a passionate fisherman Photo: EAST NEWS The fate of his books in our country is quite curious: he was translated and printed already in the 30s, the youth of that generation was fascinated by his style, but then big problems arose with the novel about the civil war in Spain “For Whom the Bell Tolls ”.
He was transferred in early 1941.
According to legend, Stalin read it and said, “It is interesting, but you can ’ t print. ”
In the novel appeared under the name Karkov journalist Mikhail Koltsov - and he was shortly before that was convicted and shot.
Hemingway was accused of both slander and the fact that the book demonstrates the “moral superiority of bourgeois-democratic ideology over communist ideology ”.
The main opponent of the book was Dolores Ibarruri, general secretary of the Communist Party of Spain, nicknamed "passionaria" and living in the USSR in exile.
Neither the Nobel Prize received by Hemingway, nor a personal meeting with the writer Anastas Mikoyan, who made a visit to Cuba, nor the rehabilitation of Koltsov, nor the intercession of Sholokhov, who advised the Minister of Culture Ekaterina Furtseva to finally publish a book, did not help - stubborn Ibarruri wrote furious letters to the Central Committee of the CPSU, and the publication of "Bell" canceled (although the translation of the novel from the 40s went to samizdat).
It was only in the late 1960s that the book was published, with notes.
It was released in 1968, when it was allowed to be printed in Franco Spain.
It was published entirely in Russian only in 2005. 4.
Hemingway ’ s most famous photograph – the one in which he is wearing a fishing sweater with a high throat – was taken by photographer Yusuf Karsh in 1957.
Despite the apparent simplicity of the sweater, it was very expensive: it was bought by Hemingway ’ s wife at Christian Dior boutique and presented to her husband for his birthday.
Despite the apparent simplicity of the sweater, it cost a very expensive 5.
It is believed that Hemingway suffered from bipolar affective disorder: at the end of life, the phases of euphoria alternated with the phases of deep depression.
The writer suffered from unreasonable fears (although he regularly paid taxes, he thought that for non-payment he was about to go to prison), paranoid fear of surveillance by the FBI (it did look after him, but Hemingway rushed at innocent people like waiters, shouting that they were the agents).
Since his youth, he drank alcohol in huge quantities and in addition a lot of pills - he had health problems, and the side effects of drugs could also provoke depression...
In general, they decided to treat him with electroconvulsive therapy.
This procedure is not as monstrous as shown in the movies (where it resembles an electric chair execution), and it can really help with depression, but it can also cause memory loss.
Hemingway began to forget the facts (and that ’ s why he couldn ’ t finish The Holiday That ’ s Always With You; he couldn ’ t write anything anymore).
Depression returned - it was again treated with ECT, already with catastrophic consequences.
“What was the point of destroying my brain, erasing my memory, which is my main capital, and throwing me to the side of life?
It was a brilliant treatment, but the patient was lost, ” Hemingway said.
It all ended in suicide. 6.
Today, Ernest Hemingway is a brand in the literal sense of the word, a registered trademark.
On the Internet there is a website where you can buy products of this brand.
For example, cologne with notes of grapefruit, bourbon, cedar, leather, amber, sandalwood, tobacco and vanilla ($69.00 per 50 ml).
Coffee harvested in Cuba or on the northern slope of Kilimanjaro ($13.99 for 340 grams).
And yet - expensive rum Papa's Pilar, named after the Hemingway yacht, glasses, fountain pens, sauces, sea salt with spices, a mixture for cooking "Bloody Mary"... 7.
Hemingway was an avid cat lover.
In the 20s, he settled in Key West, Florida, and was given a six-toed kitten named Snow-White.
It is believed that Snow White became the founder of a whole huge "dynasty" of six- and seven-fingered cats and cats, living since then in the house of Hemingway (there are now guided tours).
There are about fifty of them, they roam wherever they please, they can climb on sofas and beds, walk in the garden.
They are regularly examined by a veterinarian, they still drink water from a drinking bowl built by Hemingway from an olive can and urinal.
In the garden there is even a special cat cemetery.
By the way, there are a lot of six-toed animals not only in the house-museum, but also throughout the city, where there are four cats per inhabitant.

title: War, the sea and beloved women: how we remember Hemingway
text:
July 21, 1899 was born one of the classics of literature of the twentieth century, an American writer, Nobel Prize winner in literature, Ernest Hemingway.
Writing success came to Hemingway in 1926 after the publication of “And the Sun Rises ” – a novel about the“ lost generation ” of young people who lived in France and Spain in the 1920s.
In 1927, a collection of short stories "Men Without Women" was published, and in 1933 - "The Winner Gets Nothing", which consolidated Hemingway's success in literature.
For the most part, Hemingway became memorable with his novel "Farewell to Arms!", which was an unprecedented success in the United States.
The writer received the Nobel Prize in Literature for his philosophical novel “The Old Man and the Sea ”.
Sputnik offers to recall episodes from the life of the famous writer.

title: July 21 marks the 120th anniversary of the birth of Ernest Hemingway
text:
When I read Hemingway in my youth, I recognized it as unbreakable: the one who holds on to the end loses last.
But losing, a person should not lose dignity, because only dignity can facilitate the loss.
Hemingway's fame was exorbitant.
In the Soviet Union, for example, it was difficult to find an apartment of an intelligent person in which there was no portrait of Ham.
In the 60s of the last century, a wonderful American writer John Steinbeck (“Grapes of Wrath ”,“ Winter of Our Anxiety ”) flew to Moscow.
I stayed at the Moscow Hotel.
Going out in the evenings on Gorky Street, he greeted passers-by friendly.
He held his hands and explained, "I am an American writer." "Oh!" people were amazed. "Hemingway!" Yes. It was.
I am not a literary critic.
Not a writer.
But it seems to me that at that time there was no writer who at least once did not experience the influence of the magical Hemingway dialogues.
Few people could create literary characters, to such an extent similar to the author himself.
Thousands of epigones around the world copied the style of the author, his intonation.
Of course, Hemingway himself has repeatedly turned to the work of great predecessors.
The famous novel "For Whom the Bell Tolls" is called a phrase written 350 years before it was borrowed from the largest poet and priest, a contemporary of Shakespeare John Donne.
The biblical Ecclesiastes (“And the Sun Rises ”) inspired Hemingway and many other writers to make literal withdrawals.
But the difference is that Hemingway certainly referred to sources of borrowing.
I have never tried to decorate my work with someone else.
This is the norm today.
Hemingway was often accused of a rampant lifestyle.
Addicted to alcohol.
To the cruel spectacles (bullfighting).
Accused of cynicism, excessive irony.
Over time, it became clear that the writer, like Democritus, ironically and laughed not at life, but at its seriousness.
His tolerance for human vices — including his own — was philosophical.
He seemed to make it clear: for all his dissimilarity, their vices make people similar.
Reading Hemingway, you think about the special fragility of the human race.
And the greatest strength of the individual.
The world that Hemingway knew in endless travels, found its full reflection in his life.
He did not like New York in his lifetime.
I thought it was fake.
The best place on earth recognized Cuba.
The last 20 years of his enchanting life, the writer spent in a small settlement of San Francisco de Paula, 20 kilometers from Havana.
Here, at the comfortable cottage "La Vijia", he wrote "The old man and the sea", "For whom the bell tolls", "Islands in the ocean"...
When Hemingway's earthly journey was cut short, his wife, friend and indispensable participant of all his adventures and famous African safaris Mary Hemingway bought an apartment in the unloved Ernest New York and left Cuba, "La Vijia" by the will of Fidel Castro and with the consent of the widow became the official museum of the Nobel Prize winner Ernest Miller Hemingway.
That's the way things are going.
I was in La Vijia when nothing was touched, moved, rearranged.
Everything was as it was with him.
I have seen what has been described a thousand times by journalists from all over the world.
Hunting shoes, hunting rifles, mauser carbines, rifled carbines, 12-gauge bokflint, 28-gauge double-barrel.
On the walls - hunting trophies: heads of lions, gazelles...
Paintings, photographs.
The writer ’ s workplace is a set-top box (worked standing); two deep armchairs and a table with drinks (rested with cocktails)...
Yeah, it's just like him.
Just be quiet.
The golden sawdust of the Cuban sun silently settles on guns, paintings, clothes, the past.
In 1978, I will be visiting Mrs. Mary Hemingway.
In her New York apartment.
The house on the corner of Madison Avenue and 65th Street was no different from the others.
Not very different from the Cuban "La Vijia" and the furnishings of the apartment on the 18th floor.
Again - hunting trophies, including the lion's head - Mrs Mary's personal trophy.
On the walls of the picture: Marriage, Domingo, Andre Masson, Clay, Miro...
Part of what was in La Vijia.
To accommodate all this, it was necessary to expand the area.
"I bought two rooms from the neighbors," Mrs. Mary told me, showing the apartment. "All you see is Ernest."
A few minutes before the farewell, Mary Hemingway took my notebook and scribbled out a few lines.
“It ’ s my shortest story, ” she said.
Shortly before our meeting, she completed the main work: a book about twenty years of living together with Hemingway.
The book "As it was" immediately became a bestseller.
Did Mary Hemingway need help writing it?
Even before she became the wife of a classic, she was already a famous, experienced journalist.
Its reports from military Europe (the Second Front) were read by the whole of America.
In the warring countries on the other side of the Atlantic, Mrs. Mary represented the most popular publications of America - Time, Fortune, Life magazines.
Subsequently, Life became the first magazine to publish the masterpiece of the Pope, The Old Man and the Sea (Pulitzer Prize).
Mary Welsh was bowed by many generals and fellow journalists.
Bowed and the most famous of them: on the banner of Ernest Hemingway by that time already highlighted "Fiesta" and "Farewell, weapons!", as well as impressive reports from the fronts of the civil war in Spain.
All that was then, after the Second World War, in the years of their lives together, was a tornado, a kaleidoscope of incredible life collisions, dramas and adventures.
Each of them was followed tirelessly by a vulgar look.
Every incident in America, Africa, Asia or Europe involving Ernest and Mary Hemingway immediately became known to the world media.
And, of course, rumours.
Reading Hemingway, you think about the special fragility of the human race.
And of the greatest strength of an individual, Mrs. Mary knew what and how to write about a legendary man.
She knew that the small weaknesses of great men most excite people who have not become great.
But from the temptation to slip into this ditch, she was held back by a clear idea of the scale of the personality.
This did not prevent her, however, from dropping warm, very personal words: "It was good to be sick with him.
There was no man in the world more caring than he. ”
The recognition has been in my memory for more than 40 years!
Mrs. Mary's answer to my question about the fate of the writer's archive is in my notebook.
“The bulk of Ernest ’ s creative archive, ” said Mrs. Mary,“ was offered to me to place immediately at the university: Yale, Princeton and Columbia.
I didn't say yes.
But when Jacqueline Kennedy called, I said, "Yes."
All right. "
Since then, the Ernest archive is in perpetual storage in the John F. Kennedy Memorial Library.
My answer to Mrs. Mary's question.
The answer about royalties in the USSR.
Fragment. - The work of Ernest Hemingway is incredibly popular in the Soviet Union.
His books are in millions of copies.
"I know," Mrs. Mary says to me with a summons. "Your very great official once told me."
Mikoyan *.
We had him at La Vijia.
I wanted to ask him one question.
But Ernest forbade it.
Where does the money that Soviet people pay for Ernest ’ s books go?
"These are our laws," I replied with abominable bravery. "We are not part of the Geneva Copyright Convention.
The fees go to the needs of the national economy.
The circulation of Hemingway ’ s books was really huge.
The fees are serious.
In the days of the writer's anniversary, by the way, it is necessary to recall those who "brought" him to the Soviet Union, to Russia, to the Russian-speaking reader: the translator I. Kashkin, journalists and writers B. Gribanov, later Yu. Paporov, I. Mikhailov...
When Ernest Hemingway was awarded the Nobel Prize, Cuban radio broadcast a sensational message every 15 minutes.
Dad was at sea at the time.
With the same frequency, but already with sorrow, the Cuban radio reported the death of a great writer - in fact, a fellow countryman of every Cuban.
(The first version of death is a serious illness.)
Among the thousands and thousands of condolences is the humble word of the friend of the “Pope ” journalist Robert Mening:“ Dad ” was already approaching his twilight.
He looked older than his years.
He tried to treat a diseased liver, a cracked cranial bone, two squeezed and one broken vertebra.
Worried Hemingway and severe burns received in a plane crash in Uganda.
All these injuries - add to them half a dozen wounds to the head, more than two hundred shrapnel scars, a shot kneecap, wounds on the hands - left their mark... "
In these words, as in thousands of others spoken in different parts of the world, there is no reproach for the lead tricks of fate.
In them - the recognition of the courage of a person who found in himself at the same time the strength and the will to act and creativity.
To live and write for him was the same.
He lived and wrote.
Yeah, a shot.
But the choice is yours.

title: North Korea Seizes Russian Ship
text:
North Korea seized a Russian fishing boat with 17 sailors on board.
This was reported to Kommersant by the deputy director of the North-Eastern fishing company that owns the ship, Sergei Sedler.
The incident occurred on the night of July 17.
According to him, on the ship "Xianghailin-8" were 15 Russians and 2 South Koreans - they were heading from the South Korean port of Sokcho to the Sea of Japan for crab mining.
North Korea seized the ship 55 miles from the country ’ s border.
At the time of the arrest, the ship was unloaded.
“At 4 a.m. on July 17, border guards landed on the ship and cut off all communications.
We did not even immediately understand what happened, at first we thought that they were drifting, but then we realized that they were captured, ” Sedler explained.
He added that the reason for the arrest was the illegal crossing of the border of the “military protection zone ”, which the DPRK arbitrarily established 50 nautical miles from the shore.
The sailors were escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan, the Russian consul visited them only on Tuesday, July 23.
He said that the Russians are kept in closed cabins, where they are regularly searched and interrogated.
North Korea has not explained when the trial will begin.

title: North Korea detains Russian ship with 17 sailors
text:
North Korea on the night of July 17 seized a Russian fishing vessel with 17 sailors on board, said “Kommersant ” Sergei Sedler, Deputy Director of the North-Eastern fishing company, which owns the vessel.
According to him, 15 Russians and two South Koreans, who were heading from South Korea to the Sea of Japan for crab mining, were escorted to the DPRK, where they are still.
The Russian consul was allowed to see them only today, and he said that sailors locked in their cabins were regularly searched and interrogated.
As Mr. Sedler told Kommersant, the Xianghailin-8 vessel belonging to the Northeast Fishing Company left the South Korean port of Sokcho and headed for the area of its traditional fishing in the Sea of Japan.
The capture took place about 55 nautical miles from the territory of the DPRK.
“At four o ’ clock in the morning on July 17, the border guards landed on the ship and turned off all means of communication, ” says Sergei Sedler.“ We did not even immediately understand what happened, at first we thought that they were drifting, but then we realized that they were captured. ”
Later, as it turned out, they were escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan.
The company has no contact with the seafarers yet.
On July 23, a representative of the Russian Embassy in Pyongyang finally managed to visit the ship, and he informed the company that the sailors, with the exception of the captain, his assistant and two South Korean specialists (they were placed under arrest in a hotel), were being kept on the ship.
“There is no ventilation, the temperature is + 30-35 degrees, ” Sergei Sedler said.“ They interrogate and search twice a day, very harshly. ”
According to him, neither the Russian Embassy nor representatives of the company have been informed when the trial on their issue will begin.
As it was possible to find out RBC from the director of the company Viktor Sedler, the reason for the arrest was allegedly the illegal crossing of the border of the so-called military protection zone, which the DPRK arbitrarily established 50 nautical miles from the shore.
There is no reference in any international instruments to the possibility of establishing such a zone, there is only the concept of territorial waters (12 nautical miles from shore) and an exclusive economic zone (200 nautical miles from shore).
As reported by “Kommersant ” Sergei Sedler, the ship at the time of detention was without cargo.
The displacement of the fishing seiner is 290 tons, the length is 38 meters.
It has been fishing in the waters of the Sea of Japan for two years, but before that it had no such problems with the North Koreans.
It is worth noting that this is not the first such incident in recent years.
In 2016, the border guards of the DPRK detained the sports ship “Elfin ”, returning from the competition in the South Korean Busan.
It was escorted to one of the ports of the DPRK, but soon released.
Pyongyang described the incident as a “misunderstanding. ”
On June 19 this year, the Vladivostok Maritime Rescue Coordination Center reported that the Russian yacht Andiamo in the Sea of Japan, 112 miles off the coast of North Korea on the high seas, was allegedly trying to stop North Korean fishermen.
The yacht was later released and returned to the port of Nakhodka.
Nevertheless, this is the first time in a long time that detention has taken place for such a long time and under such harsh conditions as it is now.
Russian authorities often detain North Korean vessels engaged in poaching near the coast of Russia.
Periodically, the case takes a very dangerous turn: in October 2016, FSB border guards tried to detain a North Korean ship with 50 fishermen illegally catching crabs and squid.
Sailors resisted and border guards opened fire, injuring two Russians and nine North Koreans.
In June 2017, five more poachers from the DPRK were detained.
In June 2018, a similar incident occurred.
Usually detained North Koreans are charged under Art. 256 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (illegal extraction of aquatic biological resources) and Art. 322 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (illegal crossing of the state border of the Russian Federation).
“Kommersant ” requested comments from the Russian Foreign Ministry in connection with the current situation.
Mikhail Korostikov

title: North Korea Detains Russian Ship – 17 Seafarers Detained for a Week
text:
North Korean border guards detained the Russian fishing vessel “Xianghailin-8 ” in the Sea of Japan, on board of which there were 17 people: 15 citizens of the Russian Federation and 2 citizens of South Korea.
This is reported by the Russian Air Force Service.
The incident occurred on the night of 16 to 17 July, but it became known only on Tuesday, July 23.
The publication RBC, citing the director of the North-Eastern fishing company, which owns the seiner, reported that North Korean border guards stopped the ship 53 miles from the shore and slipped it to the port of Wonsan.
On Wednesday, the Russian Embassy in Pyongyang said that, according to representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the DPRK, the ship was detained for violating the rules of entry and stay in the territory of the DPRK.
North Korean border guards believed that the ship without notice crossed the protected area, told RIA Novosti Deputy Director of the North-Eastern fishing company Sergei Sedler.
He noted that, according to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, the territorial waters of the state are 12 miles from the shore, but the DPRK has established a military-protected zone for itself with an additional 50 miles.
According to him, the company carried out routing and made sure that the ship went along the usual route: caught a crab in the Primorye subzone, then went to the port of Zarubino, and then went to the South Korean port of Sokcho, on the way where it was detained.
On Wednesday, the Russian embassy in Pyongyang said there were 17 crew members on board the detained vessel, of whom 15 were Russian citizens and two were South Koreans.
"The embassy is taking all necessary measures to resolve the situation as soon as possible," the embassy said.
The embassy also said that on July 22 consular staff met with the crew members and made sure that they were healthy.
At the same time, the captain of the ship, his assistant and two South Korean sailors were placed in a hotel, and the rest of the fishermen were left on the ship.
The ship-owner company claims that the sailors remaining on the ship are kept in cabins and are not allowed on deck.
According to Sergei Sedler, the ship may run out of water and food.
“This is one crew, and we demand that all its members be returned on board and the ship returned to the owner, ” he said.
At the same time, the Russian news agency TASS, referring to the representative of the Embassy of the DPRK in Moscow, reports that the ship is now being inspected.
The ship was flying the South Korean flag.
The captain admitted that there was a violation of territorial waters.
Now our border guards are checking, ” said the Agency interlocutor.
The representative of the Embassy pointed out that, in his opinion, “given the good relations between Russia and the DPRK, after the check, the ship will be released to Russia. ”
The diplomat stressed that this is only his opinion, not the official position.
Recall that on November 25, 2018, Russian border guards attacked and seized two boats and a raid tug of the Ukrainian Navy along with the crew.
In this regard, on November 26, the Verkhovna Rada supported the issue of the introduction of martial law in Ukraine due to the open aggression of the FSB of the Russian Federation against the Ukrainian Navy.
In particular, the youngest of the Ukrainian sailors, Andrei Eyder was wounded during an attack by the Russian military on a Ukrainian ship and underwent surgery.
Martial law was imposed for 30 days in 10 regions: Mykolaiv, Vinnytsia, Donetsk, Zaporozhye, Luhansk, Odessa, Sumy, Kharkiv, Kherson and Chernihiv regions, as well as in the internal waters of the Azov-Kerch water area.
