הגיע המן לשלום! pic.twitter.com / AtNnQtnGZs — Donald J. Trump (@ realDonaldTrump) January 28, 2020 The head of the White House said that Israel is taking a “big step towards peace ”, embodying the US proposed“ deal of the century ”.
Trump also stressed that the plan does not pose a risk to Israel ’ s security.
The head of the White House said that the United States is forming a joint committee with Israel to implement these initiatives in order to develop a more detailed and accurate plan from the conceptual map.
It is assumed that Israel and Palestine must agree on all the details in four years.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in turn, called the “deal of the century ” a“ realistic path to peace. ”
However, he said, whatever the Palestinians decide, Israel will stick to the path of peace.
But if Palestine recognizes a Jewish state, Israel is ready for immediate peace talks.
Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas and the head of the Politburo of the Islamic movement Hamas Ismail Haniyeh after unveiling key aspects of the “deal of the century ” held telephone conversations and discussed joint steps to counter the plan put forward by Trump.
This was reported by the Al-Mayadeen TV channel.
According to Abbas, Palestine rejects this initiative.
“I want to tell Trump and Netanyahu that Jerusalem is not for sale.
All our rights are not for sale and are not subject to bargaining.
Your deal is a conspiracy, and it will not work, ” Abbas told a news conference in the city of Ramallah.
Abbas also stressed that Palestine "will not kneel and will not surrender."
In turn, the Jordanian Foreign Ministry said that unilateral Israeli measures lead to escalation in the region, the state agency Petra reports.
The ministry said that Israel is trying to impose the construction of illegal settlements, and also called for negotiations on the basis of the Arab peace initiative.
Arab League (LAS) Secretary General Ahmed Aboul Gheit said the “deal of the century ” would be successful only if the Palestinians negotiated with the Israelis“ with honest mediation, without trying to impose any solutions. ”
This is stated in the statement of the League.
As Arayik Stepanyan, a member of the Presidium of the Academy of Geopolitical Problems, notes in a conversation with RT, Trump ’ s statements on the “deal of the century ”“ quite a lot of contradictions. ”
“For example, East Jerusalem and Jerusalem cannot be the capitals of Palestine and Israel at the same time.
Also, his proposal to invest $50 billion for the needs of the future Palestinian state is not supported by anything - it is a bait to bribe Palestine, "the expert said.
At the same time, Stepanyan stressed that the head of the White House seeks to demonstrate to his voters that “he was the only one who was able to resolve the unresolved conflict. ”
However, according to the expert, the initiatives of the American leader “have no chance of success ”.
“I don ’ t see the grandiose, ingenious ‘ deal of the century ’ project that Palestine can agree to and which will be implemented later.
Netanyahu and his opponent agree to the deal, but Hamas and the Palestinian leadership have already rejected the plan.
Moreover, they will not agree to disarm, as the Palestinian leadership will hold on to the UN resolution of 2014, which stipulates that East Jerusalem is the capital of Palestine, ” the analyst explained.
The Palestinian-Israeli conflict has been ongoing since the mid-twentieth century and is part of a broader Arab-Israeli conflict.
Within its framework, the Palestinian and Israeli sides assert claims to the right and sovereignty over the same territory of the former British mandate.
The Palestinian side demands a solution to the conflict solely in the form of the establishment of two independent States on that territory, the borders of which will run along the lines that existed before the 1967 Six-Day War, when Israeli troops occupied the territory of the Jordan Valley (Judea and Samaria).
This will allow the Palestinians to establish their independent state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
However, Israel refuses to return to territorial division along the 1967 borders, and Jerusalem considers its “eternal and indivisible capital ”.
On the eve of the announcement of the American “deal of the century ”, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas refused a telephone conversation with Donald Trump and discussion of his settlement plan.
Also on the topic of the biased arbitrator: is there any prospects for a deal being prepared in the United States on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement, the American plan for the settlement of the Arab-Israeli conflict should take into account the interests of all parties, otherwise it will be rejected, he said.
“They called me from Washington, but I didn ’ t answer the call.
I said no, and I will continue to say no, ” the Palestinian leader told Al-Watan Voice.
In turn, Palestinian Prime Minister Mohammed Shtaye said that he does not accept the White House plan and called on the international community to reject the initiative of Washington.
“We reject this deal and demand that the international community not participate in it, as it runs counter to the foundations of international law and the inalienable rights of the Palestinians.
This is nothing more than a plan to destroy the Palestinian movement, "Prime Minister Al Jazeera said.
Steye added that the plan of the American president is aimed at solving the domestic political problems of Donald Trump himself, as well as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
“This plan is needed to protect Trump from impeachment and to protect Netanyahu from prison, not for a peaceful settlement, ” he said.
According to Alexander Vavilov, a professor at Moscow State University and an expert on the Middle East, Trump ’ s plan is his “usual political game. ”
“He is preparing this deal without consulting the Palestinian side and Russia, which has been dealing with this issue for 50 years.
The Trump plan assumes that the capital of Israel will be Jerusalem, and does not allow the concept of a two-state.
But his proposal is unrealistic, respectively, Palestine will not agree to its terms, ” the expert said in a conversation with RT.
As noted in the Russian Foreign Ministry, Russia will study the US proposed “deal of the century ” on the Middle East settlement.
This was stated by the Deputy head of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Mikhail Bogdanov.
According to him, “the decisions are made by the parties involved in the conflict – they are the Palestinians and the Israelis, the Americans do not make the decision. ”
"They have put forward an initiative, they will study it all.
But first of all, the parties to the conflict decide.
We are not parties to the conflict, ” — quotes the words of the diplomat RIA Novosti.
Earlier, Bogdanov, commenting on the announcement of the “deal of the century ”, stressed that the United States“ did not consult with the Palestinian leadership, which is a direct interested party. ”
The representative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also added that the United States did not consult with Russian representatives on this issue.
In addition, in October 2019, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, during a speech at the annual meeting of the Valdai International Discussion Club, noted that the proposals of the Trump administration are aimed at refusing a two-state solution to this issue.

At the same time, the Israeli side counts on interaction with Russia — on January 28, Benjamin Netanyahu ’ s press secretary said that the Israeli prime minister will fly to Moscow on January 29 to “familiarize Russian President Vladimir Putin with the“ deal of the century ” of US President Donald Trump and discuss various issues on the regional agenda. ”
The Kremlin confirmed that Vladimir Putin will meet with Netanyahu in Moscow on January 30, Thursday.
"On January 30, Moscow will host a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who will visit Russia on a brief working visit," the Kremlin said in a statement.
Elena Suponina, head of the Center for Asia and the Middle East at the Russian Institute for Strategic Studies, said the move signaled a trusting relationship between Russia and Israel, in which the Jewish state relies on Moscow ’ s possible mediation to influence Palestine.
“Recently, Russia and Israel have developed a good, trusting relationship, so Netanyahu considers it his duty to tell about the details of the initiative put forward by Trump, but he takes into account the desire of Moscow to continue to maintain relations with Palestine, ” the political scientist said.
The President of the Society for Friendship and Business Cooperation with Arab Countries, Vyacheslav Matuzov, in a conversation with RT, said that Donald Trump ’ s plan is aimed at strengthening his position in the United States, as well as helping Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a difficult situation in Israel.
In addition, the expert noted, Trump ’ s “deal of the century ” implies a change in the line of negotiations to resolve the conflict in favor of Israel.
“The goal of this initiative is to change the format of international negotiations on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement, because the United States wants to take this issue into its own hands and build a format of negotiations in favor of Israel.
Previously, the format of the international quartet operated, in which the settlement was supervised by the United States, Russia, Europe and the UN.
The United States did not like this state of affairs, because they could not put pressure on the positions of the Arab countries, ” the political scientist explained.
Now Washington is trying to reconsider the problem of the Palestinians as it will be more convenient to perceive the White House, Vyacheslav Matuzov added.
"But the Americans do not understand that there is no solution to this problem without the Palestinian people.
The Palestinian leadership, in turn, has already appealed to the Arab League to take a consolidated position.
Most likely, Palestine will achieve its goal, and this plan will not be accepted by the world community.
This Trump deal is insane, it cannot be implemented just because of sympathy for Israel, because there is a Palestinian people whose interests need to be taken into account.
If the Americans act without taking into account his interests, they will never achieve their goal, ” the expert concluded.
Source: Russia Today

title: The Kremlin commented on the “deal of the century ” trump
text:
US President Donald Trump on January 28 spoke at the White House and described the main provisions of the “deal of the century ” to resolve the conflict between Palestine and Israel.
At the announcement of the plan, next to the American leader stood the acting Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu, while representatives of Palestine were not invited to Washington.
The absence of the Palestinian side has caused a number of questions from the international community, but the greatest resonance is associated with the terms of the “deal ” itself.
The Trump plan was published on the White House website in the form of a 180-page document, it consists of two parts – political and economic.
The basis of the "deal of the century" is the provision on the recognition of two states - Arab and Jewish.
Thus, the territory of Palestine will include the Gaza Strip and the West Bank of the Jordan River, the United States proposed to link them with high-speed transport links.
At the same time, Washington is going to recognize the legal Jewish settlements on Palestinian territory - we are talking about the lands that were occupied by Israel in the West Bank of the Jordan River.
In his Twitter, Trump even published a map with the proposed changes already made, noting that this may look like a future state of Palestine.
This is what a future State of Palestine can look like, with a capital in parts of East Jerusalem.
pic.twitter.com / 39vw3pPrAL — Donald J. Trump (@ realDonaldTrump) January 28, 2020 The status of Jerusalem is highlighted in the document.
The United States proposed to make East Jerusalem the capital of Palestine, but at the same time to recognize the “indivisible capital ” of Israel all Jerusalem.
As Netanyahu explained, East Jerusalem refers to the suburb of Abu Dis, not the eastern part of the city.
In addition, the implementation of the deal presupposes the fulfillment of a number of conditions by Palestine
Thus, the authorities of the country should stop supporting the Hamas movement, which operates in the Gaza Strip, as well as abandon the methods of armed struggle.
Israel, in turn, is obliged to freeze programs for the construction of Jewish settlements in the Palestinian territory for four years — this time is set aside for negotiations on the formation of Palestinian statehood.
The economic part of Trump ’ s plan is to allocate $50 billion for various projects in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, as well as in Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon.
For this purpose, an appropriate investment fund will be created, which will support these projects for 10 years.
Nevertheless, the United States did not rule out that the presented plan can be finalized taking into account the position of all parties.
Trump ’ s senior adviser and son-in-law Jared Kushner said the terms of the “deal of the century ” are not final.
“This is a starting offer.
If the Palestinians want to make amendments, change some lines, change some wording, hold negotiations on other issues, then a flexible approach is possible, ” Kushner said.
Netanyahu ’ s Palestinian response, as expected, supported the “deal of the century ” and declared its readiness to begin negotiations with the Palestinians.
The Israeli prime minister is confident that Trump ’ s plan offers a “realistic path to lasting peace ” and gives the Jewish state a permanent eastern border.
In Palestine, they hold a diametrically opposite point of view, since the “deal of the century ” ignores the key demands of the Palestinians – the withdrawal of the Israelis from the territory of the country in the West Bank and the transfer to Palestine of the eastern part of Jerusalem.
The plan of the US president is a conspiracy that will not pass, says Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas.
“We give priority to the resistance front to thwart Israeli plans, ” the Palestinian president added.
Palestine rejects the "deal of the century" presented by Trump, the head of the country stressed, negotiations with Israel can take place only under the patronage of the "quartet" of international mediators - Russia, the United States, the UN and the EU.
Hamas also pointed out that Trump ’ s plan together with the US president “will go to the dustbin of history. ”
According to Abu Zuhri, the “deal of the century ” is not even worth the ink with which it was written.
Criticism of the Democrats negatively reacted to the “deal of the century ” even in the United States.
Democrats in the Senate sent a letter to the president criticizing his proposals.
In the message, they pointed to the unilateral nature of Trump ’ s proposal for a peaceful settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict, as it was prepared without the participation of Palestine.
The senators stressed that the implementation of the agreement by one of the parties could destroy the prospects for a peaceful settlement of the conflict within the framework of the two-state concept.
The assertion of Israeli sovereignty over the Jordan Valley and Jewish settlements in the West Bank would be a violation of international law, the letter says, it will cause a negative reaction from a number of US allies.
"Deal of Shame" Criticized the US plan also in Turkey and Iran.
The Turkish Foreign Ministry described the “deal of the century ” as an annexation aimed at usurping the territories of Palestine and destroying the very idea of ​ ​ the existence of a state.
In Ankara, they promised not to allow the implementation of plans that will legalize the tyranny of Israel.
In turn, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zafir called Trump ’ s plan a nightmare for the whole world and the Middle East.
In his opinion, the actions of the United States should be a signal for the unification of all Muslims.
The conclusions of Iran and Turkey were also supported in the Lebanese Hezbollah.
The party dubbed the "deal of the century" a "deal of shame", which was the result of the betrayal of a number of Arab countries - participants in the "behind the scenes conspiracy".
Arab support The response of Egypt and Jordan has been more restrained.
Cairo called on the parties to the conflict to carefully study the “deal ” to open channels for the resumption of negotiations under the auspices of the United States, stressing that the final agreement should meet the“ aspirations and hopes of the two peoples to achieve a comprehensive and just peace between them. ”
Jordan has declared its commitment to a two-state solution to the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and has also advocated a common position on the “deal of the century ” at the upcoming meeting of the League of Arab States (LAS).
Arab League Secretary General Ahmed Aboul Gheit called the US plan a violation of the rights of the Palestinians and noted the need for negotiations between the parties to the conflict.
At the same time, Saudi Arabia praised the efforts of the United States to resolve the crisis in the region.
Riyadh called for direct negotiations between Palestine and Israel under the auspices of Washington.
“Sustainable peace ” In Europe, responding to Trump ’ s initiative, pointed to the problematic points of the plan.
For example, Sweden noted the discrepancy of the US proposals to the position of the European Union on resolving the conflict
The Foreign Ministry called for negotiations between the two sides to achieve a sustainable peace, and also called for taking into account the demands of both Israel and Palestine.
This line was supported by German Foreign Minister Heiko Maas, according to him, the Trump plan raises a number of certain questions.
“Among other things, these are the issues of involving the parties to the conflict in the negotiation process, as well as the attitude [of the US plan] to the recognized international parameters and legal provisions, ” the German Foreign Minister stressed.
Trump ’ s plan was welcomed in Britain and France.
British Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab described the “deal of the century ” as a serious proposal that was the result of“ great efforts ”.
The French Foreign Ministry also appreciated the efforts of the United States to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
At the same time, the French Foreign Ministry promised to carefully study the US peace plan.
Meanwhile, Russia has not yet given any assessments of the document presented by the US president.
As stated by the press Secretary of the President of the Russian Federation Dmitry Peskov, the Kremlin continues to analyze the plan for a peaceful Palestinian-Israeli settlement.
“Tomorrow there will also be a meeting [of Russian President Vladimir Putin] with Netanyahu and more information will be received, as they say, first-hand, ” Peskov added.
It is worth noting that Russia officially recognizes West Jerusalem as the capital of Israel - the corresponding statement of the Russian authorities was made in April 2017.
At the same time, Moscow views East Jerusalem as the capital of future Palestine.
In addition, the Russian side does not recognize Jewish settlements in the West Bank of the Jordan River — the territory of Palestine.
Moscow, like most European countries, considers these buildings illegal.

title: Bloomberg: Is Palestine “ripe ” for Trump ’ s peace plan?
text:
It will take time for Israelis to believe in victory, just as it will take time for Palestinians to realize that what is being offered to them is not total defeat.
Alexander Belov, 10: 33 – REGNUM The “Deal of the Century ”, unveiled on Tuesday, January 28, in Washington, D.C., is not a peace agreement between Israel and the Palestinians.
The United States simply said that the Six-Day War was over and Israel had won, writes American-Israeli writer and columnist Zeev Chafetz in an article for Bloomberg.
Israel and Palestine Ivan Shilov © IA REGNUM Read also: Bloomberg: how do Johnson ’ s pink dreams relate to reality?
Palestinian authorities in the West Bank vehemently rejected the verdict.
They stated that much of the international community was opposed to the terms of the plan, which recognized Israel's sovereignty over all settlements in the West Bank, the Jordan Valley and important areas of East Jerusalem.
All of this is true.
But it will not be of any use to the Palestinians.
Foreign friends sympathize with them.
Some may even threaten to impose sanctions.
But the “international community ” and the largely dysfunctional Arab League are unable to change the US-Israeli vision.
And, surprisingly, some Sunni Arab states seem willing to at least consider a Middle East plan.
At least three Arab ambassadors abandoned the decades-long boycott and decided to attend the ceremony.
The agreement provides for the establishment of a demilitarized Palestinian entity on much of the West Coast.
This state will emerge gradually over four years, depending on the cessation of terrorism and the willingness of Palestine to recognize Israel as a Jewish state.
Israeli opposition leader Benny Gantz is also ready to support the American Middle East plan.
He just has no other choice.
Once upon a time, Palestinians could count on solidarity with the Israeli camp for the peaceful resolution of disputes, but after the Intifada in the early 2000s, the camp turned into a small herd of chirping idealists.
Benny Gantz srael Defense Forces It is said that the Palestinian authorities are preparing mass demonstrations, but according to Israeli intelligence estimates, President Mahmoud Abbas does not want an armed uprising.
In any case, it seems that the Palestinians do not want street fights.
Many West Bank residents have jobs in Israel, as well as business ties that will quickly fade in the event of a new armed uprising.
In any case, the new agreement will not change the lives of most Palestinians.
Israeli settlements already exist (and many West Bank residents work there).
Very few Palestinians live in the Jordan Valley, which has long been Israel ’ s eastern border.
It is assumed that the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem will remain under the care of the Jordanian Hashemite king and will be managed by the Waqf religious foundation.
The Middle East plan may even benefit those Palestinians who have put quality of life above national ideology.
Trump has decided to offer these Palestinians a consolation prize of $50 billion, as well as other foreign aid and investment.
It can also be expected that Israel will open its doors more widely to those who are looking for work and want to take part in joint economic and infrastructure projects.
President Abbas is offended by the fact that the Palestinian case is up for sale.
“We will never sell Palestine! ” he said.
But Abbas is already old, he is sick.
His successors are already waiting for the day when he will lose power.
They have lived their entire lives under Israeli rule, and most of them have excellent knowledge of Hebrew due to their long prison terms.
They are by no means Zionists, but they are very practical people who understand that the realization of the revolutionary dream of Arafat and Abbas is impossible.
There will be no Palestinian army, no military pacts with Arab like-minded people.
It is better to have a small state than nothing at all.
Some members of the old Palestinian guard continue to cling to the hope that this is just a bad dream that will soon end.
This week, they received support from former U.S. Ambassador to Israel Daniel Shapiro, who published an article in which he predicts the arrival of a Democratic president in 2021 or 2025.
The Democratic administration, Shapiro writes, will unilaterally reverse Trump ’ s policy.
The Israeli-Palestinian border Justin McIntosh Read also: Asia Times: US elections can decide the fate of negotiations between the EU and China I do not think that the Palestinians should count on this.
Even former US President Barack Obama at the peak of his presidency could not force Israel to agree to the creation of an armed Palestinian entity, as well as the evacuation of settlements.
However, there is no need to rush to conclusions.
53 years after the Six-Day War, what happened in Washington looks too good to be true.
It will take time for the Israelis to believe in victory, just as it will take time for the Palestinians to realize that what they are being offered is not a complete defeat.

title: Will Putin make the “deal of the century ” with Israel and the United States?
text:
MOSCOW, 30 Jan — RIA Novosti, Galiya Ibragimova, Sofia Melnichuk.
Barely returning from the United States, Benjamin Netanyahu arrives in Moscow.
He intends to disclose at a meeting with Vladimir Putin the details of the “deal of the century ” on the Arab-Israeli settlement.
The Russian Foreign Ministry has already made it clear that the deal will not take place without agreement with the Palestinian side.
However, Netanyahu has another goal, which is also quite delicate.
“Israel ’ s greatest friend ” Putin and Netanyahu met last week in Jerusalem at Holocaust commemoration events.
But the Palestinian-Israeli settlement plan, developed and published the other day in the United States, the Israeli Prime Minister considered a good reason to meet with the Russian president again.
Netanyahu expects that Moscow ’ s assessment of Washington ’ s and Tel Aviv ’ s peacekeeping initiatives may affect their perception in the world.
But the main thing is that the Palestinians can listen to the opinion of Russia, which has always been authoritative in the Arab world.
However, the Kremlin has so far reacted with extreme restraint to the deal presented by the administration of Donald Trump.
The special representative of the Russian President for the Middle East and Africa, Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov said that it is too early to draw any conclusions.
“We believe that it is necessary to enter into direct negotiations [with the Palestinians] and reach mutually acceptable compromises.
We do not know how Washington ’ s ideas are mutually acceptable for all parties to the conflict, ” Bogdanov said.
It would be necessary to listen to the opinion of the Quartet on the Middle East settlement — the EU, the United States, Russia, the UN, stressed in Moscow.
Brussels itself was not averse to participating in the preparation of the plan.
However, Trump refused the help of intermediaries.
The document was written by his adviser and son-in-law Jared Kushner.
This, in turn, took into account mainly the position of Israel.
"There is nothing more difficult in the world than to reconcile Israelis and Palestinians.
But I didn ’ t become president to deal with small issues.
“The deal of the century is beneficial to both sides, and this is a huge step towards peace, ” the US president said at the presentation of the long-awaited settlement plan.
“You have shown yourself to be Israel ’ s greatest friend who has ever been in the White House, ” Netanyahu responded to the deal by giving his full support.
© REUTERS / Joshua Roberts US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a joint press conference in Washington DC © REUTERS / Joshua Roberts US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a joint press conference in Washington The essence of the deal The text of the "deal of the century" of 181 pages consists of political and economic sections.
At the heart of the political part of the document is the principle of “two states for two peoples ”: along with Israel, Palestine will appear on the world map.
The document stipulates that Jerusalem should become the indivisible capital of Israel.
At the same time, the sovereignty of the Jewish state can extend to a significant part of the Jordan Valley.
Trump believes that the “deal of the century ” is beneficial to the Arabs, as he proposes to recognize East Jerusalem as the capital of the Palestinians.
According to the land partition map that is attached to the "deal", it refers to neighborhoods outside the separation fence built by Israel.
The old city will not enter the borders of the Palestinian capital.
"If the deal is implemented, the Palestinian territories will be twice as large as the territories they control today," Trump said.
The divided lands of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, according to the Americans, can be connected by tunnels.
And the airspace over these territories will be controlled by the Palestinians.
But first they must recognize Palestine as a demilitarized state.
The deal also calls for a number of demands on Israel.
It is important to recognize the independence of Palestine.
The construction of new settlements in the West Bank will have to be frozen for four years.
The economic part of the deal is built around projects to be implemented in the West Bank, Gaza, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon.
The investment will be $50 billion.
This money, according to Washington ’ s calculations, will be given to the Palestinians by the Arab monarchies of the Persian Gulf.
The authors of the "deal" hope for the help of private capital.
This is what a future State of Palestine can look like, with a capital in parts of East Jerusalem.
pic.twitter.com / 39vw3pPrAL — Donald J. Trump (@ realDonaldTrump) January 28, 2020 "Jerusalem is not for sale" Neither before nor after the release of information about the "deal" has any country expressed its willingness to invest in potential projects in Palestine.
Moreover, most countries in the Middle East criticized the document.
"Jerusalem is not for sale, Palestinian rights are not for sale and cannot be traded.
Your deal is a conspiracy, and it will not pass, "Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas said.
“Trump and his ‘ deal of the century ’ have a place in the dustbin of history.
The document is not even worth the ink with which it is written, ” said Sami Abu Zuhri, a spokesman for Hamas, which controls the Gaza Strip.
In protest, the Palestinians protested.
In the Gaza Strip, rallies began a few days before the presentation of the document.
The initiative was strongly criticized by Turkey and Iran.
Egypt and Jordan called for a "closer examination of the document".
Opinions were also divided in Europe.
Germany, France, and Sweden supported American peacemaking efforts, but condemned the one-sided — pro-Israel — view of the problem.
In support of the "deal" was made by the UK.
"The plan is an important step in the right direction," Johnson said.
© REUTERS / Ibraheem Abu Mustafa Protest against the Palestinian-Israeli settlement plan in the southern Gaza Strip © REUTERS / Ibraheem Abu Mustafa Protest against the Palestinian-Israeli settlement plan in the southern Gaza Strip Remove an Israeli woman from prison There is another reason why Netanyahu comes to Moscow.
On the eve of Israeli politicians did not rule out that the Prime Minister plans to personally attend the release of compatriot Naama Issachar.
In autumn, a 26-year-old Israeli woman was detained in the transit zone of Sheremetyevo airport.
In her luggage found nine grams of hashish and sentenced to seven years in prison.
The case caused a great public outcry.
With a request for pardon to the President of Russia addressed the mother Issachar.
“Everything will be fine, ” Putin promised her.
A couple of days ago, her mother arrived in Russia, and a day later it became known about the visit of the Israeli prime minister to Moscow.
The day before, Putin pardoned Naama Issachar, and this morning she was released.
Interviewed by RIA Novosti experts agreed that the central topic of negotiations between Putin and Netanyahu will still be the "deal of the century."
But they warned that Moscow ’ s skepticism about the US-Israeli initiative is unlikely to change.
“This is a completely unfinished document.
It violates the rights of Palestinians to part of Jerusalem, which are laid down by the UN Security Council resolution.
The American plan has not been approved by international organizations, has not received the approval of the Palestinians.
The Secretary General of the League of Arab States recognized that the rights of the Palestinians in the deal are infringed, ” — said in an interview with RIA Novosti scientific Director of the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences Vitaly Naumkin.
To hear the opinion of the Palestinians, the expert believes it is advisable to combine the efforts of Fatah (a paramilitary organization and a political party) and Hamas.
“These organizations, which govern the West Bank and Gaza, now it is advisable to agree among themselves and agree on a common point of view on the plan of the Americans.
Then they can be heard.
But the problem is that the split within the Palestinians hinders the promotion of their own interests in this difficult situation, ” said Naumkin.
Middle East specialist political scientist Nurlan Gasimov notes that the deal involves the transfer of a significant part of the West Bank under Israeli control.
The territory is now divided into three zones: A, B and C. Zone A includes about 17 percent of the land that is controlled by the Palestinians.
Area B is under the joint control of Palestinians and Israelis.
And the largest Area C includes almost 60 percent of the territory and is fully controlled by Israel.
At the same time, it is in zone C that the fertile lands are located.
But the main thing is that all fresh water reserves are concentrated there.
Israel in 1993, signing the Oslo agreement on the settlement of the conflict with the Palestinians, drew the map so as to populate suitable territories.
Trump ’ s “Deal of the Century ” is aimed at the final transfer of these lands to Israel.
It turns out that the Palestinians will be denied access even to fresh water, ” Gasimov explains.
The territories on which Trump proposes to create a state of Palestine, according to the political scientist, are divided enclaves.
"Mostly, these are areas A and B. But even if you connect them with bridges and tunnels, Israel can easily block them at any time.
In addition, it is difficult to manage disparate territories from the point of view of state administration.
Developing any economic projects there is also not easy.
This inferiority is understood by the Palestinians, Israelis, and Americans, ” Gasimov explains.
The settlement plan, according to the expert, is also designed for domestic audiences in Israel and the United States.
“The impeachment process of the president continues in the United States.
Israel has a third election.
Hence, it is beneficial for both Trump and Netanyahu to mobilize the right-wing electorate through the “deal of the century, ” he said.
Former Knesset deputy and expert at the Herzliya Interdisciplinary Institute in Israel, Ksenia Svetlova, agrees that the initiative under discussion is part of Netanyahu ’ s election campaign.
"Netanyahu flew to the United States before the Knesset meeting.
Parliamentarians are going to consider the issue of granting judicial immunity to the prime minister in connection with corruption charges.
Deprivation of immunity is now extremely unprofitable for him.
To many Israelis, it seems that there are no urgent circumstances that would justify the Prime Minister ’ s visits to the United States or Russia.
Moreover, the “deal of the century ” took shape about a year and a half ago and was postponed all the time, ” recalls Svetlova.

title: Winemaking from global warming will save Russia
text:
Winemaking is in danger of extinction due to global warming.
This is stated in a study by Columbia University.
If the temperature rises by two degrees Celsius, the number of grapes suitable for growing will be reduced by 56%, and with warming by four degrees - by 85%.
Vineyards in Italy, Spain and Australia are already suffering losses due to rising temperatures.
Experts suggest moving to more heat-resistant varieties.
This can reduce the loss of suitable land for viticulture from 65% to 24% with a warming of two degrees and from 85% to 58% with a temperature increase of four degrees.
The President of the Union of winegrowers and winemakers of Russia Leonid Popovich on the air NSN urged not to dramatize the situation.

title: Why Trump Needs an Impossible Middle East Peace Plan
text:
Why would Trump want an impossible Middle East peace plan? The Israeli-Palestinian conflict settlement plan, which Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu have called the deal of the century, has been perceived very differently in the world and in Israel itself, and few see it as a sincere attempt to achieve peace.
Under the terms of the plan, the capital of Israel should be in indivisible Jerusalem, the Palestinians renounce violence and receive $50 billion for the creation of a Palestinian state.
In addition, Israel's sovereignty over part of the West Bank is effectively recognized.
Despite the fact that most Israelis may want to fulfill all these conditions, many believe that this is at least impossible, and at most a threat to the security of the country.
Israeli media quoted Defense Minister Naftali Benet as saying, “There is a clear and immediate danger right before our eyes: the creation of a Palestinian state. ”
In addition, Washington, in fact, recognizes the legitimacy of the annexation of additional Palestinian territories, which is likely to lead to a new intifada.
"This is a horror, not a peace plan.
Not only will it not solve the problem, but it can lead to irreversible consequences.
What surprises me most is the reaction of the international community.
Those who applaud this plan don ’ t really want peace in the region, ” said Yossi Beilin, an ideologist of the historic Oslo talks in 1993, a former member of the Israeli government.
At one time, as deputy foreign minister of Israel, Beilin initiated secret negotiations, which resulted in the so-called Oslo agreement – the most mutually beneficial in the history of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
Then Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and the leader of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) Yasser Arafat exchanged friendly letters on mutual recognition, renunciation of all forms of violence and much more.
“All these architects of the Middle East ’ s failures are better off now, ” Jonathan Tobin, a political commentator, wrote in the Israel Hayom newspaper.
In his opinion, none of the previous American administrations managed to come up with any miraculous recipes, otherwise Israel would not have suffered from terrorism for many years.
“Yes, Trump had no experience in international politics when he became president.
And his team, which he appointed to deal with the Palestinian-Israeli problem, is also inexperienced in diplomacy.
In particular, the trio of his closest advisers — son-in-law Jared Kushner, special envoy for the Middle East Jason Greenblatt and US Ambassador to Israel David Friedman — were close to Trump in real estate, ” admits Tobin.
And therefore, writes the observer, they and their decisions are always treated with mockery and arrogance.
But we do not yet know how Trump and Kushner will leave the Middle East, but we know perfectly well how unsuccessful the attempts of all previous mediators were.
Does Trump save Bibi from prison?
The “historic agreement ” that Trump offered to Netanyahu is a cheque written out by a bankrupt.
This is a satanic, grandiose and ridiculous plan that has only two goals: to get Bibi out of prison and establish his place in history as the builder of the State of Israel, ” said Ran Edliste, a columnist for the Israeli newspaper Maariv.
This is a very popular view in Israel.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been charged with corruption.
Last November, the attorney general charged him with bribery, fraud and breach of trust.
Netanyahu does not admit guilt and in early January asked the Israeli parliament to grant him immunity from prosecution, but later withdrew this petition, deciding, as he put it, “to end this political spectacle. ”
Netanyahu ’ s position at the moment is very shaky: he was unable to form a coalition after the parliamentary elections in April last year, and in the elections in September 2019 he did not get a majority of votes, although he remained at the helm, since his opponent Benny Gantz also did not collect a coalition with a majority of votes in the Knesset.
In March, Netanyahu is waiting for his third election in less than a year, in which Israel will spend tens of millions of shekels, and Israeli Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit can bring the criminal case to court at any time.
In May last year, the country ’ s opposition parties brought tens of thousands of people to the streets of Tel Aviv, who demanded that it not be granted immunity from prosecution.
At the time, Netanyahu ’ s Likud supporters (but not himself) said they would seek his release from any charges while he was in office.
“They both have elections, but the Middle East is not a platform for an election campaign, it is a very serious issue for millions of Israelis and Palestinians, ” Yossi Beilin told the BBC.
Opinion polls have shown that 51% of Israelis favor the trial of Netanyahu and only 33% on his side.
Six weeks before the election, four weeks before the end of the election campaign, and Netanyahu will now rightly push the issue of Israeli sovereignty to divert attention from the upcoming trial, predicts Israeli journalist Mati Touchfeld.
In fact, according to Touchfeld, Netanyahu almost won on the day of the publication of the plan, since his opponents on the right have no reason to criticize him.
“Although I can ’ t find a rational explanation for his desire to annex the Jordan Valley.
Why her?
How does this part of the territory threaten the security of Israel?
Any Israeli will look at the map and ask the same question.
A very strange election move, ” comments Yossi Beilin, an old-timer of Israeli politics.
Status and power: what does Trump want?
“Trump wanted to prove to the world that he is capable of solving problems that others can ’ t.
But he probably did not know that, for example, his “green light ” for Israel ’ s annexation of the Jordan Valley is a violation of an international agreement, which was guaranteed by his own country, ” said Yossi Beilin.
Experts at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Aaron David Miller and Robert Malley, believe that Trump is pursuing much more serious goals.
In their opinion, the plan, drawn up without the participation of the Palestinian side and published at a very difficult moment in the career of the Israeli Prime Minister, should help Trump to enlist the support of the pro-Israel lobby and the most conservative Republicans.
This is an important move for a president who wants to be re-elected, experts say.
In addition, Trump can not play with power.
For Trump, they write, power that you do not use is meaningless.
“In short, this plan gives Israel everything it wants, recognizes the Palestinians for everything Israel doesn ’ t care about, tries to buy the Palestinians with $50 billion in aid promises that will never happen, and all this is called a ‘ peace plan, ’ ” Miller and Malley wrote in their analyst for Politico.
“Trump is a businessman, he thinks in appropriate categories.
He thought he would offer the Palestinians 50 billion and they would take it.
It's bullshit.
Many often say that the Palestinians themselves miss their opportunities, but in this case, no opportunities were offered to them, ” agrees Yossi Beilin.
What do the Palestinians say?
“This plan has nothing to do with the United States.
This is Netanyahu ’ s pure plan, which he presented back in 2012, just word for word, Kushner (Trump ’ s adviser and son-in-law, the author of the plan – approx.
The BBC) did not add even a comma there, ” said Saeb Erekat, head of the negotiation process on the part of the Palestinians and a representative of the head of the PA Mahmoud Abbas, in a comment to the BBC Russian Service.
After Benjamin Netanyahu took office as Prime Minister of Israel in 2009, then-US President Barack Obama asked him to take steps to resolve the conflict within a short time.
“Then he came up with a plan in which he agreed to the creation of a Palestinian state, but with limited rights.
That is, in fact, he proposed the formula “one state, two systems ” and exactly all the points that we heard in the allegedly new Trump plan.
And then, and now, the fate that these allies offer to the Palestinians is life under apartheid, ” he said.
The fact that the Palestinians did not expect anything good from the "deal of the century" for themselves is evidenced by the fact that thousands of people in the West Bank protested even before the plan was made public.
According to Saib Erekat, while the US is the mediator in the negotiations, no agreements can be reached.
“Washington is part of the problem between us, not the way to solve it.
We are grateful for the efforts made by Russia, China, Europe, the Arab world, but in the end it is only our business — the Palestinians and the Israelis.
Only we can achieve a settlement, ” he said.
Israeli politician Yossi Beilin agrees with him.
“No one, for example, even remembered about the Middle East Quartet (the union of the European Union, Russia, the United States and the UN, created to mediate in the settlement – approx.
BBC).
And the quartet swallowed it all.
They didn ’ t even say stop, and why didn ’ t you at least show us the peace plan before making it public, let alone consult with us, ” Beilin said.
Yossi Beilin also believes that the time of intermediaries is over: "They were needed before 1993, and now we can call, freely travel to each other."
Trump ’ s “peace plan ” has unexpectedly fostered unity among Palestinian factions.
Hamas and Fatah, which have been unable to reach an agreement for many years, have started talking about the need for unification.
Hamas has always opposed negotiations with Israel, while the more moderate Fatah has called for diplomatic methods of settlement.
Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday he was ready to make a visit to the Hamas-controlled Gaza Strip, which has not been the case since 2007.
Hamas officials have not yet confirmed that they are waiting for distinguished guests, but according to Saib Erekat, a delegation from the West Bank is indeed going to visit the Gaza Strip in February.
"The unification of key Palestinian parties is possible and, in fact, it is the only way to break the impasse and open a new chapter of negotiations," Saeb Erekat told the BBC.
With the participation of Anastasia Zlatopolskaya.

title: Abbas: Palestinians will break off all relations with the US and Israel
text:
The head of the Palestinian Authority, Mahmut Abbas, said that his administration will break off all relations, including security cooperation, with Israel and the United States because of disagreement with the plan for a peaceful settlement of the Middle East conflict proposed this week by US President Donald Trump.
Speaking at a meeting of Arab League foreign ministers in Cairo, Abbas said he would never accept the terms proposed by Trump.
Abbas said he would not negotiate with Israel on the basis of the plan.
The Palestinian leader said he would not talk to Trump either.
Both the Palestinian Authority leadership and the radical Hamas movement that controls the Gaza Strip have previously rejected the peace plan.
Saudi Arabia and Egypt praised the efforts of the US president to find ways out of the conflict and called on both sides of the conflict to study the US proposals, but did not directly support them.
Definitely rejected the Trump plan, in particular, Iran and Syria.
The plan, which Trump called the “deal of the century, ” provides for the creation of an independent Palestinian state, but only in part of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.
According to the plan, the Jordan Valley should go to Israel, in addition, Jerusalem should become a single and indivisible capital of Israel (although East Jerusalem is also mentioned as the capital of the Palestinian state).
The plan also provides for the allocation of up to $50 billion to Palestine.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu supported the plan.
The Palestinians, however, find many of its provisions unacceptable.
Abbas said at a meeting in Cairo that he would "not sell Jerusalem."
Protests took place in the West Bank on Friday.

title: Palestine says it is breaking relations with the United States and Israel
text:
The head of the Palestinian National Authority (PNA), Mahmoud Abbas, said that he had notified the United States and Israel of the rupture of all relations with them by Palestine because of the “deal of the century ” announced by American President Donald Trump.
"We have sent two letters - one to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the other to the United States - that Palestine will not have any relations with them, including in the field of security, in light of their denial of previously concluded agreements and international law," Abbas said at a meeting of the Arab League in Cairo, where Arab countries' reactions to the deal were discussed.
He also noted that the US is “no longer a friend ” of the PNA.
At the same time, Abbas said that he had previously informed Trump of his intention to make Palestine a demilitarized state, although some factions oppose his idea.
“I would rather build a hospital than buy a tank, ” he said.
Recall, on January 28, Donald Trump presented his “deal of the century ” to resolve the“ eternal conflict ” between Israel and the Palestinian Authority with their division into two states.
Abbas rejected the US proposal.
However, the United States said that in the short term, the opinion of Palestine does not matter.
The newspaper VZGLYAD reported that the plan announced by Trump will have only one long-term effect - this is the strengthening of Russia's position in the Middle East and in the Islamic world in general.
Last: The plane with German citizens evacuated from Chinese Wuhan, instead of a planned landing in Moscow, landed in Helsinki, reports the newspaper Helsingin Sanomat.
“Shortly before landing in Moscow, the Russian Federation refused to land the aircraft, he was forced to move to Helsinki-Vantaa ”, – quotes the message of the newspaper RIA“ Novosti ”.
The company managing the Finnish airport Finavia, confirmed the landing of the aircraft.
They noted that […]

title: Pushkov: armor-piercing trump was slapped
text:
“The deal of the century, ” proposed by US President Donald Trump,“ ended badly, ” said the head of the Federation Council Commission on information policy Alexei Pushkov.
“A lot of noise and a clear failure, ” he commented on Twitter.
Earlier today, the head of the Palestinian National Authority, Mahmoud Abbas, said at an extraordinary meeting of the Arab League in Cairo: Palestine broke off diplomatic relations with Israel and the United States.
Arab leaders gathered in the Egyptian capital to discuss Trump ’ s proposed “deal of the century ” for Palestine and Israel.
Trump proposed demilitarizing Palestine and recognizing the city of Abu Dis on the eastern outskirts of Jerusalem as its capital.
For this, Palestine would receive $50 billion in investment.
Mahmoud Abbas accused the United States and Israel of violating previous agreements and international law.
"Palestine will not have any relations with them, including in the field of security.
“The United States is no longer a friend of the PNA, ” he said.
Palestine is not going to negotiate a peace plan proposed by the Americans and insists on recognizing its state within the 1967 borders with Jerusalem as its capital.

title: Palestine breaks off relations with US and Israel over 'deal of the century'
text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announced the end of all relations with Israel and the United States.
The reason for this decision, according to him, was the so-called “deal of the century ” – the plan of the American leader Donald Trump for a peaceful settlement in the Middle East.
As noted by the head of the partially recognized state, the notifications with the refusal of Palestine from the US proposals have already been sent to the Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu, as well as to the American authorities, reports Economy Today.
“Palestine will not have any relations with them, including in the field of security, in the light of their rejection of previously concluded agreements and international law, ” Abbas said at a meeting of the Arab League in Cairo, where the Arab countries ’ reaction to the“ deal of the century ” was discussed.
Federation Council member Alexei Pushkov commented on the decision of the Palestinian leader on Twitter.

title: Palestine says it will end all relations with the US and Israel
text:
18: 19 Palestine terminates all relations with the United States and Israel after US President Donald Trump announced the “deal of the century ”.

"We have sent two letters - one to the acting Prime Minister of Israel Benjamin Netanyahu, the second to the United States - that Palestine will not have any relations with them, including in the field of security, in the light of their denial of previously concluded agreements and international law," Abbas said.
He also noted that he had previously notified the US president of his intention to make Palestine a demilitarized state, although some factions oppose this idea.
“I ’ d rather build a hospital than buy a tank, ” he said.
On January 28, Trump presented the “deal of the century ” — a draft agreement that should end the conflict between Israel and Palestine.
The plan recognizes Jerusalem as the united and indivisible capital of Israel, rejects the fundamental Palestinian problem of refugee return, opens up the possibility for Israel to annex Palestinian territories in the West Bank and extend its sovereignty over the Jordan Valley.
In the case of Palestine, the "deal of the century" presupposes the creation of a demilitarized State devoid of control over its borders and airspace.
To make the capital of this state is planned Abu Dis, a city on the eastern outskirts of Jerusalem, behind the "security fence".
The economic part of Trump ’ s plan provides for the allocation of $50 billion to Palestine over a decade, primarily at the expense of the sponsoring countries from the Persian Gulf.
The subject of the return to the 1967 borders by the "Deal of the Century" has been completely ignored.
Abbas rejected the plan, saying the Palestinians were insisting on recognizing their state within the borders that existed before the 1967 Six-Day War, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

title: “Makes you think about the viability of the plan ”: Russia pointed out the discrepancy of the“ deal of the century ” to the UN Security Council resolutions
text:

Earlier in Palestine and the Arab League confirmed that they do not accept the plan proposed by Washington to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
According to experts, the “deal of the century ” is largely needed by the US leadership to solve domestic political problems.
The Kremlin said that the US “deal of the century ” on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement does not comply with a number of UN Security Council resolutions.
Press Secretary of the President of Russia Dmitry Peskov drew attention to the reaction of a number of leaders of Arab and other countries to this proposal.
“We see the reaction of the Palestinians.
We see the reaction of a number of Arab States that stand in solidarity with the Palestinians in their rejection of this plan.
This, of course, makes you wonder about its viability.
There are a number of relevant UN Security Council resolutions.
It can be seen with the naked eye that some provisions of this plan do not quite correspond to the provisions of the Security Council resolution, "Peskov said on the Rossiya 1 channel.
Recall that in late January, US President Donald Trump unveiled the parameters of the so-called “deal of the century ”, which is designed to resolve the numerous differences between Israel and Palestine, continuing since the middle of the XX century.
According to the plan outlined by Trump, two independent states will be created - a Jewish and a Palestinian.
Jerusalem should remain the capital of Israel, but Palestine will have a capital in East Jerusalem.
In addition, the plan states that the United States and Israel are ready to recognize the Palestinian areas that are now under the control of the Palestinians, provided that they renounce terrorist acts.
In addition to this, the “deal ” provides for the preservation of Palestinian control over facilities in the ports of Haifa and Ashdod and the possibility for Palestinian refugees to choose their place of residence.
There are three options: in the future territory of Palestine, in the territories of their current residence after their integration into Israel, or in a third country.
At the same time, according to the plan, Israel gains sovereignty over large settlements in the West Bank (Judea, Samaria) and the Gaza Strip, and Hamas disarms.

It should be noted that the Palestinian Foreign Ministry said that on February 11, the leadership of the country will present its own alternative to the “deal of the century ” developed in the United States.
According to experts, the “deal of the century ” is largely aimed at solving domestic political problems in the United States and Israel.
In an interview with RT, Vladimir Bruter, an expert of the International Institute for Humanitarian and Political Studies, pointed out that the United States has demonstrated a departure from international documents.

The United States publicly declares that international documents are not a decree for them.

In turn, RUDN University professor, political scientist Yury Pochta pointed to the importance of Trump ’ s activities in the Middle East for his policy within the United States.

title: Can cause hunger: climate change affects agricultural soil
text:
Environmental news: Increased heat and constant droughts make life easier for the pathogenic fungus Pythium ultimum, which causes massive crop failures.
The aggressive fungus Pythium ultimum is transmitted through the soil and infects the seedlings of important crops such as beets and peas, as well as corn, soybeans and potatoes.
Plants develop root rot and they die.
At the same time, short-term restoration of the soil from this fungus is possible only in exceptional cases.
Biologists note that the soil has its own defense mechanisms against these fungi — for example, other pathogens that can act as protectors for plants.
In addition, there are fungi that can simply eat Pythium ultimum.
Scientists took soil samples from places with different climates - Scotland, Germany and Hungary.
Samples, including microorganisms living there, were subjected to stress in climatic chambers with high temperatures up to 40 ° C, and then infected with the aggressive fungus Pythium ultimum.
After scientists planted this soil with seeds, they were able to observe the statistics of plant death from this fungus.
It turned out that only a few plants of young peas survived.
Soils from Scotland suffered the most from heat and drought, as they had fewer microorganisms to fight Pythium ultimum.
Soil from dry Hungary proved to be more resistant to stress factors.
In addition, the scientists investigated how well different soils can recover, taking a break for several weeks after treatment with heat and drought, before infecting the soil with a harmful fungus and sowing peas.
While soil samples from Scotland showed some recovery, Hungary ’ s soil has barely recovered, despite increased resistance to pathogens.

title: Five countries demanded from Iran to return the “black boxes ” of the downed plane

title: Migrants continue to storm the British coast
text:
More than 90 migrants have been detained by UK authorities while trying to cross the English Channel, British media reported.
People in distress were picked up by the search and rescue service and taken to Dover.
Such attempts to swim across the strait on faint ships are extremely dangerous, observers say.
But illegal immigrants, who regularly take them from the French coast, argue that the danger does not stop them.
The latest incident confirms a disturbing trend, says former British Coast Guard officer Andy Roberts: “There is no navigator or helmsman on these boats.
They are simply pushed away from the shore and left to the waves.
And it often works!
In the illegal business there is a lot of money: according to my estimates, each migrant pays 3-4 thousand pounds for the crossing.
From time to time there are reports of one or two dead, but one day there will be a catastrophe. "
Residents of Dunkirk, a large port city on the banks of the English Channel, know this firsthand.
Over the past year, French coastguards have rescued 2,500 people trying to reach the British coast.
“The governments of France or the UK do not allow us to cross the border in trucks, ” one of the illegal immigrants told Euronews.
it's dangerous, but we'll keep trying! "
