title: “He 25 years could not help in Milan ”: Samara doctors for half an hour“ opened ” the eye of the Italian
text:
Milan Flavio Frigerio for 25 years saw the world around him only “half-eyes ”.
The fault was ptosis - the omission of the upper eyelid.
At the age of 10, he was injured - he fell unsuccessfully and damaged the muscle above the left eye with a shackle of glasses.
Since then, his eyelid has fallen and could no longer rise on its own.
To open the eye, until recently, a 35-year-old young man had to raise his eyebrow with all his might.
Vision problems inevitably added to difficulties in life - both in work and in communication with the opposite sex, influenced self-esteem.
Of course, Flavio tried to help Italian doctors - twice performed blepharoplasty operations, but they were not successful.
The case helped – Flavio ’ s parents left to work under a contract in Togliatti.
And when my father needed to pick up glasses, they went to the local doctor.
Evaluating the professionalism of the doctor, Flavio ’ s mother, Irina Frigerio spoke with him about the problem of her son. - He suggested - let me send you to the Yeroshevsky hospital, and in just five minutes agreed to meet with the doctor in Samara, - Irina admires. - We came for a consultation, and we were pleased - it turns out that such operations are done regularly here.
Italy is a small country, it is not easy to find a good doctor there, they lack practice for such complex operations.
Is this the case in Russia, where such operations occur all the time!
We took our chance and did not lose.
For the doctor Irina Tatarenko, such patients are really not new, and she immediately knew what to do with Flavio. - Blepharoplasty in such cases is not quite indicated.
We carried out a hanging plastic, formed a frame of allaplant threads, - says Irina Tatarenko.
In Samara, the Italian patient was accepted as a kindPhoto: Svetlana MAKOVEEVA The entire operation to rid the Italian guest of long-term ptosis took only half an hour!
Flavio recalls that when he first opened his left eye, he was overwhelmed by a wave of delight. - It was just "wow!", - he shares his impressions.
Now Flavio and his doctor are waiting for the postoperative edema to subside.
After 2-3 months, when the eye is completely in order, it will become clear whether additional resection is needed to form a cosmetic fold of the eyelid. - Usually during ptosis surgery, we immediately make a fold, but here everything was complicated by the fact that the eyelid has already been operated twice in Italy, so scars have formed.
Therefore, it is better not to hurry, resection may not be necessary, - Irina Tatarenko believes.
Flavio Frigerio for many years could not find help in Italy, and is very grateful to Russian specialistsPhoto: Svetlana MAKOVEEVA By the way, this is not the only case when foreigners periezhavut to be treated to Samara ophthalmologists.
As the head doctor of the hospital of Eroshevsky Andrey Zolotarev, recently the flow of foreigners has increased. - Basically, cataract surgery, correction of myopia with a femosecond laser, corneal transplantation, strabismus treatment, plastic surgery and glaucoma surgery are in demand, - he explained.

title: Pandora ’ s Box – Meeting with Hemingway
text:
A few days ago, Literaturnaya Gazeta turned 190 years old.
It was founded in 1830 with the participation of A.S. Pushkin, in 1929 the publication was resumed with the assistance of A.M. Gorky.
A new breath and a new meaning of "Literaturka" gave... Stalin.
It was he who suggested adding volume and frequency to the newspaper.
This historical fact was described by Konstantin Simonov, and this scene was included in my book “Stalin.
We remember together. ”
And now I would like to offer to your attention the material from the anniversary issue of the Literary Newspaper, in which interesting materials of the past years were published.
In February 1960, First Deputy Chairman of the Council of Ministers of the USSR Anastas Ivanovich Mikoyan visited the Republic of Cuba, where he arrived at the invitation of the Cuban government at the opening of the Exhibition of achievements of the Soviet Union in the field of science, technology and culture.
On his trip to Cuba, Mikoyan was accompanied by his son, journalist S. Mikoyan...
The Literary Newspaper publishes an excerpt from S. Mikoyan ’ s essays, which describes a visit by A. I. Mikoyan to the writer Ernest Hemingway, who lives twelve kilometers from Havana, in the village of San Francisco de Paula, and an excerpt from Hemingway ’ s novel “A River, in the Shadow of Trees ”.
I think it is quite characteristic how Ernest Hemingway defined the new regime in the country.
He said in Hemingway succinctly but emphatically: “This is the first honest government in the history of Cuba, the first government that sees its purpose in serving the people. ”
In front of Hemingway, several governments of Cuba changed.
“All the former rulers, ” he says,“ before they had time to come to power, began to use it for enrichment – their own and their environment – and what trifles!
Napoleon and his marshals achieved a high position by winning great battles, showing their talents and abilities.
And then some sergeant takes power, not having won any victories and not having any talents, except for the knowledge of shorthand. ”
The writer was referring to Batista, who began his career as a staff writer.
We visited Hemingway at his home in the suburbs of Havana, where he has been spending most of his time for about twenty years.
You could expect a live classic to look solemn and serious.
However, he turned out to be an extremely direct, lively and cheerful person who is somewhat ironic about being considered a great writer, and certainly does not behave as a great one.
Perhaps this is the characteristic of true greatness?
Hemingway's house stands on a hill surrounded by a small park with tall trees.
There is an announcement on the gate, which makes it clear that Hemingway rarely takes time to receive visitors.
Five or six rooms of this cozy house are full of sunlight, which freely penetrates through large windows.
In all rooms there are many different hunting trophies.
The writer ’ s wife, Mary, an elderly woman with a young character, very clearly showed how she killed a huge lion in Africa.
The skin of this lion adorns the wall of one of the rooms.
There are several paintings in the living room and dining room.
Two or three are the works of the old masters.
I especially liked two impressionist canvases depicting bullfighting – bullfighting.
A beautiful range of colors, a matador and a bull - in motion, in a desperate fight not for life, but for death.
Unfortunately, I do not remember the name of the artist whom the hostess named.
Mary Hemingway is passionate about painting and most of all in the house (except, perhaps, only the skin of a lion) is proud of his paintings. – Art gallery is the first thing I see when I come to any capital: Paris or Madrid, London or Rome.
A. I. Mikoyan could not, of course, know this, but seemed to foresee, having presented Mary Hemingway an album with reproductions of paintings of the Leningrad Hermitage.
The Hemingway spouses were very interested in other gifts, for example, the voiced model of the satellite.
Especially amused them Russian folk toy handicraft - nesting dolls - five nesting dolls of different sizes, one in the other.
We brought the writer and Russian vodka.
But we were surprised to see that among the bottles prepared for the treat there is exactly the same. – A few days ago I found out that your composer Aram Khachaturian was in Havana, and invited him to his place.
I love his music very much.
And he, like his wife Nina Makarova, I really liked it.
They had lunch with us and we had a very interesting conversation.
Hachaturian left me this bottle of vodka.
And addressing the representative of the Union of Soviet Societies of Friendship and Cultural Relations with Foreign Countries Alekseev, who caught a cold and hoarse, Hemingway said: “And you don ’ t know how to treat the throat?
I'll show you now!
Bread vodka, he almost rinsed his throat with it for a whole minute, bringing out complex roulades.
The writer showed us his workplace.
To our great surprise, we found that instead of a table, he was served by a small cupboard standing against the wall in the bedroom.
By the way, even a dozen books were scattered on the bed.
Hemingway writes standing up.
“Not to stay, ” he explained.
We climbed the tower that Mary Hemingway designed and designed as her husband ’ s workplace.
“I was thinking about getting rid of the noise I make in the house — talking, utensils, or vacuuming.
And what would you think?
He never works here.
We climb the tower only to admire the view of Havana.
You can even see the sea on that side.
Hemingway showed us his library.
The bookshelves are located in different rooms, including the famous tower.
A significant part of the books are his own works, translated into many languages and published in different countries.
To our surprise, from the Russian editions he had only the story “The Old Man and the Sea ”, sent to him from the ship“ Angara ” by the Soviet writer N.N. Mikhailov.
N.N. Mikhailov turned out to be more attentive than those of our publishing houses that have recently published Hemingway ’ s books in large editions.
For example, shortly before our departure from Moscow, a two-volume book was published, which we had the pleasure to present to the author.
And on his return to Moscow, they sent him about two dozen of his books, published in various languages of the peoples of the USSR, and even the story “The Old Man and the Sea ”, published for the blind.
A cheerful and at the same time a little shy person, Hemingway does not like official settings, ceremonies, honors, etc.
He never does anything that would prevent him from “getting up ” for work every day at 6: 00 in the morning – until 12: 00 in the morning.
Mikoyan asked Hemingway if he planned to visit the Soviet Union, where he was so popular.
The writer replied: “I am sixty years old and I cannot afford to postpone the implementation of my plans.
I am writing a new novel now.
I hope it will be no worse than Fiesta.
Until I finish it, I don't think I'll be able to interrupt.
But then I want to visit your country.
Incidentally, the writer expressed his dissatisfaction with those American journalists who reported in the press that Hemingway answered in the negative when asked if he would go to the USSR. – Of course, I could only take for a joke the question whether I would go there with President Eisenhower, and answered them accordingly with a joke, – he said.
My father introduced me to Hemingway, saying that he could explain himself to me without an interpreter.
The writer asked if I really spoke English. "A little," I replied. "Like all of us," he said at once, and it seemed to me to have been said quite seriously.
We had a conversation about the writer ’ s works, and in particular about the novel “Beyond the River, in the Shadow of the Trees ”, which has not yet been translated into Russian.
Hemingway wanted to give me this novel, the English edition of which was supposed to stand on one of the shelves, but it was not so easy to understand the bookshelves, and he promised to send the book to Moscow...
The meeting with Hemingway was very friendly and immediate, as if our acquaintance was old.
In a sunny cozy house, there was a lively conversation all the time, a cheerful laugh sounded.
Already in Moscow, a few weeks after returning from Havana, I read an article in the newspaper “Worker ”, the organ of the Communist Party of the United States,“ Hemingway and the Revolution ”, praising the writer ’ s work.
Hemingway, of course, is not a revolutionary.
But he is a great artist, a realist and at the same time a romantic.
In the ability to brilliantly combine exhilarating romance (without which there are no revolutions) with real realism (which must explain why revolutions occur), it seems that his individuality as a writer lies.
Having met him, you involuntarily discover that the literary “I ” of this modern classic fully corresponds to the appearance of Hemingway himself - a sincere, sincere, fair man with a gray beard, but with a youthful ability to get involved and enjoy life, even if life pleases very few.
He could rightly say of himself: “I am a man, and nothing human is alien to me. ”
He approaches social phenomena, perhaps, from a somewhat vague, but, I would say, impeccable position for a non-revolutionary – from the standpoint of humanism, for genuine humanism is always on the side of the revolution.
We want to put an end to all previous political leaders, to American imperialism, which is strangling us, to the tyranny of the military.
We want to start all over again and give everyone a chance in life.
We want the guajiros, that is, the peasants, to stop being slaves and the large sugar plantations to be divided among those who work for them. ”
This was not said by Fidel Castro or any other leader of the new Cuba.
These words belong to a young Cuban revolutionary from the novel To Have and Have Not, written a quarter of a century ago.
We broke up with Ernest and Mary Hemingway in the hope of meeting again, this time in Moscow.
Sergo Mikoyan, 1960, No 54

title: Iran rejects Canadian demand for $1 billion for downed plane
text:
The Canadian lawsuit against Iran for a billion dollars for the downing of a Ukrainian plane near Tehran has no grounds.
Claims for payments rejected by the Minister of foreign Affairs of Iran Mohammad Javad Zarif, reports RIA Novosti.
“Iran is taking the necessary measures on the basis of international rules, ” the foreign minister said, adding that the lawsuit has no basis.
Earlier it became known that Canadian lawyers filed a class action lawsuit against the Iranian authorities demanding to pay 1.5 billion Canadian dollars ($1.1 billion) for the death of their fellow citizens in the plane of Ukraine International Airlines, shot down in Tehran.
The name of the main plaintiff was not disclosed, as his family in Iran may be in danger of persecution by the Iranian authorities, lawyers explain.
The defendants in the case were the state of Iran, the spiritual leader of the Islamic Republic, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as well as the main commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
Minval.az

title: Abbas called the terms of negotiations with Israel
text:
Abbas called the terms of negotiations with Israel 11.02.2020, 21: 19 Mahmoud Abbas (center) Photo: Thaer Ganaim / Global Look Press This was stated by the head of Palestine at a meeting of the UN Security Council dedicated to the “deal of the century ”.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas said he was ready to stay at the UN headquarters in New York to continue negotiations with Israel.
He said this at a meeting of the UN Security Council devoted to the “deal of the century ” of the United States, reports RBC.
Earlier in his speech, he rejected the document proposed by the United States on the settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
After that, Abbas said that if the Israeli side is ready for negotiations, and the UN, the EU, the United States and Russia are ready to support them, then he can stay.
“I am talking seriously.
Right now I am ready to stay here at the UN to start negotiations, ” the Palestinian leader said.
At the end of January, US President Donald Trump proposed a plan to resolve the conflict between Israel and Palestine, which was called the “deal of the century ”.
The document provides for the creation of two states.
The capital of Israel remains Jerusalem, and the Palestinian capital is East Jerusalem.
According to the "deal of the century", the Temple Mount in Jerusalem retains the status quo, Israel extends sovereignty to the Jordan Valley, Samaria, and Judea.
Palestine is doubling its territory.
At the same time, the Palestinian radical movement Hamas should be disarmed and the Gaza Strip demilitarized.

title: “Lost the status of a mediator ”: why the Palestinian President rejected the“ deal of the century ” trump
text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas rejected the "deal of the century" proposed earlier by the United States.
Speaking at the UN Security Council, the Palestinian leader said that the implementation of this plan would lead to the establishment of an apartheid regime in the region and would deprive the Palestinians of their rights.
At the same time, Palestine does not refuse to dialogue with Israel.
Abbas appealed to Russia, the United States, the EU and the United Nations to help the warring parties find a peaceful solution to the conflict.
According to experts, the failure of the “deal of the century ”, which in recent years nurtured the Trump administration, will put an end to the mediating role of the United States in the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
President of the State of Palestine Mahmoud Abbas from the rostrum of the UN Security Council rejected the American “deal of the century ” on the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
According to the Palestinian leader, the settlement plan proposed by the United States ignores the national rights of the Palestinians and deprives them of East Jerusalem as the capital of the state.
"We do not accept this deal, which establishes an apartheid regime in Palestine, and we will oppose its implementation," Abbas said.
At the same time, the Palestinian side is committed to finding a peaceful solution to the conflict and seeks to implement UN resolutions.
“Peace remains our strategic choice, and achieving a peaceful settlement between the Palestinians and the Israelis is still possible, ” he said.
Mahmoud Abbas added that he is ready to start negotiations with Israeli representatives already in New York, at the UN headquarters.
In addition, the international community can help the parties find a compromise, the Palestinian president believes.
"An international quartet composed of Russia, the United States, the European Union and the United Nations could organize a peace conference with the participation of the Palestinians, Israel and other interested parties, which would develop a mechanism for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2334," Abbas said.
Abbas at the UN showed a map showing the history of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict Reuters © Shannon Stapleton In the future, the venue for negotiations between the leaders of Israel and Palestine may be Moscow.
This proposal was made by the Permanent Representative of Russia to the UN Vasily Nebenzia.
According to the diplomat, Russia is ready for close coordination with all parties interested in the Arab-Israeli settlement to help find a “compromise solution ”.
"We do not remove from the agenda the proposals to provide a Moscow platform for direct negotiations without preconditions between the leadership of Israel and Palestine," Nebenzia said.
The Permanent Representative of Israel to the UN Danny Dannon commented on the position of the Palestinian side.
The diplomat criticized Abbas ’ s approach, saying that the latter had rejected the deal even before he had read its terms.
However, the Israeli side is ready for direct negotiations with Palestine, the Israeli permanent representative said.
Also on the topic Friend ’ s help: what is behind Trump ’ s proposal for a military alliance with Israel US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke in favor of signing a treaty on mutual military assistance...
Earlier it became known that the Palestinian leadership refused the idea to submit a draft resolution condemning the “deal of the century ” to the UN Security Council on February 11, in connection with additional negotiations on the content of the document.
This was reported yesterday with reference to its sources in the UN Security Council, the Russian Agency TASS.
From the very beginning, Ramallah had no hope that the document would be adopted by the UN Security Council.
As the Permanent Representative of Palestine, Riyad Mansour, explained earlier, the Palestinian side understands that the draft resolution will be blocked.
Experts agreed with these assessments.
As Sergei Bespalov, a leading researcher at the RANEPA Institute of Social Sciences, noted in an interview with RT, the document would be rejected with almost one hundred percent probability, although the fact of its introduction would still be a demonstration of Palestinian disagreement with the US “peace plan ”.
“It would be a political gesture, not designed for a concrete result.
In the UN Security Council, this resolution would not have been adopted, even if it had won a majority of votes.
The United States would simply use the right of veto, ” the expert explained.
The Palestinian leadership has previously criticized the peace plan proposed by Washington.
“I want to say to Trump and Netanyahu: Jerusalem is not for sale.
All our rights are not for sale and are not subject to bargaining.
Your deal is a conspiracy, and it will not work, ” Abbas told a news conference in Ramallah after the publication of the American action plan for Palestine and Israel.
The American initiative caused a sharp negative reaction among the leadership of the Palestinian Hamas movement operating in the Gaza Strip.
“Trump ’ s statement on Jerusalem is nonsense.
Jerusalem will always be a Palestinian land.
The Palestinians will oppose this deal and Jerusalem will remain Palestinian territory, "Hamas spokesman Abu Zuhri said.
Al-Aqsa Mosque in East Jerusalem Reuters © Ammar Awad Washington ’ s initiative has met with condemnation in the international arena.
The League of Arab States (LAS) criticized the plan of the American side, supporting the position of the Palestinians.
“The Arab League has decided: to reject the Israeli-American ‘ deal of the century ’, as it does not satisfy the minimum rights and ambitions of the Palestinians and violates … international law and UN resolutions; to emphasize the refusal to cooperate with this unjust deal and all possible cooperation with the American administration in its implementation, ” the organization said in a statement.
Also on the topic “Playing into the hands of radicals ”: what can lead to the growth of tension on the border of Israel and the Gaza Strip Israeli tanks fired at Hamas positions in the Gaza Strip in response to missile launches towards the Jewish state.
All of March, Israel...
The head of EU diplomacy Josep Borrell in his statement noted that the US initiative on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement does not correspond to the parameters agreed by the international community.
“The establishment of a just and lasting peace requires the resolution of final status issues through direct negotiations with the participation of both sides, ” Borrell said, noting that the issues of the border of the Palestinian state and the final status of Jerusalem remain unresolved.
Moscow also did not support Washington ’ s initiative.
As the press Secretary of the Russian President Dmitry Peskov, commenting on the plan of the agreement, the reaction of the Palestinians and a number of Arab states makes you think about its viability.
Sergei Bespalov believes that such a reaction of the world community was predictable.
“The peace initiative of the US president will not be supported by the Palestinians, nor by the majority of Arab countries, nor by other countries of the world.
This was initially clear to everyone, including the American administration and Trump himself, ” the expert believes.
The Palestinian-Israeli conflict began with the appearance of the state of Israel on the map of the Middle East in the middle of the twentieth century.
According to the UN resolution, two independent countries were to be established on the territory of the former mandated territory of Great Britain, but due to the Arab-Israeli war that began soon, an Arab state was not created.
The confrontation between the Palestinian Arabs and the authorities has not faded in recent decades, periodically turning into a stage of aggravation.
Thus, another outbreak of violence provoked in the spring of 2018 the decision of Donald Trump to move the American Embassy to Jerusalem.
Dozens of Palestinians were killed in clashes with Israeli forces in the Gaza Strip.
Protest against the transfer of the American Embassy to Jerusalem, May 2018 Reuters © Ibraheem Abu Mustafa Acting in a destabilizing role for the region, Donald Trump nevertheless claims to be a peacemaker.
Work on a plan for a peaceful settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict was entrusted to the son-in-law of the American President Jared Kushner.
In the summer of 2019, the White House unveiled the first part of the so-called deal of the century, dealing with economic aspects.
In addition to moving the embassy to Jerusalem, U.S. authorities have declared Jewish settlements in the West Bank “legal. ”
As stated in November 2019, US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, the US leadership does not believe that the construction of settlements by the Israelis in the area is contrary to international law.
In January 2020, Donald Trump finally unveiled the widely announced “deal of the century ” plan.
The deal announced by Trump provides for the creation of two states - Arab and Jewish, but does not take into account the point of view of the Palestinian side.
According to the plan, Jerusalem will have the status of the “indivisible capital ” of Israel.
On the territory of Jerusalem, it is planned to place the Palestinian capital, it is proposed to take it to the area separated by a wall of urban development.
Donald Trump Reuters © Leah Millis At the same time, Palestine will continue to manage facilities in the ports of Haifa and Ashdod.
Transport links will be established in Palestine and the West Bank.
In addition, according to Trump ’ s idea, Palestinian refugees will be able to choose their place of residence: in the territory of future Palestine, in the territories of current residence that will be integrated into Israel, or in a third country.
However, the “deal of the century ” involves the recognition of Israel ’ s sovereignty over Jewish settlements in the West Bank, the disarmament of Hamas and the demilitarization of the Gaza Strip.
Trump posted on his Twitter page a map showing the supposed borders of the two states.
It shows that the United States and Israel are ready to recognize Palestinian sovereignty over territories it already controls, as well as add two large areas along the Egyptian border that Trump said would double Palestinian territory.
“I will always stand on the side of the State of Israel and the Jewish people.
I strongly support his right to protection and security, as well as his right to live in his historic homeland.
It is time for peace! ” added the American leader.
If the “deal of the century ” is implemented, the Arab state will also receive $50 billion in aid from the United States.
The Palestinian side is demanding a solution to the conflict within the framework of the creation of a viable Arab state, whose borders will run along the lines that existed before the 1967 Six-Day War, when Israeli troops occupied East Jerusalem and occupied the West Bank of the Jordan River.
This will create a viable State in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
However, Israel refuses to return to the 1967 borders, and Jerusalem considers the “indivisible ” capital of the Jewish state.
Yuri Zinin, a senior researcher at MGIMO, notes that the Palestinians will not accept such a peace plan, which will not comply with previously adopted UN resolutions.
From the point of view of the UN, the borders established by Israel after the Six-Day War are illegitimate.
"Palestine insists on preserving the borders that existed before the Six-Day War.
An independent Palestinian state is what Palestine needs.
The country must have a border and a capital, and the problem of refugees must be solved, ” the expert said in an interview with RT.
Experts from the very beginning doubted the viability of Trump ’ s peace plan, noting that it simply cannot be implemented in its current form.
"In its current form, the US initiative can lead to nothing but an aggravation of the situation in the Middle East, a new intifada — an uprising by the Palestinians — is not excluded," Bespalov said.
A similar point of view is shared by Yuri Zinin.
According to the expert, the reaction of the Palestinians to the US proposal is quite natural, since the deal plan does not imply the creation of a viable state of Palestine.
Palestinians rally against the American peace plan, February 2020 Reuters © Mohammed Salem “The deal of the century ” says formally that there should be two sovereign states.
But how can Palestine be independent if it has no direct access to the outside world?
If inside the state will be controlled by someone else ’ s armed security forces? ” the expert stressed.
According to Yuri Zinin, now the United States has lost the status of a mediator between the parties to the conflict, taking the side of Israel.
On September 13, 1993, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin signed the Declaration of Principles on Interim Peace and Security.
“If Washington really wanted to end the conflict, it was necessary to act as a mediator, and not to defend only Israeli interests.
Of course, now, after the refusal of Palestine to participate in the “deal ”, all the calculations of the United States have collapsed.
This plan simply has no prospects, ” the expert is sure.
At the same time, this does not mean that Palestine and Israel have lost the chance to come to a peaceful resolution of the conflict, experts believe.
As noted in an interview with RT, an expert on the Middle East, Professor of Moscow State University Alexander Vavilov, Ramallah and Tel Aviv can resolve their conflict if they themselves sit at the negotiating table.
Moreover, the theoretical basis for such agreements has been worked out by world politics and diplomacy for decades.
In addition, now Palestine is represented by rather moderate political forces, ” the expert said.
Abbas's proposal to create an international format for finding a peaceful solution is also quite realistic, since it relies on existing international practice, Vavilov believes.

title: Trump ’ s “Deal of the Century ” Discussed at UN Security Council Meeting
text:
The UN Security Council on Tuesday vigorously discussed the so-called “deal of the century ” of Donald trump on the settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
The speech of the leader of the Palestinian Authority, as one would expect, was emotional.
He angrily rejected the US plan, saying it violated international law.
Mahmoud Abbas compared the map of Palestine to Swiss cheese.
"This plan will not bring peace and stability to the region.
We will not accept this plan and will oppose its implementation.
It ’ s not Swiss cheese, it ’ s Swiss cheese.
Who among you will accept such a state and such conditions? ” shouted the leader of Palestine.
Abbas declared his readiness to negotiate with Israel, but under the auspices of an international quartet - that is, with the participation of Russia, the United States, the European Union and the UN.
Russia ’ s Permanent Representative to the United Nations also spoke about the need for joint action by the international community.
Vasily Nebenzia confirmed that Moscow is still ready to provide a platform for negotiations on the Palestinian-Israeli issue.

title: Jerusalem Post – “This is occupation and confiscation ” – Abbas refused the“ deal of the century ”
text:
12.02.2020, 11: 31, News of the day President of the State of Palestine Mahmoud Abbas unconditionally rejected the peace plan proposed by Israel and the United States, writes The Jerusalem Post.
In his view, the proposed solutions were contrary to international law and violated the rights of Palestinians to self-determination and the independence of their State.
On Tuesday, at a meeting of the UN Security Council, the head of Palestine, Mahmoud Abbas, unconditionally rejected the peace plan of the Trump administration, writes The Jerusalem Post.
“This plan, or any part of the plan, should not be seen as an international reference to negotiations, ” the president said, adding,“ This is an Israeli-American pre-emptive plan to put an end to the Palestinian issue. ”
Abbas said the proposed solution “violates international legitimacy ” and“ overrides the legitimacy of Palestinian rights, our right to self-determination, the freedom and independence of our own state. ”
The Palestinian leader called Israel ’ s planned annexation of 30% of the West Bank in his speech “legitimizing what is illegal. ”
According to him, Trump ’ s initiative is “entrenching the occupation and confiscation ” of Palestinian lands, which strengthens the apartheid regime.
Mahmoud Abbas compared the attached map to Swiss cheese, implying Israeli enclaves within the State of Palestine and vice versa.
In addition, the President of the State of Palestine expressed regret that according to the plan “Jerusalem is no longer under the sovereignty of the State of Palestine ”, although, as the newspaper emphasizes, such a state never existed.
Who gave you the right to give it as a gift to one state or another?
We came before you, ” Abbas said.
He provided a number of maps that are widely used by anti-Israel groups as evidence that Israel has appropriated territory.
They also falsely demonstrate that the Ottoman Empire and British Post-Mandate Palestine were a Palestinian state, and that Israel was built on land that belonged to a never-existing state.
The Israeli newspaper notes that the West Bank and Jerusalem were swept by a wave of protests against Israelis.
Abbas expressed his gratitude to those “thousands and hundreds of thousands ” who took to the streets despite the frost.
Finally, the Palestinian president expressed the view that the problem was not Trump, but the “terrible advice ” he received from his son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
Abbas criticized Kushner ’ s statement that the Palestinians missed one after another opportunity to achieve peace.
The leader of the unrecognized state called for the Palestinians and Israelis not to impose the peace plan from outside, but to achieve it themselves.
He recalled that in this way the two countries had already come to an agreement in Oslo and wanted to adhere to it before they found a common solution.
“However, they killed [former Prime Minister Yitzhak] Rabin, ” Abbas said, implying that the assassination did not restore peace.
Meanwhile, The Jerusalem Post adds, after the signing of the treaty and before Rabin ’ s death, Palestinian terrorists blew up 10 Israeli buses, killing 38 people.
In turn, Israel ’ s permanent representative to the UN, Dani Danon, also called for direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations, accusing Abbas of hypocrisy: “If Abbas really wanted peace, he would not be here, but in Jerusalem. ”
In his opinion, the head of Palestine should “use this opportunity to start direct negotiations ”, move to action instead of complaints.
“Abbas says he wants sovereignty for the people of Palestine, but he did everything to avoid it, ” said Danon, who called sovereignty a symbol of struggle rather than a goal.
He accused the international community of encouraging such policies because of certain voting patterns at the UN and calls for negotiations to be based on pre-1967 principles that run counter to previous bilateral agreements.
The newspaper notes that the Israeli envoy praised Trump ’ s “smart approach ” in an attempt to achieve peace in a different way and not“ accept outdated concepts. ”
[and] a formula that failed more than 70 years ago. ”
According to Danon, the leader of Palestine refuses to negotiate and to consider the problem from a practical point of view.
“Only when he retires will Israel and Palestine be able to move forward, ” he told The Jerusalem Post.

title: Iran rejects claims to pay $1.1 billion in compensation for Canadians killed in UIA plane
text:
12.02.2020, 16: 42, News of the day Iran does not intend to pay to representatives of Canada $1.1 billion in compensation for those killed in the plane of Ukraine International Airlines.
Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif told reporters on February 11, ISNA reports.
According to the diplomat, there are “no grounds ” for such a demand.
Zarif claims that the Iranian authorities acted in accordance with international law.
On February 7, it became known that a Canadian lawyer filed a lawsuit against the Iranian authorities in the High Court of Ontario in Toronto on behalf of his client John Doe.
Behind this name is a relative of one of the dead passengers.
The statement of claim says that the crash of the UIA plane was a “deliberate terrorist act. ”
A passenger plane Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines, following flight PS752 Tehran – Kiev, crashed on January 8 near the capital of Iran.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
No one survived.
Among the dead were 57 Canadians.
Initially, the Iranian authorities insisted on a technical malfunction or accident as the main reason for the crash, but on January 11, the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces admitted that the UIA plane was shot down by the Iranian military.
The ministry claimed that the disaster occurred shortly after Iran shelled US military bases in Iraq.
The aircraft, as stated in the message, approached one of the important objects of the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and “the shape and height of the flight resembled an enemy object. ”
On January 20, in an official report, Iran admitted that two Tor-M1 surface-to-air missiles were fired at the aircraft three minutes after its departure from Imam Khomeini airport.

title: Palestine does not understand Trump: why the “deal of the century ” failed
text:
US President Donald Trump ’ s plan to resolve the decades-old Israeli-Palestinian conflict seems to have no chance of realising it.
The “deal of the century ”, as the head of the White House calls it, caused an extremely negative reaction from Palestine, not only from the leadership of the country, but also from its citizens.
In the Palestinian territories, rallies are held against the Trump plan, the authorities are breaking relations with the United States and Israel, and the Israeli army meanwhile reports the launch of a missile on the territory of the country.
If the head of the White House counted on historical triumph, international recognition and gratitude from the conflicting parties, he was undoubtedly mistaken.
The territorial conflict between the two countries has been going on since 1967.
International mediators have repeatedly tried to resolve the confrontation, but this has not led to any result.
Donald Trump, however, believed he could find a solution.
The development of the “deal of the century ” by the US presidential administration lasted almost three years.
Its main architect is Jared Kushner, the adviser and son-in-law of the head of the White House.
On January 28, the American leader presented his plan.
He proposed to recognize Jerusalem as the inseparable capital of Israel, but to allow Palestine to build its capital in the eastern part of the city.
At the same time, the Arab state and the entire world community should recognize Israel ’ s sovereignty over the West Bank of the Jordan River, follows from the deal.
Palestine, according to Trump, will double its territory if it agrees to the US plan.
So, as compensation for the loss of territory in the West Bank, the head of the White House proposed to allocate to the Arab state two zones in the Negev desert south of Gaza.
In addition, the President of the United States considers it expedient to establish Palestinian control over the Gaza Strip.
Through Israel, according to Trump, it would be possible to conduct a tunnel or overpass.
This will give the Arab country access to the sea, but it will be possible to build a port there only five years after the conclusion of the agreement and, importantly, only with the permission of Israel.
Under the proposed plan, Washington is ready to allocate $50 billion.
Palestine must be demilitarized and Hamas completely disarmed.
In exchange, Israel must agree to freeze new Jewish settlement activity for a period of four years.
That is how much time is devoted to the negotiation process on the formation of Palestinian statehood.
Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas almost immediately after Trump presented his deal in the presence of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, called the plan a “slap in the face. ”
On February 2, Palestine broke off relations with both the United States and Israel.
On February 11, the UN Security Council held an open meeting to discuss the US proposal, during which Abbas announced his readiness for dialogue with Israel and the need to convene an international conference on a peaceful settlement in the Middle East with the participation of both sides of the conflict and the Middle East Quartet, which includes Russia, the US, the EU and the UN.
“This plan or any part of the plan should not be regarded as an international reference to negotiations.
This is an Israeli-American preemptive plan to put an end to the question of Palestine.
The proposal was rejected by us because it suggests that East Jerusalem is no longer under the sovereignty of Palestine, and therefore we cannot accept this plan.
We will oppose its use "on the ground".
Expectations from Abbas ’ s speech were much higher among the world public.
Palestine announced a resolution condemning Trump ’ s plan, with the country ’ s permanent representative to the UN, Riyad Mansour, promising that the resolution would be tough.
However, the document has not been submitted, work on it still seems to be underway.
And on the eve of Abbas ’ s speech in the UN Security Council in Palestine, rallies were held against the US plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
Protests took place in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with tens of thousands of people participating, according to local media reports.
“Today we are united, all factions of the PLO and the Islamic factions of Palestine have united around the position of President Mahmoud Abbas, ” Prime Minister Mohammad Shtaye said during his speech at the rally, noting that the palestinians will be able to“ stop the deal. ”
The next day, the Israeli army announced the launch of a rocket from Gaza into Israel.
Palestine continues to express its outrage at Donald Trump ’ s plan.
As expected, the initiative of the head of the White House has launched a new round of international discussion on this issue, and Palestine, at least in words, is ready for dialogue.
However, there is little hope that the US proposal will be implemented.
As Meir Kraus, a researcher at the Shalom Hartman Institute and Valdai Club expert, notes in a conversation with Gazeta.Ru, the start of negotiations between Israel and Palestine is the best of all the circumstances that a deal can lead to.
If we consider all the proposals that have been put forward over the past 53 years to resolve this conflict, it is easy to understand that the “deal of the century ” is the most pro-Israel and one-sided plan for a peaceful settlement.
This explains why Israel supports it, ” the expert explains.
By the way, Israel itself, as if not noticing the reaction of the opponent, began to implement the “deal of the century ”.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on February 8 that the Israeli-American committee had already begun to draw up a new map of Israel with the territories to be ceded to Palestine, according to the US president ’ s plan.
“We are in the process of mapping the territory that will belong to Israel under the Trump plan, ” he said.
We ’ ve been waiting since 1967, don ’ t worry about waiting for a few more weeks. ”
The expert points out that if the Palestinians went to the proposed deal, the country would become geographically fragmented.
Under Trump ’ s plan, Israel could extend its sovereignty to any Jewish settlement.
“If we look at the map, it becomes clear that in this case, most parts of the future Palestinian state will not be connected to each other.
They will be scattered.
The Palestinians agree to exchange their territories with Israel in a 1: 1 ratio so that the total area of their state remains unchanged.
According to the plan, 30% of their territories should go to Israel, and in the dry residue they will receive only 70% of the territory.
In addition, all Palestinian territories will be surrounded by Israel.
This means that in order to move outside of Palestine, they will have to cross the Israeli border in any case.
This is unlikely to suit the Palestinians, ” said Meir Kraus.
In addition, the White House proposal to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel also does not seem to be an acceptable step for Palestine.
The permission to build its capital in the eastern part of the city, behind the wall of Jerusalem, means nothing to the Arab state.
This territory is not of great importance to the Palestinians.
“I don ’ t think this plan will work in its current form.
But I think that there will be political changes in Israel and, perhaps, after the elections (early parliamentary elections will be held in Israel in the spring), we will witness peace talks between Israel and Palestine, ” the expert believes.
By the way, it is not only Netanyahu who is preparing for the elections.
In November, the United States will elect a president.
For Trump and Netanyahu, the successful implementation of a plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict would be a significant bonus in their election races.
The prime minister would emerge from the standoff with Palestine as the obvious winner, and the head of the White House would secure a weighty diplomatic victory.
However, in this direction, it seems, politicians will have to stop at what has been achieved.

title: To the British shores - by boat
text:
More and more migrants are risking their lives trying to cross the English Channel and get from France to the UK in small boats.
Our correspondent spoke with people who are waiting for their time in the area of ​ ​ the French city of Calais.
Their goal is to get to the UK, but for this it is necessary to cross the English Channel.
Until now, refugees have stormed trucks going to the UK, hid in trucks at the entrance to the tunnel under the English Channel, or hoped to travel on ferries plying between the two shores.
“When the French or British authorities do not allow us to move by truck, we have to take boats, ” admits a refugee in Calais who dreams of getting to Albion.
The French police, for their part, are doing everything possible to ensure that migrants on this side of the strait are not detained.
Every day, their natural settlements are cleaned up.
People are used to: immigrants from Iraq, Iran, Afghanistan, Syria and Africa at the time of inspection go to the city, taking their property.
Clara Wyn represents the local human rights movement.
She says: “The police carry out such operations here every day.
They're asking people to move their tents a couple of meters.
If it turns out that there is no one in the tent, they dismantle it, seize things, phones, papers.
This strategy is designed to prevent the expansion of informal settlements into giant camps, such as the "Jungle" camp, which existed in Calais a few years ago. "
Against the background of tighter police control and Brexit, migrants are in a hurry, increasingly agreeing to a new service from smugglers - to sail to the UK on a boat.
This type of transport is becoming more and more popular: it is cheaper, refugees say, and with it there is a greater chance of success.
However, the risks are huge: in February alone, British rescuers assisted 200 refugees in 48 hours, among them children.
Last year, the French authorities tried to intervene in relation to almost 3 thousand people crossing the English Channel, which is 17 times more than in 2016 (almost 2 thousand refugees reached the British coast, 125 were expelled from the country, the rest settled, at least temporarily).
“Intervening, ” experts explain, means offering to evacuate people from the boats.
Andy Roberts, former head of the British coast guard, says: "They say migrants refuse the help of the French border guards, and they have no right to insist - the use of force in the water can turn into tragedy, people resist.
So they swim to the British waters and there fall under the jurisdiction of the British authorities, who coordinate the rescue of those in trouble.
They're being taken to the British coast. "
On the French side, Raymond Randou, a local resident, says that, according to his data, the boats are brought in trucks from England: “Most guys come from England with boats, they take them in trucks.
I think they are already pumping boats in here in France.
Otherwise they would have been noticed. ”
"These boats go without a navigator, without a rudder and wind.
They are pushed away from the shore - and that's all, - explains Andy Roberts. - So far we have recorded 2-3 deaths, but one day there will be a real large-scale disaster! "
In 2016, the French authorities razed the infamous spontaneous refugee camp in Calais, nicknamed the “Jungle ”.
People were resettled, but many remained on the coast.
In the city of Dunkirk, for example, hundreds of migrants settled in an old warehouse complex.
Volunteer Colin Slotala shows, "This part of the warehouse is for families, this part is for single men.
It's very dangerous here...
There are about 800 people here.
I come here almost every day...
I don ’ t know how this can happen in France. ”
There is a fire right on the ground floor, a family with children is warming up near it.
As it turns out, they are from Iraq.
The fact that our correspondent is British causes them delight: "And we are going to you," they report.
People say they're waiting for a seat in the boat.
For the right to try your luck will have to pay from 2 to 3 thousand pounds per person.
The refugees explain: the main thing is to get to the British territorial waters.
The task is not easy, given the fact that the authorities are improving tracking systems, strengthening the patrol.
According to London, the majority of migrants trying to cross from France, nothing works.
Those who were able to survive the journey and bypass the patrol in the UK fall into special centers.
They are accepted by volunteers: in the program - language courses, assistance in solving domestic and legal issues.
“If I stayed at home, I would not be alive, ” says a young Afghan. – I do not regret anything, I live well in the UK, I am happy. ”
Refugees are arriving in the UK at a time when anti-migrant sentiment is growing.
The slogan “We have lost control of our borders ” has become one of the main reasons for the mobilization of supporters of“ Brexit ”.
The authorities are required to expel illegal refugees from the country.
Brigitte Chapman, who represents the migrant support organisation, said: “I think people with good reasons for asylum should be able to apply on the French side of the strait.
They will be registered, and they will be able to come to us in a safe, legal way.
I'm not talking about letting everyone in indiscriminately, but this measure will stop smugglers.
People entitled to asylum should not risk their lives on boats on the busiest shipping line in the world. "

title: Upward trend in Bayer shares
text:
On February 27, the German chemical and pharmaceutical company Bayer AG will publish the results for the fourth quarter of 2019.
Given recent events, in particular, lawsuits in the US in the Monsanto glyphosate herbicide case and the loss in the first US lawsuit to a Missouri farmer who accused the herbicide of destroying his peach gardens, the situation is not so good at first sight.
Last week, a federal court in Cape Girardeau ordered $265 million in the first of more than 140 lawsuits over allegations that dicamba had damaged the entire Midwest.
Farmers in these regions have found that the herbicide easily spreads to neighboring fields and gardens, thereby causing irreparable harm.
Bayer, in turn, said that when using the herbicide, manufacturers do not follow the instructions on the dicamba label.
Of course, this news will not affect the results of the fourth quarter, but it can provoke an increase in the number of lawsuits against the company, thereby negatively affecting future forecasts for profit and revenue.
Last year, a court in the United States already found the German pharmaceutical company responsible for the fact that the herbicide produced by the recently acquired company Monsanto caused cancer in the married couple.
As a result, Bayer was ordered to pay compensation in the amount of $2 billion.
The story does not end there, nor does the number of lawsuits: many expect Bayer to be able to close 75,000 claims as part of a pre-trial settlement.
On the other hand, the company still has a lawsuit in the case of the Essure contraceptive implant.
Most likely, and in this case, the company will be able to reach an agreement, besides, the market has long discounted this news.
Against this background, Bayer ’ s shares continue to grow, even despite a $250 million fine.
It is likely that investors hope that the company will be able to protest this decision or even prove its innocence.
At the moment, the stock price is in the $82 – $70 channel, and the Ichimoku indicator, also known as the Ichimoku Cloud, hints at an upward trend.
It is not excluded that interest in Bayer shares grew due to a good dividend yield (about 4.0%).

title: The Gretinist Myth of the Climate Crisis
text:
One of the most inhumane totalitarian ideologies in the history of mankind and one of the most popular aggressive sects of the present time is the myth of the climate crisis.
The mouthpieces of aggressive gretinism regularly declare about the alleged climate crisis affecting the planet: I ask the media to treat the crisis as a crisis...
We are facing an existential threat, and there is no longer time to continue on this path of madness...... as one can expect countries like India, Colombia or Nigeria to care about the climate crisis...
… I am told that I must learn to become a climatologist so that I can “solve the climate crisis ”.
The climate crisis has already been resolved.
On Monday, Greta Thunberg and 15 other children filed a complaint with the United Nations alleging that the world ’ s five largest economies violated human rights by failing to take adequate measures to stop the unfolding climate crisis.
Thunberg and 15 other children accuse countries of “inadequate ” national commitments to curb the climate crisis, as their actions will not stop the global temperature rise below 2 ° C, as agreed in the Paris climate agreement.
Without these vital actions, they argue that the climate crisis will put their livelihoods at risk – from more dangerous storms, food crises, rising sea levels and more.
The lawsuit accuses Germany, France, Brazil, Argentina and Turkey of failing to comply with their obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
These countries differ in that they are the world ’ s five largest emitters of greenhouse gases, which are the direct cause of the climate crisis.
What is a climate crisis?
Is it happening now?
Does humanity need to do something about it?
And if you do, what?
A short article will not replace large-scale and detailed studies of specialists in a number of scientific disciplines - climatology, paleoclimatology, physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, geology, astronomy, biology, medicine, economics.
It formulates only a few basic theses on the main trends in the evolution of the global climate, forecasts of climatic changes, their consequences for humans.
First of all, those interested in the topic should not mix the problems of ecology (air pollution, water, soil in places of human life and work) and climate issues (the temperature of the planet's air, its humidity, the frequency and intensity of certain natural phenomena).
Environmental problems (primarily the production and disposal of garbage, emissions of hazardous substances, industrial and energy waste, emissions of gasoline engines, etc.) caused by human activities threaten the health and lives of millions of people, deserve the most serious attention and solutions.
Citizens who advocate for the solution of environmental problems are highly respected and deserve every support.
Climate change is largely caused not by human activities, but by natural factors, their impact on the health and lives of millions of people is minimal, and in recent decades, mostly positive; in addition, the degree of their impact on human life is constantly declining.
The struggle against climate change is as expedient as the struggle to change the motion of the planets or the intensity of the radiance of the sun, and persons depicting such a struggle join the ranks of the aggressive sects of climate alarmists and gretinists.
The topic of interest should also not be confused with climate and weather.
Climate is a long-term (according to the existing agreement between climatologists - at least three decades) weather regime.
Therefore, if you hear (read) statements about the need to combat climate change because, for example, there was no snow this year, or the last two summers were especially hot, or as a result of last year ’ s fires burned so many hectares of forest, then this is a clear confirmation that the person making such statements is either incompetent in climate and climate change issues, or deliberately misleading the public.
Area of fires in Australia (ha), 1920-2020 3.
Since a crisis in the most general sense is a radical change in the state of a phenomenon, a climate crisis can be called such a significant climate change, which would have the following characteristics: - it would be large-scale (for example, there was a significant increase in air temperature, radically different in its magnitude from traditional climate changes); - it would be very rapid (for example, the increase in air temperature occurred much faster than ever before); - it would have especially severe consequences for humans (for example, long - term increases in air temperature have led to increased mortality).
If none of these signs of a climate crisis is observed, then there is therefore no climate crisis itself, and the usual climate changes are taking place instead of the crisis.
The climate of planet Earth is constantly changing.
It has changed in the past, it has changed in the present, it will change in the future – as long as our planet exists.
Constant change is an inherent feature of the global climate.
There is no fundamental disagreement about the fact of climate change among scientists.
There is indeed a scientific consensus, but only on this issue: Earth ’ s climate change is and is happening all the time.
Attempts by climate alarmists and gretinists to spread the myth that their opponents deny the very fact of climate change are unscrupulous propaganda.
Differences between experts exist not on the fact of climate change, but on other issues.
In particular, there are disagreements about: — the ratio of current and historically observed levels of global temperature, — the direction of climate change, — the magnitude (scale) of climate change, — the speed of climate change, — the causes of climate change, — the predictions of climate change, — the effects of climate change on humans, — the optimal strategy for mankind ’ s response to climate change.
The correct answers to many of these questions depend crucially on the time horizon chosen — 40, 80, 1,000, 10,000, hundreds of thousands, or millions of years.
Depending on the time horizon, the answers to these questions are different, including the exact opposite.
The global climate is one of the most complex natural systems.
The laws of climate change are currently completely unknown to mankind.
Historically, climate change has seen both long - term, relatively stable trends and cycles of varying durations and frequencies, as well as abrupt, crisis phenomena that radically changed the climate in a short time.
Over the past fifty million years, the global climate of the Earth has generally tended to cool down.
Over shorter periods of time (for example, in the last 800,000 years), climate change has been largely cyclical.
The time horizons of different climatic cycles are different - from the well-known annual cycle (winter - spring - summer - autumn) to cycles lasting 70-80 years, 1300 years, about 100 thousand years (Milankovitch cycles).
Reconstruction of temperature, CO2 concentration, dust according to the ice cores of Vostok 11 station.
In the history of global climate, there have been both climate crises and climate catastrophes (as, for example, during the late Dryas (about 12,000 years ago, when temperatures fell by about 10 ° C for a hundred years and perhaps even faster).
The current level of global temperature is not unique in historical perspective.
The average annual temperature of planet Earth is currently estimated at about 14.5 degrees Celsius.
In the history of the planet there were periods when the air temperature was lower than the current – in the early Permian period, in the Oligocene, during the periodic glaciations of the Pleistocene.
For most of the last half billion years, the air temperature on the surface of the Earth has been markedly higher than today, and for about half of this period it was about 10-15 ° C higher than today (that is, in the range of 25-30 ° C).
Global temperature over the past 60 million years 13.
During the regular glaciations of the Pleistocene, cold periods lasted about 90 thousand years and had peak temperatures about 10 ° C below the current one.
Long glaciations were replaced by short (4-6 thousand years) warm interglacial periods with temperatures 1-3 ° C higher than the current one.
About 10 thousand years ago, another sharp increase in temperature (about 10 ° C) began, thanks to which the colossal glaciers that occupied a significant part of the territory of Eurasia and North America melted.
This period, in which we were lucky to live, was called the climatic optimum of the Holocene.
Global warming of the climate has played a key role in mastering the secrets of agriculture and the transition of mankind to the civilizational stage of its development.
Over the past 10 thousand years, there have been at least 5 warm periods - the so-called "climatic optimum", during each of which for 150-300 years the temperature on the planet was 1-3 ° C higher than the current one.
The direction of climatic changes during the period of instrumental temperature measurements depends on the choice of time horizon.
For 17 years (1998-2014), the global temperature had no clear trend (there was no increase or decrease).
Global temperature according to satellite measurements, 1981-2019 In the previous 20 years (1978-1998), it increased by about 0.4 ° C.
During the previous 30 years (1945-1976) the temperature decreased by about 0.2 ° C.
Then the world media wrote about the main threat to humanity – global cooling.
During the preceding decades (1910-1946) the temperature rose by about 0.5 ° C.
During the previous 30 years (1880-1911) the temperature decreased by 0.3 ° C.
In the preceding century and a half (1740s – 1880s), the global temperature trend was generally neutral, with periodic warming followed by cooling, and subsequent warming.
Over the past three centuries (beginning at the turn of the 17th and 18th centuries), the temperature in the northern hemisphere has increased by about 1.3 ° C, and the so-called Little Ice Age (MLP), which occurred in 1400-1800, was replaced by the modern climatic optimum (SKO), which began in the late 1970s.
During the three centuries preceding MLP, temperatures in the northern hemisphere dropped from levels reached during the Medieval Climate Optimum (MCC) in the 8th – 13th centuries.
P. Bruegel the Elder.
The census in Bethlehem, 1566.
Depending on the selected time periods, the long-term temperature trend receives a different angle of inclination.
For the last 2 thousand years, the last 4 thousand years, the last 8 thousand years, the trend is negative.
For the last 1,300 years, the last 5,000 years, the last 9,000 years, it turns out to be positive.
The magnitude of modern climate change is much more modest than the scale of climate change observed earlier in the history of the planet.
The change in temperature in Central Greenland (the results are obtained by studying oxygen isotopes in ice cores) shows that over the past 50 thousand years, at least a dozen periods during which the regional temperature has increased by 10-13 ° C.
If we take into account the currently observed correlation between temperature changes at high latitudes and temperature changes across the planet, the conservative estimate of global temperature rise turns out to be 4-6 ° C during each of these periods, which is 5-7 times more than the actual increase in global temperature over the last century (0.9 ° C).
Unique in duration, a number of instrumental data are available for temperature in Central England (since 1659).
His data show that the exit from the Little Ice Age began in the late 17th and early 18th centuries.
Abraham Hondius.
The frozen Thames in 1677.
Thomas Wyke.
Winter Fair on the Thames, 1683-1684
The increase in temperature in this region in 1701-1739 was 0.98 ° C.
It turned out to be more significant than in the same region almost three centuries later, in 1987-2019 (an increase of 0.78 ° C).
At the same time, at the beginning of the 18th century, a little more than 600 million people lived on the planet, which is 13 times less people than today, and there was no economy in the modern sense of the word, massively burning hydrocarbons and emitting carbon dioxide on the planet at that time.
The rate of current climate change (the rate of current global warming) is not unique by historical standards.
According to the IPCC, the rate of temperature rise over the past fifty years has been around 0.09 ° C per decade.
According to the data obtained with the help of instrumental measurements, a higher rate of temperature rise per decade for half a century was observed at least three times: in the early 18th century, in the second half of the 18th century, in the late 19th century and early 20th century.
The current rate of warming is inferior to both the rate of warming recorded in the 18th century using instrumental measurements, and the rate of warming in at least 13 cases over the past 50,000 years, determined using paleoclimatology methods.
In the period from 1987 to 2019, the temperature in Central England grew at a rate of 5.97 ° C per century, and in 1701-1739 it was a third higher and amounted to 8.15 ° C per century.
Once again, it should be noted that the rapid increase in temperature in the 18th century took place against the background of low and stable levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, that is, solely due to natural factors.
Among the causes of significant, rapid, radical climatic changes in the pre-industrial era, there were no anthropogenic factors – due to the modest size of both the total number of people and the scale of their economic activity.
At the same time, the range of climatic fluctuations, their speed, as well as peaks in the pre - industrial era, exceeded the parameters of climate change recorded in the industrial era.
In the industrial era, the onset of which is traditionally attributed to the beginning of the 19th century, climatic changes are influenced by both natural and anthropogenic factors.
The strength (weakness) of the impact on climate from anthropogenic factors can be judged, in particular, by the parameters of climate changes in recent years in comparison with their values in previous periods.
Since the values of these parameters in the industrial era are noticeably more modest than in the pre-industrial era, there is no basis for asserting that anthropogenic factors in their strength are already equal to natural factors, especially exceeded them, and even more so allegedly caused a climate crisis. 19.
Factors of climatic changes of anthropogenic origin are very diverse and are not reduced only to carbon dioxide.
Humanity has an impact on the local, regional and global climate through the construction of buildings and structures, heating of housing, heating of industrial and public premises, deforestation and planting of forests, drainage and watering of land, plowing arable land, agriculture, industrial activities and transport, construction of dams, leveling and asphalting of territory, emission of aerosols, etc. 20.
As for the role of anthropogenic carbon dioxide in climate change, there is no consensus in the scientific community on this issue.
Some scientists believe that the role of CO2 is very large, others - that its role in comparison with other factors is marginal.
There are scientists who argue that carbon dioxide does not have a noticeable effect on the climate.
There is also serious disagreement about the direction of a possible causal relationship between carbon dioxide concentration and temperature: some researchers believe that changes in carbon dioxide concentration are the cause of temperature increases, others believe the opposite - that it is temperature fluctuations that cause long-term changes in carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere.
Unlike carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO2) is harmless to humans.
Unlike aerosols, harmful and dangerous substances, carbon dioxide does not pollute the environment.
Carbon dioxide has no color, taste, smell.
Therefore, the widely distributed propaganda materials, photos and videos presenting fuming factory pipes and car exhausts as alleged illustrations of the so-called “appearance ” of carbon dioxide are either monstrous incompetence or outright fraud.
It should also be borne in mind that the increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the air has a positive effect on increasing the productivity of plants, including many crops.
The increase in the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere in recent decades has contributed to an increase in the productivity of the plant world, led to the phenomenon of global greening.
The productivity of the global biosphere has increased by more than 6% over the past three decades.
The boundary between savannah and desert in the Sahel had moved several hundred kilometers to the north, and droughts had become more rare and less severe, saving millions of people from starvation.
The relationship between the dynamics of carbon dioxide concentrations and climate change remains a subject of vigorous discussion.
An indisputable fact is the increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere over the past two centuries from 280 parts per million air particles at the beginning of the 19th century to 415 parts in 2020.
This increase in concentration over time coincided with an increase in global air temperature of about 1.0 ° C.
However, the dynamics of CO2 concentration did not always correlate with the expected temperature changes.
Significant and rapid increases in global temperature during the interglacial periods of the Pleistocene epoch, during the climatic optimums of the last millennia, as well as in the 18th century were not preceded by periods of increasing carbon dioxide concentrations.
In the industrial era, the increase in carbon dioxide concentration was not always accompanied by an increase in global temperature.
In 1945-1976, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere increased by 24 units - from 308 to 332 parts, but the global temperature during this time fell by 0.1 ° C.
In 1998-2014, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere increased by 32 units - from 367 to 399 parts, but the global temperature remained unchanged during the same time.
In 1939-45, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere decreased by 3 units (as a result of the massive destruction of economic potential caused by the Second World War).
This did not prevent global temperatures from rising by 0.1 ° C. 23.
Global climate models, so much appreciated in the IPCC, demonstrate very limited suitability so far.
The complex nature of the climate system has prompted the creation of complex models of the global climate, trying to take into account the impact of a large number of different factors.
According to the forecasts developed on the basis of these models and included in the IPCC report of 2003, global temperature by the end of the 21st century should increase by 2.0-5.8 ° C, including during the first two decades of this century it was expected to increase by 0.7-1.7 ° C.
In fact, the global temperature rose by less than 0.2 ° C. IPCC forecast, 2003.
Comparison of IPCC forecast and actual temperature change (J. Christie, 2016).
The poor quality of the models used was demonstrated by the comparison of predicted and actual climatic changes (graph by J. Christie).
The consequences of climate change for humans vary significantly depending on their focus, scale, and speed.
An increase in temperature leads to the establishment of a warmer, milder and wetter climate, and its decrease leads to a colder, harsher and drier climate.
Human living and economic conditions in warmer and wetter climates are more favourable than in colder and drier climates, which are also facilitated by reduced heating and heating costs, less food needed to maintain energy and heat, an increase in the growing season of plants, higher crop yields, longer navigation times, etc. 25.
The increase in global air temperature has reduced the frequency of extreme natural events (droughts, floods, hurricanes), their intensity and the damage they cause to human beings.
The climate dividend for humanity as a result of global warming has been very significant.
Particularly significant effect of temperature increase was manifested in countries and territories in high latitudes.
According to the Institute for Economic Analysis, the higher average annual temperature in Russia in 1992-2005 compared with the period 1970-80 provided Russian economic entities with a total cost saving of about 1% of GDP per year.
The climate changes that have taken place in recent times are neither too large nor particularly rapid, nor do they increase the damage to humanity.
In real life, there is no sign of a climate crisis.
All current climatic changes occur within the usual, traditional limits, they do not go beyond the changes repeatedly repeated on the planet, both observed in historical times and became known in the course of paleoclimatic studies.
The methods of “combating global warming ” proposed by climate alarmists by reducing (and by gretinists by stopping) the use of hydrocarbons are not only scientifically unfounded – due to the lack of extraordinary characteristics of modern climate change, not only prohibitively expensive in economic terms, but also directed against human civilization itself.
Such measures could be particularly dangerous if applied in middle - and low - income countries, which would be condemned to guaranteed poverty, hunger and underdevelopment.
The impact of anthropogenic factors on climate change is negligible compared to the impact of all natural factors and, above all, the variability of solar activity.
The most effective strategy for human response to different types of climate change is adaptation (adaptation) of man to changing external conditions.
This is how people reacted to much larger climatic changes in previous epochs (the melting of the Eurasian glacier, the Roman and medieval climatic optimums, the small ice age of the 17th century), being less prepared than modern man.
Modern civilization has incomparably greater resources than before for its adaptation to climate fluctuations, it is better prepared for such changes scientifically, technically, psychologically.
The costs of adaptation to climate change for humanity are incomparably less than in the implementation of the totalitarian ideology imposed on it and the aggressive policy of climate alarmism and gretinism.
Echo of Moscow

title: The assembly of an important element of the international thermonuclear reactor ITER began in Russia
text:
MOSCOW, 20 feb — PRIME.
Sredne-Nevsky Shipyard (SNSZ, St. Petersburg, part of the United Shipbuilding Corporation) began assembling the coil of the poloidal field PF1 — an important element of the international experimental fusion reactor ITER under construction in France, the press service of the Russian design center ITER reported.
The ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) reactor is being built near the Cadarache Research Center in southern France jointly by the European Union, Russia, China, India, Japan, South Korea and the United States.
This will be the first large-scale attempt to demonstrate the feasibility of using a fusion reaction to generate energy on an industrial scale.
If the ITER project is successful, humanity will be able to count on the possession of an almost inexhaustible source of energy.
The PF1 coil is one of six poloidal field coils in the magnetic system that serves to hold the plasma in the ITER reactor.
"The coil is a complex product, the basis of which are eight superconducting two-layer double-start gallets.
The peculiarity of the manufacture of these biscuits was that the winding of each of them was carried out simultaneously from two cables.
For each of the 16 cables of the PF1 coil, a niobium-titanium superconductor made earlier in Russia in cooperation with Europe was used, which has superconducting properties at ultra-low temperatures, "the report said.
The completion of the production of the PF1 coil and its dispatch to the site of the ITER installation is scheduled for 2021.
