title: Agriculture in Belarus needs to adapt to climate change
text:
February 26, Minsk / Ekaterina Markovich - BELTA /.
Agriculture in Belarus needs to adapt to climate change.
This opinion was expressed by Svetlana Kuzmich, deputy head of the Republican Center for Hydrometeorology, Radioactive Pollution Control and Environmental Monitoring, BelTA has learned.
"This winter for the first time in our observations was so warm, for the first time the average seasonal temperature in winter in Belarus is plus, we have never had such a thing, - said the expert. - Our winter crops wintered satisfactorily, but climate changes are felt in agriculture.
It requires adaptation.
For example, it is recommended to preserve peatlands, swamps, forests, meadows, you can return to waterlogging, revive agriculture mixed with forest plantations.
Of course, we need to review the crops, the timing of planting and harvesting. ”
Deputy Director of the Institute of Soil Science and Agrochemistry of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus for scientific work, Doctor of Agricultural Sciences Nikolai Tsybulko also believes that it is necessary to make adjustments to the main elements of the farming system in the country.
In particular, in his opinion, it is necessary to change the structure of sown areas, increase the sowing of winter crops, increase the sowing of intermediate crops, cultivate heat-loving crops.
Speaking about the impact of climate change on the forestry of Belarus, Deputy Head of the Forestry Department of the Ministry of Forestry Viktor Zvertovsky noted that over the past 25 years it is insignificant, mainly these changes affected coniferous plantations.
However, the department has developed a number of documents that provide for measures to adapt the country's forestry to global climate change.

title: Vilfand advised the Russians to forget the word “virgin ”
text:
The development of new land for agriculture will not allow global warming.
This view was expressed during the presentation of the report "Global Climate and Soil Cover of Russia" at the Soil Institute.
Dokuchaeva RAS was expressed by the scientific director of the Hydrometeorological Center of Russia Roman Vilfand.
According to him, due to climate change, there is no possibility of expanding the range of land that is suitable for agriculture.
“The word ‘ virgin ’, which is familiar to most of those sitting here from their youth and professional activities, should be forgotten, ” RIA Novosti quoted the climatologist as saying.
But at the same time, said Vilfand, there is an opportunity to improve the yield of existing agricultural lands.
Today they occupy 22% of the territory of Russia.
In countries with comparable climatic conditions, agriculture is conducted on 13-15% of the territory.
Earlier, Roman Vilfand explained to Rossiyskaya Gazeta that each next five years will be warmer than the previous one.
And every decade will be warmer than the past.
This is all a consequence of climate warming, notes the forecaster.
He adds that the justifiability of climate forecasts (for several years ahead) is higher than for a year or six months.

title: Iranian film - in the program of the Berlinale
text:

Natasha ” by Russian director Ilya Khrzhanovsky: the prize was given to the cameraman Jürgen Jürges.

Germano played in the film “I wanted to hide ”, which tells about the Italian artist Antonio Ligabue, while Ber starred in“ Undine ”, rethinking the legend of the eponymous mythological creature film about a girl who works as a museum guide in Berlin.

title: Berlinale winner Rasuloff ordered to go to prison in Iran
text:
The Iranian authorities sent the laureate of the Berlin Film Festival, director Mohammad Rasulof, a notice of the need to serve a prison sentence.
This was announced by the lawyer of the Director Nasser Zarafshan in an interview with the Agency AP on Thursday, March 5.
In July 2019, Rasulof was sentenced in Iran to one year in prison.
He was found guilty of spreading propaganda against Iran ’ s state system through his films.
The Iranian authorities were dissatisfied with the paintings “Farewell ”,“ Manuscripts do not burn ” and “Incorruptible ”.
The director wanted to appeal the verdict, but the complaint was not accepted.
According to the lawyer, Rasulof intends to make a new attempt to appeal the verdict.
On February 29, 2020, Mohammad Rasuloff was awarded the main prize of the Berlin Film Festival "Berlinale" for the film "Evil does not exist" about the death penalty.
Since the director is forbidden to travel outside Iran, he could not get the Golden Bear in person.
This is not the first time Rasulof has been prosecuted.
In 2011, he was sentenced to six years in prison on charges of conspiring against national security and spreading propaganda against the state.
He was later reduced to one year, but never called to prison.
In 2017, Rasulof won at the Cannes Festival in the program "Un Certain Regard" with the film "Incorruptible".
After returning to his homeland, the Iranian authorities took his passport from the director and banned him from making films.
The picture “Evil does not exist ” Rasulof he shot secretly.

They replaced the long-time director Dieter Kosslick and first of all “moved ” the Berlinale away from the American Sundance Festival and the Oscars.
The new tandem at the head of the oldest festival in Germany was not limited to the postponement of its dates.

But Sally Potter, a director from the UK, in her film "The Roads Not Taken" (photo) starred such celebrities as Javier Bardem and El Fanning, as well as Salma Hayek and Laura Linney.

Natasha "and the documentary" Dow.
Degeneration ", which will be presented in the framework of special screenings.

Berlinale 2020: In a new format, the relaxed opening of the Berlinale starts this time with a film that does not participate in the competition and does not claim the Golden Bear.
The film "My Year of Salinger" is based on the book of the same name by journalist and writer Joanna Rakoff, who worked in a literary agency that represented the author of the famous novel "Over the Catcher in the Rye".

Berlinale 2020: In the new format of the Ambition Competition, the new leaders of the Berlinale have prepared another major competition for their debut.

Among the 15 competitive films of this year is the debut directorial work of Katharina Vasconcelos from Portugal "A metamorfose dos pássaros" (photo).

Berlinale 2020: in a new format "Panorama" looks at the world In the program "Panorama", too, there are always many world premieres.

title: The granddaughter of a billionaire dreamed of increasing breasts and died on the table at the surgeon
text:
A Chinese woman, the granddaughter of a famous billionaire, went from Hong Kong to Seoul to make a gift for her 35th birthday.
A woman has long dreamed of increasing her breasts and went to one of the best clinics in the world, which is famous for ideal results in the beauty industry.
Bonnie Evita Lowe wanted not only to enlarge the breasts, but also to do liposuction, as well as other cosmetic procedures, reports Life.
The dream of a perfect appearance turned into a tragedy for her.
It all began with the fact that the operation was not anesthesiologist – the drugs were administered using a special device under the supervision of a nurse and another doctor.
When Bonnie underwent breast augmentation surgery, she felt severe pain and jerked.
After that, the heiress of the billionaire began to convulse, and she twitched several more times under the scalpel.
However, the doctor only asked for an additional dose of anesthesia and did not stop the operation.
The patient ’ s blood oxygen levels soon dropped.
Her skin became pale, her lips turned blue, and her mouth and nose bled.
And then the Chinese woman fell into a coma.
The girl was urgently moved to another hospital, but the doctors did not save her, and the patient died.
Bonnie ’ s family was shocked by the news.
The girl has a small son.
And the husband of Danny Chi, with whom the girl lived for 10 years, sued the clinic, accusing two doctors and a nurse of manslaughter and falsification of documents.
According to the man, Bonnie's signature on the risk sheet was forged after her death.
In addition, the husband of the deceased requires compensation for the damage, since now he and his son have lost the right to part of the inheritance that was to go to the girl, as well as the annual allowance.
Law enforcers began an investigation, but the surgeon who carried out the operation continues to work.

Since 2016 — CEO of Syngenta. — Tell us the details of the transactions. — Nidera is a company that deals with corn and soybean seeds, one of the largest players of this level in Brazil and Argentina.
And, of course, integration with the Syngenta business turns the now merged company Syngenta-Nidera into one of the leading market makers in the markets of these countries.
With the acquisition of Nidera, we also gained access to advanced technologies in the field of sunflower and, by the way, these technologies will soon be available in Russia.
The second two important acquisitions are the digital platforms Cropio and Strider.
Digital platforms help to keep a record of the use of all those crop protection products and fertilizers used by the agricultural producer, and give him certain advice.
In this way, they help us to improve our customer service.
Among our deals are two more seed companies in the vegetable segment: Abbott & Cobb and Floranova.
These companies are mainly represented in the markets of the United States and the United Kingdom, but their hermoplasm is used far beyond these countries. – Name, if possible, the amount of each of the transactions. – This I can not do.
I will only say that all five acquisitions cost the company and its shareholders $2 billion. — Can an M & A deal similar to one of these five be concluded in Russia? — I will say at once that Chinese investors fully support our course to increase investment in Russian business.
But here we have a few other plans.
When I talk about Russia, I mean, first of all, not M & A, but the construction of a plant for the production of plant protection products near Lipetsk and the creation of the Institute for Seed Protection in the Voronezh region, which will support our business in this segment.
We also intend to significantly increase the number of full-time employees in Russia. - And how much does Russia occupy in your sales? - 4%, but at the same time we maintain a constant increase in sales here.
Of course, its pace is not as fast as in China, but our starting positions in the two countries are different. – Another question about the new digital assets of Syngenta.
The Cropio platform is relatively known in Russia, and almost nothing is known about Strider.
What is this platform where it works, what is its uniqueness for the company and synergy for the general business contour of Syngenta? - In the US market, we have historically had a fairly strong presence in the digital technology segment.
There we have a platform called AgriEdge.
And, of course, we would like to have the same strong presence in Brazil as in the United States.
Accordingly, Strider is a Brazilian company, a digital platform with an already very strong presence there.
Just like Cropio we bought to strengthen its position in Russia and, in general, in Eastern Europe. - But Cropio in Russia is almost not represented.
I think there is a small office, and that ’ s it. – Yes, maybe it is, but the platform has a huge potential and scope for scaling.
It is very important to keep in mind that Cropio has a professional team, and when integrating their platform and their team with our growth opportunities opens up very large ones.
And another strong point of Cropio is that the application in the form in which it is already available can be widely used in Russia.
You were right to say that Cropio has a limited team here.
So if you combine the Cropio software with the large team of sales managers that are in the Russian Syngenta, if you even slightly modify the platform, then there will be very great opportunities. - Are there any calculated figures on the timing, volume of space that you plan to take Cropio services in Russia? - Of course.
At the time of purchase of the service in 2019, Cropio ’ s coverage in Russia was already about 2 million hectares.
In the near future, our goal is to increase this figure to 5 million hectares.
Cropio is a tool that creates additional value for agricultural producers, and it will successfully integrate with the model of creating demand that Syngenta has in Russia.
These are people, a lot of people who will be able to use Cropio and continue to distribute this system. – I understand correctly that your future plant of the SZR near Lipetsk is a tolling model, and there will be no full-fledged localization? – We use the tolling scheme for a very long time, and we will continue to use it in the same place as now – at the Kirovo-Chepetsk Chemical Plant.
But at the same time in Lipetsk we will have our own form, our own packaging of products.
That is, there will be the same process as in Kirovo-Chepetsk.
- Then what is the fundamental difference between what is and what will be? - We see a great prospect of market growth in Russia, we see the opportunity to produce products closer to the client in the Central Black Earth region.
Therefore, we have a lot of flexibility in responding to customer requests.
At the same time, we see great opportunities for exporting our products from this new plant to the EurAsEC countries.
Syngenta.
The producer of seeds and agrochemicals was founded in 2000 on the basis of the agricultural divisions of Novartis and AstraZeneca.
In 2016, it was 100% acquired by the Chinese chemical state corporation ChemChina.
Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.
It has offices in 90 + countries of the world.
The staff is 28,000 people.
Revenue in 2019 is $13.6 billion (unchanged from 2018), EBITDA is $2.9 billion ($2.7 billion in 2018), net income is $1.45 billion against $1.44 billion a year earlier.
Two-thirds of the company's sales in monetary terms (more than $10 billion) accounted for agrochemicals, a third ($3 billion with a little) - for seeds.
Data on Russia is not disclosed.
Based on Eric Firvald ’ s estimate of Syngenta ’ s 3% share of Russian sales made in this interview, in terms of money they could be at $520 million per year.
Question to you as CEO of the company.
How can you articulate the essence of the new strategy of the company in Russia, which was publicly announced in 2019? - Our strategy in Russia is to be the leader in the segment of crop protection, strengthen our leadership position in sunflower seeds and reach the first place in sales of corn seeds and vegetable crops.
And we want to achieve this by bringing the best world technologies to the Russian market, having high-quality production of the best quality and at the same time providing comprehensive agronomic support with the help of our sales managers and our distribution partners, with the help of digital tools that we now have at our disposal.
This is Cropio.
And because we are a global company, we always think about exports.
Therefore, part of our strategy in Russia is to help your country increase its export potential in those markets where the opportunity opens, including in China.
Last June, the country ’ s ambassador to Switzerland, where Syngenta is headquartered, surprised everyone with a public statement that the takeover of ChemChina for as much as $43 billion was a mistake by the Chinese company.
We know that Chinese officials are extremely cautious in their statements, and do not say anything for nothing.
It is obvious that this was a personal opinion, not an official position of the Chinese government.
The ambassador who made the statement has never met with representatives of Syngenta, and I can assume that he has no idea what we are doing, does not know the Chinese agricultural market.
He is not at all involved in this subject.
Actually, this statement was made during an interview on Chinese investments in Switzerland, this question angered him very much and, probably, to get rid of it, he gave such an answer.
It was an emotional reaction to a question he did not expect and did not want.
Before taking up his post in Switzerland, he served in very small countries like the Maldives.
But interestingly, the next day ChemChina Chairman Frank Ning made a statement for the official Chinese newspaper.
He said that Syngenta is a great company, a company that has the full support of the Chinese leadership, that it has brilliant prospects in the Chinese market.
After that, I went to China with the President of Switzerland, we met with the top 3 leaders of the country.
And they talked again in my presence, and they made it official, that Syngenta is very important to China.
They said they were very pleased with the acquisition, as well as the fact that Syngenta maintains its headquarters in Switzerland, in Europe, and continues to use the same operating model that it had. – Eric, thanks for the comprehensive answer, but, nevertheless, this question is not the first time.
ChemChina paid for the company really big money, above the multipliers.
You know, and you told me last time, that the margin of production of seeds and agrochemicals is getting lower.
And that global deals like yours, like Bayer-Monsanto, Dow-DuPont, are primarily about cutting costs, pooling sales, and building a more efficient product portfolio.
And in this context, one hears that almost three years have passed and ChemChina is less and less likely to recoup the money, even despite the cost cuts you ’ ve made.
They also say that one of the key reasons for this situation is a very important EU market for you, that is, bans on active substances and the financial losses of the company associated with them.
How can you comment on this? - At the end of 2019, Syngenta exceeded its sales plan for the second year in a row - seeds and crop protection.
Worldwide, they reached $13.6 billion, which is 4% more than in 2018 when calculated at a constant exchange rate.
Sales of plant protection products in absolute dollar terms increased by 1%.
We were able to increase the market share in the segments of crop protection and seeds in a number of countries: India, Brazil, Argentina, Thailand.
And this is despite the weather cataclysms we faced last year.
In 2020, I expect that the same unpleasant weather phenomenon will not happen, and our sales and profits will continue to grow.
That is, for the third consecutive year, we will grow.
I also confirm the plans to bring the company to the SPO, announced at the end of the transaction with ChemChina.
We intend to do so within two years.
And we will conduct this SPO based on the Syngenta business valuation at the level of the $43 billion that China paid for the company.
Or even more, but in no case less. — And the money from SPO will go to the development of the company or in some shares — to the company and as a cash-in shareholder?
And what package will be put on the stock exchange? - Exactly I will not tell you the package, it is still being discussed, but it will be significant.
Shareholders will receive money, some of which will go to pay Syngenta ’ s debts.
As a result, we will get the owners of ChemChina, plus many others who will buy shares.
We will be listed again, on the stock exchange, we will be a public company again. – For what year is the deal scheduled? – For 2022, depending on the market situation. – At the beginning of last year, President Vladimir Putin ordered to introduce anti-dumping duties on herbicides from the European Union.
Syngenta has concluded an agreement with the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC), but still – do you see any impact of this decision and the anti-dumping investigation that preceded it on the company ’ s business, on the market atmosphere as a whole? – First of all, I want to note that we were absolutely open during the investigation, provided all the necessary information, and immediately said: we are the most expensive company on the Russian market, because we provide the latest original products. High added value.
And we were very pleased with this decision, the fact that we were actually removed from anti-dumping duties.
We have concluded this agreement, which stipulates an increase in the level of our localization in Russia.
We probably do not expect any noticeable impact of the new duties on the company ’ s business. – Now new technologies, including genome editing technologies, are playing an increasingly important role.
The most famous example of such technology is CRISPR / CAS, developed by the University of California.
- Yes, there is a separate direction of development, which is associated with genomic editing.
I would like to start with how this technology works, what is the difference between GMOs and genome editing.
In GMOs, you take a gene from a bacterium and put that gene in a plant.
And then in this plant, in which you put a foreign gene, there are changes that are very important, you need.
It becomes, for example, resistant to certain insects or, conversely, becomes immune to some disease, to some herbicides.
And when we put a herbicide on a plant, we don ’ t kill the plant itself, but only the weeds around.
The plant itself becomes resistant to this herbicide.
This is what GMO technologies are aimed at. - That is, they are aimed, so to speak, at solving one problem. - Yes.
99% of all GMO developments are aimed at solving one of the problems: resistance to pests, insects or resistance to herbicides, in order to kill only weeds with these herbicides.
Now let ’ s move on to genome editing technology.
Genome editing is the precise and specific modification of genetic sequences.
Genome editing can be compared to the “Find and Replace ” function for a genetic instruction manual.
Genome editing techniques have been around for several years, but in 2013 they were quickly overshadowed by the more efficient and accurate CRISPR / Cas9 system.
CRISPR is a natural system that bacteria use to protect against viruses.
It is an adaptive immune system of bacteria, based on genetics and capable of “learning ”.
The scientists concluded that this bacterial protection system could be easily adapted for genome editing.
CRISPR / Cas9 can allow breeders to turn genes on or off by editing certain parts of the plant ’ s DNA.
Gene editing can accelerate the domestication of plants, tame wild grapes, shrubs and herbs, and turn them into new crops.
We are now in the advanced stage of developing such a technology to protect tomatoes.
We increase the resistance of tomatoes to the effects of various kinds of viruses so that they are not treated with plant protection products.
By changing the genome, breeding new hybrids of tomatoes, we can already not process them SPR - they will protect themselves with the help of an altered genome. - That is, such vegetables do not need processing at all? - We can not say so, but we will significantly reduce the amount of SPR to protect these tomatoes.
Already because they will be resistant to a certain, very common virus, to a disease that often attacks tomatoes. – And do I understand correctly that it will be possible to process such an agricultural crop only with your herbicide? – I would not put the question this way.
It should be understood that we at Syngenta are committed to reducing the amount of plant protection products used.
Over the past 50 years, their use, if you count in the active substance, has decreased by 95% due to scientific developments, including our company.
We intend to continue research and development in order to further reduce the use of chemical POPs in the next 10-20 years.
We will develop new chemistry, use biological products that are complementary to chemical ones, apply precision farming methods, and use new hybrids.
Hybrids that are resistant to certain diseases, and therefore do not require treatment with plant protection products from them. - Under the influence of what strategic trends, in your opinion, will the world seed market and crop protection develop in the next 10-15 years? - The main global factor determining the development of agricultural production will be climate change.
That is, we will feel very sharp weather fluctuations, very unforeseen weather phenomena - floods, droughts, rising air temperatures.
I was once in the Netherlands, and they told me that now they have viruses and insects that they had not seen before, because they did not survive the winter.
Now the winters are warmer - once, and, secondly, these insects and viruses enter the country from warmer, tropical countries, and the Dutch do not yet know what to do with them.
And I am sure that the determining factor in the development of the agricultural industry in the next 10-15 years will be the creation of new technologies for agricultural producers (both in the crop and in seeds) that will help different crops cope with such climate changes as rising temperatures, floods, and drought.
The Netherlands is an agriculturally strong country, and it is very interested that these new gene-editing technologies that we talked about will eventually be allowed.
In this sense, we are concerned that the European Union has embarked on the path of banning a number of active substances.
And under it get very good, modern, promising substances.
So I think it ’ s unlikely that the EU would allow genome-editing technology — at least not now.
I think they will buy and grow more organic products.
And in this regard, I predict a certain decline in agricultural production in Europe in the coming years.
Thus, the Europeans banned insecticides based on neonicotinoids.
They were used to protect, for example, rapeseed.
As a result, rapeseed producers in the EU have greatly reduced yields, as they have been forced to use more organophosphoric, an older generation of pesticides for processing.
As a result, say, the Russian manufacturer significantly increases the area of ​ ​ rapeseed. — But after all, what you say about the EU, is prohibited in Russia? — No — say, neonicotinoids are allowed in Russia.
You, in the USA, China, Argentina, Canada, have very strong regulatory systems for the PPP industry.
They are also scientifically justified.
And if Russia maintains this scientific approach to regulating the PPP market, it will open up great opportunities.

title: Basta Tsydenov: “In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy ”
text:
Many viewers who watched the play “The Old Man and the Sea ” in the Buryat Drama Theater perceive the Cuban old man Santiago and the artist Bastu Tsydenov as one.
The actor is so harmonious in this role.
From the play of a large form “The Old Man and the Sea ” in 2015 turned into a mono-parable.
There is one actor on the stage who, with the help of symbolic objects and sounds of morin-huura, talks about the fact that “a person cannot be defeated ”.
I lacked freedom.
It is important for me to be free in my role.
When the theater critic Anna Stepanova looked, she said: “Maybe you can do a mono? ”
I told Oleg (director Oleg Yumov – approx. ed.), they did it with him, and really...
I got my freedom.
I have been playing for two or three years.
So much is opened with every show.
In this, probably, the buzz of creativity, - shares his thoughts Basta Tsydenov.
The artist admits that "The Old Man and the Sea" is one of his favorite performances, and Ernest Hemingway is one of his favorite authors: - A high word, a deep word, a deep thought, a deep pain, a deep meaningfulness of this life, tragedy, joy of man.
This, on the one hand, is a very simple pain of a simple man, a simple fisherman: just live, survive, not starve to death, remember the good, remember the love, forgive.
These are the simplest, human feelings of thought, emotions.
That's why I like Hemingway.
He is a very simple writer himself.
He has a very simple syllable.
He writes very simply, harshly, does not feel sorry for himself or for us.
He goes deep, deep.
He is a man who has lived a lot, acted a lot in his life.
He went to the hottest spots, fought, went to love, to women.
He did not do a little, so he writes also. - Can you say that you are? - I am far from that.
I have a lot of egoism, I am a person who is fond of theater.
Theatre is a broad concept...
These are literature, life, art, images, artists in a broad sense, struggles, defeats, women.
For any artist, women mean a lot.
High poetry of love - What role do women play in your life?
Have you loved? - Many times got carried away, many times fell in love, but, looking back...
These were defeats and discoveries, you will know not only women, you will know yourself, your background, your kind, tender, subtle feelings.
It's developing.
Love is always creativity.
The deeper you go into love, the more tragedy, the more pain.
It is high poetry, high art, high drama, it is always beauty and tragedy.
When it comes separately, it ’ s very boring.
She is so beautiful, that ’ s all.
Or very primitive pain.
Basta Tsydenov, a favorite of women, has loved himself more than once.
Officially, he was married three times, he has three children and one granddaughter.
However, the main love of his life is the theater. - My sacrifice for the sake of art is family.
First of all, I put on the theater, my work.
And family is always in the second, in the third plan.
There is always pity, regret.
I could have saved my family, tried, but I couldn't.
Then it seemed that something was more important.
That for me, for my work, for my art, a woman must sacrifice her personal ambition.
But I did not meet such a woman.
On the contrary, I feel sorry for them.
Although, I don't know, maybe it's a good thing we met.
That we have children in common.
I love them, I help them as much as I can.
Communicating.
The kids are nice to me, great relationships.
In the creative baggage of Basta Tsydenov more than 80 roles.
In each he never ceases to know himself, shares the actor.
His first major role was at 25.
He played the groom in the play "Wedding" in the Buryat Drama Theater.
In the difficult 90 ’ s for the whole country, Basta Guruevich admits that he was experiencing a personal crisis.
He decided to leave the storm.
- I felt devastated, I didn't know what to do, I was sad, I was sad, I was bored.
It's about me, not the theater.
Personal life kubarem.
One day I just decided to leave.
I haven't been to the theater in 12 years.
Wandering around Moscow, in Europe, he says.
Basta Tsydenov participated in the project “White Deer ” by the German director Betin Voevoda, in the seminars of the great Japanese experimental director Tadashi Suzuki.
With special warmth, Basta Guruevich recalls common projects with the students of Anatoly Vasiliev - Klim (Vladimir Klimenko, theater director, playwright, screenwriter - approx. ed.) and Boris Yukhananov (artistic director of the Stanislavsky Electrotheatre - approx. ed.): - Boris invited me to play the role of a shaman in Faust.
There was a performance for 8 hours, I went out 15-16 times, I did rituals.
He gave me total freedom.
I was thinking about the rituals I remember from the storm.
He made up whole dialogues for me.
I was with Faust, I argued with him, supported him sometimes.
We performed at the RAMT (Russian Academic Youth Theater - approx. ed.) twice, at the Stanislavsky Theater 3-4 times.
He lied to everyone there that I was a real shaman from Buryatia.
Everyone looked at me with caution.
I didn't know he was out there, lying.
In "Hamlet" he played, there were two more projects according to his script.
In the capital of Russia, the actor found, as they say, his director.
It was in the Moscow period of the artist ’ s life that he met Oleg Yumov, who studied at GITIS.
Later, returning to Buryatia, Basta Tsydenov will play the main roles in almost all Buryat performances of Yumov.
Their creative tandem is based on friendship, says the artist: - To have your own director or a person who is close in spirit, blood, interesting - this is a very great success for the actor.
I'm an actor.
I tried, I staged Duck Hunt, Moscow critics and speakers at the Vampilov Festival noted.
But I prefer to play.
For the performance of the main role in the play “Maxar.
Steppe in Blood "Basta Guruevich was nominated for the" Golden Mask "for the" Best male role ", was awarded the diploma of the festival" Siberian transit "in Barnaul in the nomination" Best male role ".
And the old man Santiago brought the artist a "Mongolian Oscar" - a victory in the festival "Gagan Muse" in Ulaanbaatar.
Today, Basta Tsydenov works as an artist in the Buryat Drama Theater, and also opened his school of oratorical skills, where he teaches children, as he says, to be free.
Although the question of whether he himself is free, he answers: - I have been striving for this all my life.
I can ’ t say I ’ m a free person, but I think there ’ s freedom.
I do what I want... what I feel, I do it.
In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy.
In a good way.
Destroy stereotypes.
Some framework, foundations, to destroy what was once done well.
A new feel.
Press service of the theater

title: Iran agreed to transfer to Ukraine the “black boxes ” of the downed Boeing – the Ambassador
text:
As a result of the plane crash near Tehran in January, 176 passengers were killed.
The Iranian side agreed to hand over the "black boxes" from the downed International Airlines plane near Tehran.
About it on Twitter wrote the Ambassador of Ukraine in Canada Andriy Shevchenko.
Read alsoCrash of MH17: Prystaiko said that not all prosecutors will be dismissed “An important result on # PS752.
Iran ’ s representative Farhad Parvares at the Council session in Montreal: Iran agrees to send “black boxes ” to Ukraine with the subsequent transfer to France in case additional expertise is needed, ” the statement said.
Reference UNIAN.
In Iran, on January 8, the plane of Ukraine International Airlines, carrying out flight PS752 on the route Tehran - Kiev, crashed.
176 people were killed.
On board the Boeing 737 were 11 citizens of Ukraine, including 9 crew members, as well as citizens of Iran, Canada, Sweden, Afghanistan, Germany and the United Kingdom.
Three days later, the Iranian president officially admitted that the Ukrainian airliner was shot down “as a result of an unintentional human error ” and promised to bring those responsible to justice.
On February 3, Director of Accident Investigation at the Iranian Civil Aviation Organization Hassan Rezaifar said that Iran will no longer share with Ukraine the evidence in the case of the downing of the UIA aircraft due to the fact that these investigations were “leaked ” to the Ukrainian media.
On February 4, the countries participating in the International Group for Coordination of Assistance to Victims of the UIA Plane Crash said that they demanded that Iran immediately hand over the “black boxes ” from the downed liner to the group.
On February 14, the Iranian Foreign Minister said that Iran does not intend to give back the “black boxes ” from the downed UIA aircraft, but also not to decrypt their data without the participation of interested parties.
On March 4, then Foreign Minister Vadim Prystaiko said that the Foreign Ministry and the National Security and Defense Council are actively working to ensure that Ukraine took the flight recorders, the so-called “black boxes ” from the UIA aircraft shot down in Iran.

title: The first manned flight of Crew Dragon to the ISS is scheduled for May. It will be the first American mission since the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.
text:
Click here to share content on Facebook.
(Opens in new window) We have previously heard from unofficial sources that NASA and SpaceX are planning the first operational Crew Dragon flight with a crew as part of the Demo-2 mission on May 7; there have also been suggestions of an earlier launch in late April.
Now NASA has officially confirmed the target date of this historic event for American astronautics (the first manned launch since the closure of the Space Shuttle in 2011) - the second half of May.
SpaceX and @ NASA are targeting no earlier than mid-to-late May for Crew Dragon ’ s launch with two @ NASA _ Astronauts on board https: / / t.co / E1GUQvEnnf https: / / t.co / 8O30eYD4vm — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) Mars Now SpaceX delivers only cargo to the International Space Station under the NASA Commercial Resupply Services (CRS) contract, using a bundle of the Falcon 9 launch vehicle and the Cargo Dragon cargo ship.
Crew Dragon is a manned spacecraft developed by SpaceX to deliver crews to the ISS.
The Demo-2 mission is the latest phase of NASA ’ s Crew Dragon certification program for manned flights.
NASA announced the composition of the crew of the first manned mission Crew Dragon back in 2018.
The first flight will go astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley, who before the final tests of the emergency rescue system of the Crew Dragon spacecraft in flight conducted a dress rehearsal of the ground part of the upcoming Demo-2 mission and tried on new SpaceX spacesuits.
Suited up!
While crew members won't be aboard # CrewDragon during tomorrow's @ SpaceX In-Flight Abort Test, astronauts Bob Behnken & Doug Hurley learned what they'll experience during @ Commercial _ Crew missions.
I'm excited we'll soon launch American astronauts from American soil! pic.twitter.com / Fr3CjGTm4s — Jim Bridenstine (@ JimBridenstine) January 17, 2020 It was originally planned that the Demo-2 mission will last about a week and a half, but in January after a successful test of the SAS in flight NASA said it was considering extending the mission to the usual 1.5-3 months.
For the past few weeks, Benken and Hurley have been actively training, preparing for a long expedition.
The big day is on the way: We're launching astronauts to space from American soil once again.
@ Astro _ Doug Hurley & @ AstroBehnken continued @ space _ station & spacewalk training this week for their upcoming flight on NASA's @ SpaceX DM-2 @ Commercial _ Crew mission.
# LaunchAmerica pic.twitter.com / Yr3vBcxQgo — Johnson Space Center (@ NASA _ Johnson) February 22, 2020 After members of the current expedition Jessica Meir and Andrew Morgan leave the station in late spring, Christopher Cassidy will have to cope on his own.
So the help of veteran Benken may well be useful.
By the way, earlier Musk mentioned the study by SpaceX engineers of the possibility of landing Crew Dragon not in the ocean, but on a ship with a large network - now the company uses this approach to catch parts of the head fairing of the Falcon 9 after launches (of many attempts, only two (1 and 2) have been successful so far).
Earlier this month, it was exactly one year since the first unmanned launch of the Crew Dragon spacecraft as part of the Demo-1 mission.
It is hardly worth saying how important for SpaceX and the entire world of cosmonautics is the first manned launch of a private spacecraft Crew Dragon.
After the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011, the only means of delivering crews to the International Space Station are the Russian Soyuz spacecraft.
And it took SpaceX eight years to make the project a reality.
In the future, SpaceX plans to use Crew Dragon not only to deliver crews to the ISS, but also for tourist flights into space.
Actually, to date, SpaceX has already announced two such missions (1 and 2) - both are scheduled for 2021.

title: Vladimir Putin proposes temporary moratorium on sanctions
text:
President Vladimir Putin during his speech at the G20 summit said that during the crisis it is important to create so-called "green corridors", free from trade wars and sanctions for the mutual supply of medicines, food, equipment and technology.
“Ideally, we should introduce a moratorium, a solidary moratorium on restrictions on essential goods, as well as on financial transactions for their purchases, ” the president said.
Putin stressed that first of all we are talking about “the countries that suffer most from this pandemic. ”
According to the President, the G20 participants need a common plan to support economies, stabilize the situation and restore confidence in world markets in the context of the spread of the coronavirus.
National economies should play a major role in increasing global demand, but borrowing opportunities for many countries in the face of market volatility are limited.
The chief economist of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Maximo Torero, also believes that in the conditions of the pandemic, it is necessary to prevent the introduction of a policy of “beggar-thy-neighbor ”, which, in the form of increased export duties or an outright ban on exports, was practiced by some countries during the global food price crisis in 2008.
“Such measures lead to a mirror reaction and worsen the situation for everyone, not just for small trading partners, ” he says (quoted on the FAO website).
Torero believes that the temporary reduction of prohibitive import tariffs, non-tariff trade barriers and value-added taxes will help stabilize global food markets.
“Temporary cash payments to low-income farmers are important, as well as subsidies for the resumption of production, ” Torero said.
Banks should abandon farm loan commissions and extend their repayment periods.
To help small and medium-sized agribusinesses and their workers stay afloat, it is possible to inject capital into the agricultural sector, he says.
And during a state of emergency, governments can conduct special purchases of agricultural products from small farmers to create emergency strategic reserves for humanitarian purposes.
According to FAO, while interruptions in the supply of products due to the pandemic are minimal, but in April-May, the organization expects disruptions in food supply chains.
For example, movement restrictions, as well as rudimentary undesirable behavior of workers, can discourage farmers and processors.
Agricultural production may also be adversely affected by the shortage of fertilizers, veterinary drugs and other resources.
The pandemic will also affect food demand.
In its beginning, there is a consumer hype, but there is the possibility of a disproportionately large reduction in the consumption of meat (as a result of scientifically unfounded fears that animals can be carriers of the virus) and other high-value products such as vegetables and fruits (which will lead to falling prices), FAO fears.
Job losses can affect consumption in less affluent countries, where food demand is more income-related.
Also, due to the fear of infection, people may visit markets less and will resort to the delivery of products, according to experts of the organization.

title: Now all hope for SpaceX. Boeing will repeat unmanned flight CST-100 Starliner after failed first launch
text:
In December 2019, the Boeing aircraft manufacturer carried out the first unmanned flight of the CST-100 Starliner manned spacecraft, which, as you know, was not without overlays - the ship was unable to enter its normal orbit and returned to Earth before reaching the ISS.
And now Boeing has finally clarified the situation: the concern decided to repeat the unmanned flight before the first flight with a crew on board.
Boeing explained that they made this decision to fully check all aspects of the flight to the ISS on another instance of the CST-100 Starliner and make sure that all subsystems are reliable.
Interestingly, this additional launch will be carried out by Boeing at its own expense.
The exact date has not yet been announced, but Boeing tentatively plans to launch in the fall of 2020.
That is, it is extremely unlikely that the CST-100 Starliner will be able to perform its first flight with a crew this year.
And now we can say with full confidence that all hope for SpaceX — the first operational flight of Crew Dragon with a crew as part of the Demo-2 mission to the ISS is still scheduled for next month.
Joint teams from @ NASA and @ SpaceX continue making progress on the first @ Commercial _ Crew crewed flight test with astronauts to the @ Space _ Station by completing a series of mission simulations from launch to landing s pic.twitter.com / 4RRBmOFgrY — NASA's Kennedy Space Center (@ NASAKKennedy) March 31, 2020 Just last week, NASA astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley conducted a full simulation of the test flight of the SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft with a crew to the ISS — from pre-launch training to docking with the station.
Symbolically, Hurley was the pilot of the Space Shuttle Atlantis during STS-135, the last mission of the Space Shuttle program in July 2011.
Benken, in turn, participated in two shuttle missions - STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010) as a flight specialist (six spacewalks).
The worm is back!
When the @ SpaceX Falcon 9 lifts off carrying @ NASA _ Astronauts aboard # CrewDragon, it will sport the iconic symbol to mark the return of human spaceflight on American rockets from American soil.
More: https: / / t.co / jQQv5ZcTY0 # TheWormIsBack pic.twitter.com / 9Ltk1nMa8j — Jim Bridenstine (@ JimBridenstine) April 2, 2020 As has been repeatedly noted, after the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011, the only means of delivering crews to the International Space Station remain Russian Soyuz ships; NASA pays $80-85 million for each seat on board the ship.
Recall that the current contract of NASA with Roscosmos, expires in the fall of 2020.
Thus, if everything goes according to plan and the first manned flight of the Crew Dragon spacecraft will perform in May, and the first regular mission to the ISS will take place in the fourth quarter under a contract with NASA, then a situation may occur when all three manned spacecraft for the ISS (Soyuz, CST-100 Starliner and Crew Dragon) will be simultaneously docked to the station for a short time.
If all goes well, an uncrewed Orbital Flight Test in the fall of 2020 will see a Crew Dragon and Starliner spacecrafts docked to the Space Station at the same time.
Dragon will be at the Station for Crew-1 – SpaceX ’ s first operational crewed mission. – Michael Baylor (@ nextspaceflight) April 6, 2020 In addition to Soyuz, CST-100 Starliner and Crew Dragon, there are two more manned spacecraft – the Chinese Shenzhou and the American Orion.
The latter has made only one unmanned space flight so far, and its first manned mission is scheduled for 2022.
Source: Boeing

title: How the Japanese Live in Self-Isolation
text:
Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe last week decided to extend the emergency regime throughout the country.
The cause was the coronavirus pandemic, which local authorities have not yet managed to stop.
Similar measures were previously introduced in Tokyo and six other prefectures of the island state.
Despite this, the total number of COVID-19 infections continues to grow steadily.
The number of infected people in the country has already exceeded 10 thousand people.
A serious concern is the situation in the metropolitan metropolis, where more than 3 thousand patients with positive tests for coronavirus were recorded.
Every day, more than a hundred new people are added to them.
Special conditions will be valid until May 6, that is, until the end of the so-called "golden week" - a period of long weekends in late April and early May, when the Japanese en masse rush to travel around the country and abroad.
The government believes that it is extremely important for citizens to stay at home during the upcoming holidays.
Shinzo Abe on April 17 at a special press conference once again urged the Japanese to limit the exit to the street and contact with other people.
The head of the Cabinet of Ministers pointed out the importance of the problem and asked the people to gather their forces in a
In support of the population during the difficult period, Abe promised to allocate 100 thousand yen (930 US dollars) to each family.
Financial aid will come in May.
In addition, residents of the Japanese archipelago will receive free face masks reusable - two pieces per family.
Local television showed the story of how postmen in Tokyo ’ s Setagaya district on red mopeds began to deliver transparent sealed envelopes with masks to their homes.
The measures of the Japanese government in comparison with the response to the pandemic of other states look too lenient.
The introduction of the emergency regime does not imply the blocking of cities or penalties for violating the self-isolation regime, only partially expands the powers of regional authorities.
Heads of prefectural administrations can now close public places, including educational and entertainment facilities, and seize plots of land and real estate for temporary use to accommodate hospitals and medical infrastructure.
Otherwise, the declaration of emergency is advisory in nature and is designed for the discipline of the Japanese.
The local population in general responded responsibly to the calls of the authorities.
There are fewer people on the streets.
For example, Tokyo on Saturday, when it rained heavily for half a day, almost deserted.
A day later, it became clear that the main factor that made people stay home was bad weather, and not fear of contracting the coronavirus.
On Sunday, the sun came out, the air temperature rose above 20 degrees, as a result, in the very center of the capital city on a small lawn near the Tokyo Tower, you could see a picture with numerous Japanese companies.
Parents with children, young couples frolic in the fresh air: someone played badminton or ball, others just sat on the mats and enjoyed a warm weekend.
In another neighborhood, I saw a playground.
The kids were rolling down the hill, running and making noise.
At the same time, on April 18, on the front page in the evening issue of the Asahi Shimbun newspaper, a picture with a similar platform covered with a special ribbon was flaunted.
Entrance was prohibited.
And yet COVID-19 changed the life of Japan.
Many in the country have switched to working in remote form.
Schools took a break in the educational process until the beginning of May.
In Tokyo, previously noisy and crowded areas have turned into quiet and calm streets.
In large hotels, where a couple of months ago scurried well-trained porters, and taxi drivers helped tourists to put suitcases in the trunk of sparkling clean cars, it is now dark and deserted.
Announcements of a break in work until at least May 6 are posted in closed doors.
At the same time, banks, food stores, medical institutions and transport continue to operate as usual.
Interestingly, hairdressing and manicure salons also did not go into quarantine.
A few days ago, I looked into a nearby barber shop.
At the counter, they explained that they were not going to curl up.
With annoyance in the voice clarified that there will be no problems with the recording, since the number of customers has decreased by half.
Local restaurants and cafes reacted differently to the introduction of emergency mode in Japanese cities.
Some restaurants, primarily located in business centers, have closed.
Some have reduced their working hours.
At the same time, most restaurants still serve customers, mainly clerks, at lunchtime and gradually begin to refocus on cooking takeaway.
It ’ s harder to find a place to hang out tonight.
In Tokyo, bars put up signs with the inscription "closed" at exactly 20: 00.
With the order for alcoholic beverages must be determined and at all until 19: 00.
In one pizzeria, I still winked, explained that they are ready to serve visitors until 22: 00, but orders are taken strictly until 21: 00.
Against the background of this situation, the Japanese are increasingly arranging feasts on the Internet.
Skype, Zoom and other applications come to the rescue.
In stores there were sets designed for drinking at home.
Popular and traditional Japanese boxes with food "o-bento".
Usually there put a portion of rice, a few pieces of meat or fish, as well as vegetables.
People are gradually getting tired of the new conditions of existence.
The Japanese are not used to working at home.
The average head of a Japanese family disappears all day in the office until late in the evening, after which he goes to have a glass of sake with his colleagues.
Such a man in everyday life does not see his household.
Now, during self-isolation, the families were locked in apartments.
Husband, wife and children are forced to be face to face for a long time in a confined space.
Given the small areas of Japanese homes, some are experiencing serious stress.
The most inventive Japanese came out of the situation in a funny way.
People set up tourist tents on balconies or directly in living rooms.
The idea especially pleased the children.
The guys climb into improvised shelters with all their belongings: toys, sweets and blankets.
They can sit there for hours.
In local stores, they were surprised to find that sales of tents have recently increased several times.
There are also some types of tents of cubic shape for office workers.
There you can retire in silence with a small table, chair and laptop.

title: 800,000 cut tulips. Stories about the epidemic in Japan
text:
The COVID-19 pandemic, which is testing the strength of the whole world, has so far seemed to bypass Japan - which seems somewhat surprising, given its geographical proximity to China and close ties with many countries, where the number of deaths is already in the tens of thousands.
By mid-afternoon on April 23, only about 300 people had died from coronavirus infection in Japan.
But according to forecasts, this is just the beginning.
How is the national character of the Japanese manifested in the coming difficult times and what losses and fundamental changes in the usual way of life await them in the future?
One of the first blows for Japan, of course, was the postponement of the XXXII Summer Olympic Games in Tokyo, scheduled for this July, which was announced a month ago.
More than $12 billion was officially invested in the preparation of the Olympics by the Japanese state alone, but in fact this amount is three times more, if you take into account the costs and investments of private business.
Local economists are still calculating losses: most believe that Japanese GDP will lose at least $40 billion.
Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi recently reiterated that the negative impact of the global crisis due to the COVID-19 pandemic on his country was the greatest since the defeat in World War II.
Last week, Prime Minister Shinzo Abe finally decided to extend the state of emergency to the entire country, primarily because in late April and early May, Japan is waiting for the so-called “Golden Week ”, a series of several important traditional holidays.
The package of anti-crisis measures in Japan, approved by the government, is estimated at an unprecedented amount - more than 1 trillion 100 billion dollars.
At the same time, all the restrictions and quarantine measures imposed by the Japanese authorities still look unusually mild, if we compare them with similar decisions and legislative acts adopted in Russia, Europe and other countries.
Modern Japanese society, due to the peculiarities of the country ’ s development and its history in the last hundred years, is extremely sensitive to any attempts by the state to somehow limit its freedoms, and Shinzo Abe ’ s cabinet has to act extremely cautiously.
For example, according to a Gallup International survey, now almost everywhere in the world, the proportion of people willing to sacrifice rights to fight COVID-19 is growing.
An average of 81 percent of respondents from 18 countries are prepared to suffer the restrictions of their freedoms if it helps to cope with the pandemic.
Among the countries with the highest number of consonants – India, Austria, Germany, Italy, from 90 to 85 percent of respondents.
In Russia, the share of respondents willing to donate rights to combat COVID-19 was 69 percent, in the United States – 68 percent.
And the last place in this ranking was taken by Japan: only 7 percent of respondents are ready to give up their rights for the sake of victory over coronavirus infection.
Vasily Golovnin, a Russian publicist and orientalist political scientist living in Tokyo, tells about the life of the Japanese during the RFE / RL epidemic for many years: “In each country, the epidemic affects the state of the people ’ s minds differently, and sometimes it takes completely bizarre forms.
Are there any features, changes in the social behavior of the majority of Japanese, such as yesterday, for example, it was difficult to imagine?
“The changes, I would say, are colossal, visible to the naked eye, right from the room where I am now.
Opposite my home is one apartment building, where the middle class lives or a little higher.
Now, I never saw lit windows there until about 11 p.m. or even later.
People always rolled up after work in some zucchini, bars, restaurants, as millions of Japanese do after work.
Now the situation is completely new and unusual: the windows are all burning, people are sitting at home, in self-isolation.
The song "Kaito" ("Kite"), which has now become the anthem of resistance to the coronavirus in Japan: A colossal event is approaching, very important for Japan, the so-called "Golden Week".
This is a series of weekends and holidays, which will begin this year on April 29 and will continue continuously until May 6.
Previously, it was something unimaginable: all of Japan removed from place, got on planes, high-speed trains, own cars and somewhere else went.
Someone flew abroad, to the Hawaiian Islands, someone to his grandmother in the village, in general, the whole country came into motion.
Children were taken to all kinds of parks with attractions.
The upper limit of activity that local businesses have been waiting for for a year, because sales of everything you can imagine jumped to the skies.
It looks like there will be no Golden Week.
The emergency mode is largely introduced just in order to somehow prevent people from moving out of place and going to other cities, carrying the coronavirus with them.
And apparently, the Japanese will respond to the call of the authorities, because it is already known that tickets for trains purchased incomparably, tens of times less than usual, for planes too.
- And in Japan now the external and internal air communication is closed, open? - External air and sea communication is not interrupted entirely, but very limited.
It is impossible to fly and arrive from 73 countries, and these are the main countries of the world - the United States, China, the countries of the European Union.
Just yesterday, April 22, Russia was added to this list.
This is also a huge blow to the economy.
For example, Tokyo ’ s main Narita International Airport has two runways, so one of them was closed because it is no longer needed.
Closed and the international terminal in the largest in all Japan Tokyo airport Haneda, which, however, has long served mainly domestic flights.
And domestic air traffic has decreased by a factor of ten.
The fact is that the Japanese are very accustomed to travel by plane, they use them almost as buses, between all the cities of the country carried out a lot of domestic flights.
In Japan, you can always fly as you like, ignoring even Tokyo and other megacities as interchange points.
So these small domestic flights from town to town disappeared completely, no one flies, and airlines suffer huge losses. – In Japan, there is any shortage of some goods related to the quarantine and epidemic?
Has everyone in the last couple of months always had enough medical masks or, say, the notorious toilet paper? – Of course, the deficit was from the very beginning, and toilet paper, and masks, and disinfectant liquids.
Toilet paper appeared later, it is now everywhere, because it disappeared at first under the influence of panic and false rumors that it was purchased in China and it will not be anymore, because in China "everything is bad."
But this was not true, because toilet paper, as a thing extremely important for the human body, the Japanese make themselves.
I just got back from a little walk in my neighborhood and saw that the shops were full of toilet paper.
But there is a shortage of the other, and it is primarily medical masks.
This is where dependence on China really hurts.
80 percent of all masks, both conventional and complex medical, were purchased from the People ’ s Republic of China, and that import disappeared.
Now Japan is trying to increase its production, masks are trying to sew even such major manufacturers of household electrical goods and equipment as Sharp, Panasonic and others who have never done this.
But this production does not catch up with demand, especially given the characteristic Japanese cleanliness and squeamishness.
Masks are trying to sew even such major manufacturers of household electrical goods and appliances as Sharp, Panasonic and others, who have never done this, the government, of course, is trying to do something.
It promised to give each Japanese family two reusable rag masks that can be washed.
The distribution began in Tokyo with the largest, most densely populated area.
Unfortunately, I don ’ t live there and I ’ m waiting for my turn.
I think it will reach me somewhere, probably at the beginning of next week.
All masks are distributed to post offices, and postmen on their motorcycles or small cars go around the house and in the mailboxes of each family throw a plastic sealed bag with these masks.
Since Japan has a population of more than 126 million people, the entire operation will cost the budget almost half a billion dollars. – The Japanese are known for their self-discipline, they will clearly observe the most stringent measures of quarantine and self-isolation, if all this becomes law, but so far the Japanese government does not resort to any harsh measures.
What indirect hints are used by the authorities to encourage the population to show less social activity?
To begin with, it must be emphasized that the government in Japan after the Second World War, because of the memory of the repressive militarist regime of that era, the powers to introduce some emergency measures are extremely small, or rather, they are almost none.
Now the Prime Minister has declared a state of emergency, but it means that only local governors can take any violent measures.
The Cabinet of Ministers can not command anyone.
And governors, since they are elected and cherish political careers, also do not want to make tough decisions that can offend the Japanese and cause them great discontent.
The Japanese, in principle, are not used to being commanded somehow, at least in all the postwar decades.
That is why we are talking about persuasion and appeals.
Lists of those enterprises and objects that are officially persuaded to close are entertainment establishments, bars, cultural facilities, museums.
For example, closed all the famous Japanese amusement parks, the same giant Tokyo Disneyland.
In other words, it closed itself, on its own initiative.
The same entertainment, very complex, computerized, park of the American company Universal Pictures, where attractions based on the Harry Potter films are created, is closed.
The entire entertainment industry, which is based on direct communication, has stopped.
Including numerous and famous local "hostess-bars", that is, specific places with girls, or with young people, which are designed for clients-ladies.
There is a lot of this in Japan, and it doesn ’ t work.
Owners are suffering huge losses.
For many years I went to one small bar, literally to several places where I had a good relationship with the bartender, he understood me, found those drinks that I like – so he closed, because no one goes to them.
There are compensations, of course, throwing some money to these people.
The story with the famous flower park in all of Japan also made a noise with the famous flower park in all of Japan, where a tulip festival takes place every year in April.
It is necessary to see at all, in words it is quite difficult to convey!
Colossal relief panoramas, paintings of fresh flowers, laid out on the slopes of the hills, in the lowlands.
It is enough to name even only their number - 800 thousand tulips.
The authorities asked not to open this festival, it was announced on TV, wrote everywhere in newspapers, on the Internet, on social networks, begged people not to go there, because it will not open.
But the people are everyone, and even the Japanese, despite all their notorious discipline, still began to slowly pull up in this park to look at these floral wonders.
So, in the end, the authorities took an unprecedented hard step: they simply cut off all these 800 thousand unique, elite tulips that were specially grown for this festival.
Are the needy subsidized, the suffering business, the money distributed at all, the credit holidays arranged? – Yes, and the assistance programs are simply, I would say, amazing size.
First, a special program with a budget of almost $1 trillion 100 billion is aimed at supporting business, small, medium, or any other.
That ’ s about 20 percent of Japan ’ s GDP.
Japan has never known such a program of assistance to the national economy and population.
Each resident of the country, and not only a citizen of Japan, but also a foreigner who has a long-term visa here, will be given about a little less than a thousand dollars, transferred to his bank account.
The central authorities did not want to adopt this program for a long time, because they believe that it will not have a great economic effect in the conditions of the emergency regime.
In general, this distribution of about a thousand dollars to each person, including infants, foreigners, homeless people, all absolutely, of course, in the first place should have a therapeutic, psychological effect to help people survive in the current difficult situation.
Every resident of the country, and not only a citizen of Japan, but also a foreigner who has a long-term visa here, will be given about a little less than a thousand dollars This trillion-dollar program includes not only cash, of course.
These include tax breaks and direct targeted assistance to local governments, which already distribute money at the grass-roots level.
For example, the same bartender I know will get about $5,000 for closing his microbarchik.
That money won't save him, but it's better than nothing.
If the company, for example, owns not one institution, but several, two or more, it will be given somewhere under 10 thousand dollars.
So help is coming, and by the way, not only from the authorities.
It is with amazement and affection that I constantly read about the examples of social solidarity shown by private business.
For example, the largest local operator in the rental market, the company "Dave House", announced that it provides a delay in the payment of rent for a quarter to residents of 500,000 apartment buildings.
This, of course, is a very tangible amount.
Or, for example, one owner of the largest chain of large shopping malls just cut his salary by a third to pay benefits not fully employed in his stores.
The Imperial family is already quite isolated in Japan, it is not the British royal house, but of course they have changes.
Cancelled literally all events with the participation of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako.
Because of the incident, the heir to the throne of Fumihito, Prince Akishino, the younger brother of the current emperor, can not hold a ceremony at which he should be presented to Japan and the world as the person who stands first in line for the Chrysanthemum throne.
This ceremony has been postponed many times, and finally it hovered in the air now. – Today, a lot of homegrown conspiracy theorists have come to light, various fantastic conspiracy theories are being discussed.
Japan has its own wonderful versions of what is happening? – Wonderful local versions I have not heard.
One theory dominates: ordinary Japanese at the household level, in general, blame China for the whole story.
That is, no one says that the Chinese did it on purpose, of course, but Beijing angers everyone here by the fact that it was silent for a long time and did not warn the world about the scale and specifics of the disaster, did not give the necessary knowledge to neighboring countries.
And, what can be attributed to conspiracy, talk has become more frequent that it all broke out of the very secret laboratory for the study of dangerous viruses, which is located in the city of Wuhan. – Japanese science, scientists and doctors are now looking for some of their own ways to combat the virus, develop vaccines, medicines?
Or are they more hopeful that help will come from outside? – Work on a vaccine is underway most actively.
Japan has a very powerful pharmaceutical industry of its own, and several world-class pharmaceutical companies are naturally working feverishly to develop a vaccine, because everyone understands that this is not only a necessity, but also a potential huge amount of money.
Already, two Japanese pharmaceutical companies have announced that they intend to start clinical trials in late June and early July.

title: NASA and SpaceX will make their first historic flight in the midst of a pandemic
text:
Director of NASA Jim Bridenstine (Jim Bridenstine) on Friday during the conference told reporters that scheduled for may 27, the first in the history of the launch of astronauts to the International space station aboard the spacecraft SpaceX is a priority for the us space Agency.
In itself, such a statement from the head of NASA is quite ordinary, but it was of particular importance during the first of three Friday press conferences of the agency, due to the situation in which Bridenstine spoke.
The supervisor joined the teleconference from his home in Tulsa, Oklahoma, rather than from NASA headquarters.
The reason is obvious — the coronavirus pandemic, because of which many Americans work from home.
Much of everyday life across America is currently unavailable due to COVID-19.
But both SpaceX and NASA say they are aiming to send humans into orbit from their native American soil for the first time since the completion of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.
The mission, called Demo-2 (or DM2), involves the launch of NASA astronauts Doug Hurley (Doug Hurley) and Bob Behnken (Bob Behnken) on the reusable spacecraft Crew Dragon as part of the Falcon 9 launch vehicle from the launch position at Cape Canaveral (Florida, USA).
The astronauts will travel to the ISS, where they will join the crew for a while before heading aboard Crew Dragon back to Earth to complete the mission demonstration.
"The moon is a testing ground for a destination, and the destination itself is, of course, Mars," Bridenstine said.
NASA is also working with SpaceX on a next-generation SpaceX Starship spacecraft that CEO Elon Musk hopes will one day take humans to Mars.
But first, NASA must launch astronauts on a brand-new spacecraft for the first time since 1981.

title: Turkey is approaching the borders of Russia
text:
Turkey is getting closer to Russia ’ s borders.
Among its allies, Ukraine and Georgia In September, the Eternity 2019 command and staff exercise was held in Azerbaijan, in which the military from Georgia and the second largest army of NATO countries, Turkey, took part.
These maneuvers are another example of how Erdogan is trying to spread Turkish influence in the post-Soviet space.
But if some countries try to maneuver between Moscow and Ankara, others risk becoming completely dependent on Turkey.
How serious this trend is and how dangerous it is for Russia, Lenta.ru found out.
Initially, it was assumed that the military forces of Ankara and Baku, which have long been considered strategic partners, would take part in the exercises.
The Turkish authorities have repeatedly stated that “relations with Azerbaijan are one of the priority areas of foreign policy ”, and friendship between the countries within the framework of the principle of“ one nation, two states ” will only be strengthened in the future.
In the summer it became known that Georgia will also participate in the maneuvers.
After a series of scandals and another cooling in relations with Russia, Tbilisi willingly accepted the invitation to join the exercises.
The Georgians are confident that this will help them increase the training of the army ’ s command staff, as well as cooperation with Turkey, NATO ’ s second most powerful army, will bring them closer to the dream of joining the North Atlantic bloc.
Ankara, in turn, interested in extending its influence to Tbilisi, has long agreed to become a mediator between the Caucasian republic, on the one hand, and the EU, along with the alliance, on the other.
“Georgia should be included in the NATO membership plan, ” Turkish Foreign Minister Mevlut Cavusoglu said.
It was decided to bring Tbilisi closer to the North Atlantic bloc in the early 1990s with the help of the NATO Partnership for Peace program for the countries of the Caucasus and Central Asia, which are not members of the organization, but receive military assistance.
Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan.
Cooperation between Turkey, Azerbaijan and Georgia has intensified since 2012.
For seven years now, the military ministers of the three countries have held regular meetings on regional security issues.
Last year, Baku, Ankara and Tbilisi signed a Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in the defense sector.
All these steps are connected with the desire of Turkey to strengthen its influence in the post-Soviet space.
First of all, we are talking about countries with Turkic-speaking populations - Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan Shadow of the Ottoman Empire In order to understand Ankara's interest in supporting the countries of the former USSR, it is worth turning to history.
For several centuries, Turkey was a huge Ottoman Empire, with the power of which the strongest powers of the world were considered.
When at the end of the 19th century it became clear that the empire was bursting at the seams, the Turks called on all Turkic-speaking peoples to unite into one state with the center in Anatolia.
However, they did not agree.
Another attempt to return to the imperial past was made during the First World War: the Turks decided to take advantage of the weakened position of Russia and take over all the territories belonging to it with the Turkic-speaking population.
Again, it did not work - Turkey was defeated in that war.
However, Ankara has not abandoned its idea.
Another opportunity to realize it presented itself with the collapse of the USSR: the newly formed states of Central Asia and the Caucasus did not know where to go and with whom to be friends.
Russia was not there for them.
The country did not have time to cope with its economic problems, besides, the priority in Moscow ’ s foreign policy at that time was the establishment of relations with the West.
The Turks decided not to miss their chance: for the first time since the death of the Ottoman Empire, they were given the opportunity to extend their influence beyond their own borders, revive their former greatness, increase their importance in the international arena, as well as get the much-desired access to gas and oil fields.
It was decided to penetrate the region from three directions at once: economic, political and ideological.
While the Turkish authorities were seriously discussing the creation of a new “Turkic-speaking community from the Adriatic Sea to the Great Wall of China, ” local media were actively assessing the chances of“ restoring Turkic unity. ”
Instead of the usual ethnic designations “Uzbek ”,“ Kyrgyz ” or “Tatar ”, words such as“ Uzbek Turk ”, “Kyrgyz Turk ” or“ Tatar Turk ” were used.
The Turkic peoples living outside the Republic of Turkey were referred to as “external Turks ”.
In December 1991, Ankara was the first to recognize the new Turkic-speaking states of Central Asia and Transcaucasia, as well as... Ukraine.
At a meeting with US President George H.W. Bush, Prime Minister Suleiman Demirel spoke about the change in the regional status of his country.
Now she had the prospect of “determining the political future of the Muslim republics of the CIS. ”
Ankara faced two tasks – to ensure the communication of Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan with the West, as well as to convince the leadership of the newly formed states that Turkey, as Demirel said, “should become a conductor of the interests of young Muslim countries in the West. ”
Washington supported this decision.
They agreed that Ankara would provide material and financial assistance to the Turkic-speaking republics of the former Soviet Union, but the money for this was given by the United States and other Western countries.
At the same time, the Agency for Turkic Cooperation and Development (TIKA) appeared under the Turkish Foreign Ministry, and a new position of minister for relations with the Turkic-speaking republics of the CIS appeared in the government.
Especially remembered in this post Abdulhalyuk Chey, who developed a rather rapid activity.
“The Turkish Republic is the successor of the great Ottoman Empire, it should create a union with Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan even at the cost of a sharp confrontation with Russia, ” he said.
One after another, structures of Turkic cooperation appeared: the Turkic Council, the World Assembly of Turkic Peoples, TURKSOY (International Organization of Turkic Culture), various meetings of local authorities with the heads of the Turkic republics of the CIS were held, as well as high-level meetings.
Educational programs have become another tool of influence on the former Soviet republics.
Students and schoolchildren are mainly trained in the territory of the Republic of Turkey, although there are special universities in Central Asian countries - the Turkish-Kazakh Akhmet Yassawi University and the Kyrgyz-Turkish Manas University.
Over the past 20 years, Turks have provided 26,000 scholarships for Turkic-speaking students.
Islam plays an important role in Turkey ’ s relations with the Transcaucasian and Central Asian states.
For this purpose, with the active assistance of the Turks, the Office for Religious Affairs was established under the supervision of the Islamic Council of Eurasia.
In all the Turkic-speaking republics of the former Soviet Union, Turkish satellite television broadcasts are shown, the main task of which is to promote the Turkish model of development.
Through friendly relations with Turkey, the post-Soviet states dreamed of establishing strong ties with the West and adjusting their flimsy financial situation.
Economic projects were also created one by one.
In 2014, the document “Turkic Council – a modern Silk Road ” was signed, the purpose of which is to make Ankara a kind of bridge between Central Asia and Europe.
Particularly close economic relations have developed between Turkey and Azerbaijan.
Ankara has already taken a leading place among the foreign trade partners of Baku, the countries cooperate on important energy projects, for example, the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline or the TANAP gas pipeline.
Turkey did a lot for the formation of the Azerbaijani armed forces after the collapse of the USSR, and also, without hesitation, took the side of Baku in the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict with Armenia.
