However, it would be wrong to say that Azerbaijan focuses exclusively on interaction with Turkey, Turkish political scientist Serkan Demirtash told Lenta.ru.
“Baku, cooperating with Ankara, maintains close ties with Moscow.
Such a balance is needed in order to protect its domestic policy from the intervention of the US and the EU.
Brussels and Washington in the framework of Euro-Atlantic integration would try to adjust the policy of Baku in respect of human rights, and Azerbaijan does not need it, ” the expert believes.
If Baku behaves rather cautiously with Ankara, Tbilisi tries to interact as actively as possible with its generous neighbor.
Turkey uses all the tools of “soft power ” in this country.
The Turkish Agency for International Cooperation and Development (TİKA), as well as the Yunus Emre Institute, which promotes the Turkish language and culture, are in operation.
Such a policy has already borne fruit: Turkey has gradually displaced Azerbaijan and Russia from the Georgian market, becoming a key trading partner and main investor.
Of particular interest from an economic point of view is Adjara, a Muslim region in Christian Georgia.
Now followers of Islam make up more than 10 percent of the total population of the country, and this figure is constantly growing.
It was in this autonomous republic that Turkish investments poured.
Being there, you forget that you came to Georgia: everywhere there are glittering signs in Turkish, muezzins from newly built mosques read azan, along the coast there are cozy expensive hotels and casinos, restaurants, bars and shops selling imported Turkish goods.
Another center of attraction for the Turks is Batumi.
The deplorable state of the local economy, cheap labor and housing, as well as low taxes attract entrepreneurs living on the border with Georgia.
In addition, they are interested in the availability of what is prohibited in Turkey.
It ’ s about drugs and casinos.
Right on the border you can buy a bus tour to all the golden places of Batumi.
Through the TIKA agency, Ankara implements various economic projects in the neighboring country related to the construction, transport and medical fields.
However, relatively recently, the Turks had to slow down with entrepreneurship in the agricultural sector.
Until 2018, they actively bought up land, but after complaints from local residents, foreigners were forbidden to own plots.
Initially, the Georgians could not enjoy the “selfless help ” of their southern neighbor, but gradually began to fear that Turkey would de facto be able to establish a kind of protectorate over Adjara, and then completely influence Georgia ’ s relations with other states.
Previously, concerns about “soft expansion ” on the part of Ankara worried only the opposition, now representatives of the authorities are thinking about this threat.
Recently, the countries agreed to double the volume of mutual trade.
However, later in Tbilisi realized that Georgia has nothing to offer in the Turkish market, therefore, the import of only Turkish goods will double, so the growth of the trade balance will be only in favor of Ankara.
The words of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan that “the interests of modern Ankara coincide with the interests of the Ottoman Empire ” were not ignored, in this context he mentioned the capital of Adjara.
“Our physical boundaries are different from those in our heart.
Is it possible to distinguish Riza from Batumi? ” the head of state asked from the rostrum.
This speech made a lot of noise in Georgia.
The Turkish embassy then had to explain for a long time that Ankara has no territorial claims to its neighbor, and the words of their leader “just misunderstood ”.
“Crimea is ours ” Relations between Turkey and Ukraine are developing quite productively.
Their interaction intensified in the 1990s, when Turkish leader Suleiman Demirel flew to Kiev, where he first spoke about “the Russian threat in the Black Sea ”, offering as“ deterrence of the Russian Federation ” to provide all Ukrainians with Tatar roots, the opportunity to return to Crimea.
In early August, the new President of Ukraine Vladimir Zelensky met in Ankara with the Turkish leader.
He confirmed that relations between the states have recently reached a new level of strategic partnership.
They were especially adjusted against the background of the acute conflict between the two countries with Moscow in 2014-2015.
Cooperation began to develop in various areas - from the economy and defense industry to tourism and culture.
At that time, Turkey began to provide material and technical assistance to the Armed Forces of Ukraine, to arrange joint naval exercises.
The parties also agreed to jointly produce radar stations, missile systems, drones, military aircraft and even conduct space research.
If earlier there was a visa-free regime between the countries, then in 2017 Turkey and Ukraine completely switched to travel on identity cards.
To take such a step, however, Ankara suggested in the peak of Russia, ignoring the calls of Turkey not only to remove the strict visa regime introduced in January 2016, but also to start flying from one country to another without passports.
Ankara is trying to actively use “soft power ” on the territory of Ukraine, as well as in the countries of Transcaucasia and Central Asia – in Kiev, new Turkish restaurants, cafes and shops are constantly opening, the Yunus Emre Cultural Center has earned, which conducts Turkish courses under the slogan“ More Turkey in Ukraine, more Ukraine in Turkey ”.
In addition, at various international platforms, Ankara declares that it will never support the annexation of Crimea to Russia, since it stands for the territorial integrity of Ukraine.
Turkey is doing this, guided solely by its own interests.
The Republic does not abandon attempts to strengthen its influence on the peninsula due to the competent involvement of the Turkic population.
“Crimean Tatars are an important element of communication between our countries.
We will continue to consider as our priority the protection of the rights of the Crimean Tatars, the preservation of their national identity, ” Erdogan said.
Trade relations between states are gaining momentum.
Kiev sells Ankara steel, coal, products of the chemical industry, Ukraine buys from Turkey industrial products, textiles and food.
The heads of state have repeatedly expressed their desire to increase the trade turnover between the countries to $10 billion a year.
To do this, Kiev and Ankara need to sign an agreement on a free trade zone, negotiations on this issue began even the former President of Ukraine Viktor Yanukovych.
It turned out that there are quite serious contradictions between the countries.
Recently, Ukraine realized that only Turkey would benefit from this agreement, since it actively protects its producers.
For example, the rate of import duty on agricultural products in this republic is 43 percent, while in Ukraine only 11 percent.
Kiev is also concerned about the fact that the Turks export industrial goods and equipment with a high level of added value, while the Ukrainians sell raw materials.
Finally, the Ukrainian authorities do not like the position of their Turkish colleagues regarding the sanctions imposed by the West against Moscow – Ankara is categorically against them, stating that “restrictive measures against our neighbors and partners have caused serious damage to our economy. ”
Kiev is also concerned about the construction of the Turkish Stream, since one of its branches can supply Russian gas to the EU bypassing the Ukrainian gas transportation system - and this is a financial loss.
The rivalry between Moscow and Ankara In the 1990s, Russia allowed Turkey to gain a firm foothold in Central Asia, the Caucasus and Ukraine.
As for education, science and culture, the Turks were much more agile.
Ankara has quite a powerful potential: demography, developed industry and a fairly favorable geographical position, in addition, Turkey is part of NATO, which cannot but attract the countries of the post-Soviet space.
According to the senior researcher of the Institute of World Economy and International Relations of the Russian Academy of Sciences named after E. M. Primakov, associate professor of the Diplomatic Academy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Russia Vladimir Avatkov, against the background of weakening of Moscow's positions in the post-Soviet space, Turkey is still strengthening its influence.
“If in the 90s it was not possible to quickly create a single Turkic alphabet, then today everything is going to this.
The post-Soviet states have almost completely switched to the Latin alphabet, now Kazakhstan is moving to it - this is the result of a very successful Turkish humanitarian policy, "the Turkologist explained.
At the same time, it is not yet possible for the Turks to completely replace Russia in the former USSR - there are not enough resources.
Currently, Ankara itself is going through hard times - the Turkish lira has greatly weakened, inflation and unemployment have increased in the country.
Central Asian and Caucasian countries hoped that Turkey would become a member of the EU, which means that with its help they will be able to approach the West, while moving away from Russia.
But realizing that Ankara ’ s membership in the European Union is not shining, they revised their foreign policy doctrines, deciding to develop cooperation with Moscow in the new conditions.
However, as Avatkov notes, if the economic situation changes again and Turkey has the opportunity to take the place of Russia in the post-Soviet space, it will not miss its chance.
“Turkish influence in Azerbaijan and the Turkic republics of Central Asia is quite large: politicians who studied in Turkey or in Turkish educational institutions are gradually coming to power, who are often not happy with their orientation towards Moscow and seek active interaction with Ankara, ” the expert explains.
If earlier Uzbekistan had a wary attitude towards Ankara, the new Uzbek authorities are more open and begin cooperation with Turkish structures.
If we talk about Turkmenistan, then in fact this rather closed country has only two partner states – Russia and Turkey.
As for Kazakhstan, Turkey still has time to nurture its own cadres there.
In many non-Turkic states of the post-Soviet space, significant Turkish influence is also emerging.
First and foremost, we are talking about Georgia.
At the state level or at the level of private business, Turkey has carried out and is carrying out many programs and infrastructure projects here.
And if in the Central Asian states the influence of Russia remains, if only because there were no objective reasons for the rupture, then in the case of Georgia there is every chance to get a branch of the Ottoman Empire at its borders.

title: The tragedy of PS752: human rights activists called on Iran to stop the persecution of protesters
text:
HRW calls on Iran not to prosecute activists for participating in protests over the downing of a Ukrainian plane.
The international human rights organization Human Rights Watch (HRW) called on the Iranian authorities to stop prosecuting those who conducted peaceful actions in the country because of the shooting down of a Ukrainian passenger plane near Tehran on January 8.
This is reported by Radio Liberty.
The human rights group said that since late April, Iranian courts had sentenced 13 people, including several students, to prison, apparently for taking part in a peaceful protest.
Iranian authorities have previously said they have arrested 30 people in connection with the protests, and details about the exact number of those arrested directly for the downing of the liner, did not specify.
“The Iranian authorities follow the usual pattern of evasion, refusing to provide any details of the investigation into the perpetrators of the deadly error, but judicial officials do not waste time sentencing people who protested over the deaths of 176 people, ” Human Rights Watch said in a statement.
HRW noted that the families of some of the victims have expressed concern that the coronavirus pandemic is slowing down the establishment of justice in this case.
The human rights organization insists that Iran should conduct a transparent investigation and cooperate with international organizations.
As previously reported, on January 8 in Iran crashed the plane "International airlines of Ukraine", performing flight on the route Tehran-Kiev.
176 people were killed.
On board the Boeing 737 were 11 citizens of Ukraine, including 9 crew members, as well as citizens of Iran, Canada, Sweden, Afghanistan, Germany and the United Kingdom.
Three days later, Iranian President Hassan Rouhani admitted that the Ukrainian airliner was shot down “as a result of an unintentional human error ” and promised to bring those responsible to justice.
On February 3, Director of Accident Investigation at the Iranian Civil Aviation Organization Hassan Rezaifar said that Iran will no longer share with Ukraine the evidence in the case of the downing of the UIA aircraft due to the fact that these investigations were “leaked ” to the Ukrainian media.
The countries participating in the International Group for the Coordination of Assistance to Victims of the UIA Plane Crash have repeatedly demanded that Iran hand over the black boxes from the downed airliner to the group.
On February 14, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Zarif said that Iran does not intend to give back the black boxes from the downed UIA aircraft, but will not decrypt their data without the participation of interested parties.
On April 6, it was reported that a representative of the Iranian parliament ’ s committee on legal and judicial issues, MP Hassan Noruzi, said that the Iranian military “did the right thing ” by shooting down a Ukrainian plane.
According to him, there were no arrests in connection with the incident.
On April 27, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba and Iranian Foreign Minister Zarif held a telephone conversation.
According to the press service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Zarif said that Noruzi ’ s words do not correspond to reality and contradict the official position of Iran.
The Minister also recalled that several people have already been detained during the investigation of the downing of the Ukrainian liner.

title: MECHANISMS OF ADAPTATION OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND RURAL TERRITORIES TO GLOBAL CLIMATIC CHANGES
text:
N.V. Zinovchuk, Doctor of Economics, Professor In our days, information has become almost familiar about the increase in the number of natural anomalous phenomena that are a consequence of climate change.
We ourselves notice that the weather is becoming atypical for one or another climatic zone.
We learn about the melting of ice at the North and South poles, the occurrence of fires, floods, storms and tornadoes in regions for which these phenomena were not inherent.
But do we think about the fact that in such areas, climate change leads to the destruction of agriculture and forces people to move to other places or countries.
In the report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change dated March 31, 2014, it was stated that some terrestrial and ocean ecosystems, water supply systems, agricultural lands have already been destroyed and cannot be restored.
Today, there are not many countries that do not face the problem of refugees.
Modern climate change is a natural process that is cyclical and occurs on the planet Earth every 12 thousand years.
The question arises: is it possible to adapt agriculture, at least in some countries, to current and future global changes?
The achievements of modern climatic geoengineering make it possible to monitor the climate, determine the vector of further development of climatic events, identify compensatory mechanisms of nature and launch local or general adaptive effects on changes in climatic conditions.
Therefore, the development of scenario forecasts of agricultural production depending on climate change is real and critically necessary.
One of the first steps is to model predictive scenarios of climate change for each country and the countries closest to it.
It is important to emphasize that the current predictive models of climate change were based on the concept of anthropological influence on the Earth's ecosystems and did not take into account all the factors and scales of the impact of various space and geological processes.
Global climate change on Earth is a derivative of astronomical processes and their cyclical nature.
Humanity will not be able to change, slow down or influence these processes in any way, so it remains to calculate the possible risks and try to adapt to climate change.
The research of the working group of scientists of the ALLATRA International Public Movement in the field of particle physics and neutrino astrophysics opens up opportunities for such calculations and forecasts.
The next step should be to predict the throughput and assimilative capacity of rural areas regarding the settlement of climate refugees, their nutrition and livelihoods.
Today, there are about 100 million people in the world with the status of climate refugees.
And their number will increase exponentially in the near future.
In any country, the likelihood of climate refugees is a serious reason for the development of certain economic instruments to maintain the required volumes of agricultural production.
Preliminary calculations and taking into account the assimilative capacity of rural areas of the country to provide a place of residence and livelihoods for climate refugees will allow systematically and purposefully solve the problems of food security.
Such calculations should be based on the idea of peaceful and tolerant coexistence of the local population and climate refugees.
Such an approach would allow for the management and resolution of territorial, social, economic and environmental conflicts.
An important component of climate change adaptation mechanisms is the introduction of a system of economic instruments.
They will regulate the economic and social processes associated with climate change and the emergence of climate refugees.
The choice of certain tools may vary depending on current situations and the degree of relevance to the tasks set.
But the main feature of such mechanisms is the inclusion of regulators in their composition, which ensure the emergence of social formations that contribute to the unification of people, the development of tolerance and mutual assistance skills in critical situations.
It should be noted that in the consumer format in which modern society lives, most people are divided by borders, political views, cultural traditions, etc.
During cataclysms of any nature, people can have panic, fear and operate the principle of domination of selfish (animal) thinking: to survive at any cost, even at the expense of the lives of other people.
Therefore, it is important to develop such tools that would contribute to the unification of people and a common resistance to climate challenges.
One such regulator may be the equitable distribution of food and drinking water among a group of people living in a particular area during a natural disaster.
But it will work only when people are morally ready to share what they have, when their life will be focused on spiritual and moral values and creative activities.
Today, there is ALLATRA International Public Movement in the world, whose activities are aimed at uniting people around the world and creating conditions for the development of a creative society.
And only united people will be able to survive the coming climate changes.
For humanity, this is a real chance to survive.

title: SpaceX released a browser simulator docking manned Crew Dragon with the ISS
text:
Click here to share content on Facebook.
(Opens in new window) On May 27, the first operational flight of SpaceX Crew Dragon with a crew as part of the Demo-2 mission to the ISS was scheduled.
The event is truly historic for American astronautics – it will be the first manned launch from the United States since the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.
In preparation for the mission, SpaceX has created a browser simulator docking manned spacecraft Crew Dragon with the ISS.
Yes, now everyone can feel like a NASA astronaut and dock Crew Dragon with the ISS.
NASA announced the composition of the crew of the first manned mission Crew Dragon back in 2018.
The first flight will go astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley, who will stay in orbit for at least a month (the maximum mission can last 119 days).
One of the important differences between Crew Dragon is that all stages of its docking with the station are automated.
In particular, the ship docks independently even at the last stage, whereas usually the robotic arm Canadarm2 is used for this on the ISS.
The automatic docking procedure using the IDA international docking adapter, designed for private spacecraft, was tested during the Crew Dragon unmanned flight last year.
The upcoming Crew Dragon flight with astronauts will also take place in full automatic mode.
But, of course, it is possible to switch to manual control.
And this simulator is an exact copy of the real interface for controlling the docking process of the ship.
According to TechCrunch, the simulator is quite simple, it has special buttons to align the orientation of the ship vertically and horizontally, and “all you need to control is patience. ”
The head of NASA Jim Bridenstine has already tested the simulator and boasted that he had the first time to dock Crew Dragon and the ISS.
Last year I got to try out the @ SpaceX # CrewDragon docking simulator with @ Astro _ Doug and @ AstroBehnken.
And yes, I nailed it on my first try!
Learn more about Crew Dragon ’ s control systems and custom-made spacesuits: https: / / t.co / 47qRMZXzIE # LaunchAmerica pic.twitter.com / Q9fHiGMZoO — Jim Bridenstine (@ JimBridenstine) May 12, 2020 Recall, Crew Dragon developed as part of the NASA Commercial Crew Program, which will allow sending astronauts to the ISS without the use of Russian Soyuz spacecraft, and for much less money - now NASA pays about $80 million for one place.
It is expected that the Crew Dragon one seat will cost $20 million (with the possibility of further reduction due to the reuse of Crew Dragon).
Just the other day, NASA published in its YouTube channel a short teaser of the upcoming Demo-2 mission with frames of flight animation and inserts of interesting facts.
Source: NASA

title: Scientists concerned about the risk of suicide among those infected with coronavirus
text:
A group of scientists from Japan, including specialists from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention of the Hospital of the National Center for Health and Medicine of Tokyo, was concerned about the risk of suicide among those infected with the coronavirus.
As reported by Report with reference to “Izvestia ”, with the appropriate letter they appealed to the community of psychiatrists.
Experts called for as much attention as possible to the condition of patients being treated in hospitals.
The scientists noted that during the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) in 2003 and the Middle East SARS outbreak in 2014, those infected faced mental health problems during and after hospital treatment.
So, hospitalized patients were observed suicidal moods, and real cases of suicide among them are also known.
Japanese scientists also examined data from patients with confirmed coronavirus admitted to the National Center between January 29 and March 13, 2020.
The researchers interviewed those who had been in the hospital for more than 20 days.
It turned out that some patients experienced fear of the future, anxiety from separation from loved ones, prejudice about the disease and depression from a prolonged lack of freedom.

title: Pandemic could lead to global mental health crisis: UN
text:
In particular, emerging from the coronavirus pandemic, warning that COVID-19 could trigger a crisis in this area.
This is reported by AR.
In a video message, Guterres said that “after decades of neglect and underinvestment in mental health services, the COVID-19 pandemic is now affecting families and societies with additional mental strain. ”
He pointed out that people are affected by “grief over the loss of loved ones, the shock of losing a job, isolation and restriction of movement, the complex dynamics of family relationships, insecurity and fear of the future. ”
Help and support are increasingly needed by health professionals, older people, adolescents, youth and those who have already had mental health problems, as well as people who are facing a crisis due to the pandemic.
“Mental health services are an important part of all government responses to COVID-19.
They should be expanded and fully funded, ” Guterres said.
The UN warned that if no action is taken, COVID-19 could trigger a mental and physical health crisis in the world.
As of the morning of May 14, the COVID-19 coronavirus had been diagnosed in 4,429,744 people, of whom 298,174 had died, and 1,659,791 had recovered.

title: How warm winter and dry spring will affect the harvest in Belarus
text:
How warm winter and dry spring will affect the harvest in Belarus 1 16.05.2020, 9: 07 1,572 Our country has begun to approach northern Ukraine in terms of climate.
Agriculture is one of the main branches of the economy, which is highly dependent on the weather.
This year we had a warm and snowless winter, dry April, and in May frosts began.
Experts say that while there is no reason to panic, but recognize that climate change leads to a deterioration in the germination of potatoes and flax, traditional for Belarus crops.
But now we have plantations of watermelons, asparagus, grapes and even walnuts.
And every year we grow more and more corn, writes tut.by.
The World Meteorological Organization calls the last decade the warmest on record (since 1850).
The average annual air temperature in Belarus is + 8.8 degrees, this is 2 degrees higher than normal.
Specialists of Belhydromet say that precipitation does not change as intensively as air temperature, and do not have a unidirectional movement towards decrease or increase.
Most often dry conditions are observed for two or more months during the period of active vegetation of plants.
More often, such dry periods were characteristic of the south of our country - Brest and Gomel regions.
If earlier droughts came in the summer, now they are shifting to earlier dates.
Deputy Head of the Hydrology and Agrometeorology Service of Belhydromet Ekaterina Istomina explains that the change in the average annual temperature by one degree leads to an increase in the growing season and an increase in the amount of temperatures in the latitudinal direction by 150 − 200 km.
By 2050, it is predicted that in the south of the Vitebsk region the weather will be as it is now in Gomel.
In general, Belarus is approaching northern Ukraine in terms of climate. – We have a new, fourth agro-climatic zone, which includes the southern part of the Brest region and the Gomel region.
Here the shortest and warmest winter within Belarus and the warmest and longest growing season, – explains Ekaterina Istomina. – Climate change affects the deterioration of the germination of crops characteristic of Belarus – flax and potatoes.
The harvest shifts over time.
Corn crops have increased markedly, rapeseed is actively sown.
In the fields of Belarus began to grow crops that are completely uncharacteristic of our country, for example, industrial plantations of watermelons and grapes.
According to the specialist, the agrometeorological situation in April was difficult. – A large shortage of precipitation, almost all of April there were frosts, this led to various damage.
And most importantly, the lack of rainfall led to the drying of the soil.
Since April 29, the rains began, continued in early May, it improved the situation, now the situation in the fields is generally favorable.
However, in the Gomel region has not yet replenished the entire area of moisture, in the Pinsk district there are still dry foci.
Experts who have worked on the strategy of adapting Belarusian agriculture to climate change note that, depending on weather conditions, the gross grain harvest can vary from 5.5 to 9.5 million tons and in some years is about 60% of the minimum level of food security of the country.
The greatest damage to agricultural production is caused by drought.
In very dry years, the yield of cereals with legumes can decrease by 10 – 20%, and in years of exceptionally severe drought, which today is observed once in 100 years, the yield can decrease by 40%.
The cost of producing crops during a large-scale drought increases by 15 – 20%.
Now, according to experts, another attack is frosts, which can damage rapeseed, corn shoots, fruit.
According to forecasts, frosts will remain until May 20, at night it is expected to minus 3.
Due to the decrease in temperature at the end of March to minus 10 in places, rapeseed died, it was necessary to cross the fields.
Part of the potatoes lost during storage Warming by two degrees affected the potato industry.
In recent years, about 30 new potato diseases have been recorded, such as wound watery rot (a fungus that loves hot potatoes, especially damaged ones).
Potatoes should be stored at a temperature of plus 2 − 3 degrees, explains Acting Director General of the Scientific and Practical Center of the NAS for Potato and Horticulture Vadim Makhanko. - Because of the warm weather, which we observed in autumn and winter, potatoes began to germinate in storage, as a result - weight loss.
It is not always economically feasible to include refrigerators, and not all storage facilities are equipped with them.
That is, part of the crop was lost during the storage stage.
The lack of moisture now on the potatoes does not affect, explains the specialist. - We planted potatoes, it develops, until the moment when it germinates and grows above 10-15 cm, it feeds from the mother tuber.
But in late June - early July (depending on the variety), the root receives nutrients from the soil, and the dependence on precipitation increases.
Bet on early varieties is not a way out of the situation, Vadim Makhanko believes. - Potatoes ripened at the end of July and what to do with it?
Firstly, it is impossible to dig potatoes at a temperature above 18 degrees, it is injured, watery rot begins, we will not be able to cool and preserve it.
In addition, Belarusians do not like watery potatoes, with a low starch content, and early varieties are mainly such.
The way out of the situation is to work hard to create heat and dry resistant varieties of potatoes.
Without potatoes, we will not remain, despite climate change.
Ukraine both produced and produced potatoes.
Africa has produced and produced.
We, Belarusians, love potatoes very much and will develop the culture further.
Last year, almost 700 tons of watermelons were harvested in Belarus This year for the first time the temperature in winter was positive, the soil did not freeze, this allowed farmers to partially conduct field work, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food said.
At the same time, dry conditions are noted for two or more months during the period of active vegetation of plants.
In the Gomel region, the recurrence of droughts with an area of coverage of at least 30% occurs every two years, in the Brest region - every two or three years.
One way to overcome the problem is to introduce drought-tolerant forage crops that are able to withstand extreme conditions.
This is not only the well-known corn and millet, but also chumiza and paisa.
Corn is grown in all regions of Belarus, including grain, it occupies about 21% of the area of ​ ​ crops, while the creation of 1 ton of dry matter consumes less moisture than oats and barley.
Corn effectively uses the precipitation of the second half of summer.
Plants are able to accumulate a large organic mass even in arid areas.
The yield of corn is almost twice that of spikes.
Belarus provides 70% of itself with corn seeds, this allows saving about $30 million annually.
One of the positive aspects of climate change is that Belarus began to grow vegetables, fruits and berries that were not typical for our country before.
Now in the open field on an industrial basis grow onions, asparagus beans, sugar corn, watermelons, melons.
Under melons, mainly watermelons, about 40-50 hectares are allotted.
Last year, almost 700 tons were collected in Belarus.
Watermelons are grown in all regions, with the exception of Vitebsk and Mogilev.
And in the Brest region, walnut plantations were laid on an area of 22 hectares.

title: In the fight against the virus, we forgot about floods, droughts and plastic pollution
text:
Our lives have changed dramatically in the last few weeks.
The inhabitants of the Earth are united by a common misfortune and anxiety for their health - perhaps never before has humanity mobilized so quickly in the face of danger and uncertainty.
But why can ’ t we also come together and join forces to save our planet from impending floods, droughts and plastic pollution?
After all, during the pandemic, the climate crisis has not gone away.
Psychologist Daria Suchilina from the project “Pure Cognitions ” tells how you can take care of the planet while we are quarantined and trying to occupy ourselves with something.
Against the backdrop of the coronavirus pandemic, the topic of the climate crisis somehow suddenly disappeared from the headlines.
Only viral photo reports of swans and dolphins returning to the canals of Venice during the quarantine remained – and they turned out to be fake.
It seems that the disease is perceived as a more understandable threat to life and health, so about the super-fast melting of glaciers and widespread natural disasters all seem to have decided not to think temporarily.
Antarctica and the Arctic lose billions of tons of ice each year, and already now the coastlines of many continents are swallowed by the expanding ocean.
Squally winds and downpours are becoming the new climate norm around the world, forest fires are threatening life on entire continents.
In August 2019, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change warned that global warming would deal an unprecedented blow to the world ’ s food resources.
Obviously, the climate crisis affects not only the environment, but also the economy, politics, food, lifestyle, health of the inhabitants of the Earth – and not only physical, but also mental.
Sharp climate change is causing jumps in suicide statistics, not to mention depression, anxiety and post-traumatic disorders in people affected by natural disasters.
Even those who have not yet personally faced the consequences of the climate crisis are already experiencing what threatens us.
New terms are emerging for the disorders of our time: climate anxiety and climate despair.
And this is another similarity between the climatic and epidemiological crises: experts expect a sharp increase in the number of anxiety disorders and depression provoked by isolation and uncertainty about the timing of the pandemic.
People with a history of mental illness and vulnerable populations are at greatest risk: stressors like losing a job or educating children at home due to a pandemic can cause a relapse.
However, we have yet to find out exactly how the current situation of self-isolation, the collapse of many enterprises, complete uncertainty and constantly fueled anxiety for their health and the lives of loved ones will affect the mental health of mankind.
Psychologists and scientists of the world have already begun to actively study the reaction of people to what is happening.
The international community calls for interdisciplinary research on this topic, but any predictions are premature.
I want to believe that there should be a spoonful of honey in this hopeless tar - for example, that the suffering of people can somehow help the planet to get out of the garbage into which we turned it.
But as much as we would like to see a ray of hope (for example, China ’ s carbon emissions fell by a quarter because consumption and industrial production fell during the pandemic), the state of the climate will not change with people sitting at home for several months.
Moreover, scientists expect that this temporary respite for our atmosphere could turn into a new wave of pollution if governments do not take active measures to transition to a green economy.
In the same China, factories have resumed work, and emissions are gradually returning to “pre-viral ”.
What do coronavirus and climate crisis have in common?
Victims of both climate change and pandemics are the most vulnerable members of society - people with low incomes, living in disadvantaged areas, without access to quality medicine, suffering from chronic diseases and age-related complications, without sufficient social support.
Both the virus and natural disasters reveal the true heroes of our time: rescuers, scientists, doctors, selfless neighbors, firefighters, who in the most difficult moment show miracles of kindness and courage.
At the same time, at the beginning of the pandemic, we managed to see the lowly features of humanity: greed, forcing us to buy much more goods than we really need, cowardice, fraud.
Tricks around the world are already finding ways to cash in on fears and social unrest.
In addition, both the pandemic and the climate crisis threaten the global economy with multibillion-dollar losses, so the authorities to the last refused to recognize the degree of threat, hoping to do with easy measures.
Finally, any natural disasters, epidemics and crises remind us how much the life to which we are accustomed depends on stability – on scheduled flights and trains, on the regular change of seasons and harvests, on the uninterrupted supply of food.
It seems that the loss of this certainty is giving rise not only to anxiety, but also to grief: what if the era of predictability has come to an end?
While protecting ourselves from the virus, we have forgotten about the planet. There is also a significant difference between a pandemic and climate change.
Coughing, fever and death statistics make us react quickly, and the invisible carbon dioxide molecules in the atmosphere and the complex numbers of climatologists seem something abstract and ephemeral — which means you can think about it sometime later.
And if the frightening exponent of infection and mortality around the world teaches us how to wash our hands properly and causes us to isolate ourselves for many weeks, then even the heartbreaking headlines about the extinction of a million species due to humans seem to many only the insanity of the “green ” and do not affect our behavior.
Could the World Health Organization ’ s prediction that malaria, diarrhoea, famine and droughts will claim 250,000 lives a year in the coming decades be more convincing?
It is as if we secretly agree to pretend that nothing happens to the planet.
Denial of fear, behavioral paralysis, ignoring the climate crisis and the paradoxical inaction of world leaders in the field of environmental initiatives – this is the real problem, and psychological.
“Psychological responses to climate change, such as avoidance of conflict, fatalism, fear, helplessness, detachment, ” says psychology professor Susan Clayton, one of the authors of the American Psychological Association ’ s manual on dealing with the psychological consequences of the climate crisis.
The climate crisis is a human problem.
We influence the well-being of the planet by our behavior: greed, fear, short-sightedness, unawareness.
In order to counter the inaction of people and protect those who will suffer from it, the heads of most of the world ’ s psychological communities signed an agreement in November 2019 to combat the consequences of the climate crisis (although there was no Russian association at this congress).
Psychologists of the world face an important mission – to organize assistance to victims, especially in vulnerable regions.
Information on how the climate crisis is affecting people ’ s mental health will be added to the training programmes.
But the most urgent task is to change the behavior of the inhabitants of the Earth.
Addressing the climate crisis requires a systematic approach: introducing new technologies and energy sources, changing urban landscapes and industries, restoring forests and eliminating carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere.
But an important part of the struggle for life on the planet is also our daily habits.
In this sense, the example of the coronavirus epidemic gives hope that people can change: elbow greetings, videoconferencing parties, remote picnics – all this has become expected and encouraged in a matter of weeks.
The dramatic changes brought about by the epidemic have shown how flexible and adaptive we are.
So maybe the same changes are possible in the field of separate garbage collection, rational consumption and energy?
The main challenge is to consolidate the effect of sudden changes and make new habits sustainable.
Environmentalists believe that the pandemic caused not only a reduction in emissions, but also difficulties in implementing long-term projects in the field of environmentally friendly production and green technologies, so now it is necessary to lower expectations about global solutions.
The more important it becomes to change our daily habits – this is the art of small steps.
How to change your behavior for the sake of what is important To fight for life on Earth is a great value for many.
People embarking on the path of sustainable lifestyles may never see the end point at which danger will finally be forgotten, and children will see extinct species not only in the pages of old textbooks.
Yet the value of struggle and hope is high enough to help us move forward even in a situation of uncertainty and powerlessness.
This explains the psychological model that underlies Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT).
People are able to commit themselves to doing what is important by recognizing and accepting even the most difficult and painful of their experiences.
It is on this principle that the process of psychotherapy is built in this approach: specialists help clients learn to be in touch with the present moment, unravel thoughts, accept their experiences and observe them in order to do something concrete for the sake of the chosen values.
Psychotherapists help clients analyze why they need avoidant behavior and what its consequences will be.
For example, if a person tries not to think about the climate crisis in order to avoid anxiety and guilt, then he will continue to buy disposable plastic and throw garbage out.
Will it reduce anxiety and guilt over how it affects the environment?
Right now, maybe just because the person will turn a blind eye to it.
In the long run, the effect will be the opposite, because the impact will be increasingly detrimental.
This is the paradoxical effect of avoidance.
Sometimes it takes time in the process of psychotherapy to realize the consequences of their habits and treat them with understanding and curiosity instead of self-criticism.
When a person understands why he avoids the unpleasant truth, he should ask himself: what can be done instead?
The client, accompanied by the therapist, begins to look for an alternative and formulates specific actions.
Ask yourself: What am I willing to do to make my behavior meaningful, to be the person I really want to be?
What can my anxiety motivate me – for example, in the field of ecology?
What could I do if I decided to face my fear and admit that the climate crisis is not a fiction?
What can you do right now?
It could be neighbors sharing your ideas about separate garbage collection, or a group of social media activists, or an international community of minimalists practicing reasonable consumption.
Join charity events in support of environmental organizations or a training group for the creation of environmental initiatives.
Contact with people makes our fear bearable and gives us hope of overcoming it together.
Examples of projects that can be adopted: waste disposal "People together - garbage separately!" and "Separate collection"; waste minimization - Zero Waste; personal eco-activism; the project "Give a tree".
Personal stories sound much more convincing than dry statistics and have a stronger impact on social norms.
Talk about what you are doing right now, such as what reasonable consumption and separate collection looks like in self-isolation mode.
Even if stories about the climate crisis make you sad and anxious for the future, it ’ s still the only way to stay honest and make informed decisions.
It is important to be aware, because from this the problems become concrete and no longer so frightening.
The monster under the bed is scary only when we don't look at it.
If we learn more about the challenges, it turns out that we can cope with them.
Eat more plant-based food The environmental impact of meat production has been the subject of many books and films.
Of course, vegetarianism has its pros and cons.
But even if you give up meat once a week, it will be your contribution to saving water on the planet.
4 R: Refuse Reduce (reduce) Reuse (reuse) Recycle (recycle) Refuse excesses that you do not need, especially disposable items such as coffee cups and plastic bags.
If possible, buy less – say, toys or clothes.
Re-use everything that can be repaired, give things a second life: even during quarantine, you can figure out what to make of torn jeans, or find video tutorials on repairing furniture and simple mechanisms on the Internet.
You can prepare things for swaps - parties for the exchange of clothes, cosmetics, books and much more.
During isolation, it is unlikely that you will exchange personally, but after quarantine, you will have something to share.
And only if all this is not possible, it makes sense to use the recycling of separate garbage, which can still be carried in blue state containers.
By the way, the service of paid contactless removal of separate garbage "Ecomobile" from the "Collector" continues to work even during quarantine.
Unfortunately, if you buy thoughtlessly everything and then hand over for processing, this will not solve systemic problems.
Analyze your household, reduce your electricity consumption; turn off water while soaping your head with shampoo; use the dishwasher to save water; dismantle the closet - perhaps you will find things that can be given to charity; install a food waste shredder in the kitchen so as not to throw leftovers of food into the common trash bin; store only “dry ” garbage that is more likely to be recycled or use again; pay attention to product labels to buy only recyclable packaging - for example, glass, aluminum or plastic labeled" 1 "instead of a mixture of plastics, tetrapack or plastic" 7 ", from which no one will be able to do anything new.
Our life has long turned into an unpredictable experiment.
We are all frozen in anticipation: what will be our life after the epidemic?
And it is largely up to us what awaits us when the panic over the coronavirus subsides: the rage of a depleted planet — or a combined effort to care for our large common home.

title: Turkey opens borders for foreign tourists
text:
At first, only medical tourism will be available in several areas, including oncology, orthopedics, traumatology, pediatric surgery and some others.
According to the Association of Tour Operators of Russia (ATOR), the Turkish authorities decided to open the borders for foreign tourists.

title: The failure of the “deal of the century ”: Palestine broke with Israel and the United States
text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announced the termination of all agreements and agreements with Israel and the United States.
The reason for this step was Israel ’ s intention to take control of the disputed territories.
“The Palestine Liberation Organization and the State of Palestine are exempted from today all agreements and arrangements with the governments of the United States and Israel and from all obligations based on these agreements and agreements, including in the field of security, ” Abbas said at an emergency meeting of the Palestinian leadership.
The Palestine Liberation Organization voted to end cooperation with Israel and the United States back in 2018 and gave Abbas the opportunity to do so.
The President has repeatedly threatened to stop cooperation, however, it is not clear how exactly his statement will affect the interaction of the parties, especially in the field of security.
Israeli media reported that Palestinian security officials were ordered to stop communicating with their Israeli counterparts.
The problem, however, is that they must coordinate with Israeli security officials even to move between areas in the West Bank.
In addition, Abbas a few weeks ago already appealed to Russian President Vladimir Putin with a request to organize a conference in Moscow on the settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict, TASS reports, citing Palestinian Ambassador to Russia Abdel Hafiz Nofal.
“This conference should create a new mechanism for negotiations between the Israelis and the Palestinians to end the confrontation on the basis of a two-state solution, ” he said.
The Palestinian concern is based on the “deal of the century ” that US President Donald Trump proposed in January 2020 to settle disputes between the parties.
The territorial conflict between Palestine and Israel has been going on since 1967.
International mediators have repeatedly tried to resolve the confrontation, but this has not led to any result.
Donald Trump, however, believed he could find a solution.
The development of the “deal of the century ” by the US presidential administration lasted almost three years.
Its main architect is Jared Kushner, the adviser and son-in-law of the head of the White House.
On January 28, the American leader presented his plan.
He proposed to recognize Jerusalem as the inseparable capital of Israel, but to allow Palestine to build its capital in the eastern part of the city.
At the same time, the Arab state and the entire world community should recognize Israel ’ s sovereignty over the West Bank of the Jordan River, follows from the deal.
Palestine was not satisfied with such a situation and there were no hopes that the leadership of the country would agree to the surrender of Jerusalem.
East Jerusalem, which the Palestinians consider the capital of their state, was occupied by Israel in 1967.
Since then, the world community has considered this territory occupied.
There are no embassies in Jerusalem.
The UN Security Council, the UN General Assembly and many other international bodies have repeatedly demanded that Israel end its occupation.
In December 2017, Donald Trump recognized Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and moved the US embassy there, which caused outrage from Palestine.
This fact, Mahmoud Abbas also recalled and referred to him when announcing his decision.
“The US administration recognized Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and moved its embassy there, it published the ‘ deal of the century ’ that laid the groundwork for the Israeli annexation declaration, ” he said.
Abbas said that Palestine holds the US authorities responsible for the “oppression of the Palestinian people ” and considers Washington the main ally of the“ Israeli occupation government in all its aggressive and unjust decisions and measures. ”
The United States is indeed Israel ’ s partner and fully supports it.
The recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of the country, the transfer of the American Embassy and the “deal of the century ” itself were vivid proof of this.
Donald Trump gave details of his plan in the presence of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
This document, among other things, is the basis of agreements on the creation of a coalition between Netanyahu ’ s Likud party and Benny Gantz ’ s Kahol Lavan bloc.
Netanyahu approved Trump ’ s plan, which, on the one hand, was a breakthrough — Israel rejected all the proposals put forward to resolve the conflict.
On the other hand, the “deal of the century ” is focused on protecting Israel ’ s interests.
At the same time, the head of the White House does not believe that his plan is unfair.
Palestine, according to Trump, will double its territory if it agrees to the US proposal.
So, as compensation for the loss of territory in the West Bank, the head of the White House proposed to allocate to the Arab state two zones in the Negev desert south of Gaza.
However, the deserts separated from the rest of the country cannot be called fair compensation for the loss of land.
In addition, the President of the United States considers it expedient to establish Palestinian control over the Gaza Strip.
To do this, Trump proposes to conduct a tunnel or trestle through Israeli lands.
This will give the Arab country access to the sea, but it will be possible to build a port there only five years after the conclusion of the agreement and, importantly, only with the permission of Israel.
Under the proposed plan, Washington is ready to allocate $50 billion.
Palestine must be demilitarized and Hamas completely disarmed.
In exchange, Israel must agree to freeze new Jewish settlement activity for a period of four years.
That is how much time is devoted to the negotiation process on the formation of Palestinian statehood.
Mahmoud Abbas called Trump ’ s “deal of the century ” a“ slap in the face ”, a wave of protests against the US administration swept through the country, and on February 2, Palestine broke off relations with both the United States and Israel.
The fact that the Israeli government of Binyamin Netanyahu and Beni Gantz is committed to annexing the West Bank has caused Abbas even more indignation, which prompted him to break all agreements and arrangements with Israel and the United States.
The Palestinian leader pointed out that, under international law, “the occupying Power has a responsibility to protect the civilian population under occupation, its property, criminalizes collective punishment, prohibits the theft of resources, the appropriation and annexation of land, prohibits the forcible transfer to the population of the occupied territory, and prohibits the transfer of colonialists to the occupied land. ”
Now Israel is indeed showing a willingness to annex, and the fact is that it may simply no longer have a chance to implement its plans.
He enjoys the full support of the United States, respectively, he can not only be prevented from annexing the West Bank, but also help with this.
This is what the US ambassador to Israel, David Friedman, has called for.
And, according to Israeli TV channel 13, Israel ’ s ambassador to the United States Ron Dermer also called for annexation in the near future.
Israel ’ s fears are related to the fact that in November the US will hold presidential elections, on the outcome of which depends, among other things, Washington ’ s support for the annexation of Palestinian territories.
“We have to push for annexation now because we don ’ t know what ’ s going to happen in the U.S. presidential election.
[Democratic candidate Joe] Biden can win, ” Dermer told the Guardian during talks in Washington. “There is a window of opportunity now, so it must be done now. ”
Although Biden is very loyal to Israel, he expressed his disagreement with the Trump plan back in January.
"The peace plan requires the consent of both sides.
This is a political ploy that can lead to unilateral measures to annex territories and further harm the prospect of peace, ” said the former vice president.
Palestine is now waiting for the support of the international community.
Abbas called on other states to prevent Israel from annexing, and also not to recognize the “deal of the century. ”
The President of Palestine also noted that the State was ready to ratify all accessions to international agreements and conventions and reaffirmed its desire to resolve the conflict with Israel, provided that negotiations were conducted under international auspices and under international legitimacy.
"We will continue to prosecute crimes against our people in all international bodies and courts," Abbas said in a statement.

title: Netanyahu will be able to start the process of annexing Israeli settlements from July. The United States should not change its mind.
text:
The Israeli government may begin discussions on the annexation of territories in the West Bank as early as July.
In response, the Palestinian authorities are threatening to withdraw from all treaties and agreements — but this is not the first such threat in recent years.
The fate of the territories is part of a complex geopolitical equation: Israeli politicians openly say that they will annex only if Washington recognizes their decision.
Jordan and other Arab allies of the United States have officially spoken out against and may use their influence to prevent the United States from unequivocally siding with Israel.
The outcome may also be influenced by the US presidential election: Israeli diplomats fear that their plans may be disrupted in the event of the defeat of Donald Trump and the victory of Joe Biden, who does not support the annexation.
The United Nations, the European Union, Russia and all Arab countries oppose Israel ’ s unilateral actions.
Why Israel decided to annex the West Bank was occupied by Israel as a result of the 1967 Six-Day War.
Since then, there has been an active establishment of Jewish settlements on its territory - now more than 400,000 Jews live in 140 settlements.
The UN Security Council considers these settlements illegal, but Israel disputes this definition.
The Arab population of the territory exceeds 2 million people.
Putting the annexation of the West Bank for discussion in the government and parliament is part of a coalition government deal struck between Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz.
The government was approved on Sunday, after a year and a half of political crisis and three elections.
The essence of the proposal is to declare part of the occupied territories a permanent part of Israel.
However, this is written with the proviso that the plans will be implemented only with the support of the United States.
Official Washington has not yet clearly expressed its position.
US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo visited Israel last week and met with Netanyahu.
He once again called on the Palestinian leadership to agree to the peace plan proposed by Trump.
Meanwhile, the American edition of Axios learned that the Israeli Ambassador to the United States Ron Dermer in communication with officials of the Trump administration, members of Congress and conservative publicists explained that Israel should begin the annexation now, before the presidential election in November.
The ambassador fears that the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden could disrupt plans.
On Tuesday, Biden publicly expressed his position for the first time — he said that he does not support the annexation and considers it a threat to a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
And on Thursday, 18 Democratic senators — including Elizabeth Warren, who is considered a potential Democratic vice presidential candidate (paired with Biden) — wrote to Netanyahu and Gantz against plans for unilateral annexation.
Netanyahu ’ s determination is due in part to a plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict developed by US President Jared Kushner ’ s son-in-law.
The plan calls for recognition of Israeli sovereignty over parts of the West Bank and the creation of a Palestinian state on 70% of the remaining West Bank territories, as well as in the Gaza Strip, with a capital on the outskirts of East Jerusalem (Israel annexed East Jerusalem in 1980 and proclaimed the entire city its "eternal and indivisible capital"; most countries of the world did not recognize this, but the Trump administration agreed in 2018).
The Trump administration has previously taken unprecedented steps in support of Netanyahu, recognizing the annexation of the Golan Heights and moving its embassy to Jerusalem.
One of Trump ’ s key support groups is evangelical Christians who advocate Israel ’ s full sovereignty over these territories.
The unprecedented threat of the Palestinian leader, the Palestinian leadership rejected Trump ’ s proposal, and in response to statements about Israeli annexation, the leader of the Palestinian Authority (PA), Mahmoud Abbas, announced the withdrawal of all agreements with Israel and the United States, including security treaties.
Abbas called on other countries to impose sanctions on Israel if Netanyahu moves to annex.
"From now on, the Israeli occupation authorities must bear all responsibility and all obligations to the international community as an occupying country," Abbas said.
Abbas had previously threatened to withdraw from the treaties, but did not take this step until the end.
On Thursday, the PA Prime Minister met with the autonomy ’ s security forces to discuss withdrawing from the agreements with Israel.
But experts say it is difficult to imagine a complete break in relations - Israel controls all entrances to the territory where the Abbas government is based.
Coordination with the Israeli forces is necessary even for simple movement within the autonomy.
King Abdullah II of Jordan, a key US ally in the region and the leader of one of the two Arab countries that signed a peace treaty with Israel, spoke out strongly against the annexation.
What threatens the collapse of the Palestinian Authority?
There will be more chaos and extremism in the region.
If Israel does annex the West Bank in July, it will lead to a large-scale conflict with the Jordanian Hashemite Queen, ” the monarch said in an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel.
Jordan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates — key U.S. allies in the Middle East — have expressed concern to the White House and the State Department over plans for annexation.
The UN special envoy to the Middle East, Nikolai Mladenov, called on Israel to renounce the annexation.
EU Foreign Affairs Representative Josep Borrell has spoken out against any unilateral action in the West Bank.
He said the EU would use all its diplomatic resources to prevent annexation and ensure respect for international law.
Russia also does not support annexation and adheres to the UN resolutions on the establishment of a Palestinian state within the 1967 borders.
Iran ’ s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Friday called on Palestinians to continue fighting Israel and likened the Israeli government to a malignant tumor in the region.
The struggle for the liberation of Palestine is an Islamic jihad obligatory for believers, Khamenei said.
This is Iran ’ s usual rhetoric about Israel.

title: NASA uses new Senator armored vehicles to support historic mission to ISS
text:
NASA uses new Senator armored vehicles to support the historic mission to the ISS NASA uses new Senator armored vehicles to support the historic mission to the ISS NASA uses new Senator armored vehicles to support the historic mission to the ISS NASA uses new Senator armored vehicles to support the historic mission to the ISS Close Send On Wednesday (May 27) astronauts will take off from American soil for the first time since 2011, using a SpaceX capsule.
It will be a historic test flight to the International Space Station.
NASA astronauts have not launched from the United States since the end of the space shuttle program in 2011, instead relying on Russian rockets as commercial companies like SpaceX and Boeing developed their vehicles.
NASA during the SpaceX Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission will use the newly ordered light armored Senator vehicles to protect astronauts Bob Benken and Colonel Doug Hurley, on a short trip from the Kennedy Space Center where they will dress, and straight to the launch pad.
The Senator is a unique car in terms of technical characteristics, design and assembly.
It is developed by Roshel Defense Solutions, which specializes in the design, development and production of a wide range of armored personnel carriers.
The Roshel Senator is a flagship model specifically designed for military, law enforcement, peacekeeping and civilian applications.
The Hubble Space Telescope turned 30 years old: NASA showed a new photo The company said that the body of the car was specially designed to use modern heat and noise insulation materials, providing an uncompromising level of comfort for its inhabitants.
The car is fully equipped for comfortable use in harsh conditions.
The perimeter of the armour of the passenger compartment and the engine compartment of the Senator is designed to provide the level of ballistic protection CEN B7.
The floor is equipped with explosion protection for the safety of passengers in the event of a simultaneous explosion of 2 DM-51 hand grenades or equivalent light anti-personnel mines.
In addition to standard security features such as perimeter armor, emergency hatches, advanced locks, external surveillance cameras, siren / speaker system, emergency lighting, Roshel equips its vehicles with advanced protective solutions to enhance the vehicle ’ s ability to carry out its mission in a safe and effective way.
Among the available security solutions are remote weapon systems, towers, escape hatches, video surveillance equipment, night vision systems, fire source detection systems, chemical protection devices and others.

title: The launch of the ship Crew Dragon – NASA flight: date, all that is known
text:
Already this week, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the ISS as part of the Demo-2 test mission.
The launch will mark the return of the United States to manned flights, which ended with the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.
How the mission will take place and why it is important, we tell in our material.
Channel 24 closely followed the process of preparation for the manned launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.
We decided to collect all the details and interesting points in one article so that you could get acquainted with the key stages of the mission.
Do not miss the US returning to the ISS: SpaceX and NASA have revealed the details of the historic mission What is happening The United States of America is returning to manned flights to the ISS using its own ships.
Already this week, on May 27, the first ever manned launch of a spacecraft to the ISS, carried out by a private company SpaceX, will take place.
Crew Dragon will have two American astronauts on board.
After launch, the ship docks with the International Space Station at an altitude of 400 kilometers above the surface of the planet.
The astronauts will get to the station, where they will continue their mission, the duration of which is not yet known and will depend on a number of factors, both during the launch and during the flight of the ship until the moment of docking with the ISS.
Despite the fact that the flight is manned, and the mission of astronauts will take a lot of time on the ISS, it is still a test, so it is called Demo-2.
Previously, SpaceX has already tested the ship Crew Dragon, but this time the company will do it for the first time as part of a crewed mission.
The broadcast of the flight will take place on Techno 24.
So visit our website on May 27 at 23: 15.
The start is scheduled for 23: 30 in Kiev.
In addition, the broadcast will be available here: NASA TV: YouTube; SpaceX: YouTube link to the broadcast will be available before launch.
The fact is that the manned launch of Demo-2 will be the first such launch from American soil in almost a decade.
The last manned spacecraft to perform such a mission was the Space Shuttle Atlantis, which landed on July 21, 2011 as part of the STS-135 mission.
After that, the shuttles to the ISS no longer flew, and NASA was forced to buy seats for its astronauts on the Russian Soyuz, which cost the United States a considerable amount.
It is worth paying attention to the fact that after the American shuttles stopped flying, Russia constantly raised the price of seats for American astronauts and other partners on board the Soyuz spacecraft.
As of today, one seat on the Soyuz costs NASA $90 million (in 2010 it cost about $30 million).
The Alpha Centauri portal notes that given the approximate prices of Russian state launch contracts, it turns out that NASA pays the entire ship and the full cost of launching as part of the mission, paying only for one of its astronauts.
According to the report of NASA OIG on the audit of the manned flight program / The Alpha Centauri Here are more interesting facts about the ISS: how to create a research bastion of humanity in space Commercial Crew Program A year before the last flight of the shuttle, NASA initiated the launch of the manned flight program.
Even then, the search for a replacement for space shuttles began, the launches of which were quite expensive for the state.
Then came the idea, which at that time was revolutionary and even strange: the delivery of astronauts to the ISS should be engaged in private space companies.
NASA in this scenario took over the control of the design and preparation for the launch and the payment of seats for astronauts.
Space Shuttle Atlantis 30 minutes after landing in the last flight of the program Finally, in 2014, two companies were selected that will continue to prepare and present manned ships that will be able to carry out the mission.
These companies are Boeing and SpaceX.
As for the first company, the launch of the Boeing Starliner was unsuccessful, despite the fact that the ship landed successfully.
The company was unable to ensure the docking of the ship with the ISS due to a number of errors.
Now Boeing is engaged in fixing all the problems and preparing for a new test launch, but for their money.
Boeing Starliner, after landing SpaceX in March 2020, successfully launched Crew Dragon, which has passed a number of tests and landed proving its ability to ensure the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.
After additional tests and final preparations, the ship was prepared for an important event - a manned launch, which will take place on May 27, 2020.
Crew Crew Dragon To the ISS will go two NASA astronauts: Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Doug" Gurley.
Both of them were test pilots and together in 2000 got to NASA as part of the 18th selection of astronauts.
Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Dag" Gurley / NASA As for Robert Benken, during his time at NASA, he took part in two missions of the shuttle Endeavour: STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010).
As part of these missions, Benken had three spacewalks.
Astronaut Robert Benken During the Demo-2 flight, Robert Benken will take command of the flight stages that will be coordinated by the mission control center.
Douglas Gurley also participated in two missions of the shuttle Endevour on missions STS-127 (2009) and STS-135 (2011).
In both missions, Gurley was a shuttle pilot, and STS-135 was the last mission to complete the space shuttle program.
During the Demo-2 flight, Douglas Hurley will be the commander of the ship and responsible for all procedures related to the launch and landing of the Crew Dragon spacecraft.
As already noted, the launch of the Crew Dragon is scheduled for May 27.
It is worth noting that the mission can still be postponed.
The reasons for this may be, as detected at the last moment technical problems or the weather, which should be favorable not only at the launch site, but also throughout the flight path of the Falcon 9 rocket.
Because in these places must pass the splashdown of the crew, if something went wrong at the time of launch or flight.
The ship Crew Dragon / SpaceX Now it is known that if the launch does not take place on May 27, then it can be postponed both on May 30 and on May 31.
If everything goes according to plan and the ship successfully enters orbit, it will spend about 19 hours there.
This is necessary for additional tests and maneuvers as part of the test – Crew Dragon can get to the ISS much faster.
In orbit, the astronauts will check the operation of all systems, switch to manual control, perform several maneuvers and eventually experience how comfortable Crew Dragon is for sleeping.
Docking with the IDA-2 node of the Harmony module on the ISS is scheduled for May 28 at about 15: 39 UTC (18: 39 Kyiv time).
Before that, the astronauts will approach the ISS and conduct several maneuvers near the station.
It is worth noting that the entire docking process with the ISS will take place automatically.
Astronauts will observe the process and will be able to intercept control in case of an emergency.
After the crew of Crew Dragon will get to the station, he will meet with members of the 63rd expedition - Chris Cassidy, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.
As noted at the beginning of the material, the duration of stay of astronauts on the ISS is still unknown.
It will finally be determined during the flight, taking into account the state of the Crew Dragon ship and the readiness of the next Crew Dragon capsule, which is already designed for flight as part of the first full-fledged mission.
Let me remind you that despite the manned flight, this is still a test flight.
In addition, NASA expects to keep Demo-2 in orbit for as long as possible.
It is necessary for that.
after returning to finish the certification of the ship and begin preparations for the next mission.
In general, Demo-2 has every chance to stay in orbit for up to 120 days.
Rehearsal of the launch of Demo-2 / SpaceX Here it is worth noting that this limitation is due to the peculiarity of the design of the Crew Dragon.
In particular, it is said about solar panels, which gradually deteriorate during their stay in orbit due to the concentration of atomic oxygen.
The next Crew Dragon ships already have a protective coating of silicon dioxide, which will allow them to stay in orbit for all 210 days.
Whatever it was, and after the expiration of their stay on the ISS, the astronauts will return to the ship, undock and land in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean near the coast of Florida.
There the crew of the ship and the capsule itself will pick up the ship SpaceX Navigator.
Try Which of you astronaut: SpaceX released a docking simulator with the ISS Interesting details NASA returns the old Falcon 9 rocket with the Crew Dragon ship already on the launch table.
You can see that in addition to the usual NASA logo on the rocket and the old logo, which was used from 1972 to 1992 and is associated with the space shuttle program.
The old NASA logo is located on the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket / Photo SpaceX The decision to return the old logo was made by the head of NASA Jim Brandenstein.
Astronauts love various rituals, and they have a number of their own peculiar superstitions.
One of the interesting artifacts was a very special American flag, which has been on the ISS for almost a decade.
The flag is a symbol of the American Space Shuttle and Space Exploration Program / NASA that was on board the Columbia shuttle during its first flight under the program in 1981 and the last flight to the ISS in 2011.
The flag was left on the ISS with the condition that it can only be taken by the crew, which started from the Kennedy Flight Center.
