title: Residents of Gomel won in the struggle for the preservation of the square near the “Tourist ”
text:
Residents of Gomel won the fight for the preservation of the park near the "Tourist" 2 27.05.2020, 11: 34 1,123 How did this become possible?
Perhaps the epic with the protection of the green area on Kozhara Street from commercial development is coming to an end, writes gomel.today.
Schemes and trees Recently, an initiative group of residents protesting against the demolition of the square received a response from the enterprise "BelNIIPgradostroitelya", which developed a scheme for landscaping Gomel.
It says that the park at the Tourist Hotel is included in the scheme of landscaped areas with an area of 2.67 hectares.
If we translate this from a dry bureaucratic language, it means that the residents of Kozhar have completely managed to defend their recreation area from the sealing building.
The history of the issue is this.
Once there was a military and then a civilian airfield.
After its construction in the 60s, a square was formed on the corner of Sovetskaya and Kozhara streets.
Most of the trees were planted by the residents themselves.
Here used to walk moms with wheelchairs, in the winter children rode on sledges from low slides.
And in September 2017, it became known that the trees are going to be cut down, and in their place to build a “town house ” with parking lots and shopping facilities.
This decision of the city authorities caused a flurry of indignation.
A meeting of residents was held on Kozhara Street, speakers said that they would lie under bulldozers.
An initiative group was established and the collection of signatures for an appeal to the authorities began.
The protest of residents was supported by the Belarusian Green Party and the Nash Dom public initiative.
Residents protested, the authorities did not yield.
But after Lukashenka ’ s speech, in which he criticized the actions of local administrations to demolish trees and said that “the media write from Gomel to Minsk ”, the construction project at“ Tourist ” was immediately frozen.
Is it possible to say that “the stars converged happily ”?
In fact, this reaction was a response to a strong public outcry and numerous protests of citizens in Minsk, Gomel and other cities.
However, the situation remained suspended.
Square the territory of the "Tourist" was not recognized and was still subject to construction.
A long positional struggle began for the official recognition of this territory as a square.
Some officials also took the side of the population.
Activists of the initiative group, students and some enterprises planted new seedlings here.
Just at this time, "BelNIIPgradostroitelstvo" began in Gomel drawing up a scheme of landscaping.
His specialists came to our city and held a mass meeting with the residents.
However, the scale fluctuated for a long time.
Moreover, the authorities all the time confirmed that part of the square will still be built.
What made it possible to solve the problem in favor of residents and trees?
Can this really be considered a final victory?
One of the coordinators of the movement in defense of the square Svetlana Goldade says: - The final point will be only the approval of the scheme of green areas of common use of all districts of the city by the Gomel City Executive Committee.
Public discussions on the environmental assessment of the scheme should also be held prior to this.
Therefore, until I would not use such a high term as “victory ”.
But the fact that the developer of "BelNIIPgradostroitelstvo", at the request of the Gomel City Executive Committee, introduced the entire territory of public use near the hotel "Tourist" in the scheme of landscaping is certainly a good result.
After all, this is what the townspeople have been fighting for since the autumn of 2017.
And this result was achieved thanks to the care, perseverance and confidence of the defenders of the square, as well as the support of Gomel residents living in other areas.
People of different professions, positions and ages spoke against the compaction, there is not enough space to list all the participants of the initiative.
Thank you so much to everyone!
Together, we are strength.
The green city is something that has always distinguished Gomel, and we have always been proud of it.
We are all responsible for what we leave to the next generations.
According to the ex-mayor of Gomel Svetlana Goldade, landscaping and landscaping of the territory was engaged not only by local residents.
But also students and teachers of the University named after Skorina, its rector and deputy of the Gomel regional council Sergey Khakhomov, deputy of the city Council, director of JSC "8 March" Sergey Komkov, other deputies and the administration of the Central district of the city, the head of the Gomel city inspectorate of natural resources and environmental protection Alexander Golubev, the enterprise "Red Carnation".
A significant part of the new plantings was made at the expense of voluntary donations from residents of houses located near the square.
The interviewer says, “And another interesting point. ”
Employees and students of the Faculty of Biology of the GSU made a valuation of the ecosystem at the Tourist Hotel.
This is the absorption of carbon dioxide, and the protective properties of trees and shrubs to absorb dust and pollutants from the air.
So, green spaces in our square provide "environmental services" to the population of the city in the amount of 340 - 350 thousand rubles per year.
And this is not counting oxygen production and recreational functions.
We have been heard, and it gives us hope.
But without the media to include a large number of citizens in the struggle for the preservation of the square would be much more difficult.
If I remember correctly, the first material about the civil initiative to protect the square appeared in “Strong News ” in early September 2017.
It was an information breakthrough.
The Green Portal also reported about us, and other media.
The plot of the program "Vremechko" about the confrontation around the square was aired on September 28.
On October 3, 2017, at a working meeting, Lukashenka expressed his own attitude to the issues of unjustified logging and sealing construction.
The city of Gomel was also mentioned.
His comments on the subject, as they say, diverged into citations.
After that, there were many more people who wanted to write about our situation, including in the state media.
Residents of the microdistrict believe that after passing all the remaining procedures, the square will be completely “legalized ” and will forever remain the property of the Gomel residents.

title: Dragon, heir to Atlantis. SpaceX is sending a man into space
text:
On May 27, shortly before midnight Moscow time, an extremely important event for world cosmonautics, and especially for the American one, should occur.
For the first time in almost 9 years, astronauts will go into space on an American spacecraft from a spaceport located in the United States.
For the first time in history, a person will fly on space technology created by the company of entrepreneur Elon Musk.
At 23 hours 33 minutes Moscow time, the launch of the SpaceX Demo-2 mission is scheduled: the place of departure is the launch complex LC-39A of the Kennedy Space Center, Florida, the place of arrival is the International Space Station.
Long-term crews have been working on the ISS since the end of 2000, the very first of them went to the station on the Russian ship Soyuz-TM-31, but returned to Earth already on the American manned spacecraft program Space Shuttle.
The next few crews to the ISS and back were carried by space shuttles, so it was supposed to happen with the sixth long-term crew, but due to the disaster of Columbia on February 1, 2003, flights under the Space Shuttle program were suspended, and the participants of the expedition had to be returned by the Russian rescue ship Soyuz TMA-1.
Until July 2006, Russian ships were responsible for crew rotation.
After the return of the American shuttles to flight and until the closure of the Space Shuttle program, the American ships rotated one of the crew members, and after the last flight under the shuttle program, which was performed by the shuttle Atlantis in July 2011, the United States stopped manned flights into space for a long time.
Now manned flights are returning to the arsenal of American cosmonautics – thanks to the company SpaceX Elon Musk.
The Crew Dragon spacecraft will be operated by a crew of two astronauts: Douglas Hurley is the ship ’ s commander, and Robert Benken is tasked with interacting with the ISS.
Each of them twice visited space as part of the crews of space shuttles, and Hurley flew to the ISS on the very last flight of Atlantis.
Benken and Hurley will spend 30 to 119 days on the ISS, more precisely the duration of the expedition will be determined later.
The Demo-2 mission will be the final test of SpaceX ’ s technology, and if it is successful, Crew Dragon ’ s flights to the ISS will become regular.
Soon after the launch of the Falcon 9 launch vehicle, its first stage will separate – it will make a soft landing on the floating platform developed by SpaceX called Of course I still love you.
The spacecraft will be placed in the right orbit, and about 19 hours later, after making several turns around the Earth, will approach the International Space Station.
Docking should take place in automatic mode – this is a standard docking scheme for Russian manned Soyuz and cargo Progress, but previous SpaceX development ships docked with the station using the Canadarm2 manipulator arm installed on it.
It is the first 10-15 minutes of the flight and its final phase that will be most interesting to observe in real time on the NASA website, they are also the most risky stages of the first part of the mission.
Crew Dragon should return to Earth in less than a month.
Although the ship is designed so that it is able to independently carry out a soft landing with the help of eight special SuperDraco engines, and almost with helicopter accuracy, this time the ship is driven by parachutes.
Moreover, although the ship is designed as a reusable, under the agreement with NASA, it will not be reused to send people – but can be used to deliver goods to the ISS.
Cosmonautics journalist Mikhail Kotov explains that NASA thus cares about the safety of astronauts: “This is NASA ’ s money, and NASA can afford it, and it shows that for this organization safety is in the foreground, it is not ready to save on manned flights, so they will use a new ship every time. ”
In addition, Kotov recalls that it was a problem with one of the SuperDraco engines that led to the accident during the ground test of Crew Dragon in April 2019.
Crew Dragon will have to return to Earth “the old way ”, but Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken will literally experience another advanced development of SpaceX – rescue suits of a completely new type.
They are created for each astronaut individually to his size, put on through a single zipper located at the bottom, from the ankle to the ankle, and helmets are printed from plastic on a 3D printer.
But the main feature is the design, which was invented by the author of superhero costumes from Hollywood blockbusters.
“The spacesuits were made by Hollywood designer Jose Fernandez, a specialist in superhero films, who participated in the Avengers, ” says Kotov. – Elon Musk gave him an order to draw a spacesuit that would be such a heroic appearance.
And only then under the guise of this spacesuit specialists worked on its technical part.
Usually in astronautics they do the opposite – the technical part is important, but either they will think about the design later, or they will not think at all. ”
Some experts already doubt that the "heroic" spacesuits will be convenient to use: they do not have hinged joints, which are very useful if the spacesuit inflates during emergency depressurization, and plastic helmets probably limit the rotation and tilt of the head.
With putting on a new suit can not cope alone – and it is unlikely that this is compensated by the ability of his gloves to work with touch keys.
However, Mikhail Kotov believes that it will be possible to judge the convenience of SpaceX spacesuits only after the first flight, and Elon Musk ’ s attention to design and marketing (astronauts will be delivered today to the launch pad in a snow-white Tesla Model X with NASA logos) is a justifiable approach.
“Space needs to be ‘ sold ’, especially in the modern world, ” the expert said.
NASA ’ s program to support the creation of a private spacecraft to deliver astronauts to the ISS was opened even before the shuttle flights ended.
However, in total, it took almost 10 years to create a replacement for the manned space shuttle.
Mikhail Kotov names two main reasons for this period: first, the designers immediately focused on the creation of a new generation of devices – reusable.
Secondly, it took a lot of time for mandatory checks to pass NASA certification - especially strict where human lives directly depend on the reliable operation of technology.
Two companies entered the final of the competition announced by NASA – SpaceX and Boeing.
In 2014, the aerospace agency signed contracts with both manufacturers, and with Boeing - for an amount of one and a half times more than with SpaceX.
The rivalry for the right to become the first American manufacturer to send a man into space after a long break came out tense, and Elon Musk had every chance to give it up.
Mikhail Kotov notes that the advantage of SpaceX was a consistent approach: unlike Boeing, the company built a manned spacecraft based on the already tested cargo version.
In March 2019, SpaceX successfully carried out the Demo-1 mission: the Crew Dragon spacecraft went to the ISS, however, instead of the crew on board there was a mannequin in a spacesuit, named after the heroine of Ridley Scott ’ s fantastic film “Alien ” Ellen Ripley.
But just a month later, during the next ground tests of the SpaceX spacecraft, an explosion occurred.
The accident slowed down the preparation of Crew Dragon for a manned flight, and in November 2019, the Boeing Starliner spacecraft went to the ISS with a mannequin on board.
The mission failed.
“It was Boeing that was considered to be the leaders of the race before, many assumed that they would have time to make their ship much faster than SpaceX, ” says Mikhail Kotov. – But first Boeing was delayed with certification, with inspections, and then, when it seemed that the device was almost ready, its first flight did not go according to plan.
The ship was saved, but it did not complete the flight mission, did not fly to the International Space Station, did not dock with it.
At least three very serious software errors have been identified, work is underway to eliminate them, at least one more fully successful test launch will be needed, and during this time Musk already flies several times, will receive money for it and, accordingly, will strengthen his reputation with NASA as a quality carrier. "
However, the expert is sure that the Starliner project will not be closed - the development of the ship will be completed and it will remain as a backup option, taking over part of the flights to the ISS.
For almost a decade, Russia ’ s Roscosmos maintained a monopoly on bringing people to the ISS, and now, if the Demo-2 mission succeeds, it will lose it again.
Mikhail Kotov says that, according to some calculations, the delivery of an astronaut to the station on Crew Dragon will be cheaper than on the Russian Soyuz - taking into account the "comfortable margin", which is now being laid by Roscosmos, taking advantage of its position.
However, for both sides – Russian and American – the question of price is unlikely to be decisive, each will prefer to use its own ship, although exchanges of places, as was customary during the Space Shuttle, are likely to occur.
“Now NASA has invested in SpaceX ships, and this is a matter of strategic security, they will not back down.
Roscosmos had nine fat years, getting extra money for transporting astronauts to the ISS, this is big enough for Roscosmos money, now it will become more difficult, ” says Kotov.
Russia ’ s new manned spacecraft, the Eagle (formerly called the Federation), has been under development for about as long as U.S. projects, but is still far from making its first spaceflight.
Its first orbital test was planned to be held in 2017, then in 2021, then the period shifted by another year, now the first launch is expected to be carried out in 2023.
"Initially, it was made based on the skin of special carbon fiber, - says Kotov. - There are no such technologies in Russia, they intended to order the skin in Europe.
But 2014 came, sanctions came, now there is no possibility to make a carbon fiber plating, so the ship began to be counted on a metal hull, almost to do from scratch. "
It is still unknown even from which cosmodrome and with which carrier rocket the Eagle will fly - initially it was about the Vostochny cosmodrome and the Angara A5P rocket, then about Baikonur and the Soyuz-5 rocket, now again about the Vostochny and Angara.
“The news comes from one, from the other, from the third.
But for quite a long time there is a single scheme that it will start at the "Angara" and this will be done from the second stage of construction of the East, when the site for the start of the "Angara" will be built.
Unfortunately, such a change of vector, a change of ideas, the lack of a clear strategic scheme – this is inherent in Roscosmos, ” the expert believes.
Astronauts Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken went through a two-week quarantine and passed tests for coronavirus infection.
Because of the epidemic, for the first time in history, hundreds of spectators will not be watching their launch at the Kennedy Space Center - there will be only specialists related to the mission, several journalists and American President Donald Trump.

title: SpaceX sends astronauts into space for the first time: online broadcast
text:
Photo: the ship Crew Dragon (nasa.gov / Joel Kowsky) The ship Crew Dragon carries out the first manned flight to the ISS SpaceX Elon Musk for the first time sends astronauts into space.
Today at 23: 33 Kyiv time, the Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the International Space Station from Cape Canaveral on the coast of the US state of Florida.
Everything you need to know about this event, as well as the online broadcast of the missile launch - in the material RBC-Ukraine.
According to the official website of NASA, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket will go into space from the launch complex 39A in Florida.
According to Kiev time, the launch will take place at 23: 33.
Due to the coronavirus pandemic and related quarantine restrictions, the launch of the rocket can be viewed exclusively online.
Only a few reporters will be present at the George Kennedy Space Center, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and possibly US President Donald Trump.
On the ISS today will go two experienced astronauts - Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken.
They were among the first cosmonauts to start working on SpaceX ’ s next-generation spacecraft.
On account of Benken's two space missions, Hurley also made two flights on the space shuttle.
In the SpaceX Demo-2 mission to the ISS, Douglas Hurley is appointed commander of the ship and will be responsible for the launch and landing processes, as well as for the autonomous flight section.
Robert Benken is the commander of joint operations with the ISS.
It will monitor the approach of Crew Dragon to the space station, automatic docking and undocking.
Since May 13, Hurley and Benken have been quarantined and tested for coronavirus as a precaution.
Today, astronauts will arrive on the launch pad in a white Tesla Model X.
Photo: astroanauts Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken (NASA / Kim Shiflett) The flight will last about a day, and on May 28, Crew Dragon will approach the docking adapter on the Harmony module in the American segment of the ISS.
There, the astronauts will join the main ISS-63 expedition - commander Christopher Cassidy (USA) and Russian flight engineers Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.
Astronauts will assess the readiness of the new spacecraft SpaceX Crew Dragon to deliver people into orbit.
In addition, they will check the functionality of the new automatic docking system (cargo Dragon docked with the ISS in manual mode with the help of a manipulator).
Hurley and Benken can stay from 30 to 119 days on the ISS.
NASA will decide on the duration of the mission after docking.
The crew will perform daily tests of all onboard systems of the ship and participate in joint tasks with other members of the expedition.
As part of the mission, Robert Benken will go into outer space and, together with Christopher Cassidy, will install new rechargeable lithium-ion batteries outside the station.
After the work is completed, Benken and Hurley will pick up the returned cargo and the Crew Dragon will automatically undock from the ISS.
Astronauts must parachute in the Atlantic Ocean near Florida.
Crew Dragon can be used multiple times for space missions.
However, under the contract with NASA, it will deliver people to the ISS only once, and in the future will carry out the transportation of goods.
The launch of Crew Dragon is a landmark in the history of modern astronautics.
For the first time since 2011, American astronauts will go to the ISS not on the Russian Soyuz, but on the ship of a private company developed jointly with NASA.
For SpaceX, this flight will be the first with a crew on board.
Previously, Elon Musk ’ s spacecraft were unmanned and carried out only cargo delivery missions.
Today ’ s Crew Dragon launch is the final step before NASA certifies SpaceX ’ s spacecraft to perform long-term missions on the space station.
If the spacecraft successfully completes all the tasks, the Roscosmos corporation could lose contracts with the US space agency, which brought it $4 billion over 9 years.

title: Foundation: Osman – Season 1
text:
The plot of the series "Foundation: Osman" Season 1 The series "Foundation: Osman" Season 1 tells the story of the brave young man Osman the First, who after the death of Ertuğrul took the reins of the Turkish lands.
The young man has great things to do.
Through courage, intelligence and determination, he will bring glory to his people.
During his reign, part of Byzantium will be annexed, he will accept Muslims who broke away from the Mongols, guarantees the country a long-awaited access to the Black and Marmara seas.

title: Go to a new class
text:
One of the most important points for business class real estate and above is the favorable environment.
Unfortunately, the urban environment is heterogeneous, and there are practically no ideal sites from the point of view of the environment.
The improvement of adjacent territories can partly solve the problem of the status of the object.
High competition in the Moscow and St. Petersburg markets encourages developers to take a comprehensive approach to the formation of the LCD environment and design it not just as an addition to houses, but as centers of attraction.
Nikolai Lavrov, vice president of ARIN Group, head of the housing program "Moving to St. Petersburg", says that today in St. Petersburg - a city on the water - the most common example of bringing the environment to the class of the project is the creation of a pier for yachts and the arrangement of a marina, but for this, of course, there must be natural conditions: a river or a lake.
“One way or another, it is important that the“ chips ” are then maintained in the proper form, ” he points out.
Mr. Lavrov also believes that it can be useful and interesting for both developers and residents of the city to create a recreational zone at some distance from expensive housing, a kind of center of attraction for the rich public.
“For example, the opening of a thematic gallery of boutiques, combined with a club for wealthy people, ” suggests Mr. Lavrov.
Nadezhda Zotova, marketing and advertising director of the construction and investment holding Aquilon Invest, also believes that one of the new trends in the market is the creation of a multifunctional public space on the territory of the residential complex.
“In Europe, residential complexes often have premises for shared use – gyms, common kitchen-bars for holidays.
I hope that this experience will be developed in Russia as well.
Even now, among the residential complexes of the high price segment, there are houses with a common cinema hall, according to the American model. ”
Sergey Tkachenko, expert of real estate agency Century 21 Capital Petersburg, says that currently the trend for environmental friendliness and domestication of the environment is intensifying.
This implies the creation of a comfortable environment for rest, development and work of a person, a high degree of landscaping, the presence of everything necessary for life at hand.
“Many developers are increasingly using the landscape design of the inner and adjacent territory, the improvement of embankments and adjacent territories (for example, the residential complex“ House on the Embankment ” from the GC “Northern City ”), the creation of parks, squares, boulevards, artificial reservoirs, canals, ” the expert lists.
Olga Smolenskaya, the head of the project association "Unicum", says that today equipped walking and park areas appear even before the houses themselves to attract buyers.
“To create a comfortable and attractive environment for residents, the first thing that a developer often does is create a stylobate on which a pedestrian area is located, free of vehicles.
The second thing that allows you to increase the level of comfort and class of housing is a landscape park with unique lighting, sculptural compositions, children ’ s and sports areas.
This is a separate architectural and design project, and the name of the architect plays an important role here.
And the third key point is the preservation and improvement of nearby natural objects.
A nearby natural park or pond always adds points to the residential complex.
Residents of modern cities need reboot places where they can stay in silence and enjoy the preserved nature.
There are many examples of such projects both abroad and in Russia.
All modern residential complexes, starting from the comfort class level, are created based on these three principles, ” says Ms. Smolenskaya.
Michael Belton, president of WAinbridge, is confident that the developer can create a comfortable space for life.
“The environment can include both social infrastructure facilities – schools, kindergartens and polyclinics, household and service services, supermarkets, and recreation areas – parks, embankments, sports and playgrounds.
These components are especially important for isolated residential complexes located at a distance from areas with functioning infrastructure, ” the expert says.
Landscaping and landscape design create conditions for a comfortable life and are able to level the errors of the urban environment, as well as strengthen the natural features of the location.
Anton Krivov, founder and CEO of the landscape-construction company Primula, talking about the improvement of the adjacent territory, notes: “Usually the building is designed for a certain class, and the landscape design is developed later as an addition.
The class of housing is determined by the level of comfort and aesthetics.
Infrastructure should be as developed as possible, but at the same time not interfere with residents.
For example, it is better to fence off the playground with densely planted bushes or thuja.
The general impression is provided by trifles: space without thresholds, high-quality finishing materials, landscaping. ”
Mr. Krivov believes that if the landscape around the building is unpleasant, then competent landscape architecture will be able to draw attention to itself.
Vasily Kostin, CEO of "KBK" Project "", with a colleague does not quite agree, he insists that the magnificent view from the window no longer guarantees that the housing will become a class higher.
“The protected house area, where well-equipped children ’ s and sports grounds are located, the availability of equipped recreation areas for residents, with landscaping and individual design, are now mandatory parameters of the comfort class, ” Mr. Kostin emphasizes.
If we talk about the cost of such improvements, then, as a rule, the costs for these purposes are relatively small - from 2 to 5% of the total construction costs.
“These costs do not increase the cost per square meter for the buyer, but can significantly increase interest in the project, ” explains Mr. Kostin.
He says that the main requirements of the customer for the improvement of the general territory of the LCD at the design stage are (in descending order): the presence of garages and parking places; landscape design with thematic zoning; the presence of children's and sports grounds; fenced area with full coverage of lighting and video surveillance.
The head of the department for working with civil initiatives of the residential complex "Dream" Andrei Khokhlushin also believes that it is sometimes impossible to limit yourself to one improvement.
"Parks, ponds and fountains on the territory of the LCD - a thing, of course, necessary.
But one of the main criteria that buyers are guided by when choosing housing is its transport accessibility and especially the possibility of direct communication with Moscow.
Therefore, our developer went to improve the quality of housing by creating its own transport company.
Our project "Dream Auto" was created specifically in order to provide communication between the residents of the village and the nearest cities and Moscow. "
However, he admits that his own transport company is not a cheap pleasure.
The cost of performing scheduled flights in accordance with all the requirements of residents (regularity, clarity in the schedule, insurance against cancellation) is quite high.
“And the price of the ticket does not cover all the costs of such a small transport company.
Monthly subsidies to the transport company are calculated in six-figure amounts.
There is a possibility of their reduction by increasing the park, but for the developer this is not always an obvious move, ” notes Mr. Khokhlushin.
Anastasia Faley, a leading analyst at Prian.ru, recalls: “The costs of maintaining general infrastructure are usually distributed among residents, each of whom pays a certain rate per square meter of his apartment per month.
Therefore, the "rich stuffing" is justified only in large-scale projects, small complexes for several dozen apartments or townhouses try to do with a minimum set ".

title: SpaceX for the first time launched astronauts on the spacecraft Crew Dragon
text:
Elon Musk ’ s company SpaceX successfully launched the Crew Dragon spacecraft with two astronauts of the US space agency NASA on board.
This is the first manned launch of SpaceX in history, as well as the first such launch made by a private company.
Crew Dragon launched from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral (Florida, USA).
It will take two astronauts — Bob Benken and Doug Hurley — to the International Space Station.
SpaceX successfully landed the spent first stage on the floating drone platform Of Course I Still Love You in the Atlantic Ocean.
Soon after, the ship successfully undocked from the second stage.
Initially, the device will be in an intermediate orbit, and then begin to adjust it to later reach the ISS, reports N + 1.
Automatic docking of the device to the station will be held on Sunday, May 31 at 19: 29 Tashkent time.
Falcon 9 booster has landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship! pic.twitter.com / 96Nd3vsrT2 — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) May 30, 2020 The current launch is the first since 2011 manned flight carried out from the United States on an American spacecraft.
NASA stopped manned flights in 2011 after completing the Space Shuttle program.
Since then, astronauts have been delivered to the ISS by Russian Soyuz.
The flight is broadcast on YouTube.

title: SpaceX spacecraft on the second attempt went to a manned flight to the ISS
text:
The SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft on the second attempt went from the Canaveral Sea in Florida in a manned flight to the International Space Station.
As on Thursday, today, May 30, NASA doubted the possibility of launching a rocket.
After launch, the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket successfully returned to Earth and landed on a platform in the Atlantic Ocean.
The US Air Force gave 50% to the fact that the launch will still take place today.
In the event of a repeated failure of the launch, Crew Dragon would try to send into space tomorrow, May 31, and June 2 and 3.
Last time Crew Dragon was canceled 16 minutes before launch.
Then it was supposed to take place at 23: 33 in Kiev.
Crew Dragon is launched into orbit by a Falcon 9 launch vehicle.
The first demonstration unmanned launch took place on March 2, 2019.
As part of the Demo-2 mission, two NASA astronauts, Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley, went to the ISS.
Last week, they said they would spend one to three months on the station (according to NASA rules, the maximum stay in space is 110 days).
Crew Dragon / Screenshot To fly to the ISS Benken and Hurley must 19 hours.
They will have to return to Earth on the same Crew Dragon: when the ship passes through the Earth's atmosphere, it will release parachutes and land in the Atlantic Ocean.
The launch of the SpaceX spacecraft is important because since 2011, the United States has not sent its astronauts into space from its own land: NASA astronauts had to go to Russia and fly into space on the Soyuz.
One place on a Russian spacecraft cost NASA as much as $86 million.
The United States had to cooperate with Russia due to the fact that two American reusable spacecraft - Challenger and Columbia - exploded along with the crew, and in 2011, during the launch of the Discovery shuttle, several pieces of thermal insulation foam again broke off from the ship.
This time, the Americans decided to go to the private sector and turned to the company of entrepreneur Elon Musk – SpaceX.
As previously reported Focus: SpaceX released a simulator docking spacecraft with the ISS.
The simulator will allow everyone to try to dock the capsule with the crew to the ISS.

title: Manned launch of SpaceX took place: Russia will lose orders?
text:
The SpaceX Falcon 9 launch vehicle with the Crew Dragon spacecraft launched from Cape Canaveral.
The Demo-2 mission will bring astronauts Bob Benken and Doug Hurley to the ISS.
This is the first manned flight from the United States in nine years - a huge step for the country's space industry.
The ship will allow the Americans to refuse to fly on the Russian Soyuz, where for each seat pay up to $60 million.
Since 2011, American astronauts have been sent into space on Russian Soyuz spacecraft.
For nine years, NASA bought 70 seats on board Russian ships for a total of $3.9 billion.
In parallel, SpaceX and Boeing worked on their own projects.
In the spring of last year, the Crew Dragon shuttle has already shown what it is capable of.
In March, it successfully docked to the ISS with a cargo.
Today ’ s launch is the final test of crew delivery.
If successful, NASA will be able to give SpaceX its certificate.
The flight is unique twice: SpaceX sends people into space for the first time and for the first time in the last nine years, astronauts will be delivered to the ISS by an American shuttle.
Video: SpaceX Docking Crew Dragon with the ISS will pass only DATA, around TIME Moscow time.
This is a complex maneuver, which will be controlled by astronauts.
On board the station, Benken and Hurley will remain for 63 days, after which they will return to Earth with the help of the shuttle on which they arrived.
But to talk about a sharp refusal of NASA from the Russian “Soyuz ” is impossible.
The head of the US space agency, Jim Bridenstine, said in early May that he was in talks to buy one space in the Russian shuttle for an astronaut to launch in the fall of this year.
A complete lineup of Falcon 9 launch vehicles.
Executive Director for manned space programs of Roscosmos, cosmonaut Sergei Krikalev believes that the Americans will not abandon the use of “Unions ” after the successful launch of SpaceX.
Just now the ability to send astronauts to the ISS have Russia and the United States.
“We just have another reserve in the program.
After the test, we will use both — and they and us.
They could have refused at any moment — yesterday, the day before, a year ago, and five years ago.
But there is a certain expediency in the implementation of the program.
It was just us.
Now it will be distributed between us and SpaceX, ” he said “360 ”.
Sergei Krikalev explained that all this is a normal working process.
He stressed that we are not talking about financial losses here either.
According to him, we are talking about partnerships, when everyone tries to do their own.
If it does not work, then they come to help, which is compensated by money.
“There was a certain moment when our partners did it until they learned how to do it themselves.
It's not a loss.
We just had extra income there.
Now it will not be or there will be other earnings in another place, ” the astronaut said.
According to Sergey Krikalev, the Americans will use Soyuz in any case even after the successful launch of the SpaceX spacecraft, and NASA and Roscosmos will continue cooperation on the International Space Station program.
Return stages (from left to right: Orbcomm 2, JCSAT-14, SpaceX CRS-8).
At the same time, the head of the Institute of space policy Ivan Moiseev believes that NASA may well abandon the use of Russian missiles, if SpaceX flight is successful.
Moreover, in the last two years, the Americans began to reduce the crew of astronauts on the ISS.
“In May, the last contract for $90 million was signed – one chair for an American, and this may be the last time.
If something happens [with Crew Dragon], then the Americans will have to buy more, because they need to keep at least one person on the ISS, ” he said.
According to the expert, the Russian space industry received up to $400 million per year for the launches of American astronauts.
But what is important now is not economic losses, but the fact that Russia is slowly leaving the international space market, and this is a very promising and fast-growing area.
Ivan Moiseev explained that before the share of Russia accounted for up to 30% of the launches of space satellites.
Now this is lost, and the production has not received a single contract.
Only small and cheap satellites remain.
We took the first place in the delivery of crews to the ISS.
In addition to the Americans, Japanese and Canadians were brought into orbit under the US quota.
“We have to state that the Russian Federation is no longer participating in the international space market.
Now she must concentrate and think how to build her strategy based on her own needs, ” the expert concluded.
Source: RIA Novosti He noted that there were negotiations about the possibility of making two tourist flights.
But so far this has remained at the discussion stage.
There is also talk about the flight of an astronaut from the United Arab Emirates.
“It will give something to some extent, but compared to what was, it ’ s just tears, ” explained Ivan Moiseev.
In his opinion, the cooperation of Roscosmos and NASA around the ISS will continue in any case.
The station will not be able to exist if one of the parties refuses to support it.

title: Crew Dragon went to the ISS
text:
The Falcon 9 rocket with two NASA astronauts aboard the Crew Dragon spacecraft launched to the International Space Station, the launch is broadcast on the website of the company SpaceX.
NASA astronauts Bob Benken and Doug Hurley took off aboard Crew Dragon.
The ship is due to dock at the ISS on Sunday.
The date of return of astronauts to Earth has not yet been determined.

This is the first manned flight of the United States since 2011 and the first space flight of a private company with people on board.
The mission is critical to the future of human spaceflight and NASA ’ s strategy of partnering with private companies.

title: The launch of the SpaceX spacecraft with astronauts took place
text:
The Crew Dragon spacecraft with astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Benken on board went to the International Space Station.
For the first time in history, the launch was carried out by a private company - SpaceX Elon Musk.
At 15.22 local time (22.22 Kiev time) from the site LA-39 Space Center in Florida (USA) launched a rocket Falcon 9, which put into orbit the ship Crew Dragon with two astronauts on board.
The event is broadcast on YouTube by a private company SpaceX, which provides a launch under a contract with NASA.
Three minutes after the launch, the first stage of the launch vehicle separated, another six and a half minutes later, the stage landed on the platform Of Course I Still Love You in the Atlantic Ocean.
The second stage of the rocket separated from the ship in the normal mode, it should burn up in the Earth's atmosphere.
The joint mission of NASA and SpaceX Crew Demo-2 is attended by astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Benken.
In the afternoon of May 31, the spacecraft is scheduled to dock with the International Space Station.
For the first time in history, a manned space launch was carried out by a private enterprise - SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk.
Until now, only the government departments of the USSR (Russia), the United States and China have sent a person into space.
The launch was to take place on May 27 at 16.33 local time (23.33 Kiev time).
The decision to cancel was made 16 minutes before the start.
The reason was called unfavorable weather conditions on the flight path.
On May 30, the organizers gave no more than 50% that the weather will allow the launch.
With the launch of the Falcon 9, the United States resumes the manned flight program, interrupted in 2011 with the end of the shuttle program.
Since then, American astronauts have flown into space on Russian Soyuz rockets.
For the launch of each astronaut, NASA paid Roscosmos more than $80 million.
At the same time, a place on the SpaceX ship costs almost half as much as $55 million, according to Space.com.

title: The United States for the first time in nine years sent people to the ISS
text:
The Falcon 9 rocket with the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon with NASA astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley on board launched from the 39th launch complex of the John Fitzgerald Kennedy Space Center in Florida to the International Space Station (ISS), SpaceX reports.
Produced on May 30 at 22: 22 Moscow time, the launch to the ISS was the second for Crew Dragon and the first to pass with a crew on board.
The docking of Crew Dragon and the ISS should take place approximately 19 hours after the start.
The spacecraft will stay in Earth orbit for one to four months, depending on the state of the Crew Dragon solar panels, after which Benken and Hurley must return to Earth.
The main purpose of the Crew Dragon mission is to check the systems of the ship and the readiness of the crew to work with it.
Successful completion of the spacecraft mission will mean the loss of Roscosmos ’ monopoly in delivering people to the ISS, which existed since July 2011, when NASA made the last flight as part of the Space Shuttle program.
Initially, the launch, scheduled for May 27 at 23: 33 Moscow time, was postponed due to unsuitable weather conditions.
Materials on the topic 11: 04 — March 2, 2019 In May 2019, the ISS was first launched (without a crew) by the Starliner spacecraft of Boeing, which due to software problems could not reach the space station, but successfully returned to Earth.
The first (unmanned) test launch of SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon to the ISS took place in March of the same year.
In September 2014, American SpaceX and Boeing were named winners of the Commercial Crew Transportation Capability program, which involves the creation of manned spacecraft in the United States for flights to Earth orbit.
Since 2011, people on the ISS are delivered exclusively by Russian manned spacecraft of the Soyuz series.
The corresponding contract of NASA and Roscosmos, which involves the delivery of one astronaut to the ISS for $90 million, ends in October 2020.

title: Private ship Сrew Dragon went to the ISS with astronauts on board
text:
SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft with two astronauts on board flew to the International Space Station.
This is the first manned space flight from the United States in nine years.
It is called historical – for the first time astronauts to the ISS will be delivered by a private ship.
The ship took off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral at 21: 22 Paris time (15: 22 EST).
Crew Dragon is expected to deliver NASA astronauts Bob Benken and Doug Hurley to the ISS in less than 24 hours.
The flight time is expected to be approximately 19 hours.
According to the plan, Crew Dragon will dock with the ISS in automatic mode, however, as specified in SpaceX, if necessary, astronauts will be able to switch to manual control.
Earlier, the company presented an online simulator of docking with the ISS.
How long the astronauts will stay on the ISS is unknown.
The decision on the duration of the mission at NASA will be made after Crew Dragon docks to the space station.
Benken and Hurley can spend 30 to 119 days in orbit.
Crew Dragon is the first private spacecraft in history to take astronauts to the ISS.
Previously, the United States used for manned flights into orbit shuttles, but in 2011, the program was closed.
After that, the United States bought seats on Russian Soyuz ships for flights to the ISS.
Earlier, SpaceX, which is headed by entrepreneur Elon Musk, has already made flights to the ISS without people on board.
The Dragon spacecraft, on a modified version of which the astronauts flew, has been used to deliver cargo to the ISS since 2012.
For SpaceX, the successful launch of Crew Dragon is a step forward in the space race.
The only competitor of the company Mask Boeing, which also receives funding from NASA, at the end of 2019 was unable to dock its unmanned spacecraft Starliner.
The re-launch, which will take place without a crew, is planned to be held in the fall of 2020.
Tourists were asked not to come to Cape Canaveral because of COVID-19 As noted by the American media, the coronavirus epidemic seriously affected the launch of the ship.
Astronauts said goodbye to relatives, observing social distance, and refused physical contact with relatives.

title: The launch of Crew Dragon: private SpaceX returned the United States to manned space
text:
The carrier rocket Falcon 9 with the ship Crew Dragon, which for the first time were people, launched from Cape Canaveral at 22.22 MSK Saturday.
NASA astronauts Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken went on a test flight aboard Crew Dragon.
After a successful launch, NASA is in no hurry to celebrate the success, stressing that the test continues.
The arrival of the ship to the ISS and automatic docking with the station is scheduled for Sunday at 17.29 MSK.
Hurley and Benken will remain in orbit for about three months, and only their return to Earth will mark the successful end of the test flight.
"I will do anything to get them home," SpaceX owner Elon Musk said at a press conference after the launch when asked what he would say to the sons of astronauts who flew into space on his spaceship.
As told in NASA, during the flight to the ISS, which will last 19 hours, the astronauts will double check the operation of the ship in manual mode, but to dock with the ISS will be automatic.
In general, the newest Crew Dragon is the word of modern technology, all control goes through touch screens, it is learned to fly itself - without pilots.
“The most difficult thing for them will be to return to the automatic flight mode, they are the testers, ” said after the launch, the head of NASA astronauts Patrick Forrester.
Today we are gathered in this wonderful place not only to celebrate the launch of a new spacecraft, but also to celebrate a bold and triumphant return to the stars.
This is a special day, "Trump said, speaking in Florida shortly after the historic launch.
America lost the possibility of independent manned flights in 2011, when the last ship of the series “Space Shuttle ” retired.
One of the pilots of the last shuttle was NASA astronaut Douglas Hurley, today he led the crew of the test flight Crew Dragon.
Not only did this become symbolic in the resumption of the US manned program interrupted for nine years – the name of their ship astronauts Hurley and Benken gave also from the era of shuttles: the new Crew Dragon will go down in history under the name Endeavor, which can be translated as “ambitious undertaking ” or“ breakthrough ”.
This was the name of the shuttle, on which both astronauts flying to the ISS aboard Crew Dragon made their first space flight.
Because of the coronavirus pandemic, for the first time in the long history of the American comic program, ordinary Americans did not observe the launch of a rocket from Cape Canaveral.
Space tourism in Florida is very popular and an event like a manned stratum could have gathered hundreds of thousands of people, but prevented COVID-19.
Only a few VIP guests led by the president managed to see the launch firsthand, the rest enjoyed it thanks to television and Internet broadcasts.
According to the British Telegraph, the launch was watched by a total of 10 million people around the world.
"A lump in the throat and tears in the eyes," commented on his emotions during the start of the Stanford University professor Scott Hubbard.
The head of NASA, in turn, said that the launch was intended for every and every American and, like everything NASA does, unites a country gripped by riots on the basis of racial problems.
After the completion of the shuttle flight, the United States bought places for the delivery of astronauts to the ISS from Russia.
The last contract for one seat on the October Soyuz flight into orbit cost Washington more than $90 million.
According to reports, the flight on the American Crew Dragon will cost NASA about $55 million.
Past leaders have made the United States dependent on foreign powers to send our astronauts into orbit.
It won't happen again.
"We are once again proud to launch American astronauts on American rockets, the best in the world, and here on American soil," Trump said after the launch.
He stressed the importance of private business for the future of the US manned program.
“Today ’ s launch clearly shows that the future belongs to the commercial space industry, ” Trump added.
Previously, the leadership of NASA has repeatedly expressed interest in the commercialization of low Earth orbit and the space program in general.
To do this, even under President Barack Obama, contracts were signed with private companies SpaceX and Boeing to create manned spacecraft to deliver people into orbit.
NASA hopes to be "one of many customers" of private space carriers, although the question of who exactly will fly into space on private ships other than NASA itself and space agencies of other countries is still open.

title: A new step in astronautics: the historic flight of Crew Dragon took place
text:
On Saturday, May 30, to the International Space Station (ISS) went the spacecraft Crew Dragon company SpaceX, on board which are NASA astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Benken.
The launch occurred at 22: 22 MSK from the cosmodrome at Cape Canaveral.
Two stages of the Falcon 9 rocket, which delivered to orbit an American manned spacecraft, successfully separated.
The first reusable stage of the launch vehicle made an automatic successful landing on a floating platform in the Atlantic.
The ship of Elon Musk went into orbit of the Earth.
Now it is moving to the ISS, docking with the International Space Station should take place 19 hours after launch.
© Joel Kowsky Nasa, Globallookpress This launch was a new serious step in the history of world astronautics.

In 2011, NASA stopped manned flights after the completion of the program to use the return spacecraft Space Shuttle.
Since then, astronauts have been delivered to the ISS by Russian Soyuz.
As the head of SpaceX Elon Musk stressed at a briefing after the launch of Crew Dragon, this launch will resonate with all those who are in the heart of the researcher.

"This opens up new opportunities and reserves for the ISS program," he said.
As the head of NASA Jim Bridenstine said, the crew called their ship Endeavor (in translation - an ambitious undertaking, aspiration).
This tradition of naming spacecraft originated in the 60s of the 20th century - in the first manned program of the United States "Mercury".
Docking Crew Dragon with the ISS should begin on May 31 at 17: 29 MSK.

title: Elon Musk sent a man into space
text:

text:
On May 30, 2020, at 19: 22 GMT, the famous American space company SpaceX successfully launched a manned mission Demo-2.

title: Why 35 countries are building the world ’ s largest fusion reactor
text:
The 1985 meeting of the heads of the USA and the USSR gave the world one of the most ambitious technological projects: the experimental thermonuclear reactor ITER ("path").
In Provence, in the south of France, thousands of scientists and builders are preparing a complex for scientific experiments that can open the way for humanity to thermonuclear power plants of the future.
Thermonuclear fusion has long stirred minds.
In theory, such power plants can be four times more efficient than modern nuclear power plants, while much cleaner and safer.
They have no problems with uncontrolled chain reactions and highly radioactive waste, and the fuel can be sea water.
The multibillion-dollar project is being worked on by the EU (46% of spending), the US, Russia, India, China, South Korea and Japan (9% each).
If it does without further delays and problems with funding, ITER will work at the end of 2025 – forty years after the negotiations of Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev in Geneva.
Present Time tells about the history, present and future of a unique project in the field of thermonuclear fusion.
Thermonuclear energy tries to copy the processes that occur inside stars: there, at ultrahigh temperatures and pressures, the nuclei of hydrogen isotopes merge and release huge energy.
To achieve this on Earth, special conditions are needed (for example, the temperature is 10 times higher than in the core of the Sun) - they are created in a fusion reactor.
It is based, at least, on the most common scheme used by ITER - tokamak, in shape resembling a bagel vacuum chamber with magnetic coils.
The first tokamaks appeared in the USSR in the 1960s, the largest tokamak in the world with a volume of 830 m3 will be built for ITER.
In tokamak, deuterium and tritium are launched, and heated to temperatures over 150 million degrees Celsius.
The gas turns into plasma, and so that the plasma of this temperature does not burn everything around, it is kept at a distance from the walls by a magnetic field; a current is passed through the plasma itself.
A powerful magnetic field is provided, in turn, by superconducting magnets, which need to be cooled in a vacuum chamber to almost absolute zero - 268 ° C.
Physically, they will be literally half a meter from hot to 150 000 000 ° C plasma.
Ensuring the trouble-free operation of equipment in such conditions is a difficult engineering task.
Modern tokamaks emit less energy than is spent on heating the system, to generate them while it is not possible to adapt.
The best result is the British JET, which returns up to 67% of the energy spent.
Due to the scale of the ITER design (it will be a huge height of a nine-storey house, and about the same diameter), the creators expect that the reactor will be able to release energy ten times more than is spent on heating plasma (give 500 MW with 50 MW).
This moment is fundamental for the construction of thermonuclear power plants in the future.
But ITER will not produce electricity: all the allocated energy will be used only to heat the walls of the tokamak.
Although if the ITER experiments are successful, the next stage (from 2030) will be a prototype fusion reactor for power plants, DEMO – they should appear in the 2040-50s.
India, Russia, South Korea and Japan expressed their desire to build such reactors.
The most important goal of ITER is to show the possibility of generating energy by a fusion reactor.
To do this, it will be necessary to ensure the controlled production of "burning plasma" (with it the synthesis reaction will be self-sustaining) and to achieve the self-reproduction of tritium, a fairly rare isotope used as a fuel.
In addition, ITER should demonstrate how ready modern technologies are for the construction of commercial thermonuclear power plants, as well as assess their reliability and safety.
Safety is one of the key advantages of fusion reactors over conventional nuclear reactors.
Here, a chain reaction with consequences is impossible: in case of problems, the plasma will instantly cool and dampen, ITER notes.
Much better is the case with the radioactivity of the fuel: tritium, a weak source of beta radiation, will be generated right in the reactor.
The design of the reactor at the same time involves several barriers for radioactive substances arising in the process of operation.
The half-life of radioactive waste for most isotopes in a fusion reactor is about 10 years, while for individual components of spent nuclear fuel these values can be thousands or even millions of years.
In November 1985, at a meeting in Geneva, the leaders of the United States and the USSR agreed on a joint study of thermonuclear energy for peaceful purposes – this was the beginning of the project.
A year later it was Euroatom, the USSR, the United States and Japan signed the treaty.
Work on the design of ITER began in 1988 and continued until the approval of the final version in 2001.
In 2003, China and South Korea joined the consortium to work on ITER, and in 2005 – India.
At the same time, a site was chosen for construction: the vicinity of Saint-Paul-le-Durance in Provence, France, near the Cadarache nuclear energy research center.
The interstate agreement on the establishment of ITER was signed by the ministers of the participating countries on November 21, 2006, and in October 2007 the ITER Organization, the legal entity responsible for the construction, operation and subsequent dismantling of the reactor, began its work.
The site began to prepare in 2007, to build in 2010.
In parallel, the participating countries began to work on the elements of the ITER complex: India is building a cryostat for the project, the United States is developing a central magnetic coil (its strength is enough to lift an aircraft carrier), the EU and Korea are preparing a vacuum chamber, China and Russia supply superconductors (a total of 100,000 km of such conductors will be needed), part of the coils and various electrical components, Japan prepares toroidal field coils.
As of the end of June 2019, the project was ready “by more than 63% ”, ITER Organization noted.
More than 70% of the buildings have been completed and the first components of the reactor have been installed.
The full installation phase is due to begin next year as all the necessary components are built and delivered: for example, China built the first 400-ton magnetic coil on September 23, and it will be delivered to the ITER construction site by December.
In terms of complexity and manufacturability, ITER surpasses many large-scale scientific buildings of the century, including the Large Hadron Collider.
“The collider is just a vacuum installation in which the beam of protons accelerates, it is a task of a simpler level.
ITER is plasma physics, and plasma is so many degrees of freedom, so many instabilities, all of them must be dealt with, – told RFE / RL head of the Russian agency of the ITER project Anatoly Krasilnikov. – From the point of view of a large number of parameters that must be taken into account at the same time, ITER, of course, is a much more complex problem than the collider.
And ITER is more expensive. ”
Such a complex international project based on advanced technologies is really expensive.
If at the start the project budget was estimated at €5 billion, then by 2017 it had already crossed the mark of €20 billion: the total figure is difficult to estimate, since governments themselves determine the level of spending on certain components they produce.
The participants of the project do not transfer money, but transfer the built components.
In the Russian budget for ITER in 2020-22 laid 11.8 billion rubles (about $180 million).
Not only ITER Bublik-tokomak is not the only option for thermonuclear fusion considered by science.
Alternative methods are being studied not only in large public institutions, but also in small start-ups.
There are now more than two dozen of them in the world, according to Bloomberg estimates.
However, so far there are no major breakthroughs and controlled energy production on a commercial scale.
The closest analogue of the tokomak is a stellarator, also a toroidal, "bagel-like" system, for all its similarity does not require maintaining a current in the plasma.
Such an installation has its pros and cons, the largest and most successful at the moment is the German Wendelstein 7-X.
German researchers set a number of records on it, although it is far from ITER in terms of characteristics and scale.
The startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems, founded by immigrants from MIT, promises to build a much smaller, cheaper, and not much less efficient than ITER reactor on a tokomak – SPARC.
How can they do that?
Scientists hope to apply the latest high-temperature superconductors and are going to show solutions in the next two years.
Another non-standard option is thermonuclear fusion with inertial retention.
It uses lasers that "squeeze" and heat the miniature deuterium fuel capsule with pulses from all sides, simulating the processes that occur when a hydrogen bomb explodes.
The largest scientific organization in the world that uses this approach is the National Ignition Facility in the United States, where 193 beams of powerful lasers are used for this purpose.
Canadian General Fusion and American Tri Alpha Energy use their own, even more exotic methods of thermonuclear fusion, but alas, so far ready for commercial operation solutions have not been presented.
Why and when?
Critics believe that fusion is too expensive and commercially inefficient, and call for investment, for example, in renewable energy.
ITER does not deny its importance, but emphasizes that the creation of new clean energy sources with a constant level of generation (independent of, say, the number of sunny days or the strength of the wind) remains an important task.
Thermonuclear energy will not replace renewable energy, but will together with it serve as an even more successful alternative to traditional “dirty ” energy sources, ITER believes.
The only question is when it will happen.
The first launch is scheduled for December 2025 ("the best technically achievable date") using hydrogen, then helium, deuterium will be added and finally full work on deuterium-tritium is planned in 2035: only then will it be possible to achieve a tenfold return on power.
Completion dates have already shifted, and given the complexity of the project, we can hardly be sure that there will be no further delays.
In addition, despite all attempts, at the current stage of technology development, fusion may be too expensive for industrial applications.
Skeptics joke that "the thermo-poison is the source of energy of the future, and will always remain so."
In a few years, humanity will be able to cool the ardor of skeptics or again strengthen their positions.
Given the complexity of the topic, hardly anyone is ready to guarantee deadlines in such projects.
One of the pioneers of the industry, Soviet academician Lev Artsimovich, to the question of when fusion energy will appear, answered simply: "Then when it becomes really necessary for humanity."

title: Partner material. Soil moisture monitoring and crop forecasting using soil sensors
text:
The agriculture industry is already adapting to climate change.
Deficit of moisture, increased temperature in the summer, uneven distribution of precipitation during the season, insufficient precipitation for winter crops at the stage of germination or in the spring - these problems are familiar to almost every manufacturer.
Whether it is irrigated or rain-fed agriculture, winter or tilled crops, farmers face such questions as: - when and how to sow (date of sowing, depth of sowing); - how much and what fertilizers to apply, whether the volume of available moisture is sufficient for the assimilation of these fertilizers, whether it is reasonable to apply such volumes in terms of profitability; - what will be the yield potential on the basis of moisture available to plants; - the need to adjust the irrigation rates in irrigation areas, depending on the phases of crop development, to form a irrigation schedule.
Let ’ s look at the winters, for example.
Since autumn, producers need to determine the appropriate conditions for sowing, the optimal temperature and the presence of moisture at the depth of sowing.
Here, a common problem at the time of sowing is an insufficient amount of moisture.
At the time of the resumption of vegetation in the spring, when planning feeding, it is important to take into account the situation on each particular field and the state of
Knowing the weather forecast and humidity in the soil, you can understand how quickly the plant will assimilate the fertilizers introduced, as well as further determine the strategy of its fertilizing for winter crops.
Under the circumstances, based on these data, the manufacturer can see that the traditional mineral nutrition system is losing its effectiveness, and in relation to this field, a different approach is needed in this situation (whether it is a method of embedding, or even a change of product).
Further, counting on a certain yield, the agronomist makes the necessary amount of fertilizers for this crop.
At the time of spring feeding, it is very important to understand whether it is realistic to get such a crop, or the lack of moisture will reduce the yield.
If you see that there is not enough moisture in the meter layer and the planned yield is unattainable, then perhaps the best solution will be to adjust the cost of fertilizers and reduce the norm.
In addition, if tilled crops are cultivated and irrigation is used, then using soil sensors it is very useful to understand the state of the soil (moisture content), reasonably plan the irrigation schedule and analyze its effectiveness (effective water consumption per unit of product obtained).
So you can significantly save on watering and prevent overmoistening of the soil.
No one can change the weather.
But modern technology can mitigate the negative impact of weather conditions on the crop and preserve its potential.
Such solutions include the installation of soil moisture sensors and field weather stations.
This combination maximally adapts production to the conditions of the farm and gives the most accurate and reliable data.
Some may argue that there is data from open sources.
Of course, there are such data, but they are not reliable enough to rely on them in solving serious production issues.
If we talk about the weather from open sources, according to Farmers Edge, when you are 20 km away from the weather station, the accuracy of the weather forecast decreases by almost 48%.
Modern agriculture requires integrated solutions.
No manufacturer wants to waste time setting up and connecting equipment and then thinking about how to unload the data and what to do with it.
Farmers Edge offer is not separate components, but a ready-made digital solution consisting of hardware – data collection tools directly from the field (soil moisture sensors, field weather stations) and software – FarmCommandtm platform, where all data flows, where they are automatically processed and analyzed.
The soil moisture sensor is 1 m long, equipped with six temperature and humidity sensors on the horizons of 10, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 cm. When installing the soil sensor, Farmers Edge employees select the soil for the study of its particle size distribution. Fig.
2 Farmers Edge soil moisture sensor installed in the What data does the user see in the FarmCommand platform?
Data for the last seven days irrigation volume; rainfall; evaporation; water balance (you can see archival data on humidity for any day of interest since the sensor was installed); Current information on temperature and humidity for all six soil horizons; the lowest field moisture capacity; yield forecast for three scenarios: Dry year; Standard; Wet; Thus, you can always compare the difference between planned yield and forecast zom.
The accuracy of the forecast is very high due to the combination of accurate data on soil moisture and local weather data.
3 Data on soil moisture in the FarmCommand platform A lot of information is good, but the data should work in favor of the manufacturer.
Soil sensors transmit information every 15 minutes, so it is always relevant.
All collected humidity data is transferred to the FarmCommand platform and converted into clear graphs.
Looking at these graphs, you can immediately determine the state of each field, moisture content on each soil horizon, understand when it is necessary to conduct watering, and see the yield forecast.
How does the system understand this?
Soil sensors determine the lowest field moisture capacity of the total moisture capacity.
Let ’ s remember what these concepts mean.
Total moisture capacity is the maximum amount of water that the soil can hold, except for the pores occupied by air.
The lowest water capacity is the maximum amount of water that remains in the soil after the excess free water drains.
It depends on the granulometric composition of the soil, the content of humus, the structure.
The lowest moisture content shows the amount of moisture available to plants in the soil.
For most agricultural plants, the optimal level of soil moisture is 60-80% of the lowest field moisture capacity.
As a rule, it is time to water when overcoming the mark below 60%.
Graphs in the FarmCommand platform capture data from soil sensors and weather stations, show an increase in moisture capacity after precipitation or watering and a decrease in moisture reserves as plants grow.
Also, information on the moisture content in the soil is used to refine the modeling of the stages of development of the main crops, which is in the FarmCommand platform.
Farmers Edge ’ s FarmCommand platform links soil sensor data, weather data and field operations data into a single system.
This data is easy to view, convenient to work with and view reports on the state of moisture supply of the field, so that here, in the FarmCommand platform, you can assign irrigation, sowing or harvesting tasks to your employees.
What benefits does the producer get from such information? - understanding of optimal conditions of temperatures and humidity for sowing; - planning of other agrotechnical operations (processing, spraying, harvesting) in optimal conditions; - accurate information on soil moisture supply, planning of terms and volumes of irrigation, reduction of irrigation costs; - forecasting of stages of crop growth taking into account the natural and climatic conditions of a particular farm; - forecasting of risks of pests and diseases on the basis of accurate meteorological data; - access to the archive of soil monitoring data; - the ability to accurately calculate the yield potential for available moisture; - if necessary - adjustment of mineral nutrition standards, reduction of unreasonable costs for fertilizers; - tracking of nutrient blocking factors; - determination of the moment of onset of moisture deficiency; - formation of irrigation schedule.
Information is a valuable asset that will help the manufacturer effectively manage other valuable assets, such as time, labor, fertilizers, seed, and more.
Reliable information on the presence of moisture in the soil, local weather conditions, data from satellite images of fields make it possible to optimize production costs and choose the most suitable agricultural technology for the conditions of a particular farm.
