title: Politics in Space Breakthrough
text:
To a certain extent, a new space age has begun.
In some ways similar to the first steps of motorization in the first years of the last century.
The successful launch of the Crew Dragon spacecraft with astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley is not just a successful solution to a technical and technological problem, but a fundamentally new situation not only in astronautics, but also in economics and politics.
For starters, Crew Dragon is a third-generation ship.
It is significantly different from its predecessors, which could be seen by those who watched live at the start.
In it, almost everything is new, including the spacesuits of the crew members, the gloves of which allow, without removing them, to work on the computers of the onboard equipment.
The second most important aspect, the impact of which is now even difficult to assess.
Space flights cease to be a monopoly of the State, acquire commercial content and become the object of significant investment.
This will be followed by a synergistic effect.
New cosmonautics will require new materials, means of communication, computer equipment.
As a result, the global network of the Internet through satellites will become as everyday as today ’ s mobile communication, without which we can no longer imagine our lives.
This is not an exhaustive list of revolutionary changes in technology and technology.
It is important to note that the arrival of private investors fundamentally changes the direction of further development of near-space exploration.
From mining on the moon to the production of ultrapure materials in the vacuum of space.
In turn, this will significantly change the direction of human activity on the planet.
Much of what is now being mined and has negative environmental consequences will not be in demand and will be squeezed out by those obtained from near space.
Trump does not accidentally score moon pegs.
As they say, the trumpet calls.
The third most important factor is political.
It is worth considering in more detail, as it has both near and far consequences.
The United States ended the monopoly of Roscosmos on the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.
Over the past nine years, Americans have paid him about $4 billion.
In fact, all Russian flights were paid for from Washington, and now this is over.
From the technical factor discussed above, political consequences follow.
Now the Russian side is more interested in cooperation.
Its technology is fundamentally inferior to the American one, as it is a modernization of the Soviet one and is becoming more and more morally and materially obsolete.
For each flight, Roscosmos took $90 million, while the Crew Dragon flight cost $55 million.
Now the Russian budget will have to look for funds for its space.
Money is not small, besides, they must be found in a somewhat depleted state pocket.
Even if they are found, the effectiveness of their use is questionable in the light of previous experience.
Hence the important aspect.
Russia is actually out of the space race, giving way to the United States and China.
At the same time, the latter will also be in the role of catch-up and the distance with the position of Elon Musk and Boeing Corporation is still increasing.
From this point of view, the successful launch of Crew Dragon means a serious image blow to Russia.
After all, space and its achievements were one of the scraps used by Russian propaganda.
In particular, the American missiles are equipped with Russian engines.
From this it was concluded that the American industry is not able to produce such devices.
The reason, of course, was not that.
In the face of some reduction in funding for space programs, NASA decided to use cheaper Russian engines than to produce their own.
In addition, several years ago it was obvious that the time of the spacecraft of the second and even more so the first generation is coming to an end and to produce engines, the age of which will be very short, there was no sense.
As relations between Moscow and Washington cooled, efforts in the United States focused on abandoning the use of Russian engines and minimizing mutual cooperation.
It was impossible to do this quickly for a number of reasons, but the process was steadily gaining speed and now came to its logical conclusion.
This is a problem for Moscow not only technical and technological, but also political.
In fact, the last area of cooperation is being reset or significantly reduced, and Moscow remains with its backward space industry in proud solitude.
By the day of voting on amendments to the constitution with an unlimited period of Putin ’ s stay in power, it is impossible for citizens to imagine the real achievements of the regime.
Of course, the parade on June 24 in Moscow will be the apotheosis of victory, but the effect is absolutely zero.
Here is the cosmic defeat against the background of past bullying comments of Russian officials about the projects of Elon Musk looks quite formed.
In addition, from the American engineer and billionaire followed a response.
Recall the mocking comments of Dmitry Rogozin, the head of Roscosmos, that the Americans without Russian technology will launch ships into space on a trampoline.
Here ’ s Musk and wrote on SpaceX “trampoline ”.
Rogozin ’ s pitiful responses caused a barrage of caustic comments, which further increased the image losses of the Russian regime.
It is impossible to ignore the last invitation to Putin to come as a guest at the G7 summit in the fall.
It has no direct relation to the space launch of Crew Dragon, but it fits into the overall picture.
Russia is planned to be invited together with Australia, India and South Korea.
They say that in this way Trump wants to organize an anti-China belt of neighboring states.
It is possible that such thoughts in the White House and roam, but for Putin it is doubly humiliating.
First, he still thinks he is ruling a great power.
Although every day this status is increasingly becoming a thing of the past.
He is invited along with those who, quite recently, were either third world countries or, like Australia, did not play a significant role in world politics.
This is one factor in reducing international weight.
The second is that until 2014, Russia was a full member of the G8, and then because of the aggression against Ukraine and for the annexation of Crimea, it was expelled from the club of large, in the political sense, states.
And now Putin is invited to attend as a guest where he was one of the hosts.
This is a very serious psychological and symbolic blow for him.
And what can you say, if the influence and achievements of Russia are reduced like a shagreen skin and this process cannot be stopped.
It has become irreversible.
What happened in space and will happen in the OPEC + negotiations on limiting oil production, where Russia will have to agree to one degree or another with the demands of Saudi Arabia and the UAE, is another confirmation of the narrowing of Moscow ’ s influence on world politics.
What remains of Russian power.
Only one thing is to engage in subversive activities along the perimeter of its borders.
And here the field for maneuvers is also narrowing.
Central Asian countries have abandoned Moscow ’ s mediation services in resolving their border conflicts.
This is the first time in years.
The significance of this fact has yet to be assessed.
The space breakthrough happened without Russia.
It will be so in the future.
Near and far away.
The world ’ s gas station is doomed to stagnation and transformation into a third-rate power.

title: The last flight of an American woman from Baikonur
text:
So those who thought the historic SpaceX Crew Demo-2 mission changed the game were wrong.
NASA plans to pay the Russian space agency to send one of its astronauts into orbit, and Russian cosmonauts are likely to go into space from Florida next year.
Within days of the American launch, when two NASA astronauts traveled to the International Space Station (ISS) from the United States for the first time in nearly a decade, ending NASA ’ s dependence on the Russian space agency Roscosmos, there was much talk of a wake-up call for the Russian space program, and there was some gloating on SpaceX ’ s part.
But it ’ s not that simple, and it certainly isn ’ t the end of U.S.-Russian cooperation.
This week, NASA announced that it would send its astronaut Kate Rubins on a six-month mission to the ISS as a flight engineer and crew member of Expedition 63 / 64.
Does that mean there will be another launch of SpaceX ’ s 55-millionth Crew Dragon in Florida?
Rubins will go on the expedition with cosmonauts Sergey Ryzhikov and Sergey Kud-Sverchkov on October 14 on the Soyuz MS-17 spacecraft from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
Its place will cost NASA $90 million, as in the days before SpaceX Crew Dragon.
“The cost of the fall contract is $9,025,2905.69 per seat, including all necessary preparations for launch, flight, landing and rescue of the crew, as well as limited supplies of cargo to and from the station, ” NASA spokeswoman Stephanie Schirholz said in an email yesterday.
However, sending Rubins to the ISS from Kazakhstan is likely to be the last launch of NASA astronauts from Baikonur.
"NASA is confident that American commercial companies will be available in 2020 / 2021 to send astronauts and that further purchases of Soyuz seats will not be required," Schirholz said.
Why won ’ t Rubins be able to join NASA colleagues Michael Hopkins, Victor Glover and Shannon Walker, as well as JAXA astronaut Soichi Noguchi on Crew-1, in SpaceX ’ s first planned Crew Dragon journey to the ISS, due to begin on August 30, 2020?
After all, there are seven seats on Crew Dragon.
“For commercial missions, NASA has awarded a four-seat contract, ” Schirholz explained.“ NASA uses an additional seat on commercial missions to deliver more than 220 pounds of cargo back and forth to the station with each flight. ”
If Rubins ’ flight into space on Soyuz is the last for NASA, the opposite trend could start on the part of Roscosmos: left without the money from NASA necessary for the profitability of using Soyuz, Russia will pay SpaceX and Boeing for seats.
“NASA is in talks with Roscosmos to ensure that both a U.S. crew member and an astronaut will be present on future Union missions and commercial missions to continue the safe operation of the space station, ” Schirholz said.
At the moment, we are working on the details of such cooperation. ”
Boeing will conduct the second flight test of its CST-100 Starliner spacecraft without a crew later in 2020.

title: It became known when Crew Dragon with astronauts will return to Earth
text:
SpaceX ’ s new US manned Crew Dragon spacecraft with astronauts Douglas Harley and Robert Benken is likely to return to Earth from a flight to the International Space Station (ISS) in August.
This is reported by Interfax-Ukraine with reference to NASA.
The exact date of Harley and Benken ’ s return will depend on several factors, such as the normal functioning of their spacecraft, their performance on the ISS and weather conditions in the landing area of the capsule in the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico, said Ken Bowersox, NASA ’ s acting head of manned missions.
According to him, the Crew Dragon mission is going according to plan, the ship has been functioning well since its launch on May 30 on a Falcon 9 rocket from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral and docking with the ISS the next day.
Even before the launch, NASA officials said that the test flight of Crew Dragon could last from one to four months, depending on a number of technical and weather factors.
“We didn ’ t plan the duration of the test mission until we put the crew into orbit and see how Crew Dragon functions, ” Bowersox said.
The practical details are still being worked out. ”
The Crew Dragon spacecraft, launched with Harley and Benken on board, has been certified by NASA to fly in space for up to four months.
The limiting factor for the duration of the flight of the ship is the degradation of its solar panels.
It is planned that Benken will make at least two spacewalks in late June and early July with the current commander of the ISS Chris Cassidy, who in April arrived at the station on the Russian spacecraft Soyuz.
The duo will have to replace outdated nickel-hydrogen batteries with new, more powerful lithium-ion ones on the support segment of the ISS farm, to which solar panels are attached.
The batteries were delivered to the ISS in May by the Japanese cargo ship HTV.
"It is likely that by the end of July we will have several spacewalks with Chris Cassidy and Bob Benken, replace some of the batteries on the ISS, and in two months we will start thinking about bringing Robert and Douglas home," Bowersox said.
Recall: on May 30, the company SpaceX Elon Musk in cooperation with NASA sent into space two American astronauts on the ship Crew Dragon.
The launch was originally scheduled for May 27, but was canceled 17 minutes before launch due to difficult weather conditions.
The launch of the rocket is special because for the first time the flight took place on a spacecraft of a private company.
The cost of sending one astronaut to the ISS by SpaceX cost NASA $50 million.
Roscosmos charges for this service almost twice as much - $90 million.

title: At the current rate of warming in 30 years in Belarus will be fundamentally new agrometeorological conditions - scientist
text:
June 16, Minsk / Corr.
BELTA /.
At the current rate of warming in 30 years in Belarus will be fundamentally new agrometeorological conditions, Director of the Institute of Nature Management of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus Sergey Lysenko told reporters today.
“The problems of soil degradation and erosion should be considered in the context of climate change.
In Belarus, due to climate change, new agrometeorological conditions are being formed, - said Sergey Lysenko. - It should be borne in mind that if the pace (warming - approx.
In 30 years, the whole territory of Belarus will have fundamentally new agrometeorological conditions, which now do not exist.
That is, the active temperatures that are now near the southern borders will be on the northern border of Belarus in 30 years. ”
According to him, it is possible to adapt to new conditions with the help of measures in forestry and agriculture.
"But the key factor in ensuring a favorable agrometeorological regime on the territory of Belarus will be the preservation and retention of moisture resources available at the regional level," the scientist believes.
The problem is that rapid warming increases potential evaporation, which is not compensated by the amount of precipitation.
“If in the 80-90s the positive balance between the annual amount of precipitation and the annual evaporation was more than zero in the whole territory of Belarus, then the negative balance in the current century is already observed in the entire territory of the Gomel and Brest regions, ” said Sergey Lysenko.
Now the zero balance line runs on the southern border of Grodno, Minsk and Mogilev regions.
"This zero-balance boundary, where rainfall equals evaporation, is moving from south to north at a speed of about 19 km per year," the director of the Institute of Nature Management of the National Academy of Sciences said.
Since 2012, winter warming has resumed.
“It was from the 60s to the early 90s, then there was a summer warming.
And now it ’ s winter warming again, ” said Sergey Lysenko.
The lack of snow cover, in turn, leads to a lack of water in the spring.
At the same time, the increase in summer temperatures has slowed since about 2011.
"All these processes are part of a natural cycle lasting about 30 years, i.e. another 20 years such processes will occur.
They are superimposed on the trend of anthropogenic global warming.
This does not mean that after the cycle the temperature will return to its previous level, there is a more significant trend - anthropogenic, "the director of the Institute of Nature Management of the National Academy of Sciences of the Russian Federation noted.

title: NASA has announced the date of return of astronauts SpaceX Crew Dragon to Earth

title: Bayer will pay compensation due to herbicides
text:
German pharmaceutical giant Bayer has agreed to pay $10 billion in damages to settle lawsuits over Monsanto ’ s weed control glyphosate.

Roundup weed killer has been sold in more than 160 countries and is widely used in the United States.

title: Tom Cruise is planning to make a film in space. Here's what we know about it.
text:
Tom Cruise is planning to make a film in space.
Rumors that Tom Cruise is going to make a movie in space have appeared repeatedly.
This time the information was confirmed by the head of NASA Jim Bridenstine.
The publication Ars Technica learned how the filmmakers plan to cope with technical difficulties and what role in overcoming them will play Space X. In recent years, the media has several times appeared materials about the space plans of the actor.
British tabloids even claimed that Cruz was preparing to fly on the space shuttle and could have died on board the Columbia in 2003, but NASA denied this information.
In 2018, a rumor began circulating that the next installment of Cruise ’ s “Mission Impossible ” franchise would be filmed in space.
Director Christopher McQuarrie quickly made it clear that this was nothing more than a rumor.
The actor himself explained that with such a film there would be a lot of difficulties: “How to get the necessary equipment there?
Remove the necessary sequence of frames?
And even if we imagine that we have coped with all the technical difficulties – how do we fit this into the “Mission ” scenario? ”
“It ’ s not the time yet, ” Cruz concluded in an interview with Collider in August 2018.
Two years later, the actor changed his mind.
Recently, the publication Deadline released another material about the possible shooting of the film in space.
And unlike previous situations, the information was confirmed by the head of NASA Jim Bridenstine.
The day after the release of the article in Deadline, he posted a tweet: “NASA is pleased to work with Tom Cruise on the film aboard the International Space Station! ”
What has changed since 2018?
Perhaps the team ’ s current optimism is due to the success of Elon Musk ’ s space project.
On May 30, SpaceX sent its first crew to the ISS — astronauts Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken.
And while the primary goal of the launch was to demonstrate to NASA that Crew Dragon is capable of successfully delivering astronauts to and from Earth ’ s orbit, the event also marked the beginning of a new era of commercial space flight.
“NASA does not want to be the owner and operator of the equipment, nor do we want to be the only customer, ” Bridenstine said after the historic launch of SpaceX.
Hollywood fits that definition.
The White House has instructed NASA to return astronauts to the moon by 2024.
To free up resources for the implementation of this project, the agency decided to transfer projects in low-Earth orbit to commercial partners.
In June 2019, it announced that it would make the space station available for commercial projects and “will promote these capabilities like never before. ”
“Private astronauts will be able to go to the space station on American ships, and companies will receive the associated profit, ” said the then CFO of NASA Jeff Devit.
Seven months later, the agency entered into negotiations with Houston-based Axiom Space to add a new module to the station.
The company, led by Michael Suffredini, who was responsible for NASA ’ s work on the ISS from 2005 to 2015, plans to launch the Axiom segment in 2024.
Before that, the company is going to send customers to the station on the SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft.
The first mission with three passengers, including an experienced astronaut as a guide, is scheduled for the fall of 2021.
After the launch of SpaceX Demo-2, "everyone is starting to wonder who's next in line," Suffredini told the Associated Press.
Axiom did not officially announce the collaboration with Cruise, but Bridenstine confirmed the company's involvement in the project in the June 15 release of the Off-Nominal podcast.
A month after the first reports of Cruz ’ s plans, several more details of the new project became known.
First, Deadline reported that the director of the future film is already known - he will be Doug Lyman: "Lyman plans to work with Tom Cruise on an adventure action movie.
The project also involves Elon Musk ’ s Space X and NASA. ”
Lyman (The Bourne Identity, Mr. and Mrs. Smith) has already worked with Cruise on Made in America and The Edge of the Future.
According to Deadline, he has already prepared the first draft of the script.
At the moment, both Lyman and Cruz are engaged in other projects - the latter is filmed with McQuarrie in the next episode of "Mission".
At the moment, it is not known which studio will undertake the implementation of the project, the timing is also not called.
It raises big questions and budget.
It is reported that the cost of a ticket to Crew Dragon is $55 million, excluding the transportation of cameras and other equipment for shooting.
Shooting on board the space station will also be expensive.
After the announcement of plans to commercialize the complex, NASA published a detailed price list, according to which the cost of simple access to orbit and work on it can exceed $178 million.
By comparison, this amount fully covers the budget of the 2018 film Mission: Impossible: Consequences.
Deadline said that Cruise and Lyman plan to go to the space station on their own, but it is not yet known whether they will succeed.
At a minimum, they will have to undergo a physical examination.
As for psychological readiness to work in space, at least one astronaut believes that Cruz can cope with the task.
“He ’ s a real professional, ” said Scott Altman, who was one of four F-14 Tomcat pilots selected by the U.S. Navy to star in Top Gun: Maverick.
Cruz was sitting behind Altman's back while performing stunts in the air.
“I was impressed by his approach.
He behaved carefully and respectfully and took the flight very seriously.
I noticed his genuine interest in aviation, ” Altman said.
Tom Cruise in the Advanced Crew Escape Suit (ACES).
In the photo (left to right): astronaut Charlie Precourt, Bill Todd, Sharon McDougle, Tom Cruise and George Brittingham.
In some articles, Cruz ’ s project is described as “the first film to be shot in space. ”
But there are other projects that can claim this status.
In April 1984, a widescreen camera was used for the filming of the 11th mission of the NASA space shuttle.
The producer and director remained on Earth, and the role of filmmakers was taken over by the astronauts.
For the 37-minute film The Dream Is Alive (1985), IMAX cameras had to be used in three missions.
IMAX cameras accompanied most of the space shuttle flights.
In later missions, astronauts shot scenes in 3D and used high-definition digital cameras.
There are five more IMAX films with scenes from space.
According to Altman, who worked on the documentary IMAX Hubble 3D (2010), there are a number of unique problems associated with filming aboard the spacecraft.
“The lighting changes very often, and this greatly complicates the shooting process.
If you don ’ t have time to shoot the scene in sunlight, you need to wait another 45 minutes until the station flies through the dark part of the orbit, ” he explains.
Another difficulty is the limited space on board the shuttle (Crew Dragon seats even less).
But there is enough space on the space station, says Altman “the ISS has grown greatly in recent years, ” he explains. – You can work on the film in one of the rooms, without interfering with the work of the crew. ”
Cruise has an idea of the size of the station — he voiced the IMAX documentary “Space Station 3D ”:“ One day you too can be on the ISS.
Maybe you ’ ll be an engineer inventing a new technology, or an environmentalist studying the Earth. ”
Perhaps the actor himself will become the author of the first feature film shot in space.
Altman and his colleagues, who worked on space movies for IMAX, did not have a script: they were tasked with recording the events taking place.
Trying to tell the story as Cruz and Lyman planned is the next level of difficulty.
“In 2008, I shot the first feature film in space, ” said Richard Garriot in an interview with KTBC. – My friend, writer Tracy Hickman, wrote the script, according to which we with the other members of the team shot and edited the film, which also premiered on the space station. ”
The seven-minute film Apogee of Fear by Garriot was created during his private flight to the space station, organized by Space Adventures.
To simplify the production of the film, Garriot wrote special cribs with cues for the actors and shot scenes in the same order in which they appeared in the film.
This rarely happens when shooting a movie under normal conditions.
“Shooting a movie and controlling a camera in space is very difficult because of inertia, ” explains Garriot. – Actors find it difficult to stay in one position because of Newton ’ s laws.
When you start moving, it ’ s hard to stop. ”
At least one more narrative film was shot in microgravity — though not in space.
Apollo 13, starring Tom Hanks, Bill Paxton and Kevin Bacon, was filmed aboard the KC-135, which is commonly used for astronaut training.
The cast and crew could change position and prepare for the next scene using 30-second breaks between periods of weightlessness.
After the release of the movie “Best Shooter ” in 1986, the number of draftees of the US Navy increased by 500%.
Bridenstine hopes Cruise ’ s space movie could have a similar effect.
"I was in elementary school when '' Best Shooter '' came out.
After watching this movie, I knew I wanted to be a Navy pilot.
“If Tom Cruise was able to infect a child with a dream of the sky, why not try to do the same with space?
Who knows, maybe among the audience of the film will be the next Elon Musk? ”
“Spacesuits, spaceships, going into orbit, going to the moon and Mars — all of this can really make kids dream about space, ” Musk said in a tweet, calling Cruz ’ s new project“ very fun. ”
Altman also sees this potential: “Movies with famous actors like Tom Cruise attract people ’ s attention.
This is a great way to make viewers think about something important and inspire them to new achievements.
Let only a few become astronauts or go to the ISS, but a huge number of people will be inspired by the achievements of human civilization. ”
Source.

title: Iran agrees to pay compensation to victims of UIA plane crash – Swedish Foreign Minister
text:
Iran has agreed to pay compensation to the victims of the crash of the UIA – Swedish Foreign Minister 02.07.2020, 19: 42, News of the day The Iranian authorities have agreed to pay compensation to the families of the victims of the downed plane of Ukraine International Airlines near Tehran.
About it on July 2 in an interview with the Agency TT, which refers to the Associated Press, said the Minister of foreign Affairs of Sweden Ann Linde.
The signed agreement of understanding is about the beginning of negotiations on payments, now there is no doubt that compensation will be, the Minister stressed.
According to her, the first meeting on the issue of payments to the closest relatives of the victims will be held in the near future.
The press service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sweden clarified in a conversation with the Associated Press that Sweden, Canada, Ukraine, the United Kingdom and Afghanistan act as an international coordinating group that puts forward uniform claims for compensation for damage.
Passenger plane Boeing 737-800 flight PS752 “International airlines of Ukraine ”, which was heading from Tehran to Kiev, crashed on January 8 near the capital of Iran.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
No one survived.
Among the dead – 11 citizens of Ukraine, 81 Iranians, 57 citizens of Canada, 13 – Afghanistan, 10 – Sweden, four citizens of Great Britain.
Iranian authorities, initially claiming that the plane crashed due to a technical malfunction, on January 11, under pressure from Western leaders, admitted that flight PS752 was shot down by an Iranian missile by mistake.
On February 7, it became known that a Canadian lawyer filed a lawsuit against the Iranian authorities in the High Court of Ontario on behalf of his client, a relative of one of the dead passengers.
The lawsuit stated that the total amount of compensation should be $1.1 billion.
The Iranian Foreign Ministry rejected the demands for payment.
In February, the then foreign Minister of Ukraine Vadym Prystaiko said that the amount of compensation from the Iranian side will exceed $80 thousand per person.
On April 14, 2020, Radio Farda (the Iranian service of Radio Liberty) reported that Iran offered to recognize “human error ” as the cause of the crash of the UIA plane and to refuse further legal proceedings in exchange for payment of compensation to the families of the victims.
Canadian Foreign Minister François-Philippe Champagne categorically rejected the possibility of concluding an agreement with the Iranian government on non-prosecution.
On June 20, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy in an interview with the Canadian newspaper Globe and Mail admitted that lawsuits will be filed against Iran in international courts if this country does not adhere to its obligations in connection with the crash of the UIA aircraft.
According to Zelensky, Ukraine is waiting for an official apology for the incident.

title: On the chalk
text:
As the world struggles with the coronavirus, Europe faces an additional threat.
The largest rivers are shallow due to severe drought and become unsuitable for navigation, and therefore for the transport of goods.
The consequences of the current disaster may surpass the anti-record set two years ago, which will further hit the European and global economy – it faces losses of billions of dollars.
So far, attempts to understand the causes have led to climate change, which is greatly influenced by the consumption of oil and gas.
In the future, the main buyers of Russian resources under the influence of common misfortune will decide to abandon them, including for the sake of environmentalists.
Dried Europe - in the material "Tape.ru".
Two years ago, European weather forecasters and farmers sounded the alarm: the first recorded the highest temperatures for many years of observations, the second lost the harvest in unprecedented volumes.
Record warm weather was even in Scandinavia and the surrounding countries: in the Norwegian polar regions it reached 33.5 degrees Celsius.
Due to the abnormal heat, the plants were deprived of the necessary moisture, the yield of some crops decreased by half at once.
Vegetable growers talked about the most serious problems in the last 40 years, grain growers assessed the situation as catastrophic, in Greece, Spain and Italy, olives were dying.
Worried even the producers of chips, left without the main raw material — potatoes.
Hydropower also suffered, on which the power supply of many countries depends, systematically closing nuclear power plants.
In addition, the authorities of the European Union and its individual members had to allocate large-scale subsidies to farmers and affected companies so that they remained afloat and did not raise prices for basic products.
The winners were only manufacturers of solar panels and sellers of hay, the demand for which rose sharply due to the fact that fresh grass was clearly not enough to fatten numerous herds.
The climatic conditions were very unevenly distributed.
While northern and central Europe languished from the heat, record rainfall fell in the south, partially compensating for critical crop shortages.
Already in the fall, increased precipitation fell on most of the continent, floods occurred in some regions.
Experts did not understand the reasons for what was happening.
In 2019, the temperature peaks were again beaten, but without a large-scale drought, and therefore the previous panic was avoided.
This summer, the consequences for people and the economy may well be even more serious.
Employees of the European-wide Copernicus Climate Change Service predict the cumulative losses of various industries — primarily agriculture — by billions of dollars.
According to their calculations, in Central and Western Europe at the end of the three summer months, precipitation will fall by 40 percent less than usual, which will entail additional budget expenditures that are already forced to spend more actively than usual due to the coronavirus of states.
The largest - for 145 billion euros - the program of support of the economy launched Germany.
At the pan-European level, there is an unprecedented quantitative easing program – the European Central Bank ’ s purchases of state and corporate debts in the secondary market for 1.3 trillion euros.
A large-scale plan of assistance to victims of 750 billion, two-thirds of which will be provided through grants, is also being prepared.
The funds will be raised through the issuance of pan-European bonds, the issuer - for the first time in this volume - will act the European Commission, which will allow it to seriously strengthen its authority and role in the matter of continental integration.
However, even unprecedented volume of financial injections can not prevent another natural cataclysm.
The Rhine, Germany ’ s main river and one of the longest in Europe, began to dry up in April – the water level has not been so low for the past nine years.
For the whole month, the country fell only five percent of the usual rainfall, which was the worst indicator since 1881.
Meteorologists hope for rain, but so far they are short-lived.
If the situation does not change in the near future, problems will be experienced not only by agriculture, but also by transport companies, and after them - most of the economy.
The Rhine traditionally fuses a variety of goods, including grain, fertilizers, chemicals, coal, petroleum products, as well as wood and metals.
They pass from the Swiss Basel through many German cities, as well as the French Strasbourg and enter the North Sea.
Due to the warm flow of the Gulf Stream, the river does not freeze even in winter, which allows supplying raw materials to the main industrial areas of Germany, and the goods produced in them to be delivered to consumers and international ports.
In Düsseldorf and Cologne, the assembly shops of the largest German automakers are located, the chemical company Hoechst, which produces fibers, plastics and medicines, is based in the industrial park of Wiesbaden, and the pharmaceutical giant Bayer is based in Leverkusen.
Many cities on the Rhine have oil refineries.
Their products are in demand in the Netherlands Rotterdam - the most important European center for trade in oil, gas, coal (mined in the Ruhr region adjacent to the Rhine) and other minerals.
It is reached by one of the many branches of the Rhine, the New Maas.
When the main German river is shallow, transportation through it becomes difficult or even impossible.
Because of this, supplies are disrupted, production is stopped.
In the current situation, when many factories are already idle in quarantine, any violation of the usual order threatens even more unemployment and, possibly, a shortage of individual goods.
Transport companies, which still continue to operate, risk their vessels - they can damage the bottom or run aground, and therefore increase the fee for services, which is reflected in the final prices.
Insurance companies can also suffer losses.
In the past two years, they have already had to pay more than usual due to frequent hurricanes near German rivers and lakes.
Weather phenomena arose so unexpectedly that vacationers did not have time to get out of the water.
According to scientists, they were also the result of too high temperatures and dry air.
Summer months in Germany have always been considered the most calm and safe from the point of view of natural disasters, which was actively used by insurers.
But now many of them are changing their strategy.
In the same boat, the problem is relevant for other states.
The Czech Republic is facing the worst drought in modern history, and its situation is aggravated by its lack of access to the sea.
Environment Minister Jiří Brabec called the drought an even more serious challenge than the coronavirus, which caused the country to be the first in the European Union to completely close its borders.
80% of groundwater sources were affected.
In recent years, the Vltava River has often overflowed and flooded the central parts of Prague (the last major flood occurred in 2002), but now it is shallower by more than three-quarters of the usual figures.
Farmers have been promised 3.5 billion kroner (about 126 million euros), but it is already obvious that such measures will not be enough.
For the past four years, the Czech budget has remained surplus, but by the end of 2020, the government will definitely have to increase debt, which is now one of the lowest in Europe and does not exceed 30 percent of GDP.
In France, almost half of all agricultural land has dried up, in Romania the reservoirs were critically crushed.
In the vicinity of the Swiss Geneva in early spring, rain waited a month and a half, which has not happened for more than a hundred years.
On the European energy exchange Epex Spot quotations of contracts for the supply of electricity fell below zero 80 percent more often than usual - in contrast to the oil market, negative prices in a short time interval are considered normal.
In fact, buyers were paid extra to stay connected to the network.
All because of the growing role of renewable energy, primarily all the same solar panels.
Problems would not be so serious if not superimposed on the coronavirus pandemic.
Some countries, such as Singapore, do not have access to fresh water and are accustomed to buying it abroad.
But in 2020 it is much more difficult to do this because of the universally closed borders, the rupture of production and trade chains.
The same goes for basic food: last year ’ s record-breaking harvest (which was not affected by the heat) has accumulated impressive supplies around the world, but it is not so easy to deliver them to those in need: there are not enough healthy loaders, drivers, and transportation disruptions everywhere.
Back in 2018, scientists said that the cause of the anomaly was the increased atmospheric pressure that persisted over most of Europe for several months.
It formed a “heat dome ” above the ground and prevented precipitation.
Like many other weather events of our day, it was caused by “man-made ” climate change.
In some countries and regions, for example, in Denmark and the Netherlands, the atmospheric pressure without active human intervention in nature could be 3-5 times lower.
In February 2018, a few weeks before the first signs of drought, the authoritative scientific journal Environmental Research Letters released a study in which it predicted serious cataclysms for 500 European cities in the near future – provided that the EU ’ s environmental policy remains the same.
The authors also spoke about possible floods and heat (a situation bordering on drought, but still less serious).
The call of nature While everything can be corrected, it was emphasized in the work, but it is necessary to act immediately.
First of all, it is necessary to reduce carbon emissions into the atmosphere, as prescribed in the Paris Agreement of 2015.
It does not impose specific obligations on States parties, but requires them to independently develop and implement a programme of action.
The overall ultimate goal is to ensure that by 2100 the average annual temperature on Earth does not rise by more than two degrees Celsius compared to the pre-industrial era (1850-1900s).
Now most of all emissions are produced by the United States, China, India and Russia.
The main source of carbon (or carbon) trace is industrial production, which burns a large amount of fuel, and aviation.
But each person contributes to the pollution of the planet and climate change individually – by driving a car or cooking at the stove.
But an even greater impact on the atmosphere is the consumption of red meat, especially beef.
At all stages of its production in different countries - from raising cows to delivery to stores - the environment receives as much harmful emissions as when driving all cars in the world.
This includes natural emissions of methane by the animals themselves during the emission of gases.
In recent years, environmentalists have focused on two areas: trying to achieve the maximum possible transition to alternative energy and reduce the ever-growing number of flights.
In the first quarter of this year, 28 percent of electricity produced worldwide came from renewable sources (compared to 26 percent at the beginning of 2019).
Such results were achieved due to the constant rise in the cost of coal and gas - traditionally the main sources of electricity generation.
During the pandemic, demand for it fell sharply, but after the victory over the coronasirus, people and companies will obviously have even less money, which means that we should expect further growth in the role of solar, wind and geothermal power plants.
In addition, many countries are purposefully spent on the development of alternative energy.
In Germany ’ s $145 billion economic recovery plan, a third of the country ’ s total is set aside.
In the future without us, similar processes are taking place in the fuel market.
Since the beginning of the 20th century, oil and gas have played a leading role in it, but gradually many countries, mainly developed, began to look for other options.
So there were electric cars, which in the foreseeable future should push cars with internal combustion engines.
Almost all EU member states have adopted laws to gradually ban the sale of the latter.
In Norway, which is not part of the union, the share of electric vehicles already exceeds 40 percent, although the global average in 2018 (the latest accurate data) did not exceed 2.2 percent.
The next step is electric planes.
Until recently, they were only a concept that was successfully implemented only in the form of small devices that can take on board only a few people and spend no more than an hour in the air.
Neither batteries nor solar panels could cope with the task due to low power and inefficiency.
But in the summer of 2019 at the air show in the French Le Bourget, the Israeli company Eviation presented a prototype of the first commercial aircraft Alice on lithium-polymer batteries.
The model is a business jet for nine passengers and two crew members and has already earned praise from aviation experts, who called it a breakthrough in the industry.
Several airlines have issued pre-orders, although serial production is not expected until 2037.
British low-cost airline EasyJet promises to start transportation on electric aircraft in the next 10 years.
Eviation emphasizes that the project is not for the sake of saving the Earth, but for reasons of economic feasibility.
According to the assurances of managers, the use of an electric motor can greatly reduce the cost of flights - from $400 per 100 miles (160.9 kilometers) to 8-12.
If the idea can really be brought to mind, the world economy ’ s need for oil will decrease significantly.
However, it is possible that this will happen even earlier – if the current drought will force politicians and businessmen to finally seriously worry about climate issues.
The coronavirus pandemic has already shown what a world can look like in which production and trade chains have changed – albeit temporarily – beyond recognition, and the price of oil can go negative.
Brussels and Moscow are equally dependent on each other.
Russia is the leader in the supply of oil (about 30 percent) and gas (about 40 percent) to Europe, and revenues from their exports exceed a third of all revenues to the Russian budget.
But it is necessary to prepare for changes now – developing technological sectors of the economy and increasing its competition.
Otherwise, in the foreseeable future, the treasury shuts down like the main European rivers.

title: People are more willing to go to plastic surgeons. Helped the quarantine
text:
In the United States, Australia, South Korea and Japan during the pandemic sharply increased the demand for plastic surgery services Demand for plastic surgery services in the era of coronavirus and quarantine in some countries, oddly enough, increased.
If earlier many postponed a visit to a plastic surgeon due to lack of time, now they decided on an operation because of the possibility in the postoperative period to sit at home, often without even interrupting work.
In some countries, plastic surgery clinics did not close, although many other companies had to temporarily stop working or transfer a significant part of employees to remote work.
Clinics introduced a number of additional measures during the pandemic to protect patients and clinic staff from contracting the coronavirus.
For example, disinfection of all premises has become more frequent, and customers before a visit to the doctor were offered to undergo a test for Covid-19.
Plastic surgery clinics in the United States, Japan, South Korea and Australia report an increase in demand for their services during the pandemic: customers come to enlarge their lips or carry out wrinkle correction with Botox, and there has also been an increase in the number of customers wanting to do a facelift and nose shape correction.
“I decided to do the procedure during the quarantine, because now I can safely recover at home, ” says a resident of Los Angeles Aaron Hernandez, who decided to enlarge the lips and liposuction (removal of fat) cheeks.
“Lip augmentation is not a procedure that men turn to, so the reaction to my choice can be different.
Therefore, I would prefer to stay home while recovering from the procedure, so that when I show up in public, no one will guess what kind of facial manipulation I was doing, ” says Aaron Hernandez.
According to him, the last time he did a similar procedure before the quarantine and was embarrassed that he had to go to work, meet people, while his lips were very swollen and bruised.
Renowned plastic surgeon Rod Rohrich, who receives clients in Texas, also says there is a significant increase in demand for his services.
“If we wanted to, now we could have operations six days a week.
Something incredible! ” he told the BBC.
According to Rod Rorich, before his clients tried to plan the operation so that they had the opportunity to sit at home, but now that many are working from home, there is no need to look for such an opportunity.
"They can recover by staying at home, and when they go outside, they have a mask on their face, so no one sees what they have recently done a rhinoplasty or a facelift.
People want to get back to normal life, and the desire to look as good as possible is part of the process of returning to normal life, ” said Rod Rohrich.
The increase in the demand for plastic surgery services is observed not only in the United States.
South Korea, where plastic surgery is highly developed, was one of the first countries where cases of Covid-19 were reported.
In South Korea, plastic surgery is very popular, and during the pandemic of those wishing to do plastic surgery became even more Instead of the introduction of a universal lockdown, South Korea adopted a plan according to which residents were to strictly observe social distance, and companies were advised to transfer employees to remote work.
At first, after the introduction of restrictive measures, plastic surgery clinics in South Korea noted a decline in the flow of foreign customers, but residents of the country, on the contrary, began to be more interested in the services of aesthetic medicine clinics.
Some clinics even provided special discounts for local customers.
A 54-year-old schoolteacher from South Korea who did blepharoplasty in February told the Joongang Daily that she couldn ’ t make an appointment right away because no matter what clinic she went to, she already had a full appointment.
In Seoul, BK Hospital said that at the beginning of the pandemic, people were confused and alarmed, but later more and more locals began to come to the clinic.
“People felt more secure and calm enough to decide on an operation.
The number of patients continues to grow, ” says an official representative of the clinic.
“According to preliminary estimates, despite the coronavirus, the number of patients we have increased by 50% compared to the same period last year, ” said BK Hospital.
According to the representative of the clinic, the number of foreign customers has recently begun to grow.
“The number of online referrals [from abroad] has increased significantly as we have had the opportunity to conduct online consultations and prepare patients in advance for a trip for surgery that they can go to once all restrictions are lifted, ” BK Hospital said in a statement.
In Japan, no quarantine was imposed, but Prime Minister Shinzo Abe declared a state of emergency, which lasted until May 31.
Residents of the country were asked to stay at home if possible.
The copyright holder of the EPA Image caption Not all Japanese have heeded the calls of the authorities to stay at home, however, in plastic surgery clinics in Japan, the number of appeals has also increased.
The increase in appeals forced the Association of Aesthetic Medicine of Japan to appeal to residents of the country to postpone aesthetic operations, since "they are not vital."
The Association urged clinic customers to refuse visits to plastic surgeons to prevent further spread of the coronavirus.
Michel Tajiri, a spokesman for the Bliss Aesthetic Medicine Clinic in Fukuoka, says that despite all the warnings from the authorities, the number of clients willing to undergo surgery has increased.
“The main reason is that they do not go to the office and they do not need to look specifically for time for rehabilitation.
In addition, now everyone wears masks and all the consequences of operations and procedures are easy to disguise, ” says Michel Tajiri.
Aaron Hernandez admits that for him, surgery during the quarantine was the best solution.
“It gave me more time to recover.
I could take the necessary medications that I wouldn ’ t be able to take if I had to drive a car.
I had the opportunity to apply ice to my lips and face after the operation, ” says Aaron Hernandez.
In many countries, during the pandemic, a ban was imposed on the operation of beauty salons and aesthetic medicine clinics.
In Russia, for example, the ban was in effect from early April to June 9.
With the introduction of the self-isolation regime in Russia, among other things, the planned reception of patients by dentists was suspended.
Exceptions were made only for those patients who needed emergency care.

title: Earth is attacking. What will China, the United States and the Emirates look for on Mars?
text:
On the night of July 15, the UAE will send its first orbiter to Mars.
Also in July, the launch of their research missions planned by China and the United States.
What and how they will look for on the red planet, says Focus October 30, 1938, the United States was engulfed in mass panic.
People called newspapers and police stations, believing that the Earth had been attacked by the Martians.
This reaction was caused by the radio play of the novel by H.G. Wells "War of the Worlds", which the audience took at face value.
After almost 100 years, we know for sure that the Martians will not arrive, because they do not exist, and in general - if there is life on the Red Planet, then microscopic and well hidden.
Earth has been conquering Mars with varying success for more than half a century.
This year, humanity will make an unprecedented breakthrough towards the Red Planet: three countries will send research missions to it at once.
Hope Country: United Arab Emirates Start date: July 15, 2020
Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: orbiter Mission duration: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: to provide a holistic picture of the Martian atmosphere and weather The times when space exploration was the monopoly of superpowers are long past.
Today, more and more countries and private companies are looking to the stars, and the United Arab Emirates seems to want to be among the pioneers.
The UAE may become the first Arab state to launch an interplanetary mission.
The UAE did not pursue a more ambitious goal of landing on the planet – in the history of Mars exploration, there were far more failed attempts to do this than successful ones.
Preferably confined to an orbital probe.
The research apparatus with a mass of 1.3 tons will make a full orbit around the planet every 55 hours, then approaching it for 20 thousand km, then moving away to 43 thousand.
On board, it will carry infrared and ultraviolet spectrometers, as well as a camera that can not only take pictures, but also shoot video in 4K resolution.
With the help of these tools, Arab scientists want to carefully study the Martian atmosphere, to understand the mechanisms due to which it loses much needed oxygen on Earth.
In addition, they are interested in the weather systems of Mars.
Thanks to the features of the orbit of the probe, they will be able to observe how the weather changes throughout the entire Martian days (24 hours).
38 minutes of Earth time) at one point or another on the planet.
This year, the UAE is sending a probe to Mars, and in 100 years they want to build a city there Data that researchers will receive during the mission will not settle in closed laboratories.
The UAE plans to share them with colleagues from 200 scientific institutions around the world in the hope that the new information will help to better understand the history and mechanisms of functioning of the Martian climate.
However, the Arab mission to Mars does not only pursue scientific goals.
Its organizers hope that the conquest of the neighboring planet will inspire young people and help educate a new generation of scientists and engineers - specialists who can prove that the Emirates is more than just a country with rich oil deposits.
“It is a matter of the future of the UAE and our survival, ” said Omran Sharaf, the head of the mission.
In the view of local scientists, Mars does play a significant role in the future, and perhaps in the survival of the state.
After all, they plan to build an entire city on the Red Planet within the next century.
With an eye on all this, it is obvious that for their first "scout" they chose the most appropriate name - "Al Amal", which means "Hope".
Question to Heaven Country: China Start date: July 23, 2020
Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: Mars rover, orbiter and lander Planned mission duration: Rover - 90 sols (equal to 92 Earth days), probe - 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: study of the magnetosphere, ionosphere and atmosphere of Mars, mapping of terrain, observation of dust storms, study of the composition of rocks and soil, mineral distribution Another debutant in the conquest of Mars will be China.
Local scientists decided to act on a much larger scale than their Arab counterparts.
They will send a rover, landing and orbiters to Mars.
The mission was named Tianwen-1 (Questions to Heaven) after a poem written more than 2,000 years ago.
Each machine has its own task.
For example, the probe, which will be located in the orbit of Mars, will study the geological structure and natural conditions of the planet, as well as transmit data to Earth.
On the lander lies perhaps the most important part of the mission - the actual delivery of equipment to Mars.
This process takes about seven minutes, but this time period is called “seven minutes of nightmare ”.
It depends on China whether it will have its own research apparatus on another planet or it will simply deliver a heap of expensive, high-tech garbage there.
China will name all missions to study other planets Tianwen ("Questions to the Sky") - after the ancient work of the poet Qu Yuan Landing will be broken down into four stages.
First, the aerodynamic brake will slow the device from 4.8 km / s to 460 m / s.
Then the parachute will open, which will reduce the speed to 95 m / s., and then reverse engines will go in the course.
They'll slow the lander down to 3.5 m / s.
The final stage of braking starts at a mark of only 100 m from the surface of the planet.
Ideally, it will end with a soft landing, after which the rover will smoothly move to the surface of the planet.
The first Chinese rover will be equipped with several scientific instruments, including a GPR.
With the help of this device, he will be able to literally look underground.
Earlier this year, this tool helped archaeologists without excavation to make a map of the ancient Roman city, which for many years rests underground.
The rover will not have to search for lost settlements, but he will be able to examine underground geological objects with the help of GPR.
As in the case of the Arab mission to Mars, the Chinese pursue not only scientific goals.
First, it will be a major test of the country ’ s technological achievements.
Secondly, it has a strong reputation subtext.
China already has a successful lunar program – in January last year, its Chang ’ e 4 research apparatus was the first in history to make a soft landing on the far side of the moon.
In early summer, the country launched the last satellite in its global navigation system, which will compete with the American GPS.
Conquering Mars will strengthen China ’ s position as the world ’ s leading space power.
Perseverance and resourcefulness Country: USA Start date: July 30, 2020
Arrival time: February 18, 2021 Type of research vehicle: Rover and helicopter Planned duration of the mission: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: search for traces of the existence of life in the past, collect samples, prepare for future missions with the participation of people In the conquest of Mars, the United States is the leader.
The local aerospace agency NASA was the first to deliver a research probe to the Red Planet, the first to land a lander there that lasted longer than a few seconds, its rovers were the first to wheel on the surface of another world.
Today, three of its probes orbit Mars, two more research vehicles are working on the surface of the planet, and soon they will be joined by another.
NASA will send a new rover Perseverance (“Perseverance ”).
The American space agency has a tradition, according to which the names for rovers come up with schoolchildren.
NASA did not deviate from it this time.
The name of the rover "Perseverance" was born in the head of seventh-grader Alexander Mazer, who believed that this feature of human character should be immortalized in it.
In an essay in which the student explained his choice, he noted that in the conquest of Mars, humanity can wait for many difficulties, but it is perseverance that will not allow him to give up and help move towards the goal, no matter what.
However, Perseverance can boast not only a loud name.
Despite its resemblance to Curiosity, which has been traveling on Mars since 2012, the new rover has the most modern technical equipment.
NASA calls Perseverance the most advanced of the rovers he created.
"There is every reason to believe that in the coming years Mars and all its secrets will become more and more understandable to the inhabitants of the Earth" Carl Sagan, astronomer He is equipped with a number of scientific tools that will help him monitor important meteorological indicators (humidity, temperature, wind speed, etc.), recognize the chemical composition of materials on the surface, consider objects the size of a grain of salt and look for organic compounds that would indicate the existence of Martian life in the past or have been exposed. impact of water.
In addition, Perseverance will be able to look under the surface of the planet using GPR and extract oxygen from carbon dioxide.
Finally, the rover will have a modern camera.
At one time, Curiosity became famous for the pictures he took.
He sent to Earth selfies, images of a solar eclipse on Mars and other stunning alien species.
Perseverance also promises to be an outstanding photojournalist.
Its camera will allow you to take color panoramic and 3D photos, as well as conduct video shooting.
This equipment will need the rover to perform the key scientific tasks assigned to it.
First of all, Perseverance will have to look for any evidence that there was life on Mars in the past.
It could be a medium in which it could exist, or a substance whose properties, chemical composition or structure would indicate that it was created by some form of life.
In addition, Perseverance will have to collect samples of soil and stones stacked and sealed in tubes.
The tubes will be stored on board the rover until scientists find a suitable place to leave them until new missions arrive on Mars and take them back to Earth.
Together with the scientific tools and the first “Martian ” Rover Perseverance will deliver to Mars three chips with the names of 10 million people and Perseverance will begin to prepare the ground for a human visit to Mars in the future.
To do this, he will need the above-mentioned tool for extracting oxygen from CO2.
In the Martian atmosphere, oxygen is contained in negligible quantities, its share is much less than 1%.
But carbon dioxide is the dominant gas, in the air of Mars it is about 95%.
Therefore, scientists want to try out the technology of extracting the much-needed gas from the most common.
If the instrument works as it should, it will mean that in the future such systems can be sent to Mars, where they will store oxygen.
And when the first astronauts arrive on the Red Planet, they will already have a resource for breathing and rocket fuel.
Perseverance will fly to Mars in the company of the Ingenuity helicopter, which may go down in history as the first device to fly on another planet.
According to calculations, it will be able to rise to a height of 3-4 m, spend up to 90 seconds in the air and cover a distance of 300 m. It would seem that not the most impressive indicators, if you do not think about how difficult it is to fly in the thin Martian atmosphere.
Its density is only 1% of the density of the Earth's atmosphere.
On our planet, such conditions can be observed only at an altitude of 30 km.
For comparison, commercial aircraft today fly at a maximum of 13 kilometers altitude.
NASA engineers have solved this problem.
Ground tests in a vacuum chamber where the Martian atmosphere was simulated showed that Ingenuity could fly.
Now they are waiting for the opportunity to test it in real alien conditions.
If successful, it could pave the way for an entirely new type of mechanical Martian explorers.
After all, aircraft are able to look into places inaccessible to land machines.
Now the main thing is that Perseverance and Ingenuity managed to squeeze into a narrow launch window, due to the favorable location of the planets.
Currently, the mission is scheduled to start on July 30, but NASA has repeatedly shifted the date.
If the agency does not have time to launch the rover before mid-August, then the next attempt will have to wait until 2022.

title: Experts alarmed: “pandemic fatigue ” of people from coronavirus is fraught with danger
text:
Millions of people are now experiencing “fatigue ” from the coronavirus.
And experts fear that “pandemic fatigue ” is forcing many to ignore COVID-19 prevention recommendations and restrictions.
Therefore, often forgotten and hand washing, and wearing masks, and keeping a distance with other people.
This crisis fatigue is understandable, but experts warn people against its consequences.
Hong Kong ’ s South China Morning Post cites the example of 28-year-old Hong Kong accountant Dick Wong, who admits that he has become less likely to wash his hands, but feels a growing need to meet friends on the street, despite knowing he shouldn ’ t.
The young man said he was tired of the precautions in place since the coronavirus hit Hong Kong in January.
At first, Dick Wong was so afraid of getting infected that he was willing to do anything to protect himself.
He followed the news closely, changed his mask every four hours, cleaned and disinfected his house every day, no matter how late he came home.
I haven ’ t seen my friends in two months.
Now he feels exhausted physically and mentally from stress due to fear of infection, social isolation and changes in his daily life.
Dick Wong is disappointed that all his efforts have failed to end the crisis.
Not only has the pandemic persisted, but it has worsened dramatically in Hong Kong, where there has been a spike in new cases this month.
“Now I can barely gain the strength to do something, ” he says. – For many months, I was kept as alert as possible and took all necessary measures to protect myself from infection.
It made me very tired. ”
According to the South China Morning Post, Dick Wong is not alone in experiencing what experts call “pandemic fatigue. ”
With the global health crisis dragging on for more than six months with no end in sight, many have become increasingly disillusioned with the precautions surrounding COVID-19.
Experts warn that such an attitude could exacerbate the consequences of the crisis.
In Hong Kong, a new surge in infections has raised the number of confirmed cases to 2,300, with 16 deaths.
Despite this new wave of coronavirus, many Hong Kongers ignore health warnings and flock to beaches, some without masks.
Others refuse to wear masks on public transport, although the government has ordered them to do so, threatening a maximum fine of HK $5,000.
Recently, it was mandatory to wear masks in all closed public places.
Clinical psychologist Cherry Lin Liong of the Hong Kong Red Cross says pandemic fatigue is a psychosocial phenomenon caused by prolonged periods of wakefulness, reduced fear of a pandemic, changing daily routines and uncertainty in life.
Those who suffer from this phenomenon feel physical and mental fatigue, some become less alert and more relaxed about precautions.
“People don ’ t wash their hands as often as they do at the beginning of an outbreak, ” says Cherry Lin, adding that others are beginning to neglect the advice that it ’ s best not to go outside.
Psychiatrist Dr. Hui Lunkit says pandemic fatigue began to hit people as early as March, when the crisis was severe, despite measures taken to limit freedom and social exclusion.
Many have been disappointed that their efforts have failed to bring the pandemic under control, he says.
“Pandemic fatigue can, on the one hand, make the public less anxious and scared, but on the other hand, it can cause people to weaken their defenses, ” the psychiatrist said.
Infectious disease expert Dr. Joseph Tsang Kaiyan believes that pandemic fatigue may have contributed to the recurrence of COVID-19 cases.
He says this change in attitude needs to be taken seriously, otherwise it could exacerbate the crisis.
The prolonged pandemic is also affecting people with mental health problems.
Chin Chikon, deputy director of the Hong Kong Mental Health Association, a non-profit organization, warns that pandemic fatigue can have a detrimental effect on both individuals and society.
“The significant changes brought about by the pandemic have put tremendous pressure on people, and prolonged stressors, both physical and emotional, can lead to mental problems, ” he says.
The expert adds that fatigue also affects people ’ s activities at work and can worsen their relationships, while at the same time making all people more calm about the precautions against the pandemic or abandoning them, which poses a threat to public health.
The expert believes that it is important to recognize and overcome pandemic fatigue, especially since the pandemic is unlikely to end in the near future.
He suggests developing new procedures to restore a sense of control in life, such as allocating time for sports, using technology to stay in touch with family and friends, and having a clear view of time for work and leisure.
Clinical psychologist Dr. Eliza Chun Yilai, head of psychological support for the Hong Kong Red Cross, says authorities and the public need a change in strategies to combat pandemic fatigue as the fear of coronavirus no longer works as it used to: “The pandemic has been going on for so long that people have passed the stage of purely motivated fear that dictates the need to take protective measures. ”
Dr. Chung says that people who know they have pandemic fatigue should recognize that taking precautions will protect themselves, their communities, and the entire community.
Source: https: / / www.mk.ru /

title: In France, with the participation of Rosatom, the assembly of a thermonuclear reactor began
text:
In the research center Kadarach in the south of France, the ceremony of the start of the assembly of the international thermonuclear reactor ITER (ITER, International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) took place.
The event was broadcast online on YouTube.
The ceremony was addressed by French President Emmanuel Macron, ITER Director General Bernard Bigot, the head of Rosatom State Corporation Alexey Likhachev and other high-ranking guests.
“There are times when different countries overcome existing differences in order to make a common contribution to history.
Such a project, which can become a scientific breakthrough and a unifying factor for many states, is ITER.
I am proud that it is in France that a project will be implemented that will become the future of humanity, ” said Emmanuel Macron, who spoke via video link from the Elysee Palace.
In turn, the head of Rosatom Alexey Likhachev voiced a welcome speech to the project participants on behalf of President Vladimir Putin, and then addressed his colleagues with a congratulatory speech on his own behalf.
“This is an important event for the entire thermonuclear community and, of course, for the entire world science.
It is important that, despite the restrictions caused by the coronavirus epidemic, the assembly and installation work begins according to the schedule, ” Likhachev said.
According to him, now the main task of the project participants is the successful installation of the installation and obtaining the first plasma by the end of 2025.
“This will allow us to demonstrate in practice the coherence of actions of all participants in the project and the final effectiveness of our international cooperation.
Russia fulfills all its obligations in the ITER project to make natural and financial contributions in full and in accordance with the schedule, ” he said.
In the creation of the experimental tokamak reactor (tokamak – toroidal chamber with magnetic coils) ITER involved 35 countries: the EU countries, as well as Russia, the United States, India, China, South Korea and Japan.
The purpose of the project is to prove the scientific and technical feasibility of obtaining thermonuclear energy for peaceful purposes.
Russia will supply high-tech equipment in the amount of 9.1% of the cost of the reactor.
In particular, the equipment system "Switching equipment, busbars and energy-absorbing resistors for power supply and protection of the superconducting magnetic system of the ITER reactor" - the most expensive and one of the most complex in the reactor - is 100% Russia's responsibility.

text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed special gratitude to French leader Emmanuel Macron for the assistance of Paris in the implementation of the project of the international experimental thermonuclear reactor ITER.

The greeting of the Russian leader to the participants of the ceremony was read by Alexey Likhachev, Director General of Rosatom State Corporation.
“I would like to sincerely thank everyone who has been working on the ITER project for many years.
Special thanks to French President Emmanuel Macron as the leader of the host country of the project, which provides a site for the reactor and provides invaluable assistance in its construction, ” Putin said in his greeting, wishing the project participants new success and all the best.
The President also called the ITER project a vivid example of effective international cooperation, RIA Novosti reports.
He recalled that Russia is one of the founding countries of the ITER initiative, which is designed to make an important contribution to ensuring the energy security of mankind, and plays an active role in the implementation of this project.
The ITER project is based on the concept of the Tokamak installation developed in Russia, the Russian leader noted.
The ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) demonstration reactor is being built near the Cadarache Research Center in southern France, jointly by the European Union, Russia, China, India, Japan, South Korea and the United States.
This will be the first large-scale attempt to show the possibility of using a thermonuclear reaction to generate energy on an industrial scale.
If the ITER project is successful, humanity will be able to count on the possession of an almost inexhaustible source of energy.
It is planned that the launch of the reactor and the production of the first plasma on it will take place in 2025.
A total of 35 countries take part in the ITER project, including 29 countries of the European Union, as well as Russia, the United States, India, China, Japan, South Korea.
United Europe, as the host country of the ITER reactor, contributes 45% of the cost of construction of the installation, the rest of the countries, including Russia, contribute 9% each.

title: In France will assemble the world ’ s first “clean ” fusion reactor
text:
The project is experimental and international – 35 countries take part in it.
One of the important features of the development is environmentally friendly technology of nuclear fusion.
In Provence, in the south of France, began to assemble an experimental thermonuclear reactor ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor).
The event took place online on July 28 and was broadcast on YouTube.
ITER is supposed to reproduce the physical reactions that occur on the Sun and other stars, and at the same time demonstrate the possibility of using fusion energy in the future.
The basis of the reactor is the tokamak magnetic trap (toroidal chamber with magnetic coils).
In it, the magnetic field holds the plasma, in which the thermonuclear reaction occurs.
Tokamaks appeared in the USSR in the 1960s.
For ITER will build the largest tokamak in the world with a volume of 830 cubic meters.
In tokamak, deuterium and tritium (heavy isotopes of hydrogen) are launched and heated to a temperature of about 150 million degrees Celsius.
See also: Bill Gates finished his Chinese nuclear program Photo: vilferelectric.com ITER will consist of a million parts and weigh 23 thousand tons at a height of 30 meters.
Now all the necessary parts for its assembly are manufactured and delivered to the construction site.
In 2025, it is planned to launch and obtain the first plasma.
The creation of ITER was agreed by the governments of the United States and the USSR in 1985, over time, the project had other participants.
Now the project is being worked on: the EU with Switzerland (46% of the costs), the US, Russia, India, China, South Korea and Japan (each – 9%).
Modern tokamaks emit less energy than is spent on heating the system, so it is not suitable for generating energy.
Due to the scale of the ITER design, the creators expect that it will be able to allocate energy ten times more than is spent on heating plasma (give 500 MW from 50 MW).
If the ITER experiments are successful, the next stage (from 2030) will be DEMO, a prototype fusion reactor for power plants.
They can appear in the 2040-2050s.
India, Russia, South Korea and Japan expressed their desire to build such reactors.
Recall, in the United States, a team of scientists said that it is going to print the core of the reactor on a 3D printer.
They have already decided on the design and components, and printed a prototype, and are currently working on improving it.
Bill Gates, one of the founders of Microsoft, is confident that nuclear energy will be able to help in the fight against climate change.
He said he was personally willing to invest $1 billion.
