title: Tyumen scientists conduct observations at the biological station "Lake Kuchak"
text:
Tyumen scientists conduct observations at the biological station "Lake Kuchak" | Photo: Tyumen State University | Photo: Tyumen State University Regular observations of the growth and development of various field crops, taking into account the impact on plants of meteorological factors on the experimental site of the biological station of Tyumen State University "Lake Kuchak" are carried out by scientists of the Institute of Biology of Tyumen State University since May 2020, according to the Department of Strategic Communications of the university.
The territory is a natural testing ground for the study of ecological plasticity of plants and the selection of forms with high adaptive potential.
As explained by the head of the Department of Botany, Biotechnology and Landscape Architecture of Tyumen State University, Professor Nina Bome, the growing season of 2020 is characterized by an extremely uneven distribution in time of precipitation and air temperature.
Drought-resistant forms of cultivated plants that have the ability to adapt to the temperature stresses of the environment acquire practical value.
The success of the introduction of cultivated species can be achieved only with the right selection of varieties and the development of elements of regional cultivation technology.
In this regard, plant forms created by scientists of the Institute of Biology with the help of modern genetic and biotechnological methods are of particular value: chemical mutagenesis, hybridization, selection.
In total, about 800 experimental variants of the genetic diversity of cultivated plants were included in the research.
Some research projects are carried out in partnership with scientific and educational Russian and foreign centers.

title: Britain and France were on the verge of a scandal - because of illegal immigrants
text:
Against the background of the heat in France and Britain, the political climate in relations between the two countries is heating up.
London has accused Paris of turning a blind eye to illegal immigrants who cross the English Channel in boats by the hundreds.
In response, France demanded 33 million euros from Britain to strengthen border control.
But in London they decided that they themselves will be able to block the English Channel for migrants.
As reported by Day.Az with reference to Vesti, the UK and France were on the verge of a diplomatic scandal due to the invasion of illegal migrants.
This year, about four thousand people have already moved from the French coast to English.
Taking advantage of the warm weather and relatively calm sea, hundreds of migrants cross the English Channel daily in inflatable boats.
One of these groups was discovered near Dover by BBC News journalists.
“We see people in the boat trying to draw water from there.
They use a plastic container for this.
The boat is obviously overloaded.
They're all wearing life jackets, but this trip doesn't look safe.
Let me talk to them, ” says a British journalist.
They reach not only in crowded boats, but even on inflatable kayaks.
Instead of oars, shovels are often used.
The British press writes about a migrant who tried to cross the English Channel by swimming, tied with empty plastic bottles.
The leader of the Brexit party Nigel Farage published on Twitter a video in which unstopped migrants quietly land on the desert coast of Kent.
He accused the French authorities of inaction.
“The French say that when they try to bring migrants back to their shores, they resist because they don ’ t want to go back to France.
As a result, French ships actually accompany them through the English Strait, ” the politician said.
Farage demands that the illegals be turned to sea and sent back to France.
So did the Australian authorities with the refugees from Indonesia.
"We transplanted them into large orange boats with a motor, towed them to a twelve-mile zone near the Indonesian coast and said goodbye to them there," said then-Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott.
Following the example of the former colony, British Home Secretary Preeti Patel is already ready to act.
The way of the boats are going to be blocked with the help of floating barriers and nets.
It is planned to involve warships and military aircraft to patrol the strait.
"The Royal Navy is always ready to come to the aid of the country and the government in order to take control of the situation," said Rear Admiral Chris Perry.
Tough measures are supported by many residents of the coastal areas of England.
“There is an unacceptable situation – people who are sailing here are already safe on French territory and should remain there.
France should be responsible for them, ” said Natalie Elfik, a member of the British House of Commons.
The British Minister for Migration Chris Philp went to Paris on August 11 to convince his French colleagues.
But on the other side of the river, they think the British are to blame.
"The British are accusing us because of their own hypocrisy.
Migrants seek to the UK because there they have the conditions for illegal work.
Nobody controls them there, ” said Philippe Mignon, deputy mayor of the French city of Calais.
In the reasoning of the British Prime Minister Boris Johnson sounded notes peculiar to his colleague and friend Donald Trump.
“We have a problem with people who come to us from all over the world because it is obvious that we have a beautiful country!
We need to cooperate with our French friends and resolve the issue with the legislative system.
It turns out that if people come to us, it is very difficult to send them back, even if they came here illegally, ” said Johnson.
A few years ago, the British insisted that the French remove a large refugee camp called the Jungle near the port of Calais.
There is no camp, but the situation has not improved.
There is a thriving criminal business of transporting people.
Those who fight illegal immigrants have their own mathematics.
London has already allocated about 114 million pounds for joint projects with France to protect the border.
If the French do not become more active, they threatened to stop funding.
Paris is unlikely to be terrified by this.
Migrants sailing in the direction of England on the French coast are also not needed.

title: Syngenta CEO: the company ’ s share in the Russian market is 4% and will grow
text:
Syngenta CEO: the company ’ s share in the Russian market is 4% and will grow Eric Firvald told Interfax about the impact of the US trade war with China, production in Russia and “green ” technologies Syngenta CEO Eric Firvald Photo: Anatoly Medved / TASS Moscow.
11 October.
The agricultural sector is increasingly in the center of attention of the world market both in connection with the trade conflict between the United States and China, in which the purchase of American agricultural products is one of the main trump cards of Beijing, and in connection with climate change issues.
Eric Firvald, CEO of the Swiss-Chinese company Syngenta, the largest supplier of plant protection products and seeds in Russia, expressed his opinion on international problems, as well as on the prospects of the Russian market in an interview with Interfax. - When the Chinese ChemChina acquired Syngenta in 2017, it was said that the company would return to the stock exchange within five years, provided the favorable market situation.
How do you assess the current market conditions, is the IPO being prepared? - Preparations are underway.
I assess the current market environment as challenging, especially this year due to flooding in the US and drought in Australia.
In Russia, however, things are relatively good.
Preparations for IPO are underway.
We plan to continue the preparatory activities next year and conduct the placement by 2022, while market conditions are favorable and the company shows strong results. - Given that you are an American leading a Chinese company, how do you assess the recent events of the US trade war with China? - Syngenta and the industry as a whole supports open trade.
We believe that the fewer trade barriers, the better for everyone, for consumers and for the growth of the global economy.
It is a pity that China and the United States are in a state of trade war, and we hope that it will end soon.
As a result of the trade conflict, American farmers have essentially lost access to the huge Chinese market, now they have to either stockpile their products or sell them to other countries.
Some agricultural products from the US have recently been shipped to Brazil, where they have been used as fodder, and Brazil has been shipping its goods to China.
This is due to additional logistics costs and a decrease in market efficiency.
In addition, the US is our largest market, and we are upset about the current state of affairs.
Syngenta ’ s position is that the trade conflict is not a catastrophic factor, but we hope that it will be resolved. – Tell us more about the situation in Russia.
- First, I would like to note the efforts of the Russian government, Russian farmers and the industry as a whole, thanks to which it was possible to significantly increase not only the self-sufficiency of the country in terms of agricultural production, but also to increase exports.
The production of many crops is increasing.
Syngenta has played its part in this success by providing its products, technology and scientific support.
This year, our business in Russia is growing, which allows us to increase investments in the Russian market, thereby demonstrating support for the agricultural sector and confidence in the future of the sector.
We expect that the growth rate of our business in Russia this year will be measured by a single digit in the range from medium to high.
- By investments, you mean plans to build a plant in the Lipetsk region, or do you have other large projects? - In addition to this project, we are creating the Institute for Seed Protection in order to provide the Russian market with the latest developments in this area, which can significantly increase yields.
We are also expanding our efforts in the field of seed production. - The two most important businesses for Syngenta are the production of seeds and plant protection products (SPP).
Two years ago, you said that in the world, the company ranks first in the SPR segment and third in the production of seeds, which you intend to strengthen.
- In addition to organic growth, which is outpacing the average market, we made a number of acquisitions, including the purchase of Nidera Seeds, which was the largest transaction in Syngenta ’ s history.
Nidera is the leader in soybean and corn seed production in Brazil and Argentina.
In addition, we acquired the American company Abbott & Cobb, which is engaged in the production of vegetable seeds and, in particular, sugar corn.
Thanks to these and other acquisitions, we have consolidated our third position in the seed production segment and remain the world leader in the production of crop protection products.
In Russia, we rank first in both segments. - What is the share of each segment in your revenue? - In Russia, seeds account for about 40% of sales, in SPR - about 60%. - How important is the Russian market for the company as a whole? - Russia accounts for slightly less than 4% of Syngenta's total revenue.
Our business in Russia demonstrates good growth rates, and it is very important for the company as a whole.
We expect that the share of the Russian market in our sales will increase in the future. - In what directions do you see the main opportunities for growth? - The production of corn is actively growing, and taking into account climate change, now corn can be grown in more northern regions, up to the Moscow region, where this crop did not grow before.
Climate change is a major global problem that also brings new opportunities, as in the example of corn.
At the same time, climate change is also fraught with droughts, especially in the southern regions, and in response we have developed a corn variety that is more resistant to arid conditions.
This is how we help farmers overcome the challenges posed by climate change.
We also have digital solutions for farmers, and they are actively gaining popularity.
We have an application that contains satellite images of agricultural land around the world.
For example, in the United States, where this year was the worst flood in history, farmers can see from the pictures where the water has already left, and begin to sow these areas in the first place.
We also offer a weather insurance program for Russian customers.
That is, customers purchase our seeds, and in case of emergency weather conditions, we reimburse them for part of the costs.
In 2018, 31 Russian agricultural companies took part in the program, including the largest agricultural holdings - Miratorg and Ekoniva.
On the part of insurance companies, our partner is Japanese Sompo Japan. - Do you see increased competition from Russian seed producers and crop protection? - Competition from Russian companies has always been strong, and I do not see changes in this regard.
Our advantage lies in the international experience, thanks to which we help local agricultural companies understand the needs of the world market with an eye on exports, including to China. - What share of products sold in Russia do you currently produce in our country, and what are the successes of Syngenta on the way to the goal - to produce 80% of products sold in the local market in Russia? - Progress is, and we will fulfill our commitment to bring the level of localization of production of plant protection products to 80%% by 2021.
Now the share of seeds produced in Russia is 35-40% of sales, SPR - a little more, and after the opening of a new plant in the Lipetsk region, the figure will grow even stronger.
It is worth noting that, moving towards this goal, we pay special attention to maintaining the highest quality standards in Russian production. - And in the future you are considering the possibility of exporting your products in Russia? - Everything is possible, and if we have free capacity, we will consider the issue of exports.
First of all, this will apply to the EAEU countries.
However, the plant in Lipetsk first of all is aimed at meeting the demand in the Russian market. - Where else do you produce your products in Russia? - In the field of crop protection is Kirovo-Chepetsk.
The construction of the plant in the Lipetsk region will begin within a few weeks, while we will continue to use the capacities of our partner in Kirovo-Chepetsk.
In terms of seeds, we produce our own hybrids in Russia.
But I would like to note that in Russia, it takes about five years to approve a new hybrid variety, which is two years longer than in the rest of the world.
Therefore, I believe that we need to work with other companies in the industry and with government representatives to accelerate the production of hybrids while maintaining strict regulatory requirements.
Thus, we will maintain the competitive position of Russia in comparison with other countries.
In addition, to maintain Russia ’ s leading position in the global agricultural market, it is necessary to establish clear and scientifically based rules for new technologies, such as genome editing.
This technology is supported by the authorities of the United States, Brazil, Canada, China.
Europe does not yet know what to do with this technology - there is talk that it can be equated with GMOs and, accordingly, abandon it.
At the same time, the technology can significantly accelerate natural selection processes without the use of third-party DNA.
We call on the Russian government to consider the development of regulations for genome editing technology in order to strengthen a competitive advantage. - Is there a demand for "green" technologies in Russia? - We see such a demand.
It is smaller than in Western Europe, but there is no doubt that demand exists.
And this applies not only to producers, but also to consumers.
Interest in environmental issues is growing, and we see this when we communicate with government officials, with our customers.
Russia is no different from other regions.
In my opinion, Russia ’ s desire to increase agricultural exports will also result in a desire to make production more environmentally friendly, because importing countries are increasingly demanding this.
I see this as a huge opportunity for Russia, and Syngenta is ready to help.
In the world, CO2 emissions are important for many large companies buying agricultural products.
In particular, this is the company Kellogg, which indicates the amount of greenhouse gas emissions in their production and, accordingly, prefers manufacturers with low emissions.
Thus, by reducing emissions and producing environmentally friendly products, farmers have the opportunity to increase profits.
Consumers increasingly want to know where their food was grown and how, and this trend carries huge opportunities for the agricultural sector. – What about the increased demand for organic agricultural products that do not use pesticides, which make up an important part of your business? – It is not.
Manufacturers of organic products use a lot of pesticides, and many of them are our customers.
Unfortunately, there is a misconception, in part caused by lack of transparency on the part of producers, that organic products are grown without pesticides.
In fact, they often use far more pesticides because their production is less efficient.
Organic farming has a negative impact on climate change.
It yields 35-40% less yield, and therefore requires more land on which trees could grow.
Organic farming technologies, including the release of CO2 from the soil into the atmosphere.
From an environmental point of view, this is not very good, but consumers like the feeling that they are buying “natural ” products, and we understand that.
We believe that the right solution is to effectively use technology to safely grow products that are healthy, of high quality and reduce the impact of the agricultural industry on climate change.
The agricultural sector and the food industry account for 25% of global greenhouse gas emissions, and given the growing population, an increase in organic farming will only exacerbate the situation.
We need to find a way to get more crops from a smaller area, while using less pesticides of higher quality.
By the way, thanks to the improvement in the quality of pesticides over the past 50 years, the amount of plant protection products per hectare of arable land has decreased by 95%.
For example, in Italy there is a high demand for organic products, and because of this farmers use copper-based preparations - and I do not think that the huge amounts of copper poured on the soil are better than a small amount of modern synthetic pesticides.
In New Zealand, the largest producer of apples has sharply reduced organic production, precisely because of the use of very large amounts of pesticides.
And this year in Austria was completely destroyed the harvest of organic potatoes due to blight.
Syngenta identifies three main areas in which the company can best help stop or slow climate change.
These are increasing yields so that farmers use less land while increasing production, improving tillage technologies so that it does not emit CO2 into the atmosphere, and restoring unsuitable land.

title: Palestine withdraws its ambassador from UAE
text:
Palestine has announced the withdrawal of its ambassador from the UAE after their decision to normalize relations with Israel.
This was stated on Thursday by the Minister of foreign Affairs of Palestine Riyad al-Maliki.
“At the direction of the President of the State of Palestine, Mahmoud Abbas, the Palestinian ambassador is urgently withdrawing from the UAE after a trilateral statement by the United States, Israel and the Emirates on the normalization of relations between Israel and the UAE, ” the minister said.
On Thursday, US President Donald Trump announced on his Twitter page that Israel and the UAE have reached an agreement on the full normalization of bilateral relations.
According to the agreements, Israel will temporarily suspend the decision to extend its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank, which is provided for by the American plan for the settlement of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
The delegations of Israel and the UAE plan to hold a meeting in the coming weeks to sign bilateral agreements, including on investment, tourism, direct flights, security, telecommunications, technology, energy, health, culture, environment, mutual establishment of embassies, as well as in other areas.
The Palestinian leadership has already reacted harshly to this move by Abu Dhabi, calling it a betrayal and “the destruction of the Arab peace initiative. ”
Nabil Abu Rudeina, spokesman for the Palestinian president, said the agreement between the UAE and Israel to normalize relations under US sponsorship "is a betrayal of al-Aqsa, Jerusalem and the Palestinian cause."
He also warned other Arab states not to “submit to the pressure of the US administration and follow in the footsteps ” of the UAE.

title: North Korea Seizes Ship With Russian Fishermen
text:
In the Sea of Japan, the North Korean military seized a Russian ship with fishermen, Kommersant writes with reference to the deputy head of the North-Eastern fishing company Sergei Sedler.
Sedler said it all happened early on the morning of July 17.
North Korean border guards on the move landed on the fishing vessel "Xianghailin-8".
It is known that on board are 15 citizens of Russia, as well as two citizens of South Korea.
The ship sailed to the Sea of Japan for crab mining.
All the people on board were sent to the DPRK.
Sailors are held in cabins, where, according to Sedler, twice a day are severely interrogated and searched.
The captain of the ship, his assistant and two South Koreans were sent under arrest to a hotel.
An interesting fact is that diplomats of the Russian Embassy in Pyongyang were able to visit the ship only on July 23, almost a week after the incident.
In North Korea, they say that the ship and sailors were detained allegedly because of illegal crossing of the border.
However, such a border, also called the “military protection zone ”, North Korea has arbitrarily established 50 nautical miles from the coast.
There are no official data in international documents on the possibility of creating such a zone.

title: Online conference of Palestinian Ambassador to Russia Abdel Hafiz Nofal
text:
On August 13, Israel and the UAE reached an agreement on the full normalization of relations, as the leaders of Israel, the UAE and the United States announced in a joint statement.
Calling the agreement historic, they expressed the hope that it will contribute to peace in the Middle East.
The Palestinian leadership regarded the signed agreement as a betrayal and an act of aggression against its people, calling it an attempt to undermine existing peace initiatives in the Middle East.
In this regard, Palestine recalled its ambassador from the UAE.

title: Palestinians protest Israeli-UAE deal
text:
Over the weekend, Palestinians held protests across the West Bank and Gaza, condemning the announced deal to normalize relations between Israel and the UAE, calling it a betrayal of their cause and a blow to Arab solidarity.
Protesters carried Palestinian flags and stomped photos of Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu before setting them on fire in the center of Ramallah in the West Bank.
They also burned photos of US President Donald Trump, who brokered the deal, and Palestinian politician Mohammed Dahlan, who currently resides in the UAE.
Similar demonstrations were also held near the Al-Aqsa Mosque on the Temple Mount (Haram al-Sharif) in Jerusalem.
Most Arab states have historically refused to formally establish diplomatic relations with Israel in protest of its occupation of lands that the Palestinians consider their own.
According to the agreement, the signing of which was announced, as reported by Pravda.Ru, at the end of last week, the UAE agreed to normalize relations with Tel Aviv in exchange for Israel suspending its plans to formally annex the West Bank.
The UAE is the third Arab country to do so, after Egypt and Jordan.
The move was seen by the US and Israel as a breakthrough towards greater peace in the region.
The Palestinians, however, overwhelmingly condemned the deal, calling it "treason" and "betrayal."
Mustafa Barghouti, general secretary of the National Initiative party, said in an interview with RT Ruptly video that the agreement is “a stab in the back of the Palestinian people ”:“ It actually violates the Arab solidarity agreed upon by the resolutions of all Arab countries. ” (RT quote) The agreement has also been criticized by Iran, with President Hassan Rouhani calling it a “huge mistake. ”

title: In France, began the assembly of an experimental fusion reactor
text:
France begins the assembly of the International Experimental Thermonuclear Reactor (ITER) - the largest research technology project in history.
More than $25 billion has already been spent on it, and the completion of the construction of the complex and its test launch is expected no earlier than 2025.
This is stated in a press release of the project, also Le Figaro writes about it.
The reactor, which will have to confirm the possibility of controlled thermonuclear fusion at industrial power, is being built at the Cadarache research center in the commune of Saint-Paul-le-Durance.
The largest components of the tokamak are already in place.
The scale of the project is comparable to the largest in the history of mankind – the creation and maintenance of the International Space Station and the Large Hadron Collider.
Tokamak is a device for magnetic plasma retention in order to achieve the conditions necessary for the flow of controlled thermonuclear fusion.
At the end of 2015 in Germany successfully passed the test launches of the fusion reactor Wendelstein 7-X Stellarator, in early February 2016 there received the first sample of hydrogen plasma.
At the same time, China successfully tested its thermonuclear reactor.
At the beginning of 2016, the efficiency of the fusion reactor was quadrupled in the United States.
At the end of 2019, the Canadian startup General Fusion received $100 million for a nuclear fusion reactor.
We'll remind you
ITER is a project of an international (EU, Japan, India, Korea, USA, China, Russia and others) experimental thermonuclear reactor based on the tokamak installation, laid down in 2005, to demonstrate the possibility of commercial use of a thermonuclear reactor, which is considered as yet unattainable.
The design capacity of ITER is about 500 MW of heat and about 200 MW of electricity.
Built since 2007 on 180 hectares of territory 60 km from Marseille.
This type of reactor is much safer than a nuclear reactor.
In Ukraine, they plan to introduce small nuclear reactors NuScale.

title: The WHO told about the consequences for the psyche of people caused by the coronavirus pandemic
text:
Millions of people around the world have faced mental problems due to coronavirus infection and related restrictions.
About the large number of inhabitants of the Earth who experienced difficulties with mental health due to the pandemic, said the Director General of the World Health Organization (WHO) Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus at a briefing in Geneva.
The recording of the speech was published on the video hosting Youtube.
Sudden changes in lifestyle and uncertainty about the future have increased anxiety in many people.
The feeling of fear has also increased.
The situation was complicated by the fact that psychological assistance services sometimes could not fully work due to restrictions.
The regime of self-isolation and the ban on the operation of many institutions has negatively affected the mental state of people in many countries.
Restrictive measures have had a bad effect on their condition.
In addition, reduced to a minimum social contacts could also lead people into a depressive state, as they often began to be alone with themselves in a confined space.
It is worth noting that psychological health problems are experienced by about 1 billion people on the planet.
At the same time, not all of them can get affordable, qualified and timely help.
Earlier, gazeta.spb.ru reported that Rospotrebnadzor allowed the possibility of re-infection with coronavirus.

title: Covid-19 does not cause significant harm to children - British scientists
text:
British researchers believe that children most often have a mild course of Covid-19.
Researchers from the UK came to the conclusion that children and young people are most often observed mild course of the disease Covid-19.
Also rarely recorded deaths among minors associated with the coronavirus.
This is reported by The Guardian.
After analyzing the course of the coronavirus in patients from 138 British medical institutions, the experts concluded that among hospitalized children, the figure is less than 1 percent.
The author of the study, Professor Malcolm Sample of the University of Liverpool, assured that Covid-19 itself does not cause significant harm to children.
The day before, the team of Professor studied the data of 651 children aged 0 to 19 years.
All were hospitalized between January 17 and July 3.
Six children died, but before being infected with the coronavirus, they suffered from serious illnesses or had health disorders.
"The six children who died had profound comorbidities, and this is a strikingly low mortality rate compared to 27% in all age groups of Covid-19 patients hospitalized in the same time interval," the experts said.
According to global data on the spread of coronavirus, children and young people account for only 1 to 2 per cent of cases worldwide.
In most of them, the disease proceeds easily or generally asymptomatic.
Scientists noted that some minors, in addition to the typical symptoms of coronavirus - fever, shortness of breath and coughing, experienced sore throat, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea and rashes.
Almost 2.5 thousand patients and 48 deaths: in Ukraine a new coronavirus record The head of the World Health Organization Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said that the pandemic Covid-19 affected the mental health of millions of people around the world.

title: The Impossible Dream of the Empire
text:
Although the Republic of Turkey has existed since 1923, there are still many people in the country who are enthusiastic about the former Ottoman Empire and its achievements.
The history of Hagia Sophia and its transformation into a mosque is a logical testament to this enthusiasm, which in a sense shows the modern face of Turkey.
Serhun Al, an associate professor at the University of Izmir, told TVNET about Hagia Sophia and Turkey ’ s worldview.
Serhoun Al PHOTO: TVNET Serhoun Al is an associate professor at the Faculty of Political Science and International Relations of the University of Izmir.
He received his doctorate from the University of Utah in the United States.
His academic interests are related to identity, ethnic conflicts and security issues in the context of Turkish-Kurdish relations.
Are the ideas of a secular state still alive? - I would say that Turkey is still a relatively European country in the Middle East.
Although the majority of the population is Muslim, the legacy of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk still lives on.
If you go to the big Turkish cities - Istanbul, Izmir, Ankara, you will see a very cosmopolitan society - people from different countries and different strata of society.
Many women will wear hijabs, but many will not wear them.
The situation, of course, is not the same as in Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Syria, Iran and many other places in our region.
Mustafa Kemal Ataturk Photo: Wikimedia Commons For reference: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was one of the founders of modern Turkey and its first president.
As a staunch supporter of nationalism, Ataturk carried out a number of important economic and social reforms that made Turkey one of the richest and strongest countries in the Middle East.
For example, it introduced the Latin alphabet, as well as international units of measurement and time counting according to the Gregorian calendar.
However, I cannot deny that a significant part of the population has left Turkey in the last decade.
These people are the westerners.
There were several reasons for that.
For example, after the 2013 Gezi Park protests, the government of Recep Tayyip Erdogan began to interfere more in people ’ s privacy.
Also in 2015, peace talks with the Kurdistan Workers ’ Party (PKK) failed, leading to military clashes in parts of the country.
At the same time, we are faced with the activities of the cells of the terrorist group "Islamic State".
In turn, after the attempted coup in 2016, a state of emergency was declared in the country, followed by a sweep of government institutions and universities.
As a result, many people lost their jobs.
Gezi Park protests Photo: AFP / Scanpix For reference: Gezi Park protests began in the summer of 2013, when Turkish authorities violently dispersed a peaceful demonstration against the government ’ s plans to build one of Istanbul ’ s last green areas, Gezi Park.
Immediately afterwards, protesters took to the streets to protest the restrictions on freedom of speech and assembly, as well as the gradual disintegration of secular Turkey.
Despite the fact that initially the protests were environmental in nature, in the end they turned into something much more.
- So, Turkish society today is divided? - Turkish society has always been like this.
Since the founding of the Republic of Turkey in 1923, people have been discussing what it really means to be a Turk and in which direction the country should move.
People have asked whether Turkey should become modern, secular and pro-Western, or modern, but more focused on the history of the Ottoman Empire, as well as its ties to Muslim civilization.
Supporters of the second camp often mention Sultan Mehmed II, who conquered the capital of the Byzantine Empire, Constantinople (modern Istanbul). – Speaking of Mehmed II, if I ’ m not mistaken, he also began today ’ s history of St. Sophia Cathedral and its transformation into a mosque.
Thanks to him, this cathedral now belongs to Turkey.
Can you comment on how important this cathedral really is for the inhabitants of your country? - The answer to this question depends on who is asked.
For critics of Kemal Ataturk ’ s legacy, Hagia Sophia, or Hagia Sophia, is the same as Mehmed II.
This conquest means glory and greatness, as well as victory over Western civilization.
I would like to emphasize that, although Mehmed II turned the Sophia Cathedral into a mosque, the Ottoman Empire did not try to eradicate the remnants of the conquered culture.
Conqueror Mehmed II PHOTO: Wikimedia Commons For reference: Conqueror Mehmed II was the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, who in Turkish history is mainly known for occupying Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, in 1453.
This event marked the actual destruction of Byzantium and the opening of the gates for further expansion into the Balkans and Europe. – I think that the history of this cathedral is unclear to many residents of Latvia.
Can you do a little sketch? - If I'm not mistaken, it was built in the 6th century.
This was the time when the Anatolian Peninsula was ruled by the heir of the Ancient Roman Empire - the Byzantine Empire.
This is important for Orthodox Christians because, as we know, the Byzantines were Orthodox.
I have already mentioned that in 1453 Constantinople was conquered by Sultan Mehmed II, who turned Hagia Sophia into a mosque.
After the formation of the Republic of Turkey, President Mustafa Kemal Ataturk decided to turn the mosque into a museum.
His calculation was as follows: Hagia Sophia should become a symbol of the fusion of Christian and Islamic civilizations, which people all over the world would like to see.
He wanted to create a new nation, reminiscent of the models adopted in the West.
This approach existed until President Erdoğan decided to turn the cathedral into a mosque again. Hagia Sophia PHOTO: ERDEM SAHIN / EPA Historical development of Hagia Sophia: In 537, Hagia Sophia was built as an Eastern Orthodox church; In 1204, the cathedral was converted into a Roman Catholic church; In 1261, it was rebuilt into an Eastern Orthodox church; In 1453, Osh In 1935, by the decision of the founder of the Turkish Republic Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Hagia Sophia was converted into a museum; on July 10, 2020, the Supreme Administrative Court of Turkey overturned the 1934 Turkish government decree granting the cathedral the status of a museum; on July 24, 2020, the first Friday prayer, or Muslim prayer, was held in the mosque.
Source: LSM - If we are talking about the present tense, you wrote earlier that this decision of Erdogan can be explained by the fact that you mentioned the wound - the struggle between Western and Islamic civilizations.
Do you agree with that? - Yes.
Ataturk once tried to create a new state, but his leadership style was relatively authoritative.
He founded the secular Turkish Republic and only then tried to gain public support.
However, this support was not so great.
There were people who had a radically different vision of where Turkey should go – the same ones who wanted to see Turkey more Islamic.
Even among Ataturk ’ s supporters there were disagreements.
It should be remembered that the Republic of Turkey was created after the expulsion of Great Britain and other Western countries from the Anatolian Peninsula.
Therefore, a paradox has emerged: on the one hand, we want to get closer to the West, and on the other hand, we are fighting against it.
This is the same thing I mentioned earlier – supporters of Turkey ’ s alternative model wanted to see a modern Turkey, but only one that would pay more attention to the Ottoman Empire ’ s past and Islamic heritage.
PHOTO: Reuters / ScanPix - So the decision to turn Hagia Sophia back into a mosque is part of this Islamic modernization? - Yes, we can say with certainty that President Erdogan belongs to a political tradition that contradicts Ataturk's vision.
Some scholars call this tradition Neo-Ottomanism.
The state seeks to emphasize Ottoman culture and Ottoman political vision in both domestic and foreign policy.
Turkey ’ s goal is not to become an empire again, but it definitely wants to be a regional power and play an important role in the former territories of the Ottoman Empire.
To do this, Ankara is trying to use the tools of “soft power ” (for example, films and TV series).
The so-called “hard power ” is also being used more and more often.
Let ’ s look at Turkey ’ s military operations in Syria and Libya, as well as its active participation in the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
The transformation of Hagia Sophia into a mosque fits perfectly into this neo-Ottoman history.
The only question is, why now?
Erdogan ’ s party has been in power for 18 years. – Is the decision to turn Hagia Sophia into a mosque sufficient to govern the Middle East? – Not just in the Middle East.
The Ottoman Sultan was also the caliph, the leader of the world Muslim community.
Perhaps, with this decision, Erdogan is trying to find an approach to the hearts of Muslims in other countries of the world, that is, to gain popularity among them.
For example, in India, Pakistan, Afghanistan and the Balkans, many people see him as the defender of Islam.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan PHOTO: PRESIDENT PRESS OFFICE / via REUTERS However, I think that Turkey ’ s statement is certainly disputed by many.
Ankara does not have very good relations with Saudi Arabia, Egypt and the United Arab Emirates.
While their interests clash in Libya, Qatar and Syria. – Does Turkey have the resources to play the role of a regional power? – It definitely does not have economic resources.
If we look at the unemployment rate and the cost of the Turkish lira, the country certainly faces problems.
Financial assistance is provided by Qatar, in a sense by China.
Turkey does not want to ask for money from the International Monetary Fund because it would mean dependence on the West.
Thus, from a financial point of view, Turkey ’ s regional government is unlikely to be sustainable.
It should be noted that the government has invested heavily in the modernization of the army and the development of military equipment.
In the arsenal of Turkey there are modern drones and high-quality military equipment of various kinds.
It should also be recalled that Turkey is in Libya to gain access to energy resources in the Mediterranean Sea.
In turn, one of the reasons for Ankara ’ s military intervention in Syria is the desire to gain access to reconstruction money.
It is possible that these investments will pay off in the future.
PHOTO: EPA / Scanpix - Is Erdogan trying to increase his domestic political support with the help of Hagia Sophia? - This could be one of the reasons for this decision.
Turkey still faces serious economic problems, and Erdogan ’ s popularity is falling.
It has become more authoritarian than it was 10 years ago and is gradually losing support in strictly religious communities.
Two former allies, Ahmet Davutoglu and Ali Babacan, also split from him and formed their own parties.
Another reason may be Turkey ’ s relationship with the West.
The situation has changed since the 1980s and 1990s, when Turkey ’ s relations with the European Union improved.
At that time, Ankara still wanted to become a member of this organization.
I think Erdogan understands very well that the situation has changed and he no longer needs the support of the West.
For this reason, he did not hesitate to take the risk.
Especially since Europe is currently busy fighting Covid-19, Brexit negotiations and efforts to stop illegal migration.
It is noteworthy that there was no serious reaction from the EU.
Of course, it cannot be said that Turkey will no longer cooperate with Western institutions at all.
For example, within NATO, Ankara continues to play an important role. - If we are talking about NATO, do you think that Turkey can still be considered a reliable ally? - It can be a reliable ally, but we must ask ourselves a similar question - can the European Union and NATO be reliable allies for Turkey?
For example, the agreement between Turkey and the EU to host Syrian refugees in our country is unethical.
The European Union has decided to give Ankara money, but that does not solve the problem.
This agreement also supports authoritarianism in Turkey.
There are serious questions about whether we can rely on these institutions to make our country more democratic.
Istanbul PHOTOS: Reuters / ScanPix - Could Hagia Sophia suffer from Erdogan ’ s decision?
If I am not mistaken, the cathedral used to be under the wing of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and now it is transferred to the Office of Religious Affairs.
On the other hand, the Office of Religious Affairs may not pay as much attention to the condition of the sanctuary.
Although Hagia Sophia is now a mosque again, the government stressed that visitors can still see it.
It will also, as before, be protected as a cultural heritage of mankind.
However, it seems to me that this news has not yet reached the masses. - So, Latvians can go to Istanbul and see Hagia Sophia? - Yes.
And now the entrance is free.
Last summer, some of my friends from the United States visited the cathedral again.
The entrance cost $20.
However, tourists now have to reckon with the fact that it is impossible to get to the cathedral during prayer. - Thank you for the interview! - Thank you!

title: Maria Shalaeva, Ilya Bachurin and others at the closing of the Strelka Film Festival
text:
Maria Shalaeva, Ilya Bachurin and others at the closing of the film festival at Strelka 07.09.2020, 19: 50, Various series of screenings that took place from August 30 to September 6 on Bersenevskaya embankment, yesterday ended with the Russian premiere of the film “Evil does not exist ” by Mohammad Rasulof.
Maria Shalaeva and Ksenia Kutepova, Philip Avdeev and Ilya Bachurin, Yura Borisov and Anna Shevchuk and other guests came to watch the film with such an optimistic name, as well as to note the closing of the film screening this evening.
Anna Nikolaeva and Maria Shalaeva Yura Borisov and Anna Shevchuk Natasha Merkulova and Alexei Chupov Ilya Bachurin Philip AvdeevThe choice of the program director of the festival Stas Tyrkin on the picture of Rasuloff as the final shows on “Strelka ” fell not by chance.
At the Berlin Film Festival, the last film screening before the global pandemic, this film won the Golden Bear, the main award.
The picture itself consists of four novels, which tell about the inhabitants of modern Iran.
The hero of the first of them is Hishmat, a man living in Tehran, who spends his day in ordinary household chores: cooking dinner, picking up his daughter from school, visiting his mother and helping his wife.
All this during the day, at night, Hishmat sets foot in the night shift - and then what is routine for him turns into a tragedy for others and a shock for the audience.
The other three stories in “Evil Does Not Exist ” also explore the paradoxes of life in modern Iranian society, and in one of the novels starred the daughter of the director Baran Rasoulof.
By the way, she received instead of her father the award in Berlin: because of the conflict with the Iranian authorities, Mohammad himself could not attend the festival.
