title: Tallinn Invites Citizens to Discuss Tondiraba Park Sketch
text:
According to the mayor of Tallinn, Mikhail Kõlvart, the city has chosen a “green ” development style and consistently adheres to this direction.
“By creating a new park, we want to give citizens of any age more opportunities to maintain a healthy lifestyle and rest in the fresh air – the infrastructure of the future park, of course, will allow us to realize this, ” said Mikhail Kylvart. – However, the same important goal for us is the preservation of species diversity in the urban environment.
The corona-crisis has reaffirmed how dependent we are – not only people on each other, but also man on nature and vice versa, so we must find opportunities to coexist with nature and in an urban environment.
In my opinion, the creation of a park that will contribute to the preservation of species diversity is a right step in this direction. ”
The largest park in Lasnamäe Tondiraba, occupying almost 23 hectares of area, is planned to be created on the site of the former eponymous swamp.
The park will become part of the so-called Lasnamäe Green Corridor, which was designed back in the days when the area was just created.
The creation of the park also reinforces the city ’ s goal as a finalist in the 2022 European Green Capital competition to win this prestigious title.
When creating the park, it is planned to preserve the local ecosystem: a forest and a small lake, animals, birds and plants living here.
The zones for active leisure activities will be located around the forest in such a way that they do not disturb the diversity of the species living in the park.
Several playgrounds will be built in the Tondiraba Park, some of which are adapted for children with disabilities.
There will also be an opportunity to play sports at different venues: gym, team sports (basketball and volleyball) and individual classes.
In addition, an obstacle course and convenient infrastructure for cyclists will be created, as well as dog walking grounds will be built.
The park will have a unique area for extreme sports - skate park and pump track.
Cyclists will have at their disposal several landscape trails.
Walking through the forest routes will allow you to directly get from one part of the park to another.
It is also planned to create a skating rink, which in the summer can be reoriented to other sports.

title: Israel and UAE to sign agreement on normalization of relations on September 15 – media
text:
Photo: AP Photo / Ariel Schalit The signing ceremony of the agreement on normalization of relations between Israel and the UAE will be held in Washington on September 15, reports Reuters.
US President Donald Trump earlier said that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and UAE Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Zayed would come for the signing.
On August 13, it was reported that Israel and the UAE reached an agreement on the normalization of bilateral relations.
The parties planned to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and cooperate in the development of a vaccine against COVID-19.
In particular, the delegations of Israel and the UAE are going to hold a meeting to conclude bilateral agreements, including in the field of investment, tourism and direct flights.
The Palestinian leadership has expressed its condemnation of the trilateral agreement on the normalization of relations between Israel and the UAE.
In this regard, the Palestinian authorities decided to recall its ambassador from the UAE.
Palestinian President Nabil Abu Rudeina said the move was an aggression against the Palestinian people.
He stressed that no country has the right to speak on behalf of the people of Palestine.

title: Political choice: the European Union can not cope with the influx of refugees
text:
On the night of September 9, a fire broke out in the Moria refugee camp on the Greek island of Lesbos.
The victims are not reported, it is only known that the largest camp in Europe completely burned down.
Many European politicians and activists regard this incident as the result of another failure of the migration policy of the European Union.
The flow of refugees to Europe increased dramatically during the coronavirus pandemic.
According to PA Media, since the start of the quarantine, almost 4.9 thousand people whose asylum applications have not been accepted by the UK have crossed the English Channel in small boats, and this is twice the number of refugees trying to break into Europe through the strait for the whole of 2019.
This year, 16,942 sea arrivals were detected in Italy, compared to 11,471 last year.
It is easy to explain this trend — some countries are still feeling the effects of war, others are shaken by the economic crisis of the pandemic.
The European Union, however, as five years ago, was not ready for an influx of refugees.
Because of the pandemic, those wishing to get to Europe have no other option but to cross the sea border.
Many of them are being turned back by the Coast Guard.
In general, such incidents occur in Greece.
Those who have reached and crossed the border are distributed in overcrowded camps.
There were 12,800 people in Moriah, four times the estimated capacity of the camp.
The fire occurred shortly after 35 cases of infection were identified among refugees living in the camp.
According to Greek public television ERT, many migrants left the camp during the fire and went to the city.
Greek authorities accuse refugees of deliberate arson as a protest against quarantine measures taken in the camp.
“It is a fact that the fire was started by asylum-seekers protesting against the quarantine, ” Greek Migration Minister Notis Mitarachi told a news conference in Lesvos.
We need a closed control center. ”
On Wednesday, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis admitted that there were no normal conditions for refugees in the Moria camp.
“I know how difficult the conditions are.
However, nothing can be an excuse for the violent reaction of refugees to medical examinations, ” he said. – The situation in Moriah cannot continue, because it is a problem of public health, humanity and national security at the same time.
Meanwhile, not everyone in Europe believes that the cause of the incident concerns only the dissatisfaction of refugees with quarantine measures.
“The fire in Moria is caused by European politics.
It was predictable and could have been prevented.
It was a political choice of the EU, followed by the Greek state.
It is a deliberate policy clearly formulated as a deterrent and punishment for these people.
The coronavirus has been used, is being used and will be used to strengthen the policy of containment and fear, as well as to justify inhuman policies, ” Apostolos Veizis, director of Médecins Sans Frontières ’ medical operations in Greece, told Politico.
Of course, the COVID-19 pandemic has affected not only the dramatic increase in the number of asylum seekers in Europe, but also the EU ’ s hospitality rules.
Moriah is just one of many examples of overcrowded camps during the pandemic era.
Referring to the lack of places, the governments of southern European countries explain the inability to accept new refugees.
As a result, migrants on boats are either refused or placed in a 14-day quarantine on ferries, oil tankers or small pleasure boats, where there are no normal conditions for detention.
In July, 180 refugees were evacuated to Italy from the SOS Mediterranee Ocean Viking after numerous suicide attempts and threats.
On the eve of the Italian government banned the flight over the territory of the country Moonbird German non-governmental organization Sea Watch, engaged in the rescue of people in the Mediterranean Sea.
The representative of the organization Georgia Lunardi said in a video message that the reason for the refusal was the attempt of Rome and the European Union to turn a blind eye to what is happening in the Mediterranean Sea.
According to her, reports by Sea Watch about “the lack of rescue operations and unacceptable delays in providing support to people, as well as illegal interception and pushing them back to Libya ” were the basis for the ban on departure.
The fire in the Moriah camp caused the European Union to react.
The President of the European Council, Charles Michel, expressed his sympathy “to all who are in danger. ”
Vice-President of the European Commission Margaritis Schinas on September 10 went to Greece.
EU Home Affairs Commissioner Ilva Johansson said on Twitter that she was already working on funding for the relocation of 400 unaccompanied children and adolescents from the Moriah camp.
Speaking to reporters, she noted that Greece with the help of the European Union over the past six months has reduced the number of people living in the camp by half.
She also hinted that the incident forced Brussels to pay attention to the problem with refugees.
“I am convinced that when I present my new proposals, there will be a discussion between the member countries.
I think we will also see their willingness to show solidarity, ” she said.
In any case, EU leaders have so far demonstrated that the refugee issue is not their primary concern.
The discussion of the European Commission on this topic is scheduled for September 30.
At the same time, it was initially planned to raise this issue “after Easter ”, which never happened.
However, even if the European Union will deal with the problem, do not forget that the old problems on the way to resolve the situation have not gone away.
The main obstacle has been and remains the contradictions between the EU members.
Southern countries, which, due to their geographical location, are forced to take the brunt on themselves, have long insisted on the introduction of a mandatory system of redistribution of asylum seekers throughout the European Union.
However, countries in Central and Eastern Europe, such as Hungary and Poland, are categorically against such an initiative.
Many have pinned their hopes on the German presidency of the Council of the European Union.
Moreover, such hopes were based not only on Berlin ’ s leadership in the commonwealth and its influence.
It is Germany that is responsible for the “open door policy ” proclaimed by Angela Merkel in 2015, so it is implied that, feeling guilty, Berlin will be more interested in solving the refugee problem.
However, according to Politico, citing sources, before the end of the German presidency of the EU Council in December, only two meetings of the interior ministers of the member states of the commonwealth are planned, at which the issue of redistribution of migrants can potentially be raised.
However, with a high degree of probability, EU members will not be able to come to a compromise.
Opponents of the redistribution system will cite the coronavirus pandemic.
The same countries that accept migrants, too, may soon finally close their doors, citing the same reason.

title: How Palestine is trying to counter the influence of the US and Israel in the Arab world
text:
Palestine is trying to find a new way to confront Israel, which is gradually gaining political points.
After the “deal of the century ” of US President Donald Trump received world condemnation, Washington and Tel Aviv went the other way – Israel abandoned plans to annex territories in the West Bank under the demonstrative leadership of the United States, and the parties decided first to weaken international support for Palestine.
In this direction, they have already managed to achieve several tangible successes.
On August 13, US President Donald Trump announced the conclusion of an agreement on the normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates.
The negotiations were held with the mediation of Washington, and its role is quite actively emphasized by all parties.
Thus, the UAE became the third country to sign the Arab-Israeli peace agreement.
The treaty was signed with Egypt in 1979 and with Jordan in 1994.
Against the background of these agreements, Palestine recalled its ambassador to the UAE, considering this step as an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.
A joint statement signed by the head of the White House, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Zayed expresses the hope that this historic breakthrough will contribute to peace in the Middle East.
Moreover, the statement claims that the result of the deal was the freezing by Israel of plans to annex territories in the West Bank.
If Israel had decided to annex the territories with the blessing of the White House, it would have received a sharp reaction from the world community, which already prevented the implementation of the “deal of the century ”.
Thus, Washington and Tel Aviv simply found a way to circumvent the abandonment of plans in a more noble way.
However, without this clause, the UAE would have been more difficult to reach an agreement with Israel because of the already established Arab solidarity against Tel Aviv ’ s plans to annex the disputed territories.
In any case, for Palestine, the agreement between the countries was an extremely alarming signal of the shattered solidarity of the Arab world.
Another sign soon followed.
On September 9, the Arab League refused to adopt a resolution condemning the UAE for normalizing relations with Israel.
The Palestinian draft did not receive the approval of the majority of the Arab League.
Abu Dhabi continues to support Palestine.
“The UAE peace treaty with Israel will not be implemented at the expense of the Palestinian cause and the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, ” UAE Foreign Minister Anwar Mohammed Gargash said after the Arab League meeting.
And while the UAE is committed to resolving the Palestinian issue, Palestine has every reason to worry that Abu Dhabi ’ s actions will create a new trend in the Arab world.
“Now in the Middle East, we see that the situation is really changing, ” Trump ’ s adviser and son-in-law Jared Kushner, who oversees the Middle East issue, said on Wednesday.
They are not going to hold back their progress now so that this conflict will continue to get stuck in the mud. ”
U.S. and Israeli officials have hinted that they are negotiating agreements with other Arab countries similar to what Tel Aviv has concluded with Abu Dhabi.
“I have met with very, very many leaders of the Arab and Islamic world, much more than you think, ” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said at a press conference last week.
Israeli Ambassador to the United States Ron Dermer told reporters that the breakthrough in relations with the UAE shows that Palestinian leaders cannot stand between Tel Aviv and Arab states.
“Instead of recognizing this reality and focusing on reaching a realistic compromise with Israel that will build a better future for both Israelis and Palestinians, unfortunately, these leaders remain mired in their rejection, they are stuck in the past, ” Dermer said. strength."
Indeed, solidarity with the Palestinians in their 70-year struggle for territory with Israel has long dominated the political discourse of the Arab world.
However, the UAE ’ s decision to move toward Israel has sparked much less controversy than similar agreements concluded by Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994.
Meanwhile, strong support for Palestine was provided by non-Arab regional players – Iran and Turkey.
Unlike the Arab League, these countries have sharply criticized the UAE ’ s actions, calling Abu Dhabi ’ s decision to reach an agreement with Israel hypocritical.
Now Palestine hopes that other countries will not follow the example of the UAE.
“The Arab League ’ s failure to condemn the agreement to normalize relations between the UAE and Israel does not mean and does not imply the consent of member states to normalize relations with Israel, ” said Saeb Erekat, head of the Palestine Liberation Organization ’ s negotiating office.
Palestine in its position refers to international agreements — the Arab Peace Initiative of 2002, which implies achieving peace with Israel and ending the Arab-Israeli conflict only if Israel withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967 (including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms) and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
“We hope that other Arab countries will not slide towards normalization of relations with Israel.
“Normalization has disastrous consequences for the future of the Palestinian cause because it prompts Israel to strengthen and prolong the occupation of Palestine, not to end it, ” Erekat said.
At the same time, Palestine refers not only to the solidarity of the Arab world and international agreements, but also claims the spread of influence of the United States and Israel.
Erekat stressed that further progress in Tel Aviv ’ s relations with Arab countries “will serve the extremist and ideological administrations of the United States and Israel, which seek to consolidate the apartheid system in Palestine, freeing the occupying power, Israel, from the burden of reckoning. ”
Faced with a serious divergence of views with traditional allies, the Palestinians attempted to unify internal disparate forces in the hope of presenting a united front.
On September 3, a meeting of competing factions was held under the leadership of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas.
Among the participants of the conference were representatives of the “Movement for the National Liberation of Palestine ” (Fatah) and the Palestinian“ Islamic Resistance Movement ” (Hamas).
“Our meeting is taking place at a very dangerous stage, when our national cause faces various conspiracies and dangers, ” Abbas said.“ To stand together in a trench of confrontation and peaceful popular resistance to the occupation, I invite you to come and agree on the formation of a national leadership. ”
A joint communiqué issued after the meeting called for the establishment of a “committee of eminent national figures ” that all parties trust to present a“ new strategic vision ” for the conflict with Israel.
Intra-Palestinian unity could pose new challenges to Israel, the United States, and even the Arab League.
"Achieving Palestinian unity through the historic meeting of Palestinian factions last week is a step towards unifying the Palestinian position against the plans for the annexation of Israel, the Trump plan and all attempts to normalize the Israeli occupation of Palestine."
In any case, Arab countries are increasingly moving away from anti-Israel positions, especially against the background of the growing influence of neighboring Shiite Iran, which has become a much more serious problem for Sunni countries.
As Alexei Malashenko, an expert at the Carnegie Center in Moscow, points out, the solidarity of the Arab world that Palestine calls for has never really existed.
“There have always been national interests, including in relation to the Middle East conflict, including in relation to Israel.
This trend did not start today.
Therefore, I think that today Israel is not the factor that could rally around itself Arabs at the level of states, — the expert notes. — I would not say that the entire Arab world in general is delighted, but the heads of state, of course, the majority are for [normalization of relations with Israel], because everyone is tired of the conflict, there are completely different problems, the same Islamic extremists.
So if we look at the future, in general, the relationship between the Arabs and Israel will mostly improve. ”

title: Emotional intelligence according to Herman Gref and unconscious consumption
text:
14 September 2020 | Reading time 17 min Galina Smirnova,, 12: 26 — REGNUM In August, the Central Bank of the Russian Federation in its data noted that it expects an increase in the number of illegal creditors.
Such a forecast during the congress of ACI Russia was voiced in particular by Valery Lyakh, Director of the Department for Countering Unfair Practices of the Bank of Russia.
According to him, as Kommersant wrote, citizens during the pandemic were more restrained in their consumer behavior, and loans from illegal immigrants are often taken for “emotional ” expenses, for example,“ a smartphone of the latest model. ”
In addition, closer to autumn, after the holiday period, there is a standard increase in “household ” spending.
This factor is also taken into account by illegal lenders, increasing the number of offers of their services in order to “satisfy ” the demand that has arisen.
“And since the indicators of debt to legal microfinance institutions are already showing growth, we assume that more than last year, the number of consumers can go to the“ gray zone ” to obtain borrowed funds, ” the representative of the Central Bank noted.
Banking analysts expressed the opinion that the growth of the illegal sector in lending is also responsible for the economic recession formed as a result of the pandemic: incomes of the population are falling, banks are tightening the conditions of consumer lending, which will force some people to turn to illegal organizations.
Raiffeisenbank analyst Denis Poryvai said that many people will be left unemployed (companies also affected by the pandemic are seriously reviewing their operating costs, including staff) or will be forced to go to a lower paid position, supporting payments from the state will end, but at the same time people will want to maintain the usual standard of living and consumption, people will be forced to turn to illegal creditors, and demand will increase. and such a proposal.
As we can see, the key factor in the growth of lending is the desire of people not so much to support their incomes as to preserve their usual lifestyle, the usual level of consumption and the desire to buy a fashionable “thing ” – something that others can afford.
Agree, credit is not a concept about the preservation and even more so the multiplication of your income, on the contrary - it is a conscious choice to increase your expenses.
Conscious, if a person understands and is sure that during the term of the loan, his financial condition will be stable.
And unconscious, when people, in fact, know that their income is not something to grow nowhere, but tomorrow they may be out of work at all, but they still make purchases, and buying on credit not the most vital goods.
It is unlikely that in this case, people are driven by the instinct of self-preservation, aimed at survival in the changed conditions, they, as quite rightly noted by the representative of the Central Bank, are driven by emotions.
You do not need to be a psychologist to understand that the banking logic of “do not save, postpone the purchase, buy today, pay tomorrow ” is built exclusively on consumer psychology, which in turn can destroy any state.
It is no secret that after a period of self-isolation in the lending market there was a revival again.
Judging by the study of one of the largest credit bureaus in Russia, young people aged 18 to 23 years often borrow flagship models of smartphones, laptops, tablets, hoverboards, electric scooters.
Is it possible to call these goods vital to purchase them on credit in rather difficult times?
Partly, yes, the truth is not all, as not vital, but imposed by the new rules of interaction in society.
Remote mode of work and study forces you to resort to the purchase of computers and laptops.
It is difficult to imagine life without smartphones, but you can imagine without flagship models and novelties.
In any case, it is the manufacturers of these products that adjust our lives and make it unthinkable in isolation from them.
And lenders make it possible to absorb goods as much as possible, earning on interest.
Last year, according to a study by IDC, Russians bought smartphones for almost $8 billion.
Is it possible to judge by this indicator about the welfare of Russians and the presence of high incomes? Hardly.
Rather, this indicator reflects the degree of emotional attachment of Russians to the consumption of fashionable, and therefore imposed by the marketing policy of foreign corporations of goods.
Actually, this was what the representative of the Central Bank said, they say, the Russians are not ready to abandon the usual way of life.
Who has benefited more from the sale of smartphones in Russia?
The leader of the Russian market was the Chinese company Huawei, which managed to sell more than 10 million smartphones for the year, 1 million more than the South Korean Samsung.
In the third position, Xiaomi is firmly entrenched.
Four closed the share of Apple.
The total market share of all four players in the Russian market was 84%.
Changing consumer habits is difficult.
The pandemic was the first blow to these habits.
And it also dealt a blow to the traditional way of the economy of many countries of the world.
Technology companies have managed to take a stronger position and win some share of consumers.
And consumers younger, coming to replace the previous generations.
According to Anastasia Sidorina, Deputy Director for Customer Relations at the Romir Research Center, cited in Rossiyskaya Gazeta at the end of April this year, the Russians sharply reduced the number of trips to stores - 58% go shopping every 7-10 days.
10% of respondents reduced visits to supermarkets in favor of online delivery of finished food - from restaurants and catering establishments.
The main share of such orders and it, according to the expert, will increase, falls on residents of cities with a population of millions.
Let ’ s also pay attention to the study of consumer behavior in Russia for 2018 under the heading “The digital revolution determines consumer habits ” by the international company PwC, which states that Russia is participating in the global study of consumer behavior organized by the company for the sixth time.
The study, conducted between August and October 2017, surveyed 22,000 consumers around the world to “understand and compare customer behavior and the use of different sales channels in 27 countries around the world. ”
PwC analyzed those areas in which customer habits have changed most noticeably, for example, how customers used certain sales channels for purchases, the speed of delivery of orders from online stores, the reasons for buying certain goods, and also considered opportunities for business development by properly responding to customer needs.
In Russia, 652 respondents took part in the survey (all respondents make at least one online purchase per year).
Among the main findings of the study, PwC experts say that companies must respond to new consumer habits, changing the direction of their priorities and investments accordingly.
Companies should pay more attention to the dynamics of sales through smartphones (!), as well as the impressions of customers from visiting stores.
By the way, already today, you can find in online stores the presence of goods absent in offline stores of certain international sellers, which can not but accustom consumers more and more to making online purchases, which means that states should prepare for the closure of traditional stores of foreign manufacturers of goods and, as a result, reduce revenues in the budget of tax revenues from them, even if the pandemic does not go to the second circle.
And smartphones.
The study states that most consumers use a smartphone for regular online purchases: in 2017, the share of regular online purchases through a smartphone in Russia increased from 36% in 2014 to 63%.
Older shoppers prefer to shop online through the most “traditional ” tool – the computer, but younger shoppers mostly use mobile devices.
In this regard, it is worth recalling the record for last year ’ s sales of smartphones.
Analyst Olga Babinina from IDC Russia, the company that cited data on the growth of smartphone sales in Russia, noted in the publication of Rossiyskaya Gazeta that the average price of a smartphone at that time did not grow and amounted to $180 (about 11.5 thousand rubles).
That is, the price has not become the determining factor in the growth of the smartphone market
According to Babinina, “the gradual strengthening of the ruble exchange rate during the year helped the market to gain momentum.
The volume of the market in value terms increased by a quarter compared to the peak of pre-crisis 2014. ”
The ruble, indeed, became the leader of growth in the financial market in 2019, strengthening against the American and European currencies.
Some analysts argued that the key role in its growth was played by the growth of world oil prices, others, on the contrary, considered the role of oil insignificant, pointing out the main factor - the inflow of foreign capital into Russian assets, they say, the optimism of foreign investors arose against the background of Washington and Beijing's refusal to a new round of exacerbation of the trade conflict.
The regulator of the financial market, the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, cited data according to which since the beginning of 2019, investors have additionally invested almost 1.53 trillion rubles in Russian debt bonds.
At the same time, among buyers of state securities, the share of foreigners increased from 24.4% to 32%.
Probably, now for the further development of mainly technological global companies and their coverage of a wide range of consumers, further demand from the population is necessary.
If we consider the pandemic a man-made affair of international technology companies, which just managed to consolidate their positions, the coronavirus still poses a threat not only as such by its spread among the population, but also by the likelihood of initiating a second round of self-isolation in countries that are in the circle of interests of these companies.
Although, it is possible that the virus simply got out of control, and went through the countries, going far beyond the interests.
A second time, the isolation regime could inflict another blow on the Russian economy, requiring even more support for Russian citizens.
Perhaps, if some politicians fail to get financial support from the states of the full circle of the population, in particular the Russians, then it is possible that the pandemic will break out again.
However, in this case, the interested parties may not achieve the desired goal at all, since the response of states may have a directly opposite to the expectations of the interested parties.
Another thing is to cope with people ’ s habits.
With consumer habits warmed up and warmed up by international corporations.
And the state with the moods of citizens who do not want to change their habits.
A more crushing or decisive force in the confrontation of elites of any kind with the political authorities of states is precisely such a factor as the dissatisfaction of the people with their own situation.
The most dissatisfied can be just among so to speak professional consumers, that is, those who soberly are not able to assess their immediate financial prospects, but at the same time are not ready to deny themselves the purchase of desired things on credit, not ready to accept today's reality and themselves in this reality.
And it is not necessary that disgruntled people rebel against the policies of the governments of countries, because you can express dissatisfaction with the elites.
Actually, the growing discontent with the growing stratification of society into poor and rich with the demands of nationalization of economies in some countries, the disappointment in capitalism and the growth of anti-globalization sentiment was spoken even before the pandemic at one of the forums in Davos.
Herman Gref at the business breakfast of Sberbank raised these issues.
The participants of the event, including foreign partners of the bank, international companies, including shareholders of the bank, as well as well-known foreign educational organizations, said that it is necessary to better understand the policy of each country, take into account the national characteristics of the countries, skillfully build a dialogue with consumers.
Later, Gref at the Gaidar Forum spoke about the genetic code and national characteristics of Russians who survived more than one war, as well as the need to take into account the cultural code of the country.
It is possible to change the cultural code of a country or mentality only through education, starting from childhood.
As you know, Gref pays attention to the development of the education system in Russia.
Back in 2016, at the congress “Innovative Practice: Science Plus Business ” at Moscow State University, the head of Sberbank said that there was a discussion of cooperation with a number of Russian universities with training programs for students that will help them be in demand in the labor market, teaching skills, including emotional intelligence.
Meanwhile, in some regions, projects are already being implemented to train schoolchildren through the introduction of technologies of social and emotional intelligence.
The author of the methodology - Victoria Shimanskaya, as we wrote earlier, in favor of her educational technology says that it makes it possible to solve several tasks in the upbringing and education of children at once: to realize yourself, your emotions and needs, calmly and constructively perceive criticism, understand the emotions and needs of others, as well as the reasons for their occurrence, kindly and effectively interact with others, which will affect the increase of self-esteem of children, improve their socialization and reduce conflict. Another – thanks to new forms of education, teachers will have the opportunity to work effectively to increase motivation for learning and cognition – this will help children to more easily and effectively perceive new information, master any educational material.
According to Shimanskaya, it has already been proven that “emotional intelligence ” affects a child ’ s development, his performance, interaction with the world around him and leads research on academic, social and emotional development and learning (The Collaborative for Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning – CASEL, USA), which shows that 83% of children enrolled in the program using SEL technology achieve high results. in school.
In open online sources, you can find works related to the development of “emotional intelligence of representatives of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Higher School of Economics.
Meanwhile, quite often you can find the opinions of foreign experts in the field of psychology, who argue that “emotional intelligence ” is a poorly studied phenomenon, also questioning many of the qualities attributed to this phenomenon, including the ability of people to become more successful due to the development of“ EI ”.
For example, in one of the critical reviews of one of the books by Daniel Goleman, released a little more than twenty years ago, which became a bestseller and allegedly still in demand, it is said that the intention of the author, most likely, was to convince people to share his views, rather than inform them in a truly scientific manner.
Moreover, it is indicated that the author obviously wanted to please the managers of the companies of the global Fortune 500 rating (the rating of the 500 largest world companies, the criterion of which is the amount of revenue), wanting to establish himself as a highly paid consultant in this area.
Open sources say that under the scientific guidance of David McClelland, Goleman received a Ph.D. from Harvard University for the financial support of which he conducted pre-doctoral research, then received a post-doctoral grant from the Research Council for the Social Sciences.
Goleman studied in India, where he also spent time with the Indian guru Nim Karoli Baba.
He is currently co-chair of the Research Consortium on Emotional Intelligence in Organizations based at Rutgers University ’ s Graduate School of Applied and Professional Psychology, facilitating research into the impact of emotional intelligence on professional performance, creative and professional growth.
It turns out that Goleman is talking about the development of certain leadership qualities through “emotional intelligence. ”
At the same time, in various materials of Russian experts, puzzled by the topic of the development of “emotional intelligence ”, it is said that“ EI ” allows you to cope with depression, helps to realize your own and the emotions of others, better interact, empathize and even pacify aggression.
So who do you intend to educate or grow in Russian schools – people who can become successful in different spheres of life or are ready to pacify their emotions and be loyal to reality?
Although these and other qualities, of course, can complement each other.
Or maybe, on the contrary, the Russian educational system will grow people dependent on the opinions of others, including those who predetermine consumer behavior?
If we think from the point of view of a strong state that wants to preserve sovereignty, then the country needs people who are able to control their emotions, who do not succumb to momentary desires and even more provocations, who do not go about the interests of, for example, transnational corporations, who soberly assess a particular situation and due to a wide range of knowledge, including the history of their country, who can predict the consequences of certain own actions. country in the event of external interference in its affairs.
But it is precisely these skills that develop systems thinking to a greater extent.
And if we are talking about the education of managers and business development, however, which may apply to the competencies of officials, it is systemic thinking that is the ability to realize the entire system as a whole - from assessing the past and current to assessing the future state of affairs.
System thinking is devoted to another book, The Fifth Discipline, which is also a bestseller and also authored by an American scientist, in which Peter Sange argues that any action has a compensating force and cites the situation with the elimination of the US trade deficit in the mid-1980s, for which the dollar rate was allowed to fall.
These actions were nullified by foreign competitors who simultaneously reduced the prices of their goods, and in countries whose currency is pegged to the dollar, the price level always automatically changes in parallel with the dollar exchange rate.
Or, in another example, the author shows how “the noblest government large-scale program to build cheap housing and retrain slum dwellers in the middle of many of America ’ s major cities ” undertaken by the US government in the 1960s also fell victim to compensatory feedback.
A lot of money was spent on the program, Sange writes, but in the 1970s the condition of many urban centers became even worse. Why?
In the cities with the best programs of housing and other assistance poured seekers of benefits from all over the country.
As a result, new apartment buildings were overcrowded and training programmes were inadequate for all those wishing to participate.
At the same time, the tax base of cities continued to decline, and the number of slums grew.
One can, of course, assume that foreign critics of the development of “emotional intelligence ”, insisting on the lack of a scientific base or explicit direct evidence of its advantages, in turn, have their own vested interests behind them.
But, after all, Victoria Shimanskaya does not refer to Russian scientists who could scientifically confirm and dispel the doubts of a number of foreign psychologists, but speaks about the evidence of the positive impact of “EI ” on the development of the child, citing studies of the American organization.
What is happening now in the United States, we see with our own eyes.
There was also much more excitement among American consumers than in Russia during the pandemic.
In principle, it is no secret that American consumers, like no other, are more susceptible to consumerism.
American scientists or psychologists were the first to talk about such a phenomenon as “emotional intelligence ”, but the United States failed to avoid today ’ s unrest.
That keeps one part of the US population from plunging into mass unrest or civil war and encourages another part of the population to rebel and overturn the old foundations of society.
On what such psychological weaknesses of the rebels are the manipulators and moderators of this whole situation playing?
What drives the rebellious – “emotional intelligence ”,“ system thinking ”?
What qualities will the Russians, who are going to replace the previous generations, have and will they care about the statehood of Russia?
Why is it not a statesman but a banker who speaks about the need to develop the skills of “emotional intelligence ” among Russian students?
Do bankers benefit from citizens who are able to manage emotions and deny themselves the pleasure of making purchases on credit?
Of course, they are not profitable, as they are unprofitable to corporations.
For example, a business needs good managers who are able to understand the emotions of customers and manage them.
But then should universities or schools at their own expense raise personnel for business, which can and / or will use the emotions of Russians for their own personal purposes?

title: Israel, UAE and Bahrain sign agreements on normalization of relations
text:
Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates have signed an agreement with Israel to normalize relations and establish diplomatic ties.
The signing ceremony took place at the White House.
Their signatures under the relevant document were put in the presence of US President Donald Trump and several dozen invited guests: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zeid al-Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latyf al-Zayani.
The agreements were signed in the framework of the previously concluded “Abraham Treaty ” with the mediation of the United States.
The title of this document refers to the common past of Islam, Christianity and Judaism, rooted in the first of the three Jewish patriarchs.
In a joint statement, the leaders of the three countries said that the signing of these agreements will allow all countries of the Middle East to continue moving towards peace.
The pathos of these words is hardly superfluous – the agreements are indeed breakthrough in nature.
To date, Israel has had formal diplomatic relations with only two Arab countries — Egypt (since 1979) and Jordan (since 1994).
The Arab-Jewish dialogue has been hampered by the Palestinian question for seven decades.
So far, the countries of the Middle East have shown solidarity with the Palestinian State in its struggle against the Israeli occupation.
The red line for a settlement for Palestine is the terms of the 2002 Arab Peace Initiative, which calls for peace with Israel and an end to the Arab-Israeli conflict only if Israel withdraws from the territories it annexed in 1967 (including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms) and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Israel not only refused to take such steps, but even planned to expand its sovereignty over the West Bank.
Such a step was planned within the framework of the “deal of the century ” prepared by the administration of Donald Trump.
However, after international condemnation of plans for a new annexation, Washington and Tel Aviv opted for a new strategy.
The result of the diplomatic efforts of the Trump administration was the normalization of Israel ’ s relations with the two Arab states at once.
However, as Andrei Chuprygin, senior lecturer at the HSE School of Oriental Studies, notes in a conversation with Gazeta.Ru, normalization of Israel ’ s relations with the countries of the Persian Gulf, including Bahrain and the UAE, began long before the recent events.
Informal cooperation between Tel Aviv and these states developed in the economic and strategic planes, through the special services and even through the political line.
According to the expert, as such, the Arab-Israeli conflict has not existed for a long time, and the problem of the Palestinian Authority is exclusively territorial in nature, rather than any other.
“The fact is that the further away from Gaza and from Ramallah towards the Persian Gulf, the more obscure these problems look for today ’ s Arab elite, especially for the large oil-producing Persian monarchies, which have their own tasks.
And these challenges do not extend as far as the solution of the Palestinian problem.
By and large, they don ’ t care much about the Palestinian issue, ” says the Arabist.
According to Andrei Chuprygin, the Arab world is tired of the Palestinian problem.
This was especially facilitated in recent years, when the dialogue between Palestine and Israel ceased to even look like an attempt to find a compromise, turning into an exchange of mutual accusations.
Another important factor in the normalization of relations between the Gulf countries and Israel, which experts point out, is the threat from Tehran.
“It so happened that they had a common enemy with Israel – Iran.
And in these circumstances, the Palestinian problem, it, of course, is relegated to the background for them.
The decision to normalize has much more to do with the security concerns they care about.
And they hope that this will give them even more opportunities to strengthen their security at the expense of the United States, ” said Irina Zvyagelskaya, head of the international affairs sector at the Center for Arab Studies of the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
At the same time, according to the expert, the normalization of relations between the Arab states and Israel does not mean the final closing of their eyes to the Palestinian problem on their part.
Such a development is seriously feared by Palestine, which is reacting rather acutely to the situation in the region.
“The normalization of some Arab countries ’ relations with Israel is a true reflection of the weakness and collapse faced by some Arab governments.
To say that normalization is in the interests of the Palestinian cause is empty, cheap and meaningless talk, ” said the special representative of the Palestinian President Nabil Shaath.
To demonstrate its opposition to the actions of the Gulf states, the Palestinian state recalled ambassadors from Bahrain and the UAE.
Nevertheless, Palestine has not been able to obtain unconditional support for its line.
On September 9, the Arab League refused to adopt a resolution condemning the UAE for normalizing relations with Israel.
The Palestinian draft did not receive the approval of the majority of the Arab League.
Despite the harsh tone from East Jerusalem, Abu Dhabi continues to speak of support for Palestine.
“The UAE peace treaty with Israel will not be implemented at the expense of the Palestinian cause and the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, ” UAE Foreign Minister Anwar Mohammed Gargash said after the Arab League meeting.
“This is not an end to the struggle for Palestine.
We are talking about strengthening the security and economic stability of Bahrain, ” said another Arab country.
“To say that by normalizing relations with Israel, they completely close the door to solving the Palestinian problem is wrong, ” Irina Zvyagelskaya agrees with the position of the Arab states.
According to the expert, the establishment of diplomatic contacts with Israel will give the Arab states more opportunities for dialogue, including on the Palestinian issue.
To some extent, normalization of relations can even be considered a deterrent: in order not to nullify the diplomatic achievement, Israel will probably refrain from provocative unilateral steps on the Palestinian track.
Thus, the official refusal of Israel to occupy the West Bank of the Jordan was recorded in the signed “Abraham Treaty ”.
Despite the fears of Palestine, the new trend towards normalization of Arab relations with Israel, according to experts, will only strengthen.
“Honestly, there is a feeling that other Arab countries will slowly join this process.
Each in its own time.
Obviously, setting certain conditions at the same time, ” Andrei Chuprygin summarizes.
Apparently, these events will not be long in coming.
During the signing ceremony, Donald Trump said that the example of the UAE and Bahrain “are ready to follow many. ”
“We have made significant progress with five more countries, ” he said.

title: In Washington, Israel officially recognized two more Arab countries - the UAE and Bahrain
text:
On Tuesday, September 15, Israel signed an agreement announced earlier by Donald Trump on the normalization of relations with Bahrain, as well as a similar document with the United Arab Emirates.
The ceremony took place in Washington on the lawn in front of the White House in the presence of the US President, First Lady Melania Trump and several guests.
This is reported by RIA Novosti.
The historic documents were signed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Ministers Abdullah bin Zeid al-Nahyan and Bahrain ’ s Abdel Latyf al-Zayani.
Three copies of documents were prepared for the ceremony: in Hebrew, Arabic and English.
Trump, through whose mediation the agreements were reached, signed the English-language versions.
In addition, Trump, Netanyahu and the foreign ministers of the UAE and Bahrain separately signed four copies of the “Abraham agreements ” (in English, Hebrew and two in Arabic).
Israel and the UAE have agreed on a full normalization of relations within the framework of the so-called Abraham Treaty, reached with the mediation of the United States.
Israel, under the terms of the deal, will temporarily postpone the decision to extend its sovereignty over the territory in the West Bank.
The agreement was later reached by Bahrain.
The Palestinian leadership has declared its strong rejection and condemnation of these agreements.
Trump said that the agreements of Israel, the UAE and Bahrain in the future may join “seven, eight or nine ” countries.
The fact is that most Arab and Muslim countries do not have diplomatic relations with Israel.
The exceptions are Egypt, which established diplomatic relations with Israel in 1979, Jordan, which established diplomatic relations with Israel in 1994, and Turkey, which was one of the first Muslim countries to recognize Israel.
Under an agreement to normalize relations between the UAE and Israel, Tel Aviv is suspending its plan to annex part of the West Bank for at least four years, Israeli media reported.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan said he was participating in the event "to reach out to peace and find peace."
“Thank you for choosing peace and suspending the annexation of Palestinian territories, ” the UAE foreign minister said in a statement to the Israeli prime minister.
Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid al-Zayani, in turn, stressed the need to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict on the basis of the creation of two states.
On Tuesday, the White House, with the mediation of the United States, held a historic ceremony of signing agreements on the normalization of relations between the UAE and Bahrain with Israel.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has signed agreements with the foreign ministers of the UAE and Bahrain.
Trump called the day “historic for peace in the Middle East. ”
According to The Guardian, Trump, during a meeting with the UAE Foreign Minister before the ceremony, answering a question about what message today ’ s event sends to the Palestinians, said: “I think one day we will see the Palestinians.
You will have a world without blood in the sand. ”
Earlier, the Palestinians criticized the decision of the UAE to normalize relations with Israel and called such an act “betrayal ”.
They also decided to withdraw their ambassador from the UAE.
The Hamas movement, commenting on the conclusion of the UAE and Bahrain agreements with Israel, said that they "cost less than the paper on which they are written."
Netanyahu said in the spring that it was time for Israel to establish its sovereignty over the West Bank.
We also reported that in the summer, Israel decided to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territories in the West Bank.

title: Palestinian leader: UAE pact with Israel is not peace in Middle East
text:
Peace in the Middle East will come when the United States and Israel recognize the right of the Palestinians to establish an independent state with East Jerusalem as its capital within the borders of June 4, 1967, WAFA reported on September 15.
The corresponding statement was made by Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas.
He also said that the condition for peace in the Middle East is a solution to the issue of Palestinian refugees in accordance with UN Security Council Resolution 194.
Abbas said in a statement that the people of Palestine are fatigued under Israeli occupation.
“Once again, we want to warn that there will be no peace, security or stability for anyone in the region without ending this occupation and restoring the full rights of the Palestinians, as stipulated in international resolutions. ”
After the signing by Israel, the UAE and Bahrain of an agreement on the full normalization of relations, American President Donald Trump said that he also expects the accession of Palestine - after some time.

title: The signing of the “Abraham Accords ” between Israel and the Arab countries. NEWSru.co.il survey
text:
On September 15, 2020, the signing ceremony of the historic agreement on the normalization of relations between Israel and the two countries of the Persian Gulf - the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain (the "Abraham Agreements") took place in Washington.
The UAE and Bahrain became the third and fourth Arab states to sign agreements with Israel, after Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994.
The agreement was signed by US President Donald Trump, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the foreign ministers of the Gulf countries – Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan (UAE) and Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayan (Bahrain).
Trump, in his speech, repeated a statement made before the signing ceremony that the UAE and Bahrain would be followed by five more Arab countries, as well as an agreement with the Palestinian Authority.
The US president was followed by Benjamin Netanyahu, followed by UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
It should be noted that in his speech, the UAE Foreign Minister thanked Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing to annex the disputed territories.
Among the guests were representatives of Oman and Sudan.
It is assumed that these countries will be the next to sign an agreement with Israel.
During the signing ceremony of the historic treaty, rockets were fired from the Gaza Strip into Ashdod and Ashkelon and wounded.
The IDF launched a series of retaliatory strikes against militant targets in Gaza.
After that, the terrorists shelled Sderot and other settlements.
The IDF again attacked the targets of the militants.

title: It Officially Happened: UAE, Bahrain and Israel Sign Agreement to Establish Diplomatic Relations
text:

The essence of the signed agreement was explained on his page in the social network expert Ilia Kusa:, informs enovosty.com / news.
However, the circumstances are still different – these states did not have a territorial conflict with Israel, and they did not fight against it.
