title: Credit Suisse names the main global consequences of the pandemic
text:
Some economists fear that the pandemic and the massive amount of fiscal and monetary stimulus around the world (according to the IMF ’ s October estimates, states spent $12 trillion on the crisis) will lead to an increase in global inflation, which has been at a low level in recent years.
According to the consulting company Yardeni Research (.pdf), the assets of leading central banks (the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of Japan and the People ’ s Bank of China), reflecting the size of cash injections into the financial sector and the real economy, by November 2020 grew by 41.5% in annual terms and reached $27.9 trillion.
The global money supply M2 (cash and non-cash) and other monetary aggregates increased sharply against the background of the pandemic.
However, Credit Suisse notes that since 1990, the growth of the money supply and the consumer price index are practically not correlated and it is unlikely that in the foreseeable future the connection between the two aggregates will recover.
Inflation risks can arise only if governments increase spending even more sharply, and the multipliers of these expenditures (that is, the degree of conversion of budget expenditures to final consumption) are much higher than they are now.
Or if central banks begin to service the political tasks of governments, however, it is unlikely that “central banks will become actual subdivisions of ministries of finance, ” emphasizes Credit Suisse.
Most likely, the postcoid world will be characterized by “sluggish economic growth and barely noticeable inflation, ” the bank writes, although rising inflation remains a“ tail ” (extreme) risk that can be realized due to demographic changes or political factors.
The end of multilateralism in international relations Multilateralism (foreign economic relations that benefit all parties to the partnership) and the role of multilateral institutions weakened even before the pandemic crisis, and it only strengthened this trend.
During the presidency of Donald Trump, the United States withdrew troops from Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria, planned a reduction in the military presence in Germany, withdrew from several international agreements.
At the same time, Americans are increasingly negative about China, and the United States is increasingly calling for a reduction in economic ties with Beijing.
“Countries around the world are looking to expand their base and reduce their dependence on others, especially China, ” Credit Suisse said.
One of the consequences of this policy will be the return of production to the native states (reshoring) and the diversification of supply chains.
China, for its part, will curtail some expansion programs in Latin America and the Middle East, focusing efforts towards Southeast Asia (the ASEAN bloc).
It is not yet clear what consequences - positive or negative - this will bring for Russia, the bank points out.
The coronavirus pandemic is the first global crisis in which global demand has sharply increased not only for American assets, but also for Chinese ones, says Konstantin Egorov, a professor at the Russian Economic School (his comments were sent by the NES press service).
“This is partly due to previous efforts by the Chinese authorities to raise the international status of their assets.
A big role was played by the fact that, in the opinion of many, China coped with the pandemic better than the United States, ” says Egorov.
The pandemic has led to an increase in the powers of states, which have devoted much more money to the fight against the crisis than, for example, during the global financial crisis of 2008-2009.
The emergency situation has allowed some state leaders to make emergency decisions bypassing parliaments through their executive decrees.
“When the crisis is over, some leaders will part with their extraordinary powers, but some will want to keep them, ” warns Credit Suisse.
Governments have helped businesses not to go bankrupt, and people not to lose jobs.
But the downside of such anti-crisis support was the risk of undermining the natural dynamics of the market and individual responsibility, the authors of the study believe.
In the context of “epidemic socialism, ” too much government power can lead to the creation of a stratum of citizens“ accustomed to relying on financial support and lacking the incentive to participate in a competitive economy, ” the bank warns.
The type of political regime (democracy or authoritarian rule) in itself does not seem to affect the effectiveness of the fight against coronavirus, Credit Suisse experts conclude.
Both options can fail as well as successfully deal with the crisis.
An effective response to a pandemic determines a set of factors, including previous experience in dealing with such circumstances, crisis management, public confidence in the authorities and reliance on scientific expertise.
Surveillance technologies and the massive collection of personal data during the pandemic opened up the possibility for states (and companies) to become “information empires, ” writes Credit Suisse.
The perennial dilemma between privacy and public safety is reemerging, raising a number of ethical questions.
For example, there are already futuristic predictions that the authorities will sooner or later want to introduce “subcutaneous ” control over citizens, when technology will provide streaming information about the state of the human body (body temperature, pressure, heart rate).
Technologies for analyzing mass personal data can also create opportunities to influence voters in democratic elections, the bank notes.
Inequality and the labor market The pandemic has led to an unprecedented expansion of remote employment.
One of the consequences of the transition to a remote mode of work will be a less binding of people to life in megacities and urban agglomerations.
“Small cities can survive the Renaissance and offer a worthy alternative to megacities, ” writes Credit Suisse.
“A year ago, it was impossible to imagine that a huge proportion of the population of a country, and even many countries, could stay at home and not go to work.
Turns out it's possible.
Technologically, we were ready to work in a remote format.
In some sectors, technology and skills have made it possible to do so virtually without loss.
I think we have yet to rethink the concept of the workplace, ” said NES Professor Natalia Volchkova.
The pandemic has also increased the risk of deepening socio-economic inequalities.
In particular, in many countries, the proportion of workers in the informal sector without basic social security is high, and it is this category that is at risk of loss of earnings due to the pandemic.
For example, in Russia from mid-2019 to mid-2020, employment in the informal sector decreased by almost 1.9 million people, the World Bank said in December.
“A comparison of this figure with data on the reduction of the total number of jobs suggests that the crisis hit workers in the informal sector most severely, ” the World Bank said in a statement.
The authors of the Credit Suisse study believe that the need to overcome inequality could lead to new redistributive taxes, triggering intercountry flows of capital and labor in response.

title: achievements in space, flight Crew Dragon
text:
In many areas, 2020 was not the best and easiest year, but for the space industry it was very fruitful for new achievements, records and discoveries.
We decided to remember only the most important events that remembered the space 2020, and remember something.
Despite the pandemic and panic on Earth, scientists and researchers continued to look into the sky and explore it.
Astronomers have discovered a black hole very close (on a cosmic scale) to Earth at a distance of only 1,000 light years from Earth.
NASA ’ s InSight probe has found that Mars is still geologically active, with “marsquakes ” occurring on it.
The Hubble Space Telescope is 30 years old.
Humanity continues its research, and Channel 24 has collected the most important achievements.
Cosmonauts reported that the air leak to the ISS is still ongoing Historical flight Crew Dragon company SpaceX After many years of refinements, the company SpaceX was finally able to send people into space and resume a nearly 10-year break in American flights.
The company passed the final stages of the NASA commercial crew qualification program, and in May for the first time delivered astronauts to the ISS.
Six months later, I was able to repeat this in the first regular mission.
As it turned out, the "space trampoline" works, and the Russian "Soyuz" has a serious competitor.
SpaceX has become the first private company to launch humans into space, and it ’ s not going to stop just at NASA astronauts.
About how the preparation for the historic flight of SpaceX and how it took place can be read in our material.
In general, 2020 for SpaceX was very successful, because in addition to regular missions to the ISS, Elon Musk continues to increase the constellations of Starlink satellites in Earth orbit and has already received the first customers in the beta test.
The ship of Elon Musk, or rather its test version under the number SN8, on December 10 passed flight tests at 12.5 kilometers and in this launch there was everything: a successful start, spectacular execution of maneuvers and an epic explosion during landing.
It should be noted at once that the tests were successful, because all the key objectives of the flight were fulfilled.
Even Elon Musk did not expect a soft landing, at first he generally believed that the test was more likely to end in failure.
Starship SN8 explosion during landing, video: As for landing, in the future it will be tested separately, because for a successful landing, SpaceX is still working on the design of the legs of the rocket and the shock absorption system.
In the meantime, the new SN9 prototype is already ready for the next tests, which will be held in early 2021.
Meanwhile, Elon Musk is very positive about the future of the ship Starship after the tests of SN8 and after the flight tests wrote in his Twitter loud “Mars, we go! ”.
Mars, here we come!! — Elon Musk (@ elonmusk) December 9, 2020 The Americans have already sent their 5th rover to Mars.
This time, in addition to the increased size and weight of the rover, for the first time on the "red planet" went and drone Ingenuity, which will perform a simple task - demonstration of work, without jokes, the only task of the helicopter - to work.
Ingenuity should safely land with the rover on the surface and separate from it, survive cold Martian nights, work autonomously and charge the batteries with solar panels.
NASA wants to demonstrate the possibility of flying a Martian helicopter in the atmosphere, which is 100 times more rarefied than on Earth.
The mission of the American spacecraft Perseverance is to search for ancient fossilized bacteria in the Jezero crater.
Also, experts hope there to find the remains of microbes or molecules stored in the clay.
Everything you need to know about the Rover Perseverance we collected in one material, which is available at this link.
All about the mission Perseverance from the Alpha Centauri team: Do not miss How it is to manage the rover: NASA engineer shared his impressions The journey of the rover is already nearing completion, it has been going on for six months and will end with a landing expected on February 18, 2021 in the Jezero crater.
As soon as the rover lands, the degree of descent will gain a little height and fall a few hundred meters from the rover.
How will the landing of Perseverance on the red planet can be read in this material.
It is also worth mentioning that in 2020, two more countries sent their devices to Mars: the United Arab Emirates with its Al-Amal, and China with its first Chinese interplanetary station Tianwen-1.
These devices will also be engaged in the study of the red planet, although they will have different tasks - the first will study Mars in order to create a climate map, and the second will search for traces of life.
Already by the end of the year there was no less important space event – Japanese researchers sent to Earth the soil of the asteroid Ryugu.
The Hayabusa-2 probe explored the asteroid for a year and successfully returned the collected samples for detailed studies.
In total, it was possible to collect about 5 grams of stones and dust from the surface of the asteroid, belonging to the early days of the Solar system.
This is the second such success (after the first Hayabusa), when people collected fragments of asteroids and delivered them to Earth.
Even more asteroid dust is already on the way to our planet, if everything goes according to plan, then pieces of the asteroid Bennu will fall into the hands of researchers in 2023.
NASA's OSIRIS-REx probe spent two years carefully studying the asteroid and even found a geyser on it.
In October, without exaggeration, the device made an impressive maneuver – it fired a pneumatic gun at the asteroid, approached it and captured soil particles.
The mission to collect samples was successful, too many soil samples were collected, so that they began to crumble, so they were safely hidden in a special capsule.
NASA engineers have preserved most of the precious material that scientists will study in three years.
Soil collection from the asteroid Bennu, video: The OSIRIS-REx space probe was launched in September 2016.
In January 2020, the spacecraft circled Bennu several times and examined the surface of the asteroid using spectrometers and cameras in search of the optimal location for soil sampling.
As a result, the mission specialists chose an area about 16 meters wide.
It is located inside a 70-meter young crater near the northern polar region of the asteroid.
We are used to seeing the Sun almost every day (if you do not take into account cloudy days), so we do not realize that researchers do not know much about the nearest star to us.
In 2018, NASA ’ s Parker Solar Probe came closer to the Sun than any other spacecraft in history – just 13.5 million kilometers, three times closer to Mercury ’ s orbit.
Although now the mission of the device is completed by only a third, it has already collected a lot of unique data about our star: for example, Parker confirmed that at such a distance from the Sun in space there is practically no dust, and the solar wind affects the rotation of the star.
In February, the European Space Agency launched its Solar Orbiter probe, which, although not as close to the Sun as Parker, has two special cameras to study the surface of the star and tools to study the solar wind, and they showed incredible results - the most detailed photos of our star.
Solar Orbiter: The world ’ s largest solar observatory, Daniel K.
Inouye Solar Telescope has also released its first data.
It is already being actively used to observe sunspots, and this data could lead to more accurate predictions of solar flares in the future.
In the meantime, the observatory showed the sharpest photo of the sunspot on the surface of the sun to date.
The striking “eye ” of the double of the Milky Way: photo of the day How first found, and then lost phosphine on Venus and why it is important Astronomers studying the clouds of Venus, in mid-September announced the discovery of traces of phosphine in high concentrations in the atmosphere of Venus, which on Earth is ejected by volcanoes and associated with the life of some organisms.
The finding caused a real stir, some research groups even began to process space missions for further exploration of Venus.
However, delight soon gave way to confusion, as other astronomers could not confirm the same discoveries and scientists withdrew their results before further research.
What is phosphine?
Phosphine or hydrogen fluoride is a poisonous colorless gas.
On Earth, this gas is produced as a result of the life processes of anaerobic organisms: some bacteria, fungi, algae and worms.
However, this is not the only source of phosphine, it can also appear in the atmosphere due to lightning, falling meteorites and volcanic activity.
Scientists began to talk about the active study of Venus after the discovery of traces of phosphine Subsequently, the presence of phosphine in the atmosphere of the planet was discovered after a detailed analysis of data from a 40-year-old NASA probe, but uncertainty still remains.
One way or another, the question of detailed study of Venus again began to vividly discuss, so in the near future we can get missions aimed at exploring this mysterious planet.
The scientific community wants to see a clearer picture of what chemicals are in the atmosphere of the planet and how they are formed, and to do this, you need to send an appropriate apparatus to Venus.
Of course, 2020 would not be complete without some negativity in the space industry, and the victim was the space observatory and one of the largest radio telescopes on the planet – Arecibo, which is based in Puerto Rico.
Problems with the telescope began at the beginning of the year, in August one of the cables broke and damaged the telescope mirror, then it was decided to begin dismantling the telescope.
However, the dismantling work did not have time to begin, because on November 30 at 23: 55 the cable that held the 900 ton structure of the reflector broke off and as a result the telescope mirror was irretrievably destroyed.
In 1974, Arecibo transmitted a powerful radio signal for possible communication with possible alien civilizations.
In 2014, the telescope was able to prove the existence of short radio bursts.
In 2016, astronomers discovered fast radio pulses that came from a single source.
However, it seems that humanity has not lost the telescope completely.
By the end of 2020 – December 28, the Governor of Puerto Rico, Wanda Vázquez, allocated $8 million for the restoration of the Arecibo Observatory.
The government of the island also declared the area at an altitude of 497 meters above sea level, where the observatory is located, and approved at the federal level an order to begin the reconstruction of the radio telescope.
The renovation and modernization of the Arecibo Observatory will be carried out by the state together with specialists from the University of Central Florida and the University of Ana G. Mendes.
The Government of Puerto Rico believed that the tragic destruction of the telescope provided the island State and radio astronomy with an opportunity to redesign the telescope, taking into account the lessons learned and the recommendations of the scientific community.
It is planned that the updated structure of the telescope will be able to serve for several more decades.
In 2020, humanity has made many discoveries and it will take a long time to list them all.
This shows that no pandemics and viruses can be a barrier to human thirst for knowledge and research, and the difficulties on the way to new discoveries only make us stronger.
2021 is sure to be no less fruitful and interesting and we will see a lot of important and spectacular missions and hear about amazing discoveries.
Therefore, follow us, and we will keep you informed of all important events in the scientific world.

title: 10 most interesting news of 2020 according to readers of 3DNews
text:
By tradition, at the beginning of each year, we remember what events we remembered the previous year.
The first days of 2021 will not be an exception.
Our website has already published a large review of what topics were the main topics in last year ’ s agenda in the world of computers and technology according to the editors.
Now we want to approach the question to the other side, and recall those news that caused the greatest resonance in our audience.
In the list below, we have collected the “golden fund ” – the top ten news of 2020 that have been read on our website the maximum number of times.
In May, the trade war between the United States and China entered a very hot phase of confrontation.
It was announced that the new rules of export trade will require obtaining permission (license) to trade with Huawei of almost any company, even outside the jurisdiction of the United States.
This was to cut off the Chinese telecommunications equipment manufacturer from all imports, including software.
It seemed that the goal of the United States was not just to slow down Huawei, but, figuratively speaking, to bury.
Seven months have passed since then.
TSMC really stopped producing semiconductor devices for Huawei.
But the Chinese foresaw this and even before the tightening of sanctions purchased from the Taiwanese partner such a number of 7-nm chips for 5G base stations that this number should be enough until the end of 2021.
And in 2022, Huawei expects to launch its own 20-nm production, which will gradually fill the shortage of imported semiconductors.
At the same time, Huawei did not fall out of international supplies.
Manufacturers began to find ways to sell products to the opal Chinese.
Samsung continued to supply displays, Qualcomm – SoC 4G, and Kioxia – server memory modules.
But there was no loss.
Huawei gives up its position to competitors both in the domestic smartphone market and in Russia, where it was displaced from the first place by Xiaomi.
In addition, the Chinese manufacturer had to sell the subsidiary brand and business Honor.
It is likely that Huawei equipment will be completely removed from the US networks, where the authorities have all the levers of influence on operators and business.
As for Europe, Huawei as a supplier of 5G base stations will retain its position in Germany and France, and, perhaps, in the UK, but things are worse there.
But in any case, the Europeans are holding on to Huawei.
In 2019, for example, a Chinese company created 220,000 jobs in the Old World and paid billions of euros in taxes.
But the attempt of the United States was a test, not to take it away.
According to the researchers, the popular TikTok application for the eponymous service of the Beijing company ByteDance for creating and watching short videos collects indecently a lot of personal data - much more than other popular mobile applications like Facebook, Instagram and Twitter.
This is worth thinking about, because you can be under the “hood ” of the Chinese special services.
But in fact, if that were the case, China ’ s intelligence services would have to applaud standing up, because they were able to turn a finger on the control and supervision services of Apple and Google app stores, which in recent years have become increasingly picky and picky about developers.
And the hype around the dangers of using TikTok has a simple explanation.
This Chinese app in the US alone has an audience of about 100 million people, and this is for the most part very, very young people.
In fact, TikTok is a potential tool of influence, which the US authorities do not want to put up with.
Donald Trump ’ s administration has tried to force ByteDance to sell the American segment of the business with its data centers to a consortium of American companies, but the election probably prevented the business from going through, and now the issue of TikTok will have to somehow resolve the administration of newly elected President Joe Biden.
Conducting thermonuclear reactions in terrestrial conditions has been a dream of scientists for 70 years.
The basis for this was laid by the Soviet physicists I. E. Tamm and A. D. Sakharov, who proposed in 1950 the idea of holding plasma in a magnetic field.
This was first reported publicly in 1956 in Oxford by I. V. Kurchatov, when he and General Secretary Nikita Khrushchev arrived in England to conclude agreements on cooperation between the two countries.
Since then, physicists have done a lot, but controlled thermonuclear reactions still last only a matter of seconds.
China took up the baton of the USSR and built (and will build) more than one experimental fusion reactor.
The HL-2M Tokamak reactor, which was commissioned in December, will allow heating plasma (hydrogen isotopes) to 150 million ° C and hold this temperature for up to 10 seconds.
However, in terms of plasma retention time, South Korea is still the leader.
South Korean tokamak KSTAR showed the ability to hold a plasma temperature of 100 million ° C for 20 seconds.
In the coming years, the Koreans will upgrade the facility to try to hold the plasma for up to 300 seconds by 2025.
All these tests precede the future launch in Europe of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), which is now being built with the participation of a dozen major countries of the world.
Tests of the Chinese HL-2M Tokamak will be a valuable source of knowledge for the future launch of ITER, because it will maintain the plasma at the same temperature level as in HL-2M.
Apple laptops are so elegant, and their components are so well fitted to each other, that the fashion to cover the lenses of built-in webcams with tape can end badly.
For example, an overhead shutter can damage the camera when closing the laptop lid or spoil the display, and the automatic brightness setting software and True Tone functions will stop working as they should.
This Apple reported in the technical support section, which can also be regarded as a hint of a possible denial of warranty service when detecting characteristic damage.
According to Apple, its security systems are fully protected, and attackers can not access the web cameras.
At the same time, three months before it became known that one of the security researchers received from the same Apple award in the amount of $75,000 for seven vulnerabilities found, three of which were directly related to the possible hacking of the camera on devices running macOS and iOS.
Should I put the camera on my laptop?
Everyone decides it for themselves in the measure of their promiscuity.
In the vast majority of cases, the ordinary user is not interested in anyone.
But he is a danger to himself.
Especially with the growing need for remote work.
Accidental activation of video communication at the most inopportune moment can easily put in an awkward position and there are many examples of this.
About once every 20 years, an event occurs when all the planets in the solar system are on one side of our star, and most of them line up roughly the same line.
In July of this year, the planets lined up just such a configuration.
The four planets — Jupiter, Saturn, Mars and Venus — could easily be observed at night and closer to morning.
Like everything related to space, astronomical phenomena were very interesting to our audience, which made the publication about the parade of planets the fifth most readable last year.
And this is natural: today for astronomical observations do not need any special knowledge or tools.
Smartphones and programs with maps of the starry sky with clear instructions will turn everyone into an astronomer, and digital cameras and multi-pixel matrices will help make photos at a good amateur level.
And if people look at the stars, then they have not lost hope for a better future, which is good in itself.
News about Russian developments always arouse interest, although passions in the comments boil, and disputants often have strictly opposite opinions.
In this case, as we understand, the degree of interest in the news was greatly increased due to the mention of the battery, because this is a sore spot of modern gadgets.
As for the battery itself, or rather the atomic battery, we are talking about the development of the National Research Technological University "MISIS".
The voltage in the described compact element is generated by converting radioactive beta radiation into an electric current.
Such cells are called beta-galvanic batteries (betavoltaic).
In principle, such batteries can remain operational for thousands or even tens of thousands of years.
Therefore, they are ideal for backup emergency power supply of low-power equipment or for organizing the power supply of electronics in remote and hard-to-reach places.
The MISiS battery is compact and can last for 20 years.
Unfortunately, it is not suitable for smartphones.
Special beta-galvanic batteries for smartphones and other consumer electronics is being developed by the American company NDB (Nano Diamond Battery), but the Russian atomic battery appears to be a much more real product than the promises of the Americans.
The popularity of the story about the battery repair of an electric car is another perfect illustration of the fact that the topic of batteries is among the “hot ” ones, especially in the context of Tesla.
The news about the “freebie ” six-year-old Tesla Model S for $15 thousand with a non-warranty and faulty battery tells how a third-party service discovered and replaced for $5,000 one faulty element in the traction battery, thanks to which the car buyer saved at least $10 thousand on a used, but fully operational and complete electric car.
As the number of electric vehicles on our streets increases, battery problems can become the main danger in the operation of personal electric vehicles.
Especially in a situation where some people want to save money and others want to make money.
But if “buckets with bolts ” in the event of a technical malfunction pose a threat primarily to the owner, then newfangled“ buckets with lithium batteries ” can cause serious fires and, as a result, large-scale damage.
Probably, in this area, we are waiting for strict regulation, to which the authorities around the world have not yet reached their hands.
However, Tesla is going to make the battery an integral part of the body design of the electric vehicle, which will require a different approach to the operation and repair of batteries.
Probably, in this case, the replacement of the cells at all will become impossible, as well as the replacement of the battery pack.
Electric cars will become disposable, which partially neutralizes the dangers associated with uncontrolled repair and operation of the machine over the period established by the manufacturer.
A swarm of military drones and a womb plane.
Sounds like a line from a science fiction piece.
Only here we are talking about real tests of prototypes of the Gremlin jet UAV, which at the end of the operation should be picked up in the air by a transport aircraft.
According to the idea, a special aircraft should collect four jet UAVs in flight within half an hour.
But the first tests of this kind failed due to design flaws in the coupling system.
Readers in the comments wondered why drones do not fly into the belly of the truck themselves?
One day there will be such, but for now it is better to “bait ”.
It's safer that way.
Praise the progress!
All over the world, the military received interesting and high-tech toys.
They would have played in them.
On the other hand, unmanned guided vehicles, UAV tankers, autonomous supply vessels and other auxiliary military equipment will reduce the need for live personnel in life-threatening combat areas.
It will be worse when computers are entrusted with making decisions to start an attack, and it goes to that.
A couple of weeks ago, during a simulation of a missile strike on an Air Force base in California, artificial intelligence on board a U-2 reconnaissance aircraft was already engaged in the search and identification of enemy missile launchers.
That is, the first experience when artificial intelligence controls the combat systems of a military aircraft already exists.
What will happen next?
A series of publications on foreign forums made it possible to look under the hood of the latest Tesla Model Y electric cars, where the cooling systems showed whether the transport packaging, which was forgotten to remove before installation, or additional fastening elements of radiators, assembled in a hurry from improvised materials.
For Tesla, this is quite a common phenomenon.
Moreover, as one of the former top ranks of the company said, in the first thousand – other serial electric vehicles Tesla, you will not find a single car that is repetitive in design.
This is partly a joke, but there is some truth to it.
As recognized by automakers with history, Tesla in terms of compliance with technology in the spotlight they are not fit.
But that has its advantage.
The management of the company with Elon Musk at the head is not afraid to change a lot on the go, compensating engineering miscalculations with the ingenuity of assemblers on the ground.
This is what allows the company to move forward at a speed that is ahead of the development of competitors.
In this case, only Chinese companies can compete with Tesla.
They have their own specifics, but they also know how to do everything quickly and profitably for themselves.
Our Milky Way galaxy is colliding with the neighboring Andromeda galaxy.
Accidents are inevitable, but the cosmic bodies of both galaxies will begin to approach dangerously only after billions of years.
Only gas halos around Andromeda and the Milky Way have come into contact so far.
Behind Andromeda and its gas halo, there are many quasars that perfectly illuminate all its unearthly beauty with ultraviolet radiation.
We can not look at ourselves from the outside, and imagine a halo around the Milky Way on the example of our neighbor.
By the way, it also turned out that once in our galaxy flew a dwarf galaxy in the course of another “cosmic accident ” and so it remained, torn into separate stars and matter.
Fantastic news becomes part of everyday life.
Exoplanets, the search for life hundreds and thousands of light years from us up to the determination of the chemical composition of the atmosphere - all this and many other discoveries give us modern science.
And it is just great that we have the opportunity to monitor all this without leaving home and almost in real time!

title: Pompeo appoints special envoy for economic normalization in the Middle East
text:
US Secretary of State Michael Pompeo appointed on Thursday, December 31, Rabbi Aryeh Lightstone to the new position of US special envoy for economic normalization between Israel and a number of Arab countries.
This is stated in a statement posted on the website of the US Foreign Ministry.
"The appointment of Lightstone will contribute to the speed and effectiveness of the normalization process and will give impetus to the Abraham Accords," the statement said.
As explained by the chief of American diplomacy, Lightstone will “represent the interests of the United States in the normalization of economic relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Sudan, Kosovo and Morocco ” and expressed the hope that other countries will join the agreements over time.
On December 10, the current US President Donald Trump announced the establishment of full-fledged diplomatic relations between Israel and Morocco.
On 23 October, Israel agreed to normalize relations with the Sudan.
Earlier that month, the Israeli Knesset approved an agreement to normalize relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.
The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.
The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.
One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.
This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.
The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.
They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.

title: Migration crisis: to catch up with Brexit
text:
French authorities reported that 237 attempts by migrants to cross the English Channel on flimsy boats were recorded in 2019, a figure three times higher than last year.
One of the attempts was made by the Ebrahimi family, they were rescued along with 19 other migrants.
Ebrahimi is said to have relatives in the United Kingdom who are ready to provide them with shelter and a table.
They say that despite the dangers to which their lives and the lives of children are exposed, they still intend to cross the English Channel.
According to the French coast guard, two years ago there were 12 attempts to cross the English Channel, in 2018 their number has increased sixfold, this year, according to official statistics, 1,400 migrants managed to get to the island, two of them died.
Their bodies were found on a beach in Calais in October.
French Coast Guard lieutenant Sebastien Maréchal said: "The farther they move away from the coast, the more difficult the weather conditions become.
And if a large cargo truck passes near their boat, it causes large waves, and their ship can simply roll over. "Smugglers, who receive large sums for each such transition and each person, keep their means of transport in places where the coast guard of the French Republic rarely visits.
Aware of this situation, the British Treasury has allocated an additional 7 million euros this year to help equip the French coast guard with the latest equipment, including drones.

title: Iran will be held accountable in order to establish justice and ensure payment of compensation to the families of the victims and affected states – statement
text:
Ukraine, Afghanistan, Great Britain, Canada and Sweden on the anniversary of the tragedy of flight PS752 near Tehran made a joint statement in which they promised to bring Iran to justice "with the aim of establishing justice and ensuring the full payment of compensation by Iran to the families of the victims and affected states," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine reported.
A year ago, in the early morning hours of January 8, 2020, Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752 was shot down by two Iranian military surface-to-air missiles near Tehran.
Today we honor the memory of the victims and express our sincere condolences to all those who mourn the victims of the tragedy PS752.
We share the grief of families, relatives and friends who have lost loved ones, "the countries said in a statement released by the press service of the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry on Friday morning.
On the anniversary of the tragic downing of flight PS752, the designated countries appealed to Iran to immediately provide comprehensive information about the tragedy.
“We urgently call on Iran to provide a full and comprehensive explanation of the events and decisions that led to this terrible plane crash, including concrete actions to ensure that it never happens again.
"Our countries will hold Iran accountable for justice and ensure Iran pays full compensation to the families of the victims and affected states," the statement said.
As reported, the passenger plane Boeing 737-800 of UIA airlines, which was supposed to perform flight PS752 on the route "Tehran-Kiev", was shot down near Imam Khomeini International Airport in Tehran immediately after take-off early in the morning of January 8, 2020.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
They're all dead.
Among the dead - 11 citizens of Ukraine (including nine crew members), 82 citizens of Iran, 63 - Canada, 10 - Sweden, four - Afghanistan, three - Germany and the UK.
Iranian authorities on January 11 admitted that the Boeing was shot down by mistake by the Iranian military.
Later, the commander of the aerospace forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Amir Ali Hajizadeh said that he takes full responsibility for the crash of the Ukrainian plane.
In late July, negotiations were held in Kiev with the Iranian side to pay compensation for the downed UIA aircraft.
On October 20, Ukraine and Iran completed the second round of negotiations on the downed UIA aircraft near Tehran.
On January 5, Ukraine received from Iran a draft technical report on the circumstances of the crash of the Boeing 737-800 aircraft.

title: The crash of the UIA aircraft: Kuleba said that he is doing everything to establish justice
text:
KIEV.
January 8. UNN.
Foreign Minister Dmitry Kuleba said that he and his team are doing everything possible to establish justice and all the circumstances of the downing of flight PS752.
On this day exactly one year ago, we all woke up in another world.
The world in which an Iranian missile killed 176 civilians – passengers of the Ukrainian Airlines flight PS 752.
They were citizens of Ukraine, Canada, Great Britain, Sweden, Afghanistan and Iran.
I bow my head in memory of each of the victims, and I share the pain of every loved one of the victims.
We remember and will never forget this tragedy, ” Kuleba said.
According to him, he and his team are taking all possible and impossible measures at all levels: consular, aviation, criminal and international law, which have only one goal – the establishment of justice.
“For us, justice is the truth.
We are doing everything to accurately establish all the circumstances of the shooting down of our aircraft.
I am sure that the day will come when absolutely all those responsible for this tragedy will be duly brought to justice, ” the minister said.
Recall that exactly at 6: 14 (Iranian time) on January 8, 2020, a Boeing 737 flight PS-752 of Ukraine International Airlines was shot down near Tehran.
As a result of the crash, 176 passengers and crew members were killed, including 11 Ukrainians and 63 citizens of Canada.
Iranian forces said on January 11 that the Ukrainian Boeing was shot down by accident, the fault was the human factor: the plane flew near a military facility of Iran and was mistaken for a “hostile target ”, namely a cruise missile.
At the same time, Iran noted that it expected an attack from the United States, in connection with which the country ’ s air defense systems were brought into full combat readiness.
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that he expects Iran to fully admit guilt, make an official apology, punish those responsible and pay compensation.

"Fiesta.

title: Project Syndicate (USA): long live biorevolution
text:
Project Syndicate (USA): long live biorevolution 00: 09 10.01.2021 Within the next 10 years, cultured meat and seafood can become a common commodity in our stores, the authors write.
Forty years ago, genetic engineering was firmly established in our world, and every year there will be only more artificially created meat, milk and other products.
Celine Pina, Michael CHUI, MATTHIAS EVERS SAN FRANCISCO - In November, the UN World Food Programme and the International Organization for Migration warned of an "unprecedented" threat to food security caused by COVES ID-19.
The collateral damage from a pandemic can be even worse than the disease itself.
Most of the leading international organizations concerned with food security have called for action to prevent future outbreaks of infectious diseases and to increase the resilience of food systems to shocks.
And we need to incorporate biological innovation into our thinking as we strive to meet the twin challenges of feeding a growing population and managing natural resources.
Even before the pandemic, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) warned that more than 820 million people were suffering from food shortages.
As the world's population is expected to grow by about two billion by 2050, improving access to affordable and healthy food will be critical to reducing malnutrition and related health costs.
Innovation in agriculture and food production is as old as agriculture itself, but today we desperately need it.
A recent study by the McKinsey Global Institute found that biological innovations in agriculture, aquaculture and food production could generate economic returns of up to $1.2 trillion over the next ten or twenty years.
For comparison: today, the world food industry and the agro-industrial complex are estimated at about $5 trillion.
What could provide such growth?
The most promising innovations include alternative proteins, selection using markers, genetic engineering of plant and animal traits, and mapping and modifying the microbiome.
Consumer interest in alternative sources of protein is growing worldwide due to concerns about animal health, the environment and welfare.
Plant-based meat substitutes are already common in many countries, although the economy of their production needs to be improved.
For example, plant-based milk accounts for 15% of retail milk sales in the US and 8% in the UK.
And companies like Clara Foods use advanced yeast engineering and fermentation technologies to produce non-animal egg protein proteins.
Similarly, in the near future, we expect the cultivation of meat and seafood, in which muscle tissue grown from cells in the laboratory mimics the protein profile of animal meat.
Earlier this month, Singapore became the first government to approve the sale of lab-grown meat (cultured chicken created by San Francisco-based Eat Just).
Over the next ten years, cultured meat and seafood could become cost competitive compared to conventional animal proteins.
Selective breeding of plants and animals is nothing new, but selection using markers has made this process cheaper and much faster, as it allows you to select the desired traits even in cases where the exact genes that generate them have not yet been identified or understood.
The drop in the cost of DNA sequencing means that thousands of potential markers can be detected simultaneously.
Previously, it took 25 years to create new varieties of crops, but today this process can take only seven.
And because marker selection is not yet as prevalent in developing countries as it is in advanced economies, the technology offers significant growth opportunities.
Since the creation of the first genetically engineered plant (tobacco) in the early 1980s, genetic engineering has firmly established itself in our world.
But, again, the technology continues to experience rapid improvement.
New tools such as CRISPR have made gene editing more accurate, allowing crops to adapt more effectively to local conditions such as temperature and soil type.
Products edited with CRISPR could appear on U.S. grocery store shelves within the next ten years, starting with sweeter strawberries with longer shelf life.
Another promising area of innovation is portable DNA sequencing devices that may soon be available to farmers to diagnose plant diseases, possibly improving quality and yield while eliminating or reducing pesticide use.
Genetic editing to improve the health and productivity of farm animals such as dairy and beef cattle, pigs and poultry is still in its infancy, but interest in the area has increased dramatically since the outbreak of African swine fever in 2019.
Similarly, mapping the microbiome, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses, helps researchers find ways to increase the resilience of crops, animals, and soils to drought and disease.
Here, advances in computation and sequencing are also accelerating the pace of discovery: for example, the biotechnology company Novozymes already offers genetically engineered microbes for use in place of chemicals designed to increase yields and quality.
Many of these biological innovations can help us cope not only with hunger, but also with resource depletion and broader climate risks.
According to FAO, raising farm animals for meat, eggs and milk generates 14.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions; and one-third of all arable land is used to produce animal feed.
Agriculture also contributes the most to deforestation, occupying 43% of the world ’ s ice-free and desert-free land.
Producing an Impossible Burger with a plant-based patty emits 89% less emissions compared to a traditional beef burger.
Climate change is increasing the need for biological innovations, for example, in crops that have been designed to withstand harsh weather conditions or grown in new conditions, including areas with extreme temperatures, high salinity or frequent droughts.
Many innovations are already contributing to food security, and over time we will unlock the full potential of affordable DNA sequencing and CRISPR technology.
Lab-grown meat will take longer to penetrate the market, but when it does, the impact is likely to be felt everywhere.
Regulation and public opinion have long played a role – both positive and negative – in biological innovation.
The first wave of commercially available genetic engineering products has yet to reach many countries, and 19 EU member states still support a partial or total ban on their sale.
In Africa, genetically modified foods are only allowed in a small number of countries.
Of course, safety should be a top priority.
However, if the safety requirements of regulators and consumers are met, the bio-revolution will be able to significantly advance us towards solving global problems such as food security and climate change.

title: In France, rescued 24 migrants trying to cross the English Channel on boats
text:
French maritime services intercepted two boats carrying migrants who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.
As reported on Sunday, the prefecture of the English Channel zone and the North Sea, a total of 24 people were rescued, Trend reports with reference to TASS.
"On January 10, the regional operational center for monitoring and rescue at Cape Gry-Ne received requests for assistance from several boats with migrants in difficult situations," the ministry's press service said.
So, 14 people were removed from the first boat and taken to the port of Dunkirk.
A few hours later, another 10 passengers from another boat were brought ashore.
After a medical examination, they were handed over to the border police.
The nationality of the detainees is not specified.
“All of them are alive and well thanks to the rapid response of the participants in the rescue operation, ” the prefecture added.
According to the prefecture of the region, in 2020 there were more than 9.6 thousand migrants who tried to illegally cross the border with the UK by sailing through the English Channel.
Of these, six people died, and at least three were missing.
A total of 868 rescue operations were carried out.
In 2019, the total number of detainees amounted to almost 2.3 thousand.

title: Dagens Nyheter: Trump ignores impeachment calls
text:
Washington, 15: 10 — REGNUM After storming the Congress building in Washington, President Donald Trump is seriously threatened by the prospect of being removed from office through the impeachment process.
However, the president himself does not plan to resign.
Instead, he will focus on resolving various issues during the working week that has begun.
This was reported by the Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter.
Follow the development of events in the broadcast: “The riot of supporters of Trump in Washington and its consequences are all the news ” The last days of the Trump presidency are“ among the most turbulent, ” the journalists emphasize.
After storming the Capitol on January 6, he is accused of “inciting ” crowds into the parliament building, and many, including members of his own Republican Party, are now demanding his resignation.
The demands for his resignation, President Trump seems to have decided to ignore.
Instead, on January 12, Trump will travel to Texas to inspect the construction of a wall on the border with Mexico.
Trump will also be working on some “transit issues ” this week, along with Pentagon officials and acting Defense Secretary Chris Miller.
Another item on this week ’ s agenda will be the completion of preparatory work for the conclusion of the so-called “Abrahamic Agreement ” between Israel and the two countries of the Persian Gulf — the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.
The document will contribute to the development of international cooperation in the region, after the three countries signed an agreement in September 2020 on the establishment of official diplomatic relations, journalists note.

title: Atlantic Council: Ukraine may not become an agrarian superpower due to climate change
text:
Ukrainian companies will have to change approaches and invest in environmentally friendly technologies if they want to continue to make money on food exports.
Last year was the hottest for the Ukrainian capital, as evidenced by data from the Central Observatory of Ukraine, published in January 2021.
In total, 36 different temperature records were recorded.
12 of them in March.
Extreme climate data of this nature are no longer shocking as the reality of climate change becomes harder to ignore.
Of course, 2020 was marked by record temperatures for the whole of Europe.
However, Ukraine ’ s role as an agrarian superpower on the rise makes the country particularly vulnerable to the negative impact of climate change.
About this in an article for the Atlantic Council writes a member of the Council of the Center for initiatives in the field of environment "Ecodia" Anna Akermann.
Read alsoLand plowing destroys the climate - expert Over the past few decades, the climate in Kiev has gradually shifted to the south.
The winter has become milder, and the summer is now much hotter.
The weather in the Ukrainian capital is increasingly reminiscent of Odessa in the middle of the 20th century, but without the Black Sea breezes.
This phenomenon applies not only to Kiev or the north of the country.
The most alarming and harmful factor in terms of changing weather conditions in Ukraine in 2020 was the shortage of rains.
The agricultural sector is heavily dependent on them.
But the rains last year were irregular.
They fell 8% below the annual norm.
In the east and south of Ukraine was the least rainy last year.
Donetsk, Luhansk and Mykolaiv regions suffered the most.
The impact of these adverse conditions is striking.
According to figures from the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources of Ukraine, the country has lost 570,000 hectares of winter crops due to prolonged droughts and unusually severe spring frosts.
Further droughts in spring and summer have led to additional losses that include 200,000 hectares of maize and smaller harvests of other crops across the country.
This threatens to undermine the status of Ukraine as one of the largest agricultural exporters in the world.
In the 2019-2020 season, Ukraine delivered 57 million tons of grain to international markets, which is 16% of global grain exports.
However, these volumes have decreased sharply in the current season, if you compare the years.
And all because of lower yields caused by arid conditions.
Read alsoThe return of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy, rising prices and a disappointing harvest: the results of 2020 in the agricultural sector of UkraineAs of December 2020, grain exports decreased by 16% compared to the same period last year.
Against the background of climate change causing damage to the Ukrainian agricultural sector, the Ministry of Environmental Protection predicts a further intensification and geographical spread of the drought.
Officials also expect an increase in desert areas.
Southern regions are gradually adapting to the lack of rain by developing advanced irrigation systems.
At this time, droughts are increasingly becoming the norm for agrarian regions in the north and northeast of Ukraine, where previously such conditions were not a problem.
Adaptation and mitigating measures are critical for maintaining Ukraine ’ s position among the main producers of agricultural products.
The lack of rain is just one of the many negative effects of climate change in Ukraine.
These include soil erosion, changes in vegetation, disruption of crop cycles, and the spread of new diseases and weeds.
Addressing these challenges requires the deployment of new practices and technologies.
Climate-oriented agricultural production can help increase productivity while increasing resistance to extreme weather events.
And also reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Meanwhile, the combination of irrigation and agrarian practices can bring a broad concomitant benefit to the water sector, while promoting the development of an agrarian economy based on more sustainable approaches to water management.
These and other decisions are likely to form the basis for Ukraine ’ s National Climate Adaptation Plan, which the government is currently preparing.
The European Green Agreement and the EU strategy “from farm to fork ” gives even more motivation for Ukraine to gradually switch to more sustainable agricultural practices.
The European Union continues to review and tighten its food and environmental safety standards.
At the same time, he plans to triple his own organic agricultural production over the next decade.
This should help convince Ukrainian agricultural producers of the need to invest in climate-compatible upgrades in order to preserve future access to the lucrative EU market.
Over the past few years, Ukraine has become one of the five largest exporters of agricultural products to the European Union.
In 2019, it was the second largest supplier of organic products to the organization ’ s countries.
Experts have estimated that Ukraine is able to increase its production of organic products 10 times in the coming years.
Lower yields will be offset by higher market prices.
The fast-growing organic product segment is just one of many areas through which Ukraine can expand its presence in the EU ’ s agricultural markets.
This makes compliance with European environmental and food standards a long-term necessity for the entire agricultural industry of the country.

title: Humanity predicted a shortage of rice
text:
Climate change will affect the areas in which most of the crop is now grown.
According to the authors of the scientific work, scientists estimate that by the beginning of the next century the population of the Earth will be about ten billion people.
For half of them, rice will be needed, but at least two billion may not have access to it.
While global warming in general should have a positive effect on plant growth, other effects of climate change could have a negative impact.
For example, a decrease in precipitation and the number of pollinators, as well as an increase in the number of pests.
To test how global warming will affect rice yields, scientists conducted a simulation experiment.
It turned out that due to the increased activity of microflora and changes in the chemical composition of groundwater and soil associated with rising temperatures and greenhouse gas emissions, arsenic will accumulate in plants.
This alone will reduce rice yields by 40%.
And in combination with other factors - one and a half times.

title: The second wave of the COVID-19 epidemic increased the suicide rate in Japan by 16%
text:
The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, increased it by 16%.
The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased it by 16%.
According to Report, this is written by scientists in the scientific journal Nature Human Behaviour.
"The COVID-19 epidemic has affected all aspects of Japanese society.
Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.
These factors may explain why suicides increased during the second wave of the pandemic, ” the researchers write.
In a new study, sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.
The country has the seventh highest suicide rate in the world.
The Japanese government constantly monitors suicidal sentiments and tries to prevent them.
The researchers used data collected by Japanese social services during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.
They were interested in how the most vulnerable sectors of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as those who had previously committed the least suicide, responded to the pandemic and its associated restrictions and unemployment.
The analysis showed that in the first wave, Japanese society reacted to the pandemic in a completely different way than in the second.
Surprisingly for scientists, in the spring of 2020, suicides in Japan became less: their number compared to the average of the past four years decreased by 14%.
But in the summer and autumn of the same year, this figure increased by 16%.
This mainly affected residents of small settlements, women and adolescents who previously committed suicide very rarely.

title: The second wave of the COVID-19 epidemic increased the suicide rate in Japan by 16%
text:
January 15, Minsk / Corr.
BELTA /.
The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased by 16%.
Such data scientists published in the scientific journal Nature Human Behaviour, reports TASS.
Sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.
This country ranks seventh in the world ranking of sad statistics.
The Japanese government monitors suicidal attitudes and tries to prevent them.
The researchers analyzed data from Japanese social services collected during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.
Particular attention was paid to the reaction of the most vulnerable segments of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as the categories that previously committed the least suicide.
"The COVID-19 epidemic has affected all aspects of Japanese society.
Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.
These factors may explain why there were more suicides during the second wave of the pandemic, "the researchers write.
This mainly affected residents of small settlements, women and adolescents who previously committed suicide very rarely.
The exact reasons are not yet known.
But the researchers suggest that these trends have both social and economic causes: rising unemployment, as well as school closures and social distancing.
Okamoto and his colleagues hope that they will be able to find out these reasons in the future and figure out how to prevent the number of suicides from increasing in the future.

title: The second wave of the pandemic led to a sharp increase in the number of suicides
text:
Aokigahara Forest on the slopes of Mount Fuji, which became known as one of the world ’ s most common suicide sites / Getty Images During the 2nd wave of the pandemic, the number of suicides in Japan increased dramatically among women and children.
These are the findings of research by Tokyo and Hong Kong scientists.
The suicide rate in the country increased by 16% in July-October last year.
This is reported by The Independent.

A possible reason was that the government offered subsidies to poor citizens, reduced working hours and closed schools.

Japan has one of the highest suicide rates in the world.

Suicide rates increased by 37% among women and by 49% among children and adolescents.
