title: New Kiev: pocket squares of the capital - how they will look and why they are needed
text:
Parks in Kiev promise to create right in the courtyards.
We learned where we got the idea and why it is important for the metropolis Kyivans rightly complain about the lack of green areas in some areas of the capital.
This problem is especially acute in the “sleeping areas ”, where maximum amenities are a bench near the entrance to the front door and a playground between the houses that has seen views.
To get to a large park, a person needs to spend time and money, and this is not convenient for everyone.
In the municipal association "Kievzelenstroy" offer to solve this problem, creating "house" or "pocket" squares, which will be within walking distance for residents and will decorate the yards.
Such squares have already appeared last year in the courtyards along Tatarskaya Street, near the houses along Academician Glushkov Avenue, at the intersection of Gonty and Teligi streets.
What they are and where they will appear in the near future, learned the site "Today". / Photo: Today Why do we need such squares In "Kievzelenstroy" say that the idea of creating pocket squares "peeped" from colleagues from Poland.
There are green areas near the houses appear everywhere.
“Large parks in megacities are far away.
It is not always convenient to get to them.
And we are well aware that the life of most citizens takes place within the boundaries of their yard: children play on the playground near the house, adults want to play sports, and pensioners go out to sit on the bench and breathe fresh air.
The yard space should be comfortable and beautiful!
We are well aware that laying two perpendicular paths, putting a lantern and two benches is not a landscaping.
Therefore, we work comprehensively and create new options for yard squares, ” explains Alexey Korol, CEO of Kievzelenstroy, to the Segodnya website.
According to him, to create "pocket" squares do not need too much money.
But it is important to take into account a lot of technical nuances.
“Engineering communications are laid near each house: warm and cold water, light, gas, telephone.
All this needs to be taken into account when repairing.
For example, on the site where the heating system is laid, it is forbidden to put a playground or plant a tree above it.
It's dangerous.
The process of creating "pocket squares" is time-consuming, deputies of the Kiev Council help us.
And with the already drawn project, we come to the residents of the house.
On the spot, we ask their opinion, discuss, make comments, explain why we offer to equip their yard in this way, why we want to plant such trees or bushes, ” says Alexey Korol.
Kyivans can appeal to the deputy of the Kyiv Council, who represents their district, with a request to initiate the overhaul of the square / park.
A local deputy submits to the KGS a proposal to include the object in the Program of Socio-Economic Development for the purpose of allocating budget funds.
For example, such a "pocket square" will soon appear on the street Enthusiasts, 3 / 1 in the Dnieper district of the capital.
Before that, the area near the house had a neglected view.
The "decoration" of the yard was the old destroyed room, garages, weeds grew around, and people walked along the trodden paths.
“We decided to make a children ’ s playground in the center.
It will be soft and safe to play.
The passage of residents to the transport stops was designed so that it did not interfere with children.
There are elderly people living in this house.
We'll arrange for them to play chess.
They are away from the tracks and the playground, equipped with canopies so that you can play even in the rain.
Throughout the territory we will install benches, urns, autonomous lighting on solar panels.
By the way, the light from them will not be bright, but muted, so as not to shine people through the windows, ” explains Alexey Korol.
In the "pocket square" on Enthusiasts there will be a flowerbed with a bridge to make it interesting for children to play here.
They will be able to run freely here - the square is far from the roadway.
Previously, simulators for outdoor sports were installed in this yard.
After repair, a rubber coating will appear under them to make it easier to jump off the horizontal bar.
Three more trainers were added.
Completely finish the work on Enthusiasts promise at the end of May, to the Day of Kiev.
Another "pocket square" will be arranged in the courtyard of the house on Lyatoshinsky Street, 26-b in the Goloseevsky district of the capital.
There is a large sports ground here.
“The elements of the old site will be dismantled.
Trees that grow in the yard will be equipped with circular benches for rest, a walking path will appear along them, we will plant lawns, "Kievzelenstroy reports.
Another adjacent square is promised to open in the courtyard of the house on the street Mashinostroitelnaya, 25-a in the Solomensky district of the capital.
By the way, this area the locals literally won from the building.
“Here we propose to make a square with a playground, a zone for sports, a place for walking dogs.
We'll install lighting, we'll lay paths, we'll make comfortable ramps.
Of course, there will be a complex landscaping of the yard.
We are currently discussing this issue with residents.
Planting of trees and perennial plants is planned here.
They will bloom all year round, ” explains Kievzelenstroy.
There will appear in Kiev and the whole house Lime alley.
Previously, it was a path of meter-long concrete slabs.
It is located between the residential buildings of Mayakovsky Avenue and Balzac Street in the Desnyansky district of the capital.
The area of ​ ​ the green zone is 2.4 hectares.
"The territory of the alley was neglected and neglected.
We took care of it last year.
More than half of the major work has been done.
The main task - the alley should be comfortable for people.
There were bike paths, a playground (near the street Architect Nikolaev), along the pedestrian zone new lighting.
Nearby - the boulevard part, plus repaired approaches to residential buildings.
By the way, linden trees along the alley were already old and in some places we had to plant new ones, ” Aleksey Korol tells us.
It is planned to finish all the works and open Lime Alley this summer, in July.
Recall that last Saturday, the site "Today" talked about what will be in Kiev parks near the water and where exactly they will open We learned how the Gostiny Dvor in the capital Podol can become.
Earlier, we told what will be after the reconstruction of Goloseevsky Park named after Rylsky.
We also reported on plans to radically change the Arsenal Square in the center of Kiev.
The buildings are planned to be covered with glass.
This year, the authorities of Kiev plan to build a bridge-wave on Obolon and improve Obolon Island.
We also wrote about the intentions of the city authorities to begin the construction of a cable car.
It can be a new form of transport for Kiev.

title: The Middle East Course: Will the Biden Administration Encourage Israel ’ s Rapprochement with Arab Countries?
text:
The Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates arrived in Israel for the first time in history to take up his duties.
Diplomatic relations between the kingdom and the Jewish state were established most recently, within the framework of the "Abraham Agreements".
Other Arab League countries have also established ties with Israel: Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan.
The main lobbyist for these decisions was Donald Trump.
Its task was to create a regional bloc to confront Iran, experts say.
The new US administration is still less inclined to the Middle Eastern monarchies.
However, experts have no doubt that Biden will eventually continue the previous policy of Washington in the Middle East.
The first ever Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to Israel, Mohammed al-Hajjah, arrived in Tel Aviv on March 1 to perform his duties.
The diplomat was sworn in as the kingdom's ambassador to Israel on February 14.
In January, an Israeli embassy was opened in the UAE.
“Today, I arrived in Tel Aviv as the UAE ’ s first ambassador to the State of Israel and met with His Excellency Gabi Ashkenazi, Israel ’ s Foreign Minister, to discuss the bilateral relations between our countries, which have been strengthening since the signing of the Abraham Accords, as well as enhancing cooperation in various fields, ” al-Hajjah wrote on Twitter.
Mohammed al-Hajj was sworn in as UAE Ambassador to Israel © wam.ae Al Arabiya reported that at a meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister Gabi Ashkenazi in Jerusalem, Mohammed al-Hajj said he was “honored to be the first UAE Ambassador ” to Israel, where he said he and the host had discussed a“ model of cooperation. ”
Also on the topic Pre-election peacekeeper: what is behind the intensification of Trump ’ s political activity in the Middle East Donald Trump announced that the United States will continue to withdraw troops from the Middle East as the situation in the region stabilizes. Head of the...
"My mission is to nurture and nurture our countries' relations... and we hope this will help bring peace and prosperity to the people of the Middle East," he said.
The UAE and Israel established diplomatic relations at a ceremony in Washington on September 15 last year.
The rapprochement took place within the framework of the so-called Abraham agreement.
The condition for the signing of the document by Abu Dhabi was the agreement of the Israeli side to suspend its expansion in the Palestinian territories.
This was stated then by the state Minister of foreign Affairs of the UAE Anwar Gargash.
“The United Arab Emirates has been able to secure Israel ’ s agreement to suspend the annexation of Palestinian territories in order to support efforts to achieve a two-state solution, ” he said.
It should be noted that the Israeli government in November ratified the agreement on visa-free regime between Israel and the UAE.
In turn, Abu Dhabi began issuing tourist visas to Israeli citizens in December.
The establishment of relations between Israel and the UAE took place with the active mediation of the administration of Donald Trump.
On August 13, 2020, the politician who held the post of head of the White House at the time, announced on Twitter that the kingdom and the Jewish state were ready to sign a peace treaty.
A statement by the United States, Israel and the UAE on the normalization of relations between Tel Aviv and Abu Dhabi was soon published, as well as a similar statement on the normalization of relations between Israel and Bahrain.
In September, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Foreign Ministers of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Bahrain Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Abdel Latif Al Zayani signed an agreement on the normalization of relations.
The ceremony took place at the White House in the presence of Donald Trump.
The signing of the “Abraham agreements ” between the UAE, Bahrain and Israel in September 2020 at the White House © REUTERS / Tom Brenner The neighbor and military partner of the UAE and Bahrain, Saudi Arabia is not in a hurry to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.
However, in 2020, Riyadh opened an air route over the territory of the kingdom for aircraft flying from the UAE to Israel and back.
Earlier, in January 2020, the Israeli authorities allowed its citizens to visit Saudi Arabia.
The administration of Donald Trump hoped that Riyadh would also join the “Abraham agreements ”.
This appeal was made in October 2020 by Mike Pompeo, then Secretary of State.
The hope that Saudi Arabia will consider the possibility of normalizing relations with Israel, the head of the state Department expressed after talks with his Saudi counterpart Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.
Also on the topic "Aggravation is not in the interests of the United States": what are the chances of maintaining the nuclear deal on Iran, the head of the IAEA, Rafael Grossi, intends to discuss with the leadership of Iran the implementation of the terms of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA)...
Following the UAE and Bahrain, Sudan joined the Abraham Accords.
This became known in October 2020.
Khartoum officially announced the normalization of relations with the Israeli side in January 2021.
The fourth Arab League country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel was Morocco.
Shortly before that, the US authorities recognized the country ’ s sovereignty over Western Sahara.
According to experts, one of the motives for the rapprochement of the Arab countries with Israel was the tense relations with Iran.
“This factor has pushed the Arab countries to establish relations with Israel, for which Iran is a key opponent.
However, this move by several Arab countries has divided the Muslim world – not all Arab states agreed to Trump ’ s terms.
Today, Syria, Lebanon, Algeria, Iran and a number of Palestinian groups continue their confrontation with Israel, ” said Boris Dolgov, a leading researcher at the Center for Arab and Islamic Studies at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Nevertheless, the conclusion of the “Abraham agreements ” was a very positive event for Israel, which is now opposed not by the entire Arab-Muslim world, the expert added.
Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia Mohammed bin Salman Reuters © Saudi Royal Cour "Israel has pledged to suspend the annexation of Palestinian territories.
So far, this is being done, ” recalled the debt.
A similar point of view is shared by Alexander Krylov, a leading researcher at the Center for Middle Eastern Studies at MGIMO.
“Tensions with Iran have become a rapprochement factor for Israel and a number of Arab countries.
As for the United States, the American leadership has long pursued such a bloc policy, seeking to bring its regional partners closer together.
And the United States tried to make sure that Israel ceased to be a regional pariah, and took an equal position in the Middle East, ” the expert said.
An important aspect of American policy Trump ’ s political rival, Democrat Joe Biden, promised to change Washington ’ s Middle East course during the 2020 election campaign.
During the election debate, the politician said that if he wins, he will stop selling weapons to Riyadh and make the leaders of the kingdom “rejected ”.
After the inauguration, Biden re-announced changes in Washington ’ s policy towards Riyadh.
This was stated by the 46th President of the United States in an interview with Univision.
In February, the Director of National Intelligence published a report on the murder of Jamal Khashoggi in 2018 in Istanbul.
The document claimed that the journalist was killed with the approval of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
After the publication, the State Department imposed visa restrictions on 76 Saudi citizens “who are suspected of threatening activities directed against dissidents abroad and including, among other things, the murder of Khashoggi. ”
“While the United States remains committed to maintaining relations with Saudi Arabia, President Biden has made it clear that this partnership must reflect American values, ” Secretary of State Anthony Blinken said in a statement.
At the same time, the White House did not impose sanctions personally against the Saudi Crown Prince.
As White House press secretary Jen Psaki explained in an interview with CNN, there are other “effective ways ” and, although the US relationship with Saudi Arabia will be adjusted, their preservation is in American interests.
Also on the topic “Advancing America ’ s Mission ”: how the new US administration will conduct its course in the Middle East, the US State Department is recruiting a team of specialists whose knowledge will play an important role“ in advancing America ’ s mission in the Middle East. ” About...
Relations between the US and the UAE are also experiencing some decline.
So, in January, the media reported that the Biden administration is studying the issue of purchasing American weapons to Abu Dhabi, including the supply of advanced F-35 fighters to the kingdom.
The suspension of a number of arms deals was confirmed by the State Department.
Also in early February, it became known about the intention of the new administration to reconsider Trump ’ s decision to cancel import duties on aluminum supplied from the UAE.
We are talking about tariffs of 10%.
However, experts doubt that the administration of Joe Biden will decide to seriously change the Middle East course of the United States and take drastic measures in relation to regional partners.
“The Palestinian-Israeli track of American policy will not change, in general, the previous course will remain, ” said Alexander Krylov.
A similar view is held by Boris Debts.
According to the expert, Washington will continue to follow the line in the Middle East, which was laid more than a decade ago - with an emphasis on partnership with the monarchies of the Persian Gulf and Israel.
Israel ’ s rapprochement with Arab countries will also continue with the support of the United States, since this is beneficial to the Israeli side and Washington, the expert believes.

title: Byakova Olga Yurievna
text:
The Olvia Center for Plastic Surgery and Aesthetic Cosmetology was founded in 1992 and is one of the first licensed clinics in the Rostov Region among private medical organizations.
Impeccable reputation is one of the priorities in the work.
The uniqueness of the Center lies in the fact that all specialists: surgeons, cosmetologists, anti-aging medicine doctor, nutritionist, reflexologist, engaged in youth and beauty, are located on the territory of one clinic.
This not only saves the patient ’ s time, but also allows you to get comprehensive advice from qualified specialists in various fields in one visit.
The main areas of work are plastic, aesthetic and reconstructive surgery, injection, laser and hardware cosmetology and anti-aging medicine, diagnosis and treatment of various diseases by restoring the normal functioning of organs.
How did you get the idea to set up your own clinic?
In fact, it was just necessary at the time.
In order to grow professionally, be able to learn from the best specialists in the world.
Very often, the rigid framework of the system does not allow talented doctors to show themselves 100% and be useful to people.
My husband - Byakov Nikolai Ivanovich - a talented surgeon, it was clear 20, and 30 years ago.
This is already known in the professional community around the world, and then we were looking for literature in English, because there were no large congresses and there was no place to study, improve qualifications.
I wanted to prevent disease.
After all, it is important not only to treat, but to be able to prevent diseases.
I thought about the fact that it is necessary not only to extend the life of a person, but also to make sure that he lives fully and qualitatively.
There were no buzzwords like “biohacking ” or“ anti-age ” yet.
Now we conduct full non-invasive check-ups, individually select treatment and correction of the condition.
No templates, each person needs his own!
In general, I can say for sure that my intuition very often helped in life, including in work.
Therefore, a decision was made: if we want to do what we dream about, then we need to go on a free voyage and create our own, as we see it.
What difficulties have you been waiting for?
How did you come this way?
Everything that happens makes us stronger, doesn ’ t it?

title: The pandemic has caused a great trauma to the world – WHO
text:

“Because World War II affected a lot of people, the world experienced massive trauma.
Now, with the COVID-19 pandemic on a large scale, even more people have been affected, almost the entire world, ” Gebreyesus said.

“Mental health and psychological support for individuals and communities should be given high priority in all recovery plans, ” Ryan said, adding that funds should be allocated for these purposes.

title: It remains to wait 80 years: scientists promise a six-month summer and two months of winter in Russia
text:
By 2100, the summer in Russia and other countries of the Northern Hemisphere will last up to six months, if measures to mitigate the effects of climate change are not taken.
This conclusion was made by researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, reports Phys.org.
According to scientists, climate change will have far-reaching negative consequences for agriculture, human health and the environment.
The scientists analyzed daily climate data from 1952 to 2011 in the Northern Hemisphere.
The study found that the length of summer on average increased from 78 to 95 days, while the length of winter decreased from 76 to 73 days.
Spring and autumn also decreased from 124 to 115 days and from 87 to 82 days, respectively.
Accordingly, spring and summer began earlier, and autumn and winter - later.
The Mediterranean region and the Tibetan Plateau experienced the biggest changes in their seasonal cycles.
If these trends continue without any effort to mitigate the effects of climate change, the researchers predict that by 2100, winter in the Northern Hemisphere will last less than two months, and transitional spring and autumn seasons will also decrease.
This in turn will have a strong impact on agriculture, human health and the environment, the researchers warn.
So, the routes and timing of migration of birds will change, the plants will bloom in an uncharacteristic period for them.
These changes can lead to large disruptions in natural communities, the scientists point out.
In addition, according to them, with a longer growing season, people will inhale more pollen, causing allergies, and mosquitoes carrying diseases will expand their habitat to the north.
Seasonal changes can also be detrimental to agriculture, the researchers said.
Moreover, such shifts in seasons can cause devastating weather events.
“A hotter and longer summer threatens to increase waves of abnormal heat and forest fires across the planet.
In addition, warmer and shorter winters can cause instability that will lead to cold waves and winter storms similar to the recent weather collapse in Texas, ” said Tsunwen Zhu, a monsoon researcher at the Institute of Climate System of the Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences.

title: How India ’ s rice production can adapt to climate change challenges
text:
How rice production in India can adapt to climate change challenges 12.03.2021, 18: 38, News of the day ✔ Subscribe to our Telegram channel "Uncensored News" - t.me / ryb24 As the world population grows, the demand for food increases and arable land decreases.
A new University of Illinois study examines how rice production in India can meet future needs by adapting to changing climatic conditions and the availability of water, according to the portal phys.org.
“Rice is a staple crop in India, China and other Southeast Asian countries.
Rice consumption is also on the rise in the U.S. and elsewhere, "said Prasanta Kalita, a professor in the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering at the University of Illinois and lead author of the study.
“If you look at where rice is traditionally grown, it ’ s countries where there ’ s a lot of water, or at least they used to be.
They have tropical weather with heavy rains on which rice production depends.
In general, the production and processing of 1 kilogram of rice takes about 4,000 liters of water, ” says the professor.
According to Kalita, climate change could affect the availability of water in the future, and rice farmers must apply new management methods to maintain production and increase yields.
According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), by 2050 the world population will grow by two billion people, and the demand for food will grow by 60%.
“We will need a lot of effort to meet this demand, ” Kalita says.
“We will also need more water for crop production, drinking water and industrial use. ”
Kalita and her colleagues conducted a study at the research farm of the Borlaug Institute in South Asia in Bihar, India.
Farmers in this region grow rice during the rainy season, when heavy rainfall allows you to get a good harvest.
The researchers collected data on rice yields and climatic conditions and then used computer simulations to create future scenarios based on four global climate models.
The aim of the study was to assess rice yields and water demand by 2050, as well as to assess how farmers can adapt to the effects of climate change.
“Weather changes affect temperature, rainfall, and carbon dioxide concentrations.
These are important ingredients for the growth of crops, especially rice.
It ’ s a complex system, ” Kalita said.
“The results of our modeling show that the stage of crop growth is decreasing.
The time of full maturity - from the day of planting to the day of harvest - becomes shorter.
Crops ripen faster, and as a result, you don ’ t use the full potential of the crop. ”
The study shows that if farmers continue their current practices, rice yields will drop significantly by 2050.
But different management strategies can mitigate the effects of climate change, and researchers make a number of recommendations.
Traditional rice cultivation involves flooding the fields with water.
Planting rice seedlings requires about 15 centimeters (6 inches) of standing water.
According to Kalita, if the fields are uneven, then even more water is needed to cover the crops.
However, if farmers use direct-sown rice instead of seedlings, they can increase production by using significantly less water.
Another practice is related to soil protection technologies.
“The surface of the soil is constantly losing water due to temperature, humidity and wind.
If you keep plant residues on the ground, it reduces evaporation and preserves water.
In addition, when plant residues decompose, it helps to improve the quality of the soil, ” explains Kalita.
The researchers also suggest implementing strategies to prevent post-harvest losses.
FAO estimates that about 30% of the crop is lost or discarded after harvest, so efforts to reduce these losses could further improve crop availability and food security.
Overall, the researchers concluded that the best approach to increase rice production by 60% while minimizing additional irrigation needs is to combine conservation strategies and reduce 30% post-harvest losses.

title: Bill Gates made another statement about the scourge that could destroy the world
text:
Bill Gates spoke about a global catastrophe that is slowly but surely changing our world, and can lead to disastrous consequences.
We are talking about climate change, which is irreversible, but we need to adapt to it.
According to the billionaire and philanthropist, now the most important task is to mitigate the effects of climate change and adapt to life in new realities.
“Just look at the frosts in Texas last month and the wildfires in California last year to see that extreme weather events are becoming more common.
But the biggest damage is done too gradually to make headlines, mostly in places near the equator, and no one is at greater risk than the world ’ s poorest people, ” Gates said.
About two-thirds of people living in poverty work in agriculture, often relying on the food they grow to feed their families.
And a warmer world would be relatively problematic for affluent farmers in America and Europe, and potentially deadly for low-income farmers in Africa and Asia.
“The closer you live to the equator, the worse the effects of climate change will be.
There will be droughts and floods, which will more often take away the harvest.
Livestock will eat less and produce less meat and milk.
Air and soil are beginning to lose moisture, leaving less water for plants; in South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa, tens of millions of acres of farmland will become substantially drier.
If people living in the most critical areas do not have the accumulated money to buy imported food, they and their children are likely to become malnourished and become sick more often.
The problem can be solved through innovation.
In agriculture, it is necessary to work on the development of plant varieties that are more resistant to drought.
In addition, we need to find carbon-free ways to move and produce electricity.
For example, farmers from Africa who grew drought-resistant corn were able to collect 500 pounds per acre more than farmers who used traditional varieties.
In addition, we need to work on innovations that will help farmers prepare for unpredictable weather.
For example, sensors that tell you when to plant seeds and phone apps that help identify pests.

title: This is not told in school: 15 stories from real life, which you have not heard about
text:

The forger who saved the lives of Adolfo Kaminski / Photo boredpanda 18-year-old Frenchman Adolfo Kaminski forged documents for Jews during World War II.
One day he worked three days in a row to produce documents for 300 children until he lost consciousness.
Adolfo kept his activities in strict secrecy.
His daughter found out about it only during the writing of the book about his father.
Samaritan Parrots African Grey Parrots / Photo Pixabay Researchers trained African Grey Parrots to buy food using tokens.

Without any intervention from the researchers, parrots with tokens began to share tokens with their partners so that everyone could get food.

The answer was checked by the US Bureau of Standards using the UNIVAC 1101 computer.
To do this, I had to write a special program to perform such a large calculation.

title: How can trees make cities healthier, cleaner and cooler?
text:
Due to the steady growth of the world population, it is more likely that most people on the planet will live in a densely populated urban area at some point in their lives.
Scientists believe that in order to preserve health, we need to make sure that cities become green.
Studies conducted at the University of East Anglia have shown that having access to green areas can reduce the risk of type II diabetes, cardiovascular disease, premature death, premature birth, stress and high blood pressure.
Several of these diseases are among the top 10 causes of world mortality by the World Health Organization.
According to the United Nations, by 2030, 60% of the world ’ s population will live in cities, and one in three will live in a city with a population of more than half a million.
Increasing population density means destroying green spaces in favor of homes, making urban landscapes even more unattractive and widening the gap between rural and urban life.
In addition to aesthetics, cities have a big problem of pollution, smog and rising temperatures.
Scientists believe that the solution to these problems can be plants and trees.
To solve the problem of lack of space, urbanists resort to unusual solutions, such as green walls and roof gardens.
They suggest that rural and urban environments are not very different from each other.
Link between green spaces and life expectancy View of Beijing, China.
Mark Schiefelbein / Copyright 2018 The Associated Press.
All rights reserved.
How much greener should our cities be to improve our health?
After analyzing nine large studies, Lancet Planetary Health found that a relatively small increase in green space around the house can affect life expectancy.
The researchers collected information from 8.3 million people in seven different countries, and found that a 10 percent increase in green space led to a reduction in early mortality by an average of four percent.
The greening of the territories was measured using the so-called "vegetation index".
On this scale, arid desert would score 0 and lush rainforest would score 1.
Increasing this index by just 0.1 points improves the rates of early death of people living within 500 meters.
Along with other projects aimed at making Paris more environmentally friendly, the mayor of the French capital, Anne Hidalgo, announced last year the creation of an "urban forest".
In four places of the city, the authorities plan to create “islands of freshness ”, designed to withstand rising temperatures in the city.
The municipality plans that by 2030 50% of the territory of Paris will be covered by forest plantations.
To solve this problem, the authorities intend to use every available centimeter, including the roofs of houses.
In the UK, the government has also committed to planting more trees in cities across the country.
The £10 million plan announced last year aims to plant 130,000 trees in many cities from London to Aberdeen in Scotland.
Former Environment Minister Michael Gove called the trees “vital in the fight against climate change. ”
According to experts, green spaces have economic benefits.
“Our research has shown that parks and green areas benefit £34.2 billion of physical and mental health each year, ” Helen Griffiths, executive director of the UK ’ s oldest charity Fields in Trust, told Euronews Living.
Atlanta Trees: An instructive story of Atlanta in the United States, formerly known as the "Forest City."
David Goldman / Copyright 2018 The Associated Press.
All rights reserved.
Among the studies noted in the Lancet, there are those that show that trees can reduce pollutants in the air.
They also help to minimize the impact of noise and heat generated by heavy urban traffic.
Once known as the “City in the Woods, ” Atlanta in the U.S. is a good example for studying the effects of replanting.
Between 1973 and 1999, more than 225,000 hectares of trees were cut down for the construction of shopping centers, roads and apartment buildings.
The loss of this dense forest cover has led to the fact that during storms, one-third more water flows from the streets, which increases the likelihood of flooding.
To deal with new threats, the authorities resort to expensive preventive measures.
The green cover also lowers the temperature in the city, as the shadow keeps the sun away from the highly reflective materials that make up the buildings.
The example of Atlanta showed that trees reduce energy consumption in the summer, preventing cities from turning into "urban heat islands", or areas where the air temperature is 1-4 degrees higher than in the surrounding rural areas.
By reducing the need for air cooling, plantations reduce energy consumption in the area.
At the same time, emissions are reduced by almost 600 thousand tons of CO2.
By comparison, 127,389 cars produce this emission per year.

title: Scientists have told how global warming has affected agriculture
text:
According to scientists, over the past 60 years, global warming has led to an average decrease in crop yields by 21%.
Farmers in the United States were the least affected.
There, the yield of crops has decreased by only 5-15% since 1961, experts say.
However, in Latin America, the Caribbean and Africa, losses ranged from 26 to 34%.
It is not even that the climate on Earth has changed unevenly, experts say.
This is due to the ability of certain countries to apply modern agricultural technologies.
Here a simple rule works: the poorer the region, the worse the consequences of climate change, experts say.

title: In Russia, there may be problems with food production
text:
The yield of agricultural products in Russia by 2040 may decrease by more than 20% only due to climate change.
This conclusion was made by the staff of the All-Russian Research Institute of Agricultural Meteorology.
The situation is worsening around the world: due to climatic factors, according to the UN, 34 million people are threatened by hunger.
Warm countries, especially the tropics, are most at risk.
According to the coordinator of climate projects of the Russian branch of Greenpeace Polina Karkina, climate change entails an increase in extreme weather events, and they become more prolonged and destructive.
“In some places it becomes drier, in others there are floods, hurricanes, and somewhere plants simply cannot survive warmer temperatures or atypical frosts during the growing season, – quotes the expert“ Gazeta.ru ”. – All these are risk factors for agriculture, if it is not adapted to new conditions. ”
“Huge efforts and investments in increasing the productivity of crops (including new technologies, genetic engineering, etc.) no longer compensate for the losses from the frequent droughts and other weather and climatic phenomena, ” said Georgy Safonov, Director of the Center for Environmental Economics and Natural Resources at the Higher School of Economics.
Decrease in climate-induced yields leads to crises in the grain and food markets, rising prices, which primarily affect low-income groups of the population.
In Russia, alarming trends began to be noted 10 years ago: in 2010, due to drought, farmers lost 33% of the grain harvest, in 2012 - 25%.
The damage for these 2 years exceeded 300 billion rubles.
Droughts increased in the lower Volga region.

In the long term, experts predict the deterioration of climatic conditions until 2050.
“Everything will depend on the situation with greenhouse gas emissions in the world, – writes Gazeta.ru. – If all countries fulfill their promises to achieve carbon neutrality, the situation for Russia as a whole will be normal, and in a negative scenario, changes can be significant. ”

title: Sustainable development: why young people choose companies that work under this credo
text:
Sustainable development as a concept in its current form started 50 years ago.
It was in the 1970s that global structures such as the United Nations or the Club of Rome realized that man was actively influencing the planet.
In the 21st century, this resulted in the UN ’ s 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
What are these goals, why are they needed, what is the situation of humanity on Earth now and why we all should somehow become conscious and responsible for the future - in the material Delo.ua in the framework of the special project "Leaders of sustainable development".
As of 2019, there were 7.674 billion people living on planet Earth.
Today, according to TheWorldCount, there are 7.85 billion people.
The good news is that the rate of population growth is still decreasing, in the 1970s it was 2%, in 2019 it was 1.1%.
But it's still a lot.
According to the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, 8.323 billion people will live in the world in 2030, and 9.3 billion by 2050.
In 2100, there will be 11 billion people in the world.
The gross domestic product of the planet in 2019 amounted to 87.8 trillion US dollars.
Faceless numbers behind which lies human interaction with the physical world.
Remember the year 2019?
You ate, drank, traveled, bought things, lost things.
They left a carbon footprint.
According to the constantly updated consumption calculator, at the current level, we need 1.8 planet Earth.
Yes, almost twice as much as there is at the moment.
And that ’ s the average cut.
At the same time, we have one Earth.
It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.
We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.
And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.
For example, if you travel by car, at least twice a year fly to conditional Egypt, live in an apartment building, buy food brought by plane, you need 4.5 Earth.
At the same time, we have one Earth.
It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.
We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.
And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.
And it can happen.
Because behind every dollar of global GDP is energy and industry that meets the needs of the population.
We plow the land, destroy the forests, warm up the permafrost - and out comes the same carbon, which, in turn, leads to the greenhouse effect.
Which, in turn, causes climate change.
And this is not warming, as many people think, but an increase in the number of extremes.
Last year, Ukraine experienced fires in the Chernobyl zone, in the Zhytomyr region, in the Luhansk region.
It is seriously affected by desertification.
Kiev and Kiev region were covered by dust storms.
Already in 2021, the Ministry of Ecology said that pesticides, pharmaceuticals and heavy metals were detected in Dnipro.
Studies show that Ukrainian lands may lose their fertility.
Half of the country was flooded with rains and floods, in the second half the harvest was scorched by the summer heat.
Abnormally low rainfall drained the land.
All these are consequences of global climate change.
According to a study conducted by an international team of scientists from Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands, since 2008 disasters caused by natural phenomena have led to the displacement of 288 million people (including evacuations).
Three times as many people have left as have been the result of wars, conflicts and violence.
About half of people are forced to leave their homes due to flooding.
Agricultural productivity is declining.
The University of Maryland, in collaboration with Cornell University and Stanford University, has for the first time quantified the anthropogenic impact of climate change on global agricultural productivity growth.
In a new study published in the journal Nature Climate Change, researchers show that global agricultural productivity has declined by 21% since 1961, which the researchers believe is equivalent to a total loss of productivity growth over the past 7 years.
"Our study suggests that climate and weather-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity," said Robert Chambers, a professor of agricultural economics and resources at the University of Maryland.
Thus, since 1961, regions such as Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, which are in regions with warmer climates, have already experienced a slowdown of 26-34%.
The United States suffered less, with growth slowing by about 5-15%.
“Some people think of climate change as a distant issue that should concern future generations first.
But this does not take into account the fact that people have already changed the climate, — says Ariel Ortiz-Bobea, lead author of the study from Cornell University. — In general, our study shows that anthropogenic climate change already has a disproportionate impact on poorer countries that depend primarily on agriculture.
It seems that technological progress has not yet led to greater resilience to climate change. "
At the same time, regions suffering from water shortages, such as Jordan, are facing an exacerbation of this problem.
According to a Stanford University study, water depletion and population growth will halve Jordan ’ s per capita water consumption by the end of this century.
Low-income areas will be hardest hit: by 2100, 91% of households will receive less than 40 liters of water per day for 11 consecutive months of the year.
If society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.
If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.
Has the Covid-19 pandemic helped the world?
Reduced inequality, reduced production?
Did humanity think about the future?
Perhaps, but a recent study by historian Bas van Bavel of the University of Utrecht and ecologist Martin Schaeffer of the University of Wageningent says that so far everything is not too good.
They looked at the impact of catastrophes — like the plague — on humanity as a whole and concluded that they could exacerbate inequality.
“In times of crisis, the rules are usually rewritten.
The most influential social groups and organizations can use this window of opportunity to adapt institutional rules, thereby shaping the long-term distribution of wealth.
Because most societies have historically been unequal, in most cases the result has been a further increase in imbalances, ” van Bavel says.
At the same time, if society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, trade unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.
If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.
In 2015, the UN, as the largest unifying structure of mankind, collected 17 goals that must be fulfilled by 2030.
This is not just a declaration, each has a clear roadmap and KPI indicators.
Here are the goals: 1.
Eradication of poverty 2.
Ending hunger 3.
Good health and well-being 4.
Quality education 5.
Gender equality 6.
Clean water and sanitation 7.
Cheap and clean energy 8.
Decent work and economic growth 9.
Industrialization, innovation and infrastructure 10.
Reducing inequality 11.
Sustainable cities and human settlements 12.
Responsible consumption and production 13.
Combating climate change 14.
Conservation of marine ecosystems 15.
Conservation of terrestrial ecosystems 16.
Peace, justice and effective institutions 17.
The answer to this question is quite obvious: so that as many people as possible on planet Earth a) survive b) can lead a comfortable life.
More and more people are becoming conscious consumers who care where the product they consume comes from, how it was made and whether environmental norms or human rights were violated in its production or in its advertising.
“Everyone has realized that sustainable development is not just a buzzword.
Everyone realized that society — especially the new generation — wants business to embody universal values.
It doesn't matter how much you make.
It is important what you do for the world, for me, for my children, for our common future, ” says Elena Zubareva, head of the Association of Sustainable Development Leaders.
Science confirms these words.
The University of Hiroshima conducted a study and found that young people are ready to sacrifice their salaries for the sake of saving humanity and the planet.
The results were published on January 31 in a special issue of the journal Clean Production, dedicated specifically to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
“Many people in the popular media or even in everyday conversations say that the younger generation is more socially conscious and has behaviors focused on achieving sustainable development goals, but the scientific evidence is limited, ” said Tomomi Yamane, a researcher at Hiroshima University.
And young people are willing to give their income to work in companies striving to achieve the SDGs. ”
In total, scientists conducted two surveys.
The first surveyed 12,998 people in 2019 and 2020 and found that people between the ages of 18 and 30 were much more likely to value and practice sustainable behaviors, such as paying more for sustainably designed products.
“Corporations wishing to engage young people to buy or work for their products or services should incorporate the SDGs into their strategies and make a serious contribution to achieving the SDGs, ” said co-author Shinji Kaneko, a professor at Hiroshima University.
The second survey involved 668 university students.
As a result, it turned out that only 28% of people will go to work in a company that does not participate in the SDGs, even if the salary is high.
But in the company, which focuses on the goals of sustainable development, even with low pay, will go 56% of the students surveyed.
Most people – 87% – logically chose to work in a company focused on SDGs with high wages.
But it ’ s not just about students.
A study by the University of Copenhagen shows that climate labels that inform about the carbon footprint of meat products are prompting many people to choose more climate-friendly alternatives.
In the experiment, 803 participants were selected between six alternatives consisting of minced meat and a plant-based mixture, all without climatic labeling.
67% of participants agreed to learn information about the carbon footprint of products, 33% of participants refused.
Then they were all asked to choose again, but now the products had a label with information about CO2 emissions.
Those who initially wanted to learn about the product reduced their climate impact by choosing more sustainably produced products by 32%.
Those who didn ’ t want it were 12%.
"Our experiments show that one in three people do not want to know about the impact of the food they eat on the climate.
But at the same time, we can see that there is a psychological effect: when people are informed about the impact on the climate, more people buy a product with less CO2, ” says Associate Professor Jonas Nordström of the Department of Economics of Food and Resources at the University of Copenhagen.
Thus, we see that people are beginning to realize the fragility of the world in which we live, which, in turn, leads to transformation – society, states, and business.
Dmitry Bunetsky, specially for Delo.ua

title: This time, no hustle and bustle. SpaceX has conducted static tests of the emergency rescue system Crew Dragon
text:
SpaceX, which recently launched the Falcon 9 for the first time with a three-time flying first stage and a one-time flying nose cone, conducted static fire tests of the engines of the emergency rescue system (SAS) manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.
These tests are the second mandatory under the NASA Commercial Crew licensing program (the first Pad Abort Test simulating a rocket crash before launch and shooting the capsule from the launch pad SpaceX conducted back in 2015).
Recall that previous such tests in April ended in an accident, as a result of which the capsule of the Crew Dragon spacecraft was completely destroyed, and the manned flight to the ISS had to be postponed again.
According to the results of the investigation, it was established that the cause of the accident was a titanium check valve of the supercharging system.
New tests at Landing Zone-1 at Cape Canaveral, Florida, used a new fuel injection configuration with bursting diaphragm valves in the boost tubes — an improvement that should prevent the very possibility of a repeat of the scenario that led to the April crash.
Crew Dragon is equipped with two types of propulsion systems (low and high pressure).
The first with sixteen Draco engines is designed for orbital maneuvers and orientation of the ship in space, and the second with eight SuperDraco engines is responsible for shooting and controlled landing of the rescue capsule in case of an emergency.
SpaceX engineers conducted a series of tests, including the launch of Draco and SuperDraco in a specific sequence, simulating a reorientation scenario for re-entry into the atmosphere.
This time there were no "anomalies" during the tests.
Full duration static fire test of Crew Dragon ’ s launch escape system complete – SpaceX and NASA teams are now reviewing test data and working towards an in-flight demonstration of Crew Dragon ’ s launch escape capabilities pic.twitter.com / HCM vMRBQcW — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) November 13, 2019 If these tests are recognized as successful (now the teams analyze the collected data), then in December the same ship is used for an additional optional test of the SAS with the shooting of the capsule in flight (this is a SpaceX initiative to demonstrate the reliability of the SAS), and then for the first operational flight (Crew-1) with a crew in the framework of the Demo mission o-2.
The latter is now scheduled for the first half of 2020.
During future tests with the firing of the capsule during flight, the Falcon 9 rocket with Crew Dragon will take off from the cosmodrome, and at the moment of maximum aerodynamic drag, the SAS will work and take the capsule away from the rocket.
Shooting the capsule will occur at the stage of the first stage, so the second stage of the rocket for obvious reasons will be simplified.
Recall, not so long ago, SpaceX successfully tested new parachutes for Crew Dragon.
The second participant of the Commercial Crew Program — Boeing — plans the first launch of its manned spacecraft CST-100 Starliner, in which it will make an unmanned flight to the ISS, in December.

title: Where and how many trees will be planted: in the coming days, Rostov should be transformed
text:
Experts believe that there is a lack of greenery in Rostov.
The representative of the administration of the Don capital on the air of the radio "KP-Rostov-on-Don" reported how many trees in the Don capital will be planted in the near future.
According to the deputy head of the city Alexei Pikalov, already on April 10, several hundred young plantations will appear in the city.
TREES INFLUENCE NOT ONLY ON ECOLOGY, BUT ON HEALTH In the first program "Urban environment" - it started on April 7 and will go every Wednesday at 17: 03 on the waves of 89.8 FM - public figure Elena Khatlamadzhiyan and the head of the expert consultation center of the botanical garden of SFU Anton Popkov discussed today's greening of Rostov.
The participants of the conversation agreed that the number of trees in the city is much less than it should be in a large metropolis.
They affect our health and ecology, - activist Elena Khatlamadzhiyan began a conversation on KP-Rostov-on-Don radio. - For reference, one tree emits oxygen per day, which is enough for a family of three people.
A green plantation in one hour on an area of ​ ​ one hectare absorbs as much carbon dioxide as 200 people emit during this time.
In addition, an array of green spaces, located on a hectare of land, reduces the air temperature by 3-5 degrees, which is relevant in the period of global warming.
It also increases the humidity of the air by up to 20 percent, prevents the wind, eliminates the negative effects of solar radiation.
Psychologists say that trees have a beneficial effect on the human psyche.
For example, they reduce stress, prevent some brain diseases, ” Elena Khatlamadzhiyan added.
In turn, Anton Popkov added that trees also perform an aesthetic function.
Green makes the city more natural and natural.
During the broadcast, the words of the deputy head of the Rostov administration for housing and communal services, Alexei Pikalov, were given.
He noted that on April 10, the day of tree planting, the city will be significantly green. - It is planned to plant more than 500 conifers.

title: Humanity predicted a shortage of French fries and chips
text:
The most common variety of potatoes, which is ideal for making chips and French fries, is the "russet bourbank", but due to global warming, it has been threatened.
This is reported by the portal YCC.
This variety grows in North America, and for its irrigation use mountain snow, which, due to global warming, is becoming less.
It is “russet burbank ” that is preferred by many fast food restaurants around the world, as it has a high starch content and a special taste when frying.
Another risk of rising temperatures is that the starch can turn into sugar, said Richard Novi, an employee of the agricultural research service of the US Department of Agriculture in Idaho.
And this leads to darkening of the potatoes during frying, which makes it unattractive to the consumer.
To solve the problem, Novi and other crop scientists are developing hybrid potato varieties that will become resistant to climate change.

title: Why Biden invited “enemies of America ” Putin and Xi Jinping to the climate summit
text:
A coronavirus pandemic is raging on the planet.
But Biden prefers to fight “global warming. ”
Photo: REUTERS Traditionally, this holiday is celebrated in many countries in March.
On the day of the spring equinox.
However, on April 22, 1971, at the initiative of the "green" American Senator - Democrat Gaylord Nelson, a new Earth Day was established.
With an environmental bias.
On the half-century anniversary of this holiday, Biden is convening a summit.
Five years ago, on the same day, April 22, the famous Paris Climate Treaty was signed in New York.
Yes, the powerful of this world love all sorts of dates, symbols.
Democrats of the United States are known fighters against global warming.
The ideology of the movement was the vice president under Clinton, Albert Gore.
In 2007, he won the Nobel Peace Prize for his "sacred struggle", and his film "Inconvenient Truth" won two Oscars (as best documentary and for best original song).
Gore also made good money in lectures on the “impending climate catastrophe. ”
For an hour horror story he received a fee of up to $100,000.
The Gore case was continued by Democratic President Obama.
Its main achievement in the international arena was the Paris Climate Treaty, approved by almost two hundred countries in December 2015.
It commits to reducing carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere in order to combat global warming.
Republican Trump, becoming president, defiantly withdrew from the treaty.
He "drowned" for oil and gas.
Biden, who came to the White House, on the first day announced the return of America to the Paris Treaty.
And he introduced the post of special representative of the President of the United States with great powers on climate issues.
It was John Kerry, former US Secretary of State, an authoritative politician.
And here is Biden ’ s first international initiative – the climate summit, to which he invited four dozen leaders of the leading countries of the planet.
This clearly shows that the main priority of the States under Biden is not the fight against the coronavirus pandemic, which has already killed about three million people, including more than half a million Americans.
And with the so-called global warming. - At the summit, the mantra will again be heard that the temperature on Earth is rising due to industrial carbon dioxide emissions and this must be urgently addressed, - says Alexander LOSEV, a member of the Presidium of the Council for Foreign and Defense Policy. - Although any powerful volcano emits more carbon dioxide (CO2) into the atmosphere than the entire world industry.
Greenhouse gas is not only CO2, but also methane, water vapor.
Up to 70 percent of the greenhouse effect is created, by the way, by this steam and clouds.
And there is no global warming.
There are just fluctuations in the climate.
Heat and cold are constantly changing each other on planet Earth.
Alexander Losev, a member of the Presidium of the Council on Foreign and Defense Policy, has been working on space and climate issues for many years.
ELECTRICITY EATERS - It is expected that Biden will hear mantras about "carbon zeroing", "decarbonization of the economy", alternative energy, "green technologies" and so on in the spirit of Greta Thunberg. - Aristotle came up with the concept of "energy" to denote active human activity that is transforming the world.
This is the main thing that drives humanity.
The quality of life of people and in general any economic activity depends on energy.
Throughout human history, the amount of energy and resources used has determined the degree of development of civilization - from fire, first mined and carefully preserved in the Paleolithic era, which launched the social evolution of the species Homosapiens (Intelligent Man) hundreds of thousands of years ago, to the development of atomic energy in the age of high technology.
From the beginning of civilization to the present, there has been a hyperbolic increase in the population of the Earth.
With the advent of steam engines in the early 19th century, world energy consumption increases in proportion to the square of this population.
There are 7.7 billion people on Earth, and more and more energy is needed.
In addition, in the 21st century, a digital economy appeared in the world.
Already now it takes 12% of all electricity generation on the planet Earth! - They say, "mining" bitcoins - "virtual digital money", requires a huge amount of electricity! - According to estimates at the end of the first quarter of 2021, the total annual electricity consumption of the bitcoin network is 127.7 terawatt-hours, which exceeds the annual energy consumption of countries such as Argentina, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ukraine...
Research shows that at the current pace of digitalization by 2040 (that is, in 19 years!), digital technologies will require the equivalent of the entire amount of energy produced worldwide in 2010.
And its sources are not so many: traditional hydrocarbons (coal, oil, gas), hydropower, peaceful atom plus solar and wind generation.
But back in the 80s of the XX century, scientists proved that all types of alternative energy – solar panels, wind turbines and hydrogen cells are ineffective from the point of view of physics.
Except for thermonuclear fusion.
But this synthesis is still a matter of the distant future.
Experimental thermonuclear installations are currently under construction.
The assembly of the most famous - ITER (International Experimental Thermonuclear Reactor) - will be completed by the end of 2025.
Then comes a series of experiments with plasma.
Thermonuclear fusion itself is only planned for 2035, if the experiments are successful.
Russia is a participant of the ITER project together with the EU, China, the USA, Japan, India and a number of other countries.
And the emergence of a network of thermonuclear power plants in the world can be expected no earlier than 2070, if, of course, the safety of such technologies is proven.
- The main problem of "green" energy - wind and solar - low density of energy flow and power, in comparison with a much more efficient and inexpensive hydrocarbon, and even more so with the atom, - continues Alexander LOSEV. - However, we see that for political reasons, nuclear energy everywhere is curtailed.
Fossil hydrocarbons still dominate.
The share of such energy exceeds 70%.
And the word “green ” in application to solar and wind energy should be put in quotes.
Because the harm done to the environment in the production, use and disposal of supposedly “clean ” power plants, batteries and the excess amount of electricity needed to connect them to regional power systems is much greater than from old coal-fired thermal power plants.
Wind turbines and solar panels are too expensive!
Photo: Shutterstock Life confirmed the findings of scientists of the 1980s.
“Green technologies ” turned out to be extremely expensive and ineffective. – Why are they actively introducing them now in Europe?
In the same America, they plan to build powerful stations "Ocean Wind", "Vineyard Wind" and "South Fork". - Such energy can only afford very rich countries, whose central banks are able to print reserve currencies in unlimited quantities.
But “green technologies ” will not allow humanity to fully provide itself with energy in the amount it would like.
At least for the next 100 years.
- And what about the grandiose successes in this area, which are trumpeted by the "greens"? - One curious fact that struck even me the other day, accustomed to everything.
According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), 17.3% of the world ’ s final energy (heat, electricity) is now provided by renewable sources.
Of these, 40 percent - attention! - is obtained from traditional biomass: firewood, firewood, dried manure... - But when firewood, soot from the pipes comes smoke, polluting the atmosphere.
There is a notorious carbon dioxide, against which Biden fights. - But the trees will grow again for firewood, camels, cows, sheep in general every day throw fresh manure, you know, sushi!
Renewable energy sources in their pure form.
And you can't argue...
SCENARIO OF THE FUTURE OF THE CATASTROPHE - Oh, these glass-wipers! - On Earth, according to the UN, about a billion people do not have electricity, and three billion people use wood and other plant organics for heating houses and cooking.
It is clear that in such conditions there can be no real “green energy ” on a global scale in the coming decades.
"Green energy", as it is seen from Washington, in my opinion - this is a scenario of a future catastrophe. - Do not frighten, Alexander Vyacheslavovich! - This "green" concept includes not only wind turbines, solar panels, but also fashionable electric cars.
Which is supposed to be the future.
But let's count.
The total number of vehicles on the planet today, including cars, trucks, buses - a billion two hundred million units.
In 5-10 years, this fleet will exceed one and a half billion.
Each car is a power plant on wheels.
Thermal energy during combustion of fuel is converted into kinetic energy of motion.
A gas tank, in fact, a large “battery ”.
The power of gasoline and diesel engines of these machines already exceeds almost 3 times the total capacity of all power plants of the earth.
Imagine what will happen when the entire traditional fleet is replaced by electric vehicles! - There are such plans.
First of all, in the United States, the European Union... - How many new power plants will it take to provide energy to this whole machine?!
What will they burn?
Gas, coal, fuel oil...
Solar panels and wind turbines alone will not power hundreds of millions of electric cars.
The IEA study shows that the cost of transferring electricity from solar and wind installations is about three times higher than from coal-fired or nuclear power plants.
Wind power generation is typically available from 25% to 35% of the time; from solar panels, from 10% to 25%.
At the same time, the power generation constantly fluctuates.
Therefore, it is necessary to build additional infrastructure and disproportionately more power lines (power lines).
They can lose up to 8% of electricity!
This will require trillions of dollars of investment, and trillions of dollars will be needed for the construction of “gas stations ”.
No one's gonna do that.
In addition, the inclusion of “green ” sources in existing power systems dramatically reduces their reliability.
February 2021 clearly showed this in the state of Texas. - But there is a free energy of the Sun! - The energy of the Sun is a lot in space.
And the surface of the Earth, even in clear weather, receives only the equivalent of 0.7 to 1 kilowatt of thermal energy per square meter.
Theoretically, you can completely cover the Sahara, other deserts, the tropics with solar panels.
But nothing happens for free.
The costs are very high.
First, the very production of “environmentally friendly solar panels ”, as well as batteries for power plants and electric vehicles, is extremely dirty from the point of view of ecology.
The technology of producing silicon from silica resembles smelting iron from ore using coking coal.
Tons of carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxide, sulfur are emitted into the atmosphere...
Mining in Latin America of lithium, used in the production of batteries, destroyed millions of hectares of selva, forests, in fact, the lungs of our planet.
For the supports and blades of wind turbines and power lines, millions of tons of steel, copper, carbon fiber, plastics, rare earth metals are needed.
The density of solar energy flow is low.
The costs of converters, drives, regulators, coolers of transformation systems, power transmission over power lines are enormous.
In addition, part of the energy is lost in the networks, and any sandstorm - a frequent phenomenon in deserts - will easily cover the project of "green" electrification of deserts. - It is expensive to pull power lines from deserts, tropics to the abodes of civilization. - Problems are also that 80 percent of solar radiation goes to heat the panels themselves, and an increase in the surface temperature of the photocell by only 10 degrees can halve its efficiency.
Therefore, more than half of the electricity generated by solar cells in hot regions, such as California, have to spend on cooling the installations themselves.
Therefore, solar panels are much more efficient to put beyond the Arctic Circle and high in the mountains, where it is cold.
This is good only for electricity supply to small villages and weather stations.
In addition, we must remember that the cost of recycling solar panels, batteries is nowhere reflected in the costs.
And processing is not free and clean. - It is not in vain that a tax is introduced on the disposal of ordinary cars, packaging of goods, etc. - I have listed only a part of the problems of "green technologies".
The last severe winter in Texas showed another.
As soon as the wind turbines freeze, snow covers the solar panels, additional power is required.
They can be taken only from traditional, hydrocarbon energy.
In addition, without fossil fuels, it is impossible to produce wind turbines, solar panels or build hydroelectric power plants.
The production of steel and cement requires a huge amount of energy.
Just roasting the limestone and clay mixture components needed to produce cement requires heating to nearly 1,500 degrees Celsius for a few hours.
And the dam of the hydroelectric power plant takes millions of tons of cement.
Solar panels will not give us so much energy.
But there are still conventional construction, roads, bridges, mechanical engineering.
There are a lot of things that can ’ t be done with renewable energy alone.
Examples I cited – steel, cement, plastic, asphalt and fertilizers.
Prices for finished products made with only “green ” energy will be exorbitant and a very small number of buyers will be able to afford it.
“Green energy ” is universally subsidized by traditional and citizens ’ taxes.
The operation of a conventional gas turbine or fuel oil generator is still an order of magnitude cheaper than alternative sources.
Maybe even more.
No wonder the largest American investment banks said, they say, forget about global warming.
There is a raw material supercycle ahead of us.
The digital economy and enthusiasm for material-intensive “green ” projects caused a sharp increase in demand and higher prices for oil and other hydrocarbon energy carriers.

title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
text:
An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: for an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.
The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).
The MOXIE unit is capable of converting this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of the processing and is released back into the atmosphere.
The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.
During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a filter to remove dust and compresses it, providing pressure at ground level.
The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.
Ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.
The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.
This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the rover electronics located next to the instrument.
Future astronauts: breathe easier.
The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPersevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / HOsguer. hYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 The maximum estimated performance of MOXIE is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.
The test program includes at least nine more tests over two years.
These tests will be carried out under different conditions to assess the performance of the plant.
In the future, more large-scale oxygen production on Mars may come in handy for practical purposes.
First, oxygen is used as an oxidizing agent for rocket fuel.
For example, to launch a rocket with four astronauts from Mars to Earth requires about 7 tons of fuel and 25 tons of oxygen.
The ability to produce this amount of oxygen during the astronauts ’ stay on Mars will prevent this oxygen from being delivered from Earth – delivering a large and productive oxygen generator modeled on MOXIE would be a more practical solution.
Secondly, oxygen, which makes up 21% of the Earth's atmosphere, is needed for breathing - four astronauts will be enough one ton of oxygen for a year on Mars.
We will remind, the Rover Perseverance landed in the area of 45-kilometer crater Jezero, named after the village in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
This crater is located on the western edge of the Isis Plain (a giant impact crater north of the equator of Mars).
As scientists suggest, in ancient times in the area of ​ ​ the crater Ezero was a river delta, where organic matter and other potential traces of microorganisms that could have lived on Mars about 3 billion years ago could have been collected.
The crater itself was then filled with water and was a lake.

text:
111 Rover Perseverance tested the technology of extracting oxygen from the Martian atmosphere using the instrument MOXIE.
This is necessary for future manned missions to the Red Planet, because the oxygen obtained in this way can be used not only for breathing Marsonauts, but also as fuel, reports TASS.
About this NASA writes on its website.
The Martian atmosphere is mostly composed of carbon dioxide (about 96%), argon (about 2%) and nitrogen (about 2%).
Oxygen is only 0.146%.
A person cannot breathe such air, so for future missions to the Red Planet, experts plan to develop installations for the extraction of oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars or other sources.
In addition, oxygen can serve as fuel for rockets – if humanity learns to extract fuel on the Red Planet, then more payloads will be placed on Martian rockets.
The first installation, which can extract oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars, is installed on board the Rover Perseverance.
The device is called MOXIE and is comparable in size to a toaster.
To obtain oxygen, the device breaks down carbon dioxide (CO2), taking one oxygen atom from it.
A by-product of the reaction – carbon monoxide – MOXIE releases back into the planet ’ s atmosphere.
The device is made of heat-resistant materials, since MOXIE needs a temperature of about 800 ° C. Mission specialists first launched it on April 20.
As a result of the test launch, MOXIE received about 5 g of oxygen - this amount is enough for a person for about 10 minutes.
In total, the device is designed to receive about 10 g of oxygen per hour.
"This is a vital first step towards converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars," said Jim Reuter, deputy director of NASA's Science Directorate.
“MOXIE has a lot of work to do, but the results from this demonstration are very promising in light of the fact that we are approaching our goal: someday to see humans on Mars.
Photo by NASA

title: The expert assessed the prospects of creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars
text:
Creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars will not work, but it is possible to produce oxygen there for a small team of researchers, scientists or colonists, said Vladimir Surdin, a senior researcher at the Sternberg State Astronomical Institute, commenting on the NASA report on the successful extraction of oxygen from the atmosphere of this planet.
NASA reported that the Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time extracted oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars.
It is expected that this technology in the future will help astronauts produce rocket fuel on this planet, as well as create a breathable atmosphere for them.
“Creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars, of course, will not work.
There are no resources for that.
But creating oxygen, for a small team of researchers, scientists or colonists on Mars, of course, is necessary.
Carrying oxygen from Earth is too expensive, you need to get it on Mars, ” says Surdin.
To get a small amount of oxygen on Mars has all the resources, the expert is sure.
The atmosphere of the planet is made up of carbon dioxide, which is carbon and oxygen associated with CO2.
In addition, Mars has water consisting of hydrogen and oxygen.
That is, in fact, oxygen on the planet is already there, but it is in a related form.
"Of course, it would be possible to break down water molecules - this is a process of hydrolysis, which in chemical terms, maybe, would be easier.
But there is very little water on Mars, and it lies in the polar caps, so it still needs to be reached.
And the atmosphere is everywhere, so humanity went a more difficult way, but so that at any point on the planet it would be possible to provide astronauts with oxygen.
That is, they decided to break down carbon dioxide molecules, ” the source said.
He emphasizes that the device that stands on the rover, rather cunning.
Nevertheless, it has proven its efficiency, which means it can be scaled - to send to Mars already larger vehicles of the same type.
They will be able to provide not only astronauts with oxygen for breathing, but also rockets that will be refueled with fuel - they need liquid oxygen as an oxidizer for the operation of engines.
Naturally, all this is quite expensive pleasure, as well as astronautics in general.
For example, the last rover that arrived on Mars in February is worth $3 billion.
This is a small car that weighs about a ton.
It is clear that any space flight is very expensive, but if there is a desire to explore a new planet, then you have to spend a lot, ” Surdin concluded.
Earlier, American scientists found that most of the water that previously covered the surface of Mars, did not escape into space, as it was believed until now, and is in the minerals that make up the rocks of the planet.
