title: During the pandemic, residents of megacities began to appreciate “islands of nature ” more
text:
Sociologists interviewed residents of Moscow and Perth to find out what role urban green zones played for them during the pandemic.
It turned out that the majority of respondents in both cities consider contact with nature to be extremely important for mental well-being and many of them went for walks in their free time, despite the restrictions.
The results of the study, supported by a grant from the RSF, are published in the journal Sustainability.
For more than a year, the daily lives of people around the world have been subject to the harsh rules of the COVID-19 pandemic.
A particularly important component of urban infrastructure in quarantine were available green areas and water bodies.
Until now, the impact of the pandemic on the role of green spaces in the lives of citizens has been studied mainly on the example of large European cities, which is not enough for a comprehensive assessment of the situation.
Therefore, sociologists turned their attention to the comparison of such radically different in climate, culture and infrastructure megacities as Moscow and Perth.
Researchers from the Peoples ’ Friendship University of Russia (Moscow) and their foreign colleagues conducted a survey among 330 residents of Moscow and Perth, Australia.
The questionnaire contained 25 questions about the role of urban green areas and water bodies in the daily lives of people, the impact of quarantine on their pastime and well-being, as well as possible ways of developing green areas of the city.
According to the data obtained, more than 50 percent of residents of Moscow and 72 percent of residents of Perth during the pandemic, despite the restrictions, preferred to spend their free time on a walk.
At the same time, it should be emphasized that there was a significant difference in the degree of quarantine measures between the cities studied: in Perth, urban green areas (public parks, reserves, gardens, beaches) were opened during the entire period of the 2020 pandemic, while in Moscow for 1.5 months there was a complete ban on visiting public places.
This is due to the difference in the frequency of visits to green areas during quarantine: in Moscow, 56.9 percent of respondents visited green areas less often, while 59.4 percent of Perth residents did not change their frequency of visits, and 26.7 percent even increased.
However, immediately after the removal of restrictive measures in Moscow, the attendance of green areas relative to the pre-quarantine period increased significantly.
At the same time, residents of both cities stressed the importance of urban green areas in their daily lives.
The majority of respondents in both Moscow and Perth rated contact with nature as important or very important for physical and mental well-being (more than 97 percent of respondents from Perth indicated significance for mental and 85 percent for physical well-being, and more than 76 percent and 70 percent of respondents from Moscow, respectively).
When asked about the current state and possible improvements in urban green areas, the majority of respondents from both Moscow (55 percent) and Perth (77 percent) indicated that street greening activities would be the most desirable for them.
Also a popular response was an increase in the number of public parks and green spaces near their own homes.
In terms of infrastructure, respondents in both cities indicated the need for more benches, as well as shady places and canopies from rain.
Residents of Moscow additionally noted the need to create water bodies (fountains and ponds) and gazebos, as well as modern elements of the landscape, such as green walls.
This highlights the importance of improving urban green spaces to improve both the urban environment itself and the well-being of its residents.
Having analyzed the attitude of residents of Moscow and Perth to green zones and water objects within the city, we can conclude that, despite the differences in climate and socio-economic situation, the availability of "natural islands" is highly appreciated by all respondents.
This reinforces the idea that greening plays a crucial role in ensuring the sustainability of cities in a crisis, including one such as the COVID-19 pandemic.
“With our research, we wanted to emphasize that urban greening and environmental issues in general should be fully worked out and included in program documents aimed at the strategic development of urban agglomerations.
For modern urban dwellers, places that will allow them to maintain their health and well-being are fundamentally needed.
Such places, based on the results of our study, are parks, urban forests, squares, green courtyards - green spaces in the open air.
Rational planning of these places will allow not to close them in crises like the COVID-19 pandemic, but, on the contrary, to make them available.
This will be crucial for improving the overall sustainability of cities, ” concludes Anastasia Konstantinova, project manager for the grant of the Russian Science Foundation, candidate of sociological sciences, researcher at the Smart Urban Nature laboratory of the Peoples ’ Friendship University of Russia.

title: Among Japanese women who have had an abortion, about 8% decided to do this because of COVID-19
text:
Among women who had an abortion in Japan, about 8% decided to take this step because of COVID-19 1 minute The survey involved 1,965 Japanese women who applied to 178 medical institutions with the intention of having an abortion, the newspaper The Japan Times reported.
Of these, 152 patients, or 7.7%, reported that their decision was directly related to the pandemic.
Most of them (46 women) are in the age group 25-29 years and 20-24 years (35 patients).
When asked to name the specific reasons that prompted them to make this choice, 87 reported being forced to have an abortion because of the loss of their partner ’ s job or a decrease in their income.
Another 74 admitted that they themselves faced a fall in monthly income or unemployment.
42 patients said they were afraid of contracting the coronavirus during pregnancy.
The authors of the study stressed that at least 152 women could give birth if they had the economic resources to support themselves and the child.
At the same time, none of the patients reported termination of pregnancy due to domestic violence, which has faced a surge in Japan and many other countries after the introduction of the restriction due to COVID-19.
“Since the coronavirus tends to have a stronger impact on low-income people, measures need to be taken to support these women, such as improving counseling systems and providing financial assistance, ” the authors of the study said.
Earlier, Canadian scientists found that during the pandemic, the level of anxiety among mothers almost doubled.
Of the 1,300 participants in the survey, an average of 35% of mothers of school-age children reported symptoms of depression, while until 2020, the prevalence of this mental disorder did not exceed 19%.
In 31% of women, scientists identified clinically significant symptoms of anxiety disorder.
A key factor in the deterioration of mental health, the authors of the study consider the additional burden associated with the need to engage in distance learning of children and at the same time work from home, performing household duties.
Most mothers reported finding it difficult to maintain balance in their daily care, and this group had the highest rate of mental health impairment: 40% reported depression, 35% reported chronic anxiety.

title: British Border Guards Detain 39 Iranian Migrants in English Channel
text:
British border guards detained in the English Channel four boats with illegal migrants who were trying to reach the shores of the United Kingdom.
The incident occurred on Sunday.
A total of 39 people were on board.
All of them introduced themselves as immigrants from Iran, the Evening Standard newspaper reports, citing data from the British Interior Ministry.
Next, the detainees will undergo a medical examination, and then will be transferred to the migration service.
According to experts, illegal migrants are looking for any opportunity to cross the English Channel and be in the UK, where they are attracted by the social program, the possibility of obtaining refugee status and financial benefits, RIA Novosti writes.
Since the beginning of this year, about 1,500 asylum seekers have arrived in the UK, most of whom have risked their lives.
The Home Office is spending millions of pounds to combat illegal immigration.

title: The world ’ s largest aircraft took off for the second time
text:
The task of Stratolaunch has not been disclosed.
The world ’ s largest aircraft took off for the second time.
This was told by representatives of the developer company.
They said it was on board.
Stratolaunch is considered to be the largest operational aircraft in the world.
He was able to rise into the air from the site of the aerospace port of Mojave, located in the US state of California.
The test flight was recognized by experts as successful.
Recall that for the first time Stratolaunch took off in the sky in April 2019, the aircraft was developed with the participation of Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen.
The ship has the largest wing span.
It was designed to launch space rockets.
After Allen's death, the company's plans changed.
Experts abandoned the idea of ​ ​ creating their own rocket and decided to switch attention to the field of hypersonic technologies.

Video: Twitter / @ Stratolaunch

title: The world ’ s largest Stratolaunch aircraft completed its second flight
text:
Stratolaunch has taken another step towards its goal of launching hypersonic devices from the air.
On Thursday, the company completed the second test flight of its vehicle, which is now known as the world ’ s largest aircraft by wingspan.
The carrier rocket with a double fuselage and a wingspan of 112 meters for 3 hours and 14 minutes flew over the Mojave Desert at an altitude of 4300 meters.
Although it did not take off as high as during its first test flight a year ago (5,200 meters), it flew 44 minutes longer than before.
According to Stratolaunch, the successful flight confirms the flight characteristics and capabilities of the aircraft, and also confirms the improvements made to the carrier aircraft since its previous flight.
Dr Daniel R. Millman, CTO, said: “Stratolaunch is expanding our country ’ s ability to become a global leader in hypersonic technology.
“Today ’ s flight brings us one step closer to our promise to provide the world ’ s best hypersonic flight test services. ”
The company has already begun assembling a consumable version of its Talon-A hypersonic ship, which is expected to fly for the first time early next year.
The company has also begun assembling a reusable version of the Talon-A, which is scheduled to begin testing in 2023.
The goal of Stratolaunch is to be able to launch a reusable version of Talon-A from its carrier aircraft.
The Mach 6 hypersonic vehicle is expected to provide 60 seconds of hypersonic flight before returning back for an autonomous landing on a conventional runway.
As noted by Space, the activities of Stratolaunch may be of interest to the US military, since hypersonic vehicles are good weapon delivery systems due to their maneuverability.
Millman said the company is looking for ways to help the Department of Defense mitigate the risks for many costly flight tests.
He added: “Our test bench can carry a payload.
It has the ability to test materials and manage various profiles that are of interest to people across the spectrum in both attack and defense in terms of hypersonic. ”

title: Stratolaunch completes second test flight of world ’ s largest aircraft

title: The world ’ s largest aircraft returned to the sky after a two-year hiatus » DailyTechInfo
text:
Two years ago, the world ’ s largest Stratolaunch Roc aircraft took to the skies for the first time and made its first test flight.
And recently, the same plane took off again after a two-year hiatus, breaking away from the runway of the Mojave Air and Space Port, it, according to the planned test plan, made several maneuvers in the air and successfully landed on the same runway.Recall our readers that the Stratolaunch aircraft has two fuselages and a wingspan of 117 meters, which is more the wingspan of any other aircraft that has ever taken to the sky.
After a very long period of design and construction of this aircraft, he first took off in the air in April 2019 and spent more than two hours in the sky over the Mojava desert.Stratolaunch aircraft, later called Roc, which means "bird Ruh", was originally developed as part of a system of rapid space launches.
In the central part of the wing of the aircraft was to be attached to the rocket, which, being launched from a high-altitude aircraft, was to deliver its cargo to Earth orbit.However, after the death of the founder of the company Stratolaunch Paul Allen, the company had new owners who radically changed the direction of its activities.
Now the Stratolaunch Roc aircraft is already considered as a carrier, which in the future will raise to the height and launch supersonic reusable transport aircraft.Such a supersonic aircraft called Talon-A was presented to the public in April last year.

But it can also be launched by being lifted to a high altitude with the help of a Stratolaunch Roc aircraft.
And while the Talon-A aircraft is planned to be used as a flying test bench for aircraft electronics of the next generations and other similar technics.It was the possibility of future launches of Talon-A aircraft that was the goal of the second test flight of the Stratolaunch Roc aircraft.
The aircraft, powered by six engines from the Boeing 747, took off and performed a number of maneuvers, including a low pass over the runway.

title: Thaw squared: will wheat boil in the Arctic due to melting permafrost
text:
The topic of global warming is actively discussed largely due to the “green ” rise in the West and Greta Thunberg, who was given the floor even at the UN rostrum.
In Russia, many experts are rather skeptical about climate change, but the problem of warming is reflected in the Climate Doctrine of Russia, and officials from time to time make statements on this issue.
So, the other day, the Minister of Natural Resources and Ecology of the Russian Federation Alexander Kozlov said that over the past quarter century, the climate has changed, in connection with which due to the melting of permafrost, northern regions can become agricultural in the foreseeable future.
However, not all scientists and environmentalists share his position.
Thus, Greenpeace believes that warming will not create conditions for the development of agro-industrial infrastructure, and recall the failure of the Soviet program for the development of the Non-Black Earth region.
In turn, academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences Vladimir Kotlyakov is sure that we must prepare wisely for climate change.
Details - in the material NEWS.ru.
According to the head of the Ministry of Natural Resources of the Russian Federation Alexander Kozlov, since 1996 the climate has changed and in the northern territories "the concept of" permafrost "goes away."
In this regard, according to the Minister, it is necessary to learn how to manage what is happening now.
The official said that “every such region understands what will happen to it in 20-30 years – it will cease to be northern or suddenly become bright agricultural.
We have to adapt to that. ”
However, experts with such estimates do not always agree.
Ecologist Vladimir Chuprov said in a conversation with NEWS.ru that in his opinion, only the melting of ice and the increase in temperature will not create conditions for the cultivation of agricultural crops.
Any biologist and soil scientist will say that for agriculture, in addition to solar radiation and temperature, you still need appropriate soils and a certain humidity.
There is no such thing in the permafrost area.
There are wetted areas - the amount of precipitation exceeds the amount of fumes, which leads to waterlogging.
Chernozem we have been formed for 10 thousand years, and in the first decades [after the “departure ” of the permafrost] everything will“ float ”.
Yes, it will be warmer, but the moisture will be an unfavorable regime for growing crops in the open field.
And in any case, you need soil with a nutrient layer.
I do not know where the stories come from in the spirit of “we have mastered virgin soil, we will also master the Arctic, in which global warming helps us. ”
To develop agriculture in the conditions of melting permafrost is an erroneous and scientifically unfounded concept that can cost billions — not even rubles.
Vladimir Chuprov, project director of Greenpeace, project director of Greenpeace Chuprov noted that warming will create problems for the Russian hydrocarbon industry.
He said that as a result of thawing permafrost, hundreds of thousands of kilometers of oil and gas pipelines could lose stability, recalling that according to one version, thawing of soils on which a fuel tank stood could lead to last year ’ s environmental disaster in Norilsk.
In this regard, Chuprov warned that in Chukotka near Bilibino there are four nuclear reactors, in Yakutia - Vilyuyskaya HPP.
In addition, there is a port infrastructure in the Far North, and when there is less ice, the coast is “eaten ” by the sea.
Since we are talking about the Northern Sea Route, there are questions to ensure the safety of navigation.
In addition, the representative of Greenpeace recalled that dozens of methane craters were found in Yamal and other northern regions, representing colossal dips in the soil several tens of meters deep.
And if such deformations appear near or on the site of oil and gas infrastructure, the latter is threatened with destruction.
Chuprov believes that the only choice is the expensive strengthening of already built structures and the refusal to build new ones, such as plans to put a railway through Yamal.
As an alternative, he proposed to use the great potential of renewable energy, from which you can make “green ” hydrogen and, using the infrastructure of Gazprom ’ s gas pipelines, drive hydrogen for export instead of methane.
Leading researcher of the Institute of Geography of the Russian Academy of Sciences Maria Ananicheva notes that warming began in the late 1950s, but the permafrost melts very slowly.
She also believes that soon the transformation of the northern regions into agricultural is impossible, unlike the appearance of funnels, which Chuprov spoke about.
It is much worse - methane funnels are formed there.
Methane is a greenhouse gas, and everyone should be concerned.
The first persons at the meetings on climate declare that ecology in Russia is a priority.
But, judging by the huge number of accidents, such as at the Norilsk Nickel enterprise, we do not have a priority, or rather, we have the main thing - profit and poor control.
In the West, these are huge fines and endless checks.
For 30 years, the Arctic does not melt to such an extent that wheat will spikes.
I would like to know from Minister Kozlov what calculations led to such estimates.
What kind of work he referred to.
A well-known Soviet and Russian geographer, glacier researcher and academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences Vladimir Kotlyakov said that the permafrost border today is shifting to the north, which is very important for the economy and in general the structure of Russia.
However, he cautioned against being carried away by dubious theories that warming is an inescapable trend.
The economy has to be rebuilt, and this is very important.
The question is, how long will it last?
There is no direct answer to it, but the statement that warming will continue indefinitely is incorrect.
There is absolutely no evidence that it will only be warmer and warmer, and by the end of the century the annual temperature will rise by five degrees.
In my opinion, this cannot happen, because there are many factors of climate change, and anthropogenic is only one small factor compared to natural ones acting more powerfully.
Indeed, now there is warming, the permafrost recedes, which greatly affects the economy of the northern regions, but it is pointless to make any predictions for the distant future.
Vladimir Kotlyakov Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Doctor of Geographical Sciences, glacier researcher Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Doctor of Geographical Sciences, glacier researcher Kotlyakov noted that the Climate Doctrine of our country, which was signed by the President, says not just about climate warming, but that the economy should adapt to it.
This requires a lot of money, and in terms of changing the mind of a person.
Nevertheless, I would not define the future in such a way that it will necessarily warm and necessarily melt.
Warming on the Earth was repeatedly replaced by cold weather, and vice versa, — said the academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
The scientist added that a person “should always put his head on ”, aware of the impact of climate change on infrastructure.
He gave an example that melting permafrost would destroy oil and gas pipelines if they were simply put in a trench.
Therefore, such communications are laid above the surface of the earth, installing on special supports, under which cooling devices are placed, which in the case of thaws freeze the soil with freon and make it look like a stone.
Earlier, the scientific director of the Hydrometeorological Center of Russia Roman Vilfand noted that due to global warming, the concept of “permafrost ” may soon disappear and society will have to change approaches to the construction of infrastructure.
Later, Mikhail Zheleznyak, director of the Melnikov Institute of Permafrost Studies of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, emphasized that about 60% of the territory of Russia is occupied by “permafrost rocks of continuous and intermittent distribution ”.
They are not homogeneous in composition, properties, depth of occurrence and genesis.
Therefore, I am sure that it is not serious to say that half of Russia is under threat due to the melting of permafrost, although such a danger exists.
For example, in Yakutsk, which stands on stilts, there are many problems with the stability of engineering structures, however, according to Zheleznyak, they are associated more with operating conditions than with the melting of permafrost.
And in more southern regions with island and intermittent permafrost, for example, in the Trans-Baikal Territory or the Amur Region, this problem exists, since there is an intensive process of “degradation of permafrost ”.
This leads to intensive subsidence of the soil and deformation of engineering structures, as, in particular, in certain neighborhoods of Chita.
As for climate change, the melting of glaciers, it is, and we see and feel it.
Natural changes, sometimes catastrophic, associated with these phenomena are present.
Only natural disasters, as far as I remember, were in the 1960s, when there was no significant warming.
In the territories of human life, accidents and catastrophes are caused to a greater extent by human activity, as well as unwillingness to control the state of the environment and engineering structures <... >.
Climatic changes in this process occupy a small share, - said Zheleznyak.
In his opinion, today, when designing engineering structures, little attention is paid to the calculations of their long-term operation in critical scenarios, for a period of 50-100 years.
This, according to the scientist, puts the problem of life and livelihood in areas with the spread of permafrost in the first place.
Marina Yagodkina also participated in the preparation of the material.

title: 7 Foods That May Disappear Soon
text:
It seems that very soon we will not eat chocolate, drink wine and cook rice From pleasant, although not comforting - these products will begin to disappear irrevocably in thirty years.
Yes, it is hard to believe, but in the foreseeable future, chocolate, wine, coffee and avocado will cease to please us.
The reason is global climate change.
Clearly not for the better.
The foods we eat almost every day will become history for generations to come.
In this collection of 8 positions, they, according to research scientists, confidently disappear.
If you are in search of the most original gift, you will find options in our May holidays calendar.
Chocolate in 2050.
There is a very high probability that chocolate will not be produced by this time.
Cocoa trees bear fruit exclusively in humid climates.
Thirty years from now, Ghana and Côte d ’ Ivoire, the main suppliers of cocoa beans, will become too hot and dry.
Yes, cocoa is grown in other countries, but, according to scientists, a reduction in chocolate production cannot be avoided.
Another culture that will suffer from climate change is the banana.
A recent study by the University of Exeter (UK) says that by 2050, due to adverse climatic conditions in 10 countries, bananas may disappear.
They will be threatened not only in South America, but also in Asia and India.
According to a report by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), rising temperatures, sea levels and changing rain patterns due to global climate change will lead to scarcity of water and land resources.
And this is unacceptable when growing rice.
In Asia, the "viability" of land for rice cultivation could decline by more than 50% over the next century.
Another food product that is threatened with extinction is coffee.
We will feel it in 30 years.
The reason is the erosion of the soil on which coffee is grown.
The study, published in the journal Science Advances, says that popular varieties of coffee are at risk, including Arabica, which accounts for 60% of global production.
Robusta trees, which do not tolerate heat, will also suffer.

title: Business is unprofitable, and the authorities have no time: why residents of new buildings have nowhere to walk
text:
In the central districts of major cities, such as Moscow and St. Petersburg, there are more and more public spaces for citizens to relax.
These places become the center of attraction of residents and organically fit into the urban environment, which attracts investors and businessmen.
The situation on the outskirts of megacities is exactly the opposite.
Why is this happening and can the residents of new buildings somehow affect the number of green areas?
These questions were answered by Deputy of the Ministry of Defense of Shushary of St. Petersburg Olga Krasnova in the framework of a live broadcast organized by the Patriot Media Group and the FAN.
According to Olga Krasnova, if in the center of St. Petersburg there is a sufficient number of comfortable places for citizens to relax - parks, gardens, squares, then in new areas, where active construction and settlement, they are not always provided.
“In Shushary, there used to be sovkhozny land - fields, then they were transferred for construction.
The project did not include recreation areas.
Now we have two official green spaces of common use.
And one of them is a paved area where events take place.
And a small empty square.
“That ’ s it, ” said Red.
Plots of land for parks and squares, as the deputy said, there are, but they are privately owned.
Neither the developer nor the owner are going to invest in the development of green areas, and the city authorities can not do this, since the territory is private.
The issue of land redemption in state ownership is also not worth it.
According to Krasnova, usually the area is bought out for major federal projects or for the street and road network, but not for parks.
At the same time, she noted that, from the point of view of the business project, park areas on the outskirts of the city are not very attractive for investors.
“If it was profitable, then long ago took advantage of the opportunity – developers and owners would have made a shopping and entertainment zone.
But the park has to grow, it takes time.
But if the park was planned at the beginning of construction, then yes, ” she explained.
Private business in the development of green areas is not ready to invest, and the city authorities have many other problems to deal with the owners of plots.
In the same Shushary, the issue of transport accessibility and crowded schools is acute, so the construction of parks and squares will be considered last.
Such projects as “Your budget ”, in which residents offer their ideas, and the best of them are then implemented at the expense of the city, are also not quite effective, said Olga Krasnova.
Since the project budget is limited to 15 million rubles.
“It ’ s a good playground or two smaller ones.
There are not enough funds to create a park, first of all.
The second point is that residents offer from the heart, but when there is an in-depth stage of consideration of the application by the committee, nuances emerge.
The resident suggested, but he does not know that there may be networks on the territory, this imposes restrictions, ” the deputy explained.
All the problems in the new areas arise due to ill-conceived planning, Krasnova is sure: it is difficult to solve them when the developer has already handed over the objects.
Then, as a rule, it turns out that the newcomers lack clinics, green areas, dog walking areas and other amenities.
Since the land for this was not originally provided, it is virtually impossible to build them into the microdistrict.

title: A third of food and forests will disappear due to climate change
text:
“Our research suggests that a rapid, uncontrolled increase in greenhouse gas emissions could, by the end of the century, result in more than a third of the world ’ s current food production falling into conditions where food is not produced.
The good news is that only a fraction of food production will face unprecedented conditions if we collectively reduce emissions and the warming is limited to 1.5 – 2 ° C, ” said Matti Kummu, professor of global water and nutrition at Aalto University.
Changes in rainfall and aridity, as well as climate warming, are particularly threatening food production in South and South-East Asia, as well as in the Sahel region of Africa.
These are areas in which the ability to adapt to changing conditions is lacking.
Food production developed in a fairly stable climate, during the period of slow warming that followed the last ice age.
Continuous increases in greenhouse gas emissions could create new conditions, and food crop production and livestock simply won ’ t have enough time to adapt.
The study used two future scenarios of climate change: one in which carbon dioxide emissions are drastically reduced, limiting global warming to 1.5 – 2 ° C, and the other in which emissions continue to rise steadily.

title: Digital border and point system: how the rules of entry to the UK will change
text:
Digital border and point system: how to change the rules of entry into the UK 24.05.2021, 8: 08 1,566 London will introduce electronic entry permits in the American style.
Home Secretary Priti Patel said on Sunday that the UK will announce plans for a “fully digital border ”, including the introduction of an American-style electronic entry permit for pre-screening travelers to the UK, Mirror of the Week. Ukraine writes.
The minister will announce plans in parliament on Monday as part of a broader overhaul of the country ’ s immigration system, which will also include the introduction of a point-based migration system.
“Our new fully digital border will provide an opportunity to count people entering and leaving the country, giving us control over who comes to the UK, ” Patel said in a statement.
“Our new approach will make it easier to identify potential threats before they reach the border, ” she added.
Tightening immigration rules and ensuring border security were key promises by people like Patel and Prime Minister Boris Johnson, who advocated leaving the EU in Britain ’ s 2016 Brexit referendum.
Under the new plans, which will be made public on Monday, Patel intends to announce that people coming to the UK without a visa or immigration status will have to apply for an American-style electronic travel authorization (ETA).
The Home Office expects about 30 million ETA applications to be processed annually.
“What I am presenting and proposing tomorrow is a new legal migration and border strategy … that is based on digitalizing our borders but also on simplifying our immigration laws, ” Patel told Sky News on Sunday.
“I am introducing a new border law, which will be submitted to parliament next month, and in it we will specifically suppress and address the problems associated with illegal migration, ” she added.
“Not only will we have stricter checks, we already have very, very important law enforcement operations going on in France, in Belgium … and we ’ re really prosecuting and arresting smugglers. ”
Last year, about 8,500 people arrived in the UK, making a dangerous crossing across the English Channel, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, in small boats.

title: A repeat of the nightmare of 2015. Europe is facing a new migration crisis
text:
https: / / ria.ru / 20210525 / migratsiya-1733716124.html A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.
Europe is facing a new migration crisis, a repeat of the nightmare of 2015.
Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.
Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis.
And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from countries...
RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.
And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.
The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.
According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).
The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.
According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.
Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.
Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.
And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.
How long it took, no one can say.
According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.
While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.
The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.
Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.
And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.
Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.
Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.
However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.
And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.
In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).
It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.
Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).
Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.
And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.
It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.
For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.
This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.
Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.
However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.
This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.
That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.
After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.
Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.
At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.
Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.
Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.
Liberals can breathe freely.
But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.
According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.
Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.
If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.
They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.
This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.
There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.
Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.
And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise.
The readiness of Brussels to these challenges looks very doubtful.

title: The crash of the MAU plane. Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the UK put forward demands on Iran
text:
The crash of the MAU plane.
Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom put forward demands to Iran “The actions and inaction of the Islamic Republic of Iran are a violation of international law.
Our statement notes that our states, their citizens and residents on board flight PS752 suffered substantial and irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its obligations to ensure full reparation to the group of states.
The signatories demand that Iran acknowledge the wrongdoing and provide a full account of the circumstances that led to the downing of the plane.
Also, the foreign ministers of Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom demand a public apology, the return of the missing and stolen personal belongings of the victims, assurances of the prevention of such actions in the future, ensuring the transparency of the criminal investigation, as well as fair compensation to the families of those killed in the accident, regardless of nationality.
“We call on Iran to cooperate in order to determine the date of the official start of negotiations on reparations, which we will conduct in good faith, ” the authors of the appeal added.
Context: A Boeing 737-800 passenger plane of Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752, which was en route from Tehran to Kiev, crashed on January 8, 2020 near the capital of Iran.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
No one survived.
Among the dead were 11 citizens of Ukraine.
Most of the passengers were citizens of Iran and Canada.
Iranian authorities, initially claiming that the plane crashed due to a technical malfunction, on January 11, under pressure from Western leaders, admitted that flight PS752 was shot down by an Iranian missile by mistake.
Deputy Foreign Minister of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin July 23 said that the decryption of the black boxes, which was completed in France, confirmed the illegal interference in the work of the passenger liner.
On August 23, the Civil Aviation Organization of Iran released a series of data obtained from the onboard voice recorder and flight data recorder of the UIA aircraft.
According to the records, the crew knew about the emergency situation and tried to control the plane to the last.
The New York Times reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif gave an interview to Iranian economist Said Leilaz in March 2020.
In it, he admitted that the Iranian military immediately learned that the plane “International airlines of Ukraine ” was shot down.
Iran on February 20, 2021 announced the completion of the investigation of the disaster.
The Iranian prosecutor ’ s office accuses 10 people of involvement in the crash, among them the top military commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The Minister of foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmitry Kuleba called the report of Iran biased and promised to continue to seek punishment of Iran for this crime.
Yenin said that Ukraine will demand from Iran to continue the investigation.
The court of the Canadian province of Ontario on May 20 recognized the crash of the UIA airline as a deliberate terrorist act.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Saeed Khatibzadeh said the court had no jurisdiction to decide on a claim for damages in the plane crash because it occurred outside of Canada.
The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine is inclined to believe that the crash of the UIA plane in Iran was a terrorist attack.
Tehran insists on the version of the unintentional shooting down of the plane.

title: The country has the lowest number of births in the last 120 years
text:
Traditional marriage in Japan / Getty Images In Japan, with a population of 126 million people, more than 840,800 children were born in 2020.
This is the lowest number since 1899, when the Japanese government began to keep such statistics.
The number of births in 2020 was 24,407 less than in 2019, when it fell below 900,000 for the first time since 1899.
This writes Rzeczpospolita.
READ ALSO: Japan is accelerating mass vaccination against coronavirus These data show that the rate of aging of Japan ’ s population accelerated during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The average number of children per Japanese woman in 2020 decreased by 0.02 compared to 2019 - to 1.34.
At the same time, according to the Ministry of Health and Labor of Japan, the number of marriages in 2020 decreased to almost 525.5 thousand.
This is the lowest rate since the Second World War.
The number of divorces has decreased to more than 193,000.
Analysts expect that the impact of the pandemic on fertility will be even more noticeable in 2021.
According to preliminary data, from January to March 2021, the number of births in Japan fell by 9.2% year on year.
During the year, this number may fall to the level of 700 thousand.
Which means reaching this mark 10 years earlier than previously predicted.
Japan ’ s birth rate has been declining since 1973, when it was 2.09 million newborns.
The average age of a woman who has given birth to her first child is 30.7 years.
Tokyo has the lowest birth rate at 1.13 children per woman.
The highest in Okinawa Prefecture is 1.86.

title: Payment of compensation for the crash of flight PS752 should be preceded by bringing the perpetrators to justice – the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
text:
The circumstances under which the plane of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) flight PS752 was shot down near Teregan should be established before the start of the process of payment of compensation by Iran, said the speaker of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Oleg Nikolenko.
“The ultimate goal of the efforts of Ukraine and other affected states should be to ensure justice for the victims of the tragedy of the Ukrainian flight PS752 and their relatives and the non-repetition of such a crime in the future.
Of course, the issue of compensation is an important element of this process.
At the same time, it should be preceded by establishing all the circumstances of Iran ’ s downing of the aircraft and bringing the perpetrators to justice.
Only after that, we can talk about the amount of cash payments, "Nikolenko told Interfax-Ukraine on Friday.
He stressed that the specific amount of compensation should be the result of an agreement of the governments of all states whose citizens died in the plane crash, and not a unilateral decision.
"We expect Iran to faithfully implement the agreements reached during the third round of consultations on June 2-3 in Kiev, as well as the previous two rounds," Nikolenko added.
Earlier, Iranian Ambassador to Ukraine Manouchehr Moradi said that during the third round of negotiations between the deputy foreign ministers of Iran and Ukraine on the downing of the UIA aircraft, the Iranian delegation announced its readiness to pay compensation to the Ukrainian families of the victims in the amount of $150,000 for each.
As reported, this week in Kiev held talks on the downed near Tehran UIA flight PS752.
On January 8, 2020, a passenger aircraft Boeing 737-800 of UIA airlines, which was supposed to perform flight PS752 on the route Tehran - Kiev, was shot down in the area of Imam Khomeini International Airport in Tehran immediately after take-off.
There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.
They're all dead.
Among the dead - 11 citizens of Ukraine (including nine crew members), 82 citizens of Iran, 63 - Canada, 10 - Sweden, four - Afghanistan, three - Germany and the UK.
Iranian authorities on January 11 admitted that the Boeing was shot down by mistake by the Iranian military.
Later, the commander of the aerospace forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Amir Ali Hajizadeh, said that he takes full responsibility for the crash of the Ukrainian plane.
In late July, negotiations were held in Kiev with the Iranian side to pay compensation for the downed UIA aircraft.
On October 20, Ukraine and Iran completed the second round of negotiations on the downed UIA aircraft near Tehran.
On January 5, 2021, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmytro Kuleba reported that the country received from Iran a draft technical report on the circumstances of the crash of the Boeing 737 UIA aircraft on January 8, 2020.
In February, the media released an audio recording in which a man identified by sources as Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Zarif discusses the possibility that the destruction of flight PS752 was a deliberate act.
Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Yevhen Yenin said that the pre-trial investigation and the Prosecutor ’ s Office of Ukraine are investigating the audio recording.

title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
text:
Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.
"Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.
Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.
Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.
For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.
Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.
The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.
For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.
According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).
This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.
Surgeons here are like hairdressers.
The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.
Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.
Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.
The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.
Almost all patients are from the United States.
About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.
From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.
There are more surgeons in South Korea.
It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.
The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.
In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.
The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.
Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.
Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.
For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).
According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.
Most are from the Middle East.
Popular destinations for dental tourism are Thailand, which is called the "Land of Smiles", Vietnam, Mexico and Costa Rica, in Europe - Hungary and Poland.
The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.
For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.
This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies.
Another two popular areas of tourism are the restoration of sleep and weight loss, but not just on detox programs, but thanks to sports in the camps.
Fitness camps are actually recreational sports camps for adults, where in the circle of like-minded people you can surf in Sri Lanka with the Good Story Surf school, go skating on Lake Baikal with Team Trip or learn how to ski in the vicinity of Gstaad with Pro Trener, World Class or SlimFitClub trainers.
Six Senses Douro Valley The newest wellness trend is slip-retreats, which literally teach you to sleep.
As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.
For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.
Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.
For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.
Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.
Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.
Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.
Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.
According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.
Daria Bogomolova

title: In Europe, due to drought may begin a shortage of chocolate and coffee – study
text:
Other effects of climate change, such as floods and an increase in pest numbers, could further worsen the food situation.
Dutch scientists have predicted a sharp increase in the risk of drought for agricultural imports into the EU.
Only 7% of such imports have been vulnerable over the past 25 years, but in the next 25 years this share will rise to 37% even if carbon emissions are drastically reduced.
Lack of supply can lead to higher prices for products.
Focus on Google News.
Subscribe - and always be aware of events.
This is stated in the study, the results of which are published in the journal Nature Communications.
The supply of coffee and cocoa to Europe could soon be disrupted due to drought in the producing countries.
The study also revealed the high vulnerability of imports of palm oil, used in many food and domestic products, and soybeans, which are the main feed for chickens and pigs in the European Union.
Of the climate changes, the analysis took into account only drought.
Other climate impacts, such as floods and an increase in pest numbers, could further worsen the situation.
However, in some regions, the risk of future drought may be lower than currently believed, and they may partially offset crop loss elsewhere.
The study notes that the EU consumes a third of the world ’ s coffee, and half of it comes from Brazil and Vietnam.
These countries are very vulnerable to drought due to global warming, although Colombia and Kenya are becoming less vulnerable.
Heat waves and leaf rust fungus also harm coffee cultivation.
The EU produces only about 3% of the soybeans it uses.
60% of soybean imports by 2050 will come from regions that are highly vulnerable to drought.
As soybeans play a key role in raising livestock, “this makes the EU very vulnerable to any disruption to soybean production, ” the scientists said.
The European Union is 100% dependent on the import of cocoa for the production of chocolate.
The analysis showed that the likelihood of drought will increase dramatically in Indonesia and Malaysia and, to a lesser extent, in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana.
It is estimated that in 2050, 28% of cocoa imports will come from regions with high drought vulnerability.
61% of palm oil imports are becoming very vulnerable to drought, especially from Indonesia.
Sugar cane is mainly imported into Europe in the form of processed foods, and 73% of that imports become very vulnerable.
At the same time, the vulnerability of imports of corn and sunflower is low.
The analysis took into account the ability of exporting countries to adapt to drought, for example, through the construction of additional reservoirs.
Mike Rivington of the James Hutton Institute in Scotland, who is not part of the research team, said the study was correct.
But he noted that drought is only one of the climatic risks for crops.
There are more such risks: floods, an increase in diseases, a loss of labor, a decrease in biodiversity, for example, pollinators.
“Food systems need to become more flexible to adapt to the extremes of regional climate change.
Open trade should continue without export restrictions to allow such flexibility, ” said Rivington.
We will remind, earlier Focus understood how global warming affects agriculture and the cost of products.
They also wrote about the threat of drought in Ukraine.

title: Covid's on his nerves. How the pandemic has brought rich countries back to mental health
text:
The Covid-19 pandemic has left people out of balance and pushed prosperous countries back decades on the path to an already elusive goal of improving or at least not harming their mental health.
If you do nothing about it, then all attempts to draw attention to the problem of mental health and begin to solve it by health care will be nullified even in those countries that can afford it, warned the club of 38 rich OECD countries.
And the way out of the corona-crisis will be even longer and more expensive.
For many years, the resources allocated were inadequate, but the overall level of mental illness has remained relatively stable over the past 20 years at about 18% of the population of OECD countries.
The coid crisis broke this trend in 2020, ” the organization said in a recent study.
During these two decades, the key indicator — the number of suicides — has decreased by 21%.
Similar data for a year and a half of the pandemic are not yet available, but others point to an aggravation: levels of anxiety, anxiety and depression have risen everywhere, and have doubled in many countries.
Young people have been particularly affected, according to the OECD.
The reasons to get out of balance over the past year and a half were at least enough, and young people took the main blow.
Lockdown deprived the people of communication and entertainment, broke the usual routine of life.
The ensuing crisis created unemployment and financial problems.
In addition, all the forces of health systems have been thrown into the fight against the pandemic at the expense of the treatment of other diseases.
Doctors and beds were not enough even for patients with cancer and heart, and patients with mental disorders again went to the end of the long queue to see the doctor.
A lot of people need it there.
At the height of the pandemic, 44% of Austrians, 41% of Americans and 78% of Australians admitted to deteriorating mental health.
Even in South Korea and New Zealand, which quickly controlled the virus, more than a third of the population, polls showed.
In general, according to the statistics cited in the study, every second person at least once in his life faces mental problems.
Those who have such conditions turn into chronic, it is more difficult to get a job in life, it is harder for them to study, it is more difficult to find a job and lead a full life.
The World Health Organization defines health in general not only as the absence of disease and physical defects, but as the harmony of physical, mental and social well-being.
Mental health is a state of well-being in which a person is able to realize his abilities, withstand the hardships of life and contribute to the development of society.
Violation of this harmony, in addition to medical and social problems, has quite tangible financial consequences.
According to the OECD, losses amount to 4.2% of GDP of the club countries, which account for three-quarters of all economic activity in the world.
Last year, their total GDP exceeded $60 trillion, which means that the lack of mental equilibrium costs rich countries at least $2.5 trillion a year.
In the corona-crisis, they can not afford to scatter such money, lamented the OECD and proposed a solution.
It ’ s time to fix the system.
“The deterioration of mental health of the population in 2020-2021 has highlighted the seriousness of the problem more than ever.
It is critical that authorities take measures to protect mental health and establish a system for effective treatment of disorders, ” says the study, in which the OECD first tried to describe what such a system should look like and how to assess whether the country is doing well.
Rich countries have been engaged in mental health for a long time, and in 2017 they decided to create a set of recommendations and evaluation criteria - but the hands have reached only now.
They have developed 23 indicators — from stigma to access to psychological care — by which countries can measure the effectiveness of their health care system in maintaining a nation ’ s mental equilibrium.
Now there are only two universal indicators by which developed countries from the OECD club can be compared: life satisfaction and the number of suicides.
And polls show that the problem is far from black and white.
Two-thirds of those who asked for help admitted that it was not easy to get it.
And one in five people admitted to the hospital with a mental disorder complained of disrespect for themselves and the severity of the disease.
Now is the chance to fix it all.
The authorities of wealthy countries are actively financing the recovery from the corona-crisis from the budget, and significant allocations go to the crisis-worn health care pandemic.
If at least some of them go to mental health care (as in Australia, which doubled its mental health budget in 2020), whole nations will have a chance to fix the nerves worn out by the lockdowns and restore peace of mind.

title: Canadian experts did not confirm the deliberate downing of the UIA aircraft by Iran
text:
The official forensic examination of the crash of the UIA plane, which was conducted in Canada, allegedly found no evidence that the plane was shot down intentionally, referring to international media, reports Mirror of the Week.
At the same time, Iran has not provided a reliable explanation of why and how its military shot down the plane.
The report said the forensic team analyzed the information available, but “only Iran has full access to the evidence, the crash site and witnesses. ”
“Iran is obliged to provide clear answers on all aspects of this tragedy, ” the document says.
“Taking into account the totality of available information, the forensic team concluded that a number of actions and inactions of the Iranian civilian and military authorities led to a dangerous situation in which previously certain risks were underestimated and not taken into account. ”
The relevant analysis gives Canada the opportunity to impose sanctions against Iran.
“Iran ’ s civil and military authorities, through their actions and inaction, directly exposed PS752 and other civilian aircraft to danger, creating an environment in which the combat system operator was able to launch missiles without being able to take adequate measures to reduce this high risk, ” the report said.
On the morning of January 8, 2020, Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752 took off from Tehran to Kiev, but was shot down by the Iranian military shortly after takeoff.
All 176 people on board were killed.
Iran has long denied the involvement of the IRGC in the disaster and continues to hide information until now.
In Tehran, limited the message of “bringing to justice ” ten people, but who they are is unknown.
Human Rights Watch said Iran was threatening the families of those killed in the plane crash by trying to deflect charges from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for shooting down a civilian airliner with a missile.
Kiev is seeking to bring to justice those responsible for the tragedy and to obtain from Tehran decent compensation for the relatives of the victims.
Iran, however, does not show readiness to conduct an objective investigation, wants to quickly file the case.

title: Foreign Ministry welcomes creation of report by Canadian group of forensic experts on Iran ’ s defeat of UIA aircraft
text:
While Iran has still not told Ukraine about the 10 accused of downing a Ukrainian International Airlines (UIA) flight over Tehran in 2020, the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry says it welcomes the creation by a Canadian panel of forensic experts of a report on the crash.
This is stated in the message of the press service of the Ministry, transmit Ukrainian News.
“The Ukrainian side welcomes the efforts of the Government of Canada aimed at establishing the truth and achieving justice in the downing of the Ukrainian Boeing flight PS752 in the sky over Tehran on January 8, 2020.
A report by a Canadian panel of forensic experts confirms that Iran ’ s civilian and military authorities bear full responsibility for the downing of flight PS752.
The document also emphasizes the disregard for human life by the Iranian authorities.
"The panel of forensic experts came to the following three key conclusions.
First, Iran did not ensure the safety of its airspace and did not inform the airline about the risks, thus creating the basis for such a terrible tragedy.
Secondly, the operator of the anti-missile system TOR 1M deliberately committed a number of gross violations of the rules of conduct of combat firing, launching two surface-to-air missiles, which led to the downing of a civilian aircraft.
Third, Iran ’ s military command failed to take appropriate actions to prevent violations by the operator of the surface-to-air missile unit of the established order of combat duty and unauthorized launch of missiles, ” it said.
Moreover, it is reported that Iran has taken a number of steps aimed at concealing the real circumstances of the disaster.
The technical report prepared by Iran does not fully establish the chain of events preceding the tragedy.
It was emphasized that the recommendations proposed by Iran to eliminate shortcomings in the security system of civil aviation are irrelevant and, accordingly, all the risks that led to the downing of the Ukrainian aircraft remain to this day.
“That is why the attempt to reduce the cause of the tragedy to the“ false ” actions of the operator of the missile unit does not stand up to any criticism!
The facts are clear: Iran is responsible for the deaths of 176 innocent people.
Ukraine and the partner states continue to adhere to the position of Iran committing gross violations of the Chicago and Montreal Conventions.
Consequently, Iran must be held accountable and ensure restitution in accordance with international law, ” it said.
This includes, among other things, the obligation of Iran to ensure an objective and impartial criminal investigation and to bring all those responsible to justice, as well as the adoption of measures by Iran aimed at preventing similar tragedies in the future.
“Otherwise, no country, airline or passenger can be confident in the safety of Iran ’ s airspace, ” the statement added.

title: Mass blockage at the cycling race "Tour de France" because of the antics of the cheerleader: the girl hit the racers with a poster and ran away
text:
The girl showed the camera a poster with a joke inscription, knocked down the racers on the asphalt and fled from the scene.
45 km before the end of the first stage of the legendary cycling race "Tour de France" there was a massive blockage, as a result of which more than two dozen athletes were injured.
Almost half of the peloton fell, including the main favorites.
The culprit of the accident was a cheerleader who put up a poster with a joke inscription right in front of the riders.
Now she is wanted by the police, who asked witnesses for help through social networks.
The organizers of the race promised her legal proceedings.
"Allez Opi-Omi" The cheerleader intervened in the battle of the strongest riders of the world at the most famous stage race in history at the first stage from Brest to Landerno.
About 45 km before the finish, the girl in blue jeans and a bright yellow jacket jumped from the side of the road and put on camera in front of the athletes a poster with the inscription “Allez Opi-Omi ” (a joke and caressing appeal to grandparents in German, something like“ Go, old men ”).
Driving on the right side of the rider of the team “Jumbo Wisma ” German Tony Martin had no chance to dodge the collision with the poster and fell, which led to a major blockage.
Not escaped this and the main favorites: Slovenes Tadej Pogacar and Primož Roglic.
But they at least cost bruises and abrasions, but Spaniard Mark Soler of “Movistar ” broke the radial bones on both hands.
By some miracle, he reached the finish line, but he will not be able to continue the race.
Like the German Jascha Sutterlin.
Those who continued the Tour de France lost a lot of time.
“We had everything under control, I led the guys on the right side of the road, but crashed into a fan poster.
It all happened very quickly, all of a sudden, almost everyone was on the ground.
Many viewers behave respectfully, but in this case this was not the case, unfortunately.
I hope that there will be no consequences for the health of all the guys who fell into the rubble, ” said Tony Martin.
A year behind bars and a 15,000 euro fine The cheerleader, who became the culprit of the accident, quickly disappeared.
The Gendarmerie Landerno put her on the wanted list and asked for help from witnesses, posting a post on social media.
However, the comments are more negative towards the police than the desire to help find a negligent fan.
The organizers of the Tour de France have already promised that the culprit of the collision is awaiting trial.
“We must not allow a small number of hooligans to spoil the sporting event for participants and fans, ” said Pierre-Yves Tuo, deputy director of the race.
What threatens the offender?
While injured in the accident riders did not submit a statement to the police – a fine of 1500 euros.
But if Soler and Sutterlin write such a statement, the case will be reclassified.
Now the fan is accused that failure to comply with the required security measures led to harm to health.
In the case of a statement from the riders unknown until the violator faces a fine ten times more and up to a year in prison.
The organizers appealed to all fans with a request to observe security measures and even released a special video reminding how dangerous such clashes can be.
There are a lot of fans in the current Tour de France.
And almost no one follows the antiquated rules.
The organizers are ready to turn a blind eye to this, but when the physical safety of athletes is threatened, it is quite another matter.
The athletes themselves also urged fans to be more restrained in the display of emotions, although clashes with fans in cycling are quite regular.
But now it has crossed all boundaries.
“I hope Opi-Omi are proud of you, ” Belgian cyclist Jasper Stuyven wrote on Twitter.
It is wonderful to see that there are so many fans who love our sport and support us.
But please stay on the side of the road, not on the road! ”
The participants of the Tour de France quite cope with the organization of force majeure and without the participation of fans.

title: Toshiba has completed the production of the world ’ s first and largest toroidal coil for the ITER reactor electromagnet » DailyTechInfo
text:
Representatives of Toshiba Energy Systems & Solutions (Toshiba ESS) announced the successful completion of the first section of the toroidal winding for an electromagnet, the field of which will hold high-temperature plasma in the chamber of the experimental fusion reactor ITER.
The construction of this reactor has been underway in the south of France for quite some time, and after the launch, the reactor will be used as a research facility, which will test technologies that can give humanity an endless source of clean energy in the future.
The main role in the implementation of the project is played by seven of the most technologically advanced countries - Japan, the European Union, the United States, Russia, China, South Korea and India.We remind our readers that the electrical energy in fusion reactors is produced by thermal energy released during the fusion reactions of the nucleus of atoms of light elements, hydrogen and helium, in the nuclei of heavier elements.
Such reactions do not produce radioactive waste and do not emit large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
The design of toroidal coil sections for the ITER reactor electromagnet was carried out by specialists of the Japanese Institute QST (Quantum and Radiological Science and Technology).
At 16.5 meters tall, 9 meters wide and weighing approximately 300 tons, this coil is the world ’ s largest such structure to date.
The ITER reactor will use 18 sections of interconnected electromagnet windings, 4 of which will be manufactured by Toshiba ESS.
In addition, the company Toshiba ESS will produce 6 more shell bases for similar coils, the "filling" of which will be engaged in specialists of other companies.And in conclusion, we note that the launch of the ITER reactor, if everything goes according to the planned plans, is scheduled for 2025.

title: In Britain, they intend to tighten immigration laws
text:
In a statement, the department noted that the proposals to reform immigration legislation are designed to “put in order the outdated asylum system. ”
In turn, the experts of the PA agency pointed out that this reform will allow to hold accountable those who try to arrive in the country by sea, in particular through the English Channel.
According to the agency, only in the first six months of 2021, about 6 thousand people tried to reach the British coast through the English Channel in inflatable boats, while for the whole of last year this figure was 8.4 thousand migrants.
The bill sends a clear signal to migrants to think seriously before paying money to smugglers for a dangerous and illegal journey to the UK.
“We welcome everyone who uses safe and legal routes [to enter the country], but at the same time fight against illegal migration and related crime, ” said UK Home Secretary Priti Patel.
The ministry added that often migrants who try to get into the kingdom on inflatable boats, “go on a journey from safe countries of the European Union, where they could ask for asylum. ”
Tightening immigration laws was one of the pre-election points of the ruling Conservative Party led by Prime Minister Boris Johnson.
Earlier, the British authorities stressed that about 62% of people seeking asylum in the kingdom, were in the country illegally.
At the same time, more than 40 thousand people who were denied asylum still live in the UK.

title: Mitigating agricultural losses under climate change Agricultural Research Institute develops crop life buoys - Life
text:
Chen Junbi, director of the Puli Branch of the Taichung Agricultural Reform Department of the Council of Agriculture, picked up cucumbers and passion fruit, stressing that these crops can reduce the problem of fruit loss through the use of "mushroom and abalone composting".
(photo by Lin Xinyi) Climate change has become an important issue for global discussion, and the problem of crop damage caused by it has received great attention. The Agricultural Experiment Institute of the Council of Agriculture tries to use waste materials of Apricot mushroom, adding wood chips and other materials to make it into a “mushroom abalone composting ” and placing it in the fields. 8% of the rate of loss.
On the display stand, Chen Chun-yi, director of the Puli Branch of the Taichung Agricultural Improvement Center of the Council of Agriculture, said that after many mushrooms were harvested in the new community, the agricultural waste left behind was piled up in the local area, often resulting in odor and environmental health problems.
Chen Chun-yi said that the farm tried to use the leftover materials after the mushroom harvest, adding waste wood chips and other materials and fermenting with wood mold to make "mushroom abalone composting". Chen Junyi takes bitter gourd as an example, he said that during the continuous heavy rain in July and August this year, many bitter gourds are soaked in water and their roots are rotting, and the fruit falling rate is as high as 80%.
Lin Xuexi, director of the Institute of Agricultural Research, pointed out that in recent years, the rapid global climate change, including warming and changes in rainfall patterns, has seriously affected the growth of crops.
