title: Fighting climate change, mushroom waste into melon fruit "life buoy"
text:
To combat climate change, mushroom waste into melon fruit "life buoy" 2019-11-27 19: 30 United Daily News reporter Huang Yin / Immediately reported on the crop damage caused by climate change, the Taichung Agricultural Improvement Station of the Council of Agriculture of the Executive Yuan tried to use mushroom waste materials, adding wood chips and other materials to make "mushroom abalone composting" and placed in the field, which can attract root growth to reduce. The damage caused by heavy rain and drought caused by climate change can reduce the fruit falling rate by about 80%.
There are many examples of the Council of Agriculture ’ s improvement sites fighting climate change, and the Agricultural Testing Institute is now holding an exhibition to showcase these results.
Director Lin Xuexi also pointed out that the rapid global climate change in recent years, including warming and changes in rainfall patterns, has seriously affected the growth of crops. Through different aspects of adjusting crop growth and coping with the damage caused by climate change, the agricultural laboratory hopes to solve the problem of crop growth and harvest.
Chen Chun-yi, director of the Puli Branch of the Taichung Agricultural Improvement Station, says that the mushroom and fruit composting has indeed produced an effect on melons and fruits' resistance to heavy rain and accumulation of water, which is like a "life buoy" for melons and fruits when they accumulate water.
Take bitter gourd as an example, in July and August this year, continuous heavy rain, many bitter gourd are soaked in water, the root rot, fruit rate up to 80%, but the use of mushroom abalone composting to grow the bitter gourd is protected by the root, not only the crop is not soaked, the fruit rate is also greatly reduced.
Others such as tomatoes, cucumbers and lychee are also effective.
In particular, mushroom abalone composting is the use of many shiitake mushrooms harvested in the new community, and the waste left behind is added to waste wood chips and other materials and fermented with wood mold. In the past, these waste materials were piled in the local area, often resulting in odor and environmental health problems.

title: Taiwan ’ s Water Resource Dilemma: An Interview with Hsu Hoang-hsiung
text:
“Earth Simulator ” and Climate Change Taiwan faced a severe drought in the first half of 2021, and the water situation in central and southern Taiwan was red, making local residents very worried.
Is this drought the result of climate change? Hsu Wang-hsiung, a special researcher at the Center for Environmental Change Research at Academia Sinica, points out that the climate system is extremely complex and it is not appropriate to draw a sudden conclusion.
How do scientists assess the climate?
First, we need an “Earth Simulator ” that handles complex computing, and Hsu is the main promoter of the“ Taiwan Earth System Model. ”
How do we view drought in terms of climate models?
Get to know each other through a research interview.
"In the long run, Taiwan's water resources and natural disasters will not be optimistic if it rains in the future," Hsu said. According to estimates of climate change, although this is known as the once-in-a-century drought, similar droughts are likely to occur more frequently in the future.
Will there be a drought in the future?
The land god temple and the chief stone standing in the Taoyuan Shihmen Reservoir, with the water storage tight, the wonders of the whole appeared in front of tourists; under the drought, Sun Moon Lake continued to dry up, mobile phones, license plates, gravestones during the dry years, and large canoes sunk by the Shao people were also found at the bottom of the pond.
In the first half of 2021, Taiwan suffered the largest drought in 100 years, and there was no precipitation in the central and southern parts of the country.
Things need to go back to the year before, which was deeply affected by the epidemic, in early summer of 2020, there was less plum rain, and typhoons rarely passed through the door in summer and autumn.
Relieving drought always depends on God ’ s face, and estimating the future climate trend is the core mission of the Academia Sinica ’ s “Research Center on Environmental Change – Center for Human Climate Change. ”
"In the long run, the future rain situation, Taiwan's water resources, natural disasters are not optimistic." Hsu Hoang-hsiung, a special researcher at the Center for Environmental Change at the Academia Sinica, believes that according to the situation of climate change, although this is known as the once-in-a-century drought, similar droughts in the future are likely to be more frequent.
This year ’ s drought should be seen as an important warning for water management, reminding Taiwan to make an early and appropriate response to climate change.
Before planning a response, it is of course necessary to understand what changes and changes Taiwan ’ s climate will face in the context of climate change.
Since 2010, with the support of the Ministry of Science and Technology and the support of Academia Sinica, researchers from several universities in Taiwan have formed the Climate Change Research Alliance to build the key capabilities needed for climate change simulation and interpretation in Taiwan.
In addition to developing and improving the Climate Model System, we also use this model to determine the impact of climate change and extreme weather in the future.
How do scientists “calculate ” the climate system?
What is the climate model?
How do you estimate the future climate?
"(The climate model system) is a bit like building an 'earth simulator' in computer language. The computer can basically simulate the phenomena we observe, such as the atmosphere, circulation, ocean, water cycle, and clouds." Hsu explained that by cutting the earth into tens of thousands of meshes in the horizontal direction (about 60-100 kilometers per grid) and tens of layers in the vertical direction, you can use a supercomputer to simulate and calculate the climate grid. Condition.
Hsu said that there are currently about 40 to 50 "earth simulators" in the world, but there is no consensus that the best simulators or estimators have the best capabilities, and the results of each unit have their own strengths and weaknesses.
At this stage, for example, when the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) prepares climate change assessment reports, it is common to adopt a similar “majority decision ” and use multiple models to obtain important estimates through multi-mode simulations and ensemble simulations.
Many of the existing models of climate systems involve the efforts of many scientists, but there is still a long way to go to perfect simulations.
From the perspective of earth science, the earth can be divided into five subsystems, such as atmosphere, ice and snow, water, land and biology, and the interaction of these five systems will affect the earth's climate.
Therefore, considering the physical processes that affect each other between these subsystems, according to the equations of physics, heat, and chemical laws, written into a computer program, you can simulate the changes of the atmosphere, land, and ocean over time on a supercomputer.
However, the resolution of the global climate model is still not fine-grained, with each grid size of tens to hundreds of kilometers, and at this scale, it is not possible to deal with the smaller scale, but very important physical processes (such as atmospheric radiation, convection, aerosol, clouds, etc.), which need to be simplified with parameters, which also results of the climate simulation are not accurate enough.
"For example, in the original climate model, it is difficult to define 'a cloud'."
Hsu explains that factors such as clouds and terrain radiation, which are important in regional weather, are difficult to accurately represent in the original parameters.
And this is the goal that many scientists continue to strive for, and Taiwan's research team is naturally not absent here.
The Taiwan Earth System Model (TaiESM) has been developed by the Taiwan Climate Change Research Alliance team with limited human and financial resources, with a resolution of about 100 km and no possibility of simulating typhoons. The existing US National Center for Atmospheric Research (CESM1) and the US Ocean and Atmospheric Geophysical Dynamics Laboratory (HIRAM) have a resolution of about 25 km. Typhoon), and then incorporated the module of Taiwan's unique research expertise to improve atmospheric physics parameterization, as well as the adjustment of the ocean module.
For example, one of the features of TaiESM is the inclusion of the cloud and aerosol module developed by the Department of Atmospheric Sciences at NTU, which greatly improves the simulation ability of the microphysical interaction between aerosols and clouds in computing. The module, which has a very high resolution for the one-dimensional snow, ice, and ocean modules, and coupled with the global atmospheric model, can successfully present tropical "intraseasonal Oscillation" (ISO), which is second only to the El Niño phenomenon in terms of impact on global weather.
The climate model system is a bit like building an “earth simulator ” in computer language to simulate the phenomena we observe.
The climate model system cuts the Earth into tens of thousands of grids horizontally (about 60 to 100 kilometers per grid) and tens of layers vertically, so the simulation is huge and requires a supercomputer to calculate the climate of each grid.
Hsu shares that although the research manpower and resources of the Taiwan Earth System Model are far inferior to those of foreign related teams, they have achieved good results in a short period of ten years.
In recent years, Taiwan has joined the sixth phase of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) under the World Meteorological Organization ’ s World Climate Research Program, and Taiwan has become one of the few countries with the ability to model and estimate long-term climate change, and will contribute relevant results to the world. Simulating modern climate is no different from the world ’ s leading model of the Earth system.
Of course, the research team of the Center for Human Climate Change is also expected to deal with local issues, and the difficulty of simulating the climate system near Taiwan is higher than in other parts of the world.
“Taiwan belongs to the Asian monsoon region, the most complex of the monsoon regions in the world.
In this area, there are multiple scale interactions that must be handled simultaneously.
"The Wizard Explains".
The weather and climate of Taiwan are heavily affected by typhoons and monsoons, but there are certain differences in scale, but there will be complex interactions between them. Typhoons themselves affect large-scale circulation, thus affecting the monsoon system; the conditions of the monsoon system itself will also affect the generation of typhoons. The intersection of multiple systems is vulnerable to distant climatic factors.
Today's drought originated from the high temperature of the past year, the Pacific subtropical high pressure, the formation of a weak typhoon on the sea surface and a short life span; some studies have pointed out that last year's Indian Ocean sea temperature broke records, it may affect the formation of Pacific typhoons; and in the context of climate change, the Indian Ocean is indeed the fastest sea temperature rise in the ocean basin......
This relationship is intricate.
Xu Huangxiong reminded that the climate system is extremely complex, although some phenomena are similar to estimates, but the reasons are different, and it is not appropriate to conclude that this drought in Taiwan is caused by climate change.
"The atmosphere is continuous, and Taiwan (weather) will be affected by the outside monsoon and climate change."
Since there is no way to change the world, we must strive to build our own research capabilities.
The ultimate development direction in the future will be towards the continuous development of "seamless weather forecast system", breaking the traditional concept of atmospheric phenomena according to spatial and temporal scales, which is the ultimate goal of climate simulation and estimation research.
Drought and High Temperature: With the research tools needed for the impact of climate change on Taiwan, what are the high risks that Taiwan will encounter in the face of inevitable climate change trends?
First, of course, there are changes in the rainfall associated with the people.
In collaboration with the Taiwan Climate Change Assessment Information and Adaptation Knowledge Platform (TCCIP) of the Ministry of Science and Technology, and with the support of the Center for Sustainable Science of Academia Sinica, the 2018 study “Drought Research in Taiwan: Change, Water Impact, Risk Awareness, and Communication Plan ” indicates that the future spring drought in Taiwan (2040 – 2060) may become more severe. The rate of water shortage in agriculture will increase significantly.
The TCCIP study estimated the future precipitation changes in Taiwan, and also found that the uneven precipitation period will be more extreme, the drier the dry period, the wetter the flood period; the number of days without rain during the dry period will increase, and the dry period may prolong the dry period. It creates a greater burden.
"The drought in Taiwan is usually not particularly severe, usually in a few months, unlike the continental drought in Australia and the United States."
For everyone easy to forget that the water situation is often in jeopardy, Xu Huangxiong, for example, in 2002-2004, there were intermittent droughts, and even the large Taipei area experienced regional water supply.
However, because the disaster situation can usually be alleviated in the rainy season or typhoon season, the drought is rare for more than a year, so it is less easy to stay in everyone's memory, and the awareness of cherishing water resources is also weaker.
However, in fact, Taiwan's special geographical environment has led to a lot of rain, but the management of water resources is relatively difficult, and the Shimen Reservoir, for example, must be replenished at least four times a year.
The study also pointed out that the spring rain in Taiwan from February to April is often an important source of irrigation water for the first period of rice, so the amount of rain during the spring rain is related to the water situation and farming in the year.
Climate simulations from the previous study show that spring rain in Taiwan is expected to decrease by 13.2% in the middle of the century and increase by 55.7% in consecutive dry days.
Another climate change scenario that Taiwan is likely to face is high temperatures.
Relevant studies have pointed out that the increase in the average temperature in Taiwan in the future is inevitable.
In the past 100 years, Taiwan ’ s climate has gradually changed from winter and summer to summer and winter, and it is estimated that the next summer can be as long as 150 days. “Heatwaves will not be many, but only one, and by current standards, the whole summer will be a heatwave in the future. ”
According to Hsu ’ s previous climate simulation report, spring rain in Taiwan is expected to decrease by 13.2% in the middle of the century and increase by 55.7% in consecutive dry days.
Figure │ Research has a full understanding of the impact, and then the adaptation strategy planning climate change is imminent, so how should we respond to this?
Mr Hui said that the study on the impact of climate change should be completed as soon as possible at this stage, before it is appropriate to further develop adaptation strategies.
The impact of climate change is very broad, and it is likely to have a significant impact on the environment, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and animal husbandry, public health, health, and ecology.
However, at this stage, the relevant research content in this field is still insufficient, and there is no sufficient understanding of the "impact", so it is possible to hastily carry out the "adjustment" planning, which is doubly successful.
For example, the Center for Environmental Change ’ s “Drought Research ” has pointed out that in the future, rainfall in the main catchment areas in northern Taiwan will decrease most significantly in the spring, so due to climate change, the water shortage rate in the north will exceed 20% at most until the middle of the century, and even the water shortage rate in northern agriculture may exceed 40%.
Such an impact perception is still relatively sketchy, and in more detail, which areas will be most severely impacted in the context of water scarcity require more detailed research.
"What was discussed in the past (climate change) was natural science, and now the direction of the discussion has permeated into every level of human life, which is quite different." 」
Hsu Wang-hsiung, who co-authored the book “Introduction to Global Environmental Change ” with Professor Wei Guo-yen in 1997, has been immersed in the issue for decades. He said that the issue of climate change has become so widespread that everyone should participate.
There is no need to stick to the field of science, chemistry, engineering, biology, health, environment, economics, and social science, as long as you have expertise.
In the near future, we must make technological and institutional breakthroughs in all aspects, while saving energy and reducing carbon, but also responding to the impact of climate change.
The issue of climate change is wide-ranging and far-reaching, and will bring about many impactful changes.
However, if we can deal with it as soon as possible, Taiwan will not be able to take a turn through various new development crises.

title: Urban Resilience Challenge: Can Our Cities Get Better After the Outbreak?
text:
Text: Chen Qiaoqi (Taiwan Environmental Planning Association, also an analyst) COVID-19 (severe special infectious pneumonia, COVID-19, Wuhan pneumonia) has been a year, not only caused a reshuffle of order in the international community, but also for the internal systems and planning of various countries, but also because of the outbreak itself and the occurrence of complex disasters, so that in the past, the governance planners have made a chance to plan for the resilience of urban organisms. Revisited.
Under the standard measures of city closure and safe social distance, the original mobility within the city has been disrupted, and the activity distance and living habits between individuals have been redefined. It also highlights the importance of urban spatial layout for public health and health, such as the bubble measures of Dolores Park in San Francisco, and the distance park (Parc de la Distance) designed by Precht, an Austrian architecture team.), show that the people under the closure also need to open space activities, let us once again reflect on the urban green space not only has the physical carbon reduction, ecological significance, but also helps the people in the closure measures under the physiological and psychological adjustment.
In May 2020, the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Alliance released a rethinking of transport models, emphasizing people-oriented safe transport to promote economic recovery and urban revitalization planning (Zhao Jiawei, 2020). In order to strengthen the implementation of the EU Green New Deal, the European Cities Organization (Eurocities) also issued an open letter to the EU in October 2020, hoping that the EU can invest more resources related to the recovery. Under the epidemic, we have been more active in achieving the goal of reducing carbon by 65%.
These include a massive investment in public transport, green infrastructure and building refurbishment for the EU ’ s recovery plan, with the expectation that the EU will invest funds where they are most needed to achieve a green and fair recovery, and the emphasis on conditionally providing fossil-fuel-intensive sector recovery funds to meet decarbonisation targets (Alex Godson, 2020).
Photo Credit: Reuters / Dolores Park, San Francisco (USA) Bubble measures for epidemic prevention In addition to the short-term urban recovery phase mentioned above, the impact of the long-term epidemic on the city will not only permanently change the way people move, but also may make large cities more vulnerable or perceived as more risky venues.
With the current economic activities and institutions, it is impossible to disrupt the development of cities, but how can urban governance move towards a more resilient path in the face of the epidemic and the climate crisis, rather than just a short-term rebound to the old state after the epidemic?
The positive impact of the epidemic on cities in the post-epidemic period includes short-term sky clarity and urban ecological restoration. The negative impact of the epidemic has not only caused inconvenience to the people in the short term, but also highlighted long-term issues that have not been solved, making urban and rural disparities, poverty and the environment, and carbon reduction issues on the table.
In addition to creating jobs and developing innovative strategies, cities are also key to achieving the goal of carbon reduction. The epidemic and climate impact require us to re-examine the living environment of people, take stock of the advantages and disadvantages of urban governance in the past, and recognize the advantages and disadvantages of the global north and the global south in urban planning. According to the epburn and Stern report, low-carbon urban transformation in the post-pandemic period will not only help to address climate change, but also increase resilience as the best path to economic recovery (Hepburn et al., 2020).
In particular, developing countries are experiencing rapid urban growth, and their cities ’ carbon reduction or resilient urban planning are seen as important measures to reduce their vulnerability to future climate impacts.
Therefore, using cities with the highest degree of human activity as nodes of green recovery, and making good use of urban resources and organizational capabilities, can accelerate the overall economic recovery.
Good urban governance At this year ’ s Climate Adaptation Summit, 1,000 cities signed a joint declaration that COVID-19, climate change and social inequality are closely related. Therefore, the post-pandemic era requires a city-led green recovery. Smart investment and implementation of resilient policies can promote economic recovery, improve climate and health adaptation, and pursue equity and justice.
The cities joining the 1000 Cities Adapt Now programme will follow five principles to achieve the green recovery of COVID-19 in the context of climate adaptation (GCA, 2021): strengthen and prioritize urban adaptation and climate resilience, targeting the most vulnerable and poorest communities; and improve resilient cities in the water sector and develop nature-based solutions; advocate decentralization and investment in cities and strengthen coordinated leadership for greater political influence and funding; strengthen knowledge and capacity for urban adaptation to support partnerships with deep, long-term and systemic change; and maximize and accelerate the impact of the program through coordination and smart innovation, partnerships and investments. The Global Mayors COVID-19 Recovery Task Force, established a knowledge platform to help policymakers to have better governance models when rebuilding, improve public health, reduce inequality, and respond to the climate crisis. It proposes nine principles that emphasize that urban governance should not be restored as usual, increase good public services, public investment, and community resilience, and repeatedly emphasize fairness. and new job opportunities to achieve climate justice, investing resources to address potential future impacts such as climate risks.
The six call for action proposals include: green policies alone to stimulate recovery, a commitment to fair and inclusive recovery, public transport, prioritizing investment in clean energy, investing in resilient cities, and ending all public investment in fossil fuels (C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group, 2020a).
The urban epidemic of green recovery has given cities the opportunity to restart, and European cities are actively strengthening more climate-resilient infrastructure, increasing public spaces, creating traffic-free streets, building bike lanes, renovating old buildings, and more.
Because of the epidemic lockdown or curfew measures, people find that different areas of the city in recent years have caused great inconvenience in life, and reflect on the allocation of urban space.
The concept of City of Proximities is not new. Over the past few decades, a number of planners and scholars have discussed walkable cities (Marquet & Miralles-Guasch, 2015), emphasizing the need to meet people ’ s needs within walking distance.
Portland ’ s 2015 Climate Action Plan envisioned 80% of the city ’ s population to move on foot or bike to meet their basic needs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.
Paris Mayor Anne Hidalgo and the governance team proposed the “15 Minute City ” plan during the 2020 campaign, which aims to reduce the range of activities required by the people in the city by spatial resetting. The past pedestrian city focused on mobility, walkability and public services. The“ 15 Minute City ” considers the community in a comprehensive way, and people can walk or bike to their homes in 15 minutes. offices, schools, cultural events, hospitals and parks.
15 Minute City Ideas | Source: Paris En Commun (2020) Moreno says that past smart city designs have revealed weaknesses in this epidemic – even with the most advanced technology, people still cannot meet their most basic needs when facing life restrictions, causing social and economic collapse.
The “15 Minute City ” plan adds more social compatibility and resilience, while reducing air pollution and reducing traffic carbon emissions (Moreno et al., 2021).
As the epidemic rages in Paris, Mayor Hidalgo has begun to develop policies and launched a pilot site in early 2021 to accelerate the implementation of the “15 minute city ”. In addition, many cities around the world such as Melbourne, Milan, Houston, and Ottawa have also launched a rolling policy development, using walking communities or 15 minute cities as urban future planning (C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group, 2020b).
In addition, the most cities are using this opportunity to transform their transportation patterns, from the impact of reduced commuting rates during the pandemic to making it obvious that healthier cities are within reach, and the more popular alternative transportation such as walking or cycling is.
Cities also have better air quality due to reduced traffic, which is an opportunity to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by improving traffic patterns.
In response to South Korea ’ s Green New Deal, the city of Seoul, in addition to implementing green energy policies, has also re-planned smart green transportation policies, planned car-free streets, robot delivery services, and increased the bicycle rapid lane system to reach the goal of 15% of vehicles as bicycles by 2030 (OECD, 2020).
Other cities are also undergoing a transformation of transport patterns, such as London and Seattle, which have transformed temporary traffic measures into permanent measures to permanently convert carriageways closed during the pandemic into sidewalks or bike lanes, and Cairo, which has accelerated the provision of mass transport with a metro capacity of 6 million passengers by 2025 (C40, 2020).
The combination of other digital and innovative technologies with existing urban planning can also help cities to better manage the mobility of the commuter population and the poor. It can further help cities to allocate money and supplies and reduce vulnerability to future climate impacts.
Photo Credit: Reuters / Tachih Image “Reset for resilience ” In the past, our planning for resilient cities focused on the ability of cities to withstand physical hazards, such as flooding or earthquakes, to improve the resilience of cities. Systemic risk.
Compared with Western cities, Asian cities have been less affected by the epidemic. Especially when Taiwan was hit by the drought last year, because the epidemic was properly controlled and did not cause a complex disaster, our urban transformation plans have been less scrutinized by the public.
Cities around the world are taking advantage of this opportunity to improve their cities, and Taiwan ’ s cities should also take advantage of the opportunity to relaunch, plan comprehensive resilience measures, especially urban open spaces, green spaces, and transportation systems, and improve public-private and social cooperation opportunities to attract more private investment to close the financing gap, help cities invest in green infrastructure and replan urban spaces to cope with the potential disasters of climate change.

title: UAE opens embassy in Israel, first in Gulf region
text:
Following the recent inauguration of the Israeli embassy in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates opened its first embassy in Israel on Wednesday, a key step in normalizing relations between the two countries.
With the opening of a diplomatic mission at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange building, the UAE became the third Arab country to establish an embassy on Israeli territory after Egypt and Jordan, according to AFP.
It was also the first country in the Gulf to open an embassy in Israel.
"The UAE and Israel are two innovative countries, and we can use this creativity to work together for a more prosperous and stable future for our two countries and the region," said Mohammed Mahmoud Fat-Ali Hajjah, UAE's ambassador to Israel, at the embassy's opening ceremony.
"This historic agreement must be extended to other countries seeking peace with Israel," Israeli President Isaac Herzog said, according to an Agence France-Presse report in the area. "Israeli President Isaac Herzog attended the ceremony in the hall of the stock exchange, which is located on two floors below the office of the UAE embassy.
Inspired by Donald Trump, the former US administration, the UAE and Israel announced normalization of relations in the summer of 2020.
Bahrain, another Gulf monarchy, as well as Morocco and Sudan, have also announced normalization agreements with Israel in recent months.
According to the report, at the end of June, Israel ’ s new Foreign Minister Yair Lapid visited the UAE and inaugurated Israel ’ s first embassy in the Gulf state.
But Palestinians, from Mahmoud Abbas ’ s secular Fatah to radical Hamas, have denounced the normalization agreements, calling them “traitors ” to Arab states.
They believe that this process should take place after the settlement of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
According to Yoel Guzansky, a researcher at Israel ’ s National Security Institute in Tel Aviv, normalization between Arab countries and Israel passed an “important test ” in an 11-day military conflict between Israel and Hamas, the Palestinian Islamist movement that governs the Gaza Strip, in May.
According to Jordan-Guzansky, "It was a success because no country canceled the agreement, not even Sudan or Morocco."
While these normalization talks are still ongoing, their development has “slowed down ” in recent months, Guzansky qualified in an online chat with reporters.
Joel Guzansky believes that "the excitement of today is no longer there," and he wants to know the specific support of U.S. President Joe Biden for these normalization agreements advocated by Donald Trump.
According to Abdullah Baqer, chairman of the Israel / Pirate Business Council, the UAE has increased its investment in Israel, but ultimately wants to invest in the Palestinian territories, including Gaza, where Qatar, its rival monarchy, is pouring millions of dollars in aid.

title: Climate change makes eating more challenging for Australian farmers
text:
Climate change makes eating more challenging Australian farmers actively respond 2019-11-30 10: 26 United Daily News compiled by the United Daily News / Instant report Australian wine farmer Jeff Burch laughed when asked if he would become an environmentalist in the future: “I don ’ t know if it will be so exaggerated! ”
That ’ s because he ’ s just spent a few hours mulling the climate-change measures he ’ s introducing for his vineyard in the Margaret River region of Western Australia, including covering rows of Portuguese vines with dark green strips to protect them from the sun, composting and laying hay under trees to preserve water.
The most exaggerated is to spray "sunscreen" on precious grapes to prevent the skin of grapes from cracking, just like people rub sunscreen lotion on their faces and avoid sunburn.
This is the way modern farming must respond to climate change, says Berch: “I ’ m not a climate scientist, I just know that we get less rain and more weather patterns. ”
He called on politicians who deny climate change to “wake up. ”
Annual rainfall has fallen by 20% at his Magritte River region vineyard and by more than 50% further south in Mount Barker.
Records show that the weather is getting hotter and Berch is planning to move.
He will move the best chardonnay white grapes to the south, which is expected to cost $3 million (about $62 million).
He said that the relocation is planned for 10 or 15 or even 20 years later, and hopes to produce high-quality chardonnay by then.
Bertrand is not alone.
In fact, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation ’ s Australia Talks National Survey, a whopping 79 per cent of Australians believe Australia has a responsibility to take action against climate change, even if other carbon emitters refuse to follow suit.
To get rid of chemicals, North Queensland farmer Deb McLucas uses her farm in her sugar cane country to produce eggs and raise beef cattle.
She said: “In this area, compared to most other farms, we are absolutely abnormal.
It doesn ’ t stop us, we don ’ t care if there ’ s an ex.
She switched the farm to organic farming, believing it would help retain more water and gas and make better use of rainwater when it rains.
Young Western Australian farmer Rohan Thorn and his brother have begun harvesting one of this year ’ s crop varieties: mustard blossoms.
He said that before there was only one crop per crop, now there are two or three, and the crops are more diverse, which can spread the risk.
The degree of frost resistance and drought resistance of each crop varies. "Planting is always about eating from the sky, and climate change increases variability and risks are higher."

title: The 2nd Hainan Island International Film Festival Opening Iranian director Farhadi will appear at this film festival
text:

title: Overseas medical treatment is on the rise, and the medical tourism industry in Asia is booming.
text:
SEOUL, Oct. 4 (Reuters) - This is one of the fastest growing industries in Asia, and it is not showing signs of weakness even as the global economy falters.
Today, medical tourism has become a billion-dollar industry.
From cosmetic surgery to heart bypass, hospitals in India, Singapore and South Korea receive more than 1 million foreign patients a year for no less than the following reasons: cost-effective surgery, no waiting in line for treatment, advanced technology and well-trained doctors.
Industry experts predict that as the number of new affluent people in the region increases, the medical tourism industry in the region will grow at a rate of 15-20% per year.
“As Asia has become richer and more mobile, medical tourism in Asia … seems to be growing, ” said David Vequist, director of the Center for Medical Tourism Research at the University of the Incarnate Word in Texas.
“Consumer choice is now a powerful force in the healthcare industry, with Asia ’ s aging population, growing obesity, sicker populations and more in need all having an impact on the healthcare industry. ”
Medscape News predicts that Asia ’ s medical tourism industry could generate $4.4 billion in value by 2012.
Among them, the largest number of patients came from the United States.
To avoid the high cost of private treatment at home, many Americans seek medical treatment overseas.
In general, this can save Americans 40% -50% of the cost of treatment.
Now, a new patient has been added to the operating table - the Chinese.
Many Chinese people try to solve their problems at any cost.
"No matter how expensive it is, I will do it," said Liu Xiaoyang, a 34-year-old Shanghainese who has just undergone double eyelid surgery, plastic surgery and jaw correction in Seoul, South Korea.
The rise of China's affluent class and the fascination with the "Korean Wave", to the popularity of pop music and Korean dramas, has led to a huge increase in the medical tourism industry in South Korea, especially the plastic surgery industry.
"Every time I watch Korean dramas and TV programs, I think the characters on TV are beautiful, and I hope I can be like them," Liu said.
Kim Byung-gun, a plastic surgeon at BK Dongyang Plastic Surgery Clinic in Seoul, says his patients are as young as six and as old as 70.
On average, their surgery costs about $5,000-10,000.
"The medical tourism industry will become one of the engines of the Korean economy," Kim said, adding that the "Korean Wave" is a key factor in promoting the development of the medical tourism industry in the country.

title: The future of food is not nutritious? The global food shortage crisis is hidden
text:
The nutritional value of these foods changes when the quantity and locality of the food changes.
Image Source: Health 365 Atlanta experts say climate change will affect the world ’ s food supply in three ways. Dr. Meyers, who studies environmental health at Harvard University, says the amount and quality of food we produce will be affected by the increasing demand for food, coupled with climate change.
Dr Myers told Life Sciences Online that there has never been a rapid increase in food production to supply global demand, but at this time, people are changing the biological basis of food production. "Researchers are looking at the biological and physical changes caused by climate change, and how food production can be changed," Dr Myers said at the Climate and Health conference on February 16, 2017. Public health organizations are also actively advocating for the health impact of climate change. ” 1.
Food production: Climate change will eventually reduce the production of food, which is likely to happen around the world. At first, experts thought that carbon dioxide may be used as a fertilizer to increase food production. However, recent research has found that the impact of climate change means that food production will decline. This is especially true in tropical areas.
At present, pests cause crop losses of 25% to 40%. In the future, with climate change, it may cause the scope of these pests to expand the range of crops.
Regional: Most of the world ’ s agricultural areas will also affect global food supply due to warming. Agriculture in the tropics may have the most severe impact. Global warming will make it difficult for farmers to work, resulting in a significant reduction in production; in fact, studies have shown that in the tropics and subtropics, working hours will be limited due to excessive temperatures at certain times.
Other food sources, such as fish, may migrate to the poles due to warmer ocean temperatures, resulting in a significant reduction in their numbers. Although the regions near the poles will be warmer due to climate change and have longer growing seasons, these changes are not enough to compensate for the loss to the planet.
3. Food quality: When the number and regional changes of food, the nutritional value of these foods will change, in the study, the researchers in more carbon dioxide, and under normal conditions to grow wheat and corn, they found that in the case of higher carbon dioxide concentration, the growing crops produced a large reduction in protein, zinc and iron.
However, reduced nutrients will cause humans to remain undernourished after eating food; in the future, 200 million people worldwide may be deficient in zinc, and this situation will only worsen due to climate change and cannot be improved in the short term.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: Hunting 330 whales, 5 whaling ships returning from Antarctic waters
text:
(Photo / Associated Press) Five Japanese whalers returned from Antarctic waters today to hunt 330 whales this year, sparking yet another serious protest from environmental and animal protection groups. It is mainly about exploring the local environment and ecology.
After an international ban on commercial whale hunting in 1986, the International Court of Justice issued a ban on the capture of Japanese whales in 2014, but Japanese officials have repeatedly violated the ban in the name of traditional customs and scientific research.
Japan ’ s Asahi Shimbun reports that five Japanese whaling vessels that completed four months of “exploration ” in Antarctica ’ s waters returned home today, bringing back 330 local whales that were hunted, setting off yet another serious protest from the international community and environmental groups.
This is the second year after Japan resumes its large-scale whale research program, and it is the second year of ocean-going whaling. Although the official has always insisted that these hunts are one of the projects of the research program, many organizations have criticized the so-called scientific research, which is basically "lamb head selling dog meat", and the actual whales returned to Japan, and eventually flowed into the commercial market and the bellies of the elderly.
In order to protect the endangered large cetaceans, the International Court of Justice issued a ban on the capture of Japan in 2014, but less than two years later, the Japanese government began to resume whaling with a research project.
One of the five whaling ships returning from the Antarctic this time: the Nihsin Maru. (Photo / Associated Press) The killer whale that has become popular around the world because of the movie "Whale Breaks the Sky".
(Graphic / Associated Press) In the oceans of the 19th and 20th centuries, in order to reap the rich and expensive economic benefits of whales, humans hunted and killed a large number of large whales in the global ocean, causing the population of all kinds of large whales to plummet to a dangerous stage.
In order to protect them and maintain the ecological balance of the sea, the international community formed the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after many negotiations, and in 1986 passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Whaling, which banned commercial whaling, but Japan, Norway, South Korea, Peru, Brazil, China and other countries voted against it.
Among them, Canada finally did not want to be ruled by the government, and in 1982, Japan, which has a tradition of eating whale meat, has become the main target of environmental groups every year with Norway.
Faced with criticism from the outside world, the Japanese government also strongly responded that whaling ships to the Antarctic waters, all acts are carried out in compliance with the Convention on the Prohibition of Whaling, mainly to investigate the number of whales and try to protect them.
On the eve of the return of the Japanese whaling ship, Norway was bombarded by international public opinion for killing pregnant whales due to cruelty, and it seems that whaling is still a controversial issue in the international community whether it is commercial or scientific research.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: The world ’ s largest aircraft can launch three rockets for the first time.
text:
Stratolaunch Systems created the world ’ s largest aircraft and debuted on May 31 at the Mojave Space Station in California. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The airborne giant has 28 wheels.
Stratolaunch Systems (Stratolaunch Systems), founded by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, announced on May 31 that the world ’ s largest aircraft will be launched for the first time at the Mojave Air and Space Port in California.
According to SPACENEWS and CNN, the huge object has a double body, a wingspan of more than 117 meters, a net weight of 226,800 kg, a maximum fuel load of 113,400 kg, and an external weight of 250,000 kg.
It has 28 wheels in addition to six engines used in the Boeing 747.
The company was originally set up in late 2011 to launch the mid-size SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, but as the two companies parted ways a year later, Stratolaunch then signed a contract with Orbital Sciences Corp, now known as Orbital ATK, to launch the mid-size rocket.
However, due to the increasing need to launch small satellites, Stratolaunch is now focusing on providing related services.
Allen ’ s newly unveiled baby can launch up to three Pegasus XL small rockets with just one flight.
Stratosphere Launch Systems said in a statement that since this is the world ’ s first new aircraft, it is expected that the giant will fly as early as 2019 after thorough testing for the safety of the pilot and crew.
It will begin with a series of ground tests, including refueling tests, with six tanks on board. The refueling mechanism will be tested separately and whether oil leaks will occur.
Stratolaunch is working on technology to reduce launch costs, and its CEO, Jean Floyd, believes they have shown results.
He pointed out that Allen ’ s motivation for investing is not to make big money, but to change the human environment.
Stratolaunch ’ s world ’ s largest aircraft can launch three small rockets at a time. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The world ’ s largest aircraft, nicknamed Roc, can carry a rocket weighing up to 110 tons to an altitude of nearly 11,000 meters in the stratosphere to launch the rocket. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The aircraft can carry a 110-ton rocket from the ground to 35,000 feet (nearly 11,000 meters) in the stratosphere, and then fire the rocket, launch it out of the atmosphere, and then send satellites into low Earth orbit.
Air-launched rockets have advantages and disadvantages compared to ground-launched rockets.
The advantage is that the air-launched rocket can avoid the dense atmosphere on the surface, greatly reducing the thrust / lift required for the rocket to enter the orbit, thus reducing the cost.
Overall, this launch method can quickly launch a launch object into space at a lower cost, without the need for complex launch site equipment.
In addition, the research of air-launched rocket technology has great military value.
The disadvantage of air-launched rockets is that during take-off, liftoff and flight, the rocket may be accidentally damaged, which increases the uncertainty of the launch.
SpaceX founder Elon Musk believes that the advantages of an air-launched rocket are not enough to make up for its shortcomings. “From SpaceX ’ s point of view, to launch a rocket with a huge aircraft, or to increase the first stage capacity of the rocket by 5%? I will choose the latter. ”

title: The world ’ s largest aircraft is finally ready for testing.
text:
Back in August 2015, Stratolaunch Systems, which was invested by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, announced that it would fly the world ’ s largest aircraft, Stratolaunch, in 2016.
But the final plan did not come to fruition, and it is only today that the situation has finally made new progress.
Earlier, Allen posted a photo of the plane leaving the hangar on Twitter, and wrote below that the move was for “fuel testing. ” The Stratolaunch, the largest all-combined aircraft in history, could almost be seen in length as a combination of two Boeing 747s propelled by six 747 engines with a payload of nearly 230 tons.
The original intention of building such an aircraft was to launch rockets in the air, so that fuel would be saved and the launch would not be affected by the weather.
Previously, Stratolaunch Systems had expressed the hope that Stratolaunch will be officially put into use by 2020, and although the process has changed somewhat, it should be hopeful to achieve the original goal.

title: World's largest twin-fuselage aircraft debuts capable of launching rockets in the air
text:
Beijing, June 2 (Reporter Jiang Xiaochen) According to the Voice of China "News" report, the United States local time on May 31, the world's largest dual-fuselage aircraft "stratospheric launch" nicknamed "Dapeng", in the United States California Mojave Air Base for the first time out of the hangar.
This "Dapeng" is not small, with a dual fuselage design, equipped with six engines, 72.5 meters long, 15 meters high, the wingspan of 117 meters, easily more than a football field, far more than the Boeing 747 airliner 59.6 meters.
With a self-weight of nearly 227 tons, it can carry 113 tons of fuel at a time, and it is no exaggeration to claim that the world's largest aircraft.
Some people may think, such a luxurious configuration, how comfortable people sit up! After a sigh, I can only regret to tell you that this plane is not manned, there is a more exciting use than manned to it, that is to carry rockets.
It is understood that the two bodies can carry a rocket weighing up to 275 tons.
The previous rockets were launched standing, but now they are launched lying down.
In the end, what is the origin of this "Dapeng" and what impact will it have on the rocket launch?
In the heavens, there are two sides, one side and the other side, and the earth is not visible.
Why can't you see it clearly?
Because it's too big!
This "Dapeng" looks like two aircraft spliced together, the choice of such a strange shape is because it is a specially built aircraft for space launch, the position in the middle of the double fuselage can be mounted a "thunder" three stage carrier rocket, the total weight of the aircraft and rocket will reach 589.6 tons, second only to the former Soviet developed super large military transport aircraft "An-225 transport aircraft" 640 tons. The man. "
As the saying goes, "layman watch the bustle, insiders watch the doorway." For the debut of the world's largest double-fuselage aircraft, how do experts see it?
Wang Xinbang, editor of Aviation Knowledge magazine, said: "From the perspective of the composition of the aircraft, this is not a very new concept.
Back at Virgin Atlantic, there was a Brandon who used a similar layout to create a white machine for launching suborbital space travel.
The two planes were the same designers, but the plane was larger than the White 2.
At present, many people have made similar attempts, or have a similar idea, that is, to carry rockets with super large aircraft.
As a rocket launch, the lower the latitude, the more conducive to launch, it can maximize the use of the Earth's rotation, like why China should use Wenchang launch site, because the dimension is low.
As for whether this method of launching can be better explored, the requirements for the rocket itself may be very high, that is to say, it can carry a very powerful rocket to achieve such an effect.
In the past, the traditional rocket launch was achieved by means of a ground launch pad, and can the "Dapeng" wingspan rocket launch really change the traditional launch mode? The answer is feasible.
In the early 1990s, the United States launched a Pegasus rocket with a B-52.
At that time, the Pegasus carrier rocket, carrying a Brazilian satellite, was successfully sent to orbit more than 700 kilometers.
So, compared to ground launch, what are the advantages of sky launch rockets?
Yang Yuguang, an expert of the Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation, said that the reason for trying to launch the sky is to reduce the cost and launch threshold of the rocket by this way. "The cost of launching a carrier rocket and the rocket engine is very high, and some companies have tried to reuse the rocket engine, but whether the cost can be reduced is still controversial.
And the aero engine has been very mature through so many years of development.
The carrier rocket can be sent to a high altitude by aircraft, and when it has a certain speed, the launch vehicle can be much better than the launch vehicle on the ground under the condition of the same payload capacity, thus saving the cost of launching the carrier rocket to a certain extent.
Yang Yuguang also said that objectively speaking, ground launch and sky launch have their own advantages and disadvantages.
The technology of launching a carrier rocket from the air is relatively complicated, and because of the aircraft flying in the air, there is a certain vibration environment, which is equivalent to launching from a moving benchmark.
Prior to launch, these benchmarks are transmitted to the launch vehicle, which itself requires sophisticated technology, whereas on ground launch, the rocket takes off in a stationary state and is therefore much simpler.
Conversely, there are some other advantages to launching from the air, such as launching a carrier rocket on the ground, which is relatively affected by the surrounding environment, and there are certain restrictions in the direction to ensure that when a subset of the carrier rocket falls, it will not hurt people and objects on the ground.
Launching a carrier rocket from the air allows the aircraft to fly to the right place, for example, at a sparsely populated altitude, with less restrictions.

title: Study: Heat wave hits big grain silos at the same time, causing food shortages
text:
Climate change could lead to more intense heatwaves across the globe, hitting major grain silos at the same time, causing food shortages and causing chaos.
Researchers warned today that climate change could lead to more intense heat waves around the world, hitting major grain silos at the same time, causing food shortages and causing chaos.
Dim Coumou, a climatologist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany and an associate professor at VU University Amsterdam in the Netherlands, co-authored the study published in the journal Nature Climate Change.
Crops failure in some parts of the world due to climate disasters would have offset increased trading in other areas with normal harvests or good harvests, Kum said, but strong jets of air over the planet, coupled with higher temperatures caused by climate, could strike at the same time, threatening crops in multiple grain silos.
The regions most vulnerable to this heatwave include western North America, western Europe, western Russia and Ukraine, which produce about a quarter of the world ’ s staple foods of wheat, corn, soybeans and rice.
Koum said the jet pattern was linked to the devastating heatwaves that struck Russia in 2003 and 2018 in Western Europe and in 2010.
“Our analysis shows that whenever these heatwaves occur, crops in these areas are adversely affected at the same time, ” he told the Thomson Reuters Foundation.
According to the report, as long as the weather pattern is in place for more than two weeks in summer, the affected areas lose 4% of their crops and up to 11% more in the wider region.
Reduced production in these regions could lead to a spike in global food prices if affected countries impose export bans to ensure food supplies in their own countries are safe, the report added.

title: Farm of the Future in Asia
text:
MANILA - Food shortages are a distant memory for many Asians.
But as the region struggles to provide enough food and nutrition for a growing population, food shortages will once again become a painful reality.
Already the world ’ s largest food market, Asia ’ s population is expected to grow to 5 billion by 2050 – an increase of 900 million people.
Thanks to a growing middle class, annual beef and poultry consumption in the region will account for half of the global increase between now and 2030, and fish consumption will account for more than three-quarters of the global increase.
By then, 60 per cent of the developing world's grain demand will come from South and East Asia.
To keep up with this growing demand, food production needs to increase by 60-70% from a decade ago.
Ideally, farms in Asia could well increase production.
But they are completely unprepared for that.
To provide adequate food, Asia ’ s farms need a 21st-century transformation.
Helping Asian farmers deal with climate change should be at the heart of this effort.
A warming planet could increase agricultural output in some regions, but it could also severely limit production elsewhere in Asia, triggering a long-term food crisis.
In traditional fertile areas, such as the Indus – Ganges Plain, water is decreasing and rising sea levels will engulf large tracts of good land.
If the sea level rises by one meter, the resulting salt surge will threaten 70 percent of Vietnam's coastal farmland.
As water temperatures rise and tidal flows change, the vast fishing grounds of the Mekong Delta may collapse.
According to research by the Asian Development Bank, irrigated rice and wheat yields could fall by as much as 20 percent and 44 percent, respectively, by 2050.
This will lead to a 70 per cent increase in the price of cereals, soybeans and wheat, and an increase of 11 million malnourished children in the region.
But this is not the fate of Asia, if Asian farmers can make adjustments.
Today, most farmers produce at home, lacking the capital and expertise to improve productivity and crop quality.
In Myanmar, for example, only 16 per cent of peasant households use microtillers and tractors to plow their fields.
In addition, environmental damage has led to the abandonment of a large number of farmland.
According to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, nearly 40 percent of Asia's total land area is facing various forms of desertification.
Governments cannot create new arable land, but they can – and must – adopt policies to support, integrate, and concentrate agricultural operations on still arable land.
First, governments in the region could promote farm cooperatives.
Farm cooperatives are different from the collective farms of the past.
Today ’ s cooperatives are entirely commercial and focus on efficiency and profit.
They include agribusiness and farmers, with participants pooling resources to create economies of scale, reduce costs and raise incomes.
If cooperative bulk purchases were possible, inputs such as fertilizers and agricultural machinery would be cheaper and harvested.
Cooperatives in India and Nepal plan to make it possible for each participant ’ s crops to be sown and harvested in a unified machine, without the need for manual operation as before.
Cooperatives can also increase post-harvest value by making it easier to clean, screen, pack, store and transport crops.
This could increase food supplies and boost farmers' incomes, especially in Bangladesh, where more than a third of perishable crops are now being wasted before they reach consumers.
China has begun to modernize its farms through cooperatives, or use digital e-commerce platforms to break into the high-end market.
In Viet Nam, a cooperative programme improved the quality of agricultural products for urban consumers, increasing tea, fruit and vegetable income by nearly one third.
Although cooperatives are gradually being rolled out in Asia, more support is needed.
Cooperatives in most of Asia are vulnerable and informal arrangements.
But with the right legal framework in place, they can greatly improve efficiency and sustainability.
The 2007 Law of the People ’ s Republic of China on Farmers ’ Professional Cooperatives is a very good model.
The law provides incentives such as VAT relief to encourage cooperatives and other agricultural organizations to collaborate to create economies of scale.
Within three years of the law ’ s implementation, the number of cooperatives in China had increased nine-fold to 400,000.
Cooperation can also form networks where members share difficult adjustment strategies, such as switching from growing crops to fishing for shrimp in areas affected by salt tides, which can help farmers fight the effects of climate change.
With the additional income provided by cooperatives, farmers can purchase greenhouses to extend the production season and combat unstable weather.
Cooperatives also allow farmers to benefit from previously unavailable technologies, such as irrigation fertilization – that is, the delivery of liquid fertilizers using irrigation techniques.
Finally, cooperatives make climate-smart technologies more affordable.
With new digital technologies, farmers can better manage their land, water and energy use and be prepared for bad weather.
For example, the Philippines has tried to promote the use of information on plant and animal diseases and pests to farmers, information on the best places to buy and sell farm output, and weather event warnings.
By using less labor and more capital and technology, Asia ’ s future farms can grow enough food to feed everyone in the region.
Cooperatives are one way to translate this vision into reality. Only then can food shortages truly become history.

title: Warming will lead to a decline in global rice production
text:
Singapore's "United Morning Post" reported on the 17th, research shows that global warming may lead to a reduction in global production of major crops such as wheat, rice, corn and so on.
An international team of researchers analyzed 70 reports on the relationship between global warming and agriculture and published the results in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
These studies use a variety of different research models, including simulating how crops react to different global and local temperatures, probabilistic models based on past climate and harvest data, human-made studies of farmland warming, and more.
All of the above models conclude that “rising temperatures may have a negative effect on wheat, rice, and corn production, ” the report said.
The report concludes: “Every 1 degree Celsius rise in the median global temperature is estimated to result in a 6% decline in global average wheat production. ”
At the same time, rice production will decline by 3.2% and corn production by 7.4%.
“Soybean production hasn ’ t changed much.
University of Florida professor Szentholde Arsen, who led the study, said these four types of crops are critical to human survival because two-thirds of human calorie intake comes from wheat, rice, corn and soybeans.
The study also found that the impact of global warming on different crops and different regions is very different, and that rising temperatures may increase crop production in some regions, but the impact on the vast majority of regions is negative.
Therefore, it is necessary to take corresponding measures according to regional and crop conditions to ensure food security in the context of global population growth.
This is not the first time scientists have warned that climate change will affect food security and even human survival.
Earlier this month, a report published in the Environmental Research Letters, led by Harvard University in the United States, warned that global warming and rising levels of carbon dioxide will lead to a sharp reduction in protein in human staples such as rice and wheat, which will put more vulnerable groups in the population at risk of delayed development and premature death.
The report said that by 2050, the number of people at risk of protein deficiency will increase by 150 million globally.
The most affected regions are expected to be sub-Saharan Africa, where hunger is a chronic problem, and South Asia, where rice is a staple food.
In fact, the effects of warming are already showing up.
In July, when southern Europe experienced its worst drought in a decade, the cereal harvest was severely affected.
In some parts of Italy and Spain, cereal harvests are estimated to have fallen to their lowest levels in 20 years, causing heavy losses to farmers.

title: Klimt painting worth 79.3 billion won found in garbage bag
text:
A Klimt painting worth 79.3 billion won was found in a garbage bag.
13, 2019 07: 35. by Ren Bo-mei bom @ donga.com.
Gustav Klimt ’ s supposedly stolen work reappeared in the gallery ’ s walls 22 years later.
Italy ’ s Ansa news agency reported on the 10th (local time) that the Ritchie Audi Museum of Modern Art in Piacenza has found a work suspected to have been lost in 1997 and presumed to be Klimt ’ s Portrait of a Woman (photo).
According to the Daily Telegraph, gardeners at the museum found metal plates attached to the wall while cleaning the climbing tiger on the outer wall of the building.
After opening, you see the gap that connects the inner wall and outer wall of the building, and there are black bags inside.
"At first I thought it was rubbish," said the gardener, Laura Bonpanti, deputy curator of the museum. "It seems to be the real thing from the privateed seal or seal on the back of the work.
This seems to be the best Christmas gift. "If it is authentic, its value is estimated to reach 60 million euros (about 79,306.92 million won).
The head of the Cultural Advisory Council of Piacenza did not rule out the possibility of thieves returning the works after stealing them.
"Immediately after the theft, we conducted a thorough search of all parts of the art gallery and courtyards at the time," the official said in a statement.
The strangest thing is that the work is in very good condition.
I can't see it staying there for 22 years, "he said.
“Portrait of a Woman, ” which disappeared about 10 months ago in 1996, was revealed to be the only work Klimt had painted in other works, and was once the subject of discussion.
X-ray analysis at the time showed that Portrait of a Woman was supposedly painted on another of Klimt's paintings, Portrait of a Young Woman, stolen in 1912.

title: Klimt disappeared for 23 years and found the famous painting - International
text:
The Ricci-Oddi Museum of Modern Art in Italy has discovered a painting by Austrian painter Gustav Klimt that was stolen 23 years ago, worth 60 million euros (about NT $2 billion).
The painting, Portrait of a Lady, which was stolen by thieves with a fishing line in his later years, was found in a groove in the museum ’ s exterior wall.
According to the museum, a gardener was cleaning the ivy of the museum ’ s outer wall when he found a metal plate on the wall, and when he opened it, he found a canvas painting in a black sackcloth bag.
Experts are now working on the authenticity of the painting, but Laura Bonfanti, the museum ’ s deputy curator, said, “The retrieval of the painting is the best Christmas gift ever. ”
He also expressed confidence that the wax seal and stamp on the back of the canvas would appear to be the painting that was stolen on February 22, 1997.
The Portrait of a Lady was painted by Klimt between 1916 and 1917, in his later years of life, and died of illness in 1918.
Klimt is an Austrian symbolist painter whose works often focus on women, sex and love, which has led to criticism from conservative painters.
His most famous work is Der Kuss.
