title: Austrian master Klimt has been stolen for 23 years, and the gardener has been found under an external wall.
text:
A portrait of a lady by Austrian symbolist Klimt was stolen 23 years ago.
Photo / CNN Share facebook Gustav Klimt, an Austrian symbolist painter whose famous painting Portrait of a Lady was stolen 23 years ago while on display at the Ricci Oddi Modern Art in Piacenza, Italy.
Unexpectedly, last week, a museum gardener was cleaning the ivy on the outer wall when he accidentally found a painting suspected to be stolen in a black plastic bag, and the museum and police are actively working to confirm whether the painting is actually a real Klimt.
According to The Art Newspaper, last week a Ricciardi museum gardener found a metal door plate while cleaning the ivy on the outer wall. After the gardener removed the door plate, he found a cave with a black plastic bag inside, which turned out to be a complete painting.
The gardener met Dario Gallinari, who had just finished his lunch, and told him what had happened.
"At first I thought it was just a joke," Dario said, "until I saw a corner of the painting from under a black plastic bag, and I immediately realized that it could be Klimt's painting that had been missing for 23 years..."
Klimt is the representative master of Austrian symbolism. The painting features a special symbolic pattern, and this Portrait of a Lady was created in 1917 and acquired by the Ricciotti Gallery in Piacenza, northern Italy, in 1925.
But this found painting is completely preserved and does not seem to have been left out. If this painting is really a real sign of Klimt, it may have never left the Richie Ordi Museum.
Massimo Ferrari, the museum ’ s curator, said that the stamp after the painting appeared to be genuine and related to Klimt ’ s other works, while Laura Bonfanti, the deputy curator, said the painting ’ s property number had yet to be confirmed and it could take months to confirm its authenticity.

title: World's Largest Aircraft Gets Ground Test at 74 km / h
text:
Feb 27, 2018 14: 03 China Times News Yang Yulan has a wingspan of more than 117 meters, and the world ’ s largest aircraft with six engines is rapidly flying headfirst.
Recently, it has been seen moving rapidly at the Mojave Air and Space Port.
According to "The Drive" network reported on the 26th, now Stratolaunch Systems main sponsor Paul Allen took advantage of it before the first flight, released a wonderful picture of the roc rapid ground test.
Allen tweeted that it can reach a top speed of 46 miles per hour (74 km / h), which is quite fast for a big baby with a net weight of 226,800 kg, a maximum fuel load of 113,400 kg and an external weight of 250,000 kg.
Because in recent months, the Pentagon has sought to increase the flexibility and agility of its space capabilities, and has even been actively considering space as the next battleground, the tools to launch smaller satellites into orbit quickly and cheaply appear to be full of business opportunities.
(Stratolaunch Systems) To achieve this goal, the US Air Force ’ s 2019 budget for space “small launches ” lists a five-year plan with a budget of nearly US $200 million (nearly NT $6 billion), which will fund companies that can provide related services in the future.
U.S. Air Force Secretary Heather Wilson said the goal of the project is to develop a variety of launch capabilities to ensure access to space.
The world's largest aircraft, nicknamed Dapeng, can carry a 110-ton rocket from the ground to 35,000 feet (nearly 11,000 meters) in the stratosphere below the wings and in the middle of the fuselage, and then let the rocket ignite, launch, escape from the atmosphere, and then send satellites into low-Earth orbit.
Air-launched rockets have advantages and disadvantages compared to ground-launched rockets.
The advantage is that the air-launched rocket can avoid the dense atmosphere on the surface, greatly reducing the thrust / lift required for the rocket to enter the orbit, thus reducing the cost.
Overall, this launch method can quickly launch a launch object into space at a lower cost, without the need for complex launch site equipment.
In addition, the research of air-launched rocket technology has great military value.
The disadvantage of air-launched rockets is that during take-off, liftoff and flight, the rocket may be accidentally damaged, which increases the uncertainty of the launch.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: More than 250,000 Americans die each year from medical negligence.
text:
According to a Johns Hopkins University study, "medical negligence" ranks third in American causes of death, behind only heart disease and cancer; more than 250,000 people die of medical negligence each year, and may even be as many as 440,000.
Experts call for improvements to the health care system ’ s shortcomings and for patients to be reminded of their rights.
Jerry ’ s one-and-a-half year old daughter, Emily, has a huge tumor in her lower abdomen, and has undergone many painful surgeries and chemotherapy, and is finally about to recover.
In order to ensure that the cancer cells are completely removed, the doctor recommends completing the last course of chemotherapy.
On the last day of a three-day chemotherapy session, on the eve of Emily ’ s second birthday, a pharmacist mistakenly injected more than 20 times the amount of salt as she prepared for a physical saline drop.
In less than a few hours, Emily ’ s condition deteriorated dramatically, installed a life support system, and declared brain dead, and died three days later.
On the day of Emily ’ s accident, the hospital pharmacy was understaffed, the pharmacy computer was not working properly, and there was a loophole in the doctor ’ s instructions, which caused this tragedy.
A study conducted by Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Professor Makali, who analyzed data for eight consecutive years, found that there were about 35.41 million doctor visits each year, and 250.14 million people died from medical negligence, accounting for about 9.5% of the total number of deaths.
Causes of medical negligence include unskilled health care personnel, diagnostic or treatment errors, deficiencies in the medical system, and preventable adverse reactions.
To improve medical negligence, you can start by strengthening communication and recording, such as digitizing medical records, archiving work conversations of health care personnel, and so on.
Patients can also get more protection when visiting their doctor in different ways, such as: bravely asking questions, asking doctors about possible benefits, disadvantages, and side effects of medical procedures and medications; seeking second opinions, visiting other doctors, asking their opinions, and so on.
Given the absurdly high cost of medical care in the United States, it is not surprising that medical tourism has flourished in recent years.
Last year, nearly 1.5 million Americans sought medical treatment abroad to save money, a tenfold increase from a decade ago, according to Sans Frontieres.
The global market for medical tourism is expected to grow by as much as 25% per year, with the largest increases in Costa Rica, Brazil and India, all of which are considered to be cheap and save money ranging from 20% to 90%.
Of course, you may have heard terrible stories of cosmetic or improper teeth removal and be skeptical about medical tourism overseas.
But you may not have heard too many stories of successful completion of medical care, recently someone on the social networking site Reddit asked about the good or bad experience of medical tourism, and the response was mostly positive.
The account name JPLucas14 says he needs a gum transplant, but in the United States, even if he has insurance, he still has to pay $5,000.
He went to Mexico to do it, and the air tickets, medical expenses, car rental and AirBnb short-term rental combined were less than $2,100, and the process went smoothly.
This person uses the Medigo.com website, which certifies clinics and recommends only those that have been thoroughly researched and are completely legal.
Another woman, named Starvard11, said she lived in Thailand half the time and became full-time when she was 30 weeks pregnant.
Four days of hospitalization, maternity care, full day baby care, plus private room, couple meals, only spent $900.
Another said he had a female friend who went to Italy for artificial insemination for only $4,000 and enjoyed an Italian holiday.
Artificial insemination in the United States costs between 15,000 and 20,000 yuan.
To have a positive overseas medical experience, remember to do a few things: consult with doctors and travel medical practitioners to make sure you are going to the right place; arrange residential care during recovery; inform the bank that you are going abroad to prevent identity theft; and keep in touch with your family, according to Medical Tourism magazine.

title: US plans to build world ’ s first nuclear fusion plant in 15 years
text:
Building on the tokamak device, MIT plans to build a compact fusion experimental device, SPARC, the key to which is to build a powerful superconducting electromagnetic magnet.
Using the principle of nuclear fission, humans have built hundreds of nuclear power plants.
Now, start moving toward fusion utilization.
According to the British "Guardian" and other foreign media reports, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in the United States is carrying out a nuclear fusion research project, plans to build the world's first nuclear fusion power station in the next 15 years, and connect it to the power grid.
The plant is designed to have a capacity of 200 megawatts.
Developed by MIT in partnership with CFS (Commonwealth Fusion Systems), a private company, the project aims to transform nuclear fusion from an expensive stage of scientific experimentation into an economically viable commercial project.
MIT said the project attracted investment from Italian energy company ENI.
ENI has invested $50 million in CFS, of which $30 million will be used for MIT research on the project over the next three years.
There are two main ways to develop nuclear energy: the fission of heavy elements and the fusion of light elements.
Nuclear fusion produces a huge amount of energy higher than nuclear fission, and has long been regarded by the scientific community as the ultimate energy source for mankind.
One kilogram of nuclear fusion fuel produces electricity equivalent to 11,000 tons of coal, and the fuel required for nuclear fusion deuterium, tritium, in nature storage is very large, can be extracted in seawater.
However, nuclear fusion is highly uncontrollable.
Human control of fusion reaction, currently mainly rely on a ring descriptor, by binding electromagnetic wave drive, to create deuterium, tritium to achieve fusion environment and ultra-high temperature, to achieve controlled nuclear fusion.
The device is called Tokamak, and its name comes from its keywords – toroidal, kamera, magnet, and kotushka.
At the end of the 20th century, scientists applied emerging superconducting technology to tokamak devices, resulting in superconducting tokamak devices.
Its imitation principle is the thermonuclear fusion reaction inside the sun, so the industry calls this device "artificial sun".
MIT has expanded on the tokamak device and plans to build a compact fusion experimental device, SPARC.
The key to SPARC is to build a powerful superconducting electromagnetic magnet.
MIT and the CFS team plan to complete their research on superconducting electromagnets in three years.
According to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the superconducting material that makes the superconducting magnet is a steel strip coated with yttrium-barium copper oxide (YBCO) composite material.
The use of this material can make superconducting magnets have advantages such as high magnetic field strength and low cost.
At present, China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the United States are carrying out a project called the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) Program, which is equivalent to building a large-scale “artificial sun. ”
According to the ITER project planning, 2007-2025 is the construction phase, the first ignition is achieved at the end of 2025, and the operation phase will enter in 2035, and finally the commercial application of nuclear fusion energy will be realized before and after 2050.
The project involves seven parties, including the European Union, China, the United States, Japan, Russia and other countries.
China joined the ITER program in 2003 and will undertake 12 of the 137 procurement package manufacturing tasks in ITER installations, which is close to 10% of the total.
At the same time, China is also making its own "artificial sun" - the fully superconducting tokamak nuclear fusion experimental device EAST.
In July last year, EAST achieved a stable 101.2-second stable long-pulse high-beam mode plasma operation for the first time in the world, setting a new world record.
Duan Xu, deputy director of the Southwest Institute of Physics of the nuclear industry, said that after nearly ten years, China's technical research on nuclear fusion has gone from the past "following" to the current part of the technology to achieve "leading".
On March 18, according to the Science and Technology Daily, it was learned from the Hefei Institute of Materials Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences that the nuclear energy safety of China's neutron irradiation resistant steel (CLAM steel) is the raw material, and the use of 3D printing technology to achieve the key components of the fusion reactor - the first wall sample of the cladding, and its structure and performance have been studied and analyzed.
This is the first time that China has achieved 3D printing of samples of key components of a fusion reactor.
The research shows that 3D printing technology has good application prospects in the manufacturing of complex components of advanced nuclear power systems such as fusion reactors.

title: Oil is cheap, it is difficult to switch to renewable energy, and the environmental pollution cycle in North Africa and the Middle East
text:
By Christophe Maroun The 23rd Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) (COP23), held in Bonn, Germany, mentioned that 2017 will be the top three warmest years on record.
Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry and the Cyprus Institute in Nicosia predict that climate change will severely impact the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region.
Without international climate policy and action, the country ’ s rainfall could be reduced by 30% by 2100, with average annual temperatures likely to rise by 4.5 degrees Celsius.
In 2015, the 21st Conference of the Parties adopted the landmark Paris Agreement, which is the first truly global agreement on climate change. The 2017 Bonn Conference is to further establish the rules of the Paris Agreement and strengthen national action to achieve the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 2 degrees Celsius.
In October 2015, the journal Nature Climate Change predicted that heatwaves in parts of the Persian Gulf could threaten human survival by the end of the century. Even if greenhouse gas emissions decline again after 2040, heatwaves in the Middle East and North Africa will continue significantly longer, with a current average of 16 days, by the middle of the century. It lasts 80 days and will last 118 days by the end of the century.
There are no restrictions on agricultural water use in the region, resulting in overpumping of groundwater, deterioration of water quality and land degradation, including salinization (increased salt content in the soil).
Climate change will exacerbate the situation and the agriculture sector will suffer a severe blow.
More frequent and intense heat waves, combined with reduced rainfall, will inhibit crop growth.
As rainfall decreases, so does soil moisture, river runoff, and water supply.
Increased climate uncertainty will affect productivity and make agricultural planning more difficult.
As Safa ’ Al-Jayoussi of CAN-International said: “The Arab region is currently suffering from drought, and this is only the beginning of the consequences of climate change.
Therefore, discussions on climate change should take into account the regions that have been severely affected and how to compensate for the damage caused by this phenomenon. ”
Jordan, for example, pumps 160% more groundwater than nature ’ s water storage, but they lack the incentive to conserve this precious resource.
Wastage is a problem as governments continue to heavily and unsustainably subsidize irrigation water.
More than half of Jordan ’ s water is used for agriculture, but production only supplies a fraction of the local food needs.
An estimated 50% of the water supply is wasted due to misuse or theft.
Egypt faces a similar problem: “Climate change accelerates the extent of famine, severely impacting already vulnerable and struggling countries. ”
Egyptian farmers are trying to adapt, "he said.
Climate change drives hunger – it hits the most vulnerable the hardest.
As Egyptian farmers struggle to adapt, @ WFP is there to help.
# COP23 pic.twitter.com / 3a7QQutIDB — WFP Middle East (@ WFP _ MENA) Nov 6, 2017 Utilizing Solar and Wind Energy The Middle East is eating its own fruit because it relies too much on fossil fuels, and air pollution and polluted water come at a heavy cost.
Increasing desertification has a negative impact on agriculture, while fisheries have significantly reduced their catches due to the deterioration of coastal water quality and changes in sea temperature.
However, fossil fuels continue to receive huge subsidies, and at extremely low prices, it is difficult to encourage people to use renewable energy.
Because fossil fuels also have some off-the-shelf subsidies, locals believe that renewable energy is not competitive in terms of cost.
Some countries in the region have become rich by mining fossil fuels, with less than 1% of their electricity coming from renewable sources.
Almost all countries in the Middle East and North Africa have plenty of sunshine and great potential for solar and wind, but investment in renewable energy is among the lowest in the world.
In this regard, the Middle East and North Africa lags behind many countries with similar economic capabilities, and even behind many countries that are poorer than they are.
Countries in the Arab World have voluntary committed to renewable energy targets as a percentage of overall electricity generation capacity.
# CANAWA # FESMENA # COP23 pic.twitter.com / gWeGGMFg2O — @ CANArabWorld (@ CAN _ ArabWorld) November 8, 2017 The Middle East and North Africa should be prepared for extreme weather, according to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change of the UN (IPCC). Climate change has led to a significant increase in the frequency of extreme weather events such as heat waves, floods, and wildfires.
Unless action is taken now to significantly reduce global carbon emissions, the impact of these natural disasters will cause irreversible and severe damage to billions of people.
Over the past decade, countries have announced long-term and medium-term plans to replace fossil fuels.
For example, Morocco and Jordan have promoted energy diversification to meet the dependence on and demand for imported fuels with increasing costs.
The Moroccan government is on the verge of meeting its target of producing 2 gigawatts (GW) of solar energy, with wind currently exceeding 750 megawatts (MV) and 2 gigawatts of wind energy by 2020.
The Jordanian government plans to increase the current 600 megawatts of solar energy to 1 gigawatt by 2020.
Experts warn that the world's current commitment to reducing carbon emissions means global warming affecting at least 3 degrees Celsius and serious damage.
Without serious confidence-building and agreement, policies are likely to be delayed, as at the 2009 Copenhagen Conference of the Parties.

title: Will China's nuclear fusion power generation technology become the world's first?
text:
Image caption China claims to be leading the world in nuclear energy development
At a time when the world's demand for energy is increasing, but the damage to the environment is also relatively intensified, Chinese scientists are leading the development of energy that some people regard as the holy grail. BBC reporter Stephen McDonell visited a factory in Anhui that is not easy to access.
Imagine generating an infinite amount of energy with virtually no material waste – the lofty promise of nuclear fusion.
On the "Science Island" on the western outskirts of Hefei City, Anhui Province, a shiny giant circle is housed in a large circular box about the same height as two buildings, which is the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST).
In the device, hydrogen atoms fuse into helium, which can gather heat several times higher than the sun's core.
The reaction is controlled by a powerful battery.
If maintained properly, a large amount of electricity can be generated in a day.
Many countries in the world are committed to mastering nuclear fusion technology, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and the European Union are all working hard, but no team can maintain the stability of nuclear fusion like the team in Anhui.
Now it ’ s 100 seconds, and it ’ s getting longer every year.
In Anhui, scientists have begun discussions about setting the goal of extending the time by ten times, with temperatures at 100 million degrees Celsius.
Image caption Hundreds of experts work here.
But since the Soviet Union began nuclear fusion technology in the early 1950s, scientists and engineers have been unsuccessful for a reason.
Because it was really, really difficult.
Maintaining a limited fusion reaction in a controlled environment has proven feasible over the past 50 years, but the duration of fusion is still far shorter than it takes to transform into a large amount of thermal energy.
The EAST system is an enhanced version of the Russian design.
On the day of our interview, we witnessed a live debate in the control room.
There is a leakage problem — not the matter escaping but the air being sucked into the vacuum inside — and scientists have to figure out how to fix it.
The other group contacted the control room with a walkie-talkie.
They surround EAST ’ s pipelines, power rooms and ladders to find holes and fix them.
When Xi Jinping came to visit, he wanted to understand the dangers of this technology, so we asked them how they responded to the Chinese president.
"Nuclear fusion reactors are relatively safe compared to fission reactors, and magnetic confinement fusion can control fusion," said Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
I can turn off the power supply, which is extremely safe and will not cause any nuclear crisis.
The Chinese design is based on early Russian research.
Nuclear reactions now rely on fission and atomic fragmentation, the result of which is toxic waste that must be stored in a safe place for perhaps thousands of years.
A nuclear fusion plant is a fusion of two nuclei into a single nucleus, and then the magnetic force of the inner wall of the circle (known as plasma) reacts inside a huge pipeline.
Crucially, we were told that this would hardly produce any waste.
But this technology is not cheap.
It costs $150,000 a day just to start a machine, not including the salaries and hardware of hundreds of experts.
The Chinese government has invested heavily in the project, even though it knows that it may take decades to get fusion to power cities.
“Scientists and engineers will make a major breakthrough in fusion, plus government financial support, ” Song said.“ This is a huge project, but I personally think it will be a great sustainable development for humanity. ”
We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor.
Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is looking for possible international cooperation in nuclear fusion technology because it is so expensive and difficult.
For example, China has contributed to the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in southern France, in addition to the EU countries, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea and the United States, which is expected to be tested in 2025.
At the same time, China is also accelerating its own pace of development.
The next goal proposed by the Anhui team is to design a fully fledged fusion reactor capable of generating electricity.
To achieve this, it must be larger than what we see now, and be able to contain infinite plasma reactions instead of the existing minute and a half.
"Every country has a great demand for power, and China has a clear path map for fusion power," Song said. "We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor."
The ultimate goal is that nuclear fusion can produce more electricity than people dream of.
While it may sound far-fetched, the Chinese government is serious about the challenge.
If successful, China will eventually outperform the rest of the world in power generation in the future.

title: Sad Influence of Chinese Entering South Korea Fewer Thais Surge
text:
April 19, 2018 12: 51 Wang reported that the number of foreign patients visiting South Korea last year decreased for the first time due to the impact of the Saad anti-missile system.
However, Chinese patients still account for one-third of patients abroad.
The place that Chinese people go the most is plastic surgery.
South Korea ’ s “East Asia Daily ” revealed on the 18th that the number of foreign patients visiting Korea last year was 321,574, a decrease of 12% compared to 364,189 in 2016.
In particular, patients in China experienced the largest reduction of 21.8% compared to 2016.
Since March last year, the number of visitors to South Korea has dropped sharply due to the fallout of Sade ’ s revenge.
However, among foreigners, the proportion of Chinese is still the highest.
Last year, there were 99,837 Chinese patients, accounting for 31% of the total.
This was followed by the United States (13.8%) and Japan (8.5%).
Interestingly, there were 6,137 patients in Thailand, an increase of 56% compared to the previous year.
This is explained by the influence of korea.
Patients of different nationalities often go to different clinics.
The Chinese people see the most are plastic surgery (19.3%) and dermatology (16.3%), both in the field of beauty.
Japanese patients also frequent dermatology (30.3%) and plastic surgery (19.5%).
And 62.5% of Thai patients visited plastic surgery.
From this, it can be seen that Asians are highly concerned about plastic surgery in South Korea.
In contrast, the main departments visited by patients in the United States were internal medicine (25.7%) and screening centers (8.8%).
From the overall situation of foreign patients, this is not much different from the previous year when internal medicine (20.2%), plastic surgery (12.3%) and dermatology (10.9%) were in the top three respectively.
(WANG Pao)

title: Yunus: The government ’ s focus on supporting mega-institutions is suggesting that the problems of billions of poor people are “too small to be important. ”
text:
Muhammad Yunus suddenly realized how the crisis of capitalism has exacerbated the problem of poverty, thanks in part to the revolution in knowledge, science and technology (especially information technology), all of humanity is now living in an era of unprecedented prosperity.
Prosperity has changed the lives of many people, yet at the same time billions of people still suffer from poverty, hunger and disease.
In the past decade, the combined effects of several major crises have led to even greater misery and frustration for the 4 billion people living at the bottom.
Few people foresee these crises.
The dream of hope and idealism is the beginning of the 21st century and encapsulated in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) launched by the United Nations.
Many of us believe that in the coming decades, we will welcome unprecedented wealth and prosperity, not just for the few, but for the people who live on this planet.
As I will discuss later in this book, the establishment of the MDGs has indeed made significant progress in this battle against poverty.
It is sad that the year 2008 will be entered into the annals of history, because it is the year when people finally awaken to the serious weaknesses of the capitalist system. The food price crisis, the oil price crisis, the financial crisis, and the worsening environmental crisis all erupted in this year.
In the combined effects of these crises, people have lost faith in the global system that they thought they had fully understood and controlled.
These crises have also prevented the MDGs from delivering on their promising promises.
Let ’ s start with the food crisis.
In early 2008, the United Nations ’ World Food Program (WFP) report revealed the terrible news: more than 73 million people in 78 countries faced a decline in food rations.
Headlines tell us what we thought would never happen again: the price of staples such as cereals and vegetables has soared (wheat prices alone have risen by 200% since 2000), food shortages have hit many countries, deaths from malnutrition have risen, and riots have threatened stability around the world.
In June 2008, global food prices reached a peak.
Since then, prices have continued to fluctuate, reaching new highs in 2011.
Prices fell slightly in 2016, allowing millions to take a breather.
However, persistently high food prices have put enormous pressure on the lives of the poor, as they spend up to two-thirds of their income on basic subsistence food alone.
In order to avoid the worst consequences of the food crisis, the emergency plan did have some effect.
However, in order to prevent the immediate effects of food shortages and the spread of famine, short-term relief programmes are needed, and, just as importantly, we must look back at the factors that contributed to today ’ s crisis.
We have to think about how the world economy has evolved, especially the evolution of food production and distribution systems, and why we are in the predicament we are in today.
Perhaps we will be surprised to find that the economic, political, and commercial operations of the developed world have such a profound impact on the food supply of other poor countries.
Therefore, to solve the global food problem, we need to redesign the global architecture, which cannot be achieved by local and regional reforms alone.
The challenges we face today are rooted in history.
The Green Revolution of the 1950s and 1960s increased crop yields in Asia and Latin America, and many countries that were previously dependent on imports became self-sufficient. Rates of famine and malnutrition declined significantly.
The increase in grain production due to the “green revolution ” is also seen as a hero for saving up to a billion lives.
Today, however, a series of interrelated trends have partially reversed the gains made by the green revolution.
Part of the problem stems from the way food markets have been globalized over the past three decades.
I am a strong advocate of free trade, and I believe that encouraging the exchange of goods and services between people and countries will, in the long run, lead to greater prosperity for all.
But like all markets, global markets need sound rules to ensure that all players have the opportunity to benefit from them.
Unfortunately, today ’ s global market is only a partially free market with many restrictions and distortions that have devastating consequences for poor countries.
The imbalance created by this semi-freedom distorts markets, raises prices, and even destroys agriculture in poor countries that once prided themselves on food surpluses.
Ethanol subsidies in some countries, including the United States, are an example of such problems.
In order to partially replace fossil fuels in gasoline, the government has encouraged the cultivation of corn and soybeans in a subsidized manner.
At a time when the price of oil is only $20 a barrel, this subsidy makes some sense.
The government plans to use biofuels as a partial replacement for relatively cheap, production-rich oil, and the subsidies are intended to make the program economically viable.
As expected, in 2007, a quarter of all corn crops in the United States were used to produce ethanol.
But when the price of oil exceeds $50 a barrel (as it was in early 2017), the same subsidies don ’ t stand.
And it doesn ’ t make sense for big, profitable companies like ExxonMobil to continue to receive subsidies for oil production.
Both of these subsidies distort the market and lead to unintended ecological, social and economic consequences, so they should be eliminated as soon as possible.
Otherwise, it will continue to directly or indirectly drive up the price of basic food, and will also promote the conversion of arable land and other agricultural resources from food production to energy production.
In addition, increased demand for meat has also contributed to distortions in the structure of food prices, making the problem of global food shortages worse.
It is a good thing that some of the world ’ s poorest countries are becoming more and more prosperous.
Millions of people have been lifted out of poverty over the past three decades thanks to increasingly open free markets and technological developments, as well as programs such as microcredit, which give people who were otherwise excluded from capitalism access to investment funds.
But prosperity also brings challenges.
The average intake of meat in China has increased from 20 kilograms per year in 1958 to more than 50 kilograms now (slightly below the US average of about 57 kilograms).
Similar situations have occurred in other large countries, such as Indonesia and Bangladesh.
Not just because the number of people who can afford meat in these countries is increasing, but also because they are switching to meat (instead of traditional low-meat diets), which is an expression of their adaptation to a “modern ” life.
Unfortunately, meat is relatively inefficient for the use of natural resources.
Meat provides far less nutritious calories than can be absorbed by direct intake of grains.
But today, more and more grain and food is being fed to cattle, not to people.
It is estimated that up to a third of global grain production and a third of global fisheries are used to feed livestock.
Moreover, more and more plant arable land is shifting from producing human food to growing grain for cattle.
These changes add several costly steps to the process of sustaining human life.
Abnormal agricultural choices, such as shifting land use to ethanol and meat production, also make basic food increasingly expensive.
There are other factors that make food problems worse in developing countries.
One is that farmers in poor countries are becoming less competitive in an increasingly competitive international food market.
In fact, small farmers in developing countries suffer from having to compete with large producers in developed countries.
So far, it has been a one-sided battle, and it has brought devastating damage to poor farmers.
Photo Credit: CORBIS / Dazhi Image Enterprises are increasing their control over agricultural resources and hurting smallholder farmers in the developing world.
Large agribusiness has almost monopolized seed stocks and controlled the supply of high-cost synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, resulting in an increasing number of small farms being forced to shut down because they can ’ t afford the supplies they need to compete in the new global food market.
Oil prices are also an important factor.
For example, many fertilizers contain oil, so an increase in the price of oil per barrel is bound to drive up fertilizer prices.
What ’ s more, higher oil prices are bound to drive up the cost of all energy-related activities, including irrigation, farm equipment operations, transportation of goods to and from the market, and the movement of food between processing plants.
As these economic and social problems continue to worsen, the changing global environment threatens the development of agriculture around the world.
Climate change and drought have turned vast areas of once-fertile land into deserts. Over-cropping and urban sprawl have led to deforestation and further accelerated global warming.
Through scientific simulations, it can be estimated that even if climate change can increase the total area of arable land, the overall quality of arable land will decrease.
Moreover, the regions most likely to face loss of arable land are those already facing economic hardship, including sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, and North Africa.
One of the first countries to bear the brunt, including my homeland, Bangladesh.
It is the most densely populated country in the world. Its land is flat and 20% of the land is less than a meter above sea level.
As the sea level continues to rise, the flood problem in Bangladesh will also gradually worsen, and the extent of damage will become more and more serious.
This is a new type of case in which environmental disasters immediately lead to human disasters.
Looking back at 2008, after the food crisis, the oil crisis, and the environmental crisis, there was the biggest crisis in history, the collapse of the US financial system.
Many giant financial institutions and manufacturing leaders, such as the auto industry, have either declared bankruptcy or relied on government bailouts to survive.
There are many reasons for this historic economic collapse, including the rampant greed in the trading market, the deterioration of the investment market such as casinos, the dereliction of management and so on.
But it is clear that the financial system collapsed because it was fundamentally distorted at the point of departure.
The original purpose of the credit market was to provide the funds needed to start or expand a company in response to people ’ s needs, and bankers and financiers can earn a reasonable profit as a reward.
Everyone can profit from it.
In the 21st century, however, credit markets are being distorted by a relatively small number of self-interested individuals and companies who want to earn unrealistically high rates of return through clever financial engineering techniques.
They repackage mortgages and other loans into complex investment goods and hide or embellish the level of risk and other characteristics.
Then sell these items over and over again, and take a share of each transaction.
At the same time, investors are eager to raise prices and seize growth opportunities that are simply not sustainable, betting that the potential flaws of the system will never be revealed.
However, when the time comes, what should have happened has happened.
The house of cards collapsed.
And because of globalization, this financial tsunami quickly swept the world.
In the end, the people who suffered the most in this financial crisis were not the rich.
On the contrary, the greatest suffering falls on the four billion people at the bottom of the planet, even though they were not the cause of the crisis.
While the rich continue to enjoy the benefits of their lives, the bottom four billion people have to face life-and-death changes such as losing their jobs and income.
The combined effects of the financial crisis, the food crisis, the energy crisis, and the environmental crisis have had a huge impact on the lives of the bottom four billion people.
While governments have responded to the crisis by launching many emergency programs, including costly bailouts, to prop up financially troubled financial institutions and mega-consortia, not enough has been done to tackle the chronic problem of poverty.
By focusing on supporting mega-institutions because they are “too big to fail, ” the government is suggesting that the problems of billions of poor people are“ too small to matter. ”
Therefore, a new capitalist approach that allows social enterprises to also have room to operate offers hope for solving the problem of poverty.
Related books ▶ Yunus: Whether social enterprises take root in the economy, it depends on the decision of universities and young people. Book introduction This excerpt is from "The Three Zero World: Turning the Disgusted Generation, Seeing the Future, A New Economic Solution for Zero Poverty, Zero Unemployment, and Zero Net Carbon Emissions".
Author: Muhammad Yunus Translated by: Leslie Lin Nobel Peace Prize Laureate Muhammad Yunus The latest decision we make today affects the quality of life of the next generation for 30 years Get rid of the side effects of capitalism / Your own work Create your own environment Protect yourself now!
Yunus, who invented microcredit, social enterprise and was awarded the Nobel Prize for his work in alleviating poverty, is today ’ s most perceptive social commentator.
He argues that the time has come to acknowledge the failure of the capitalist engine, which in its current form inevitably leads to severe income inequality, massive unemployment, and environmental destruction.
We need a new economic system that can fully harness the creative power of altruism, just like a strong egoistic mindset.
Is this daydreaming? Not at all.
Over the past decade, thousands of individuals and organizations have embraced Yunus ’ vision of a new form of capitalism and created innovative social enterprises designed to meet people ’ s needs rather than accumulate wealth.
They are bringing solar power to millions of households in Bangladesh; turning thousands of unemployed youth into entrepreneurs through equity investments; financing small businesses owned by women in major cities across the country; bringing cars, housing and other services to the rural poor in France; and creating a global support network to help young entrepreneurs set up start-ups.
In this book, Yunus tells the story of a new civilization that was inspired by his work on economic experiments.
He will explain how international companies such as McCann Foods, Renault Motors, Iconic and Danone are making a difference through their social action teams; describe the ingenuity of new financial instruments that are now funding social enterprises; and finally describe the legal and regulatory reforms necessary to kickstart the next wave of innovation driven by solving social problems.
He invites young people, business and political leaders, and the general public to join the movement and work together to create the better, brighter world we all dream of.

title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
text:
Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.
It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.
Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.
Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.
In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.
For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.
In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.
More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.
If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.
But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.
According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.
Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.
Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".
Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.
At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.
Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.
In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.
Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.
The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.
The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.
The actual number may be more than that.
Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.
This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.
The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.
The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.
Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.
According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.
However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.
Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.
For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.
Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.
It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

title: California ’ s Clean Energy Dream: By 2030, 50% of total electricity will be generated from renewable sources
text:
By Anne Schukat (a freelance journalist who writes about science and technology for The Economist) Clean energy – California Dream ’ s global capacity to store electricity is very small compared to the capacity to produce electricity, but this will change in the coming decades.
California has taken on a mission to generate 50% of its total electricity from renewable sources by 2030.
As a result, three large investor-owned utilities in California must add 1.3 gigawatts (1.3 GW) of storage capacity to the grid by 2020.
Southern California Edison Corporation (SCE), one of the largest utilities that supplies electricity to 14 million residents of Los Angeles and the surrounding area, currently has 261 megawatts (261 MW) of stored energy.
AES Energy Storage, a subsidiary of U.S. independent power supply giant AES, is installing a 100-megawatt (100 MW) large lithium-ion battery system for its business that will provide up to four hours of power quickly and flexibly.
SCE is also working with Stem, a Silicon Valley-based smart grid software company that combines smart software with a modular, small lithium-ion battery storage system to reduce the company ’ s electricity costs and support the grid.
The goal is to install 85 megawatts (85 MW) of distributed storage for about 1,000 clients over a decade.
Ravi Manghani, a senior analyst in the energy storage sector at GTM ’ s industry research consultancy, points out that by 2020, most of the new energy storage equipment will be deployed on the demand side (i.e., the back end of the meter), not just in enterprises, but in households.
Christian Metzger, an energy storage specialist at RWE, Germany ’ s largest electricity supplier, made the same prediction.
He believes that in the next few decades, decentralized storage facilities will be spread throughout Germany, and the capacity will be large enough to meet the needs of the grid, so expensive large-scale storage projects will not be necessary.
After 2050, renewable energy can supply more than 80% of Germany's electricity, long-term energy storage equipment is necessary.
Navigant, a US market consultancy, pointed out that the world's new energy storage systems are dominated by lithium-ion batteries, accounting for more than 85% of the total energy storage capacity deployed in 2015.
Tesla, a California automaker that started with electric vehicles, is investing $5 billion in Nevada with battery supplier Panasonic to build a Gigafactory to meet the rising demand for its electric vehicles. In addition, it is also building modular energy storage systems called Powerwall and Powerpack for the needs of families and businesses.
Large manufacturers of lithium-ion batteries such as LG Chem and Samsung are also gradually increasing their productivity.
Through economies of scale, vertical integration and other efficiency measures, these companies should be able to significantly reduce the cost of battery packs.
According to Bloomberg New Energy Finance, the cost of battery pack power for electric vehicles, currently $350 per unit, should drop to less than $120 by 2030.
Without any subsidies, such a low price will create a situation where electric vehicles and conventional vehicles will compete. Bloomberg New Energy Finance reports that by 2040, 35% of global sales of new vehicles should be electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.
Once the share of renewable energy in the energy industry increases, the energy source of electric vehicles will gradually be replaced by clean energy.
In addition, electric car owners will also be able to output the power of the car battery to the grid, and pay a little less electricity.
The grid will become cleaner, more connected and more fragmented.
In the future, residential and commercial customers will not only be able to store energy in their own batteries, but will also be able to sell excess energy to other users.
Although renewable energy and related technologies will bring about drastic changes between now and 2050, other energy technologies will continue to evolve.
Like renewables, nuclear power can generate electricity without releasing greenhouse gases.
Nuclear fission is a nuclear reaction that refers to the splitting of a heavier nucleus like uranium into a lighter nucleus, producing energy in the process.
The first nuclear power plant began operation in the 1950s, and there are currently 445 nuclear reactors in the world, accounting for 11% of the world's electricity generation.
According to estimates by the International Energy Agency, the amount of nuclear power generated so far at the current rate of carbon dioxide emissions is equal to the amount of carbon dioxide emitted for nearly two years.
The 2011 earthquake in the Pacific Ocean off Tohoku, Japan, triggered a tsunami that severely damaged the Fukushima nuclear power plant. Although no one was killed in the radiation leak, the local government evacuated 150,000 residents.
The public is not only worried about more accidents in the future, but also worried about the treatment of radioactive waste, so the construction of new nuclear power plants is difficult, especially in Western democracies.
Sixty-three nuclear reactors are currently under construction in China, India and Russia, which have fewer laws and regulations and are therefore less expensive to build.
Nearly 200 nuclear reactors facing an aging crisis, mostly located in the United States, Europe, Russia, and Japan, should be retired in a dozen years.
Therefore, the International Energy Agency estimates that the share of nuclear power generation in the total global electricity generation will only increase, and may not increase.
Another form of nuclear power generation is nuclear fusion, which may provide a safer, near-infinite amount of energy without the generation of radioactive nuclear waste or the threat of core meltdown.
Nuclear fusion is the main source of energy for the Sun and stars to glow and heat. It is when two very light nuclei (such as hydrogen) are collided in an extremely high temperature and pressure environment, creating a heavier atom (such as helium) and releasing huge amounts of energy in the process.
Since the 1950s, nuclear powers have poured billions of dollars into fusion technology, and scientists at the time predicted that a nuclear fusion reactor could be built within two decades.
But replicating fusion reactions on Earth is even more difficult than originally expected, and the prediction at that time has become a joke for many years, and the target completion date will always be 20 or 30 years from now.
At present, the world's largest and most ambitious international joint venture project, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER, Latin for "road"), has also been stalled recently.
Originally based in France, this large reactor is expected to be launched in 2016, but the budget has exceeded the target by several billion yuan, the progress is also several years behind, according to the current situation, it will be almost ten years before it is possible to officially operate.
Scientists in this field have high hopes for ITER, despite the difficulty of achieving their goals.
To achieve nuclear fusion, it is necessary to build a reactor that produces several times more energy than it consumes.
It ’ s just that there ’ s still a long way to go.
According to the 1997 world record, nuclear fusion produced 16 megawatts (16 MW) of electricity, but imported 24 megawatts (24 MW) of electricity.
Some private companies are also starting to invest in nuclear fusion projects, and they believe they can achieve their goals faster and at lower cost.
Each company offers a different solution to the most basic problem: how to control and maintain fuel particles (plasma) at extremely high temperatures to facilitate nuclear fusion reactions.
California ’ s TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) has attracted hundreds of millions of dollars in funding, as has Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen.
Their plan is to surround the plasma with high-energy particle beams in extremely hot environments.
Other companies have also received funding from well-known investors, such as General Fusion in Canada, which has won the favor of Amazon CEO Bezos, and Helion Energy near Seattle, which has won the support of PayPal co-founder Tyre.
General Fusion uses piston devices to compress and heat fuel particles, while Helium Nuclear Energy uses pulsed magnetic fields.
What these companies have in common is that they all believe nuclear fusion can be achieved in five to ten years.
But some experts don ’ t think so.
Steven Cowley, director of the Corning Nuclear Fusion Centre (CCFE) in the UK, said: “Calling out such a slogan will only discredit us.
He believes it will take 30 or 40 years for commercial fusion reactors to become a reality.

title: Master Think Tank Forum / Macaw: Promoting a Green Economy to Fight the Threat of Warming
text:
Master Think Tank Forum / Macaw: Pushing the Green Economy to Fight the Threat of Warming 2018-05-19 01: 09 Economic Daily reporter Jiang Ruizhi / Taipei Report Bruce A. McCarl, Chair Professor at Texas Agricultural University and an important member of the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize winning organization IPCC in the economic field, said that climate change is like an unstoppable bulldozer and has profound effects on global food production.
Bruce A. McCarl, a professor at Texas Agricultural University and an important member of the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize winning organization in the field of economics, said yesterday (18) that the past four consecutive years have been the hottest four years on record in the world, and climate change has had a profound impact on global food production, resulting in reduced production and rising prices.
Civil society and government must pay high attention to this phenomenon and work together to adapt to the effects of climate change.

Ma Kao made the above remarks when delivering a keynote speech on “The Impact of Climate Change on the Food Crisis and the Regional Economy. ”
He pointed out that around 1880, the global temperature increased by 0.7 degrees Celsius every 10 years, but since the 21st century, the rate of warming has accelerated; although the total rainfall has not changed, but seriously uneven, whether it is a rainstorm or a major drought, now the probability of major floods and droughts is greater than in history, the United States government has an extreme climate index, will be extremely hot, heavy rain, drought, the index has been rising.
Macaw said that climate change has a profound impact on agriculture.
Reduced water supply, affecting agricultural farming.
Sea level rise, which has risen by 82 millimetres since 1990, has flooded farmland and led to the loss of farmland.
Rising temperatures not only affect crop growth, but also cause an increase in pest and disease.
In the United States, where 15% of the land was arid before 1980, 30% today, this has serious implications for food security.

title: An absent director at the Cannes Film Festival.
text:
May 23, 2018 04: 10 China Times News The Cannes Film Festival is not only the temple of film art in the minds of many people; the strength of market transactions and media effects can not be underestimated.
Therefore, Fei thought to set foot on this red carpet, there are both hard-working creators, and there are artists and strangers who do not use their desperate layout, immersed in the spotlight, mixed with applause and shouts.
No matter what the purpose, the city of Cannes should be crowded; but there are still people who are absent.
For example, Jean-Luc Godard, the French New Wave master who asked about the Golden Palm eight times in The Image Book, did not attend the premiere.
The elderly people are old and well-behaved, and it is no wonder that everyone has already seen them.
Half a century ago, Gundam was one of the leading figures to shut down Cannes in the May storm, but the two comics have been back for a long time, and this year ’ s poster was based on his “Pierrot le Fou ” (1965). Although he was not expected to attend the premiere, Gundam was at least videoed at the press conference.
Still avant-garde at the age of 90, his new work is like more than 80 minutes of self-talk, with arguments about reproducing and interpreting images, as well as discussions about morality, law, language, race, and war.
But what is even more interesting is that when some viewers think that the film is over and applaud without thinking about it, they realize that there is still a large segment behind it, and this embarrassment is also quite “high ”.
But the others did not come, but they did not want to come.
One of them was Russian director Kirill Serebrennikov.
His previous work, The Student (2016), gave a startling portrayal of the insane horrors of religious extremism, which sparked heated debate in the “one eye ” section of Cannes and caused him some trouble in Russia.
The Russian government placed him under house arrest for illegal embezzlement of public funds, and stressed that the arrest had nothing to do with the content of his creation.
His short film “Summer ” depicts the rise of Russian rock and punk among youth in the early 1980s, with a special focus on how Korean-born singer-songwriter Viktor Tsoi was influenced by idol Mike and his beautiful wife Natacha, who naturally stood against conservatives.
The seats deliberately set aside at the press conference, and the famous article held high at the premiere, all explained the fact that they were not present.
The political persecution of Iranian director Jafar Panahi is well known in the film industry. In 2010, he was suddenly arrested at home and released on bail until he went on hunger strike, but at the end of the same year a Tehran court sentenced him to six years in prison and up to 20 years without being allowed to film, go abroad or be interviewed for “conspiring to threaten national security and spread subversive speech. ”
Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Oliver Stone and Abbas Kiarostami, Panahi ’ s master, have spoken out in support of him, and Juliette Binoch has revealed the name “Jafar Panahi ” when she picked up the Cannes film. Man.
Even under house arrest by the Iranian government, Jaffa Panahi tried his best to film.
Early fame, his debut film The White Balloon (1995) won the Golden Camera Award for Best New Director in Cannes, and later won the Golden Lion Award at the Venice Film Festival and the Golden Bear Award at the Berlin Palms Film Festival for “The Circle of Life ” (2000) and“ Taxi, ” (2015). It became the subject of Cannes.
His “Three Faces ” depicts a well-known actress receiving a shocking video of a young girl who can ’ t help but decide to live.
Unperturbed, she is not sure if this is a prank or a secret book, and implores director Jafar Panahi to accompany her to clarify.
The two original gods appeared to play themselves, allowing the film to permeate the texture of the fake documentary.
It also reveals that even in modern times, some places and people still feel like a disgrace to women, and even threaten them.
Some are obedient, some are rebellious, and there is a price to pay.
The rescuers and pursuers in the film, as well as the invisible women who extend from them, structure this state of effort and powerlessness.
People can't get to the scene, the film can still sound strong.
(China Times)

title: Global Warming Threatens Livelihood: Threatening Rice Nutrient Loss
text:
"We found that global warming, climate change, and especially the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide, affect the nutritional content of the plants we eat," said study co-author Adam Drewnowski, a professor of epidemiology at the University of Washington.
According to the report, published in the journal Science Advances, the change has a particularly severe impact on Southeast Asia, where rice is a staple food.
WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Rice will lose some of its protein and vitamin content, putting millions of people at risk of malnutrition, scientists warned today, as carbon dioxide emissions from burning fossil fuels increase.
“This will have a devastating impact on countries where rice is a staple food.
About 70% of the calories and most of the nutrients in these countries come from rice. "
Lack of protein and vitamins can lead to developmental delays, birth defects, diarrhea, infection, and death.
The countries most at risk include those with the highest rice consumption and the lowest gross domestic product (GDP), such as Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia, Drunowski said.
Based on field surveys in Japan and China, the study simulated atmospheric CO2 concentrations in the second half of the century, estimated at 568 to 590 ppm.
It is currently over 400 ppm.
In the experiment, 18 different varieties of rice were planted in open fields, which were surrounded by a 17-meter-wide octagonal plastic tube, releasing extra carbon dioxide.
The researchers found that growing in an environment with high carbon dioxide levels reduced the amount of iron, zinc, protein and vitamins B1, B2, B5 and B9 in the rice. These nutrients help the body convert food into energy.
Compared to the current carbon dioxide environment, protein content decreased by an average of 10.3%, iron decreased by 8%, and zinc decreased by 5.1%.
Vitamin B6 and calcium were not affected, and vitamin E increased in most varieties.
Studies have shown that carbon dioxide levels affect plant structure and growth, increase carbohydrate content, and reduce protein and mineral content.
The higher the concentration of carbon dioxide means less exposure to nitrogen, which also affects vitamin content, the researchers said.

title: Studying or eating? Japanese ship goes to Antarctica to hunt 122 pregnant whales
text:
June 01, 2018 10: 01 China Times E-News Li Jingtang According to the British Independent, Japan has once again become the target of international criticism for its "scientific research" whale-hunting mission, and the Nisshin Maru in the Antarctic Sea has been accused by the International Whaling Commission (IWC) of not only using explosives to hunt whales cruelly. In addition, 122 pregnant whales and 114 baby whales were captured and slaughtered. After the so-called scientific research, these whales were sold to restaurants and shops and became a delicious dish for many gourmets.
From November last year, the Nihsin Maru spent several weeks tracking Minke whales in the Antarctic waters, and within 12 weeks completed the capture operation, returning to Japan in March this year.
The IWC found in its report that the team captured and killed a total of 333 minke whales in the Southern Ocean, of which 152 were male and 181 were female; 122 were killed during pregnancy; and 114 were hunted, shocking the international community and conservation groups.
The humpback whale is a huge marine creature. (Photo / Associated Press) In order to reap the rich and expensive economic benefits of whales, humans have hunted in large numbers in the world's oceans, causing the number of large whales of all kinds to plummet to a dangerous level.
In order to protect them and maintain the ecological balance of the sea, the international community formed the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after many negotiations, and in 1986 passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Whaling, which banned commercial whaling, but Japan, Norway, South Korea, Peru, Brazil, China and other countries voted against it.
Among them, Canada completely withdrew in 1982, and Japan, which has a tradition of eating whale meat, has become the main target of environmental groups every year with Norway.
Although the International Court of Justice ordered Japan to ban whale hunting in 2014, Japanese officials continue to hunt whales on ships in the name of traditional customs and scientific research.
In April last year, the Nihsin Maru just completed its “research mission ” and brought back 330 hunted whales from the Antarctic waters.
But Japan, which has become increasingly sophisticated in its whaling technology, has fewer groups to contend with. Even the Australian group Sea Shepherd, which has blocked whaling missions for years, announced in August that it was abandoning the confrontation, threatening to make Japan ’ s future whaling operations even more unscrupulous.
Alexia Wellbelove, a long-time expert on whale conservation and conservation, lamented this move and the reason, “This is evidence of Japan ’ s brutal hunting and killing of whales! ”
He called on Australia and other countries to protest and condemn Japan, but Japan has always insisted that whaling and practical whales are one of the cultural characteristics of the country, and unless there is a more mandatory decision, this kind of whaling "scientific mission" will continue.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: Global warming of 4 ° C will affect vegetable and drought-tolerant crop yields
text:
(Taiwan English News / Lin Jingyi) Global warming is becoming more serious, causing sea level rise, the speed of ice melting in the north and south poles, and land drought due to high temperature and no rain. The latest research report released by the British and American international research team on the 11th pointed out that if global temperature rises by 4 ° C, it will affect the harvest of vegetables grown by humans and crops that can adapt to high temperature.
Alan Dangour, of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, says this is the first time 174 studies have been compiled on the impact of climate anomalies on the quality of crops, vegetables and legumes.
He said that if humanity continues to ignore it, the abnormal climate will affect the harvest of important food crops around the world.
An international team of researchers from the United Kingdom and the United States collected a total of 174 research papers from 1975, analyzing the impact of farming environment, vegetable nutrients and legume crops. Based on the current rate of temperature increase, it is estimated that if global temperature rises by 4 ° C by 2100, the average crop will be reduced by 31.5%. The new research report was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) on the 11th.
The report also pointed out that as long as the increase in heat and water resources will cause a one-third of the world's vegetable harvest to be reduced, and this impact will affect southern Europe, Africa and South Asia.
The study also looked at “corn, ” which is widely grown around the world, which has an“ 86% chance of a 4 ° C temperature rise, making the world ’ s top four exporters, such as the United States, Brazil, Argentina and Ukraine, feel the worst year of harvests. ”
Alan Dangour stressed that urgent action, including support for food crops that are resistant to and resilient to high temperatures, must be a priority for governments around the world.

title: Japan to seek partial recovery of commercial whaling
text:
The following content is from our partners, so we cannot guarantee that it will be displayed properly.
TOKYO, June 27, 2018 (AFP) Japan will seek a partial resumption of commercial whaling later this year at a meeting of the International Whaling Commission (IWC), officials said today.
Tokyo, which often seeks an easing of the IWC ’ s ban on commercial whaling, continues to hunt whales in defiance of international criticism as part of what he calls a “scientific research ” program.
Hideki Moronuki, head of whaling at the Japan Fisheries Agency, told AFP that at a meeting to be held in Brazil in September, “there will be a proposal to set a hunting quota for whale species identified by the IWC Scientific Committee as having a significant population. ”
He said the proposal would not specify what species of whales Japan would like to hunt.
But he said the IWC classified several whale species as no longer depleted.
A ban on commercial whaling began in 1986, and Japan's previous attempts to partially lift the ban have failed.
Japan will also propose measures to change the decision-making process of the IWC, reducing the threshold for proposals from three-quarters of the membership to half.

title: Herbicide Cancer-Caused Judgment May Change Bayer Stock Price Rises
text:
(Getty Images) Share Facebook Shares of Bayer rose after a federal appeals court ruled that Monsanto ’ s Roundup herbicide cause cancer should be overturned.
In a summary filed with the San Francisco Court of Appeals on Tuesday, the EPA said it had reviewed and approved the warning label for the weed control product and that a jury ruling based on California law should be rescinded.
The Justice Department and EPA jointly considered the federal jury's decision.
A federal magistrate this summer cut the amount awarded to a man claiming to have non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma after years of using Roundup to $25 million, but refused to overturn a jury ’ s finding that Roundup was flawed because its label did not contain a carcinogenic warning and Monsanto insisted Roundup was safe.
Roundup contains glyphosate, which is being tested by courts and American families over concerns about its safety.
Testing by environmental groups has added to consumer concerns, such as a study that found that 21 oat cereal and snack products contain trace amounts of glyphosate.
Glyphosate is the most widely used herbicide in U.S. agriculture, and farmers spray it on golf courses and on the lawns of homes to kill weeds.
The EPA said in May that it “continues to find that using glyphosate in accordance with the current labeling instructions is not harmful to public health and that glyphosate is not a carcinogen. ” But environmentalists and other advocates oppose the decision.
Four years after the World Health Organization deemed glyphosate “possibly a human carcinogen, ” the EPA made the decision.
Bayer acquired Monsanto for about $63 billion in 2018 and has taken on tens of thousands of lawsuits related to Roundup, and has lost three of them.
Bayer appealed the decision, but this month said it agreed to delay two lawsuits pending federal approval of a possible settlement.
In an email, Bayer said it was “encouraged ” by the choice of the U.S. government and others to provide legal advice in support of the company ’ s appeal.
In addition, Bayer also received Wall Street support, and its stock price rose to a 14-month high of 73.93 yuan, an increase of 3.5%.
