title: "The Great Gatsby": Spring heart without flowers, one inch of love, one inch of gray time code word committee film
text:
When "The Great Gatsby" director Baz Luhrmann chose to present the film in 3D, it may be doomed to the film's interpretation and possible repercussions.
Luhrmann is good at depicting love and loves to be strong and gorgeous, which was played in The Great Gatsby, and even his wife won two Golden Men for Best Costume Design and Best Art Direction.
But in fact, it also stops here. Behind the dazzling, lavish scenes, the essence of the original is almost impossible to reflect, and even the "love" as the focus is shallow. The box office of 350 million seems to be a lot, can be counted as a cost and publicity, and finally I am afraid it is a small loss.
It is no wonder that before pulling to Xiao Li, Warner did not look at this version of the adaptation at all.
To be sure, Baz Ruman ’ s desire to find another way is understandable, after all, the original novel has been on the big screen four times since its birth, and it is difficult to make new breakthroughs.
However, it is a pity that the director threw the whole watermelon aside while meticulously carving a sesame seed.
What is Fitzgerald's dissecting confusion and loneliness? Why is The Great Gatsby called the commanding heights of American literature?
What's so great about Gatsby? At least I can't find it in this movie.
The greatness of the original work need not be said, can be called a masterpiece of the era by Hemingway, can be Murakami Haruki as the benchmark of his literary creation, has explained everything, Francis Scott Fitzgerald has become the top figure in the American literary world with this work.
In a smaller dimension, The Great Gatsby tells the story of a man ’ s dream breaking a little bit.
In the larger dimension, Fitzgerald analyzed and criticized an era, which has far-reaching practical significance.
It is set in the 1920s, exactly the decade between 1919, after World War I, and 1929, before the Great Depression.
During this decade, the United States made a huge war fortune as a result of World War I, turning from a pre-war debtor to a creditor.
The government ’ s laissez-faire economic policies allowed capitalism to flourish, creating the miraculous “Coolidge Prosperity Era. ”
The good economic situation has led to the rapid growth of a large number of emerging industries, countless speculators overnight rich, hedonism, Spencer's social Darwinism, James's pragmatic philosophy, people began to blindly make money, the amount of wealth has become the only criterion for judging a person's success or not.
This period is called the “tumultuous twenties, ” and Fitzgerald summed it up as“ the age of wonder, the age of art, the age of distress, the age of satire. ”
As a writer, the author has a deep understanding.
In the early 1920s, Fitzgerald, a famous writer, earned a lot of money, and the couple indulged in fun and spendthrift, but in the later period, he was addicted to alcohol, his wife was schizophrenic, and the luxury of life brought a heavy burden.
After the Great Depression, the golden age of Fitzgerald also passed away, and the vices of alcoholism and drafts, coupled with the untimely writing style, caused many magazines and newspapers to stop writing to him, until he died of a heart attack in 1940.
The Great Gatsby was written in 1925, at a time when Fitzgerald ’ s life and career had turned from strength to strength.
Like most of his novels, this work is based on his own real life, immersed in his personal emotional experience of life, as well as his critique of human, social and epochal thinking.
The characters "Nick" and "Gatsby" in the story have more or less the shadow of the author himself.
Especially as a participant and narrator of the story, Nick ’ s origins, his values, his initial pursuit of the “American Dream ”, and finally his loathing of people ’ s humility are almost all in line with Fitzgerald ’ s experience.
The novel's first protagonist, Gatsby, inherits Fitzgerald's other experiences of life's ups and downs.
Like the author, Gatsby's limited life is both brilliant and sad, but the difference is that Gatsby's origins are much poorer and lower.
As a result, he grew up with a dream of one day getting ahead, and after enlisting in the army, he met Miss Rich Daisy. When war broke out, a lover was forced to separate, and by the time Gatsby returned to the United States, Daisy had already married someone else.
In order to regain his sweetheart, he made a huge fortune through the bootlegging business, and bought a mansion near Daisy's house to feast and celebrate every day and night, just to attract Daisy's attention.
With all the myths surrounding Gatsby and Nick's help, he's finally waiting for Daisy.
So, the two of them talk to each other, old feelings rekindled.
Although Daisy becomes Gatsby's mistress, she can never be his wife, she only treats their affair as a thrill. Daisy accidentally kills her husband's mistress in a car accident.
In order to protect him, Gatsby took the initiative to take the blame, and by this time Daisy had decided to abandon Gatsby.
At the instigation of Daisy's husband, Tom Buchanan, his mistress's husband shot and killed Gatsby.
At the time of the funeral, Daisy chose to travel to Europe with her husband.
From the caravan to the sparrow, the prosperity that painstakingly got left him, leaving only indifference and loneliness.
What is so great about Gatsby, then? His greatness lies in his belief in his dreams for the rest of his life.
As Nick said, Gatsby is the most promising person he has ever met in New York, and he has boundless hope of clinging to his dreams.
Although he told some big lies in order to create his identity, he also engaged in illegal activities in order to accumulate wealth.
But to his friends, he was sincere and kind, to love, he was faithful and romantic.
He worked hard to build golden palaces and lively parties, but he was practically uninterested in all the hubbub of pleasure.
It can be said that Gatsby has a sincere soul, especially in the selfish and filthy crowd, his pure romance has become more and more noble.
But in those days, Gatsby ’ s pure sincerity also meant naivety.
First, he failed to recognize the huge gulf between the classes.
Although he was superficially integrated into the upper class society, but he represented the bottom of the upstart family, has always had a natural sense of inferiority, for the life of the upper class, appearance, behavior has always been based on imitation, in Daisy's husband Buchanan as the representative of the family has always set boundaries with them.
Therefore, Gatsby will never be his opponent compared to Buchanan, who is sophisticated, selfish, arbitrary, and unscrupulous, who can abandon moral principles for profit.
Second, Gatsby took the love he sought, wishfully, as the whole world.
Of course, in a way, this is right, but the most fatal thing is that he mistakenly sees Daisy as the embodiment of love and happiness. Daisy is a typical upper-class figure who is vain and selfish and ruthless.
She initially chose to marry Buchanan because she was attracted to each other's status and wealth, and when she met Gatsby again, although there was a certain "old love" factor, but the most important thing was that Gatsby also had no less wealth than Buchanan.
However, when she learned that Gatsby may have been involved in illegal trade, her attitude changed.
Until he got into a car accident, Gatsby acted as a scapegoat with peace of mind, even indifferent to his death and funeral, its cold and hypocrisy can be seen.
Was Gatsby unaware of such a woman?
The film is very ambiguous about this.
But in the novel, Gatsby utters a heart-wrenching remark: "There is a smell of money in her voice." It can be seen in his heart that Daisy loves vanity, not him.
Li Shangyin has a poem cloud: "Sa the east wind drizzle, there is a light thunder outside Furong Tong."
The golden frog robs the incense to burn, the jade tiger leads the silk back. Jia 's prying curtains Han Yuan less, Mi Fei Liu pillow Wei Wang Cai.
"The heart of spring is full of flowers, and the heart of spring is full of flowers, and the heart of spring is full of love, and the heart of spring is full of love, and the heart of spring is full of ashes."
In addition to the above two points, the more important point is that the "American dream" that Gatsby pursued and fought for is itself false.
Fitzgerald had seen that when money was everything, the idealistic elements of the American dream no longer existed.
If a dream, only the pursuit of material and the desire for fame and fortune, but lack of thinking about why to have wealth and how to survive after having wealth, such a dream is ultimately a mirage.
Because no society can rely only on a high level of material life to maintain people's meaning and interests for a long time, human beings want to live a spiritual life, and only spiritual life has unlimited space for rich development.
The dream is broken and there is no way out, creating a "lost generation" represented by Fitzgerald and Hemingway.
In fact, their confusion is also our confusion.
The American drama of the "tumultuous twenties" also played out after the war in Japan, and now it is our turn.
The current China and the era in the novel how similar, many people in the pursuit of "XX dream" at the same time fell into a strange circle - the material enjoyment as the goal of life, but also no longer believe in dreams.
What is hidden by the values of hedonism and consumerism is a spiritual desert, and various and endless ugly phenomena.
The World Cup, which ended last month, has the most ready examples.
Our neighbor, Japan, has successfully achieved the goal of advancing to the top 16 in the group, and the word "dream" has been highlighted before the Japanese team's recent participation in the tournament.
Strength is important, but when the players step onto the court with the determination to win and the belief to pursue their dreams, everything is likely to make them forget the huge gap in strength.
In fact, in Japan, in the field of football alone, the Football Association organizes dozens of games, large and small, in addition to professional teams, from elementary school students to the elderly.
In other words, as long as you have a football dream and are willing to act for your dream, then anyone can qualify for the green.
Under the influence of such an environment, countless young people who love football dream of participating in training and competitions.
"I think it's a good idea for us to play in Europe and the United States," he said.
On the contrary, our players have long lost the motivation to go abroad and pursue higher level ball skills in the face of the rich salary in China, and play health ball in the country with ease.
Even more, a large number of young players see going abroad as an opportunity to turn their money into domestic sales.
In my opinion, football is just a career.
In The Great Gatsby, Gatsby is the only person who has not been assimilated by matter, the only person who has flesh and blood, and the only person who is sentimental in that crazy and flashy age.
I dare not say that such people are our example, but I still hope that everyone can retain a little bit of innocence in this era.
“There ’ s something inside me, it ’ s hard to explain. ”

title: Billed as a "drinkable herbicide" may actually cause cancer, Monsanto was awarded nearly 9 billion US dollars for "annual spring"
text:
A San Francisco jury ruled yesterday (10) that Monsanto failed to warn a cancer worker that its herbicide, Roundup, is causing cancer. Monsanto said it would continue to appeal, but the ruling ruled. It may just be the first shot in a series of lawsuits.
A 46-year-old California man, Dewayne Johnson, a school herb administrator, has sued Monsanto for causing his cancer with its weed products in the spring without warning.
The jury ruled yesterday that Johnson ’ s cancer was “largely ” attributable to the company ’ s herbicide, the“ spring of the year ”, and that the company should have warned the product on the label of possible health risks.
Johnson, who worked as a school gardener in San Francisco for many years, used "spring" and another professional herbicide, "Ranger Pro," and sprayed a large amount of pesticide in a strong wind to spread the pesticide all over his body, Johnson's lawyers said.
On another occasion, the pipe ruptured, causing the pesticide to penetrate his entire skin.
Johnson contacted a Monsanto employee with a rash, but was not told he was likely to have cancer.
Johnson was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma in April 2014.
Johnson, a 46-year-old father of three who has worked as a school gardener since 2012, said he spent several hours a day spraying herbicides on the school grounds to control weeds, and that exposure to the chemicals caused him to develop cancer. According to doctors, Johnson may only have a few months to live.
“I ’ ve been through a lot of pain, ” Johnson said, adding that Monsanto shouldn ’ t have let him use herbicides near school children.“ If I knew it was going to hurt them, I would never have sprayed that product on or around school. ”
Monsanto lawyers stressed that non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma develops for several years, believing that Johnson had developed the disease well before the use of “spring ”.
Monsanto also stressed that multiple scientific studies have confirmed that “spring ” is harmless to humans and meets U.S. government standards.
Monsanto Vice President Scott Partridge also claimed that the herb did not cause cancer and did not cause Johnson ’ s cancer. “We sympathize with Mr. Johnson and his family, ” said Partridge, but he said that with a 40-year history of safe use this spring, Monsanto will continue to appeal to defend the product as an important, effective and safe tool for farmers and others.
# Monsanto ordered to pay $289Million in # Roundup weed killer cancer case: https: / / t.co / cKt5DF1E3i pic.twitter.com / X8IVgLPe7V — Lisa McGonagle (@ Lisamcgonagle) August 11, 2018 If Monsanto loses the case, it will open the door to hundreds of other lawsuits. According to Johnson & Johnson ’ s team of lawyers, Monsanto faces more than 4,000 similar cases in the United States, and the next judicial case will be tried in October in Monsanto ’ s hometown of St. Louis, Missouri.
“This case is bigger than my personal experience, ” Johnson said at a press conference in the attorney ’ s office after the verdict.“ I hope it gets the attention it needs. ”
Johnson & Johnson ’ s lawyer, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., said the jury found Monsanto ’ s actions to be full of “malice ” and“ oppression, ” “because they knew what they were doing was wrong and they were reckless about human life. ” He said the verdict should send a strong signal to the Monsanto board.
Monsanto has long argued that the spring is safe and has nothing to do with cancer, and Monsanto has also filed research in the lawsuit against the research and testimony submitted by the team of lawyers.
The herbicide has been registered in 130 countries and is allowed to be used on more than 100 crops, but in 2015, the World Health Organization ’ s International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classified the ingredient Glyphosate as “possibly carcinogenic to humans, ” sparking a wave of legal legislative challenges.
California, USA In 2017, legislation required that the product must be labeled on the packaging when it is sold in California every spring to remind users of the carcinogenic risk of the product.
The European Commission is also under pressure to ban products containing glyphosate by 2022.
In 2015, American farmer Jack McCall died of non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma, and her wife filed a complaint with Monsanto.
“At least it needs to have a warning label so people can make informed decisions, ” she said, adding that her husband felt it was safe and had used thousands of gallons for 40 years. McCaul had no habit of smoking or drinking, exercised regularly and had no family history of cancer, and McCaul ’ s dog had died of the same type of cancer.
The most used herbicide in Taiwan, the Bureau of Defense and Inspection: not to cause food problems in the spring of 1974, will not ban the "upstream and downstream" report, Monsanto launched in the spring of 1974, claiming that it is "a herbicide that can be drunk", relying on low-acute toxicity publicity to open the market.
After the introduction of GM seeds that are resistant to glyphosate (one of the active ingredients in spring) in 1994 (which means that farmers can kill weeds without harming their crops), the drug became the unwithered flower on the market in spring.
Glyphosate is easy to use, high in efficacy and low in price. Glyphosate is also popular in the European Union, where it is banned from planting GM crops. It is also used not only in fields, but also to clean weeds in yards, parks and roads.
The report pointed out that if glyphosate is banned because of carcinogenic concerns, it is equivalent to cutting off the life of the genetically modified seeds sold with it. (Monsanto is a multinational agricultural biotechnology company in the United States, and is the main producer of GM seeds worldwide, more than 70% of the world's GM seeds are derived from Monsanto).
The United Daily News reported that Monsanto ’ s herbicide “Annual Spring ” is the largest amount of non-selective herbicides in Taiwan, accounting for half of all herbicides, and the other two“ killer ” herbicides are herbicides and barra mowing.
Feng Haidong, director of the Bureau of Prevention and Inspection of the Council of Agriculture, said that last year, it has been announced that barra mowing will be banned from February next year, and the global supply of fixed weeds has risen in recent years so that the price will fall.
Feng Haidong said that the California incident was a judicial decision, not a scientific argument, and that the subject was a long-term drug worker, and the exposure was completely different from that of the average consumer.
There are still differences of opinion in China on whether the spring is carcinogenic, the spring is a herbicide, will not be used in fruits and vegetables and other general crops, does not cause food safety problems, but in the future will review the exposure of occupational users is appropriate.

title: Herbicide May Cause Cancer Monsanto to Pay $9 Billion
text:
August 12, 2018 04: 10 China Times Chen Wenhe / Roundup / Roundup, a multinational agrochemical and biotech company, has awarded Johnson nearly US $290 million (about US $290 million) in damages after a jury of the California Superior Court of San Francisco ruled on the 10th that a multinational agrochemical and biotech company, Monsanto, containing carcinogens, caused the death of a sports field administrator. $898 million).
The case marks a milestone for more than 800 similar lawsuits.
Monsanto has said it will appeal.
Monsanto insists it will not cause cancer. Dewayne Johnson, 46, has non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and is now in the final stages of cancer.
He used herbicides 20 to 30 times a year during his time as a stadium administrator.
He testified that he had been soaked in herbicide twice during his work, the first time in 2012, two years after he was diagnosed with malignant non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
Johnson and his wife have two sons, and their wife now works two 40-hour workweeks to support the family.
In court, Johnson made emotional statements about how he told his son that he was a terminal cancer patient and that he feared he would die soon.
After eight weeks of trial, the jury unanimously found that Monsanto failed to properly warn consumers about the possibility of cancer in spring, acted “maliciously ” or deliberately concealed the truth, and that Johnson ’ s cancer was“ largely ” attributable to “spring ” and“ Ranger Pro, ” another professional herbicide produced by Monsanto, and therefore ruled that Monsanto should pay $250 million in punitive damages. Including other damages and expenses of nearly US $0.4 billion, the total amount is about US $290 million.
It is the most widely used herbicide in the world. It contains Glyphosate, a major ingredient listed by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) of the World Health Organization as a Category 2A substance “likely to be carcinogenic to humans ”.
However, some scientists believe that spring is safe to use.
The biggest problem is not glyphosate, but that glyphosate will interact with other ingredients in the spring, creating a "synergistic effect" that makes the spring more carcinogenic, according to Johnson & Johnson ’ s lawyer.
He added that the jury ’ s decision will allow the public and government agencies to further examine the need for a ban.
A similar lawsuit threatens thousands of Monsanto ’ s recent acquisition by the German chemical and pharmaceutical company Bayer.
In a statement released after the sentencing, Monsanto insisted that research showed it did not cause cancer in the spring. “The jury got it wrong, ” Scott Partridge, Monsanto ’ s vice president, told reporters outside the court.
Johnson & Johnson ’ s lawyer, Lee Senberg, said Monsanto ’ s appeal would be costly because the company would have to pay interest on damages during the appeal, amounting to about $25 million a year.
This is the first time a cancer related lawsuit has been heard in the United States.
Observers point out that Johnson ’ s case will serve as a precedent for more than 800 similar lawsuits currently pending in the United States.
The loss of Monsanto will prompt more people to file charges against Monsanto, and it is expected that the number of similar lawsuits may reach thousands.
(China Times)

title: Euronext Stoxx 600 hits 3-week low amid fears of Turkish financial crisis
text:
The Turkish lira fell, investors worried that the situation may further deteriorate into a financial crisis; this (13) morning European shares, the main index fell, the pan-European Stoxx 600 index hit a three-week low.
At 5: 34 p.m. on Monday, Taipei time, CNBC data showed that the pan-European Stoxx 600 index fell 0.40%, the German DAX index fell 0.57%, the French CAC 40 index fell 0.29%, and the British FTSE index fell 0.53%.
On Monday morning, the pan-European Stoxx 600 index fell, and healthcare stocks performed the worst.
Agrochemical maker Monsanto has been awarded $290 million in damages by a court for failing to label its herbicide Roundup as potentially carcinogenic, a news that sent the shares of Bayer, the German pharmaceutical company that recently acquired Monsanto, down more than 10 percent.
Shares of Air France-KLM fell nearly 4% due to the strike.
Since August, the United States has imposed economic sanctions on two Turkish officials and re-examined the tax exemption measures on Turkish imports, causing the lira to collapse.
U.S. President Donald Trump last week ordered a doubling of tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from Turkey, aggravating the decline of the lira against the dollar; but Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan did not want to be weak and said that Turkey will not lose in this economic war.
Markets are worried that Turkey could trigger a financial crisis, and Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has warned of a repeat of the Asian financial crisis if Turkey fails to respond properly.

With black and white as the main color, the seats and devices are designed to be simple and stylish, like the Tesla that makes a flying ship a flying version.
SpaceX Dragon V2 | Flight Animation has always cherished the dream of space exploration Musk, its SPACE X company in cooperation with the United States Space Agency (NASA) to launch a commercial version of the space program, after a number of trials and adjustments, on the 3rd of this month announced the list of nine astronauts who will fly on the Dragon spacecraft to work at the International Space Station (International Space Station).
The launch will be powered by its own Falcon Heavy rocket; SPACE X is expected to conduct unmanned tests on the spacecraft by the end of this year and human trials around April next year.

It can be confirmed that the manned test flight in April next year will be conducted by two veteran astronauts: Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley, who will be the final check before the Dragon launches into operation.

title: SpaceX unveils crewed spacecraft that could send astronauts into space next year
text:
SpaceX public display manned spacecraft next year is expected to send astronauts into space (original title: SpaceX readies its spacecraft and astronauts for crewed missions) technology media network NetEase technology news August 16 news, according to Engadget reported, the United States SpaceX's first task is to put humans into space, and eventually send humans to Mars.
At present, the rocket launching company needs to work on sending astronauts to the International Space Station.
To that end, it recently demonstrated parts of the hardware and astronauts that carry out this historic mission.
The last U.S. manned space mission, STS-135, was launched from Kennedy Space Center in 2011.
Since then, American astronauts have been traveling to the space station aboard Russian rockets.
Meanwhile, SpaceX, Boeing and NASA are implementing the Commercial Crew Program to revive the U.S. manned flight industry.
While the project ’ s name sounds prosaic, it has excited not only NASA, but also the four astronauts who are testing (and will eventually board) SpaceX ’ s Dragon spacecraft.
To achieve this, SpaceX has spent years working closely with NASA and astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to help get everything ready.
Over the past three years, these seasoned astronauts have shared their expertise with SpaceX, from putting buttons where the spacecraft is, to making chairs that are best suited to escape velocity (the speed needed to escape gravity), to constantly improving the design of stylish spacesuits.
Both Ben and Hurley had two space shuttle flights, and Hurley even participated in the last space launch of the space shuttle in the United States.
They and astronauts Victor Glover and Michael Hopkins plan to participate in a manned launch (Demo-2) in April 2019. SpaceX also plans to conduct an unmanned test flight (Demo-1) in November this year.
There ’ s a lot to do before those two dates, but before launch, SpaceX wants to show it ’ s ready.
SpaceX has invited the media to visit and learn about its Dragon Crew spacecraft and talk to astronauts and managers.
The ship itself was the biggest surprise.
If you ’ ve seen photos of the interior of the space shuttle, you probably remember plenty of gauges, knobs, levers, and lights.
It ’ s a lot like the cockpit of a commercial airline flight, but there ’ s more to it.
The interior space of the Dragon spacecraft is larger.
There are four chairs and a three-screen control panel, with a touchscreen in the middle of the front two seats.
The screen on the left is Situational Awareness and Timeline, which will show the spacecraft ’ s orbit and when it is expected to lose contact with the ground.
The middle screen shows the attitude (the direction of the plane or spacecraft), as well as the position of the International Space Station and the Sun.
The latter is used for solar charging.
Below the screen are various buttons (instructions, rollers, screens, power, etc.), most of which are covered with plastic panels.
The Crew Dragon spacecraft is unmanned, and these controls will only take effect if the system fails.
At the center of all these controls is a pop-up button.
At any moment when the rocket takes off or takes off, the spacecraft can be ejected from the rocket.
What you can't see is the joystick.
Conversely, if the autopilot system fails and the pilot has to take over, they can use the touchscreen in the middle to control the aircraft.
When asked about the lack of joysticks, Benken said working with SpaceX is really like test-pilots working with aircraft manufacturers.
Hopkins added that there will always be changes and improvements in the aircraft.
In other words, technological progress continues, and these astronauts have been an important driver of technological advances in aircraft for decades.
The astronauts pointed out that they were test pilots, and SpaceX worked closely with NASA. “We don ’ t rush until we can ensure a safe flight, ” said Gwynne Shotwell, SpaceX ’ s president and chief operating officer.
The flight will house the astronauts in a capsule about the size of an apartment bathroom.
Although there are four chairs inside, it can accommodate seven passengers.
Although the other three astronauts will sit below the other four, the area is currently used as storage space.
According to SpaceX, NASA now only needs to send four astronauts, and it can easily expand the number of astronauts in the future.
The company also showed off a simulator for the capsule.
SpaceX feeds into the simulator any scenario they can think of to see how the system and astronauts react, and they will continue to use it until a few weeks before the launch in November 2019.
They have adjusted the order of operation of the mission and how to get in and out of the top of the hatch under different circumstances.
When they appear on the International Space Station, they may be the best-dressed astronauts.
They can wear spacesuits that look tame, like so many other aspects of the Crew Dragon spacecraft, whose design has improved over time with the help of NASA and astronauts.
Hurley said the old spacesuit was large and had a lot of metal in it, and the helmet did not perform very well in terms of visibility.
In contrast, SpaceX ’ s spacesuits and helmets are lighter.
"Bob and I have worn spacesuits 20 or 30 times and are almost ready now," Hurley said.
Preparations are particularly complicated, with each link having to undergo repeated testing. Dragon's rockets have already delivered cargo to the International Space Station six times.
But this time the object of transport is people, and everyone understands the risks involved.
"The only thing I'm afraid of is not being able to go home," Glover said, adding that he takes this into account every time the army goes out.
He is looking forward to his first experience on the International Space Station.
Benken was so excited about the return of the United States to the space flight field that his friends and family could see the scene of him taking off from the coast of Florida instead of watching it on Russian television.
"It would be completely different if it were in our own backyard," he said, adding that this was SpaceX's first manned flight, and it would be a high-profile event.
Even the unmanned launch in November attracted more eyeballs than the typical Falcon rocket launch.
The media question-and-answer session was held at the SpaceX plant, which is located in front of the Dragon spacecraft ’ s clean room.
Sometimes, in the noise of employees building rockets for space, it is difficult to hear the answer.
Glover took a moment to remind everyone that it wasn ’ t just the four astronauts we interviewed who made history.
"All the background noise indicates that something amazing is happening," he said. title: 8 years, 8 times the growth of Vietnamese plastic surgery
text:
August 27, 2018 13: 09 The number of Vietnamese plastic surgery patients in South Korea last year was 7,447, eight times the number in 2010 (921), according to statistics from the South Korean Health Industry Zhenxing Institute. The number of Vietnamese plastic surgery tourists to South Korea is growing, with young Vietnamese women affected by K-POP or K-BEAUTY accounting for the majority.
The price of plastic tourism products is between 3 million and 10 million won (about NT $824-274,600), which is higher than the per capita national income of Vietnam last year (US $2,385, about NT $73,410).
With the increase in the number of patients in Vietnam, the larger plastic surgery department in Gangnam, Seoul, followed by English, Chinese, Japanese and Russian, began to recruit Vietnamese translators.
In the hospital ’ s recovery room, in addition to K-POP music, songs by popular Vietnamese singers are played.
Hospitals also sign contracts with nearby Vietnamese restaurants to provide patients with Vietnamese food.
Ms. Lai (30), a Vietnamese employee who works in a plastic surgery department in Sinsa-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, said that the number of patients has increased recently and that she can ’ t cope with it alone.
The number of patients in Vietnam has more than doubled compared to last year, surpassing the number of patients from mainland China, according to a plastic surgeon in Pho Tingdong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul.
Affected by the retaliation of Sade (the last high-altitude area defense system), the number of plastic surgery tourists in mainland China has decreased, and plastic surgery hospitals are about to set their sights on the Southeast Asian market.
Agency companies that attract Vietnamese patients are also in hot business.
Hospitals pay great attention to word of mouth, because most Vietnamese patients go to Korea for plastic surgery through acquaintances.
(WANG Pao)

title: How to improve the mental health of residents? Try "Clean and Greening"
text:
Text: JAMIE DUCHARME translation: Researchers have been advocating the effect of green space and outdoor activities to boost mood, and a new study also emphasizes that a person ’ s environment has a great impact on mental health.
A study published Friday (July 20) in JAMA Network Open found a link between urban restoration projects in Philadelphia and the state of mental health of citizens.
The study notes that “clean and green ” Philadelphia ’ s urban open spaces reduce the level of depression or worthlessness felt by neighborhood residents, and slightly improve overall residents ’ mental health.
Dr. Eugenia South, assistant professor of emergency medicine at the University of Pennsylvania ’ s Perelman School of Medicine and co-author of the study, said, “Greening vacant spaces is a relatively low-cost, very simple, structural intervention that can have an impact on a large population.
You can improve your health by changing your living environment in a simple way. ”
To investigate, a team of researchers identified 541 vacant lots in Philadelphia that had “urban wither ” phenomena within a quarter of a mile, such as illegal dumping of garbage, abandoned cars, and weeds.
Next, they interviewed 442 adults who lived in these open spaces.
Participants were told to be selected to participate in a study to improve understanding of urban health and to have them answer questions about mental health.
They did not know that these researchers were involved in future urban greening efforts.
After completing the initial survey, the researchers randomly selected 37 clusters for green interventions, including removing garbage and waste, planting grass and trees, installing fences, and maintaining them regularly.
Another 36 clusters removed garbage and carried out minor maintenance, but less green vegetation was added.
In the end, the former cluster of 37 has been maintained.
After the restoration project was completed within 18 months, the researchers interviewed the original 342 participants, about a third of whom lived in the cluster where the greening intervention took place.
The results showed that those who lived in open spaces with green interventions were 41% less likely to feel depressed and 51% less likely to feel worthless than those who lived in open spaces with no improved environment.
While the overall improvement in mental health has not been statistically significant, Sasse said researchers are confident that it can help people improve their mental health.
The results of this study show that green space has special significance because people who live near empty spaces that have only been cleaned up with less green vegetation have seen significant improvements in their mental health.
According to Sasse, “The green space itself is very important.
We can use it to implement several mechanisms, including improving social connections and eliminating mental fatigue and stress in life.
The point is that it is a green space, not an empty space such as a parking lot.
The wooden fence is also very important as it marks the space that everyone cares about and is taking care of. ”
Greening has a deeper impact on people living below the poverty line. “When living in dilapidated conditions, the poorer communities are hit harder, ” says Sasse.
Those people ’ s health is usually the most affected by their living environment, so changing the environment can be very beneficial to them. ”
Taken together, these results point to urban greening as an opportunity for cities that want to improve their residents ’ mental health, especially if it costs only $1,600 to change a vacant space and spend an additional $180 a year to maintain it, Sasse said.
She and her colleagues have partnered with the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society to promote and implement the program in Philadelphia, and other cities have expressed interest.
"This is not a comprehensive treatment for depression, and it must be combined with other individual treatments," says Sasse.
But when you consider the cost of a small amount, you can understand that this is a very low-cost change. "

title: British mother dies on operating table in Turkey plastic surgery hospital - News Morning Post
text:
Morning News reporter Xu Huifen comprehensive report According to the British "Daily Mail" reported on the 29th, a 29-year-old British mother went to a well-known clinic in Turkey to undergo "Brazilian hip lift", but died on the operating table due to complications, the safety of the operation once again caused heated discussion.
"Brazilian hip lift" has been hot in recent years, but a working group composed of five international plastic surgery groups released a report that the mortality rate of the operation is about 1 / 3000, ranking first in all kinds of plastic and cosmetic surgery.
Leah, 29, from Leeds, England, is a mother of three.
This month, Leah flew to Izmir, Turkey, to undergo hip surgery at a clinic called Elite Regeneration.
The clinic is famous, and in June this year, former Spurs player Jamie O ’ Hara performed a fat suction operation at the clinic.
Many reality TV stars are also its customers, Leah himself is a beautician, often chasing the information of some reality TV stars, so also moved to Turkey for plastic surgery heart.
Moreover, plastic surgery in Turkey is cheaper than in the UK, sometimes as much as 70% cheaper.
In Turkey, face or neck lifting usually costs £2,640, while in the UK it costs around £4,500; breast implants cost around £2,275 and in the UK it costs around £5,500.
Leah's choice of "Brazilian hip lift" costs £3,000.
The so-called "Brazilian hip lift" is to extract fat from the abdomen or other parts, and then inject it into the buttocks to create a more perfect hip shape.
According to the clinic's website, the operation usually lasts 1 to 2 hours and can be full or local anesthesia.
The website said that this operation can not be underestimated, but the probability of complications of the operation is very small.
However, when Leah underwent surgery soon after suffering complications, initially stabilized, and later suffered three heart attacks, doctors and nurses finally failed to save her, Leah died on the operating table.

title: The future of whales: Japan demands permission for sustainable commercial killing
text:
Image copyright BARCROFT MEDIA Image caption Whales are thought to be socially intelligent creatures.
Whaling is perhaps the most touching issue in animal protection, and it is now possible to slaughter whales for profit.
Due to hundreds of years of human hunts, many kinds of whales are endangered.
Commercial whaling has been banned for more than 30 years.
But the International Whaling Commission (IWC), which is currently meeting in Brazil, will decide next week on Japan's request to end the whaling ban.
While Japan has been hunting whales, BBC correspondent Andreas Illmer says the issue is complicated.
Members of the International Whaling Commission (IWC) agreed in 1986 on a ban on commercial whaling aimed at restoring whale populations in the oceans.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan continues to kill whales using scientific fishing terms.
But pro-whaling nations see the ban as temporary, arguing that an agreement can be reached on whaling quotas to keep whaling sustainable.
Conservationists are pleased that the ban has become semi-permanent, but whaling nations like Japan, Norway and Iceland are unhappy.
They say whaling is part of their culture and that sustainable whaling can continue.
Allowing whaling for scientific purposes became an exception to the 1986 ban, and Japan has killed about 200-1,200 whales a year since 1986, including baby whales and pregnant females.
Among the reasons given by Japan for whaling are to investigate the current number of whales and find out whether they are endangered.
But critics say this is no more than an excuse for Japan to continue killing whales for consumption, and whale meat from scientific whaling is usually sold.
Image copyright AFP Image caption Japan kills between 300 and 400 whales a year
Japan's senior fisheries negotiator for sustainable fishing and IWC commissioner Hideki Makuchi told the BBC that Japan hopes the IWC can return to the organization's original purpose of protecting whales but at the same time "using whales sustainably."
Whaling in large numbers in the 19th and 20th centuries brought whales to the brink of extinction. In the 1960s, restrictions on whaling became a pressing issue due to the advent of whaling technology and large processing vessels.
The restrictions on whaling led to the ban, and now whale populations are strictly monitored, some whale species are still endangered, while minke whales, the main target of Japanese fishing, are not endangered.
Therefore, Japan, the current Chair of the International Whaling Commission (IWC), has proposed a series of measures, including the establishment of a sustainable whaling commission to establish sustainable fishing quotas for “abundant whale species ”.
In addition to commercial value, there are also ethical issues involved in whaling, and many people think that whaling is immoral.
Animal protection activists have been prepared to oppose Japan's proposal to allow commercial whaling.
Image copyright SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY Image caption Minke whales, the main target of Japanese fishing, are not an endangered species.
Kitty Block, president of the Humane Society International, said that these huge and elegant animals in the ocean are already facing many threats, such as plastic pollution, noise pollution, collision entanglement, climate change and so on, and they do not need to be targeted by whaling guns again.
It is also said that whales are highly intelligent animals with highly developed social structures.
Killing whales causes whales to fear and causes them pain.
The old-fashioned whaling javelin brings a slow and painful death to whales, while modern whaling guns use a javelin that can blow open, but conservationists say that even then, catching and killing whales will go through a slow process of death.
Two years ago, the Australian government released a 2008 video that showed a Japanese research vessel killing a whale that marine conservation NGO Sea Shepherd said died 20 minutes after being shot by a javelin.
But pro-whaling advocates say the above is the exception.
Similar accidents can occur in slaughterhouses.
Moreover, the sustainable killing of whales is no different from the industrial production of meat, such as raising and slaughtering pigs, cattle and chickens.
Australia, a major anti-whaling country, has said it will join other countries in opposing Japan's attempt to undermine the current ban on commercial whaling.
Image copyright AFP Image caption Many of the whale meat from Japan's scientific whaling comes into the market for consumption.
Hideki Makuchi, director of the Japan Fisheries Agency's whaling operations, told the BBC that they hoped the new proposal would be adopted so that the whaling issue would be resolved on the basis of science and international law and not involve so much emotion.
Professor Donald R Rothwell, of the Australian National University, told the BBC that ending the ban may ultimately not bring much change.
He said that if Japan is willing to end its scientific whaling program, future commercial whaling quotas may not result in more whales being killed.
At present, according to Japan's so-called scientific whaling, Japan kills 300 to 400 whales a year, and commercial whaling quotas may limit the number of catches to a lower level.
At present, the Antarctic is a refuge for some whales, but there are also whaling interactions there.
Japan says the sanctuary is for commercial whaling and that scientific whaling should not be restricted.
In the future, if Japan hunts whales in accordance with commercial quotas, then Japan will abide by the regulations of whale sanctuaries.
At present, the demand for whale meat in the Japanese market has been declining, and the whaling industry has been sustained by state subsidies, so ultimately changing tastes means that commercial whaling will eventually become unsustainable because it is not commercially viable.

title: Extreme weather in progress
text:
September 10, 2018 04: 11 China Times Typhoon Li Wuzhong and the Hokkaido earthquake caused major damage to Japan, allowing people to see the horrors of complex natural disasters.
The heavy rainfall in the past few days has turned the southwest into a watery country, and people's lives have been greatly affected.
The northern region was not spared in the two days, and heavy rainfall caused severe flooding in several places.
The impact of extreme weather is already ongoing, especially in Taiwan, which is at high risk of extreme weather, and it is necessary to comprehensively improve disaster resilience in order to allow people to live and work in peace and contentment.
Regrettably, the current rulers are far more attentive to elections and political calculations than reacting to extreme weather.
People depend on food for their livelihood, but agriculture is the most sensitive and vulnerable industry to climate change.
According to statistics, the number of natural disasters worldwide increased by 26% compared to the previous decade, with extreme weather increasing by a factor of 2.3, greatly increasing the uncertainty of agricultural production and farmers ’ income.
This heavy rain in the south actually caused more than 700 million yuan of agricultural and fishery products loss, not only farmers and fishermen suffering, but also consumers because of rising prices and crying.
Since extreme weather cannot be avoided, the government and farmers cannot rely on rescue alone, and should have more positive thinking and practices.
For low-lying prone to flooding, soil deterioration, lack of surface irrigation water, poor drainage system, soil has been seriously subsidence and other unsuitable for continued operation of agricultural land, the government instead of spending money to subsidize farming, so that farmers fall into a vicious cycle, it is better to put forward the exit mechanism and carry out overall planning, under the principle of taking care of farmers' livelihood, make more efficient use of these land.
Given that consumers are the end of the food supply chain, in the face of extreme weather, they can encourage farmers to reduce environmental damage and help save energy and reduce carbon through purchasing behaviors such as low-carbon, friendly farming, and certified agricultural products.
In an era of increasing potential threats, government departments can no longer be standardised, and must build a set of early warning systems and rapid response mechanisms as soon as possible through cross-domain integration, and constantly rehearse and revise at any time to gather the wisdom of all people to combat the impending natural and human disasters, and maintain a high degree of resilience.
With the Mid-Autumn Festival approaching, the Meteorological Bureau estimates that there will likely be a typhoon or heavy rain to hit Taiwan. In order to allow the public to have a good holiday, government departments must tighten their nerves and all flood control and drainage systems should be comprehensively cleaned.
Since the Chinese people are accustomed to roast meat to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival, the agricultural authorities are invited to gather relevant institutions to make contingency measures in advance, first to stabilize the biological price of the people, and second to avoid the recurrence of the chaos in the northern farmers' market, so that people will not lose heart again!
(The author is a scholar of agriculture and economics) (China Times)

title: 25 Countries Oppose New Whale Sanctuary
text:
At a meeting of the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in Florianópolis, Brazil, a motion to establish a whale sanctuary in the South Atlantic was rejected.
The motion submitted by Brazil, Argentina and South Africa failed to obtain the required three-fourths majority in the vote. Among the 39 endorsing countries, the European Union and Switzerland were among the sponsors.
Twenty-five countries have voted against the deal, including Japan, Norway and Iceland, which have called for the resumption of commercial whaling.
South Korea and Russia also voted against setting up protected areas.
For 22 years, Brazil has been trying to convince the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to set up a whale sanctuary.
His delegation had suggested that a simple majority procedure should be accepted in the voting, provided that Japan's proposal to limit whaling also followed the principle of a simple majority vote.
The proponents of the protected area, however, refused to accept the proposal.
In a statement, Pro Wildlife, an environmental group that does not trade on the protection of Japanese whalers, said that “the worrying bargaining practices that Japan has openly presented to Brazil have failed ”, giving reason to hope that Japan ’ s proposal to end the commercial whaling ban will also fail.
On Friday, the end of the meeting, a Japanese motion calling for the lifting of the whaling ban will be voted on.
The ban has been in place since 1986.
Allowed "subsistence hunting" quotas were also the subject of discussion.
Livelihood hunting refers to whaling for self-consumption.
Indigenous peoples in Greenland, Russia, the United States, Saint Vincent and Grenada currently have annual whaling quotas of about 2,800.
The countries concerned want to implement an automatic quota renewal process for the next seven years, under which quotas that have not been used up in the previous year can be partially allocated to the following year.
Environmental groups fear the move could encourage commercial whaling that goes beyond indigenous needs.
Brazil is committed to reforming the International Whaling Commission.
The draft of the Florianopolis Declaration, submitted by the host country, said that the Whaling Commission should be transformed into a Whaling Commission.
The draft emphasizes that "whale watching" tourists observing whales from ships is the only sustainable use of whales.
The draft says whale populations should return to pre-industrial whaling levels.
It is estimated that about 3 million whales were killed in the 20th century alone.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling violated the Convention and that Japan's whaling will become history.
Since the International Whaling Commission (IWC) adopted the Global Whaling Convention in 1986, banning commercial whaling, Norway, Iceland and Japan have continued to catch, especially Japan, under the guise of “scientific research ”.
The International Court of Justice in The Hague handed down its judgment on March 31 in Australia's case against Japan for whale hunting.
The International Court of Justice has ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling violates the Convention and that Australia has been trying to stop Japan's whaling activities through diplomatic means for 20 years, but to no avail.
In June last year, Australia filed a lawsuit against Japan in the International Court of Justice in The Hague.
The International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled on March 31 that Japan's current whaling activities were in violation of the Convention and prohibited it from continuing to hunt whales.
Since the adoption of the Global Whaling Ban Convention, many whale species have stabilized.
However, blue whales, baleen whales, sei whales, southern right whales and sperm whales continue to be threatened and even threatened with extinction. Whales are mammals, up to 33 metres in length and up to 190 tons in weight, making them the largest animal on Earth.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling violated the Convention and that Japanese whalers continued to hunt whales in the Arctic this year.
Although Japanese officials say whaling is used for scientific research, the meat is sold at fish markets and specialty restaurants in Japan.
The Japan Whale Institute was established exactly one year after the International Whaling Commission adopted the Global Whaling Convention.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling violated the treaty, and that Japan's traditional whale meat was served on the Japanese table long ago.
Especially after World War II, whale meat became one of the foods that Japanese residents relied on for their survival.
Schools and restaurants use a lot of whale meat because whale meat is cheaper than beef.
But tastes are changing: only 1% of Japanese meat currently comes from whales.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Japanese Antarctic whaling violated the Convention by dumping 7,000 tons of whale meat in cold storage in Japan.
Because no one bought fish from fin whales, a Japanese company turned it into dog food.
At present, the company has also announced that it will stop selling this kind of dog food.
The protests of the International Organization for the Protection of Animals are too loud.
Despite the International Court of Justice ruling that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling violated the Convention, many Japanese still support whaling and condemn the actions of environmental groups such as Greenpeace as eco-terrorism.
The Japanese did not want to succumb to international pressure.
Japan has to pay the price: for the past 25 years, the country has paid about 6.3 million euros a year in subsidies to the whaling industry.
The International Court of Justice has ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling is not a violation of the Convention. Iceland and Norway also continue to hunt openly.
When the International Whaling Commission adopted the Global Whaling Convention in 1986, Iceland and Norway opposed the proposal, arguing that they were not bound by the ban.
Despite protests, this month Icelandic fishing boats went out to sea as usual to hunt finke whales.
The fish they catch will be sold to Japan.
The International Court of Justice has ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling is in violation of the Convention and that indigenous peoples such as the Chukchi of Russia and the Inuit of Canada can continue whaling as long as they do not engage in commercial activities related to whales.
Whaling has a centuries-old tradition for them.
This marine mammal provides the indigenous population with fish meat, fish oil and fish bones. Whales are used for everything.
The International Court of Justice has found Japan's Antarctic whaling to be in violation of the Convention, and Greenpeace and Sea Shepherd's Whaling is now banned largely thanks to environmental groups.
For decades, these groups have engaged in high-profile campaigns to draw attention to whaling, and they have called for public action.
The anti-whaling group Sea Shepherd has gained notoriety and controversy for its fierce conservation efforts.
International Court of Justice Finds Japan's Antarctic Whaling in Violation of the Convention Whale Watching Many countries that previously engaged in whaling are now in the business of whale watching.
Some whale watchers in Japan and Norway, who used to be whalers, now share their knowledge of whales with tourists.
More and more Japanese prefer to see whales in the ocean than fish on the dinner table.
Author: Michael Hartlep / Quiet condensation / Li Yu (DXS, Agence France-Presse)

title: Japan vetoed proposal to resume commercial whaling, threatens to withdraw from IWC
text:
The following content is from our partners, so we cannot guarantee that it will be displayed properly.
This content was posted on Sep 15, 2018 at 2: 35 AM Last updated - Sep 15, 2018 - 02: 35 (Agence France-Presse, Brazil) Japan's proposal to lift the ban on commercial whaling was rejected today by the International Whaling Commission (IWC).
Japanese officials expressed regret over the vote and threatened to withdraw from the IWC if commercial whaling could not be resumed.
"If scientific evidence and diversity are not respected, and if commercial whaling is completely rejected, Japan will have to make a fundamental reassessment of its position as a member of the International Whaling Commission."
IWC has 89 member states.
Asked if this would be the last time Japan would attend the IWC, Japanese government representative Shoji Mori declined to comment.
Mr. Mori has served as IWC chairman for two years and his term ends today.
Japan ’ s “The Way Forward ” proposal was defeated by 41 votes to 27 by anti-whaling nations led by Australia, the European Union and the United States.
He said Japan, which had sought consensus with other countries on its plan, was forced to push for a vote on the proposal to “show overwhelming support ” for the resumption of sustainable commercial whaling.
Japan is supported by the Pacific and Caribbean island countries, the African countries of Nicaragua, Morocco, Kenya and Tanzania, as well as the Asian countries of Laos and Cambodia.
South Korea abstained.
Russia said it abstained in the vote to avoid a deterioration in the already deeply divided situation at the IWC.
Russia, like several other countries, allows aboriginal subsistence whaling under IWC supervision.
IWC was established in 1964 to conserve and manage the global population of cetaceans.
The IWC imposed a moratorium on commercial whaling in 1986 because several whale species were endangered.
But Japan insists the whale population has recovered enough to restart commercial whaling.
Although Japan currently abides by the moratorium on commercial whaling, it still uses the loophole of "scientific purposes" to hunt hundreds of whales every year and sell whale meat.
Norway and Iceland have also ignored the ban and are major supporters of Japan's efforts to resume commercial whaling.
As more and more IWC developing member states support Japan, if Japan withdraws, it will have a profound impact on the organization.

title: Last year, nearly 50,000 foreigners came to South Korea for cosmetic surgery, which cost 215 billion won.
text:
Photo: YONHAP News Korea International Radio reported: According to statistics, nearly 50,000 foreigners visited South Korea for cosmetic surgery last year.
Last year, cosmetic hospitals accounted for more than 30 percent of the total cost of foreign patients.
A total of 397,882 foreign patients visited South Korea last year and paid a total of 639.9 billion won for the treatment, according to the information submitted by the Ministry of Health and Welfare to South Jin-sun, a member of the Common Democratic Party of the Health and Welfare Committee.
The number of patients decreased by 6.5% compared to the previous year and the cost of treatment decreased by 25.6% compared to the previous year.
However, the number of foreigners receiving treatment in Korean cosmetic hospitals increased by 968 compared with the previous year to 48,849, accounting for 12.3% of all foreign patients, and the cost of treatment reached 215 billion won, a three-fold increase from 52.5 billion won in 2012.
Since South Korea launched the project to attract foreign patients, the proportion of cosmetic hospital consultation fees has continued to rise.

title: France intercepts stowaways in English Channel to bring back 50 migrants – Radio France Internationale
text:
(AFP, Lille, France) French authorities said today that 19 migrants trying to sneak into Britain were intercepted in the English Channel yesterday night, and 31 migrants were rescued at sea earlier yesterday and brought back to France.
This year, more and more migrants from Africa, the Middle East and South Asia are attempting to sneak into Britain from the northern French coast, challenging the cold and rough English Channel.
Human rights groups say the crackdown on migrants by French police to prevent them from gathering and setting up camps in Calais and other areas along the French coast has led to an increase in migrants crossing the sea.
The French navy said it rescued 19 migrants, including a woman and two children, from a boat last night.
The men were sent back to France shortly after midnight, and some of them lost heat.
The French navy also said that two maritime interceptions carried out before dawn yesterday found a boat carrying 11 migrants and another boat carrying 20 migrants.
French and British officials announced on the 26th that several vessels have been found in the English Channel to intercept 71 migrants, some of whom have been hospitalized due to heat loss.
Four migrants have died trying to cross the English Channel so far this year.
The English Channel is one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, and with strong currents and low water temperatures, it is very dangerous to cross.

title: Paul Allen's Last Wish: Biggest Plane Sliding Closer to Take-off
text:
The Stratolaunch is definitely an ambitious engineering challenge. It is the world ’ s largest aircraft, with a record volume and payload. It is designed to be able to transport small satellites to Earth ’ s orbit as a means of launching satellites.
The sponsor of the project, Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen (Paul Allen), unfortunately he did not come and saw the stratosphere launch.
However, the stratospheric launch has recently completed the ground high-speed test slip, and it seems that it is not far from the sky.
New Atlas reported that the stratospheric launch series began development in 2011, and in mid-2017, it finally left the hangar to meet the public, and then it went through a series of engine tests, earlier this year, it sailed on a desert runway in Mojave, California, and began to adjust its glide speed, the old record is 74 kilometers per hour, but recently it has increased to 128 kilometers. The test has reached 145 kilometers, more than twice the initial test, indicating that the engine is running smoothly and has successfully driven the aircraft forward.
However, the design team of the stratospheric launch has been bittersweet in recent days, and the successful taxiing of the aircraft is of course a good thing, but the main funder Paul Allen died a few days ago.
It is said that Allen has had a big aviation dream since childhood, and investing in stratospheric launch is a step towards realizing his dream.
Jean Floyd, CEO of Stratosphere Launch, expressed his condolences following Allen ’ s death, saying that all those involved in the project will work to fulfill Allen ’ s legacy.
In the future, the stratospheric launch system may carry a small space shuttle to send people to space. (Figure / Stratolaunch) In the future, the stratospheric launch system can hoist a 230-ton space rocket in the middle of a huge body.
(China Times Newsletter)

That is, in the face of climate change that they cannot control, especially those who have experienced floods and forest fires and lost their homes in an instant, the psychological damage is far more serious than previously thought.

title: France warns migrants risk surging across the sea
text:

This content was posted on Nov 22, 2018 at 7: 50 PM Last updated Nov 22, 2018 - 19: 50 (Agence France-Presse, Lille, France) French authorities warned today that attempts by migrants to risk crossing the English Channel by boat have recently increased, reflecting fears that borders could be closed after Brexit.
Last night alone, a total of 18 people were rescued by the French maritime police on two occasions, and 30 people have attempted to cross the Channel since the beginning of this year.
On the other hand, the Home Office also said that 14 people were rescued last night, a total of 78 people in the past two weeks.
The Home Office said: "Due to recent incidents, we have taken measures to deploy coastal patrol boats on the southeast coast." For a long time, migrants have gathered on the northern coast of France to smuggle into the UK by truck, some of whom have family members there and others believe they have a better chance of finding work or seeking asylum in the UK.
But since 2016, authorities have begun to monitor migrants using rubber dinghies and inflatable rafts to cross the 33-kilometer-wide Dover Strait, the world ’ s busiest shipping lane.
Ingrid Parrot, a spokesman for the French maritime police unit in Cherbourg, said that according to reports, 23 people attempted to cross the Channel in 2016, down to 13 in 2017.
But since the UK will leave the European Union in March next year, stricter immigration controls are expected, prompting more migrants to attempt to cross the sea to replace the use of car tools in the French port of Calais.
"We think migrants want to come to the UK before the UK leaves the EU, at all costs," said Mr Parrot.

title: Monsanto Lawsuit Affects 1 in 10 Bayer Employees Worldwide
text:
BAYRY-US, the German drugmaker that acquired Monsanto, a U.S. subsidiary, announced on Thursday that it would sell some business groups, lay off about 12,000 employees (about a tenth of the number) and 3.3 billion euros (about $3.8 billion) in losses due to ongoing legal proceedings and other factors.
Bayer has endured more than 35% share price declines so far this year as CEO Werner Baumann tries to redeem the city amid fears that Monsanto ’ s Roundup herbicide is being dragged down by more than 9,000 lawsuits over its alleged carcinogenic properties.
Bayer stock price trend chart / chart: According to Google's cost reduction plan, Bayer will cut about 12,000 of its 118,200 jobs worldwide in response to its $63 billion acquisition of Monsanto.
In the consumer health and pharmaceuticals sector, Bayer will reduce impairment and write-off costs by approximately €3.3 billion in the fourth quarter.
The consumer healthcare sector, which sells over-the-counter drugs, has seen revenue decline as U.S. consumers shift from established pharmacies to online stores, often switching to cheaper brands.
In the first nine months of 2018, revenue from Bayer ’ s consumer health products fell 0.4% after currency fluctuations, compared with 1.7% for the full year of 2017.
The Financial Times reported that the group said it was considering selling consumer healthcare units such as Coppertone sunscreen and Dr. Scholl ’ s foot care products that it purchased from Merck (MRK-US) for $14 billion in 2014.
In order to raise funds, Bayer will also seek a buyer to acquire Currenta, a German chemical production site service provider with a 60% stake.
Markus Mayer, an analyst at Baader Helvea, said the Coppertone and Dr. Scholl brands should receive €1 billion and Currenta ’ s shares should receive €1.5 billion.
Reuters reports that Bayer will also cut its animal health division, the fifth-largest market share in the industry, with analysts saying it could get 6 billion to 7 billion euros (about $7.9 billion).
The division is the largest manufacturer of flea and tick control products for cats and dogs, as well as a supplier of veterinary drugs for livestock, with sales of 1.57 billion euros in 2017, representing approximately 4.5% of the Group ’ s revenue.
The animal health industry has consolidated, with Pfizer (PFE-US) and Eli Lilly (LLY-US) both successfully listing their veterinary division on the stock market as separate entities.
Pfizer's spin-off company is Zoetis (ZTS-US) and Elanco (ELAN-US).
The investment banker, who asked not to be named, said Reckitt Benckiser (RB-LN) and Procter & Gamble (PG-US) could be among the suitors for consumer brands.
Looking ahead, the company aims to set core net profit EPS per share at 6.80 euros in 2019, up from 5.70 euros to 5.90 euros expected this year, with a target price of around 10 euros in 2022.
The group ’ s EBITDA and sales margin for special items should increase to more than 30% in 2022, up from 26.5% last year.

title: Hong Kong is expected to continue its efforts to reduce carbon emissions and slow down warming this year ｜ News ｜ Hong Kong and Macao ｜ on.cc

Last year was the hottest year in Hong Kong since 1884, the Environmental Protection Education Foundation (EEF) held a forum today (3) to introduce global warming and ecological issues to the public.
The Acting Director of the Hong Kong Observatory, Mr Cheng Chu-ming, pointed out that the temperature was higher than normal for 11 months last year, with an average temperature of 24.5 degrees. It is believed that the temperature in Hong Kong will still be high this year, and there may be 1-2 days of cold weather, but the number of days will not be too much.
The temperature in Hong Kong last year was abnormal, and the hot night surged from the normal 18 days to 46 days, increasing by multiple. In previous years, there were only 1 to 2 hot nights in September, and last year there were 7 consecutive hot nights.
The Hong Kong Observatory issued a total of 33 cool and hot weather warnings last year, more than 80% more than the average of 18 days in the previous year. Last year, there was only one cold day below 12 degrees, which was much less than the normal 17 days.
Mr Cheng stressed that climate warming was not unique to Hong Kong. Countries around the world also experienced increasingly hot weather last year, calling on people to reduce carbon emissions in their daily lives and stop global warming.
Warmer weather also brings many problems. For example, elderly people will get sick due to extreme weather, resulting in a significant increase in hospital admissions.
Global warming will affect the taste of crops. The taste of vegetables depends on four factors, including genes, nutrients, climate and growth period. Acquired factors are very important. Excessive temperature is not conducive to plant growth, resulting in decreased sweetness of vegetables and vegetables.
Agriculture Management Director of Agriculture, Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department Wang Haoyun also said that agriculture and climate change are inseparable. In the past, humans burned forests to obtain agricultural land, which is equivalent to transforming the environment and changing the climate.

title: US report: global warming will reduce GDP by 10% - 20181125 - International
text:
This new version of the "National Climate Assessment" report is authorized by Congress and written by more than 300 scientists, and is released every four years. This is the fourth edition of Volume 2, with a total of 1,656 pages.
According to the report, the quality and quantity of crops in the United States will decline in the face of rising temperatures, droughts and floods. In some parts of the Midwest, farmers can only produce less than 75% of their current corn, and may lose more than 25% of their soybean production.
Over the next 12 years, hot temperatures will cause average dairy production to fall by 1.35%.
In addition to the economic losses, the report warns that rising temperatures will lead to more premature deaths, with the largest increase in extreme temperatures expected in the Midwest, where 2,000 people will die prematurely each year by 2090.
Mosquito-borne diseases such as Zika, dengue fever and chikungunya will increase, and West Nile disease cases will more than double by 2050.
Global warming will also wreak havoc on the natural environment and infrastructure. The report predicts that the wildfire season will grow longer and engulf larger areas, and that public infrastructure and more than $1 trillion in real estate in coastal areas of the United States will be threatened by rising sea levels, flooding and storms.
The report warns that “as carbon emissions continue to grow at record rates, annual losses in some sectors of the economy are expected to reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, exceeding the current GDP of many U.S. states. ”
Experts in the report proposed three solutions: first, the "pricing" of greenhouse gas emissions, which means levying taxes or fees on companies that emit carbon dioxide; second, the government's legislation to regulate greenhouse gas emissions; third, the use of public funds to develop clean energy.
Trump has always stressed that there is no evidence that climate change is caused by humans, and White House spokesman Lindsay Walters also criticized the report as inaccurate. “It is largely based on the most extreme scenario of global warming, which contradicts the long-term trend … It assumes limited technology and innovation, and rapid population growth. ”
“Trump continues to ignore the threat of climate change, but his administration is sounding the alarm, ” said Abigail Dillen, president of Earthjustice, an environmental group. The US media questioned whether the release of the report on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, was intended to lessen the shock.
A spokesman for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said the report was completed “earlier than expected. ”
