title: In order to break the 30-year moratorium on whaling, Japan threatens to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission in 2019
text:
The Japanese government, which has repeatedly clashed at sea over the issue of whaling, announced on the 20th that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and hope to resume its previously banned commercial whaling activities after withdrawing from the meeting.
If Japan withdraws from the IWC, it will get rid of the 30-year moratorium on whaling, and may conduct commercial whaling in Japan ’ s offshore and exclusive economic zones in the future, which may also expose Japan to criticism from international anti-whaling organizations and countries.
Japan has a long history of whaling, is currently one of the world's largest whaling, whale-eating countries, "Central News Agency" reported, after World War II, Japan's food crisis, coupled with the progress of logistics and preservation technology, whale meat has become a substitute for beef and pig meat shortage, has become an important source of food for the Japanese people. The whale and the whale.
However, the modern awareness of protecting marine life has risen, and Japan's whaling culture has been condemned by many Western countries. The well-known documentary "Bloody Bay" is suing Japan's whaling culture.
Since then, Japan, which is unable to conduct commercial whaling, has mostly relied on Iceland and other countries to import whale meat, but the market is not widely circulated, and consumption has fallen sharply.
Although there are fewer and fewer people eating whale meat in Japan, the Japanese have not given up on whaling and claim that whaling and eating whales are a precious part of Japanese culture. At the 2007 General Assembly, Japan also said that it would withdraw, and finally the United States coordinated to allow Japan to stay.
In the name of science, commercial whaling?
In the past few decades, international pressure and protests against Japan ’ s whaling have not diminished, and there have even been repeated incidents of collisions and sabotage of fishing vessels between the two sides, because Japan has not completely stopped whaling. In 1986, the IWC allowed Japan to conduct “research and whaling ” in Antarctica and the North Pacific for“ scientific research ” purposes, but did not agree to its commercial use. Food for sale, etc.
Many anti-whaling nations, scientists and environmental groups, such as Green and Equality, have accused Japan ’ s scientific program of whaling, hidden under the “name of investigation and research, ” of actually illegal commercial whaling.
The International Court of Justice ruled in 2014 that Japan had used scientific research to cover up commercial whaling.
The newspaper reported that in June this year, a Japanese Nisshin Maru (Nisshin Maru), accused by IWC, not only used explosives to brutally hunt whales, but also captured and killed 122 pregnant whales and 114 juvenile whales.
In order to restart commercial whaling at an early date, the Japanese government "seeks all possibilities" between Japan and other countries that support whaling and Australia and other countries that oppose whaling. The "Central News Agency" reported that "Hokkaido News" reported that at the IWC meeting held in September this year, Japan again proposed to restart commercial whaling of some resource-rich whales, but it was again rejected.
The Japanese government assessed that it would be difficult to restart commercial whaling if IWC were to remain, so it intends to announce its intention to withdraw before the end of the year.
At that time, as vice minister of agriculture, forestry and aquatic products, the Gomei-party senator Masaki Tanigaki said, "have to carefully study the possible solutions," Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe also said in the interim parliament a few days ago, in order to restart commercial whaling at an early date, the government will seek all possibilities.
Japanese government sources have revealed that Japan has basically decided to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in order to restart commercial whaling activities, and will announce its intention to withdraw as soon as next week.
“NHK ” pointed out that some people in the ruling party believe that staying in IWC will never be able to restart commercial whaling, and the government has judged it necessary to open the situation through withdrawal, and has informed the relevant members of the Liberal Democratic Party of this decision.
Since the notice period for withdrawal next year ends on the 1st of next month, Japan will state its position as soon as next week, and it will take effect on June 30 next year.
What is "IWC"?
The International Whaling Commission (IWC), which aims to conserve global whales, was established in 1948, and Japan officially joined in 1951. Of the 89 member countries in total, 35 countries, including Norway and Iceland, are the “pro-whaling faction ” in the IWC, while the mainstream in the IWC is still dominated by the“ anti-whaling faction ” of 50 countries, including Australia, Britain and the United States. For the Neutrals.
The IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling in 1982 and has strictly prohibited commercial whaling since 1986.
At that time, seven countries opposed it: Brazil, Iceland, Japan, Norway, Peru, South Korea, and the Soviet Union.
China, Chile, the Philippines, South Africa and Switzerland abstained.
In the past two centuries, humans have hunted large numbers of large whales around the world in order to reap the rich and expensive economic benefits of whales, resulting in a dramatic decline in the number of large whales of all kinds to a dangerous stage.
In order to protect them and maintain the ecological balance of the sea, the international community, after many negotiations, formed the IWC and adopted the Convention on the Prohibition of Whaling in 1986, which banned commercial whaling.
Japan, Norway, South Korea, Peru, Brazil, China and other countries voted against the resolution; among them, Canada, because of its reluctance to restrict, simply withdrew from the Commission in 1982, and Japan, which has a tradition of eating whale meat, has become the main target of environmental groups every year with Norway.
Now that Japan has decided to withdraw from the IWC, it is expected to break the moratorium on whaling that has been in place for about 30 years and restart commercial whaling, but not commercial whaling in the Antarctic Sea in the future, but in the coastal waters of Japan and in the exclusive economic zone of Japan (EEZ).
These include Hokkaido Abashiri, Kushiro City, Ishinomaki City, Miyagi Prefecture, Nanfang City, Chiba Prefecture, Taiji Town, Wakayama Prefecture, and Shimonoseki City, Yamaguchi Prefecture.
In doing so, Japan will lose the power of the IWC ’ s biannual meeting, but for now, the Japanese government wants to continue to participate as an observer in the scientific committee that investigates whale ecology.
Japan's "Yomiuri News" reported that once the Japanese government withdraws from the meeting, it is expected to cause an international backlash such as anti-whaling countries.
Conservation group Marine Conservation Australia has blasted Japan for setting a dangerous precedent and threatening other international treaties and agreements.
Greenpeace ’ s accusation that Japan is flouting the international architecture would be a big mistake.
The Kyodo News Agency also warned that Japan may be unable to avoid following the criticism of US President Donald Trump ’ s “America First ” doctrine.
Although Japan ’ s withdrawal will increase the feasibility of resuming commercial whaling, under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), whaling must be properly managed through international agencies, and Japan is also a party to the treaty.

Japanese government spokesman and cabinet chief Yoshihide Suga said that from July next year, commercial whaling will resume in restricted areas such as Japanese territorial waters and withdraw from the IWC.

Japan proposed to the IWC in September to restart commercial whaling, which was opposed by Australia and other countries, the proposal was rejected, and Japan decided to withdraw from the IWC.

After Japan withdraws from the IWC, it will not be able to investigate whaling in the Antarctic Sea. In view of the backlash of anti-whaling countries, Japan has restricted the resumption of commercial whaling to Japanese territorial waters and Japan ’ s economic waters.
The Japanese government maintains that there has been a culture of eating whale meat in Japan since ancient times, and that moderate whaling is justified, which is why Japan has resumed commercial whaling.

title: Japan resumes commercial whaling, prompting strong opposition from the international community
text:
Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.
The Japanese government has announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and will resume commercial whaling in July 2019.
This is likely to attract strong criticism from the international community.
Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.
For years, Japan has been hunting whales and selling whale meat in the name of “scientific research, ” which animal advocates have condemned.
Because some whale species are endangered, the International Whaling Commission, which works to protect whales, has banned commercial whaling since 1986.
Japan joined the committee in 1951.
Although the Japanese government ’ s stance has been expected, animal protection groups have warned that the move will have serious consequences, which means that Japan will be free to catch species such as minke whales that are protected by the International Whaling Commission.
Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Whale meat made sushi is sold in Miyagi, Japan.
What does the Japanese government say?
Japan ’ s cabinet chief Yoshihide Suga said commercial whaling would be confined to Japan ’ s territorial waters and economic zones in the future.
As a result, Japan will stop fishing in Antarctic waters and the southern hemisphere. Whale conservation groups have previously welcomed the move.
In a statement, the Japanese government said that the IWC focused only on the goal of protecting whale populations and failed to meet its other goal of supporting sustainable commercial whaling.
Whale fishing has been practiced in some coastal areas of Japan for hundreds of years.
After the end of World War II, Japanese citizens used whales as their main source of meat, and consumption of whale meat soared, but consumption has declined sharply in recent decades.
According to Japan ’ s Asahi Shimbun, whale meat accounts for only 0.1% of all meat sold in Japan.
Image copyright AFP Image caption For years, Japan has been hunting whales and selling whale meat in the name of "scientific research."
Australian Foreign Minister Marise Payne and Environment Minister Melissa Price said in a joint statement that they were “very disappointed ” by Japan ’ s decision.
Australia remains adamant against all forms of commercial and so-called "scientific" whaling.
Ahead of Japan ’ s official announcement, Nicola Beynon, head of campaigns at Humane Society International in Australia, said Japan would “operate entirely outside the purview of international law. ”
It ’ s a step on Japan ’ s path to a “pirate whaling nation, ” according to Bannon, and this contempt for international rules is troubling.
Greenpeace urged the Japanese government to reconsider the decision.
Greenpeace has warned that this could draw criticism from Japan, the host of the Group of 20 summit next June.
Sam Annesley, executive director of Greenpeace Japan, said that the Japanese government ’ s announcement at the end of the year was an obvious attempt to avoid the attention of the international media, but the whole world understood the Japanese government ’ s intentions.
“Today ’ s decision is at odds with the behavior of the international community and, more importantly, with the need to protect the oceans and the future of these great creatures, ” Anisseri said.
What is the current whaling ban?
In 1986, members of the International Whaling Commission unanimously agreed to suspend whaling in order to restore whale populations.
At the time, the moratorium was seen by pro-whaling nations as temporary and would continue after a consensus on sustainable fishing quotas was reached.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Commercial whaling has put some whale species on the brink of extinction.
However, it became a permanent ban.
Countries such as Japan, Norway and Iceland, which support whaling, believe that whaling is part of their culture and should continue in a sustainable manner.
Today, whale populations are closely monitored, with many species still on the brink of extinction, but others, like Japan ’ s predominant minke whale, are not endangered.
In September, Tokyo tried to get the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to agree to the allocation of commercial fishing quotas, but that proposal was rejected by the commission.
Can Japan give up?
Although Japan has withdrawn from the International Whaling Commission, it will still be subject to certain international laws.
The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea requires States to cooperate “through appropriate international organizations ” to protect, manage and study whale conservation.
However, the convention does not specify the name of the international organization.
If other countries are willing to cooperate, Japan could try to establish another international organization or join an existing organization like the North Atlantic Marine Mammal Commission (Nammco).
Compared to the International Whaling Commission (IWC), the North Atlantic Marine Mammal Commission (NAMMC) is a smaller body of pro-whaling countries and territories, such as Norway, Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands, which have disappointed the IWC.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan catches hundreds of whales each year.
Isn't Japan always whaling?
Yes. Although Japan has been whaling for the past 30 years, it is all in the name of a scientific project and is an exception to the International Whaling Commission ’ s ban.
Critics say the practice is effectively a cover for commercial whaling.
This practice in Japan means that captured whales are used for scientific research, and whale meat can be used for consumption and sale in the future.
Japan catches between 200 and 1,200 whales a year.
Japan says it is investigating whale populations to determine if they are endangered.
Why couldn't the IWC agree?
Japan has been trying to overturn the moratorium on whaling and is pushing hard for the Commission to reach an agreement on sustainable fishing quotas.
In September, Japan made its last attempt at the IWC summit in Brazil.
Japan has put forward a series of proposals, including the establishment of a Sustainable Whaling Commission and the establishment of sustainable fishing limits for “abundant whale populations / species ”.
The proposal was rejected by the committee.
Since then, there have been rumors that Japan will withdraw from the organization in order not to be bound by the rules of the Commission.

title: Japan to resume commercial whaling after more than 30 years
text:
Commercial whaling in Japan, which has been banned for more than 30 years, will resume next year.
On December 26, the Japanese government announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission and plans to restart commercial whaling in July next year.
Japan ’ s Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga said the country has been working for more than 30 years to find solutions to achieve sustainable commercial whaling, but has so far been unable to reach a compromise with countries that value the conservation of whale resources, so it decided to withdraw.
"Some members of the Committee are concerned only with whale protection and refuse to allow the rational use of such resources."
At present, Japan's planned whaling sites will be limited to Japan's territorial waters and exclusive economic waters, and will not hunt whales in the Antarctic waters and the southern hemisphere, and in accordance with international law, the whaling volume will be controlled within the calculation methods adopted by the International Whaling Commission.
In fact, at its annual meeting in September, the International Whaling Commission voted against Japan ’ s proposal to resume commercial whaling and simplify its decision-making rules.
Japan has repeatedly threatened to "retreat" on the grounds that members have "serious differences" on the issue of whaling.
Japan's decision to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission has also been criticized at home and abroad.
Masayuki Komatsu, a senior researcher at the Tokyo Foundation and a former Japanese negotiator for the International Whaling Commission, said the move was “irritable and emotional ” and questioned whether Japan would really benefit from resuming commercial whaling.
Australia, which is also a member of the International Whaling Commission, is "extremely disappointed" by Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling.
Australian Foreign Secretary Marise Payne and Environment Minister Melissa Price said in a joint statement that Japan ’ s decision to withdraw was regrettable and Australia would urge Japan to return to the IWC as soon as possible.
According to public data, Japan ’ s commercial whaling began in the Edo period and is currently the largest whaling and whale-eating country in the world.
But Japan's massive commercial whaling ended in the 20th century after the International Whaling Commission banned commercial whaling.
Japan ’ s whaling activities have been restricted for decades by the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and the Japan Cetacean Institute. In 1986, the IWC allowed Japan to hunt whales in Antarctica and the North Pacific for “scientific research ” purposes, but did not allow them to be used commercially, such as for food.
However, anti-whaling countries, scientists and environmental groups argue that Japan ’ s scientific project is unnecessary and is simply a commercial whaling disguise.
The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) has seriously criticized Japan ’ s so-called “scientific whaling ” activities:“ Japan ’ s whaling program is commercial and political, not real scientific research. ” The International Court of Justice ruled in 2014 that Japan was using scientific research to cover up commercial whaling.
Japan ’ s Ministry of Foreign Affairs claims that annual quantitative whaling is necessary for scientific research and the preservation of whale populations.
According to statistics from the Japan Cetacean Research Institute, the annual wholesale volume of the Japanese whaling industry is more than 32 million US dollars.
Japanese markets and restaurants sell more than 2,000 tons of whale meat each year.
According to the report of the International Fund for Animal Welfare, a variety of endangered whale species are sold in the Japanese market, including humpback whales, baleen whales and gray whales.
Since the end of World War II, Japan's domestic food shortage, whale meat used to be an important food supply, as a source of protein for a nutritious lunch, so the elderly Japanese have a fondness for whale meat. Antarctic whaling, however, is not traditional.
Japan's first Antarctic whaling was in the mid-1930s, and large-scale whaling did not begin until after World War II.
After the end of World War II, there was a food shortage in Japan, and whale meat was an important food supply for the next 20 years, serving as an important source of protein for daily meals.
Encouraged by the US military, Japan converted two huge US Navy ships into processing vessels for the Southern Ocean. At its peak in 1964, the country killed up to 24,000 whales a year, the vast majority of which were humpback and sperm whales.

I insist on whaling because...

(Reuters) - The recent wave of illegal immigration is likely to be related to the approaching Brexit deadline, some experts said.
The future of Brexit is uncertain, and the future of border arrangements is still unknown.
Leonard Doyle, a spokesman for the International Organization for Migration (IOM), said that if people believe that border security will change after Brexit, people smugglers may use immigration to make money.
Migrants living in the French coastal city of Dunkirk said they expected more police at the border after Brexit, which would make it harder to sneak into the UK.
Some believe that the Brexit deadline is the last chance to sneak into the UK.
Anti-immigrant sentiment in Europe is still high, and populist governments in some countries, such as Italy, have announced that they will not open ports to migrants.
Nando Sigona, an associate professor at the University of Birmingham and an international migration scholar, said many migrants living in Europe now see more and more European countries closing their doors, and believe that this is the only opportunity to travel to the UK.
(BBC / American Cable News Network)

title: Japan to reopen commercial whaling land scholars: the United States to attract "firepower" is the best time
text:
At 14: 01 on December 31, 2018, Yang Jiaxin pointed out that Japan has recently announced that it will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and resume commercial whaling in July next year.
Shu Jun, a researcher at the Japan Studies Center of Overseas Studies University in Shanghai's "Surging News", pointed out that although it is feared to have a negative impact on its international image, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.
Among them, there are elements of the whale-eating plot of the older generation of Japanese, as well as factors that politicians and local whaling industry interest groups transfer interests and carry each other.
Coupled with the "retreat" wave set off by the United States, has attracted international public fire, Japan believes this is the best time to withdraw.
Shanghai "surging news" published a Sujun article pointed out that for Japan, international coordination is its post-war repair and enhance the international image of an important link, in order to reopen commercial whaling and even withdraw from the international organization inevitably gives people the impression that it will have a negative impact on its international image.
But even so, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.
In the post-war era of scarcity, whale meat once again became the main non-fish meat source on the Japanese table, and whale meat dishes even appeared in free lunches for elementary school students paid for by the Japanese government.
However, today, Japan ’ s social economy has developed, whale meat is no longer irreplaceable, and many young people have never even eaten whale meat, but some older Japanese who lived in the 1950s and 1960s still occasionally miss it.
The article pointed out that, on the other hand, the real demand for whale meat in the Japanese market is very limited and shrinking, and it is better to say that the Japanese government is trying to maintain the existence of the whaling industry than to say that it is the Japanese people who cannot give up the taste of whale meat.
The Japanese government is doing this mainly out of domestic political considerations.
A whaling county-born politician who wants to stand out from his constituency as a member of Congress must look after the interests of whaling industry interests.
For example, Japan's current prime minister, Shinzo Abe, was born in Yamaguchi Prefecture, a whaling prefecture.
The article said that the reason why Japan chose to withdraw at this time should be that the ruling Abe government believes that the current international environment is the best time to withdraw.
The "retreat" of the United States, the growing anti-refugee wave in Europe, and the Brexit of the United Kingdom show that anti-globalization has risen.
There is everywhere "retreat" of the United States to attract international public opinion "firepower", Japan "homeward" withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission, in addition to the media rhetoric and criticism of individual politicians, Western countries may find it difficult to put any substantial pressure on Japan.

title: Brexit is on the verge of a surge in the number of people crossing the sea to test British border controls
text:

British Border Agency agents inspect what they have discarded.
Soon after Brexit, a large number of stowaways in small rubber dinghies flooded from the European continent to England.
At the request of the Home Secretary, the Royal Navy and the Air Force sent aircraft and warships to help resolve the crisis.
Once the formal Brexit, both Britain and the EU will no longer be bound by the Dublin Agreement, which originally defined refugee ownership, but the UK may find it difficult to repatriate any influx of migrants to the EU.
The 2019 New Year holiday has been a rough ride for Home Secretary David Javid: he ended his holiday in South Africa early and rushed back to London to discuss the crisis of stowaways arriving on British shores by boat from the sea.
The UK plans to leave the EU by the end of March 2019.
The BBC ’ s investigation found that the group tricked refugees who had arrived in the Calais region of France to “sell tickets for the last chance to sneak into the UK in front of the UK ’ s closed border gates ”.
Stowaways who board a small rubber dinghy to get to Britain pay a fee of £6,000.
They rode in small rubber dinghies that the British border radar could not see.
The shortest distance from Calais, France, to the British coast in the English Channel is only 33.3 kilometers, so how many people come by boat from mainland Europe?
No one knows the exact number.
However, on New Year ’ s Eve 2019, the number of illegal immigrants suddenly increased significantly.
Why in the coldest, the English Channel wind and high waves when risking life and death to smuggle people? The reason is still related to Brexit!
Image copyright @ premarmanche Image caption Britain and France have stepped up efforts to crack down on smuggling across the Channel.
A small boat was stopped off the coast of France.
Under the Dublin Agreement, refugees arriving in the EU must be registered in the country they first arrive in.
Although they are all under the EU agreement, the treatment and even development prospects of refugees vary from country to country.
Britain has begun to worry that once Britain leaves the EU, there will be no reason for Britain to return refugees from the continent to their original EU countries, whether France, Spain, the Netherlands or other EU countries, according to the principle of first arrival.
After urgent consultations, the British Home Secretary ordered that the two ships involved in the search and rescue project in the Mediterranean Sea be sent back to the English Channel to intercept the smugglers along with the border ships already patrolling the Channel.
But the Home Office is feeling overwhelmed.
Home Secretary David Javid said the deployment of the Royal Navy and Air Force was the only way to avoid the tragedy of the sudden death of so many refugees at sea.
The British defense secretary immediately sent the Mersey coastal patrol ship, the Royal Air Force aircraft to help solve the problem of refugee smuggling.
Javid said Britain would continue to deliver on its promise to give asylum to those in genuine need, but would not allow criminals to exploit the system to exploit the most vulnerable.
Who are the stowaways?
According to the BBC, from November to December 2018, more than 239 people successfully crossed the English Channel in rubber boats from coastal locations such as Calais, France, where refugees are concentrated.
This includes women and children.
Most of those arriving in Britain by rubber boats are from the Middle East, such as Iran.
Javid said the reasons for the sudden increase in the number of people trying to sneak into Britain by dinghy were complex, including the turmoil in the Middle East, organized crime operations and Britain's efforts to prevent stowaways from travelling to Britain by truck, train and ferry.
Many of them will come to the police and ask the British government for asylum.
Although these people will be detained by the police, the British side will always need to provide basic humanitarian guarantees to these refugees, especially the children among them.
Although France has promised to help strengthen the fight against illegal immigration in the English Channel, the departure of illegal immigrants from France does not appear to have caused any pressure on French society.
How many people are currently applying for asylum in the UK?
The United Kingdom grants "refugee status" to those who are unable to live in their country because of fear of persecution on various grounds, such as race, religion, nationality, political opinion or sexual orientation, and provides the basic necessities of living, food, shelter and welfare, as well as cash assistance.
Successful applications usually allow applicants to stay in the UK legally for five years, after which they can apply for permanent residence in the UK as long as they meet the conditions such as no criminal record.
The applicants include those who arrived in Britain by rubber boats, but also stowaways who arrived in Britain by ferry, truck and other means.
According to the Home Office, in 2017, the Home Office received more than 26,000 asylum applications.
This is a small number compared to the number of asylum applications received by other large countries in Western Europe during the same period: 198,000 in Germany, 126,000 in Italy and 91,000 in France.
The EU has been critical of Britain over the number of refugees it has received.
In the same period, the Home Office issued more than 21,000 applications, and granted 31.8% of them asylum needs.
At the end of 2018, more than 24,500 people in the UK were waiting for the Home Office to approve their asylum applications, of which 42% had been waiting for more than six months.
Most asylum seekers rejected by the Home Office go to court. In 2017, out of more than 14,000 asylum applications rejected by the Home Office, more than 5,000 were approved by court decisions, meaning that the Home Office ’ s initial refusal to approve was overturned.
Image copyright Lewis Morris Image caption A large number of migrants, many of them Iranians, have recently arrived in Britain by boat from France.
It is noteworthy that the number of illegal immigrants from China to Britain, which attracted attention more than a decade ago, has been greatly reduced in today's refugee influx.
More than a decade ago, many Chinese people smuggled into Britain through Russia and Europe. The deaths of 58 stowaways in the port of Dover in 2000 and 23 scavengers in Merkham Bay in 2004 reflect the problem of a large number of illegal immigrants from China sneaking into Britain more than a decade ago.
The British government has also stepped up its efforts to crack down on illegal immigrants and illegal workers in the wake of the Merkham Bay tragedy, but due to the high appeal of Britain's welfare social and humanitarian policies to war-torn and economically backward areas, the problem of illegal immigration in other countries is still very serious.
The top 10 countries with the largest number of asylum seekers are Syria, Eritrea, Sudan, Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh and India.
Most of the stowaways who enter the UK find it difficult to repatriate if their asylum claims are rejected. In 2016, the British government spent a huge amount of money to repatriate 6,000 foreign criminals.
Britain has a population of 70 million, but there are huge numbers of illegal immigrants, including stowaways and people who have overstayed their visas in the UK illegally.
On the one hand, these people's work income, welfare and even human rights are difficult to be guaranteed, such as being exploited by people's groups, and on the other hand, they live in society to increase the invisible pressure on the British system of free medical care, education and other systems, and the crime problem that a few people breed has caused serious losses to society.
How many illegal immigrants are there in the UK?
There are no accurate official figures, and no one seems to be able to tell.
In 2001, the Home Office estimated the number of illegal immigrants in the UK at around 430,000.
A 2017 report in the British “Guardian ” quoted senior Home Office officials as saying that 150,000 to 250,000 foreigners leave the UK each year without due dates, including 26,000 who were denied asylum applications in 2016, and more than 1.2 million people may be living in the UK illegally.

title: France to implement action plan to prevent migrants crossing the English Channel
text:
Paris, January 5, 2019 (AFP) The French government announced today that it will use a "plan of action" to counter migrants attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK, pledging to end the phenomenon, which the British Conservative government fears.
The increase in asylum seekers across the sea, mostly Iranians, has put pressure on the British government to respond, with Home Secretary Sajid Javid declaring it a “major event ”.
French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner said in a statement today: "This project should allow us to put an end to the sea crossing," adding that these actions are not only illegal but also extremely dangerous.
"It is in our interest and that of the United Kingdom to do everything possible to prevent the development of new networks that would again attract irregular migrants to our shores," the statement added.
The plan will increase police patrols near ports where some migrants try to steal boats and monitor beaches where rubber boats have been deployed.
In addition to four British coastal patrol vessels, a British naval vessel was also patrolling the English Channel today.
A spokesman for French maritime operations in the region told AFP this week that France had doubled the number of coast guard vessels in the Channel depending on the weather.

title: Taiwan Beauty and Medical Tourism Launches Ministry of Health and Welfare to Establish a Promotion Team Wang Zhengkun to Provide Practical Advice
text:
▲ Dr. Wang Zhengkun was invited to participate in the Beauty Medical Tourism Launching Conference, with Lin Dai (middle) and Liu Yueh-ping (right) of the Ministry of Health and Welfare. (photo / photo by Lin Yue-fan) Reporter Lin Yue / Tainan reported that the Ministry of Health and Welfare held the Beauty Medical Tourism Launching Conference on January 7. The Tourism Bureau, the Taiwan Society of Dermatology, the Society of Plastic Surgery, the Society of Aesthetic Surgery and other related units have jointly discussed how to successfully promote medical tourism in Taiwan.
Dr. Wang Zhengkun attended the meeting on behalf of the Taiwan Society of Dermatology and put forward suggestions based on practical experience, hoping to expand the number of hospital clinics to participate in, reduce barriers to promote and create a national brand of beauty and medical tourism in Taiwan, so that the supply chain of beauty and medical tourism can reach foreign end consumers, that is, foreign patients can know about medical beauty and tourism in Taiwan.
Taiwan ’ s medical technology surpasses Singapore, but the value of medical tourism has long been lost to Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia and South Korea. Foreign patients who go to Asia for medical treatment will choose the above countries first, but will not choose Taiwan.
Dr. Wang Zhengkun is a dermatologist. He served as president of the Medical Laser Photonics Association of the Republic of China and president of the Greater Tainan Tourism Alliance. He is currently the director of the International Association for the Promotion of Medical Health.
Legislator Lin Dai-hua, referring to the opinions of the participants, asked the Ministry of Health and Welfare to set up a "beauty medical tourism promotion group" to deal with the promotion of matters, and carry out inter-ministerial integration, hoping that foreign guests will come to Taiwan in large numbers, Taiwan's medical treatment will be sold to foreigners in large numbers, and Taiwan's economy will flourish.
The meeting resolved to select model medical institutions, simplify the content and certification process of aesthetic medicine certification, make it easy for legal clinics to pass the audit, expand clinic participation, relax international medical advertising regulations, establish an international medical dispute mediation mechanism and invite relevant medical associations to provide suggestions.
Dr. Wang Zhengkun said that the international medical programs are comprehensive, including acute and severe diseases, disease treatment, health examination, medical aesthetics, and dental aesthetics.
Medical tourism in Taiwan has been planned in various departments, but it has not been able to attract foreign patients to the door because of the supply chain, the entire industry supply chain can not reach foreign patients.
In the past 10 years, hospitals, clinics, travel agencies and government departments have developed many programs, perhaps because of the lack of marketing in Taiwan, foreign patients are a little unfamiliar to Taiwan's medical reputation, and no foreign agents are willing to bring a large number of patients to Taiwan for treatment.
Wang Zhengkun said that although Taiwan's hospitals and clinics are ready, they have not seen a large influx of foreign patients into Taiwan.
Therefore, to learn the success factors of other countries is a key point, Korea's medical beauty can successfully develop, is to use the power of the whole country in the world to market medical beauty, film, form a culture, expand international advertising, in-depth life, deeply rooted in the hearts of the people, Korean medical beauty marketing strength, breadth and depth are tens of times that of Taiwan, so that foreign patients talk about medical beauty think of Korea.
Then, Korean hospital clinics and agents around the world to form a supply chain, negotiate cooperation conditions, agents from various countries to bring foreign patients to South Korea, this implementation of the concept of supply chain management, in order to really contact foreign patients, in order to bring foreigners into the country for consumption.
If beauty medical tourism can be developed, it is not only medical institutions that benefit, but the entire hotel accommodation industry, transportation industry, tourism industry, and private consumption can be greatly improved.

title: Xindian Qiaoren Park to create a pocket park in the hearts of residents with participatory budget
text:
The Qiaoren Park in Xindian District, due to the old game facilities and the difference in the height of the trails, provides a safe and convenient recreational space, and cooperates with the participatory budget concept, so that residents and children can jointly plan a special park.
Through the improvement works, in addition to updating the amusement equipment, the access line has also adopted barrier-free design to provide a more diverse recreational environment.
Located near the intersection of Chiao-Ren Road and Chiao-Xin Road, the game facilities in the park are too old and do not meet safety regulations.
In order to provide a safe and convenient recreational space for the public and children, the Xindian District Office has promoted the concept of “Participatory Budgeting ” to allow community residents and children to participate in the design of the playground and plan their own pocket park.
According to the public office, this game is designed to climb the game facilities as the main axis, and then with swings, bars, etc., where the climbing game equipment can test, train children's sense of coordination, space, and learn how to protect themselves in play.
In addition, the playground also features a "jump house" game and adds a jump color change to the floor mat, so that friends and small can enjoy the space and play together.
District Governor Lin Huangyuan said that the initial design was to allow the public to participate in the regeneration of the playground through the holding of street game activities and park game park workshops.
According to statistics, the climbing and swing type of play equipment were the first and second choices of the children. Therefore, when designing the park play equipment, the climbing and swing type of play equipment was added to the terrain to create a distinctive neighborhood park.
Through this improvement project, in addition to the addition of amusement equipment, Qiaoren Park will also be the game field into and out of the barriers friendly design, so that the park is no longer a simple green space, to provide a more diverse recreational environment.

title: No medical care, no medical care, no teeth.
text:
2019-01-29 17: 36 World Daily Compilation / World Daily Compilation 28 Days For many Americans who do not have medical insurance, Vicente Guerrero, a small Mexican town adjacent to California, is the first choice for medical tourism. Among them, there are more than 350 dentists in the area. Get glasses or buy cheap medicines.
The Mexican town is named after the former president of the same name, Los Algodones, or Molar City, because of the large number of Americans visiting the town.
People who travel to Mexico often do not have insurance, and they can see a dentist, plastic surgery, glasses or buy medicine in Guerrero for a relatively small amount of money.
Visitors to the clinic can enter Mexico by car, or they can park in a parking lot for as little as eight yuan a day, walk through the customs, enter the city of Agodones, Mexico; Americans can bring many items to enter Mexico through this checkpoint, but the inspection will be more stringent when returning to the United States.
Guerrero is only four blocks old, but this mini-town is home to 350 dentists, as well as plastic surgeons, optometrists and pharmacists.
Winter is the busiest season in Guerrero. During an earlier visit by Business Insider photojournalist Andrew Waits, he found that some dental clinics had a two-line phone in response to a large number of appointments.
Hospitality tourism drives the local economy, with restaurants, bars, hair salons and accessories stores, and local mobile vendors are also able to sell baskets, hats, jewelry or cheap jewelry to people waiting to see a doctor.
Grello ’ s main industry is health care, and the dental industry supports the development of five other dental laboratories, including crown, implants and other dental hardware.
Dental implants and artificial crowns are the most common dental procedures and can be completed on the same day, Wes said. Even custom dental equipment can be made and installed in a patient ’ s mouth in just a few hours.
Purple Pharmacy is one of the most popular pharmacies in Guerrero. Brokers take to the streets to buy cheap prescription drugs without prescription.
The U.S. – Mexico border is littered with purple drug stores ’ distinctive purple shopping bags, and people sometimes complain about buying counterfeit drugs, while the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is concerned about a significant number of Americans going to Mexico to buy drugs.
There is a travel agency in Arizona that specializes in helping people go to Mexico for medical treatment. The staff of the travel agency said that there are many dentists in Guerrero, and it is best to do homework before you can buy high-quality services.
“Many career projects are very modern and clean, but there are also ones that seem to be idle for weeks, ” says Wes.
Mexico labor and real estate are not expensive, the cost of dentistry is relatively low; the government subsidizes dental education, and few dentists are in debt once they graduate, so the fees are lower.
The cost of cleaning teeth in Mexico is about 30 yuan per time, the root canal treatment is 200 yuan, the artificial crown is set at 300 yuan, and the cost of dental implants ranges from 1200 yuan to 1700 yuan. Many patients are frequent visitors to Guerrero, and they are very satisfied with the medical services in Mexico.

title: Ukrainian Airlines passenger plane crashes into Iran, Ukraine president confirmed dead – Radio France Internationale
text:
KIEV, May 8 (AFP) Ukrainian President Leonid Zelensky confirmed the death of all passengers and crew on board a Ukrainian International Airlines Boeing 737 that crashed shortly after takeoff from Tehran, the capital of Iran.
In a Facebook post, Volodymyr Zelensky mentioned the crash of Ukraine International Airlines, which was scheduled to fly to Kiev.
"According to preliminary information, all passengers and crew were killed," he wrote.

title: South Korea 's beauty trend is burning "kindergarten girls go to school with makeup", children' s beauty is a positive and negative debate
text:
South Korea ’ s beauty trend is burning to kindergarten girls.
(Photo / Courtesy of Instagram / w.chaeeun _ mom) The international center / roundup report Yang Huizhi, a seven-year-old South Korean girl, developed the habit of getting up early when she started kindergarten in 2018.
In addition to checking her uniform and homework, makeup is also her daily routine before she goes to school.
“Make-up makes me look beautiful, ” she said on her second visit to ShuShu & Sassy Children ’ s Beauty Spa in Seoul.
She was wearing a child-sized pink bathrobe and a rabbit hair band, her cheeks were gently touched by pink, and her lips had a pink glow.
The Washington Post reported on the 16th that the South Korean beauty industry, known as K-beauty, has become a superpower in Asia and a global phenomenon in recent years, but the stringent beauty standards have also brought huge pressure on women, making South Korea one of the world's largest cosmetic countries, and the age group of beauty industry target customers is getting lower and lower.
This is a worrying question that touches on many of South Korea ’ s core social issues, including how much society values appearance, whether the desire to look is squeezed out of other dreams of young girls, and whether it should add more stress to children in a life that is already tense, with long school hours, and full of exams.
▲ Girls go to beauty parlors to make up. (Photo / Courtesy of Instagram / sson.c) Yin Kim Ji-yen, a female athlete and former professor at the Institute of Body Culture at Jianguo University in Seoul, said, “The bright and beautiful cartoon heroines that young girls adore are made up of cosmetics from head to toe. ”
When they make up and wear similar clothes and imitate the characters in the play, they think deep down that women ’ s success is closely related to beauty. ”
Advertisers are also driving the trend, with an ad for a beauty group for 6-year-olds saying, “I look at my mother and follow her. ”
Today I grew up ", and a girl in a uniform is rubbing her lipstick.
In addition, a YouTube video titled “I Want to Make Up Like My Mother ”, where a seven-year-old girl rubs her lipstick, has attracted 4.3 million views, and other similar videos, such as little girls sharing their daily makeup steps and“ Hello Kitty Cosmetics Set Out of the Box ”, are popular.
Shu Shu is a pioneer in the promotion of children ’ s cosmetics, operating 19 boutiques across South Korea since 2013, focusing on “healthier ” cosmetics for children, such as water-soluble nail polish and non-toxic lip gloss pencils, which are colorful and even edible, as well as sticker earrings and tattoos, sunscreen cleansers, soap called“ Pretty Girl ” and goat ’ s milk shampoo, It says, “I am not a child. ”
▲ Children ’ s beauty parlors can apply makeup, peritoneal membranes, etc. (Photo / Courtesy of Instagram / leeeunhee0219) Girls between the ages of 4 and 10 can enjoy a spa experience that costs $25 to $35 (about NT $770 to 1077), including foot baths, foot and calf massages, masks and cosmetics, as well as nail and foot treatments. Grace Kim, manager of u Shu, said, “Our company ’ s motto is that we want children to be able to communicate with their mothers when they play with them.
Our products are also safe for pregnant women. ” The report noted that this trend in children ’ s cosmetics is not unique to South Korea.
American celebrity Kylie Jenner has built a $900 million cosmetics empire with a focus on teenage girls, and children ’ s beauty bloggers are popular in the United States and around the world. ShuShu has also expanded into Singapore and Thailand, with plans to expand to the United States and beyond.
Scholars of all stripes have studied the effects of stress on adolescents and young women in the West for decades, which requires them to follow unreasonable standards in terms of appearance and size.
But in South Korea, these ethnic groups are getting younger, and they can ’ t even read the text on cosmetics packaging.
(Photo / Courtesy of Instagram / min _ 041211) South Korea is one of the world ’ s top 10 beauty industry giants, with an output value of more than $10 billion, according to market research firm Mintel. A Gallup survey showed that South Korea has one of the highest plastic surgery rates in the world; one-third of women aged 19 to 29 claim to have undergone plastic surgery. They also have a large number of eyelids.
According to a 2017 survey by the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery, South Korea also has the highest number of plastic surgeons per capita in the world.
As makeup is promoted as a “new game culture ” for children, the children ’ s beauty market is expanding, according to Lee Hua-jun, a South Korean beauty industry expert.“ As potential new consumers, South Korean cosmetics companies are becoming more interested in children. ”
He noted that relatively small startups are leading the trend, and that cosmetics giants have expressed interest in expanding their customer base to younger women, but are carefully weighing the pros and cons because targeting children could trigger a backlash.
In fact, many women have countered this trend of children's makeup.
Xu Jialan, a liberal makeup artist, said on Facebook that she would refuse all requests to make up for children's models. "I think it is strange that the makeup group has replaced the toys that children play with."
Please stop looking at pictures of children with red lips and curly hair. "
However, Kim Joo-teh, a professor of cosmetology at Seoul ’ s Honest Women ’ s University, said the trend was hard to stop as the media increasingly showed photos of young girls making up, as well as makeup products available to children under the age of 10.
He surveyed 288 primary school girls in 2016, and found that 42% of them had a makeup habit, and the proportion is increasing year by year.

title: Ukrainian passenger plane crashes in Iran, no one survives
text:
According to information obtained so far, the Boeing 737 belonging to Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) suffered a technical failure.
The rescue team said on television that the plane was on fire before it crashed.
Rescue organization Red Crescent failed to find survivors.
Ukrainian President Leonid Zelensky said on Twitter that according to existing reports, all passengers and crew on board were killed.
He has appointed a crisis management committee.
The plane, designated PS752, caught fire shortly after takeoff at 5: 00 a.m. local time and crashed into a wilderness near Khomeini International Airport in Tehran.
The plane was supposed to land in the Ukrainian capital of Kiev on Wednesday morning.
The air crash comes amid heightened tensions amid heightened military conflict between the United States and Iran.
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has banned all U.S. aircraft from flying through parts of the Middle East after Iran launched a missile attack on Iraqi military bases.
The agency said in a statement that "due to increased military activity and increased political tensions", the risk of misidentification of aircraft has increased, so all US-registered aircraft are not allowed to enter the Persian Gulf, Amman Gulf, Iraq and Iran airspace.
Lufthansa also canceled flights from Frankfurt to Tehran on Wednesday.
Boeing, the aircraft manufacturer, said it was verifying all clues about the technical failure.
The company tweeted: "We are aware of media reports from Iran and are gathering more information."
The plane was not part of the 737 Max that caused the Boeing crisis.
The aircraft has had two crashes.

title: Xi Jinping sends condolences to Iranian President Hassan Rouhani on Ukrainian passenger plane crash
text:
Iranian National News Agency (IRNA): On January 9, 2020, President Xi Jinping sent condolences to President Zelensky of Ukraine and President Rouhani of Iran on the crash of a Ukrainian passenger plane in Tehran.
In a message of condolence, Xi Jinping said that he was shocked to learn that a Ukrainian passenger plane crashed in Tehran, killing all passengers and crew. On behalf of the Chinese government and the Chinese people, and in my own name, I would like to express deep condolences to the victims of various countries and express sincere condolences to the families of the victims.
On January 8, local time, all the people on board the Ukrainian Airlines Boeing 737 crashed after taking off from Khomeini International Airport in Tehran, the capital of Iran.
About three minutes after takeoff, Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752 crashed.
The plane, which was supposed to be flying from Tehran to Kiev, was carrying about 170 people, including a large number of Iranian citizens, as well as some holidaymakers in Iran.
The aircraft was a Boeing 737-800 that was delivered in July 2016 and is only 3.6 years old.
According to FR24, everything was normal during the climb, but at an altitude of about 2400 meters, the aircraft suddenly lost its ADS-B signal.
A spokesman for the Iranian Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) confirmed that all the people on board the Ukrainian Airlines flight were killed, including 167 passengers and nine crew members.
The cause of the crash may have been a technical failure.
A spokesman for Tehran's Khomeini International Airport said it would release the passenger list information as soon as possible.
Kassim Bisi, head of the Communication and Information Center of the Iranian Ministry of Roads and Urban Construction, said on the 8th local time that a Ukrainian Boeing 737 passenger plane fell from Tehran shortly after takeoff because of engine failure caused the body to fire, if the plane fell because of being hit by a missile, the body will certainly explode in the air.

title: Ukraine Airlines plane crashes in Tehran, killing 176
text:
(Wired News) A Ukrainian International Airlines Boeing 737-800 crashed shortly after takeoff in Tehran, the capital of Iran, killing all 176 people on board. The authorities have recovered the plane's black box and are investigating the cause of the crash.
The plane crashed in a farmland in southwest Tehran, many places were on fire, and the scene was full of flames; there was still smoke at the scene after daylight, and passengers' luggage, parts and debris were scattered everywhere; a large number of rescue workers and officials rushed to the scene and transported the bodies of the victims.
Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752, which took off from Tehran Khomeini International Airport at around 6: 00 am on Wednesday, was scheduled to go to Kiev, the capital of Ukraine, but lost signal a few minutes after takeoff and crashed about 10 kilometers from the airport.
Iranian state media quoted transport officials as saying that one of the engines caught fire after the plane took off, suspected to be a mechanical failure, and the plane lost control and did not send a distress signal. Two flight recorders, commonly known as black boxes, have been recovered.
Ukraine International Airlines lobbyists passed the routine inspection two days before the accident, the aircraft was more than 3 years old, and the experienced pilot decided to immediately stop the flight to and from Tehran.
All 167 passengers and nine crew members were killed, including 82 Iranians and 63 Canadians, and 11 Ukrainians, most of them transiting through Kiev.
The Boeing 737-800 is a third-generation NG series of 737 aircraft. Qantas discovered at the end of last year that three of its 737NG aircraft had structural cracks and needed to be stopped for maintenance. As for the upgraded version of NG and the fourth-generation MAX series, two large air disasters have also been involved in recent years.

title: SpaceX successfully launches manned space capsule
text:
On Saturday, space exploration technology company SpaceX launched its first crew Dragon, a critical flight to prove to NASA the safety of astronauts in future flights.
The mission, called Demo-1, was launched on a Falcon 9 rocket from the Kennedy Air Center in California.
This space capsule does not carry a human, but a model of an astronaut called Ripley, wearing sensors to measure various indicators of the human body in the space capsule.
This is the first of two SpaceX test flights under NASA ’ s Commercial Crew Program. Demo-2 will be the first to fly with a human pilot, scheduled for July of this year.
According to NASA ’ s plan, SpaceX will be the first company to send astronauts into space since 2011.
NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine later stated that the successful launch marked a new chapter in American excellence, bringing us once again closer to carrying American astronauts from American soil on American rockets.
Since the retirement of the Space Shuttle in 2011, the United States has been unable to use its own rockets to transport astronauts to space on its own. NASA is working with private companies to develop the future of human spaceflight.
Currently, SpaceX and NASA have a contract value of $2.6 billion, and Boeing is $4.2 billion.

title: SpaceX Dragonfly 2 successfully connected to the International Space Station
text:
SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon, also known as Dragon 2, successfully connected to the International Space Station about 400 kilometers above New Zealand ’ s northern Pacific Ocean on Sunday with a dummy model.
Dragonfly 2 was launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Saturday with a Falcon 9 rocket, carrying only a dummy model that simulates what happens when a real astronaut takes off.
The launch was the first time in eight years that the United States had flown a domestically built spacecraft to the International Space Station.
After NASA pulled out of the US Space Shuttle program in 2011, astronauts could only travel to the International Space Station on a Russian spacecraft, allegedly costing US $82 million (about HK $640 million) per astronaut round trip.
Dragonfly 2 will depart the International Space Station on Friday and is expected to land hundreds of kilometers off the coast of Florida in the Atlantic Ocean.
(Roundup)

title: Shade / Woman 's face is exposed like a steel bar
text:
The face of a woman abroad is exposed like a steel bar 2019-03-05 11: 05 United Daily News reporter Xiu Ruiying / Immediately reported that a Taiwanese woman went abroad to receive a buried wire skin, hoping that the face is tight, and the foreign doctors' wire burying skills are not good, resulting in the face surfacing long thick lines, and the face is like a steel bar exposed, and like a train rail.
Women seek help from Dr. Wang Zhengkun, former president of the Medical Laser Photonics Association of the Republic of China. Dr. Wang calls for full communication with doctors, understanding of the side effects, and signing an informed consent form before receiving treatment, and do not be deceived by medical aesthetics marketing terminology.
Wang Zhengkun said that in recent years, South Korea has achieved great results in promoting medical beauty and medical tourism to the world, and Asian countries are not willing to let go of it.
Taiwanese girls are also attracted by foreign advertisements, buying air tickets to countries with more developed economies than Taiwan, accepting foreign doctors to bury lines and skin, but the foreign moon is not much round, and the Taiwanese woman's face is almost disfigured.
He said that foreign doctors use too thick lines, causing skin absorption difficulties, and tying several thick lines in the cheeks, causing the skin of the cheeks to protrude, and a thick line surfacing on the left side of the mouth, when laughing, the whole line floats on the face, as if the steel bar is exposed or the railway track, and the face is strange, which makes the woman ashamed to meet.
Wang Zhengkun ’ s treatment for this side effect is to open a hole in the skin, look for the position of the thick line, pull the whole thick line out, and let the woman ’ s appearance recover.
Recently, the media also greatly reported that a patient spent 100,000 yuan in Taiwan to pay for skin care, and the result was that his face was uneven like the surface of the moon, and his mood was extremely stressed.
Wang Zhengkun said that to prevent sunken scars, do not tie the skin too tightly, do not tie the face as uneven as zongzi, and reserve "remedial measures".
For buried wire, it is safer to choose "absorbable material", and it is necessary to use the legal wire approved by the Ministry of Health and Welfare. Doctors and patients should not be too greedy, do not deliberately choose a very thick wire to pull more tightly, very thick wire is difficult to absorb, in case of body rejection, and buried too shallow, it will be like a steel bar exposed.

title: Herbicide cancer-causing controversy again: whether China's manufacturing and agriculture will be affected
text:
Image copyright AFP Image caption A large amount of pesticides are sprayed in Argentina's soybean fields.
A jury in the United States has ruled that the ingredients of one of the world's most commonly used herbicides are a "key factor" in causing cancer in a man.
What impact does this have on mainland China and Taiwan?
But German chemical and pharmaceutical giant Bayer has strongly denied claims that its Monsanto unit, Roundup, which makes glyphosate ingredients, causes cancer.
But a jury in San Francisco ruled unanimously that the product caused California resident Edwin Hardman to develop non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
The next phase of the court trial will consider the issue of damages and liability for Bayer products.
At this stage of the trial, Hardman ’ s lawyers are expected to provide evidence of Bayer ’ s efforts to influence scientists, regulators and the public ’ s perception of the safety implications of its products.
After the news came to light, Bayer's share price plunged about 12 percent.
1,200 related cases In 2018, Germany's Bayer company bought US rival Monsanto for $66 billion, and Monsanto's product Roundup was also part of the acquisition.
Bayer said it was disappointed by the ruling.
The company will present evidence of the safety of Monsanto ’ s products, as well as a strong belief in scientific proof that glyphosate-based herbicides do not cause cancer.
The case is only the second of about 1,200 lawsuits against Roundup in the United States.
In August 2018, a California court jury found another California man was awarded $289 million in damages because Roundup caused his cancer.
The ruling in the case at the time also caused Bayer's share price to plummet.
The case was later reduced to 78 million dollars, and Bayer is still appealing the case.
As an agricultural power, China, GM and Roundup have become the largest producer and exporter of glyphosate in the world, and are also one of the largest users of glyphosate.
More than half of glyphosate produced in China is exported, including the Roundup herbicide that Monsanto manufactures and distributes globally.
At the same time, China also imports a lot of processed glyphosate.
According to statistics, Roundup products account for 80% of herbicide products in China.
Glyphosate use and consumption are mainly concentrated in some agricultural countries, especially large countries that produce genetically modified crops.
There are thousands of glyphosate pesticide products in mainland China.
In Taiwan and Hong Kong, there are also Roundup sales, which in Taiwan is translated as “Spring of the Year ”.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Monsanto's popular glyphosate product Roundup sells worldwide.
In Taiwan, its translation is Spring of the Year.
What is glyphosate and is it dangerous?
Glyphosate is a herbicide invented by Monsanto in 1974, but its patent expired in 2000.
It is currently the highest selling pesticide in the world.
In 2015, the World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) concluded that glyphosate "may be carcinogenic."
However, the EPA insists that careful use of glyphosate is safe.
The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) also said glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer.
However, due to the excessive use of glyphosate, improper spraying of glyphosate has a lot of incidents that directly lead to human poisoning.
In addition, glyphosate has been found in rain, rivers, agricultural products, food (including beer, bread, etc.), meat products and human bodies, leading to an international campaign against the use of glyphosate.
In November 2017, the European Union decided to extend the license for glyphosate use for five years.
California lists glyphosate as a chemical known to cause cancer.
But the agricultural industry is opposed to putting such a label on glyphosate.
