In 2015, the World Health Organization ’ s International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) concluded that glyphosate “may be carcinogenic. ”
However, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency insists that it is safe to use glyphosate sparingly.
The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) also said glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer.
However, due to the excessive use of glyphosate, improper spraying of glyphosate has a lot of incidents that directly lead to human poisoning.
In addition, the presence of glyphosate in rain, rivers, agricultural products, food (including beer, bread, etc.), meat products, and humans has led to the international movement against glyphosate use.
In November 2017, the European Union decided to extend the license for glyphosate use for five years.
California lists glyphosate as a chemical known to cause cancer.
But the agricultural industry is opposed to putting such a label on glyphosate.

title: Behind the news: The United States mistakenly believed that the enemy aircraft shot down the Iranian aircraft ｜ News ｜ Asia Europe ｜ on.cc Eastern Network
text:
The Persian Gulf War began on Wednesday when a Ukrainian passenger plane flying from Iran crashed in Tehran, killing 176 people.
Iran initially claimed an engine failure, but the military admitted Saturday that it was hit by a missile, stressing that it was a human error.
In the past, there have been a number of international incidents in which civil aviation aircraft were shot down in the war zone, and now there is one more.
On July 3, 1988, during the Iran-Iraq War, the Iranian Airlines IR655 Airbus A300 was shot down in Iranian waters by a missile fired by the U.S. Navy Aegis cruiser Vincennes while flying from Bandar Abbas, Iran to Dubai, UAE, killing all 290 passengers and crew members on board.
The Iranian government accused the U.S. military of deliberately shooting down the aircraft, but Washington argued that the warship mistakenly recognized the aircraft as an Iranian F14 fighter that was carrying out an attack mission, and shot it down.
On November 22, 2003, an Airbus A300 cargo plane of the international transportation company DHL was attacked by Iraqi militia with shoulder-mounted missiles after taking off from Baghdad International Airport, the Iraqi capital, and lost hydraulic pressure on its left wing.
The crew adjusted the engine to stabilize the fuselage and landed safely at Baghdad International Airport, resulting in no casualties.
Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 On July 17, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 crashed from Amsterdam, Netherlands to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, near the Russian border in eastern Ukraine, killing all 283 passengers and 15 crew members.
A four-year investigation claimed that the plane was shot down by Russian-made missiles from pro-Russian rebels, but Russia denied the conclusion.
On January 8, 2020, the Ukrainian Airlines PS752 crashed into a fireball shortly after takeoff from Tehran, Iran, becoming the first aviation accident in the history of Ukraine.
All 176 people on board were killed, including several Canadian and Iranian citizens.
Iran once claimed that the plane was wrecked due to engine problems, but the United States and Europe accused Iran of shooting down the plane.
The Iranian military finally admitted responsibility after three days, stressing that it was unintentional.

title: Monsanto Herbicide Carcinogen Lawsuit Finds $2.5 Billion
text:
SAN FRANCISCO, March 27, 2019 (AFP) A US jury ruled today that Monsanto, a subsidiary of Bayer Group, should pay US man Hardiman $81 million (about NT $2.578 million) in damages.
Hardiman claimed that Monsanto's herbicide "every spring" caused his cancer.
Edwin Hardeman, 70, was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma after regularly using the herbicide from Monsanto, an agricultural biotechnology company, in his yard in Sonoma, California, between 1980 and 2012.
A San Francisco jury found that Monsanto “failed to exercise reasonable care ” by failing to warn about the risks of the product and ordered Hadiman to pay $75 million in punitive damages, $5.6 million in damages and $200,000 in medical expenses.
The jury previously found that Hardiman ’ s exposure to the herbicide for more than 20 years was a “significant factor ” in his development of non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma.
The main ingredient is the controversial chemical Glyphosate.
“Monsanto ’ s actions clearly show that the company is not particularly concerned about whether or not its products actually cause cancer, but is focused on manipulating public opinion and suppressing anyone who has genuine legitimate concerns, ” Hardiman ’ s lawyers Aimee Wagstaff and Jennifer Moore said in a joint statement.
In the United States alone, the case is one of more than 11,200 similar lawsuits involving herbicides in the spring of this year.
Monsanto has always denied that spring is a cause of cancer, a company previously bought by Germany's Bayer Group for $63 billion.

title: A female passenger called her husband 20 minutes before takeoff.
text:
20 minutes before the flight PS-752 took off, the wife called her husband, and it turned out to be the last conversation between the husband and wife.
Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) flight PS-752 crashed in Iran on the 8th, when a female passenger, Sheyda Shadkhoo, suddenly had an ominous feeling, so she called her husband 20 minutes before the flight, hoping that the other side would calm her uneasiness.
In the end, all the passengers were killed in the crash, and her husband was devastated.
According to foreign media reports, Sheida flew back to Iran to visit her family on the 8th, and was preparing to fly back to Canada to reunite with her husband, but she suddenly felt an unusual feeling before taking off, so she called her husband for comfort.
Husband Hassan Shadkhoo said, “I promised her that there would be no war, don ’ t worry that nothing will happen. ”
Hassan said his wife mentioned to him on the evening of the 8th that US President Donald Trump ’ s killing of Iranian military general Qassem Soleimani has caused tensions between the two sides to rise and worried about what will happen in the future.
The plane crashed shortly after take-off, killing 176 people on board. Husband Hassan was deeply saddened and saddened to hear the news.
Hassan mentioned that his wife had a feeling that the plane would crash and was worried that she would no longer be able to take care of her family, so she posted a selfie on Instagram, writing, “I ’ m leaving, but I ’ m worried about the people who stay. ”
Hassan described his wife as an angel who could not imagine life without her. “I wish I didn ’ t exist now. ”
Iran originally refused to hand over the black box to Boeing or the United States, but on the 9th changed its attitude and formally invited the United States National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) to participate in the investigation of the Ukrainian Airlines plane crash, and the NTSB agreed to send investigators.

title: Jane Jacobs, The Birth and Fall of a Great City, Introduction: Vitality is the basic condition of a great city, and it is also the highest state.
text:
A Woman ’ s View on Everyday Life and User Perspectives: The Human Dimension of Body Space, Use of Participation, Street Life, and Organic Order Although Jane Jacobs has not received academic training in orthodox urban planning and landscape architecture, she does not cite difficult theoretical terms to build large and complex urban narratives; However, she tried to cut into the organic perspective of urban life and living cities, criticizing the blueprint urban planning process in the United States from the end of the 19th century to the time, the planning principles of predictive development and zoning control, and the leveling urban renewal methods in the United States in everyday language that people can understand and the actual cases of American cities.
At the same time, she also proposed some planning and renewal principles that can ensure the fun and economic vitality of urban life.
In fact, the principle of planning and renewal outlined by Jane Jacobs is a simple one: to see how real cities work from the perspective of urban physiology.
From her experience of living in Greenwich Village, New York, and reporting on many cases of urban renewal in the United States, she summed up a simple truth: cities need a complex, elaborate, and diverse way of using land that supports each other economically and socially.
Only in this way can urban planning enhance the vitality of the city and promote the convenience of urban life.
Otherwise, it will be futile to plan only for the appearance of the city without thinking about the inherent functional order of the city.
In the book, Jane Jacobs describes the specific meaning of a living city from four aspects: the importance of street neighborhoods in urban life, including safety, social contact, parenting of children, and the use of neighborhood parks, and then proposes a specific concept of urban neighborhoods; and the four conditions necessary to generate urban diversity, including a mix of different primary and secondary uses, small streets, old buildings, and dense populations. Essential elements of economic vitality; key elements of urban decline and regeneration, including the self-destruction of diversity, the problem of border vacuums, the myth of slum removal and the way money is spent; and several tactical applications that bring cities back to life, including how to subsidize housing (rather than build national housing), how to effectively use cities to clamp down on cars (rather than allowing them to erode them), and how to build cities The orderly visual order in the chaos (rather than the monotonous and repetitive geometric order), how to lay a concrete strategy for urban self-reconstruction on the existing basis (rather than a flattened stove), and the structural problems of urban planning and urban renewal in the administrative organization.
Finally, Jane.
James stressed that we must treat cities as an organism of complex order, and address the complex problems of urban planning with the social engineering of life sciences, rather than as simplified two-dimensional variable relations or unorganized complex problems, so that we can give life and vitality to cities and make them a sustainable environment for human collective life.
These views of Jane Jacob have important theoretical implications.
First, it represents the “body-city-space ” discourse of the everyday user perspective of urban residents, especially from the urban neighborhood perspective where the gender roles of women and mothers are the starting point.
In short, Jane.
Jacob tries to build a dynamic urban neighborhood concept with street life at its core.
The streets of the city, especially sidewalks and walkable neighborhood parks, may seem like an environment full of strangers on the surface, but through proper use, especially commercial and recreational facilities that can meet the needs of the basic neighborhood, it attracts a lot of effective public surveillance and physical participation, creating a lively and interesting “street ballet ”.
With lively street life, not only can we effectively protect the safety of urban streets without the use of police force, but also can form the basic structure of an urban neighborhood through the continuous reproduction of urban public life, including social interaction that effectively maintains personal privacy and street games that foster children into society.
This kind of street life is the best place to build mutual trust and care and teach children about social life lessons: even if people are not related by blood or friends, people have to shoulder some public responsibilities to each other.
This use of participation and local identity embodied by actual physical experience is the most lacking "human scale" of rational planning from the top down and based on hardware construction.
The scale of human nature here is not blindly advocating the scale of "small is beautiful", but emphasizing that the construction of the urban environment should pay attention to the relationship between people and people and the environment: a good city with vitality must be a living city that can make all citizens feel convenient and comfortable, which is the basic condition of a great city, and it is also the highest state.
This, in turn, has forced us to revisit the role of neighborhood parks and neighborhood neighborhoods, which are relatively important to the elderly, women and children, in modern cities.
Traditional planning theory believes that more open space and neighborhood parks are the only way to improve the quality of the urban environment, but in real life, neighborhood parks can only function if they have a rich, interesting and safe street life and are constantly used by people.
The same goes for streets, shops, schools, etc., all of which are important places to practice neighborhood relations.
What ’ s more, an urban neighborhood is a dynamic and open social relationship, not a fixed and closed geographical boundary.
Urban populations are mobile, so urban neighborhoods have no starting point or ending point to define them as a distinct unit.
Even in the same place, it can be different for different people.
The value of the city lies in the wide selection and rich opportunities!
Therefore, to plan a good city must also return to the fundamentals of people, that is, to pay attention to the human scale of the city, rather than sticking to the place and space.
Jane Jacobs identified three types of urban neighborhoods that come alive: the city as a whole as a gathering place for a community, the neighborhood as a concrete manifestation of the territorial community, and the neighborhood as a collective mobilization of community consciousness.
These different types of urban neighborhoods have different functions, but complement each other with extremely complex relationships.
Through these dynamic networks of open connections between different urban neighbourhoods, the basic characteristics of modern urban life are demonstrated - the multi-mixed institutional network: modern urbanites live in a multi-dimensional world that spans different geographical boundaries at the same time.
This is the charm of urban life and the source of vitality of the city.
This is an important issue that traditional planning theory needs to face up to, and it is also the theoretical core of the book "The Birth and Fall of Great Cities" - diversity is the basic value of great cities: on the one hand, it can meet the different living needs of urban residents, on the other hand, it also needs to establish the planning principles of street life and mixed use.
Just as biodiversity is a necessary condition for the stable development of an ecological system, demographic, commercial, social, cultural and architectural diversity is also a key element in sustaining urban life.
Specifically, building urban diversity requires what I call a regional strategy of “diversity integration. ”
In short, in order to ensure the diversity of mixed use, a vibrant city must try to have at least one or two main uses of the area within the city, to ensure that people will go out to the streets at different times and for different purposes, and use the various public facilities on the streets.
Second, the area should try to maintain the spatial shape of the small street, so that there are more opportunities and changes in the corner.
At the same time, it is also necessary to mix buildings of different ages and conditions as much as possible. In addition to creating a detailed and varied architectural landscape, it is also possible to find suitable places for various needs.
Finally, there must also be a sufficiently dense population, including a simple residential population, so that many different needs can be met within a reasonable walking distance.
In other words, Jane.
Jacob's claim to urban diversity is not a hodgepodge of mixed uses.
Instead, she advocates a pluralistic integration between primary and secondary uses that can support each other.
Therefore, mixed use is not chaos and disorder, but a complex and highly developed organic order.
Like all organic life, there is absolutely no pure geometric order of straight lines, circles, right angles, perfect symmetry.
The order of the city should also be like the beauty of life, a dynamic, approaching vitality, not a rigid, mechanical order.
The latter is the biggest problem with land-use zoning as the main tool of urban planning.
Architectural and planning scholar Christopher Alexander, in a classic article entitled “A City is Not a Tree ” published in the Architectural Forum in 1965, called the concept of land-use zoning a tree-like planning thought, a mechanical order that lacks intersections between events and spatial patterns.
On the contrary, real urban life is a semi-lattice relationship of complex order, and there are many possible intersections and rearrangements between elements and systems, which is also where the value of cities lies.
Therefore, good urban planning should be able to strengthen the possible relationships of the semi-lattice, rather than limit the diversity and vitality of the city by using rigid patterns of tree branches.
However, cities also have a number of self-harming problems, including: the tendency of highly successful diversity to self-destruct; the barrier of boundary vacuums created by large-scale single elements within cities; the tendency of slums to self-regenerate and counteract the growth of diversity due to demographic instability; and the tendency to have too much or insufficient public and private funding for reconstruction to hinder development and change.
Without these considerations, even the best planning for a city ’ s vibrancy can be doubly effective.
From these negative factors, Jane Jacobs summed up the renewal and development of the city: the need to avoid the drastic pattern of large-scale leveling and development, but the need to adopt a piecemeal, organic and gradual model.
When a mixed use of diversity becomes very successful in a location within a city, the fierce competition for space will naturally unfold in that location.
If left to its own devices, as is the case with fashion, one or two of the most profitable uses tend to be copied over and over again, suppressing and crowding out other less profitable forms of use.
From then on, the site will become more homogeneous and monotonous, and gradually abandoned by people who come for other purposes of use.
Preventing overreplication in one place and then channeling its power of diversity to other areas can be improved through diversity zoning, anchoring of public buildings, and competitive migration.
Photo Credit: Shutterstock / Dazhi Image Located in Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York City, their vacuum-filled borders often have a destructive blocking effect when large single-use areas such as large parks, schools, hospitals, administrative centers, and even pedestrian walkways occur within the city.
Looking at the most buzzing places in the city, we will find that these lucky places rarely fall in the vacuum of the adjacent boundary.
The fundamental problem with borders is that they can easily form dead corners and obstacles in the streets.
However, this does not mean that these institutions and facilities are to be considered enemies of the city.
On the contrary, cities need universities, large medical centers, large urban parks, etc., but we need to encourage these institutions and facilities to expand their use of their boundaries, such as removing walls, or setting up suitable facilities or interesting scenery in these peripheral locations – rather than hiding them, then these boundaries will become seams, not barriers.
As for the rehabilitation of slums and the renewal of shabby areas, the urban renewal policy of the time attempted to break the chain of this vicious cycle by directly eliminating slums and removing their populations, and replaced it with large-scale housing projects to reclaim the urban middle class and generate higher tax revenues.
In the best case, this will simply move the slums elsewhere; in the worst case, it will destroy neighbourhoods that can actively improve themselves.
On the contrary, Jane.
We need to understand, respect, and build on the regenerative power that exists in the slums themselves to create a lively, vibrant, and safe neighborhood where those who can pursue a better life are willing to stay and improve their living environment, that is, the gradual self-diversification of the population itself, and other cities that generate diversity. Conditions also occur naturally.
Cities do not need to “bring back ” the middle class, the city itself will produce a middle class.
It is only when the middle class is growing that a self-diverse population needs to be maintained as a form of stabilizing force, and they often bring the slums back to life in the most insignificant way, which is the inner resource needed to remove the slums.
At this time, how the government and the private sector use reconstruction funds has a very significant impact on the success or failure of urban renewal, which is a key force in urban decline and regeneration.
Of course, money is not a panacea, and when the basic conditions for success are lacking, money cannot buy the necessary way for a city to succeed.
And when the real conditions needed to succeed are broken, money can do more damage.
This is exactly the secondary damage of large-scale flattening urban renewal: the concentration of flood funds into a region, bringing drastic changes to the region, causing multiple self-destruction, and even many funds flowing not into the city, but into the periphery of the city.
This is certainly not a constructive way to nourish the city.
The endless suburban sprawl of American cities is no accident.
The way money is spent must be transformed from violent measures that flood and flood into gentle, slow and gradual changes that can have a positive impact on local diversity and bring about the springs of life that cities need for stable growth.
Jane Jacobs went on to propose actionable tactics to deal with the traffic problems and visual disturbances that plague many large American cities.
This tactical operation of the view of life in recent years has gradually been paid attention to by the British and American academic circles, its four or two thousand jin of clever response is often better than the costly strategic layout (strategies), for the freezing of three feet is not a day of cold urban problems, but easy to produce the grand effect of reversing the situation.
From this perspective, in the process of urban planning and urban design, problem setting may be a more fundamental core issue than problem solving.
For example, we often complain that too many cars cause traffic problems in cities.
However, how much of the damage that cars bring to cities is really caused by the demand for transportation and transportation, and how much is caused by the lack of respect for the needs, uses and functions of other cities?
Cities are a lot of choices.
To have multiple choices, you have to be able to walk around easily.
If multiple mixtures are not stimulated, then multiple options will not exist.
In other words, cars (or other means of transportation) are the means to solve urban transportation needs, not the end of urban life itself.
To solve the congestion, pollution, accidents, and energy problems caused by cars (or other means of transportation), it is necessary to go back and explore why modern urban life has to spend so much time and effort traveling between homes, workplaces, shopping places, and leisure facilities scattered across different places.
Photo Credit: Shutterstock / Dazhi Image Due to the period of mass adoption of automobiles, coinciding with the development of suburban expansion, in the stages of construction, social, legislative and financial development, we have turned the automobile into a scapegoat for this reason.
So the question is how to adapt to the transportation needs of the city without destroying the diversity and concentration of land use.
Oversimplifying the urban problem into a problem between pedestrians and cars, and using the separation of people and cars, and even various vehicles to solve the city's traffic problems in their own way, is a wasteful approach, which will only deepen the vicious cycle of cars eroding the city, resulting in the disintegration of the city, rather than saving the city.
The traffic problems of the city are inseparable from the diversity, vitality and concentration of urban uses.
The key is how to reduce the absolute number of vehicles and make all vehicles more efficient.
At this time, using cities to clamp down on cars may be a pragmatic way to effectively reduce the number of cars, while stimulating the efficient construction and use of mass transit systems, and to promote and adapt to denser, more dynamic urban uses.
Similarly, in the face of turbulent urban landscapes, urban design often tries to find a way to express the “skeleton ” of the city clearly and simply.
It seems to Jacob that this is all about fishing.
Because the real structure of a city is composed of mixed use, when we are exposed to the conditions that produce diversity, it is the closest to its structural secrets.
Only complex and dynamic use can give the proper structure and shape to the various parts of the city.
This is the basic order that urban design can make the effort.
Whatever the outcome of this order, the intricate urban life must be achieved by the tactics of emphasis and implication, which are the main means of artistic communication; the tactics we need are to be able to help people create for themselves hints of order and meaning from what they see.
All these different tactics of grasping the visual order of the city are concerned with the fragmentary things in the city, and the fragmentary things woven into the continuous use and uninterrupted organization.
This is the basic way of urban life, and this is the city itself.
Their intricate order shows the interconnectedness of countless people in the formulation and execution of countless plans that underpin the economic advantages, social vitality and attractiveness of cities.
The planning of a dynamic city must aim at clarifying the visual order of the city. It must promote and illuminate the functional order, not hinder or reject it.
To achieve this, planners must diagnose the missing elements that can produce diversity in a given place, and then provide what is missing.
Finally, Jane.
James raises a fundamental question as the conclusion of the book: What is the nature of the city?
Mainstream urban planning theory has a habit of imagining a city as an unorganized complex system that needs to be organized “rationally ” by urban planning, that is, planning and designing cities in a two-dimensional way of thinking and analysis, such as the relationship between open space and population size.
Even with the later introduction of new techniques for investigation and statistical forecasting, there is no substitute for simplified thinking about two-dimensional variables.
Jane Jacobs believes that urban planning as a field of expertise has stagnated compared to life sciences or other fields.
It ’ s scary, but I don ’ t see any progress.
For Jane.
For Jacob, the biggest problem is that urban planning has not always understood and treated cities as organized, complex systems.
This means that urban planning should see the city as a living organism, understand the mechanism of urban operation from a physiological point of view, think about the content and process of urban life, and then try to master these key things.
This is the only way that urban planning and urban design can bring life and vitality to cities.
This view is very similar to the Gaia theory of the British scholar James Lovelock: from the mechanism of the various life support systems on Earth, it is like a living organism.
However, considering a city as a complex organism does not mean that urban planning and life sciences are facing the same problems, and they cannot be viewed under the same microscope.
But the tactics needed to understand and solve these two problems are similar: they both require thinking simultaneously about the complex relationships between individual cells, organs, systems, and entire organisms.
In other words, Jane.
According to Jacob, what is lacking in urban planning today is an in-depth understanding of urban life and urban processes. Planners ignore the seeds of self-regeneration in dynamic, diverse, and dense cities, which are the eternal ways in which urban planning must flourish.
It is worth mentioning that the concept of the city as an organism took on a new development after the 1990s.
That is to think of the city as a cyborg that combines nature, machinery and humans. It is an urban environment built by humans collectively in order to adapt to the natural environment and thus use various mechanical and man-made facilities.
This view echoes Donna Haraway ’ s exploration of the new human condition in the rapidly changing science, technology and gender relations of the late 20th century.
It seems that urban planning will have to do more to keep up with the new environment.
Jane Jacobs, The Birth and Fall of Great Cities: Without Old Buildings, Cities May Not Develop Vibrant Streets Book Introduction This excerpt is from The Birth and Fall of Great Cities: Inspiration for the Life of American Urban Streets (Classics of the Century, New Straight Line Review Edition), published jointly.

On April 25, 2006, the CBS, The New York Times, The Washington Post and other major media outlets in North America reported on the death of an old woman without a college degree and a "professional" background.
This is her first book, but also a famous work, a complete subversion of the European and American planning theory of the classic. When it was first published in 1961, it was deeply rooted in the hearts of the people with a simple and understandable view.
From the perspective of urban physiology, this book points out that the planning and reconstruction of cities are the first to understand the mysteries and complex ways of operation of cities, as well as the real life of urban people.
The first part of the book summarizes the importance of street neighborhoods in urban life from many real-life cases.
The second part focuses on the general principle that cities need a very complex, detailed and diverse form of land use that supports each other economically and socially from time to time.
This is also the core of the author ’ s argument.
The third section makes recommendations on housing, transportation, design, and planning, and discusses the various problems cities face in dealing with organizational complexity.
In the end, it is emphasized that the city must be viewed as an organism with a complex order, and the complex problems of urban planning must be handled with the social engineering of life science, so that it can give life and vitality to the city.
This is the basic condition of a great city, and it is also the highest state.
Otherwise, only the appearance of the city planning, without thinking about what the city has inherent functional order, is doomed to failure.
Starting from the concept of a “living city ” such as the street life of a neighborhood and the diversity of business and culture, the book emphasizes that only a“ human scale ” of diversity and diversity can create a “ordinary and great city. ”
In 1996, the New York City Library selected "The Good Book of the Century", along with Weber's "Protestant Ethics and the Spirit of Capitalism", Keynes's "The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money", and Weber's "The Idle Class Theory", among other books, as one of the "economic and technical" books of the 20th century. One of the most important books.
This book features the story of the rise and fall of American cities in simple words and practical examples of life.
The foundation of the thesis is based on real urban life, and with these specific life experiences, the mainstream planning and architecture theory of the 20th century to reflect on and criticize.
Seeing the city as a living organism and understanding how it works from a physiological point of view helps to reflect on how urban planning fits seamlessly into the lives of citizens.
The “mixed use ” diversity strategy explored in this book reminds readers how to make good use of existing valuable city assets to create a magical city of life.

title: Ukraine passenger plane crashes, Iran denies missile downing – Radio France Internationale
text:
TEHRAN (AFP) - The head of Iran's civil aviation organization today denied that a missile shot down a Ukrainian passenger plane, refuting Western claims that Iran's anti-aircraft missiles were mistakenly fired.
Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed shortly after takeoff from Tehran, Iran, killing all 176 people on board, most of them Iranian and Iranian-Canadian citizens, but also Ukrainians, Afghans, British and Swedes.
International pressure continues on Iran for a “credible ” investigation.

title: China to promote artificial solar project to master clean energy technology
text:

The advanced experimental superconducting tokamak experimental device is part of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) program.
The International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor Project, funded and operated by seven members of the European Union (EU), India, Japan, China, Russia, South Korea and the United States, aims to prove the feasibility of nuclear fusion energy.
The use of nuclear fusion for power generation is the holy grail of energy development.
Unlike nuclear fission, nuclear fusion does not emit greenhouse gases, and the risk of accidents and theft of nuclear raw materials is low.
But to achieve nuclear fusion is not only extremely difficult, the cost is also astronomical, the total cost of the international thermal fusion experimental reactor project is estimated at 22.5 billion US dollars (about NT $695.4 billion).
Wu Songtao, a senior Chinese engineer of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor Project, admitted that China's technology in nuclear fusion still lags behind some more advanced countries, such as the United States and Japan's Tokamak have achieved more valuable overall results.
However, the test nuclear fusion reactor in Anhui highlights China ’ s rapid catch up in scientific progress and its commitment to further progress.
Wu Songtao said that China's strength "has leapt forward in the past 20 years, especially after catching the ITER high-speed train."

"Face Time" "Opener" new column "Korean Stream Daily", easy to read the current Korean stream problems, and you to make a "knowledge meal".
Story Outline "The Age of Faces" tells the story of a very ugly male middle school student who is often bullied by other classmates due to appearance problems such as looks and body shape.
One night, his soul suddenly runs away and awakens to find himself in the body of a handsome man.
If he sleeps in the body of a handsome man, the soul will return to its original body.
So, he lived a life of "handsome by day, ugly by night", a soul and two bodies.
Because his identity is unknown (he has no family or friends), he left his hometown to study at an art school.
Because it looks good, I encountered a completely different treatment in school than before.
The left side is the original appearance of the male protagonist, and the right side is the appearance of the soul after the change. ("Face Time") The content realistically reflects social problems This comic book is so popular for several reasons.
First, be realistic.
South Korea is a "superstitious" society.
This comic is a reflection of this phenomenon.
Many people who have seen it have said, "The appearance is really so important, and I want to see it."
Second, the protagonist ’ s mood changes very well.
In the early days of the handsome man's life, the male protagonist's heart is still very inferior and cowardly.
But after the stage of adaptation and growth, he gradually became a confident and courageous person to face himself.
Third, bring out a lot of social issues.
Through the experience of the male protagonist, many problems faced by Korean society, such as juvenile delinquency, young people running away from home, etc.
Cartoon writer (right) Park Tae-joon himself is also a big handsome "appearance supremacist" formation of Korean pop star popularity in recent years has also been very high around the world.
In addition to singing, dancing, singing and other musical skills, even the appearance is "perfect".
With the development of information technology, smartphones have become the main tool for the public to receive information, and the mass media have continuously reported and promoted these Korean celebrities who are perfect in all aspects through the Internet.
The so-called appearance supremacy, that is, the first condition of doing anything is to "appearance" first.
Many Korean pop stars have been criticized by the public because of their appearance, such as the captain of TWICE, Wendy of Red Velvet, and the strict wisdom of GFRIEND.
The world's first cosmetic surgery country wants to plastic surgery, the first place to think of must be South Korea.

According to a 2013 survey by American Biweekly magazine, 62% of South Korean women surveyed said they had had a facelift.

Attaching a photo of yourself to your resume is not a necessity in Hong Kong.
However, if you do not do this when applying for a job in Korea, no matter what industry you are applying for, almost no company will hire.
On the other hand, in 2017, South Korean TV station SBS even revealed that a university professor directly criticized the appearance of students in an interview: “You seem to be quite fat, do you eat a lot? ”
Most secondary schools in Hong Kong, regardless of age, have banned the use of makeup in their schools.
But if you travel to South Korea, you can see that most of the Korean middle school students are wearing school uniforms and makeup.
According to Korea Expose, 73.8% of middle school students have used cosmetics.
More seriously, many Korean parents even give their children the “cosmetic treatment ” as a gift to encourage them to change their appearance.
Last year's popular Korean drama My ID is Gangnam Beauty reflected this phenomenon.
The heroine has been teased since she was young because she was ugly, and her mother told her to "make a big change" before she entered college in order to regain her confidence.
"My ID is Gangnam Beauty" The pursuit of appearance style is getting younger In addition to the psychology of the flock, in fact, the mass media in South Korea are constantly spreading this awareness.
The current Korean pop stars are getting younger and younger, such as Zhang Yuanying, who took the No. 1 spot in last year ’ s “PRODUCE 48 ”, only 14 years old.
In front of the camera, she often has to show people with gorgeous makeup.
And she has a similar age of middle school students, over time has also been infected with this pursuit of beauty consciousness.
In addition, many Korean dramas with the theme of school life, such as the recently popular "A-TEEN", include many students in the school makeup picture.
As the trend of "greed and beauty" is getting younger and younger, the mass media does have to bear a lot of responsibility.
"A-TEEN" often features the heroine "Duhona" with lipstick.
And after each application, someone asked: "Lipstick is beautiful, where did you buy it?" (A-TEEN) How about plain face?
In June 2018, a Korean beauty YouTuber “Lina bae ” posted a video titled“ I ’ m not pretty. ”
She shows off her plain face at the beginning of the video, and then starts putting on makeup.
During this time, the film continued to criticize her appearance.
Finally, she chose to erase the heavy makeup, smiled and showed her face, and said, "I am not beautiful."
But it doesn ’ t matter if it ’ s not beautiful.
“Don ’ t bury your true self because of the words of others. ”
After the video was released, it was supported by many Korean girls.
Everyone responded to the “Take Off the Clothes Campaign ” by uploading photos of cosmetic damage and plain face photos to social networking sites to protest the phenomenon of Koreans judging people by their looks.

title: 〈 North 〉《 Bamboo County 》 Bamboo 25 Park Fountain is idle for the rest of the year
text:
2019-05-24 [Reporter Liao Xueju / Zhubei Report] There is a fountain in the center of the 25th Park in Zhubei City, Hsinchu County. It was originally a well-intended hydrophilic design, but it has not been sprayed for more than a year.
According to the public utilities section of the county government's International Industrial Development Office, the park was opened by the county government's Public Works Office in the Shih Hsing area of the county government in early 2017, and was sprayed with water for a while, but later received reports from the public that there were safety concerns about children playing with water and adults not watching. It was decided to temporarily shut down the water fountain.
Tsai, a representative of the citizens of Zhubei, said that the fountain at the center of the Children ’ s 25th Park at the intersection of Shih Hsing 3rd Street and Jiaxing 1st Street had a good view of the city ’ s waterfront, but somehow, he had not seen the water spray in more than a year; the whole water fountain occupied half of the park, and garbage was easy to be thrown in the reservoir.
In addition, the fan-shaped grassy and concrete spaces of the park, which currently do not have trees or seats, have become an unusable area, reducing the overall utilization rate of the park.
Tsai said that in recent years, counties and cities have actively created "special inclusive parks", and have diversified game facilities and fitness and recreation equipment to replace the original "plastic canned" amusement equipment, such as bamboo city central park, Miaoli cat park or Taoyuan city Fenghe park.
In addition to increasing the public entertainment venues and improving the utilization rate of public land, the park can also promote the development of nearby businesses, and even benefit the surrounding housing prices, which can be said to be low investment and high efficiency.
Zhubei Children 25 Park clearly needs to be improved, and the relevant units should consider the overall plan.
It will coordinate with the public office for a limited time to spray water or rebuild the public affairs section of the county government's International Industry Development Office, said that there are 201 parks in Chuanzhubei City, and the Zhubei City Public Office has taken over 157 of them, and is actively striving to take over all of them for overall planning.
Therefore, in the near future, the county government will coordinate with the public office to include the 25th child in the review, with the direction of integration and participation of citizens, to evaluate the use of limited time for water spraying or reconstruction of other facilities.

title: Unyielding brilliance
text:
Leslie M. M. Broome, in the ending of the story “All Paris Belongs to Me ” about Hemingway ’ s youth living in Paris, describes Mrs. Poolette Ashley in Hemingway ’ s“ The Sun Always Rises ” – a member of the tour group Duff who also went to Spain with Hemingway to watch bullfighting. Mrs. Twiston, quoting the poet Banner ’ s portrayal of Duff, who had tuberculosis and spent the last days of his life in a nursing home.
Share facebook Under Hemingway ’ s pen, Lady Paulette Ashley in “The Sun Also Rises ” is a“ model of unbridled charm, and will never grow old ”; Duff in life, also as unbridled as Leslie sketched, would rather give up the title of aristocratic lady and pursue the life she wants.
Although fate did not care for her in the end, she kept her strength of defiance until the end of her life, and the body that had been thought of by writers had been “as thin and weak as a wind-dried seahorse ”, but still maintained its“ unyielding brilliance. ”
As the spokesperson of the "Lost Generation", Hemingway fell into a low ebb after his great success, and his new work was ridiculed.
Unlike many people who find it difficult to be brilliant after success, Hemingway soon returned with The Old Man and the Sea, a novel that won him not only the Pulitzer Prize, but also the Nobel Prize in Literature.
In the past, we used to call Hemingway ’ s end of his life “suicide ” — a cowardly act in the eyes of the world — but, to paraphrase resistance fighter, Auschwitz survivor, and Austrian writer Jean Emery, it ’ s called“ suicide. ”
"The cause of free death (self-death) is not disease... free death is the prerogative of human beings", "voluntary death is the right of man to act according to his own standards, which cannot be denied by the outside world, and is the greatest freedom of man".
Emory also chose to “die by yourself ” two years after the publication of his last book,“ Walk Alone to the End of Your Life. ”
His trilogy, including the other two, Beyond Sin and Punishment: The Difficult Attempt of a Riot, and The Philosophy of Aging: Resistance and Abandonment, both shine with this “unyielding brilliance ” in the face of fate.
To paraphrase Bodleian, it is “not a slave to time. ”
Unyielding brilliance, Susan Sontag is also very apt to describe after breast cancer.
Daniel Schreiber describes in his book Susan Sontag: Spirit and Charm that in 1975, at the age of 42, she was diagnosed with terminal breast cancer during a routine physical examination, and doctors estimated that she would only live for half a year and have a 10% chance of surviving for two years.
After an initial panic, Sontag had his breasts removed and went through five more surgeries.
The cancer left visible marks on Sontag ’ s exterior — some of her hair fell out during chemotherapy and grew white — and her “dark hair, with a strange gray hair on her forehead, became the ‘ iconic look ’ for Americans for the next 20 years. ”
Of course, looks alone can ’ t be an “iconic look ”.
In 1998, at the age of 65, Sontag developed cervical cancer.
After the surgery, Sontag woke up and said, "I want to work."
During her second time with cancer, Sontag wrote a foreword for a series called Women, where she kept talking, reading, watching movies, finished her novel In America, and even began to learn to play the piano — “It ’ s only 24 hours a day, but I ’ m trying to deal with it for 48 hours. ”
Nearly 30 years after she was first discovered and fought cancer, Susan Sontag ’ s battle with the disease ended.
The disease eventually defeated her, but the idea and image of Santagna's eternal "great dissident", in the field of political culture, and her spirit of fighting the disease, remained forever in the world, which the disease could never defeat.

title: World's Largest Aircraft May Be Sold - Air Force
text:
Less than a year after the death of Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, the Stratolaunch Systems company he set up nearly a decade ago could face a permanent shutdown.
According to Reuters and The Drive, multiple sources familiar with the matter, but who requested anonymity, Vulcan Inc., which Allen founded to fund the stratospheric launch system, and many other projects, will sell all of its physical assets and intellectual property.
However, the world ’ s largest plane, nicknamed the “roc, ” made its maiden flight on April 13, and 65-year-old Allen died of cancer last October.
Following his death, Vulcan announced in January that it was canceling a series of space launch vehicles, including a reusable space plane codenamed “Black Ice. ”
For years, the stratospheric launch system has been associated with billionaire Richard Branson ’ s Virgin Galactic, Blue Origin of Amazon, founder and CEO Jeff Bezos, the world ’ s largest e-commerce company, and SpaceX, the electric car maker Tesla CEO Elon Musk. Parallels.
As the demand for launching satellites is increasing, they all want to make money by providing such services.
In addition, they also want to get involved in space travel.
With a wingspan of more than 117 meters and six engines on board, Dapeng is at the heart of the stratospheric launch system business strategy. In August 2018, the company said that the medium-lift rocket was expected to take off as early as 2022, and that it was initially developing a larger payload aircraft.
Allen once said that he had long dreamed of space. When he founded the Stratospheric Launch System in 2011, he said, “I dream of being an astronaut. ”
However, his poor eyesight ruined his dream of flying.
However, Allen also said that his ambition for space travel has not disappeared.
Just three months after Allen ’ s death, the Stratospheric Launch System announced in January that it would give up building rockets but would still work on large aircraft.
However, in December, the company had 77 employees, and by April 1, it had only 21 employees.
Most of the remaining employees are committed to completing the first test flight of "Da Peng".
Sources said Allen ’ s sister, Jody Allen, decided at the end of last year to develop an exit strategy, and she is not only the chairman of Vulcan, but also a trustee of the Paul G. Allen Trust.
She decided to let the big plane fly for the first time, in order to fulfill her brother's wishes and prove that the big plane and related concepts are indeed feasible, but later decided to turn off the stratospheric launch system.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: The late Alan Space Dream Broken sister takes over the company ’ s “world ’ s largest aircraft ”
text:
Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, who died on October 15, 2018, said in 2011 that he had a dream of space. Although myopia does not allow him to be a pilot, he has never forgotten his dream of exploring space.
However, Stratolaunch Systems, the aircraft manufacturer he founded in the past, is facing a crisis of termination and may never see their “world ’ s largest aircraft ” again in the future.
Alan was very active in developing the world ’ s largest aircraft.
Stratolaunch, the world ’ s largest aircraft with the longest wingspan, successfully flew in California in mid-April, aiming to complete the idea of carrying a medium-sized rocket on the aircraft and launching it from the air into outer space by 2022, Reuters reported.
But a number of insiders recently revealed that parent company Vulcan Inc. is planning to sell Stratolaunch, ending its dream of entering space.
The world ’ s largest aircraft flew successfully in California on April 13.
(Photo / Reuters) Since Allen died last year, Stratolaunch ’ s operations have gradually stopped, and employees have shrunk from 77 to 21, and they have moved to other aerospace companies.
Allen ’ s sister, Jody Allen, is the chairman of Stratolaunch ’ s parent company, Vulcan Inc., and the executor of Allen ’ s estate. She was planning to take over Stratolaunch last year, and later flew the world ’ s largest aircraft in memory of her brother.

title: Japan to resume commercial whaling green organization table regret
text:
Japan Resumption of Commercial Whaling Green Organization2019-06-12 17: 31 Taiwan Awakening Reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that commercial whaling was banned in 1986, but Japan has deliberately avoided continuing whaling under other names.
Japan has decided to resume commercial whaling from July this year. Although Japan joined the International Whaling Commission and has not conducted commercial whaling for more than 30 years, there have been occasional reports of whaling under other names.
Greenpeace expressed regret over Japan ’ s unilateral decision to restart commercial whaling.
Japan joined the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in 1982 and stopped commercial whaling in 1986, according to the British Independent.
According to local media reports, from July 1 this year, five Japanese fishing vessels will hunt beaked whales in the local waters for a period of two months, and then go to the northeastern waters of Japan to catch minke whales.
Japan is currently not allowed to hunt cacao in international waters.
According to statistics, from November 2017 to March of the following year, Japan hunted 333 minke whales in the name of scientific research, of which 122 were pregnant females.
Even with the resumption of whaling, local demand for whale meat has reached a record low.
In the 1960s, about 200,000 tons of whale meat were eaten each year, but the current size is only 5,000 tons, and the industry employs about 1,000 people.
“Our oceans and their ecosystems are threatened by rising sea temperatures and acidification due to climate change, industrial fisheries and plastic pollution, and whales are also greatly affected by bycatch from climate change, plastic pollution, oil exploration and industrial fishing, ” said Kudo Takada, director of Greenpeace Japan.
According to Stuff, Japan announced its withdrawal from the IWC in December last year, when Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga said that the resumption of whaling was in line with Japan ’ s basic policy of promoting the sustainable use of marine living resources based on scientific evidence.
The resumption of whaling will take place only in Japan ’ s territorial waters and 323 kilometers of exclusive coastal waters, not in the Antarctic and the Northwest Pacific, where most research has been done in the past.

title: Unexpected Beneficiaries Global warming makes rich countries richer
text:
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Global temperatures are rising, but the impact on countries is not the same.
For half a century, climate change has increased inequality among nations, slowed development in the poorest countries, and seemed to have made some rich countries more prosperous, according to a new study.
Researchers at Stanford University in California say that the gap between rich and poor countries has widened, with more than 25% contributing to global warming.
Tropical African countries were hardest hit, with GDP per capita in Mauritania and Niger growing by 40 per cent less because of warming.
"Global warming is responsible for more than 25 per cent of the widening gap between rich and poor countries."
The International Monetary Fund predicts India will grow to become the world ’ s fifth-largest economy this year, but the study says India ’ s per capita GDP is 31% lower than in 2010 because of global warming.
For Brazil, the world ’ s ninth-largest economy, the figure is 25 percent.
On the other hand, an article published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences writes that warming appears to be making a positive contribution to GDP per capita in some rich countries, several of which are the world ’ s leading emitters of greenhouse gases.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Nigeria is also seeking international assistance to combat the effects of climate change (Credit: Getty Images) The cost of warming Marshall Burke is a professor in the Department of Earth Sciences at Stanford University and a member of the research team.
He spent years studying the relationship between temperature and economic fluctuations in 165 countries between 1961 and 2010.
His study used more than 20 climate models to analyze how much human-caused climate change has affected individual countries ’ temperature increases, and then used 20,000 methods to calculate how much each country ’ s annual growth rate would be without rising temperatures.
Studies have shown that in warmer than average years, the growth rate of countries with lower temperatures will accelerate, while the growth rate of hot countries will slow down.
"Historical data clearly show that when the temperature is not high or low, the crop yield is higher, the people are healthier and the work efficiency is higher," he said.
He believes that the temperature rise has given cold countries the "warming benefit", while the temperature in hot countries is far away from the ideal temperature, and has been punished by the "warming penalty".
Study leader Noah Diffenbaugh said: "The effect of temperature on economic activity is in all its aspects."
“Agriculture, for example.
Winter has limited crop growth in cold countries, but there is also ample evidence of significant declines in crop yields during high temperatures. "
"Similarly, people's productivity decreases at high temperatures, their cognitive abilities deteriorate, and their conflicts increase."
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Sixteen-year-old Greta Thunberg, an environmental activist, inspired teenagers around the world to launch an environmental campaign (Credit: Getty Images)
Researchers say it ’ s hard to say what benefits climate change has brought to colder, richer countries; but historical data has shown how hotter countries will be affected.
If we set the starting point for climate change as the beginning of the industrial revolution, we will find that its effects are even more far-reaching.
“We have always known that climate change will double the threat, that already serious problems will bear the brunt of it and that the already dangerous situation will worsen, ” said Happy Khambule, senior political adviser at Greenpeace Africa.
In other words, the poorest and most vulnerable countries are the first to suffer from climate change.
Addressing the increasingly severe climate impacts, developing countries will come at the expense of their own development, he said.
Similar severe problems may soon become the norm after a 2015 heatwave killed thousands in India and Pakistan (Credit: Getty Images) Mozambique ’ s apparent lack of response to Hurricane Kenneth, which has killed more than 40 people since the cyclone caused mudslides on April 25, Cabler added.
In March, Hurricane Idai killed more than 900 people in Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe.
Kable also said that even a well-established country like South Africa will have a water crisis called Day Zero in 2018 due to extreme weather (there is no running water available and limited water needs to be collected at water stations), and there have been several recent floods in Kwa-Zulu Natal province.
"Not many African countries are responsible for climate change, but they are still severely affected and simply unable to cope with it."
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption The fight against extinction calls for governments to tell the truth about the extent of the climate crisis and enact laws to completely eliminate carbon emissions by 2025 (Credit: Getty Images) Rich countries were spared a median of 18 countries with historical carbon dioxide emissions below 10 metric tons (9 metric tons) per capita from 1961 to 2010, according to the study 27 percent.
Fourteen of the 19 countries with a total per capita carbon dioxide emissions of more than 300 metric tons (272 metric tons) benefited from warming, with a median per capita GDP increase of 13 per cent.
Research shows that not only do poor countries not enjoy the full benefits of energy consumption, but many also become poorer (relatively speaking) because rich countries use energy.
However, the results of the study have also been criticized.
Solomon Hsiang, a professor of public policy at the University of California, Berkeley, who has previously worked with Burke and Diefenbaff, believes that while the negative impact of global warming on poorer, hotter countries is “absolutely true, ” rich countries have not been spared.
"In their analysis, the impact on rich countries will not be felt until later," he said.
A few years after the impact began, observations show that the colder, wealthier countries suffer just as much as the hotter, poorer countries. "
The extent of the impact on mid-latitude countries, which include the world ’ s three largest economies, the United States, China and Japan, is unclear.
"Climate change is not good for anyone in the long run," he said.
If the momentum of change does not abate, it will eventually get out of control.
The world's major emitters of greenhouse gases must act quickly to reduce their emissions.
"Policymakers need to take climate change more seriously and immediately stop using fossil fuels and switch to renewable sources of energy."

title: Iran plane crash: Video cameraman and protesters crushed by authorities
text:

Video of how the plane was shot down after Iran admitted to accidentally shooting down a Ukrainian passenger plane continued to flow. Over the past weekend, people demonstrated for two days in a row, and Iranian officials denied that they had shot dead protesters.

title: 【 TAIWAN HEALTH INSPECTION 】 How does Kaohsiung win after Asia 's leading medical tourism? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
text:
Kaohsiung has designated 2019 as the “first year of medical tourism ” and is aggressively marketing local medical products.
However, looking at other advanced cities in Asia, it is certainly not a pioneer in the development of medical tourism.
Bangkok in Thailand, Seoul in Korea, Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia and other places have been implementing medical tourism for many years, each with its own characteristics.
Can Kaohsiung, a rising star, develop a unique chain of medical tourism industry to compete with other Asian cities?
(This is the sixth feature of the "Taiwan Health Insurance" series) Can hospitals in Kaohsiung capture a share of the medical tourism industry among the best in Asia? (photo by Yang Yalin) Chang Hung-tai, director of Kaohsiung Municipal Union Hospital, believes that the advantages of Kaohsiung and the whole of Taiwan are its internationally recognized medical standards and low medical service prices.
"Taiwan medical care because of the relationship of health insurance, the cost is very low, almost one-tenth of that of other countries, cheaper than the mainland, our drug prices are also low, many mainlanders are willing to come to Taiwan."
First, the price is low, and the second is high quality credibility.
Taiwan ’ s Ministry of Health and Welfare has strict management, and health insurance audits are conducted from time to time. ”
Zhang Hongtai believes that the surrounding potential competitors have their own advantages. For example, Thailand has a lot of experience in tourism medicine, and even several hospitals are specialized in tourism medicine, so the service personnel of the entire hospital have been carefully trained and tailored according to the principles of tourism medicine.
Medical tourism in the capital Bangkok is mature enough to be a "package tour" and receive thousands of medical tourists.
“Many hospitals have even scheduled their annual schedules … Taiwan can make this kind of money. ” Thailand is the world ’ s largest medical tourism destination, with more than 2 million foreign tourists coming to Thailand each year to receive medical services, and the related industries make an average annual profit of 120 billion baht (about HK $29.6 billion).
Thailand is famous for its rich tourism resources, coupled with the maturity of medical technology in health examination, plastic surgery, dentistry and other aspects, the average price of related services is only about half of that of European and American countries, so medical tourism has been one of the alternative tourism projects in Thailand.
The famous CBS news program “60 Minutes Magazine ” reported on Bangkok ’ s famous“ Bumrungrad Hospital ” in a feature way back in 2005.
The hospital receives more than 500,000 foreign patients from more than 190 countries around the world every year. It has the largest health screening center in Bangkok, serving more than 60,000 people every year, which shows that its medical tourism resources are very sufficient.
Bangkok ’ s famous “Regal Hospital ” (Bumrungrad Hospital). (online picture) When it comes to medical tourism, it has to mention Seoul, South Korea. Its advanced medical minimally invasive technology has always led Asia, and it has a mature operating system and supporting medical aesthetic technology such as microplastic surgery, which has become the Asian plastic surgery center.
Since 2009, the annual growth rate of medical tourists visiting Korea has exceeded 34%, and they come from China, the United States, Russia, Japan and other countries.
In December last year, the Korean Medical Tourism Service Center at Incheon International Airport was officially opened, allowing foreign travelers to book local consultation services, nearby dining and accommodation facilities, transportation to the hospital, and more.
The service center also has a resident nurse who is fluent in multiple languages, providing tourists with professional consulting services for medical tourism.
The government has partnered with the industry to make it the number one driver of medical tourism.
The medical tourism industry in Seoul is mainly engaged in microsurgery and cosmetic surgery.
(Online photo) Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia has always been the best destination for medical tourism. In 2016, Kuala Lumpur was named the Best Medical Tourism Destination of the Year by International Medical Tourism Magazine.
Kuala Lumpur also has a language advantage. Due to its multi-ethnic society, there is no shortage of health care workers fluent in Chinese and English. In addition to this, it has been favored by medical tourists from Europe and the United States, and it has also helped it to seize the huge Chinese market and become a rival to Kaohsiung.
(Hong Kong 01 map) Kaohsiung needs to "decorate" first to enter the market. Zhang Hongtai admitted that Kaohsiung still needs to prepare a lot of things in medical tourism and do a good job of supporting the work.
He cited the United Hospital, where he worked, as an example, because it belongs to the regional hospital level, it has the conditions to build medical aesthetics equipment.
He pointed out that the first thing to do is to redecorate the internal facilities and renovate them into a new type of ward.
"Medical beauty is not the same as general medical treatment, can not be treated as a general patient."
They want to have a private, safe and beautiful ward, "he said.
Another problem is professionalism.
Zhang Hongtai believes that at present, Taiwan does not restrict what doctors can do medical aesthetics, as long as they have a doctor's license, so there are many people doing it, and the quality is difficult to control.
He does not mean that doctors have problems with their medical skills, but that the medical community should have a unique professional process and code for medical aesthetics in order to enhance the attractiveness of medical tourism in Kaohsiung and compete with neighboring regions.
For example, laser, if used inappropriately, may cause burns.
Therefore, even if you do medical aesthetics, you still need a professional evaluation by a specialist.
If Kaohsiung is to do a good job in medical tourism, it must pay attention to the professionalism of medical aesthetics.
"What we do is a medical beauty with a certain standard, and it can't be seen as a night market selling things."
"The Big Thing".
With professionalism, we can have the quality and safety that the international medical industry has always emphasized. There are already large medical and aesthetic teams in nearby cities, who value the quality of their services and treat their customers as valued guests rather than simply patients.
