title: Taiwan People News
text:
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) recently released its Special Report on Climate Change and Land, highlighting the environmental impact of agriculture and the need to make full use of existing farmland to prevent further destruction.
Today, about 75% of the earth ’ s land is dedicated to feeding the world ’ s population.
As the population increases (expected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050), the pressure on farmland will intensify.
Some environmentalists say they oppose genetic engineering, while the modern environmental movement and organic agriculture are also passionate about it.
In the IPCC ’ s report on food safety, there ’ s even no mention of organic farming.
This is because if your goal is to protect the land, this is one of the worst ways to farm. In 2017, researchers at the Swiss Institute of Organic Agriculture, an organization funded in part by the organic industry, found that if the world were to switch entirely to organic agriculture, we would need 16% to 81% more land to feed the planet ’ s population.
We need genetic engineering to avoid global hunger caused by climate change, the IPCC report by 107 experts from 52 countries.
It warns: “Land is a vital resource.
He also pointed to rising food prices and hunger among the world ’ s poor.
In fact, after all the numbers and probabilistic estimates, it is an ever-present truth that climate change is especially difficult for the poor and people in the tropics.
The IPCC concluded that as carbon dioxide levels rise and the planet warms, the unit production of farms in temperate regions (i.e. wealthier countries such as Europe and North America) will actually increase.
The real disruption will occur in the Global South, which will reduce the production of fruits and vegetables, thereby causing the world ’ s most at-risk populations to decline, both in terms of the number of calories available and the nutritional quality of food.
The report concludes that production of certain vegetables will fall by as much as 30%, pulses will be reduced by 30% to 60% in Africa, and up to 40% of banana-growing areas will no longer be available.
The report also states that up to 183 million people will be at risk of starvation due to climate change and the resulting rise in food prices.
But the report is also particularly shocking to find that the solutions we need to mitigate climate change alone will lead to an increase in the number of hungry people in Africa, Southeast Asia and India by about 20%.
For people who live near the equator, this population of 3 billion, there are no good results there.
What can help reduce the global disappearance of agriculture?
One solution that often appears in IPCC reports is “genetic improvement ” of crops.
The report highlights that improving food productivity through technological solutions such as “new varieties from breeding or biotechnology ” will be an important part of adapting to climate change.
In fact, the report explicitly mentions crops that use CRISPR-Cas9 for genomic editing, a genetic tool that the European Court of Justice just decided to ban last year, and major environmental NGOs, such as green groups and the organic farming community, are ideologically opposed.
First let me explain what CRISPR (clustered regularly spaced short palindromic repeat) is? DNA is the blueprint of life, directing cells to produce proteins, maintaining the growth and operation of the human body.
When the important location of DNA is mutated, the “cell factory ” operation can get out of control, which can cause physiological disorders, and even major genetic diseases such as leukemia.
If you are sick, you can take medication.
However, in the case of diseases caused by genetic mutations, drugs can only control the disease.
Because the blueprint is wrong, the cell can never make the wrong protein.
If you want a cure, it is best to correct the blueprint and modify the DNA.
Gene editing can start from the source, find the wrong DNA fragment, use a molecular “scissors ” (Cas9) to cut open, eliminate the wrong gene, or“ paste ” the correct DNA fragment at the gap.
So first of all, there is a good pair of accurate scissors that can cut the double helix of DNA, and CRISPR is the best one to use.
Innovative biotechnologies, such as gene editing, are expected to slow the expansion of farmland by enabling farms to grow more food on less land and fewer resources.
Although it is far from a panacea, the potential of gene editing can make every acre more productive even in the face of climate change, which attracts the imagination of plant scientists, the agro-tech industry, and the government.
Today, they are increasingly focusing on the ability of CRISPR to ensure that the world ’ s food supply in the future is protected from increasingly unpredictable environmental threats.
CRISPR is thought to be the “molecular scissors ” used to cut and edit DNA, but researchers are now looking far beyond these applications.
In a new comprehensive review, they explore the current state of CRISPR in crops and how scientists are tackling climate change, diseases and pests to enhance traditional breeding techniques in non-traditional ways to cope with a growing population.
Explore the current state of CRISPR in crops and how scientists are using CRISPR to enhance traditional breeding techniques in non-traditional ways, with the aim of ensuring global food and nutrition security and feeding a growing population in the face of climate change, disease and pests.
In recent years, innovations in crop engineering have ranged from cassava plants to starches that produce better resistance to deadly diseases, bananas and eggplants, to vitamin-rich rice and micronutrients.
Visionary scientists in climate-smart agriculture, government-funded, genome-edited crops that use local crop varieties and are compatible with agriculture in the form of low chemical inputs.
Personally, this vision deserves the support of the environmental movement and the organic farming community, which, as the IPCC points out, is necessary if we are to adapt to climate change.
Scientists at the University of Texas have discovered a gene in coral that is activated when corals are threatened by heat.
Warm waters caused by climate change often cause stressed corals to expel the algae they depend on for their survival from energy in a so-called bleaching process, resulting in coral blooms.
Scientists believe that the gene is present in many coral species and hope to detect stressed corals before bleaching, allowing them to prioritize conservation.
Climate Friendly Cows Researchers have found that cows can be raised selectively to make them more environmentally friendly.
The amount of methane produced by microbes in the cow ’ s first stomach (rumen) is influenced by the cow ’ s genetics.
Professor John Williams, of the University of Adelaide, said that this means we can choose cows that permanently produce less methane, which will contribute to slowing global warming.
Scientists in California are developing an “ideal factory ” that could help slow global warming.
This superplant is designed to absorb carbon dioxide from the air and deposit it in the roots as a carbon-rich, cork-like substance called Suberin.
It is resistant to decomposition and can store CO2 underground for a long time.
A team of researchers from the University of Copenhagen identified a gene last year that allows rice to fight floods and droughts, so that leaves are coated with wax crystals that repel water.
During droughts, this prevents water loss due to evaporation; in floods, the waxy surface retains a thin gas for several days to prevent large rice from drowning.
Scientists aim to manipulate the gene to improve long-term flood resistance.
Biofuel Bacteria In 2018, scientists at the National University of Singapore discovered a strain of bacteria capable of converting plant matter into biobutanol: a biofuel that can be used in car engines instead of gasoline.
Now, researchers are genetically modifying bacteria to improve the conversion efficiency of biobutanol.
When people think of CRISPR, they think of genome editing, but the fact is that CRISPR is actually a universal system that allows you to do a lot of things to target, recruit, or promote certain aspects of DNA that are already there.
You can regulate the activation or inhibition of certain genes by using CRISPR, not as a cutting tool, but as a binding tool to attract an activator or blocker to induce the trait.
We call this genetic modification.
The purpose of this is to bring very important trait genes close to each other, so that physically and genetically, they are linked together, so they are always tightly bound in traditional hybrids, thus making it easier to choose crops with all the desired traits.
This includes the process of applying CRISPR to animals and humans and applying it to crops.
For example, CRISPR technology has enhanced screening of genes and traits in human health by using thousands of libraries of guiding molecules that are specifically designed for selected gene sets at genome-scale.
The system can potentially be used for screening in plants, contributing to pest resistance, resilience and crop yield traits.
This not only helps with breeding, but also makes it easier to categorize gene functions.
For the most part, these studies are done in human cells, while crops lag behind.
Gene editing can lead to three solutions to the challenge of climate change and how to help farmers make the most of their existing land: Keeping the land healthy: Agriculture is taking a toll on the land.
During each growing season, the planet absorbs more and more nutrients that are essential for the growth of crops.
As a result, farmers will farm to the land to restore soil health, but this will release carbon into the atmosphere.
Farmers also often use fertilizers to supplement nutritional deficiencies.
However, thanks to gene editing, researchers are modifying microbes in the soil to deliver more key nutrients, such as nitrogen, to the plants.
More with less: As the population grows, farmers may be forced to use land in poor conditions to grow their crops.
Fortunately, through gene editing, we can enhance the growth of plants in these areas.
Currently, a research team in the United States is working to improve rice varieties that can grow on marginal soils. As the area of arable land decreases, the ability to grow staple foods such as rice will become increasingly important.
Resilient crops: The effects of climate change already exist.
Popular foods, such as oranges and coffee, have become victims of the spread of the disease, while warmer areas have accelerated the spread of the disease.
With gene editing, we can develop disease-resistant crops that resist disease and thrive in a warm world.
Crops that have enhanced disease resistance are nothing new, but advances in gene editing technology have allowed researchers to develop these traits in a very short time compared to conventional breeding, which can take decades.
If we are to feed a growing population in a warm world, we must embrace innovations such as gene editing to enable farmers to do more with less.

title: Deyang Dongfang Electric Co., Ltd.
text:
Deyang Dongfang Electric Helps Artificial Solar Research 2019-06-19 03: 57 United Daily News Mainland Special Agent Wang Yuyan / Taipei-Deyang Report Recently, the main magnetic coil center column of the new generation of nuclear fusion experimental device in mainland China, the Cyclist No.2 M (HL-2M), was successfully delivered, marking the beginning of the overall installation of the new generation of artificial solar device independently developed in mainland. The dream of fusion clean energy is one step closer.
As a production enterprise of this core component, Dongfang Electric Co., Ltd. (Dongfang Electric), located in Deyang, Sichuan, has also become the first enterprise in China to manufacture circulators with large magnetic coils.
Circulator No. 2 M device is a large-scale conventional magnetic tokamak fusion research device in mainland China. It is a key platform for conducting research on the core technology of fusion reactors, which will greatly improve the means and capabilities of fusion research.
The device is constructed by the Southwest Institute of Physics of Nuclear Industry of China Nuclear Power Group (NWRI), and Oriental Electric undertakes the manufacture of the host magnetic coil, the core component of the current device.
The main coil system is one of the core components of the main unit of the device. The development of the central column is the most challenging task of the entire coil system. It is the first time in the mainland that it is large in scale, high in parameters, difficult to manufacture and high in process accuracy.
Nuclear Western Institute and Eastern Electric combined the advantages of their respective technical fields, and achieved a number of key technological breakthroughs.
The internal technical team of Dongfang Electric completed 28 key process tests, and finally all parts meet the technical requirements of mechanical parameters, electrical parameters and other technical requirements.
Nuclear fusion produces energy similar to the principle of the sun's luminous heating, so the controlled nuclear fusion research device on Earth for the purpose of exploring clean energy has gained the reputation of "artificial sun".
China has undertaken 12 categories of product tasks in the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) project, among which, Dongfang Electric has successfully completed the research and development task of the cladding mask module certification, standing in the forefront of this field in the world.
It is reported that the Cyclone No. 2 M device is expected to be completed before the end of the year, when the mainland's most advanced and internationally leading "artificial sun" experimental device will be born in Sichuan.

title: Japan officially resumes commercial whaling government: 227 in the second half of the year
text:
Japan has resumed commercial whaling.
Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on July 1, and fishermen will resume commercial whaling for the first time in 31 years.
Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries said that the planned capture of 227 whales in the second half of this year was determined on the basis of not affecting the amount of whale resources.
Over the years, Japanese fishing vessels have repeatedly used loopholes in the IWC rules to hunt whales in the name of "science", and the hunt has been fiercely criticized by the outside world. "Whaling has no scientific value, and Japan's move is equivalent to secret whaling."
In response, Japan repeatedly fought for the resumption of commercial whaling, but the argument was fruitless, and finally announced in December last year that it would withdraw from the IWC, which was officially implemented in July this year.
The Japanese whaling ship sails from Shimonoseki Port in Yamaguchi Prefecture and Kushiro Port in Hokkaido to celebrate the resumption of whaling symbolically with a week-long minke whale hunt.
Japanese whalers have hailed the resumption of commercial whaling, and the Japanese authorities believe that whaling is one of the Japanese traditions and should not be disturbed.
Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries said that in the past, the so-called survey whaling hunted 637 minke whales in a year, but from now to the end of December, they only intend to hunt 277, which is a small number compared to the past, and this number is calculated on the basis that "even if the hunt continues for 100 years, it will not affect the whale's resources."
Now that Japan has resumed commercial whaling, although the number of hunts is small, the area is small and far from the international conservation waters, but it has still caused dissatisfaction from the outside world, and criticized the whaling behavior as outdated and harmful, and has no interests.

title: In 30 years, the quota for commercial whaling will be set at 227.
text:
Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan, July 1, 2019 (AFP) Five Japanese ships went to sea to hunt whales today, the first time in more than 30 years that Japan has resumed commercial whaling since it formally withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) yesterday.

title: Japan restarts whaling with 'extreme restraint' quotas
text:
Japan on Sunday (June 30) formally withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC), resuming commercial whaling for the first time in more than 30 years and setting an upper limit of 227 whaling by the end of 2019.
It is said that the Japanese government has set a quota of "extreme restraint" compared to ordinary fishing in order to slow down the condemnation of the international community.
Japan ’ s Aquaculture Agency said on Monday (July 1) that it has set a whaling limit of 227 whales by the end of December 2019, including 52 minke whales, 25 sei whales and 150 Bud ’ s whales.
Reuters quoted industry sources as saying that the Department of Fisheries ’ whaling limit will be adjusted annually.
As whaling will be confined to exclusive economic waters, Japan will no longer hunt about 330 Antarctic baleen whales as it has done in recent years.
The Kyodo News Agency reported that the government set quotas for fishing that were extremely restrained compared to fishing for ordinary fish.
The Japanese government stressed: "With this amount of (whaling), even if it is hunted for 100 years, it will not have a negative impact on resources."
The government also intends to explain its ideas to whaling support countries, promote and strengthen cooperation.
The Department of Fisheries calculates the total number of available catches that will be capped for the full year fishing quota set after 2020, including 171 minke whales, 187 Bryde whales and 25 Sei whales.
Calculation Using the IWC approach, each head count is less than 1% of the estimated amount of resources.
The catch quota for other species along the coast of Japan is said to be around 3% to 30%, and whaling quotas are extremely strict.
Considering the accusations of foreign researchers, the quota for Sei whales is set at a particularly strict 0.07%.
The Japanese government plans to participate in the IWC as an observer in the future and provide the data collected on the whales.

title: After 31 years, commercial whaling will resume this year, and will the Japanese still eat whale meat?
text:
Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on June 30, resuming "commercial whaling" for the first time in 31 years. Yesterday (1), five whaling vessels went out to sea and caught two gray baleen whales in the afternoon. It will not be overfished for 100 years.
It remains to be seen whether the Japanese people, who once used whale meat as their main meat, will return to the habit of eating whale meat.
Japan announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in December last year, and now is coming into effect. Although the area where fishermen plan to hunt whales is small and far from international conservation waters, some countries are still dissatisfied, saying that whaling is outdated and harmful.
Japanese whalers have hailed the resumption of whaling, and Tokyo authorities have stressed that whaling is part of the Japanese tradition and should not be disturbed.
The issue of whaling has been a diplomatic problem for Japan for years, and Japanese ships have been repeatedly attacked for exploiting the IWC loophole to kill whales in the name of “science. ”
Critics say that whaling has no scientific value, accusing Japan of doing so almost as much as clandestine whaling; Tokyo is continuing to fight for permission to fully resume commercial whaling.
After Japan ’ s withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission, whaling vessels that used to go to sea in the name of scientific research will sail from Shimonoseki Port in Yamaguchi Prefecture in western Japan to hunt whales.
While whalers are cheering criticism from anti-whaling nations and advocates, local whaling groups are cheering, as five small whaling vessels from all over Japan gathered at the port of Kushiro, Hokkaido, yesterday to launch a week of small baleen whale hunting activities, symbolically celebrating the resumption of whaling.
The five whale-hunting boats set sail with whaling forks at the sound of their horns, AFP reported.
Photo credit: AP / Dazhi Image The port of Kushiro in Hokkaido, Japan, holds many ceremonies and performances to send the whaling ship to sea.
The ships will join ships sailing from Shimonoseki Port in Yamaguchi Prefecture in southern Japan, where they will be busy hunting whales for much of the summer.
Five whalers sailed from Kushiro, Hokkaido, early in the morning and recovered two gray baleen whales in the afternoon.
One of the whales, measuring more than 8 meters in length, was lifted from the boat, put into a truck, and transported to a warehouse.
The whaling fisherman uses water pipes to wash the baby whale and douse it with sake, not only to symbolize the ritual purification, but also to celebrate the harvest.
Yoshifumi Kai, president of the Japan Small Whaling Association, which is affiliated with the Wakayama Taiji Fisheries Co-operative, said before setting sail: “Today is the best day.
We are very excited about the resumption of commercial whaling, and my heart is full of hope. ”
Do Japanese eat whale meat?
Whale meat is the main source of protein for poor Japanese society after World War II, but consumption has declined significantly in recent decades. In one year, the Japanese consumed only 0.1% of all meat.
Regarding the resumption of whaling, Sachiko Sakai, a 66-year-old taxi driver in Hokkaido, said: “If there is more whale meat to eat, we will eat more, which is part of Japan ’ s food culture. ”
The international community is against whaling, why not talk about animals that are raised on land and killed by us for food? ”
Hideki Abe, a 23-year-old whaler, said: “I don ’ t think young people today know how to cook or eat whale meat.
I want more people to have tasted whale meat at least once. "
Key to the resumption of whaling: Japan ’ s Fisheries Agency says it has set a whaling limit of 227 whales by the end of December this year, including 52 minke whales, 25 Sei whales and 150 Buji whales.
Reuters reported that according to industry sources, the Japan Fisheries Agency's whaling limit will be adjusted annually.
As whaling will be confined to exclusive economic waters, Japan will no longer hunt about 330 Antarctic baleen whales as it has done in recent years.

title: The worst nightmare for whales and dolphins! Japan 's sad song about the resumption of commercial whaling
text:
The worst nightmare of whales and dolphins! The sad song of Japan ’ s resumption of commercial whaling 2019-07-03 09: 06 United News Network Article / VisionJapan is a world-renowned seafood power, and whale meat is one of the people ’ s favorite sashimi.
For conservation, they are more concerned about lust This week, in the port of Kushiro in northern Japan, several whaling ships sailed to the sea with a simple purpose: to find the whales and catch them back home.
Commercial whaling was officially restarted in Japan on July 1, and after only 31 years of compliance, Japan has officially withdrawn from the International Whaling Commission in 2019. At present, it is meeting the Japanese market that wants to eat whale meat with a large, arrogant and unrestricted fishing scale.
In the past few days, the helpless and unsuspecting whale has been sent to port with the blood of a whaler, but the big ticket buyers have long been waiting for bidding in the auction area - despite the concerns of conservation and cruelty, and the reduced demand for whale meat from consumers, Japan continues to insist on the path of whaling despite international criticism.
For the world's oceans, Japan is a world-renowned seafood power, not only the Japanese people love seafood to a crazy point, a variety of sashimi and food culture has emerged, it also provides the world's important seafood market, but also boasts a rich export fish harvest, the past few years ranked first in the world.
In fact, even in the face of public opinion, Japan has never changed its wanton insistence, in addition to the original hunting of dolphins, in early 2019 announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC), now officially out of international jurisdiction, but also on behalf of the international hard-won conservation road, has fallen.
The International Whaling Commission (IWC) is an international organization established in 1949 to focus on the protection and management of the whaling industry. In 1982, it declared a moratorium on whaling. In addition to observing the rules, member states must also protect the oceans as far as possible without harming the ecosystem.
However, the current cabinet chief, Yoshihide Suga, said, “Japan ’ s withdrawal is due to the Commission ’ s failure to develop a sustainable whaling industry, but it is blindly over-protective. ” Be bound by anything and kill the wisest and most massive creatures in the sea."
At present, only Japan, Iceland and Norway continue to kill whales, and Japan, in the name of “scientific research, ” defends the annual whaling in Antarctica, stressing that it is necessary to assess the population of whales.
Even in 2016, Japan slaughtered 333 whales.
In a new statistical report, the Animal Welfare Institute found that Japan, Norway and Iceland have killed 38,539 whales since their statistics began, with about 22,000 of them killed by Japanese ships.
Over the past few years, Japanese whalers have continued to kill whales in the Antarctic Ocean and throughout the Southern Hemisphere in the name of scientific research.
Although Japan says the practice is primarily to help determine whale quotas, scientists still see whale meat being subsequently sold.
To quell the outrage, Japan has promised to use friendly methods approved by the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to catch whales, but Humane Society International says no way to kill whales makes sense. As long-lived and spiritual mammals, whales are highly vulnerable to human activities and ocean pollution is already a test for them.
Whale populations have been overfishing by humans for centuries, and their numbers are at a critical point, and it is difficult to regain their former glory, and the pace of recovery is even slower. At the same time, they have to deal with the existential threats of climate change and ocean pollution, including plastic waste, chemical pollution and noise.
The idea of hunting and killing whales has aroused widespread disgust in the West, and many Japanese people have spontaneously protested in whaling ports by holding up a banner.
Commercial whaling resumed in Japan on July 1.
The Associated Press shared a history of Japanese love for whale meat Whale meat is an important source of protein in Japan, helping Japan recover quickly from the ravages and wounds of World War II.
At that time, Japan's domestic food shortage, whale meat used to be an important food supply, as one of the protein sources of nutritional lunch, so the older generation of Japanese people have a fondness for whale meat.
But now that whale meat is no longer so popular, young people are no longer taking it as their first choice, and the whaling ban has put many fishermen ’ s livelihoods at risk.
However, some markets can still buy raw meat, cooked food or whale canned food.
For this reason, the Japanese government believes that this is part of traditional culture, dating back centuries, and cannot be erased or disappear.
On the other hand, in 2009, a documentary film "The Cove" exposing the bloody dolphin hunting culture in Taiji Town, Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, was released. Director Louie Psihoyos told the world about this unspeakable cruel culture by means of adventure, undersea camouflage photography, private records, and interviews. This film won the Oscar for Best Documentary.
In the film, the director reveals that at least 20,000 dolphins are killed in the area every year, most of which are used to supply a market for dolphin meat lovers throughout Japan, while some of the healthier, youthful dolphins are captured alive and sold to various marine parks for entertainment.
When the film was released, it aroused the disgust of the people around the world. A large number of environmental groups gathered in Taiji to hold a protest, hoping to put an end to this reprehensible blind tradition, especially in the tragic bay that was dyed red, expressing the human desire, unscrupulous arrogance and selfishness.
In this era of the 21st century, the International Whaling Commission says, the world should strengthen international cooperation to express its demands by refusing to eat whale and dolphin meat, and to protect our natural environment and wildlife.
The whale was taken ashore.

title: 【 News Classroom 】 Despite global criticism, when did Japan restart commercial whaling after 32 years? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
text:
Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday (June 30), after 32 years to restart commercial whaling.
A number of whalers were greeted by local residents and sailed out of the harbour.
Japan is one of the few countries that still hunt whales. Today, let ’ s introduce Japan ’ s whaling history, the reasons for restarting whaling and the current state of the whaling industry.
A number of whaling vessels are moored at the wharf in Kushiro City, Hokkaido, waiting to sail. (Reuters) ↓ ↓ For more photos of whaling, please click to enlarge: + 4 + 3 + 2 Japan Whaling History Japan has a long history of whaling, which began in prehistoric times.
The word "fish" in the Nara period "Manye Collection" is an ancient Japanese word for whaling.
In the Edo period, whaling gradually became an industry. In addition to being used for food, various parts of the whale were fully utilized, such as whale oil as a pesticide, bone nata as carving, and ambergris as a perfume.
After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In the 1950s, Japan became the world ’ s largest whaling nation, with domestic consumption peaking at 233,000 tons in 1962.
In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. Japan initially objected, but after the objection was rejected in 1986, Japan finally promised to gradually ban commercial whaling, and commercial whaling ceased in 1988.
However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. In fact, Japan has set up a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research".
According to the report of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, the annual consumption of whale meat in Japan since the 1990s has been about 2,000 to 6,000 tons, and the latest figure in 2018 totals 3,000 tons.
Japan has a long history of whaling, which has become an industry as early as the Edo period. (Getty Images) Revitalizing the economy with the help of Whaling Japan ’ s Small Whaling Association President Yoshinori Abe called the news of the resumption of commercial whaling “a shock of joy and a sense of limitlessness. ” Prosperity again.
Some areas that used to make a living from whaling also hope to revitalize the economy by restarting whale hunting, such as the Amikawa area in the east of Miyagi Prefecture, which was the base of the whaling port of that year.
After extensive damage during the Great East Japan Earthquake, residents hope to revive the local economy by reviving the whaling industry. A museum dedicated to introducing whaling culture is planned for April 2020 to attract visitors.
Whale meat is quite nutritious and has become an important food item for the Japanese since the end of World War II. (Reuters) Whale meat is not expensive, but it should be noted that since the 1970s, whaling in Japan has declined year by year, and today whale meat is no longer a common dish in Japan.
Compared to the annual consumption of 6 million tons of pork and chicken, only 3,000 tons of whale meat is really insignificant.
And interestingly, whale meat has not become expensive due to reduced availability.
In the Tokyo market price in 2018, the price of "red meat level 1" whale meat used for sashimi is 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram, and the price of "umu" whale meat used for high-grade smoked is 3,000 yen (about HK $210) per kilogram.
In fact, the price of salmon to tuna is about the price, can not say how expensive.
This means that the actual market demand for whale meat is not high.
Therefore, public opinion in Japan is worried that in the reality of low supply and demand, even if the resumption of whaling, it will be difficult to let this already sunset industry "rise back to life", and the desire to revitalize the regional economy will be difficult to achieve.
Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.
Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling.
Therefore, there are allegations that the government is strongly promoting the resumption of whale hunting in order to continue to gain the support of local residents.
However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

title: Japan ’ s Trap: How Resumption of Commercial Whaling Affects the Nation ’ s Image
text:
HONG KONG, July 6 (Xinhua) -- Japan has resumed commercial whaling for the first time in 33 years, despite repeated calls from the international community.
This was made possible by Japan ’ s withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC).
According to satellite news, Japanese authorities insist that eating whale meat is a national tradition, so Japan has long been planning to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission.
Vasily Shvedko, head of the economic and social department of the Moscow Institute of International Relations of the Russian Academy of Sciences, believes that in this case, the Japanese government has successfully selected a moment, and the above steps have become a bonus in favor of the ruling party.
“Russian fishermen ’ s organizations have lobbied the government on this issue for years.
Because they think they have suffered greatly because of the ban on whale hunting.
Japan ’ s withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission has shown them that the ruling cabinet cares about the interests of the country ’ s fishing industry. ” However, there are data showing that whale populations have recovered over the past 30 years.
It is now possible to restore whaling without causing ecological damage and without worrying about destroying their populations.
What ’ s more, Tokyo stressed that this would not be an uncontrolled whaling industry, but rather a quota and on a limited scale.
Since 1987, Japan has hunted between 200 and 1,200 whales every year in the framework of scientific research projects.
Now the Japanese authorities have set a quota: 227 whales of three species will be hunted by the end of this year.
Shivedko believes that although whale meat is not as popular in Japan as it used to be, keeping whale meat in Japanese recipes is still a national treasure.
“Over the years, whale meat on Japanese stalls has become a delicacy, no longer a daily food.
However, the consumption of whale meat is highly prized. The whale meat in the restaurant can be attractive to visitors, just like the exotic element. ”
In the early 19th century, whales were on the brink of extinction due to the popularity of the whaling industry.
At that time, Norway, the United Kingdom, the United States, Russia, and Japan were once the world's leading whaling countries. The main whaling area at the beginning of the 20th century was the Antarctic.
In 1946, in order to maintain the whale population and regulate the development of the whale industry, the International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling was signed.
In accordance with the Convention, the International Whaling Commission (IWC) was established.
The United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union became members in 1948, and Japan became a member in 1951.
Since 1986, the International Whaling Commission has temporarily suspended commercial whaling in order to restore populations of various whale species.

title: Withdrawal from the "cultural imperialist" Whaling Commission, Japan's diplomacy turned to "Trumpism"?
text:
On July 1, Japan officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years. 9 days ago, the first batch of whalers returned to the port, bringing back a total of more than a dozen baleen whales large and small.
From Kushiro, Hokkaido, south to Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, the whaling craze that has not been seen for a long time, whales are slaughtered and sold in various markets, attracting many people to come and buy.
In the Kushiro market, people who have tried it have a feeling of nostalgia in addition to admiring the delicious food.
On December 26, 2018, Japan announced that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after six months, and decided to reopen the commercial whaling route, prompting criticism from many countries.
At that time, there was also a debate in Japan that the government's decision-making process was not transparent, and the idea of reviewing whether to hunt whales was also repeated and fell into heated discussion for a time.
Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Takayama Yoshikawa, said that the resumption of whaling was the "sad wish of the people involved in the national whaling" and that although Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission, it still hoped that Japan would rejoin as an observer in the future to express its concern for the development of the international fishing industry.
According to Article 65 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the conservation and management of cetaceans is to be determined by "appropriate international authorities".
Originally, the International Whaling Commission was responsible for this task, after Japan's withdrawal, there will be a future Japanese whaling ship triggered by the international case may be against the court, Yoshikawa said only that "whether it will go to both sides of the complaint, but also depends on the policy judgment of various countries", now I am afraid it is too early to say.
The International Whaling Commission was established in 1946 to focus on whale conservation around the world. Japan has a long tradition of whaling since the Edo period and is the world ’ s largest consumer of whales. During the recovery period at the end of World War II, whales were once used as a source of protein for a nutritious lunch.
However, after 1970, the world's whale population significantly reduced, in order to protect the whale population, the IWC interrupted commercial whaling in 1982, and Japan finally complied with the agreement to stop commercial whaling in 1988.
However, although there is no commercial whaling, Japan continues to carry out whaling activities under the name of “survey whaling ”, but in fact, there is still a lot of whale meat coming into the market. Although the quota for survey whaling is strictly limited, it is judged that there are still many illegal sales of whale meat that are privately caught.
The taste of raw whale meat is slightly hard. It is a bit like horse meat, and the fiber is thick. It is usually eaten with ground ginger.
This time, the Japanese government has also stressed the use of a fairly high standard, from the IWC official calculation method of "no bad impact in 100 years" of the three categories of minke whales, sei whales and cloth whales.
Unlike survey whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the North Pacific, Japan has resumed commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan.
However, according to the International Convention on the Control of Whaling, signed in Washington in 1946, these three species are still listed as threatened with extinction, so the Japanese decision still attracts strong criticism from conservation groups and other foreign media.
Photo Credit: Reuters / Tachih Image Preserving Whale Culture?
Although Japan says that whaling is inherent in its traditional culture, the overall whaling market has declined significantly since it withdrew from commercial whaling in 1988, with 383 whales captured in 2018, 40% less than in 2017.
In addition to not eating whales, many young people do not know that this species has been their traditional culture.
The president of the Japan Small Whaling Association, Berryman, said: "The expansion of new routes and financial austerity, or continue to explore."
Young people do not understand whales, and in the future, they hope to at least let the local people in the fishing port experience whale cuisine again. "After 31 years of no whaling, Japan's whaling industry aging is also quite obvious, and the operators only spent a lot of time repairing their boats and whaling habitat, and they also privately told the Japanese media when they left the port:" It is a fact that they are intertwined with hope and uneasy. "In addition, because of the inability to hunt whales for the past 31 years, the Japanese government has allocated a fixed subsidy to whalers every day. Now that whaling resumes, it is like they can“ feed themselves ” and the subsidy is likely to be cut or even cancelled in 2020.
The Wall Street Journal also published an article saying that Japan's foreign policy in the future is likely to adopt a harder "Trump" line, one is to restart commercial whaling for 31 years, and the other is to directly impose semiconductor export restrictions on South Korea, the article said: "For some Japanese nationalists, after withdrawing from the IWC, which is a symbol of cultural imperialism in Europe and the United States, it is also about national independence. Say a good claim.
This use of trade as a bargaining chip in international politics is also Trump ’ s usual trick, and the newspaper said that Japan also responded to “Trump flow. ”
In addition, the Japanese government has also invested about 1.9 billion yen (about 544 million Taiwan dollars) in the resumption of whale hunting for fishing grounds and technical support for decomposition.
However, if the next 10 years still rely on government funds to continue to invest, it will still be difficult to become a self-supporting industry.
While the Japanese government is advocating the resumption of whaling, in addition to the pressure of international disapproval, what is more cruel is that the next generation has no special ideas about whaling or not.

title: Cities in the wild. Beneficiaries aren't just wild animals.
text:
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Urban rewilding projects are drawing nature back to our cities, including creating urban meadows for butterflies and building incredible homes for deadly raptors.
For Britain ’ s rarest birds, it seems unlikely that the busy city centre of London ’ s West End will be its habitat.
It is estimated that there are only 20-40 breeding pairs of red redstart robins in the country.
But in recent years, the rare bird has begun to settle in this crowded area of central London, where it has not been introduced artificially.
In addition to the ochre redtailed robin, there are some unexpected wildlife that are beginning to live in the striking urban landscape.
Moths, butterflies, woodpeckers and even the large brown bat – these species are common in rural pastures and are on the rise in this part of London.
This is a growing trend on a global scale.
The falcons were once endangered in the United States, but now in New York, they are often seen swooping down from skyscrapers and passing through the city at breakneck speed.
These changes are the result of increasing conservation efforts, transforming densely populated cities from wild animal dead ends into attractive habitats where wildlife can live in harmony with city dwellers.
A new initiative even advocates keeping bees in office buildings.
You don ’ t have to completely redesign a city ’ s layout to do this, says Emily Woodason, senior landscape designer at design and planning firm Arup.
Sometimes creating small patches of green space at regular intervals is enough to attract wildlife back to an area.
The Wild West End project, which involves six of London ’ s largest landowners, is seeking to set up 100 square metres of green space every 100 metres.
“It ’ s an ambitious goal, ” says Mr Woodson.“ The ultimate goal is to create a green corridor between London ’ s parks. ”
Endangered red-tailed robins have recently returned to central London (Credit: Getty Images) In addition to planning more green areas, many landowners have chosen to retrofit existing buildings with green walls or roofs.
So far, it seems to have worked.
Since the wildlife baseline assessment two years ago, a number of unexpected species have returned to the area, including the ochre redtailed robin.
“Create spaces where wildlife can live, including rock heaps and log heaps.
They are very good at attracting different insects, and over time, they can allow more species to reproduce naturally, ” says Woodarson. “These conditions are perfect for this bird. ”
Attracting rare species back to the city isn ’ t just because “it ’ s a good thing ”, although it does make city life more diverse and interesting.
Some of the species that these projects have attracted back are ones we rely heavily on for food safety, such as pollinating insects such as bees and butterflies.
Their numbers are declining globally.
“We realized that planning, development, architecture and industrial design together led to the extinction of other species on the planet, ” said Mitchell Joachim, director and co-founder of Terreform, an eco-planning and architecture company.“ I ’ m very passionate about trying to restore these habitats in cities and integrate them into our building plans. ”
Sometimes, that means planning a giant eight-story transparent vertical lawn on the walls of an office building in Manhattan.
Monarch butterflies are native to North America, but since the 1980s, the butterfly has been rapidly extinct due to widespread destruction of milkweed (milkweed), its breeding habitat.
“Males are a highly invasive species, and humans don ’ t like it — it can make you rash or invade your beautiful American lawn, ” Joachim said.
The construction of a space in the building for the Black-Med butterflies is part of an effort to slow their rapid decline.
View copyright Getty Images Image caption The butterflies lay their eggs on the milkweed, but gardeners believe the milkweed is a harmful plant (Credit: Getty Images) "It's a sanctuary for the butterflies, it's where they breed, it's a warm bed for caterpillars and a habitat for chrysalis and adult butterflies," says Joachim A few weeks, and then it flew away. "
In order to have a real impact on the Blackweed population, just one protected area is not enough.
The most important thing is to restore the butterfly ’ s natural habitat – inside and outside the city, on its route to Mexico – and especially to provide more mileage.
In the city, the roof garden is clearly where the milkweed begins to grow.
One of the rooftop gardens is planned to be built on the top of the Butterfly Building where people can say hello to butterflies when they are released outdoors.
This is a contribution that every owner and tenant can make, not just the owners of large landmarks.
In order to make long-term changes, people need to ignore the condition of the lawn for a while so that the milkweed can grow well.
Sometimes wildlife returns to the city not because people have opened up a specific space for them, but because what is harmful to them has been cleared.
Originally considered a magical chemical product, DDT has been widely used in agriculture since the 1940s.
It wasn ’ t until decades later that it was discovered to be highly toxic to many species, including humans, and was banned by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 1972.
The most affected by DDT are birds of prey, as this toxin accumulates in the food chain.
The peregrine falcon, the world ’ s fastest bird of prey, was on the brink of extinction in the United States by 1970.
A group of scientists has launched a conservation campaign called the Peregrine Fund to try to breed falcons in captivity until they can be released into the wild.
The place where the falcon thrives is unexpected.
Planting grass and other plants on roofs can help form a “green corridor ” connecting larger reserves and parks (Credit: Getty Images)“ They ’ re starting to try to put the peregrine falcons back into the city, ” says Erin Katzner, Global Engagement Director at the Peregrine Falcon Foundation.
Skyscrapers provide a suitable habitat for birds – on high, with steep falls and nests away from potential predators such as raccoons or foxes.
Scientists worked with homeowners to build walls on which birds could build nests.
Adequate food for pigeons and migratory birds. As DDT contaminates the food chain, the number of urban game falcons has soared.
“Now, you can find them in almost every city in the United States, including Manhattan, ” says Kazner,“ and you can walk into downtown New York and see falcons flying between skyscrapers. ” Even the birds that have been released to the countryside, there are now a lot of reports of them actively migrating to the city, because the city has become a good habitat.
Birds of prey in cities not only excite birdwatchers, but also help reduce the number of rodents in cities.
Urban rewilding programs often have multiple benefits — green spaces make people happier, they also help solve drainage problems and prevent flooding, as well as provide a home for pollinating insects and other animals.
But perhaps one of their most valuable features is making people feel more connected to nature and more aware of our relationship with the environment.
In the long run, it is not only necessary to plant green plants in existing urban areas, but also to change the urban development model.
Until recent years, urbanisation also meant turning green areas grey with concrete, asphalt and glass from traditional buildings and infrastructure.
There is no doubt that this transformation is harmful to our mental health, physical health, the environment, the ecosystem, and wildlife.
Urban rewilding is one way to reverse this process: Prioritize plants and animals first, and the benefits that come with it for our health, well-being, and the urban environment that comes with it.

title: Canada hosts international conference on Ukraine airliner incident in London, calls for independent criminal investigation
text:
On Thursday, Canadian Foreign Minister François-Philippe Champagne chaired an international panel in London to discuss a thorough investigation into Iran ’ s shooting down of a Ukrainian passenger plane.
Radio-canada This is the first meeting of the International Coordination and Response Team on the downing of the Ukrainian passenger plane, which is made up of countries whose citizens were killed in the crash, including Canada, Ukraine, Sweden, Afghanistan and the United Kingdom.
The meeting took place at the Canada House in Trafalgar Square, London, and began with a small memorial service in which five ministers lit a separate wick with candles and observed a moment of silence.
After a day of closed-door meetings, ministers from the five countries outlined a framework for cooperation with the Iranian authorities in the investigation.
Canadian Foreign Minister Jean-Pierre Champagne said, among other requirements, the framework of cooperation established by the five foreign ministers called for "an independent criminal investigation, followed by a transparent and impartial judicial process" into the shooting down of the Ukrainian airliner.

title: In the future, Lychee and Longan may not be rich enough to buy farmers.
text:
In the future, Lychee and Longan may have money and can not buy farmers how to argue with God?
[Text / Liu Guangying; Photo / Liu Guotai] In the future, the fruit calendar in Taiwan may no longer be litchi and longan, but red mulberry and mangosteen.
Affected by the warm winter this year, not only did lychee and longan not flower and bear fruit, but also prevented bees from harvesting honey, and modern shen farmers were helpless.
The impact of climate change is even greater than we think, and it is even related to the face and rise and fall of the industry.
Taiwan, long known as the king of orchids, has introduced tropical varieties to spread market risks; Hsinchu, which has not been waiting for spring rain, has changed its paddy fields to dry fields to relieve the water shortage crisis; Pingtung fruit farmers have changed to tropical fruits to overcome the problem of poor harvests.
Under the threat of extreme weather, modern Shennong must accelerate the ability to adapt to the environment and develop countermeasures to win this climate war.
In response to climate change, Pingtung farmers have introduced tropical fruits such as durian honey, which are native to Southeast Asian countries, to open up new business opportunities.
(photo by Liu Guotai) Share facebook In the middle of the month, on the wall of a bee breeding and marketing class in Taichung's Waipu, there is a plaque for Cheng Chin-kun to be awarded the Shin Farming Award.
There is no honey this year.
"Beekeeping for 30 years has never been so hard, and the amount of honey is less than 10% in previous years," said Cheng Jinkun, president of the Beekeeping Association.
Because last year was a rare warm winter, the lychee and dragon's eye, which beekeepers rely on, could not blossom, and Shennong could not think of a way.
In the past, more than a dozen barrels of honey were harvested a month, and this year less than two barrels were harvested.
“In a few decades, there may be no winter in Taiwan, ” says Wang Pao-kuan, an Academician at Academia Sinica.
The impact of climate change on Taiwan ’ s agriculture is already underway.
Pingtung: Farewell to betel nuts, red mulberry and durian honey In Pingtung, south of the border, "betel nuts on high trees" are a common sight; but when you look closer, the betel nut trees are filled with durian honey and mandarin.
The chief executive and director brother of Pingtung Jiuru Farmers Association found that climate change brought new opportunities for farmers, and let tropical fruits take root in Pingtung when betel nuts left the market.
Driving to the Hakka settlement of Jiulu Yuquan Village, the road is lined with high betel nut trees, swaying in the hot sun. 78-year-old farmer Huang Shaoming ’ s Hammer Garden, began planting durian honey three years ago, and this summer the official harvest, the largest fruit can reach 9 kg.
At present, the fruit has not been collected and put on the shelves, and many people have already reserved it, and the supply is not in demand.
In the betel nut garden, farmers switch to planting tropical fruit red mulberry.
(Photo by Liu Guotai) Share facebookDurian honey is actually a type of pineapple honey. It is a tropical fruit native to Indonesia and Malaysia. The pulp has a flexible taste, similar to pineapple honey, but it also carries the smell of durian. It is nicknamed durian honey.
"My father doesn't eat betel nuts himself, and the government encourages them to switch to betel nuts, and knows that betel nuts are bad for health," says Huang Shaoming's son, Huang Junjie, who works in Nantou and occasionally returns to Gutian.
They think that if the price of durian honey is good and someone wants to buy it, betel nuts can gradually disappear.
Gong Taiwen, general secretary of the Jiulu Farmers' Association, said that there are about 200 farmers growing durian honey, with a total of more than 2,000 plants.
In recent years, the Association has promoted durian honey to help farmers change their crops and help them sell it.
As the temperature rises, the role of tropical fruits will be heavier.
The heat of the fire is unbearable.
According to statistics from Taiwan ’ s Climate Change Prediction Information and Adaptation Knowledge Platform, the average annual temperature of the Central Weather Bureau ’ s Hengchun Station in the past 100 years has risen by more than 26 ° C, and the number of extreme high temperature days (10% hot days before summer) has increased from zero to 62 days.
In the past year, the average temperature in Pingtung has exceeded 28 ° C for 11 months, which is close to Kuala Lumpur.
It is no wonder that durian honey from Malaysia and mangosteen from Thailand are gaining a foothold in Pingtung.
"We have no power to change climate change, we can only adapt," Gong said, stressing that Taiwan's spirit is to change and survive.
Japanese farmers also have similar ideas with him. Gong Taiwen said that he recently took farmers to visit Okinawa, and found that because the weather is getting hot, more and more farmers are planting mangoes and pineapples. "Japan is importing and replacing them, why not Taiwan?" he asked.
Under the vigorous promotion of Kung Tai-wen (left), the general director of the Pingtung Jiuru Rural Farmers Association, farmers who originally planted betel nuts have turned to tropical fruits, including durian honey and red mulberry.
(photo by Liu Guotai) Share facebook But tropical fruits are still unfamiliar to many people in Taiwan. When the durian honey is ripe, the taste is very heavy. Some farmers collect the durian honey at home, and the fire brigade knocks on the door.
At first, Gong Tai-wen wondered if durian, which also comes from the tropics, could survive.
In the past, many people in Pingtung tried to grow durian in the courtyard, and cut it down after seven or eight years without results.
This year, farmers will vigorously promote the use of grafting, Durian can blossom in 3 to 5 years, durian honey can be fruit in 2 years.
In order to lead the way, Kung and his younger brother, Gong Tai-an, who is the director of the farmers' association, began planting tropical fruits such as mangosteen, mandarin, golden fruit, longgong, and persimmons on their own land 10 years ago. "They want to prove that they can really grow them, so they are willing to change," he said.
His other pride is red mullet. Gong Taiwen said that the sweetness of the new varieties of red mullet is not only improved, but the taste is also closer to lychee.
"Because of the warm winter, lychee and longan are no longer blossoming, people can change to red mullet," said the farmers who grow red mullet.
As for mangosteen, it takes 7 years to plant it to blossom, and Gong Tai'an planted it for a few years, and it also yielded few 3 fruits.
But he was confident, “I ’ ve seen a tree grow 5,000 fruits. ”
The area of betel nut cultivation in Jiuru was originally not much, because the promotion of lemon and tropical fruits has reduced by nearly 40% in the past 10 years, leaving only about 170 hectares.
In September, Gong family relatives of more than 1 hectare of champagne garden, will also be abandoned in September this year, turned into a tropical fruit garden.
Under the efforts of the farmers' association brothers, JiuRu has found new opportunities from climate change.

title: Arrest 17 Crew Including 2 Koreans in Illegal Entry to Russia ｜ News ｜ Eurasia ｜ on.cc
text:
On Wednesday, the Russian embassy in North Korea announced that North Korea had detained a Russian fishing boat and detained 15 Russian and two South Korean crew members on board for illegal entry.
The Russian Embassy in North Korea said in a Facebook post that the crew was detained by North Korean border guards last Wednesday (17) and is currently detained in a hotel in Wonsan city, Gangwon Province.
The vessel, named Xianghailin-8, belongs to the northeastern region fishing company of Nevelsk, the port city of Sakhalin state, and is currently detained in Wonsan city.
The North Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs alleged that the crew members were detained for violating entry regulations and illegally remaining in North Korean waters.
Russian consular officials were allowed to visit the crew on Monday to confirm their health.
South Korea's Unification Ministry said on Wednesday that the two South Korean crew members were also safe and were working to secure their release.

title: 17 Crew Detained in North Korea, Including Korean Nationals _ Hong Kong 01 _ Real Time International
text:
A Russian fishing vessel suspected of mechanical failure, including its engine, drifted to the North Korean coast and is being detained by the North Korean authorities.
South Korea is keeping the North Korean and Russian authorities informed of the incident.
A Russian flag fishing vessel belonging to the “Tohoku Fisheries Company ” of Nevelsk, Russia, departed from Sokcho city in northern South Korea on July 17, according to Russian sources.
The fishing boat was originally scheduled to go fishing in the Sea of Japan, but it was suspected that due to mechanical problems such as engine failure, it drifted to the coast of North Korea.
There were 15 Russian and two South Korean crew members on board, who were reportedly placed in the hotel in good health, and the North Korean authorities were seeking information on the vessel through two South Koreans.
17 people are being detained for illegal entry.
The South Korean government is seeking information from the North Korean authorities, but has not received a response, and the information is now available from Russia.
The United Department said it had sought the assistance of the Russian authorities through diplomatic channels, which was agreed by the Russian side.

title: North Korea seizes Russian fishing boat for 10 days 17 Crew Included 2 Korean Men Not Returned to South Korea
text:
▲ The Russian fishing boat Xiang Hai Lin 8 was detained by North Korea. (Photo / Reproduced by Marine Traffic) reporter Chen Wanzhen / Compilation The Russian Embassy in North Korea recently told the TASS news agency, the North Korean border guard team about 4: 30 am on the 17th detained an Russian fishing boat, Xiang Hai Lin, flying a South Korean flag, into the North Korean territorial sea. There were 15 Russians and two South Koreans on board.
Today, entering the 10th day of the incident, the South Korean Ministry of Unification sent several letters to North Korea on the 18th, and only received a response on the 26th, confirming that the two South Korean crew members on board were safe and sound.
On the 16th, Xiang Hai Lin 8, carrying 17 crew members, departed from the South Korean port of Sokcho and drifted due to a fault on its way to the Russian port of Zarubino, and entered the North Korean Sea in the East Sea (Sea of Japan) on the 17th.
The Russian embassy in North Korea quoted the North Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs as saying that the fishing vessel violated the "entry and stay in the territory of North Korea" and was extradited to the North Korean port of Wonsan.
"Pyongyang is currently investigating the Xiang Hai Lin 8, and based on the friendly relations between Russia and North Korea, it is expected that North Korea will return the fishing boat and its crew to Russia after the investigation," the Russian embassy in North Korea said.
Two South Korean crew members, men in their 50s and 60s, signed a technical guidance contract with a Russian shipping company to board the ship as fishing instructors and supervisors, according to Korean media reports.
The day after the incident, the South Korean authorities learned that the fishing boat was detained, and on the evening of the 18th, they requested a response from North Korea through the Joint Liaison Office in Kaesong.
Due to the delay in waiting for an answer, the United National Assembly issued a notice to North Korea in the name of the president of the Red Cross on the 19th. In addition to two official letters, it also responded to the seven requests of the North and South Korean representatives meeting, which is routine twice a day in the joint liaison office of the two Koreas.
Nine days later, the spokesman of the United Department, Lee Sang-min, said in a briefing on the 26th, "Fortunately, it has been confirmed that the Chinese people and the Russian crew are safely in the hotel together, and will do their best to ensure the safe return of our nationals as soon as possible."
On the other hand, Russian maritime authorities said on the 24th, “We believe that it is illegal for North Korea to seize fishing vessels, because international law allows other countries ’ vessels to sail through economic waters. ”
According to the monitoring system, the Chinese fishing boat was far from the coast of North Korea at that time and was sailing in waters beyond the territorial sea of North Korea. "

title: North Korea detains Russian fishing boat carrying 2 South Koreans
text:
Photo: YONHAP News: A Russian fishing boat carrying two South Koreans was seized by North Korea as it drifted in North Korean territorial waters in the East Sea of the Korean Peninsula.
The 300-tonne Russian fishing boat, which left the port of Sokcho in South Korea on Wednesday afternoon, was taken to Wonsan port after its engine failed on its way to the port of Zarubino in Russia.
They are now staying at a hotel in Wonsan and are under investigation by the North Korean authorities.
The South Korean government immediately contacted the North through the North-South Joint Liaison Office to request the return of the South Korean crew, but the North Korean side has not yet responded.

title: Klimt's stolen masterpiece found 23 years ago, but still questionable - International
text:
Twenty-three years ago, Gustav Klimt ’ s Portrait of a Lady was stolen from the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in Piacenza, Italy.
On February 22, 1997, the gallery was being renovated for a special exhibition.
The painting mysteriously disappeared, only the outer frame of the painting was found by the roof skylight. When the police determined that the thief removed the frame, the entire painting was rolled up and carried out of the skylight, but no suspects were found. In 2014, the Italian police reopened the investigation and found the suspected painting, but it was later confirmed to be a fake or a copy.
In December last year, a gardener at the Ricci Oddi Gallery found a plastic bag inside the sandwich of the wall, which turned out to be the famous painting.
At that time, everyone suspected that this was the original painting.
After careful examination by experts, it was announced to the outside on Friday that it was confirmed to be the original painting.
In the future, the police still have to clarify the suspicion of the theft, such as: Is the painting hidden in the gallery from the beginning to the end?
Or was it returned after being stolen?
Who did it again?
(Photo / Associated Press) The Ricci Oddi Gallery sent police officers to guard the painting, which was protected by a specially made frame, when it announced the news.
Prosecutor Ornella Chicca said excitedly: "After infrared radiation and other non-invasive detection methods, we are excited to determine that this is the real Klimt."
Klimt completed this masterpiece in 1917, the last year of his life, and the Ricci Oddi Gallery acquired it in 1925 until it was stolen in 1997.
The expert said that the painting is in good condition, only the edge of the canvas is slightly damaged, and it is suspected that the suspect left traces when he hurriedly removed the frame.
(China Times Newsletter)

title: Russian fishing boat detained by North Korea for 10 days and 17 crew released
text:
SEOUL, July 28, 2019 (AFP) The Russian Embassy in North Korea said today that North Korea has released a Russian fishing boat detained for violating immigration regulations.
The South Korean side confirmed that the fishing boat had arrived in Sokcho this afternoon.
The Russian Embassy in North Korea said on Thursday that North Korea had detained a fishing boat carrying 15 Russian and two South Korean crew members for violating entry rules.
Russia said the ship did not violate any regulations.
The embassy said in a Facebook post that the two South Korean crew members had also been released, adding that the boat had left Wonsan, North Korea, last night.
"The vessel has separated from the Kwon San port terminal at 7.30 pm (yesterday) and is headed for Sokcho, South Korea, where the two South Korean crew members will disembark."
The embassy said it would continue to investigate the "circumstances" of the vessel's detention.
South Korea's Unification Ministry, which handles relations between the two Koreas, welcomed the "safe release" of the fishing vessel, saying it was "a positive move from a humanitarian point of view."

title: North Korea Seizes Russian Fishing Vessel for Second Interviews, Releases 2 South Korean Crew

South Koreans.
The South Korean government sent letters to North Korea several times after the incident, asking for the return of two South Korean citizens, but there was no response, only to confirm that they were safe in Wonsan. The latest news on the 28th pointed out that after 11 days of the incident, two South Korean crew members finally returned home safely.
According to the Korean Associated Press, the Xiang Hai Lin 8 returned to the South Korean port of Sokcho around 1: 00 p.m. local time on the 28th, and the 17 people on board were in good health.

title: North Korea Releases Detained Russian Fishing Vessel 2 South Korean Crew ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ Real-time International
text:
South Korea ’ s Ministry of National Defense said on July 28 that a Russian fishing vessel was detained by the DPRK on July 17 for violating immigration regulations.
It was released on the 27th, and took all the crew to Sokcho Port, Gangwon Province, South Korea, around 1: 00 p.m. on the 28th.
The Russian embassy in North Korea said it had released a Russian fishing vessel that had been detained 11 days earlier, saying it was leaving for a South Korean port where two South Korean crew members would come ashore.
The Russian fishing vessel, Xiang Hai Lin 8, departed from South Korea ’ s Sokcho port for the port of Zarubino in Russia on the afternoon of the 16th.
It broke down on the way and was detained on the 17th after entering the waters of North Korea in the eastern part of the peninsula.
Russia stressed that it did not enter North Korean waters at the time. However, Tass quoted the company that owned the fishing boat as saying that the boat had entered a 50-mile area at the time, which was the reason for its detention.
After undergoing maintenance, it departed from Wonsan Port, North Korea, at about 7 p.m. on the 28th.
All 17 people on board were unharmed (except for two Korean crew members and the other 15 Russian crew members).
In an interview with Russia ’ s Tass news agency, a crew member said North Korea had not fined the fishing vessel and the incident was over.
South Korea's Unification Ministry highly praised North Korea for allowing ships and crew to leave.

title: Russian fishing boat and South Korean crew detained by North Korea arrive safely in South Korea
text:
North Korea has released the Russian fishing boat and all its crew.
After being detained for 11 days, all 17 crew members, including 15 Russians and two South Koreans, arrived safely in South Korea.
The smooth resolution of the whole incident should be influenced by the recent close relations between Russia and North Korea.
The ship, which left the South Korean port of Sokcho on Monday for the Russian port of Zarubino, suffered engine failure and was detained in the North Korean waters on Thursday.
Two of the crew members were reportedly contracted by the Russian ship owner to conduct fishery guidance and supervision liaison. The two were investigated in a hotel in Wonsan, along with other Russian crew members.
In this incident, the deadlocked relations between the two Koreas stand in contrast to the close relations between Russia and North Korea.
The Ministry of Unification of the Republic of Korea (ROK) sent several letters to the South Korean Liaison Office to clarify the situation after learning of the arrest of the fishing boat on Wednesday, but did not receive a response.
North Korea did not notify the South Korean side until the fishing boat was released to the port of Sokcho on the afternoon of August 28.
On the contrary, the North and the Russian authorities have held close consultations on the return of the fishing boat.
South Korea has cooperated with Russia through diplomatic channels.
It is believed that the North Korean decision to release the ship has nothing to do with the strengthening of cooperation between the two sides after the Russian-North summit.
South Korea's Unification Ministry said the move was a humanitarian measure and had nothing to do with inter-Korean relations.
In fact, relations between North and South Korea have not yet entered a stable situation.
North Korea refused 50,000 tons of rice aid to South Korea, saying the latest missile launch was a "warning" to South Korea.
However, the measures taken by North Korea this time also reflect positive factors.
In the past 10 years, there have been two incidents of South Korean fishing boats being detained by North Korea, in August 2010, the "Dasheng" into North Korean waters was detained for 31 days, and the "Xingzhen" was detained for seven days in October 2017, which shows that the incident was handled relatively smoothly.
The past is not without examples of seemingly insignificant events that have opened the door to North-South dialogue.
North Korea's move to negotiate with Russia and maintain a "value neutral" stance with South Korea does not seem to have a positive impact on inter-Korean relations, but coincidentally, the North's wooden boat crossed the border and South Korea quickly returned three North Korean crew members.
Such incidents will continue to accumulate, or will bring unexpected opportunities for inter-Korean relations.

title: Russian fishing boat and South Korean crew detained by North Korea arrive safely in South Korea

title: 60 million euros of famous paintings stolen 23 years ago _ News _ Asia Europe and Africa _ on.cc
text:
A gardener in Italy found an oil painting when he was cleaning vines on the exterior wall of a gallery last month.
According to experts, the painting is the work of Austrian symbolist Gustav Klimt, stolen from the same gallery in 1997.
The mystery of the lost painting that has plagued the local area for 23 years has been solved in a dramatic manner.
The stolen painting “Portrait of a Woman ” is Klimt ’ s only painting with a value of 60 million euros (about HK $516 million).
In 1997, before the painting was exhibited at the gallery in Piacenza, the police speculated that the prisoner had removed the frame from the roof of the gallery and hung the work, but the search was fruitless for many years.
The authorities reopened the investigation in 2016 after new evidence of the suspect ’ s DNA was found in the frame, but the painting remains unaccounted for.
Until last month, when two gardeners were cleaning the vines of the gallery, they found a painting in a bag in the dark room behind a metal door on the outer wall.
The authorities initially thought the painting was just a reproduction of 1917, but experts used ultraviolet light and other tests to compare the 1996 photo to confirm that it was genuine. Prosecutors will test whether the painting has been hidden in the wall or has been returned recently, and the painting can be re-exhibited after completion.
However, the biggest mystery of Piacenza ’ s literary world still remains unsolved.
After the reappearance of the famous painting, the local media received a letter from two mysterious people claiming to be painting thieves, saying that they had stolen it and hidden it in the wall. Guido Cauzzi, an art expert, said that the painting was in good condition and whether it had been hidden inside the wall remained to be investigated.
It is worth mentioning that someone told a local newspaper in 2015 that the painting would be returned to Zhao on the 20th anniversary of the theft, but there was no mention of it; it is unknown whether it is related to this discovery.

title: Canada grants $750,000 each to victims of Ukraine Airlines: Iran must pay compensation
text:
Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has announced that funds will be allocated to help the families of the victims.
(Reuters) - Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said on Thursday that he will provide $25,000 (about NT $750,000) in emergency assistance to the families of Canadian citizens who died in the Ukraine air crash, hoping that the families of the victims can smoothly arrange for the fate of the victims.
Trudeau said Canada wanted Iran to compensate the families, but they couldn ’ t wait weeks, so the government decided to help first.
"I want to make it clear that we want Iran to compensate these families, but these families can't wait for weeks and they need help right now," Trudeau said at a press conference.
As a result, the Canadian government has decided to grant $25,000 in emergency aid to each of the families of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have died, with a guarantee that it will be disbursed within a few days.
Trudeau also stressed that Iran's compensation will not reach the government's pocket, "we do not know what the final compensation will be, but I guarantee that the families of the victims will receive it directly, not the Canadian government."
Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed shortly after takeoff from Tehran, Iran, killing all 176 people on board, including 63 Canadians, at least 30 residents of Alberta, and at least a dozen Ontario university students and professors. Professionals.
The first victims are expected to arrive in Canada within a few days.
Iranian authorities finally admitted on Wednesday that it was a mistake, and Gholamhossein Esmaili, a spokesman for the Iranian Ministry of Justice, announced on Thursday that it had “conducted an extensive investigation and arrested a number of people ” in the incident, without giving further details.
