title: 2 billion paintings mysteriously stolen … Changchun vine has climbed the outer wall of the gardener to find: 23 years have not left
text:
Austrian painter Gustav Klimt ’ s Portrait of a Lady was stolen for 23 years.
A gardener in Italy recently found a painting in the outer wall of a gallery in the northern city of Piacenza, “Portrait of a Lady ”, which was stolen from the same gallery in 1997.
The painting disappeared for 23 years and was found in the same place.
According to the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), "Portrait of a Lady" is a work by Austrian painter Klimt, completed between 1916 and 1917, belonging to the late Klimt painting.
Italian collector Giuseppe Ricci Oddi bought it in 1925 and kept it in the Audi Gallery of Modern Art of the same name until it was stolen on February 22, 1997, while the museum was preparing a special exhibition.
At that time, the thief deliberately left the frame on the roof of the gallery, making people think that the thief was trying to steal the words through the skylight in an attempt to mislead the direction of the case.
However, after the actual investigation by the police, it was found that the size of the skylight was too small to allow the painting to pass, and the investigation lost its clues.
Until December 2019, when the gallery gardener was cleaning the outer wall of the ivy, he accidentally found a metal plate on the wall, and the missing “Portrait of a Lady ” was hidden in the mezzanine behind the metal plate, and was found wrapped in a black bag, and kept in generally good condition.
The report pointed out that the "lady portrait" is estimated to be worth 60 million euros (about NT $2 billion), why it appeared in the gallery wall is still a mystery.
Italian prosecutor Ornella Chicca said the actual painting was verified as authentic, but it remains unclear whether the painting was later smuggled back into the wall mezzanine or was hidden there from the beginning, pending further examination and clarification.
It is reported that the wall has not been cleaned of ivy for at least 10 years.

title: 23 year old Klimt painting accidentally found in a stolen museum
text:
A painting by well-known Austrian painter Klimt was stolen in an Italian art museum nearly 23 years ago, but was accidentally recovered when a gardener cleaned the ivy on the museum ’ s exterior.
But exactly why the painting was hidden in the niche of the museum ’ s exterior wall remains a mystery.
Italian authorities have confirmed that the painting found last December at the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in the northern Italian city of Piacenza is indeed a Portrait of a Lady by Gustav Klimt, which was stolen from the museum in 1997.
The painting, painted by Klimt in 1916 – 1917, was purchased by Italian collector Giuseppe RicciOddi in 1925 and kept in his own museum of the same name until it was stolen in preparation for a special exhibition on February 22, 1997.
The painting is estimated to be worth at least €60 million (about NT $2 billion).
Just when everyone thought that the “lady portrait ” would evaporate forever, in December last year, when the gardener cleaned the ivy on the exterior wall of the Ricciotti Museum of Modern Art, he accidentally found a metal door plate and opened it to find a niche with a black bag in it, which was suspected to contain the painting.
In order to determine the authenticity of the painting found, the expert used infrared and ultraviolet light to irradiate the study, and compared it with the image taken during the examination of the original painting in 1996.
“I can tell you with emotion that this work is authentic, ” said Italian prosecutor Ornella Chicca.
As for whether the painting was stolen and kept in this niche, or put in later, more tests are still needed to clarify.
According to the museum ’ s official account, the exterior wall of the painting has not been trimmed for nearly 10 years.
Zika said that once the relevant tests are completed, the works will be displayed again at the museum. (Translator: Hou Wen-ting / Authored by: Zhang Zhengqian) 1090118

title: Industrial emission reduction is difficult to stop the climate crisis, the United States advocates vegetarian stop intensive agriculture - 20190805 - International
text:
Agriculture, forestry and other land uses account for nearly a quarter of global greenhouse gas emissions. About half of the greenhouse gas emissions are methane, the first draft of the IPCC report said, humans are using 72% of the world ’ s ice-free land to provide food, clothing, etc., to support the global population. The lands further increase carbon emissions.
In addition, intensive agriculture also increases land erosion and reduces the content of organic matter on the ground.
With frequent and severe weather phenomena such as floods and droughts caused by climate change, and land degradation exacerbated by hot weather and sea level rise, the problem will worsen in the future.
Global warming of 1.2 ° C in Arctic sea ice also shows a grim picture of the global environment, including the Arctic sea ice cover fell to a near record low in July this year, the heat wave hit Europe last month, and the global temperature in July was 1.5 ° C to 3 ° C higher than usual, and the global temperature in July was 1.2 ° C higher than in July before the industrial revolution.
The last of these figures is of particular concern, as the IPCC has warned that a temperature rise of more than 1.5 ° C would make the climate unstable, while a 2 ° C rise would make the risk even greater.
The report proposes other ways to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, including switching to a vegetarian diet, adopting a healthy and sustainable diet, such as eating more coarse grains, vegetables, nuts and seeds, reducing methane emissions by eating less meat, and reducing food waste.
Countries should manage their land in a more sustainable manner to reduce carbon emissions, including by stopping drainage works to protect peatlands. Policies such as strengthening land use rights and establishing weather, crop yields and seasonal climate warning systems should also be put in place.
Bob Ward, director of policy at the Grantham Institute for Climate Change and Environment in London, said the IPCC report showed that the emissions reduction targets needed to stop the climate crisis will become increasingly difficult to achieve.
(The Guardian)

title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
text:
The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.
(Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.
The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.
Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.
According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.
If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.
Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.
“If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.
In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.
Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.
Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.
Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.
Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.
Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.
“Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”

title: Report: Climate and food supply threats must accelerate emissions reduction ｜ News ｜ Americas ｜ on.cc
text:
The United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) issued a report on Thursday (8), warning that the food security and global warming crises facing humanity in the coming decades will become increasingly serious, and that it is necessary to accelerate the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and stop unsustainable farming and deforestation.
Experts say that as long as global temperatures rise by two degrees Celsius, the risk to food supply will be very high.
The report says that if people do not change their land-use habits, efforts to stop global warming and solve food supply problems will be wasted, and most importantly, to protect the rainforest.
Land and climate are not unrelated, forests, plants, soils, etc. can absorb 1 / 3 of the greenhouse gases emitted by human activities.
With the increase in population and the continuous deforestation of agricultural land to produce food and fuel, a large number of trees have disappeared; and agriculture uses 70% of the world ’ s water, human activities in forests have also released carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
The Committee stressed that any measures to combat climate change and increase food supply will not succeed unless they are accompanied by significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions; how governments, industry and farmers use land and manage greenhouse gas emissions will be key.

title: UN calls for change in response to world agricultural crisis
text:
The United Nations report on the impact of climate change on agriculture released Thursday said that changes must be made from the use of farmland, the production of crops and human food consumption, otherwise it will be difficult to guarantee human food supply, maintain human health and maintain the diversity of the earth's species in the face of increasing global warming.
A summary of the report published by the United Nations ’ Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the world ’ s population growth and food composition tend to be high in protein. The massive increase in demand has led to unprecedented levels of demand for farmland and fresh water.
The United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) met in Geneva this week to discuss and approve the report as a guidance document for the Conference on the Implementation of the Paris Climate Agreement to be held later this year in Chile.
Before the start of the Geneva conference, Greenpeace demonstrators from the international environmental protection organization called “Less Meat = Less Heat. ”
"Climate Action Now".
Radio-canada experts pointed out that the continuous development of agricultural technology to improve the yield of each unit of farmland, such as cross breeding, genetic modification, agricultural farming digital technology, etc., these are positive factors to promote the improvement of agricultural output; and the earth's warming caused by soil erosion, land desertification, water and drought and insect diseases have led to the reduction of crop yield in many parts of the world.
www.rcinet.ca Wechat: radio-canada Eat less meat and www.rcinet.ca Wechat: radio-canada One of the solutions proposed in the above-mentioned United Nations report to the problem of food shortages and the excessive use of resources in agriculture is to eat less meat.
The consensus among radio-canada experts is that animal husbandry that produces meat consumes significantly more resources than crops, so reducing meat consumption can feed more of the world ’ s population with existing agricultural resources.
Radio-canada Reducing meat consumption can be achieved in three ways, one is to encourage people to eat less meat and eat more plant-based foods; the other is to encourage people to replace animal meat with plant-based meat; and the third is to operate livestock in a sustainable manner.
The United Nations estimates show that if the world population changes the composition of food and reduces meat consumption, the world could use millions of square kilometers less farmland by 2050 and reduce greenhouse gases by 0.7 to 800 million tons.
Radio-canada experts point out that reducing meat consumption in the food composition also has health benefits for many people around the world.
Two billion adults in the world are overweight or obese, while 820 million people in the world suffer from malnutrition due to lack of food.
Radio-canada statistics show that the world ’ s per capita consumption of edible oil and meat has doubled in more than half a century, while 25 to 30 percent of the world ’ s food is wasted.
In its 60-page summary of its report, the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) noted that the temperature of the earth's farmland topsoil has risen by 1.53 degrees Celsius compared to pre-industrial times, almost twice the average temperature of 0.87 degrees Celsius on the Earth's surface during the same period.
Rapid warming of farmland topsoil directly leads to more frequent heatwaves, droughts, heavy rains, soil degradation and desertification.
Radio-canada The land used by humans in various ways accounts for 70% of the Earth ’ s available land without ice cover, and agricultural water accounts for 70% of the Earth ’ s fresh water.
In the 10-year period from 2007 to 2016, agriculture, forestry and livestock accounted for 23% of the world ’ s total greenhouse gas emissions.
Radio-canada gives a concrete example. Statistics from Canada in 2017 show that the greenhouse gas emissions from fertilizer use in Canadian agriculture in a year are equal to the greenhouse gas emissions of 2.7 million cars in a year.
The United Nations stresses that the key is to act as soon as possible; if human action is slow, the damage to agro-ecosystems caused by global warming could be irreversible in many ways.

title: Stop global warming by reducing meat consumption
text:
2019-08-09 Changing the management of land, agricultural products and diets The United Nations released a report on the impact of climate change on land on the 8th, warning that the food security and global warming crises facing humanity in the next few decades will become increasingly serious. To curb greenhouse gas emissions, the world must change the management of land, agricultural products and diets, such as cutting meat and stopping farming practices that are not conducive to sustainable development. and deforestation, or humanity will face painful choices over food security and rising temperatures in the coming decades.
In this special report on climate change and land, the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) pointed out that changes in global population growth and consumption patterns have led to the consumption of land and water resources at an unprecedented rate. Without a radical change in the way people use land, efforts to curb global warming while supporting a growing population could be nullified.
The report highlights the need to protect remaining rainforests as a barrier to climate change mitigation.
In response to the belief that large-scale afforestation and biofuel projects will offset the effects of human destruction of the environment, the IPCC pointed out that these large-scale projects may endanger food security, and that emission reduction is the key to avoiding disaster.
According to the report, plant-based food, along with sustainable food from animals, may release up to 7 million square kilometers of land by 2050, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by 700 to 800 million tons per year.
Delaying action could have an irreversible impact on some ecosystems and, in the long run, release more greenhouse gases from ecosystems that accelerate global warming.
Although the report does not explicitly advocate a meat-free diet, it calls for major changes in farming and eating habits to limit the impact of population growth and to change consumption patterns for uncontrolled use of land and water resources.
The IPCC report helps guide governments on how to implement the 2015 Paris Agreement when they attend the United Nations Climate Change Conference in Chile this year to avoid runaway climate change.
One of the authors of the report, IPCC Vice President Shi Kei, said that improving the way land is used to produce food plays a necessary role in tackling climate change. Changing to a more balanced diet can help adapt to and limit climate change. Some diets require more land and water, resulting in more carbon emissions, but some diets not only have a lower carbon footprint but also reduce stress on the land.
Land is closely linked to climate, with a third of human emissions absorbed by forests, plants and soils.
Intensive development of land resources to produce large amounts of carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide to accelerate global warming.
If the land is cultivated more sustainably, the soil will absorb more carbon.

title: UN Report: Over-Reclamation Threatens Food Future
text:
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), a United Nations agency, assembled 103 scientists from 52 countries to conduct research and published a climate assessment report on August 8.
The report stressed that human beings should change the way they use land and produce food, or else they will face food security problems not only in the next few decades, but also in the next few decades.
According to the report, in addition to accelerating climate change, unhealthy soils and forests can in turn cause land degradation, desertification, further exacerbate climate problems and even cause food security problems.
The report also said that if the temperature of the earth does rise above the previous Paris agreement of two degrees Celsius, the now plump soil is likely to become barren.
Extreme weather can also cause the production of food crops to fluctuate.
In addition, infrastructure built on permafrost, such as railways, will collapse after global warming due to the melting of permafrost.
The main elements of the report are summarized as follows: 1.
Land use activities, such as food production and livestock, account for 23 per cent of global emissions. 2.
If carbon emissions continue at current levels, extreme weather events will become more frequent, agricultural areas will be reduced and nutritional content will decline, and food security will be in full crisis. 3.
If global temperatures rise by 1.5 degrees Celsius, an estimated 178 million people will face water scarcity and land desertification by 2050.
If global temperatures rise by 2 degrees Celsius, the number of victims will increase to 220 million.
If countries around the world can use land in a more sustainable way, trees and soils will significantly curb the negative effects of climate change.
Methane emissions from animal husbandry are also one of the reasons for the rise in global temperatures The importance of grassland ecosystems At present, about 70% of the earth's ice-free land area has been developed for food production.
Steppe ecosystems can store carbon dioxide, which is important for climate stability, but is often overlooked.
If the grassland is directly used for animal husbandry, there is no need to cut down the forest.
But now a lot of grasslands are being developed and converted to crops, resulting in a lot of carbon dioxide being released into the atmosphere.
Joao Campari, WWF ’ s global food action leader, told Deutsche Welle: “Most people focus on forests, but we want to promote the importance of grasslands.
“If we were to increase food productivity, perhaps more than 50 percent of the changes would occur in temperate grasslands and savannas, ” she said.
Campari also told Deutsche Welle that if carbon emissions continue to increase, climate change will cause soybean and corn production in the United States to plummet by 80% in the next 60 years.
In addition, the Asian Development Bank has warned that climate change will affect the production of major food crops.
Rice production in southern India, for example, could be reduced by 5% by 2030 and by 14% over the next three decades.
Falling food production also contributes to higher food prices.
About a third of food is now discarded or wasted in the production process.
Unnecessary production and the release of carbon dioxide from food decay account for an astonishing 8% of global carbon emissions.
The researchers also found that the concentration of carbon dioxide also affects the nutritional value of food: the more carbon dioxide, the lower the nutritional value.
“Food does not come from the plate, ” Alisher Mirzabaev, co-author of the IPCC report, told Deutsche Welle in her own name, adding that the IPCC report was not just a warning but a call to action:“ The solution is possible. ”
In most cases, this involves scaling up the application.
"First of all, stop deforestation and stop reclaiming land for food."
Campari also hopes to raise consumer awareness of the environment.
“Consumers should be aware that what they eat doesn ’ t come out of a plate.
Behind the food they see, there is also a lot of labor and natural resources involved.
He called for a reduction in food waste and for consumers to diversify their diets.
He said that only 12 species of plants and five species of animals account for 75 percent of the food consumed by humans.
Barron Joseph Orr, chief scientist at the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, said that asking consumers to make some changes does not make consumers uncomfortable.
People concerned about the impact of food crops on the land should find easier and easier ways to track it; efforts to promote conscious consumer spending should also improve land and climate in the long run.
Orr called on people not to be discouraged by the latest report of the United Nations, but to be more determined to look ahead and take action.

title: UN report: Eating less meat and more vegetables could help fight climate warming
text:
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption The bigger carbon footprint of meat is almost a cliché.
Although many people are concerned about the living environment and future of the planet and future generations, they do not know what they can do as individuals.
Experts from the United Nations have suggested that in order to slow global warming, it is best to change eating habits to a plant-based diet.
In other words, it is an appeal to everyone to protect the environment, must eat more vegetables, eat less meat.
The United Nations has produced a major report on climate change.
According to the report, the carnivorous diet in the West is accelerating global warming.
The report was written by 107 scientists from the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
The report pointed out that more efficient and rational use of land could make it better to absorb human-generated carbon dioxide.
With global warming, 2019 has become one of the hottest three years in human history.
Experts in the United Nations climate change report say they are not telling people to stop eating meat, but to eat less or consider changing their eating habits from meat-based to vegetarian.
The report also called for an end to the destruction of land and desertification.
Image caption Burping and farting can also produce more greenhouse gases First, climate change poses a threat to humanity's food supply.
Rising temperatures, increased rainfall and more extreme weather events have affected arable land, crops and livestock.
The food production process itself also contributes to global warming.
Agriculture and animal husbandry account for a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions.
For example, raising livestock such as cattle and sheep will consume more land and resources.
In addition, methane emissions from animals can also contribute to climate warming.
Animal products account for 58% of total CO2 emissions from food production.
At the same time, deforestation to expand rangelands for livestock breeding is further contributing to climate change.
Agriculture expert Stephenson said that reducing meat consumption is necessary and necessary if we are to meet climate change targets.
Reduce food waste Image caption The Swiss charity buys food to stop waste.
In addition to reducing meat consumption, experts also encourage people to minimize food waste.
A charity in Switzerland has sent food not sold in supermarkets to local families and charities to reduce food waste.
At the same time, they made some expired bread into biscuits.
All of this helps to reduce CO2 emissions from the production of food.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Although forests can absorb carbon dioxide, too many forests cannot cope.
Trees and forests can absorb carbon dioxide from human activities, especially in the northern hemisphere.
It can help mitigate climate change.
However, it is alarming that further warming of the Earth will also affect the growth of vegetation and forests.
The United Nations report also said that some areas near the Earth's equator have become too overheated to allow vegetation to grow.
Dr. Katrin Fleischer of the Technical University of Munich, Germany, warned that phosphorus deficiency in the soil is already occurring in some areas.
Less phosphorus in the soil will cause trees to grow slowly.
This means that the rainforest has reached its limit and will no longer be able to absorb any excess carbon dioxide, she said.
If this is the case, the overheating of the earth will accelerate significantly.
Soil and Climate Change Image caption Restoring soil in muddy marshes is a key factor in climate change.
Soils are second only to oceans in terms of carbon dioxide uptake and storage.
Plants in the soil absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it in the soil.
However, deforestation and poor farming practices can undermine the ability of soils to absorb carbon dioxide.
When the soil degrades, it releases carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere.
At the same time, plant growth will also be affected, resulting in a vicious circle.
Climate change is expected to accelerate this process.
High temperatures exacerbate the decomposition of organic matter in the soil and increase greenhouse gas emissions.
Reducing and reversing soil damage can bring immediate benefits to local communities, according to the report.
At the same time, better land management, including controlled grazing and tree planting, can make the soil more fertile.
This will help reduce poverty and promote food security, forming a virtuous circle.
Solution Image caption What individuals can do is eat more vegetables and eat less meat.
Given that land plays such an important role in climate change, how can we reverse the trend of further destruction of land and make it part of the solution?
Experts say humans must change the way they use land.
Of course, this will be a daunting challenge, especially when it comes to major changes in farming practices.
Scientists said that in addition to the following measures can be taken to protect the natural tropical rainforest resources, eat less red meat, eat more vegetables.
Preservation and restoration of peatlands Encourage "agroforestry", where food crops are combined with trees for cultivation

title: Prime Minister John Johnson does not welcome refugees, threatens to send back refugees crossing the English Channel - International
text:
Nearly 100 refugees crossed the English Channel this week by boat, trying to reach Britain from France to seek asylum.
British Prime Minister John Johnson warned refugees not to cross the British Channel on Friday, saying they "will send you back".
Immigrants who enter illegally will be considered illegal immigrants and will be treated as illegal immigrants.
The speech was criticized by opposition Labour and Liberal Democrats, who described it as misleading, creating tension and antagonism, and violating international law.
"The most important thing is to stop them from crossing the sea from France, so we are working very closely with the French authorities," Johnson told reporters.
I hope these people will know that crossing the sea is very dangerous, you may think the weather is very good, but it is very dangerous.
Johnson also said he would “send the refugees back. ”
He said the UK should not be seen as a place where people can come and break the law by entering the country illegally.
If someone enters the country illegally, they are illegal immigrants, and they will be legally defined as such.
Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn has stressed that consideration should be given to whether refugees come from areas affected by the war. The Liberal Democrats have described Johnson ’ s comments as inhumane and contrary to international law.
Liberal Democrat MP Christine Jardine criticized the labeling of “illegal immigrants ” as completely wrong.
Human rights groups say the UK has an obligation under the EU ’ s Dublin Regulation to ensure asylum claims are assessed and considered.
The British Border Protection Agency intercepted two small boats carrying nine and 11 people, claiming to be from countries such as Iran, Guinea and Kuwait.

title: Iraqi migrant drowns off Belgian coast after crossing English Channel
text:
BRUSSELS, Aug 27, 2019 (AFP) The body of an Iraqi migrant attempting to swim from France to Britain drowned while crossing the English Channel, Belgian authorities said today.
The Bruges prosecutor's office said the 48-year-old was found near the coastal resort of Zeebrugge on Wednesday wearing a life jacket made of empty plastic bottles and carrying a small bag containing identification documents.
"This is the first time we have found the bodies of migrants," Carl Decaluwe, governor of West Flanders, told AFP today. Officials believe the dead drowned while trying to swim from a beach in northern France to Britain.
His body is believed to have been brought to Belgian waters by ocean currents.
The Belgian news agency Belga reported that the dead were found drifting near a wind power plant about 30 kilometers offshore of Zebruze.
According to the Belgian news agency, the dead man was unable to obtain asylum in Germany after trying to swim to Britain.
Eight days ago, a Belgian sailor spotted a man, wearing a belt made of empty plastic bottles, shouting for help in the sea off Dunkirk, France.
The sailor informed the French maritime authorities of the incident on the 18th, indicating that he had tried to save the man, but that he had been swept away by the current.
Migrants are now at greater risk of migrating from France to Britain because of its uncompromising approach to economic migrants seeking a better life in Europe than those fleeing war or persecution at home.
Some 1,450 migrants have been rescued by British or French coastguard teams since January, nearly double the number of people trying to cross the Channel in 2018.

title: Arab League rejects Middle East peace plan
text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas took up a map showing the decline of Palestinian territory over the past decades at a meeting of the League of Arab States on the 1st. (photo by Internet screenshot) Share facebook "The peace plan defies the minimum rights and aspirations of the Palestinians!" Rejects Trump ’ s and Israel ’ s “Deal of the Century, ” saying the plan ignores Palestinian rights and does not lead to a just peace agreement.
According to Al Jazeera, the Arab League mentioned in a statement that the resolution will not cooperate with the United States on the plan, and called on Israel to refrain from imposing it by force.
The Palestinian side argues that Israel and Palestine should draw up a "two-state solution" that would allow Palestine to have territory that existed before the 1967 Middle East war, with East Jerusalem as its capital, during which Israel occupied the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, and East Jerusalem.
Trump ’ s Middle East peace plan, proposed last week, allows Israel to annex large swathes of the West Bank formerly occupied by Palestine, including the Jordan Valley, and the current illegal Israeli settlements, leaving only part of East Jerusalem for Palestine as a symbolic capital.
Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas threatened to sever all relations with Israel and the United States, including security.
Abbas said there had been “no real progress ” on the Palestinian issue since the United States intervened in the Israeli-Palestinian negotiations, and that the Palestinians had withdrawn from the negotiations after the United States recognized Jerusalem as Israel ’ s capital in 2017.
According to the Financial Times, although the Palestinians reiterated their support for the "two-state solution" at the meeting, some Arab countries did not take a firm stand.
Critics argue that the divergence of opinion among the Arab states is due to the fact that some Gulf states see Iran as the biggest current threat in the Middle East.
These countries are attached to the United States and Israel under the strategy of "enemy is friend", so try to avoid confrontation with Trump on the Israeli-Palestinian issue.

title: Warming Effect Wheat Planting Decreased
text:
Wheat production has fallen to its lowest level in more than a century due to excessive rainfall and excessive soil moisture during the spring planting season in the Midwest, potentially impacting the supply of biscuits such as soda and Oreo, making these products the latest victims of climate change.
Soft red winter wheat has been particularly hard hit, with sowing in key growing states such as Illinois declining by 25%.
This can be bad news for those who love small snacks, as soft red winter wheat is the raw material for popular products such as cookies, Oreo and Cheez-It.
Last year ’ s record rainfall caused farmers in the United States to sow at the slowest pace ever, even abandoning the “double cropping ” strategy of planting soybeans in the spring and wheat in the fall on the same farm.
These farmers chose to give up their wheat cultivation.
Climate change is disrupting traditional farming schedules around the world.
Some measurements show that the United States is in its second warmest winter in 70 years, causing southern fruit trees to blossom weeks earlier.
In Vietnam, early soil salinization in the Mekong Delta is threatening rice paddies, while changing global rainfall times, wildfires in Australia and droughts in Russia are also threatening food production.
For wheat growing regions in the United States, the record rainfall last spring led to an unprecedented delay in planting, and the harvest time was also extended to fall, but autumn is the time when farmers have always wanted to plant winter wheat.
“Weather dominates the decision-making process, ” said Sezer, vice president of cereals at Citizens Elevator in Michigan. U.S. government data shows that soft red winter wheat cultivation in Michigan has fallen 7 percent.
Reduced production is reversing the price trend.
Soft red winter wheat is usually cheaper than hard red winter wheat, which is used to make bread flour. However, with the reduction of planting area, soft red winter wheat has rarely been more expensive than hard red winter wheat.
Fewer cultivation is not the only threat, as warmer and wetter weather in the United States may help fungi to multiply before the June harvest season begins.
Last year, fungal problems led to a decline in the quality of agricultural products, and the price of good quality agricultural products that can be used to make food increased.
In last month's financial report, the head of Yizi International mentioned that the first half of this year suffered from unfavourable raw material cost factors.

title: Palestine Faced with Oppression and Betrayal
text:
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas on Tuesday (10) at the United Nations Security Council, not only criticized the Middle East peace plan proposed by the United States, "the legitimacy of the abolition of Palestinian rights", but also described the land as "Swiss cheese", in order to reiterate "the Palestinians will resolutely reject the Israeli-American proposal".
Although Abbas ’ s position is supported by three transnational organizations, the League of Arab States, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and the African Union, the Palestinian people, in addition to hoping to attract the attention of the international community, can only rely on a weak force to resist.
Trump (right) and Netanyahu held a joint press conference at the White House on January 28 to announce a Middle East peace plan to resolve Israeli-Palestinian relations in the absence of Palestine.
(Reuters) Trump calls the Middle East peace plan the “deal of the century, ” but the internal provisions are more harsh than the Oslo Accord of 1993, and the country is greatly reduced, while making the Palestinians a marginal person under the fence.
First, the Agreement of the Century supported the creation of “enclave communities ” in the form of land that Israel could forcibly take back in its settlement policy, which in turn legitimized the current colonial policy.
Second, in the dispute over the sovereignty of Jerusalem, Trump not only shamelessly suggested that the Palestinians could establish a capital in Abu Dis, the border suburb of East Jerusalem, but also denied that refugees displaced by the war should have the “right of return. ”
In addition, the agreement ignores the right of a normal state to have military and security control, and seeks to regularize the current Israeli siege by military control, leaving only civil administration to the Palestinians.
These provisions are far more stringent than the Oslo Accords, and are in violation of Security Council Resolution 242, which requires Israel to return land illegally appropriated during the 1967 war.
On the Israeli-Palestinian issue, although Trump seems to be actively mediating, it is clear from the recent relocation of the US embassy to Jerusalem, the cessation of opposition to the settlement policy, and the recognition of the sovereignty of Tel Aviv in the Golan Heights that the United States has lost its neutrality.
However, Arab countries that have historically been on the same side as Palestine have been on the same level of hypocrisy as the United States.
Although Abbas ’ s speech was endorsed by three international organizations, the organization ’ s members ’ private interactions with Israel and the United States have long departed from the traditional Arab positions.
When Trump unveiled the century-old agreement at the White House last month, attendees included not only Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but also ambassadors to the United States from Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Amman as guests of the White House.
In particular, Saudi Arabia and the UAE have publicly thanked Trump for his efforts and called for direct dialogue between Israel and the Palestinians.
In addition, Egypt, which has fought with Israel in the past, has only stated that it will “carefully and thoroughly review the American vision, ” moving away from its supposed position of categorically rejecting it.
There are two main reasons why Arab countries are abandoning the positions of the last century and moving closer to the United States and Israel.
After several wars in the Middle East in the last century, the United States has successfully induced many countries to become puppets of Washington.
Middle Eastern countries, such as Jordan and Egypt, have suffered years of “fragmentation and polarization ” as a result of governance failures, making them dependent on the assistance provided by the United States to maintain their political power, and the latter has received more than $1.6 billion in economic and military assistance every year since 1979, making their foreign policy subordinate to Washington.
Moreover, under the utilitarian calculation of "enemy is friend", the conflict between the United States and Iran has escalated in recent years, and the Gulf countries such as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain have abandoned their support for Palestine and turned to Israel.
Although the situation of the Palestinians is far worse than the apartheid era in South Africa in the last century, not only do they have no bargaining chips to negotiate with Israel, but in recent years have been abandoned by Arab countries, but they can not give in to the fist. In 2005, the British organization launched a global civil political movement to pressure Israel through boycotts, divestments and sanctions (BDS) to force the authorities to stop the occupation of Palestinian communities. Equal rights and the realization of the right of return of Palestinian refugees.
Even if the “victims ” of the BDS are the entire population of Israel, not the officials who have imposed the policy of apartheid, the potential losses in the event of extinction are limited to the economic level, like the terrorist attacks carried out by armed groups such as Black September and Fatah in the last century.
When the chin people accept the humiliating isolation policy, or only the power of the BDS can speak for them.

title: Hsinkang Driver Park opens into a little life of dirty spots
text:
Chiayi County's first labor residence, located in Chiayi County, near the "driver's union" in the village of Gongqian, Xingang Township, Chiayi County, has been called a "dirty spot in the community." Chiayi County Mayor Chiu Tsung-yi and Hsin-gang Township Office have won the project funds for the heart of the city. The driver park this piece of land is not large, but the land ownership rights belong to the Xingang Township Office, the State Property Bureau, the Water Conservancy Association, Taiwan Sugar and other units, coupled with some private occupation, the formation of a lack of management of dirty spots, breeding mosquitoes, rats and ants, resulting in the deterioration of the living environment of residents.
Chiayi County Mayor Weng Chang-liang said that after a year of hard work, Chiu Tsung-yi and the township government turned this open space into a green park, because the neighboring "driver's union" named the park as the driver's park.
Lin Maosheng, mayor of Xingang, said that the park's predecessor was filthy, and many people stepped into the land for the first time after the park was built. They were surprised that it was difficult to imagine its original appearance, even if the park was not large, but it could make the surrounding residents feel the small happiness of living in a green environment.

title: It is to be “resilient ”! Create a neutral urban forest and improve environmental resilience
text:
For the first time, the National Taiwan Library, in collaboration with the Forestry Experiment Institute of the Council of Agriculture of the Executive Yuan and the New Taipei City Zhonghe District Office, will conduct the first “Resilient Urban Forest Project ” in Taiwan in Zhonghe Park (Park No. 4) to increase the variety of trees and biodiversity in the park, improve the responsiveness of Park No. 4 to the environment, and create a better recreational environment.
Cheng Lai, director of the National Taiwan Library, said that the “Just Resilience ” project brought together a number of forestry experts to introduce the biodiversity of Taiwan ’ s native tree rich Park No. 4, and create artificial urban forests to enhance the city ’ s resilience, tolerance and resilience to environmental change.
Ge Zhaonian, director of the Forest Protection Section of the Resilient Urban Forest Project, pointed out that the project can not only increase the urban green area, plant diversity and improve soil quality, but also regulate the urban heat island effect, absorb carbon dioxide, produce fresh oxygen and fentoxin, and adsorb suspended particulates from air pollution.
The “Resilient Urban Forest Vision Briefing Session ” will be held on Sunday, February 23 at 9: 30 a.m. in the Music Room on the ground floor of the National Taiwan Library. People living in Central, Yonghe and other places are welcome to participate and understand the importance of urban forests.

title: US Peach Farmers sue German chemical giant Jury for US $265 million – Radio France Internationale
text:
WASHINGTON (AFP) - A U.S. jury has awarded $265 million ($7.9 billion) to a Missouri farmer who accused chemical giants Bayer AG and BASF of destroying his peach orchard with herbicides.
A federal court jury in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, ruled in favor of local peach farmer Bill Bader on Friday.
Bayer and BASF irresponsibly encourage farmers to use dicamba herbicides, Bayer claims.
Bloomberg News reports that this is the first case in the United States involving a weedkiller that allegedly spreads to other irresistible plants and destroys crops in the Midwest.
Oxfam herbicides have been on the market for years, as has the much-criticized herbicide Roundup by US agricultural biotech giant Monsanto.
Monsanto was acquired by Bayer in 2018.
The use of herbicides increased dramatically after Monsanto introduced herbicide-resistant seeds.

title: Dolphin hunting season starts in Taiji Town. Catch 10 in two days.
text:
This hunting season will last for six months. Before the start of the hunting season, the authorities were worried about international animal protection organizations blocking dolphin hunting. The police set up a temporary police station near the port and stationed police officers, and the Maritime Security Agency also sent officers to patrol the area.
Taiji Town is the birthplace of Japanese ancient methods of whale hunting and dolphin hunting. Dolphin meat obtained is sent to supermarkets and restaurants, and some dolphins are sold to aquariums.
From September to March of next year, fishermen can catch 1,700 dolphins.
Some conservation groups have criticized the fisherman for violating animal welfare laws, hunting more than the government approved limit, and calling on the fisherman to stop hunting dolphins. However, the fisherman denies that the excessive hunting of dolphins is inhumane, and is also called a traditional livelihood.
Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on June 30 this year, and has resumed commercial whaling that has been interrupted for about 30 years, drawing international criticism.
(Japan Today / Kyodo)

title: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Taiwan ’ s Human Resources (Part I)

Rising temperatures are expected to reduce the efficiency of power generation and increase energy demand, which in turn increases the cost of electricity.
Climate change is also expected to increasingly affect trade and the economy, including import and export prices, as well as businesses with overseas operations and supply chains.
In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.
However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.
It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions.
Agriculture is highly challenged and threatened by rising temperatures, heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rains, which are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.
Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.
Climate change poses many challenges to maintaining and improving crop productivity, livestock health and the economic viability of rural communities.
While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.
Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.
If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.
The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.
Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.
These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.
Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.
Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.
There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production.
These include changes in production content, production inputs, the adoption of new technologies, and changes in management principles.
However, these strategies have limitations under severe climate change impacts and require both long-term and short-term investments.

It also changes and expands the geographical distribution of disease-carrying insects and pests, exposing more people to the lice that bring Lyme disease and the mosquitoes that transmit Zika virus (such as dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nile virus), which affect different transregions.
For example, communities in southwestern Taiwan are particularly vulnerable to the combined health effects of vector-borne diseases and high temperatures and floods.
Extreme and climate-related weather can have lasting mental health effects on communities, with adverse consequences, in particular resulting in degradation of livelihoods or relocation of communities.
Including the elderly, children, people in low-income communities and some indigenous and new communities, they tend to be disproportionately affected by the health impacts of climate change and are less resilient.
This helps individuals, communities, and counties to prepare for climate change risks with policies and programs to adapt and mitigate to reduce the number of injuries, illnesses, and deaths from adverse health outcomes.
According to the study, if the average temperature in Taiwan increases by 1 ° C in the future, the high risk of dengue fever will increase to 86, affecting more than 7 million people. In addition, the number of medium-risk areas has also increased to 203, and the future warming status will significantly increase the prevalence of dengue fever in Taiwan.
In addition, the increase in temperature in Taiwan will also increase the risk of related infectious diseases, and the impact of rainfall changes on infectious diseases will be more significant when the "daily extreme rainfall" is greater than 200mm.
In the face of the impact of climate change on public health, the adaptation that must be considered and prepared can be classified as at least three major aspects of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases and emergency medical care.
The main adjustment policies can basically be considered from the angle of strengthening and prevention.

title: Restarting commercial whaling activities with 17 Bud ’ s Whale Capture by Fleet ｜ News ｜ Eurasia / Europe ｜ on.cc
text:
After Japan announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year, commercial whaling has resumed in 31 years.
Shimonoseki City, Yamaguchi Prefecture, as an important base for commercial whaling fleets, held its first sea ceremony this year on Monday (24). The fleet is expected to sail for a month, returning on the 27th of next month, during which 17 Bui whales will be captured.
The ship, headed by the parent ship of the Common Shipping Company, “Nisin-Maru ”, sailed slowly out of the port after the ceremony. About 200 members of the crew ’ s family were seen at the port.
In addition to targeting whaling, the fleet will also investigate the survival of whales in areas where previous catches have been low in order to develop new fishing grounds.
It has been reported that Nihsin Maru last year caught 223 whales, including Bui ’ s whales, in three months.
Japan has been criticized for many years for its scientific research in the Northwest Pacific and Antarctic waters, and the authorities withdrew from the IWC last year to restart commercial whaling in the territorial waters and exclusive economic zones, causing strong dissatisfaction from international conservation organizations.

title: Northwest Warming Gobi Desert Pan-Green Official Media: Or Affect the Economic Pattern - 20190920 - China
text:
Temperatures rise and drought is the lightest in Dunhuang, thousands of miles away from Lanzhou, and the dry climate has kept Mogao Grottoes for thousands of years.
However, this year, the Gobi desert near Mogao Cave has also become green due to abundant rain.
In addition, the increase of glacial meltwater, the increase of river flow, and the rise of lake water levels are also occurring in the northwest.
These sporadic changes have long appeared in the eyes of scientists. In the 1980s, Shi Yafeng, a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, was concerned about the changes in rainfall in the northwest, suggesting that the northwest's climate may be shifting from warm dry to warm wet.
Ding Yihui, deputy director of the National Committee of Experts on Climate Change, said, “The situation over the past 30 years has confirmed this inference. ”
The increase in precipitation is mainly due to warmer weather, and the trend is expected to continue into the middle of the 21st century. "
Ding Yihui said, "The positive cycle of natural warming and the positive trend of human activities leading to global warming overlap, resulting in this situation."
This is a trend, not a cyclical one. ”
Zhang Qiang, deputy director of the Gansu Provincial Meteorological Bureau, said that the northwest region is more sensitive to global warming and the impact of climate change is more significant.
Such as the western ecological safety barrier Qilian Mountain, from 1973 to 2016, the average temperature rose 0.45 degrees Celsius every 10 years, significantly higher than the national and global average.
Last year, the rainfall in Gansu Province was the second in nearly 60 years, and the drought in the main growing season of crops was the lowest in history.
Vegetation coverage in the province is the highest in the past 18 years, the area of Gobi and desert has been reduced, and the ecological environment has been significantly restored.
However, experts believe that the warming climate is also a double-edged sword, and the new situation of "drought and floods coexist and increase" in the northwest region, and the increase in extreme weather has increased the pressure of disaster prevention and reduction.
With global warming, sea levels are rising.
According to the data, mainland netizens speculate that this will have a major adverse impact on China's coastal areas, and many areas will be flooded by sea water.
Rising sea levels threaten to flood the eastern coast of the Xinhua News Agency, "Global" magazine deputy editor-in-chief Liu Hong's WeChat public number "Niuqin" believes that the northwest is warming and wetting in line with the global warming trend.
Under the warming trend of the global climate, the re-emergence of the Northwest will change China and even the world.
However, this change will be a relatively long history, but also a relatively long game.

title: 70th Berlin Film Festival dissident director wins Golden Bear for directing Iranian film
text:
The film "There Is No Evil", directed by Iranian dissident director Mohammad Rasoulof, won the Golden Bear Award for Best Picture at the Berlin Film Festival.
Mohammad Rasulov, 48, is currently barred from leaving Iran and is unable to arrive in Berlin to receive the prize.
When his daughter Baran accepted the award in his place, he said, “It ’ s for him. ”
Producer Farzad Pak also thanked "the outstanding cast and crew who risked their lives to make the film."
The film depicts four loosely related individual stories about the death penalty in Iran, including the executioner and the families of the victims.
Variety, an entertainment magazine, described it as "the most blatant critical statement to date".
Mohammad Rasulov was sentenced in 2019 to one year in prison for “attacks on national security ” and banned from filming for life, and his passport was confiscated in 2017.
"The imposition of such restrictions very clearly exposes the narrow and tyrannical nature of the Iranian government," he said in a statement.
Actress Eliza Hittman ’ s “Never Rarely Sometimes Always ” won a Silver Bear.
German actress Paula Beer won the Silver Bear for best actress (after the film) for her superb performance in "Undine" directed by German director Christian Petzold.
The Silver Bear Award for Best Actor was won by Italian actor Elio Germano.
He won the prize for his portrayal of the mental and physical struggles of the Italian painter Antonio Ligabue in “Hidden Away. ”
Another Italian film, Bad Tales, with which Elio Giemano worked, won the Silver Bear for best screenplay.
The film was directed by Italian twin directors Fabio and Damiano D'Innocenzo.
South Korean director Hong Sangsoo ’ s “The Woman Who Ran ” won the Silver Bear Award for Best Director.
The French comedy "Delete History", which describes the society of the Internet age, "won the 70th anniversary Silver Bear, formerly known as the Alfred Bauer Prize, which was dropped by the Berlin Film Festival after Alfred Bauer was kicked out as a high-ranking Nazi official.

title: Agritech Brings Smart Agriculture and IT to Expand Transformation Applications
text:
Global warming has caused an abnormal climate. For agriculture, which has always depended on the weather, it has caused a turbulent growth cycle, resulting in crop damage and poor harvests. It is not easy for the global food supply to maintain a stable supply.
But the crisis is also a turning point, in the context of environmental changes, market demand and IT applications mature, but also opened up the opportunity for agriculture and IT integration.
According to the “World Population Prospects 2019 ” report released by the United Nations, the global population was 7.7 billion in 2019 and is expected to grow to 9.7 billion by 2050, which means that the global population will increase by 2 billion in the next 30 years.
As the global population continues to grow, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has pointed out that crop production must increase by 70% in 2050 compared to 2009 to meet the needs of the global population.
On the contrary, global warming has caused climate anomalies, not only disrupting the timing of seasonal changes, but extreme weather phenomena such as heavy snow, heat, drought, and heavy rain have also been transmitted around the world.
In the case of frequent climate anomalies, the impact on agriculture that has always depended on the sky to eat is more profound, and the abnormal climate has caused turbulence in the crop growth cycle. In addition to causing crop damage and poor harvests, the global food supply is not easy to maintain, and many uncertain factors are added to the increase of production.
Based on the consideration of "people taking food as their day" as the most basic human needs, if the related problems are not solved, the imbalance between food supply and demand will become increasingly serious, resulting in a widening gap, rising prices, and even various social problems.
In the past, we mainly used chemical technology research and development to provide low-cost fertilizers, pesticides, etc., to improve the production of agricultural land.
However, in addition to the limited expansion of arable farmland and the general aging of farmers, excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides has also led to problems such as environmental protection and food safety.
Combining IT to solve agricultural problems In the context of environmental change, market demand and IT application maturity, open the opportunity of combining agriculture and IT.
The development of agricultural IT not only allows crop cultivation to be free from climate and seasonal restrictions, but also to control the quality and quantity.
In particular, the rapid evolution of technology, the cost continues to decline, and the benefits are beginning to appear, prompting the emergence of agricultural technology (Agritech) in the field of agriculture and IT, and gradually forming a trend of smart agriculture.
Smart agriculture Through professional evaluation, find out the best planting methods of various crops, and carry out intelligent production with automated facilities and control systems, and carry out market analysis with data, not only to establish a stable agricultural product supply system to achieve a balance of production and sales, but also to produce agricultural products that meet the needs of consumers for safety and peace of mind.
In this way, it can reduce the cost and risk of farmers' labor, improve the overall income, and thus attract young farmers to join, driving the overall agricultural development.
Therefore, in the future, the production mode of agriculture towards industrialization or intelligent management should become a universal business model.
Companies actively expand the layout of the market to seize market opportunities and potential demand, including electronics, traditional manufacturing, information services, etc. are actively layout into the agricultural field.
Approximate, direct, indirect, or both, depending on individual capabilities, resources, or strategic layout.
The direct method is mainly used in the electronics industry and traditional manufacturing industry, which uses abandoned or old factories, idle land, etc., to introduce IT solutions, combined with long-term production management technology, and directly invest in the cultivation of crops.
The indirect way to information services, system integration business, is not directly involved in the cultivation of crops, but for farmers or related enterprises, the development and sale of plant factories or outdoor farmland management related systems, solutions or services business.
Manufacturing experience Although applicable, the operation is still challenging compared to the past operating mode relying on the rule of thumb, the manufacturing industry enters the agricultural field, and only needs to strengthen the relevant agricultural expertise, or cooperate with the relevant industry. One of them.
In addition, in addition to the cost effectiveness of the original operation and the analysis of the return on investment, the production and sales capacity planning, channels, product strategies, etc., can also be applied to the production and sales side.
For example, in order to avoid overlapping with the traditional crop market, the production side can be scheduled at the wrong time of the season, and the channel part is matched with high-end restaurants such as health and hygiene, and the products are consumed by specific patients such as diabetes to form a differentiated response strategy.
Although the production process of industrial products may be more complicated than agricultural products, the difficulty of controlling the growth of crops is much higher than that of ordinary industrial products.
In terms of related solutions or services indirect input methods, high import costs and low IT capacity are bottlenecks in the development of agricultural IT in the past. Recently, due to the increasing maturity of LED light sources, sensors, energy saving technologies, cloud computing, Internet of Things, artificial intelligence and other technologies, the price continues to decline, and the related solutions and services are emerging, and the application market is gradually expanding.
In addition to the overall solution of plant factories, operators also provide agricultural operation support services with lower initial investment threshold through cloud services to help farmers pre-evaluate planning and improve operational efficiency.
Before planting crops, based on the planting method, land area, soil characteristics, etc., and based on data such as planting methods, costs, and customer-specific delivery patterns, the profitability simulation is carried out, and the planting planning and subsequent detailed management and business performance analysis are carried out from the perspective of operation.
In addition, in the process of crop cultivation, various technologies can also be introduced to remotely monitor, reduce manual load, and improve operational efficiency.
For example, the use of global positioning system to manage agricultural land, use drones and other aircraft for fertilizer delivery, crop production status and yield monitoring, or install sensors on agricultural equipment and aircraft to collect temperature, humidity and other environmental data, and monitor the content of nitrogen, phosphorus and other substances in chemical fertilizers. Condition.
The application of science and technology in the fishery industry has also shown diversified development. Taking the artificial farming industry as an example, the use of image recognition and other technologies to carry out climate change warning, water quality monitoring, bait and other farming conditions monitoring, providing real-time information on fish health, feeding conditions, environmental health, positioning and tracking, and thus driving the comprehensive upgrading and transformation of the farming industry.
After more than 20 years of development, IT applications such as computerization and information systems have become the key factors for manufacturing and service industries to enhance business efficiency and competitiveness.
Faced with subjective and objective factors such as extreme climate, rural aging, and improved quality requirements, IT applications driving agriculture continue to expand, and it is expected to bring traditional agriculture into the transition period, toward the development of smart agriculture, and also bring new market opportunities for IT applications.

title: FAO: North Korea ’ s harvest this autumn will be the lowest in five years
text:
Photo: YONHAP News Korea International Radio reported that the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) expects North Korea ’ s autumn crop harvest to be the lowest in five years due to climate change. The FAO said in its “Harvest Outlook and Food Situation ” report for the third quarter of 2019, released on the 19th of this month, that in the April-July farming season, the North Korean region received less rainfall and insufficient irrigation water.
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has placed North Korea on a list of 41 countries in need of food aid.
The list of countries in need of external assistance due to food shortages includes 31 African countries, 8 Asian countries and 2 Latin American countries and the Caribbean.
In addition to North Korea, there are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iraq, Myanmar, Pakistan, Syria and Yemen.

Kuo Huaren, an emeritus professor in the Department of Agrology at National Taiwan University, said that agriculture needs to be more integrated in response to climate change, but the most important thing is to re-study the crop cultivation system, such as which crops should be planted earlier or delayed, and provide farmers with a new set of strategies; and strengthen efforts to restore soil health in order to grow stronger crops.
Guo Huaren said that when the soil returns to health, the crops planted will be stronger, and the resistance to harsh weather such as heavy rain and drought will be stronger; or by increasing the organic quality of the soil through natural farming methods, it will be able to resist more diseases and pests, and its water retention capacity will be enhanced.
Guo Huaren suggested that the crop cultivation system should be restudied, such as the first stage of rice transplanting in central China, seedling transplanting in February, harvesting in June, etc., planting miscellaneous grain crops in winter, but now the climate is very different from the past, and some crops are suitable for early or late planting.
In addition, the crop management model also needs to change. Guo Huaren said that if farmers produce only one crop, the risk is very high, the harvest may be ruined in the event of heavy rain, and the promotion of diversified cultivation should be expanded, while planting crops with different tolerance to the climate, so that a natural disaster will not "completely annihilate", which is the true essence of resilient agriculture.
Yang Mingxian, a professor of international trade at Feng Chia University who has long studied agriculture, said that in the past, emphasis was placed on the development of anti-stress varieties, but farmers should also start to change their management of cultivation.
Yang Mingxian said that in the past, in order to evenly distribute water resources, the northern part occasionally had forced fallow compensation for stopping irrigation, and now the frequency is higher, and even a complete mechanism has been formed, and the central and southern parts also have to start to do the corresponding distribution; because extreme weather has not appeared occasionally, but occurs year after year, it is necessary to normalize various adjustment strategies.

title: Reporter Lai Hung: Food crisis burned to Japan?

Inside the historic Ueno Park in central Tokyo, a normal-looking group of people is staring intently at the tree.

Scientists used these records to extrapolate the effects of climate change on cherry blossoms.
In recent years, cherry blossoms have opened about four days earlier than the perennial average.
Experts worry that cherry blossoms could open two weeks earlier by the end of the century, based on some global warming projections.
I think Japan should be able to cope with this change.

These figures on rice, maize and wheat yields are alarming.

“We don ’ t know how long these countries will be willing to export cheap food to Japan. ”
After the situation has changed, Japan must find new suppliers as soon as possible. "

Japanese farmers are getting older and fewer.

I think there has to be a major change in consumer psychology. "

The key is how to turn some difficult life choices into fashion.
In the field of food, can this be done?

title: CNNC Delivers First Batch of “Artificial Sun ” Safety Components Expected to Arrive in France in Mid-May _ Hong Kong 01 _ Instant China
text:
Recently, CNNC delivered the first batch of gas injection system composite pipelines for the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (commonly known as the "artificial sun").
At present, the parts have been shipped to France and are expected to arrive in mid-May.
CNNC Group delivered the first gas injection system composite pipeline for the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (commonly known as the "artificial sun"). The principle of energy generation from nuclear fusion is similar to that of the sun, so the controlled fusion research device on Earth for the purpose of exploring clean energy is also known as the "artificial sun".
It is also considered to be the ideal energy source to solve the future energy dilemma of mankind.
The gas injection system composite pipe is one of the nuclear safety components of the "artificial sun", and plays an important role in the ignition, maintenance and control of the plasma, as well as the cleaning of the vacuum container wall.
Unlike the pipelines used in nuclear reactors currently operating nuclear power plants, this pipeline involves more bends and has a smaller radius, making it more difficult and demanding to manufacture.
Zhang Kai, chairman of China National Nuclear Group ’ s 23 Construction Company, said, “During the epidemic, we have grasped the epidemic prevention and control with one hand, and concentrated our efforts to ensure that this batch of pipelines is manufactured and the first batch of products is delivered in time. ”
It is expected to arrive in France in mid-May. ”
The International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) is the largest international scientific engineering project after the International Space Station. It is currently one of the largest and most influential international scientific research cooperation projects in the world.

title: Japan ’ s Dolphin Killing Festival and the Resumption of Commercial Whaling
text:
Image copyright AFP Image caption Every year for six months starting from September 1, a large-scale dolphin hunt is held in the fishing village of Taiji, Wakayama, in southern Japan.
Japan began its controversial annual dolphin hunt in the coastal town of Taiji.
Not long ago, Japan resumed commercial whaling despite international criticism.
In 2010, Dolphin Bay, a documentary film, won the Academy Award for Best Documentary, drawing global attention to the mass killing of dolphins in Japan.
The decades-old tradition in Taiji, Japan, has drawn criticism from nature and animal conservationists around the world following the release of this bloody documentary.
Dolphins are not fish, they are aquatic mammals, and they are cetaceans.
Dolphins are one of the most intelligent animals, with a friendly appearance and a playful personality, has always been very popular in human culture.
But Japan ’ s dolphin festival is their nightmare.
Dolphin killing festival and Dolphin Bay Every year for six months starting from September 1, a celebration called Dolphin Festival is held in the fishing village of Taiji Town in Wakayama, southern Japan.
Hunters drive these animals to a bay and then slaughter most of the trapped dolphins with knives and harpoons in the shallow water.
The slaughtered dolphin meat is used for food.
The remaining dolphins were sold to aquariums and marine parks.
In the past, the media reported that in the next six months, more than 20,000 dolphins and thousands of whales will be slaughtered in Taiji Bay, and the blood of the dolphins will almost stain the sea water in the bay.
In 2009, European and American marine conservationists broke through the Japanese blockade and secretly filmed a documentary, Dolphin Bay, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Film the following year.
The video showing the brutal killing of dolphins by fishermen in Taiji Town for the sale of dolphin meat has put the region under international pressure and controversy.
Image copyright AFP Image caption There has been much international opposition and condemnation of Japan's commercial whaling.
Environmentalists: The Hunting Extremely Cruel As the annual Dolphin Festival begins in 2019, it has become a focus of media and animal protection organizations.
Japanese media reported that the ship that went to Dolphin Bay on September 1 did not bring back any dolphins.
According to the Dolphin Project, five dolphins were killed on September 2.
The official total quota for this season allows for the killing or capture of more than 1,700 dolphins or whales.
Environmentalists say driving to hunt is extremely cruel and it can take up to 30 minutes for a dolphin to die from asphyxiation or drowning.
However, fishermen from Taiji say the livelihood of the people in the community depends on the trade.
Image copyright Getty Images / De Agostini Picture Library Image caption Japan says it is part of its culture to kill cetaceans such as dolphins.
On July 1, 2019, after Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to resume commercial whaling, its whaling fleet began a period of several months of whaling.
Commercial whaling has been banned in Japan for 31 years.
Kyodo said it was the first major international organization that Japan had withdrawn from since the end of World War II in 1945.
Whaling to the Antarctic is not a Japanese cultural tradition, but has emerged since World War II.
At that time, Japan was in ruins and its citizens lacked food and clothing.
With the encouragement of General MacArthur of the United States, Japan converted two huge US Navy ships into whaling processing vessels to travel to the Southern Ocean, which played an important role in solving the problem of Japan ’ s extreme food shortage.
Even when commercial whaling has been banned since 1986, Japanese whaling ships have killed hundreds of whales every year in the name of scientific research.
Image copyright AFP Image caption Commercial whaling after World War II played an important role in solving Japan's food shortage problem.
Japan ’ s agriculture, forestry and aquaculture officials gave the reason for whaling because eating whale meat is Japan ’ s traditional food culture, and the resumption of commercial whaling can lead to a revival of the local economy.
Apart from the reasons of cultural tradition, why does Japan insist on ignoring the international opposition to whaling?
Junko Sakuma, a former Greenpeace Japan employee interviewed by the BBC, said that whaling is operated by the Japanese government and is a huge bureaucratic structure, with research budgets, annual plans, career promotion and pension insurance benefits for relevant officials.
The constituencies concerned share the same close interests as the politicians.
