title: 13 Refugees Rescued in Smuggling to Sea in Northern England ｜ News ｜ Eurasia ｜ on.cc
text:
(Internet) 13 French refugees were rescued on Saturday (August 31) after attempting to cross the English Channel from the northern province of Calais to Britain in a small rubber boat.
The Northern Sea and Channel Maritime Police (PGM) received a report at around 5 a.m. local time that there was a boat carrying 13 refugees at sea.
A helicopter was dispatched to locate the boat and found that the men were all on board, and they were rescued and taken to the port of Calais, where they were handed over to border police. The number of refugees attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK this year has more than doubled over the past year, according to a PGM report.
Reporting by Lui Ching-yee, French journalist

title: Japan ’ s suicide rate falls
text:
Japan's suicide rate fell 20% in April from a year ago, the biggest drop in five years, experts said, possibly due to the coronavirus outbreak caused schools to close, many office workers work from home, and people have more time to spend with their families.
In Japan, 1,455 people committed suicide in April, 359 fewer than in the same month last year.
Affected by the epidemic, about 40% of suicide prevention organizations have temporarily closed their doors or reduced their work hours, raising concerns that people with suicidal tendencies may lack assistance.
Although the suicide rate in Japan has decreased in recent years, there has been an increase in the number of school deaths, including school bullying, and the start of the new school term in April every year, which is even more stressful for some people.
However, the suspension of classes in Japan since March may temporarily reduce the pressure on students.
As for adults, Seito Saito, former director of the telephone consultation department of the Life Hotline Alliance, points out that they often do not think of suicide in times of national crisis and disaster.
A significant reduction in the number of commuters who regularly work overtime could also lead to a drop in suicide rates.

title: Japan 's suicide rate fell 20% in April to prevent suicide President: the epidemic will rebound for too long
text:
▲ The rush of Japanese subway people at work peak hours, the thought of going to work is very boring.
Japan's suicide rate fell 20% in April compared with the same period last year, hitting a five-year low. Although the epidemic brought many inconvenience and even panic, it also gave many people breathing time and more opportunities to get along with their relatives.
However, the former president of the Suicide Prevention Association also warned to be careful that the epidemic has dragged on for too long and the suicide rate has rebounded.
According to The Guardian, there were 1,455 suicides in Japan in April, 359 fewer than in the same month last year.
In fact, there has been a downward trend in the number of suicides in Japan in recent years, from 34,000 to 20,000 fewer cases last year than in 2003.
Japan ’ s epidemic reached a peak of 500 cases per day on April 16, with 40% of people forced to suspend work and stay at home or reduce their working hours. These forced anti-epidemic measures also raise concerns that some people ’ s suicide intentions will not be exacerbated.
However, although the overall suicide rate has decreased in recent years, the suicide rate among young people has increased, because of bullying in school or other reasons, resulting in excessive pressure on young people.
However, due to the suspension of classes due to the epidemic, these students have a breathing space.
Yukio Saito, former president of the Japan Suicide Prevention Association, said that people usually do not think of suicide in times of crisis or disaster in the country.
For example, in 2011, when the number of suicides fell, there was the Fukushima nuclear disaster, earthquake and tsunami in March.
In addition, the decline in suicide rate may be related to shorter working hours, and people who normally have to be “bored ” to work and commute can now work remotely from home or take a break.
Mr Saito also warned that economic and work pressures are the main factors affecting the suicide rate, such as the Asian financial crisis in 1997, which caused a dramatic increase of 35% in the number of suicides.
If the epidemic dragged on too long, the number of suicides might rebound.

title: Young illegal immigrants crossing the sea during the British epidemic surge
text:
LONDON, May 21, 2020 (AFP) Local officials say the number of young illegal migrants arriving in the UK by boat across the English Channel from France alone has surged during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) outbreak, as travel restrictions forced them to use boats instead of trucks.
Kent County Council chief executive Roger Gough said between 230 and 250 young illegal immigrants were being processed a year ago.
"But now the number of illegal immigrants has almost doubled," Gough told AFP.
There are now almost 470, and new illegal immigrants are coming in. "

title: Bayer expected to settle tens of thousands of Roundup weed killer lawsuits
text:
Bayer has reached a verbal agreement to end a large portion of the roughly 125,000 cancer-related lawsuits that Roundup herbicides have triggered in the United States, according to people familiar with the talks, Bloomberg reported.
The pending agreements, which are estimated to cover between 50,000 and 85,000 lawsuits, are part of Bayer ’ s $10 billion legal battle settlement plan, which aims to end legal disputes following its acquisition of Monsanto in 2018.
Those who did not want to be named said that the amount of compensation for each case that has been settled will be in the millions to thousands of dollars, although some lawyers have not yet agreed.
After Bayer ’ s $63 billion acquisition of agricultural giant Monsanto, a surge in compensation cases caused by Monsanto ’ s past production of Roundup herbicides, coupled with some major setbacks in the courts, Bayer has been under a lot of pressure, and its stock price has fallen 42% since the acquisition was completed in June 2018, and the company ’ s market value has evaporated by about $39 billion.
Markus Mayer, an analyst at Baader Bank, believes that the $10 billion settlement related to the US lawsuit should be the main cause of the decline in Bayer's stock price.
None of the agreements have yet been signed and still need to be approved by the company ’ s supervisory board, a person familiar with the matter said, which Bayer may announce in June.
To date, there is no exact number of settlements, but it is estimated that there are at least 125,000 claims, more than double the number of lawsuits related to Roundup that Bayer has disclosed so far.
Some people familiar with the settlement said Bayer said it would set aside $8 billion to resolve all current cases, including those pending.

title: NASA and SpaceX ’ s new mission: unravel space travel that marks the commercialization of space travel
text:
Image copyright NASA Image caption Bob Benken (left) and Doug Hurley (right) are about to embark on a new era of human spaceflight.
SpaceX, a California-based aerospace technology company, will launch a mission to the International Space Station (ISS) on Wednesday.
The company has done this many times, but this time, they will carry people.
This is one of those futuristic moments in space history.
NASA astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken will disengage from the Falcon-9 rocket in their Crew Dragon capsule for the first time in nearly nine years.
But beyond that, it also marks a turning point in the commercialization of human spaceflight — businesses will sell space travel to governments and any other agency or individual that wants to buy a service.
This chart details several key steps of the mission.
The launch will take place on launch pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center.
The Apollo 11 lunar lander and the first spaceflight, Columbia, both launched their missions at this prestigious launch center in Florida.
The time is precise. The Falcon must leave the ground at 16: 33 Eastern Daylight Time (20: 33 GMT), otherwise the astronauts will not be able to encounter the International Space Station, which is passing over Earth at 27,000 km / h.
The Falcon 9 is a two-stage rocket.
The lower part will burn for two and a half minutes before turning off and separating.
After that, the second structure will burn for six minutes, sending the crewed Dragon capsule into orbit.
After separation from the rocket, the capsule will use its own booster for the rest of the journey to the International Space Station.
Image copyright SPACEX Image caption During the drill, the astronauts attached themselves to the dragon-carrying ship with a seatbelt.
Image copyright NASA Image caption Hurley and Bancon appear at the Kennedy Space Center where countless space pioneers have visited.
Image copyright NASA Image caption The space mission will launch Wednesday at 16: 33 local time, weather permitting.
The second stage of the rocket shall be burned up in the atmosphere.
The lower end of the booster program is landing on an unmanned ship in the Atlantic Ocean.
This is SpaceX ’ s proprietary operation, making its Falcon rocket different from other orbital rockets in use today.
What seems inconceivable is that the spacecraft design used by NASA astronauts hasn ’ t been updated in 39 years. The old design hasn ’ t been updated since John Young and Bob Crippen ’ s Columbia orbiter.
They used buttons, toggle switches and control levers on their spaceflight, and Dragon spacecraft were all touch-screen.
It is an automated spacecraft that makes its own route to the International Space Station, but in order to avoid anomalies, Hurley and Banken must fly manually.
The construction of a man-carrying dragon cabin is used in every situation in the ideal image, including failures on the launch pad or during flight.
If this happens, the spacecraft will use a powerful built-in propulsion system to push itself to a safe distance.
SpaceX has rehearsed this possibility in ground and air rehearsals.
The crewed Dragon spacecraft on this mission should arrive at the International Space Station after a 19-hour flight.
The capsule is aligned with the front end of the space station and then approaches at a relative speed of a few centimeters per second.
Once attached, a tight, airtight bond is formed with the hook.
How long Hurley and Banken will stay at the International Space Station, 420 kilometers from the ground, is uncertain.
It is expected to be more than two months, but it is likely to be no longer than 120 days.
Engineers say that the solar cells on board the Dragon spacecraft will wear out in space orbit, so NASA must ensure that there is enough time to bring the astronauts back to Earth before the hardware performance is reduced.
They are not in a hurry to land on the surface of the earth.
The astronauts will continue to fly freely for two days to further test the ship ’ s systems and procedures.
After the spacecraft is finally out of orbit, it is protected by a thermal barrier as it descends through the atmosphere.
Four large parachutes will slow the ship down and gently land in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of the United States.
The SpaceX team has rehearsed the process of retrieving the capsule several times.

title: SpaceX: Top 10 Concerns for Commercial First-Time Human Space Missions
text:
SpaceX Image caption The Crew Dragon will be the first private company to send people into space.
Elon Musk ’ s company, SpaceX, is about to launch its spacecraft Crew Dragon and launch a human into space for the first time.
Here, we answer some of the questions that are commonly asked about this mission.
Why do private companies send NASA astronauts to space?
Since the beginning of the 21st century, NASA has had plans to find other agencies to take over the mission of sending astronauts to the International Space Station (ISS).
Following the explosion of the Columbia spacecraft during its return to Earth in 2003, NASA focused on developing an alternative spacecraft capable of reaching the Moon.
A necessary step to be able to afford the project would be to partner with private companies on the mission of transporting people and equipment to the International Space Station. In 2014, SpaceX, the company owned by entrepreneur Elon Musk, and Boeing, the aerospace giant, declared winners, entering into a human spaceflight contract with NASA.
SpaceX launched its first spaceflight.
The Crew Dragon will be launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday (May 27) on a Falcon 9 rocket.
What is SpaceX?
SpaceX is an American company that provides commercial and government official space launch services on Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets.
Elon Musk founded the company in 2002 with the goal of reducing the cost of space transportation and making it possible for humans to live on Mars.
SpaceX is the first private company to bring a booster rocket back to Earth into regular operation so they can reuse the rocket instead of just throwing it away.
The company is already regularly shipping cargo to the International Space Station and now plans to begin shipping astronauts.
Musk ’ s company is also developing a larger manned “Starship ” — which could be the first step toward Mars settlement.
Image copyright SpaceX Image caption The Crew Dragon will be carrying four people on this mission.
Who's Elon Musk?
South African-born Elon Musk sold online payment service PayPal to eBay for more than $160 million.
His desire to see humanity become a true space shuttle civilization was the driving force behind his founding of SpaceX.
He also co-founded a number of other companies, such as electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla.
He also envisioned a project called Hyperloop, a high-speed transportation system that would allow automatic separation tanks to operate in a series of pipes.
His colourful personality and lifestyle also inspired actor Robert Downey Jr ’ s rendition of the Marvel character Tony Stark.
Musk has no shortage of controversy: his Twitter posts have led to lawsuits and forced him to step down as chairman of Tesla (though he remains CEO).
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Elon Musk inspired actor Robert Downey Jr's interpretation of Iron Man.
Why is this launch important?
Since NASA ’ s spaceflight retired in 2011, NASA has been paying Russia tens of millions of dollars to send their astronauts into space aboard the Soyuz spacecraft.
Crew Dragon lifted off from Florida, marking the first time in nine years that an astronaut has lifted off from the US mainland.
This is seen as essential to maintaining America ’ s dominant position in manned space.
It will also be the first time a private company has flown people into space.
What is a human dragon?
The Crew Dragon is the spacecraft that sent astronauts into space on Wednesday.
It is an evolution of the Dragon series spacecraft that previously carried cargo into outer space orbit.
The Crew Dragon is designed to carry up to seven people, but NASA will carry four people on this mission and the remaining space will be used for storage of supplies.
The spacecraft is equipped with a propeller that allows it to move through space, and to dock at the space station and make autonomous connections.
Unlike previous manned spacecraft designs, the buttons are now replaced with touch control panels.
Image copyright NASA Image caption Crew Dragon was tested in orbit last year and did not carry a person at the time.
Who is the man in space?
Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley are NASA astronauts.
They were selected in 2000 and have flown in space twice each.
They are among the most experienced members of NASA ’ s astronaut team, and both have been trained as test pilots – a crucial step in the process of using the new spacecraft.
Hurley spent a total of 28 days and 11 hours in space, while Banco spent 29 days and 12 hours, including 37 hours of spacewalk.
Both spouses are also astronauts.
Image copyright Reuters Image caption Bob Benken (left) and Doug Hurley arrived in Florida on May 20 to prepare for the launch mission.
What will the astronauts do this time?
Man-carrying spacecraft must go through a process to ensure they can operate safely.
The launch is essentially the final step in such a process.
Once in space orbit, Bancken and Hurley will test the spacecraft ’ s environmental control system, display and control system, and thrusters.
They will monitor the autonomous parking system as they approach the station and become part of the International Space Station team.
At the space station, they will continue to test the Crew and complete other related tasks of the space station.
On its return to Earth, it will fall into the Atlantic Ocean with a parachute.
The cabin and team will be recovered by a steamer called Go Navigator.
What if something goes wrong with the launch?
Crew Dragon has a built-in abandonment system designed to save lives in an emergency.
If there is a problem during the liftoff phase, such as when the rocket engine is turned off, the Crew will ignite the cabin engine and push the cabin and crew away from the rocket.
The cabin will then land safely with the help of a parachute.
SpaceX successfully tested the in-flight abandonment system on January 19, 2020.
The spacesuit that Banken and Hurley will be wearing will look a lot different than before.
Unlike the large pumpkin-colored spacesuit and round helmets of the spaceflight era, SpaceX ’ s spacesuit is a white spacesuit with a compact line and a smooth helmet made of 3D printing.
Each one is tailor-made for a specific astronaut.
If they look like they ’ re from a sci-fi movie, it ’ s probably because they ’ re designed by Hollywood costume designer Jose Fernadez.
He worked on the Batman, X-Men and Thor films.
However, the suit must still be practical; it is designed to save the life of the astronaut in the absence of pressure and air in the cabin.
Image copyright NASA Image caption The new suit is futuristic, but also practical.
What's next?
If the Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission is successful, SpaceX will continue to conduct six physical operations with the International Space Station, as required by their $2.6 billion contract with NASA.
A similar agreement exists in Boeing ’ s $4.2 billion contract to carry people aboard the company ’ s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft to the International Space Station.

title: The News Lens
text:
Text: Ma Xuelun (PhD, Department of Microbiology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong) Photo: RTHK "Irrigation" Cities - Reintegrating "People" into Urban Renovation and Development "Greenhouse Effect", "Global Warming", "Global Extreme Weather", I believe we are not unfamiliar with the words, but the public is not necessarily aware of the consequences of these phenomena.
In addition to increasing temperatures, melting glaciers, and rising sea levels, it will also bring more and more intense typhoons, heavy rains during the rainy season, and the dry season will be longer.
Urbanization has caused people to live in a hotter, noisier and more polluted environment.
Cities separate humans from nature, from other people, from living space.
Harnessing the Wrong Water – Seaside Buffers and Underground Parking in Cities Now 70% of the world ’ s population lives in large cities, most of which are bordering Haiti, where rising sea levels flood the land and wreak havoc when hurricanes hit.
One of the reasons for this is the lack of planning for hydrophobic facilities in cities, and architects from all over the world are coming up with new designs to solve the problem.
New York City was hit by Hurricane Sandy in 2012, bringing severe flooding, and the local people realized that the situation was serious, and meteorologists predicted that more hurricane-force typhoons would hit New York every year, and that the sea level would only continue to rise, not fall, and the New York government needs to act quickly.
Originally, the most direct method is to build a wall at the seaside, but this method to treat the symptoms but not the root cause, and the wall can not be indefinitely raised, will affect the city landscape and the lives of citizens.
An innovative solution proposed by architects is to build small islands by the sea, and to build parks and leisure facilities on top of them, which are used by residents on weekdays and serve as buffer areas when flooding occurs.
They piloted the project in the southern part of Manhattan, part of which was the construction of bridges and slopes to block incoming water, which could be converted into a baseball stadium auditorium and integrated into the community.
Another solution has been proposed by architects, including the construction of underground car parks in the city centre to collect rainwater in the event of heavy rain.
The design of this building has a very special place, that is, at the same time the water storage, the parking part of the building will be raised, the vehicle does not need to be covered by water, and the stored water can be used in the dry season, to store the outdated water to the appropriate time.
There are even architects who have designed hollow floor tiles with drainage holes to resurface New York ’ s walkways, storing and draining water from the source.
Turning concrete forests back into forests – planting plants on every surface of buildings Another place where creativity is used to improve the urban environment and the quality of life of its inhabitants is Paris, a busy city filled with viaduct flyovers.
The local government has proposed that “urban greening ” is not just about setting aside land for parks, but should be“ comprehensive ” greening.
They fill the surfaces of buildings, such as external walls and roofs, with plants, and the types of plants are not random, mainly those that block dust, sound insulation and purify the air, so that a good atmosphere of public space in the city can be established.
With space, residents will get together, drink coffee in coffee shops, plant on farmland, raise animals, adults can chat, children can play, and build a closer community.
With the new generation of farming technology, crops grown in these green spaces, such as tea leaves, fruits and vegetables, can be safely eaten, and can be directly supplied to the community to reduce the carbon footprint.
Change the concept of building - using construction waste and synthetic materials to build new design houses In Copenhagen, Denmark, there is a house built with materials that were originally to be discarded. The use of water jams as flooring, large and small glass spliced into large glass windows, mainly made of wood, rather than prefabricated stone components that cause a lot of carbon emissions when manufactured, not only reduces waste, but also has a new appearance. The feeling of “waste ” is welcomed by the local people.

title: SpaceX becomes first private company to put NASA astronauts into orbit
text:
SpaceX became the first private company in history to put astronauts into orbit, overcoming myriad industry, bureaucratic, technical and weather hurdles to get NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the International Space Station (ISS).
Astronauts and space exploration experts said that although this is not an easy moment in history, it may actually be the ideal time to launch a manned space mission.
It was the first manned mission to orbit from the United States in nearly a decade since NASA's Space Shuttle program ended in 2011.
According to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, the part of the mission that worries him most will take place after about a month or months of orbital operation is over: atmospheric re-entry. Crew Dragon will travel at about 8 km / s (~ 5 mi / s), ripping off its expendable trunk, using its Draco thrusters for a few minutes of retrograde combustion, ablation of its PICA-X. The plate points to its velocity vector and then goes straight through the Earth ’ s atmosphere, reaching an astonishing high temperature.
With four bulging SuperDraco abort propeller pods, Musk believes reentry into the plane could be (albeit small) destabilizing, causing the Crew Dragon to lose control.
In addition to completing the most important U.S. launch mission in nearly a decade, SpaceX successfully landed the Falcon 9 Block 5 booster B1058 on an O Courtesy drone ship moored hundreds of miles away in the Atlantic Ocean.
Once safely returned to land, SpaceX will be able to reuse the booster for any number of upcoming commercial launches, which could include NASA missions.
At the same time, this is also the first manned space launch mission since SpaceX was founded 18 years ago.
It marks the beginning of a new era of space exploration and a new era led by commercial companies.
NASA also expects that the first operational mission of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft, Crew-1, is likely to launch at the end of August this year.

title: SpaceX rocket successfully sent people to space, marking the beginning of the space race ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
text:
After a two-day delay, private aerospace manufacturer SpaceX and NASA successfully launched the Crew Dragon Falcon-9 rocket on May 30 to carry two astronauts to the International Space Station (ISS).
This is the first time in human history that a private company has put an astronaut into orbit, marking a historic moment for the development of American aerospace, and also marking the beginning of the era of commercial manned spaceflight, and space developers are expected to move forward at full speed.
Shortly after the launch of the Falcon 9 rocket from the Kennedy Space Center, the first rocket booster successfully disengaged and landed on the surface recovery platform for recovery, while the spacecraft took almost 19 hours to complete the docking.
Two American astronauts, Douglas Hurley and Robert Behnken, use high-tech touch screens to control the capsule, conduct a test flight at a distance, and then switch back to fully automatic operation to complete the bonding.
Hurley described the capsule's operation as "really, really good, very clean."
The hatch then opened a few hours later, allowing the two astronauts to enter the Orbital Laboratory to meet and hug the three astronauts on the station.
However, Hurley accidentally hit his head while entering the space station, and frequently touched his forehead during the welcome ceremony.
During the ceremony, NASA astronaut Chris Cassidy rang the ISS bell to greet the newly arrived members.
Two SpaceX astronauts and an International Space Station astronaut spoke to Earth's control center over the radio. (AP) The SpaceX Mission Control Center in Hawthorne, California, said over the radio: "Congratulations on this extraordinary achievement and welcome to the ISS.
The two astronauts will later join the crew of the space station, which is expected to remain on the International Space Station for four months.
In addition to the research work of the space station, they will also conduct tests on the Dragon spacecraft.
According to NASA, more than 3 million viewers watched the historic moment online.
This manned space mission was completed after nearly a decade of efforts by NASA and SpaceX.
Following the success of the mission, SpaceX will begin regular missions to the International Space Station, transporting astronauts and supplies to and from Earth, and will conduct private space missions.
SpaceX: Crew Dragon's test flight in graphics https: / / t.co / oe7qxu0fZ2 pic.twitter.com / OQqKum7nrn — BBC News Graphics (@ BBCNewsGraphics) March 8, 2019 As the space shuttle is about to be retired, NASA is launching the Commercial Crew Program, which encourages private aerospace companies to develop commercial space vehicles to transport astronauts to and from the International Space Station.
On July 21, the Space Transportation System (STS), a 30-year, 135-mission mission mission, came to an end when the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis returned to Earth on its last mission to the International Space Station.
The idea behind making a shuttle is to explore the universe in a cheap, simple and safe way. Not only is it the best tool for carrying large objects such as satellites and space telescopes into space, it is also a major contributor to the shuttle and assembly of the International Space Station.
However, there were significant deviations in its expected cost and lifespan, as well as significant safety deficiencies, and there were two fatal disasters, including the disintegration of Challenger and Columbia.
Trump and Pence were present at the same time, reflecting the significance of the rocket launch to the country. (AP) In September 2014, after open competition, Boeing and SpaceX successfully obtained two contracts from NASA, worth $4.2 billion (about HK $32.5 billion) and $2.6 billion (about HK $20.1 billion) respectively.
Both will need to transport NASA astronauts to and from the International Space Station by the end of 2017.
Therefore, the two companies actually failed to complete the task on time, but SpaceX, which has received less funds, has “lowered ” the aerospace giant Boeing in the process.
Making a spacecraft designed to fly with humans is a huge challenge for both companies.
Both suffered setbacks and delays and delayed initial launch dates. In September 2016, the Falcon 9 rocket exploded during a regular static ignition test prior to launch.
Musk described the incident as "the most difficult and complex failure" in SpaceX's history.
Although the accident was not a launch failure, the company was stuck in a four-month standstill to study the cause of the accident, and in January 2017, SpaceX resumed the launch.
(Reuters) On the other hand, no one thought SpaceX could compete with Boeing, especially Boeing, which played a role at every important moment in NASA ’ s history.
Some members of Congress have even questioned why the contract was awarded to SpaceX.
The success of the mission has brought together Elon Musk and SpaceX.
Of course, this is also the first time in nine years that the United States no longer needs to rely on Russia to carry out a manned space mission on American soil.
If this mission is successfully completed, it means that SpaceX ’ s reusable spacecraft meets NASA ’ s requirements and will continue to carry astronauts to the space station.
Jeff Bezos ’ Blue Origin is also involved in space development. (Reuters)
Currently, in addition to SpaceX and Boeing, the two billionaires are each investing in space projects, Jeff Bezos ’ Blue Origin and Richard Branson ’ s Virgin Galactic are all developing ways to reduce the cost of space travel in the long run or to the moon or Mars.
This mission also reflects the reality of space development, which is that international cooperation will be more important than ever in research and exploration in this field.
Aerospace agencies in different countries not only need to share data and resources, but are increasingly working together on joint missions.
The International Space Station itself is a good example of international cooperation in the space sector.
The space facility is scheduled to be decommissioned around 2028, and the planned replacement program is likely to involve at least ten countries and private agencies.

title: Two American astronauts arrive at the International Space Station
text:
The US Space Exploration Technology Corporation (SpaceX) has successfully sent NASA veteran astronauts Hurley and Beacon to the International Space Station (ISS) nearly 24 hours after the launch of the manned Dragon spacecraft.
Hurley (53) and Beacon (49) entered the space station on Sunday (May 31) at 1: 25 p.m. (1: 25 a.m. Singapore time on June 1), hugging and shaking hands with the station's existing team members, Reuters reported.
"The whole world has seen this mission, and we are very proud of what you have done for our country," NASA Administrator Brendan Stein told the two astronauts by phone from the mission control center.
"It is an exciting thing for the United States to restart its manned space program and we are very happy to be here at this magnificent research facility," Hurley said.
It is unclear how long Hurley and Becken will stay on the ISS, and Bridenstine has previously said they may return to Earth in early August.
SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft sent two American astronauts to the International Space Station on May 30.
This is the first time that the United States has used domestic rockets and spacecraft to send astronauts from home to the space station since the retirement of the space shuttle in 2011, and it is also a key step for commercial manned spaceflight.

title: Travel to space is not a dream
text:
SpaceX became the first commercial company to successfully launch a human into space, and it was also the first time in nine years that the United States launched a rocket to launch a human into space. (File picture) After carrying the Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station, the Falcon 9 rocket successfully landed vertically on a barge in the Atlantic Ocean, marking a major breakthrough in rocket recovery technology.
The barge is called “Of Course I Still Love You. ” (online photo) [Ming Pao News]“ I ’ m going to be an astronaut! ” is no longer a fantasy. SpaceX successfully launched a manned flight at the end of last month, making commercial space travel a reality.
Hong Kong Space Museum Director Li Weijun bluntly said that he has not seen a human liftoff for a long time, and he is deeply shocked by the success of SpaceX.
Since the United States ended the moon landing in 1972, there have been no new breakthroughs in manned liftoff technology for nearly half a century.
However, all three respondents who are familiar with astronomy are excited to say that 2020 is starting to enter an interesting year, and they believe that they may see humans return to the moon and landing on Mars in their lifetimes.
Since ancient times, humans have always looked up at the sky and wanted to understand the stars, the moon and the sun.
Tesla boss Elon Musk, who has been fascinated by space science fiction, founded SpaceX in 2002, hoping to reduce the cost of space transportation and eventually reach the ambition of bringing people to Mars. After 18 years, SpaceX finally took a big step at the end of last month, launching the Dragon spacecraft at 3: 22 pm EST on May 30 at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The Falcon 9 rocket carrying two American astronauts successfully docked with the International Space Station (ISS) at 10: 16 a.m. the following day.
This trip is the United States after nine years of carrying people into space on the mainland, and SpaceX became the first private commercial company to carry people into space.
Li Weijun explained that the most amazing technology of SpaceX's liftoff is that the rocket can be reused and can land vertically.
"Vertical launch and landing (VTVL) technology is very difficult because the center of gravity of the rocket is high, and the first stage needs to slow down when recovering, and the wind speed interference around it is very large."
Online videos have seen previous SpaceX rocket recoveries when it was unstable, collapsed, and exploded.
So this witness to the vertical landing of the rocket is wonderful, and personally it is a shocking technology. "
In the live video of the day, it can be seen that "Falcon 9" passed through the smoke and cloud layer, and about 1 minute after liftoff, passed the maximum resistance position Max-Q (maximum dynamic pressure point), and then the first-stage thruster was turned off.
About 9 minutes after liftoff, the first stage propulsion successfully landed vertically on the unmanned barge in the Atlantic Ocean and completed the recovery.
The Falcon 9 rocket was first launched in 2010, carrying supplies to the ISS several times over the past 10 years, and successfully retrieving the rocket booster for the first time in December 2015, making Falcon 9 the world ’ s first liquid fuel rocket that can be used multiple times.
Breaking the Russian “Galaxy Only ”?
Many media have said that Russia is the only country that can carry people to the sky in the past 10 years, but wait, has China not carried people to the sky many times since Yang Liwei successfully launched in 2003?
Quentin Parker, Director of the Space Research Laboratory and Director of the Master ’ s Program in Space Science at the University of Hong Kong, clarified that at present, only the United States, Russia and China can carry people in space, but the United States has suspended manned space since the retirement of the space shuttle in 2011, and China has only developed its space program since 1992.
He also mentioned that Japan, India and other countries are planning to launch manned spaceflight.
Li Wenkai, an associate professor of the Department of Earth Sciences and the Department of Physics at the University of Hong Kong, said that compared to the United States, Russia ’ s manned space technology is well-known and reliable. The current service of the Soyuz series spacecraft, as early as 1966, that is, before the dissolution of the Soviet Union, has been in use for more than 50 years and more than 1,700 flights.
Why is it reliable?
People used to joke that the difference between Russia and the United States is that Russia does not use sophisticated technology, but uses the most basic methods to solve the problem.
I don ’ t know if this is true or not, but for example, some people say that the invention of the pen was related to the US space program, because the United States said that it would invent a pen that can be used by astronauts in space; but the Russian solution is to use a pencil, and there is no need to think about anything. ”
There are two types of space travel separated from the earth with high and low payloads is not new. Since the United States and the Soviet Union fought for hegemony during the Cold War, the first Soviet astronaut Gagarin successfully went into space in 1961, making history.
But the most classic picture, always count July 20, 1969, the American astronaut Istom "Apollo 11" landing on the moon.
Li explained that space travel is currently divided into two main types, the first is sub-orbital flight, that is, the spacecraft rushed to the edge of space 100 kilometers from the ground, and then slowly glided back to the ground.
Virgin Atlantic boss Branson ’ s Virgin Galactic successfully launched last year and plans to launch its first commercial space trip this year.
Amazon founder Bezos ’ Blue Origin is also experimenting with a similar approach to commercial space travel, where travelers will have about four minutes to look down on Earth and experience zero gravity.
The second type is to carry people to stay inside the space station and follow the space station in orbit around the Earth.
Russia conducted this commercial space tourism program between 2001 and 2009, with seven space travelers flying to the ISS.
American businessman Dennis Tito, the first space traveller, revealed that he spent nearly US $20 million (about HK $155 million) on an eight-day trip to space.
According to the New York Times reported in March this year, SpaceX commercial spacecraft can launch as soon as the second half of next year, and can carry three passengers and a professional astronaut to the International Space Station, with a 10-day journey asking for $55 million.
According to the Commercial Crew Development contract awarded by NASA to SpaceX, when SpaceX starts sending spacecraft to the ISS on a regular basis, it can carry commercial passengers to the space station once or twice a year.
Li Wenkai said that the ISS is about 350 kilometers from the earth, and the concept of time is no different from the Earth; however, the ISS will circle the Earth every 90 minutes, that is, every 90 minutes will witness a sunrise and sunset.
Li Weijun believes that you can see the whole earth and the stars are already worth the price of the return ticket, and the rare and valuable experience is to truly experience the state of weightlessness, because even on Earth, the weightlessness flight training machine commonly known as "vomiting comet" can only experience the state of weightlessness for up to 30 seconds.
Li Wenkai added that the research found that the state of zero gravity will affect the bone density of human beings, and the height will be slightly higher in space. If you are lucky enough to travel to space, you may wish to pay attention.
Li Weijun said that he will wait until the manned liftoff technology is very safe to dare to challenge space tourism.
Speaking of the two accidents that occurred in the US space shuttle program, he is still worried.
During the US space shuttle program from 1981 to 2011, there were 135 flights and two serious accidents, the Challenger in 1986 and the Columbia in 2003.
"It was such a shock in 1986, I was scared and stupid before I joined the Space Museum."
In 1986, the Challenger was an accident when the rocket was launched, and in 2003, the Columbia was an accident when it returned to Earth. Li Wenkai pointed out that the most difficult part of launching people is always the rocket design, in addition to ensuring safety and heat protection, enough to withstand the huge friction when crossing the atmosphere, but also accurately calculate whether the fuel is enough.
To this day, the problem of rockets exploding during liftoff still arises from time to time.
It turns out that even SpaceX is using the basic fuel, kerosene (kerosene), "usually used in oil lamps, of course, will use a higher level, but the principle is to add oxygen will burn", Li Wenkai explained.
Li said that the space company has been studying whether there is a lighter, cheaper and faster release of energy alternative fuel, he said, noting that SpaceX has begun to think about whether it can re-use methane fuel, known as biogas.
In addition, Quentin Parker added that space junk is also a serious problem. There are many abandoned satellites and rockets in space. Because spacecraft travel at high speed, even if they hit a very small piece of junk, they can explode.
Once space travel is widespread, and there are plenty of space hotels and other packages, it is important to think about how to deal with garbage, such as studying burning it up in space or removing it completely.
Various technical difficulties led Li Weijun to believe that in the short term space travel cannot be significantly reduced to the civilian level, and spaceships will not be as popular as airplanes.
Space Research Hong Kong has read that since the last US moon landing in 1972, humans have not set foot on planets other than Earth, instead using unmanned probes to explore space.
Therefore, even if commercial space travel is carried out, it is believed that passengers can only float in the universe and cannot walk on the moon.
Li Wenkai bluntly said that in the past 48 years, there has been no major breakthrough in manned space.
Li Weijun said that with the successful launch of SpaceX, and the United States NASA has begun to prepare for the 2024 human return to the moon plan, I believe that in his lifetime, he will witness the return of humans to the moon, and even landing on Mars.
Li Weijun on the numbers: "Because the average distance of the moon is 384,400 kilometers from the earth, Mars is 56 million kilometers from us, and the farthest distance is 400 million kilometers, which is an average of more than 200 million kilometers, compared with the distance of the moon hundreds of times."
It will take a year to send people to Mars at the fastest, and it will be a very difficult task to send people back, but the development of science and technology has improved a lot. "
As commercial space travel becomes possible, Morgan Stanley ’ s latest report says the space economy could reach $1 trillion by 2040.
Quentin Parker believes that Hong Kong can provide downstream space technology products, such as research in space communication technology, robotics and big data. He revealed that the University of Hong Kong and Nanjing University will launch an artificial satellite to explore the sky in July this year.
Is it worth spending a lot of money and sacrificing human lives to explore the infinite universe? 3 interviewees agreed that the earth's population continues to rise, the earth's resources will be exhausted one day, and immigration to other planets may become the only way to continue human civilization, and it is necessary to continue to explore the universe.
Quentin Parker says it ’ s more important to be human because you care not only about survival, but also about dreaming.

title: French authorities rescue 31 migrants in the English Channel
text:
French maritime authorities said rescuers rescued 31 migrants who were trying to cross the sea to Britain on two inflatable boats in the rough English Channel in Walrus today.
French maritime authorities said in a statement that 31 migrants, including a teenager and four children, were in distress in the English Channel and contacted emergency services for assistance.
The migrants, who said they were from Iran, Iraq and Afghanistan, were rescued early this morning and sent to France, where some had hypothermia.
The statement also said that two inflatable boats were trapped in rough seas, one of which sank shortly after the crew was rescued.
More than 1,400 migrants have been rescued by British or French coastguards in the English Channel since January, more than double the number for the whole of 2018, according to official figures from French authorities.

title: Bayer cancer case: $10 billion settlement reached
text:
According to the German "Handelsblatt" (Handelsblatt) reported that the Bayer Group has reached a settlement agreement on its Roundup herbicide carcinogen lawsuit, the amount of the settlement will be between 10.1 billion and 10.9 billion US dollars. The compensation case cannot end all legal disputes, but 75% of the litigation will be agreed through the terms of the settlement.
The Bayer Board of Supervisors has just discussed and voted on the settlement, which includes a $2 billion provision for future claims.
In 2018, Bayer acquired Monsanto for $63 billion.
The company said in April it was facing a lawsuit from 100,000 plaintiffs in the United States alleging that Roundup and other glyphosate-based herbicides caused them to develop cancer.
Surging May 25 reported that Bayer reached an understanding with most US plaintiffs in the glyphosate litigation case.
The pharmaceutical and chemical multinational group based in Leverkusen, Germany, reached a settlement of between 50,000 and 85,000 plaintiffs.
Reported that the amount of compensation will range from thousands of dollars to millions of dollars on a case-by-case basis.
Bayer was sued by 52,500 plaintiffs in the United States over a suspected carcinogen caused by the herbicide glyphosate.
A spokesman for the company said Bayer had made progress in mediation talks.
He stressed that the relevant procedures will continue to be carried out behind closed doors.
He stressed that Bayer would only consider accepting a solution that would not suffer too much financially and would allow the group to settle future legal disputes as soon as possible.

text:
Bayer AG (BAYRY) will announce Wednesday that it has reached an approximately $10.5 billion agreement with plaintiffs in the United States who have accused its Roundup herbicide of causing cancer to settle tens of thousands of lawsuits, according to a person familiar with the matter.
It was a milestone for the German company in the legal battle that has dragged down Bayer ’ s share price for nearly two years.
As part of an agreement with plaintiffs ’ lawyers, Bayer will pay about $9.5 billion to settle claims filed by lawyers representing some 95,000 plaintiffs, the person said.
Bayer will set aside an additional $1.1 billion to establish and fund a panel to assess whether the product causes cancer to help influence the outcome of future litigation.

title: Herbicide cancer case: Bayer "bleeding" reached a settlement
text:
Bayer, a German chemical and pharmaceutical company, has reached a settlement with many plaintiffs in the United States in a legal dispute over a herbicide containing glyphosate (Glyphosate).
The company announced the news, saying it would pay $10.1 billion to $10.9 billion for it.
By doing so, most of the litigation process against glyphosate can be ended, and possible future legal risks can be avoided.
Bayer said that after the settlement, 75% of the current legal disputes against the Roundup brand herbicide will be closed -- a total of about 125,000 cases, including cases that have been filed and those that have not been filed.
The rest will also be closed in the coming months.
For the outstanding claims, Bayer pays a fixed amount of compensation, which is also included in the tens of billions of dollars.
The company's chairman, Werner Baumann, told German broadcaster NTV that it was doing so to "look to the future" and "defuse unease" now.
Bayer said: "With the participation of a specially established legal committee on glyphosate, the settlement agreement was unanimously approved by Bayer's Board of Directors and Supervisory Board.
However, in the agreement, Bayer did not admit fault or misconduct at all.
In 2018, Bayer, a Dax company based in Leverkusen, Germany, bought American agrochemical giant Monsanto for more than $60 billion. Monsanto ’ s glyphosate-containing herbicides — which include the brand name Roundup as well as Dicamba and PCB herbicides — are suspected to be carcinogenic.
After Bayer was ordered to pay high compensation in three lawsuits, a growing number of people sued the company for cancer through the use of Monsanto ’ s herbicide.
The indictments were based on a 2015 assessment by the World Health Organization ’ s Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).
Unlike other agencies, the IARC rated glyphosate as "possibly carcinogenic."
Bayer dismissed the accusations and recently received support from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which determined that there were no health risks when glyphosate was used as directed.
However, Bayer has still decided to accept the settlement, claiming that the final cost of the marathon may be higher considering the outcome of the pending litigation in the United States.
In a video news conference with the media, Bayer chairman Bauman expressed his hope to look forward and pay more attention to the company's core business.
He also said the settlement would not have an impact on Bayer ’ s products and decisions about whether glyphosate will be used in the future.
In addition, Bayer announced that an independent “scientific committee ” will be formed for possible future herbicide cases, which will assess whether and at what doses Roundup may cause lymphoma.
The wave of lawsuits against the herbicide, which is scheduled to begin this year, has weighed on the stock market and led to criticism from management, led by chairman Werner Baumann.
Financially, Bayer could cover the cost.
The sale of the animal medicine segment alone will bring Bayer $7.6 billion in revenue, most of which will be paid in cash and a small share of the shares of the buyer, Elanco.
Bayer plans to start paying out this year.
Investors are divided on the news that Bayer has reached a settlement.
On the trading platform Tradegate, Bayer first rose nearly 9%, but did not show much in regular trading, and finally closed down.
One investor said that this is a typical "sell on good news" (sell on good news), and investors have recently received signals that a settlement should be reached and sold off after the boots have landed.
Wang Fan / Hong Sha (DXS, Agence France-Presse, Reuters)

title: Investigate the forest! Urban residents care the most about trees to regulate the climate function - Life
text:
In addition to allowing people living in large cities to rest, but also to provide many different benefits, the Council of Agriculture Forestry Research Institute for people living in urban areas, the survey on the living environment surrounding trees can bring 19 benefits, the results of trees on the environmental micro-climate adjustment related benefits most urban residents pay attention to.
The Lin Institute surveyed Taipei residents ’ views on the importance of 19 tree benefits, the most important of which was “microclimate regulation ”, followed by“ rest and education culture ”, “environmental quality improvement ”, and“ environmental service function ”.
In addition to the “micro-climate adjustment ” benefits of photosynthesis, air purification and shade, trees grown in urban areas can also provide“ environmental quality improvement ” of noise barrier, increase privacy, “environmental service function ” of various biological habitats, and“ recreational and educational culture ” benefits such as providing open space, aesthetic landscape and precious old tree culture.
Zhang Bin, director of the Institute of Forestry, said that trees in the city are one of the important green infrastructure and the most accessible green resources for residents. These trees can not only maintain the balance of urban ecology and environment, but also be an important resource for residents to adjust their body and mind, and let residents often unconsciously enjoy the benefits of various trees.
Chen Yen-chang, director of the Lin Lab, said that because people usually use parks with trees to engage in recreational activities such as walking and sports, their feelings about the benefits of trees are more important than the general impression of photosynthesis and shade, and the benefits of recreation and education and culture are also more important.
Because of the characteristics of buildings in Taiwan, most people do not have trees outside their homes, so they have a lower degree of feeling for benefits such as trees reducing noise or blocking strong light from entering their houses.
According to Lin Shih, trees and green spaces are an important foundation of the overall urban ecosystem. Through good planting planning and appropriate management and maintenance, keeping trees healthy can provide stable urban diversity benefits and reduce the risks and problems that may arise.

title: Iran shoots down Ukrainian plane, Canada and Sweden pave way for compensation talks – Radio France Internationale
text:
OTTAWA (AFP) - Iran shot down a Ukrainian International Airlines plane in January, carrying passengers from Canada, Sweden and other countries.
Canada said today it would launch an agreement with Iran to negotiate compensation for the families of the victims.
Sweden is confident that the Tehran authorities will pay compensation.
According to a Canadian government statement, an international "coordination and response team" of the countries whose nationals were killed has signed a memorandum of understanding to officially start negotiations with the Iranian authorities.
Ukraine International Airlines PS-752 was accidentally shot down by the Iranian military in January, killing five countries, including Canada, the United Kingdom, Ukraine, Sweden and Afghanistan.
Canadian Foreign Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne told AFP: "The five countries have completed the legal framework required for the negotiations."
This is the first step, though necessary, but only the first step in negotiations to secure compensation for the families of the victims. ”
Swedish Foreign Minister Ann Linde told Swedish news agency TT earlier today that Tehran has agreed to compensate the families of the foreign victims.
Lindh said there was "no doubt" that Iran would pay, but it was unclear how much it would pay.
Ukraine, the group's designated spokesman for the talks, will be responsible for proposing a date for talks with Iran, Shen said, adding: "However, such talks usually take months, if not years."
All 176 people aboard a Ukrainian International Airlines plane, 85 of them Canadian citizens or permanent residents, were killed when it crashed shortly after takeoff from Tehran Airport on Jan. 8.

In the midst of the world economic downturn during the COVID-19 pandemic, the number of visitors to many surgical and plastic clinics is increasing.
Because masks can hide their face after surgery or recover from work at home.
The pandemic has caused many stores around the world to close, but many orthopaedic clinics remain open to the public.
They take more stringent measures, such as (body temperature) testing for the new coronavirus and more frequent cleaning.
In clinics in the United States, Japan, Korea and Australia, more people do lip augmentation, botulinum injection, facial lift and rhinoplasty / nasal pad.
Aaron Hernandez, who performed lip and cheek fat removal in Los Angeles, told the BBC: “I decided to do all the treatments during the quarantine because I was able to recover at home. Lip plump is something not everyone does, so some people may find it different.
I ’ d rather stay home until I ’ m fully recovered, and people don ’ t know I ’ ve had these surgeries when I go out. ”
He said he had a similar operation before the quarantine, but had to go to work in public when his lips were “extremely swollen and bruised. ”
Rod J Rohrich, a cosmetic surgeon in Texas, said he saw more patients during the outbreak.
He told the BBC: "Even more than normal.
We can work six days a week if we want.
This is amazing. "
Usually people have to factor in home recovery when considering surgery, he said, but since many people now work from home, there is no need to consider this.
“They can actually recover at home or wear a mask when they go out after a rhinoplasty or cosmetic surgery. ”
People want to get back to normal life and want to look and feel as good as they do. ”
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption The number of foreign visitors to South Korea for plastic surgery has decreased, and the number of locals has increased.
During the pandemic, not only the number of plastic surgeries in the United States increased.
South Korea, known for plastic surgery, was one of the first countries to discover the new coronavirus.
Instead of a nationwide lockdown, South Korea has focused on social alienation, encouraging people to work from home.
Foreign tourists to Korean beauty clinics decreased, but locals began to become the main flow of visitors to clinics.
Many clinics offer discounts to locals.
A 54-year-old secondary school teacher who underwent double eyelid surgery in February told the Central Daily News: “Every plastic surgery clinic I ’ ve been to is full of people. ”
BK Hospital in Seoul told the BBC that people were nervous at the start of the pandemic, but more locals have started coming to the clinic.
The hospital spokesman said: "Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, plastic surgeons are slowly feeling safe and comfortable to operate, and the number of customers is steadily increasing.
Compared with the same quarter last year, the number of people is estimated to have increased by half. "
Foreign consultations are also on the rise, the spokesman said.
“The number of online queries has increased significantly.
Because once travel restrictions are lifted, an online consultation can prepare for a possible trip. ”
Image copyright EPA Image caption Japanese nationals were urged to stay home as much as possible during the outbreak, but Prime Minister Shinzo Abe declared a state of emergency in Japan, which lasted until May 31.
People are asked to stay at home.
Nevertheless, the number of people wishing to see a doctor has also increased.
The surge prompted the Japan Aesthetic Medicine Association to warn that beauty is “not essential for many people. ”
The association asked people to stay away from surgery to "prevent further spread of the virus."
“As an outpatient plastic surgery clinic that offers same-day surgery, we see an influx of patients who want to be treated during the pandemic, ” said Michelle Tajiri, clinical coordinator at Bliss Clinic in Fukuoka.
“The main reason is that they are off work, the rest time is not a problem, and everyone wears a mask, so it is easy to cover up any traces of facial surgery. ”
For Hernandez, it ’ s the right time to choose surgery during the pandemic.
“It definitely gives me more time to recover.
I can do medication, not if I drive.
And I can put more ice on my lips and face. "

title: Iran announces shooting down of Ukrainian passenger plane: Radar deviation caused
text:
Iran's Civil Aviation Authority released an investigation report on the crash of Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 on the evening of July 11 local time.
The report said that the radar system was deviated due to human errors during the radar calibration operation. On June 29, the military prosecutor of Tehran Province, Gram Abbas Torki, said that the reason for the shooting down of the Ukrainian passenger plane in Iran was "human error".
Three people have been arrested in connection with the accident.
On January 8, a Ukrainian International Airlines Boeing 737-800 crashed near Tehran's Khomeini International Airport, killing 167 passengers and nine crew members.
The Iranian military later admitted to shooting down the Ukrainian airliner due to a mistake.
According to the report, the plane received permission from the control tower of Iran's Imam Khomeini International Airport at 6: 10 a.m. local time on Tuesday to move to the take-off channel and then fly along the scheduled route and altitude.
At this point, an Iranian air defense system was repositioned and the position changed, but the operator did not reposition the radar system, resulting in a 107-degree error.
At 06: 13 on the same day, the operator spotted a target at 250 degrees north, and at this time, after taking off, Ukrainian Airlines Flight 752 was heading toward the system at 143 degrees.
Operators frequently reported to the Coordination Command Center that they found the target approaching the system from the southwest, but that the target was actually Ukrainian Airlines Flight 752, which was flying on the scheduled route.
As the operator did not receive a reply, the target was self-analysed as a threat and the first missile was fired at 0614 hours.
Since the anti-aircraft missile system was activated at this time, the target was tracked and the radar system was locked in, the operator fired the second missile within 30 seconds, at 0615 hours.
Later, the Iranian military issued a statement saying that the plane took off near a sensitive location of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, before the accident, Iran had just fired missiles at the US base in Iraq, and all Iranian air defense systems were on high alert, and then the plane was hit by "human error".
Earlier, Ukrainian Deputy Foreign Minister Evgeny Yenin said on July 1 that France had invited Ukrainian experts to participate in the interpretation of the black box of the Ukrainian Airlines downed plane.
Yenin wrote on Twitter: “Today I received an invitation from France to send Ukrainian experts to participate in the interpretation of the black box of flight РS752.
Iran has promised to deliver the black boxes to Lyon on July 20.

title: "Artificial solar" nuclear fusion becomes the best solution to energy and climate problems
text:
The International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), the world ’ s largest nuclear fusion plant, began assembly in France on July 28.
The new device will be used to experiment and study the feasibility of nuclear fusion for practical use. If successful, it will be able to generate large amounts of energy with a small amount of clean fuel, making it an ideal solution for solving energy and climate problems.
Pictured is the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) in France on July 28.
ITER officially began assembly on the 28th, and the possibility of commercial nuclear fusion power generation will be tested and verified in the future. (Getty) The Guardian reported on July 28 that representatives of the participating countries participated in the installation and launch of the "artificial sun" ITER on the same day.
The project was jointly built by the European Union, China, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, India, Japan and South Korea at a total cost of 20 billion euros.
Nuclear fusion is a type of nuclear reaction.
However, unlike nuclear fission, which involves splitting heavier atoms into lighter ones, nuclear fusion is a fusion process in which light becomes heavier.
Both can also release energy during the process, so the same is considered to be one of the energy sources.
Why is it called the “artificial sun ”?
The best example of nuclear fusion in nature is the Sun, which compresses hydrogen with a massive mass, causing hydrogen atoms to collide.
Because the nucleus is positively charged, the hydrogen atoms repel each other at the same time of compression. When the pressure reaches a certain level, the energy discharged will be greater than the energy required for compression, and this is the energy source of the sun, which is also ITER "artificial sun".
↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ For more photos of ITER's site and buildings, please click the image to enlarge to view: + 4 + 3 + 2 The role of nuclear fusion was discovered as early as the time of human research on nuclear fission, and the earliest application of nuclear fusion is hydrogen bomb, which can produce a big explosion through nuclear fission and fusion at the same time.
But for nuclear fusion to become a source of energy, it must be controlled.
One of the ultimate goals of the construction of ITER today is to find the feasibility of commercial nuclear fusion power generation.
Unlike conventional nuclear power plants that use nuclear fission technology, nuclear fusion requires deuterium or helium-3 (isotopes of hydrogen and helium), seawater has a large amount of deuterium, and the lunar surface has a large amount of helium-3, which is much richer in raw materials than uranium.
Nuclear fusion will not produce waste gas compared with conventional nuclear power safe nuclear fusion, and the half-life of nuclear waste generated is much shorter than that of conventional nuclear energy, which greatly reduces the difficulty and cost of processing nuclear waste.
At the same time, the limitation of nuclear fusion makes it possible to prevent accidents at power plants, such as conventional nuclear power plants.
Nuclear fusion requires the right temperature and pressure to proceed. Once the environment changes (such as the container is damaged), the fusion will stop itself.
Unlike nuclear fission, when the raw materials begin to fission, they will continue indefinitely until the raw materials are depleted, nuclear fusion will theoretically be much safer in power generation, so that nuclear fusion power generation can be the most ideal solution to energy and climate problems.

title: ITER – The Controlled Fire of the Sun on Earth
text:
The fusion reactor is located near the southern French coastal city of Marseille.
French President Emmanuel Macron held a "virtual" celebration of the latest progress of the project.
European Commission President von der Leyen, European Commission Energy Commissioner Kadri Simson and South Korean President Moon Jae-in participated in the ceremony by video.
The project, which was launched 35 years ago by the East and West camps, is now in its last major stage. Workers, engineers and physicists have been involved in the project for nine years.
In 1988, ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) was launched as a landmark project of the East and West camps. In 1985, French President Francois Mitterrand, US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Communist Party General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev jointly launched the project.
Until this year, the reactor building stood.
Reactor completion is expected to take another four and a half years.
Tuesday ’ s celebration was largely a symbolic signpost highlighting the progress made in the construction project.
For years, ITER has been under pressure due to cost explosions and delays.
The goal of the ITER project, which has no radioactive waste, is to show that a fusion reactor can generate enough heat over a long period of time to maintain a fusion plasma.
This will prove that human beings can make nuclear fusion and sustain it for a period of time.
In addition, ITER should be able to safely conduct the energy generated – at temperatures up to hundreds of millions of degrees Celsius.
However, this energy will not be used to generate electricity.
ITER is still a basic research.
For the time being, the engineers only want to prove that the technology is in principle suitable for obtaining clean energy through the combination of the hydrogen isotope deuterium and tritium for human use.
In the future, the annular vacuum container that will hold plasma is such that nuclear fusion is installed piece by piece instead of nuclear fission that our sun is generating enormous energy in this way.
If ITER succeeds in imitating the sun, humanity will realize the dream of creating a “controlled solar fire ” on Earth – with inexhaustible and inexhaustible energy, because the raw materials required are infinite.
However, there is also a dark cloud over the project: critics say the experiment is a deep pit engulfing tens of billions of euros.
Originally expected to cost 5 billion euros, it has now more than quadrupled.
In addition, developers are still struggling with a number of physical problems: how to safely transport heat from the reactor and how to add new fuel.
Are large facilities obsolete?
The main argument of opponents is that fusion technology has taken too long to reverse climate change in time.
They believe that the money should be used more for renewable energy such as wind and solar, as well as for smart transmission networks.
Proponents argue that the future cannot cover all of humanity ’ s energy needs through decentralized renewable energy sources.
Therefore, large power generation facilities will always be needed.
ITER ’ s ability to meet its ambitious goal of igniting the first plasma by 2025 also depends on the continued involvement of 30 project partners.
In international research projects, countries usually do not provide funding, but rather technical components, research and engineering contributions.
In addition to the EU, China, India, Japan, South Korea, the United States and the United Kingdom are participating in ITER.
The EU bears the largest share of the costs, accounting for 45.6 per cent.
Other partners each contributed 9.1%.
China joined the ITER program in 2006.
Chinese media reported on Tuesday that "the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project bears the beautiful wish of mankind for the peaceful use of nuclear fusion energy", and President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the launch ceremony of the major project of the project.
Chinese media stressed that since the implementation of the plan, "China has always abided by its international commitments, made concerted efforts with its international counterparts, and contributed Chinese wisdom and Chinese strength to the smooth advancement of the plan."

title: Nuclear fusion power scientists assemble artificial sun in France
text:
Fourteen years after receiving official approval, scientists began assembling a machine in southern France on Monday to determine whether nuclear fusion could be a safe and reliable source of energy for the planet.
In the groundbreaking International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), components from around the world have arrived in Saint-Paul-les-Durance, a small town in the south of France, in recent months.
These components must now be painstakingly assembled to complete the much-heralded “World ’ s Largest Puzzle ” ITER.
The purpose of this experimental facility is to demonstrate that nuclear fusion can generate electricity on a large, safe and commercial scale.
“Nuclear fusion provides clean, reliable and carbon-free energy, ” the 35 countries participating in ITER said in a joint statement. These countries include the 27 members of the European Union, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, the United States and China.
In addition, fuel for nuclear fusion can be obtained from seawater and lithium metal, which are abundant enough to supply humans for millions of years.
The statement said that a pineapple-sized fuel of this type is equivalent to 10,000 tons of coal.
ITER will be built from approximately 1 million components, with initial experiments scheduled to begin in December 2025.
This man-made solar facility is designed to generate about 500 megawatts of thermal energy, which, if it continues to operate, can be converted into about 200 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about 200,000 homes.

title: 【 Technology ． Future 】 How can China catch up with the United States? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ Weekly Report
text:
At more than 54 million kilometers, the distance between Mars and Earth is the shortest distance that occurs only once every 26 months.
In order to seize the opportunity of Mars exploration from mid-July to mid-August, the United Arab Emirates and China launched the "Al-Amal" and "Tianmen-1" Mars probes respectively last week, and the United States is expected to launch the "Perseverance" rover this week.
The Atlas V rocket, carrying NASA ’ s Persevance Mars rover, successfully launched yesterday from Cape Canaveral Air Force Base in Florida. (Reuters) - The three nations that have recently embarked on a mission to Mars are looking for life.
For the United States, which is extremely capable of space science and technology, perseverance will continue to be the basic research of NASA with the most cutting-edge technology.
For the first time, Perseverance will be specifically tasked with collecting samples of Martian rocks.
NASA currently plans to partner with the European Space Agency (ESA) to launch a Mars mission in 2026 and bring the rocks back to Earth in 2031, which will be the first samples of Mars.
The USS Perseverance is scheduled to land on Mars in February next year. In addition to collecting samples to explore past signs of life, it will also fly the small spacecraft Ingenuity for the first time. (NASA) Perseverance will conduct other forward-looking experiments on Mars.
One is to try to generate oxygen from the carbon-rich atmosphere of Mars to test whether it can support future human landing on Mars.
Another is an unprecedented experiment: a small helicopter called Ingenuity will attempt to fly on Mars.
As for China, on the one hand, Tianmu No. 1 will have its scientific research contributions.
It is actually made up of orbiters, landers, and rovers to conduct “extensive global surveys of the entire planet. ”
Examples include mapping geological structures and looking for water and ice; collecting images of landscapes such as dunes, glaciers, and volcanoes to give clues to how they formed; and studying the composition of soil and rocks, especially looking for evidence of how water changes geological features.
In addition, Tianquan 1 will also study the Martian magnetic field.
Since 2014, NASA ’ s Mars Atmospheric and Volatile Evolution Mission (MAVEN) has found plenty of evidence to support this idea, but scientists still want a fuller understanding.
Jim Bell, principal investigator on the main camera on Perseverance, said Tianwen-1 could provide more evidence from different orbits and ground.
(Reuters) China, on the other hand, has shown quite clearly its determination and ability to catch up with the United States. Although, Brian Weeden, program planning director of the Secure World Foundation (SWF), pointed out that China has largely “done a lot of what the United States has done in the past few decades, one by one. ” It is clear that China wants to demonstrate in one mission its ability to catch up with what the United States has achieved over the years.
The Soviet Mars-3 became the first soft landing Mars probe in 1971, but lost contact just over ten seconds later.
The second one was NASA ’ s Viking-1, which took pictures from the surface of Mars for the first time since landing in 1976. (NASA) Regarding China ’ s space “initiative, ” Joan S. Johnson-Freese, a professor of national security at the U.S. Naval War College, pointed out:“ The Chinese are keenly aware that many people feel they are simply repeating what others have done in the past.
So they do something very carefully. "She also believes that the recent Mars mission can be seen between China and the United States, and NASA's progress is derived from its experience. She describes" the United States is building a Mercedes ", and China is only" driving a Ford ".
The launch of the “Tianmen-1 ” Mars probe demonstrates the strength of China ’ s deep space exploration. (Xinhua) The above excerpt is from the 224th issue of Hong Kong 01 (27 July 2020).

title: SpaceX Space Shuttle Endeavour Returns 2 Astronauts to the United States! Forty-five years of trying to land at sea.
text:
(Photo / Reuters) - Veteran astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken took off from the surface of the International Space Station in May aboard SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft.
After two months of sailing, they will return to the Gulf of Mexico on the 2nd, US Eastern Time, and challenge to land at sea after 45 years.
SpaceX launched Dragon on May 31, becoming the first private company to put a human into orbit.
NASA has relied on Russian rockets to carry astronauts since 2011, and this time it has launched a manned space rocket on the US mainland for nine years.
After successfully docking with the International Space Station, the spacecraft was renamed Endeavour.
Endeavour separated from the space station at 7: 35 p.m. EST on the 1st. It is expected to "splash down" (also known as "splash down") on the coast of Pensacola, Florida, after 2: 40 p.m. EST on the 2nd.
A successful landing would prove that the United States once again has a fully viable and proven method of transporting its own astronauts to and from space.
The last time a U.S. manned spacecraft landed at sea was in 1975, when Apollo and the Soviet Union space vehicle splashed into the Pacific Ocean after successfully docking in Earth orbit.
NASA and SpaceX chose Florida as the landing site to stay as far away from Hurricane Isaias as possible.
Mission personnel will follow strict guidelines, confirm the weather conditions allow, and then issue instructions to the astronauts to leave.
Hurley and Benken will ignite the thrusters and begin to deorbit, descending at a speed of several kilometers per second, and will experience a high temperature of 2,000 degrees Celsius as they cross the atmosphere.
As the spacecraft continues to descend at a speed of 560 kilometers per hour, two parachutes will open at an altitude of 5,500 meters, and four main parachutes will unfold at an altitude of 1,800 meters, slowly landing the spacecraft.
