title: Space fans all over the world! 2 astronauts return to Earth on SpaceX Dragon 2
text:
NASA and SpaceX teamed up to deliver two astronauts to the International Space Station on the Dragon 2 spacecraft, completing a historic feat.
After a 2-month mission, two NASA astronauts are preparing to return to Earth on Dragon 2, once again attracting the attention of space fans around the world. (Photo taken from SpaceX Live) 2020-08-02 13: 33: 09 [News / roundup] NASA and SpaceX, a space company, launched the Dragon 2 spacecraft on May 31, Taiwan time, to send two American astronauts to the International Space Station. Finish the history.
After a 2-month mission, NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley are set to return to Earth aboard Dragon 2, once again attracting the attention of space fans around the world.
Banken and Hurley have boarded the Dragon 2 and separated from the International Space Station at 7: 35 a.m. Taiwan time on the 2nd.
The Dragon 2 is expected to ignite its engine again at about 1: 49 a.m. PDT on the 3rd, detach from orbit, and land in the surface ocean within an hour, that is, 2: 40 a.m.
Please continue reading...
The Dragon 2 is expected to land in the Gulf of Mexico, but as Hurricane Isias approaches the east coast of Florida, NASA and SpaceX are still evaluating the landing site.
On the return journey, the Dragon 2 will travel at 28,160 km / h, slow down after entering the atmosphere and withstand a high temperature of 3,500 degrees.
At 5.5 km above sea level, the Dragon 2 will open two cone-shaped parachutes at a speed of 560 km / h; at 1.8 km above sea level, the Dragon 2 will open four main parachutes to smoothly land on the surface of the sea.
NASA and SpaceX successfully sent two astronauts to the International Space Station two months ago with the Falcon 9 rocket and the Dragon 2, the first time the United States has sent an astronaut from the territory of the earth since 2011, and the first manned launch of a commercial spacecraft in human history.

title: SpaceX Dragon spacecraft completes 64 days of operation to return two astronauts to Earth - International
text:
Crew Dragon, the first manned spacecraft, will return to Earth with two astronauts after two months of space flight. They have left the International Space Station and entered the deceleration process. It is expected to enter the atmosphere at 6: 20 pm GMT on August 2 (2: 20 am Taipei time on August 3). Landing point (depending on the weather).
Space flight now Astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken entered the new spacecraft from the International Space Station at 7: 30 p.m. EST on August 1 (7: 30 a.m. PDT on August 2) (this mission is called Demo-2, the spacecraft is also named Endeavour), and they will continue their orbits. Earth slows down, then enters the atmosphere, parachutes open above the intended location in the Gulf of Mexico and fall into the sea waiting for logistics personnel to respond.
The current International Space Station, with two Russian astronauts, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Vagner, will stay until October, when they will return to Kazakhstan on the Russian Soyuz spacecraft, which landed on land.
Before they leave, three new crew members (also Russian cosmonauts) will arrive at the station on October 14 aboard a new Soyuz spacecraft to complete the replacement procedures.
SpaceX Demo-2's Crew Dragon undocks from space station During their two-month stay on the space station, Hurley and Bakken performed important experiments and maintenance of the station's equipment.
In June and July, Bakken walked out in a spacesuit to replace the station ’ s solar cells and power generation modules.
"Our mission isn't really over until we actually get back to Earth," said Hurley, one of the two astronauts.
"The hardest part is getting us to the space station, but the most important part is getting us home safely," said another astronaut.
Astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken. (Image / NASA) Assuming favorable weather conditions in the waters off Pensacola, Florida, the spacecraft will enter a recognizable atmosphere on August 2 at 14: 36 EST (August 3, 0236 Taipei time) and land at 28,000 kilometers per hour, when the temperature of the spacecraft ’ s heat shield will be as high as 1900. Degrees.
Such high heat will not be able to communicate, about 6 minutes, into the lower atmosphere, will leave the hottest part, but also to resume communication, about 5500 meters above sea level, let out the parachute.
The parachute will slow down the spacecraft. It is expected to land at 14: 48 EST (0248 Taipei time), but there is a tropical storm Isaias in the sea, so NASA envisioned seven Haiti points, four of which are in the Gulf of Mexico, and three in the Atlantic Ocean, depending on the weather conditions.
If the weather conditions in the Gulf of Mexico deteriorate, the astronauts may stay for a while, but fortunately the crew has at least three days of spare food and water and other supplies on board.
This time, the astronauts brought back about 150 kilograms of cargo, including frozen experimental samples, personal equipment and the American flag left on the space station in 2011, the last space shuttle flight.
At that time, the space shuttle was called "Endeavour", and this time the crew of the Dragon was also called "Endeavour", which obviously had the meaning of carrying forward the first and the second.
Hurley, one of the two astronauts, was also the pilot of the last Space Shuttle mission that year.
Taking back the flag is also a comparison, it is a competition between SpaceX and Boeing to capture the flag, and obviously SpaceX has succeeded in capturing the flag.
With the success of the first manned flight of the Crew Dragon, SpaceX will analyze the data of the mission Demo-2 with NASA before formally issuing commercial certification for the rotation of the crew.
Soon, this fall, SpaceX will receive the first Zhao's "regular crew rotation", the mission is called Crew-1, this time with four astronauts on board.
(China Times News Network)

title: Dragonfly successfully returns to Earth from space
text:
At around 2: 48 p.m. on August 2, Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley returned to Earth aboard the Dragon spacecraft and landed in the Gulf of Mexico.
President Trump congratulated them on their successful return to Earth.
Welcome back to Earth, said the head of Space Exploration Technologies to Banken and Hurley! Thank you for riding the Dragon spacecraft developed by SpaceX.
According to the official website of the US space exploration technology company SpaceX, the final phase of the mission will take 19 hours, landing in the Gulf of Mexico in western Florida at 2: 48 pm EST on August 2.
Hurricane Isaias is currently hitting the Gulf of Mexico.
NASA considered postponing its return to Earth program at one point, but ultimately decided to hold it as scheduled.
NASA and private aerospace company SpaceX have chosen the coast of Pensacola, Florida as the first landing site for the Dragon spacecraft on August 2. The US Air Force tracked the course of the "Isaias" on August 2, and the landing site was changed to the Gulf of Mexico and landed at sea.
The last time an American astronaut landed at sea was in July 1975. Since then, most astronauts have landed on land using NASA shuttles or the Russian Soyuz.
Since the retirement of the shuttle fleet in 2011, the United States has been leasing the Russian Soyuz spacecraft to carry people to the International Space Station, and NASA has outsourced the development of new manned spacecraft to private companies, including the US space exploration technology company SpaceX and Boeing, to improve efficiency.
Elon Musk, founder of the US space exploration technology company SpaceX, stressed that although it was smooth, he did not dare to rejoice too early, because “landing can be much more dangerous than taking off … We have to make sure that they come back safely and make sure that we have done everything in place to minimize the risk of landing. ”
Two months ago, at 3: 22 p.m. on May 30, Bancon and Hurley were launched from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida on a U.S. SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Thirteen minutes later, the Dragon spacecraft separated from the second booster rocket and entered Earth orbit a few minutes later.

title: Three meanings of the success of SpaceX ’ s manned space mission
text:
SpaceX ’ s first manned mission ended with the successful landing of the Crew Dragon with two astronauts on board.
This symbolizes the reopening of the US space mission after a nine-year hiatus and the success of the private sector ’ s space program.
On August 2, two astronauts in the Dragon Flyer controlled the landing process.
SpaceX ’ s Dragon capsule features a new touchscreen design. (Reuters) The United States launched another manned space mission nine years apart, and the last manned space mission in the United States was in 2011, during which the International Space Station ’ s personnel had to rely on Russian assistance.
This caused a lot of trouble: if the weather on the Russian launch site was bad, or the spacecraft was in trouble, the US space station mission would have to be postponed.
SpaceX ’ s success allows the United States to resume manned space missions, which means a lot to NASA.
Significantly reduce the cost of space missions The cost of borrowing Russian spacecraft from the United States is becoming more and more expensive.
According to the US space information network "SpaceNews" reported that in May, NASA and Russia reached an agreement to allow the Soyuz spacecraft to carry American astronauts to the space station, but the ticket price is up to 90 million US dollars.
Instead, NASA uses SpaceX to pick up astronauts at an average cost of just $50 million per launch.
That ’ s down to SpaceX ’ s technical focus: SpaceX ’ s Falcon rockets are recyclable and can be launched at a much lower cost than conventional, disposable rockets.
This not only reduces the cost of developing U.S. space missions, but also makes it more feasible for private companies to participate in space operations.
↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ More photos of the rocket launch, you can click on the image to enlarge: + 3 + 2 The Dragon capsule landed safely in the Gulf of Mexico on August 2. (Reuters) The first private company successfully completed the space mission in the history of the space mission is a state-driven program, but this mission uses a variety of key technologies such as rockets and space suits, which are mainly developed and provided by SpaceX.
The success of the mission means opening a new chapter for commercial space missions.
SpaceX signed a contract with space travel company Space Adventures in February.
Axiom Space, a company founded by senior NASA employees, also signed a contract with SpaceX in March, marking a major step toward launching space tourism.
In addition to space tourism, SpaceX plans to participate in manned missions to the Moon and Mars.
SpaceX ’ s success may attract more private companies to participate in the space program, allowing space missions to become investment projects and rapid development.

title: US Dragon spacecraft leaves space station to send two astronauts back to Earth
text:
WASHINGTON, August 1 (Xinhua) -- A U.S. space exploration technology company's Dragon spacecraft left the International Space Station on Saturday to carry two U.S. astronauts back to Earth after a two-month stay on the International Space Station (ISS).
The Dragon spacecraft left the International Space Station (ISS) at 19: 35 local time (07: 35 local time (07: 35 local time) on Tuesday, according to NASA.
Its engines ignited twice to help the spacecraft escape from the space station, sending astronauts Douglas Hurley and Robert Benken and some supplies back to Earth.
It is the first time a privately owned spacecraft has flown U.S. astronauts back to Earth since they were sent to the space station.
According to the plan, the Dragon spacecraft will splash off the coast of Florida at 14: 41 EST (02: 41 Singapore time) on Tuesday after about 19 hours of flight.
NASA said this will bring an end to the two-month test flight of the manned Dragon spacecraft.
On May 30, the Dragon was launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.
After nearly 19 hours of flight, the spacecraft arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) and docked with it.
Later, the two astronauts entered the space station and carried out a series of experiments and research missions with other astronauts on board.
This is the first time that the United States has used domestic rockets and spacecraft to send astronauts from home to the space station since the retirement of the space shuttle in 2011, and it is also a key step for commercial manned spaceflight.
The mission is designed to test the ability of the Dragon spacecraft to safely transport astronauts to and from the space station, including details of on-orbit flights, docking with the space station and returning to the ground.

title: SpaceX manned spacecraft successfully completes first manned space mission
text:
A manned spacecraft developed by US private aerospace company SpaceX has successfully landed in the waters off Florida, completing its first manned space mission.
This is the first time in 45 years that an American astronaut has landed at sea.
A Dragon spaceship carrying two American astronauts crosses the atmosphere and opens its parachute.
At 2: 48 p.m. on Sunday, it successfully made a soft landing near the Gulf of Mexico off the west coast of Florida, completing its first manned test flight.
Hurley and Benken conclude their two-month space mission with a 21-hour journey back to Earth from the International Space Station.
NASA sent a support ship to the spacecraft's position and lifted the Dragon out of the water to the deck.
The two astronauts leave the plane for medical examination and are sent to NASA's Jansen Space Center in Houston.
President Trump congratulated and thanked the crew on the social networking site, and said he was excited to have another astronaut landing on the surface for 45 years.

title: How does Space X open up the commercialization of manned aviation? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
text:
On August 2, the Crew Dragon, developed and designed by space exploration company Space X, successfully completed a historic space journey, bringing two astronauts from NASA back to Earth safely. With the spacecraft accurately landing in the Gulf of Mexico, this space flight became the first flight in human history by a commercial spacecraft, opening the door to the full commercialization of space flight.
The mission officially began on May 30, when two astronauts, Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken, flew aboard the Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station.
During the 63-day stay on the space station, the astronauts completed basic station countermissions and conducted a total of four spacewalks.
This flight is also the last test of Space X ’ s manned space mission, after which Space X will be able to officially open business and charge “passengers ” for transportation.
For ordinary people, the dream of flying into space seems to be within reach. How did Space X do this?
How is the commercialization of space flight achieved?
All along, almost all human spaceflight practice has been carried out under the guidance of national governments, the reason is obvious - no private enterprise has the ability to pay the sky-high costs behind the rocket launch.
Even with a certain amount of financial support from the government, reducing costs is still the biggest challenge to achieve commercialization.
A mock-up of SpaceX ’ s Dragon Crew.
After the first recovery of the spacecraft in 2015, the company carried out refurbishment and safety inspections of the spacecraft and re-launched the spacecraft into space two years later, resulting in the reuse of the spacecraft.
(Getty) Imagine a Boeing 747 worth more than $300 million each time it completes a flight that would be useless if an ordinary aircraft could not be reused.
In this way, passengers will have to bear the cost of the whole price of the aircraft, so that the company will not lose money.
At such a high price, no passengers would want to fly.
This is the dilemma facing the commercialization of space flight. Only by allowing space ships and spaceship boosters to be reused like airplanes can companies make a profit.
Space X understands the importance of this, and since its founding in 2002, the company has been experimenting with the recycling and reuse of spacecraft and rockets. In 2010, Space X first recycled the Dragon spacecraft, which was then used for cargo transportation, and two years later, the spacecraft officially began commercial operations to carry cargo for the International Space Station.
However, the rocket used as a spacecraft booster at the same time was still used up and discarded, and it was not until December 2015 that the Falcon 9 booster developed by Space X was recovered and reused in 2017.
SpaceX is not the only company aiming to commercialize manned and cold air flights.
Aircraft manufacturer Boeing, Blue Origin, founded by Amazon founder Jeff Bezo, and Virgin Galactic, part of the British Virgin Group, are all participants in the space race.
On December 20, 2019, Boeing launched its first manned spacecraft, the CST-100 Starliner, but it did not successfully enter orbit with the International Space Station.
(Getty) For the time being, however, Space X is still far ahead.
So far, Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic have failed to put their spacecraft into orbit.
Another closer competitor, aircraft manufacturer Boeing, also lagged behind SpaceX in this collaboration with NASA.
In 2014, both Boeing and SpaceX were awarded contracts for NASA ’ s Commercial Crew Program, and in fact, as an established aerospace company, Boeing received 60% of the NASA-based funding, compared to the corporate philosophy of the deviant and somewhat unreliable Space X is not favored.
“Congress, industry, and most of NASA ’ s leaders feel the need to give money directly to Boeing and hold them accountable, ” said Lori Garver, a former deputy administrator at NASA.
Tesla Motors founder Elon Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, is constantly innovating technology with the goal of reducing the cost of space transportation and colonizing Mars. (Getty) SpaceX founder Elon Musk told The Washington Post: “We had to deal with it in an extremely messy way.
If we had followed the standard procedure, we would have run out of money.
For years, we ’ ve had to run our money every week and spend it in a matter of weeks.
This has led us to think carefully.
Adopt obsolete parts, or fail – that ’ s the choice we face.
Buy obsolete parts, fix them, and let them work properly.
Perhaps in this spirit, SpaceX ended up with the remaining 40% of funding provided by NASA, far ahead of rival Boeing.
In a flight test last year to send an unmanned space capsule to the International Space Station, the Boeing designed space capsule failed to enter the planned orbit.
Since then, NASA has made more than 80 suggestions for improvements, and the company has announced that it will resume the test flight at the end of this year.
This commercial model adopted by NASA shows its advantages.
After the aviation project is handed over to private enterprises, only a fixed amount of capital is provided, and enterprises have to use limited funds to create profits, so they have to find ways to reduce the construction cost, which creates a prerequisite for the future normalization of the aviation industry.
Today, the success of SpaceX ’ s manned spacecraft officially opens the way for the commercialization of manned aviation, but for ambitious entrepreneurs, the race is just beginning.
The introduction of reusable rockets and spacecraft is the first step, and companies will strive to increase the number of times rockets and spacecraft can be reused, and shorten the repair cycle after use, so that it is possible to win competitors in the cost war and achieve sustainable development.

title: SpaceX ’ s SN-5 successfully jumps 150 meters high in test video
text:
▲ A journey of thousands of miles begins with a single step! The great journey of space is forged from countless tests! The video of the giant barrel shaking and rising is super healing.
Intern reporter Chien Li-yu / Comprehensive report Space Exploration Technology (SpaceX) "Crew Dragon" successfully took two astronauts to the International Space Station and returned to the Gulf of Mexico on the 2nd to challenge the sea landing.
In addition, there was an amazing breakthrough, the "SN-5's 150m jump test" was successful, the official channel released this test video, the huge steel barrel slowly rising, the thruster ejected a long column of fire, sending the SN-5 150 meters into the sky, and then landing on the ground.
According to spaceflightnow, the test combines a full-size fuel tank with a Raptor engine that can generate 440,000 pounds of thrust at full speed, making it the most powerful “methane fuel rocket engine ” in history!
However, because this is only for testing, there is no nose cone and tail, but the SN-5, which is 30 meters high and 9 meters in diameter, is still very large. If the nose cone is added, it will become 50 meters high, which is about half the length of a Boeing 747.
▼ SN-5 does not have the appearance of a nose cone and tail, which is a bit like a stainless steel environmental straw. (Photo / from SpaceX official website) SpaceX founder Elon Musk said that he will make several more short jumps to simplify the launch process and finally enter the high altitude.
The test video is interspersed with three lenses, you can see the SN-5 before landing, the bottom six supports open, close to the ground when the heat of the flame makes the picture look like boiling water, and finally stops in the landing area, which is very interesting.
Prior to this ground test did not go well, SpaceX lost four starship prototypes.

title: Hemingway ’ s Novels Revealed Hundreds of Mistakes Scholar: It ’ s Not His Wrong
text:
According to a recently released study, the late American writer and Nobel laureate Ernest Hemingway (1899-1961) published works, most of the works do not accurately express the author's original intention, due to editing or typography errors, his work has hundreds of errors, and has not been corrected.
Ernest Hemingway is a famous 20th-century novelist who has written 13 novels and more than 80 short stories, including The Old Man and the Sea, The Sun Also Rises and A Farewell to Arms. He won the Nobel Prize for Literature and Literature in 1952. Pulitzer Prize.
He is known for his concise, direct writing style, which rarely uses decorative words, but tells the story of the courage, strength and dignity that some people have shown in their lives in simple sentences.
Robert W Trogdon, a scholar of 20th-century American literature, recently published his research. He visited the Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum in Boston, which houses most of Hemingway ’ s manuscripts, and compared the published books with the original.
He found that these errors were minor errors, but minor errors were errors, mostly caused by editing and typesetting.
Ernest Hemingway worked as a journalist in Cuba. (WIKI) He cites the 1926 novel The Sun Rises Normal, which recounts the disillusionment that France and Spain experienced after the war.
The characters in the novel include the bullfighter Maricia Lalanda, but the letters L and S look so similar that the editors at the time misunderstood "Maricia Laland" as "Maricia Saland".
In addition, because it is difficult to distinguish the "s" and "q" of the author, it is easy to mistake Hemingway's reference to a real restaurant in Paris, "Cigogue", for "Ciqoque".
In Hemingway ’ s 1933 short story A Way You ’ ll Never Be, the original manuscript was written as “hat ”, but the book was mistakenly replaced by“ bat ”, making the original meaning “hit with a hat ” become“ hit with a bat. ” ent supply of these insects for a day ’ s fishing by pursuing them with your hands or trying to hit them with a hat.)
In addition to editing errors, typographers changed the punctuation and verb tenses in Hemingway ’ s original text when typesetting.
For example, in Hemingway ’ s 1933 short story The Light of the World, the original is actually “she just kept on laughing and shaking ”, but when typesetting it becomes“ she just keep on laughing and shaking ”, changing the original tense incorrectly.
He notes that with the exception of The Snows Of Kilimanjar and A Moveable Feast, published in 2005 and 2009, Hemingway ’ s current book has not been edited to retain the meaning he really wants to express.
Hemingway ’ s contemporaries, F. Scott Fitzgerald and William Faulkner, have since reprinted and corrected their original errors.
(Getty) The New Hemingway Studies and The Letters of Ernest Hemingway: Volume 5, 1932-1934, to be published by Cambridge University Press. A letter about his feelings after his published work was edited.
Sandra Spanier, editor-in-chief of Epistles, said that Hemingway had objected to the editor ’ s deletion of his work in his letter, and said that if the story could be shorter, he would have shortened it, which is already his best and most complete story, otherwise he would not show the story to anyone.
This just reflects that Hemingway cherishes the word like gold and does not want others to change his creation casually.

title: Dragon spacecraft descends into Gulf of Mexico to escape dependence on Russian SpaceX to make history - 20200804 - International
text:
Astronauts Douglas Hurley and Bob Behnken ended their two-month mission aboard the Dragon spacecraft Endeavour, which separated from the International Space Station at 4: 35 p.m. on August 1.
"Dragon spacecraft" first threw its "suitcase" equipped with heat, power and other systems into the atmosphere to burn, then activated the thruster, entered the Earth orbit and return trajectory, at a speed of 28,000 kilometers per hour, withstand high temperatures of up to 1900 ° C through the atmosphere, to the scheduled time to open four parachutes to speed of 24 kilometers per hour. Gulf of Mexico near Pensacola, Florida.
Two astronauts return to Earth Trump Obama congratulates SpaceX control headquarters: "Welcome back to Earth."
President Trump, former President Barack Obama, Democratic presidential candidate Joe Biden, as well as SpaceX rival Boeing, Amazon founder Bezos ’ private space company Blue Origin, have congratulated.
It was the first U.S. manned spacecraft to land at sea since the Apollo – Soyuz mission in 1975.
The team rehearsed the return flight procedure several times in advance, and drew up seven landing sites.
Later, about 40 miles offshore of Pensacola was selected. The nearby ship then hoisted the capsule and recovered the parachute to dispose of the toxic fuel vapor remaining outside the capsule, before separating the capsule at 3: 59 to allow the two astronauts to come out.
The Dragon capsule, which has a significant burn mark on its outer shell, will be inspected for six weeks.
The success of this mission marks the culmination of many years for Musk.
Musk founded SpaceX in 2002, and the company won a nearly US $7 billion (HK $54.6 billion) contract with Boeing in 2014 for the United States to develop the manned launch vehicle "space taxi", and now SpaceX is clearly surpassing Boeing.
Boeing tested sending unmanned space capsules to the space station last year, but failed.
SpaceX ’ s next mission is to launch four astronauts at the end of September, and plans to launch a paid space tour of Earth orbit and even the moon.
At a press conference, NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine described the mission as making history, “entering a new era of human spaceflight, ” and marking a shift in NASA ’ s role from a former hardware buyer, owner and operator to one of the customers of commercial human spaceflight today.
(Bloomberg / AFP / CNN)

title: Israel and UAE to sign peace deal at White House
text:
Israel and the United Arab Emirates on Thursday (August 13) announced the establishment of full diplomatic relations, which also means that Israel has suspended its annexation of occupied areas in the West Bank.
The agreement was brokered by the United States and the two countries will sign a peace agreement at the White House in about three weeks.
Trump said in a Twitter post: "Today is a huge breakthrough! Two of our great friends, Israel and the United Arab Emirates, have reached a historic peace agreement."
It is the third peace agreement reached between Israel and Arab countries since Israel's founding in 1948.
A statement from the UAE Foreign Ministry said the two delegations will meet in the coming weeks to sign bilateral agreements in areas such as energy, tourism, direct flights, investment, security, communications and technology.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the breakthrough agreement was a "historic day" for Israel and welcomed a "new era" in relations between Israel and the Arab world.
Under the agreement, Trump asked Israel to suspend its annexation of the West Bank.
Netanyahu pointed out that the annexation may still take place one day, but must be done in cooperation with Washington, "My plan has not changed, that is, to expand our sovereignty in Judea and Samaria in full coordination with the United States."
Israel calls the occupied areas of the West Bank "Judea and Samaria" and considers the territory part of the historic Jewish homeland, but the area is considered by the Palestinians as territory.
Crown Prince Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan of Abu Dhabi confirmed on Twitter the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
“During the call with President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu, an agreement was reached to prevent further Israeli annexation of Palestinian territories … The UAE and Israel also agreed to cooperate and draw a blueprint for bilateral relations, ” he said.
Trump: More Arab countries will follow US President Donald Trump ’ s statement at the White House: “After 49 years, Israel and the United Arab Emirates will fully normalize diplomatic relations. ”
Having broken the ice, I expect more Arab and Muslim countries to follow in the footsteps of the UAE. "
Israel ’ s ambassador to Washington, Ron Dermer, described the day as “a great day of peace, ” adding:“ Israel is deeply grateful to President Trump for everything he has done to achieve this breakthrough. ”
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi agreed.
“I read with interest the joint statement between the United States, the brotherly United Arab Emirates and Israel on the cessation of Israel ’ s annexation of Palestinian land and deeply appreciate it, ” he wrote on Twitter.
British Prime Minister Boris Johnson welcomed the normalization of relations between the two countries and Israel's decision not to annex the occupied West Bank.
"I had a deep desire not to annex the West Bank, and today's agreement to suspend the program is a welcome step on the road to a more peaceful Middle East," he tweeted.
A spokesman for Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas said the agreement amounted to "treason", while Foreign Minister Riyad al-Malki also stressed that the Palestinian ambassador to the UAE would be recalled immediately.
Hamas, the Islamist group that controls the Gaza Strip northeast of the Sinai Peninsula in the West Bank, described the incident as "a reward for the crime of Israeli occupation" and Hamas spokesman Fawzi Barhoum said: "Normalization [of Israeli-Arab relations] is a stab in the back of our people."

title: The United Arab Emirates and Israel broke the ice on the land of Palestine in the century _ Hong Kong 01 _ 01 Point of View
text:
On Thursday, the United Arab Emirates and Israel announced an agreement to normalize relations, the Abraham Agreement, paving the way for cooperation between the two countries in economic and trade, science and technology, and medical care.
Although the agreement may be a turning point in the sense of peace between the Arab states and Israel, it is conditional on the holding of land originally belonging to Palestine as a condition of an equivalent deal.
This not only implies that the UAE has turned its back on the Arab world ’ s established position on historical justice, but also pushes Palestine into even greater isolation.
A joint statement issued by the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates said the agreement would “promote peace in the Middle East and demonstrate the bold diplomacy and vision of the leaders of the three countries, ” which Trump later described as a“ truly historic moment. ”
At the same time, in addition to Iran and Palestine, many regional and Western countries, such as Jordan, Egypt, the United Kingdom and France, have welcomed the thawing of relations between the two countries.
As the third country to normalize relations with Israel, after Egypt and Jordan, the UAE should have been the boon of more than half a century of bloody conflict in the Middle East, but the price of peace is not cheap.
The two countries will sign a bilateral agreement in the coming weeks to develop trade in areas such as tourism, telecommunications and medical care; strengthen economic integration and coordination of security services; open up the holy city of Jerusalem to Muslims; and expand and accelerate cooperation between the two countries in the treatment of COVID-19 and the development of vaccines.
But the most expensive price is that Israel agrees to “suspend ” its“ declaration of sovereignty ” over its forcible occupation of the West Bank, which is as absurd as allowing thieves to keep a low profile and have the goods they can rob.
As a small country in the Gulf region, the United Arab Emirates has at least three points to consider in its diplomatic turn.
The establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries will not only expand the oil and natural oil export market of the UAE, but also bring in more tourists and foreign investment to ease the pandemic economy. Finally, although the population of the UAE is only more than 9 million, there are more than 60,000 cases of COVID-19 in the UAE. Therefore, there is a real need to cooperate with Israel, a country that is mature in biological and medical technology.
Although the UAE does not have a close military relationship with Israel, like Egypt, this official turn of the UAE is tantamount to abandoning the established position of the Arab world in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
The Arab Peace Initiative, adopted in the early years by the Arab League of which the UAE belongs, wrote that the prerequisites for normalization of relations with Israel included the acceptance by Israel of a sovereign and independent state on its territory, with East Jerusalem as its capital, and the borders of the West Bank and Gaza Strip on June 4, 1967 (before the Third Middle East War). Withdrawal from the Golan Heights in Syria.
However, the agreement has reflected the UAE's diplomatic position of taking the wind and steering the wheel.
Since the 1967 Middle East war, Israel has used illegal colonial policies to transfer land seized from the Palestinians to Jewish “settlements ” to gradually expand the territory that Tel Aviv actually controls.
After half a century of deportation and demolition, there are now as many as 430,000 Israeli Jews in 132 settlements in the West Bank.
Even though the United Nations has repeatedly stated that the land occupied by Israel after 1967 is a “flagrant violation of international law ” and“ devoid of any legal effect, ” weak protests cannot stop Israel ’ s colonialism.
Judging by the reaction of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, it seems to be a false illusion among leaders that the agreement will contribute to peace and stability in the Middle East.
After the agreement, Netanyahu said that he only agreed to "postpone" the plan, but "will not give up the right to our land", which in fact refers to the "land", including the Jordan River, covering a third of the West Bank, indicating that the agreement did not induce Israel to abandon its colonial plan.
So how can a country that has not abandoned expansionism promote peace and stability?

US President Donald Trump suddenly announced at the White House today that Israel and the United Arab Emirates have reached a historic peace agreement and that the two sides will normalize their relations in full.
"A huge breakthrough today! Two of our great friends, Israel and the United Arab Emirates, have reached a historic peace agreement," Trump said in a tweet.
Trump later hinted at a press conference that more diplomatic breakthroughs were expected between Israel and its Muslim neighbors in the Middle East.
“It ’ s happening, I can ’ t talk about it, ” Trump said. U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo described it as“ a historic day, a big step toward peace in the Middle East. ”
“The United States hopes that this courageous step will be the first in a series of agreements to end 72 years of hostility in the Middle East, ” Pompeo said.
The peace deal was sealed over the phone between Prime Minister Netanyahu, Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Zayed and President Trump https: / / t.co / bgrMvg5s7U pic.twitter.com / WYL24TrN1x — Reuters (@ Reuters) August 13, 2020 In a joint statement, Benjamin Netanyahu and Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan, the crown prince of Abu Dhabi, said they had a telephone conversation today “and agreed to the full normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates. ”
Representatives of Israel and the Arab League will meet in the coming weeks to sign bilateral agreements on investment, tourism, direct flights, security guarantees and the opening of an embassy.
“At the request of U.S. President Donald Trump and with the support of the United Arab Emirates, Israel will suspend its declaration of sovereignty over the region outlined in President Trump ’ s Vision for Peace and will now focus on expanding relations with other countries in the Arab and Muslim world, ” the statement said.
"The United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates are confident that more diplomatic breakthroughs with other countries are possible and will work together to achieve this goal," the statement added.
Israeli Prime Minister: Delay the annexation, but not renounce the “right to claim territory ” According to the Israel Times, hours after Trump announced the news on Twitter, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said in a televised speech that he would establish ambassadors for“ comprehensive ” exchanges such as economic exchanges and direct flights.
“Through our shared strengths, we can bring a better future for our people and our region, ” Netanyahu said. He said the two countries will share their advanced technological knowledge to achieve mutual benefit.
Netanyahu said that as part of an agreement to normalize relations with the United Arab Emirates, he agreed to suspend the annexation of the occupied West Bank, but that the plan was still "under discussion".
Netanyahu said the deal was not meant to be a quid pro quo, saying that “my merger plan has not changed, in full coordination with the United States. ”
He has "postponed" the annexation of the West Bank, but he "will never give up his rights to our land."
Today we use in a new era of peace between Israel and the Arab world.
I just came from an historical virtual conference between myself, President Donald Trump and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Zayed of the United Arab Emirates.pic.twitter.com / tmugY7XrAT — Benjamin Netanyahu (@ netanyahu) August 13, 2020 Palestine says betrayed, demands Arab League emergency meeting Mahmud Abbas, president of the Palestinian Authority, complained about the deal, calling it a betrayal of the Palestinians. He expressed strong dissatisfaction and condemnation, and called for an emergency meeting of the Arab League.
Palestinians feel betrayed, a move at a crucial moment that undermines their struggle for independence, the report said.
Former Iranian Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian wrote on Twitter that it was the wrong strategy.
All parties have short-term interests: The historic decision by the former U.S. envoy to the Middle East to normalize full-scale relations between Israel and the Arab League is an important step forward in diplomacy.
Inevitably, however, questions arise.
Will all the promises of this agreement be fulfilled?
According to the BBC, this is far from the Middle East peace plan that Trump has long advocated.
However, there are short-term benefits for all parties.
Trump ’ s prospects for re-election appear to be in jeopardy, and the deal allows him to claim credit.
White House national security adviser Robert C. O ’ Brien even declared that Trump deserved the Nobel Peace Prize.
“It really doesn ’ t surprise me if the president is actually nominated for the Nobel Prize because of his efforts today, which is why he should be a candidate for the Nobel Peace Prize, ” O ’ Brien said.
Analysis pointed out that for the embattled Prime Minister of Israel, Netanyahu, this allowed him to get out of his own predicament.
He made a big promise to annex key areas of the occupied West Bank. This proved impossible, especially due to contradictions in the United States and strong international opposition.
Analysis believes that for the United Arab Emirates, although it can strengthen relations with the United States, and the agreement with Israel may produce significant economic and security benefits, but it is difficult to say exactly what the direct benefits are.
Aaron David Miller, a former U.S. Middle East peace envoy, described the deal as a “three-win, one-loss ” historic decision.
Miller believes that this is a victory for Israel, the United Arab Emirates and American leaders, but a loss for the Palestinians.

title: Interpretation of the Israeli-Arab Peace Agreement: The Way to Survive in a Wealthy Small Country Surrounded by Strong Enemies
text:
On August 13, 2020, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) announced that it will normalize relations with Israel.
The Abraham Accord, brokered by the Trump administration, is the first peace agreement in the Middle East in the past 26 years after Israel and Jordan signed a peace deal in 1994, which New York Times columnist Thomas Friedman described as a “geopolitical earthquake. ”
Many commentators have pointed out that the agreement has helped raise their fading reputation at home for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump, and some polls in recent days seem to support these predictions.
But simply viewing the agreement as a way for politicians to salvage the domestic downturn is likely to underestimate the years of quiet work by Israeli and Arab diplomats and the efforts of their leaders to achieve their respective regional political goals.
Looking at the interaction between Israel and the Arab League in recent years, as well as the actions of the two countries in the Middle East and North Africa, it is not difficult to find that this agreement has already occurred.
In view of the existence of the common enemies of Israel and the United Arab Emirates in the region: Iran and the Islamic State (ISIS), the two countries have been cooperating on defense security and intelligence technology for more than a decade.
After Barack Obama took office in 2009, Israel and the Arab League joined forces to pressure the Obama administration to take Iran ’ s nuclear weapons development seriously.
In addition, it has been reported that the Emirates Center for Strategic Studies and Research, established in 1994 with the support of the UAE government, has effectively served as a conduit between the UAE and the Israeli government.
In addition to defense, intelligence, and other areas involving more classified information, the two sides also exchanged economic, cultural, and technological issues. In 2015, Israel established an official diplomatic mission under the International Renewable Energy Agency (IREA) in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Abu Dhabi attended the meeting of the agency.
In October 2018, Israeli Minister of Culture and Sports Miri Regev visited Abu Dhabi to watch Israeli athletes compete at the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam. After the Israeli judoka won gold, Regev also witnessed the historic moment when the Israeli national anthem was played in Abu Dhabi for the first time. Visit Abu Dhabi and Dubai in July.
In July this year, Group 42, based in Abu Dhabi and specializing in artificial intelligence and cloud technology, signed a memorandum of understanding with Israel ’ s Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) to collaborate on COVID-19 solutions. Tel Aviv, delivery of medical supplies to Palestine.
Video Description: Israeli Foreign Minister Regev witnesses the historic moment when the Israeli national anthem is played in Abu Dhabi In recent years, there have been many similar public exchanges between Israel and the Arab League.
Looking back now, it seems that the two countries have long paved the way for normalization.
The ultimate goal stated in the Abrahamic Agreement is “full normalization of relations. ” In the past few days, both Israel and the Arab League have continued to take various actions, including direct hotlines between the two foreign ministers, to carry out the determination to normalize relations.
The two countries also announced that in the coming weeks, the two sides will sign bilateral agreements on direct flights, tourism, defense, culture and other matters, as well as discuss the establishment of embassies and other areas of mutual benefit.
The United Arab Emirates is the third Arab country to sign a peace agreement with Israel, after Egypt and Jordan signed peace agreements with Israel in 1979 and 1994, respectively.
However, Israel ’ s agreements with Egypt and Jordan involve territorial disputes, and the Israeli-Arab peace accords do not address this issue.
Israel said it would suspend plans for the annexation of the West Bank in order to normalize relations with the Arab League, while the Arab League said it remained concerned about the Israeli-Palestinian peace process and stressed that normalizing relations with Israel would help buy time on settlement issues. A more equitable Israeli-Palestinian peace agreement.
Although the agreement has surprised many, it is not surprising that the leaders of the two countries have also been criticized at home and abroad.
The United Arab Emirates has been criticized by some Arab countries, Turkey, Iran, the Palestinian Authority and Hamas, which controls the Gaza Strip, and even criticized the move as "betraying the Palestinians."
Led by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Turkey, which has had strained relations with Israel in recent years, has even dropped the rhetoric that it may suspend relations with the Arab League, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been criticized by some right-wing leaders in the country for promising to postpone annexation of the West Bank (Note 2).
It is unlikely that policymakers in both countries did not expect the historic agreement to attract some criticism.
They are still determined to sign the agreement, and they must have their own considerations behind it.
For Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, cultivating relations with relatively friendly countries in the region, with limited expectations, can help boost Israel ’ s status and security in the region, focus on its main “enemies ” like Iran, and perhaps marginalize the Palestinian issue in the face of a stalemate with the Palestinian peace process.
As for the logic of the Arab League ’ s policymakers, it can be seen from observing the country ’ s long-term regional foreign policy.
Photo Credit: Reuters / Dashcam Image Wealthy small country, tough environment: The way the UAE survives William Rugh, a scholar with practical diplomatic experience who has studied Middle Eastern relations, observed in the 1990s that the leaders of the UAE know that the country is a rich small country in difficult circumstances, and this strategic environment has largely shaped the logic of the UAE ’ s foreign policy.: How to make good use of the country ’ s abundant oil resources and lead a small country to create a relatively stable environment in the Gulf region surrounded by a large country.
In this context, for Arab foreign policy makers (Note 3), Iran, Saddam Hussein ’ s Iraq and the 2011 Arab Spring are arguably the main challenges facing the country ’ s regional foreign and security policies.
In addition to worrying about the ambitions of Iran, a non-Arab Shia state, in the region, they have also long had sovereignty disputes with Iran on three Gulf islands (Note 4); Saddam Hussein era Iraq, but also to the surrounding Gulf states, showing the ambition that makes Arab leaders feel threatened; and the "Arab Spring" anti-government demonstrations that began to affect many neighboring Arab countries in 2011 have caused waves. As a "non-democratic country", the UAE is under pressure. As you can imagine, the UAE government is like the Gulf monarchies such as Saudi Arabia, and it is not happy to see the spread of democratic forces in the region.
At the same time, the current chief decision-maker of the UAE, Crown Prince Muhammad bin Zayed Al-Nahayan (MBZ), is also the soul behind the UAE ’ s regional security and foreign policy.
In 2004, after the death of Shaikh Zayed bin Sultan Al-Nahayan, the father of the founding father of the UAE, MBZ was appointed Crown Prince. His brother, Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayid Al-Nahayan, was appointed Crown Prince. an) succeeded his father as president; in theory, his brother Khalifa should rule, but due to Khalifa ’ s health, MBZ has been the de facto ruler of the UAE since 2004.
With the consolidation of MBZ, the Arab League ’ s army rose to become the most powerful army in the Middle East, with the exception of Israel.
Influenced by the Arab Spring wave, the Arab League has become more active in some internal or external conflicts in the region over the past few years: the country has been involved in internal military conflicts in Libya and Yemen since 2014 and 2015, respectively; in Egypt, the Arab League has supported a military coup to overthrow the current president of former President Mohamed Morsi, Abdel Fattah el Sisi. It will also establish a military base in northern Somalia, and since 2017, it has joined several Gulf and African countries in accusing neighboring Qatar of supporting terrorism and maintaining close ties with Iran.
It can be said that these actions, as well as the cooperation between the Arab League and Israel in various aspects in recent years, and even the signing of the peace agreement, are aimed at giving this small country a place in difficult circumstances.
Evaluating the Israeli-Arab peace deal is definitely historically significant, but it remains to be seen whether it is truly a “geopolitical earthquake, ” as the New York Times columnist Friedman put it.
If you look at Egypt and Jordan, which signed peace agreements with Israel many years ago, you can see that the existence of a formal peace agreement does not mean that the two sides have never discussed and cooperated closely.
The Palestinian side once again appears to be the loser of this regional political development. Although the Arab League emphasizes that the country is still concerned about the Israeli-Palestinian peace process and Palestinian rights, at least the signing of the agreement symbolizes the Arab League's willingness to formally recognize Israel's statehood and to compromise on the Israeli-Palestinian issue.
As for other neighboring Arab countries, Turkey and other countries that denounce the Arab League or have long criticized Israel ’ s policy toward the Palestinians, it seems that they often talk more on paper than on actual deeds on the Israeli-Palestinian issue; more seriously, many leaders of neighboring Arab countries have from time to time achieved their political goals by speaking harshly on the Palestinian issue, but have not given tangible help to the Palestinians.
In addition to continuing to observe how Israel and the Arab League are taking practical steps to normalize relations, many people have begun to wonder whether neighboring Gulf countries such as Bahrain, Oman, and even Lebanon, which borders Israel, will follow suit and become the next Arab country to recognize Israel and even establish diplomatic relations with it.
If this trend does materialize, it is likely that the Palestinian Authority will come under increased pressure to fear that the Israeli-Palestinian issue will be further marginalized.
Note 1: Although both sides have expressed their willingness to fly directly, there may be considerable difficulties in implementation. Direct flights from Abu Dhabi or Dubai to Israel ’ s Ben Gurion International Airport in Tel Aviv, a 2,000-kilometer distance, must pass through neighboring Arab countries such as Bahrain, Iraq and Saudi Arabia, although Emirates Airline and Etihad Airways are allowed to pass through the airspace of these countries, and El Al is still prohibited from entering the airspace of these Arab countries.
The nearest way to bypass these countries is to bypass the Arabian Peninsula and then enter Israel from the Red Sea to the west of the peninsula, but this is about twice the distance of the straight line.
Note 2: It is important to note that in the peace process plan previously announced by Trump and Netanyahu, the part about the West Bank settlement has also caused some of the so-called right political leaders and settlement residents in the country to feel that Israel will give up part of the West Bank territory that should belong to the country.
Note 3: Although the United Arab Emirates is a federal system of seven emirates, and the leaders of each emirate have a great deal of freedom in many internal affairs, the federal government, or president, basically located in Abu Dhabi, has relatively strong diplomatic decision-making power, and other emirates are less likely to challenge their foreign policy decisions.
Note 4: Iran unilaterally occupied the Greater and Lesser Tunbs islands in the eastern part of the Gulf in November 1971, a few hours before the declaration of the UAE, which were part of Ras al-Khaimah, which later joined the UAE. A memorandum of understanding was signed allowing both sides to jointly govern Abu Musa. The United Arab Emirates quickly declared its sovereignty over the three islands, and the dispute over the sovereignty of the three islands began.
However, the UAE, under the leadership of the Crown Prince MBZ, has continued to develop limited economic and trade relations with Iran in recent years.
See also Rugh, William A. 1996.
"The Foreign Policy of the United Arab Emirates."

With so many enemies in the CIA and the Pentagon, he knows that America ’ s “deep state ” will fight back if Trump is not in office.

This is what I have been pushing for years: it is possible to create peace without sacrificing our land, without dividing Jerusalem, without endangering our future.

Trade, unhindered telecommunications, travel, mutual recognition with Israel and the Persian Gulf neighbors will all become the new “fait accompli. ”
But the Palestinians will never raise a white flag, and they will not accept economic solutions and take money from their political rights.
The Palestinian Authority called the decision "despicable" and a betrayal of the Palestinians, Jerusalem and the al-Aqsa Mosque.
The Arab position on this issue largely reflects the resentment of the Palestinians.
According to the Arab Opinion Index, opposition to diplomatic recognition of Israel increased from 84% in 2011 to 87% in 2018.
Overall, the Palestinians and the streets of Arab countries will respond to the agreement, and there may be two trends.
On the Palestinian side, the agreement will bring the rival Palestinian factions Hamas and Fatah to each other.
This is already the case for their younger generation, and the Arab-Israeli agreement has brought anger and a strong sense of betrayal to the senior ranks of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO).
And throughout the Arab world, the Arab Spring for democracy will converge with the demands for Palestinian sovereignty.
This agreement will provoke a new wave of uprisings, not only in Palestine, but also in the Arab world, and I am afraid it has already begun.

title: Global Warming + Yellowleaf Disease Study: Bananas may disappear by 2050
text:
▲ Experts say that by 2050, people may no longer eat bananas. (Graphic / Reporter Minjun Tsai) The International Center / Synthesis report “Scince Daily ” website quoted an article published in the journal Nature Climate Change on Monday (2nd), by Dr. Dan Bebber, University of Exeter, UK. A leading study found that changes in temperature and rainfall due to global warming have a significant impact on crop growth. At the current rate of development, it is estimated that fragile bananas may disappear completely by 2050.
A study of bananas from 27 countries, which account for 87% of the world ’ s banana production, found that despite an improved operating environment, banana production has not increased since 1961 due to global warming.
And the temperature continues to rise, which may make the situation more and more serious.
By 2050, bananas may disappear completely.
It is understood that the current banana production in 10 countries is decreasing every year, and India and Brazil may face severe banana shortages in the future.
The most serious threat to bananas is yellow leaf disease (also known as Panama disease).
It is a plant disease caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense in the root of bananas.
By secreting toxins, Sickle Spore can cause programmed cell death in bananas, resulting in the destruction of entire banana plantations.
Because this fungus is resistant to pesticides (fungicides), there is still no cure for yellow leaf disease.
It is called "banana cancer".
But everyone is concerned about the killing power of yellow leaf disease, but ignores the impact of global warming on banana growth.

From the official website of the Agricultural Experiment Institute of the Council of Agriculture of the Executive Yuan share facebook In the past 20 years, Taiwan's agriculture has been affected by abnormal weather and diseases and pests, and the maximum amount of agricultural damage has risen from 12.7 billion yuan in 1998 to 38.3 billion yuan in 2016.???
Every day to bowl of fragrant white rice, or eat a sweet fruit, may have been your daily life.
But while enjoying good food, it may be hard to imagine that these ordinary foods around you are facing the threat of extreme weather every day.
Take the case of Typhoon Mita, which hit northern Taiwan in early October, for example, although it did not make landfall, it caused more than one million yuan in agricultural losses; as for Typhoon Bailu, which hit on August 24, this year, it caused enough agricultural damage of 170 million yuan.
The two cases are just the tip of the iceberg of natural disaster damage.
According to the annual report of the Council of Agriculture, the amount of agricultural losses in the past 20 years will be broken almost every few years, from 12.7 billion in 1998, 21.1 billion in 2005, 29.1 billion in 2009 and 38.3 billion in 2016.
It is worth noting that each wave of highs continues to break records, and 2016 has been three times as high as 1998.
Zhou Miaofang, deputy director of the Planning Office of the Council of Agriculture, said that the trend of increasing agricultural losses represents the result of worsening global climate change.
Because of the frequent impact of extreme weather on agriculture, farmers and agriculture-related units have made great efforts to combat natural disasters.
Chen Jizhong, chairman of the Council of Agriculture, said that in the future, 600 million yuan will be invested annually to cope with the impact of climate change.
In addition to the “hardware ” technologies known to the public, such as greenhouses and fencing, recently they have been transferred to biotechnology. Among them, the Agricultural Experiment Institute of the Council of Agriculture has developed a number of disaster prevention crops.
Photo Credit / VisionShare facebookRice Fever has hit Taiwan, and “Tainan 81 ” has become a lifesaver for rice farmers. For example, in April this year, the weather was suddenly cold and hot, and the humidity was high, and the weather changed dramatically, causing up to 42% of the rice in Yunjianan area to be infected with moderate or more rice fever.
The Agricultural Testing Institute has predicted that the climate that is turning its face faster than turning the books will inevitably cause agricultural disasters. Last year, the rice “Tainong No. 81 ”, which can withstand the“ sudden cold and heat ”, was indeed in use.
Many farmers who suffered from rice fever in April of this year changed to Tainan No. 81 in August, not only successfully preventing the epidemic, but also saving a lot of spraying costs.
In the farmers rushed to tell each other, Tainan 81 was widely planted, just one month, the total coverage area of Taiwan has more than 6000 hectares, at the same time, Tainan 81 is not only strong tolerance to climate change, more pest resistance, responsible for the research and development of Tainan No. 81 Chiayi Agricultural Test Institute researcher Wu Yongpei bluntly said, "Pesticide money, at least 20,000 yuan per hectare." ""
In addition to rice farmers, the disaster relief project of fruit farmers is also in full swing.
In the past, in Taiwan, sweet and juicy peaches, which belong to temperate fruits, are only suitable for growing at an altitude of about 1000 meters, and the temperature is lower in the hills.
To this end, the Taichung Agricultural Research Institute has developed a new type of peach called "Taitai Nong No. 7", which breaks through the temperature and time limits.
In the past, peaches were divided into early peaches and late peaches according to the harvest season. Early peaches were harvested in mid-July, and late peaches were harvested in mid-August.
In order to meet the high season of Mother ’ s Day, Taiwan has tried to improve, and early peaches can be harvested in early May.
And Taitung No. 7 is the world's "premature baby", Taiwan has become the only supplier of fresh peaches in April.
Today, in the Wufeng area of Taichung, in April you can see a fruity peach growing in the plains less than 100 meters above sea level.
According to Wen Ying-chieh, head of the original crop division of the Taichung Agricultural Laboratory, Taotai No. 7 is based on Taiwan's local "Yingge peach", and then mixed with Western honey peaches, and is one of the few peaches that can be harvested at low altitudes.
Although humans have tried to “win over the heavens ” and developed various new crops that“ resist adversity ”, under the conditions of increasingly severe extreme weather, the agricultural status quo of “man versus heaven ” is unlikely to change for a while.

title: The historic direct flight of the Israeli Arab League over Saudi airspace
text:
Representatives of Israel and the United States flew to the United Arab Emirates.
White House senior adviser John Kushner (from left), White House national security adviser John O'Brien, and Israeli national security adviser Ben Shabbat. (AFP) 2020-08-31 21: 13: 09 2020-08-31 - Israeli and US representatives flew to the United Arab Emirates on a special plane and were given permission to fly over Saudi Arabian airspace.
White House senior adviser Jared Kushner (center, Jared Kushner), White House national security adviser Robert O ’ Brien (right, Robert O ’ Brien), and Israeli national security adviser Meir Ben-Shabbat led the two delegations.
A man wearing a mask bearing the national flags of USA, Israel and United Arab Emirates, a senior Israeli and American delegation flew to the United Arab Emirates to finalise the agreement on normalization of relations between Israel and the UAE.
The flight was the first commercial flight between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, while Saudi Arabia agreed for the first time to allow an Israeli aircraft to pass through airspace.
Please continue reading...
Al Jazeera reported that Israel ’ s state-run El Al flight number LY971, with the word “peace ” painted in English, Hebrew and Arabic, took off from Tel Aviv at 11: 21 a.m. local time and landed in Abu Dhabi shortly after 4 p.m.
Israel ’ s request for a special flight over Saudi Arabia was approved yesterday.
According to the aircraft tracking website Flightradar24, the LY971 crossed the border between Jordan and Saudi Arabia about 25 minutes after taking off, entering the northwestern province of Al Jawf, Israel ’ s Haaretz reported.
This is the first known Israeli aircraft to enter Saudi airspace since Saudi Arabia does not recognize Israel.
Through the mediation of the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates announced on the 13th that they had reached the "Abraham Accord", and Israel agreed to suspend the annexation of the occupied West Bank in exchange for the normalization of relations between the United Arab Emirates and Israel.
The UAE is the first Arab country in more than 20 years to reach a settlement of bilateral tensions with Israel, with Iran, the two countries ’ main enemy, the main reason for the agreement.
But the Arab League ’ s move sparked Palestinian discontent, fearing that the pan-Arab statehood that pushed Israel to withdraw from the occupied territories and accept the establishment of a Palestinian state would be shaken.
Jared Kushner, White House senior adviser and son-in-law of US President Donald Trump; Robert O ’ Brien, White House national security adviser; and Meir Ben-Shabbat, Israel ’ s national security adviser, led the two delegations.
"This is a historic flight and we look forward to it opening up a more historic process for the Middle East and beyond," Kushner said before boarding the flight.
The delegation will explore opportunities for bilateral cooperation in areas such as business and tourism, and Israel will also send a special defense envoy to visit the UAE.
Israeli officials expect the two-day trip, which begins today, to set a date for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Prince Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan to sign an agreement in Washington, possibly as early as September.
The signing ceremony is expected to be a major foreign policy announcement on Trump's path to re-election.
The Trump administration has also tried to broker relations with Israel among other Arab countries that have concerns about Iran, most notably Saudi Arabia.
Riad, however, has hinted that he is not ready yet.
King Salman of Saudi Arabia and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman disagree on whether to normalize relations with Israel, Israel ’ s Yedioth Ahronoth reported, saying the king opposes the peace deal, but the crown prince “has shown a more open attitude, but has not approved it. ”
Mr O'Brien said yesterday it was likely that more Arab and Muslim countries would follow in Abu Dhabi's footsteps "very soon."
He did not name names, but Israeli officials have publicly mentioned Oman, Bahrain and Sudan.
Morocco may also be considering entering into a similar agreement with Israel in exchange for economic and military assistance.
Moroccan Prime Minister Saad Eddine el Othmani said last week that he refused to normalize relations with the Jewish National Movement entity.
UAE President Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al-Nahyan has officially lifted the economic boycott of Israel.
According to the United Arab Emirates News Agency (WAM), the caliphate issued an order allowing Israelis and Israeli businesses to do business in the UAE, which also allows the UAE to buy and trade Israeli goods.
The representatives of Israel and the United States flew to Abu Dhabi Airport in the United Arab Emirates on a special plane. The mask worn by the local man also printed the flags of the three countries of the United Arab Emirates, Israel and the United States.

title: 1.9 million Americans travel to Latin America every year for medical treatment ｜ News ｜ Americas ｜ on.cc
text:
According to the US medical travel guide, Patient Beyond Borders (PBB), an estimated 20 million medical travelers worldwide seek treatment internationally each year, of which about 1.9 million are Americans, with Latin American countries such as Mexico, Colombia, Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic among the most popular destinations.
Latin American countries offer lower healthcare costs, as well as high-quality healthcare infrastructure.
Veronica Merrill, a 50-year-old American woman who weighs 95 kilograms, decided to undergo stomach surgery to lose weight and found that she had two options: one is to pay $12,000 (about HK $100,000) for the operation in the United States, and the other is to operate in Mexico, which costs only US $4,000 (about HK $30,000).
After searching for medical travel options, Merrill saved up and contacted a specialist agency to arrange a cross-border trip to the Mexican border city of Tijuana for medical treatment.
Tijuana is a popular destination for weight-loss surgery and dental treatment. Other travelers seek treatment for cardiovascular problems, or for cancer, orthopedic and fertility care, as well as buying medications.
“It ’ s sad that I have to go to another country for this surgery, ” Merrill said.
Gerald Kominski, a professor at the Center for Medical Policy at the University of California, Los Angeles, points out that compared to all other high-income countries, the United States does very little to regulate prices, and medical tourism in high-income countries such as the United States is an indicator of affordability problems.

title: More than 400 people smuggled across the Channel to the UK, a new high in a single day ｜ News ｜ Asia Europe and Africa ｜ on.cc
text:
Since January this year, more than 7,400 refugees have been smuggled into the UK through the British Channel, the British Border Protection Agency said on Wednesday (2), the number of migrants across the British Channel intercepted on the same day, the highest number in a single day.
On the same day, Prime Minister Johnson addressed the issue of illegal immigration in Parliament, saying that he had compassion for refugees, but said that illegal immigration was against the law and harmed the interests of legal immigrants.
The Border Protection Agency has intercepted 27 stowaways in the English Channel, including unidentified children, and 53 stowaways who were unable to reach British waters have been rescued by the French government.
In August alone, 1,468 people were smuggled across the Channel to the UK, and the Home Office said on Wednesday that the government was trying to repatriate 1,000 people who had previously sought asylum in other European countries.
Johnson told the House of Commons that he sympathised with those who wanted children to cross the Channel to the UK, but that they were breaking the law, becoming victims of criminals and harming those who sought asylum in the UK through legal channels.

title: Save a lot, good quality Americans like to go overseas for medical tourism
text:
The Mexican border city of Tijuana has become famous for its medical tourism, showing Meriel taking a ride to the U.S.-Mexico border crossing after undergoing gastric surgery in Tijuana. (Getty Images) Share Facebook When Rael decided to have gastric reduction surgery to lose weight, she faced two choices: spend $12,000 to operate in the United States, or spend $4,000 to do the same in Mexico.
Agence France-Presse said her insurance covers the procedure only for people who are morbidly obese and have diabetes and high blood pressure, but 50-year-old Meryl is not eligible.
She wants to lose 210 pounds to 160 pounds to avoid these ailments.
After doing some research, Merrell contacted the Medical Tourism Corporation and went to the Mexican border town of Tijuana for surgery.
Tijuana has long been famous for its medical tourism, where people come to do weight loss surgery, dental visits, plastic surgery, treatment of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, pregnancy assistance, and drug purchases.
Each year, an estimated 20 million “medical tourists ” travel to other countries to seek medical care, including about 1.9 million Americans.
Mexico, Colombia, Costa Rica, and the Dominican Republic are America ’ s favorite places to visit for medical tourism, with low prices and good quality of medical care.
Founded 13 years ago, the medical tourism company helps Meryl arrange everything, including a flight from Phoenix to San Diego and a driver driving her across the U.S.-Mexico border to a luxury hotel.
The airfare, hotel and hospital surgeries all together cost a total of $3,800.
The company sends 60 to 70 people a month to various countries around the world for medical treatment, mostly to Mexico.
Merrill ’ s surgeons operate on at least two foreigners a day, the busiest tax refund season in the United States after April each year.
Obamacare, introduced in 2010, requires all adults to have health insurance provided by their employer or the government, but medical tourism in the United States has increased.
Some employers almost doubled their health insurance costs after the introduction of Oak Health Insurance and encouraged employees to travel abroad for treatment.
One company sent its employees abroad for plastic surgery and weight loss surgery, saving 20 million yuan over five years.
Experts say that even with universal health coverage, the United States may not be able to stop medical tourism, becoming like Canada and Europe, where non-emergency procedures such as gastric contractions may have to wait in line for years to get their turn, forcing people to seek medical treatment abroad.
In fact, Tijuana, who operated on Merrill, wanted Oasis Hospital to have many foreign patients from Canada.
Americans also enjoy visiting Europe for medical treatment, although European countries are not as active in promoting medical tourism as Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines.
America ’ s highly advanced medical system has also attracted wealthy Arabs and Asians to treat their diseases.
It's just that Meryl doesn't deserve it.

title: CNNC Group: “Artificial Sun ” Gravity Support Equipment Officially Launched
text:
China Nuclear Industry Group disclosed on Saturday (12) that the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) gravity support batch products developed by China has officially launched in Zunyi City, Guizhou on Friday (11).
According to the report, the equipment is one of the important structural safety components of ITER, which was jointly developed by the Southwest Institute of Physics of Nuclear Group Nuclear Industry and Guizhou Aerospace Xinli Technology Co., Ltd., and will be installed on the Dewar base ring after arriving at the scene, which not only carries the weight of tens of thousands of tons of magnetic system, but also bears the complex working conditions such as strong thermal stress, strong electromagnetism, instantaneous load.
It is understood that the controllable nuclear fusion device, commonly known as the "artificial sun", is regarded as an energy device to illuminate the future of mankind, and the ITER project is the world's largest fusion reactor experimental project, China officially signed in 2006, responsible for the production of ITER magnetic support task.
The gravity support products launched this time are the most complex and difficult components in the magnetic support procurement package, with many parts, complex assembly process and high dimensional accuracy requirements. Whether they can be delivered on time is related to the assembly progress of the entire ITER device and the stability of the later experimental device.

title: Bahrain, Israel develop diplomatic relations with Palestine isolated – Radio France Internationale
text:
JERUSALEM (AFP) Analysts pointed out that the Palestinian Authority has long established strong relations with Middle Eastern countries with different interests, but is gradually isolated in the changing regional alliance and needs to attract new allies.
US President Donald Trump announced in Washington earlier on the 11th that Israel and Bahrain had reached a "peace agreement."
The decision by Bahrain to establish diplomatic relations with its former enemy was a major blow to the Palestinians.
Palestinian anger came quickly, with a senior Palestinian authority official telling AFP that the deal was "a stab in the back of the Palestinian Authority and the Palestinian people."
The 22-member Arab League, which met at a summit this week, did not support Palestinian actions and did not voice its condemnation of the U.S.-brokered normalization agreement between Israel and the United Arab Emirates in August.
After the Israeli-Arab agreement was announced in August, Hanan Ashrawi, a senior official of the Palestine Liberation Organization, tweeted: “May you never be betrayed by ‘ friends ’. ”
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) will sign an agreement with Israel at the White House on Wednesday, making it the third Arab country to establish full relations with Israel after Egypt and Jordan decades ago.
In a Twitter statement about the Bahrain-Israel agreement, Trump said that the signing ceremony of the Israeli-Arab agreement will be attended by Bahraini officials.
© 2020 AFP

title: Bahrain develops diplomatic relations with Israel, Palestine isolated – Radio France Internationale
text:

US President Donald Trump announced in Washington earlier on the 11th that Israel and Bahrain had reached a "peace agreement."
Bahrain ’ s decision to enter into diplomatic relations with its Palestinian enemies was a major blow to the Palestinians.

After the Israeli-Arab agreement was announced in August, Hanan Ashrawi, a senior official at the Palestine Liberation Organisation, tweeted: “May you never be betrayed by ‘ friends ’. ”
The United Arab Emirates will sign an agreement with Israel at the White House on Wednesday, making it the third Arab country to establish full relations with Israel after Egypt and Jordan decades ago.
In a tweet about the Bahrain-Israel agreement, Trump said that Bahraini officials will be present at the signing ceremony.
