title: The Arab World Caught Palestinians Seeking Turkey's Help - 20200913 - International
text:
According to Palestinian analyst Ghassan Khatib, “There are various problems in the Arab world, including disputes, revolutions, civil wars, and tensions among Arab countries. ”
The Palestinians are now paying the price for the damage to Arab unity.
The 22-nation Arab League held a meeting of foreign ministers last week, but a Palestinian initiative to condemn the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates failed to pass.
The Palestinian self-government insists that the so-called "Arab consensus" is valid, that is, only if Israel meets certain conditions will Arab countries establish diplomatic relations with Israel, including the need for Israel to recognize the Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital.
“We hope that the Arab countries will remain committed to this consensus, ” said Jibril Rajoub, a senior Palestinian official.
With the Arab world cold, Palestine began to turn its hopes to other countries in the region, especially Iran and Turkey.
"We will not ignore any country, Turkey is the superpower of the region, it is also an Islamic country, and we are getting along well," Raju said.
However, Khatib urged the Palestinians to distance themselves from Turkey, Iran and Qatar, which are at odds with the other Gulf powers. “It is not wise for the Palestinians to get involved in regional tensions and competition between big powers. ”
If you go to Iran, you will lose Saudi Arabia, and if you go to Turkey, you will lose other countries.
It is best for Palestine to maintain a safe distance from these regional powers. ”

title: Bahrain normalizes relations with Israel, PLO launches military alliance ｜ News ｜ Eurasia ｜ on.cc Eastern Network
text:
Israel and Bahrain signed a normalization agreement mediated by the United States on Friday, stirring up discontent in some Persian Gulf countries.
Palestinians demonstrated in Gaza on Saturday to protest against the decision of Bahrain, burning images of leaders of the United States, Israel, Bahrain and other countries.
The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) blames Israel not for peace, but for a military alliance.
The demonstration in Gaza was initiated by Hamas, a Palestinian militant group, to fight the "normalization virus", to stop all routes and prevent its spread until it succeeds.
Demonstrators burned images of US President Donald Trump, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Bahrain ’ s King Hamad and Abu Dhabi ’ s Crown Prince Ne Hayan, the first Persian Gulf state to normalize relations with Israel last month.
PLO Secretary General Saeb Erekat criticized that normalizing relations between Bahrain and Israel would not bring peace without first resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which has nothing to do with state-to-state relations. “We are witnessing the establishment of a military alliance in the region. ”
Iran also condemned Bahrain for complicating the Israeli issue and threatening regional security, and the Revolutionary Guard warned Bahrain of severe retaliation from its people and the Palestinians.
Turkey accuses the normalization agreement of harming Palestine and further encouraging Israel ’ s illegal actions in an attempt to permanently occupy Palestinian territory.

title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
text:
Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.
A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.
U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.
The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.
Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.
They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.
The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.
In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.
The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.
But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.
Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.
The same goes for Bahrain.
Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.
Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.
The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.
They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.
In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.
There are business opportunities everywhere.
For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.
In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.
The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.
Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.
Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.
They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.
Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.
Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.
He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.
Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.
His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.
Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.
The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.

Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.
This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.
In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.
Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.
These are important parts of his constituency.
If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.
Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.
But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.
Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.
The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.
The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.
The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.
But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.
Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.
At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.
The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.
Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.
Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.
Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.
King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.
He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.
His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so.
Image copyright EPA Image caption An agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Israel sparked protests in Iran
Iran Has New Strategic Trouble The deal has been roundly condemned by Iran's leaders.
It ’ s not just about words, the Abrahamic Agreement puts them under even more pressure.
Trump ’ s sanctions have caused real economic pain in Iran.
Now they also have strategic problems.
Israel ’ s home air base is far from Iran, but the UAE ’ s air base is opposite the Gulf waters.
It is very important if we talk again about air strikes on Iranian nuclear bases.

Iran has found that their room for manoeuvre has been reduced.

title: The normalization of relations between Israel and Bahrain – Radio France Internationale

title: Protest the "normalization of relations" agreement! Palestinian protests roar with condemnation: disgrace and betrayal
text:

(Photo / Reuters) - The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Bahrain signed a normalization agreement with Israel on the 15th under the auspices of US President Donald Trump, reaching a milestone of peace in the Middle East.
But the Palestinians were so dissatisfied that hundreds of people demonstrated in Nablus in the West Bank and Hebron in the Gaza Strip to condemn it.
Demonstrators waved Palestinian flags and held up signs reading “Treason, ”“ Oppose Normalization with Occupiers, ” and “Shame Agreement, ” Al Jazeera reported.
Some burned pictures of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Bahrain ’ s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, UAE ’ s Prince Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan and Trump.
Protesters burned photos of the leaders of four countries.
Demonstrators Emad Essa said that many young people in Gaza lost their feet and limped for life simply because they demonstrated against Israel. “In the West Bank and Jerusalem, Israeli bulldozers continue to demolish Palestinian homes and carry out daily ethnic cleansing in Palestinian villages and cities, ” and these are just the tip of the iceberg.
Issa argued that the Arab League and Bahrain were “rewarding ” Israel for its crimes, and that“ these agreements are a point of shame on the leader ’ s forehead, selling the Palestinian cause at a very low price. ”
The Palestinians view the agreement between the Arab states and Israel as a betrayal. Ibrahim Ouda, another protester, said the Palestinians would unite against “all conspiracies that seek to undermine the rights of the Palestinians ” and that“ the only way to achieve peace in this region is to give us freedom and end the occupation. ”
Another protester, Osama Hasan, described the deal as a "stab in the back" of the Palestinians, but vowed to continue the fight to win freedom.
In addition, about 200 people poured into the demonstration in Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian government.
Small-scale demonstrations also took place in northern Bahrain, with dozens taking to the streets against Israel.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas also condemned the move.
(Reuters) - The Palestinians say the agreement is a betrayal of them.
Mahmoud Abbas, the president of the autonomous government, said that "peace, security and stability in the region will not be achieved unless Israel ends its occupation."
The United Command of the Palestinian People's Resistance called on the demonstrators to reject the agreement, saying that the 15th day should be seen as "a day of mourning for the black flags being raised in all squares, buildings and homes."
Hamas, the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement, said the deal would not bring peace and that "the people of this region will continue to regard occupation as their real enemy."
The Fatah Party, the Palestinian national liberation movement, also said that “what happened in Washington today is the collapse of the official Arab order. ”
Many Palestinians see the deal as a “betrayal, ” and activists have launched the hashtag“ Black Day ” in Arabic on social media.
Trump announced at the White House that Israel and the United Arab Emirates had reached a peace agreement.

title: Why do Arab countries collectively turn to feuds?
text:
Following the normalization of relations between the United Arab Emirates and Israel a month ago, Bahrain is yet another test in this round of Arab-Israeli détente. On September 15, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Israel formally signed a normalization agreement at the White House under the auspices of US President Donald Trump.
In addition to the UAE and Bahrain, according to Trump himself, “in the near future, five or six other Arab countries will sign similar reconciliation agreements with Israel, ” and specifically named Saudi Arabia as the next crab eater.
Many analysts believe that this reconciliation is signed in the United States, and Trump's campaign needs to be inseparable, Trump needs Middle East diplomatic achievements.
This is not unreasonable, but it is clear that the Arab countries are not just pandering to Trump.
Some analysts pointed out that the UAE Bahrain is only a superficial country, which cannot be separated from the support of regional powers such as Saudi Arabia and Egypt.
Instead of saying that the UAE and Bahrain are reconciling with Israel, it is better to say that the major Arab countries have relaxed their attitude towards reconciliation with Israel.
Analysis believes that this "Arab-Israeli joint" is mainly aimed at Turkey, which has become increasingly aggressive in the geopolitical competition in the Middle East under the rule of Erdogan.
Members of the Turkish Parliament wearing masks visit the mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal during a ceremony marking the centenary of the founding of the Parliament of the Turkish Republic in Ankara, Turkey, April 23, 2020.
However, behind the continued ritual reverence, it is the Erdoğan administration ’ s strategic turn away from the principles of Kemalist diplomacy. (AP) Ankara ’ s geo-strategic reach into the Middle East began in Erdoğan ’ s second term as prime minister, and was directly driven by the setback in Turkey ’ s European accession process, which led to the Erdoğan administration ’ s need to look beyond the EU process. The strategy is to maintain the basis of its own governance.
The Erdoğan administration ’ s geostrategic expansion in the Middle East is mainly composed of two pillars: one is the political united front and the other is the cultural united front.
With regard to the former, the Erdoğan authorities usually use two means to achieve their goals: first, to continue to support the Palestinians on the Palestinian-Israeli issue and to confront Israel head-on.
It is fair to say that this approach of the Erdogan authorities has indeed yielded many of the expected strategic results.
Mainstream public opinion in most Middle Eastern countries has cast Erdoğan as the patron saint of Islamic civilization, and has used it as a model to mock some of the Islamic powers that they expect to assume similar responsibilities, but are in reality “scared ”, such as the leadership of Saudi Arabia and Egypt.
On December 6, 2017, Turkish citizens staged a demonstration in the capital, Ankara, against the recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel by the United States. (Reuters) The second was to support political Islamic forces in other Middle Eastern countries, either explicitly or implicitly, and encourage them to continue to attack their country ’ s “decadent institutions ” – most typical of which was the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt (hereinafter referred to as the Muslim Brotherhood). si) was heartened by the election, and Turkish-Egyptian relations reached an unprecedented level of intimacy during the Muslim Brotherhood ’ s rule in Egypt.
Although Morsi was later toppled by the coup, the Brotherhood ’ s deep roots in Egyptian society and the organization ’ s special relationship with Ankara forced the successor Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to face significant pressure from the Brotherhood ’ s opposition.
May 8, 2014, in Cairo, Egypt, former Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi is tried in court.
According to reports, in addition to Morsi, 130 former Muslim Brotherhood members were tried on the same day, accused of planning to escape from prison in the 2011 revolution that toppled the Mubarak regime. (VCG) If the political united front is a sword directly aimed at the current system of Arab countries, then the cultural united front is a soft knife to dig the corner of the above system: most Arab countries due to the lack of mature local cultural industries. The degree of dependence on cultural products is extremely high.
By contrast, Turkey ’ s high level of cultural industry development, coupled with its own special historical ties to the Arab region, has allowed Turkey ’ s cultural products to flood into the Arab countries and quickly become one of the popular culture in the region.
It is also under the influence of these popular culture that the three views of the Arab grassroots and the younger generation have been subtly shifted in the direction of Ankara ’ s expectations – and this is undoubtedly a rather negative signal for the stability of the existing institutions in these countries.
For example, a few months ago, the Egyptian Ministry of Culture tried to ban the Turkish popular historical drama El Ertugrul from broadcasting in the country on the grounds that the show ’ s propaganda values were at odds with the country ’ s mainstream values – resulting in a backlash in public opinion, so much so that the official Twitter of the Egyptian Ministry of Culture was forced to temporarily shut down, and finally ended.
In summary, under the “two-card ” unified offensive of the Erdoğan authorities, the current system of most Arab countries is facing increasing pressure of“ color revolution ”: Politically, Turkey ’ s relatively open political system is envied by the opposition in these countries, often with Turkey as a reference, and exerting pressure on its own authorities to open up space for political participation; economically, Turkey is relatively sound. The developed industrial system has always been a benchmark in the Middle East and has an irresistible appeal to young generations in Arab countries; culturally, as mentioned earlier, the “cultural unification war ” represented by Turkish popular culture is increasing the internal alienation of Arab countries.

title: White House experts from three countries in the Middle East: the crux of the problem is not solved, the position of the Palestinian people is divided, and the peace is not yet in place.
text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah and Bahraini Foreign Minister Sheikh Zayed Al-Zayed signed the Abraham Accords statement on Monday on the South Lawn of the White House, which spells out the idea of a Washington-led agreement, including the signatories ’ recognition of the importance of maintaining and strengthening peace in the Middle East based on mutual understanding and coexistence, and encouraging interfaith and intercultural dialogue.
In addition, the text of the agreement refers to the establishment of embassies between the three parliaments and the opening of a series of economic and diplomatic contacts.
The "Abraham Agreement" is a separate term for the normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates. The US media said that Israel has also signed a normalization agreement with Bahrain, but the White House website published only the text of the agreement between Israel and the United Arab Emirates.
Detailed arrangements for the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and the two countries will be announced later.
The UAE and Bahrain are the third group of Arab countries to sign diplomatic relations agreements with Israel after Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994.
The last such ceremony in Washington was in 1994 when US President Bill Clinton witnessed the signing of a declaration by representatives of Israel and Jordan, paving the way for a peace agreement.
Speaking to Netanyahu at the White House Oval Office earlier, Trump said five or six other Arab countries were ready to normalize relations with Israel, arguing that Israel was no longer isolated.
He said relations between Saudi Arabia and Israel would be normalized "at the right time."
Palestine is seen as a big loser in the establishment of diplomatic relations between the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain and Israel. The text of the agreement barely mentions Palestine.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas said in a statement on Tuesday that “peace, security and stability in the region can only be achieved if Israel ends its occupation. ”
Netanyahu later said that Israel's plan to implement the West Bank portion of the Jordan River will not change, Trump only asked Israel to "suspend" the implementation of the plan.
As the signing ceremony took place, Palestinian militants fired two rockets at Israel from the Gaza Strip, injuring at least 13 people, and Israel retaliated by bombing Gaza.
Trump made it clear before the signing ceremony that the deal would put pressure on the Palestinians to return to the negotiating table.
Middle East experts believe that normalizing relations between countries in the Arab world and Israel, while ignoring Palestinian rights, has the goal of isolating and deterring Iran, or will exacerbate instability in the Middle East.
Liu Zhongmin, a professor at the Institute of Middle East Studies at Shanghai Overseas Studies University, said that the Palestinian issue is the core of the Middle East issue, and the normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain has weakened the common position of the Arab countries as a whole on the Palestinian issue, which is not conducive to the solution of the Palestinian issue.
In addition, the Arab countries are being pushed by the United States to join Israel in building a regional alliance against Iran, which will bring many factors of instability and exacerbate geopolitical tensions.
Jon Alterman, director of the Middle East Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), believes that these normalization agreements represent the collapse of Arab solidarity over the Palestinian question for decades.
This is the beginning of a new era in the Middle East, but this new era is not necessarily more peaceful and is likely to be more volatile in the short term.
(New York Times / Reuters / AFP / Xinhua)

title: A peaceful Middle East is taking shape - Perspectives
text:
The establishment of full diplomatic relations between Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Bahrain is a watershed moment in the Middle East situation.
Although the area is generally seen as a place of dysfunction in the family, the Abrahamic Agreement represents a conscious decision rather than an ordinary one.
This is a new starting point and a historic landmark event for the region, and it means that in addition to peace, there are other tangible results that can be felt immediately.
This agreement represents an alternative option and paradigm shift for the region to move forward.
It gave other Arab countries a revolutionary opportunity to establish formal relations with Israel, a concept that was previously considered too powerful and unattainable.
It offers an alternative to radical approaches that oppose peace and prefer to keep the war going rather than resolve the conflict peacefully.
Moreover, in the face of the extremism that Iran and its followers are spreading throughout the region, this agreement can effectively strengthen the forces of stable moderation.
It is our sincere hope that other countries will see the relationship established between peoples and economies under this agreement and realize the benefits that they can also enjoy.
This agreement is an important stage in ending the conflict in the Middle East, and we believe that such an agreement will effectively save countries from the scourge of extremism, and that peace is the only remedy.
Most importantly, this landmark agreement opens up a special opportunity for the Palestinians to negotiate directly with Israel.
Israel is ready to do so and will face the negotiations on the basis of the U.S. government ’ s “peace initiative. ”
The United States led the mediation effort to reach this agreement, and has been a true ally of all parties and a central player in the region.
The Abrahamic Agreement also represents a unity of values.
Israel, the United Arab Emirates, and Bahrain are all facing the challenges of climate change, reduced resources, and the new coronavirus.
We must focus on reaching consensus, not creating dissent, and do all we can to work together for the well-being of our people, which is what this agreement is all about.
The Abrahamic Agreement should be a guide to the benefits that all other countries in the region can bring to establishing peace with Israel.
A new Middle East is taking shape before our eyes.
Naturally, new doors have opened, creating prospects for foreign investment and economic cooperation.
Given these incredible developments, the Middle East seems to have no limits.
Therefore, it is time for Taiwan ’ s leaders to travel to the other side of the Asian continent and seize the opportunity.
(The author is the representative of Israel)

title: Iranian film master Asha Fahati praised China's envy of Chinese film deep cultural roots
text:
Iranian National News Agency (IRNA): In the past ten years, Iranian films have been widely recognized by the international community for their profound analysis of social significance, criticism of the times, and the revelation of various strange aspects of social reality, and have been regarded by the film industry as the benchmark of realistic films.
Among the seven special referees of the 7th Silk Road International Film Festival, Asha Farhatti, a social film master from Iran, recommended the 17 shortlisted films of the festival. On the morning of the 11th, the reporter interviewed Asha Farhatti, an Iranian social film master, through an international connection. Asha Farhatti praised the profound foundation of Chinese film and the huge market advantages of Chinese film.
Asha Farhatti is known as a film master because of his observation and reflection on the local society and daily life, allowing him to show the current situation of Iranian society in a real and profound way, transformed into a mature image language. In 2009, Asha Farhatti was awarded the Best Director Award at the Berlin International Film Festival. Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
He also became the first director in Iranian film history to win an Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film, and “Once Upon a Time ” won the Golden Bear for Best Picture at the 2011 Berlin International Film Festival.
Asha Farhatti last came to China more than a year ago, he said, "China's film industry is a very large market in the world, I did not watch all Chinese films, but I think Chinese films, especially commercial films, have its advantages, have their own deep roots, such a foundation is from an ancient civilization with a long history."
For me there are a lot of historical treasures that can be excavated in China, and every year there are definitely some very good historical value films in China.
It may be ten years and fifteen years before I can judge these films, and I will wait for the next few years to do so. "Asha Farhatti, who has not been to Xi'an, said eagerly," I hope to visit Xi'an one day. "
After the outbreak, I hope to visit Xi'an.
Because the Silk Road Film Festival held in Xi'an has allowed films from different countries and different cultural backgrounds to gather together, this is a good opportunity to watch movies, which I cherish very much.
At the same time, we communicate with judges from different countries, which is a bit like a film seminar.
We had a variety of dialogues and in-depth discussions, and exchanged ideas with people in the industry from other countries, which produced a great spark of ideas. "
Asha Farhatti also gave advice to young Chinese filmmakers, "to use the heart to shoot movies, not with the rational brain to shoot movies, if your film is taken from the heart, it is very moving, no matter which country the audience will buy, will like."

title: Yip Wenqi and Wong Lok Yin: Three Directions for Coping with the New Normal of Post-Epidemic Urban Planning - 20201016 - Perspectives
text:
Early prevention of Sick Building Syndrome First, COVID-19 will accelerate the pace of upgrading existing public health guidelines in town planning and early prevention of Sick Building Syndrome.
According to the World Health Organization, "sick building syndrome" refers to the long-term and short-term illness that occurs when people live or work in buildings for a long period of time.
As the coronavirus can be attached to the surface of a building or transmitted through a building ’ s pipes, people who “work from home ” may still be infected indoors or in public spaces of the building if the ventilation or disinfection system is not satisfactory.
In addition, the housing units in Hong Kong are generally small, and it is inevitable that friction will occur in sharing a room with family members for a long time. In particular, subdivided housing tenants, coupled with the impact of “epidemic fatigue ”, the physical and mental pressure of the public is doubled, and the“ sick building syndrome ” is more likely to occur.
Therefore, in terms of housing, it is imperative to increase the per capita living area.
The per capita living area in Hong Kong is only about 170 square feet, which is similar to 1.5 standard parking spaces and far lower than other nearby cities.
In Singapore, for example, although its land area is smaller than that of Hong Kong, its per capita living area is 270 square feet, while Tokyo ’ s per capita living area is 210 square feet, which is about 60% and about 25% higher than Hong Kong ’ s.
When people have more time to work from home, it is obviously more desirable to increase the size of the house.
As for recreation and culture, the Town Planning Programme should introduce more public and green spaces and implement the concept of “Green Therapy ” to protect the physical and mental health of Hong Kong people.
Research shows that 20 minutes of “green time ” every day can help improve our mood and make us more optimistic.
In fact, Hong Kong has a very high proportion of country park land (accounting for nearly 40% of the total land area). If we add other green land areas subject to different development restrictions, such as conservation areas, green belt, etc., it accounts for more than 60%.
However, Hong Kong has only a quarter of the developed land, so the population density of Hong Kong ’ s developed urban areas is among the highest in the world, reaching 27,400 people per square kilometer, about 2.5 times that of Singapore and London, and even higher than that of Mumbai, India.
On the other hand, Hong Kong has only 2.7 square meters of open space per capita, far lower than other nearby cities such as Shanghai (4 square meters), Tokyo (5.8 square meters) and Seoul (6.1 square meters).
The above differences are due to the fact that, in terms of town planning, Hong Kong now adopts a concept similar to “Garden in a City ”, and large areas of land outside the development area are designated as country parks and other conservation areas.
Increasing Land Supply Step by Step Towards “City in a Garden ” The author believes that Hong Kong should gradually move towards“ City in a Garden ” urban planning, by vigorously increasing the area of development, reducing population density, and striving to provide more public green space for all social strata, so that the whole city itself becomes a “big garden ”.
Of course, to practice the relevant design concept, you must pass the perfect planning.
Of course, the “city in the garden ” table is Singapore, whose developed urban areas account for nearly three-quarters of the total land area, but the urban areas have a large number of public green space, the most famous is Gardens by the Bay.
However, to practice better urban design, there is a necessary condition: increase the area of development.
When this condition is met, the windscreen effect can be alleviated by widening the street, adopting Ladder-style building, and adopting “Retreat along the Street ”.
Tokyo ’ s “Vertical Plantation ”, Detroit ’ s“ Urban Farming ” and New York ’ s “Open Street ” can all be applied to urban design in Hong Kong.
Second, the Coronavirus will accelerate the transformation of the business world to the “Total Workplace Ecosystem ”. With the development of communication technology, excellent network connectivity has promoted the mobility of some of the workforce, so that the workspace is no longer limited to the office or single space, and the future workspace will gradually be transformed from the traditional office to the office, flexible rental space and working from home. Combine.
Under the new normal, employees may only need to return to the office two to three days a week, and only focus on activities that require people-to-people interaction, such as cooperation, cultural exchanges, and business gatherings. As the transition to the new “three-in-one ” workspace format, the demand for traditional office space is likely to decrease, but the demand for residential space and more semi-formal office space will increase.
E-commerce and Reindustrialisation Third, the Coronavirus has increased the demand for e-commerce and reshaped today ’ s consumption model.
According to data released by JPMorgan Chase this year, the growth rate of e-commerce in Hong Kong was 10.2% in response to the epidemic driving more online spending.
According to Oberlo, e-commerce ’ s share of total retail sales surged from 10.4% in 2017 to 22% in 2023 (expected). Statista also pointed out that as of August 2020, 5.2 million of Hong Kong ’ s approximately 7.5 million people had used e-commerce related services in the past year.
With the advent of e-commerce, the demand for land for logistics warehouses, cross-border transportation and logistics control centers will continue to rise.
In addition, in response to the future trend of technology and digitalization, the development of 5G, mechanical programs and artificial intelligence will increase the demand for related data centers, intelligent R & D and other facilities in Hong Kong.
Early adoption of "Adaptive Planning" to enhance Hong Kong's long-term resilience This novel coronavirus outbreak has indeed brought about tremendous changes in land, housing and town planning.
Looking ahead, it is imperative to adopt adaptive planning as soon as possible to enhance Hong Kong ’ s competitiveness. Therefore, it is necessary to enhance Hong Kong ’ s resilience to prevent and respond to future challenges and to ensure recovery from adversity.
But at the end of the day, to adopt a new planning method to meet the emerging demand for land and housing, there is no adequate land reserve but it is absolutely impossible.
Therefore, to "make a cake" and have better urban planning, the prerequisite must be to "make a big cake" and drastically increase the land supply.
I would like to wish Hong Kong a breakthrough in land and housing development in the post-pandemic era, so that this internationally renowned “Pearl of the Orient ” will continue to shine.

title: Suicide rate rises in Japan amid economic and social problems
text:
Experts believe that the social and economic impact of the epidemic has caused many Japanese people to have mental health problems, which is also a factor in the increase in the suicide rate. (Reuters) 2020 / 10 / 19 09: 05 [Live News / Comprehensive Report] The Wuhan pneumonia (COVID-19) epidemic in various countries around the world has not subsided, and people's daily lives have also been greatly affected by the epidemic, the Japanese government pointed out that the number of suicides have increased since July this year. Many Japanese have mental health problems due to the social and economic impact of the epidemic, which experts believe is one of the factors contributing to the rise in suicide rates.
According to the German Voice, experts believe that the increase in suicide cases and the outbreak of the epidemic are directly related. After the outbreak, the daily life of the people is restricted, and interpersonal communication has sharply decreased. Although the number of suicides in Japan fell by 10% from January to June, the number of suicides in July has returned to the same period last year.
Please continue reading...
Japan ’ s unemployment rate soared from 2.4% in February to 3.0% in August, with 2.1 million people unemployed, and many small shops and small businesses declared bankrupt due to falling incomes.
The social and economic consequences of the pandemic have also led to mental health problems for many Japanese.
The report pointed out that Japan so far, there are about 1,600 cases of pneumonia in Wuhan, but as many as 13,000 suicide deaths, including a surge in female suicides, compared with the same period last year, the number of female suicides rose by 40% in August this year to 651 people, mostly young and middle-aged women aged 20 to 40.
Masaji Maeda, a health expert at Fukushima University, believes that most suicide cases are related to economic reasons, and the economic downturn caused by the epidemic has a much greater impact on women than on men.
Because most Japanese women ’ s jobs are short-term or temporary, they also bear the brunt of layoffs.
In addition, the problem of juvenile suicide is also of concern, with 59 primary and secondary school students committing suicide in August this year, double the number in the same period last year.
The causes of suicide include bullying on campus and excessive academic pressure. Due to the impact of the epidemic, many schools in Japan were closed for a time, and the pressure to catch up after the resumption of school has also made some students overwhelmed.

title: Israel and four Arab countries sign peace agreement, Middle East reconciliation
text:

Saudi Arabia says it still supports Palestinian statehood.
Whether Israel will end its encroachment on the West Bank, as stipulated in the Abrahamic Agreement, whether the United States can persuade Saudi Arabia to establish diplomatic relations with Israel, and which Arab countries will sign peace agreements with Israel in the future, will have a strong impact on the future of the Middle East.

text:
Thursday, 5 November 2020, 10: 00 HKT / SGT Share: Sources Tanaka Precious Metals, Tanaka Holdings Co., Ltd.: “2020 Catalyst Industry Association Technology Award ” Awarded for Contribution to Hydrogen Oxidation Treatment and Hydrogen Infrastructure for“ Development of Hydrophobic Precious Metals ” Tokyo, 5 November 2020 - (APRNewswire) - Tanaka Holdings Co., Ltd. (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Executive President: Tanaka) Tanaka Precious Metals Industry Co., Ltd. (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; CEO: Koichiro Tanaka), which is engaged in the manufacturing of Tanaka Precious Metals Group, has been awarded the “Industrial Catalyst of the Year 2020 ” by the Catalyst Industry Association, a national association for research and development of quantum science and technology. Technology Award" was awarded in the "2020 Annual Catalyst Industry Association Award Ceremony" held online on October 14, while Hitoshi Kubo of Tanaka Precious Metals Industry and Bobo Iwai of Masuharu respectively delivered winning speeches.
Hydrophobic Precious Metals Catalyst Floating Hydrophobic Precious Metals Catalyst Product Examples Less Hydrophobic Precious Metals Catalyst "Hydrophobic Precious Metals Catalyst" The hydrophobic Precious Metals Catalyst is a room-temperature hydrogen oxidation technology jointly developed by Tanaka Precious Metals Industry and Quantitative Research Institute and applied in nuclear Fusion Research Facilities such as ITER.
As mentioned above, the noble metal catalyst is used in the oxidation of hydrogen, and is characterized by "hydrophobicity" which can also maintain the reaction of the catalyst at room temperature.
Since the previous catalyst will be covered by water contained in the treated gas and water vapor generated by the reaction, so that the catalyst reaction is stopped, it is necessary to prevent it from being covered by water vapor caused by heating.
In addition, the catalysts commonly used with plastic as the carrier are not heat-resistant, such as combustion due to the increase in the temperature of the catalyst caused by the reaction.
In this development, as a catalyst base carrier, the use of more heat-resistant and radiation-resistant inorganic matter than plastic, by giving its hydrophobic base (substances difficult to mix with water), evenly cover the surface of the carrier for hydrophobization, so it has both heat resistance and hydrophobicity.
Precious metal catalysts coated with platinum on the carrier were confirmed to maintain hydrophobicity for 24 hours at a temperature of 450 ° C in an internal evaluation by Tanaka Precious Metals Industry.
The catalyst is not limited to nuclear fusion facilities, and does not need a heater when oxidizing hydrogen and combustible gas.
Considering the characteristics of the effective use of its hydrophobicity, it is considered to be suitable for safety equipment to prevent explosive disasters, especially in the effective application of the infrastructure construction of hydrogen energy society.

title: Israel ’ s loss of Trump, Biden gives Palestinians hope
text:
On September 15, 2020, on the South Lawn of the White House, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stands with U.S. President Donald Trump after signing the Abraham Accord to normalize relations with a number of countries in the Middle East.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost his strategic ally to Trump, sent a timely congratulatory message to President-elect Joe Biden, whose election gave hope to the Palestinians after four years of disillusionment with Trump.
The recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel, the support of Israel ’ s colonization of the West Bank and the engulfing of the Golan Heights, led Israel to normalize historical relations with several Arab countries, and indeed, Trump has left a deep mark in Israel.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described Trump as “Israel ’ s best friend never met in the White House, ” and on Sunday thanked Trump for pushing the bilateral relationship to a new height.
However, Netanyahu turned the page on Trump and congratulated Biden in the tone of a friend: “Joe, we have known each other for 40 years, our relationship is very warm, I know you are a great friend of Israel … I hope to deepen the special relationship between the United States and Israel with you two. ”
If you say Joe.
Biden has long been familiar with Israel, but he is not known there.
According to a recent poll, 63 percent want Trump to be elected and only 17 percent want Biden to be elected.
Some Israeli elected representatives are concerned about the emergence of a new generation in the US Democratic Party that is less friendly or even hostile to Israel, and the easing of relations with Iran, Israel ’ s number one enemy, under Biden.
The relationship between the United States and Israel was gradually damaged when Obama was president, and the relationship fell to a low point when the "Iran nuclear treaty" was signed.
Trump quickly tore up the pact and reinstated sanctions on Iran.
Will Biden reactivate the Iran Nuclear Treaty, which the United States signed when he was vice president?
The Israeli side believes the possibility is very high.
In the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas expressed a strong desire to work with Biden to improve and strengthen bilateral relations and safeguard the dignity and fairness of the Palestinians.
Trump ’ s pro-Israel policies led to the severing of relations between the Palestinians and Washington. Under Trump, the United States closed the consulate in East Jerusalem, which Palestinians claim to belong to their territory, cut off aid to Palestinians, and stopped the allocation of special aid to United Nations agencies for Palestinians.
In addition, Trump ’ s support for Israel and the swallowing of parts of the West Bank of the Jordan River and the future Palestinian state on a reduced map have also been strongly opposed by the Palestinians.
Biden and Harris had explicitly opposed the plan and the expansion of Jewish immigration.
“There is nothing worse than the Trump era, and his end is a victory, ” said Abbas ’ s adviser.

title: The second Dragon will carry four astronauts to the ISS.
text:
SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will carry out its second manned mission, unlike the previous one with only two pilots, this time with four astronauts who will travel to the International Space Station (ISS) to perform a six-month residency in space.
The Falcon 9 and Dragon spacecraft are ready for launch on Saturday, November 14.
Space Flight Now reported that this space mission is called Crew-1, which is the first official personnel transportation, because the manned mission at the end of May this year is still testing.
Crew-1 astronauts include Commander Mike Hopkins, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Shannon Walker and Japanese astronaut Soichi Noguchi.
(Photo / NASA) Hopkins and his crew, who have completed the COVID-19 quarantine period and completed most of their training, will try on their new spacesuits in the coming days.
On Wednesday, the crew will conduct a harvest and platoon to get on board the spacecraft to adjust to the environment.
The Crew-1 mission, scheduled to depart from the famous launch pad 39A at 7: 49 p.m. EST on Saturday night, will mark the official launch of SpaceX ’ s Dragon spacecraft as the primary means of transportation to and from the station. Before that, the United States must purchase seats in the Soyuz space capsule from Russia.
Assuming the mission takes off on Saturday night, the four astronauts will arrive at the International Space Station about eight and a half hours later, at 4: 20 a.m.
The current concern is Tropical Storm Eta in the Caribbean, which may delay the launch preparations if it hits the space center, and NASA is currently monitoring the weather forecast.
(China Times News Network)

title: International Industry makes real progress in herbicide lawsuit against Bayer - Finance
text:
The court-appointed mediator noted Monday that Bayer has made “substantial progress ” in resolving legal proceedings against herbicide carcinogens.
Bayer has been accused by farmers of causing cancer by the Roundup herbicide product, which has been claimed by thousands of people.
Mediator Feinberg said in a San Francisco federal court hearing that although it has not been successful, "but we have definitely made real progress," Feinberg, who participated in the 9 / 11 terrorist attacks compensation and compensation for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, further said that now is the time to solve the problem.
U.S. District Judge Chhabria previously suspended the federal lawsuit, giving Bayer time to resolve the issue by November 2.
Bayer noted that 1,861 of the 3,787 plaintiffs in the lawsuit remain unsettled, and Judge Chhabria did not extend the deadline, meaning some cases may enter the trial stage.
Bayer says Roundup herbicide is safe, has settled 88,500 of 125,000 claims, and the company is “fully committed ” to settling the lawsuit.
Bayer also took on legal action after acquiring Monsanto in 2018 to become the world ’ s largest herbicide company.
In June, Bayer had expected to settle the herbicide lawsuit with $10.9 billion, mostly for existing litigation and $1.25 billion for future litigation.
Last week, Bayer increased the cost of future claims to $2 billion and reduced its agricultural science business by €9.25 billion.
(Times Information)

title: More than 2,000 suicides in Japan in October
text:
Newsfrom Japan On November 10, the Police Agency released statistics showing that the number of suicides in October was 2,153 (estimated), an increase of 39.9% (an increase of 614).
The number of suicides has increased year-on-year for four consecutive months, and the analysis of the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare believes that it is mainly affected by factors such as the spread of the COVID-19 epidemic.
The cumulative number of suicides from January to October was 17,219 (estimated), an increase of 160 over the same period last year.
While there was a year-over-year decrease in January-June, it turned to an increase again in July.
Among those who committed suicide in October, 1,302 were men and 851 were women.
According to the administrative region where the remains were found, the largest number was found in Tokyo, with a total of 255 bodies found.
More than 100 bodies were found, followed by 151 in Saitama Prefecture, 148 in Kanagawa Prefecture, 126 in Aichi Prefecture, 116 in Osaka Prefecture and 105 in Fukuoka Prefecture.

title: More than 60 small port landings on the east coast of England "unattended" - 20191025 - International
text:
According to official statistics from France, Belgium and the United Kingdom, the top 10 nationalities of illegal immigrants attempting to sneak into the United Kingdom from France and Belgium are Eritrea, Iraq, Afghanistan, Iran, Albania, Sudan, Vietnam, Pakistan, Syria and Ethiopia.
In recent months, refugees from the Philippines, Nigeria and Guinea have also attempted to cross the Channel by boat.
Many illegal immigrants who arrive in the UK never leave for life.
Some 40,000 failed asylum seekers have been asked to leave the UK, but the proportion of those who have to return has actually fallen by 42% in the past four years.
Speaking to the BBC, Shaun Sawyer, who is responsible for smuggling and slavery at the National Association of Police Chiefs (NPCC), said Britain was seen as a relatively easy target by criminal groups.
“You can ’ t turn Britain into a strategic fortress, ” he said, referring to some small ports that are easy to spot and relatively weak security. Detectable CO2 Containers Snake The frozen container where the 39 dead were found was at the Thames port of Beverley in Essex.
According to the UK ’ s National Crime Agency, this is one of the “less busy ” ports and one that stowaways use more often.
Other East Coast ports commonly used for smuggling are Tilbury and Hull, also in Essex.
According to a Border Survey report released in 2016, there are around 62 small ports and landings on the east coast of the UK that are “unmanaged ”.
Technically, CO2 detectors are available to check containers for stowaways, but the report says many eastern ports lack manpower and equipment.

title: Musk ’ s SpaceX seeks to normalize human spaceflight with NASA missions
text:
Elon Musk ’ s SpaceX launched four astronauts into orbit late Sunday, marking the company ’ s first official manned space mission and beginning regular commercial flights to the International Space Station.
SpaceX is the first company to receive approval from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to send astronauts into space on a regular basis, and this manned mission has elevated that status.
The move also provides important lessons for NASA ’ s strategy of using public-private partnerships to accelerate human space exploration.
At 7: 27 p.m. EDT on Sunday, the manned Dragon spacecraft, called Resilience, launched into space, beginning a roughly 27-hour journey aimed at docking with the International Space Station.
NASA last week officially determined that SpaceX ’ s Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft can safely transport astronauts to perform routine astronaut rotations on the International Space Station, as well as other operational flights.
A few months ago, two other NASA astronauts successfully completed the test flight of an earlier version of Dragon to the International Space Station.

title: SpaceX Dragon takes a big step toward democratizing space travel
text:
SpaceX footage shows four astronauts waiting for the rocket to separate after a successful liftoff of the Dragon spacecraft. (Getty Images) The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft successfully lifted off on the 15th to carry four astronauts to the International Space Station.
This is SpaceX ’ s first commercial manned mission for NASA.
The New York Times reported that the successful launch of the Dragon spacecraft is an important step in the popularization and normalization of space travel. In the future, NASA astronauts and anyone who can afford to pay will no longer have to rely on NASA or any government-built spacecraft to go to space, but can travel on commercial rockets.
McAllister, NASA ’ s director of commercial space flight development, said it marked the end of the development phase of the commercial human flight program. “For the first time in history, private companies have the ability to safely and reliably send people into space. ”
At 7: 27 p.m. EST on the 15th, the Falcon 9 rocket launched from the Kennedy Space Center launch pad in Florida, carrying the Crew Dragon spacecraft with four astronauts into orbit.
The Dragon is a manned spacecraft of the SpaceX Dragon family, with a cargo version.
This is SpaceX ’ s second manned mission.
In May this year, American astronauts Beacon and Hurley flew to the International Space Station on the Dragon spacecraft and returned to Earth in August to successfully complete a manned flight test mission.
This is the first time since the US Space Shuttle retired in 2011 that the US has sent astronauts into space from the US mainland.
Based on this test mission, NASA completed the certification of the Dragon spacecraft last week, meaning that the SpaceX spacecraft can regularly transport astronauts to and from the International Space Station.
The four astronauts on the mission, American Hopkins, Grover, Walker and Japanese Tsunichi Noguchi, arrived at the launch pad at around 4 p.m. wearing a white space suit designed by SpaceX.
Hopkins was the commander of the mission.
The spacecraft is named “Resilience ”, a symbol of the world ’ s many challenges this year, including COVID-19.
U.S. President-elect John Brendan tweeted, praising the launch of the SpaceX spacecraft, describing it as “proof that we are achieving our goals through innovation, creativity, and determination. ”
Mr. and Mrs. Pence, chairman of the National Space Council and vice president of the United States, and Mr. and Mrs. Bradenstein, NASA administrator, came to the launch site to applaud the rocket. Pence said that this is "a new era of human space exploration missions in the United States." SpaceX founder Musk suspected of having mild new coronary lung inflammation, can only watch from a distance, can not visit the scene.
The spacecraft arrived in orbit nine minutes after launch, and was scheduled to dock with the International Space Station, which orbits about 400 kilometers above Earth, on the night of the 16th. The four astronauts will join two Russians and one American on the station for six months.

title: 【 Technology ． Future 】 International Space Station Decommissioning Is Coming in the Era of Space Business ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ Weekly Report
text:
The International Space Station is tentatively scheduled to be operational until at least 2028, but it will one day be decommissioned. With its lifespan counted, and NASA ’ s desire to focus its limited resources on other space exploration projects, some commercial space stations operated by private companies may be replaced in the post-International Space Station era.
Phil McAlister, director of NASA ’ s Commercial Space Flight Program, said: “The International Space Station is a government monopoly on space destinations.
I think it ’ s time to leave the International Space Station and move on to the private sector.
Now it ’ s time for NASA to start looking at deep space exploration, and for businesses to follow suit. ” The United States has fractured its space development after the moon landing mission ended and the shuttle was decommissioned.
When it was only a matter of time before the International Space Station was decommissioned and China emerged as a space power, the United States wanted to replace the International Space Station with a commercial space station to maintain its space supremacy. (NASA) Axiom Space, founded by former International Space Station project manager Michael Suffredini, is developing the space station.
“The government realized very early on that it wouldn ’ t be able to afford to build the next space station for the next step in space exploration, ” he said.
That ’ s why we ’ re building a space station to replace the International Space Station when it ’ s decommissioned. ”
In fact, Freedom, the predecessor of the International Space Station, was already planning to use it as a springboard for the commercialization of low-Earth orbit.
In a 1982 memo, James Beggs, then NASA administrator, wrote that he “firmly believed that the space station was the bold next step in space ” and that it was“ an important part of our long-term plan to strike a balance between commercial interests and scientific value. ”
Likewise, the business world has long imagined.
Two years before the Apollo 11 mission to the moon, the 13th American Astronomical Society (AAS) conference in 1967 had the theme of "outer space tourism" and invited Barron Hilton, son of the founder of the Hilton Hotel, to speak on the space hotel.
In recent years, NASA has been actively engaged as a customer, promoting private company participation and space commercialization.
SpaceX launched its first official commercial crew-1 mission last week, successfully carrying four NASA astronauts to the International Space Station on the Falcon 9 rocket and the Crew Dragon spacecraft. (NASA) Under the generous goal of commercializing low-Earth orbit transformation, NASA has gradually changed to play a customer role in recent years.
For example, in 2014, it awarded commercial contracts to SpaceX and Boeing for the development of the spacecraft Crew Dragon and Starliner under the Commercial Crew Program.
NASA has commissioned SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Dynetics to develop a lunar lander in the Artemis program to return to the moon. In September, it publicly solicited commercial companies to collect lunar rocks.
On the other hand, NASA is also developing business opportunities for the International Space Station, paving the way for future commercial space stations.
Robyn Gatens, acting director of the International Space Station, explained: “We ’ re going to be customers, but beyond NASA, we need other customers to have the ability to purchase services on those commercial platforms to support their operations.
With today ’ s space station, we are launching projects that will enable different companies to try out commercial activities on the space station and see if there is anything that can be done. ”
Last June at the NASDAQ Exchange in the United States, NASA announced the opening of the International Space Station to commercial activities, in addition to allowing passengers to stay, private enterprises can conduct more commercial activities on the International Space Station.
NASA announced last year that it would open up part of its International Space Station for commercial use, spurring a transition to space commercialization. Jeff DeWit, then NASA ’ s chief financial officer, explained: “NASA didn ’ t expect to make money on open travel, and our pricing was only a fraction of what it would cost to keep the station running. ”
That ’ s just part of our spending, and we can use that money to go further into space or to Mars. ”
Recently, there have been some commercial collaborations on the International Space Station.
Last year, DoubleTree by Hilton tested baked chocolate cookies on the International Space Station.
Cosmetics brand Estée Lauder announced in September that it would shoot promotional photos and videos of a product on the International Space Station for social media advertising and would auction at least 10 products for charity.
According to ABC, filming costs $17,500 per hour.
NASA also confirmed in May that it was in talks with Hollywood star Tom Cruise to shoot a film on the International Space Station.
Television production company Space Hero has scheduled a live-action show, with the winner heading to the International Space Station in 2023. Gatens explained that NASA hopes these commercial activities can “open up opportunities to companies that have never considered space activities. ”
Axiom signed a commercial contract with NASA in the beginning of the year to connect its space station to the International Space Station and expand it in phases, pending the decommissioning of the International Space Station. (Axiom) In preparation for the decommissioning of the International Space Station, NASA has begun to look for the possibility of a private company operating the station.
In January, it signed a $140 million contract with Axiom Space to allow commercial space station modules developed by Axiom to be connected to the International Space Station. Matt Ondler, Axiom ’ s technical director, expects the station module to be launched in 2024, providing additional space for astronauts to live and study.
The Axiom space station is similar in appearance to the International Space Station. Suffredini expects the station to be favored by different customers.
It can serve as a research and development base for government space agencies and commercial companies, like the International Space Station; it can also be a destination for the first wave of space travelers, so it has a well-known designer Philippe Starck, and the interior decoration is much more luxurious than the International Space Station.
Axiom ’ s plan is to use the International Space Station as a springboard to gradually launch and expand its space station. Suffredini revealed that Axiom has plans to add at least two additional modules, one for a laboratory and production facility, and the other for a panoramic observatory, similar to the Cupola currently on the International Space Station.
These modules will be connected to the International Space Station all the time, with the addition of an autonomous power module.
By the time the International Space Station is decommissioned in 2028, Axiom will be the first commercial space station to operate independently.
“Building a platform that connects to the International Space Station allows commercial or government users on the station a transition space, which is particularly important for the success of economic development in low-Earth orbit, ” explains Suffredini.
Axiom wants its space station design to be very different from the International Space Station, and expects to customize commercial space stations for different companies in the future.
In addition to Axiom, which has made early progress, other companies are also designing commercial space stations.
For example, Nanoracks is working on converting some of the rocket's upper nodes left in orbit into small space stations it calls "Outposts." Sierra Nevada has also developed an inflatable, three-story space shelter that claims to be used as an orbiting space station or lunar surface base.
Ondler expects the earliest commercial space market to come from private astronauts, including space tourists, or astronauts from countries that lack autonomous launch capabilities.
In the end, he expects to cover most of the cost of space station construction in areas such as space pharmaceuticals and the production of fiber optic cables: “Initially, private astronauts will be important, but in the future, the manufacturing industry will catch up. ”
In the post-International Space Station era, Suffredini predicts that in the future, low-Earth orbit will be full of space stations, many of which will dwarf the International Space Station.
He revealed that when Axiom builds the first space station, the next step will be to customize the station for companies that want to produce goods in orbit.
Suffredini hopes that within 50 years, Axiom will be able to build a large rotating space station with parks, schools, and shopping malls, so that the astronaut ’ s family can live in space.
The idea is very similar to that of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.
He said that one of the goals of Blue Origin, a space company, was to lay the foundation for a space economy that would allow millions of people to work and live outside of Earth.
His idea came from the late American physicist Gerard K. O'Neill's idea of the "O'Neill Colony" in the 1970s, where the space station is two columns rotating in opposite directions, creating gravity.
At a press conference last year, he claimed that each could accommodate 1 million people, with high-speed transportation, agricultural areas, and adjustable gravity and weather.
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos claimed at last year ’ s Blue Moon launch that building colonies in space would keep the planet habitable and promote human civilization. (Getty Images) Bezos doesn ’ t seem to be joking, according to Blue Origin ’ s “director of orbital home composition ” position announced in September this year.
The job advertisement states that its early space station was “very different from the ‘ exploratory ’ residence designed for use in deep space by a small number of professional flight teams ”:“ To develop Blue Origin ’ s vision of millions of people living and working in space, where humans need to live and work, that is, to create a space destination system where valuable economic activity can take place … reference to the International Space Station and beyond its low Earth orbit habitable space station is the first step. ”
Of course, to build these more futuristic and larger space stations, there will be greater engineering challenges, and to ship a large amount of building materials into space, it will have to significantly reduce the cost of liftoff.
Suffredini believes that these are the problems the world needs to solve if humanity wants civilization to expand into the solar system: “We want to move towards that goal and really settle in low Earth orbit. ”
The evolution from exploration to settlement is the next step humanity must take to live permanently outside the Earth.
That is our long-term goal. "
With all kinds of commercial activities in space that the rich can afford, some lawyers expect that the wealth gap controversy triggered by the United States sending people to the moon will resurface.
Civil rights leader Ralph Abernathy (front) demonstrated prior to the launch of Apollo 11 (Getty Images), but civil rights lawyer Robert Patilo revealed another problem. In July 1969, on the eve of the launch of Apollo 11, a group of black South Americans gathered at Cape Canaveral to protest against the country ’ s sending people into space while there were still many poor people.
Patillo expects a similar debate to return: “By the 1950s, we ’ ll have private space stations where you can take a vacation if you have enough income. ”
We may have a space station on the moon by the end of the century.
“The question is how does our society ensure that those who are capable of going into space contribute reasonably to the Earth, so that we have health care, clean water, education systems, and so on? ”
The above section is from the 240th issue of Hong Kong 01 (16 November 2020), “The International Space Station Decommissioning Is Coming in the Era of Space Commerce ”.

title: [Open Box] “Night Watch ” Hong Kong Short Film“ Golden Horse ” and “Iranian Taxi Laugh at Life ”
text:
[Ming Pao News] The Golden Horse Award, which was held at the awards ceremony on Saturday, was most impressed by the Taiwanese male star Mo Zi Yi, who was praised by "Dear Tenant", and the words of thanks were not humble, "To freedom, to equality, to human rights; To film, to create, to live".
Of course, Hong Kong film "Illusion" has won the best adaptation of the screenplay, Hong Kong film Lee Che-hsin spent several years shooting the Wukan incident "Trek", last year after the screening of the Hong Kong Asian Film Festival, has been said to be positive, pressure "Occupy Legislative Council" to win the best documentary, I believe.
Kwok Chun ’ s “Night Watch ” also won the best short film. He and Chow Kwun Wai are the directors of the Hong Kong Golden Image Awards Best Film“ Ten Years ” chapter “Fuckin ” and“ The Self-Immolator ” respectively. In the film about Hui On Wah ’ s documentary “Make a Good Film ”, he once said that in recent years, Hong Kong ’ s new directors have made good local theme films at low cost. Void.
On the eve of the Golden Horse Awards, taxi drivers met with different political opinions, there is a Taiwan website for a limited time to upload "Night Watch" to the audience to enjoy, about 20 minutes of the short film, at that time, it felt very neat to watch, after the award, the Hong Kong media put the short film on the Internet for subscribers to watch.
The story tells the night watch taxi driver took the girl to Mong Kok, saw her in the car to change into a black bloc, presumably guessed that she was ready to "go out of town" to participate in the demonstration.
The driver used the cynicism of the old uncle, reprimanded the protesters for obstructing people's access to food, and triggered a heated argument with the girl. Finally, the driver in the vicinity of the Prince, for fear of colliding with the safety of the demonstration, asked the girl to get out of the car, the fare was 200, and the girl was angry enough to put down the folded heart-shaped 500 yuan banknote, refusing to find redemption, and even more angry to buy freedom for the driver's children.
The driver looked at the other person's figure in the distance, looking back at the car to see the girl's left ID, so he put it together with the 500 yuan heart-shaped banknote.
Later, two middle-aged women, aged about 30 or 40, who claim to be politically neutral drivers, then fight with the two women, “Blue ”, who get out of the car and rage.
The driver made a video call with his daughter who was studying overseas, discussed the current situation, and exhorted her to study hard. Then she met the riot police and witnessed the situation.
The driver picked up young men and women, from their conversation, knew that a protester left a backpack, did not know whether the other party was arrested, the driver looked at the backpack, a little familiar, asked one or two.
The female passenger is a little older and decides to keep the backpack; the boyish and skinny boy, who is neither a friend nor the same window with her, only met during the protest, asked the woman if there was room for him to stay in the house? The girl refused to ask other friends, and finally the boy said no.
Before the girl got out of the car, the two exchanged online names and promised to see you again in the next "dream".
The driver asked the boy where in the end to go? The latter took him "to stay first", and finally decided to get out of the car in the park, and asked the driver if he could get a bottle of water before leaving.
The driver saw the boy ’ s figure getting smaller and smaller, buried in the night.
The next day, according to the documents left by the girl, the driver waited outside the school door to see the students in groups.
The film ends here.
The taxi driver theme film has never been short of "Night Watch" is just a short film. It is not a Korean film based on historical facts, nor is it like Jim Jarmusch's absurd comedy "Night on Earth" nearly 30 years ago, which filmed the tragic lives of five taxi drivers.
What comes to mind may be closer to Iranian dissident director Jafar Panahi ’ s “Taxi in Iran ”, which won the Golden Bear, the highest honor at the Berlin Film Festival, a few years ago.
Banahi was accused of anti-government propaganda, sentenced to house arrest, and banned from making movies until 2030, but the strong-willed always find a sky that can make him look up.
Banahi shot "Iranian Taxi Laugh at Life", and installed several lenses in the taxi cab, so it was made into a film.
He also appeared, incarnated as a taxi driver, listening to passengers from different walks of life tell different stories, and write about the social and political situation.
For example, the vendors who sell pirated movie discs have seen the many restrictions on film and thought in the country, so that this supposedly illegal industry can survive; Barnahy and his niece discuss the definition of "good" film, which turns out to be an absurd rule.
Among them, there are the woman who took her seriously injured husband to the hospital, who learned that the other party was not in danger of life, and insisted on retrieving the will, and the elderly woman who wanted to release the feng shui fish...
At the end of the film, the thief destroys the car window and tries to take the footage of the camera, but can not find the memory stick, full of irony.

title: New agreement between Britain and France strengthens the interception of stowaways in the British Channel ｜ News ｜ Asia Europe and Africa ｜ on.cc
text:
British Home Secretary Theresa May and French Home Secretary Charles D ’ Armanin signed a new agreement on the interception of stowaways on Saturday (28), agreeing to step up efforts to crack down on the smuggling of refugees from France through the British Channel.
The number of police officers patrolling French beaches will double, and new equipment such as drones and radar will be deployed to intercept refugees crossing to the UK, Ms Pang said.
She added that increased patrolling of beaches by French police, increased intelligence exchange between French and French law enforcement and security agencies had reduced the number of stowaways, and that about 5,000 refugees had been stopped from leaving France this year.
The British side has provided 150 million pounds (about 1.55 billion Hong Kong dollars) to France in the past 10 years to combat illegal immigration. Pang said that the two countries are now cracking down on the smuggling of refugees in small boats, which means they will change the way they hide containers across the British Channel.
Discussions between the two countries will continue next year, and the UK plans to introduce a new asylum policy.

title: France, France Sign Agreement to Stop Illegal Migrants from Crossing the English Channel – Radio France Internationale
text:
LONDON (AFP) Britain and France have signed a new deal to stop illegal migrants from venturing across the English Channel by stepping up patrols and deploying technology on French beaches.
In recent months, a growing number of migrants have attempted to cross the dangerous and busy transport route from southern France to the south of Britain, killing four people last year and seven so far this year.
Home Secretary Priti Patel said today that under the agreement, French patrols will double from December 1 and use drones and radar to detect any attempts across the sea.
Bartel said the two countries share a "common mission to make the crossing completely unworkable" and that the new agreement would be useful in fulfilling that mission.
The problem of migrants crossing the English Channel has always been the crux of tensions between Britain and France, and London has condemned the Paris authorities for not doing enough to stop the smuggling of migrants.
From January 1 to the end of August this year, some 6,200 people attempted to cross the Channel by using inflatable boats, paddle boards, canoes and even life jackets to stay on the water. © 2020 AFP

title: After 20 years, the number of consecutive dry days increased 1.5 times, and scholars warn that the drought crisis will continue to expand.
text:
Taiwan is facing the worst drought in 56 years, leading to large-scale water shortages and agricultural stoppages in some counties and cities. Scholars say that early disasters and stoppages have been scientifically proven not to be accidental, and the frequency of extreme weather is getting higher and higher.
According to the study, the spring rainfall in Taiwan may decrease by 13.2% in 20 years, and the number of consecutive dry days will be 1.5 times that of today. The drought crisis will continue to expand, and governments, enterprises and communities must significantly increase greenhouse gas reduction measures to cope.
The domestic water situation continues to be severe, the Council of Agriculture and the Ministry of Economic Affairs have announced that the irrigation in the Jiannan area will stop next year, Taozhu Miaotai, the fastest will also be announced in mid-December, academic experts today (30) held a press conference in the Legislative Yuan said that climate change is normal, extreme climate is threatening the world.
Hsu Wang-hsiung, deputy director of the Environmental Change Research Center at Academia Sinica, said that according to the "Taiwan's future drought problem and response" research plan carried out by the Research Center for Environmental Change at Academia Sinica, it is estimated that the trend of drought in Taiwan in 2040 to 2060 will reduce spring rainfall by 13.2% in 20 years, and the number of consecutive dry days will be 1.5 times the current. The decrease in traffic is most obvious in the spring.
In addition, under the influence of climate change, the agricultural water shortage rate in Shimen Irrigation District and Taoyuan Irrigation District may exceed 40%, and the overall water supply capacity in the northern region will decrease by 24%.
Liu Chung-en, an associate professor in the Department of Sociology at National Taiwan University, said that climate change may significantly change the face of Taiwan's agricultural industry. In 2019, lychee and longan production dropped by nearly 90% due to excessive air temperature.
Liu Zhongen mentioned that climate change often causes inequality of responsibility, and most of Taiwan ’ s carbon emissions come from the industrial sector, emphasizing that “no amount of personal effort can help without stronger industrial energy conservation. ” Hong Shen-han, a legislator of the Democratic Progressive Party, said that this summer, a record high of 39.7 degrees Celsius, and the natural science community is constantly presenting new climate scientific evidence to emphasize that change has no time to wait.
