title: Suicides in Japan in October exceed the total number of deaths from COVID-19
text:
In Japan alone, the number of people who died by suicide in October exceeded the number of deaths due to COVID-19 in Japan, with the most significant impact on women and students.
Experts have warned that the epidemic could lead to a mental health crisis, mass unemployment and social isolation, and anxiety is affecting people around the world.
Japan ’ s official figures show that the number of people who died by suicide in October this year exceeded the number of deaths due to COVID-19 in Japan, with the most significant impact on women and students.
According to data from Japan ’ s police agency, a total of 2,153 Japanese committed suicide in October this year, while 2,087 people have died from COVID-19 in Japan so far, according to data from the Ministry of Labor and Health.
Among them, the number of female suicides increased especially, by 83% over the same period, and by 22% compared with the same period for men.
The reason for this situation is that women are mostly employed in industries such as hotels, restaurants and retail, which have been most affected by the epidemic, and many have been laid off.
According to a survey of more than 10,000 people worldwide by CARE, 27% of women believe they face mental health challenges during the pandemic, compared with 10% of men.
In addition to worrying about income, women also need to continue to pay for household chores.
For women who still have jobs, parental pressure increases when their children can ’ t go to school because of the epidemic.
And during the epidemic, worrying about the physical and mental health of children also brings an additional burden to many women.
In addition, the epidemic also has a great impact on the student population. Affected by the epidemic, students are forced to leave school and social environment, at home to face the relationship with their parents and the pressure of not completing homework.
A recent online survey of more than 8,700 parents and children conducted by the Japan Center for Child Health and Development found that 75% of Japanese schoolchildren showed signs of stress due to the outbreak.

title: Federal Court Rejects Bayer ’ s $648 Million Pollution Settlement
text:
A U.S. federal court has rejected a $648 million settlement from German chemical company Bayer, which is facing class action lawsuits by cities and farmers over contamination of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) made by former Monsanto.
Los Angeles Judge Olguin said the agreement was too broad and would exempt Bayer from future claims and asked for a settlement of the plaintiffs' claims against Bayer.
Most of the 2,528 group filing members will receive very small payments, about $15,000 to $30,000.
Bayer noted that it will work with the plaintiffs in an effort to address the judge ’ s concerns and complete the amended preliminary settlement by the December 31 settlement deadline.
Plaintiffs include Los Angeles, San Diego, Baltimore, and Portland.
Bayer originally planned to pay $550 million to its members and $98 million to cover legal costs.
Bayer announced plans in June to settle all legal lawsuits against Monsanto for $12 billion; most of the charges relate to the carcinogenic component of Monsanto ’ s Roundup herbicide.

title: New technology turns Martian salt water into usable fuel and oxygen
text:
According to past research, there is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen and the rest is combined with salt and cannot be used as a supply for astronauts who will visit Mars in 2033.
However, Ars Technica recently reported that a team at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a new technology that uses electricity to break down salt water into oxygen and hydrogen, convert it into usable fuel and oxygen, and can operate in the minus 36 degrees Celsius Martian atmosphere.
The device also produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment in July.
Scientists earlier discovered that astronauts need to breathe oxygen and fuel to return to Earth, even if they are only living on Mars for a short time.
At present, the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Mars 2020 mission to Mars is equipped with high-temperature electrolysis instruments, which can only produce oxygen from carbon dioxide in the air, but not hydrogen.
Vijay Ramani, a professor at the University of Washington, said that the latest technology could break down salt water into oxygen and hydrogen, changing the Mars program and even “turning the oceans into usable sources of oxygen and fuel on Earth. ”
The University of Washington research team looks forward to working with NASA to develop the technology, which it hopes will be used in the development of deep sea resources on Earth.

title: Japanese women ’ s unemployment rate is 1.4 times higher than men ’ s
text:
According to the Japan Broadcasting Association (NHK), the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on employment, especially for female workers, is even greater, with 26% of women forced to fire, close down or have their jobs affected, 1.4 times that of men.
NHK collaborates with independent administrative law firm Labor Policy Research on the impact of COVID-19 on employment.
The survey was conducted on 68,000 Japanese workers between the ages of 20 and 64.
The survey results show that since April this year, people who have been forced to fire, stop work, leave work, etc., have been affected by their work, 18.7% of men and 26.3% of women; the proportion of women affected by their work is 1.4 times that of men.
Among those who answered that their jobs were affected, 4,000 of them conducted a detailed survey, saying that the monthly salary in October this year was more than 30% lower than before the epidemic expanded, with 15.6% of men and 21.9% of women.
There are also more women than men who earn less and have not recovered.
In addition, 24.1% of men and 38.5% of women were unemployed after April this year, and the proportion of women who were still unemployed was about 1.6 times that of men.
Labor policy research.
Zhou Yanfei, director of the research institute, pointed out that the impact of COVID-19 on women's employment is greater, mainly due to the fact that more women are employed informally, and more women are engaged in the catering and retail industries, which are more affected by the epidemic.

title: NASA ’ s Mars Oxygen Meter Paves the Way for a Manned Mission to Mars ｜ News ｜ Americas ｜ on.cc
text:
NASA plans to send astronauts to Mars by 2030, but it has not yet resolved how to deliver enough oxygen and fuel to support a mission to Mars.
For this purpose, NASA is developing an instrument called Moxie, which can collect carbon dioxide on Mars, extract the oxygen atoms, and assemble them to create oxygen, which is expected to pave the way for a manned mission to Mars.
Mars ’ atmosphere contains only 0.13% oxygen, much less than Earth ’ s 21%.
A team of scientists from the University of Washington, St. Louis, USA, published a study in the Journal of the American Academy of Sciences, proposing that the MOXIE system is used to produce oxygen on Mars, converting 96% of the carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere into oxygen, and the remaining carbon monoxide will be emitted by the instrument and converted into fuel.
Most of the water known to exist on Mars is ice, and the team hypothesized that it could electrolysis salt water in lakes beneath the surface of Mars, eventually using instruments to produce oxygen and methane fuel.
The MOXIE system, which is in the testing phase, has been installed on the Mars rover "Keen", which was launched in July this year and is expected to reach Mars in February next year.
NASA is developing a prototype of a 1,000-kilogram instrument that will study how it will operate on the Endeavour to understand how environmental factors such as dust storms, wind and radiation affect the MOXIE system for a manned mission to Mars in the next 10 to 15 years.

title: China Science and Technology 2020 ｜ How far is the ultimate energy for mankind?
text:
At the economic work conference of the CPC Central Committee at the end of 2020, the government deployed eight major tasks for the development of 2021.
This working meeting of top officials of the Communist Party of China not only listed "strengthening the national strategic scientific and technological strength" as the top priority for economic development next year, but also admitted to developing high technology through the advantages of the national system, "as soon as possible to solve a number of" neck jam "problems.
Looking back at 2020, China has a bright performance or national strategic deployment in the fields of lunar exploration, Mars exploration, satellite navigation, manned deep diving, quantum research, database technology replacement, international participation in nuclear fusion technology, and neutrino experiments and chip manufacturing.
What is the practical significance of scientific and technological research in these fields? What is China ’ s competitive advantage and realistic challenge?
Where is the next step?
The sun is the source of human energy, and the ultimate energy for human beings is still to be found inside the sun, which simulates the internal fusion reaction of the sun on the earth, that is, controlled nuclear fusion, and has also become the "artificial sun".
This is an incredible image of a solar “explosion ” released by NASA in 2018.
The Sun, the closest star to humans, is actually a supernuclear fusion reactor, with 600 million tons of hydrogen being converted into helium by fusion reactions every second. In the process, about 4.2 million tons of net energy is released into the universe, equivalent to 3.78 × 10 ^ 26 joules of energy.
The Earth obtained only 1.72 × 10 ^ 17 joules from it, equivalent to a net energy release of about 19 kilograms per second, creating a livable Earth ecosystem, which shows the power of nuclear fusion energy.
Compared with fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas, clean energy such as solar energy, and even cracking energy as nuclear energy, nuclear fusion energy has obvious advantages in energy density and environmental protection.
Take a power plant with 1 million kilowatts as an example, using coal, 2.5 million tons per year, requiring 250 trains of 100 sections to transport; using fuel, 110,000 barrels of oil per year, requiring 11 supertankers to transport; using a fission reactor, consuming 28 tons of uranium dioxide per year; using solar energy, requiring 5,000 acres of land and energy storage space; using a nuclear fusion reactor, requiring only 400 pounds of deuterium and 600 pounds. A ton of tritium, 1,300 pounds of lithium-6 can meet the need, and a small car can be transported.
At the same time, with coal, fuel oil as fuel, will produce tens of millions of tons of waste every year, human air pollution, greenhouse effect has long been intolerable; nuclear fission will produce 28 tons of highly radioactive waste, the current global nuclear waste treatment landfill as the main, the processing capacity has been saturated, these nuclear waste landfill tens of thousands of years after the human is still harmful; and nuclear fusion only produces 900 pounds of helium, zero environmental pollution.
More importantly, compared to coal, oil, natural gas and other fossil energy reserves are limited, solar energy, wind energy and other clean energy energy density is low, nuclear fusion energy has a very high energy density at the same time also has almost unlimited storage.
One liter of deuterium in seawater is equivalent to 300 liters of gasoline released by nuclear fusion, and there are more than 45 trillion tons of deuterium in seawater alone, releasing enough energy for humans to use for hundreds of millions of years.
Because of this, nuclear fusion energy is regarded as the "ultimate energy" of mankind. The so-called controlled nuclear fusion is actually simulating the nuclear fusion reaction inside the sun on Earth, so it is called the "artificial sun".
China's habitual confinement nuclear fusion experimental device "Shenguang" has so far developed to "Shenguang III", its ultimate goal is to achieve laser controlled nuclear fusion ignition.
(Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery, Chinese Academy of Sciences) The US national ignition device and China's Shenguang controlled nuclear fusion technology are two major difficulties, one is how to trigger nuclear fusion, hydrogen bomb is formed by atomic bomb explosion high temperature and high pressure triggered fusion reaction, obviously can not be applied to controlled nuclear fusion; the first is how to control nuclear fusion under human control. Provide energy instead of releasing the power of destruction like a hydrogen bomb.
In addition, no material on Earth can withstand the high temperature and pressure required for nuclear fusion.
After several decades of development, there are currently two main branches of technology in the world controlled nuclear fusion research, one is the route of inertial confinement fusion (ICF), one is the route of magnetic confinement fusion (MCF).
The core of the device is that, through inertial or magnetic constraints, nuclear fusion occurs inside the device, while the entire device operates at a tolerable temperature and even ultra-low temperature.
For China, whether it is inertial restraint or magnetic restraint, there are research institutions that continue to exert efforts and walk on two legs.
The so-called inertial confinement, that is, the use of laser shock waves to make the fuel ball, which usually contains deuterium and tritium, reach extremely high temperature and pressure, and then "ignite" the nuclear fusion reaction inside the fuel ball.
Based on the way that the laser directly triggers the fusion reaction, the results of inertial confinement research can be used to produce pure fusion nuclear weapons, so most of the nuclear weapons research institutions in various countries are responsible for inertial confinement research, such as the United States Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), China Institute of Engineering Physics, and there is very little exchange and cooperation between countries.
The National Ignition Facility (NIF), built by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States, is the world ’ s highest energy inertial confinement fusion experimental device. The building that houses the NIF device is 215 meters long and 120 meters wide, equivalent to three football fields, and can focus 2 million joules of energy through 192 laser beams to one point.
At present, NIF has successfully achieved "energy gain", that is, the energy generated by the fusion reaction exceeds the energy absorbed by the fuel for the first time, and also proves the feasibility of using a powerful pulse laser to "ignite" artificial thermonuclear fusion.
The "Shenguang-III" device, built in 2015 by the China Institute of Engineering Physics and the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is the world's second largest laser driver after the NIF in the United States.
In addition, Russia, France and others are building similar high-energy laser devices.
US National Ignition Facility Detailed explanation (click to view high-definition big picture): + 6 + 6 At present, the ICF technology route is still a long way ahead, compared with the magnetic confinement fusion route, the road ahead is much brighter, which can be called the field of modern nuclear fusion research.
Magnetic confinement fusion is currently focused on the Tokamak technology route, the Tokamak device was first developed by Igor of the Kurchatov Institute in the Soviet Union.
Igor Tamm, Andrei Sakharov, Lev Artsimovich and others invented it in the 1950s. In 1968, at the Third International Conference on Plasma Physics and Controlled Nuclear Fusion Research, the research results were first presented – plasma up to 1KeV was confined for a few milliseconds to shock the world, opening up magnetic confinement. The New World of Nuclear Fusion Research.
The center of the Tokamak device is an annular vacuum chamber, wrapped around a wire, and the inside of the Tokamak will generate a huge helical magnetic field when powered on, heating the plasma to a very high temperature to achieve the purpose of nuclear fusion.
After decades of research, the current Tokamak device has developed to the stage of superconducting Tokamak, and different from the ICF technical route, there has been continuous international cooperation and exchanges since the 1950s.
In the 1980s, the United States, the Soviet Union, the European Union, and Japan launched the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) construction plan, which was later stopped due to budget and other problems.
In 2006, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union signed the ITER plan to build a superconducting Kamake-type fusion reactor in Cadarache, southern France, to explore the scientific and engineering feasibility of using fusion energy for peaceful purposes.
It is understood that ITER will become the world's first power station level fusion experimental reactor, which is an indispensable step to finally realize the commercialization of magnetic confinement fusion, which is also the largest international cooperation project that China has participated in as an equal partner for the first time.
According to the plan, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan and South Korea each shoulder about 9% of the budget for a total of 65%, and the European Union as the equipment organizer provides the remaining 45% of the budget.
For example, India is responsible for the manufacture of low temperature constant, the United States is responsible for the central spiral tube, South Korea and the European Union are responsible for the vacuum container, and the annular field coil in the magnet is provided by China, South Korea and Russia.
Construction and civil engineering are the responsibility of the European Union. China Nuclear Industry Group has also successfully won the contract for the installation of TAC-1, the Tokamak main unit, and successfully completed the installation of the cryostat base on May 28, 2020.
It is expected that ITER will complete the construction phase in 2021, start the reactor in the same year, start plasma experiments in 2025, and start full-deuterium-tritium fusion experiments in 2035.
At the same time as participating in the ITER project international cooperation, China's domestic magnetic confinement nuclear fusion research is also carried out simultaneously, and its main responsible units include the China Institute of Science Plasma Physics in Hefei, Anhui, and the China Nuclear Industry Group Southwest Physics Research Institute in Chengdu, Sichuan.
The Advanced Experimental Superconductivity Tokamak Experimental Device (EAST), built in 2005 by the Institute of Plasma Physics of China, is the world's first fully superconducting magnetic Tokamak nuclear fusion reaction experimental device. In 2006, it successfully achieved discharge, and in 2018, the heating power exceeded 10 megawatts, the storage energy of the plasma was increased to 300,000 joules, and the electronic temperature of the plasma center reached 100 million degrees for the first time.
On December 4, 2020, China Circulator No. 2 M (HL-2M), the largest and most advanced tokamak device in China, was completed and discharged for the first time at the Southwest Institute of Physics, marking that China has mastered the design, construction and operation technology of large-scale advanced tokamak devices.
On December 4, 2020, China Circulator No. 2 M was completed at the Southwest Institute of Physics of the Nuclear Industry in Chengdu.
(Xinhua) -- In fact, the China Institute of Science Plasma Physics and the China Nuclear Industry Group Southwest Institute of Physics, as one of the main units of China's controlled nuclear fusion research, are also the main force and component subcontractor of China's participation in the ITER project. Development of related disciplines and industries.
According to researchers in the field of nuclear fusion in China, for a long time, the United States, Japan and the European Union have maintained a clear advantage in international controlled nuclear fusion research.
The Future China Fusion Engineering Experimental Reactor (CFETR), similar to ITER, is planned to complete controlled fusion research in three steps.
The first stage to 2021, CFETR began construction; the second stage to 2035, plans to build the fusion engineering experimental reactor, began large-scale scientific experiments; the third stage to 2050, the fusion engineering experimental reactor successfully, the construction of the fusion commercial demonstration reactor, complete the ultimate energy for mankind.
At present, the international community generally expects to achieve controlled nuclear fusion by 2050.

title: The first step in colonizing Mars? NASA probe to land next year to challenge oxygen-making experiments
text:
NASA hopes that astronauts will land on Mars in 10 years, but if humans want to colonize another planet, how can we solve the problem of oxygen supply?
First, carrying oxygen and fuel far from Earth was not feasible in the past, and a way must be found to be self-sufficient on Mars.
Since 96% of the Martian atmosphere is carbon dioxide, NASA ’ s response is to use an experimental device, like trees on Earth, to convert carbon dioxide into oxygen.
NASA launched the probe "perseverance" at the end of July this year, and it is expected to land on Mars on February 18 next year.
In addition to continuing to survey the Martian terrain, Perseverance has a special mission to make oxygen on the red planet, using a device as small as a toaster called MOXIE.
In addition to MOXIE, Washington University in St. Louis recently proposed another method of oxygen production, which is to use a large amount of salt water stored in Mars' underground lakes to electrolysis to separate hydrogen and oxygen.
In this regard, MOXIE program host Michael Hecht pointed out that the electrolysis of water will one day play an important role in the production of fuel on Mars, but "the air is everywhere, and it is relatively easy to extract oxygen from it.
Musk, the tech mogul, also has a bold idea for solving the Martian atmosphere: detonating a nuclear weapon at the north and south poles of Mars.

title: Anti-epidemic masks are the best cover for Korean medical beauty demand
text:
South Korean 20-year-old university student Liu Hanna had a nose implant in mid-December last year for a simple reason: this may be her last chance to undergo plastic surgery, after all, everyone wearing a mask to prevent the disease may soon end due to vaccination.
According to Reuters, Ryu Han-na has been taking distance classes over the Internet all year last year under the influence of COVID-19.
She said that being able to convalesce at home after cosmetic surgery, and wearing a mask to cover the wound in public to avoid abnormal vision, was the decisive factor in her decision to use the knife at this time.
“I ’ ve always wanted to get my nose full … People won ’ t be wearing masks anymore after the vaccine starts in 2021, so I think now is the best time to move the knife. ”
Her plastic surgery cost 4.4 million won (about NT $120,000).
"There will be bruises and swelling after surgery, but everyone wears masks, which is somewhat helpful," she added.
This kind of thinking has led to a huge increase in the demand for such medical and aesthetic surgeries in South Korea, which saw an upward trend last year.
South Korea is the world ’ s medical capital even during the non-epidemic period.
According to an estimate by Gangnam Unni, South Korea ’ s largest online medical beauty platform, the total value of Korea ’ s medical beauty industry last year was about US $10.7 billion, an increase of 9.2% over the same period in 2019, and the total value this year is about US $11.8 billion.
Shin Sang-ho, a surgeon who runs an aesthetic clinic in the heart of Gangnam District, said many people spent government-subsidized economic emergency subsidies on hospitals and clinics, driving the hospital ’ s third and fourth quarter revenue last year.
“I feel like a bit of a retaliatory expenditure, ” said Shin.“ I feel like customers are using medical procedures to vent their emotions that have been suppressed by the coronavirus epidemic. ”
However, the third wave of the epidemic has caused new daily confirmed cases in South Korea to hit a new high. Some medical clinics said that many people have avoided going out of the door, and there are not a small number of people who have called to cancel the consultation.

title: The Meat Atlas: It's Time to Rethink What We Eat
text:
"Industrialized meat production not only creates unsafe working conditions, but also drives people out of their homes and leads to deforestation, biodiversity loss and pesticide abuse - one of the main drivers of the climate crisis."
This is the warning of Barbara Unmüssig, head of the Heinrich Böll Foundation, a think-tank that cares about the environment, at the launch of the “Meat Atlas 2021 ” in Berlin.
This special 50-page atlas, published in collaboration with the Böhl Foundation, German Friends of the Earth (BUND) and the international monthly Le Monde Diplomatique, provides an overview of global trends in meat production and its implications for human health and the ecology of the planet.
For example, it highlights how the abuse of antibiotics in intensive animal husbandry has led to a growing number of drug-resistant germs that threaten the effectiveness of human medical drugs.
Similarly, deforestation for animal feed poses a threat to human health.
Due to the loss of natural habitats, animals and humans are in closer contact and viruses are more likely to spread to each other, which may lead to new pandemic plagues.
According to a survey presented at the conference, when young people aged 15 to 29 were asked their views on meat, most of them refused to accept the current method of meat production.
The disappearance of rainforests Global population growth and economic development are driving the increased demand for meat. In 1960, there were only 3 billion people on the planet.
According to the report, meat consumption at that time was about 70 million metric tons, equivalent to the global average consumption of 23 kilograms per person per year.
By 2018, the population had grown to 7.6 billion, and meat consumption had increased sevenfold to around 350 million metric tons, or an average of 46 kilograms per person per year globally.
A key issue that accompanies this consumption is that meat production requires a lot of land.
As global demand for meat continues to grow, so does the pressure on available arable land.
As a result, in countries such as Brazil, large tracts of forest are disappearing in order to grow animal feed crops.
To feed the planet, stop deforestation and plan some land reforestation, experts are calling for a rethink of diet: eat less meat and eat more vegetables.
The land area required for the production of plant-based ingredients is much smaller.
In a report on the health of the planet published last year, top global scientists such as Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK), recommended that humans change their eating habits and limit their annual intake of meat and dairy products to 16 kilograms and 33 kilograms.
In addition to revealing the destructive power of the global meat processing industry, the authors of the Meat Atlas shed light on the relationship between meat consumption and the global chemical industry.
Large chemical companies are still selling dangerous and even banned pesticides, they wrote.
These include chemical giants such as Europe ’ s Bayer, BASF, Syngenta and the United States ’ Codiva.
According to Umsig, the abuse of pesticides threatens the lives of thousands of people.
Olaf Bandt, president of Friends of the Earth, said: “The German government must make every effort to ensure that German companies no longer export poisons that are banned by the European Union. ”
Umsig warned that the MERCOSUR agreement between the European Union and South American countries will increase the use of hazardous substances. "The removal of tariffs will lead to more pesticides being shipped to Latin America and more rainforests being transformed into soybean plantations and meat production sites."
Experts concluded that establishing a model of farming that does not harm the climate and the environment, and does not abuse animals, requires a profound change in agricultural policy and a rethinking of consumption and production concepts.
“So far, we haven ’ t seen the real beginning of the meat transition, ” says Umsig.
How environmental protection benefits human health Clean energy means cleaner air According to the WHO, outdoor air pollution causes about 4.2 million deaths each year from heart disease and pneumonia.
The transition to green energy is good for the health of people and the planet.
How environmental protection benefits human health Carbon dioxide reduces our food intake Reducing greenhouse gas emissions will not only slow down the warming of the planet, but also ensure the nutritional content of the foods we eat.
After absorbing excess carbon dioxide, plants will reduce the production of protein and nutrients such as zinc and iron.
Lack of these nutrients can affect the health of children in particular.
If carbon dioxide in the atmosphere continues to increase, it could lead to hundreds of millions of people being malnourished.
How environmental protection benefits human health Protecting species is protecting human plant and animal species is disappearing at an unprecedented rate.
These species and the ecosystems they live in are central to all life on Earth, including humans.
They provide food, energy, water, medicine and form the basis of our existence.
To protect the ecological system, we can guarantee the health of all life in the world.
How environmental protection benefits human health Environmentally sound transport promotes health More than half of the world's population lives in cities, and their numbers are increasing.
City dwellers today suffer from air pollution caused by road traffic and industry.
An environmentally friendly transportation network composed of buses, trams and bicycles can leave more space for pedestrians, improve air quality, reduce noise pollution and traffic accidents, and promote a more active lifestyle.
How environmental protection benefits human health Land conservation As shown in this diagram, deforestation for palm oil plantations in Borneo, the use of life space by industry and agriculture is the main cause of the damage to biodiversity.
The exploitation of land may contribute to the creation and spread of infectious diseases, and in addition, agriculture and industry pollute water and air.
More nature reserves and sustainable land-use practices could help.
How environmental protection benefits human health Dangerous weather Global warming increases the likelihood of super hurricanes, forest fires, floods and droughts.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the consequences of climate disasters are more severe, especially in developing countries, leading to more than 60,000 deaths each year.
Countermeasures, as well as keeping warming to no more than 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, will help to reduce the impact of climate disasters and reduce the number of deaths.
How environmental protection benefits human health The severe impact of extreme weather caused by environmental damage will put local residents under great pressure after the disaster, especially those who have lost their homes.
Climate and environmental damage affect people ’ s mental health on a global scale.
Therefore, protecting nature and curbing the climate crisis also means reducing people ’ s psychological stress.

title: Suicide rate increased by 16% during Japan ’ s second coronavirus outbreak
text:
Japan's Tokyo Metropolitan Health and Longevity Medical Center and other teams on Friday (January 15) published in the British scientific journal, the results of a survey of the spread of the coronavirus epidemic in Japan from February to October last year found that the suicide rate during the "first wave" of the epidemic in June decreased by 14% compared with the same period last year, but the "second wave" from July to October increased by 16%.
According to Kyodo News, the team analyzed the decrease during the first wave, saying that not only did government subsidies, labor and commuting time shorten the mental burden, but also the school suspension reduced the burden on children.
In March and April of last year, the suicide rate among adults decreased significantly.
The decrease was 27% for women and 21% for men.
On the other hand, during the second wave, the suicide rate for women increased by 37 per cent, five times that of men; for children under the age of 20, it rose by 49 per cent.
The team believes that one of the reasons is the increased time spent at home, which creates an excessive burden on mothers, noting that "appropriate measures should be taken according to the situation of the population such as gender and age."

title: Japanese suicide toll rises for first time in 10 years – Radio France Internationale
text:
TOKYO (AFP) - The Japanese government's progress in curbing the high suicide rate for years has been reversed by the epidemic.
The number of suicides in Japan last year was higher than the previous year, the first in 10 years.
Japan ’ s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said today that according to preliminary data, 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7% over the previous year.
In the same period, 3,460 people died from COVID-19.
This means that for the first time in more than a decade, the number of suicides has increased year on year, with particularly high rates among women and children.
Japan has long had the highest suicide rate among the Group of Seven, but South Korea is even higher in Asia.
The Japanese government has made continuous efforts in recent years to provide better help to people with mental health needs.
Compared to some other countries, Japan ’ s epidemic is relatively mild, so it does not have to adopt strict lockdown measures like other countries. Suicide rates fell in the first half of 2020, raising hopes that the impact of the epidemic may be limited.
But the number of suicides began to rise in July after the nationwide emergency was lifted in May.
According to experts, tracking data shows that suicides usually fall in the first phase of crises, such as conflict and natural disasters, before rising sharply.
Luko Ueda, an associate professor of political economy at Waseda University in Tokyo who studies suicide in Japan, said that the increase in the number of suicides in Japan is a big deal, and she believes it is a major turning point.
She told AFP that COVID-19 was definitely an important factor, warning: “We cannot deny the possibility that the numbers will rise again this year. ” © 2021 AFP

Under the impact of the third wave of the epidemic, the heat of the plastic surgery industry in South Korea has not decreased.

In recent years, the Japanese government has made continuous efforts to provide better help to people in need of mental health.
Compared to some other countries, Japan has a relatively mild epidemic, so it does not have to adopt strict lockdown measures like other countries. Suicide rates fell in the first half of 2020, raising hopes that the impact of the epidemic may be limited.
However, the number of suicides began to rise in July following the lifting of the emergency situation throughout Japan in May.
Experts say tracking data shows that suicides typically fall in the first phase of crises, such as conflict and natural disasters, before rising sharply.
Luko Ueda, an associate professor of political economy at Waseda University in Tokyo who studies suicide in Japan, said that the increase in the number of suicides in Japan is a big deal, and she believes it is a major turning point.
She told AFP that COVID-19 was definitely an important factor, warning: “We cannot deny the possibility that data will rise again this year. ” © 2021 AFP

title: Suicides in Japan increased in 2020 compared to previous year
text:
(Morning News) According to the rapid report data released by the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare on the 22nd, the number of suicides in Japan reached 20,919 in 2020, an increase of 750 over 2019.
Japanese media said that due to the impact of the coronavirus epidemic, Japan's economic situation has deteriorated and the family environment has changed, which may be the reason for the rise in the number of suicides in Japan.
Statistics show that among the suicide victims, 13,943 were men, down 135 from the previous year, while among women, 6,976 were suicides, up 885 from the previous year.
In addition, the number of suicides among schoolchildren in Japan has increased significantly.
Statistics from the Japan Police Agency show that as of the end of November 2020, a total of 440 primary and secondary school students in Japan committed suicide that year, a record high.

title: Japan's suicide rate falls in 10 years due to epidemic - 20210123 - International
text:
Experts: Japan, which has long ranked first among the seven major industrial countries in terms of gender gap suicide rate, reported 20,919 suicides last year, an increase of 3.7% (750) over the previous year. It is the first time since 2009 that the number of suicides has risen since the financial tsunami, of which more than 13,000 were men, 135 fewer than the previous year, and more than 6,900 were women, an increase of 885. Over the past five years, local consultation counters have frequently received complaints from women about "being unemployed due to the epidemic and being reprimanded by their families". The Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare pointed out that the epidemic has exacerbated women's worries about work, childcare, care and domestic violence.
Some experts believe that many women are employed on temporary employment contracts, especially in industries such as tourism and hotels that have been hit hard by the epidemic, and the problem reflects the gender gap in Japan.
A survey last month by the Japan Broadcasting Association (NHK) also showed that 26% of women said they had faced employment problems such as layoffs since April, compared with 19% of men. Another survey showed that 28% of women said they had spent more time doing housework during the epidemic, compared with 19% of men.
Experts: It is difficult to meet in the face of the epidemic to talk about the trend of suicide among schoolchildren. From January to November last year, 440 primary and secondary students committed suicide, the highest in the first 11 months.
A counselor at the Tokyo Suicide Prevention Center told AFP that the students were anxious about their future. “They didn ’ t know what to do, and in the past they could talk to friends to relieve the pressure, but now they can ’ t even go to karaoke. ”
A 30-year-old woman who was convalescing at home after being infected with the epidemic in Tokyo was found dead at her home this month, inferring from the situation at the scene that she committed suicide, NHK quoted a news report.
There was a note at the scene that said, "Because of my relationship to bring trouble to everyone", she was reported to have no symptoms, but said that she was worried about spreading the infection to people around her.
Michiko Ueda, an associate professor at Waseda University and an expert on suicide, said that many patients are not only worried about their personal health, but also worried about problems such as contagious family members and social dissent.
(NHK / Yomiuri News / AFP)

title: UAE approves opening of embassy in Tel Aviv, Israel
text:
Written by Changyang Last updated: 2021-01-25 00: 43 The UAE government tweeted on January 24, 2021 local time that the UAE Cabinet passed a resolution approving the establishment of an embassy in Tel Aviv, Israel.
The United Arab Emirates was the first Gulf Arab country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel, and the changes in relations between the two countries have been described as historical changes.
The UAE and Israel signed a peace agreement in August 2020 to normalize relations.
President Donald Trump announced the United States, Israel, and the United Arab Emirates Joint Declaration on August 13, announcing that Israel and the United Arab Emirates had signed a peace agreement, which is also known as the Abraham Accords.
The agreement made the UAE the first Gulf Arab country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel and the third Arab country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.
Before that, only Egypt and Jordan, which borders Israel, had diplomatic relations with Israel.
At that time, the three sides adopted a declaration that the two countries will soon set up embassies and exchange ambassadors.

title: The world ’ s first private space travel will set sail 2 The rich will each spend 1.58 billion to buy a ticket - Finance
text:
The dream of human space travel is about to take an important step, Houston startup Axiom Space announced that two billionaires will participate in the AX-1 mission scheduled to be carried out by January next year, and will stay on the International Space Station for eight days after leaving Earth, one of them will also serve as a pilot and the vehicle is SpaceX's Crew Dragon spacecraft.
This is the world ’ s first private space trip, and tickets aren ’ t cheap, costing $55 million each.
SpaceX, the sole startup of Elon Musk, co-founder and CEO of Tesla, has spent more time and energy at the company in the past six months than Tesla, which is already on orbit. Crew Dragon will be launched on a Falcon 9 rocket, which has successfully sent two astronauts to NASA. Space. The AX-1 mission was originally scheduled for October this year, but was delayed for technical reasons.
The two people who bought the tickets with huge sums of money were US real estate investor Larry Connor, Canadian businessman Mark Pathy, accompanied by Israeli former fighter pilot Eytan Stibbe, and former NASA American astronaut Michael López-Alegría. Commander, Connor will be the first private space flight pilot.
López Alegría, who had four space missions at NASA, said: “This is truly groundbreaking.
No space mission has ever had an entire crew of non-professional astronauts.
I think the success and safety of the AX-1 mission is very important, and we will open the way for a lot of things and developments after that, ” he said. He said that around the fall this year, he will start to take the other three people for about 15 weeks of training, including physical fitness and ship operation, and ensure that the three non-professional people can spend “safe and productive ” time.
Connor and Patsy have both visited the interior of the Crew Dragon and witnessed the initial launch.
Connor said he was not worried about the risk of a failed launch: “Crew Dragon is excellent in quality and professionalism, and NASA and SpaceX have excellent flight records.
We feel confident and comfortable, able to complete the task and come back safely. ”
However, this private space trip is not exactly a holiday, with each research mission except for the flight commander. Conner works with two clinics, Patsy, who comes from a wealthy family, and with Canadian Aerospace, Montreal Children ’ s Hospital, and Stibe represents Israel Aerospace and a foundation.
In addition to expensive air tickets, NASA will charge an additional US $35,000 (about 100.3 million Taiwan dollars) per person to compensate for the cost of food and data services.
Such spending makes private space travel unlikely to become an emerging industry in the short term.
López-Allegría said: “We expect fees to start falling and at some point we can make it available to the general public. ”
It will take a while, but getting there will always start somewhere.
Connor predicted that universal access could take 25 years or more, but it will happen: “Would it be rare for humans to go into space?
So someone has to explore and set standards. ” (China Times News Network)

title: How to design a "natural play space" in the city, so that outdoor play can become a free place for children?
text:
Christine Lee: Have you ever felt that the upbringing of children, the way of caring for the elderly and children, and the behavioral interactions between people have been profoundly affected by the overall social environment and urban space planning and design?
The initiative of the Alliance for Action on Homecoming Parks has repeatedly stressed that what we should discuss is not the success or failure of different parenting or care work, because urban planning and landscape design for the overall environment lack planning and design to support parents or care workers, and indirectly or directly limit the living needs of children and young people.
The basic life needs of children and young people, let me use a simple diagram (Figure 1) to express, the society's most voiceless users - that is, children and young people - in the end what they need most, in order to be accompanied by a good system in Taiwan's urban environment, and grow up well: A good companion system.
Children deprived of play due to the COVID-19 pandemic The period of home isolation should be the time when everyone feels the most: suburbs, small towns or rural areas, maybe next door is a farmland canal, or at least there is a backyard or balcony to breathe.
However, the urban core of densely populated housing, when isolated from home, can only move indoors in a few square meters, and may not even have a park within walking distance.
As COVID-19 continues to spread, Tokyo Play in Japan is the first advocacy group to issue a statement warning people that during COVID-19, isolation measures to avoid adult-thinking can harm children ’ s physical and mental development, such as: (1) avoiding long-term 3C abuse; (2) active activities to maintain children ’ s mental, physical and mental health; and (3) families that do not need to be isolated should look for fewer people. Play with the kids.
Further calls for children under one year old to play multiple forms of body games several times a day; and children over one year old, at least three hours of play and exercise of various intensities, and take children to the neighborhood, nature, streams and other outdoor environment, stay for a period of time, absorb fresh air, so that the physical and mental health of children and adults can be protected to the causal relationship between nature and health. There are 21 potential causal relationships between “nature ” and“ health. ”
Walking in nature, green space play, distance from the park, residential green space, park quality, etc., will increase the common soil of Mycobacterium, fentosine, negative ions, natural scenery and sound, environmental and ecological diversity, but also reduce air pollution, heat and violence, affecting DHEA steroid hormones, protein secreted by fat cells, maintain normal blood sugar, let people relax, Resilience, attention reorganization, improved immune function, healthy sleep and social connections, and a decline in various conditions such as: acute cystitis, attention deficit hyperactivity, irritability, cancer, cardiovascular disease, depression, diabetes, mumps, migraines, musculoskeletal diseases, respiratory diseases, dizziness, upper respiratory tract infections, allergies, asthma and atopic dermatitis (Figure 2).
Photo Credit: Ming Kuo Research Report Figure 2: 21 potential causal relationships between “nature ” and“ health. ”
A few years ago, Ming Kuo said in an interview with Science Daily: “Nature is more like a complex vitamin that provides all the nutrients humans need.
The core of these 21 causal relationships ultimately points to the “improvement of the human immune system ”, which means that walking in nature, playing in green spaces, proximity to parks, residential green spaces, and the quality of parks all have a profound impact on our physical and mental health, especially the more vulnerable children in the ecosystem.
No matter what happens in the world, COVID-19 or more natural or man-made diseases in the future, children need games and sports to promote their growth.
As adults, what can we do?
Understanding the plight of children who have lost nature and play Richard Love proposed the phenomenon of Nature-Deficit Disorder as early as 2005; the National Trust recommends that every child should play in the outdoor nature before the age of 11 and 3 ⁄ 4 (Figure 3) shows 50 activities. Physical and mental problems, including obesity, feeling sluggish, lack of concentration, excessive stress, mania, poor academic performance and low creativity, also want to naturally not respect, cherish and maintain the sustainability of the natural environment.
National Trust Figure 3: 50 activities that children should play outdoors in nature before they are 11 and 3 ⁄ 4 years old.
However, even in a country like Taiwan that can reach the sea or mountains within a few hours, how can families or institutions without resources bring their children to nature such as mountains, wild streams or the sea, so that children and young people who lack outdoor resources can engage in expensive outdoor activities?
In a community of urban spaces, without the support of innovative talent, project and maintenance budgets and professional landscape design within the government, how can we create a natural space that is like daily life, so that children can play games or make friends with neighbors on the way to and from school on foot or after work before dinner?
Calculate, how much does it cost to raise healthy children, take care of happy relatives, and enhance the immune system of everyone?
In order to prevent the next global pandemic, “nature ” must be brought back into urban spaces, and more natural elements should be put back into artificial spaces.
Such planning and design, of course, is to call "natural game space" and excellent "natural game space landscape design talent" appearance.
This is a global disaster, after Canada announced the closure of children ’ s playgrounds due to plastic surfaces left with the COVID-19 virus, and the cancellation of the Canada Blooms!, which is expected to be visited by 150,000 people due to the epidemic, an advocacy landscape consulting company called “Bienenenstock Natural Playground ” has once again moved to the table to call for serious attention.
Originally, the company planned to build a “giant nature playground ” in the outdoor venue of Huabo, installing more than 2,000 tons of natural materials, including 500 cubic meters of sand pit, and installing polished tree piles with improved safety to give children who love to climb more interesting challenges.
On the trial day before the opening ceremony, sand, bark, wood chips and soil covered the hands and feet of the test child, and the child's face was full of a bright smile.
Bunkers, red oak slides, chalk graffiti boards and hidden bases are all very popular.
However, the hydraulic engineering game makes the children do not want to play in other areas, and some small hands pull the lever, and some pull the handle to pour water from the tap into the wooden groove, and then into the sand pit or bucket (Figure 4).
The author provides Figure 4: Children's play space in Berlin Zoo, Germany, with sand, magic hide and play space with wood materials.
Unfortunately, the relationship with Flower Expo was canceled due to the epidemic, and these beautiful scenes that occurred during the trial could not be seen again.
Adam, head of the landscape consulting firm, said that the original idea of all of this design came from his childhood - he was a child in the 1960s, his mother kicked him out of the door in the morning until he came home to eat at night, spent all day playing in nature, countless hours in the forest, creek, looking for pollen, whistling with grass, digging and digging in the sand until the other side of the earth. Or climb trees all day.
In a natural environment, playing outdoor games (materials not including plastic, metal and rubber) is a "natural cure / nature therapy" for children, which is the same concept as the historical Shinrin-Yoku (Forest Bathing) in Japan, which advocates spending more time in nature in order to provide the body's protection against various diseases.
However, like forests, mountains, wild streams, and oceans, not all children can go to the large nature theme park every day to explore the experience.
The urban population is getting denser and denser, and children can only get close to nature in the adjacent public space.
The Belgian city of Antwerp, now vigorously promoted is in the school front yard, the school walkway and the pocket park in the city, make a small "Play Valley" (Figure 5), so that urban children can enjoy a piece of nature close to the city, with game elements, basic climbing tree trunks, running into the passage, crossing the net bridge over the pool, using imagination to create a place. Situations to play.
At the same time, these materials are also symbols that welcome children to “Free Play ”, with no standard gameplay and regulations (Figure 6).
Photo 5: Amsterdam, the Netherlands, has also created a “Play Valley ” that simulates nature on a walking trail or a pocket park.
Photo 6: A children's play garden in London, England, with a foundation of climbing irregular tree trunks and a net bridge through the sky.
The design of such a natural play space is closely related to the greening and sustainability of the city.
In Susan G. Soloman ’ s book, The Science of Play, emerging towns and new communities are more capable of implementing greening policy declarations and integrating physical elements of nature.
For example, cities close to the valley and mountains are easier to introduce walkers and bike-friendly facilities, and become a transitional zone for nature and urban bustling cities, so that more than 70% of residents do not have to drive.
This healthy and progressive lifestyle is reinforced by a natural play space, which becomes a “Node ” in the town community, interspersed between different buildings.
In addition, in streets with low traffic due to planning, children often play with dead wood placed on sand or gravel (Figure 7), and these places are usually located not far from the child ’ s home or parent caregiver.
Photo 7: The natural playground in Hamburg, Germany, where children often play in the sand pool and their homes are not far away.
When children play in a natural play space, it is as natural as daily life, because this design and the original landscape elements have long been linked together, but also echo the community's core values of low energy consumption, nature conservation, and scattered walking.
Close to the street, there are bunkers, trees, and large and shaped stones protruding from the walkway.
Some play spaces directly make full use of the natural landscape design, slightly deliberately put sand, stones and tree roots, children will play in the high grass or along the gully along the shallow stream, such a place can also be a place to play after rainwater recycling (see Figure 8).
Helle Nebelong, an inclusive design architect in Denmark, said: “When children play in nature, they are fully, wholeheartedly, and fully exploring and using the environment they encounter and are in, which is the best way for children to actively learn. ”
Figure 8: Make full use of the natural landscape design, slightly deliberately put in sand and stone and placed on the sand or gravel of the dead tree roots.
Looking at the case of the United States, the landscape design company Studio Ludo studied the game space in the United Kingdom and the United States, and from the analysis report found that the natural playground in London compared to the industrial / commercial / artificial playground in the United States, 55% more visitors; children who go to the former play compared to the latter play, 20% more vitality (that is, healthier, better physical fitness). The following five design points of "natural play space": providing children with electricity discharge is very satisfying, and the accompanying person can also have other activities at the same time: between the park and the play space, there is no obvious gap between each other, overlapping and fusion, or the game elements interspersed throughout the park; and the accompanying person can have coffee, activities, and even toilet can be conveniently planned.
Create an affordable, naturalistic play space: for example, large stones, trunks, plants that children can create their own play at a glance, and terrain changes that require little money but are immediately interesting.
Free from the game catalog: designers need to think about the five stars of the game — “grass, sand, crawl, roll, and slide. ”
If you add water and loose material elements, it will be a big plus, not just for the selection of game equipment.
Create a play space where everything can be "played" in the play space, including paving, planting, landscape furniture.
In other words, designers should prioritize “fun ” and“ play value ” before considering “safety ” and“ maintenance ” issues.
Try a design with “risk ”: designers need to think that taking“ risk ” is very beneficial for children.
The best playground is “looks dangerous ”, but in fact, the foundation of safety is to ensure — increasing the child ’ s alertness, responsiveness, and relative safety can be improved — and the design can provide a variety of different levels of play according to the child ’ s“ skill ”, “fitness ” and“ bravery ” (Figure 9).
Photo 9: The "dangerous-looking" Turquoise Bay natural playground at the Elizabeth Olympic Park in London, UK.
From a longer-term perspective, designers should also know that children need to establish a relationship and emotional connection with nature! If children do not experience the beauty of nature through play, they will not love nature; if children do not like nature, they will not want to help the ecological restoration of animals and plants associated with human coexistence.
To love nature and protect nature, children should use "play" to guide.
Just preaching (education), moral kidnapping (environmental plastic reduction) or putting "children and nature" together (think that let the park leave blank, the children themselves will play), for the modern city grew up, from childhood is restricted, has been brainwashed to think that the sand is dirty, water to save or climb trees will fall to death, never know how to play freely for children, nature is strange, harmful and deadly. Do you have “true love ”?
Five years ago, at the beginning of the autumn, the core idea of the Special Parks Movement was to remind government departments and landscape architects to open a window to listen to users in their professional fields, especially the simplest, but most difficult, needs of children.
Five years later, are children well heard, understood and cared for?
As adults, we recall that when we were young, the rich natural resources, endless use of them, everything can be played, all can not be played (Figure 10).
Now that natural resources have been exhausted, playing with sand and water and getting close to nature in the city have become taboo facilities.
Give back to children a good system for natural participation, for children and young children to participate in, for parents or care workers to participate in, so that the natural play space, has long lost the rich natural resources of children enjoy a little "can play" freedom, let them grow up with us healthy, laugh and live, it is really not too much!

title: "International Industry" Herbicide Law Dispute Bayer $2 Billion Settlement - Finance
text:
Bayer, the German chemical company, said on Wednesday that a legal dispute over cancer caused by its Roundup brand herbicide has reached a $2 billion settlement with regulators.
Bayer acquired Monsanto for $63 billion in 2018, taking over the company ’ s business and litigation.
Bayer says decades of research have shown that Roundup herbicides and glyphosate are safe for human use.
Wednesday ’ s settlement also includes claims for individuals exposed to Roundup herbicides and diagnosed with non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma in the future.
Under the agreement, Bayer will provide $2 billion for four years and for diagnostic assistance; each individual requesting a claim will receive up to $200,000.
The settlement is subject to approval by the San Francisco Court.
Under the amended agreement, any individual who has not filed a claim within a four-year period can appeal to the court for a better outcome.
Bayer has faced more than 100,000 lawsuits in the United States for its herbicide.
(Times Information)

title: Lost women and atypical workers: COVID-19 brings Japan ’ s labor and social welfare loopholes to the table again
text:
On the afternoon of December 1, 2020, the School of Public Policy, Hokkaido University, Japan (Graduate School of Public Policy), held an online forum “Labor, Welfare, and Social Voice in the Era of Coronavirus: Atypical Workers, Foreigners, and Sexual Minorities. ” We invite university teachers and non-profit organization workers to share the difficulties and current situation of labor conditions and social welfare in Japan under the impact of COVID-19.
First, Hyunjoo Naomi Chi, a teacher at the School of Public Policy at Hokkaido University in Japan, introduced the three speakers who participated in the forum, namely, Takadori Fujita, a lecturer at Hokkaido University and a director of HOTPLUS Nonprofit Organization, Haruki Imano, a representative of the POSSE Nonprofit Organization, and Makoto Iwashi of the POSSE Labor Support Center for Foreigners.
The three had come to Taiwan in 2019 to participate in the “Workers ’ Movement under Labor Flexibility: Exchange of Experience in East Asia ” international conference organized by the Taiwan Workers ’ Association to share the situation of atypical workers in Japan and to exchange views with labor groups in Taiwan, Korea and Hong Kong.
This article is mainly a record of the forum activities, and I also share my observations in Taiwan.
Fujita first explained that the epidemic has made Japan's existing social problems worse: labor problems, poverty, harassment, discrimination, and so on.
In response to this situation, Japan's trade unions, non-profit organizations, scholars, journalists spontaneously formed a network for advocacy and case assistance, on the one hand, the organization and regional information exchange, on the other hand, also want to contribute their own strength to help deal with case problems, and according to this to put forward specific policy recommendations.
They launched a free telephone consultation service to catch up on anxious emotions and refer resources to the public to help solve housing problems, emergency crisis problems, labor problems, and loan problems.
Since June 2020, this free telephone consultation service has received many calls for help from people, hoping to restore their lives as soon as possible.
They found that the problem facing the vast majority of Japanese people is the poverty caused by the labor problem: because of the loss of work and the loss of income, the original living situation is lack of savings, so they fell into a state of poverty, and then because of the epidemic, they can not find a job and fell into a vicious circle.
The outbreak of this epidemic has brought to the surface loopholes in labor and social welfare that people have not seen in the past.
The plight of female atypical workers From the statistics of the consultation phone, it will be found that there are many female consultants, mainly in the catering industry, retail industry, accommodation industry, tourism industry, these women participate in the atypical labor industry [1].
Compared to male atypical workers, mainly in the manufacturing industry, the problems faced by different genders under the epidemic are very different.
Fujita even boldly predicted that the reason why there has not been a large number of poverty problems in the first half of last year is mainly because there are unemployment benefits of employment insurance, after the unemployment benefits are completed, there may be a large number of women poor at the end of the year.
For example, a 20-year-old woman is a dispatcher who works in an automobile factory for 10 months, but at the end of June last year, the dispatching contract expired and failed to renew.
Her dispatching company unilaterally changed the original one-year contract to a short-term contract of three months, and since the Japanese epidemic worsened in June, she has not received a new dispatching job; A woman B, who is about 30 years old, is a dispatcher, working in a travel agency. Since March, there is no income, and the husband is in hospital, not sure whether he can apply for the government's "life protection", full of uneasiness about life.
This is a real situation in Japan.
According to government statistics, the average salary in Japan in 2018 was 4.41 million yen per year, but if you look at men and women separately, you will find that the average annual salary of men and women is 5.45 million yen, while the average annual salary of women is only 2.93 million yen (Japan ’ s Internal Revenue Service 2019 data).
In addition, in terms of savings, the proportion of Japanese households with more than two people without savings grew from 7.9% in 1995, 23.8% in 2005, and 22.3% in 2010 to 31.2% in 2017.
In addition, single-parent poverty is also getting worse, with the poverty rate for single-parent families reaching 48.1% in 2018.
In terms of elderly single people, 36.4% of men of single height live alone, while 56.2% of women of single height live alone. In 2012, the Japan Economic News Agency reported that one in three women aged 20-64 live alone, while the proportion of single women in relative poverty is as high as 32%.
These figures show that women in Japan, regardless of age, regardless of marriage, are in a relatively difficult position to survive, lack of social safety nets, lack of government assistance, when the family is dysfunctional, these women directly fall. In October 2020, the number of suicides in Japan was 2,158, including those who committed suicide due to the epidemic, and those who chose to leave because the epidemic felt unbearable. This represents an increase of 21.3%, and a significant increase of 82.6% for women compared to the same month a year earlier.
Because of the anxiety about the future, the number of patients with mental illness has continued to increase, from 2.041 million in 1999 to 3.924 million in 2014, making people's physical and psychological conditions suffer under difficult living conditions.
From the analysis of labor problems brought about by COVID-19, the president of POSSE began to talk about the original problems of atypical workers (dispatch, appointment, etc.), which have been exacerbated by the epidemic, and the social welfare system has not been able to form a social safety net to catch these people.
They also provided a telephone consultation service, receiving more than 2,800 consultation calls from February to July alone.
The most frequently asked questions about government regulations and practices related to temporary suspension of business, followed by dismissals and cancellations due to the epidemic.
More than half of the people who call for help are atypical workers in terms of employment type (64.5%). In terms of gender, age and occupation, they are 60.7% of women and 28.1% of men. The largest number is 30-49 years old, and the service industry (retail, catering).
In addition to the atypical workers mentioned by Takatori Fujita, there are also a high proportion of caregivers (corresponding to the "caregivers" of Taiwan's childcare centers) who call to inquire, mainly because of the epidemic, the Japanese government requires that care institutions, including childcare centers, be temporarily closed.
However, according to Japan ’ s Labor Standards Law [2], if a work stoppage is due to an employer ’ s problem, the employer is required to pay more than 60% of the average wage as a stoppage subsidy during the period of the work stoppage (called “stoppage handicraft ”).
However, these caregivers did not receive compensation or instructions from any company, so there was an influx of consultation calls.
In order to cope with the impact of the epidemic on enterprises, the Japanese government urgently relaxed the "Employment Adjustment Grant" (employment subsidy) to encourage enterprises to continue to hire and reduce unemployment.
Under normal circumstances, small and medium-sized enterprises applying for employment subsidies can receive 80% of the rest allowance; if the company does not fire employees during the emergency response period, the subsidy can be further increased to 90%.
Even so, many companies still do not apply for employment adjustment and directly fire workers.
The Japanese government ’ s emergency policy does not effectively stabilize existing employment relationships.
In addition, Japan ’ s Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare (equivalent to Taiwan ’ s Ministry of Labor) has constantly promoted the 60% stoppage subsidy in the Labor Standards Law, but completely ignored the 100% salary income that can be claimed in civil law, and publicly stated that “the outbreak of the epidemic cannot be attributed to enterprises ” (suddenly reminded of the Ministry of Labor ’ s statement when promoting“ disaster prevention leave ” in Taiwan). To interpret the epidemic, we warmly call on enterprises to continue to employ workers, and we do not see the imbalance of power in labor relations in reality.
For example, Japan's Salia did not apply for the employment adjustment assistance provided by the government, and set up a special leave system for the company. Compared with the government's vacation support, Salia only gave employees 2,000 yen a day (about NT $540), which is only half of the subsidy provided by the government, thereby reducing the company's expenses.
KONAMI group under the sports center, the main employees are hourly wage workers, when the government requested a general temporary closure, these employees also did not receive any subsidies at all. One of the employees is a single mother who supports three children, she had no choice but to take her own paid leave, but the paid leave was used up in two weeks, she had to spend a month's living expenses to use children. The school fees have to be paid, which causes her to fall into a state of left and right crunch.
Enterprises do not cooperate with epidemic prevention, to make money first, still for my employees, to get the rest of the support money difficult place is, workers must through the enterprise to apply for rest of the support money, although then the government also opened up by the workers themselves to apply, but enterprises are not necessarily willing to cooperate with the application of workers to help prove, the government's level of payment also has a big gap.
For workers, it is difficult to apply for support money enough to live. In addition to the traditional Japanese culture of "don't give people trouble" and "help is weak" ideas, so that fewer people apply.
Moreover, whether the enterprise is honest in applying for government subsidies according to its own needs, and there is no mechanism for monitoring and checking, which is likely to be abused.
In order to prevent the epidemic, the Japanese government proposed the policy of epidemic prevention, including: three closed spaces, dense crowds, close contact, remote work (TEYWANAKU), missed commuting hours to avoid intensive commuting contact (jet-lag commuting).
But at the same time, some companies take advantage of other peers are closing down, making atypical workers more dangerous work environment.
For example, Cafe Veloce, a large chain coffee shop brand, opened against the trend when most of the catering service industry was closed, and received a large number of guests with the same number of employees at ordinary times (because other colleagues are temporarily closed), and even workers in franchisees complained that "the company considers the interests more important than people."
However, there are still companies that completely ignore the epidemic prevention measures and ask their employees to continue working.
For example, Evolva, a service outsourcing center owned by well-known group KDDI, more than 100 wire attendants were forced to work in high-rise offices with no windows and ventilation. The wire attendants ’ seats are only 1 meter away, and there is no partition between the seats, and they are not required to wear masks and alcohol disinfection.
The use and loss of women and atypical workers is reminiscent of the Japanese director Shisui Fukuda ’ s film “Lost and Found Workers ” on the streets of Japan at the 2017 and 2018 Taipei Labor Film Festivals.
These women and atypical employment workers also work hard in the workplace, pay the same or even more time and energy, but only because they are women, because atypical workers, and can not obtain the promise of stable work compared to regular employees (contracts), can not insure social insurance, can not control their own life, can only rely on luck in different workplaces, barely survive.
Of course, regular employees in Japan are often high-pressure, high-working hours. It is precisely because of the fear that after leaving regular jobs, they will become more difficult and unstable atypical workers, so they can only strive for better life in the workplace, cautious fear, because such thoughts lead to overwork, suicide, depression and other conditions in Japan.
Japan's past labor system based on the principle of "lifetime employment" and "annual merit system", as long as you accept a certain company, it is like getting a ticket to become a life victory group, the company will take care of you for a lifetime, according to the age of promotion, as long as you do not make too big mistakes, the probability of being fired by the company is close to zero, and the labor will identify with the company, and give their life to the company. Be proud.
However, such a system from the late 1990s began to be greatly relaxed, so that the income of men in the family gradually unable to support family expenses, women also began to leave the family to enter the workplace, but the burden of care is still on women, enterprises in order to pressure low costs and began to use a large number of atypical workers, and these people are the first abandonment of enterprises when they encounter difficulties.
Although the impact of the epidemic is small, there are still vulnerable workers forgotten in Taiwan After the political lifting of martial law (1989), because of the efforts of the Women's New Knowledge Foundation and other women's groups and labor groups, women's labor rights have leapt forward in law: the Gender Equality Act regulates the mechanism for handling sexual harassment in the workplace, employers' responsibilities and handling obligations, protection of the right to work, and no discrimination based on age and other factors. Leave, maternity leave, childcare leave without pay... etc., after 12 years of advocacy, finally passed the third reading of the legislation in 2001, the next year (2002) on March 8 Mother's Day implementation.
However, Taiwan has not achieved a hundred years of rapid progress in gender equality because of the passage of legislation.
When we look back at the gender issues in the workplace in recent years, we can be proud to say that we have indeed moved forward a bit compared to 30 or 50 years ago.
In the past, there was no way to seek help for problems, and now there are provisions in the Gender Equality at Work Act that can be dealt with in accordance with the law.
But take a closer look at the actual situation of female workers and workers of multiple genders / sexual orientation in Taiwan, marriage and child discrimination, sexual harassment, and gender discrimination are still occurring.
Although Taiwan was less affected by the epidemic last year, in April last year, hotels and dance halls suddenly received a notice from the government that they had to close down, and there were almost no supporting measures, so that employees who lost their income due to the closure also fell into economic difficulties.
From this point of view, there are also places in Taiwan that seem to be similar to Japan.
However, because of this wave of hotel ballroom closures, the Taiwanese government has also prompted a group of young practitioners to come forward to form a union, and it is hoped that the young unions can use legal tools to improve the situation of the industry.
Note [1] This article refers to "atypical labor" including labor dispatch, labor contract, business outsourcing, part-time work, and teleportation.
[2] Article 26: User 's liability is due to the circumstances of the closure of the business, the user' s employment, the employee 's employment during the period of closure, and the company' s average salary of more than 60% of the company 's income.
