text:
Many times during the epidemic, however, the LCSD ’ s parks and recreational facilities were closed, and some employees were forced to eat at street corners, flower troughs and staircases to withstand the sun and rain, reflecting the lack of public leisure space for sitting and rest in Hong Kong.
Studies have found that the per capita recreational open space in Hong Kong is only 2.7 square meters, far lower than that of other major Asian cities.
Concerned groups believe that the government plans open space from a management perspective, making the park facilities less humane.
A 2017 report by the Civic Exchange Policy Institute found that the per capita recreational open space in Hong Kong is only 2.7 square meters, which is equivalent to the size of a latrine. Although it is higher than the 2 square meters per capita standard of the Planning Department ’ s Hong Kong Planning Standards and Guidelines, it is far lower than other major Asian cities, such as 5.8 square meters in Tokyo, 6.1 square meters in Seoul and 7.4 square meters in Singapore.
What is more, there are 20 subdistricts with sub-standard open space per capita, and Mong Kok and Wan Chai with only 0.6 and 0.7 square metres respectively.
Public Relations Manager for Expanding Public Spaces, Wong Ka-chi, said that open space plays an important role in improving the quality of life of individuals, rallying community power and balancing urban development.
She pointed out that the government generally plans open space from a management perspective, making the design and form of many "micro parks" rigid, focusing on hardware equipment.
She believes that when planning open space in the future, the Government should start from the perspective of users and consider what kind of facilities the community needs, so that the public can participate in the construction of the ideal community model from the bottom up.

title: Rising suicide rate under COVID-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?
text:
Rising suicide rate under Covid-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?
Rupert Wingfield-Hayes, BBC reporter in Tokyo.
Japan reports suicides faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.
Unlike most countries, the number of suicides is counted at the end of each month.
These figures reveal disturbing stories during the coronavirus pandemic.
In 2020, Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years.
Most surprisingly, while the number of male suicides declined slightly, the rate of female suicides surged by nearly 15%.
In the month of October 2020, the female suicide rate in Japan rose by more than 70% compared to the same period last year.
Why does the pandemic seem to hit women much harder than men?
Warning: The story may contain uncomfortable content.
Talking face-to-face with a young woman who has attempted suicide multiple times is a disturbing experience.
It gives me a new respect for those who work on suicide prevention.
I was sitting at a walking center in Yokohama ’ s Red Light District, run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project. Across the table was a 19-year-old woman with a wave head.
She sat motionless.
The image is annotated with text, Tachibana hopes that "Bond Project" can help women.
Quietly, without any emotion, she began to tell her story.
She said it all started when she was 15, when her brother violently abused her.
Eventually she ran away from home, but that didn ’ t end the pain and loneliness.
Ending life seems to be the only way out.
“Since about this time last year, I have been in and out of the hospital many times.
She told me, “I tried to kill myself many times, but it didn ’ t work out, so now I ’ ve given up trying to kill myself. ”
The "Bond Plan" intervened to stop her.
They found a safe place for her and began to give her intensive counseling.
Jun Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project.
She is a strong woman in her 40s with a relentless optimism.
“When girls are in real trouble and pain, they really don ’ t know what to do.
“We ’ re ready to listen to them and tell them, ‘ We ’ re with you, ’ ” she said. Tachibana said the coronavirus appears to be pushing those who are already vulnerable to the brink.
She described some distressing phone calls that employees have received in recent months.
“We hear a lot of people saying ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she said.
“They said, ‘ It ’ s too painful, I ’ m lonely, I want to disappear. ’ ”
For those who have suffered physical or sexual abuse, the COVID-19 pandemic has made things worse.
“A girl I talked to the other day said she was being sexually harassed by her father, ” Tachibana told me.“ Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, her father doesn ’ t work much, so she is often at home and she can ’ t escape him. ”
If you look at past crisis periods in Japan, such as the banking crisis in 2008, or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and real estate bubble in the early 1990s, it was mainly middle-aged men who were affected.
The rate of male suicide has risen sharply.
But COVID-19 is different. It affects young people, especially young women.
The reasons are complicated.
Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.
Its huge success over the past decade has reduced the suicide rate by about a third.
The image is annotated with text, and Professor Michiko Ueda believes that the suicide trend of Japanese women during the COVID-19 pandemic is "unusual".
Professor Michiko Ueda is a leading suicide expert in Japan.
She told me that it was shocking to witness the dramatic reversals of the past few months.
“This pattern of female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she told me.
“I have never seen so much increase in my research career in this field.
The sectors most impacted by COVID-19 are those with female employees, such as travel and retail and food. ”
The number of single women living alone in Japan has increased significantly.
Many people choose to be single, rather than a marriage that then requires traditional gender roles.
Professor Michiko Ueda said that young women are also significantly more likely to take up so-called precarious jobs.
“A lot of women don ’ t get married, ” she said.
“They have to feed themselves, and they don ’ t have regular jobs.
So when the crisis happens, of course, they will be hit very, very hard.
This has been the case in the last eight months with a very large number of unemployed non-permanent workers. ”
One month was really outstanding.
Last October, 879 women committed suicide.
This is more than 70% higher than the same period in 2019.
Newspaper headlines sounded the alarm.
The total number of men and women who committed suicide in October (2,199) was compared to the total number of COVID-19 deaths in Japan up to that time (2,087).
Something particularly strange happened.
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Yuko Takeuchi, a famous Japanese actress, was found dead in her home on September 27 last year at the age of 40.
It was later reported that she committed suicide.
Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist and now runs a non-profit organization (NPO) dedicated to solving Japan ’ s suicide problem, “From the day news of celebrity suicides is reported, the number of suicides will increase, and this will continue for about 10 days. ”
"From the data, we can see that the suicide of the actress on September 27 led to 207 more female suicides in the next 10 days," he said.
If you look at the suicide data of women the same age as Takuchi, the statistical results are even more obvious.
“Of all ages, women in their 40s are most affected, ” Mr. Shimizu said.
“For this group, it has more than doubled. ”
Other experts also believe there is a very strong link between celebrity suicides and an immediate rise in suicide rates in subsequent days.
This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it is so difficult to report suicides.
After celebrity suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.
Mai Suganuma is one of the NPO researchers.
She was also a victim of suicide.
When she was a teenager, her father committed suicide.
Now she offers help and support to other families of suicides.
Just as COVID-19 has made it impossible for relatives to grieve for those who have died of the virus, it has also made life harder for families of suicides.
“When I talk to my family, they have a very strong feeling that they can ’ t save their loved ones, which often leads them to blame themselves. ”
Massena told me.
I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.
Now they were told they had to stay at home.
I ’ m afraid the feeling of guilt is getting stronger.
Japanese people do not like to talk about death at the beginning of their daily conversation.
We don't talk about suicide. "
Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan is now in the midst of the third wave of COVID-19, with restaurants, hotels and bars closing.
Japan is now in the midst of the so-called third wave of COVID-19, and the government has ordered a second state of national emergency.
More restaurants, hotels and bars are closing, and more people are unemployed.

title: 3 countries Mars competition NASA "perseverance" first landing into the atmosphere "horror 7 minutes"
text:
NASA ’ s Mars 2020 mission, which began last July, sent the largest and most sophisticated Mars probe ever, Persistence, weighing about 1 ton, equipped with robotic arms, 19 cameras and two microphones to record Martian images and sounds.
It will land on the surface of Mars at 3: 55 p.m. EST today (4: 55 a.m. Hong Kong time Friday). If successful, it will be the fifth U.S. probe to land on Mars since 1997.
China ’ s Tianmu 1 is expected to land in May and June this year, while the UAE ’ s Hope will not land.
From entering the Martian atmosphere to landing, Fortitude will experience what NASA ’ s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) engineers describe as a “terrifying seven minutes ” because the process is extremely critical and dangerous.
First, the protective shell will pass through the Martian atmosphere at a speed of about 19,000 kilometers per hour. After entering the atmosphere for 75 seconds, the outer temperature of the protective shell will reach a maximum of 1300 ° C, then the parachute is opened to help slow down, the heat shield is separated, and finally the "perseverance" is lowered to the surface of Mars by a rope by an aerial boom.
Since Mars is about 190 million kilometers from Earth, it takes 11 minutes for the signal to be transmitted back to Earth, meaning that if there is any error in the landing process, NASA engineers will not know until 11 minutes later.
Perseverance will land in the northern hemisphere of Mars at Jezero Crater, a 45-kilometer-wide basin that scientists believe was home to lakes and river deltas 3.5 billion years ago, possibly with fossil evidence of ancient microbes.
In addition to searching for evidence of life, perseverance will also study the climate and geology of Mars, collect rock and soil samples and send them back to Earth in the 2030s. It will also do oxygen experiments. The Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) on the perseverance spacecraft is as large as a car battery and will try to convert Martian carbon dioxide into oxygen. Oxygen.
This will not only help NASA engineers learn how to make rocket fuel on Mars, but the converted oxygen can also be used for future human exploration of Mars.
In another high-profile test, the first unmanned helicopter to fly on Mars, the Ingenuity helicopter will be carried on the belly of the perseverance spacecraft, which will be separated from the spacecraft after landing, and will initially fly five times in a month, each time for about 90 seconds.
Because the density of Mars ’ atmosphere is only 1% of that of Earth, and the gravity is 1 / 3 of that of Earth, it is specially designed to weigh about 1.8 kg, has a longer propeller blade, 5 times the speed of ordinary helicopters per minute, and can fly in a thin atmosphere.
(AFP / CNN / Reuters)

title: City of the Future: Wanchai District 28 Public Spaces "Ride It" Sitting-out Area Most Popular
text:
Did you know that there is a playground on the roof of the Gooseneck Market in Wan Chai?
There are no signs and no lifts to reach the market. You must get lost on your first visit, and then return to the footbridge that runs through the north and south of the market. Finally, you can find a ladder to the roof! Good place, and there are people lying on the table tennis table in the venue to take a nap!
In the past six months, the Neighbourhood Relations Research Institute, an urban research organization, conducted a field survey on the use and satisfaction of 28 public spaces in Wan Chai. Among them, the playground at Gok Keng Market was the most surprising.
The survey also found that although there are many "riding" public spaces in Wan Chai, such as a humble resting place with only two chairs and an area of only 100 square meters, it has become one of the "most popular" leisure spots.
This survey has revealed the most diverse and most popular public spaces in Wan Chai. At the same time, it has revealed the worst public spaces and the least used public spaces. You will find that many facilities and convenient transportation are not popular, but sparse people flow is not a bad thing.
It turns out that what is a good public space, there is more than one answer.
Public Spaces Wan Chai The second smallest population in Hong Kong According to the 2016 Wan Chai Population By-census, Wan Chai has a total population of 180,000, and a population density of 17,000 people per square kilometer, ranking ninth in the 18 districts in Hong Kong.
However, Wan Chai has the second lowest per capita public space in Hong Kong. According to the 2017 survey report of the Civic Exchange Policy Institute, the per capita public space area in Hong Kong is 2.7 to 2.8 square meters, of which Mong Kok and Wan Chai are the least, and the per capita public space area is only 0.6 and 0.7 square meters.
In August last year, the Wan Chai District Council invited academic institutions to submit proposals for the "Wan Chai District Public Spaces and Parks Study". The purpose of the study was to assess the current state of public space in the district and explore the feasibility of improvement.
The successful application is the Neighbourhood Relations Institute, which was established in 2018 under the leadership of local architecture firm Architecture Commons.
From August last year to February this year, architect Eric Ho, together with 40 kaifong researchers and 40 public space research assistants, conducted a field survey of 28 public spaces in Wan Chai. The minimum area is 100 square meters of Queen's Road East / Shantou Street Sitting-out Area; the largest area is 9700 square meters of Wan Chai Park.
The study was conducted at four designated times per location (weekday morning, weekday afternoon, Saturday peak, Sunday evening), with a duration of 2 to 3 hours per session.
According to the Town Planning Board, as of March 2018, there were 68 open spaces in Wan Chai, including 16 district open spaces and 52 neighbourhood open spaces. Eric explained that the criteria for selecting 28 of the parks in the survey were mainly different types of public space, leaving aside the largest Victoria Park and Happy Valley Playground in the area.
In addition, the Wan Chai District Council constituency covers 11 small planning and statistics districts (TPUs), so it is hoped that each district will be represented.
In addition, we collected the views of people in the area and selected a few more special public spaces, such as Tai Hang Lung Path, where many people go to walk their dogs, although it is only a pedestrian road; and St James' Settlement suggested that they should definitely visit the rooftop children's playground in Ngau Kau Street Market.
Eric believes that the lack of public space in Wan Chai is a historical problem, because Wan Chai, one of the oldest communities in Hong Kong, did not have a sense of public space planning at that time.
According to a 2010 study on Wan Chai published by CUHK, Wan Chai was the first place to develop since Hong Kong became a British colony in 1842.
He laughs at the fact that government departments and some private enterprises have "done their part" to install public space wherever possible, but this has led to the emergence of a number of strange public spaces in Wan Chai, and the distribution of public space is extremely uneven.
According to the survey, the most common types of public space in Wan Chai District are small public spaces or "pocket parks", that is, sitting-out areas or gardens.
Among the 11 TPU in Wan Chai, the Pocket Park in the Queen ’ s Road East area with TPU # 131 is the most densely packed.
However, TPU # 133, the fourth most densely populated area in Wan Chai, between Percival Street, Jaffe Road and Lockhart Road, Fleming Road, is not a public space.
Discovery 2: Gloucester Gardens less is more?
During the survey period, a total of 25,600 people were recorded in 28 public spaces, but 74% of the users used public spaces for non-leisure activities (including walking, using public toilets, working); 26% were passive leisure activities (sitting, eating, reading, playing chess, etc.); and only 5% were active leisure activities, namely walking, dog walking or various sports.
The most popular public spaces are Lee Tung Street (ground and rooftop) and Gloucester Gardens, with an average of over 1300 and 1200 users per session.
The researchers observed that the large number of people passing by does not mean that people will stay. The reason may be that there is no potential for casual rest and use of space.
Results showed that the ratio of leisure and non-leisure activities in Lee Tung Street and Gloucester Road Gardens was about 1: 9.
However, Eric mentioned an interesting discovery that Gloucester Road Garden is a temporary stop for many people to wait to go to the Immigration Department for business on weekdays, but there are many children gathered on Sundays. There are no children play facilities there, which means that the family can give new use to the space. "One of the criteria for assessing the quality of the public space is plasticity, that is, in addition to the preset space use, few people do other activities.? Why are so many children in an open space with no play facilities? Or because there is no play facilities, so there is a space."
Finding 3: The most successful example in Wan Chai Park?
Wan Chai Park is the largest public space in the survey. It is surrounded by schools and hospitals, and has many public facilities.
Therefore, it is not surprising that Wan Chai Park is ranked third in terms of pedestrian flow, but the ratio of leisure and non-leisure activities is about 6: 4, reflecting that it is also a popular leisure park in the region. The average number of users during the four periods of the survey was 616, and the proportion of elderly and ethnic minority users was 46% and 35%.
According to the report, Wan Chai Park is the most diverse open space of all, in terms of ethnicity and age.
Eric said that the feeling of going to Wan Chai Park on Sunday is very interesting, unlike Lee Tung Street, where people come and go often, where it is static, people come in on Sunday morning, and then stay for the whole day, "I think Wan Chai Park is a good example of public space, although when it comes to Wan Chai Park, people immediately say," Oh, the facilities are good old. "
However, the park also allows different people to use the space together, and everyone respects each other.
I interviewed an uncle, and he said that it was okay, although there were many foreign domestic helpers on Sunday, there was enough space. ”
Survey Finds 4: Gooseneck Market Rooftop Foreign Domestic Helpers have peace of mind to say that the most favorite space for ethnic minorities in the area, must count Gooseneck Market Rooftop Children ’ s Playground, ethnic minorities account for nearly 90% of the users! Eric jokes that the first time and the researchers find the playground location is completely lost, and finally to ask for directions. The ratio is 9: 1! Unlike most of the rest of the space are static leisure activities such as sitting down and reading, 80% of the leisure activities here are social activities, that is, chatting and dining with friends.
"The first time to go is on a weekday morning, there are many people, the maid sister may buy food downstairs in the market, come up to chat, and Sunday is more exaggerated."
When Eric visited the domestic helper, he found that they saw this as a “living room ” where they could get together with friends. The original place was also a public space factor that attracted people to go to,“ making them feel private during their holidays, and it is also a rare space not to worry about disturbing others. ”
Survey Finds 5: Shantou Street Sitting-out Area The most popular office of the Neighbourhood Relations Research Institute is located on Queen ’ s Road East in Wan Chai, that is, the street where many pocket parks are gathered, and the most “riding ” is the Queen ’ s Road East / Shantou Street Sitting-out Area. The official data area is 200 square meters. The Chair.
There are reports that this resting place is strange and there is little flow of people, but this investigation has vindicated it.
In order to compare the density of people doing leisure activities at the site, they divided the number of people by the area, and found that the area was the most densely populated, with 0.9 average users per square meter. Although it may be thought that the area of the site was small to arrive at this result, the fact is that it really beat the other space 9 streets, and the second and third are the temporary resting place with an area of 200 square meters (0.6 average user / square meter) and 1500 square meters. Keng Market Rooftop Children ’ s Playground (0.4 average user / m2).
Eric added that the Shantou Street sitting-out area used to be less crowded, only a few elderly people sat waiting for the bus, but because there was a coffee shop nearby earlier, people came to enjoy coffee after buying it.
"Why are foreign squares comfortable and many people go?"
Because there are shops and shops nearby, it attracts people to sit.
According to the survey data, each square metre of Shantou Street Sitting-out Area is the most used public space, rather than passing by.
He stressed that calculating the average number of users is only one of the indicators for measuring the most popular parks in the region.
Survey Finding 6: Leighton Hill Park has the lowest score. So how do park users feel? The worst score of all public spaces is the Leighton Hill Public Recreation Park, next to Leighton Hill, which has a low score on natural light, vandalism and formal economic (commercial activities).
As for Tin Hau Temple Park, which has the highest rating, Causeway Bay, half of the 16 projects received positive reviews.
Space for improvement: additional facilities vs.
How do I get it in my spare room?
Eric said that the final proposal to be made to the district board is still being discussed.
Overall, he believes that diversity in public space is bound to be a good thing, but the definition of diversity needs to be defined. "For example, Wan Chai Park has different types of stakeholders to use, but Gooseneck is a certain type of stakeholders are used well, in fact, we think that both are good, as long as Wan Chai is regarded as the entire network of public space."
However, many people think that goose neck is only used by one type of stakeholders, and it will sacrifice other types of stakeholders (use rights). "
Does the public space need a lot of people to use?
“Since Wan Chai has the least public space per capita in Hong Kong, we certainly want to use it to the fullest.
However, many people interviewed said that the space is quiet, you can look at the trees are almost good, hope that there is no activation, and pets are available and facilities are added, there are two different sounds. "
Finally, the example of turning from Gloucester Road Garden Sunday into a playground for children shows that the balance of play facilities and space needs to be evaluated and crammed.
The report highlights that children use only a small percentage of all public spaces, accounting for only 3% of total leisure activity.
"There have been teachers who said that students leave school after school, how can they know what is a public space? And some teachers even said that because there is a board boy in the Morrison Hill Park, it is dangerous."
In this project, we want to reflect our views to the Government from the bottom up. People will know more about the public space in the community, so that children will know that they have room to express their views. "

title: The “suicide rate ” has risen for the first time in 11 years! Japan to appoint ‘ Minister of Solitude ’
text:
Japan ’ s suicide rate in 2020 is rising due to the epidemic. (Photo / Reuters) - Japan ’ s suicide rate remains high, and in 2020, affected by COVID-19, people are forced to work far away and people are less sociable, resulting in the suicide rate breaking the record of the past 11 years and increasing for the first time.
Among them, the proportion of women who have committed suicide due to financial distress caused by the loss of their jobs due to the epidemic has increased significantly, and the number of young people who have committed suicide has broken a 40-year record.
In response, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga decided to appoint the cabinet as Minister for Solitary Affairs, Tetsuji Sakamoto, to address the worsening suicide problem.
According to the latest data from Japan ’ s Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare, the number of suicides in 2020 reached 20,919, the first increase since the financial crisis in 2009.
The Japanese government attributed the result to economic pressures such as social dysfunction and unemployment caused by the epidemic.
Not only that, but the suicide rate among women also rose for the first time in two years, to 6,976.
In fact, many women who work in the frontline are the first to be laid off because of the impact of the epidemic on the tourism and retail industry in Japan.
According to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), Japan ’ s suicide rate is the highest in the G7, with 14.9 suicides per 100,000 people, mostly due to health factors and economic problems. However, as the epidemic continues to spread, the related problems will only continue to worsen.
To this end, the Japanese government decided to follow the British example and set up the post of "Minister of Solitude" to solve the relevant problems.
Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga appointed the current cabinet as the first Minister for Solitary Affairs, Tetsuji Sakamoto. In the future, Tetsuji Sakamoto will be responsible for coordinating various departments and agencies and proposing relevant measures.

title: Ukrainian airliner shot down Iran claims UN investigators lied – Radio France Internationale
text:
UNITED NATIONS (AFP) - A Ukrainian passenger plane was shot down near Tehran last year at the height of tensions between Iran and the United States, United Nations officials today accused the Iranian government of lying in explaining the cause of the crash.
On January 8, 2020, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed shortly after takeoff from Tehran, Iran, killing all 176 people on board, including 55 Canadian citizens.
Three days later, Iran admitted that its forces had fired two missiles and accidentally shot down the Boeing 737-800, which was scheduled to fly to Kiev, Ukraine.
The UN special rapporteur on extrajudicial executions, Agnes Callamard, released the findings of the tragedy, saying the explanation provided by the Iranian government was full of contradictions.
"What is most troubling is that the Iranian authorities are simply unreasonable about the mistakes that have been made, whether it be a single mistake or a number of mistakes," she told reporters.
She said Iran's explanation of the crash was "full of contradictions, contradicts the facts and does not conform to the technical assessments made by many experts."
"There is really no alternative to saying that Iran is lying, but why are they doing it?"
Karamarde said that Iran could not explain how the military made such a serious mistake that it shot down a passenger plane.
Karamarde said that under international law, "manslaughter" is possible, and the Institute of Law determines whether the fault was committed in good faith.
"My conclusion is that Iran cannot justify its mistakes on the basis of international law," he added. "Relations between Iran and the United States were strained when Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down.
Five days before the incident, the United States launched a drone attack on Baghdad International Airport in Iraq, killing Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the elite Quds Force of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard; Iran launched a missile attack on an Iraqi military base for the use of the United States.
Iran is also on high alert in response to the US counterattack, there has been a accidental attack on the passenger plane.
© 2021 AFP

title: Japan ’ s new “Minister of Solitude ” wants to reduce the suicide rate, how to find people in need from a“ one-person ” culture?
text:
In an effort to address Japan ’ s record-breaking suicide rate, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga announced earlier this month the creation of a new “minister of loneliness ” in his cabinet, with Tetsushi Sakamoto appointed as minister by the Cabinet Office.
How to deal with social problems caused by loneliness is very difficult for Japan.
On the one hand, popular culture promotes the so-called "one person" (ohitorisama, that is, one can live alone), and on the other hand, it is closely related to the Japanese workplace environment and culture.
The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated the frequency of people feeling lonely.
Suicides hit record numbers in 2020, women and young people noticeably increased The Japan Times reports that Sakamoto is also responsible for saving the country ’ s declining birth rate and reviving the local economy.
This position was first created by the UK in 2018, and the Australian government has a similar role.
Because loneliness is related to social issues such as suicide, poverty, and “cocooning ”, the Japanese cabinet has set up an inter-departmental task force to understand the problem of loneliness and investigate its impact.
According to data released by the Japanese Police Agency, nearly 21,000 people committed suicide last year (2020), 750 more than the previous year (2019), breaking the record of the past 11 years.
The rise in suicides is evident among women and young people.
Photo Credit: AP / Takashi Imaging Cabinet Office Special Minister Tetsushi Sakamoto has been appointed by Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga to deal with Japan ’ s high suicide rate.
Suga told Sakamoto at a conference, "Women are suffering more from isolation than men, and the number of suicides is also on the rise."
I hope that you can identify the relevant problems and propose corresponding prevention and control policies. "
However, this does not mean that the Japanese government only wants to deal with the problem of suicide among women and young people.
In his report to the House of Representatives Budget Committee earlier this month, Suga mentioned that people from all walks of life in Japan, including the elderly who are trapped at home and college students who cannot attend school, have become increasingly isolated during the Wuhan pneumonia epidemic.
Sakamoto later said at a press conference that he hoped to implement activities to prevent social isolation and isolation and to maintain interpersonal connections.
Sakamoto also revealed that he will host a forum at the end of February to hear from workers who help people deal with loneliness and discuss related support strategies.
Suga is also planning to attend.
Japanese society that promotes “one person ” needs to point out which kind of loneliness needs help.“ What is loneliness ” is a thornier problem in Japan. In Japanese, the word “kodoku ” often includes loneliness, which makes people feel lonely and uneasy, and solitude, which allows them to enjoy time alone. Communication strategist Okako According to Junko Okamoto, this has led to a trend in Japan in recent years, which sees being alone as positive and even beautifies the situation.
The best example of how the publishing market shapes isolation as proof of independence, introspection, and superiority over others is the bestselling book “The Best of Loneliness ” published by Chung Xiaozi in 2018.
The Japanese word “ohitorisama ” has also been promoted in the mass media to show that a person is independent enough to go shopping, eat, or even travel alone.
Junko Okamoto says that the Japanese society's near-cult culture of solitude has left the public unaware of the almost hopeless, unbearable nature of suffering in loneliness.
Therefore, one of the challenges for the Japanese government will be to define and identify the conditions under which people are struggling with unsettling solitude and therefore need help, rather than simply enjoying the time alone.
Social isolation among middle-aged men In Japan, the high risk group often mentioned includes the elderly and middle-aged men.
In particular, Japan is known for “kodokushi ”, which refers to those who live alone until the last moment of their lives and are not discovered by others until they die.
In an international survey conducted by the Cabinet Office in 2015, Japanese people over the age of 60 reported the highest proportion of people in need of help (16.1%), compared with 13% in the United States, 10.8% in Sweden and 5.8% in Germany.
Photo Credit: Shutterstock / Dazhi Image An OECD survey in 2005 also showed that Japanese society struggles to address social isolation, especially among men.
The survey found that a high proportion of Japanese men spend “little or no ” time with friends, peers, or other groups.
That ’ s 17%, well above the OECD average of about 6%.
The report pointed out that part of the reason can be attributed to the long working hours in Japan's workplace environment, as well as the lifelong employment system.
"Into Japan" pointed out that in addition to the beautification of "loneliness", Japan is also a "high context" culture, that is, most people have a common cultural background, which requires everyone to be able to read the air through observation, even without speaking a language.
Junko Okamoto points out that many Japanese people believe that through "heart to heart", they can achieve the state of "everything in silence", resulting in awkward language expression.
Especially those middle-aged and elderly men who struggle all the way through the corporate culture of long hours of labor, vertical communication methods and convergent pressure are very dependent on the workplace and lack the "skills" to deal with "outside" people, so they are prone to loneliness.
Pneumonia exacerbates the risk of loneliness for those living alone, and fears about living alone are growing in Japan.
A 2018 survey by real estate advertising firm Lifull Co and its think-tank found that as many as 75% of single households in Japan had little or no communication with their neighbors, compared to 54.1% for two or more households.
According to the survey report, part of the reason may be that in Japan, the ease of working for the company and the importance of privacy determine where these single families live (especially in the city), even if they have to move to an environment they do not know.
“Before the outbreak, the typical day for single-family households living in the city might have been like this: working from day to night, eating or drinking with friends after work, and then commuting home, ” said Manjo Shimahara, head of the think tank.
“For them, home is just a place where they can sleep after work, ” Mr. Shimabara said.
But the pandemic has changed that, with remote work drastically reducing the interaction of lone workers with their work colleagues, forcing them to spend time with their neighbors who have little emotional attachment.
Such a drastic change in lifestyle has exacerbated the risk of feeling lonely, says Mr. Shimahara.
“I think the Wuhan pneumonia epidemic has forced the lone residents to realize the fact that they don ’ t know any of their neighbors near their homes or can ’ t even name any of the bars near where they live. ”

title: The epidemic has increased the suicide rate, and the appointment of a "minister of loneliness" is urgent.
text:
Japan suffered from COVID-19 in 2020, forcing people to work remotely and reducing social interaction, which led to the suicide rate breaking the previous 11 years ’ record. (AP) Japan ’ s suicide rate in 2020 broke the previous 11 years ’ record, and increased for the first time in the past 11 years, especially among women and young people.
To this end, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga has appointed a “Minister for Solitude ” to address the worsening suicide problem.
According to data from the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare, the number of suicides in 2020 reached 20,919, the first increase since the financial crisis in 2009, with 6,976 women accounting for nearly 15% more than in 2019.
The Japanese government blamed the outbreak on social dysfunction and economic pressures such as unemployment.
For this reason, the Japanese government decided to follow the British example and set up the post of "Minister of Solitude".
On the 12th, Suga appointed the current cabinet as the first minister of loneliness, Tetsuji Sakamoto. On the 16th, he established the “Office of Solitude and Isolation Measures ” to deal with the serious problem of loneliness and isolation.
In announcing her appointment in January 2018, Prime Minister Theresa May described loneliness as a “sad reality of modern life ” and looked forward to helping those who had no way of expressing their grief.
Japan ’ s Nikkei Shimbun commented that since Suga decided to follow the British example, he should also send a stronger and stronger message to the people, like May, to encourage the people to work together to solve their psychological pain.
Japanese media reported that because of the strong reaction of public opinion, the Japanese government tends to continue to lock the country. (European News Agency) Japanese media: lifting the state of emergency will still lock the country In addition, the Korean news reported that the Japanese government has basically decided on the 24th, even if the state of emergency is lifted across the country, it will continue to maintain the state of lock, and the business bubble in 11 countries / regions will not reopen temporarily.
On the other hand, the International Olympic Committee said that the decision on whether to allow foreign tourists to enter Japan at the Tokyo Olympics is expected to be made at the end of April.
The epidemic in Japan has slowed down, and the state of emergency was originally issued by the prefectural governments of the ten prefectures until March 7, but now the rest of the region is expected to be lifted by the end of February.

title: Infectious diseases affect physical and mental health.
text:
(Getty Images) Countries around the world have taken many public health precautions to stem the spread of the coronavirus, such as isolation, social distancing, and closing schools, according to the study.
The social and economic consequences of these measures can lead to business closures, unemployment and debt-related domestic violence.
According to a report by the National Center for Biotechnology Information, young people are more vulnerable to unemployment than people of other ages.
In Japan, the term hikikomori (or long-term social withdrawal) is used to describe young people who are chronically isolated from society due to unemployment or school dropout.
The emergence of the term "stinginess" can be explained from two broader perspectives.
First, from a clinical point of view, "stinginess" coexists with multiple psychiatric disorders, such as adaptive disorders, anxiety-related disorders, and severe depression.
Second, the non-clinical view is that as the world becomes more globalized, young people face more intense competition for education and employment than in the past, and they are forced to accelerate their learning and development from childhood, leading to social withdrawal.
According to the report, there are four possible effects of COVID-19 on the phenomenon of "stinging".
First, social distancing and isolation can cause fear, frustration, or boredom, leading to post-traumatic stress syndrome.
Prolonged school closures can have a negative mental impact on students, and the number of students who are truant and drop out may increase as a result.
Second, with global unemployment expected to rise, young people who were already vulnerable in the job market before the outbreak of COVID-19, and those who are about to graduate from school, will find it more difficult to find work, leading to further self-isolation and social withdrawal.
Third, it is not only young people, but also their family members, who are affected by rising unemployment.
However, it is unclear what negative effects parents who have just lost their jobs will have on their young children.
Fourthly, this is a more positive point.
Because many people experience many months of social isolation, they will have more awareness of the phenomenon of "stingy", and more sympathy for the young people who retreat, which is beneficial to the future development of "stingy" social work in the community.
The report concludes that investing in young people ’ s mental health is the most cost-effective approach in the long run.
The report recommends that more paid or unpaid work opportunities should be created for young people, and that any activities to protect the rights of young people should involve young people in person and be paid accordingly.
The report also said that individual interventions targeting young people can improve effectiveness through support from parents and partners, and the government should also address the creativity, innovation and initiative of young people to help build a “new normal ” lifestyle after the pandemic.

title: Spring and autumn are gone. At the end of the century, half a year in the northern hemisphere is summer.
text:
Although this winter is more obvious than in previous years, but looking at the long-term trend, winter time is getting shorter and warmer, and autumn is not obvious, only feel the increasingly hot summer, the time to wear short sleeves is also getting longer.
Recent research has found that summers are indeed getting longer, and by 2100 the northern hemisphere may be summer for half a year, with potentially far-reaching implications for agriculture, human health and the environment.
Summer is getting longer because the planet is warming and disrupting the balance of seasons.
The researchers defined the beginning of summer as the warmest 25% of the time, while winter began at the coldest 25% of the time. Using daily climate data from 1952 to 2011, the researchers measured the length of the four seasons in the Northern Hemisphere and the timing of the start of the season, and then used established climate change models to predict the characteristics of future seasons.
The study found that the global warming, the summer is getting hotter, and the winter is shorter and warmer.
Average summer days increased from 78 to 95 days, while winter months decreased from 76 to 73 days.
Spring reduced from 124 days to 115 days, and autumn reduced from 87 days to 82 days.
Spring and summer start earlier, autumn and winter start later.
Among them, the seasonal cycle changes the most in the Mediterranean and the Tibetan Plateau.
If these trends continue, the researchers said, humans will do nothing to mitigate climate change, and by 2100 winter will last less than two months, and spring and fall will be shorter.
Previous studies have found the same trend.
US climate scientists examined the hottest and coldest 90 days of the year in the past two 30 years, 1960-1989 and 1990-2019 respectively, and found that the hottest temperature in the previous 30 years has increased by a few days in the last 30 years, and the number of days defining the coldest temperature in the previous 30 years has decreased.
Scientists looked at 6,000 weather stations around the world and found that most of them had longer summers and shorter winters.
High latitudes have seen the greatest reduction in winter days, but parts of Southern California and South Florida have also seen significant reductions in winter.
They also found that the closer to the ocean, the longer the summer.
This makes sense because the oceans are warming dramatically and have a huge impact on the climate.
There is also the urban heat island effect, which results in longer summers in cities than in nearby rural areas.
Seasonal changes bring significant environmental and health risks.
For example, birds change the way they migrate, and plants grow in a chaotic season.
These changes can create imbalances between animals and their food sources, disrupting ecological communities.
Seasonal changes can also wreak havoc on agriculture.
This shift in the season can lead to more severe weather events.
Hot summers will be longer and hot events will be more frequent and intensified, including heatwaves and wildfires.
Warmer, shorter winters can increase climate instability, such as cold spells and winter storms, and more frequent extreme weather events such as the recent Texas blizzard.
The study was published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters.

A large number of women are unemployed during the epidemic.
According to the Ministry of General Affairs of Japan, when comparing the average number of female workers per month from April to July 2019 and 2020, the number of people working in the hotel and restaurant industry, the industry related to lifestyle and leisure activities, and the wholesale and retail industry decreased by 280,000, 140,000 and 110,000 respectively, but in these three areas, the number of men working decreased by less than 100,000.
South Korea ’ s statistics office pointed out that the number of people employed in the country in October was 27.09 million, a year-on-year decrease of 421,000 due to the epidemic.
According to the Korean Women ’ s Policy Research Institute and the Statistics Agency, there were 283,000 fewer women in employment in September than in 2019, and 109,000 fewer men.

Part-time jobs are mostly low-paid, low-benefits, and insecure, making them more vulnerable to dismissal.
Many of his friends have been fired.
She said that Japan has always ignored women, and in this society, when something bad happens, the weakest people are the first to be abandoned.
This type of work for Japanese women is socially and culturally related.
They are expected to take on the responsibility of caring for their children and doing housework, which makes it difficult for them to develop a career. Some women “voluntarily ” choose part-time or less important positions to retain more time to care for their families and reduce their income to obtain the tax deduction provided by the government for married families.

Japanese women who work part-time or stop working due to childbirth keep their average salary roughly unchanged from late 20s to 60s.
Korean women are in the same situation.
In November 2018, French media reported that a university graduate named Casey Lee was harassed because of her female identity when she applied for a job. Some interviewers complained that women tended to resign once they had children, and some interviewers criticized her as an "irresponsible young woman" who gave up "having children for the future of the country."
Some of the cases heard by Korean courts in recent years have also seen large companies deliberately eliminate female candidates in recruitment, including three large banks and the state-run Korea Gas Safety Corporation.
A group of women who are more vulnerable in the recession may not get the same treatment even if they get a job.
Research on Japanese Labor Policy.
According to the 2018 International Labor Comparison Report, Japanese women ’ s salaries in 2016 were only 73% of men ’ s, and Korean women ’ s salaries were only 68.6%.
Long-term lower income means that savings will be relatively small.
According to a June 2019 study by the World Economic Forum, Japanese women ’ s retirement savings will be exhausted 20 years before they die, and normal people will feel uncertain about their lives in this situation.
Young Taek Kim, a researcher at the Korean Women ’ s Development Institute, believes that women tend to lack money and social resources compared to men, both of which are necessary for good health.
This makes them more vulnerable to all the problems created by the recession.

Japan ’ s police agency found that of 485 female suicides with known causes of suicide in August 2020, only 29 were directly related to poverty, and 380 were due to depression and other health problems.
In addition to worrying about income during the pandemic, women with families also need to spend more time on unpaid work, such as caring for children who are studying at home and preventing family members from contracting diseases.
This will increase their mental pressure.
Japanese university student Koki Ozora opened a 24-hour mental health helpline in March 2020, receiving an average of more than 200 calls a day, mostly from women.
He said the most common request for help in April was for mothers to feel pressured to raise their children, and some even admitted to wanting to kill their children.

The COVID-19 crisis may end soon, but she believes that even if the epidemic ends, it will not help her much.
Psychiatrist Toshiko Kamo said in the report that "no future" may explain better than any single direct reason why the number of female suicides has soared.
According to Toshiko Kamo, a global pandemic causes more fear than a local natural disaster.
“What escape routes are there? Families, maybe, but isolated families become some kind of prison, sowing the seeds of family tension and exacerbating it, which puts pressure on women, especially as traditional housewives and caregivers, ” she said.

title: Suicides among Japanese primary and secondary school students hit new high in 2020
text:
Newsfrom Japan (Kyodo News, March 16) On the 16th, the number of Japanese primary and secondary school students who committed suicide reached 499 in 2020, a record high since 1980, an increase of 100 over the previous year.
In terms of age, the number of suicides in their teens and 20s increased significantly, by 522 compared to the previous year.
The total number of suicides was 21081, an increase of 912 from the previous year and exceeding the previous year for the first time since 2009.
Female suicides have also increased significantly, with an increase of 935 from the previous year to 7,026.
According to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare Suicide Policy Promotion Office, “Due to the prolonged closure of schools and the increase in time spent with family due to people avoiding going out during the COVID-19 pandemic, there may be an increase in people who are worried about their studies, future, family discord, etc. ”
Among primary and secondary school students, there were 14 primary school students (an increase of 6 over the previous year), 146 junior high school students (an increase of 34), and 339 high school students (an increase of 60).
The number of girls in high school increased by 60 compared with the previous year.
The number of minor suicides reached 777 (an increase of 118).
In terms of causes and motivations, mental illnesses such as depression and worries about the future, academic dissatisfaction, etc. account for the majority.
Of the total number of suicides, 14,055 were men (a decrease of 23).
Men decreased for 11 consecutive years, but women increased.
The reasons women chose suicide were health problems (4,519), family problems (1,292), and financial and life problems (425).
From month to month, July to December increased from the previous year, with the most in October reaching 2,230 (an increase of 691).
It has also been suggested that this may be due to celebrity suicides.
According to prefectures, the number of suicides was 2,231 in Tokyo (an increase of 124), 1,409 in Osaka (an increase of 178), and 1 in Kanagawa (an increase of 124).

title: The number of suicides in 2020 has increased again after 11 years
text:
The year 2020 is a year of great changes in people ’ s living environment.
It is not only manifested in daily life, perhaps some people even their own life plans have been completely disrupted.
The number of female suicides increased by 885 from the previous year.
The number of suicides nationwide in Japan in 2020 increased by 750 (3.7%) compared to 2019 to 20,919 (estimate).
After Lehman, the number of suicides in Japan has fallen for 10 consecutive years since 2009, and this time it is the first time in 11 years that the number has exceeded the previous year.
The number of suicides per 100,000 population (suicide mortality rate) also rose again after 11 years, reaching 16.6.
The number of male suicides decreased by 135 from the previous year to 13,943, the 11th consecutive year of decline.
On the other hand, the number of female suicides increased by 885 year-on-year to 6,976.
According to the analysis, this may be due to changes in living environment caused by the expansion of the COVID-19 epidemic, as well as increased psychological burdens such as fear of future job insecurity.
The number of suicides among women and men increased by 660 to 2,199 in October, compared with the same period last year.
This may be due to the impact of previous celebrity suicides.
According to prefectures, the suicide mortality rate is highest in Yamanashi and Iwate prefectures, at 22.3, and lowest at 13.5 in Kanagawa prefectures.
Tokyo and Osaka had 16.1 and 15.7 respectively.
As of 1997, the annual number of suicides in Japan has remained at about 20,000 for many years, but since 1998, the annual number has exceeded 30,000 for 14 consecutive years and reached 34,427 in 2003, a record high.
Since then, the number of suicides has been on the decline for 10 consecutive years, thanks to the economic recovery and preventive measures taken in various localities and the strengthening of the counselling system.
The Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare pointed out that suicide is a social problem, and most people choose to die because they are driven to the end of the road, and many are preventable, so it is trying to take measures jointly with health, medical care, welfare, education, labor and other relevant departments to promote comprehensive suicide prevention measures.
On the homepage of the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Welfare, “Let ’ s Protect the Mind Together ”, a window for psychological counseling using social networks (SNS) such as LINE or the telephone is summarized, and various suicide countermeasures are provided in a concise and understandable manner.

title: Loneliness ● Discussion ｜ “I ’ m afraid I ’ ll kill my children ”, the pressure of the women epidemic has increased, and Japan has set up a department to deal with it ｜ Apple Daily
text:
"I am worried that I will kill my own child." A Japanese mother was emotionally unstable, and asked for help on the online counseling platform to express her contradictory and terrible worries, and it turned out that more than one mother had such terrible thoughts.
In the past year, the Wuhan pneumonia epidemic has exacerbated the gap between people, and the family is trapped under the same roof all day. The relationship is not becoming more intimate, but because the friction has become more alienated and lonely. Even Jiang Tao also launched the song "Loneliness Disease" to talk about loneliness.
Last year, the number of suicides in Japan rose for the first time since 2009, and the number of people who committed suicide due to “loneliness ” increased by more than 30% year-on-year. In mid-February, the Japanese government announced the establishment of the“ Solitude and Isolation Response Chamber ”, with “100 million active ministers ” Sakamoto Tetsuji as minister.
“I feel like I ’ m going to be poor again, and I can ’ t see the end of the tunnel. ” 43-year-old Eriko Kobayashi, who was plagued by emotional problems, committed suicide four times in the past, but she was originally out of the emotional haze and published a comic to explain other people who wanted to die.
She criticized Japanese society for neglecting women, and often "cutting" the most vulnerable women in times of adversity.
It is true that compared with men, retail, tourism, hotels, catering and other industries with more female employees are seriously affected by the epidemic, and young female employees can not go to work, even if they live with their families, friction with their families has increased under the epidemic, and even domestic violence by male family members.
The founder of Anata no Ibasho, a Japanese online counseling platform, said that since last summer, more and more women have turned to the platform for help, and children are also unhappy because they are unable to go to school. The Bond Project, a counseling organization in Yokohama, also said that many people have called for help in recent months, saying that they feel lonely and painful and that they want to die.
"Your Place" platform has received many women's help, some mothers admit that they are "worried that they will kill their children", some women said that they hate themselves after being sexually assaulted by their parents, and some even said that "my husband wants to kill me."
He believes that the root cause of the suicide problem is loneliness, and said that many Japanese people do not understand the difference between healthy "solitude" and "loneliness" that cause trouble, and expect the government to follow up.
Women, children and part-time workers have become the most vulnerable groups in society. We urge the government to strengthen the social safety net, and the media should not over-report celebrity suicides so as not to create a copycat effect.
According to the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, 21,077 suicides were recorded in Japan last year, an increase of 11 years after 2009, with a marked increase in the number of suicides in the second half of the year and a peak of nearly 2,200 in October.
After analyzing the motives of suicides, the authorities found that 434 people committed suicide because of "loneliness", an increase of 31.5% year-on-year, and the number of primary and secondary school students who committed suicide also increased to 479, an increase of 41.3% year-on-year.
In terms of gender distribution, the number of female suicides increased by 15% year-on-year, offsetting the decline in the number of male suicides.
The proportion of families living alone is expected to increase to 40%. Working from home weakens social structure and culture in Japan also encourages suicide.
Japan ’ s population living alone has continued to grow in recent years, and it is estimated that by 2040, families living alone will account for 40% of all households, nearly double the number in 1970.
Japanese social culture itself tends to be isolated, coupled with long working hours, and people find it difficult to make other friends. Therefore, most of the people living alone rarely communicate with their neighbors, and most of their social life revolves around work.
A study published in February by Tokushima University in Japan found that about half of respondents said they were under severe stress during the pandemic and were tired of staying at home for long periods of time, and 11.5% said they felt that their emotional problems had reached the point where they needed medical help.
Advocating the concept that "the responsibility of loneliness is not their own" When Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga announced the establishment of a loneliness and isolation countermeasures room, he mentioned that the number of women in the epidemic of loneliness and suicide increased, hoping that Sakamoto Tetsuki proposed comprehensive measures.
Some members of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party have also proposed the establishment of an inter-departmental meeting to strengthen support for the lonely and reconnect them with their communities.
They pointed out that social isolation is related to a variety of causes such as rapid changes in living conditions, poverty, domestic violence, etc., and the government should send the message to citizens that the responsibility of loneliness is not its own, and hope that the government will take lasting measures.
In addition to Japan, the UK also set up a "Minister of Loneliness" in 2018, which is not a cabinet post, to explore the problem of loneliness. Prime Minister Theresa May said at the time that as many as 9 million people in the UK often feel lonely. Since then, the British Secretary of State for Loneliness has introduced more than 100 measures to address the problem of loneliness, such as funding to local groups to let young people teach the elderly. Use the computer and instruct the postman to communicate more with the elderly.
Japan should follow the example of the United Kingdom and set clear definitions and measures for loneliness and isolation, and should not rely solely on psychiatric theory as a policy basis, Okemoto said.
There are also voices in Australia advocating the establishment of a dedicated official to deal with the problem of loneliness. Fiona Patten, a local MP, proposed in 2018 to create more loneliness ministers at the local level to improve social isolation, and the opposition Labor Party proposed the establishment of a federal anti-loneliness minister in the 2019 Australian election platform.
Labor MP Andrew Giles said the government should strengthen community ties and expect politicians to take the challenge of loneliness seriously.
Michelle, Senior Lecturer in Clinical Psychology, Swinburne University of Technology, Australia.
According to Michelle H. Lim, more than half of people in Australia feel lonely at least one day a week, describing loneliness as a problem that can affect society and can be “passed on from person to person ”. It is recommended that Australia ’ s public health policy include a part to deal with loneliness, correct people ’ s misconceptions about loneliness, and understand that being alone can also be healthy.

title: World News Network
text:
Although the elderly are the most vulnerable people to the new coronavirus attack, the elderly at home are a relatively lucky group, do not need to work outside, there is social security or other pension, automatically deposited into a bank account at the time of the month, life is not affected by the epidemic, the government issued relief money turned into an additional gift; Third, the elderly people with children do not even have to go out to buy necessities and food, they will buy the door.
In this way, we become the safest group.
But when the epidemic is raging, no one can maintain a normal life.
Our plan to visit Hawaii in 2020 was ruined, and other day trips were afraid to participate, so as not to get together with outsiders; although the self-driving tour was good, we were already at the age of eight and nine, and had no intention of driving.
Once a week the cinema is gone, restaurants can not eat, shopping malls dare not visit......, the only place to go is the park, my neighborhood has two regional parks and two small community parks, but the epidemic is endless, repeated to these parks, it is inevitable that monotonous.
One day, happiness to the heart: the nearby city also has a park! Check the Internet, of course, the drive is no more than 20 minutes.
So once or twice a week, take turns to go, and so far have been to more than 20 different parks, the beautiful name is "walking around the park."
Community parks are basically made up of six elements: a children ’ s playground, a playground, trails, pavilions, trees, and large green grasses.
The difference is nothing more than the size of the area, the walk is good or bad and the number of trees.
The two smallest parks we have visited are only the size of a basketball court, and they are all on street corners, only for people to sit and rest, and the large parks can cover tens of times; individual parks do not even have concrete or gravel walkways, and their function is limited to providing a play area for children.
Nevertheless, these parks have provided a good place for people in the midst of the epidemic.
In the park, the grass is green, the trees are green, the air is fresh, and people can breathe freely; the sun is shining, so that people can supplement vitamin D; the area is sparse, and people can maintain enough social distance; whether it is walking, walking the dog or doing gymnastics, it is very convenient.
Everything is relative, there is no absolute good or bad and very beautiful and ugly, in abnormal circumstances, things or places that are usually ignored show their value.
We don ’ t know its size and characteristics before we go to a park, it ’ s like a blind date, where we get to know what it looks like, so there ’ s no expectation and disappointment, and there ’ s no sense of repetition and anathema.
We were overjoyed when we encountered a park that exceeded normal standards.
There is a park built on the top of a hill, and it is very pleasant to look at the city; there is a park built at the intersection of the main road, and walking into it is a natural depression, and the central depression and the surrounding slopes are filled with cactuses of various colors. In the park where you can see the sparkling lake water after entering the door, waterbirds fly down and down comfortably, hundreds of water ducks float on the lake to compete, turtles bask in the sun lazily, and in the shade of a gorgeous tree, people may lie with their eyes closed, or sit on their legs to enjoy a picnic, forgetting the existence of the epidemic.
Generally speaking, the parks in affluent communities are not only exquisite, but also clean and tidy, so you will definitely come back next time.
There is a good tradition in the United States. Every year from the beginning of July to the mid-August evening, the larger parks will hold free summer concerts, so that ordinary people who do not enter the concert hall can enjoy the music while enjoying the cool, but because of the epidemic has to stop.
We hope that the epidemic will be effectively brought under control and that concerts in the park will be resumed this summer.

title: Japanese primary school student suicides hit record high in 2020
text:
After the government issued a declaration of state of emergency, all school principals suspended classes.
Neither can participate in community activities, nor can I travel with my family, and I can only spend day after day at home.
Energetic energy is nowhere to be released, and the children undoubtedly feel different pressure than the adults.
Based on the suicide statistics of the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology calculated that in 2020, a total of 479 small country high school students committed suicide, an increase of 140 over the previous year, a record high.
Among them, 14 primary school students (6 in the previous year), 136 middle school students (96 in the previous year), and 329 high school students (237 in the previous year).
In particular, there were 138 high school girls, more than double the number of 67 in the previous year.
From the monthly situation, the more prominent is June 45, August 64, September 53, November 48. June is in line with the first emergency declaration of the implementation of the long-term suspension measures to lift the ban, the formal resumption of normal teaching period. August is affected by the long-term suspension of the summer vacation period shortened.
The main reasons for suicide are “anxiety about going to school ”,“ poor grades ” and “discord with parents ”, which is similar to the previous year in general. On the other hand, the number of suicides affected by mental illness and depression has increased compared to the previous year.
The Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology believes that the impact of the new coronavirus epidemic has led to an increase in the number of primary and secondary school students committing suicide to a certain extent, and will be analyzed in detail.
In addition, we will actively promote the "24-hour Children's SOS Hotline" (0120-0-78310), a free consultation window that can also accept elementary and junior high school students at night and holidays, and improve the construction of school psychological counselors and strengthen the school's care and guidance.

title: Warming continues to warm India's rainy season will expand
text:
Warming will make India ’ s summer rainy season more visible.
European studies have found that as Earth ’ s temperature gets warmer, every 1 degree Celsius increase in temperature is expected to lead to a 5% increase in summer rainfall in India, with consequences that will not only affect local crop yields in India, but also increase the chance of major flooding.
According to The Independent, India, which accounts for one fifth of the world ’ s population, relies on seasonal rains from June to September each year as a source of drinking water and farming.
However, the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany found that global warming will make the rainy season stronger and more unstable.
Using 31 new climate models, the researchers analyzed possible changes in India ’ s rainy season in four future climate scenarios, including successful efforts to limit warming to 2 degrees Celsius and ineffective efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
It was found that if we managed to keep the temperature within 2 degrees, the seasonal rainfall would increase by 10% between 1985 and 2015 by the end of the century, but if humans did nothing, the rainfall would increase by 24%.
In addition, for every 1 degree increase in global temperature, rainfall increases by 5%, compared to 3% in previous studies using earlier models.
In response to this, researcher Anders Leverman said, “As the difference becomes more pronounced from year to year, it will make the annual rainy season more unpredictable. ”
We also found that the increase in rainfall during the rainy season was more pronounced than in past climate models. ”
He also pointed out that climate change makes the rainy season more intense for many reasons, one of which is that warmer air will carry more water.
Andrew Turner, a scientist at the University of Reading in the United Kingdom, also believes that “the results also support the conclusion of earlier studies that rainfall will increase in India during the rainy season when greenhouse gases increase. ” According to CNN, India ’ s agricultural production accounts for nearly 20% of GDP, which plays an important role in the smooth development of the country.
Crops need rainfall, but too much or too little can harm plants.
In this regard, agricultural policy expert Devender Sharma pointed out that agricultural practices must adapt to climate change, but the specific way is still unknown.
“We don ’ t know how climate change will develop, and there is a possibility that a period of heavy rain will be followed by droughts or hurricanes, with no consistency, ” he said.
This will create a lot of problems for the agricultural sector and the economy, "he said.
The results of the study are published in the journal Earth Dynamics Systems.

title: Daren said that the biggest frost in 30 years hit the French vineyard production.
text:
Burgundy vineyards have been hit by a cold snap, leaving farmers crying. (Euronews) The winemaking industry, one of France ’ s biggest export industries, was hit by an unusually severe frost earlier this month, hitting vineyards across the country and dealing a devastating blow to a winery that has been ravaged by the COVID-19 pandemic and high US tariffs.
According to the European Wine Companies Committee, the frost affects 80% of the vineyards in the main wine regions of France, “It is expected that this will lead to loss of production from 25% to up to 50% in some regions. ”
Anne Colombo, president of Cornas, a wine region in the Rhone region, said the areas hit were the Rhone Valley, Bordeaux, Burgundy, Champagne, Provence and Loire Valley.
She said: “This year, grape production is very rare in some areas.
She added that the frost damage in Cornas was the worst in more than half a century.
Winemakers try to keep the temperature warm by lighting candles and fire pots in the vineyard, but in many cases this is not enough to protect budding vines.
Christophe Chateau, director of communications at the Bordeaux Wine Association, said: “We have lost important harvests and are not yet able to give a preliminary estimate.
But in any case, this is a tragedy for the grape farmers who have been hit.
The National Union of Farmers said the frost also threatened other crops, including beet and mustard.
The group issued a statement in mid-April saying: “This damage is enormous for vineyards, orchards and farms.
French Prime Minister Jean Castex said the farm had not experienced such a catastrophic weather event since 1991.
Gabriel Attal, a spokesman for the French government, told reporters that in some areas, some crops could lose “almost full year production. ”
France ’ s Ministry of Agriculture and Food has launched the “Agricultural Disaster ” programme, initiating tax relief and other financial support measures for farmers.
French President Emmanuel Macron tweeted, “To all the farmers across France who are fighting day and night to protect the fruits of their own labor, I would like to say that we will give our full support in this war. ”
Stay strong! We will always support you. ”
For French winemakers, this crisis has come at a more opportune time.
French winemakers are facing weak sales as key international markets remain locked in a state of COVID-19, the collapse of the tourism industry caused by the pandemic, and high tariffs imposed by the United States over a subsidy dispute with the European Union.
The United States and the European Union are locked in a dispute over subsidies for aircraft manufacturers Airbus and Boeing.
According to the Federation of French Wine and Spirits Exporters, French wine and spirits exports fell by nearly 14% to 12.1 billion euros (about $14.5 billion) in 2020, and sales to the United States fell by 18%.
Winemakers deal with the damage of climate crisis frosts in particular, as it tends to appear after unusually warm temperatures, which means that vines will initially grow faster than usual, making them more sensitive to the cold.
“France experienced near-record warmth from late March to early April, ” said Chad Myers, a meteorologist. This was followed by an“ intense Arctic cyclone ” over the Easter weekend.
In less than a week, temperatures in the Champagne region dropped from close to 26 ° C (80 ° F) to around -6 ° C (22 ° F). “Even now temperatures are close to normal, another cold wave is coming, ” Myers said.
“When they start to grow, that ’ s when they become more vulnerable, ” Colombo said. He added that temperature changes also affect harvests.
“Now we start harvesting in the first week of September, 20 years ago in the last week of September, ” she said. The National Federation of Migrant Workers ’ Unions said the event was a“ clear reminder ” of the importance of precautionary measures and “risk management systems to address climate challenges. ”
