title: Milestone! "Perseverance" Mars rover successfully produces oxygen on Mars for the first time!
text:
The perseverance rover has successfully made oxygen from carbon dioxide in the atmosphere on Mars.
(Reuters) - NASA said on Wednesday that the "Perseverance" Mars rover made oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide on Mars for the first time.
This is the first time humans have created oxygen on an extrasolar planet.
On February 18 this year, the "perseverance" Mars rover successfully landed on Mars.
NASA said in a statement that the oxygen production mission was carried out by the "Mars Oxygen in situ Resource Utilization Experiment" (MOXIE) equipment carried by the "perseverance".
It operated for the first time on the 60th "Mars Day" (April 20, US Eastern Time) after landing on Mars, successfully separating the oxygen atoms of carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere to make about 5 grams of oxygen, equivalent to the amount of oxygen an astronaut needs to breathe for about 10 minutes of normal activity.
Carbon monoxide produced during the oxygen production process is released into the Martian atmosphere.
"This is a critical first step in converting carbon dioxide to oxygen on Mars," said Dr. Ruth, head of NASA's Space Technology Directorate.
According to NASA, about 96% of the Martian atmosphere is carbon dioxide. MOXIE is only a small experimental device, but it is expected to drive the development of larger and more efficient oxygen generators.
This will not only help solve the problem of oxygen supply for future astronauts on Mars, but also provide oxygen fuel for the rockets that humans will use to return to Earth from Mars.
MOXIE is designed by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the United States. It has a cuboid body with a gold appearance and is the size of a car battery. It is located in the right front of the interior of the Mars rover.
Because the oxygen production process requires a high temperature of around 800 degrees Celsius, MOXIE is made of heat-resistant materials, including the use of 3D printing, nickel alloy parts that heat or cool the passing gas, and lightweight aerogels that help keep the temperature.
It has a thin gold coating on the outside that prevents heat from being radiated outwards to avoid damage to the rest of the Perseverance.
NASA said in a statement that the device is expected to perform at least nine more oxygenation activities in a "Martian year" (equivalent to nearly two years on Earth).
It is designed to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.
MIT engineer Hector was quoted by AFP as saying that if the device is converted to a ton, it can make about 25 tons of oxygen for the rocket to take off from Mars.
According to the NASA website, in the future, if four astronauts work and live on Mars for a year, they may need 1 ton of oxygen.
The perseverance rover was launched on July 30 last year and landed on Mars on February 18 this year.
Its mission includes searching for signs of life that may have existed in the Martian past, as well as exploring the Martian geology and climate features to explore the future of human exploration and landing on Mars.
The robotic helicopter on board the Mars rover successfully completed its first flight on Mars on the 19th of this month, rising 3 meters and suspended for 30 seconds.
This is the first time an artificial aircraft has flown under control on another planet.

title: US "perseverance" Mars probe: local materials to produce oxygen successfully
text:

NASA ’ s “Perseverance ” Mars probe has completed a ground-breaking mission – to obtain in-situ oxygen production on Mars, light installation for the future of mankind. Going to Mars adds a bit of hope.
Oxygen is the source of life.
This is the second time Perseverance has made history since landing on Mars; the first was the first successful flight of the unmanned helicopter Curiosity.
Oxygen equipment called Mars oxygen field resource utilization experimental instrument, MOXIE.
It makes 5 grams of oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere, roughly the same amount of oxygen that astronauts need to breathe on Mars for 10 minutes.
The purpose of NASA's Mars Oxygen Experiment is to explore whether humans can "get oxygen" on Mars in the future, without having to carry oxygen with them for interstellar travel.
The atmosphere of Mars is dominated by carbon dioxide, accounting for 96%, and oxygen only 0.13%; oxygen accounts for 21% of the Earth's atmosphere.
Moxie separates oxygen atoms (O2) from carbon dioxide (CO2) molecules, and the resulting carbon monoxide is released into the Martian atmosphere as an exhaust gas.
The goal is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.
Trudy Kortes of NASA ’ s Space Technology Division explained that Moxie is not only the first instrument to successfully produce oxygen in other worlds beyond Earth, but also a pioneer in similar technologies that will help future space exploration teams rely on water and water to adapt to local conditions.
The process of separating oxygen from carbon dioxide means that an inexhaustible amount of local resources can be converted into acceptable supplies: breathable gases, jet fuels, and mixed with hydrogen to produce water.
Previously, the unmanned helicopter "Innovation" brought to Mars by perseverance made two test flights to Mars on April 19 and 22, setting a record.
The second flight experiment involved lifting from the surface of Mars to an altitude of 5 meters, then translating 2 meters, spinning, taking some photos, and then returning to the landing site.

It is believed that, billions of years ago, Jezero had a huge lake.
Where there is water, there may be life.
Perseverance is the second one-tonne Mars rover launched by NASA.
The first probe, Curiosity, landed in another crater in 2012.
The first powered flight of a mini-helicopter on Mars has been hailed as the "Wright Brothers moment" on Mars, the first time humans have tried to fly on another planet.
Why is Yezero Crater so interesting?
Jezero, 45 km wide, is named after a town in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
In some Slavic languages, "jezero" means "lake", which also explains its attraction.
Jezero showed multiple rock types, including clay and carbonates, that may preserve some kind of organic molecule, suggesting life once existed.
Particularly attractive is the bath-ring sediment that extends along the shoreline of ancient lakes on Mars.
In these places, Perseverance can find something similar to what is known on Earth as stacking stones.
Image source, NASA image annotated with text, second photo sent back from the Yezero crater The most interesting rocks discovered by Perseverance will be packed into small tubes left on the Martian surface.
NASA and the European Space Agency have developed a multi-billion dollar plan to bring them back by the end of the century.
It will be a complex operation involving a second probe, a Mars rocket, and a giant satellite that will bring the specimen of Jezero back to Earth.
But bringing back samples is the next step in Mars exploration, which is both logical and necessary.
Even if Perseverance finds something that looks like a biomarker, the evidence will almost certainly be controversial, as is the claim that there are traces of ancient life on Earth.

title: Living City Garden Plants Greenery in Healing House
text:
(DECO Magazine) Photographer - unseen views by Charis Solomou Data and Photo Courtesy - Christos Pavlou Architecture KIBRIS The Garden House in the City For many highly developed cities, in order to obtain more space and resources, the first thing to be squeezed out is the local native natural fauna and flora. Bringing nature back to the city, though not a new idea, is a priority, especially for a city like Nicosia, the capital of Cyprus, where greening of public areas is not a priority. The design team can only turn to “The Garden House in the City ” to let plant greenery settle in the houses and let the vitality silently heal every day of daily life.
This year, due to the impact of the epidemic, many cities around the world have implemented the policy of lockdown isolation, people are staying at home more time, nature began to review the basic value of the home, but also once again noted the importance of outdoor areas in addition to indoor venues, balcony and roof space is the best place to talk to nature.
"During the pandemic, being able to breathe fresh air in the open air or naturally connect with your family is invaluable. However, the virus is only a reminder of how to get back to things that are routinely ignored or forgotten in our daily lives, such as open skies, bright sunlight, vibrant plant greenery, and dynamic lines that are not bound by space, how to make these habits more creative again." The way to introduce the interior, to fill and enrich the vitality of a city, is the problem we have been thinking about.
This is what Christos Pavlou Architecture ’ s design team says.
“The Garden House in the City was born with the idea of bringing nature back to the city, to design a house that would allow residents to share their living space and have regular social conversations, ” the design team explained.“ Our design emphasizes the potential of private urban gardens and the micro-climate they create to improve living conditions in the city and mitigate global warming. ”
With the ambition to bring nature back into the city, Christos Pavlou Architecture ’ s design team actively linked the entire house to the surrounding environment in a semi-open manner, rather than creating a fence like a traditional housing building to isolate the house. The design team wanted The Garden House to be a physical continuation of the adjacent public green space. Communities, private gardens, and parks are interdependent, as if urban elements such as buildings, streets, and public spaces are not unconnected individuals, but are more connected when the home becomes part of the park or the park landscape enters the home landscape.
The design team integrated the planting area of green plants into the entire interior layout. In addition to living space, kitchen and dining area, about 60% of the floor area of the house is planned as a courtyard garden, which is planted with various leafy green plants. All the interiors have smooth lines attached to the exterior space and are arranged around a green central courtyard, which guards between two white building cubes. The large glass curtain becomes a transparent and open presence, connecting the two building volumes, bringing more natural light and free flowing air, and blurring the indoor and outdoor spaces. This is the boundary line that allows homeowners to have a sense of openness in the outdoors even when they are inside.
As the design team envisioned, creating a place for nature in the city will not only bring another layer of decoration to the urban structure, but also encourage the return of local birds and honey, thereby maintaining the city ’ s biodiversity and making urban life more healthy and natural.

title: World's Largest Aircraft Completes Second Test Flight, Expected to Test Launch Ultrasound in Two Years

(Reuters) - The US aerospace company Stratolaunch Systems announced that the world ’ s largest aircraft, the Roc, has completed its second test flight on April 29, 2021, two years after its first test flight.
At 10: 00 a.m. EST on April 29 (10: 00 p.m. Taiwan time on April 29), Stratolaunch ’ s ultra-large aircraft successfully completed its second test flight at the Mojave Space Launch Center in California, USA, flying at an altitude of 14,000 feet (about 4.267 kilometers) and a top speed of 320 kilometers per hour, with a total flight time of 3 hours and 14 minutes.
Stratolaunch is pleased with the results of this test flight, which is intended to confirm the aircraft ’ s performance and capacity, as well as to review the results of a series of previous improvements.
Please continue reading...
The world ’ s largest aircraft, known as the Roc, is reportedly built with six engines and has a wingspan of 117 meters, longer than the length of a standard American football stadium (110 meters).
"Roc" was originally designed as a "small satellite launch platform", hoping to launch a rocket at an altitude of about 10 kilometers to send a satellite directly into space orbit. In the future, it is planned to be used as a launch platform for a hypersonic spacecraft.
In response to the successful completion of the test flight, Stratolaunch insiders said it was a major milestone in the development of "ultra-sonic" flight services.
It is reported that Stratolaunch is currently developing a reusable Talon-A polar sonic aircraft with a maximum speed of 6 Mach (more than 5 times the speed of sound), which can provide about 1 minute of polar sonic flight, and plans to carry Talon-A with "Roc" and ignite its liquid rocket booster in the air to launch and take off. Talon-A is expected to be completed in 2022. Testing begins in 2023.

title: Ten more trees is like a salary, 280,000 more trees, the happier they really are.
text:
Recently, research teams from universities around the world have been exploring the benefits of nature for humans, an area of research that has grown rapidly in recent years.
The positive impact of urban parks and gardens on mental health may not be as great as strong interpersonal relationships, but they can still quietly affect us and increase our resilience to stress.
Research shows that when we are in a green space, hostility and anxiety are reduced.
In addition, green space has the effect of improving mood and reducing mental fatigue.
In addition, it will change human behavior, encouraging us to exercise more and interact with our neighbors.
But while many studies have confirmed these effects, in many ways we are just beginning to understand the complex physical and mental responses to the natural environment.
The concept of “green nature ” can refer to a lawn, but complexity and diversity are important when it comes to nature ’ s effect of helping to restore vitality.
Ecologist Richard.
Richard Fuller conducted research in Sheffield, UK, and found a clear link between the benefits people get when they walk around the park and the biodiversity of the plants in the park.
The results of these studies tell us that the ancients' concept of "pastoral city" has its importance: when building urban parks and gardens, the more vibrant and natural the garden, the better the beneficial effect will be.
The city is very crowded, and we are very crowded in our hearts, but when we visit the park, we can expand our sense of psychological space.
A view of Da ’ an Forest Park in Taipei City.
If we want to promote the increase of green space in the city and improve public health, we must conduct quantitative research in groups, and this is not easy.
Fuller recently led a study in Brisbane, Australia, to explore the relationship between the number of visits people make to urban parks and their physical and mental health, but encountered some problems in the research process.
For example, healthier and wealthier people can choose and live in green areas with more green space.
With this in mind, Fuller ’ s team adjusted to use the large amount of data they collected to make a series of calculations to try to exclude major socio-economic factors known to affect health.
The results tell us that if everyone in Brisbane went to the park every week, the number of people with depression could be reduced by seven per cent and the number of people with high blood pressure could be reduced by nine per cent.
This is just a study of one city, but Fuller hopes other researchers will be able to do similar research in other parts of the world.
There is always a correlation between health and income, so the people most affected by social deprivation in a city tend to be the people with the worst mental health conditions.
There are many complex factors behind this, but a team led by Richard Mitchell from the Centre for Environmental, Social and Health Research at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh has conducted large-scale research in European cities to explore the relationship between social, economic and health disparities and community welfare facilities.
The researchers analyzed the shops, public transport, cultural facilities and green spaces provided by each district, with only one variable having a significant impact: the presence or absence of community parks and gardens.
After calculation, the research team believes that mental health inequality is related to low income, but if green space is provided to low-income households, it can improve the mental health of these people, and the improvement can be as high as 40%.
The numbers surprised the researchers, and Olmsted was right that the parks he designed did contribute to the health of low-income workers in the city.
Just planting a trail tree can affect people ’ s mental health.
Studies have also found that roadway trees can significantly affect how people feel about their lives.
Marc Berman, of the University of Chicago ’ s Environmental Neuroscience Laboratory, led the study on the distribution of street trees in Toronto ’ s residential areas and combined this information with the results of a questionnaire that asked residents to rate their health. After adjusting for data such as income, education, and work, the results showed that if there were only 10 more street trees in a metropolitan area, the psychological discomfort of residents in that area would be reduced. And the salary suddenly ten thousand US dollars (compiler: about NT $280,000) about the same.
It ’ s amazing to quantify nature ’ s wealth in this way, but if you let someone choose, most people should choose money instead of trees.
In addition to promoting mental health, green spaces and trees seem to reduce community violence and domestic violence.
University of Illinois ecologists Frances Kuo and William Sullivan have published several influential studies showing the effects of green space in the late 20th and early 21st centuries.
People living in resource-poor social housing communities in Chicago are full of green plants, while others are less.
Their research shows that people who are more exposed to green space are more hopeful, less likely to feel too helpless in their lives, and less likely to feel hostility and irritability at home.
In another study, Guo and Sullivan analyzed the incidence of theft and violent crime and found that such crimes were less common around nearby buildings with trees and gardens.
They also concluded from their calculations that building green spaces in areas where greenery is lacking could reduce crime by up to seven percent.
Gardens can attract people to go outside and make the community safer. They are also a kind of intermediary space where residents gather in the garden, interact with neighbors, tear down barriers between people, and help people build new friendships.
In cities, changing abandoned spaces and alienating spaces through greening can have an impact that cannot be underestimated.
The city is very crowded, and we are very crowded in our hearts, but when we visit the park, we can expand our sense of psychological space.
In the park, we can take a step back and think more clearly; when we leave the park, we will feel more free and less bound by the previous troubles.
This effect of the park is consistent with the brain changes measured in a study by the University of Washington School of Ecology.
Participants in the study were randomly divided into groups, one group walking alone in the park for 90 minutes and one group walking alone along the highway for 90 minutes.
Mental health scores improved in the park group, with much less anxiety or negative thoughts.
For your heart, let the plants heal.
The behavior of publishing houses providing repeated negative thoughts is related to the activity of the prefrontal cortex under the knee of the brain.
The research team used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to observe the brain activity of the subjects and found that in the park group, the blood flow to the lower knee prefrontal cortex was reduced, which was consistent with the meditation effect.
In the past, our hunter-gatherer ancestors walked in the natural environment and had to be completely focused on what was around them and carefully observe everything around them to be safe.
So from an evolutionary point of view, when we are in the natural environment, the brain should of course cut out the thoughts that make us anxious and promote a sense of relaxation and alertness — after all, we have a much lower chance of survival if we are trapped in a loop of negative thoughts.
(This article is from "Your Heart, Let the Plants Heal", which is published without permission.)

title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
text:
David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.
However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.
In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.
Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.
On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.
Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.
In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.
Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.
And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.
Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.
Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.
In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.
In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.
It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.
On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.
Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.
Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.
Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.
When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.
In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.
In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.
When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.
In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).
There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.
In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.
If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.
In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.
Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.
This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.
The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.
Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change.
Therefore, the calculated cost can only depend on the assumptions made, and it is very difficult to accurately grasp the costs of such things, such as melted permafrost, so it is extremely difficult to analyze the chart below.
Photo Credit: Business Week Publishing / Produced by Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Because of these high levels of uncertainty, it is very difficult to know exactly what climate protection measures should be taken and how much it should be interfered with from a purely economic point of view.
If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.
Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.
Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.
It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased.
Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse conclude that climate change is not a distant vision of the future, and that it represents more than just melting icebergs and rising sea levels, which are already threatening many people and their livelihoods.
In addition, it also shows that the temperature rise observed since the beginning of the industrial era is mainly due to man-made greenhouse gas emissions.
Fortunately, there ’ s also some ironic good news: we have the opportunity to influence the future of the climate, and we ’ re not completely powerless against climate change!
Climate model simulations show that as long as humans reduce greenhouse gas emissions, it is expected to limit the development of global warming.
Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produced a global average temperature forecast for greenhouse gas emissions, but since the United Nations Climate Conference (UN-Klimakonferenz) was first held in Berlin in 1995, global greenhouse gas emissions have risen by 50%, reaching a record high.
If human beings continue to produce large quantities of greenhouse gases, it is not impossible to imagine that global temperatures will rise by another 5 ° C by the end of the century.
Therefore, we must all be aware of our responsibility: how the future of the climate, and the extent to which the impact of global warming will worsen, is entirely in our hands!

title: When global temperatures rise by another 2 ° C, we will be forever separated from five foods: seafood, chocolate, wine, and more.
text:
In the face of the dramatic changes brought about by climate change, agriculture and food production can be said to be the first line of disaster. As the temperature increases year by year, ocean acidification and unusual extreme weather have had a great impact on the human diet structure.
Animal and plant ecology closely related to human diet, the impact of rising temperatures is far greater than expected.
In an analysis published on January 14, 2021, NASA said that the 2020 surface temperature was the highest in history at the same time as 2016, pointing to the past 10 years as the hottest period in history.
In 2020, the global average annual temperature rose by more than 1.02 ° C compared with the average temperature from 1951 to 1980.
Even if there is a global consensus that we should try to control carbon dioxide emissions, according to NASA analysis, even if the COVID-19 epidemic swept the world in 2020, industrial, agricultural and other industries have been affected and reduced production, and the number of air and shipping flights has also been significantly reduced. Average temperatures are also forecast to continue to climb in 2021.
Surface temperature records from the Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) instrument on NASA ’ s Aqua satellite confirm that NASA ’ s GISTEMP database over the past seven years is the warmest on record: Rising temperatures will wipe out five foods. This refers to the total greenhouse gas emissions from the food life cycle, starting with raw materials, production processes, transportation, and more.
The following five products are food types with a high carbon footprint: 1. Wheat and wheat as an important staple food source for human beings, due to climate change, there are more challenges in cultivation, including rising temperatures year by year, decreasing rainfall and growing plant diseases and pests.
According to a 2019 study by the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center, a nonprofit organization, ongoing climate change and drought will affect 60% of the world ’ s wheat production, potentially triggering food shortages and famine in the future.
Maple syrup is a representative agricultural product in North America, which can be almost directly equated with Canada, and the production of maple syrup, including sugar content and the flow of syrup, is highly correlated with temperature and rainfall.
According to relevant research, the rising temperature until 2100, the entire maple sugar harvest season will be one month ahead of schedule, and the sugar content will decline by 0.7 ° Brix, so far as Canada's maple sugar industry is facing a decline in production.
3, seafood due to the rise in global carbon dioxide content, seawater acidity is constantly increasing, the current acidity value of seawater compared with before industrialization, has been 25% higher.
Coupled with rising temperatures, marine life is also facing changes in its physiological structure.
At present, relevant research has pointed out that marine organisms that have been exposed to acidified seawater for a long time have had direct and indirect effects related to physiology, such as bone changes and metabolic changes.
The study also pointed out that such a mutation will become a genetic inheritance of marine life, and as the temperature continues to rise, marine life may die due to poor adaptation, or the destruction of the original habitat of the sea, resulting in the depletion of fishing.
4, chocolate Although the raw material of chocolate "cocoa" is a drought-tolerant crop, it can withstand the high temperature of the festival, but the cocoa tree can not withstand the resulting lack of water.
By 2050, the average temperature in West Africa is likely to increase by more than 2 ° C, and in a state of limited rainfall, cocoa trees will expel the necessary water from their bodies to sustain life.
In short, without a stable source of water, cocoa production will decline, and the price of chocolate will rise in the future.
5, wine the most direct impact on grape production factors, including climate, soil and grape varieties, all factors combined will constitute a complete cultivation system. Temperature and water affect the maturity of grapes, grape yield and quality, when the grape yield and quality changes, it may fluctuate to the price.
According to a 2010 study, if temperatures rise by more than 2 ° C by 2100, 56% of the world ’ s grape growing areas will be destroyed.
This is not imaginary, it is happening. In mid-March 2021, the temperature in parts of France soared to 26 ° C, and suddenly the high temperature caused the grapes in the French vineyards to start to blossom early, and by the beginning of April, the temperature suddenly dropped to -7 ° C, which was followed by frost freezing, and 80% of the vineyards in France were severely affected. This year, the harvest of French grapes may reach a record low due to climate change.
The French Federation of Agriculture (FNSEA) believes that this spring frost is not only a threat to viticulture, but also to tree cultivation, and the impact of these two will bring about a loss of nearly 3 billion euros (NT $101 billion).
Not only the food crisis, but also the survival challenge of the whole human race "only" to rise by 2 ° C, it may sound like the human body's feelings may not be great, but behind it is a larger problem and challenge, environmental changes are affecting the global food ecosystem.
The reasons that affect these things are related to human life habits and habits, and carbon emissions from large to the entire supply chain, small to the use of automobiles and motorcycles, will have an impact on the environment and harm.
When all of humanity works together to reduce carbon emissions, it is possible to contribute to the current environmental crisis facing the planet.

title: Arab countries support Palestinian Trump-Trump peace deal "broken"?
text:
(Getty Images) Israel ’ s bombardment of Gaza has killed more than 100 people. (Getty Images) The deadliest war in recent years between Israel and the Palestinians has seen a surge in Palestinian deaths and a wave of outcry from many countries in the Middle East, including the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Bahrain, which signed the Abraham Accord last September under former President Donald Trump to normalize relations with Israel.
Whether the Middle East peace deal, seen by Trump as a major diplomatic achievement and the complete marginalisation of Palestine, has “failed ” has attracted much attention.
Analysts point out that the Middle East ’ s anger at this time has seriously overturned the central assumption of the Abraham Accord: “The Arab world no longer cares about the suffering of the Palestinians, but is content to let its own government embrace Israel based on other common interests. ” Tareq Baconi, an analyst at the International Crisis Group, said that the Middle East peace agreement signed under the Trump administration, Take the view that the Palestinians will not act; but now, the situation has changed and“ the Palestinians are moving. ”
Demonstrations in solidarity with the Palestinians have taken place, including in Bahrain and Morocco, which signed an agreement with Israel last year.
As for Saudi Arabia, which had previously suggested that its relationship with Israel was heating up because both Saudi Arabia and Israel had to face Iran as a common enemy, the tone of comments in pro-government newspapers in Saudi Arabia has suddenly shifted, accusing Israel of “criminal acts ” against the Palestinians and drawing parallels between Israel and Iran.
The “Abrahamic Agreement, ” signed at the White House in September last year, fully or partially normalizes Israel ’ s relations with the Arab League, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco; Trump claimed the agreement would“ change the course of history ” and “this is a bloodless Middle East peace. ”
Critics point out that some of the agreements were made by authoritarian governments that did not truly represent the people, and that the United States offered incentives like bribes to those governments to nodded and sign.
As for the Palestinians, the agreement is a dangerous milestone as Arab governments abandon a peace initiative first proposed by Saudi Arabia decades ago that requires Arab states to normalize full relations with Israel only if a peace agreement is reached between Israel and the Palestinians.

title: Stanford University draws new city model to encourage walking, cycling
text:
Researchers at Stanford University have combined decades of public health information and urban landscapes to create new models of cities. (Photo: courtesy of Stanford University) New research from Stanford University shows that trees along the street can encourage people to spend more time walking or cycling to work, and people can use these natural environments to exercise and improve their health.
To this end, researchers at the University of History have combined decades of public health information and urban landscapes to create new urban models that, through new planning, can lead people to live healthier lives.
The study, published in the National Academy of Sciences, describes how people can improve their health by exercising directly in cities through natural resources.
According to the study, Americans often lack exercise and other physical activities, resulting in $117 billion a year in related medical costs.
Globally, 3.2 million people die from illness due to lack of exercise.
Therefore, how people can increase their sports opportunities is also an important well-being.
Roy Remme, an environmental scientist at Stanford University, said that 2020 coincides with the epidemic, and in the prevention of the epidemic at home, we have learned how precious and valuable it is for city residents to spend time outdoors in nature.
Therefore, urban planners should review the creation of green space in the city, which not only supports people's health, but also allows everyone to benefit from nature.
He said that the research team combined decades of public health research with information such as the benefits of nature to city residents, and simultaneously considered the planning of dog walking, jogging, cycling, gardening activities, and considering the security and feasibility of urban greening, and established a model framework for the city to create a natural state in the city to make people's bodies better.
According to Gretchen Daily, senior author of the Stanford Natural Capital Project, living in nature can enhance memory, attention and creativity, as well as happiness, while also increasing social engagement and meaning in life.
Nature also stimulates physical activity, reduces cancer risk, boosts metabolism, and makes other body functions more effective.
As the world becomes more urbanized and city-centric, the ability to easily access natural resources is becoming less and less, says Daley.
The problem is even more acute, especially in communities where there is an explosion of residential capacity.
So how to identify these overburdened communities, communities that lack natural resources, and try to solve the problem to provide people with a more valuable way of life has become a new challenge.

title: Federal appeals court upholds Monsanto herbicide cancer-causing award of $25.2 million
text:
(Getty Images) A federal appeals court today upheld a ruling in a Bay Area lawsuit against Roundup, the world ’ s best-known herbicide maker, Monsanto, to pay damages to a Bay Area man who died of cancer after using Roundup for more than 26 years. The man was $25.2 million.
This is the first federal decision in thousands of Monsanto lawsuits.
The Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco said that the evidence presented in the case of Edwin Hardeman, a Bay Area man, supported the jury ’ s findings, while Monsanto deliberately downplayed and ignored calls to test Roundup for cancer risk.
However, a judge objected, saying the amount of compensation should be reduced to $10.4 million.
Hardman lawyer David Wool said the ruling was a victory for consumers around the world.
Monsanto ’ s parent company, Bayer AG, said it was disappointed, stressing that its products were safe and would seek a review by the U.S. Supreme Court.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency considers Roundup and its main ingredient glyphosate to be safe and allows it to be marketed without warning labels.
However, in 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer, affiliated with the International Health Organization (WHO), concluded that gafossa is carcinogenic.
(Getty Images) The 72-year-old Hardman began using Roundup when he lived in Gualala, Mendocino County, and continued using it after moving to Santa Rosa, Bay Area.
He was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma in 2015.
After four years of chemotherapy and other treatments, doctors say his condition has eased, but he will have a higher risk of cancer in the future.
After finding that Roundup was a substantial cause of Hardman ’ s cancer, a federal court in San Francisco in July 2019 ordered Monsanto to pay Hardman $5.2 million and $75 million in punitive damages to Monsanto ’ s sales office for knowingly unsafe products.
However, federal judge Vince Chhabria reduced the amount of punitive damages to $20 million on the 14th.
In most cases, he said, the Supreme Court limits punitive damages to four times the amount of the party ’ s compensation.

title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
text:
OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.
On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".
The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.
Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”
The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”
"This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.
The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).
They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.
A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.
Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.
The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.
Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.
The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near the Iranian capital of Tehran on January 8, 2020, killing all 176 passengers and crew, including 55 Canadian citizens and 30 permanent residents.
On the 20th, a court in Ontario, Canada, based on written evidence provided by the family, ruled that Iran ’ s actions were deliberate “terrorism. ” Judge Edward Belobaba declared that under the National Immunity Act, the Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act and the Criminal Code,“ the plaintiff ’ s allegation is true, and the defendant ’ s shooting down of PS752 with a missile is a deliberate act of terrorism. ”
The Iranian government initially denied the accusation, but admitted on the third day after the crash that the missile was an inadvertent "catastrophic mistake" by Iranian forces who mistakenly identified the aircraft as a hostile target on high alert prior to the confrontation with the United States.
The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, states that Iran deliberately used missiles to attack the protests in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps Quds Force.
The judge has not yet made a final decision on the amount of compensation, and will continue to discuss it at a future hearing. In the first lawsuit, the family of the victim asked for up to 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion) in compensation.

title: Bayer to reconsider Roundup Herbicide Formulation for U.S. Consumers
text:
Bayer AG (BAYRY) said it will evaluate whether to continue to use the active ingredient in its popular Roundup herbicide in the U.S. residential supplies market.
On Wednesday, Bayer's attempts to limit future liability for whether the product could cause cancer suffered a setback in court.
Bayer said it would pay up to $9.6 billion in damages to settle an existing Roundup case related to non-Hodgkin lymphoma and another $2 billion for future claims.
The German company lost three lawsuits filed between 2018 and 2019 by Roundup users who said the product caused them to develop cancer, and the company is working to resolve about 125,000 similar claims.
Bayer is seeking to resolve future cases in a novel form of class-action settlement that seeks to involve Roundup users who have used Roundup but are not yet sick, and those who have cancer but are yet to be prosecuted.
U.S. District Court Judge Vince...

title: Monsanto ’ s $2 Billion Settlement Rejected
text:
San Francisco federal judge dismisses Monsanto Co.
Proposed $2 billion settlement.
The latter originally intended to reach a settlement with cancer victims who used Roundup herbicide to file a class action lawsuit, but was rejected by a judge on the 26th, arguing that the content of the settlement proposal would not be helpful to people who may be diagnosed with cancer in the future because of the use of Roundup.
More than 100,000 people nationwide with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and other cancers have sued Monsanto and its parent company Bayer AG.
However, the company cites multiple investigations by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), stating that Roundup is the most widely used herbicide in the world and is safe and can be legally sold without warning labels.
However, the International Association for Research on Cancer, a branch of the World Health Organization (WHO), said in 2015 that Roundup ’ s main ingredient is glyphosate, which is a possible cause of cancer in humans.
As a result of this discovery and other scientific evidence, three Bay Area juries awarded tens of millions of dollars in damages to cancer victims. On May 14, a federal appeals court awarded $25.2 million to a Sonoma man.
He has been spraying Roundup herbicide for 26 years and has been diagnosed with cancer.
Bayer also proposed a $9.6 billion settlement, hoping to settle pending litigation.
At present, about two-thirds of the cases have been resolved. The $2 billion settlement proposal that was rejected on the 26th was originally intended to settle the lawsuit that may be filed by herbicide users in the future.
Federal Judge Vince Chhabria said the settlement proposal was “clearly unreasonable ” for Roundup users who had not yet been diagnosed with cancer.
He noted that non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a potentially fatal lymphoma with a typical incubation period of 10-15 years, so four years of medical monitoring is of limited value for potential victims.
By the time they are diagnosed with cancer, the proposed compensation fund may have run out.
Thus, an independent panel to evaluate glyphosate seems a more reasonable proposal, but Monsanto has “lost the battle of experts ” in all three trials, including the case before the federal court in Sumatra.
Require the plaintiff to waive punitive damages in future litigation and reduce leverage in settlement negotiations.
In response to the ruling, Bayer said it would re-evaluate the future of glyphosate products in the U.S. residential market and reconsider the proposed settlement.
San Francisco attorney Elizabeth Cabraser, who agreed on the proposed settlement, was disappointed by the ruling and remains convinced that the settlement proposal could provide significant financial, health and safety benefits to Roundup users.
However, Bill Greese, scientific director of the nonprofit Center for Food Safety, believes the settlement will limit Bayer / Monsanto ’ s liability for cancer-causing herbicides, leaving many herbicide users in trouble.

title: Earth ’ s “artificial sun ” set a new record for nuclear fusion at 120 million ° C for 101 seconds
text:
▲ Total Superconducting Tokamak Nuclear Fusion Experiment (EAST). (Photo / Xinhua News Agency) reporter Cai Shaojian / Comprehensive report The Hefei Institute of Material Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China successfully achieved the new world record of "Artificial Sun" Total Superconducting Tokamak Nuclear Fusion Experiment (EAST) running at 120 million ° C for 101 seconds on the morning of the 28th.
The new record further demonstrates the feasibility of nuclear fusion energy and lays the physical and engineering foundation for commercial use, the researchers said.
According to the Guangming Daily, the fully superconducting tokamak nuclear fusion experimental device (EAST) is known as the "artificial sun", and the Hefei Institute of Material Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences successfully realized the reproducible operation of 120 million ° C101 seconds and 160 million ° C20 seconds plasma in the early morning of the 28th.
The report mentioned that the Plasma Institute of Hefei Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences launched the upgrade and transformation of the EAST device in June last year, and the upgrade and transformation of the device has comprehensively improved the performance of the device in a year.
The report pointed out that the realization of the 1.2 ° C 101-second plasma operation has increased the world record of 100 million ° C20 seconds achieved by the physical experiment of the EAST device last year by a factor of five, indicating a major breakthrough in the comprehensive research capacity of the EAST device.
The report mentioned that continuous steady state operation under the condition of hundreds of millions of ° C high temperature plasma is a necessary condition for future fusion power generation. At present, the EAST device is the only magnetic confinement nuclear fusion experimental device in the world with a heating method and a filter structure similar to ITER, and is the only experimental device that can fully demonstrate and verify the scientific research of ITER in the next 400 seconds.
The report pointed out that nuclear fusion energy has outstanding advantages such as abundant resources, no carbon emissions and clean and safe, and is one of the ideal clean energy sources for the future of mankind, which can make an important contribution to achieving carbon neutrality.
The two major difficulties in achieving nuclear fusion power generation are how to achieve hundreds of millions of ° C ignition and plasma stable long-term confinement control, and at the same time to achieve hundreds of millions of ° C plasma long-term maintenance is particularly difficult, which requires the hundreds of millions of ° C plasma and minus 269 ° C superconducting magnets, high thermal load plasma, wall materials interaction, and high integration under extreme conditions such as dynamic precision control. The organic combination, the difficulty and the challenge are very large, and the maximum duration of the plasma operation in excess of 100 million ° C in the world before is 20 seconds.
The report stressed that the results of this physical experiment are the verification of a series of key technologies that must be adopted in future fusion reactors such as the first all-metal active water-cooled wall, high-performance tungsten filter, stable high-power wave heating, and plasma positional precision control for the first time in the world.

title: Food and climate: which foods you love are at risk of extinction, and how do you deal with them?
text:
Food and Climate: Which foods you love are at risk of extinction, and how do you deal with them?
59 minutes ago Image source, Getty Images Image annotated text, bananas are people's favorite fruit, but bananas face the threat of fungal disease.
We are used to picking out food items from all over the world in our stores.
But have you ever wondered what would happen if your favorite ingredients became scarce?
Two-fifths of the world ’ s plants are at risk of extinction, according to a new report from the Royal Botanic Gardens, which has a significant impact on our food materials.
There are more than 7,000 edible plants in the world, but we often eat relatively few foods, only 15, but they account for 90% of the global calorie intake.
Moreover, farming is concentrated on only a few commercial varieties.
You may feel like you don ’ t have to worry about food that we don ’ t eat very much or that we have enough.
But all plants are part of the ecosystem.
With plant habitats disappearing (mainly due to farming) or under pressure from climate change, it is difficult to predict the impact it will have on human food security.
And concerns about some of our favorite ingredients highlight a series of pressing environmental issues.
People are also looking for solutions and solutions to move forward.
First, let ’ s look at what foods are at risk of extinction.
Wheat: Staples at risk of climate change?
Image Source, Getty Images Images Image annotated with text, wheat is the main ingredient in bread and pasta.
Wheat is one of the staple foods of many countries around the world.
In the United Kingdom, for example, wheat production has declined significantly due to climate change.
Wheat is the most important grain in the UK, and the flour, bread, pasta and other staple foods on the shelves rely on wheat.
But warmer, wetter and worse weather conditions brought about by climate change have made life harder for wheat farmers.
The autumn of 2019 was too wet and it was very difficult to sow wheat. The spring of 2020 was also extremely dry, and the lack of rain on wheat sown in the spring resulted in a decline of nearly 18% in the UK wheat harvest in 2020.
As a result of climate change, extreme weather such as droughts and floods are becoming more frequent, said Robert Roberts, head of the British Farmers Federation.
These extreme weather conditions pose challenges for growers on the front lines of wheat production.
Wheat will continue to be the main crop in the UK, but farmers will have to change their farming practices, for example by rotating wheat with other crops, Roberts said.
Also, look for other plant protein varieties, such as soybeans, peas, and other legumes.
These all play a role in people ’ s healthy eating.
But in relatively poor countries, crop uncertainty can also lead to political unrest, as well as disease and famine.
Four billion people depend on three main crops: rice, maize and wheat.
In response, Britain ’ s environment minister, Lord Goldsmith, warned that a large-scale pest could destroy all of these crops, so people need to be resilient and sustainable.
So what can you do?
You can change your diet and eat more cereals and a variety of beans in addition to bread, which is part of a healthy diet.
Bananas: This popular fruit is at risk of disease Image source, Getty Images image annotated with text, the future of the banana is worrying.
In the UK, people eat 100 bananas a year.
But there is only one species in the global banana export market: Cavendish, which is increasingly vulnerable to the devastating Panamanian fungus disease.
This has happened before too.
The Rice Seven Banana (also known as the Big Mike banana, the Gros Michel or "Big Mike") was formerly a major commercial banana variety.
It is said to taste more banana.
But in the 1950s it was swept away by the same fungal disease.
Today, this deadly fungus is still present and has spread to wild bananas.
It also affects another staple food, plantain.
Kew ’ s Millennium Seed Bank in the UK may provide a solution to the problem of banana disease. Kew ’ s Seed Bank is the world ’ s largest wild seed bank.
Kew ’ s partners in Vietnam and Malaysia have been collecting seeds from 80 species of wild bananas around the world, storing them in seed banks and sending them to banana growers to develop new varieties that are more resistant to disease.
All of our ingredients are modified to make them either more productive, larger, better shaped or colourful, says Dr. Kirk, an expert at the Churchill Adaptation Agriculture Program.
But in doing so, they lose some of the most important features of plants that make them more resilient to climate change and other problems.
Wild varieties of these improved crops are better able to survive and adapt to harsh external environments.
One of the problems with modern ingredients is that we rely on too few types and varieties, which is not limited to fruits and our favorite bananas.
For example, the UK has excellent climatic conditions for growing apples and pears.
As long as you look carefully, there are actually many different species.
In addition, there are many varieties of berries that, although not seasonal fruits, can be picked and frozen at the peak of the season, and they are often worth the price.
Honey: Do bees get hungry?
Image source, Getty Images Image annotated text, in recent years, the decline in bee population has caused concern.
We rely on bees to pollinate crops and provide us with honey. Bees are small, but their impact on our plate meal is huge.
According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, a third of our food crops rely on insect pollination, in which bees play an important role.
However, it is estimated that one in 10 insects is at risk of extinction.
Bees have also made headlines in the United States because of the rapid disappearance of adult bee populations (colony collapse syndrome).
The “Lost Bees ” video tells people that people in China have to resort to artificial pollination because of the disappearance of bee colonies.
According to Ms. Lewis of Sustainable Beekeeping UK, lack of food is a major problem for all bee colonies, including bees.
She says that a single crop (growing the same crop year after year on a piece of land) leaves the colony with little food to feed on.
At the same time, habitat loss, overcrowding in urban hives, and weakened insect immune systems have reduced their ability to resist various shock waves, including pesticides, parasites, and various diseases, all contributing to the decline in bee population.
Despite this, the number of hives around the world continues to grow (currently 92 million), and people replace those who are sick and dead by breeding more bees.
The problem, however, is that starving bees themselves pose a threat to other insects, including wild pollinators, an important part of nature.
So what can we do?
The answer is to protect different habitats and plant some of the bees' favorite flowers and grasses in their own gardens; beekeepers should also consider the location of the hive when choosing the location of the hive to avoid placing the hive in a place where the diversity of pollinators is already threatened.
In addition, when buying honey, be careful not to buy honey that has the word "mixed" on the logo.
This means beekeepers are more concerned with local identity than just producing goods.
Cocoa: Will Drought and Global Warming Lead to Big Cuts?
Image Source, Getty Images Images Images Images with annotated text can be the raw material for making chocolate.
Tropical cocoa trees are at the forefront of global warming.
Global warming is particularly worrying for tropical crops, not just because cocoa trees are a source of chocolate.
According to the International Centre for Tropical Agriculture, drought and lack of moisture will prevent cocoa from growing in parts of the West African region (which accounts for 70% of the world ’ s chocolate sources) unless farmers adopt a more sustainable approach.
One of the biggest concerns, explained Geaton, founder of the World Cocoa Foundation, is the change in precipitation.
Almost all cocoa trees are watered by rain, and even minor weather disturbances can affect cocoa production and harvest season, says Gayton.
Also, single planting is common, leading to soil degradation.
Soil degradation, on the other hand, makes land more vulnerable to drought and crop failure.
As large producers recognize this problem, there is a global trend towards more sustainable cocoa production, especially in the artisanal chocolate sector.
This segment currently accounts for an estimated 10-12% of the chocolate market share.
Gatton says artisanal chocolate companies, including his, are working to promote agroforestry or agroforestry — a way to combine land use between forestry and agriculture.
This method helps protect fragile soil and provides shade for cocoa trees.
But he said this method must be used with caution to ensure trees grow with enough sunlight.
At the same time, keep the temperature cool to provide the best growing conditions with enough moisture.
Cody, a British chocolate expert, says that mixed planting conditions in tropical rainforests are very effective for sustainability and organic production.
This means that growers have to focus on soil fertility.
And those who are involved in the whole process of making chocolate are usually small businesses, and they pay more attention to the source of cocoa.
As a consumer, you can try to buy organic chocolate, it is not always as expensive as we think.
Tuna: Will we be out of stock?
Image source, Getty Images Images Image annotated text, you can eat more other fish.
Large fish such as tuna are at the top of the food chain, and overfishing can affect marine ecology.
According to the latest UN report on the state of the world ’ s fisheries and aquaculture, nearly 94% of the world ’ s fish resources are either completely or overexploited.
The canned bonito and yellow-fin tuna we usually buy are two of the top 10 fish caught in the world.
We need to be careful not to catch too much.
The Blue Ocean Foundation recently highlighted the problem of tuna fishing in the Indian Ocean, but the problem is global.
Atlantic bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, and bigeye tuna (also known as bigeye tuna) are all declining, raising serious concerns about future fish resources.
Bonito is considered more viable due to its smaller size and faster reproduction.
In addition to the species and location, the way of fishing is also important.
The most common method of net fishing is to catch young goldfinned goldfish.
This affects the reproduction and sustainability of the fish.
Rattle of the Blue Ocean Foundation said that the fishing rod and line method is better because it is semi-manual, like the hand-fishing method, and the fish is caught one by one.
She warned that if fish resources were in trouble, there would be no way to catch fish.
In addition, eating large fish such as tuna can also bring other problems.
These fish are predators and have an unknown impact on organisms at the bottom of the food chain, Rattle said.
As consumers, we can find more detailed information about specific fisheries in the Marine Conservation Society ’ s Guide to Sustainable Seafood Fish.
At the same time, you can check the origin and sustainability information of tuna canned or packaged foods.
Sales of tuna canned fish soared during the UK lockdown.
Instead of eating tuna cans, try sardines or mackerel cans or other fish, especially those that are less common and cheaper.
What can we do?
Many environmental issues are related to the importance of dietary diversity and the benefits of sustainable agriculture and fisheries.
We are used to eating the same things over and over again.
But in fact, we can find many alternative ingredients that are equally cheap or even cheaper.
Small changes in dietary structure, such as eating more plant protein and eating less meat and fish, can help reduce costs.
To ensure the safety of the ingredients we love, the whole environment, not just the farms, is very important, because different habitats have wild relatives of the commercial crops we eat, and many other plants that may be useful to us in the future.
Professor Antonelli, director of science at Kew Gardens, said it was like a “treasure ”.
But he warned that we are losing this “treasure ” due to the destruction of the natural environment and the interconnected networks between plants, insects and animals.
At the end of the day, we rely on nature to provide us with food.
David Attenborough made clear on the BBC programme Extinction Truth that the dangers of the planet will affect our daily lives.
From a single pond to a rainforest, everything is interconnected, says Attenborough.
“We think we ’ re not in it, but we ’ re part of it and depend on it, ” he said.
As environmental problems worsen, the sustainability of farming and food has become a necessity.
We need to change our thinking and eat more of what the earth can provide for us, rather than what we want to eat and want to eat.
Standing in such a different position, we can ensure the safety of the food supply through our own basket and dishes.

title: 120 million degrees of combustion 101 seconds land "artificial sun" new record
text:
In the process of exploring fusion reactors, Lu reached another milestone, and the "artificial sun" of the Hefei Institute of Materials of the Chinese Academy of Sciences successfully achieved a new record of 120 million degrees Celsius burning for 101 seconds, five times the original record.
The comprehensive land media report said that the fully superconducting tokamak nuclear fusion experimental device (EAST) of the Hefei Institute of Materials of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has successfully achieved repeatable 120 million degrees centigrade and 101 seconds of plasma operation.
The report said that it also successfully achieved 160 million degrees Celsius in 20 seconds of plasma operation.
EAST previously held a record of 100 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.
This experiment means that land scientists have made the duration of extreme heat five times the original.
These facilities are part of the exploration of continental fusion reactors, and they offer hope for limitless clean energy on land.
However, there are still many challenges to overcome.
For the world ’ s scientists, this is a journey of discovery that has been going on for decades.
In fact, similar studies are being conducted in the United States, Europe, Russia, and South Korea.
China is also one of more than 30 countries participating in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.
So-called “artificial suns ” because they are designed to replicate the nuclear fusion reactions that power the Sun.
During this reaction, a lot of energy is released.
To do this on Earth, scientists need to achieve extreme heat and keep it for longer.
Despite the progress made, there is still a long way to go to make fusion reactors a reality.
It is understood that the ITER project in southern France has been postponed several times, with the latest target being the generation of plasma by 2025. In February, the European Union pledged new funding for this, and China Nuclear Group will participate in the installation of the core equipment of ITER.
