title: Middle East drama: Saudi Arabia, Turkey fight for TV audience
text:
By Paul Law Last updated: 2021-06-03 13: 00 Turkey has been a soft power powerhouse in the Middle East for more than a decade, and its TV series have swept the entire Arab region.
Last year, local dramas became the annual hit in the Arab region, including “The Ambassador ’ s Daughter ” in Saudi Arabia,“ You Knock on My Door, ” which was popular with Arab audiences, and “Miracle Doctor, ” which was adapted from a Korean drama. It is also a good word.
In the face of the threat of domestic drama, Saudi Arabia, another big brother in the Arab world, naturally does not dare to ignore it. In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.
Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?
With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.
The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.
Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.
Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.
Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.
Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.
These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.
(Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.
However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.
Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.
The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.
As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.
Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.
Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.
“Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.
(Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.
At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.
The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.
To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.
It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.
Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.
In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.
All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.
Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.
The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.
Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.
Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.
The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).
The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.
On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.
Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.
In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.
Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.
Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.
According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television.
Currently, the industry ’ s main funding and artistic support comes from three government funding agencies: the King Abdulaziz Center for World Cultures, the Film and Television Commission of the Cultural Affairs Bureau, and the Red Sea Film Festival.
Saudi director Hana Alomair said: "We are hungry for more, we are still talking about government support, investors have not yet taken concrete action."
She added that the increase in the number of cinemas should help encourage investment.
Crown Prince Mohammed has been actively developing the Saudi film and television industry in recent years.
In fact, Saudi Arabia is vigorously developing the film and television industry and shooting high-quality television series. In addition to economic reform factors, it also hopes to shape the national image through the film and television industry, promote its own views and values, and avoid the Turkish side's monopoly on the Middle East.
This is clearly due to the fact that over the past decade or so, Turkey has successfully capitalized on its soft power advantages by investing heavily in the film and television industry.
UAE producer Y u s e r Hareb, who works with Saudi Arabia, believes that Saudi Arabia is developing the film and television industry to create alternative options to offset the impact of local dramas on Arabs.
He believes that the Ottoman period was not honorable for the Arabs, even a "dark period", full of repression and criminal acts against the Arabs.
The Saudi and Emirati works are intended to break Turkey ’ s cultural influence in the region by telling “true Arab history ” that the Ottomans were neither protectors nor revivalists of Muslims.
Saudi Arabia also wants to export its cultural influence through the film and television industry. (Getty) The Saudi “drama ” is that both sides want to influence the Middle East by promoting their national characteristics and culture, and both countries ’ film and television industries want to beautify history and influence audiences, especially in which countries should be praised and reprimanded.
However, Saudi Arabia ’ s development of the film and television industry is short of fashion, and it seems difficult to say whether it can resist Turkish influence on a regional and global scale with its film and television works.

title: One minute to see the world _ Israel changes days, Trump returns, the Olympic Games countdown 50 days

text:
Home Secretary Priti Patel has ordered major social media platforms such as Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, Instagram and YouTube to remove posts that “glorify ” illegal entry into the UK across the Channel.
In her strongly-worded letter, Ms Pang demanded that these social media sites stop being used as propaganda tools to lure as many people as she had never seen before to cross the Channel dangerously.
People Snake Group used these social networking sites to promote illegal crossing of the English Channel by boat and forgery of passports and visa services. One video showing people crossing the Channel from Calais, France, to Dover, UK, was viewed by 800,000 people on TikTok.
In her letter, Ms Pang warned: “It is totally unacceptable that posts advocating or even glorifying these deadly and illegal crossings, whether by boat or by hiding behind the back of a lorry, are published. ”
She said the posts did not mention how many people were buried in the sea while trying to cross the channel, or had to endure a 13-hour storm in uncomfortable dinghies on the icy surface of the sea.
In her letter, Ms Pang made a strong appeal: “These advertisements directly lead to casualties, and I urge you to do everything in your power to promptly and proactively remove posts about illegal crossings of the Straits so as to prevent more men, women and young children from being killed in the Straits or in the process of illegal entry. ”
At least 4,300 people have crossed the Channel illegally into the UK so far this year, including more than 1,000 last week.
Last year, a total of 8,400 people entered the UK this way, and this year the number is expected to be even higher.

title: 1 year old refugee carcasses washed ashore! Wreck in English Channel disappears, floats to Norway in February
text:
▲ Iranian Kurdish boy Artin (Artin) is only 1 year old, and his family took the risk of crossing the English Channel, unfortunately drowned in a shipwreck.
(Photo / Reuters) - The body of a baby boy was found on a beach on Kam Island in southeastern Norway on January 1. After months of investigation, local police announced on the 7th that the identity of the dead was that of a 1-year-old Iranian Kurdish boy, Artin, who died in the English Channel shipwreck in October last year.
It is reported that the family had spent three or four days in the refugee camp in Dunkerque, France, before venturing across the sea to try to enter Britain; Artemis has also been described as a beloved "happy baby".
Norwegian police officer Camilla Tjelle Waage said the authorities had not received reports of the baby missing and no family had contacted the police. "Blue baby clothing is not a Norwegian brand, meaning the baby is not Norwegian."
The University of Oslo forensics department managed to find matching DNA data and, after months of efforts, finally identified the deceased.
According to reports, Yatin ’ s relatives have been informed that the baby ’ s body will be returned to Iran for burial.
▲ Artin ’ s body was found on a beach in southeastern Norway on January 1. (Photo / Reuters) Artin ’ s family from the western Iranian city of Sardasht, whose father, Rasul Iran Nezhad, was a low-paid worker and his wife, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, was unemployed. At least 100 pounds (about NT $3931), but also find a place to live, so I hope to bring my family to the UK to start a new life.
The family tried to enter the UK by train, but failed twice, so they found a smuggling group, paid at least 5,000 euros (nearly NT $170,000), entered Turkey from Iran in the summer of 2020, and then crossed Europe to France, carrying three children and 23 other people across the English Channel in a small fishing boat.
The bodies of Nizhad, his wife, his nine-year-old daughter, and his six-year-old son were found, but Yatin was missing at the time and listed as missing.
▲ Attien ’ s family tried to go to England to start a new life, but all of them died. (Photo / hengaw.net) French prosecutors are investigating in Dunkirk, where officials found the bodies of 19 people, including relatives of Attien, in the water.
But Iran ’ s Kurdistan Hengaw Organization for Human Rights said there should be 28 people on board, meaning more are still missing.
The Kurds are located in the border mountains of Turkey, Iraq, Syria, Iran and Armenia, with a population of about 25 million to 35 million. They are the fourth largest ethnic group in the Middle East, but they have never established a nation-state.

title: International briefing ｜ New Year 's Day in Norway, the identity of the child washed ashore, confirmed _ Australian power company sued Greenpeace, lost _ Mexican journalist murder case again committed _ rare double eagle gold coins broke records _ Apple Daily
text:
The body of a child washed ashore on New Year ’ s Day in Norway confirmed that Norwegian police found the body of a young child on the shore on New Year ’ s Day this year, and after months of investigation by the authorities, it was confirmed that it was an Iranian Kurdish boy, Artin Irannezhad, who was only one year old and three months old.
In October last year, he and his family were killed when the speedboat sank in the English Channel in an attempt to smuggle them from France to Britain.
After his body was found on the island of Karmoy in southwestern Norway, police conducted DNA tests to identify him as Artin Irannezhad.
Police said in a statement on Monday that five members of the Artin family had been smuggled into the UK from France through the British Channel and that the speedboat sank on October 27 last year.
The Norwegian police later found Artin's aunt in Norway, who described her feelings as mixed, "happy to finally find Artin's body, but also sad that he left us".
Artin's body will be transferred to Iran for burial.
Greenpeace launched a campaign last month against AGL Energy, Australia ’ s largest electricity supplier, for being the largest source of environmental pollution in the region and for using each other ’ s company logo in posters, social posts and placards. AGL has filed a lawsuit against Greenpeace for violating copyright and trademark laws, the Federal Court of Sydney ruled on Tuesday.
Greenpeace mocks AGL, which mainly produces electricity from coal, but claims to be a leading investor in renewable energy, using the AGL logo in its manifesto and lambasting AGL as “Australia ’ s Greatest Liability ”.
Justice Stephen Burley ruled that in the vast majority of cases, Greenpeace ’ s use of AGL ’ s logo was clearly ironic, described as “dark humor ”, did not infringe copyright and refused AGL ’ s claim for compensation.
Katrina Bullock, a Greenpeace lawyer, said Tuesday ’ s ruling was a victory for free speech and set an important legal precedent for copyright laws that protect the freedom of speech of advocacy groups, satirists or anyone who can criticize or satirize the group. Greenpeace will continue its campaign to pressure AGL to shut down its three coal plants by 2030.
Javier Valdez, a well-known Mexican journalist who has long reported drug dealers and gangsters, was convicted on Tuesday of murder by masked gunmen in the street and faces up to 50 years in prison for the murder of Juan Francisco Picos Berrueta.
Valdez is the founder of the investigative reporting publication Riodoce, which has long reported on drug dealers and gangsters, and was awarded the International Press Freedom Award in 2011 by the Committee to Protect Journalists.
His killing in 2017 drew international attention to the safety of journalists in Mexico.
The indictment alleges that Lopez Serrano, the son of a drug dealer, was outraged by Riodoce ’ s criticism and ordered Valdez ’ s assassination.
Beroda and another gunman, Luis Idelfonso Sanchez, shot and killed Valdez outside his office.
Berruda, who is considered the main culprit at trial, denies the charges and will later be sentenced to a maximum of 50 years in prison.
The driver, who drove the two men on the same day, was sentenced to 14 years and eight months in prison in February last year. Serrano was charged with the purchase of a homicide and the supply of a weapon, but denied the charges.
NEW YORK (AFP) Two eagles, one of the rare pieces of the U.S. Statue of Liberty, sold at auction in New York on Tuesday for a record $18.9 million, nearly double the previous record.
Auction house Sotheby ’ s noted that this rare 1933 “double eagle ” coin is the most valuable coin ever auctioned, and this is the second time it has set an auction price record.
The pair was last sold in 2002 for $7.6 million (HK $59.28 million).
On one side of the coin is a Statue of Liberty and on the other is a flying eagle with a face value of US $20 (HK $155).
It has never been in circulation, and almost all of the gold coins have been returned to the U.S. government and melted.

title: Japan ’ s new white paper says women ’ s employment situation is not good under the epidemic
text:
Newsfrom Japan (Kyodo News, June 11) On the 11th, the Japanese government finalized the 2021 edition of the White Paper on the Joint Participation of Men and Women, which analyzes the impact of COVID-19 on women.
The White Paper highlights that female informal workers, who are mainly in the service industry, are particularly hard hit when it comes to hiring, which is known as the “women ’ s situation ”.
In addition, previously hidden problems such as the plight of single parents and poverty have surfaced. The White Paper points out that “the slow progress of women and men ’ s participation in society ”.
According to the Ministry of General Affairs Labor Force Survey, the number of employed men (seasonally adjusted) decreased by 390,000 in April 2020, when the first emergency declaration was issued, while the number of women decreased by 700,000.
It is reported that women are more likely to work in service industries, such as accommodation and catering, living and entertainment, where the situation is dire during the pandemic, and the proportion of informal employees is also high, so they are more affected than men.
The impact of the epidemic on parents of single-parent families is particularly significant.
According to a survey by the Labor Policy Research and Training Institute, which asked about life trends at the end of last year, 60.8% of single-parent parents said life was difficult, and 35.6% said they had been unable to afford the food they needed in the past month.
The number of female suicides in 2020 was 7,026, an increase of 935 from the previous year.
The number of domestic violence (DV) consultations in 2020 also increased to about 1.6 times the number of consultations in the previous year.
In addition, the number of sexual violence, sexual crimes counseling also increased to about 1.2 times, according to the analysis of its background in the epidemic life instability and increased stress.

title: How can Africa, which has no four seasons but a short rainy season, ensure its precious water resources?
text:
The Osbo Sahara Desert spans Africa and is even larger than the United States!
In recent days, Taiwan is experiencing a severe drought, and for a long time, there has been insufficient rainfall, and the water supply has begun to tighten, making everyone once again concerned about the problem of global extreme weather.
Extreme weather is caused by global warming, which is caused by greenhouse gas emissions.
If so, African countries are the world ’ s worst industrialised, and economic activity is still dominated by primary industries, emitting far less carbon dioxide than developed and developing countries, yet Africa is suffering from extreme weather.
The general impression of Africa is that the climate is dry, in addition to the tropical rainforests of the Congo Basin, most of the region is dry and rainy wilderness and desert, the Sahara Desert is synonymous with the desert on the earth, covering more than 10 countries in North Africa, East Africa, West Africa and Central Africa, the total area is larger than the 50 states of the United States combined.
Photo Credit: Global warming has shortened the rainy season of six months, leaving less than three months to preserve precious water resources. In a vast desert of artificial lake reservoirs in Africa, a record drought has been set for several years without any rain.
Areas with more rain, or rivers flowing through them gradually formed tribes with concentrated populations, and developed into cities that became later capitals, such as Ngamena in Chad and Niamey in Niger, which were large cities in the desert, like large oases.
Where these populations are concentrated, water resources are very precious, rainfall is scarce, and the use is large.
The solution that the local government can think of is to set up a reservoir, literally a reservoir, but at best it is an artificial lake, providing water storage when the rainy season comes, that is all, and the rest of the flood control, power generation, irrigation... and other systems are very rare in Central and West Africa.
Photo Credit: English Island Even if there is artificial lake water storage, it can not solve the situation of annual rainfall There are no four seasons in Africa, only the "two seasons" of dry season, in the face of high temperatures above 40 degrees, large evaporation, artificial lakes are commonplace; many rivers, there are seasonal changes, there is water flow in a few months of the year, and the other months are dry.
In addition, many roads are seasonal, and the local map will see roads with dotted lines, indicating that there are several months of dry season, vehicles can walk, and when the rainy season comes, the road becomes a riverbed.
If you rush in during the rainy season, the end may be that the vehicle is trapped in the mud, and you need to ask the trailer or the villagers to collectively push the car out.
The local landscape also changes greatly with the season. The same location, the scenery of the dry season and the scenery of the rainy season will make people feel different from the country.
During the rainy season, the sky is cloudy, the land is green, the shrubs grow higher than people, and the original bald wilderness has become small lakes everywhere, and farming and animal husbandry are also thriving.
The climate is getting wet and cool, and whether you see photos or live in the area, it will not make you think of Africa, which is very different from the general stereotype of Africa.
In the French-speaking regions of Central and West Africa, the rainy season has a unique word "hivernage", in their vocabulary, there is no spring, summer, autumn and winter, but the dry season and the rainy season.
Photo Credit: The extreme climate of the English speaking island has intensified, and major floods in West Africa have become more frequent but in recent years, the dry season and rainy season, which are already quite polarized, have become even more extreme, and the dry season is getting longer and longer, and no matter how many artificial lakes are built, it can not cope with the long-term consumption of domestic water and a large amount of natural evaporation.
The rainy season is getting shorter and shorter, so short that it is no longer enough to support one round of cultivation a year.
Ideally, the first rain falls around mid-April each year and lasts until the last rain in October, with enough time for the rice seeds to spike and the crops to be harvested.
But in recent years often wait until June to look forward to the first rain, and then August, September rains gradually scarce, a large number of cultivated crops in the final stage of fruit, due to lack of water and poor harvest, food shortage problem, because the rainy season shortened and floated again on the table.
During the short rainy season, the rainfall is becoming more and more uneven, often without rain for several days, and it is a series of rainstorms.
In Central and West African countries, flood prevention facilities are very limited. Not every road has drainage ditches on either side. A rainstorm can make a road accumulate water everywhere, and vehicles and pedestrians can not get through.
If there is heavy rain for the next few days, water disasters are also very common.
During the 2020 rainy season, from mid-August to early September, Niger in West Africa dropped heavy rains for several weeks, and the entire capital, Niamey, was soaked in muddy water.
The urban development conditions of Niamey are excellent in West Africa, with the Niger River flowing through, non-seasonal rivers, which can irrigate and regulate the amount of water.
But increasingly uneven rainfall has led to more frequent floods in Niger in recent years, and last year the disaster was unprecedented.
Photo Credit: Is the English language island a miracle or a disaster, where the snow falls in the desert?
In addition to heavy rains and floods, extreme weather has brought snowfall to Africa.
For example, there are more than a dozen words in Icelandic for different types of snow, and most of the hundreds of dialects in West Africa do not have the word snow. Some dialects only borrow the French pronunciation of snow "neige", which is not a word of their own language.
Even if the word is in the language, most of the local people do not know what snow is.
In normal climates, the only mountains to see snow on the African continent are the mountains, and the summit of Mount Gilimazaro, the highest mountain in Africa, is covered with snow all year round.
Snow on the top of the mountain and wild animals racing on the grasslands under the mountain have become the most representative scenery postcard in East Africa.
But snowfall on flat ground, even in extremely dry desert areas, is very unusual. In January 2018, Algeria dropped 40 centimeters of snow overnight in Aïn Séfra, a small city in the Sahara Desert, and the yellow sand was mixed with snowflakes of silver, which did not look like a picture on Earth.
Photo Credit: English Island In the face of worse climate change, no one is an outsider in the world. Earlier this year, a heavy snow fell again in the same area because of the cold and wet air from the Mediterranean. Although the sun will immediately melt by the high temperature, but when the local people wake up early in the morning, they see the familiar yellow desert turned into a silver carpet. The pages of many international newspapers.
In addition to Algeria, Chad and Libya border, Tunisia and Egypt have also seen records of sudden snow in previously hot desert areas.
In Central and West Africa, where temperatures are high and humidity are low, heavy rain and snow are unimaginable.
However, under the trend of extreme weather affecting the world, Africa is also difficult to escape the impact of climate change.
Climate issues don ’ t have borders, and the world ’ s population is in the same boat.
African countries with lower levels of development and lack of infrastructure are also more likely to be victims of climate disasters.

title: UN Climate Report: Warming Causes Drought, Hunger Threatens Human Health - Technology
text:
A warming planet has a major impact on human health, with hunger, drought and disease afflicting tens of millions of people over decades, according to a draft report released by the United Nations today.
After more than a year of pandemics that have completely turned the world upside down, the forthcoming report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) offers even more dire predictions of malnutrition, water scarcity and plague in the coming decades.
Policy choices such as the promotion of plant-based diets can limit these health consequences, but many will remain unavoidable in the short term, the report said.
Babies born today may face a variety of climate-related health threats before they reach the age of 30, depending on how well humans handle carbon emissions and rising temperatures, according to the report.
The 4,000-page draft report, expected to be released next year, is the most complete report yet on the impact of climate change on the planet and species.
The report estimates that 80 million more people are at risk of hunger by 2050 than today.
The report estimates that disruptions to the water cycle will reduce harvests of rain-fed staple crops in sub-Saharan Africa.
As many as 40% of India ’ s rice-producing areas are unsuitable for farming.
Rising temperatures not only affect crop yields, but also reduce nutritional values, such as rice, wheat, barley and potatoes, by 6% to 14%, the report said, adding that the number of people at risk of protein deficiency is nearly 150 million more than today.
Food prices are expected to rise by as much as a third in 2050 as climate change reduces crop yields and increases demand for biofuel crops and carbon dioxide-absorbing forests, increasing the number of low-income households facing chronic hunger by 183 million.
Across Asia and Africa, the number of undernourished and stunted children by the middle of the century will increase by 10 million, creating a new generation of better socioeconomic development, but lifelong health problems.
As with most climate change impacts, the impact on human health varies from place to place, with 80% of the population at risk of hunger living in Africa and Southeast Asia, according to the report.
According to the report, studies on freshwater supply, agriculture and sea level rise show that between 30 million and 140 million people will be displaced in Africa, Southeast Asia and Latin America by 2050.

title: On the Rise of the Land Value Economy, South Koreans Go to the Land for Plastic Surgery - Cross-Strait
text:
In the past, many people chose to go to Korea to do medical and aesthetic surgery, but with the rise of the mainland's "face value economy", more capital is invested in the medical and aesthetic industry, and technology is constantly upgrading, people in the mainland industry said that in the past two years, it has attracted a lot of Korean and Japanese people to the mainland for plastic surgery.
The search for the keyword "medical beauty" in the "small red book" of the mainland beauty consumption app, the related information is more than 950,000 articles, and the product is more than 200 items.
A large number of handsome men and women carefully share the beauty process in the Little Red Book, and with the rise of the face value economy, plastic surgery seems to no longer be a thing to hide.
Park Yongbaht is a Korean who works in the mainland. As a translator, Park Yongbaht has worked and lived in the mainland for five years, not only proficient in Chinese, but also social software such as WeChat, TikTok and Little Red Book.
He said that the first two years of coming to the mainland, will regularly fly back to Korea to do medical beauty, but the time cost and transportation costs are very high, some medical beauty projects need to be done regularly, if time is not allowed, it will be missed, which has a great impact on the effect.
However, Park Yongbah said, now without this worry, after learning about the mainland plastic surgery institutions through social platforms, he ended the troubled experience of land and Korea.
In his opinion, the instruments in the mainland hospitals are better than the general clinics in South Korea, he said: "The hot magi instruments in this plastic surgery hospital I chose are the latest generation, and some clinics in South Korea use the original instruments, and the prices are similar, so I do it in the mainland."
Another Korean girl, Hua Mei-yan, went to the mainland two years ago for a rhinoplasty surgery. She was attracted by a Korean doctor molding case of a Sino-Korean cooperative institution through the Internet, and came to the mainland specifically to find the Korean doctor, but was finally "ring powder" by the mainland doctor, she said: "After I came to the mainland, the surgery is the Korean doctor and a knife, the result is very nice."
In addition to Koreans, there are also Japanese people to do cosmetic surgery in the mainland, and Hezi is one of them. In 2019, Hezi learned that the liposuction technology of a plastic surgery hospital in Sichuan in mainland China is not worse than Japan through a branch established by a mainland cosmetic institution in Japan.
Once went to Korea to form a kind of craze, spawned a hundred billion scale plastic market for South Korea.
This frenzy has faded with the rise of China ’ s nominal economy and increasing reports of detention for trans-national rights violations under South Korean law.
At the same time, more and more Koreans, Japanese, and foreign students are going to the mainland for plastic surgery.
Du Xiaoyan, deputy secretary general of the China Plastic and Cosmetic Association, once said in a public forum that, unlike the annual increase of 10-15% in the plastic surgery failure rate from the mainland to Korea, the failure rate of foreign plastic surgery to the mainland is almost zero.
At the same time, it also reflects the progress of medical and aesthetic technology in the mainland, and the development of the medical and aesthetic industry in the mainland is gradually recognized by the industry.
Zhou Jie, market leader in the southwest region of China's New Oxygen Technology, said that although South Korea is a world-famous "cosmetic country", there have been many negative reports about Korean cosmetic surgery.
South Korean doctors are more bold, some doctors dare to do anything, so there are many disputes, compared to the next, mainland cosmetic doctors are more cautious.
More importantly, after the influx of capital into the medical and aesthetic industry in these two years, the once small medical and aesthetic clinics are gradually evolving, and medical conditions are gradually improving, and medical facilities and other conditions are much better than the small institutions on the street in Korea.
Gan Cheng, deputy director of plastic surgery at the Plastic Surgery Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, also said that the theory, technology and operation level of the top doctors in mainland China are not fundamentally different from that of the top doctors in South Korea, and they are basically on an equal footing in the international academic circle.
However, it is undeniable that there are still some drawbacks in mainland medical beauty, such as opaque fees, immature technology of small institutions, exaggerated propaganda, etc., but it is certain that the mainland medical beauty industry is in a period of rapid development, rapid development of technology, high transparency and standardization of the industry is attracting more and more consumers.

title: A major accident at the Tour de France, the driver crashed into a car because of a fueling plate.

title: The Tour de France has a massive rollover! White spectators hit the competitors with a slogan and caused a disaster - Sports
text:
Cyril Lemoine of France was forced to withdraw from the race due to injuries. (Reuters) - In a series of car accidents in the first stage of the Tour de France, a spectator approached the track with a sign, and one of the competitors, Tony Martin, crashed into the sign and overturned due to the very crowded track at the start.
After Martin fell to the ground, he stumbled over more competitors, and from the perspective of the sky, a large group of competitors in the second half of the track all fell!
GREAT TO SEE SPECTATORS BACK INVOLVED IN SPORTS EH pic.twitter.com / Kwxj8be2Qh — Timothy Burke (@ bubbaprog) June 26 2021 The worst Tour de France crash I've ever seen pic.twitter.com / 1jngQE1Yg — daniel (@ cyclingreporter) June 26 2021 The spectator quickly fled after the “hit-and-run ”, with a cardboard sign reading“ Allez Opi-Omi! ”, the first meaning “Go ” in French, and the second meaning“ Grandparents ” in German, presumably a greeting to Grandpa and Grandma.
From this, it seems that this person is not deliberately sabotaging, but is an eyewitness.
Germany ’ s Jasha Sütterlin and France ’ s Cyril Lemoine were injured and some were forced to withdraw.
The Tour de France official tweeted: “We are delighted that the spectators are back on the road, but we hope that everyone respects the safety of the athletes and does not pose a danger for taking photos or snatching TV footage! ”
The organiser, Christian Prudhomme, decided to sue the white spectator, speculating that he was German, but he was no longer seen.

title: Water shortage threatens 40% of irrigated crops after 20 years ｜ News ｜ Americas ｜ on.cc
text:
The World Resources Institute (WRI), a think tank, said on Monday (25) that water shortages could endanger 40% of the world ’ s irrigated crops by 2040, threatening the global food crisis.
Climate change is causing erratic rainfall, threatening a third of crops that rely on water during the rainy season, according to the World Resources Institute.
According to the scientific team, water supply is affected by multiple factors, including climate change and poor management, but agriculture is one of the biggest factors, accounting for 70% of fresh water. WRI also found that nearly 67% of wheat, 64% of corn and 19% of rice in many irrigated crops could be under extreme water stress by 2040.
Rutger Hofste, a staff member at the Institute, said: “Humans don ’ t understand how to react before a crisis occurs. We understand crisis management, but we need to have a strong response. ”
He also reminded that this is a silent crisis, and that humanity must act with caution before it is too late.
